reviews.comment: well-intentioned professor, but the course is just not very professionally managed. Quiz questions are often ill-defined and highly subjective, requiring students to guess what he wants. Too much focus on memorizing the specifics of the (ancient and cryptic) xv6 teaching OS rather than understanding general and useful OS concepts.

Really hard to learn in this class. For how hard the material was, the organization of the class could have been way better. The average exam scores were around 50%, but you only need around a 30% to pass. I felt a little let down because I really liked Computer Systems.

Lectures were disjointed. Assignment/quiz publishing and grading were sporadic and inconsistent. Auto-graders took weeks to publish and frequently had bugs. Attendance was graded using poorly written, ill-defined poll questions. Assignments contained many typos. Overall, the course felt disorganized and poorly run.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Big letdown, I was really excited for this class. Lectures & slides were incredibly convoluted. Plays "guess what I'm thinking" all the time in lectures. Midterm average was a 40/70 due to a failure to effectively teach the content. You will not learn much in this class, but you will spend a lot of time studying. Also grading is really weird/slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
I took Fall 2022. 

He's a super reachable professor, always on discord to answer questions. His expectations for the class are VERY skewed. He expects students to comprehend things that are not reasonable for the level of the class. I feel like I learned nothing from the lectures because of how much he ranted. He was very generous with the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Anton is a super nice guy. He tries hard to help students succeed, he's active in Discord, and extends deadlines. But he's super disorganized and has no grasp of what sophomore CS students do and don't know. Get ready for tons of rambling about Rust and x86. I only passed because of Rajeev Balusabramonian's videos, the textbook, and extra credit.

He is a very understanding professor and extended due dates on many occasions. Prioritizes making sure students learned. The tests were reasonable and overall shouldn't be worried taking this class with him.

Anton seems like a great guy, but this class was not organized nor tought well. Most of the class had to refer to outside lectures (youtube rajeev balasubramonian). Tests felt seperated from homework / lecture materials so they pretty little tricky. However, Anton did curve tests and provide a good amount of extra credit and extended due dates.

Anton struggled with setting expectations for this class. 

The homework was very easy, but the exams were very difficult and often presented material we hadn't seen before.

His lectures were very hard to follow, and many of my peers and I relied on a previous professor's lectures on YouTube.

I feel very unprepared for CS 4400 after this class.

He was very nice, always extending due dates and giving extra credit. But the downside is that his lectures are difficult to grasp, and his tests are extremely difficult (but graded very leniently). He assumes the student knows a lot more than they actually do. I'm sure he'll be better in the following semesters, as this was his first time.

Dr. Burtsev is a professor that really cares about you succeeding. His first time teaching this course was somewhat disorganized, but he is extremely knowledgeable on the subject and provides students many opportunities to succeed. Exams are somewhat hard, but he curves, provides a large amount of extra credit, and is passionate about the subject.

Don't let the other ratings scare you, as long as you show up to class and participate in the lectures like a regular student should you will be totally fine. Tests are super easy, like passing with 95% easy, and if you can read her dry humor and sarcasm you might actually laugh a little and have fun during the class. Go into it with an open mind!
The class itself is pretty easy if you pay attention to the lectures (which are sometimes very boring). Tests are very easy, just do your homework and participate as much as possible.
A really good teacher. She cares about her students succeeding. Ran like an interactive highschool class. Tough grader, make sure to raise your hand and study for exams.

Dr Vashist is incredibly passionate about the content she teaches. She has an impressive background in the industry and is very knowledgeable. This class is participation and attendance based and you take out of it what you put into it. She does not put up with disrespectful behavior and fosters a safe space for students to learn.

If you want to feel like you are in a middle school classroom and get snarky comments because you are maybe two minutes late this is the professor for you. Has pre class reading, small notecard assignments for attendance in class activities that make you think why you pay so much for a class like this. Find another way to get this credit

Can for sure get good credit, just isn't a fun class to attend. 1/3 of the tests are questions using readings from textbook. 
Feels like a Highschool class/teacher, uses name tags, tries to run the class room like she isn't dealing with adults and more of kids that are being forced to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I haven't even had her for a week yet and I can already confirm that all the negative reviews are true. She is very condescending and is extremely repulsive in her mannerisms. She is a professor but makes it difficult to merit the respect all professors deserve because of how unreasonably unforgiving she is for an easy class.

Repetitive content which becomes evident when you view the slides provided on Canvas for each day's lecture. Really unforgiving when it comes to.. about everything. Do not expect grace from her. The course content isn't difficult: it's the professor, environment, and expectations that are. Try to find another offering with a different professor.

Extremely strict participation grading, unforgiving of absences unless a doctor's note which really hurt my grade because I got the stomach flu for a week. Did not have grades visible in the cavas module and had to check registrar at the end of the semester to see how I did. She is the ONLY professor that's grade section was hidden.

The professor holds grades hostage, so you have to play a guessing game to determine whether you passed the class or not. The TA is absolutely useless, will just give you 3/10 on assignments for no reason and no explanation. Also, this class is an absolute snoozefest; I almost lost my mind about ten times this semester from how boring it is.
terrrible. course..... experience...........
This course does not show your grade so you don't know where you are at.
Grades are never public. IF you think you're going to get an A think otherwise.
Not a great class if you don't like repetitive lectures.
Horrible…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class and the content was repetitive and just generally uninteresting and she definitely didn't help with that. The TA was useless and would pretty much give you a bad grade on "Thought Essays" no matter what you did and with no feedback. Don't class this class from her if you have the option.
If you don't like a lecture heavy class that isn't interesting. I would not recommend this professor.

TA needs to rework the feedback a little bit because they form assumptions in order to make you lose a point or two even if the work is turned in on time. It will be difficult to get a 10/10 on a thought essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't get fooled by the criteria even if it says under 500 words. IT IS NOT under 500 words. The TAs and the syllabus do not make it clear that it has to be 500 minimum. Beware when writing your thought essays for this professor.
The feedback received on the assignments aren't as good as expected. They also take sooo long to grade.
Grade is not shown. Has favoritism towards specific students.
Long lectures. A lot of it will be repetitive.

The class is a daily information dump, with lectures the entire class period every single time the class meets. She's a harsh grader, and zooms through lectures so fast it's hard to take notes or ask questions. Grades are unviewable throughout the semester, so you have absolutely 0 idea what your grade is or where you need to improve.

Entire class is straight monologue. Grades? Held hostage. You basically turn in your work and pray. It's like academic roulette. The TA is awful. Literally wrote notes that said nothing, corrected nothing, and yet somehow STILL managed to take points off. The exams are literal hieroglyphics.

Lectures are very boring and repetitive, withholds the class grade until the end of the semester, ta's grading assignments give bad grades without any feedback and her tone in class can make it hard to ask questions.

I understand why people dislike her. The class material is definitely opinionated, the TA graded very poorly and was just weird, and exams were very tricky—every question almost seems like there's no "right" answer. Overall, the class was pretty easy.
bad professor lowers your grade based on assumptions. Treats you terribly. Rigs exams. treats other nationalities as the worse.
awful lectures, repetitive.

She is a pretty good professor. She is passionate about her content, but the lectures can get repetitive sometimes, and it is easy to get distracted. She definitely likes certain students and dislikes certain students, so get on her good side early. Lots of reading for homework, but most of it is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, the class is easy and she makes things clear. She lets you use notes for the tests and helps guide you to make good notes. Participation is mandatory but it's nothing hard, she was never rude to me and was overall kind.

She's chill as a person, and doesn't assign lots of work; the only essays you will write have a word cap of 500. Your participation in class does matter, and if you are on your phone or doing anything on your computer, you will get docked points. 

I think most of the hate comes from the course itself being pretty buns and the content being vague
Does not care at all and very rude

I liked the class, don't understand the hate. There was hardly any work except very simple essays, the exams were a little messed up but curved heavily. The participation boosted the grade heavily at the end. I thought the lectures were extremely interesting.

First of all, I highly encourage you to not read the 5 star reviews. I know multiple students she has cooerced to give a good rating, and she definitely has favorites she treats better. she grades slowly, poorly, and does not provide feedback of use (same for everyone). She is also punitive, discriminatory,& rude, which is odd for an ethics class.

This professor is rough! Lectures are boring and VERY repetitive. An ethics class is already unnecessary, but her teaching style made it worse. The tests were confusing, and presentation grading was broad. No connection with students, and came across condescending at times. Was excited for this class at the beginning, now happy it's over!!

This wasn't my favorite class but the professor made it interesting. She's energetic and funny and always available to help. To get a good grade you just have to go to class and do the assignments. The tests are petty easy if you study.

One of the worst professors I've had. Her classes were so uninteresting and irrelevant. The content of the class itself isn't difficult, it is her that designs the exams to trick you into getting questions wrong. Also, if you have the misfortune of taking her make sure to refer to her as Dr. or Prof. in your emails, or she will crash out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why she has bad reviews, But she really is an amazing professor, she gives out reasonable amount of homework and going to class matters because it is a discussion based class. I went to her office hours to review my exams, which helped a lot, and she really seemed to care about my success.

Those complaining about Professor Vashist are probably the ones in the class who are not working hard or paying attention.  This professor gives us everything we need to succeed, but you must do the work.  I enjoyed this professor and the class.  The topics are interesting, and it's taught in a way that's easy to understand.

Professor Aditi is not as bad as the course itself. MGT 1030 just sucks, but she doesn't help make it any better. She is extremely harsh with participation (if you miss more than 3 classes, your grade will drop significantly). Every class is usually just her talking at you and her review sessions are not helpful at all. She is not a great teacher.

I really don't understand the hate for Professor Vashist. The class was super easy if you did the reading and the essays. As long as you show up to class and do the bare minimum you will be fine. There is a considerable amount of reading that comes with this class but it's super easy and you can get away with not doing it to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I have ever had in my educational experience. A little hard to explain all of the bad things about the class, but it just goes to show how annoying this class was. Exams are made to trick you, participation matters more than most assignments, and the class is overall unenjoyable. MGT 1030 should not be this difficult.

She annoyed me a lot. Almost got an A-, but she didn't want to give us any extra credit or anything . Wouldn't ever take again, but we were able to have a double sided sheet on all exams tho, barely helped with her exams
By far the worst professor I have ever had. Tests are designed to trick you. The curve was the only reason anyone passed the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you're just looking for an easy A, you probably won't like her. She's pretty straightforward and has high expectations, but she's super helpful if you actually want to learn. Just show up to class and pay attention to the slides!
Worst class I've ever taken, structure sucks, and tests are strictly made to trick you into getting the wrong answer. This Business Ethics class should not be harder than accounting.

Professor Aditi is great. She's the only teacher from my first semester who actually seemed to care about teaching and whether students learned anything. Exams are not simple, but having a cheat sheet was super useful. Going to office hours helped a lot!! She even scheduled extra time with me when I couldn't make the regular office hours.
Professor Vashist is really smart and direct. Exams are hard, but she really wants students to succeed and helped us to do better and was flexible about curving the exams that were hardest.

I had a hard time with this professor. Her grading system was awful and made absolutely no sense. Feedback on assignments was worthless. I would get feedback such as "Great Job!" and receive a 9/10 every time. Tests were so confusing and no one understood. I did all the readings and attended every lecture but still struggled on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Many struggled with her teaching style, but I appreciated how it pushed me to engage deeply with the material. I did well by staying on top of readings and focusing on understanding concepts. For tests, review PowerPoint slides and take detailed notes—precision and exact definitions matter. It's challenging, but the effort is worth it!
Single handedly made my first semester in college unlikeable. Should never be allowed to teach again, let alone to first years.

Everyone in my class despised her but I loved the topics/teaching. Ended up doing well bc I spent time doing the readings and trying to conceptualize. For tests copy EVERYTHING from ppt slides on sheet. Questions are specific & wording/exact definitions matter. If you are willing to work it can be beneficial but it definitely is not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not understand your situation when you reached out, and do not care.

This course was unnecessarily difficult for the material we were given. 3-hour lectures were often unbearable with how strict she was in regard to talking, even during sanctioned collaboration time with our tables. Exams guides were misleading. Repetitive lectures, harsh gradings, and condescending professor is a recipe for disaster.

Professor Vashist knew the topic she was teaching well and seemed knowledgeable. But when it came to teaching it she made it unnecessarily difficult to earn a good grade and understand the subject. Assignments were graded harshly and tests seemed to be made to trick students. Rivaled the difficulty of my calculus class. Avoid if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take this class if you want to listen to her lecture for 3 hours straight. Essays every other week that are never given more than a 90%. Exams are hard and she gives participation assignments every class that are worth 30% of your grade. Endless podcasts and way too much reading from the textbook.

this was literally the most unnecessarily hard class I have ever taken. There was absolutely no reason for an ethics class to rival my math classes. She doesn't give out 100%, only 90%. and as someone who usually does good on tests, I could never get above an 80. curved.

She is not a bad professor, but she can be rude and condescending. She gave us one of our exam study guides four hours before the exam. Get ready to read a lot and listen to many podcasts and documentaries. Also weekly short essays that can be graded in a way that is almost impossible to get full points. Overall don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The homework and quiz load is manageable. He seems like a nice professor, but the assignments don't leave much room for feedback. Exams can be difficult and can, at times, seem worded in another way compared to the notes. The material of the class is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A very chill class. Pro. Anderson made sure I understood the concept when I had a question. Kind enough to take the time to help.
Genuinely one of my favorite classes. I looked forward to each day, excited to sit down and watch Geology videos and learn about the Earth. It was like a break from my other classes.
Super easy class, he is super kind and on top of everything each week. Very clear insturctions.
Funnest easiest class for credit (fills two different degree requirements btw) I can get the whole weeks work done during my lunch break
Super easy to skim. Same thing every week: geology assignment and a culture quiz. Exams are also pretty easy. Content is pretty cool. Lenient late policy.

The class has two pretty easy canvas quizzes per week equating to at most an hour of homework, there are also two readings that he posts each week, for the most part thses can be skimmed to get the material for the quiz and videos can be plays on 2x speed although most of the videos are under 10 minutes. The material is also very interesting.

The assignments were not that hard, but the directions were often unclear or outlined only pieces of the expectations Andrea actually had for her students. There was always something wrong with my work, it was never good enough for her standards, turning a class that could have been very fun and impactful into an anxiety-inducing class of busy work
does not grade anything until the very last week of classes, final grades are due in a day and 4 major assignments have still not been graded.

Worst, toughest, and latest grader. I have stuff from February and January not graded yet (it's the end of April). If you can avoid this class, I would. The content is really interesting, but there is so much of it, and I feel it's a lot of work for only a 3-credit class.

Professor Stark has yet to grade assignments that were submitted over two months ago. She simply reads off the lecture slides are rarly gives deeper insight into the topic she is covering, unless it pertains to dancing. Clearly does not put much effort into the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is not good at her job. She does not respond to emails. She doesnt grade anything until the end of the semester so you have 0 clue if you are going to pass or fail. I would really not recommend taking her class

. don't take any of her classes she sets you up for failure, grades are never posted on time, and she literally DOES NOT RESPOND TO EMAILS. 

PLEASE FIRE HER UTAH
Please don't take a class with her.

She sets students up for failure. Failure as a professor, failure as a mentor, and failure as a leader. The U emphasizes student success but allows someone as toxic as her to be in charge of a course that is REQUIRED by students to take. The negative reviews are all by students who have experienced this toxicity. Do your best to navigate through it

We were told we would get site selections a month before school starts and we just got them about two weeks before the start of the semester. Not only did we just get informed of mandatory community outreach times but they are all on the same two days which she never warned us about. She expects you to have a fully open schedule to accommodate her.

NEVER take her class AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS! She was the worst professor I have ever experienced. she did not grade anything and her expectations were unclear. when she finally would grade 1/2 way through the semester telling us our weekly assignments were wrong. She doesn't care about you or the CEL, she only cares about getting paid.

Worst teacher I have ever had, even though she is a psychology teacher, she is unfair and mentally abusive towards students, she causes so much stress and anxiety that I would get stomach cramps just thinking about going to class and dealing with her. Dont make the same mistake I did, she is a TOUGH grader, to her, you are always wrong.

I really enjoyed this class and still refer to the information I learned. If you work through the study guide a couple times and really conceptualize the information, you will do amazing on the tests! Her tests are literally the study guide which is so nice. I thought the content was super interesting and she was good at explaining everything!

Her disregard for students' well-being and her disrespectful attitude make her unfit to teach at University. It is my sincere hope that the administration takes appropriate action to address these issues and ensures that students are provided with a safe and supportive learning environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stark's teaching style has caused me significant stress and anxiety this semester, leading to two emergency room visits. I strongly advise against enrolling in any courses taught by her. She is  the worst professor I have ever had. Her behavior is unacceptable and has no place in a university setting.

If you at all have the choice and care about your grade-do not take Stark. She is the most difficult teacher I've had in college. The course material is not too hard and the homework load is very manageable. Incredibly slow grader. Grades everything very harshly-you can know everything on her tests and still somehow get a C.

Do not take a class with her, unless you do not want to learn concepts and applications. If you want to memorize research papers, and still fail all of the exams then go ahead. You have several group assignments with short time frames, and everything is graded beyond harshly. The exams are open response and she will dock point unnecessarily.

Stark needs to be fired. She makes lectures harder than they actually need to be. She'll also take until the end of the semester to grade assignments from two months prior, will take off points on tests even though they could have correct answers, and does not care about her students. Not worth it. Take Exercise Psychology with Nick Galli instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For a professor teaching a course on psychology, she has little to no concept of what the word empathy means. She does not care about her students, their physical, or mental well-being despite lecturing on rates of mental illness are the highest they've ever been among college students. Completely unapproachable with vague at best grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Currently taking the class. While most of the information given in the lecture is common sense regarding exercise psychology, she lectures with such a condescending attitude it is mentally draining and demoralizing. No one in class participates; fearing that their comments will be shot down if they give a wrong answer.

This class was incredibly frustrating and difficult. None of the material is hard or difficult she just grades incredibly hard, she is looking for mistakes and it seems she has no desire for her students to do well. I would avoid taking this teacher if at all possible. She found a way to ruin an interesting topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For a teacher who absolutely will not accept late work for any reason, you would think that she would have the same respect for her student's time. It is a month past the end of the semester and unit 3 assignments are still not graded. Unacceptable for someone who cares so much about late work.

Getting an A in anatomy and physiology was easier than taking this class. The material is not hard, is actually painfully simple concepts that a kindergartner could understand but she grades so harshly that even a detailed, correct answer is not "correct enough". She grades to find fault, not to measure understanding.

Extremely harsh and non-understanding grading style complemented by the worst discussion/lecturing I have ever experienced in college. Put in maximum effort and just hope that you get the grade you deserve, but probably won't. Stark is opinionated when it comes to lecturing and has vague criteria for semester long assignments.

Stark is a nice person and the class was overall positive. However, she is not very specific when it comes to criteria and grades harshly for no reason. The worst thing is that on the last day of the semester, 3/36 assignments were graded...

Everything the other ratings mention are true. she has EXTREMELY specific requirements for assignments but makes no effort to be accessible to answer questions. This class will make you literally have a stomachache after turning in assignments b/c you don't know what kind of inconsequential points will be taken off and she grades on SO little
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Takes off tacky points for assignments that don't make sense, takes forever to grade, almost all of the homework is participation based and doesn't count towards anything, harsh grader, and nonaccommodating. The only somewhat good part is that everything you see on the exams is on the study guides, but even then, it has to be precise.

Terrible professor. Absolutely no help when you have questions for her. I'm about to graduate and have almost none of my grades in for this (KINES capstone course) class. Feels like you've done something wrong when you talk to her and she frequently talks in a very demeaning tone.

I'm a 2nd year in Kinesiology and this was the hardest course I've taken so far for a 3-credit class. Still hasn't graded major assignments or labs from the beginning of the year. TL;DR avoid taking her if you hate professors who don't grade until the last possible minute.

This class required a lot more effort for a 3 credit hour course. The papers were asking for too much. But I found it nice that the study guide was almost everything on exams. Lectures felt draining and confusing at times. Overall it wasn't too bad, you just have to set aside a lot of time if you want a good grade in this class.

I read all these "1"s coming in and expected the worst. She wasn't that bad, you just have to at least say something in lecture and that should count towards most of the "participation". Tests were literally the study guide given, and most of the answers were found in the book, with the rest being covered in lecture. Did take forever to grade tho.

Going along with about every other review on here, Stark is NOT good. Grades are due to be submitted to the university today (Dec 27) and a 100 point paper and 100 point final have not be graded. Stark is also not kind and hard to approach. Often times I found she responded to students in a demeaning tone, like she was trying to make us feed stupid

I did well in this class, but it required basically memorizing the study guide and I still only got around 90% on the exams. Professor Stark crams every lecture with information and lectures every class and all class long. She takes eons to grade things and is a very tough grader. I would NOT take this class again. Avoid Stark at all costs.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND STARK!! The only way to pass her class is if you memorize her study guide and answers word for word. She takes FOREVER to grade assignments and I didn't know my grade until the very last week of school. Not to mention she doesn't allow her TA to answer questions given on the study guide so we never know the correct answer.

DON'T TAKE FROM STARK. Her exams are actually insane and will cross out sentences and just put the word "psychology?". She teaches her own case studies and expects you to memorize hers plus a millions others. Her group projects and essays are just busy work. Take this class online from a different professor.

I'd recommend staying away from this professor. Prof. Stark goes far beyond expectations for what a 3 hour credit class should be like. She likes to cram a lot of lectures based on research articles that can be very difficult to comprehend, will take weeks or months to grade your assignments, and doesn't communicate very well with her students.

TL:DR; don't take. Andrea Stark does not teach, she just reads off her lecture sheets and expects you to memorize every minute detail. The test reviews are graded heavily and are not just for helping you study. You lose points if you don't show up for class every day. Papers are harshly graded long after submission.

Prof. Stark is the most difficult professor I have even worked with. When you ask questions or just want to clarify something, she tells you it is in the syllabus. Also, the site areas are far from the U so get ready to drive. I found her condescending and rude. Does not grade quickly. Discussions are so boring and the only class I dreamed at the U

I heard back from her 3 WEEKS later. She is AWFUL. She doesn't care about students. She is the worst professor I have ever had, hands down. Do not take a class from her, she doesn't know how to communicate or help students. She expects you to think the same way as her, even when you ask for help she has nothing to give.

AVOID PROFESSOR! She has unclear directions for assignments and then once she grades them she is mad that you didn't submit what she was looking for. The exams are all open ended questions based off a ton of different chapters in the textbook and is very specific about your answers. She takes forever to grade assignments and only reads from slides

Regardless of her personal attitude her class is simply too difficult given the material. She mostly grades off of "gotcha" questions or unnecessary details about obscure studies. Exercise psychology is basically "physical activity is good for your mental health" but she believes that this class should be hard in order to prove it's worthwhile.

I had an assignment worth 15% of my grade due, which I finished on time. I made some final adjustments and tried to submit 20 minutes before the deadline. My canvas was acting up and wouldn't let me submit, so I emailed her my assignment, proving it was done on time. She still wouldn't accept and gave me a zero, dropping my grade from an A to a C+.

She demands to much for a three credit course and never grades anything literally takes her more than a month to grade papers and we been out of school for a week and half now. The exams are too much. She wonders why the class average is bad is because her way of communicating and explaining things are horrible .Save yourself a mental breakdown.

The reviews on here for Andrea are too harsh. If you are looking for an easy A this isnt a class for you. Andrea gives you feedback on assignments, you have to click on your canvas assignment to see them. She challenges your thinking, and prepares your for careers and grad school. DO NOT PROCRASTINATE. She doesnt hold you hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I cannot say enough of how little I recommend this teacher. Honestly, I am not sure how she is even still a teacher. She just refers you to the syllabus and class schedule even if that is what you are trying to clarify. She does not extend to her students the same human decency and respect that she asks of them. I wish I could write more. HORRIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was my 2nd year at The U, and Stark is by far the worst professor Ive ever encountered. Taking her class was so bad I had to drop it. She was condescending and would get angry when students asked her a question or challenged her on a topic. She also gave out way too much assignments that were graded harshly. No idea how she still employed.

Exam content is not taught in in-class lectures. Exams are not true/false or multiple choice. Does not work with you if you have to miss the final due to something you could not have predicted. Takes FOREVER to grade assignments.
