Avery is an amazing professor you can honestly tell he loves what he is doing. He is always willing to help you out when you ask! Great class so glad I switched into his class I learned a lot!
Avery is the kind of professor who inspires you to do more. He gives us the tools we need and let's us create with them. Just a very nice guy who really cares about us.

Dr. Battaglia gives great lectures that cover basically all of the material, but he sometimes asks too many questions. His grading on homework is strict and it's hard to get 100% (their weight is also 30%). Midterms aren't bad and based off of the homework and are almost identical to the practice exams; the final also replaces the lowest midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are incredibly boring and barely anyone shows up to them. There is a project worth 10% of your grade but its not that hard. Lets you skip the final if your midterm grades are good enough.

Solid lectures and posted lecture slides to review or read if you missed class. The textbook was free, not mandatory, and helpful. Replied to emails quickly. His grading was pretty strict. It was very difficult to get A's on assignments. Instead of a final exam, there was a final group project which was not too bad.

Overall he was alright, he responded quickly to emails, accomidating, lectures were okay. The only issue most of us had was his extremely strict grading scheme. On tests you can have each step you do written out, but if not explained in words or you do it in a way he wouldn't have done it he would take 50-75% off for that problem.

He is a very tough grader; it is almost impossible to get a 100% on an assignment (2 out of 9 homeworks had a high score of 100). There is also a big final group project, but it isn't too bad. He strongly supports the TA's grading choices, so don't expect to get any points back for things that were graded incorrectly. He does have good lectures.

I was a nontraditional student who took a lot of courses from different departments. And I remember Dr. Barrios as being one of my favorites. He brings a lot of passion and curiosity to his field. Couldn't recommend him more.

Grade based on discussions, quizzes, 3 short written assignments, two exams and a final essay. Discussions and quizzes are pretty easy if you watch the lectures. Assignments are graded a little tough but not bad at all. If you watch the lectures you'll do fine. I think sometimes he adds more info that makes it a little overwhelming, but good overal

Class was structured in a easy to read manner. Grading and expectations were clear. Quiz and discussion each week, 2 exams, 3 papers (1 was a final paper done with a group). The lectures corresponded with what was expected on the quizzes and papers. Replied quickly when emailed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Barrios was one of the best professors I had at the University of Utah. His level of expertise is impressive, he structures his courses with a breadth that gives students a lot of opportunities to find what interests them the most, and his lectures are fun to attend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was a really good professor, but relies heavily on the readings. He was always available for questions and always gave feedback on discussions, quizzes and exams. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Barrios definitely knows his stuff but can sometimes overcomplicate things in his lectures, which are usually long. He gives more than enough time to complete assignments. He also gives good feedback if he can tell you're struggling and sets you up to pass by giving tons of practice quizzes and tests. Extra credit assignments are rough though.
He don't know how to grade assignment. You always lose scores for no reason. Thoung you read all the content he posted online, you will never pass the quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Barrios wasn't the best professor, not because he didn't try, but because his explanations weren't very helpful. The set up of the class was very clear, along with his grading criteria. His study guides were too broad for his very specific exams.  The class was interesting and there wasn't too big of a workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Barrios is an excellent professor. You will read a lot of material, and yes he will grade hard. However, if you show up to class, do the readings and ask questions to deepen your knowledge, then you will be successful with your papers. Barrios also gives really good/helpful feedback on assignments. If I could, I would take more of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Edison is very knowledgeable in the subject and uses very good examples to help students grasp the harder concepts. There is a lot of reading, some of which is difficult to grasp, but he always went over the material in class.
He is a good professor who wants you to take an active role in your learning and provides a clear path for that.

Edison is a nice guy, but he is very tough on grading and tests are the most important thing in the class and there are five of them. He doesn't often explain assignments well or mention due dates often. Don't get caught off guard. Overall he wasn't bad. Just not that good.
So bad.. like worst deal. Worthless class as well as instructor. Don't take it, it's not worth it

Sometimes unclear, but if you can ask a clarifying question you will always understand.  This is a professor who cares about his students and the subject. Be prepared to participate in class, it creates a better experience for everyone.

I was impressed by his knowledge of technical material; for example, when I asked him after class, he offhandedly explained how to construct a functionally complete set of logic gates from neural net nodes and weights. He also has a dry, witty sense of humor.

The subject material is tough and he's hard to understand and  whenever he asks questions in class only a handful of students reply . With that being said he teaches the material expertly and fosters discussion.  you get out of this class what you put in , if you expect him to spoon feed you dont , expect to get blown away day after day.

The worst philosophy teacher, I would not recommend him at all. Hes not helpful at all, very confusing on everything in the class. You will not pass. The response papers are only 4 points and he grades it like its your dissertation.  The term paper are worse. Not worth the headache. Trust me, our class started at 40 now its 12 !!

If you love philosophy he will make you hate it. His grading is tough, the comments are not helpful even if you were a writing major. Office hours suck,! Even one on one hes not helpful. I would not recommed this class to anyone, it will only hurt your gpa and you will walk away having learned nothing.

If you love philosophy he will make you hate it. His grading is tough, the comments are not helpful even if you were a writing major. I would not recommed this class to anyone, it will only hurt your gpa and you will walk away having learned nothing.

Barrios gave out four response papers. They are only worth 6 points each and are graded very strictly. He gave out pop quizzes which were also tough. His exam reviews had nothing to do with the actual exams and were very difficult. Your grade is based mostly off exams. Get ready to read everyday and pay attention to boring slides in class.
Bad subject, worse instructor

Not very clear about the assignments he gives us. His lectures are not clear and it's difficult to pay attention in his class. If you're up for a challenge and don't really care about your GPA, take it. Good luck!

Professor Barrios fumbled over the lecture material and was always disorganized.  He seemed flustered every lecture, was late more than once, and missed a lecture without informing the class of the cancellation.  I was so excited for this class, and ended up getting nothing from his teaching.  I was very disappointed.

He doesn't give clear answers, in class or outside of class when asked specific questions. He doesn't really know how to get to a clear point. Be prepared to read several pages every day. Quizzes, tests and participation make up the grade for the most part, beyond a couple short papers.
He honestly not hard to understand and will explain things until you understand them if you ask. He is also really available and willing to help.

I get that you have to participate in class but this guy literally forces you. The reading makes no sense his lectures are a bore  and you might drown in pop quizzes. Took my interest for philosophy and shattered it.

In this class, we pretty much just sat as he went through slides. I know a few people who fell asleep more than once during this class. He put all the readings online and asked some questions about them, but otherwise it was a very boring lecture, although he tried to make it more interesting. If you ask for feedback he will give it.

I went in to this class very interested in the topic but was very frustrated by the lectures, as they were confusing even after reading the given material. In addition, the study guides were not helpful and your grade is based almost entirely on your test scores. He was a nice professor but this methods were not effective for me at all.

Barrios is an interesting guy. He has a Latino accent and a very deep voice so you may find it helpful to sit at the front of the class to hear him better. The final grade was based on 2 exams, 2 papers, and several smaller writing assignments. Make sure you do the full reading every night or you'll be totally lost the next day. You'll learn a lot.
Didnt learn a single thing in this class. Attendance based. Tests are on canvas so chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He just mumbles and teaches himself. He also gets upset when you don't understand anything, and will tell you to read the book, which he doesn't even base most of the tests on. Only take him if you are good at teaching yourself or are already good at finance.

A relatively easy class, but the worst teacher. Class is graded on 4 simple exams and attendance, so a good grade is easy, but attendance is mandatory for every class, with a check-in and check-out at the end. His lectures consist of him mumbling simple, repeated info from old slides, split up by rambling personal stories or yelling at the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want an easy path to completing finance 2020 take his class. He's pretty chill, yaps the entire time. He grades based off attendance and exams. You wont learn much to about anything but exams are chill.
You won't learn a single thing about finance. Great time to nap between classes and you'll still get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very chill guy, not going to learn too much, but you will get an A if you show up.

From long, jumbled, and pointless (required) lectures to unaddressed changes in the curriculum this is one of the most painful classes I have ever taken. There is no structure, there is no teaching, and honestly this class was a major waste of time. Do not take this professor if you can help it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never prepared for class, doesn't know how to use technology, and can not teach material properly. Tests are hard, and no one knows how to solve problems because he can't teach the material.

Run. Please, save yourself. He doesn't know how to teach it (like AT ALL). Slides are cluttered and reused from 4 years ago. Test has nothing to do with what was "taught" in class. Had high hopes for the class but he effectively destroyed my hopes of getting anything meaningful out of it. Buddy truly doesn't care.

Professor seems very smart, however gives absolutely no direction on what you are supposed to do. Class is good practice and learning; however you will likely be completely lost throughout the duration of your presentations. Please do not take this :(

Dont take this class. Professor didn't change his syllabus dates from the fall, which is extremely confusing for exams. The exams are a lot of information. Got a TA and started grading attendance. During lectures, professor doesn't know how to use a mic so half the time you cant even hear him. During lectures its difficult to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 1/10 would not recommend. Didn't learn a thing from him, had to learn subject via the book and slides. He often goes on side lectures that aren't relevant to the actual course. Exams are poorly written and often have mistakes. Very boring lectures, he is constantly mumbling, yet he makes them mandatory. Don't take his class.

Definitely the worst professor in the Business School and maybe even the university. Canvas course wasn't published on the first day of class and syllabus had test dates from previous semester. Incoherent and mumbles while teaching his lectures. Tests are very hard and several questions had no correct answers. Yells at students in class frequently
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only leactures off the slides and barely goes through them. Also, he moves twice as fast as the other classes without actually teaching anything. 10/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He clearly has no interest in teaching for the betterment of the students. He is excited to leave every class and saves little time for questions both during class and at the end. He makes the claim that his class should reflect the real world and supplies no advice for success in the class. Suggesting figuring it out yourself. To recall one isssue
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Barely talks about material that is on exams. Expects students to just know how to do things without teaching them. He also has zero clue how to use canvas. If you want to be extremely lost and not be taught anything, take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know what he was doing during classes. He never talked about info that was on the exams. He also doesn't know how to really use tech or Canvas what so ever.
Is he really teaching. It's beyond boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson's lectures were amazing, engaging, and easy to follow. Homework is easy and consists of 10-20 questions, with unlimited attempts. He allows a page of notes on every exam, and allows 3 for the final. He is willing to help and went over my exams with me question by question, in office hours. Ended with an ~86, which curved to an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson was great overall, and I genuinely enjoyed his class. The tests are challenging but manageable with proper preparation. He conveys the material clearly and makes for a solid learning experience.

Super knowledgeable professor. He has enormous field experience. He introduces lots of cases when he was at work. Never reads the slides. Study hard and you should do fine on exams. This class is mostly dependent on exam scores. Beware of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff, and he makes it interesting. Exams are going to be difficult if you don't study, you'll prolly fail. He allows cheat sheets on the exams tho and outlines what's going to be on it. You can do better as a professor, but not by much.

THE BEST! While finance is not always fun, Prof Johnson did his part. Wonderful speaker and super knowledgable. His tests are challenging but he was helpful when it came to study guides and cheat sheets. The textbook is not necessary! Fav prof of the semester!!

Professor Johnson is a corporate finance expert who delivers a well-structured and organized course. For success - make sure to study the materials for quizzes, case studies, and exams. This class was one of the most impactful in terms of practical learning, providing valuable knowledge that I will apply in my future career prospects.

Professor Johnson is a great finance professor. He is knowledgeable in his field and can always answer any question you might have. His lectures are long and boring, but the information is easy to remember.

My biggest complaint about this class are the tests. SO DIFFICULT. They count towards a large portion of your grade, so there's very little cushion if you don't do well on an exam. The exam questions are MUCH harder than the homeworks. Know how to do every. Single. Claculation. that ever pops up in class or the textbook or the homeworks or get a 70
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is a very nice and smart guy. His class is interesting and his exams and assignments are very fair. The workload is very manageable and Professor Johnson is always willing to help. I had a very positive experience in this class and would recommend him to anyone!

Super nice caring professor that use to be the CFO of IBM Japan so he knows what he is talking about and relates lots of in class topics to real world stuff he had to deal with.  Not the hardest stuff in the world but you'll definitely need to study for his tests but everything you'll need to know is in the practice test.

Johnson cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. The class is quite similar to BCOR 3020 but he makes it interesting by using real world examples. Tests are not terrible, and he gives you a 3 page formula sheet so you don't have to memorize them. Would take any class that he taught!
Read the book to get the extra little questions not covered in the lecture. Average amount of work, he is very caring and flexible. Not a blow off but not too hard either.

Professor Johnson makes the material much easier to understand than the textbook because of the real-world examples and demonstrations he gives in class. The grade is quite heavily weighted on the quizzes and exams though. Material isn't very difficult, but there's a lot of it.
Professor Johnson was so nice and knowledgeable. Even though it was an online class, I really like his lectures.

Brian is the best professor I've ever had. He explains thoroughly concepts and is always using examples so that we understand it. He's really repetitive when it came to explaining how to use formulas but it's REALLY helpful because in the midterms and finals, you never forget. Highly recommend.
Super easy. If you are not majoring in finance, this is the instructor to take. I failed the final and still got a good grade.

Awesome guy! He knows so much and is great at lecturing. Problem is the topic is boring. Never used the textbook and I got an A-. Exams were very hard and the final exam was brutal. Be prepared to study and memorize concepts. Not a super difficult class if you work smart. Offers great insight into the way international finance works. Fair grader.

Professor Johnson is a great professor. He provides lecture slides ahead of class time, which helps a lot when you're following along during lectures. He's easy to understand and willing to meet with students to ensure they know the info.
Best Prof at the university. If you study and keep up the work the class is awesome. Johnson is always willing to help if you seek it!

Brian is a good professor. Definitely not my favorite by any means, and at times his lectures can be a bit dry. He focuses on the conceptual rather than calculations, and his experience as CFO of IBM Japan is very helpful in teaching the class. Be prepared to take good notes or read the book, because his slides are fairly bare.

Did a good job teaching international finance. Really focuses most on the concepts rather than calculations. Has real life knowledge of the subject and gives many examples from his experiences at IBM Japan. Super nice guy that you can tell just wants you to succeed and do well in his class. Wants you to understand and retain the material.

Professor Johnson did a great job explaining the concepts and used real-world examples. He was always prepared with great slides and suggested practice problems at the end of each chapter for which he provided the answers worked out on Canvas. There are also take-home quizzes which can be re-worked for full credit as often as needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is one of the best teachers I have had. His class is difficult but he does a great job explaining the concept and really cares that each student understands the material. He is very quick with his grading and feedback and is always ready to help students with questions. Would absolutely recommend Professor Johnson to anyone.

This is Brians first semester teaching International Finance and I thought he did an amazing job. He is really smart and knows what he is talking about. He doesn't think the equations are important so he focuses most on the conceptual, if you go to class and study for the quizzes you should get a good grade.

It's evident how much she cares about students. One low-stakes quiz per week derived almost verbatim from the hw. Her biggest strength is making sure everyone understands lectures without being patronizing or going too slow. HW can be rigorous (set aside a couple days min) & graded a bit strictly but if you're on top of it, you're golden for exams.

The exams are also difficult to complete in the one hour given, and the expectations are not always clear. Overall, the class feels overwhelming, and I did not feel supported in understanding the material. I am honestly considering dropping this class because of how the course is structured 50%

i mean, she is not the other prof, but she wants you to do a lot of assignments in class and out of class as well. You will have 3 home quizzes every week and 4 exams. She doesn't give u a lot of time during the exam so it's kinda hard to finish those questions in 40 minutes, i mean if you not good at math , just don't take this professor.
She's the best prof I've taken at uwb. Very caring, wants students to succeed. Exams are straightforward, she doesn't try to trick you. Super organized and easy to talk to as well.

Extremely kind.

I was going through a very rough semester and I needed lots of help. Even though I showed up late to almost every class if I showed up at all, she always helped me when I needed it.

The class structure may not be for everyone, it's very group-oriented and the homework can be tedious. Nevertheless, I think she is a great professor.

Lectures are generally good, but they do not prepare you for the homework. Even for a fourth year course, this is kind of ridiculous. Also takes FOREVER to reply to emails which is extremely frustrating. I often email her about homework problems then dont hear back until AFTER the due date like ok thanks? Topology is cool but take from someone else

Dr. Field is a very kind professor and puts in effort to make sure everyone succeeds. She is always requesting feedback to see if anyone has any questions. Unfortunately, her lectures can be rather confusing and people don't ask questions. Homework is difficult and not really based on lecture materials. Exams are relatively easy and heavily curved.

Okay... I've already seen a bunch of rate my professor reviews for this professor that perfectly reflect my experience in the same class, so I'll keep this short. Don't take her class. She's a horrible professor, her class is too difficult, the tests have nothing to do with the homework, its not worth it. Find another professor. Final average; 59%.

Professor Field's lectures were organized and overall I thought she was a great lecturer. The homework was difficult but manageable. The exams on the other hand were open-note but were the most difficult exams I've ever done, unlike the homework at all. I would've preferred to have closed exams and exam problems like the homework/practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's very nice, but the jumps from the lectures to homework are very large and she is a very tough grader. Doesn't have TAs to help answer questions, and, as someone who always has loved math, I hated this class.

She seems like a very nice lady with good intentions but this is the worst class I have taken so far in college. Myself and many other students have expressed that we have put in more effort into this class than any other class and yet it is many of our lowest grades. I think she has great potential as a teacher but has a very long way to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. Her exams and homework are a bit hard but not impossible. Make sure to attend her lectures and revisit the homework problems before exams. The exam difficulty is close to homework problems.

Professor Field is that she does seem like a genuinely nice person. That said. Do not take this class from her. Her lectures are quite confusing and don't cover everything on the homework so you have to spend lots of time outside of class working on learning the material. The tests are hard with the preparation given being limited. Do not recommend

Her lecture is so confusing! I have to wait after class to write down my notes. Not only that, her exam and homework are also confusing that I have to get help from my peers to get a better understanding. Since I have to take this class for my major, it's very complicated when I know Calculus 3 is the hardest course. Therefore, don't take her class

I have mixed feelings about this class, because I think the curriculum was what bothered me more than the prof. Nona was really kind and flexible about deadlines when I needed. However, the grading criteria was a little unclear, and sometimes her instructions contained redundancies. The saving grace was her availability to talk about it.

Discussion posts are due once a week, and they are always uploaded a few weeks ahead. The readings are directly related to the posts, so pretty easy. There a few big projects during the semester, but you have time to do them. She's also flexible with due dates as long as you communicate with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nona is a really nice and fun teacher. She is very helpful and fun to work with. She is clear about here assignments and what you should know before class and etc. She does have a lot of readings and some very large intensive projects but she gives you a lot of time to work on it. Attendance isn't mandatory but she really likes people who show up.

I think he is okay, the lectures were VERY boring. The discussion section was difficult, but the class is not hard to get an A in. Overall, I'd try to get a better professor, but he wasn't bad at all.
Pretty easy class, lectures were boring, but a nice professor. Exams are very similar to practice exams.

I found his class difficult, but it was because of the material and not because of the professor. Bergman's great at identifying the core concepts and then having homework that feels like it derives from what's taught. I'd highly recommend giving the material the time it's worth. The final was difficult, and the homework can take its time.

Great prof, really cares about his students. He isn't afraid to be poignant or blunt. Bergman is quite accessible and is more than happy to answer questions. His classes are hard, but they'll force you to really learn the subject material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was very flexible about deadlines on lab reports, but was very unclear on what he expected on them. Even his feedback once the reports were graded was unclear.
Had a B and missed and exam because I had the flu and she refused to let me make it up and now I have to retake.

I LOVE Dr. Cunningham, my favorite professor by far. Her class is very enganging and she cares very much about her students. She makes sure you are prepared for all exams and it is nearly impossible to use AI on any of her assignments.I only opened that textbook one time the whole semester, and that was during the final review
Pretty good teacher, the lessons were understandably. You do have to do a lot of in class participation but it just helps with the learning.

By far my favorite professor I've had so far at the U. She makes everything very easy to understand and she's incredibly caring. I always knew what was expected of us, and the concepts were really interesting & will help in real life in a business career. Always left class with a smile on my face! She loves her students & wants everyone to succeed.

Dr Cunningham was very kind and easy to talk to. Attendance was required for her class as well as a lot of in class assignments and group projects. She made class very enjoyable and was very understanding/helpful.

Lame class, but great professor. The lectures were entertaining; she knew what she was talking about. There was a lot of assigned reading, but I got by just fine without doing it. Be prepared for many icebreaker activities, peer discussions, and group projects. Her slides and canvas were very well organized, and she was accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're reading this, consider this a warning—avoid this professor at all cost. She rushes through slides, talks to students like we're in kindergarten, and grades harshly. Group work is random—I got stuck with people who couldn't speak english, and it tanked my grade. There are much better options for this course. Choose wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This Professor was okay I thought. I took a three hour lecture with her so maybe that's the reason I really didn't enjoy the class. She goes too fast through her slides and treats you like a kindergartners. She's more fit to teach high school. She was a nice person tho.

Dr. Cunningham is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is very caring and always sets you up for success. She is also open to feedback about her teaching methods. I honestly was never stressed about the workload of her class. I would take another class with her if I could. If you have the opportunity to take one of her classes, do it!

This was Professor Cunningham's first semester at the University of Utah and is hands down the best professor I've had yet at this University. She is very caring and personable with her students. She made a 3 hour class fun and enjoyable. Course content isn't hard at all just participate and stay on top of projects. Highly recommend!!

She was always very helpful and included everything you needed. Although the exams, I felt like I didn't have enough time because it was multiple choice, fill in the blank, and then you had to write two essays. She was very nice though!

Her lectures don't have a lot to do with the exams, and the reading is heavy. There are homework assignments based on short documentaries that she can be pretty tough on. Overall, the lectures drag on and on, and she doesn't cover a lot of material for exams. Even with the study guides, she misses the point a lot, the class is pretty boring
Dr. Milicic is a great professor! I thought this class was very easy and a lot of fun. She's very caring and gives awesome feedback. Would take again!

Lectures are kinda bland if you've already read the articles because they mostly summarize the material. Assignments super easy, open book exams, you'll have to do a presentation & research paper for the final. 
Overall pretty easy class but instructions and due dates were obnoxiously unclear throughout the semester.
You learn the material pretty well, but you are graded on less than 8 assignments the whole semester. Lots of readings too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class. Lectures aren't mandatory and aren't particularly useful either. Your grade is determined by a final paper, final presentation and 3 exams. For the exams, I would just self study a few days before because she posts all the lecture notes. Extra credit questions are given on the exam so it's not hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She uses so much content that isn't even relevant to what is in the exams. Assignments are light but the exams are long and redundant. She has film reviews that she wrongly accused me of plagiarism on and failed me on them. Overall, ineffective and unnecessary. Consider taking a different class.

She was very nice, but it was hard to tell what she wanted when she graded and gave feedback. She would grade my assignments during the day, and then at night she would go back and re-grade them and dock me for silly things. This class was way more work than a gen ed. needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take this if you want an easy A or are into the Mediterranean. Two exams and a final, plus a final paper. Exams are "not open note"...multiple choice and fill-in-the-blank, essay and extra credit questions at the end. She gives good feedback on the paper proposal and the prompt is more or less open-ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Very simple class. She assigns readings from various books, but I never read them and I got an A. Just make sure you attend class and LISTEN. This class is mostly lectures, but they're not boring at all. The exams are online and open note, so take lots of notes as well and you'll pass. 
You don't need any anthropology background to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took the fall intensive and I loved it. The content was interesting, and Dr. Milicic was a very interesting lecturer. Most of my grade relied on tests, but there was a final paper. There was a lot of reading that I do recommend doing before the class.

Bojka is super nice and super understanding as well. There were a few classes where I was either sick or just didn't feel great, and she allowed em to zoom into class. Her study guides are clear and are taken straight out of the lectures, and the tests are basically the study guide. She's a fun teacher!

Many others have stated the same. She is great and certainly interesting, but her slides are so long. I have never seen a 105 slide doc. before and it is just filled with content, then there are 6+ other presentations like that. Quizzes cover material and she offers extra credit. Group was was managable, plenty of time to work on the paper.

I really tried to like this class. Unfortunately, Bojka is an ineffective professor and her terrible powerpoints make me want to yell and cry at the same time. She's a nice enough person, but I didn't learn anything of even minor use in this class. Her presentations are so confusing and full of very useless information. Don't take this class!

This class is death-by-powerpoint in its truest form. Bojka is a very nice person, but not a good professor. The slides are all very text heavy, and her ideas in lecture are scattered and difficult to follow. Some of the course content is interesting, but in my opinion the painful lectures aren't worth it. I do not recommend taking this class.

Prof. Milicic is one of my favorite professors at the U! I took a second class from her just because of how great my experience was in Symbolic Anth. She really knows her stuff, often from her own personal travels, so she's a lot of fun to listen to. If you pay attention in class and at least have an idea of the readings, you'll be good.

Bojka is the best. She really wants all her students to succeed. She met with me multiple times to help me understand and learn the material. She is so caring about all her students and really fair when it comes to group projects and making sure everyone is participating equally. Take her class, she is one of the best professors I have ever had!
Super caring. She'll help you A LOT if you show up to at least one office hour.

Dr. Milicic was a good professor, but there were lots of powerpoint presentations with lots and lots of bullet points. She made the lectures interesting by discussing her own fieldwork experiences and how it related to what we were learning. It was a really interesting class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Milicic has a great insight on the cultural aspects of anthropology. She relates her own fieldwork experiences to the class which makes it more interesting. It's an interesting topic, however, sometimes the lectures seem to go forever as it's just slide of bullet points after slide. Really nice professor though, would take again!

Bojka is a fun person and loves anthropology, but I think it is just too hard to make anthropology interesting. I found myself constantly trying to stay awake during lectures and had a hard time focusing on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a fantastic teacher and knows her material well. Although the lectures, which are all powerpoint based, can be a bit hard to stay focused on the material itself is fascinating and she explains it in simple and easy to understand ways. She puts up study guides a week or so in advanced and she is VERY fair on her grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great teacher really knows her stuff. She discusses the reading so if you go to class and do the study guide you don't need to read all of it. She really likes in class discussion, really interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Milicic teaches an interesting class. She gives information clearly and if you miss class the notes are online! I attended class, took notes, and got an A on both tests and the final paper. Best Anthro teacher I've had. Only warning is that her accent is a bit hard to understand at first, but her mastery of the english language is awesome

Easy class& exams+helpful study guide and 1 paper stubborn+ if she disagrees with your opinion + sources provided for your paper there is no way, but to obey  forces you to OVERUSE the example paper  that she chose from an " excellent student"which was something I stood up to! everyone writes unique and I was sick of her referring me to the paper

Clear lectures, clear expectations, amazing study guides that cover every aspect you will be tested on, and even better, someone that is great to just talk to.  I have taken three classes from her, each consist of lectures with 1 or 2 movies, (with a couple test related questions on the movies), two tests, and 1 paper. Worth it.
shes montonous but if you get passed that she explains everything well and in depth so chuck a red bull or a shot of espresso before attending her class

Extremely helpful! Lectures can be boring, but overall you learn alot. Tests are not difficult. You have to read a lot of books, but if you go over the notes she posts and put a little time into it, you should be fine. I didn't read all the texts books and still passed the exams. I would highly recommend her.
an excellent professor

Her lectures tend drag and she has a habit over explaining things. I didn't have any one-on-one interaction but I get the impression that she would be helpful with question and fair with issues. Overall, I thought she was good, not great. To do well in the class you will have to do a lot of reading, but it is not a very difficult course.

Prof. Milicic is one of the best professors at the University of Utah!!! I really liked her, her class was very interesting, not hard at all, she usually has three exams and a term paper and all of them are very very easy if you put just a little bit of your time. You can understand her perfectly her english is good!I strongly recommend her:)

Professor Milicic was great! She is incredibly helpful if you take advantage of her office hours or speak with her after class. I thought she was pretty funny in class too. The class wasn't easy, lots of reading, challenging tests, and lots of material covered in this class but if you're up for a challenge and are actually in school to learn something, she's great. Classy, foxy, mature woman to boot.

Milicic is great.  Three tests, one term paper.  Her class is pure lecture with power point, so it can get boring at times.  Her in-class tests are pretty easy, but take-homes aren't.  I've had her twice and would recommend her.

Professor Milicic is a great professor. Her lectures are extremely useful and supplement the texts. The material she has you read is also great, which helps because some times there can be a lot. Amazingly helpful, and really flexible on missing an exam (for good reasons of course). She tries to keep classes interesting by asking questions.

There were some comments about not being able to understand her accent, but I understood her just fine!  She is extremely helpful if you just ask, it's incredible how quickly she responds to email.  If you put in the effort required you will get a good grade.  Vote for the in-class tests, they are so much easier than the take home tests!
She was impossible to understand most of the time but overall, the class was easy as long as you read the notes she posts online.
i felt like she was willing to help a lot. i loved he as a teach...she was awesome... i learned so much. take her

Bojka was the worst professor I have ever had.  I agree with the person above me.  Completely unclear, terrible lecturer, very insecure and prejudiced.  Her syllabus was unorganized, written poorly and difficult to follow and her lectures nearly unbearable.  She shouldn't be teaching.  I have a strong opinion about her, and it is for good reason

I've taken several of her classes and I really enjoy them.  I think that she is very clear in what she expects with assignments and grades fairly.  Her accent is fairly thick but you'll get used to it.
My fav anthro prof so far

Her accent did make it hard to understand her sometimes but she always put her notes online after class. The assignments were sometimes hard to understand but she would explain them if asked. I did learn new information in her class but it was hard to hear her or read the overhead in class so the notes were very helpful to have.

very difficult to understand, she has a heavy accent but that is not the problem.  She cannot explain anything, her syllabus is unclear--Her assignments are extremely unclear aand if you ask her to elaborate she becomes defensive. extremely poor communicater and difficult to contact for 1 on 1.
Very patient, kindly, responsible, smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Hacon goes through lectures quickly, but he always made it interesting. He is a very generous grader and wants the students in his class to succeed.

Warning though, in this class the grade distribution was 60% quizzes and 40% final. So you're going to have to put some hard work into this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good teacher. Accessible, gracious, and funny.
talks quickly and with huge classes its hard to understand (especially if you're not good at math)

I took Math 1050 with Professor Hacon and it was a very well-structured class. I had it four days a week, and it was only 50 minutes which made it easy not to lose concentration. A quiz and two online homework assignments every week. He is a very kind professor who explains concepts very clearly. It was a good class, not too much homework.

Professor Hacon was an amazing professor who would take time during lectures to make sure everyone understood the material. The class had a weekly quiz, which helped keep me ready to take the midterms and final. If you do all the homework, the quizzes and midterms are less challenging, and you will never be surprised with material you don't know.

Chris is an amazing professor. This was the last math class I needed to take to finish my bachelors in math, so I was a little unmotivated to pay attention in class, but the material is easy enough to learn on your own; just know that the weekly quizzes might have a question (proof) from one of the previous lectures, so make sure to go to class!

If you are math major and need to take number theory, take it with Chris if you get the opportunity. He goes more in depth with the subject, has great examples during his lecture for you to better understand.
Great teacher.  Clear in his expectations and easy to understand.  He is very personable.
Chrisssss my homie! Duuude, this man is my homeslice. Your boy gives great lectures and he be lookin fly. No homework either!! b

Chris is my boy. Although statistics is not the most interesting class, he made it enjoyable. His lectures are short and he provides no workload besides quizzes and tests. He works a lot with students and if you as for help he'll work with you. Pretty stand-up and cool guy and a great teacher. I got an A by only going to class and barely studying.
Amazing professor. Probably the best professor here at the University of Utah. Very helpful in and out of class. If you ever get the chance to take a class with Hacon then DO IT!
An excellent Statistics teacher.  Most people who are geniuses tend to not connect with other people well but Chris is great! Very understandable and funny, too.  Keep up the good work!
This is as straight forward as it gets.  If you go to class take good notes and can easily do the problems he does in class you are golden for an A.  Very easy class.

Chris is a really good teacher and really likes what he does. He is very approachable and encourages questions. He has review sheets for every quiz and test  as well. In my class he didn't assign homework so I didn't need the book. If you take good notes you could easily get a good grade. I'm HORRIBLE at math and I got an A-.Definitely takehisclass

Good professor, but his accent is a little difficult at times to understand. He honestly tries to help you understand the difficult math. Some of his test questions are difficult, but it is not unmanageable.
He's not a bad teacher.  His accent makes him hard to understand sometimes, but he is always willing to help you if you need it.  He's even funny.
No Comments

Chris is one of the best math professors I've learned from. His lectures are amazing, he's funny and care for his students. Doing and understand the homework is a must to success in his class, bc all you get in your exam is your homework exercises, maybe a little harder. SUPER lenient grader, smart and understanding prof. I LOVE Chris and 3070!
For MATH 3070, Chris explained everything you needed to know clearly and did example problems during lectures. The tests, and the class overall, were easy.
He is a very nice teacher. As long as you work hard, you will get a good grade.
This is a great teacher. He respects all of us. His tests are not that tough. I learned a lot from his classes.
One of the best instructors in the math department. Course content in strongly reflected in the quizzes and exams, which makes them extremely fair. Explains concepts and material very thoroughly.
Good lectures. Flexible with a small class.

Great Professor.  He cares about students and is understanding that occasionally people are gone/sick/whatever else and is willing to make accommodations.  Labs are a bit tough, but he is always willing to sit down and explain it until you understand.  Quizzes every week give you a good idea of where you should be without destroying your grade.

Chris is a great guy who augments the textbook with outstanding lectures and explanations. He's a real resource when it comes to the nuts and bolts of math. While the class may have been derivation-heavy for this future engineer, by the end I appreciated his perspective even more and everything made sense in the big picture. Knows his stuff.
Pretty chill guy.  Lectures were never awful, tests weren't too difficult.  minimal homework was given.

Lectures were clear and hilarious. Chris was super helpful in lectures, office hours, and over email, and was willing to meet outside of scheduled office hours. Tests were long, but the content was fair. Labs were the hardest part. Definitely not an easy A, but also not an impossible one.

Chris is the best math professor I have had so far. He is extremely helpful and engaged with his students. He does his best to be available whenever students need him. His class is not easy but he is clear about what will be on the tests/quizzes and grades fairly. He respects his students and never makes you feel stupid for being confused.

Chris is awesome!  He is very good at motivating the math with biology, physics, and engineering examples and applications which was really helpful for me.  He keeps students engaged and is easy to reach out to in office hours for extra help.  Very relateable and knowledgeable.  I would take another math class from him.

I took his class twice,  best Math classes i have taken so far. Chris has a unique style of teaching, fairly straightforward and  always there to help. His class is thoroughly entertaining. He taught the classes for the first time but he did a splendid job. The tests and the workload were fairly reasonable. I would take every math class from him.
Chris was one of the best teachers I've ever had. He listens to the opinions of the students and is the most fair grader I've ever had. Also, hilarious.
He's a great professor that takes the time to work with students.

Chis is the best math professor I have had in college.  He teaches extremely well and is very straightforward and clear when he explains things. He connects with his students a ton, and very much is someone I didn't feel weird about going to for help.  Chris is amazing, if you have the chance to take a class from him DO IT! he is the greatest.

Very insightful and concise math professor. He was able to explain complex differential equation ideas in ways that made perfect sense to me. His homework is difficult but necessary for the exams. Our lab section was very difficult and the TA's were not helpful at all.

Chris is hands down the best math teacher I've ever had. Besides being hilarious and clear, he seems to genuinely be interested in teaching. He's always very amiable before and after class and he's always answered my questions to the best of his ability - even ones from other classes.

Chris is a hilarious and personable math professor. He isn't easy, but he isn't hard. I really would consider him very fair. He wants to improve as an instructor, and takes advice well. Go to office hours! He wants to help! I learned so much, and would take his class again. He dresses well, he teaches well, and I highly enjoyed my time here.

Chris is a fairly young professor. He has quizzes once a week and the homework is due once a week which is really nice. He will help you if you ask him for help. Attending all of the lectures will be very helpful. Because Math 1320 is faster paced than the regular Calc 1220 class. So, there are less examples,  but study hard and you will pass.

Chris is a young helpful professor.  He has a quiz every friday about 2-3 questions long.  His tests are not terrible, and he grades somewhat generously.  Homework is a regular load, but due weekly so thats nice.
Her lectures covered exactly what was in the textbook for the day, and no mandatory attendance made coming to class difficult. It's an easy class but I don't recommend

I dont think I have ever had a prof this boring and lectured as uninterestingly as dr cottiero. the class itself was not super difficult, pop quizzes were not bad if you did readings. The final was extensive but not super difficult, about 20 pages. if you love to be bored and zone out shes for you!

Literally, what was this woman talking about? She is beyond boring, doesn't engage, and drones on without providing clarification of topics. She also goes through the slides way too quickly, like let me take notes please.

Dr. Cottiero was one of my favorite professors so far at the U. Her lectures were interesting and more entertaining than other professors. Pop quizzes were common at the start of the semester but stopped in February, not sure why. They weren't difficult if you even skimmed the readings, so not difficult. The final project was quite intensive though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class is interesting. The professor is funny and always explains everything clearly. If you need help, she is very responsive via email and holds office hours twice a week. The pop quizzes are incredibly easy if you have done the reading. As a non-native speaker, I had no trouble understanding the material and currently have a 99% in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not an easy A but a very interesting class if you apply yourself. Weekly quizzes that aren't bad if you come to class + read. Papers were graded inconsistently by the TA, and the exams are tough, she gives no study guide. Super interesting class but you need to apply yourself to earn an A from her - she's very knowledgeable in her field for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Cottiero was excellent. Her lectures were engaging and relevant to real world problems. She clearly knows the topics well and was available for office hours as needed. The class was centered around 3 papers, a midterm and final, and semi-regular quizzes. The class was not an easy A, but I would definitely recommend the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Cottiero was a great professor who was very smart and knew a lot. I would recommend her to almost anyone. The lectures were not too fun, but the class went by fast, so that's a good thing! If you try, I really believe you will do well in her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment:
Unprofessional and unreasonable. 

Total Karen of a professor. Super entitled and full of herself
