Davenport is one of the only good professors in the U's physics department. His grade scale was extremely generous, though there was a lot of work to do. Final project instead of a final exam, but it wasn't too bad. If you can, he's the way to go for Physics 2.

Amazing class. He had a great lecture environment and always made the material interesting. He was slightly on the more difficult side but if you do your homework and go to class you will succeed. 10/10 would take another class.

I loved Prof Davenport's class. As someone who didn't do great with calc, the material was difficult, but Prof Davenport worked hard to present the material in a way that minimizes the amount of calculus needed and ensures it is highly understandable. Beyond that, he was respectful, pleasant to work with, and engaging as a lecturer. Would recommend

Davenport clearly cares about physics; he's a great lecturer, asks for feedback and tries to positively change the class based on that feedback, and has the A cutoff at 90%. The class grade is 50% hw, and there are multiple smaller exams, but you can do test corrections with other students to make up points. Highly recommend taking physics with him

Professor Davenport was very great at taking feedback from his students and changing the course based on what the students liked/disliked. He also dropped multiple homework scores and 2 quiz scores which really helped considering the difficulty of this class. My only complaint is that the homework/quizzes were harder than what the lectures covered.

Definitely one of the hardest classes I've ever taken & I wouldn't have done as well as I did without this prof. He genuinely cares about student's success. He gives surveys throughout the semester, then adjusts the class according to feedback. There are 6 TA/LAs who have office hrs throughout the week so you can always get help outside of class.

Good professor overall but syllabus was vague about participation and Dichio only clarified about participation after grades were submitted. It was the only thing that prevented me from getting an A in his class. Interesting overall but would not recommend based on class expectations.

Dr. Dichio is amazing! I have taken multiple of his classes at the U and have enjoyed every single one. He is very knowledgeable, engaged with his students, and is a great lecturer. His classes are not difficult if you do the readings.

Grade is made up of one paper, an exam, and weekly quizzes. They are all definitely challenging, but paying attention to the lectures and putting in effort will get you a B. Everyone loves and respects him. Lectures are great and it's clear he cares about his students. The papers he assigns are always really fun and interesting. 

100% recommend!

What I like about Dichio is that he cares about students. Despite receiving an A, my problem with this class was that it was graded by few things (easy weekly quizzes, midterm report, and final report or final exam) but with little to no constructive feedback. Assessments were graded by a TA we had never met or seen in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dichio is a great guy and an amazing professor. He is an average grader and his lectures are high quality. I would absolutely take a class from him again in a heartbeat and would recommend others take this class.
This is my second class from this professor and it was just as good as the first one. Cannot recommend enough, just make sure you do your reading.
There is a lot of reading for this class, but it is all covered in the lecture. Graded by a few papers and by weekly reading quizzes. Easy class, learned a lot, and super fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dichio is a great professor who allows students to participate in thought provoking discussions. I would recommend taking his Law and Politics course if you are considering law!
Very knowledgeable and entertaining lectures.

I will always only have great things to say about Dichio. He truly cares about his students and the content that he is presenting. Nonetheless, this class can be very difficult at times and covers some intensely debated content, but Dichio is nothing but open and respectful to all different ideas. Come to class with readings done ready to discuss.

I have taken all 3 of the courses that Professor Dichio gives here at the U. He is an extremely fair grader and really cares for his students. The classroom environment is very comfortable, which helps with participation! There is a lot of reading, but it correlates directly to what you'll be tested on. VERY interesting lectures!
Dichio is an all time professor, great class, fair grader, real good.

Professor Dichio was by far one of my favorites. He was extremely passionate and went above and beyond to help and care for his students. The course was interesting and engaging. His lectures were full of great, thoughtful content. The classroom environment was positive and those who normally wouldnt share felt comfortable to do so. 5 stars!!!

I took 2 classes from Professor Dichio, and to be honest, the class itself was great. Good discussions about important topics, and he discusses perspectives on both sides. However, his 5000 level class and his 3000 level class had the same expectations and he was a very harsh grader, and I was left with a grade far lower than I felt I deserved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures. A lot of reading but weekly reading quizzes are easy if you read. Participate! 2 papers. I typically receive A+ on my papers but I found myself with B+ for once. Read the rubrics and talk to him about what he's looking for in your writing. Very accessible outside of class so use that resource. Genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dichio is amazing! He has great lectures and is passionate about what he teaches. He is also very caring and gets to know every student in his class. He knows every student by name which is very unusual in college classes. The class does have a lot of reading but if you focus in class, it isn't too hard. I've taken every course he teaches

This is my third class with Professor Dichio and he is definitely one of the best professors in Political Science at the U. He is very knowledgable and his lectures are always interesting. There is a lot of work but if you do readings and show up to lectures, you'll be good. If you enjoy learning about the law, this is the perfect class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bad communicator. Demeaning and rude to students. Does not respond to emailed questions. Exams are closed-book, closed-note. Do not recommend this professor.

He does not explain anything as he goes through the material.He just assumes that everyone is a seasoned investment banker.Its not about learning excel but following along.The grading is based on a couple exams and some quizzes which have some very weirdly worded questions.If it was actually about students learning, there's better ways to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I recommend not taking this professor. He does not actively teach during class and instead relies on videos, which does not help students fully understand the material. The homework is very difficult and takes an excessive amount of time to complete. Overall, it seems like he is no longer invested in teaching.

Lot's of good things in this class, but his assignments were weird. He said that he purposefully made instructions unclear because that's how the real world is. Usually it just ended up being typos and inconsistencies in his instructions. Overall it was fine.

This guy made me question my sanity. The Excel homework assignments took 8+ hours each to complete. I had to dedicate entire Sundays to this class. Not only that.. but if you don't answer all of the quiz questions correctly, you don't get full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The University should really consider fire this guy. He literally says follow my lead like monkeys, and all we did was just to follow how we solves financial problems using excel. He does not explain the material nor the concept or even the applicability of it, and honestly it is just a waste of time and most importantly money.

Highly discourage generally everyone from taking Dubil's courses. The one exception would be that you are Wall Street bound and want extremely challenging work. Dubil almost exclusively draws on his statistical and quantitative derivative trading experience to teach each of his classes.
aw hell nah

One of the best professors I've ever had. He is a great teacher and truly makes learning finance easier. As long as you put in some effort, than you should be able to pass his classes no problem. Oh... and be ready to deal with his sarcasm lol.
Out of every professor I have EVER had the past 5 years, he is THE WORST by far. He makes way too much money to be treating people the way he does.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. This professor is shockingly rude. Prepare for none of your questions to be answered and for him to belittle you for not knowing as much as he does. He will not teach the equations in the textbook so when it is time for the exam you won't understand much of the equation page provided. For your sake do not take his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Idk why everyone hates on him, he was a funny professor and I always laughed in his class. He has sarcastic humor but he's just a joker. The course itself is hard so I dont blame him for that. The finals and midterms make up your entire grade and he is strict grader.

I would avoid professor Dubil at all costs. The tests are 100% of your grade and each answer needs to be exact up to 4 decimal places leaving no room for error. He prides himself on being the toughest finance professor and it really shows. Our class average was a 62%. He is very very tough and if you can avoid him I for sure would.

Overall, the class was ok, but Professor Dubil is the strictest grader I've encountered thus far. It would be helpful if he recognized that small mistakes, like typos, happen and offered a second attempt on Canvas for assignments. This was my final semester at the U, and this class just ruined my mood. First time I've ever argued with a professor.

This is one of the hardest classes in the business school. The expectations are that you have high level finance, math, and python programming knowledge. You are expected to program portfolios and apply sharpe ratios within 1 week of class. I took this class purposely because of Dubil and to my surprise, he was totally different from undergrad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Certified yaper. Guy talks the entire lecture about nothingness related to the class. Impossible to stay focused as he rants a lot about nothing.

Out of the 40-something college professors I have had in my lifetime, Robert is by far the worst, and it's not even close. I literally have no idea how this guy is a professor at the U. But... I will give you guys a tip!! Look his name up on YouTube, all of the answers are there :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid taking his classes for 6360 and 6380. His questions are worded very vaguely and answers are hard to get correct. Almost none of my peers in the class understand what is going on. His expectations for understanding are extremely high and his willingness to help is extremely low. Most that I know have struggled with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very rude. Makes fun of students who answer incorrectly. No slides and no clear expectations. Questions on tests are worded vaguely and graded harshly. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil is super straightforward and blunt, but if you have thick skin he is hilarious and super fun to joke around with. He is a passionate teacher and really cares to help you succeed, even if that means tough love. 10/10 would take again. Way better than many "easier" teachers.
Professor Dubil is a great teacher. Go to class prepared to take class notes. The note worksheets help extremely with the homework.
Toughest professor in the finance department and his class is just full of math problems. No clear lecture slides and no TA for his class either. Horrible!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Taking classes with Professor Dubil is a complete waste of your money and time. He prides himself on the fact that most students hate him and his class is just an excuse for him to massage his ego. He refuses to teach to the extent that you will basically have to teach yourself the entire course through youtube.

Will openly make fun of students for asking "stupid questions", but then will call out the class for being "shy and will never amount to anything" when no one raises their hand. If you don't grasp the information the first time around, chances are you will fail the exams. Your grade is based off of three exams which are worth 75% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor will talk about things that are completely unrelated to the course and will confuse you. He gives you a blank worksheet to fill out while he talks for 3 hours. He often is wrong on homework problems and does not like to be corrected. Hard class, awful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil's class is very straightforward and he offers plenty of opportunities to learn the material. You will need to do ALL of the homework, pay attention in the lectures and then ask questions. This class is not for anyone looking to breeze through finance, its for those that actually want to learn. 10 out of 10 would recommend.

I deeply regret taking this course. I understand that some people are just blunt, but what I dont appreciate is being asked if I'm drinking/drunk after asking a clarifying question about new material. He would get annoyed if you asked him questions during the break in the lecture or outside of class. TA had no clue what Dubil was covering in class.

The guy lays out the instructions on how to succeed in his class first day and in his syllabus. He expects you to just study and practice/understand the material individually, rather than just give you busy work homework, of which there isn't a lot in his class. Practicing the worksheet and asking questions is how you'll do good.

Professor was seriously rude and demeaning throughout the course.  Wouldn't answer questions he perceived as "dumb" and wouldn't really offer to help students... If you didn't grasp the material first time you would fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dubil doesn't care. Take that how you will. Don't be soft. Do the homework he tells you to do because he's smarter than you. I liked taking his class, it was super straightforward, and honestly, Dubil is a crack-up. Rate him badly all you want, he won't lose sleep. Take good notes and ask questions, even if he heckles you. Would take it again.

This guy gives 5-minute tests in class that regularly have the entire class get zero points, and he literally stands there at the front of the class just watching the entire class fail tests, the textbook is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easily the most disrespectful, unprofessional, and demeaning professor I've ever had a class with. For your own sake, do not take a class with this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: worst professor I have had by a long shot.

During one of our classes the teacher walked out of our class because we didn't understand the concept. Long story short, this guy is incredibly unprofessional and should not be teaching. Do not take a class with this teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very hash and has little time nor care for students. is unreasonable with holidays and exam dates.
This guy is terrible. Avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is very hard to follow during his lectures. He makes the students teach the lessons and will correct them once their explanation is over. If a student gets the first or second step wrong, he won't correct them until the very end. This makes taking notes impractical. He will not show up to classes or exams without giving prior notice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I so badly want to like this class because I feel like outside of the classroom he is a funny and nice guy. I draw the line though when my grade and ability to learn are affected by him trying to be funny. One of the biggest problems was limited test time and not having adequate notes from class to do a similar question again.

Actually the worst professor I've ever had, by far. He does not teach you - he will fill out a worksheet with you and that's your lesson - there are no lectures, no slides, or any extra material to help you understand a relatively hard subject. He yells at you to read the textbook, but then tells you that the way the textbook teaches is wrong.

Robert Dubil is a great person but a horrible professor. His lectures are hard to follow and he gets upset with the class if they don't know the answer. He punished my section with quizzes at the beginning of each class and then laughed at us since most of us failed. I reccomend you find another professor or section to be in to avoid this.

Professor Dubil is very intelligent when it comes to finance. Unfortunately, he sucks at teaching it. He doesn't like to answer questions. He is extremely hard to follow during lectures. He would rather watch your world burn than lift you up and help you as a student. There are endless instances of unfair treatment. Avoid Dubil at all costs.

Terrible professor. Doesn't care about students at all. Expected us to understand a new topic he hadn't taught us yet and because we didn't, ended class early without explanation and gave us a lengthy quiz due in five minutes the next class. He's the worst professor I've ever had and honestly should not teach here at the U. Find a different class.

Professor Dubil, is not helpful at all; he is not accommodating of cda, I expressed my health issues to him and he took a couple of days to respond and said "thanks." He makes it difficult for the student to feel comfortable asking questions in class due to him constantly blaming the students for not understanding the material. Find another teacher
Is very smart and knows the material but does not teach the basics well, makes you feel stupid for asking questions and does not work well with his students.

The class is difficult which is expected, but Dubil's teaching style is hard to understand. He doesn't follow the textbook, so it's difficult to study outside of class to better understand the material. If you ask him questions after class or send him emails, expect zero guidance or help. Doesn't seem to care about his students or their success.
This man could make anyone laugh. However, I wouldn't recommend taking his classes for finance. He jumps through it and I get lost. It's not his fault his class is hard, buckle down.

He's very intelligent, but a terrible teacher. I spent more money on a tutor (a previous student of his) than tuition for the class. He jokes saying "if it's wrong, it's probably your fault" as students average 55% on his tests. He grades on a curve, so if you somehow get 65% you'll probably end up with a B-. I advise a different teacher

This class was part of an MBA program. He is very knowledgeable, but as a lecturer, he is incredibly dull and boring. His online videos are so dry and monotonous, it's hard to keep interest. He compacts so much content in such a short amount of time. He expects double the homework than other classes in my program. Absolutely do not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil is a really intelligent guy when it comes to the subject of finance. But teaching wise, I've felt that he really is not a good teacher since he just dives into each lesson without setting any foundation on what the topic will cover. Also, I've felt that using the textbook has been pretty much useless since he uses a different method
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First off, dont buy the book, its useless unless you want to teach yourself a completely different way of solving problems than in class. Secondly, get ready to be set up for failure, he doesnt lay down any basics and immediately tries to confuse students with no explanation. If you try to ask a question he will ostracize you for it. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good teacher. Doesn't explain the subject and expects you to know the materials. He says things like "it was probably you, not me" and everyone laughs till his students average 60% on there midterms. Then its still your fault.

Solid professor. Follow his instructions regarding homework and studying exactly if you want to do well. Tests are difficult but there typically is a curve. He has a dry sense of humor which can be a little intimidating, but you can tell he really knows the material and enjoys teaching.

This course is extremely challenging, plan to spend a lot of time on the assignments. Professor Dubil is extremely intelligent and a great resource. He comes off as hard to talk to and so asking for help is intimidating. Overall you'll learn a lot if you put the time and effort in, but it is very tough.

Dubil is a tough prof. He will make you feel like you will fail. Don't be intimidated, since most people do fail, he curves the final grade a lot. Actually do the HMK A worksheets before class, and the course will be effective. If you're not willing to do that, you're in for a rough go.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Once you get to know Dubil's sense of humor and teaching style, he'll quickly become one of your favorite professors. He tells it like it is and doesn't sugar coat anything. He is tough, but he pushes you to be a better student and future business leader. He gives great random life advice throughout the class and truly helps students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Robert Dubil is NOT an online professor and it shows. He has no empathy for answering students questions and comes across really demeaning upon students asking for clarification. He usually responds to your messages in a sentence or less, typically not addressing most of your emails content. Sometimes he just doesnt respond! Find another prof.

Robert is quite literally one of the best professors at the U. I am completely biased because I am a Finance major and I knew half of the material before going in but Robert tells you how it is and I respect it. Also, he wants to help you succeed so go to office hours and ask questions.

As long as you pay attention to him in class and do the homeworks each week, you should have no problem with the tests in this class. He is really good at explaining how to do the problems, and is interesting to listen to.

Professor Dubil is a great professor. His lectures cover everything on the homework. All of the homework assignments lead to the Pre-Tests. The midterms are almost identical to the Pre-Tests. Go to class. Practice the material provided. He gives you everything you need to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I can't stress this enough, but take Acctg 3600 before Fin 3040. I would also take this class from a different professor. Dubils tests are not that difficult but they do not prepare you for the final at all. The average on the final is around 60% and there is no study guide.

Dubil is a great guy and if you enjoy day humor you're in for a treat. He prepares you for the final with the most simple steps so be prepared to learn a lot if you take this class. Dubil also gives really easy tests during the semester but just be prepared for the final. It's not easy.

Textbook doesnt provide specific examples of problems to solve nor does it properly define topics taught in class! He is very confusing, speaks very fast and doesnt slow down for people new to finance. He forgets hes been doing this for decades. Dumb it down and teach us. Show us. Instead he talks down to students and isnt helpful to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My #1 tip: take Acctg 3600 before 3040. It will make a lot of the concepts taught so much easier, as it's pretty much the same thing, with the finance class changing the vocabulary in an attempt to make itself harder (and failing miserably, lol). Do the end of chapter problems. Personally, I would not recommend this teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Take anyone but him. Super knowledgeable. Doesnt test you to prepare for real world application. Only cares about keeping the required grading scores. I did better when I started going to TA sessions vs his lecturers. Not that hes a bad professor. He will just make you learn it the hardest way.

DO NOT take a class from Prof Dubil. He was the worst teacher I have had and cared more about showing his students how smart he was opposed to teaching them anything. He was awful at answering questions and would look down his nose at students who asked questions and weren't fortunate enough to follow along with him. Take ANY other teacher

Dubil was one of the best professors I have ever had. You go over practice problems at home then he explains the process in class. You have to learn through practice and repetition but once you get that down the class is not too difficult. If you're confused just ask questions and he will clarify. Final was wild. Would definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives you pre-tests that are identical to his exams, so you really can't lose points there, if you study. He also helps with writing the department final, so the way that he words questions is familiar to what you'll see on the final exam.

A good choice for a finance professor. He was a funny guy and taught the subject rather well. He did dumb it down a lot which was nice for the class but made some things difficult on the school-wide final. He tells you the pre-tests are identical to the tests, listen to him.

Great professor, he really knows his stuff. Knows how to teach, there is ho,ework but you learn everything you need to know before hand. Pre test identical to the actual test. 10 out of 10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of the learning in this class comes from experience and repetition. You'll be discouraged at first, but practice will get you there. The pre tests are lifesavers. I would recommend taking acct 3600 as those classes go over the reasoning of finance. The professor wants you to succeed but he's not going to give it to you for free.
Great professor, he teaches finance well and the TA is great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He doesn't really teach you any concept in class. Instead you just go over answers. Taking ACTG 3600 prior to his class really helped me due to his lack of explaining concepts. Using the textbook felt useless because the methods were taught differently. I'm an auditory learner so textbooks usually do me no good anyways.

Dubil hardly teaches. You are given the questions before class and you are to figure out how to do it at home. All he does is go over the answers in class. You give me an answer key and I'm as useful as a professor as Dubil. I haven't learned anything from him its all been from youtube and Chegg. If you've already learned finance you'll like it.

What a great professor! I really enjoyed this class with him. Clearly taught the material, had some tangents but for the most part kept it all relevant to the material. I would definitely take a class from him again. What a cool guy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil was great. I didn't have a hard time understanding his lectures at all. He sets up the course very well, very organized and the expectations are clear. He is rather sarcastic and cynical which I appreciated but if that's not your style he may not be for you. Overall I would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Very odd, socially-awkward person. Very hard lecturer, has a very interesting way of teaching and explaining things. I mainly taught myself and used Google, and I got an A in the class.

Great professor and tells it how it is, but not an easy class. The tests are very similar to the practice homework he gives the week before, but it requires a lot of memorizing how to do the Excel tests. Only 3 or 4 questions per test so its easy to miss a lot of points. A nice curve at the end, but study enough, you can get 100's on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil is a great finance teacher. If you are searching for an easy class, do not take from him. If you are searching for an honest, NY attitude finance professor, who teaches well, and you are willing to work hard, take from him. Professor Dubil provides a great foundation for future finance courses and gives great advice for your future.

Dubil was a good prof. He explains things pretty thoroughly but goes somewhat fast, so it can be hard to understand. The class in general is very hard because of all the information you are expected to know, so the professor doesn't really matter a whole lot. Dubil gives speeches every class period about how you need to join a club. Waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil is brilliant, but he is really tough.  Be prepared to teach yourself how to do the problems in this class from reading the book.   Dubil preaches tough loves, but you will learn a lot in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Dubil is a good teacher, but he teaches super fast. Although going to class isn't mandatory, it is key to getting a good grade.

Dubil is seriously the best professor I have ever had. He is able to explain complicated concepts in a simple way, which helped me understand class materials well. He is always there whenever you need help and he really goes out of his way  to help you succeed.  I also loved his sarcasm and sense of humor.  He's a full package, take his class!

This professor has something special. I would take other classes from him in future in spite of the fact I could probably get a better grade from someone else. There's value in inspiration and insight. He has made me aware of the need to raise the bar and challenge myself more. He won't hold your hand, but gives helpful advice.

Absolutely awful professor. Least favorite at the U so far. Really pompous, goes off on tangents that he and some super-finance-students think are funny. Teaches in a way that if you don't kind of already know the concept, it is easy to get lost and confused. Highly recommend to NOT take Dubil.
You have to go to class and print the class lectures otherwise you won't pass...

Dubil is a great professor and loves to see his students succeed. This class in nature is not easy, and Dubil forces you to work hard. The class is composed of HW assignments and then tests. He prepares you really well by giving great examples in class and has half the notes made for you. He will not test you something he hasn't taught.
Hard class but he has worksheets for every week that help you understand the material. The worksheets are key to studying for the tests.

Dubil was awesome.  By all means, not an easy class, but if you actually do what he recommends when it comes to completing the homework and listening to the lectures you will do great.  He prepares you for the final and teaches real world application of the material.  I would take any class that he teaches.
Very helpful if you seek him out. Class material is not accessible so notes are a must.
The textbook is OK for some of the homework, but if you weren't there for the lecture you better already know the material. And don't expect the tests to be like the homework.

He is really prideful that his class average is really low. He sets his lessons up in a way that makes doing homework pretty easy. He only allows an hour for tests which is shorter than the allotted class time and unnecessary. He easily went off on tangents that had little to do with class, not the worst prof but far from great.

I enjoyed Mr Dubil. He taught things very clearly although he has wierd analogies to help understand, which didn't help me. He gives A LOT of homework. Do all of it and use them as study guides for the tests and you should do fine although the tests were a little different than the homework. He prepares you for the final since he helps write it.
I loved him, he was really knowledgeable and funny. The tests are hard though.

Robert is the one who writes the department final for 3040, his class is the hardest section offered but he will prepare you for whats on the final. He is very clear what is required and if you follow his homework's you will be fine. He is easy to understand, a little sarcastic but willing to help once he teases you a bit he really isn't mean.

I really enjoyed taking this class from Robert. The class is very hard but i learned a lot. Robert is a great professor, very knowledgeable, helpful and funny. He is from the east coast and is quite sarcastic which may be a little too much for some tender Utah students. Take this class from him if you really want to learn finance.

While the intro to finance has a lot of ground to cover, I felt it was taught rather poorly.  Questions are usually greeted with sarcasm.  If you don't read the book before class you will likely get nothing out of the lectures.

Dubil is an awesome professor. His class is hard a crap but it's worth it. He teaches the same way they'd teach at a bank and you learn the material that you'll actually use to find an execute arbitrage

ROBERT DUBIL might have a lot of Wall Street experience, but he is completely incompetent when it comes to academics. He uses humiliation tactics in class and his teaching is limited to making fun of other departments/professions.
Great way of explaining PV and FV and how to add and subtract money at different time periods. Don't care for the subject matter, but he explained it really well.

Once a professional in the field, Dubil has turned to teaching.  I don't know why, because he doesn't seem to care about students.  He does have a bit of a God complex, so that's probably why.  Lectures are boring, and tests are more difficult than the homework he assigns.  AVOID.

The real value in his class is wall-street perspective. Otherwise, this is basically an intro to investments course. If you already know short straddles and net variation margins, you are well on your way to an A grade. If you understand the homeworks completely (visit him during office hours if not) you are guaranteed >95% on the exams.

Lectures were very boring.  He was always available to answer questions and provide help.  Dubil uses humiliation tactics--it seems that he thought he was being funny, but was quite rude to people, even when they were trying to participate during the lectures.
No Comments

A good guy but needs to be louder and more entertaining in class. Finance is not a cup of tea for everyone in an MBA class and you need to build the interest. The class gets monotonus and its easy to loose interest even though the subject can get exciting if read from the text book.

Prof. Dubil is difficult, but interesting. Class lectures are funny and he can be somewhat aggressive in his style, but lectures were interesting and applicable to real-world. If you study and do the homework you will do well. He is always available for helping students and wants them to succeed, but only if you are serious about it.

I took Freedom & Constraint to satisfy my first IT requirement; this was an amazing course. Dale is kind, facilitates conversations very well, and provides helpful feedback. He is a lenient grader, with two shorter essays and one longer manifesto. Other than that, coming to class having read the selected text and ready to discuss is all.

Class discussions and material were interesting, there were only a few writing assignments throughout the semester that were weighed fairly heavily but easy to complete and get a good grade on. Dale is very caring and gives good feedback on writing assignments. I would recommend this class to anyone looking to fulfill their Honors IT requirement!
Great professor, lots of reading but class discussions are interesting! Would highly recommend Freedom and Constraints class, it is easy and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Awesome class with Freedom and Constraints be ready to read and participate but he makes lecture super engaging and entertaining I definitely recommend 2810 as an IT!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was essentially entirely reading and discussion which was appreciated, however it was a struggle at 8am. I would recommend Dr. Enggass and this course.
Dale was the greatest!!!! I loved all the readings and enjoyed how the course was structured. 10/10 recommend freedom and constraint if you're looking for an IT credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dale is awesome! The readings he assigned were always interesting, which meant I was significantly more inclined to read them, and he led good class discussions. HONOR2211 was my favorite honors class I've taken, so if you have to take it, take it with Dale :)

Really liked Dale and his class Freedom and Constraint! Lots of reading, but you can get by skimming a lot of the material before class. Two papers, one short midterm and a little bit longer final, but he gives you a lot of creative freedom with the final. I found a lot of the content of the class a bit boring, but others loved it.

Honors ITs can be boring at times and there were lots of readings, but you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and wants you to participate. Overall not the most interesting class but he graded fairly and made the discussions engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: So nice! Way better than taking a regular writing class. If you have to take 2211 take Dale.

Dale is a kind-hearted and amazing professor. In my writing class we only wrote 2 papers the entire semester but I learned more than I have learned in any writing class. We had amazing class participations and discussions, mostly interesting course content, an accessible canvas page, and an enjoyable class in general. Thank you Dale Enggass!

Professor Enggass really cares about his students, he is also clear about what he is looking for in their writing. He gives lots of opportunities for revisions and helps you in what/how to revise essays.

Dale is a G, I had him for Honors Freedom and Constraint.  There was a reading before each class.  The readings were never too long but often confusing.  Class time was spent looking at the reading and trying to figure out what they mean.  Pretty fun and based on participation.  Once a week we had to write little thoughts on what we were reading.

Excellent professor; very accessible, always willing to meet, and provides great feedback. It is evident that he wants his students to succeed and creates many opportunities for them to do so. Homework is minimal. It is the perfect course to get undergraduate English credit as majority of assignments are based on participation/completion.
Great Professor who assigned interesting readings. The papers were very flexible and allowed students to write about what we wanted to.

Dale Enggass is a great professor to take honors writing 2211 with. He is flexible in his schedule and cares more about his students learning than how well their grammar is. You will have to read and participate in conversations but he keeps them interesting. He is easy in a sense that his homework isn't going to take you all day to complete.
Professor Enggass is a truly nice person. I enjoy his class and his funny remarks. He can lead a great discussion!

Prof. Enggass was an amazing professor. There were very few assignments, biggest one was the final at the end but you can choose what you want to write about. In order to get an A you just have to show up, do the assignments on time, and present your final to the class or revise your other essay. Very kind professor and always willing to help :)

He is an awesome professor. He gives amazing feedback and very clearly wants students to do well in class. He grades based off participation and effort, rather than actual content, which is extremely refreshing. If you are willing to try, but don't have the best writing skills, it is perfect. Awesome content in class- very interesting readings.

- Not a lot of hw besides readings/papers
- Attendance encouraged 
- Discussion-based class, but speaking up isn't required to get participation points
- Professor is very easy to talk to, straight-forward, offers helpful feedback for papers, and finds interesting material to discuss
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this class! This is a discussion based class and you have to read the assigned readings! But theres are few assignments that are graded and if you do the work you will get an A. Fake is very caring and supportive, you can tell he loves what he does.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Dale as a professor. He was kind, engaging, inspired his students to do the work and think critically, was very responsive and provided great feedback. I truly wish my major had more required classes that were taught by him. He is a great human and professor overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: (Online due to Covid) Very quirky and warm sense of humor. Grades leniently while providing very helpful and detailed feedback on how to improve your writing. In the course we engaged with very relevant rhetorical material, and had interesting discussions as a class. Very approachable outside of class. I would definitely take his class again.

He has the quirkiest dry humor and is very personable. He cares about his students and is clear about what he wants out of them. Generous grader as long as you show you care. Take this class if you get the chance.

Dale is a honest person and is very insightful. Hes gives good feedback on papers and opens your mind in a more analytical way. At the same time, he is also a human that has a sense of humor. Dale truly involves himself in your learning and offers office hours and is open to email questions.

Dale is so awesome. I cannot recommend this class highly enough. Here's a good, unbiased rating: You have a few papers throughout the class but he gives you MORE than enough time to do them and is really helpful. He is super understanding and totally reasonable if you are having difficulties. The class is super easy and pretty enjoyable! Trust me!

Dale is awesome he creates such a great class environment. I met my two best friends in this class. Dale is such a witty and intelligent teacher but he for sure is shy so its hard to see at the beginning. I met up with him a lot to work on my essay final and he literally taught me how to write a good essay. I would recommend this teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Utah needs to require this class for all students. The content is critical and the organization of the online course makes it easy to stay on track. For my own personal reasons I fell behind during the semester, and Prof. Graham was my only professor to reach out and check in. The generous late policy helps you get caught up if you do fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: The online class consisted of only discussion posts each week and a final project at the end. An easy A if you enjoy discussion posts but there is a lot of reading so spend your time accordingly. The final project isn't hard but it does require knowledge of module topics so definitely read up on each one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This should be a required class for all students! Prof. Graham is clearly deeply knowledgeable about Gender Studies and this comes through even in an online course. When I was struggling, she replied quickly and offered help and guidance. I have learned so much this semester and wish that everyone had the chance to take a class like this!

I loved this class, and you can tell that Professor Graham really cares about her students. She gives clear guidance and is quick to respond to feedback. The person who wrote the review on February 1 may be a troll. I was in her class last spring and my friend had the same class in the fall. There are no tests. Strong intro course.
Profesor does not give much feedback. Very tough grader. Most boring online class because it was just test heavy. They were not involved and gave minimal examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Graham is an amazing instructor. She is always available to students. I had a lot of questions about the class and she always made time to answer my questions by email and when we met on Zoom. There is quite a bit of work required for the class, but because the class is so well organized and interesting it makes it easy to complete.
If gender studies is not your major, then this class might be more challenging for you. Additionally, the lecture videos often experience frame drops and low volume.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a nice professor, but it's advisable to avoid taking her class unless no other options exist. Her class demands a significant time investment in the short term, with endless discussions, readings, and analyses awaiting you. + low-quality lecture videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Overrall she is a Good teacher and probably the best one to teach CS2420 , However she is a very tough grader and nit picky. For some reason she thinks this is Harvard. But overrall apply your self from the beginning of the semester and not towards the end and you should pass. Dont be afraid to ask questions. She knows the material very well.

Lectures were condensed and sometimes hard to understand, but I think she teaches every topic well. Some of the homework problems could be written in a less confusing way, but overall the class is structured very well, and the labs and TAs will be helpful for exams if you pay attention.

Professor Parker is an amazing lecturer. Her class is organized very well. Showing up to class and doing the HW well in advance is all you need to succeed in her class. Exams are fair and what you need to know is clearly laid out on Canvas. People complain about her attitude, but I think it is more of a reflection of how applied you are in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend not taking this class. Although the coursework isn't necessarily hard, the professor is often rude with students and seems to want to take away as many points as possible from the students. She makes it so that students don't feel comfortable asking her question as her answers are often belittling.
Class is hard. Very uncomfortable class and the exams are hard.

Erin Parker runs her class in a frustrating manner. Only does lectures off powerpoints with a very uninterested attitude, youtube does a better job. Grading is meant to punish. Exams are written vaguely and regrading is limited to a week after the exam. Assignments are confusing and have hidden autograder tests. Other grading is extremely harsh

Erin Parker may be the worst professor I have ever had, and that is no exaggeration. Please do not take her as a professor for an already difficult course like this one. Save yourself, this is your warning.
When you ask her a question she responds with a somewhat condescending tone and attitudem as if to say why would you ask me that? i really feel like she doesn't respect her students
This professor is very strict, so if you take her class you're going to have a hard time...

I would not recommend taking this professor's class, she doesn't use a microphone and only speaks in a very quiet voice in a lecture hall of about 200 students, the exams and assignments are very challenging. Even if you prepare a lot, it's still easy to end up with a low score
She's ok. Kinda mean.
Attending this class is like participating in a self-humiliation ritual. I would avoid unless you have a degradation kink.

If you like feeling like a respected person, take this course from a different professor. Never have I ever had a teacher so consistently condescending. She is truly a specimen to be studied on the effective use of professional language to talk down to, belittle, and otherwise degrade students. 

She is proficient in Java, that's all I can say.
Very lecture heavy but did not do a good job explaining topics well. Felt very elitist and talked down to students.

Dr. Parker was an excellent lecturer. She was always clear and concise with the material she covered. I believe her greatest weakness is that she tends to be dismissive with students who are asking questions or answering her questions in class. I would recommend her class if you do not need extra help from your professor.

Prof. Parker is very intelligent and knows/ explains concepts well. Tests are directly related to assignments and lectures, so be sure to study each topic throughly before moving on. TA hours are good if you need help debugging.

Great lecturer and instills a problem solving mindset quite well but she is overtly condescending if your question is even slightly off topic and the later programming assignments are difficult and time consuming. Tests were on the easier side especially if you attend lectures and study a teeny bit.

This instructor legitimately docked me points because I had 5 spaces in between two major sections of my program and apparently that is "too many spaces". She's mean in person, passive aggressive as hell, and seems to constantly be in a crappy mood. Take this class from someone else if you want a comfortable classroom experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: For a course that introduces computer science, Prof. Parker does a great job of explaining the material clearly and answering any questions you might have, given you don't fall behind. She is an amazing lecturer, and the pace of the class is not terrible. However, she does not seem to care much about her students or foster a positive climate.
Lecture quality is superb. Though, be cautious about answering questions and asking them because she does not mind cooking you in front of the class.

Very challenging professor to approach let alone ask questions to. I, along with many others felt as if we were on a time crunch the second we walked in the door. I used TA's (who were bothered doing their own hw during ta hours) and met with her outside of class to get extra help. VERY test heavy class and the assignments grew unproportionally hrd

Erin Parker is straight up mean. If you fall behind on material she will not give you any grace. Horrible learning environment because she is so discouraging and rude to students. Ask a question and get "You would know that if you listened" type of stuff from her all the time. No answer either, she will just move on.

This professor was very hard to work with. The lectures took far longer than necessary, and she doesn't listen to student feedback, like when the majority of the class doesn't understand a topic. The assignments are very involved, and the lectures don't prepare you at all for them.
Worst professor I have ever had at Utah so far.

Professor Parker was a decent instructor, but in my experience, she was very strict and unapproachable. If you needed help, she often discouraged rather than supported you, sometimes making harsh remarks like “you shouldn't be in the program.” It didn't feel like she genuinely wanted to teach or motivate students,given of doing it for the pay

2420 is the pair programming class. Parker's class is difficult, yet relatively cut and dry. I'm under the impression the CS courses are being mandated to be kept difficult for competition sake, however, she was very accommodating when students ask for help. Some condescension, very specific tests, and TA help often nets a 90% grade on assignments.

It seems like most people's experiences with Prof. Parker were pretty bipolar. I think that in the 1410 class, she did tend to have a bit of a demeaning tone to the students, but what else can you do to deal with 120 freshman CS majors? Despite that, she taught really well, and was helpful when you would ask her things outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are somewhat uninspiring, and the content is manageable to learn outside of class, if you are already a very good coder. Otherwise, attending class is probably best, and it does get mind-numbing at times. She can also be a bit rude to people, but I think I would prefer her over the other CS 2420 teachers, as they are not good either.

It's important to know that this is a very hard CS class, since it's a weed-out class. So, that reflects badly on anyone who teaches it, in my opinion. But I don't really have any issues with Dr Parker. She was very nice in class and was very active in answering questions and on Piazza.
Exams were not as hard, but a lot of homework.

She's an amazing professor. She teaches clearly and takes her classes very seriously. She doesn't stand for people who don't put in any effort. If you are sincerely trying to learn, she will work with you and will be very caring. She can seem intimidating at first, but halfway through the semester you realize that she is actually awesome.
Very rude professor that belittled me for not understanding the material and stated that I should not be in Computer Science even though I went to every lecture and went to TA hours.
She was fine. Not the best Professor. Won't respond to emails if you don't call her by professor. Took bott camp previously and her class made no sense sometimes.

She was very difficult when questions about the material. The TAs were practically the only reason why I was able to pass. Very uncaring and felt like she didn't really feel like helping her students succeed or improve. The material she trying to teach was interesting to me, but she made it hard to learn effectively for the reasons stated before.

Great at teaching, you don't have to study if at all outside of class if you pay attention during the lectures, unlike some of the other teachers here at the U, all content on the exam is content she will have already prepared you for during lecture. If you waste others time during lectures then she is mean (a good thing), otherwise caring. 10/10

Told one of the foreign exchange students in class that he was using translation tools as a crutch and that he was doing poorly in the class because he wasn't thinking in english. I've never had a professor act this disgusting to any student in class before. Avoid at all costs.
She just doesn't motivate you at all. She just tears you down and makes a point of you. Which can be good for learning but she could totally do it in a better way

Prof. Parker is competent, but having her as my professor wasn't really enjoyable. She passes "the bar" to be a good enough professor to not be a barrier in your learning. Start on assignment early and devote enough time to the class. Review concepts you do not understand. Do the practice tests before midterms and the final and you should be fine.

Professor Parker is a good professor. She's not there to be your friend but to teach, and she does a good job of teaching the class and structuring the course. She will not cut you slack, so stay on top of your work. Her midterm study guides and practice exams were great prep for exams. She is kind and helpful at office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can't say I enjoyed her class very much. A noticeable step down compared to the other CS professors I've had. Classes often felt hostile towards asking questions, and the workload requires quite the commitment as well. There are definitely worse professors out there, but I wouldn't recommend regardless.

2420 is the weeder class for the major. If you show that you care and are putting in the effort and ask questions, she will put in effort to support you. She's not a warm personality - don't mistake this for "she doesn't care about students", she does, but won't save you if you want to coast along. Do beware occasional ambiguous grading criteria.

Professor Parker is a good professor. She can be a little stern in class, but explains things clearly and concisely. If you have a strong Java background, this class will be a breeze, but make sure you find a good partner. Tests were fair and clear, TAs provided lots of support. (This class was co-taught with another professor over the summer.)

Professor Parker's CS2420 is challenging, but engaging. Lectures are clear, and she provides useful resources. The workload is heavy, but manageable if you stay on top of it. unstuck AI was a game-changer for my study prep. Overall, a rewarding experience.

Professor Parker is knowledgable, concise, and direct; but, seems to hold genuine contempt for her students. Someone who should be in the field and not teaching. Asking a question in any context feels like an imposition. Skip.
Prof. Parker is great. I learned so much in 2420 and really enjoyed it. It's definitely one of the most time-consuming classes I've taken but if you put in the effort, you will get a lot out of it.

First - she is a great lecturer. She's go that going for her. BUT, the workload far exceeds the typical 6-9 hours expected from a 3 credit-hour course. Weekly workload is AT LEAST 15 hours - often 20 to 25. It's insane! I get straight A's except here. I already know most of the material, yet I can barely keep up. It's unconscionable. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Erin Parker often talked down to students, insulting people for having "bad" questions, and was generally unhelpful when students had innocent questions. Her slides and teaching style were incredibly boring, making the content much harder to grasp than it actually was. I had more success using google over her hyperregulated intranet forum "Piazza"

My experience with Prof. Parker was pretty good. If you meet with her one on one she is very supportive and gives great feedback/advice. This specific class is rough but she makes it as bearable as it can be. Her lecture slides tend to be a bit more convoluted than I think they can be. The extra practice questions and TAs are your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I think Professor Parker is a good professor, not the greatest that I've had during my CS journey but I think she is good. Great at answering questions and is very knowledgeable. I can see why a lot of people like her but the one thing I don't like is her slides as much for learning these subjects. Love how she gives tons of practice each lecture.

I had Dr Parker in CS1420 and CS1810 and she is quite a polarizing professor to say the least. It's clear she knows her stuff although I can see why people view her as mean. She was much more relaxed in 1810 with a smaller class than 1420. If you put an effort into learning she will put effort into helping you. She's not vague in any way.

Professor Parker gets a lot of bad rep for being a professor who is straight to the point takes no bs. Definitely the best CS professor I have ever had. Most people writing a 1.0 review are students who do not understand what respect is, take a class with Professor Parker if you get the chance.

Lectures weren't great. They were hard to sit through and felt lacking at times. She nurtured a terrible learning environment by putting down students and sometimes the class as a whole constantly. She feels out of touch when she rambles. Try to get as much as you can from the reading and TAs as she won't be much help both in and out of class.

A professor's role extends beyond just delivering lectures. It is crucial for professors to create an environment where students feel comfortable seeking help and guidance especially in a difficult class such as this. Erin Parker did not make any effort to help struggling students and even put them down, making them feel unfit for computer science.
She might be okay at lecturing, but its the most capricious, stuck up, apathetic person you will ever meet. Don't bother meeting outside of class or emailing.

Professor Parker is really great. She is very knowledgeable and organized, but also quite strict. This class is fairly difficult, but you'll do well if you put in the work. The exams can also be a bit challenging, so make sure you understand everything. I've learned a ton in this class and had an overall good experience.

Parker is a really good instructor. Lectures are clear and very informative. The class can be challenging, however she makes sure to lay out topics in a very logical way. Assignment are time intensive, however they help you to become a better programmer and understand the content. Grading is tough, but fair so long as you know the content.

Erin Parker is an incredible professor. If you're taking a class because you're fundamentally interested in computer science then you love her for her straightforwardness with concepts, well prepared lectures, and extremely useful office hours. Some may say she's strict or uptight, but I believe this shows how professional and direct she is.

I think Erin gets a bad rap, she is pretty blunt and intimidating but she is really helpful if you ask for help. She is one of the better professors in terms of looking at your code and helping you understand what the issue is. If you are respectful and come prepared she will be great and help you out.

Parker is condescending and her teaching style is of one of obedience through fear. I ignored the red flags around Parker. I thought her rating outweighed what I found. I was wrong. Avoid this professor, not because she's 'hard', but because she doesn't respect others while still demanding respect from them.
She is clever professor. But, the lecture is so difficult and it isn't to get a good grade on assignments or exams.

Erin Parker gets mad when you do not refer to her as PROFESSOR. If you do not refer to her as PROFESSOR when emailing her, she will be offended. This has to be one of the most pretentious professors at the U. It is a nightmare having to talk to her. She will also be very mad if you show up to her office without an appointment. She is judgemental
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have another option for a professor, check them out first. She answers questions in a super vague, non-answer way. She considers everything to be cheating, even asking and talking to your fellow students about code or course material. You are only allowed to ask her and the Ta's for help, anyone else and she considered you to have cheated.

The structure to 2100 is the same for all professors. Erin's exams are no harder than her hw and exam reviews. If you understand the hw, you'll know how to do her exams. My one major complaint is that she's a nitpicky grader. You will lose lots of points for skipping seemingly minor steps. If not for this, she would be my favorite professor.
Hard to get a good grade on exams and lots of homework but she is a really nice professor.

Dr. Parker's lectures are always organized and clear, as are her assignments. She cares about her students and will answer their questions understandably. She gives good feedback, but sometimes it can come out a bit abrasive, which might offend students if they don't realize she's only doing it to help. Overall, I found her to be very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Parker is a very tough professor, but she is fair.  Doing well in 2420 was a huge time commitment but Dr. Parker gives you the resources you need (it's just a lot of resources to work through).  This class was definitely stressful, but I learned a lot, and Dr. Parker was very responsive to any questions I ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is extremely well organized and will teach you a lot. Parker does an excellent job at choosing assignments and exam questions but everything requires a large time commitment. Only students willing to put in the time and utilize her many resources (TA's, readings, labs, etc) will do well in this class. I would recommend Parker any day.

I think the best way to explain it is that she scares you into committing 300% of your effort to this class and learning the content. This is a stressful technique, but also effective. I learned a lot but at a very large time cost. In her class, there is a such thing as a "dumb" question, and she's rude about it.

The negative reviews cannot distinguish between difficult course material and a poor professor. Professor Parker's course was extremely rigorous but equally fair and organized. If you're adequately prepared for the material and find interest in it, you will learn many important concepts that will set you up for future CS courses/a career in CS.

She's as tough as her reputation, but she's an incredible teacher. She's organized, and fits as much into a lecture as she can. Assignments are hard, but you will grow so much as a programmer for having her class. Talk to her one on one and she is very sweet and answers any questions without making you feel bad. Her class is hard but very worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Parker seems like a good professor at first but she makes her tests insanely hard and doesn't teach all the material necessary. Stay away from her if you can!

To be honest, it's a rough class for students who just finished CS1410, but it doesn't mean that Erin Parker is a bad professor. Assignments are rough, but most of them are not IMPOSSIBLE to complete unless you spend the whole weekend just hanging out. Also, if your score is lower than average from Exam 2, you just didn't study

Assignments are very tedious, and the requirements are not particularly clear. In addition, in the exam, there are a lot of questions to read and understand. This is very time-consuming. I don't think I would take this professor's course again.

Why do you need to pay attention to written grammar and word correctness in the test, there are so many short answer questions. And she has a huge amount of homework, which takes about 12 hours a week to complete. And her verbal skills are poor, you spend a long time understanding what she wants you to achieve before every programming and test
Prof. Parker once said in my class "a C student will always be a C student". Likewise, a terrible professor will always be a terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Horrible prof, but hey at least I don't have to deal with her anymore!

I want to say Erin is a good professor. She's organized, lectures are insightful, and the class is structured well. However, she is NOT NICE. Ask a dumb question in class? She'll roast you in front of everyone. If you struggle to learn in her office hours, she'll just be irritated and make you feel pressured because of this. FAILURE of a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Why the University of Utah does not hire other professors?

Absolute dog sh**. Spend 15-20 hours a week on the homework then oh wait you're not done, you have to do a post assignment "analysis document" and tests which can take hours. Expectations are WAY higher than she says in the rubric. Absolutely terrible human and terrible class. Do a month of code academy on data structures and you'll learn better.

Erin parker is the worst professor I have ever had. I credit her for pushing me out of the computer science major. Like others are saying, she knows her stuff, but the constant snapping at students who ask questions, the weird smug way she carries herself, and her unapproachable cold demeanor makes this class miserable. Not to mention it is HARD.

Read/watch information before class, then session consisted of going over that information and having the class answer practice problems. Parker was always clear in her lectures and able to answer all questions. Her or her TAs were always available outside of class to answer questions. Quizzes before every class and tests on every unit, plus final.

Tests count for a majority of your grade and are made very difficult. That's not the bad part however, this professor gives you a pre-class quiz for EVERY class, which adds a lot of unnecessary work and stress before each class and makes you not want to go to class. The professor is also very intimidating.

The structure of this class makes no sense. If you don't do even a single problem on the homework you cannot receive a higher grade than a 33 percent on it. 1/3 of the class gets a D or lower on every test. Also extremely condescending teacher. Avoid both the class and prof at all costs. More work than my 4 credit coding course.

CS2100 was the second class I've taken with Parker. CS2100 (discrete math) lends itself better than 2420 does to her ultra-precise, no-nonsense lecture style. Parker's classes are very difficult, but fair. While she comes off as rather harsh during lectures, 1-on-1 she is quite kind and patient 1-on-1 so don't be afraid to go to office hours!
Worst professor I have ever suffered through. Rigid course structure isn't helped by the fact that she is condescending and unapproachable at every opportunity.

I took CS2100 with Professor Parker (Don't call her anything else, or else) and it was extremely difficult. The workload is insane, and the tests are frequent and difficult. If you don't study/understand the material, you will not pass. Asking questions in email/piazza were met with condescending tones making getting help difficult and frustrating.

My friend took this class with a different teacher and did about half the work. Her ego makes her very hard to talk to or ask questions. Wait to take this class until you don't have to her her as a teacher. god bless the TAs for doing all the actual work for the class. Don't make the mistake of not addressing her as professor or doctor parker
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Parker is a good professor. She has gone out of her way several times when I needed extra help, all you have to do is ask. You can tell that she really cares about her students success. The only thing I didn't like was the harsh grading, everything is graded based on her opinion making it hard to get the exact correct answer.

Professor Parker is a good professor. Any time I needed extra help, and asked her, she went out of her way to help me to understand anything I had trouble with. She literally spent an hour with me going over things I struggled with (one of the times I asked her). This class is very time consuming. I spent 18+ hours for this class every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prepare to spend 15-20 hours a week on just the assignment, not including recitation, lab, reading, videos, etc. Her grading of multiple choice questions is harsh and arbitrary. The "comprehensive" covered maybe 10% of the curriculum so if you didn't COMPLETELY understand that small part it, sucks to be you. Average was 68% and she won't curve it.

Though she is very knowledgeable about CS and all the topics in this class, I was shocked by her awful attitude and condescending tone. I have never felt less respected by anyone in my life. Be ready to spend 15-20 hours a week doing the projects, which by the way are not easy. Lectures were pretentious and mediocre. Avoid Parker at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would describe Prof. Parker as "CS: The Person." Parker is a very clear instructor, says everything that she needs to say, and doesn't say a thing more. On the exams, the grading criteria for free response was unclear/poor, and I wouldn't bother w/ a regrade request, but other than that I think the class was very well done for covid time.

Erin Parker is a very strict professor and it's next to impossible to do well in this class without spending 15+ hours on each of the 11 assignments (except maybe the first one). The tests represent the material well but are too long. It'd be nice if she explained the material better and had more recitation time rather than lecture time.

Professor Parker is incredibly strict with her class structure. She isn't the warmest or coziest professor but she is incredibly knowledgeable. Partner work is expected after the first assignment, class is super tough if you don't have a good partner and are new to coding. Start early on assignments otherwise you'll have a bad time.

Essentially it's Professor Parker's way or the highway. Your average snobby professor with very little real world insight. We're forced to work with partners in a way the industry will never have us do. You will do poorly if you don't follow the rigid class structure. This class is great if you're a tool with no free will, otherwise look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She definitely knows what she's talking about, and I like how organized she is. She can seem a little intimidating, but personally, I like how professional she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Every assignment but the first was a partner assignment. The assignments and quizzes were fair enough, but the average on every one of her tests for my class was a failing grade. This could be because it was all online this semester, but when everyone is failing, it can't just be that the students aren't working hard enough.

This class probably the hardest thing I've ever done in my life. I've never done CS till I got to the U, but man the assignments and exams are tough as hell. I'm retaking it next semester. Find a good partner and make sure you have a light semester for this class. Very intense, and the prof isn't very nice.. Make use of TA hours

EXTREMELY organized. doesn't take any nonsense but is NOT rude. She is incredibly knowledgeable and is very helpful in office hours. Lectures are clear and she has a to-do list for each week on canvas. HW takes 15+ hours AT LEAST each week but it's just a very demanding course. Parker is great and I wish she taught more classes. fair and clear.

The assignment is really heavy, you have to spend around 18-25 hours/week to do that assignment and there are 11 of them. Also, the midterms and final are extremely hard and the grading is strict too. If you miss a small thing, you lost the point. I got an A during the semester for all the assignment and quiz but midterms and final low it to B+
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know how Parker has such a high rating. Her grading scheme is arbitrary and harsh. She is rude and does not take well to polite questions. I would highly advise taking this class from a different professor, the material is not difficult the professor is.

She's a nitpicky grader when it comes to exams. You're never 100% confident if your answers satisfices her. Even if your answer is almost correct she may refuse partial credit. She grades written responses open ended. One small mistake and she deduces alot. Your answer can't just be right, it has to be right specifically to her satisfaction.

Professor Parker is strict, but very clear and concise in her lectures. She explains concepts thoroughly and replies quickly to questions posted on Piazza. The TAs during my semester were very helpful and you could tell they took their time helping students with assignments and other questions.
Take another professor unless you want to be stressed all the time. She is ruthless and does use condescending language.

Dr. Parker is an amazing professor, she is extremely thorough with her lectures and material. If you want an amazing understanding of a course, definitely take it from her. She can come off as patronizing at times, but she really does care about the students. Definitely a difficult class, but a great experience nonetheless.
