Professor Feldman is honestly amazing. I would 100% recommend his office hours, sometimes rambles in lectures but just go to his office hours. Also, his exams are JUST LIKE the practice exams which is great. He makes calculus super easy, I did have to do outside work for his class but his class is an easy B, and not impossible to get an A.

I thought his lectures were very fun but I know others got confused by his longer rambles. The weekly homework is time consuming but not too difficult, the exams were graded rather generously with lots of partial credit, and the labs were honestly the hardest part of the class but you could get plenty of help from the TAs.

great and clear lecturer and sometimes pretty funny. takes his time to address students questions, does plenty of examples on each topic. tests were generally pretty easy. he definitely wants each student to succeed. Sometimes the homeworks did feel tedious though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, I really struggled but he was very nice and very helpful when it came to doing practice problems and getting the topic explained in a new way! Well organized page and wants students to succeed and understand the topic, take online math from him if you have to do it online!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall good class, Canvas page was organized so it was easy navigate. You do have weekly assignments on like 3-4 topics, with recorded lectures that vary from 20 to around 50 minutes on each topic. It's doable and the assignments correlate with the lectures. Professor answers questions and is attentive, would take a class from him again!

Dr. Fu was given a bad hand. The final exam was challenging, but if you studied enough for it (most people did not), it was easily passable. Me and a few friends studied the class for a day and made a cheat sheet with all info from the study guide and we all got above 80%. Very intelligent, but maybe doesn't teach in the most effective way.

There are 3 auto-fail conditions to his class and he is obviously looking for any excuse to fail students. HW isn't bad.  The mastery quizzes are based off the idea that MEs don't know topics from their past classes well enough, autofail if you don't get 4/5 these perfectly. Studied for final for at least 20 hours and still felt very bad on it.

He is probably the most intelligent professor I have ever had. While the 'mastery questions' were the most tedious quizzes, I hate to admit they were successful in what they are supposed to do. Exams were manageable if you go into the class prepared to learn and not just use ai on all assignments.The lab attached to this class is unnecessary though

In office hours, he makes you feel like you are d for asking questions. You must pass 9 out of 13 quizzes perfectly (no mistakes at all) to pass the class with a C/C+. When you learn your mistake and retake the same chapter quiz the following week, it is something else that he doesn't like and fails you. He is very knowledgeable, but very tough

Henry Fu, he is a prime example for why research professors should not teach, he is graded on a pass or fail system, that relies on two midterms, and passing 4 out of 5 quizzes, he gives, but he grades them extremely harshly, as in one minor mistake, and you fail, and his lectures revolve around him reading off slides.

Henry Fu is an example of how not to be a teacher, his lectures are mandatory, but they only cover the baseline of the material, the class runs on a pass or fail system where in if you don't pass 4/5 quizzes throughout the semester, the 1 midterm and final, than you will fail the course, and he takes 1-2 days to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes taken throughout the semester that were pass fail. If you didn't pass 4/5 of them, the best grade you could get was a C-. Our last opportunity to take them was 2 weeks before the final. He refused to grade them before the final, so everyone would have to take the final no matter what. That's just disrespectful of other peoples time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No exams during the semester—just pass/fail quizzes. They do not reflect the difficulty of the final. I did well in the rest of the class, but failed the final and the class. The final felt like a new course. If you expect your work throughout the semester to matter, it doesn't. One high-stakes final decides if you pass.

Terrible way of teaching and a terrible professor overall. If you ask him a question he's like a deer in headlights. He has an understanding of concepts but no communication skills/common sense. There's no point in taking this class because you'll have to take it at least twice. He doesn't teach, his final is a guessing game for who gets to pass.

Professor Fu's class was a nightmare. Most students failed the final, which had lots of material that none of us had seen before. His "fail final, fail course" policy is ridiculous, especially considering only half the class passed after a curve. His teaching is unlike anything I've seen before, avoid him at all costs.

The grading criteria of this class is a joke, I had an A in both the lab and lecture with near perfect scores on every assignment. However, with his “accurate test of knowledge” final, we had an outstanding 27 ish % pass the test with this initial criteria. Hats off to this guy for being the most incompetent professor in my two years of school.

I had an A in both sections of this class until the final exam. I still would have passed the class if it weren't for his “fail the final and you fail the semester” policy. He isn't a terrible lecturer — but between the final project taking me 50 hours and surprise subjects on the final exam, this class is difficult to pass — few were able to.

The class itself was a ridiculous amount of work for only three credit hours. There were no exams before the final, so it was completely unclear what to expect. 60% on the final was needed to pass the class, which left more than half of the students failing. Completely unfair. The final had content that wasn't covered in class or on the study guide
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fu should not actually be a professor, it is clear that he understands each concept but does not convey them well in class. There is only one test, the final, which 11/13 people I talked to failed. Lots of the stuff on the final I had never seen in class or on the study guide. I spent upwards of 10 hours studying and failed the final.

Fluid mechanics. The flipped classroom format is weird, but you'll be fine if you don't procrastinate and go to the extra question lectures. Getting stuck due to minor mistakes was frustrating though.

Flipped class. Watch lectures on own time, then take PASS/FAIL quiz each Friday, which has infinite retakes however requires 100%. Seriously love the guy, but this curriculum was brutal. Very disheartening to fail a quiz multiple times due to small mistakes. Success is possible and rewarding, start early, get ahead, and STUDY HARD for each quiz.

This class was poorly set up. Expect at least a couple hours of lectures to watch outside of class. Every Friday was quiz day, and if you don't get 100% then you don't pass the quiz. There is no room for error and even small mistakes will make the quiz "incomplete" and you have to retake it. Terrible set up and brutal grading.

This is a flipped classroom that makes you watch his old lecture videos from 2021 on your own time. The lecture time then becomes office hours or time to take practice quizzes. I think this style is very lazy, but the content of the class is not too bad if you take your time understanding the videos and homeworks. Stop doing flipped classrooms.

Henry Fu is one of the worst professors I've ever had. This class was taught so lazily, and he used mundane prerecorded lectures from years ago that did not apply to homework or quizzes. Performance in the class is based on passing quizzes, but you won't pass quizzes unless you do them perfectly. He then offers no help in aiding you to pass quizzes

He does not teach, just makes the class watch insanely dry videos that do not correlate to the quizzes or homework. Sure he lets you retake quizzes which if you do not get a perfect score you fail, but this is the laziest formatted class I've ever taken. Researchers are not capable of teaching, seems to be a trend in University of Utah.

Given a bad hand. Curriculum isn't his. Lecture and teaching wise he is great; personal and willing to explain. Homework can be vague and hard to decode. Spend more time understanding question than doing it. Coding aspect is a slap to the face for average Mech E students. Exams are medium difficult. Final project is a nightmare, but possible.

One of the most difficult classes I've ever taken, but it wasn't Fu's fault. He was given confusing homeworks that took longer to understand the question than formulating a solution. Really tough grading, prepare to spend 10-20 hours/week on homework. Will respond to emails quickly and meet with you outside of class time. Wants students to learn.

Professor Fu is just out of his mind when it comes to homework vs lectures. Lectures focus primarily on computations while the labs focus on coding. The homework is the combination of the two but the expectation is you know how to code at an advanced level and the labs do not relate to the homework at all. There are exams for both labs and lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is go-at-your-own-pace. It works great for some people, but not for others. It's important not to procrastinate! He's very helpful and wants you to succeed. There are quizzes you need to pass on every unit, and he's a pretty strict grader (but can retake the quizzes as much as needed). You need ~100% to pass tho. Hard but generally fair.

One homework, one quiz, each week. Expectations are very clear. Videos are informative and do practice problems. Feedback is useful and on time. The guy even offers replacement quizzes for midterm and final. My only gripe with him is that his midterm and final were significantly harder than expected.

I really enjoyed this class and how it was structured. There were no exams in this class, but instead weekly quizzes that were very similar to the HW material you learned during the week. During midterm and final exam periods, he would allow you to take replacement quizzes that would replace your scores from previous quizzes. Highly recommend!

Henry Fu is the most organized professor I have ever had. You know everything that you need to do and when you need to do it. He gets grades back in under a week. He grades fair and I love his quiz system where you just take weekly quizzes and the "exams" are quiz retakes. He is great at explaining complex and new topics. He's also just a good guy.

Fengjiao Weng is someone who is not cut out to be a professor. She makes it known that this is a hard course. Whether that be her difficult grading criteria, homework, and lab assignments that don't count for anything, lackluster review questions, and tests that are worth 44% of your grade. This is supposed to be an intro class. Go to SLCC.

Spring Semester 2026, COMP 1010 was the worst class that I've taken as a student here at the University of Utah. Fengjiao Weng makes it known that this is a difficult class. Between the harsh grading criteria, labs, and homework that count for nothing. Tests count for 40% of your grade, and will have trick questions; reviews don't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is a review for CS 1000. This course is quite test heavy with 6 midterms, a final project, and a final exam. The test questions are usually very different from the study guides provided. Be careful asking question in this class, as they are regularly answered with a strong condescending tone. I would not recommend taking this class.

Practice tests not useful at all for preparing for the tests. Makes it extremely hard to study for them, and in my opinion it is unfair to have a test in a different format with much harder problems than the study guide. Most in class appear to be falling asleep. Mandatory polls for attendance and they are too quick on screen for half a second.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures feel very long, and are unhelpful. Attendance is mandatory and 10% of your grade, so if you don't show up to most lectures it's impossible for you to receive an A. She grades very harshly and is not very forgiving, the class material is very easy if you have any kind of coding background, but she makes it difficult to receive a decent grad

Professor Wang was very kind and has very clear lectures. Lecture slides had everything I needed, and she did a great job at expanding on what is taught in them with examples. Some assignments seemed daunting at first due to the way the instructions were given, but by the end I always found them very doable and usually fun. A very enjoyable class.

Professor Fleck is a poor-lecturer who cares about his class. His lectures are sometimes difficult to follow as he doesn't really do examples. I kind of lost track of what was going on by the end of the semester. Despite this, he is very good at answering questions, and his practice exams are incredibly helpful.

This professor is great, his teaching style might not be the best but he makes up for it by making it clear what the exam questions will be, if you study the practice exams then you're guaranteed to pass. Never had a math class this easy even though it is calculus 3. gives extra credit and replace one of the two exams with the final if it is higher

I didn't like his lecture at all because I only learn from math from watching someone solve a problem, but he want to make sure you learn the concept, I learned it in the summer with 1 months and a half time and I couldn't really learn anything because the way he teach. But the class is very easy to get an A even if you don't like the class.
tests are hard, writes in chalk, eat a frank

Mr. Fleck is my favorite instructor so far. His lectures were straight and related to the textbook, and he gave us extra credits. The best memory was he gave one point to everyone who showed up at class on the last day before fall break. It was easy to get good grades in his class as long as you were hard-working.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Engineering calc is hard, Jonathon made it a little less so. Lectures are often straight from the textbook, so if you're a self-starter and can put in the work on your own, the lectures aren't very necessary. Quizzes are easy and open note, exams will challenge you as there are no calculators/notes allowed. Lots of homework because it's calculus.

I can tell that he wants people to succeed in his class. He was very generous with extra credit and dropping grades. Calculus is a hard concept, but he explained it better than anyone has in the past. I would highly recommend him if you are looking for a good professor for an introductory calculus class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved Jonathon. Had him for multivariable calculus for summer 2022. His assignments are made such that you can easily learn the material elsewhere. He gave extensions to the entire class a lot. VERY flexible online; accommodating when I asked to take my final a few days earlier. Recommended if you plan to take a math class, especially online.

Professor Feng made Thermodynamics one of my favorite courses I've taken. His lectures were easy to follow, and he explained concepts clearly and thoroughly while doing practice problems. He prints out lecture notes every class so you can have those on hand. The exams are really easy and are open note. Highly recommend taking his class

This class was one of my favourites for my degree, it was so hard but I learned so much and feel I understood the material so well. He might be the perfect professor for this class, it's hard but his system of notes and teaching feels refined
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher tests are really fair. Homework is easy doable go to class!

A little difficult without going to lecture. Should be a breeze if you attend. Laid back and a good lecturer. Homework is a good amount, and tests are open note and book. Hone in on homework and focus on details in the tests. Lecture consists of real world examples and helpful examples of problems.

Really enjoyed this class. You can tell a lot of effort was put in by Dr.Feng to make this a more straightforward and intuitive class. He gave a lot of resources to the students and will do a lot of review before a test. He will go out of his way for you if you need it. Truly, he wants you to pass.

Professor Feng did a great job teaching the concepts he expected us to know, and he stayed within those concepts for homeworks and exams. Tests were open note, and he supplies his lecture notes, and equation sheet for students to use. I thought he was also excellent at interpreting questions and giving clear and useful answers to those questions.

Tianli Feng was a pretty good teacher. However, lectures felt very disjointed and hard to follow (maybe it's just thermo). He kept erasing, re-writing, explaining, drawing, and erasing again until the chalk board was just a mess of thermo concepts. The saving grace was the provided lectures that we could mark up. Fair homework, quizzes, and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a fantastic professor, just be prepared to put in a lot of time and effort since this is a hard class in general. He printed out all his lectures, which summarized and condensed everything we needed to know. The grades were fair and he showed that he wants us to succeed. Thoroughly study the packets and homework problems, then you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Feng was awesome! This was his first semester teaching. For his thermo class, he made note packets for each lecture and they were very well put together. The homework was helpful and fair. Exams were very fair. The only thing I feel Prof. Feng could improve on is concise explanations--there was a bit of a language barrier.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No notes. A very good and fair professor. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I still showed up every morning because his lectures were super helpful. His exams are also super fair and you are guaranteed to do well on them if you study.
Thermodynamics is tough, but he is an incredibly organized and helpful instructor. He is very generous with his time and helped clarify the complex concepts for me. Highly recommend.

I have never had a professor who seemed more like he did not want his students to succeed. He went out of his way to make the course more difficult and tedious than it needed to be. Francoeur is the kind of professor who will allow you to have one two sided page of notes on an exam, but calls you a cheater for having two one sided pages of notes.

Favorite professor at the university so far.  Would absolutely take a class from him again (even though I am not very fond of heat transfer).  Going to class is not required, but will he give significant test/HW help.  Excellent lecture notes posted online.
One of the best professors I have ever had. He explains the concepts very clearly and simply. His class is not the easiest class but it is fair.

Francoeur is an amazing professor. Thermo I isn't easy, but if you show up and do the homework you will be fine. He sets aside a lot of time for office hours each week. Very clear about what is on tests (works through old exams in class before each test) , and very willing to help you when you're struggling. I hope I have him for future classes

Professor Francoeur is a clear teacher.  Thermo I ended up being one of my favorite courses during the semester because of him.  He is very black and white about his expectations for the class. Tests are worth 90%.  You take 2 midterms and final, but they are more than fair with good preparation.
Super passionate and actually wants you to learn. Participation matters but he gives lots of opportunities beyond speaking in class.
Dr. Drews is an excellent professor—easily one of the top three I had during my four years at the University of Utah. I highly recommend him.
Dr Drews was the best Prof I had during my years at the U.

Prof Drews was a great professor and all of his tests were very straight forward. I never felt like he had the intention of tricking me with the test questions. As long as you come to class and take notes, you'll be fine when it comes to test day. He is very funny as well.
Great professor! Interesting lectures and knows what he is talking about. Easy grading and extra credit opportunities. Would definitely take again!

Prof Drews is great. His lectures are engaging and highly relevant for everyone who is working. This class helped me develop insights into issues and problems at the workplace. Highly recommend this class.
Amazing professor. Highly knowledgeable. He cares about his students.
Prof. Drews is absolutely amazing. Highly recommend.
Excellent class

I took this professor in Spring 2024. They're intelligent, respected, and their lectures were always engaging and the professor made it easy for students to participate on topics and ask questions. My favorite memory was the final exam, where we could score 100% by answering every question wrong. My friend and I did that and both got 100%!

Frank Drews was a great teacher. Very understanding and will go out of his way to help you out. He is really into airplanes so a lot of this course is about human errors that are made within airplanes and things like that. There is a ton of information on the lecture slides which makes it very hard to retain and focus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable professor and is passionate about what he teaches, thus keeping lectures interesting and engaging despite the content being somewhat uninteresting. There is one super easy group presentation that helps boost your grade. Has an odd quirk of grading everything out of 11, but this helps your grade more than it hurts you.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny, cool guy. Explains things in a simple way and generally the material is pretty intuitive. Humorous and engaging in his lectures.

Prof. Drews is such a wonderful teacher. Although I often found the course material a bit boring, he made it more interesting. I appreciated his honesty with the class, his humor, and his passion for Human Factors. He graded fairly as well. There is one class presentation, but it was rather easy and pretty chill. Attendance matters!
He has some interesting quirks (grading almost all assignments out of 11), but he's very friendly and encouraging, plus it's obvious he is super passionate about the topics he talks about.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A great course, with fascinating content, taught by a great professor. Drews structures his tests and assignments in such a manner as to set his students up to do well. There is a single class presentation, but it is pretty chill and mostly geared towards being a bit of practice with presenting.

Dr. Drews is an amazing instructor! He cares about his students. He also presents the material in a very engaging manner. The textbook can be very helpful but is not absolutely critical.  Beware of a couple group projects, though.

Prof. Drews is an excellent instructor and is very passionate about cognitive psychology and human factors. His lectures can be a bit dull at times, but his anecdotes are awesome. Prof. Drews is someone you should definitely get close to if your considering the human factors certificate.  The textbook is helpful but not necessary.

Frank Drews is a nice guy and really passionate about Human Factors. His way of presenting the material, however, wasn't very engaging. I found myself getting really bored during lectures. Someone more interested in Human Factors might have a different experience, but I didn't enjoy his class overall.
Fantastic professor. Very engaging. I took this class because it was the only one that fit my schedule and it was by far my favorite this semester. Highly recommend the class and professor.

People are hyper-critical of Arwen. She clearly cares about her students and will work with you to be successful in her courses, but she does hold expectations so that people will respect her and her course (as a professor should). Her classes aren't insanely fun and her lectures can be long but if you do the work, you'll learn a lot and do well.
An amazing professor who cares a lot about what she is teaching.

Everyone here is being a little bit dramatic, her online lecture videos are long but necessary. She makes herself very available to students outside of class, which students don't take advantage of because kines students can't be bothered to put in the effort. Pretty easy to pull a good grade out of the class, she offers lots of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Arwen is a very nice lady, but she is one of the worst professors I've had. This class consists of 1-3 hours of online lectures a week. When you do go to class, she hands you a worksheet and rarely goes over the lecture material. She also loves to put you on the spot when you have questions. This class has entirely too much content to be hybrid

She is very confusing to follow, and all content is delivered by long, boring online videos that you have to watch before class. In class is a useless time to work on an in-class assignment. She teaches like we are 3rd graders. Do not recommend.

Arwen Fuller writes the worst quizzes/exams, all being multiple choice based on "most correct" or select all answers. This class also only had 6 assignments, so the final exam could take you from an A to a B easily. I did not have to do a lot of work for this class, but the quizzes were very stressful. Would not recommend, sorry kines majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Arwen Fuller used past professors videos and none of her own content. The entire class was based on very minimal assignments and was very test heavy. Although the tests were online, they were hard to do well on. I had a high, easy A until the final exam lowered it significantly. She puts no effort into her class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire grade was based on 6 assignments. Arwen did not record any of the lecture videos herself and only talked to her students whenever an assignment was due. Was confident that this would be an easy A until the final exam lowered my grade significantly. Found it unfair that the weighting was as low as it was.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a nitpicky teacher for the most unserious things

More of a hybrid class so about 3-4 hours of online lectures before class. There is an in-class assignment every week that took years off my life. If you keep up with the lectures, ask questions, and study you will be fine. 30 points of ec are available at the end. Got a 60% on exam 1 and 50% on exam 2 and still finishing with an A. Love Fuller!!

She is not a bad person, but her teaching can be confusing. It would average around 3 hours of online lectures per week. Her exam grading on short answer can be weird. If you miss anything you can not make it up. She is good at answering questions and leading you to figuring it out. But be prepared to spend a long time on this class.

Every week there are at least 3 hours of lectures online to watch before class. The lectures are long and very boring. In-class time is used to work on assignments and ask questions. She was very helpful when we would ask questions during class but the online lectures were hard to understand and outdated.

If you like to watch long Youtube videos with adds from 4 years ago, this class is for you. Be prepared to answer a lot of "select all that apply" questions on quizzes and exams. The concepts are not impossible, but trying to prove your knowledge to this professor is very difficult considering the structure and lack of communication in the course.

For an online class, it was pretty good. I liked her lectures online, it takes effort to fully understand some concepts like afterload or partial pressures, but its a video so you can rewind it and look up other sources to help. Some of the test questions are tough, but the homework and quizzes are free 100s every week, provides nice buffering.

The class is set up so you watch lecture videos before coming to class, and then complete an in-class assignment on the topics. Some weeks there was more lecture content than others, but if you stay on top of watching them the class is very doable. I wouldn't call it an easy A, but if you put in the work and go to class it is not hard.

Dr. Fuller by far was one of my favorite professors at the U. I took 3 classes from her and I feel like she broke down concepts that were pretty hard into more understandable pieces. Her classes aren't necessarily easy A's, but if you watch the lectures, do the work, and ask questions when you have them, you will most likely succeed in her classes.

Dr. Fuller is kind and considerate. I was able to turn in work from my absence for full credit. We were given a Life Card and extra credit as well. Lectures can be quite long and time consuming but I just went through the slides without them some weeks and I was fine. Exams were not too difficult either.

Such a hard class and her online lectures will put you to sleep. You have to really study hard and keep up on the assignments to do well. She bumped me up from a B- to a B even though I was three percentage points away from getting a B. I didn't even ask her. Super cool of her.
For a 3 credit hour class, it was horrible. Some weeks we had 6+ hours of dense and hard to understand lectures. Exams and quizzes were difficult and hard to study for. Take with another professor

There is no way to prepare for the tests other than making your own study guide from the lectures which is very difficult because the lectures every week are incredibly long and tedious. Her TA grades everything so harshly.

Arwen was straight up the worst professor I have ever had. She was rude in her messages, if she even answered, and completely unreasonable to work with. She posted hours and hours of lecture videos each week that were flat out boring and hard to learn from. I wish I wouldn't have taken this course from her.
Never again
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, you can get through this class without watching lectures, but may bomb the tests. The homework is in the form of a quiz format on canvas and quizzes are just normal quizzes. Overall, she tries to do the bare minimum. Tests: 80 mins, 50ish Q's, most Q's are hard AF, not proctored. Publishes assign/HW ONLY on the weekly. Frustrating.

Arwen is a great lecturer that I wish I could have had actual lectures from. All her lectures are done online and prerecorded. There is a lot of material, but if you put in the effort you'll do great.
Gives no announcement of an exam until the day of it, and changes due dates without announcing them.

The lectures were so unbearably long with her just reading off her slides and scribbling everywhere. There were random cuts in the middle of her explaining things, slides given to us that she doesn't even go over, and unnecessary information that just wasted so much time. She never even replied to my email about questions. So frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fuller is an incredibly sweet person, but she never answered emails. In fact, I should have gotten an A-, but because she didn't answer my emails I received a B+. Her lectures are incredibly long, but it's not because of the content, but because how much she over explains everything. She makes things more complicated than they should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is disorganized, asks vague questions on assignments/exams, and rarely answers her email. All of her lectures were recorded during the beginning of Covid and she re-uses them so she doesn't always know what material is in which lecture. This creates problems when she tells you to watch a lecture but tests you on stuff you haven't learned yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have had Arwen for three classes now (not necessarily by choice), and they have all been the same in the fact she pushes back assignments/quizzes until the very last minute, and then at the end of the semester, there's a ton to do. Her lectures are boring but not unbearable. Sometimes responds, sometimes does not which can be frustrating.

She lacks enthusiasm but she's very clear and straight to the point, which made learning physiology a bit more doable. I thought she explained complicated topics better than David Temme (the human physiology teacher). She basically just reads through her Powerpoints so attendance not a huge deal, although I only had her online.

Each of our exams seemed to test stuff that was never directly discussed, but required some background knowledge and deduction. It wasn't the hardest class of all time, but if you don't take a lot of time to know every single thing inside and out you'll get hurt on the exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I did not mind this class and I am sure it is better in person but online was just a mess. A quiz got lost/deleted, lectures are long and not the easiest to focus through, and assignments were often posted last minute then took a long time to be graded. Overall it felt very disorganized and was a tough class to get through.

Fuller is so nice and easy going. Her content is clear and she is pretty straightforward. Ask her questions if you have them and youll be fine. Super down to earth and wants you to succeed. 10 outta 10.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Arwen is easily the most boring lecturer of any professor I've had at the University of Utah. She reads off the slides for the entire lecture with no class interaction. The class could be really interesting but she soaks the interesting right out of it. Her tests are also "pick the best answer" many answers could be correct but still marked wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aging & Exercise isn't a class Arwen has normally taught but I felt she did a good job for this being a new class for her. Class is lecture heavy but if you're struggling she is very helpful during office hours.

This class was challenging. Luckily, Fuller gives plenty of opportunities for points. Biweekly quizzes were difficult, tests not as bad. She phrases questions in odd ways and we constantly asked for clarification. Lectures are long and dry, but apparently this is not the case in her other classes - I hear she just doesn't like teaching physiology.

Professor Fuller is a great person but a sub-par professor at best. Her lectures are quite boring because she lectures from the side of the room in a very mono-tone and slow way. She doesn't seem to know the material very well. Be prepared for quizzes and do homework on time. It hurts your grade way more than it should if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is not a great choice. The issue with her teaching style is that she teaches everything in 3 different styles constantly switching in between her methods. This confused me deeply and caused the class to be way harder then it should have been. Take this class in the summer when it is taught by her TAs. You'll thank me later.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fuller is an incredible professor! She is super understanding and will push exams/quizzes back if she feels like the class needs an extra day to clarify anything. Her lectures can be a bit dry, but she tells you exactly what you need to know for the exams/quizzes and gives you plenty of opportunities to get it right. I totally recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Arwen was great. She really understands the material she is teaching and gives you a lot of opportunities (in the form of hw assignments and quizzes) to practice what you know before the 2 midterms and final. She is happy to answer questions. Expects you to work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the poorest structured classes Ive taken in my whole college career. This class has potential to be great. However, I felt over and over again that Arwen is extremely poor at communication. It was difficult to decode what she was trying to asking often on quizzes. Sure nice lady but that doesnt discount her poorly structured course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Fuller is a bit confusing as a lecturer and makes things more complicated than they need to be. Her exams are very wordy and she tends to not know how to simplify things. With that said, she cares deeply about her students and their performance. If you study for the class and look over the slides, you could get an A very easily.

I think Dr. Fuller is an okay lecturer. Personally, I think she over complicates the material more than she needs to. Although her exams aren't hard, she asks questions in very weird ways, which makes the exam more on the exam than on the material. She isn't mean, however, just confusing. She is open to consultation which certainly helps.

Dr. Fuller is honestly a great teacher as well as person. She is clear in what is expected from you. Advice- Ask questions in class and see her during office hours, take advantage of the TA's, do your homework and be professional. Exams are fine if you study. Go into her class with a clear, unbiased head and you might like her teaching style.
Arwen gives you all the material you need to pass. If you study for exams you should pass with an easy A. Overall great class and not extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved this class. The textbook is great, because it gives you a lot of background information, however, tests come straight from her slides and assignments. If you talk to her, she's willing to work with you, and wants to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fuller was really respectful and created a nice classroom environment. She cared about students and got to know a lot of names. She seems intense at first but really lightens up when she gets into her teachings. A great teacher!

I have had the pleasure of having Arwen for two classes. She is completely disorganized and often stumbles through her own material (confusing adduction/abduction). Arwen's incompetence also shows in quizzes and tests. Questions are often vague and strangely worded, and tests are constantly being regraded due to errors in her answer keys.

She was an alright professor. I liked her as a person, but her lectures were incredibly dull, she read right from the slides. Almost all of the test material was from the slides and she provides study guides that are beneficial. The tests can be hard at times due to trick and ambiguous questions. Should've done better, make sure you study

Although this class seemed interesting, it was very very hard to understand what the teacher was talking about. she doesnt have a full grasp on what she is teaching which isnt fair to a student she gets many things mixed up and is very disorganized. Her tests are confusing and often i found the study guides to not be very useful. Lots of in class

Very confusing professor. Always got important words mixed up i.e. Abduction and adduction. Didn't seem to know a lot about kinesiology. Reads straight off the PowerPoint slides everyday. Exams are very straightforward, 50 multiple choice questions almost straight from the slides. Sometimes has in class assignments.

I was a little worried taking Arwen's class from what I've heard, but she actually wasn't that bad. She gives assignments in class and out of class and some of the questions are on the test. 3 midterms and a final. Gives opportunity to increase grade. Just study 2-3 days before the test and you'll be fine. Most answers come from power points.

Arwen clearly doesn't want to be teaching Kinesiology. She reads the slides off her powerpoint for 50 minutes and is very unengaged.  She often sends out the slides right before class or at the very most an hour before class, giving you no time to print them or prepare. She also cancels her office hours frequently. TAKE THIS CLASS ELSEWHERE!

She is an awful professor that is too busy with other things to be teaching the class. She is disorganized and blows through lecture slides during class. She does not prepare you for her exams. She ran review sessions without having the test written.  Our exam averages were in the 60's and she did not curve them. I would not take a class from her.

Not hard to get an A, but wouldn't drop test questions that were ambiguous.  She didn't seem to know certain material very well.  On last exam, never unlocked answers from online test and it was poorly written.  Didn't find teacher or book helpful- material was taken from the book and was wrong on several counts (checked against Anatomy book).
Very boring lectures, but i recommend attending class because she changes slides from what has been posted. study guides are very beneficial for the multiple choice exams.

Attend lecture, although boring, is best because she often omit's items from the students copy of the lecture slides. Her test are multiple choice and she provides study guides. If you study you are guaranteed an A.

Easy class. Professor Fuller is nice and funny. Exams and quizzes are multiple choice and she pretty much spells out what she expects you to know so if you don't get an 'A'...well, there is just no hope for you. Class was boring! I only went because I was worried I'd miss something, but near the end I started skipping and still got an A
She really doesn't have a clear understanding of the material, and she is far from organized.

I would strongly recommend this course and instructor for any Honors students writing a thesis. I left the class with a solid roadmap and material I can use. Professor Gills knows his stuff. He will definitely push you as a writer and a researcher, but the classes and discussions are engaging, he gives good feedback, and the work is valuable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Spending a semester in creative writing with Michael Gills was an amazing experience. The class size is small, and everyone sits at a round table together to go over the week's writing and talk about assigned readings. I've made some amazing friends in this class, and my writing process has improved so much. If you love writing, take this class!!

I love Michael Gills! Definitely recommend him if you love writing. If you don't love writing, it's literally what he teaches so better off not taking a course with him. He helps you put together amazing creative portfolios. You might get burnt out, we did have two students drop out before we finished the course. But you will probably be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I hate writing but loved this class-- it was all thanks to Michael. Definitely work hard on your first few papers specifically, since he grades these tough then gauges your writing ability through the rest of the semester. He gives great feedback, fosters a relationship between all of us and with him, and is fair. BEST Honors College course by far.

This class really helped me with my thesis, which was the point of the class. Gills helped garner a good class environment. The only real complaint of mine is that he seemed to grade some papers easier than others depending on how technical/jargon-filled their papers were. Other than that was a great professor and encouraged rewrites.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was THE best class I have taken in the Honors College. I have learned more from this class than I have from any other class I have ever taken. I would recommend this class to everyone.

Gills' class changed my life.  He is very good at building a supportive environment among classmates, and he really reads your papers.  While he may grade them toughly, he gives opportunities to improve.  Note: the beginning of the semester is slow, assignment-wise.  It gets very quick and difficult later.
Michael Gills is a wonderfully warm, charismatic, and unforgettable man! While Travel Writing is a rigorous course, I now have only the fondest memories in hindsight.

MIchael gills is a really smart, accomplished and critical writer. His class is hard! But your writing will be so much better afterwards. Also, he is a published novelist; he knows what he is doing. Take classes from him, believe me.

This class was online during the COVID pandemic. It consisted of three 4-5 page essays, a thesis analysis, a presentation, and a 10-20 page final paper. It was a heavy workload class and included daily discussions, but it helped us build relationships with peers. We got good feedback and Gills was supportive and respectful.

Gills is a great man, but be ready to work! He is very fair with his grading and is very reasonable. He has a great heart and truly wants you to succeed, you have to want to work though. He cares about his students without a doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS GUY. An absolute lunatic of a writer, he is extremely talented himself so you're learning from the best. This class will test your writing but there is no wrong answer! You put your best effort in, write the pages and no matter how garbage you think your storytelling is you'll leave this class with 15x more skill. 1000% recommend.

Travel writing is such an amazing class. Gills truly cares about all of his students, especially in this challenging class. You have to write a page a day and log in daily to canvas, but the payoff in the end is all worth it. I would recommend this class and this professor to anyone wanting to fulfill their CW credit. Gills is a talented writer.

All feedback is given in difficult to read cursive. Gills is not clear on what he wants with revisions and takes a substantial amount of time to get papers and revisions back to students. He is a respectable writer and professor but I found his class confusing and his manner irritating and disrespectful.

This class really forces you to be a better writer. It's an upper-division writing class for a reason. I would highly recommend taking this class if you're working on a research paper or honors thesis. If you're taking STEM classes, writing these big papers is going to be a challenge, but he can and will help you if you make the effort to see him.

Michael's instructions are vague and he refuses to answer questions even when directly asked. Very disrespectful towards students and will publicly shame and humiliate them for having poor writing skills or disagreeing opinions. Feedback generally felt inapplicable, especially for STEM students. My enjoyment of writing tanked after this class.

Gills is amazing!!! Hands down the best professor I've had. He is so passionate and willing to work with you. Tips: develop some thick skin and internalize his critique. Be ready to work. But he is so good. Grades on the effort you put into his class. 10/10 would recommend!

Personally, I enjoyed having Professor Gills as my writing professor. His lectures are my favorite part of the class, as they are engaging and force you to think. He also tells the class wise lessons that you will never forget which I loved! ONE PROBLEM: You can't see your grade until the END of the semester so stay on top of things!
Disrespectful and hard to get along with. The class was okay, just his teaching style was not very effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: What this class consists of: A total of 6 (4-10 page) papers, about 2 oral presentations (lasting from 7 to 10 minutes each), & everyday participation in class discussions (usually for giving feedback on each other's papers). Tough. But Gills is a respectable professor who is passionate about writing and teaching students.

I hated every second of this class. He is rude to students, will tell you that your opinion is wrong unless it coincides with his. He makes you have "discussions", more like arguments. He doesn't put any grades in until end of term. Made fun of our writing errors in front of the class. Doesn't answer questions when you ask for help. Don't take this

Professor Gills has really helped me improve on my writing as a student. Though his rigor coursework may be a deterrent, he offers a plethora of extra credit as well as rewrites to raise the grades on your paper. The only people who'd dislike this class are usually the students who don't want to put in so much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I have NEVER been more frustrated with a class. I got 5s on my AP English and Literature tests so I know that my writing is passable, but professor gills dishes out Bs to everyone in the class. I went to him several times to find out how to ace his class but he was very vague and rather rude. He often tries to embarrass students for fun.

Professor Gills cannot be trusted. He has no grading rubrics and gives very vague instructions. He is often very rude to students and constantly demeans  writing efforts. Your tuition money will be better spent with a professor who is clear on his grading methods and is respectful to his students.

Professor Gills is a good professor. He really cares about seeing student improvement. He makes you work for the A. Work hard, give it your best effort, and take advantage of his policies about revision. If you do this, you will be fine.

He cares about how much effort you put in, and about how effectively you can use your life experiences to write.  He's a good writing teacher, even though he can be tough and the work he assigns may be intimidating.  His feedback can be harsh sometimes, but he means well.

Gills took the time to help me through out the semester.  I didn't realize it when I took the class but looking at professors that I have dealt with now Gills was there to help and wanted to see me succeed with my writing.  If you like to write, you will love this class.  You have to commit to the work to get the grade.

This class was predominantly nightmarish. Prof. Gills was condescending and rude to students. He only provided feedback on final drafts, and often it was vague. Grading seemed arbitrary because the prof. lacked rubrics and never assigned a percentage/point value to papers, he merely provided a letter grade. I will never take this professor again.
Very poor in all aspects of teaching and communication

I took Prof. Gills class online because I was working over 20 hours each week. While Prof. Gills gives students plenty of time to do each paper, his expectations and the objectives of each assignment are unclear until after they are graded. This class is okay, but don't expect to be taught anything or to get an easy A.
Very nice! Took over our class when our professor passed away. Very helpful and will do anything to help you to understand what is expected and grades very fairly.

Professor Gills was very friendly and willing to help students if they asked for it. I took this class online and it was very easy considering that it is an upper division writing course. A lot of peer reviews and online participation are mandatory to pass the class.
He was very helpful, but if you are hoping for an easy A Gills is not for you. On the first day he told us "If you are getting an A that means you are writing one of the best papers in the country."

I took this class online and it was exactly what I needed. The assignments were spread out, there were extra credit chances, and Gills was extremely helpful and understanding in certain situations. Definitely recommed him!

Take it from somebody else.  This class was a disaster.  I had to do so much more work in this class than my upper division science classes.  If you are busy or just want the easy grade don't take it from him.  This was the most frustrating class.  I ended up getting an A, so I'm not biased because of a bad grade.
Prof. Gills is a great teacher.  He approaches the class from a writing standpoint, which is different.  His comments are always very helpful.  He improved my writing skills immensely.

This class was a joke. Nothing was very clear as to the direction he wanted you to go in. It would be better as an online class. The nice thing was it was easy and little work was required but if you want to learn something get into another class.

DO NOT take this class online if: 1) you want to improve your writing ability, 2) want a good grade for the work you do, 3) want a teacher to actually teach you something.this class was a waste of my time, the teacher was essentialy non-existent. It was basically a joke.

Prof Gills takes a couple weeks to get used to.  Its hard to know exactly when things are due.  Nice guy.  Going to class is useless, but you have to go for credit.  The job search portfolio is a great way to kill 2 birds with 1 stone and he gives you good feedback on it.

Prof. Gills approaches the class from a writer's standpoint, not a teacher's. He loves what he does and it shows. He is very helpful in fixing little problems you might have, but he also wants students to figure things out on their own. Writing isn't always my favorite class, but I enjoyed this one.

Other friends who took Professional Wriitng had to do A LOT more work. Basically, the whole course was spent revising your resume and working on a group project. We'd take Friday's off, and do group work on M and W, so it was cake.

Very tough grader. Decent work is worth a C; you have to write like a pro to get an A. He does a lot of in-class workshop stuff, but gives no feedback or clear direction prior to handing in assignments. That can kill your grade, considering there are few assignments and each one is worth a lot.

If you want to learn to write, this is the place to be.  However, there are many other teachers at the U who will let you get away with a lot more.  Tough teacher, semi-hard grader, but if you can make it through, you will feel like a better student.
Nit-Picky about Resumes, but very helpful.  Makes you work for your grade.

Assigns a lot of homework and writing assignments.  Not always helpful, tends to be excited when students have a hard time - he wants them to get it on their own. Can be good but also annoying and hard. Overall okay

Groot is an amazing professor! Don't be discouraged by how hard you might hear anatomy to be. It is a lot of work but anyone can do well if you make the time and put in the effort. He has incredibly engaging lectures, his grading policy is clear, and the class is well organized. I wish I could take this class again! It is amazing!

This course provides a significant academic challenge that requires consistent effort. I felt a great sense of achievement after finishing. The professor is incredibly passionate about the material and ensures students develop a genuine interest in the subject. If you stay dedicated to the work, you will succeed. A very rewarding experience!

This class is incredibly difficult to keep up with if you have anything else time-consuming in your life. Definitely do not take this with any other hard classes. You're gonna fight for your grade like your life depends on it, just stay motivated. The content is really cool, and Groot knows it really well.

This class was made more difficult cuz of Groot himself, doesn't make learning accessible to those that have outside obligations and the grading on the exams is too inconsistent for them to be 90% of the grade. Rely on the workbook and finish all the content for the exam the week before. Lab was hard, final was based on structures seen once.

Professor Groot is probably the best professor I've had. In no means is this class easy, and you have to fight for a good grade. BUT, Groot makes learning anatomy fun, relevant, and simply taught. He said that this program is arguably the best in the nation, and I agree. The previous teacher made amazing resources for effectively learning anatomy.

By no means is anatomy easy, but if you put in the right amount of work, you can get an A. Groot gives you 15 extra points for doing weekly assignments. Don't take it with other hard or harder classes and spend at least 15 minutes a day reviewing. Groot's rating isn't justified; he is much better. Don't let slackers deter you.

this class was incredibly difficult but groot makes it so much easier to understand. his lectures are very clear and interesting. i personally love the organization of the class, although it is very self motivated. its very easy to fall behind. the tests are all based on the workbook and are formatted very similarly. the lab definitely helps!

This class should be the most failed bio class at the U. The content in this class is not hard, Groot makes it near impossible to access without going to office hours or lecture for no reason. The workbooks that help you learn don't even have keys released, even though they aren't graded. No logical reason for this, bad class structure.

Groot is an amazing lecturer, however...This class literally sent me to the ER from stress and looking at anything anatomy related genuinely gives me a trauma response. If you cannot dedicate your entire life to this class you will probably get the worst grade of your life. Take the class at SLCC if you actually want to do well the first time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best lecturer I've had in university. Groot cares a TON about student understanding and delivering clear engaging content and it shows. He has a genuine love for the material that is quite infectious. Focus on truly understanding the material, cultivate passion for anatomy as a whole, and stay up on studying; anyone who genuinly cares can succeed.

Yes, the class is very difficult and you need to put in a good amount of hours every week, but I'd say this is because of the content and not Groot. He makes it very clear how you can succeed and the rest is dependent on yourself. Definitely schedule this with some easier classes.

The lectures are really quick and difficult to follow but you can tell Groot is very knowledgeable and passionate.  The exams are really challenging.  The lab is your best resource to do well in this class.  The TAs are very helpful in learning and the pre class quizzes are very easy to do well on if you study.  DO the extra credit HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good luck taking this class. You'll literally be dedicating your whole life to it. Groot isn't a good teacher & will briefly mention something only for it to be heavily tested on. There's no homework to even out your grade. Just a bunch of material to memorize & be tested on, not to mention he makes the test incredibly hard to trick you.

Groot is a great professor and you learn a lot of really interesting content. He's a very smart and cool dude however the course is very very difficult in terms of content. This is probably the most content heavy class I've ever taken so its really important to study and stay on top of things.

Groot is a great lecturer and sets up the class well. This class does not have any concepts that will challenge you, but rather an information overload of memorization on a systemic/regional level. Exams are straightforward. I studied ~10 hours on exam weeks and ~3 hours on non-exam weeks, went to all lectures/labs, and got an A.

This guy is a horrible teacher. He gatekeeps all the information you are supposed to know because he does not discuss it in class, and it is not included on his slides. I stopped attending class and instead had ChatGPT guide me through the workbook to do well in the class.

Groot is the best professor I have ever had. He is intelligent, incredible lecturer, and it is clear that he loves his job.
However, this class is extremely difficult and the volume of content is crazy. It is doable but make sure to stay ahead and have plenty of time in your week to dedicate to this class.
Most TA's are amazing, some aren't nice.

Groot was an amazing professor! 
Best advice: show up, put in the work, and take advantage of TA hours. It was my first time taking it and got a B+, so don't let the slackers in the reviews stress you out. also, If you want to take it at slcc you're signing up for poor education compared to the anatomy program at the U. Invest in your education!
It's a HARD class but Groot is a good guy. Honestly nothing more to be said.

If you take this class, be prepared to study nonstop, quit your job maybe, and get those antidepressants on the line. The 45% fail rate says enough about Groot. If you have a job or any life outside school, take the course at SLCC with Andy Munguia instead. When I retook it there, I understood the material so much better and passed with an A.

This class made me regret taking it. If you fall behind once just drop the class. You will not pass if you have a job or get sick. Unfortunately this is required for my major so I will be retaking it at SLCC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Groot presents well but isn't a great teacher, reflected in his average grade for the course. His exams are extremely hard, workbooks often irrelevant, and TAs are terrible at grading & have god complexes. Study 20-40 hrs/week for labs and exams to earn at least a B. This course is unnecessarily difficult for a 2000 level course. Avoid it at the U.
I would not have done well in this class with a different professor. He's the GROAT.

I retook this class three times. I kept earning C's but I really needed the B for my science gpa. I finally achieved it after my third time. Anatomy is unlike any other class I have taken at the U. Dr. Groot is friendly & intelligent but I always struggled with the tests each time I took this class. DON'T take this with any other hard course.

Groot's class was unbearably difficult. I spent over 15 hrs a week studying and over 20 on test weeks. Used TA hours, attended all lectures, followed tools for success and still bombed the tests getting 50-60% (which groot said was NORMAL). If you are a pre nursing student take at SLCC for a much easier route. He does not care about STUDENT SUCCESS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard, period. One of the hardest classes I have ever had to take but it was also my favorite.  He is an amazing teacher but has very high expectations. The TAs are amazing. Go to office hours, don't skip lecture, do the coloring, watch the videos DON'T get behind. Homework is like a giant gift of extra credit at the end so do it all.
The class was very hard! But Dr. Groot is easily the best teacher I have ever had! Makes the lectures super easy. I will defiantly take another class from him if I am able to.

The class is very content heavy. It's very interesting, and if you're interested in the medical field, you'll probably love it. I studied about 10 hours a week to get an A. The professor is amazing , his class is hard but he tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed, and he is amazing at teaching. Go to TA hours, that's the key for exams.

If you're looking to be a medical professional in the future, this is the guy who will show you whether you really love it or if maybe you'd benefit from other routes. He will probably be the best teacher you'll get in college, but your gonna have to go the distance to get an A. Don't worry about the bad reviews and sharpen those colored pencils.

Groot is the greatest professor I've ever had in college. He is truly passionate about what he teaches and loves seeing students learn.TAs are so helpful. This class is difficult and requires lots of effort. Go to lecture, go to office hours, follow the formula for success and you will succeed. Those who rate him poorly are those who didn't try.

Groot is by far one of the best lecturers I've ever had, he was amazing and his lectures were my favorite. His tests are hard, and you're only graded on tests, lab quizzes, and practical's. You will need to dedicate a lot of time to this class, it's a ton of memorizing. Stay caught up in the workbook, go to lecture, and go to office hours.

groot is so passionate about teaching anatomy and truly cares about his students. anatomy is very content heavy, but he makes it very enjoyable and very fair to gain points whenever possible. i would recommend this course to anyone and him as a professor to everyone.
Jon Groot is the man plus he knows karate i think or something, best professor in the health department.

Groot is the best lecturer I have ever had. He is incredibly well spoken and engaging with his students, and is always incredibly prepared and excited during lecture. He is amazing. This class is very rigorous, I spend 30ish hours a week studying for it, but really good to know this stuff for healthcare. If you put in the time, you will do well.

Groot is an amazing professor! I thoroughly learning enjoyed Anatomy from him. He is extremely prepared for his lectures and it shows. Although the class is difficult and requires you to put in lots of work, Groot provides the tools necessary to succeed. If you put in the work and use the resources provided you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Groot's anatomy class is quite challenging, but engaging if you stay on top of the material. Attend lectures, use the textbook, and try out helpful tools like unstuck study for study prep. With dedication, you can excel in this rigorous course.
Great teacher if you go to every class. Hard class and this is why people rate him badly.

This guy should NOT be a university instructor.  He is cold and does not care about the student.  I did fine in the class, but would definately NOT recommend him.  Perhaps he is better suited to research.  Definately NOT interested in helping student succeed.

Professor Groot was an amazing professor. As long as you pay attention in class and during the labs you will do just fine. You don't need to study more than the day before the test to do well. If you are good at memorization then this is the class for you. to anyone who hates on Groot for doing bad in this class, that is entirely on you.

Go to lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory but your grade will reflect how you attend lectures and how many questions you ask. Be sure to study daily for at least an hour. Your test scores will be determined by how much effort you put in. Groot is awesome and his lectures are great. Low scores for Groot are probably by people who didn't work hard.

Groot is an amazing teacher. He is extremely knowledgable and knows his stuff. He uses lots of examples to explain hard to grasp concepts. This class is SO HARD. I spent 70+ hours a week on this class studying. For me, this resulted in an A. Make sure you put in the time and the work and you can do well.

Groot is an amazing professor. You can tell how passionate he is about anatomy and cares for his students. He clearly explains what you are expected to know and what he wants you to put on exams. The textbook is so helpful and the workbook is a great study guide. It was the hardest class I had taken yet, and it consumed all my time, but I loved it.

Groot is an incredible professor that teaches an incredible class. He makes anatomy so so interesting, but you have to put effort into this class to pass it. By far the hardest class I've ever taken, but also the most rewarding. Use the workbook to your advantage, it is the ideal study guide for the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is a weed-out class and will humble anyone who thinks they can just slip by. Anyone who complains about Groot because of this class didn't try and blamed it on Groot. He is the best lecturer you will ever have. Study every day, live in office hours, DON'T GET WEEDED OUT!

Groot is very passionate and will answer any question you have with enthusiasm. Lectures are detailed, organized, and clear. This is a very tough class, but those that don't like him, fail the class because they complain and don't want to put in the effort to succeed. If you want a career in medicine, Groot will give you the proper foundation.

Groot is far and away the best lecturer I have ever had. He is extremely knowledgeable and makes sure that everything he talks about transitions smoothly and also corresponds with your lecture manual so don't overcomplicate it, just take notes in the manual. Pay attention and don't miss lecture, participate in lab, and do your workbook.

He is an amazing professor and the class is amazing. It is exceedingly difficult. You will have to devote large amounts of time to study or do well in the class. I would 10/10 take this class again if I didn't have to take the tests again.

Study with the TAs, go to the SI sessions, and prepare for class. This will help you do well!

Anatomy was by far the hardest class I have ever taken but if you're willing to commit a lot of your time to learning it, you'll do great. Groot tells you exactly what you need to do to be successful so if you listen to him and study hard you'll be fine. The worst thing you can do is assume you don't need to put in the work and then get behind.

This class is super interesting and there is a lot of information. Attendance is not required but make sure to go to the lectures every day or you will get behind fast. There are lab quizzes each week as well as extra credit homework assignments (do these!). Study/review every day to stay on top of all the information!
Groot makes Anatomy unbearably difficult. He rushes through lectures expecting us to know everything already. The slides he post are not helpful and questions from t

Groot is an amazing teacher and I strongly suggest that you follow the formula for success if you want a good grade in this class. Tests, quizzes, and practicums make up for the majority of your grade but he does offer some extra credit. My best advice is DO YOUR WORKBOOK! The exam questions are similar and help you understand the material.

Groot was an amazing professor. His teaching methods were easy to follow and he made the class very enjoyable. Nevertheless, his class is very rigorous. I would not recommend taking any other rigorous courses with it. The grade is based only on exams/ quizzes, and they are not easy. Remember to follow the steps for success outlined in the syllabus!

Lecture is the most important aspect of this class. I missed quite a few lectures due to some unforseen circumstances and Groot kindly worked with me to make up my lab quiz. BUT the lectures I did miss I missed all the questions on the exam pertaining to that day. GO TO LECTURE, TAKE GOOD NOTES, STUDY THEM EVERYDAY. Make summary sheets.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. The curriculum is incredibly difficult and awful. He covers the material too fast and expects the information to stick to us like we're glue. Cadaver lab was interesting but was drowned out by the fact that there was a never ending list of structures to memorize. All in all awful experience. Do not take.

I was excited for this class in the beginning, but Groot made it more difficult. (Why make it harder?) Exams were vague since they didn't include questions from the workbook. He went super fast in his lectures. Slides had no text on them. The cadavers in lab were also so old and hard to study for. Very frustrating. Take Anatomy at SLCC instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a life and responsibilities outside of school then don't take this class. Groot's lectures were entertaining but he dumps info that you will never see or hear again till your exams (which are free response) Your lab practicum will be 60+ questions on old cadaver structures that you only got to see once (maybe twice) in person.

Groot was great and knows what he is talking about. He outlines the very first lecture what you need to do to be successful in the class. Although it is a lot of work, the grade you get is reflective of the work and time you are willing to put in. Be prepared to spend 10+ hours studying for exams, but genuine effort is what gets you the grade.

Groot knows his stuff but is not understanding at all. I got a concussion from a car accident right around a midterm and he advised me to not wait to take it, even though I was concussed. He even gave pushback to the ADA. Well, I did wait to take it, and he made my exam way harder than the original exam. If you have to do a makeup exam, good luck

Groot's an incredible professor! While attendance isn't mandatory you'll miss a ton of info if you skip even one day. Be prepared to learn lots of information and study anatomy every day. The class is extremely difficult but Groot explains super well in lecture and knows so much outside of the content you're expected to know. Fav professor by far

Groot was decent at lecturing but the class it self.. so much memorization. Remember that this class is combined with labs. On top of 4 exams (that are fairly hard), Each week, you'll have to memorize ~30 new words each week for the labs and it is cumulative). In ALL of my classes, I had As except this one. I hope this tells you how hard it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Go to all his class write everything and know all of it. No resources available outside of class. We have a workbook (I don't recommend using it to study) that set people up to fail. Great TAs who are very helpful. Does require lots of studying he says don't cram before the test but I did that for all 4 of them and did better than average.

Groot would tell us if we studied and knew everything in the workbook we would do great on exams, when in reality almost every exam had multiple questions that were not discussed in the workbook at all. To pass an exam you had to know every single thing he talked over, even things that he barely touched on in class. TAs were great and helped a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Groot's nice, but he made this class severely hard that lacked accessibility. He would go over material so fast in his lectures sometimes in less than a few minutes where it was hard to keep up at times. Slides had no text written on them making it hard to get information. Some exam questions were also vague that weren't found in the workbook.
Groot is a great professor but the content is very hard. Be prepared and go to class and you will be okay.

This class was crazy. Groot is a great teacher and there are plenty of resources, just make sure you are ready to take this class. It is not necessarily hard, it's just very voluminous. You will have to spend 2-3 hours studying every day AT LEAST. The exams are all free-response and insanely difficult. Hardest class I've ever taken.

class moves fast but isnt harder than other stem classes .Keep up with terminology and reference flashcards for lab/lecture. Groot is an engaging lecturer and gives you all tools needed to succeed and then some. Exams are free response and require memorization. not graded on spelling but will be marked wrong if error lends to another structure.

Groot's a nice guy if you get to know him, but his class is very brutal. Expect to study at least 1 to 2 hours a day going over material you've just learned in lecture. The lab is going to have a lot of new structures to memorize each week. Take this class with a lighter course load or you'll struggle. Also go to as many help sessions as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Groot makes lectures entertaining and interactive. He connects new material we are learning to old material, and it is vital to have those basic building blocks of anatomy down in the first weeks of class. Groot obviously cares about his students' success. This class is challenging, and you must devote much time to studying. Lots of memorization!

Intense class that requires 3+ hours of study a day. Groot makes comments in class that are frustrating and misogynistic. No assignments or quizzes to help raise grades. Tests make up 95% of the grade. Tested on small minor details. Traces are ridiculously hard! I learned the names of obscure veins even med students don't learn. TAKE ANYWHERE ELSE.

Anatomy is one of the hardest classes at the U. However, if you're willing to put in the effort and follow Groot's "Keys to Success" then you will be able to do well. Study after each lecture so you won't fall behind, the amount of content is overwhelming.The grade you get will depend on the amount of effort you put into this challenging course.

Groot is a great teacher but he doesn't make a hard class like anatomy any easier. Class isn't mandatory but you will miss out on information you can't find in class slides or the textbook.
