The grade is made up of 4 exams and the lab. Be sure to study consistently and try not to take any other hard classes at the same time. Go to review sessions!

I've never taken anatomy before so this class was entirely new to me. It was difficult getting used to that much studying but groot was awesome. He makes lectures super interesting and worth going to. Though attendance isnt mandatory the online slides arent nearly as helpful as going to class and taking notes, so it really isnt the class to skip.

Jon Groot is an amazing professor and teacher. He can simplify the vast majority of complicated anatomy topics to be more understandable. The class is very difficult, as all anatomy classes are. His class is rated as the hardest nonivy League anatomy course. Your grade is basically of 4 exams that are all fill-in-the-blank about random details said

Although Groot is a very great professor and makes concepts discussed in lecture seem easy, this class is wild. I have never experienced a class this difficult. I would consider O-chem easier, I think I cried like 50 times over anatomy whereas that was probably only in the 35 range
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is tough. However, I think the professor does a great job at teaching, and is very clear on what you need to do in order to be succesful in this class. Lectures in itself are "mandatory" but if you miss one you will fall behind quick. Get ready to study because you're going to need it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: HATED THIS CLASS. Anatomy meets 4 days a week with enough content to make your head spin. Tests are free responses. Requires memorization of 40+ structures. Should be a 10 credit class. Traces are useless. This class goes into wayy too much depth that even med school students don't need to know
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is almost entirely muscles. It's ridiculous. The lab is stupid, and there is basically no way to study for the lab final because the online pictures don't match the pieces you see in lab. You won't do well unless you study an ungodly amount for this one class. I was really excited for this class, but I cried so hard too many times.

The class was mid. The textbook helped a little bit if you wrote good notes. The lab was a joke, only way passing is acing all the exams and lab materials. The ones saying "well no duh its anatomy" bffr rn like it was hard, take it at slcc instead. Everything is free response and the slides have nothing to help study on. people have repeated.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You better not have this class during a hard semester. Had this with O chem and I barely passed. The lab is a joke. It's very cool but this class is legit only muscles. Anatomy should be more than just muscles. Your lab final is going around a room and trying to name every single part no matter how small. I've only heard that happening in medschool

Groot is a really passionate professor but he teaches a really brutal class. Exams are worth 70% of your grade and it is ALL FREE RESPONSE!!!! The other 30% are lab quizzes and practicums which are all CUMULATIVE with 60+ new terms every week. It doesn't help that the atlas (which u study on) has new cadavers while the cadavers in the labs are OLD

One of the hardest courses I have taken at the University of Utah. If you miss one day, you will fall behind. It's too much for a single class. If you are willing to study every single day, review 40+ terms, and study new 20+ terms cumulative every week, then take the class. But if you have classes on par or even close, take it somewhere else.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Groot is a great teacher and makes lectures interesting/engaging. But this class is a beast. The amount of hours of work needed to do well just isn't feasible for most college students and their schedules. Take this when you have an otherwise light semester or you will struggle.

Listen, I really like Groot as a teacher. This course is just really hard. You need to put more than just 4 credit worth of hours into this class a week. This should be a 3000 upper divison class. I took anatomy and Phys at Weber state and it was a cake walk compared to this class. Be prepared to study long hours just on the back muscles alone
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough it is a must that you study extra outside of class. Plenty of material which adds up over time. Mandatory labs which will add extra study content to the already high load. Quizzes in lab every week which are cumulative of previous content. Material near the end of the course becomes very intensive. Cool material but you'll have to put in work

This class is awful! The majority of our grade is determined by three exams, a final, and a lab final. There is a lab component requiring you to memorize 50+ structures each week. One time, we had a quiz, practicum, and a model due in one lab. Lecture is content heavy, requires 2 hours of study a day. Exams are brutal and test on minor details.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Groot is one of the best professors that I have ever have. All the negative comments don't understand that anatomy is going to be a hard class no matter who teaches it, it's not meant to be easy. Groot's lectures are fantastic. He is very knowledgeable and clearly loves teaching. He is very clear on what you need to do to do well in the class.

If you are considering anatomy, I recommend taking it at SLCC. The hardest part of this class are the traces. You will be tested on problems such as "Trace a drop of blood from the heart to oxygen in the lungs. " If you look closely, all of the positive reviews for this class were written by teaching assistants for anatomy, so disregard them.

This class is a beast! It is the most failed class at the U. In each class, there is a ton of content covered. Expect to spend at least 1-2 hours a day going over the content you learned. The majority of your grade is based off of three enormous exams and a comprehensive final. There are over 70 structures to memorize for a weekly lab quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Groot is very passionate about his work. You can definitely tell through his lectures. But his tests are a beast. They are so hard and leave you questioning the material. His test are one of the hardest tests I have taken. Although lecture attendance is not required, lecture is still very heavy with material.

Groot cares about the topic of anatomy, as well as teaching it to his students. He explains concepts well and is clear as to what you need to know for exams. Those who complained about the difficulty of the class may not realize that memorizing functions of muscles, systemic traces, locations of structures, etc is necessary in the medical field.

Groot is an awesome professor; definitely one of my favorite! He is very passionate about anatomy and it shows. He is always happy to answer questions and provides time for extra help outside of class. Human Anatomy is only difficult because the amount of material covered. If you want to succeed, go to lecture and do the workbook.

Groot is an amazing teacher. However, if you are not prepared to treat this class like it is a full time job do not expect to get a good grade. There is always an opportunity to get help outside of class and the labs are super interesting, but prepare to give the majority of your time to this class.

This was by far my favorite class I have taken in college, and that is definitely thanks to Dr. Groot. He is a very engaging lecturer and genuinely cares that you learn the content. The class requires a lot of study time outside of the lectures, but if you fill out the workbook and go to office hours you will have a good shot at doing well.

Groot is my favorite teacher I have had at the U by far. This class is difficult due to the amount of content, but he explains every topic very thoroughly. I felt that he was very understanding and gives every student the opportunity to succeed. The tests require a lot of studying, but the content is pulled directly from concepts taught in class.

Groot is amazing at lectures, he made anatomy super engaging even at 8 in the morning. However, his tests aren't an accurate representation of what's taught in class. He tests on the most random things, rather than making sure we understand the important topics. This class requires a lot of study time, but TA's are super helpful and labs are fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Groot is a great professor his class is practically impossible to get a good grade in. Expect to study for well over 20 hours each week and still not do well on the exams. If it weren't for the TA's I would have never made it through. His class is extremely harder then it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Groot was one of my favorite professors. He made me care about anatomy, when I took the course just to take it. His 8am lectures kept me awake and engaged, and I like that he upheld the class structure and material that Mark instituted. He answered every question I had, and always emailed back promptly. You want to sit in the front for this class!

Groot is not fit to be teaching an intro anatomy course. His slides on canvas had 0 information on them. Lab was interesting but didn't help at all for exams. Exams always focused on somethig niche that was mentioned once in lecture. He is a very tough grader and if you don't use the exact wording he wants, you won't get the points.

Horrible teacher along with grader. Didn't care for anything but himself. Reached out for help and said "you probably just dont understand. Take somewhere else to even better change your major so you dont have to suffer through this.

The Anatomy curriculum Groot teaches is extremely difficult. That being said, I found him to be upbeat, helpful, and very educated in what he is teaching. This class requires at least 24 hours of outside studying a week if you're looking to be successful. I have never studied so much to still find exams so difficult. Tough class but Groot is good.

HORRIBLE!! Probably one of the worst professors I have ever had and have ever met. He has no consideration for his students and does not communicate with TAs. We were taught material that we did not need to know and then tested on things we were not even taught. Honestly just a horrible person with ugly ass outfits too. I worked too hard for a C+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr.Groot is not fit to teach anatomy. His exams are extremely hard, and he does not even tell you what to study for. His answer every time someone asked was "study everything". If a student is coming to you for help, take time out to give a constructive answer. Dr.Groot seemed bitter and upset in his office hours, and he made students uncomfortable

Be ready to put in a ton of work and be sure to go to office hours or TA hours. Those helped a ton. Do your workbook and study for the exams, but don't get too wrapped up in the details that you forget the very basic words listed in the lecture manual. Lab was super interesting and helped keep me enjoying the class. Study for lab quizzes.

Sure he can lecture but does 20+ hours of weekly studying, superfluous labs w/ quizzes + practical exam (had one until 8:30 PM the DAY BEFORE Thanksgiving), 300+ pages worth of memorization you HAVE to commit to memory incl 100+ muscles' attachments + C- avg. redeem him? Tidbit: It's the hardest non-Ivy League intro anatomy class. Anki everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: By far the hardest class I took the U. Be prepared to spend an unreasonable amount of time outside of class studying if you want a good grade. The average exam scores were in the C- range. Groot knows the material well and can teach it well but chooses to read slides. When he got out from behind his computer and taught, it was spectacular.

Definitely make sure you have enough time in your schedule to study DAILY. And do your workbook! most exam questions are at least inspired from it. Take good notes. Most of the exam material are strictly from lecture and the textbook is not helpful. While lab was something I performed very well in, exams matter more. So focus on prioritizing exams

It says 4 credits but be prepared to put in 20-25 hours a week studying. He doesn't drop quizzes, or offer extra credit, his final is partially cumulative, and he doesn't share recordings of his lectures. I aced the lab but ended up with a C because his exams are what really matters. He's a genius but be prepared to take it on like a second job.

People that are saying Groot is a bad professor didn't take the right measures to succeed in the class (measures that he explicitly explains at the beginning of the semester). He is so knowledgable, articulate, and really encourages people to ask questions until they understand. The tests were hard but very manageable if you study the material

Groot took all the teaching materials from Mark Nielsen but made all the tests harder. TA's commented on how much harder tests were. Absolutely ridiculous how hard this class was and how weird one off questions were worth so many points. Take anatomy at SLCC or in the summer with shawn miller.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was genuinely one of the hardest classes I have taken so far. I felt very unsupported as a student by the professor. The TA's were the reason I did okay in the class. He does not care about his students at all. Not helpful at all. If you want to do well, make are this is your only hardest class, go to TA hours and fill out that workbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Groot is an amazing lecturer, but that's the only good part about this class. If you have no life outside of anatomy then you will do great but if you are a normal person and have a life, then good luck. I have a job and couldn't make it to any of the TA/office hours bc they are only on weekdays. Really hard to succeed unless you can attend those

The homework's length varies each week which means 1 question could be a whole point one week vs .05 points the next which is very frustrating, especially considering there aren't drops. Lab quizzes are every week, including during midterms, and take up way too much time to study for. He often acts like this is our only class and demeans students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ok lecturer but the course has a severe lack of accessibility. No posted lectures & the slides he does post don't have any helpful material. The only way to get info is to absorb everything in person while he goes really quickly & doesn't write anything on the board. Lab is supposed to help your grade but won't. No drops. Rude during office hours.

Grading is harsh - average grade in my class was 68.42%. Writing down word for word what Groot says in lecture is the only way you're guaranteed to get full points on a question. Docks points for including additional examples. Recorded lectures are interesting and well done. I never used textbook, it's not great and all questions based on lectures.

I have no issue with Dr. Groot himself, though his course was one of the most difficult classes I have taken. His questions are very vague, each test varies in difficulty and study guides are not pertinent to the test. I heavily recommend going to his tutoring and SI sessions as it is incredibly difficult to get a good grade in this class.

By far the hardest class I've ever taken; not because of the material but due to the professor. Exams are filled with vague questions and docks you for not answering with exact description (WORD FOR WORD). Groot does not care about student success and simply wants to be the smartest person in the room.

Groot is a cool guy, but the toughest grader I have had my entire time in college. You can write an entire paragraph answer & you will get docked points for not using a specific word or term. This is a VERY hard class. He has great lectures & gives the tools to succeed but getting good grades on the tests & assignments is near impossible.

Ive taken over 130 credits, and this was the single worst class Ive taken. No matter how well you do on the answers to the test questions, you will get docked points, with zero explanation apart from " -2 points. Muscles" or " -3 points. Joints", when your answer had the exact muscles or joints needed. The grading is completely unjust and incorrect
groot is the best. his lectures are engaging and he makes the content interesting. he cares a lot about getting to know everyone.

Professor Groot is an amazing professor. He is very passionate about what he teaches and truly cares about his students. His class is difficult and he has high expectations. You will have to work hard to get a good grade, however, he provides you with all of the resources that you need to succeed. Take advantage of his and his SI/TA's office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unclear expectations regarding answers on all assignments. His questions are always vague, but the answers he wants for full credit are overly detailed. If you don't mention each and every tiny detail about something you have no chance for an A on an assignment, quiz or exam. Fun guy, but horrible when it comes to having him in control of a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fun to listen to his lectures, but when it comes to graded material, you'll get docked for just about anything. For almost every assignment, quiz and test in the class I was docked points on free response questions when the questions didn't specifically ask for certain details. The only way to get 100% is to copy what he says word for word.

Groot is passionate about KINES 3092 but he could care less about your personal success in this class. This professor nit picks every single test and assignment, so make sure you know exactly what he's looking for EVEN though his assignment/test questions are vague & confusing. Unwilling to work with you if life situations arise, plan accordingly.

I loved taking Groots class, he is awesome. The graders of the class I feel look for every little detail and are not shy about taking points away. Overall fun class and I learned a lot but lecture videos, homework, and studying took up the majority of my week

I loved taking this class form Groot. It was clear to me that he was passionate about this subject and teaching it to students. He was a great resource when studying for exams and his TAs were always very helpful and available. Would take again for any kines class!!

Professor Groot made kinesiology interesting, however is very tedious with his grading. You will miss points for leaving out key words or a phrase. You have to study every week and do extra work to pass. Go to SI, TA office hours, & meet with him if you are stuck, before its too late. Test are all free response. Be prepared for a hard class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Be prepared for Groot to expect you to know everything he knows. The tests are graded unfairly, make sure you go to SI sessions so you know what "key words" you have to use to get credit for the answers. If you do not use his "key words" and just phrase CORRECT answers differently than he wants, you will get marked wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really fun class with a really fun professor. Not your typical lab. Class is mainly graded based on lab reports written on your own. Class is only 1214 people in it so you will have many opportunities to engage with your peers and professor. Get ready to sweat b/c you will be running (literally) the tests yourselves, which what made the class fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Audio lectures (10-20 min) and in person lectures. Would recommend recording lectures bc he goes through concepts fast. Group assignments are in class, but he provides little direction with how specific you need to be (the answer is very specific). Late assignments arent accepted and each bring you down a grade if missed. Go to SI sessions!!!

Kinesiology is an incredibly difficult class, and be prepared to know all of the origins and insertions of every muscle in the body throughout the semester. Groot is an AMAZING lecturer but has incredibly picky grading for exams and assignments. SI is a must!! This is a very interesting and applicable class for kinesiology majors.

Groot cares about being the smartest person/alpha in the classroom. Helping students succeed is low priority, as he states "its your job as a student to learn the information, not mine to teach". If you're not over specific in your answers, you'll miss the whole question. Unbelievable how such a genius can be so out of tune with teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Groot's exams were conceptually hard and he had very vague questions. He had questions that were only discussed in lecture once which I found to be unfair. His TA's were unfair with the grading. His exams were long for the amount of material given. Take the summer course instead.
My favorite professor at the U. Super awesome guy to talk to, loves his job and it shows. Study for the tests from your notes and you'll be ok. Assignments are easy. Loved this class.

If you have a disability, do not take this class from this professor! He does not give accommodations in emergency situations (he expects your emergencies to be planned?) I didnt think the class was difficult but found him to be completely unreasonable and should have reported him to the Office for Equal Opprtunity and Affirmative Action.

Dr. Groot is wonderful teacher and is very straight foward. Is intimidating at first, but once you get to know him, is really friendly. Kinesiology is the hardest class in the major, so it makes sense for his exams to be challenging and mentally stimulating. Ask questions in and outside class. No question is a dumb one. SI is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Groot is a great professor, his class is not easy by any means but he is very fair with the grading and he makes you work for your grade. Assignments reinforced my knowledge and forced me to study. Easy to contact and meet with, regarding any questions. Extremely knowledgeable guy, would take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I have ever taken at U of U! Groot is amazing and is such a good resource for learning so many other kinesiology concepts that maybe aren't taught as well in other classes. The lab is fun. He makes you work for it but he eases you into it and is always available for office hour help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Groot is really hard to work with. He will only respond to his emails between 9 and 12. Most people have taken the class before. He kinda sets you up for failure if he deems you unlikable. His tests are really challenging. The answers have to be 100% correct to do well. He talks really fast while lecturing It is hard to keep up while taking notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great teaching style, entertaining lectures, plenty of class engagement. The assignments correlate with the lectures, critical analysis is key. Good amount of resources to succeed, SI is essential for test prep and overall understanding. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Groot was an amazing professor. He actually cares for his students if they're willing to work with him. Go to his office hours, it really helps! Final Group project that he grades very hard on, and 3 exams. Go to class, take notes, find a study group and practice the material because this class isn't easy with just attending and taking notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Groot teaches Kinesiology different than the ways that other professors have taught Kinesiology at the University of Utah. He focuses more on the functional implication of muscles and therefore his tests are much more conceptual and harder than just memorizing names of muscles. Don't get me wrong I still think Groot is a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Groot is an AWESOME teacher! He is incredible at lecturing. You can tell he loves what he does, also he is SO nice and So willing to help out with all your questions! Definitely go to his office hours! :D It's not easy by any means, but if you go to class and study you will be just fine. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You might be able to pass without attending class, but he gives lots of info that isn't on the PowerPoints, plus Dr. Groot is super knowledgeable and enthusiastic, and he has a sense of humor which keeps lectures interesting. Textbook not required, but it was a great resource while studying. Fair grader, but expect to work for it; it's worth it.

Jon is a fantastic professor. Anyone who says different clearly didn't put in the work or show up to class. He has a lot of passion for what he does, don't be mistaken though, his class is challenging. But if you ask questions and take advantage of his office hours, you can get a great grade.

This is his first semester teaching this class and it is a joke. His tests are the hardest I've ever taken. He is strictly powerpoints. If you don't come to class for him to explain the powerpoints, you won't pass. Tests are all that affect your grade. I have A's in all quizzes and assignments, I still won't get an A.  PICK ANOTHER TEACHER!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jon is a great teacher who's also working on his graduated degree so he understand what's it like being a student so he won't push you too hard.  He is extremely knowledgeable with his stuff since he also TA the human anatomy class.  If you attend class everyday, you shouldn't have probably getting good grade in his class.

His teaching skills are dry, and they're often boring. There is almost no point in going to his lectures, as you can learn everything on your own, as the textbook is excellent. Very strict grader, but I respect what his expectations are. The low rating is primarily for the lectures more than anything else. Read the textbook, and you'll be fine.

Lectures are long and boring, and exams are difficult. It is not always clear what material is to be expected on exams, however he is lenient in grading. The discussion sections are helpful to learn the material, and attendence is for a grade, but worth it. Professor Gondolo also seems to forget what is on his own syllabus grading wise.

Gondolo is excellent! E&M is hard, but if you do the work and come to class, you'll definitely learn something from his lectures. He has you read chapters outside of class, then works problems in class with demonstrations and discussions to help you understand the concepts. Plus, he offers a lot of extra credit. If you work hard, you'll do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The worst class experience I've had thus far, and I liked physics going in. He has to make it easy to get an A with his point system to compensate for his horrid teaching style. Most people didn't go to class when I took it, because he confused them more than being self taught. Lots of homework that doesn't reflect the problem style on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Though he knows his stuff and his demonstrations are fun, he's pretty bad at explaining the concepts to those that haven't seen something like it before. Be prepared for a tough class; though, if you show up, and take good notes, you should pass. Just barely though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Electricity and Magnetism is a tough class, but with this professor, you have to be trying not to get a good grade. He has a point system for grading where you have to get a minimum number of points on homework AND exams for an A. When I took it, you needed to get about a 48% average on the tests to reach the exam point threshold. Very easy prof.

Terrible instructor.  It seems like he hasn't thought about basic physics in about 20 years and is therefore unable to understand that you are learning it for the first time.  I went for help once and never went back because we spent an hour arguing about what I didn't understand.

Run away from this teacher! Gondolo's lectures are easily the most boring and most uninformative I have ever had. He literally reads everything from the book and then complicates the formulas to the point where they are inapplicable. I had to teach myself the entire second semester of physics due to his confusing teaching style.

Pretty hard, but he gave me  what I want from a graduate class - Learning!!! He's simply atonishing, no way!! Highly recommended. If you guys rate profs from the easiness, you'd better stop doing physics!!

Good professor, but I echo previous posts, the tests are extremely difficult. Class averages were usually around 45-50% Its true you can get a decent grade, but I ended up with a B+ with 10-15+ hours of study each week. I know that someone ended up with an A, but to me (who HAD a 4.0 GPA) it was impossible. If you can, take from another professor.
the class definitely is time consuming. it takes time to study and do the work if you want a good grade. it is possible to get a good grade, it is just how uch you work for it. nice guy overall.

He's very nice and more than willing to help you, BUT his tests are insane.  Unless you're a physics wizard, I wouldn't recommend taking it from Gondolo.  He used to be easier, but he's under a lot of pressure to make the class harder, and that is exactly what he had done.  BEWARE this class will KILL your GPA.
No Comments
He's a nice teacher, but it's hard to understand him sometimes and he doesn't always answer the questions that you ask.

One of the funniest, most high-energy professors I've ever witnessed. Somehow takes a boring class like accounting and makes it very interesting and engaging. Could not recommend this class enough. Your grade pretty directly reflects the effort you put into the class, as all study guides and practice tests are available from the start of the year.
Best professor I've ever had

Geoffrey was the best professor I've had so far at the U. I loved taking his 2100 class. I learned so much and want to possibly major in accounting now. His practice tests are amazing for the exams. I wish every professor made practice tests and videos explaining how to do them. I will definitely try to get Geoffrey for ACCTG 3100 in the fall.

One of if not the best professor I have ever had. So nice and cares about every single one of his students. His sections of 2100 did significantly better in accounting than most other professors and he somehow made accounting lectures entertaining. HEAVILY recommend taking his class.

Financial Accounting is not my strong suit, but even still, I really enjoyed being in Geoffrey's class. I was also in his 2100 class, so I've got to know him very well. Yes, this intermediate class is tough, but Geoffery makes expectations very clear and it is 100% possible to pass with an A. Always accessible and very friendly. Highly reccomend!
Best professor I have ever had. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

***TAKE THIS CLASS*** Geoffrey is by far the best professor I have had in University. No question about it. Slides are informational and he is hilarious. This class will whoop you but he is always on call for help. 10/10 would recommend.

Easily a top professor at the U, is great at explaining the subject and also provides oodles of material for you to study with for exams. Makes a point to know every persons name in the entire lecture hall on the first day of class. Also one of the kindest and most out going teachers I've ever met. Very friendly and wants to see students do well.
Absolute beast! Knows every student in a 300 person lecture. Makes a hard class easy by explaining the material well. If you pay attention and listen to him it's an easy A.
Literally the GOAT professor at the U. Never seen a more high energy professor at the U that cares about his students more. Also an amazing teacher that makes accounting make sense.

Professor Pears is one of the best instructors you could ask for. His lectures are pretty engaging and he does a good job of being very relatable and down to earth, while also juggling the difficult concepts within accounting. His practice tests do a great job preparing you for the exams, if you put in the time to learn the material you'll do great

Coming to this class, I had low expectations and was ready to fail or get a C- but the way he teaches the class is so amusing. He would start by explaining things using professional business terms, and then would give us the simpler terms and which really helped me. I also enjoyed his step-by-step exam practice videos; they really helped me a lot.

Great professor. Exams are hard, but he gives you everything you need to prepare, and if you can do the practice exam from the previous semester, you're guaranteed to do well. Honestly, not a difficult class if tackled the correct way. Geoffrey is also incredibly friendly, caring, and accessible outside of class. Highly highly recommend.
If you have the chance to take from this professor, do it! Makes lectures very interesting in what most would consider a not very interesting topic.
Best professor I've ever had. Made accounting interesting. Helped me when I was struggling in the class.

Loved him. He memorized everyone's names before the first class. Was engaging and entertaining. Very helpful and as long as you went to class you should easily pass the course. He was also very understanding and helpful if you needed help or failed or had outside circumstances that caused you to do poorly on something.
Really cares about his students' learning. Very personable and fun to learn from.
best professor i've had so far, very caring, so funny and understanding.

Great professor! He explains accounting concepts clearly and makes sure students really understand the material. Very approachable, organized, and always willing to answer questions. His lectures are engaging and tie concepts to real-world examples, which makes learning easier. If you put in the effort you'll do well in his class. Highly recommend!

Best teacher I've ever had! Extremely helpful, and is willing to help you with concepts you don't understand. Went over my exams with me after and explained what was done wrong. Made me want to pursue accounting because of how engaging his class was, he put up practice problems on the board and then went around helping people solve them. 10/10 clas

Professor Pears is seriously the best teacher you could ever ask for. He is more than willing to help the struggling students and makes time for them. If you do understand concept he will go through different ways of teaching it until it sticks!! You would be doing yourself a disservice if you did not take this class from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Geoffrey was one of my favorite professors. His teaching style was unique but it worked. He provided lots of feedback on tests and responded to emails so quickly. He's a very sharp guy and knows his stuff. He is also very thoughtful and knew everyone in the class by name which I really do think engages students more.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: he made accounting way more interesting

One of my favorite professors of all time. You can tell he puts a lot of effort into his lectures, and wants every student to succeed. Genuinely enjoyed going to his class- he is effortlessly funny. Provides amazing resources to study, and is always there for help. Might just take his bowling class since he was so fun.

I'd strongly recommend taking a class from Geoffrey if you get the chance. His lectures are energetic, entertaining, and filled with jokes and stores. I appreciated how he sets aside time in class to individually help students with in class exercises. Each test had a test review video that made studying easy.

This professor is probably one of the best professors I've had. Really cares and understands the students and you can see he is passionate about the subject. I felt like I really learned accounting and this was one of the classes i looked forward to even though accounting is not the most interesting subject.

Geoffrey Pears is one of my absolute favorite professors. He is hilarious and never lets a lecture get too stale or boring. He understands that accounting is difficult for many students and creates an environment where we aren't afraid to ask questions. You can tell that he truly wants his students to succeed. I recommend him 1000% times over.

By far one of the best Professors I have had at the U. Made Accounting fun with the examples he provided. I never found myself bored in any of his lectures either. I would definitely take an accounting class with him again if it was required. GOAT.
Absolutely killed it throughout the year. Responded to emails quickly and was very clear on what the class required from students. Great teacher, would totally take again.

Pears is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He is engaging, funny, and understanding of situations that affect our performance. He truly cares about the students and what he is teaching. I would love to take another one of his classes and he is the reason I am majoring in accounting. 10/10 professor!

Professor Pears made learning accounting super fun and easy and honestly the best professor I've had at the U so far. Don't get me wrong, the class is still hard but the way he teaches (examples over reading from the power point) really makes it stick. He provides practice tests, with videos, for the exams. You're missing out if you don't take him!

Pears is the GOAT. You will regret taking accounting from anyone other than him. Out of all the other accounting professors Pears provides the most out of class help, and gives out super helpful videos for each test going over every kind of problem you will see. No other professors do that, many wont even be clear on what you will see on exams.

THE BEST! Prof Pears is an amazing instructor. I wish I had him for every class till I graduate. He is funny, in tune with his students, and always willing to help. He won't judge you for not understanding material. He wants you to succeed in his class and he wants you to have fun. 
Tip: go to his office for extra help and you WILL ace every test.

he is AMAZING. Accounting was so fun and he explained things incredibly well. By far one of the best professors I've taken. The exams are difficult, but if you go to class, pay attention, and practice, you will do incredibly well. I highly HIGHLY recommend you take Geoffrey for your accounting class, you will not regret at all.

Geoffrey was phenomenal. Fin. Acctg 2 is challenging, but he is incredible at teaching difficult concepts and is always available if you have any questions. Geoffrey is hands down the best accounting professor at the U and is incredibly personable.

Best professor I've had at the U. His lectures are engaging, and he's just a cool person. He's amazing at explaining concepts and provides lots of examples, provides practice exams and videos of him going over them, and is very transparent about what will be on exams.
GREAT! Love him would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Geoffery is the BEST professor I have experienced at the UofU so far. His lectures are not boring and they are helpful, informative, and lots of in-class practice problems. He gives lots of material to study with for the midterms/final and if you put in the work you will easily score well on the exams and get an A.

HIGHLY recommend Geoffery

Geoffrey Pears is an exceptional instructor who has significantly enhanced my academic experience. His teaching style combines intellectual rigor with genuine accessibility, creating an optimal learning environment.
He is the goat

One of the best professors I've had so far! He is super helpful and sets you up for success, his class wasn't super easy but he is aware of that and offers you every resource possible to make you do well. I highly recommend taking him for accounting!!

Best professor ever!!! His lectures are fun and easy to learn/understand. Midterms and final are easy as long as you come to class and are familiar with the concepts. His class is by far the only class I've enjoyed and liked!!
Really great guy. I actually took this class semester but I still see him around campus all the time and he always says hi to me. Very thoughtful and good at teaching accounting.

I wish every one of my professors taught like he does. You can tell that he puts in the hours to give his students the best opportunities both in and outside of class. Makes the lectures interesting by encouraging questions, minimal use of slides or prewritten notes, and encourages students to be curious and ask questions.

10/10 professor. Assignments can be tough if you aren't familiar with accounting beforehand, but he makes it easy and fun. Tests aren't too bad but do require a decent amount of study time and memorization. He also shows up to class in a different suit every day (brownie points). Very nice and remembers everyone's names. Take him if you can!

Great Guy, highly recommend, actually cares and will know you quite well even after the second day of class. Wish all my teachers taught and prepared us like he does. If you have him on your schedule you are very lucky.

Best professor in the business school. Knew everyones name on day 1. Engaging lectures. Acctg is a class where you have to be engaged from day 1. Take notes, pay attention and Geoffrey will make sure you succeed. Cares about every student. I wish he could teach everyone of my classes. I plan on doing finance but if I ever do acctg its b/c of him.
the best professor i've had at the U.

Geoffrey is the best college professor at the business school! He knows all of our names and balances critical thinking with teaching direct subject material. He teaches us what we need to know instead on confusing us on the test. 10/10 would recommend
He has been my favorite professor so far. He teaches so well and is making me want to switch to accounting. Highly Recommend.
The GOAT, he understands the concepts he teaches are difficult and makes his powerpoints and lectures easy to follow and understand.

Geoffrey was a great professor. The course was inherently difficult, but he tried to make the topics as easy to understand as possible. There were two pre-class quizzes and one post-class quiz per week. Geoffrey was very accessible outside of class and was very easy to reach. I highly recommend him.

Geoffrey was by far the best professor I have had and will definitely remain one of my favorites. He made every class fun and engaging. He is a new teacher and young so he relates with college kids very well and creates a very inviting space. Not a single negative thing to say about him and 100% would make sure you take one of his classes.

This was Geoffrey's first year teaching and he was an amazing professor. The subject and class material is pretty boring and Geoffrey tried his hardest to make it interesting with his fun personally and jokes. For being a first year professor, he is a great teacher and is VERY accessible outside class. He tries his hardest to make sure you succeed

Geoffrey has been one of my favorite professors ever. He makes class super engaging and wants everyone to learn the material. He is always willing to help with whatever questions you have and he never makes you feel stupid if you don't know something. He is young so he realtes a lot with what we have going on. 100% need to take him if you can.

Geoffrey is by far the best professor I have had! He sparked my passion for accounting. Classes consist of lots of hands-on examples. He is willing to meet outside of class and will even miss his Taco Bell run to make sure you understand. He is so kind, has a great sense of humor, and manages to keep everyone engaged. He has cool suit jackets too!

Geoffrey is 100% my favorite professor I have ever had at the U! I was so scared to take accounting but he made it one of my favorite classes. His love for accounting is infectious and almost makes me want to major in it ;) Also, he never makes you feel stupid for not understanding something which for me happens a lot. You'll want to go to class!
GEOFFREY IS THE BEST!! If you have the opportunity to take any classes with him you totally should he is so funny and nice and has so many office hours he is available for help whenever you need it.

Geoffrey was the best college professor I have ever had. He always opened his doors for extra help, is great at lectures, and always knows what he is talking about. He is very engaging and makes a boring topic interesting. He is young so he is very relateable and empathetic towards his students. He is also hilarious. TAKE HIM FOR ACCOUNTING
Very funny guy. Good at making material clear to understand. Also considerate regarding late assignments and whatnot.

Professor Pears is good at dumbing down the material to make it understanding. He is clear at teaching and doesn't give an overwhelming amount of information. His tests are a lot harder than class and he gives pre-class quizzes every class. Show up to class, pay attention, and do the in class problems to do good in the class. The class is curved.

Mr. Pears brings a lot of energy to the classroom. He is engaging and funny, and his teaching style is interactive and effective. You can tell he wants us all to understand the concepts and do well in the class and accounting. He uses real-world examples to show the utility of accounting in situations that involve real companies.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Went into this class with low expectations with it being accounting which is usually perceived as boring. But Geoffrey made accounting fun and some how I genuinely really enjoyed the topics. Even if you may not be entertained by the learning in class, he does a great job making it fun and engaging. Also is incredibly helpful with questions.

Prof. Guerra teaches pretty fast, but for me that was perfect. She doesn't bore you with prerequisite material which is very nice. Each topic is thoroughly explained and taught. Overall, I had no confusion on anything from this semester. 10/10 would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Guerra was the best math teacher I have ever had! Her lectures were very informative. You could tell she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

BEWARE!! She doesn't even know the lessons herself, always messing up and asking us as if we know. She's pretty chill but the lectures are messy and unclear since she moves really quickly between topics making it confusing. Quizzes are harder than tests and the ALEKS homework system is hell.

She did an excellent job of retaining engagement and explaining topics in a way that was easy to understand. She goes through enough practice problems that students become familiar with the process, but not so many that interest is lost.

Dalyana has been by far the best professor at the University of Utah for me. I took calculus 1 and 2 from her and have missed being in her class ever since. She has note packets for every lecture so that everyone can keep up with what she is doing. She is very clear with expectations, grading and how to succeed in the class.

Caring, nice teacher. Extra credit, exam retake, late hw accepted, and answers get partial credit. Attendance is mandatory. I'm retaking the course because lack thereof. Lots of hw and it's REALLY tedious. DO IT. You're good at math and do the work you'll get an A. Horribly boring class. Her jokes certainly aren't the highlight of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Guerra was awesome! Everyone told me that 1080 was going to be a very difficult class, but Professor Guerra made it so much smoother. She is a very caring and understanding instructor.

She was an amazing professor, and I highly recommend her for Math 1050. She had extremely detailed and easy-to-follow lectures and provided students with handy note packets to use during classes. Furthermore, she had a very upbeat and nice attitude which made attending class enjoyable!

Professor Guerra is a great math professor who genuinely cares about her students' success. Exams are manageable if you attend office hours, and she offers extra credit opportunities. There's a lot of homework, but it's manageable if you stay on top of it. Highly recommend her class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Guerra is an exceptional instructor who is always willing to provide assistance and clearly explains concepts. Her extra credit opportunities and grading system are highly beneficial, significantly contributing to improving my grade by two letter grades.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dalyana is awesome! She made  notoriously difficult calc ll feel very doable. She made giant note packets for us (which I found very helpful) and had a quiz and a homework due each week, which might seem overwhelming but really helped me solidify my understanding of the material. Her LA's were great too! I would definitely recommend her :)

As an individual who has never liked math, Dalyana does an excellent job at changing that. She is very engaged with her students and super sweet. The are a lot of quizzes, however, they are group based, and tests on the other hand are individual work. The LA's host HW Workshops daily as well which is extremely helpful.

I think her exams and quizzes were extremely fair. She always made sure we had plenty of examples to practice beforehand, and her lectures were well structured. This is a pretty easy class to get an A as long as you stay organized with all your work.

She's a great professor but the class just moves insanely slow. If you're good at math, get ready to be bored in lecture. She also creates giant note packets for each student to follow, these can be helpful, but theyre a pain to print out if you don't have a way do them on an ipad or something. Overall good professor but just goes way too slow.

Professor Guerra is a great lecturer. She puts in a lot of effort towards her classes and assignments to ensure they are plenty of productive learning opportunities. Canvas is full of extra problems and solutions for each topic in case we needed extra practice, and her quizzes were good indicators of how the tests would be formatted.

Professor Guerra took material that could be quite hard to understand, and broke it down, ensuring that her students had a grasp on the content. I did poorly on the last midterm of the semester, and she helped me review all of the exams material until I had a full understanding, ensuring success on the final exam (which replaced my low exam grade).

INCREDIBLE teacher. Was extremely scared going into Calc II, but was met with the most caring, respectful, kind professor!!! She genuinely enjoys her field, and she gives chance after chance if she knows you're willing to put in the work. Incredible with lectures, tests were accurate to what we were learning.

Professor Guerra is the best professor I have ever had. She cares a great deal about her students, getting to know them by name. Her class format is rigorous, with frequent quizzes and exams designed to push her students to embrace the material throughout the semester, but always in a way that feels manageable. Fantastic professor!

Professor Guerra is a really really nice person. She clearly cares about students. However, she provides and intends that you follow a set of lecture notes that she creates. While these notes are great, I had a really hard time retaining class info. It is nearly impossible to try to make your own notes. Also, calc 2 is just hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes that force you to study and retain the information. Weekly homework that isn't too hard. I love how structured the class is and she really wants to help us learn it. Content is hard but she provides so many resources it's great.

Prof Guerra makes what is a notoriously difficult class much more manageable. There aren't surprises on the exams, she will always answer questions during or after class, and provides plenty of study resources. She is extremely kind and understanding. Sometimes she can go a little too slow with the course materials but overall that isn't an issue.

Prof Guerra holds your hand through everything with her note packets. This is great for a lot of students, but I prefer to learn on my own with more independence. I sometimes attended lectures just to get the attendance points but didn't pay attention. She is the nicest professor I've ever had, but I didn't like her teaching style.

Taking Calculus was really just because I need it for my major. I am not a big fan whatsoever of math and struggle a lot with it but if I do have to say, take Dalyana. She is amazing at explaining topics and really goes over it again if she notices that students are missing the concept. I took Trig and got a worse grade in Trig than I did Calc 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dalyana clearly cared for us students and clearly knew a lot about the subject but after the 2nd or 3rd week we were constantly behind which made her lectures feel rushed. She had guided notes which helped a lot. The mandatory labs were annoying but manageable if you knew the concepts and practiced we learned in class. Attendance is mandatory btw

Prof. Guerra was very caring, and she dropped lowest grades including one midterm which took a lot of stress off, but she was not great at actually conveying the material. A lot of students I knew would struggle with problems that weren't exactly like the ones in class and her TA was constantly having to give explanations in labs.

She's honestly such an amazing professor. It's almost impossible to find professors who are good humans as well as good teachers. She is both. You will get the grade you deserve. Her tests are very fair, and are never a surprise for students. I would 100% recommend her. I love her sm.

Took Calc II in Spring 2023, and Professor Guerra is probably the best math teacher I have ever had! 
It was a hard class, but she provided note sheets for the lectures that made the material clear and easy to follow. She is compassionate, willing to answer questions, and adapts based on the needs of her students. Highly recommend taking her class!

Best Calc 2 professor ever! She gave us a lot of extra credits. She provided us with detailed materials, a lot of opportunities for practicing and a successful habit activity every week for extra credit. I would love to take her class again if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Greenhalgh is a caring, knowledgeable professor. She receives more criticism than she deserves. Her expectations are clear, and it is my opinion that a lot of her criticism comes from students who are unprepared for the course.

I really enjoyed all her lectures. I loved this class and enjoyed what I was learning. She was able to present lots of things in ways that made sense despite being somewhat difficult topics. The lab reports were a lot of work and difficult at times, but overall I'm really glad I took this class and learned a lot.

I was in a car crash and she told me to just fail the class because she would not be willing to help students in serious situations. She also fired me from my TA job because I was in the hospital for one week with prior notice to her, then refused to pay me and gaslit the receptionist that I didn't exist. Lo key not a good teacher or person.
She told me that I don't deserve an education.

An amazing professor who makes a very difficult subject very accessible. Lots of resources to learn, discussion worksheets and practice exams. Content for the exam was clear lectures were well done, slides were great for note taking in class. It is a hard class, but she really cares about her student and gives all the resources you need to succeed

One of the greatest professors at the U. Her knowledge stems from years of experience. She is at home in this arena and her strengths lie in her experience, much of which is right-brained. An authentic person. The TA is incredible,  sophisticated, and caring.

Get prepared. It's a hard class. Grade is largely tied to the 3 exams + final that are worth 500 of the 600 total points. A lot of time is required outside of lecture to get an A but the resources are certainly there if you put in the effort. She goes through the material at light speed and says “um” every other sentence. TA office hours are a must
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only saw her in passing once over the whole semester, so this review is mostly for the TAs, which were great. The labs were fun but some of the lab materials could be quite confusing and riddled with typos. Overall I enjoyed the lab. It really helped solidify my chemistry knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken lab and biochem 1 lecture with this professor and she has been utterly unfair in both occurrences. Her exams and quizzes focus on minuscule details of the lecture slides and she phrases them in a way impossible to comprehend. The lab TAs grade poorly due to the manuals being very unclear. Good luck!

Elizabeth is smart, and she seems kind, but the lab was difficult. Reports consumed hours of my time, and large projects using software to visualize proteins were complex. The TAs were difficult to work with, and many had harsh grading tactics. There weren't nearly enough outside resources either (like office hours), and experiments rarely worked.

This was unnecessarily hard for a Gen Chem 1 lab. TAs do not care to help you or explain properly. I emailed my TA and he answered my question wrong and then docked me for said grade. 0/10 Take this class in the fall, not the spring.

Never saw her this semester. The lab is run by the TA and LA (who contradicted each other) but thats not Elizabeth's fault. The only interaction I had with her was over email when I had trouble submitting an assignment on time and she fixed my grade since the class' Canvas gives a 0 to late work (no tolerance) and she gave me full credit
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Greenhalgh is one of the best professors I have attended lectures from. You can tell she puts in the time and effort to fully understand the concepts that she teaches. Unfortunately many students don't put in the effort needed to succeed and complain. The lab was super interesting but lab report grading was a bit tough (due to TAs)

During the GFP lab no one got the experiment to work. Post labs take HOURS. Our TA was a harsh grader (by no fault of Dr. Greenhalgh, although I do believe she should curve seeing as some of us got a TA that docked points for little things while others got one that gave credit for turning in a report).

I never once met Elizabeth Greenhalgh, only her TA. This is a chemistry lab that is 100% taught and graded by TA's. The lab wasn't awful, but you had to keep up with assignments, reading, and attendance to succeed. Grading wasn't always the clearest, but it wasn't incredibly harsh. You always work with a partner and some labs are fun, but not all.

The class was mostly ran by TAs, I did not much see or interact with Elizabeth. Despite this, the lab was mostly well run; although I personally did not care for my TA, I can't fault Elizabeth for this. Overall a serviceable experience.

Dr. Greenhalgh gives students plenty of resources to be successful if they are willing to work for it. This is a tough class, it's literally Biochem so yeah, it's gonna be hard. You will have to work hard, but discussion worksheets are super helpful, there are plenty of office hours including her own, and many chances to ask questions in lecture.

This class has been a headache from the beginning. I think Dr. Greenhalgh is very intelligent, but none of the experiments work and the TAs seem like they dont want to be there and dont know what is going on. The lab manual is too vague and the post lab reports take forever. I would seriously avoid taking this class for your mental sanity.
The Biochem lab does not work. Experiments have been failing throughout the semestes. I don't if it's the TAs or Elizabeth's responsibility but it seems like no one knows what's going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely have a very interesting way of teaching being a very fast paste lecture, the material will build on each other, she tried to teach some pneumonic to help you memorize the amino acid, I think she have a hard time writing a exam that is within the students limit but overall not too bad

Professor Greenhalgh is smart, reasonable, and created a rigorous but doable course environment. Discussion worksheets are a great resource for exams. Although exams determine a heavy chunk of your grade, weekly homework assignments helped to cushion grades. Beware of the negative reviews, Greenhalgh was fair and relatively helpful to all students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: With some professors, you can tell that they care for their students and genuinely want them to succeed. Greenhalgh is not one of these people. It was as if she tried her best to bring us down. Her tests were extremely difficult and I never knew what to expect. She was passive-aggressive and rude. Smart but a bad teacher. Overall, she sucks.

A very interesting professor to say the least, some of the question was very abstract where I kind of see where she is coming from but the wording was very vague. I think she need to be more specific on wording. The SI worksheet had so many mistake it seems like no one ever check before they are posted.

Professor Greenhalgh would examine us on questions that were briefly mentioned on one slide, and not test concepts we went over heavily. Although there were practice questions, they were not worded the same way exam questions were. This made the exams unnecessarily hard, and they are the main component of your grade. Avoid if possible.

More times than I can count, she gave a snarky response to a student's question - but then would complain about not being asked questions again. Tests weren't impossibly difficult, but the grading was incredibly unclear. The large number of multiple choice questions made for a lot of all or nothing scoring. Biggest takeaway – she's condescending.

Dr. Greenhalgh is incredibly difficult to work with. She never publishes actual exam averages, although several TAs have said she mis-reports what the averages were. Along with this, she is not flexible or understanding about circumstances. Her exams are incredibly difficult and do not align with the discussion worksheets like she says they do.

Professor Greenhalgh is a super difficult teacher to learn anything from. I'm an honors student and she is the worst professor I've ever had my whole 4 years at the U. She doesn't teach what you ends up testing you on and I would stay away from taking a class from her.

Professor Greenhalgh did not teach the material well and had very hard tests. I am in the honors program and I have never had such a difficult teacher to learn from. Don't recommend having her as a teacher.

While the course content is challenging, it is doable if you put in the effort. However, Dr. Greenhalgh's condescending attitude and unwillingness to work with students was what made it a very negative experience. She was largely unapproachable and would frequently become frustrated with students, contributing to a difficult learning environment.

Dr. Greenhalgh's class is ok. The course layout was fine and the content was not too bad either. She is not a very flexible professor, so make sure you do not have any extenuating circumstances somehow. There is very little wiggle room to get the grade you desire as the class is very exam/quiz heavy with no extra credit available.

Very difficult course, but great to teach critical thinking skills. Greenhalgh forces you to engage with the material deeply, especially since most of her questions require you to give a justification for your answers. Expect to study frequently, and explain all her material in your own words.

This class was extremely challenging, and she did not teach the content well. I am an honors student, and I found that this was my most difficult class. I would not recommend taking this course from Professor Greenhalgh.

She has some really bad reviews here and although those are all valid, I took organic chem ll  at the same time and I will say her class was very challenging but doable. She is a nice professor and is open to answering any questions you may have. She also gives practice every week that reflect how she words exams and quizzes.

I think her class is fair for a 3000 level chem course! Similar workload as ochem. Lots of ways to get help via canvas discussion boards (she usually answers quickly!), TAs, & the actual discussion. Her lectures are good. She puts helpful tutorials on canvas. I just wish the class was 4 credits instead of 3, & had more points aside from exams.

She doesn't teach the content very well. I ended up having to teach myself everything, and the practice materials she provides have nothing to do with the exams. If she provided previous exams to get a feel for what she expects us to study, that would be immensely helpful. She is also fairly inconsiderate when working with her students.

It seems most of the bad reviews come from people who did not attend discussions. Biochem is a hard class and lectures have 300 people. She does an amazing job in lectures and gives fair tests. They are challenging, but everything you need is gone over in the discussions with plenty of TAs to help. People will complain regardless of professor.

Biochemistry is a hard subject, and in a class of 300. This makes it a hard subject (it's a 3000 level class). But this does not mean the professor is bad, she is actually really good. She cares, and has great lectures. Her tests are hard, but she gives plenty of study material in the discussions. I think others would complain regardless of teacher

She is a nice person and easily accessible. Her test questions are out in left field from the topics covered. You can study and learn absolutely everything provided and still get a low grade because of the poorly worded and confusing test questions. She seems disconnected from understanding how and what her students are learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was undoubtedly challenging, but I never felt that it was unfair. I believe she did an excellent job. Once you reach a certain point in your college career, the classes will undoubtedly be difficult. This is even more true of you're on a pre- medical career path. You should expect this and be prepared to work hard.She is reasonable &fair
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a nice teacher, and admittedly a chemist, not a biologist, which shows in her teaching. The lectures will give you the basic concept only, but the tests will test you on its application, which is rarely taught during lecture. The questions and wording are designed to throw you off instead of test your knowledge. Avoid if possible.

She changes her pitch at the end of every sentence to a mumble.Even CC in her videos can't translate. You can't hear the questions people ask, then she calls you out for asking the same question again. I had to learn all the material on my own. Easy material, but she is a chemist, def not a teacher. I was looking forward to this class. Unfortunate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a nice person, but her exams are really poorly written. She has also been caught lying about the class averages - they are much lower than she is reporting and the TAs themselves are telling student students this. Course desperately needs to be curved and extra credit needs to be provided to counter the terrible exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take her for Biochem. Terrible teacher and had to do all the learning for the course myself, despite going to lectures. Weirdly written exams with questions that either she said would not be on the test or questions we had never seen before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful! 350 characters is not nearly enough to describe the tragedy of taking a class from Dr. Greenhalgh. She asks niche questions on her exams and if you don't know one part you'll miss the next few questions. She is a very tough grader, and she is inflexible.This was the worst class and professor I have had in my college career!
Avoid. At. All. Costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can tell that she is really trying. This class will definitely take up a lot of your time but Biochemistry is like that. Overall she is a good professor. You will just have to be on top of your grades yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs
Have to love when half of the course is graded at the end of the semester. A lot of work is expected without any clear guidance. Honestly, I wouldn't ever take her again.

This Gen Chem 1 lab was challenging. We had a remarkably tough midterm where we couldn't use any resources but an easier final where we could look at past lab reports which doesn't make any sense. The lab reports are insanely long and take lots of time. The only good thing I had was my TA. Do not recommend taking this class in the spring semester.

This lab class was extremely hard for General Chemistry 1. We had a midterm and final and couldn't use our lab notebooks like we were told in the beginning. The lab reports are insanely long and take lots of time. The only good thing I had was my TA. Don't recommend if you don't need it.

Never have I taken a lab that requires attendance of two lectures outside of lab, and somehow still feel lost in lab. Oh yeah, maybe because she and the TA's running lab give literally no instruction before or show us where anything is, and the workload outside of the lab is actually a joke. Biochem lecture has basically no correlation of info!

I took biochem and biochem lab with Dr. Greenhalgh, she's pretty good and fair. Responds to emails quickly. I wouldn't be scared to take another class with her. Grading can be bit tough sometimes, her TAs are not great but that will probably change.

Unnecessarily hard class for being an intro to chem lab. Seems like the goal of the lab is to try to fail students, not learn. She never is in lab which is fine, but unhelpful and does not help students if special circumstances arise. Professor and TAs all think way too much of themselves for being bad at running the lab. Don't take unless required

Lectures are often not ready and it seems like she does not dominate the topics she teaches. She is rude and I also took the lab with her and the experiments were not working properly. The class was overall bad.

Why would you pay the salary of a professor who is never present and not interested in teaching? Would rather pay the salaries of the TA's who do teach. TA's are somewhat kind, but again, not very interested in teaching.

She is often condescending and rude when you ask questions, especially on piazza. You are only graded on your exams, quizzes, and discussion participation. Discussion was not helpful, it doesn't help u prepare for exams. Her teaching style was not for me, she didn't explain things very well at all. I relied heavily on the textbook to teach myself.

I thought Greenhalgh was great. If you pay attention and take notes, everything is fairly easy to understand; but don't get behind.

My advice is to not get caught up in extra study material. Her tests are easier than her review stuff. I studied only my lecture notes for the entire semester (don't read the textbook!) and averaged 90% on exams.

This class was challenging, no doubt, but at no point in time did I think that it was unfair. Considering she was a brand new professor this year, I think she did a great job. Once you get to a certain point in your degree (especially if you're pre-med) the classes WILL BE hard. You should expect that. You should expect to have to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor's lectures were challenging to extract meaningful comprehension, leaving students overwhelmed by course content with minimal relevance to assessments. The course structure heavily relied on exams, yet the material provided for preparation failed to align with the exam format.

Lacks control over the course's subject matter and lacks the perspective and experience characteristic of a good professor. Expect bland lectures, mandatory but unrelated discussions, rude/condescending TAs, and frequently misgraded exams. Fortunately, the class isn't THAT hard, but overall not enjoyable. Good luck getting ahold of her too.

She was extremely fair in her grading and testing. I though the exams reflected what we covered in class well. People complain about the difficulty of the class, but the numerous office hours offered rarely had students attending. Maybe if you're having trouble with the material, you might want to put the effort in to get help. Great content/class!

This professor was not a great lecturer. She knows chemistry well no doubt, but maybe isn't fit to lecture a large class. The content covered in this class was pretty easy, but it seemed like useless information that didn't quite grasp the fundamental concepts needed to understand biochemistry, but also biology.

Nice professor, has greatly improved over the semester. Exams are fair, less about straight memorization of little details and more about being confident with the general concepts and interpreting data/graphs. Discussion attendance is mandatory, but I feel that the material covered typically doesn't correlate to what is seen on exams and quizzes.

This class had so much potential. She's new, and is a nice person, but not a nice professor unfortunately. She comes off condescending to students. I've never had a class be so heavily graded on exams and quizzes. This class single handedly tanked my GPA, which affected my chances for grad school. It's really not worth trying to give her a shot.

PLEASE AVOID. 90% of your grade is exams & quizzes (discussion = 10%), NO curves. Almost no guidance for exams, "everything is fair game". I averaged 82% on exams, 92% on quizzes, attended every discussion & STILL got a B+ (usually am a 4.0 student). This class is NOT worth the stress, anxiety, and tears it caused me and many other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is exams and quizzes BUT that means no homework. You only work when studying for exams and I felt the practice materials were good, and matched exams stylistically (she has a distinct style). Didn't get the textbook but would recommend it. I bombed Ochem 1 and didn't take Ochem 2 but did fine here. Low emphasis on memorization. Good luck!

Dr. Owens is amazing! The chemistry content can be difficult, but his lectures are very clear. Your grade is simply a reflection of your work ethic. I wish he could teach all my classes. Very challenging. I was scared to take chemistry because I never thought I'd pass. Instead I got an “A.” Best teacher I've ever had.

Make sure you take the time to study and use all of the materials given. He wants students to succeed.

This was an extremely difficult class, but the prof made all the difference. Not only was he kind and willing to answer all of my questions, but he made sure that we had enough resources to understand the material. Many practice quizzes were available, all with answer keys. It takes a minute to figure out how you're going to study.

IF YOU ARE ON SCHEDULE, YOU ARE BEHIND! Do things ahead of time as often as possible so you can do the practice quizzes!
