reviews.comment: Worst prof ever. He thinks we are complaining about the difficulty of the class, but we really are complaining about his attitude and lack of professionalism. Loves to blame and degrade students. Great person, but teaching is not for him. A good educator would never shift blames on students but to do a self-reflection. Avoid at all cost.

This is by far the worst professor I have ever taken at the U. Grade is based off of 3 exams and EC is 10% from the MasteringChem. The other chem class is 25% extra credit from MC and allows test corrections. There is no curve or test corrections in this class. He blames students for everything and is unprofessional in his emails + announcements.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Owens was extremely unprofessional throughout the course, and progressively got worse. I was always so afraid of talking to him and asking for help because of all the horrible experiences my peers were having, being blamed for everything even if we were trying our hardest. I dont know how he still works here.

Please do not take this professor. His grading criteria is based on only three exams. He is extremely unprofessional and send the students emails late at night basically shifting the blame to them for not understanding the material even though I gave you everything to pass mentality. He is condescending in his announcements as well. Just beware.

All I can say is that he is incredibly rude to students and thinks he can get away with saying whatever he likes. The course material is hard and when A LOT of students reached out for help, he refused to take accountability for his part in the problem. He should not be a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is extremely not professional. He makes tons of number typos on his exam which doesn't make sense. Even though he makes typos, he requires students to be smart enough to catch it and blame those who couldn't solve it. Furthermore, he is overreacting to all the emails that students send and believes students are blaming him

Entire grade was based on 3 exams with only 10% extra credit for completing mastering chemistry assignments. He treated us students very disrespectfully, emailing us things such as "Thank you for adding considerable to the hell that students have put me through" and "Do not message me again." DO NOT TAKE CLASSES FROM THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is definitely one of those professors you should actively try to avoid, especially for an online class. He is condescending, blames the students for poor grades, and the homework takes 10+ hours/week if you want to stay caught up. Everything in this course is self-taught and too difficult (extremely low average grades on tests (50%) show this).

Owens is not a good professor. He did little to help students succeed and blamed poor grades on students. One announcement sent to us said you are taking a giant dump on your opportunities when referencing poor exam performance. He is not good at accommodating students. He is condescending, arrogant, and unprofessional in emails.

I took CHEM 1210 w/ him over the summer thinking he's tough but fair but this class was TERRIBLE. He did not care at all about his students (ex: he posted an extremely rude & unprofessional announcement at 10 pm scolding all of us after the exam average was too low). His videos are good but you'll need to spend 15+hr/wk to get a B (if you're lucky)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FULLY ONLINE. There are only 3 tests that go on your grade during the semester. The course is formatted very poorly and gives limited resources. Any time a student has reached out to him, we have gotten rude and unprofessional responses; no empathy. There have been enough of us that we have contacted the dean, to no avail.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Proff. Owens seems very proficient in the course material, and his video lectures do a good job of explaining the concepts, but the online course structure was terrible.

Professor Owens is probably one of the highest quality professors I've ever had in an online course. The material you need more than anything for this class mostly comes from his lecture videos which are pretty good and actually show you how the chemistry applies to fields like medicine. Grade is based on 3 exams, so be wary of that.

Don't get me wrong, Chem II is hard. Chemistry in general is a hard subject that takes a lot of practice. Yes, he grades off of 3 tests, but his assignments count for 10% extra credit. Each assignment is similar to the questions he uses on his tests. If you do the assignments, watch the lectures, and practice, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Owens is very hands-off when it comes to his sections, his lecture videos are fast, long, numerous, and his answer keys are vague. The sheer volume of information you are expected to retain is unprecedented. If you do not prioritize his course beyond all others you are taking , you will NOT receive a passing grade, let alone an "A".

This is my second time taking a class with professor Owens, I gave him the benefit of a doubt after my first course with him, but after this second course, I am in utter disbelief. He has made his tests nearly impossible to pass unless you spend more than 20+ hours on the course the week. DO NOT go to him expecting help or guidance.

Mr. Owens has an ego, is extremely condescending, literally shames his students for their mistakes or when they ask for help, takes no accountability, is not approachable; to name a few. He doesn't want students to succeed & it shows in the fact that final grades are solely based on exams (despite the fact that there is loads of homework). RUN!

does not really teach alot. only grade is exams and they were nothing like he said. homeworks not really graded and theres no actual lecture times just videos. to do well you have to teach yourself. this class made me rethink school. i would not take it online ever again. i have to retake the class in person.

Professor Owens is great at teaching and helping you learn. His online classes are very helpful as he gives you access to so many resources. If you communicate and are clearly going all of the homework assignments and putting in the time, he is very accommodating and understanding of mental health as well. His classes help lay a great foundation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was rough but Owens provides all the resources needed to do well. The textbook explained stuff really well and the learning center tutors were tons of help. But overall my mental health took a toll. Too much stress for one course.

I enjoyed my semester with Professor Owens. He is a teacher that cares about the success of his students. Our course was completely online and Professor Owens prepared pre-recorded 10-20 minute lectures for each chapter. This format allowed me to pause and take notes and rewatch lectures to study for exams.

Owens seems to be a polarizing; it's because he pushes you to actually learn and work. If you don't want to do the work for the class yet still want to pass, he's not the professor for you. If that's you, he cares about what you learn more than you do, quite frankly. I was looking to gain knowledge, and Owens' $spent to info learned ratio is ideal

Very difficult course. Grades are basically based off of 4 exams. So many mastering chemistry assignments, that do not relate to exams. TA's weren't helpful at all during the office hours. Would not recommended this course, fully online.

I took this class over the summer and it was completely online. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE. Greg is very difficult to reach and so were the TAs. The exams were heavily weighed on the grade and were graded very harshly. For each exam, the average was about 50%. Yes, grades get curved, but the exams are nearly impossible. Don't take this online.

Prof Owens is a really good guy. His lectures are interesting and he explains things well. Hard to get a super good gauge because it was totally asynchronous but he is very willing to work with students. He restructured the whole curriculum before this semester and cares about students learning the material.

I didn't end with a great grade (B-) in 1210. HW is usually due Monday, Wednesday, and Fridays, but Owens gives you all the resources to understand everything. There are some really helpful lecture videos, and the book explains concepts well. I worked 40+ hours this sem., but if you have the time and dedication you can certainly pass with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class was online for Spring 2021, not sure if the same class format will be used in the future but we did not have exams, which was an absolute life saver. There were weekly quizzes and homework which forces you to stay on top of the material. Don't go looking to Prof Owens for kind words of hope or simple questions- he will treat you poorly.

Overall was a fine class, although I didn't interact with him very much as it was an online class. The class wasn't very difficult, just assignments and quizzes, which we had 3 attempts on. My only complaint is that we can't see the right answer if we got a question wrong, even though the questions changed. I emailed him and he was helpful though.

My biggest complaint would be that the tests weren't always reflective of the homework from that week, but the TAs were more than happy to help if you were confused. When I took the class, there was homework due Mon/Wed/Fri and there was a weekly quiz. You had three attempts on the quiz and there was no final. Pretty easy class but it took effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cynical professor. He was rude in the emails and would accuse of not reading or watching videos if questions were present. The course was easy, took no time, and a monkey could pass. However, the professor was extremely unprofessional in his comments and openly degraded students for not understanding. Avoid him.

Super chill guy. Really uplifting during covid and cares about his students. Hes always there to help and is super clear and forward with what needs to be done. Tests are tricky if you dont study beforehand

Prof. Owens taught very well during COVID-19 in Fall 2020. We used Pearson's Mastering Chemistry which really helped solidify concepts into my head. Exams are a bit rough, and there's a weekly quiz, but it really wasn't as bad of a class as I thought. The last time I took chemistry was 3 years ago and I still did amazing. I recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online, so I had to use the textbook heavily. The quizzes and tests are similar to the homework but harder. There is no extra credit offered but he did curve the grades at the end. There are two homework assignments and a quiz every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Owens is a great teacher. I took Chemistry 1210 and 1220 from him online over the last two semesters. He posts lecture videos on canvas that are packed with information. At times I didn't need to read the textbook and instead spent time watching the videos which saved time. Very caring professor who is always willing to work with you.

I do the mastering reading and assignments and feel very up to pace, but as soon as I take an exam written by Owens I can barely get through a single problem. The probs on exams are NOT reflective of hw and are MUCH harder than anything we encounter prior to the exam. Feels as if he takes pride in his exams being too difficult for most ppl to pass.

Professor Owens' online course is organized and flexible. The tests are more difficult than the homework and lecture problems, but the prerecorded lectures and material available give you the resources you need to do well. For a self-guided, online class I don't think I could have asked for much better.

Incredibly difficulty class and not much interaction with the new class update of online class only. The tests did not at all reflect the homework, review sessions, or concepts taught in class. Instead of teaching the class the professor just threw everyone on huge twists to see everyone fail. The tests or any of the assignments are not curved.

Oh man, oh man. It is back-and-forth with Prof. Owens... I took two semesters of chemistry with him and both suffered the same downfalls but the second semester was far worse. He comes off as exceptionally arrogant and his tests don't reflect any of the homework material. It is as though he enjoys seeing his students suffer on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My favorite Professor of all time! He will work you hard and it is not an easy A, but if you care and put in actual effort he will notice you. Definitely have a zoom meeting with him because he is awesome to talk to and will really help you improve. Such a great guy! I took both Chem 1210 and 1220. Best decision ever made!

Took it a couple of semesters ago but the grade was based off only 3 tests, which were incredibly stressful and difficult. Optional homework for practice, and he seemed to be passionate, but the difficulty of the tests just weren't worth it.

He was an average chemistry teacher. While there wasn't a ton of mandatory homework, you had to do lots of optional homework if you wanted a good grade. The tests and quizzes are insanely difficult, but the homework itself isn't too bad. The tests and quizzes also hardly ever give you enough time or enough tries to get the correct answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Owens is, so far, one of my best professors. He is very thorough in his correspondence with students and he makes online learning feel warmer than you'd expect. He is very understanding and you can tell he has a passion for what he does.

Professor Owen's class is a two for one deal, sign up for chemistry and get radical liberal politics for free. He's very good at teaching the material, but it isn't at all worth the baggage of the class. Be very careful what you say around him because he's very touchy about people with wrong opinions.

Grade is only made up of 3 tests, but there is an optional final that can replace 1 of your test grades. The tests are so incredibly difficult. I studied a lot and did a lot of chem in high school but still didn't do great. Most of the class scored around 50%. The final is the one from ACS so it's a ton easier than his tests. Chem online is rough

Really great professor! Cares a lot about his students and their success. Beware of TOUGH tests... average always in 50-60%. He does curve and has a generous grading scale. Great class if youre not scared of tough tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class thinking Chemistry would be an easy (and interesting) fill for my math/science elective. While definitely interesting, I wouldn't take the class again unless it was required. Part of this was the difficulty. The exams were very difficult and most people got very low scores for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Owens is great! The class is somewhat difficult if you have a hard time managing your time, but if you really utilize the materials he provides, you have a pretty good chance of doing well. There are only 3 tests (and curves them pretty generously) and a final, but he drops the lowest exam or makes the final optional. Super smart & funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Owens straight up told my class he did not care if 95% of the class failed we would all receive F's on our transcripts. He refused to curve the test or the class ( you are only graded on 3 tests) and does not care how you do in his class. I was told if i didn't like this policy I should drop.... so thats exactly what i did.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took chem 1 with Owens and loved it, i got an A, but he has completely changed the way he "teaches"the course and in my opinion has given up. The whole class is graded on 3 test the average being 60%, he believes the problem is his students not studying and not his lack of teaching. He said if i don't like my grade then i should just withdraw.

Greg Owens is an outstanding professor and true educator. His passion for teaching is evident and he does all he can to set you up for success. It is uncommon to have a professor of this caliber more than once or twice in a college career. Take advantage, if you can. Brilliant guy. Chemistry is challenging, but taking Greg's course is worth it.

Owens seems to genuinely care about his students. He made the final optional and lets you make up missed exam questions for half credit. The course primarily uses ALEKS, which you'll end up spending around 6 hours a week on. The program is super frustrating at times though. Plan your time accordingly and you will do well. Best prof for gen chem.
I love Aleks the course was amazing and I never imagined I'd be able to get such a good grade in a chemistry course! He makes it easy to understand and interesting to learn!

Professor Owens outlook on learning chemistry is respectable. He is more focused on his students efforts towards learning the material, than he is on test grades. He lets you rework test questions missed for half credit. Just do the homework on time, and study for the test and you'll pass with a surprisingly good grade.

Online chem 1210, although there were a ton of quizzes on random days he gives 3 tries, i never got less than 100% on a quiz, and its ALEKS heavy. Each exam builds on eachother so if you do better on the second or third (final) exam, it replaces your worse score(s). Im taking chem 1220 with him next semester!

Professor Owens was pretty chill, as long as you can manage your time the class isn't that hard. A lot of people hate Aleks, but its not that bad if you can figure out the patterns you are golden, owens was always able to meet with me when i needed help and some of the ta's were great at helping to, best part was when he made the final optional!

NO TESTS! More like online quizzes which are exactly like the homework so if you do homework, then you'll ace the "tests". If you're taking this course online be aware of due dates because some homework assignments will creep up on you. The module quizzes are just like the lectures/videos so pay attention to those.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Taking this chemistry class online was my biggest mistake. I had a very high college GPA and this class just tanked it. He uses the ALEKS system so all homework and exams are through that. If youve ever used it before, you know how awful it is and if you havent, stay away from it at all costs. Only think not on ALEKS are quizzes random. DO NOT TAKE

The online class is easy, but Owens is rather rude and unprofessional if you make him take time out of his real life to ask questions. So if you take the class, just make sure that you dont have to interact with him and the experience will be 10x better.

Owens is uber intelligent & teaches at that level. I love his broad vocabulary and humor. His lecture videos are well-executed & helpful. His grading policy is unique & generous. As long as you can devote plenty of time, you'll do well. This course is challenging but prepares you well for 1210. You will grow as a student if you work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Summer. Owens uses ALEKS, which is a lot of work and requires students to look into the explanation tab a lot. Combined with his video lectures, we're looking at a lot of time spent on this one class. The videos aren't super useful but are required for the quiz. However messing up a bit on exams seems to be fine if you put in the work all along.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: As someone who also took Owen's 1210 class, 1220 is much, much harder. Owens changed the way the online classes work, and its clear he and the department are still working out how to do it effectively. This class demands work, lots of work, and the knowledge checks don't always seem fair, but your grade may be better than in a normal class here.

Owen is a professor who will make you work for it, but don't view that as a bad thing. He posts weekly videos (for the online class) and you have homework due weekly. The homework can be tedious because he uses a program called ALEKS which is super obnoxious. Make sure to ALWAYS watch the videos - quizzes are all based on the videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Owens is a solid Chem professor, and I wish I had the chance to meet him in person. He is informative and will answer any questions you have quickly. The only problem is the online platform that he uses for homework, ALEKS, is infuriating, and will make you want to punch your computer more than once. Oh, and we never had exams or a final!

If you're someone who doesn't have good time management skills, just don't. I don't and its just been constant stress this semester. He also isn't like super understanding. Probably just doesn't like me, but never gave me extension and I like have dyslexia and paperwork from the CDA. Good lectures though.

Greg has changed his class so that there are no tests. Sounds great right, wrong. First off he is not helpful, he will not meet with you in person for office hours, and you learn nothing from his videos. Finally, although you don't have tests, you have a final knowledge check which is an exam in the testing center that is worse than an actual test

With the way that the class is structured as an online-only class, Professor Owens gives you all the tools you need to succeed, and the rest is up to you. You work for your grade, and he provides resources for additional help and support to make sure you can do your best.

In my experience, it's extremely difficult to find a likable chemist. Greg Owens is a rare exception. Chemistry 1210 is the hardest class I've ever taken, but Owens is the best chem professor I've ever had. His lectures are the best I've encountered in an online course, he's funny, accessible, and seems to genuinely cares about student success.

Professor Owens is an amazing teacher and I would 10/10 take him again.I won't lie, it is a difficult class, and it was probably more difficult because I took it online, but Professor Owens is always willing to help if you message him. As long as you make sure you get the assignments done on time, and put effort in, he is more than fair with grades

Greg is a good teacher and I like the way his class is set up. I have done well in this class, but have a lot of chemistry background. I believe the tests in this class are unfair. They are extremely difficult and cover material beyond our course. He also does not curve. If the tests were toned down or curved, this would be an amazing class.

Dr Owens is by far the best professor I have had at the University of Utah, which should be saying something because I've never actually met him!! Chemistry is a hard subject but he prepares you well! The test are exactly like the homework problems and the homework problems are exactly like to example problems in the book! He's also hilarious!

I expected to teach myself the material for this class, seeing as it was online. However, Owens's videos were extremely helpful and I found myself not even needing to use the textbook. His tests are very straightforward and his expectations are clear. I would HIGHLY recommend this course to anyone who is looking for a competent chemistry professor.
The online videos were helpful but to fully understand the material you really need to read the textbook. He sometimes glazes over topics in the lecture videos.

Owens is a fantastic professor who knows what he's talking about and really gets the material across. He makes you work for your grade but you learn a lot by the end of the semester. Very clear in his expectations from the start. I highly recommend taking chemistry from him.

I took this class online, and although Chemistry is a hard subject for me, I felt like the lectures were very helpful. I suggest taking it online because then you can watch them whenever and replay the videos later if you need to. He was a great professor for a subject I hate.

Greg Owens is brilliant, and has created a great online version of chem 1 and 2. These classes are brutal, but you're learning chemistry, so buck up buttercup. Any low rating on here is from an angry student that gave up and needed to blame somebody else.. period. I'll take what Owens taught me through the rest of my life, and that's sayin somethin

I have loved the online Gen Chem 2 Course. I have still managed to learn from it, which I was worried about seeing as it was online. The lecture videos he does are great and some of them are even kind of funny. He includes questions to answer along the videos so that you know if you're understanding the material. I recommend the online course.

Stay away from Greg Owens. I'm currently in his online course and it's the worst class I've ever been in. lots of homework and the tests/quizzes are full of questions that are nothing like the material in lecture videos or homework. I used to love chem but I now hate it because of this course. No need to study, the test will be a surprise anyway.

Professor Owens changed my perspective on chemistry! He was the best professor I've ever had, by far. He cares about his students and actually wants you to succeed. The class material is tough, but he gives so many resources, it makes it easier to succeed. I felt like he got to know each student, which is rare in an online class. He's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I highly recommend his online chem 1210 class. Well organized online class, great lecture videos, not overbearing, and not hard to get an A as long as you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Owens was amazing at helping me out when i was failing this class somehow i managed to pass. He has weekly homework, quizzes, and lecture videos that are graded exams are really hard you need to know your stuff however everyone who's not taken it with him regret it because other professor are much harder he actually wants you to pass and succeed.

Owens is great. I had him for Gen Chem 2, and I took it online which was difficult, but so worth it. He had great video lectures, which had 1-10 questions embedded in them.  One of my favorite things was that he broke down the scores and sent a weekly email telling you what the average was on each assignment. Would definitely recommend him.

Owens was such a great professor. I had never taken a chemistry class up until this point, but the professor was so great and did an excellent job at relating the topics we learned in class to everyday life. He  is understanding and very helpful. I took it online and he did his lectures through videos. And he has a bit of a sense of humor
Best professor at the U!  Tough? ...sure.  But he's amazing!

I was extremely impressed with Professor Owens. He spent time teaching us the material clearly, then made it applicable through demonstrations and videos. He was very fair and always provided histograms after tests. I would recommend him to anyone.

Professor Owens knows a lot and is passionate about his teaching. He is a very fair about earning the grade you deserve. You definitely have to work for your grade, but he wants you to succeed and you will end up liking chemistry a lot more than you thought. I certainly never thought I could like Chemistry, but if anyone can do it, Dr. Owens can!

I HATE chemistry. But Professor Owens made me love it! He is engaging, caring, funny, and one of the most interesting people I've ever met. If you do the work and focus on the lectures, the grade will come. It's also nice that the final can make up for all horrible grades! What's more is Owens is really nice to look at, which spices up the lecture.

Professors like Dr. Owens are one in a million. Before I took the class, I *dreaded* it. Within a week, however, I'd fallen in love with chemistry.  Dr. Owens explains concepts clearly and simply. He's engaging, approachable, and has a great sense of humor. Plus, lectures almost always include some sort of (really interesting) demo!

Loved him. So hottttt! Apart from looks, he's very smart, and funny, and is very helpful to his students. Highly recommended, esp. if you like cute professors, lol. Be prepared to pay attention though!

He is an amazing teacher!! I suck at chemistry and his tests were the EASIEST THING ON THIS PLANET! People who struggled just never studied! My GPA in Highschool was a 2.8 PE student. And i got an A- in his class. And i never talked to the guy... I just did all the homework which is worth worth 70% of the grade.

This professor is my hero.  His class is hard, but he is a supportive and helpful teacher if you are willing to work.  I am not the best at chemistry, but he thought I could handle things I didn't have faith in myself for and encouraged me to do my best. He recommended me to be a TA, and I appreciate him so much for believing in me!

The tests are hard if you do not go to discussion, if you do go, the packets are pretty much exactly what will be on the test. I passed the class skipping all of the: discussions,homework problems and 1 of the tests. I do not understand how some people can say you should avoid him.
Owens is one of the better professors I've had. He clearly covers the material, effectively uses class time, and openly offers assistance.

He is a super helpful teacher. A lot of people complain about how hard he is, but it is chemistry, and it just doesn't come to you, you do have to study and follow the 2-3 hours of studying for each credit hour. I was VERY impressed by his teaching style and how approachable he was. His tests were difficult but not out of reach.

This isn't that hard if you put in some effort. He goes over everything you need to know in class, and be sure to do the worksheets given in discussion and understand them, then you should easily do well in the class.

This class was by far the most difficult class I have taken. However, I feel like I have learned SO much, and he really cared about everyone learning the material and doing their best. He was very clear about what was expected and taught us how to really learn. Tests were very challenging, but if you put in the work, you get a whole lot out of it.

Owens gives you all the tools you need to pass. But for people that have to work full time and have other things on top of school, this class might not be ideal. You HAVE to devote a lot of time to pass. I didn't do as well as I would have liked because I work full time and probably didn't study as much as I should have. But he knows his chemistry.

Nice guy, not open to feedback. He got disappointed in the class for what like 2 students posted about him on this website, so a lot of these comments were given on that exact day, so don't let all of those influence your decision in taking class from him. Extremely hard tests and it is hard to be prepared for them. I'd recommend someone else.

Pretty good guy, wants you to learn, but makes ridiculous tests ad tries to make them pretty difficult. Very smart, and sometimes show-offy about his intelligence. I thought he was good at explaining things simply though. Not very open minded to what other students think of his class, but he is pretty cool. I'd give him 8/10. We all have our flaws.

This guy is amazing. I've never had a professor care so much about his students.  He was very helpful and has tons of tools and resources to help you learn.  I would recommend him to anybody. And the demonstrations he does are very cool and give you a good understanding of what you are learning.

Owens is the perfect human being! He's so encouraging and supportive, not just about chemistry, but about life. There are no inane rules in this class (like having a textbook you don't use, not knowing when stuff is due, not knowing what's on the test, etc.) He's just so awesome he makes angels cry.

Professor Owens is indeed one of the greatest professor in the University. He is really helpful towards students. When questions are asked, he would explain it briefly and he would always ask if we have any questions. He makes a lot of changes such as adding more practice problems,he stop class lecture just to ask students what he can do to improve

Great Professor - inspiring and genuine.  His classes are interesting and extremely helpful.  His presentations definitely teach the concepts, allowing them to stay with you.  His tests ARE challenging. I appreciate that students actually have to put forth effort to achieve a good grade.  Grateful I took this course from him - enhances perspective.

I am at the University of Utah for my second degree and of all the professors I have had at both Universities, Owens has cared most about the success of his students. There are some many resources available to students of the class to practice, ask questions, and just get extra help. Owens is a top notch professor.

Amazing teacher! I took this class several years ago at a diff Univ and hated it.  Dr. Owens made it fun.  I went from dreadin chem to enjoying it.  The class itself is hard (what Chem isnt?) but he's thorough and explains very well. He also makes class fun.  He even took time out of his schedule to do a ?/ans session befor a test. Highly recommend

Contrary to some reviews, Dr. Owens is one of the most helpful professors I've had this year (im a freshman). I think the reason the ratings for this class are as low as they are is that a lot of students in this class are used to grades being handed to them, which is unrealistic in college. Besides, they can use the SI, homework, and office hours.

Owens is department chair in CHEM, but I honestly think he takes teaching even more seriously than chemistry. The guy gives us every kind of support if we want to learn, and if class is pretty challenging, it's also fun! I've had very few teachers that are better at teaching and more dedicated to helping students succeed. This guy is an A teacher.

Owens is a GREAT chem teacher. Chem is a hard subject that actually requires studying. In response to some of the negative comments below, these individuals probably dont complete the homework assignments, attend class, or try at all. This class isn't an "easy A". Owens actually wants you to learn chemistry and is great at helping you get there.

It really breaks my heart to see comments about him that are disappointingly rude. He's a professor that is truly dedicated to helping students learn, and in my opinion, if you try hard to learn, the good grade usually comes with it. If you don't get a desired grade, study harder. Nothings truly hard if you really try, right?

Professor Owens is a great teacher. He is very willing to help his students pass the class and he makes it challenging enough that you actually have to study the material. In class clicker questions help to make sure you understand what he is saying in class and the homework solidifies it. Tests can be difficult, but they ARE to judge what you know

This professor is very helpful and has a great class, it may not be the easiest class but there is no reason to fail or do poorly unless you do not even bother to try, attend and read and it is a great class!

This guy is a great teacher. He really knows his stuff. He uses a lot of different materials to teach including the clicker questions during lectures, online homework questions, the book, etc. Great professor. He doesn't make the class easy but isn't that the point? It's difficult enough to push you to truly learn the material. I recommend him.

He's a lean, mean, chemistry machine. He can be arrogant at times, but he always tells you how it is with less BS on the side. Exams are hard, but all the Q's are from the book.His lectures are really good and he does demos quite often.If you wish to learn chemistry take it from Owens, none of the other professors invest their time for us like him.
I agree with the comment posted below. Try to avoid him unless you want to fail at Chemistry. There are very few tools for success in this class.

I absolutely HATE this class. I would definitely try to avoid him if possible. He is also very arrogant and almost makes you feel stupid when you don't know something. tests are hard. and lectures do not cover anything that he tests on. He barely mentions the material that is on the tests so you don't learn it in lecture and must teach yourself.

I love this class! Owens is always available to give help and his lectures are interesting and he teaches the material very clearly. He gives you everything you need to know for tests and doesn't make keeping a good grade impossible. He's one of my favorite teachers!

Characteristic, funny individual, but barely covers important info in lectures. The quizzes and homework are incredibly challenging (took me a week to do 10 problems), and require for you to practically teach yourself. Testing on very involved info that was not covered in lecture is fairly bad style. Other than that, his courses are very reasonable

Very poor with regards to going over concepts or the basics which is a problem in Gen Chem I.  Glosses over all basics and rushes to advanced material which is hard to understand without basics. Got nothing from lecture, felt like taught myself the class, tests very hard. Too much time spent on unnecessary tangents(not all chem related )

Greg's amazing!  He's extremely intimidating, but he's really the nicest down to earth guy.  His class inspired me to change my major to chemistry.  His exams are hard but the knowledge you get from his class stays with you for years after.  Well worth the challenge.
Great lecturer. Hard tests.

He is a good professor. I just had a rough time with him. He actually ended up writing us a letter telling us he is quiting and that someone else was going to finish the last three weeks of class. He ended up staying but it was hard to respect someone who is so intelligent and actually likes what he does to do something like that.

Don't take Ernst! Owens is way better! His class is super hard, but totally worth it because you will walk out of it with a true knowledge of chemistry. Great lecturer, always interesting. You can't rely on the book or book exercises because he tests off his lectures, which are at a much higher level and of course harder coursework. Life-changing.

Owens is an excellent professor. I would say this class made me develop a love hate relationship with chemistry. Owens inspires me to learn it well so I study a lot for this class, but the tests will literally kick your *ss. So that is kind of discouraging. Still. And yes, yes he is very good looking.
Best lecturer that I have had. You will not fall asleep in his class. He does not use tricky multiple choice tests. Tests are hard but fair. Very hard class.
Good guy, but his tests are ridiculously hard. I suggest going to his office hours to get to know him and he will help you out a TON.

The best teacher I've had at the U. He's the kind of teacher who makes you a better student and person just from having taken his class. His dedication to what he does is really inspiring and encouraging. He's a really funny, really cool guy and he really inspired me to like chemistry a lot. I highly recomend taking his class.
His exams are hard but otherwise hes a good teacher

Best Teacher I have ever had at the University of Utah. If you have to take a chem. class try your hardest to get into owens class. You won't regret it! He's not easy but he's interesting and he actually teaches you. Wants you to succeed not fail. Tis wonderful!!
he is the best teacher of chemistry that i ever had!!!

Okay, so I think Dr. Owens really knows his stuff. He is a very intelligent man.  His biggest problem is that he is far too arrogant.  I have seen him act disrespectful to students, yet he demands respect because of his position.  His tests are really difficult and sometimes tricky.  He hasn't been at U of U long only a few years.  If his attitude
Awesome professor, intimidating, but he really knows his stuff and he keeps his lectures interesting.

His lecture style was really easy to follow and he had lecture notes posted on the internet which proved usefull. The tests are very difficult and require a high level of comprehension. He's a great teacher but his class requires a lot of independant study. Do the practice problems and you should be fine!
Best professor I have ever had.  Work hard and you will learn chemistry very well with Owens.   He is totally willing to help you out outside of class as well.
His lectures were very informative and his side comments were fun too. His exams are very challenging so just study hard and you'll do fine. He's very willing to answer questions for you also.
Has been my favorite prof in college so far.
kind of arrogant and not very friendly at all, but funny none the less. hard class

Owens is probably the best chemistry teacher currently out there.  He really wants you to understand the material and will actually go the extra mile with you one on one until you get it.  You definetly have  to work hard, but Owens will make it worth your while if you do.

He is a great Professor that wants his students to succeed in his class and in life. He is really helpful one on one.

owens basically only cares about himself. he is pretty good at giving lectures, but he finds every way possible to give you the worst grade possible. he will tell us things that we will for sure have to know for the test, and come test time, none of will be there. his tests are rediculous.
VERY difficult class.  Exams were next to impossible.  Nice guy with a sense of humor.

Owens motivates you by failing you on just about every exam.  The emphasis isn't on learning... it's on passing the class. No matter how hard you study you'll still fail. He's one of the better Chem teachers here... if that tells you anything.

Great teacher. Lectures are very fun and interesting to go to. He loves this stuff, and you can tell it by the amount of prep he puts into the class. His tests are very tough, and require more prep than any other class, but at the end of the semester he finds a way to help out his students make up for the difficulty. Highly recommended teahcer.
No Comments

Owens is one of those professors that actually cares about his students learning the material. Chemistry is tough, but he has a way of explaining it so that it can actually be understood!  I thought the lectures were very helpful, I wouldn't skip them, he even gave extra credit once for being in class, so go!  He is a good guy, great professor!

Professor Owens works his ass off to make sure every one of his many, many students has the opportunity to do well in his class and learn Chemistry inside and out. One of the most awesome things about his class is the way he motivates his students.
Awesome teacher, makes it easy to understand chemistry, plus he makes class fun, is very willing to help outside of class, awesome!
Very funny and concise. Test questions are very fair; they could be far more difficult. He also provides practice tests and as long as you do all the exercises you should be golden.

Owens is a great professor. Although the class is very hard (I took AP Chem in high school, and I struggle with it). He explains things very clearly and is always very friendly and willing to help in any way he can. Very fair dude.
owens is a great professor, gen chem 2, 1220, is a hard class but he is willing to help you out and make sure you understand it. he has an amazing attitude and is a great guy.
Great teacher and nice to look at.  Almost made me switch to chemistry.  Includes a good amount of physics in his presentation of general chem.
Not an easy course but he explains things really well... and then explains them again if you don't get it. Plus the guy's just cool.
I had AP chem in Highschool so his class is easy, but Owens still does a great job at explaining chemistry. He is Freakin awesome

probably the best prof i've ever had.  his class is way tough, but he is always willing to help you. his lectures are amazing cause he actually teaches the material during them and he holds his own review sessions before tests (instead of having a TA do it
freakin amazing teacher!!

although i barely passed owens' class, i appreciate all the time he spent helping me when i asked for it.  i decided that if you put the time into the course, the material is presented well enough that you can recieve a fairly high grade.
He is a good teacher but very sarcastic in a funny way, PS dont ever have a phone on during a test
No Comments
owens is amazing. no way did i think chemistry would be interesting until i started his class. he definitally knows what he's talking about and is a funny funny guy!
Probably the best professor at the U.  ALWAYS willing to help out and answer questions and hold extra review sessions.  Wants you to love chemistry as much as he does and understand it.

Very challenging and tough but all his notes really help and prepare u to take the next step in chem. for good. He's not definitely what u expect from old school, great sense of humor, interested in things other than chem. like sports and etc. great guy!
No Comments

VERY hard class, definatly not the class one would take to boost their GPA.  If you want to learn general chemistry and you are willing to put in the time, Owens is the teacher for you.  He cares a lot about his students and enjoys teaching a lot.
By far the best chemistry prof at u of u.
Excellent.
Dr. Owens truly cares about the success of his students.  The material and tests are difficult, but not impossible.  One can tell that he enjoys teaching.

The best chemistry professor at the U.  If you want to learn a good foundation for the rest of your classes, then make sure you get him.  Knew how to explain things very well, and made the class challenging.
he's willing to stay all night to help, as well as always willing to help.  sticks to his notes, if you keep up you'll be fine.  solid professor.

he explains things very well, I enjoyed his class very much.

Professor Owens had a good sense of humor as long as he was the one telling the jokes.  In the two years I've attended the University I've never met someone so cocky and full of themself.  Very unhelpful.
Dr. Owens is incredibly easy to learn from. Previously difficult subjects are simply and clearly explained. And, he is never to busy to see a student.

I wasn't a fan. If you need to take a class from them I would see if it is taught by a different teacher. Old school teaching style.

Professor Hoff is one of the best professors I have ever had. He cares so much about history and the content that he is teaching. reviews.comment: Derek Hoff first off was one of the worst professors I have ever had in my entire life. This guys straight up sucks. Talk about reading and test. He assigns an unrealistic amount of reading which needs be done in 2 days not to mention when I reached out saying I do not understand he demoralized me over email and on class. STAY AWAY! F THIS GUY!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take from Professor Hoff. He is very unreasonable and is hard to get in contact with. He expects first-year college students to be writing at the same level as someone who is in their Master's degree. His lectures are often long and have little to no direction/offer no help to the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff is a great professor. But, this class is tough. He expects crazy writing skills and it is almost impossible to get a 100 on an assignment. The worst part of this class is that the tests (every 3 weeks) open Saturday morning and close Sunday night. Be ready to. write A LOT. Hoff knows a lot but can be condescending on grading comments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: guy CARES about citing, punctuation, and grammar. he has millions of rules, his syllabus is literally 23 pgs. interesting material, but the readings are beyond boring. i'm a good student and writer when i try, but i only got 100 on ONE ASSIGNMENT. he's intimidating at first, but don't let him scare you, or don't take the class from him. good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you're going to complain about having to work hard in college, if you refuse to follow the citation and grammar guidelines Hoff clearly lays out, or if you can't take sometimes being wrong. The class is difficult, but interesting. Hoff's lectures are complicated, and not always clear, but he and the TAs will always help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. He is the worst professor I have EVER had. There are weekly essays that need to be about 1,300 words. He does not give you the prompt or open the assignment until SATURDAY and then it is due SUNDAY NIGHT. Literally so horrible, he did this even on Halloween weekend. I am a good writer and a good student, and I struggled. HATE.

Quite possibly the worst professor I've ever had. This was a business class, but the material makes it feel more like philosophy. And he grades like it's an English or writing class. Have no idea what the material was supposed to actually teach. Do not take this professor for any class, your gpa will suffer. Refuses to give anyone 100% on anything.
Hes a pretty difficult teacher but if you read the textbook and work hard youll do well as long as you dont use first person point of view in your essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff has by far been the worst professor I have encountered and taken a course from. He cares more about grammar and punctuation rather than the actual material of the class. Although, feedback is needed when attending class, RUDE and STANDOFFISH criticism is unnecessarily. The comments made it feel personal. DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE!!

Terrible Professor, cares more about some outlandish grammar and punctuation style than making sure you understand the material of the course that's supposed to be taught. And don't write any papers using your own words, you get docked points for thinking on your own. Make sure you just repeat what others have said and cite sources in obscure way.

Very rude and standoffish. Would give bad grades, but would not explain why. Has a citation style I have never seen. I would cite in the correct MLA or Chicago style, but would deduct points because it wasnt in his special style.

Everything that is said about Professor Hoff is at least mostly true. However, I believe he just appears arrogant to try to start a debate in his class. No matter what your view point is, he will challenge you and I love that about his class. He is a very tough grader, but if you go to office hours with him he'll usually bump your score up a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff was intense, but in the best possible way. You can truly tell that he wants you to improve and better your analysis and writing skills. As a professor, he is extremely discussion based in class and encourages you to be wrong in order to understand better. It is a challenge, but if you want to improve, I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ive never worked so hard for a B. Professor Hoff cares more about proving how much he knows than your success. You get the feeling that he finds joy in putting you down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: We had a test every 3 weeks. Hoff posts the tests less than 24 hours before they're due and takes off 5 points a day every day you don't have it turned it with NO EXCEPTIONS. The tests are to write 3 short essays about 3 topics. He posted his last test today and all my finals are tomorrow. Asked for an extension because of this and was denied.

Derek Hoff is wish washy at best. Assignments that I should have been getting better grades for weren't given comments for grades. He doesn't feel concise or give helpful feedback at times. It does not feel like he wants you to improve in your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I wanted to switch to a different professor at first. I could tell it would be hard and he comes off pretty intimidating at first. One I got into it I really loved it. It was my favorite class so far. I loved the readings and discussions. It was my hardest class so far as well but the one i put the most effort into. I got an A. I loved the topic

Professor is very knowledgeable, but can be quite haughty and won't accept defeat, even though he may be wrong. Participation is optional, but he'll use it to round your grade up or down if your grade is on the fence. There's a TON of reading; I spent 5 hrs the days before class combing through the readings. Make sure you understand them very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff is often hated because he's just a smart-ass. He likes to brag how much he knows on the subject, but that doesn't mean he's a bad teacher. Just show up to lectures, try and do the reading. My personal tip is just to look up on google "READING QUIZLET". Most of the reading has already been made into flashcards, so read those. GL
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff is a very knowledgeable and respectable professor. He always makes it a point to best engage the class with the material, whether that be through the "professor's shots" or in-depth class discussions. I highly recommend going into his office hours, as this is a tough class and requires much reading and effort to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is hard for no reason. I feel like I'm questioned more about what I know rather than being taught. He likes to challenge any answer a student gives him which leads to more confusion than clarification. I have learned more in the TA reviews than sitting in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes actually really funny. Just soooo much reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Hoff is an amazing professor. I had absolutely 0 interest in business when I first started, but his lectures are so intriguing and he interacts with the students and adds some humor into his lectures. Lots of reading but it is beneficial to class and helps you do well on the tests. 10/10 would recommend him!!
The class had a LOT of reading, and Hoff was not very clear on what was expected and what we were graded on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awful teacher. Reading are boring and hard to understand. Goes on tangents that have nothing to do with the assigned work. Quizzes are easy but you get to the midterms and you fail. Drop this class and get a different teacher ASAP. ANY teacher is better

This class has a lot of reading, with lots of it being very difficult and long reading. He gives a quiz at least once a week on the readings, but as they are only 4-5 questions long you will be fine as long as you read. Participation in class is expected and graded. He gives 3 tests all of which are short answer comparing themes you find in the hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall Professor Hoff is someone you either love or hate. He can have a very arrogant and condescending personality, but his teaching of the course content is top tier. You will learn something from his class and he truly makes you think about the ideas you write about. If you can handle his off-putting attitude then take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff is a hard but good and knowledgeable teacher. Attendance every day isn't technically mandatory but he does give out pop quizzes often. Regardless, if you do the readings and pay attention in the lectures you will do fine. I would recommend taking foundations of business with Hoff.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I was worried to take BUS 1051 from Hoff upon reading poor reviews, but he was a really good professor. If you show up to class, and especially do the readings, the tests and essays are fair. He had a really annoying group essay assignment, but other than that the assignments were fine. He really knows his stuff and I would recommend his BUS 1051.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Hoff loves to play the arrogant card to provoke people into discussion, but it can actually be fun to argue with him. Remember to question the things he says, take very detailed lecture notes, and don't let him shove opinions down your throat. Lots of reading, lots of pop quizzes, but nothing that can't be handled if you stay up to date on work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff -- a true professor -- challenges your ideas no matter how smart you think you are. Yes, he is direct and sometimes arrogant, yet there is a great deal of value in how he teaches the class. Professor Hoff likes to focus on the big picture, and ask questions that we never consider in our free time. Be prepared to discuss readings!
Did not like him as a professor, full of himself and only right answer is his opinion. Doesn't post lecture guides and dicussions are hard to follow.

This class requires a fair amount of time and reading to pass. Tests are all done in short answer format, but aren't too difficult if you read the material and studied. Hates cell phones, don't bring them to class. Won't post lecture notes online, so if you need clarification on the readings, you have to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Theres only one answer that is correct and its the one that aligns with his personal views. He is very full of himself and teaches this class to hear himself speak. The questions on his quizzes have nothing to do with the reading, yet you are expected to know the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Smart person but not cut out to be a professor. Loves to hear himself talk more than have discussions and be around students. Doesn't seem to be willing to answer questions in a constructive way and all grades are based on essays that he grades very harshly.

I really enjoyed Professor Hoff's class. He made you really think about business in lots of different ways. He occasionally argued the other side in order to have us think critically. I learned a lot about business, critical thinking, and the world in general. The class is a little challenging. I would definitely recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Would take again

reviews.comment: Hoff was a tough professor but did a good job engaging everyone in his lessons. Would not always give good feed back on the tests. Over all I liked the class but there was a lot of reading, much of which was irrelevant on tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Hoff has a strong personality, so if your a snowflake who likes to be in their own bubble, do not take this class. He does cut you off as other people said but it's not in a mean way and he is usually just playing devil's advocate. That being said, would not take him again based on his middle school phone policy alone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hoff is a very good professor, especially when it comes to lectures. I found them to be very enriching and thought-provoking, but this class requires a lot of engagement to do well in. If you do the readings, you'll do fine in this class as quizzes and tests aren't too difficult. Grading on the 2 semester essays kind of killed my grade in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pretty good teacher. Lecture Heavy. Quizzes in class so attendance is almost mandatory. Two papers and three tests. Tough grader for writing. His tests are a lot easier than the other professors; short writings as opposed to 50, in-depth, multiple choice questions. Do the reading and you'll do fine. Cuts you off while talking, get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Honestly really enjoy Professor Hoff's class. At the beginning of the semester I felt like most of the other students that have rated him poorly on here, but then I checked my ego and tried a little harder and the class became enjoyable. I went in to make up a quiz and instead of just giving me the quiz he went over the readings with me personally

I wish I would have read up on Hoff's ratings before taking the course. Hoff is extremely full of himself. He acts like he wants to hear your opinion but once you speak he makes you feel stupid. If he disagrees with you he will just move on like you haven't spoken. His lectures are very scattered and hard to make sense of. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Full of himself but the class isn't too hard as long as you take good notes. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS

reviews.comment: Although he's very smart and definitely knows his history... he's very condescending and almost comes off as rude. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hoff is really passionate about what he teaches, and challenges his students on very controversial topics which makes the class more engaging. Hoff is very organized and specific of what he wants you to know for the material and tests. This is a class where your grade only depends on tests. You should take solid notes. Lots of reading but managable

Attendance is not mandatory, but It is important you show up and actually listen because you could be missing a lot of information that could be on the test (he does not put power points online). Your grade depends on 3 exams (they aren't easy questions unless you took good notes and learned the material).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: very bad at leading discussions. includes a lot of unnecessary materials in his lectures and self promotes his books. Don't take his class.

In this class, your entire grade is based off of three tests.  I have always struggled with tests in general, so this class was extremely stressful for me.  He sends out his powerpoint topics for study help but that's all.  Just found myself very frustrated with this class overall.

Only homework is reading. Exam 1 is 30% of your grade, exam 2 is 35%, and the final is 35%. They're essay exams and you won't know the questions until the day of. Lectures were very difficult to follow (quick-paced and a little jumpy). Honestly, I never read and only crammed for the exams the night before. Aced them by luck. Intolerant of phones.

I could understand maybe half of what Prof Hoff was saying. The Exams are not too hard you just really need to study and write out your outlines before taking the test (answering essay questions). I haven't gotten my grade yet but I probably got a C or something. So you will pass but its tough.

Don't be intimidated on the first day.  He is way smart and knows history.  You will get better grades if you sit in front and participate.  Don't be afraid to chime in and ask questions, he will answer them!  He will teach you to look at business history in a scholar way and you WILL become smarter after finishing this course! Make sure you read!

I would never take another class from Professor Hoff. While he is clearly very knowledgeable, he is incompetent at teaching. He reads straight from his notes and doesn't personally engage the subject. When students give incorrect answers to his questions he moves on instead of teaching. Very condescending and seems to be in love with himself.

Im studying history for my major & after taking a class from Mr. Hoff, I honestly debated changing it.  From the textbook, to his lecture-style class, to his humor, everything was DRY. Hoff wasnt engaging in his lectures & came off extremely condescending. The only learning I did was through the textbook; Hoff assigned a chapter a night (20+ pages)
he talks about random stuff in class and makes you read to learn

I wanted to like holly and this class but i just didnt. Shes a fine teacher, and a lot of the TA's are helpful, but her exams are so hard. She puts questions that are meant to trick you, which is the worst kind of test. She gives a lot of EC which is nice but i would prefer a class that actually tested my knowledge instead of " twisty mechanisms".

I have had Holly for both Ochem 1 and 2. I can confidently say that she is the best professor I have ever had. Ochem is a very hard course, but she makes the material very enjoyable and digestible. She also has great TAs who try their best to make sure you understand the content. You can tell Holly loves teaching, as well as her TAs.

Holly is the best OChem professor. She knows she teaches a difficult subject but she also makes it possible for students to succeed. She's passionate about what she studies and lectures on, and it comes through in the way she teaches it. Holly's brilliant and really cares about the students she teaches. Her good reputation is extremely deserved.

Holly is an amazing professor who is very passionate about organic chemistry. It's a difficult subject, and the class and exams can be hard, but she gives lots of opportunities for practice and extra credit.
RUN WHILE YOU CAN. This is by far one of the worst professors I have ever had. She makes ochem unbearable and her exams do not align properly with class material. Do not take her.

Holly is an amazing person who cares about your success in OChem. Lectures are very helpful. There is an outstanding group of TAs to support you. Exams are hard, but not misleading and manageable to study for. About 3% of your grade is available in extra credit, which helps.

I love Holly. She's genuinely the best professor I have ever had. She made the class super enjoyable and made me fall in love with ochem. Im looking forward to ochem 2 with her. I'd recommend her to anyone who gets the chance to take ochem with her.

O Chem with Holly was a good overall experience and I enjoyed the lecture topics, and her teaching style. Even though I enjoyed her class, it was hard. O-Chem is inherently a challenging subject, but Holly made it digestible. I kept an A throughout most of the semester, but it got away from me for both the 3rd and Final exams, I could not keep up.
She makes her class very memorization heavy. Applying the concepts are not important to her. By far one of the worst teachers I've ever had.

I don't even know where to start except don't take her class. She does not curve exams (average on one of the exams was 60). She also grades so strict you could lose 3 points for something you didn't even think you could lose points on. Do not take ochem with Holly.
Best teacher at the U hands down. OChem is hard, but Holly is awesome and the TAs for this class are super helpful and there are a ton of them.

She means well but her grading is widely strict. She cares about very specific things on tests but will ignore many other important questions. While I succeeded in her class I had to work hard and spent a lot of time memorizing. She made the class much more difficult than it needed to be. Never take a class from her if you can.

I took both OChem 1 & 2 from Holly, she is the best of the best. Her class is inherently challenging but she gives you all the tools you need to succeed. She likes to throw curveballs on exams but I truly believe she loves her students and is exhausting all her efforts to prepare them for grad programs and successful careers. Take a class from her!

TAKE THIS CLASS! One of the best chem teachers ever - She changed my life. Textbook optional, but helpful (and online...). Get help from the TAs, and really try to understand your mistakes! The material is hard, and Holly breaks it down really well, but you cannot do well in this course if you do not practice and study. Homework is extra credit.

Holly is the greatest teacher I've ever had. Her class is set up flawlessly, and there is ample support for this notoriously tough class. Tons of extra credit, and she is willing to help you in every way. She restored my faith in myself academically after a tough year in gen chem. Tip: make use of the TAs. They are amazing and there to help.

Great teacher, extremely passionate about her work, and cares deeply for the students. The class is obviously very intensive in terms of workload and studying, but she has made the process very streamlined and efficient.

Holly is an amazing professor. I was terrified to take Organic Chemistry but she made the class go smooth. She really knows how to break down difficult concepts and build off of previous information. I appreciated the extra credit opportunities and test drops because it allows room for some failures without destroying your grade.
Holly restored my faith in professors at the University of Utah. I wish every class was taught by a Holly Sebahar!

Holly is a nuanced person: cool, professional, and kind. Beneath this facade is a brilliant, ruthless woman, who righteously expects excellence. 
To me, Holly was very accommodating; I think she might have thought I was mentally disabled. Her lectures are organised, but her style of teaching ochem didn't align with my way of thinking well.
Professor Sebahar makes ochem fun and manageable. She genuinely cares about students' success. With hard work and resources like Unstuck ai, you can do well in her class.

Ochem is not so much hard as it is memorization. Its like learning 4d chess. Holly does go over everything in lecture at least once, She does reiterate a lot of the things that are important. It really is up to you. She loves her job and it shows. Several times throughout the semester it felt overwhelming with what we needed to memorize.

Holly assigns a lot of work - you're expected to complete a quiz, a homework assignment, and textbook readings nearly every week - but it's useful and helps you understand the material better. Plus, she explains difficult ochem concepts well and genuinely cares about her students' success - she and her excellent TAs make ochem doable!

OChem is a tough class. Holly is an incredible teacher who knows the material well and knows how to teach it in a way that students understand it. She's easy to talk to and gives good feedback, and you can tell she really cares about her students.

Holly is by far the best professor i have every had. She cares about her students and actually sets you up to succeed. Ochem 2 was definitely difficult, but holly and her amazing TAs made it possible. Take ochem 2 with Holly! She is the best :)

I cannot say enough amazing things about Holly. Yes, OChem is hard, and I can't say that I necessarily succeeded in it as many of my peers did. However, Holly is genuinely the best professor at this University. She gives you ample resources and tells you how to study for her exams. Not only that, she deeply cares about her students.

Terrible, don't take this course with Holly, exam are unfair because her questions are designed to trick you. It doesn't matter how much time you spend studying you have 50 minutes on the exam to solve all her riddles. Graders are merciless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Holly and Ochem is what made me like school again. Thank you so much for such a great Ochem 1 semester and showing me I can do hard things! Take from her and you will never regret it!

I had to retake this class after taking it with Ming Lee Tang (do not recommend), but Holly was amazing. She actually explains and cares. Don't get me wrong, it's a hard class, but she makes it as easy as it can be. She's so enthusiastic and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. I'm already registered to take ochem 2 with her next semester :)

Holly is an absolute blessing. This was my second time taking ochem as I am also a transfer student. She makes it known that she wants you to succeed, which I believe to be half the battle. Put in the work, come to class, and don't fall behind and you will do well. Take ochem with Holly!!!

Holly is a really nice and caring person. Her pep talks were the best. To anyone taking the class, I would say you need to be ready to put the work in and make sure you ask questions. My biggest complaint would be that the end of the semester was VERY rushed and we had to teach ourself very difficult concepts.
Holly is the most AMAZING professor. I was terrified to take OCHEM, but she made it such an awesome experience.

I started to dislike chemistry before taking OChem with Holly, her class made me enjoy it again. One of the best professors I've had at the U. Tons of extra credit available which is lovely, and removes the stereotype that OChem is just "one of those classes that is hard to do well in". If you try to succeed in Holly's class, you likely will.

It is obvious that Professor Sebahar cares about you, and the course seems to have been set up for success. 

Extra credit opportunities do exist. 

Easy to know what the exams or quizzes will be like, as there are practice ones provided that are very similar.

I love Holly! One of the only professors I believe that actually love to teach. She always explains everything down to the bone and makes O Chem not so bad! Make sure you put time in your week to study because it can be confusing! TA's are amazing help and there are so many help sessions. Duscussions are meaningful and very helpful.

Holly is the best professor I have had during my time at the U. Her lectures are clear and she doesn't present the material in an overly complicated way like lots of STEM professors typically enjoy doing. You will not pass this class if you don't put in effort, but she has dozens of TAs and plenty of other resources to help you succeed.

Holly is seriously the best professor the chemistry department has to offer at the U. She wants all of her students to succeed and feel confident taking ochem. I've never felt more prepared for an exam; extra credit homework problems, pdq problems, old exams, discussion worksheets, old quizzes, saturday review, and more. Take ochem 2 with Holly!

Sebahar is a great teacher. She has many TA's who are very helpful and host many events outside of class to help students learn. Holly is a fun and understanding person, her lectures are great, and she gives out a lot of extra credit if you put in a little extra work. While Ochem can be a difficult course for some, the grading and tests are fair.
Very caring, great a lecturing, and receptive to feed back. Work hard, do the homework, extra credit and you will be fine.

Holly is an excellent lecturer who cares about student success and provides the resources to do so. The material can be challenging at times but she always makes her expectations very clear and creates a great learning environment with the help of her army of TA's.

Get ready to replace the Oxygen you breathe with Ochem because you are gonna be occupiedddd with this class. Holy is an amazing professor, funny, caring, and passionate. She is the best professor to take OChem with but be prepared to practice a ton outside of class. AND USE her TAs. There are over 50 of them!!!

Professor Sebahar is one of the best professors you could take as an undergrad at the U. She's clearly very passionate about the content she teaches. Orgo is a notoriously difficult class, but if you can put in the effort you will be ready for all of her quiz/exams (~64% of our final grade). Each homework assignment is worth extra credit.

Professor Sebahar is an angel in disguise. She cares about her students and she is so passionate about what she teaches which make lectures easier. The course load is rigorous but she gives you every opportunity to succeed. All homework is extra credit and the 50+ TAs host office hours frequently. Do not take OChem from anyone other than Holly!

Professor Sebahar is fair, kind, and an entertaining lecturer. She lays down clear expectations for grading and exams, and provides a vast array of resources for students to use to succeed. She makes organic chemistry fun and approachable, and truly seems as though she wants her students to succeed!

Holly is an amazing professor! She truly cares about her students and wants them to be successful! She provides so many resources to help you do your best in her class! I took ochem 1 and 2 with her and she was the best teacher I could have had for those classes. I enjoyed learning in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sebahar is the reason I decided to major in chemistry. She is incredibly kind and more than willing to work with students. Her teaching method is refined and oriented to help students actually learn organic chemistry, not punish them for being unknowledgeable.

Holly is probably the best professor I'll ever have at the U. She is extremely caring, personable, and knows so much about organic chemistry.
