She is extremely accommodating and wants so badly for all of her students to succeed and see the beauty of ochem. 11/10 would recommend her class. Her TAs are so helpful. Hard but doable if you put work in

Amazing class!  I took it on a whim to get a break from my Art history classes and ended up falling in love with O chem!  Changed my major to chemistry because of this class!  Pre med kids always complain O chem is so hard but its not that bad!

Dr. Sebahar hands down is the most caring professor I have ever had. She is always willing to work with you and her army of TAs provide countless office hours to get any and all questions answered. I took 17 credits and still managed to do well thanks to her student success attitude. Amazing teacher, amazing class.

Holly is an amazing professor who really does care about each of her students. All of the homework assignments are extra credit. I did mediocre on the exams, but ended with an A because of all the extra credit that I got. Exams aren't too hard, especially since she gives you practice exams that are formatted almost identically to the exam.

Holly is simply the best Ochem professor you can get. She has extra credit and doesnt throw curveballs on tests. She always had exam scores given back a day after the exam. She is caring and kind and has some cool TAs too. Be sure to find a good study group because I met some of my best friends in this class!
Holly is easily the best professor Ive ever had. She cares about all her students and will help in any way to get you to succeed. She makes a hard subject reasonable. Amazing teacher.

AMAZING TAKE W/HER. Ochem wasn't hard for me but Holly just made class so motivating and fun. Gave you so much room to mess up and recover (AKA THE EXTRA CREDIT). I have never loved a class so much. Does require at least 10hr/wk like she says so make the time or take this another semester. So many TA all different but all great in their own way!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Holly is by far the best professor Ive had at the U, and her *literal* army of TAs are incredible. She is super easy to talk to, and always gives good feedback, or good suggestions how to study better. I attended almost every lecture, but I had friends who came to a lot fewer and they did much worse in the class. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, it will help
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She has one of the largest bodies of undergraduate TAs at the U. There is so much help in her class and she makes herself as available as possible to students needing extra help. You will not do well if you don't go to lecture. Her class is not homework heavy. OChem is difficult. You will spend 10 hours/week outside of lecture studying to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Holly has an incredible support system of TAs and offers scheduling for one-on-one instruction if needed. She is very understanding and accommodating. She cares about her students and their success, and puts in the time and effort to make that happen. O chem is a very difficult class for many, but if you follow Holly's suggestions, you'll do well.

Professor Sebahar was one of, if not the best professors I have had the opportunity of being taught from at the U. She and her team of TAs make the class experience so supportive in a subject that can seem very daunting going in. No matter how good a prof. is, OCHEM is gonna be hard, but she truly believes in every student's ability to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Anyone who gives Dr. Sebahar a bad rating is someone who didn't try. She gives SO MUCH extra credit. If you pay attention in class, go and do the PDQ's and PS, YOU WILL GET AN A! She cares so much about her students and TA's, her lectures are fun and interactive. Best ochem professor at the U.

Took ochem1 got a B-, had rough patch in life. In ochem2 can't get a bit of help from Holly or TA's. Spent easily 300$+ on personal tutors. Answers are class specific (no google). Getting a B- she said I should rethink med school cuz I'm sturggling. She treats this as a 20 credit hour class, be warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Holly is the best chemistry professor (or any subject for that matter) that I have ever had. I have never felt more cared for by a teacher and her supporting cast of TA's than in Holly's class. It is not an easy subject but the number of resources she provides is unmatched. She made learning online (quarantine) easier than ever. Take her class!

Went from a B in Ochem 1 to A in Ochem 2. Holly is very understanding of life circumstances and has a charismatic personality. She want's everyone to succeed and does everything she can to accommodate to students' needs. She's the reason why most students in the class get A/A-. Made learning ochem stress-free.
Very good at explaining what you need to know simply and easily. She is accessible outside of class which makes a big difference with everything being online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVED Professor Sebahar. One of the greatest professors I have ever had. The only issue I have with is class is that it is a flipped course. Meaning that you teach yourself 1/2 of the stuff you need to know. Only reason I got the grade I got is because of the textbook. If this class was not flipped It would have been my favorite class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best chemistry professor I have had. Gives fantastic explanations of why things happen and encourages problem solving rather than memorization. Tons of resources and TA's allow anyone who puts the work in to succeed in this course. I feel she makes what could be a challenging class completely manageable.
I loved Holly's class. She is an incredible teacher and her class is great, but only if a flipped learning environment is your thing. I would much rather this class be a 2 hour class

Most amazing professor I've ever had. She really cares about her students and is passionate about organic chemistry. Course work is intense, PDQ, discussion sheets, long and really difficult exams, lot's of hw, but little in the way of memorization, and more towards the WHY - fundamental understanding. She's the reason I absolute LOVE ochem
Pretty much everything positive about her has already been said on here. Believe the hype. She is that good.

Holly was an amazing professor for OChem 1 and 2, I did well in both. Her class is not easy, it may be one of the hardest organic chemistry classes, but she gives you all of the resources you need to do well. I failed a test my first semester and still managed an A-, lots of extra credit opportunities. Take advantage of TA's and her office hours!

Love, love, love her! She's one of the few professors that actually cares about having her students succeed! The class is challenging, but if you do the work and ask lots (lots!) of questions, you'll be fine :)

Go to class to do the tophat questions. Do the smith homework weekly for extra credit. Read the textbook before class. Utilize tutoring center for PDQs. Go to SI sessions for practice exams. Usually offers extra credit for exam corrections. Never went to office hours, but heard it's helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Sebahar is one of the better professors you can have for o-chem, albeit the most challenging. She is very engaged in your learning but will pile the work on you to ensure you understand it. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on the class but, again, you will walk away with a great understanding. The tests, however, are advanced.

Do not take O chem 2 lab with Holly! You will end up hating your entire semester, and spend more time studying for lab than the actual class. I took o chem 2 with a different professor and got an A, but had Holly for lab and it was horrible. The post labs are brutal, the TAs didn't help much. Way too much work and time for a 2 credit lab.

Holly has the right idea for teaching a class, but makes it harder than is required to learn the subject. Her tests are generally unfair and tricky. She also requires some memorization that is not translatable to real life job use. Busy work is common, I suggest taking it from Rainier.

Do yourself a favor and take ochem from Holly. She is such an amazing, passionate, and caring teacher who genuinely wants all her students to succeed  even beyond academics. Her class isnt easy, it requires doing PDQs, discussion worksheets, homework problems and more, but its worth it. Take this class from Dr. Sebahar!

Holly is incredible. Her lectures are very informative, and she's great at answering questions. Redoing the discussion worksheets and PDQ's is really helpful for the tests. The tests have a pretty short time limit, but they're doable if you understand how to apply the concepts to new situations. I took 2310, 20 and 25 from her. Loved all of them.

Holly is probably one of the more challenging O-Chem professors at the U, but she is undoubtedly the best professor I have ever had. She has high expectations because she wants you to succeed, and she has a deep love for her students and the subject. Definitely take O Chem 1 and 2 with her!

Holly is phenomenal. She's one of the rare breed of professors who truly want you to understand organic chemistry. She is engaging in her lectures, and her tests are really hard, so be prepared to work. But she 100% gives you all the materials you need (plus more)-recorded lectures, extra charts, reaction sheets, tutorials, websites, past exams

Holly is a fabulous lecturer. Even having taken the Honors O Chem sequence, I still uncovered some new details of reactions I had learned in the previous semester. The labs were fun and long (but totally worth it). Her quizzes are easy (if you attend lecture and do your pre lab). Her class teaches you to be a better practising chemist.

I think this professor may be a little overrated. She had so many examinations that you didn't have time to study 4 them. Personally, I thought she gave an excessive amount of hw and it didn't help a lot. And yeah sure, it was ec but her exams are long and the time is short. You're bound to need the ec. I suggest you don't take it with her but ydy.

Holly is an amazing professor! Going into organic chemistry was frightening and she made her expectations absolutely clear. She provides everything you will ever need to succeed in the course however it is up to you to take advantage of it. Attendance isnt mandatory however, its easier to understand if you do go! Dont expect an easy A, work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Holly was nice and helpful. She gives tons of extra credit and your final exam score can replace your final grade. I didn't study way too much for this class and I did well on the tests and on the final and felt the class was reasonable. I would take Holly over any of the other professors. Just keep up with the material and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: This was a 2 credit lab and it seemed like it should have been a 10 credit lab. She makes you do so many stupid things for this lab and the lab write ups are ridiculous. Prepare to do bad on her quizzes before every lab that are done individually and not with your lab partner. Don't take this lab with any other heavy classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have taken. Holly is the one to take for O Chem. Make sure you have time for this class. Take a lighter course load and get it done. Hard class, amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR EVER. LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE Holly. Please stop everything you're doing and take O-chem from her. There are many horror stories about ochem but she makes it so easy and fun and also is so helpful. Love her so much!

Best professor I've ever had.  She is so kind and will spend hours with you till you get the material.   She gives the most amazing pep-talks before all the exams.  Her lectures are clear and she focuses on developing a deep concept of the material rather than memorizing.  There is an army of TAs too! They are so helpful! Best class I ever took!
By far the best professor. Her exams are hard but if you study hard then it's pretty easy. She cares about her students a lot. Take OChem 1 and 2 from her. Adios.

If you're reading this review, just take Holly's class. I have NEVER had a teacher more knowledgeable and passionate for a subject while being so kind, caring, and willing to help you succeed. She offers countless opportunities to improve your grade while at the same time mastering difficult topics. Seriously, Holly is one in a million.

Holly is one of the all time best instructors I've ever had.  She WANTS you to succeed.  Organic chemistry is really hard and she expects you to know it backwards and forwards, but she does EVERYTHING in her power to help you.  Tests are brutal, but do all the optional homework (its also extra credit), and use the TA's! Best choice of instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great instructor. Really cares about her students. Very knowledgeable and knows how to explain very complex concepts very simply.

Holly was an awesome instructor. Expectations are very clear, and she really does her best to make sure all of her students are successful. Extra credit is helpful, and her grading policy makes success attainable for everyone. Go to class, study early and often, and do your work and you will pass. Definitely the best class i have taken at the U!

TA was a pain in the ass, but she normalizes grades and offers a ton of extra credit. Lectures were amazing and very clear. She requires you to turn a lot of things in, so other than some occasional confusion over grading, the lab was an easy A.

She expects a great amount from you as the student to go and learn outside of class.  In class clickers are free points.  Tons of optional/extra credit homework assignments that you can do to help buffer your grade.  Tests and quizzes are very difficult, but doable if you study.  Definitively use your book and be ready to work a lot.

Holly is amazing. Makes O Chem a very accessible subject. Extra credit EVERY week, totally saved my grade. Exams can be rough--she likes to throw unfamiliar reagents/reactions in for fun. But meet her after the test and go over it; often times, she'll give you back points on some problems if she thinks you deserve it. Super nice & approachable lady
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Holly is probably the best teacher I've ever had. Everything she does helps you succeed. She is a hilarious, honest,  and enthusiastic lecturer and she will take the time necessary for you to understand the answer to your question in person. She is extremely good at slowly building on practical concepts throughout the course. She is simply awesome.

I wrote the review right below this one. PLEASE ignore that review I wrote. I tried to remove but I couldn't. Sorry. She is very passionate and spends her time really a lot for students. Take this class with her if you are not good at Chemistry. She will make you ace on that. Believe her and follow her.

she always makes students nervous before tests coming. Especially, at the end of semester, you will have midterm3. She taught chapter 10 in two days and chapter 11 in one day right before test and it will be on the test. Also, right before midterms she uploaded tons of stuff that makes you very nervous as well. STRESSFUL!

You will never find a better Ochem teacher. Going into this year, I thought Ochem would be the course I'd have to devote the most studying to, but it's definitely not. She actually teaches you, and the problems in homework/discussion sets align well with tests. This class solidified my desire to go into chemistry.
She is a nice person but the class is pretty difficult as you would expect from an O chem class.

Fantastic chem teacher, but the tests are ridiculous. Less than 50 minutes to complete 6 solid pages of organic chemistry makes the tests less about how well you know the material, and more about how much material you've already done. Would have done a lot better if class was 10 minutes longer on test days.
Very passionate about organic chemistry, and caring for students.

Holly is hands down one of the best professors that I have ever had.  She cares about every student, but she makes them work hard for the grade that they receive.  The TAs that she hires are incredible and I would take any class that she was teaching during the semester.  I also had her for the 2315 lab, and also a wonderful class to be in.  A+!!

Holly is an amazing human being. She honestly loves chemistry and wants to show you how cool it is. She's not easy, but she's there for office hours and extra help. Do the Smith problems, worksheets, and put in the time and you'll do great. She wants you to do well, unlike other professors that try to make their class hard. Go Holly for O-chem!
Holly is wonderful. If you have the chance to take any chemistry from her, DO IT! She is supportive, funny, clear, and always brings things back to the basics.

Holly is amazing. She really is. She takes time to learn the names of her students, and cares about their lives. Easily one of my favorite teachers on campus. She likes to talk about basketball, and she is super helpful. Organic Chemistry is not an easy subject though, and to do well you really need to attend lecture and study. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT!

This class had two things due each week, 1. a post discussion worksheet and 2. back of the book problems, lots of them.   These assignments and Holly's lecture really teach you O-Chem. this is one of the hardest classes I have taken, however Holly is the best prof and there to help.   Be glad she is your professor.

Holly is absolutely wonderful. Go to lecture, do the extra credit problems, do all the problem sets (twice) and you will do well. She prepares you well for tests; she tells you exactly what is coming. She really wants you to do well.

Holly is THE best professor I've had in my 3 years at the U. She provides all necessary materials needed to pass the class. I worked harder for this grade than ever before but I learned to like chemistry!  Do each problem set three times before each exam and you will pass! I didn't read more than 2 pages of the textbook. Use Klein for reading!

Holly is the best chemistry professor, she's so passionate about chemistry! No matter what she teaches, she will make you love it. You will want to come back and be a TA so don't hesitate taking her class!
So good. Super cute. Wish she would teach all my classes.

There is so many amazing things I could say about her. She gives you everything you need to be prepared for exams, in office hours she really tries to help, and the lab actually follows what she teaches in lectures!!

One of the best teachers I have ever had. She is so passionate about the subject and her students. She truly cares for her students and wants to see them succeed. It takes loads of time to get an A in this class but it is definitely possible with Holly as a teacher. I'm even a TA for this class now cause she made me love it so much!

Holly does a phenomenal job teaching a hard subject. She is passionate about her job and her students. Her exams are very fair. She provides you with all of the material you need to get an A. Read the textbook, it is very helpful and do ALL of her problem sets twice as well as additional problems from the textbook and you'll get your A!

Holly is a great professor.  She teaches things clearly and thoroughly.  The only problem is that she will sometimes rush the material when it gets thick.  She also doesn't respond to emails.  But she was very friendly and a great teacher. I recommend her for OChem.

Honestly the best professor I have ever had! She is passionate about what she teaches and she wants everyone in her class to not only succeed but to actually understand what she is teaching. She goes that extra mile to help her students do well. She gives you ALL the resources you need to do well in her class.
Reasonable professor for a difficult class.  Tests are manageable if you put the time in and Holly is good at giving you problems in class.

Holly is the best professor I have ever had. She is the most genuine individual who cares about each student. Her lectures can sometimes be slightly confusing and rushed, but she is always willing to meet with you for extra help. I would give no other professor a higher rating.
Spends way too much effort trying to get through all her slides without answering questions.
Goes through slides way to quickly. Does not pause for questions

The best professor I have ever had. Her interest in chemistry shows in her lectures. Difficult, but very fair in testing. I would give no other professor a higher rating. Has a passion for organic chemistry and can easily portray concepts at a fundamental level. SHE IS PHENOMENAL!

Phenomenal professor, still a very challenging class but Holly is such a great teacher I got really into Organic Chemistry and did well in the class.  Very interesting lecturer and her TAs really went above and beyond to help.  Great experience all around.
She's an amazing teacher! Her lectures were clear. She's very helpful and provides a lot for you to succeed. Organic chemistry is going to be really hard, but she helps you through it.

Fabulous professor. She and professor Owens are tied for my favorite teachers, the chemistry department at the U is phenomenal. If you are willing to work hard, she gives you all the tools you need to succeed.  Use everything she gives you, and you will ace the class. Hands down, her discussion sheets are the most helpful. Love this teacher!
She is so nice and she will slow it down if nessecary:)

Holly is a very caring professor. My friends and I often joked that she's the "motherly one" and the only professor who's competent at teaching throughout the gen chem/o chem series. Definitely spend time studying and doing problems though, since there are way too many reactions to remember and too many reagents to learn how to use
Excellent!  Very clear, tests reflect the lectures, and she's always willing to help.
Complete contrast to my bad experience in CHEM2310, Holly made me like organic chemistry and actually look forward to class.
AMAZING professor!
Took O Chem 2 from her and loved it.  Great lectures and very helpful teacher.  You need to work lots of problems because the subject is tough so the tests are tough.

Had her for O chem 2 and the lab- she is amazing! I have never had a professor that actually went to the discussions and walked around with the TAs answering questions. She is really passionate about chemistry and you can tell she really loves teaching and helping students succeed!

I had Holly for ochem 1&2 and culinary chem and I would take any other class she teaches.  She's so eager to help you succeed in her classes. The material is difficult but way she presents it to you makes you believe you can conquer the challenge.  Do the discussion worksheets, read the text, go to class and you'll do well. Ask her questions.

Holly was amazing.  She really wanted you to understand the material.  Her lectures made perfect sense and if you just pay attention to that then you can get an A in the class.  Don't fear organic II, just take it from Holly and pay attention.
An absolutely fantastic professor, who cares about her students. Don't pass up a chance to take Organic Chemistry with Professor Sebahar.
Holly is an amazing teacher, she really tries hard to help her students succeed and make  the material understandable. It is a difficult class no matter who the teacher, but Holly is just awesome.

Holly is a great teacher! She uses alot of examples as she teaches so it's easy to apply it to your life so you can remember all the information. There is alot to learn though. No homework required but it helps alot in studying for the tests.

Harry is an amazing professor! He is genuine and cares about students. Options and Futures was one of the hardest classes I have taken at the U, but Harry is also one of the best professors I have had. Tough class and tests are huge, but with the practice problems, practice tests, and office hours, it is everything you want in a class.

Test heavy classes make me nervous since I'm not a good test taker, but Professor Burke showed immense care in his students and their success. He offered many office hours and would send regular announcements to update everyone. 10/10 professor, would take again!
Very good teacher and wants to see his students succeed. No homework grades are very dependent on your test scores. Would recommend
good class. cool dude...saw him skiing at snowbird and we took a couple laps.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gives a lot of homework but he is my favorite professor this semester! Cares.

Very exam heavy class but he really helps prepare you for the exams with practice sets given. Super nice and funny. Makes lectures engaging and you can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching about. Awesome guy.
DONT TAKE. DONT TAKEDONT TAKE

No study guide for a final that was 40% of the final grade. Also gave us a group project he said we would present in class, even though that would have been about 60 presentations in the last two weeks of class. He then switched it to video submissions a week before in class presentations would have started. He seems nice, but I'd avoid his class

It's definitely not a class I would take again. The final was worth 40% of our grade, and we weren't given any sort of study guide. The only other things our grade depended on were 3 quizzes, 5 homeworks, and one group project. Attendance was also required, but taken at random. Even though Miao is a really nice guy, he truly isn't a good professor.

This class is set up in a way that makes it very difficult to pass. Attendance is taken on random days. And none of what is taught truly helps on the final. This class was supposed to be a introductory class but it is very disorganized and terms are not explained. NO STUDY GUIDE AT ALL, and the final was worth 40% if the total grade.

If you fail the final, you basically out of luck. Has very little assignments that is weighted very little, and the final exam is like 40% of your grade. He also throws random information and expects you to understand them.

This class gives you incredibly limited opportunities to succeed whatsoever. The material is set up in a way that is very difficult to wrap your mind around or memorize. He doesn't explain things from the beginning, and jumps around leaving you confused and unable to grasp important concepts. The final was impossible to prepare for; no study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buy the physical textbook, it will save you for the final. You are essentially teaching yourself; attendance is mandatory, and it will impact your grade if you do not attend. The class itself is very draining but relatively easy. The final is a lot harder than you think/he leads on, and it is weighted heavily. The other negative reviews are true.

Nice guy but a poor teacher. The pace of the class was very strange as we had like two assignments for the first couple months but then once a week for the last month. He also doesn't make things available until like a week before they are due. It was frustrating to watch his review videos and feel ready for the quizzes and then not do well on them
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but awful at teaching
If you want to fail, then go ahead and take his class
Miao needs to work on his teaching skills. He wants students to succeed but he teaches simple terms in a complicated way. He takes forever to get grades back.

Professor Miao is one of the worst professors I've had. He cannot teach or explain clearly and presents material as if we already know all finance terms, even though it's an introductory class. His tests are out of 120 points, seemingly to prevent curves. I used the textbook, tutors, office hours, and TAs but still struggled to understand.

Miao is by far the worst professor I have taken at the U. For an introductory class his methods might have been the worst way to teach it. His slides have little to go off of in terms of studying, half of them being needless and pointless. Along with that he does not reply to emails for the life of him. The dude should not be teaching here at the U

Professor He is a nice person, but unfortunately, he cannot teach. For an introductory class, I found it to be rather stressful. His slides are extremely vague, which makes the quizzes and final exam rather difficult. Although I was able to get help from him and his TAs, it did not seem to make the class easier. I would avoid this professor.

Miao is a very nice guy, but his lectures are subpar. He finds a way to make simple topics very confusing and overcomplicated. The topics on the homework and final are not taught well in class, and you are expected to learn many of the topics on your own. Attendance is also mandatory for his very boring lectures. Would not recommend.

Miao He is not a good professor. He explains concepts in a very complicated way, which should not be the case for an introductory course. His slides are vague, filled with grammatical errors, and they don't cover everything taught in class. He is not very accessible and never responded to any of my emails. He doesn't provide good exam or quiz prep.

Professor Miao is a very kind and understanding instructor. Homework and quizzes are pretty straightforward, and the class is graded on only a few things, which can make it less stressful. However, he's a poor teacher—lectures are hard to follow, he rushes through material, and there's little structure. Avoid this instructor if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Miao He is a very nice guy. But his class is terrible. Attendance is mandatory, and you fail automatically if you miss eight classes. The lectures are long and some of the most boring at the U. Some of the slides themselves have little to no context. We also did not even get to finish the last unit before the final exam.

Professor He is very caring and kind towards his students, but his lectures are very long and boring. I didn't really learn that much from his finance class because his lectures were really disengaging, but his class is very simple with HW and quizzes, and only 1 exam, which is the final. Also gives students the opportunity to earn extra credit.

Miao is a great professor I've been learning a lot in this class. He cares about his students and is willing to help if you just go to his office hours or just go talk to him after class. This might be a crazy concept to some business students but If all you do during class is talk, sleep, watch football, you probably won't do well?

Professor Miao works hard to ensure that his lectures and exams are fair, and while he may go through content quickly, it is up to the student to stop him and ask questions if they have concerns or are confused. I think people forget that we are responsible for our own grades, and that a curve can negatively affect you if your peers do very well.

Professor He is nice for sure, however I never fail to fall asleep in his class. It takes him long amounts of time to get through points and I have not learned much about finance. He has an easier class format but still it's hard to follow him sometimes. Great guy, still needs to work on lecture quality.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a nice person, and he expects students to do well. As a new professor to the U, Miao has been improving his teaching methods as the semester goes on. However, his lectures, homework, and exams are the hardest I have ever seen on campus. If you were to take this course, ensure that your other courses are easy enough to mainly focus on this.

I had an A all semester until the final, which tanked me to a B-. The homework and quizzes were online and open-note, but the final was on paper with only printed/written notes allowed. This drastic change in format felt unfair and poorly thought out. It didn't reflect the rest of the course, making it harder to succeed despite consistent effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors at the U. He lectures the whole time without acknowledging the class. The class is cumulative and he doesn't give any mid terms. He doesn't do exam review and actually taught new material the day before the exam just to not test us on it. He then “curved” the class by LOWERING peoples grades by over 3%.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor and wants his students to do well, but he is an awful teacher. The class consisted of all lectures except one group project, where he says any group project content could be on the final exam. It wasn't, it was just said to make people feel like they have to go in, especially the week before a holiday. Lectures are long,not engaging.

Professor He is a kind person, however, his course is all over the place and poorly put together. Paying attention in class is near impossible. Attendance is mandatory, which can be frustrating. The final exam is far too broad to study well for. Would not recommend this course or this professor.

Miao is a great teacher and I learned pretty fast that if you go to class and follow along you will do great on the tests. Not a lot of HW and they're pretty easy. Tests you get a cheat sheet so it makes it super easy. This class will teach you what you really need to know to be an analyst and Miao goes slow and will go back and answer any question

Professor He was newer at the time when I took his course, but he tries his hardest. Lectures were long and very content heavy. Had only one test at the end of the semester. Class itself was not very hard, but hard to digest the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No external resources to learn from, boring lectures, mandatory attendance(miss 8 and fail), syllabus doesn't match dates. Slides don't typically cover what's on the quizzes/homeworks.

You will be modifying PDFs for homework and quizzes instead of simply using Canvas (even though it would make grading much easier). 
Mandatory attendance + bad lectures = huge waste of time 
no online resources. 
No attempt to set students up for success. 
expect random minor deductions without explanations. 
Worst prof I've had at the U by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Miao gets a lot of hate but he is a great guy. I asked him to put slides on before class and he did. While don't think I was able to comprehend all of the course concepts (sparse lectures) I did gain a good foundation of markets. While he is not the best professor I think Miao is a good guy who honestly works to improve the student experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wanted to wait until after the final to write a review. The final was ridiculously difficult. He provided no study guide, told us to study the homework and quizzes. Come to find out, most of the questions on the final covered nothing from the homework or quizzes. One of the hardest finals I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture-heavy class but answers questions well. Felt disorganized, toward the end of the semester forgot about assigning us some assignments, and in the last two weeks assigned 2 homework assignments and 1 quiz. The group project was kinda pointless. Make sure to pay attention to what he says that won't be on the slides but will be on the exam

I genuinely think he is the worst professor at the U. I have never encountered a professor so disconnected from his students. His personality is non-existent, never smiles. Attendance is mandatory, and he will hold you hostage every class until you complete the required poll. If you miss a certain number of classes, you fail. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've never taken a professor so uninspiring when it comes to finance. While I am ok with a difficult class, this is a whole different story. When he realized his schedule was off by 2+ weeks, he crammed the coursework into the last week. He mended the syllabus without telling us. 65% of our final grade was determined be the last four days. insane

This professor has many problems. First he is very new and does seem to know how to set students up for success or manage a course. Boring slides, grades aren't entered until the end, he puts a bunch of work right during the week of finals,& offers little to no practice work for you. He also makes the class much harder than other professors. Avoid.

He's trying; I think he will get better at pacing the class the more he teaches. He's a nice guy and is always willing to meet outside of class. The reviews here are a bit harsh, at least for 3100. The content of the class itself is a repeat of other classes so that does not help.

This class was by far one of the best finance courses I have taken at the U. Learning how to financial model is an extremely useful tool, and Maio has a great understanding of the subject. He is very caring as a professor and is willing to meet with his students any time if they need any assistance.

Worst professor I've ever had. His math is wrong in class and can't recreate it when we ask him. Doesn't explain things except for in terms of math, and then is very bad at that. Why he became a professor, I don't know. Absolutely no pride in his craft. 

AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Professor He is brand new and it shows. He tried to cram everything into the last two weeks and gave us no idea what our grades could be. His lectures are impossible to pay attention to and this class was just a repeat of finance 4030 and 4070. Quiz questions were unfairly worded at times and had material that was barely covered in class. Avoid.

Professor He was personally my least favorite professor I have experienced during my time at the University of Utah. Between boring 3-hour lectures, insufficient testing time, assigning 75% of the coursework the last 2 weeks of the semester before/during finals, and being extremely hard to understand, AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In all my years of learning, this is by far the worst teacher or professor I have ever had. The lecture are long, dull, and nearly impossible to pay attention to or understand. There is little to no content available online, and I have never felt less prepared going into the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor. 0 feedback, 0 help. Finally got my previous two midterm scores back on the day of the final. Leaves slides blank on purpose. Back loads the class with a group project, quizzes, tests. Average for all tests was a failing grade. Doesn't give you the full class time to take the midterms either.
I would not recommend this prof. Does not set you up for success at all.

This is the worst class that I have taken at the University of Utah. He is a terrible lecturer and makes interesting information very boring. During the semester, people got up and walked out during the middle of the class. He also crammed 2 homework assignments, 2 quizzes, a project and a final into the last three weeks of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very very inteligent guy that clearly knows what he is talking about but drones on and on using boring powerpoint slides. If you are interested in finance its quite an interesting class but otherwise you'll find it to be confusing and convoluted. Only 4 homeworks and 3 quizs plus a final so no busy work.

He is new to the U, but his classes are bound to improve in the future. Here's my experience: The class has 3 Exams and 6 Homework assignments. There is no busy work! His slide can be confusing but you can get an easy A if you pay a little attention and practice by yourself. He will answer all questions and will always make time for you to meet up.

Theory-focused lectures lack real-world application. Long, uninteresting classes leave you scrambling to take notes of what he wrote on the whiteboard before he erases it. Homework and exams don't align with class content, causing frustration. Disorganized teaching and syllabus deviations add to disappointment. I recommend taking a different prof.

Could not pace the class. He gets behind on material and then just pushes it all to be due the same week. Lectures are so insanely boring and looking over the slides after class doesn't help because there really isn't much on them. This class has been a dumpster fire from day 1.

0/10. His investments class is one of the worst courses I have ever taken. This might be the worst professor I've ever had. He does not prepare you for tests, he makes you feel dumb when you ask questions, and he has no idea how to pace the class. The last two weeks of this semester he assigned 3 homeworks, one excel lab, a midterm and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have had at the University of Utah.  His classes are boring and he takes extremely long to rewrite the same formulas that are on his slides. With 1 month left in the semester, he informed us that we had only completed 12% of the graded material, and he crammed in 2 quizzes and the final in the last 3 weeks of school.

Very poor professor. Knows course material well however does a VERY poor job at teaching it to the class.

-Offers no practice quizzes 
-Lectures are mundane and boring
-Poor/hard to understand English speaking proficiency
-Very minimal practice problems
-Leaves students very unprepared for exams
-Doesn't show full solutions on in-class slides

This was the worst class I have ever taken at the U. I walked out on the 2nd day and dropped it. It is really hard to understand his english and he talks like he is talking straight to a wall with zero emotion. I thought he was joking at first but it was real. DO NOT TAKE.

Undoubtedly the worst professor I have ever had. Two-and-a-half-hour lectures with no stopping and usually no breaks. Does not engage the class at all, and answers questions half-heartedly. More than half the class leaves during the middle of class, so he puts quizzes at the end to force students to stay for lectures. AVOID AT ALL COSTS
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rappleye is a personable, passionate professor. He clearly loves what he does, yet understands that many people are only taking the class to fulfill a credit. There are weekly assignments related to what you learn in the lecture and lab. The grading isn't bad, but it's slow. There are two in-person MC exams - STUDY THE PROVIDED QUIZLET.
Ian gave us room for creativity while providing helpful feedback. Really a great class for personal growth.

Ian is super helpful, he gives great project feedback when prompted, is knowledgeable in many different software, and is always there to help troubleshoot. Keep good communication with him and you will thrive in and out of class.
Chill guy. Fun class. Not much busy work. Lots of freedom for creativity.

I was able to learn a lot during the semester. I learned the entire process of game modeling. he always takes care to answer questions and proactively checks and asks if there are any difficult parts!  the best professor :)
Her lectures are great and easy to follow. there are a lot of helpful pre-class and pos-class resources available.

Amanda was a fantastic Professor. Her lectures were interesting so you won't get bored, and she cares a LOT about the subject. Not too much homework, and it's easy, too. The only thing to know: she is very specific about how you write down your answers on the exams, but if you go to the Exam Prep, they basically give you the answers. Ask for tips!

Amanda was a good professor who was definitely passionate about what she was teaching. However, her lectures almost always felt rushed, so I could not take in lots of information. Half the time, I had to end up teaching myself concepts. The TAs in this class were very helpful when it came to exam reviews and discussion questions.

Amanda was a beautifully sweet person who very obviously has a passion for the material she's teaching. However, the material was delivered in extremely confusing ways, and the entire course felt like navigating fog. LA's (most biochem majors) made ppl feel silly for asking questions, I guess they didn't get that this is an intro to bio course.
Good lectures and easy exams but you gotta show up to the lectue to get an A. A decent amount of homework too
Decnet amlount of homework and the tests are easy, but you gotta show up to the lecture to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was pretty straightforward and everything was on the syllabus, just go to class and discussion and you'll be fine I barley studied and got an A. But I highly recommend taking bio with Colby tanner since all their exam averages were way higher including on the final.

I selected tough grader because I always got lower on my exams than expected and I think it's a little hard to get 100. Participation matters because she uses iClicker. She's fine here but I think she's a much better prof for BIOL 1620
Her tests are ah, and f'd my grade cause of attendance. I was at an A and went to a B- for attendance right at the end of the semester.

Professor Hoepfner doesn't respond to emails other than “refer to the syllabus” regardless as to what your question is. Along with that, her lectures are a snooze festival that if missed will completely tank your grade. Her tests are also very difficult, and are often based on random little tidbits of info that she doesn't emphasize during class.

Her attendance policy is ridiculous. Her lectures are almost completely pointless if you know any biology, while her tests are based on the most niche things that are barely mentioned. She responds to emails in a late fashion, never offering any response that isn't "refer to the syllabus." avoid this class and teacher.

Honestly my grade in this class was 100% on me. I never went to class or did the draw to learns and I kinda cooked myself. Go to class and do the work and it should be a relatively easy A. Her tests are a little bit harder than they should be for this kinda class. She is very passionate and upbeat, kinda a bubbly personality. Do what ur supposed to
I enjoyed this class as much as I could enjoy bio. As long as you regularly go to the lectures and do the homework, it is a relatively easy-to-moderate class.

She's a fantastic lecturer, the only time I found myself confused it was because I wasn't paying attention. There definitely is a lot of homework but it all helps you learn. She's great at explaining things and her slides are awesome, make sure to actually go to class, attendance matters.

Professor Hoepfner loves to do so many assignments every week, and while she claims to have a "generous" drop policy there are so many assignments plus in class clickers that you are in big trouble if you forget to do stuff for even one day. Her tests are also extremely hard, getting an 80% puts you above the interquartile range. Avoid taking her.

Amanda is great! You're never gonna get a 100% on her exams, but if you study then you should be able to achieve an A. I wouldn't even say I study all too much. Quizzes are a great source (but they only have one attempt so be sure you know the content beforehand). Also make sure to use the study guides she puts at the end of each slide.

Amanda is one of the best professors I've had. She made the material easy to understand and it is clear she is very passionate about what she teaches. Her tests were super easy, quizzes were a good indicator of test material. Pay attention, go to class, go to discussion, do the homework, and you're sure to get an A.

Amanda was nice but the tests were difficult for literally no reason at all. You had no idea how in depth she wanted you to go for the short answer questions and they were long too. She would also put stuff on there that she talked about for 10 seconds. Don't think me or my friends got an A on a single exam so be ready for a solid B in this class.
the tests aren't hard. she covers every single thing in her lectures and you can go back to the slides to study

Amanda is my favorite professor! Overall, an easy class; however, exams are difficult compared to everything else. Tests are designed so that nobody gets 100%, but if you review the study guide for each lecture slideshow + attend discussions, an A grade is doable. Flashcards are also a great way to prepare since this class relies on definitions.

Hoepfner was a good lecturer with reasonable exams. She's nice, responsive to questions, and passionate. My only complaint is that her quizzes could be too difficult, but I was left well prepared for the final. There was consistent homework, but it was never too time consuming, which I appreciated. There were textbook readings, but I didn't do them

Super easy class if you are engaged in lectures or even reading the slides. 
Barely had to study for tests as getting the main idea made it enough to be successful. 
Though of the questions are challenging (wording wise at least), understanding the concept is enough to get you an A.
This class is mostly about understanding with a bit of memorizing.

She is genuinely the sweetest human on Earth. She cares about her students and is easy to access outside of class. Only 2 midterms that are pretty easy if you study, but there's is a lot of "select all that apply". She breaks lectures down so they're easy to understand and I really enjoyed her and want to take more classes with her in the future.

Amanda makes Ecology and Evolution very fascinating, she makes this class into one of the easiest class in bio major. The slides and homework gives a lot of helpful examples to help me thinking about how nature and life work. If you don't understand the concept, she is more than willing to help you if you asked her questions after class.

I took 1620 with Amanda and wasn't a huge fan, but when I took her class for BIOL 3410, she was great! Her lectures were super interesting, and she talked a lot about climate change, which was amazing. Her exams are pretty straightforward if you study, and attendance is extra credit.

Pros:

- Amanda is passionate about her work and it shows in class.
- Amanda tries her hardest to make the material interesting.

Cons:

- Terrible slides; good luck studying on your own
- vague questions on tests
- Discussions are not helpful 
- Mandatory Attendance for a class that should be online
- Zero flexibility for nontraditional students

The class is completely useless and there is no reason it should be required. If you took bio 2 you'll do fine but she teaches as if the material is rocket science. She might be the most condescending person I have ever met in my life and it just makes an already unenjoyable class irritating to be in. Also, exam questions have terrible wording.

She was fine. Boring lectures that felt like I was sitting in my highschool biology class. Attendance was mandatory but all the information was on the slides so you can miss a few times and be fine. Once you understand how she formats her tests the class gets pretty easy.
overall this class made me want to die everyday :(
Just please…avoid this class….the tests made me want to die.

Great lecturer, the material was easy to understand. The exams were near impossible unless you have a degree already in biology. She was easy to meet with but even if your answers are correct, she will mark it with 0 points because she's looking for google ai overview level answers. I didn't see one person get a 100% on any of the exams. Be weary.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Amanda Hoepfner was overall a good teacher. Her tests and quizzes were kind of difficult because a lot of the questions were "select all that apply" which can be hard to suss out. I wish she would have provided more practice materials for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my fav classes ever taken! Loved her passion and her way of lecture. Super willing to help and obviously cares about you and wants to get to know you. I really thought that I would hate this class but her enthusiasm made it so fun. Just take notes, attend all the lectures, form study groups, and go to office hours to really learn.

The sweetest, kindest professer here. She really is passionate about what she teaches. It can be hard in a big lecture hall such as for 1610 so I think its wise to sit closer and build a relationship. I've had her for 3 semesters and she has helped me so much build my love for science and biology, I totally would take her for the rest of my degree!

She is a great teacher and explains things clearly. Her tests are never convoluted, and she pulls questions directly from the slides. Understand the slides + practice questions and an A is easy. The things other reviews say about her being a little condescending are not wrong, but that doesn't mean the class is hard. Only con: mandatory attendance.

She's a good professor, very interested in what she's talking about and very good takes always. However, attendance is so strict and you can get points off even if you're in class. Not super straightforward test questions.

I usually drive without holding the steering wheel on the way to her class. I personally think she is a decent person but not as a professor. Her tone is condescending, like she's talking to children, and the wording of her tests is very confusing and unclear. If you can take this class with someone else, just RUN.

She is super enthusiastic about what she does and even though lectures are long it is easy to stay focused. The grading also feels really fair, and you will do well in this class as long as you are willing to put in a little effort.

Really enthusiastic and fun professor! I really enjoyed her presentations and her enthusiasm and energy it worth it despite my class being so early in the morning. The class isn't too hard outside of that as well. Really recommended!

This class was frustrating due to the required attendance via iclicker. I feel like I could have done just as well in class without going to lecture. Lectures were long and boring, even though Amanda is passionate. Also, it may seem like "common sense," but she will test you on very specific/nitpicky things from the slides.

Truly an angel. Amanda cares about her students and their success. She is passionate about teaching and explains things well. If you do not utilize her resources, you will not do well. Show up to class and discussions. Go to her office hours as much as you can. Great way to get to know her, especially if you are a Bio major as she teaches 1620 too.
I had her for Bio 1 and thought she was great! You definitely need to attend class, but if you do you will do well.
Amanda is seriously so kind and energetic. I loved her as a professor but just did not like the class very much. Make sure to pay attention during lecture and get ready to study a lot on your own.

I LOVE AMANDA!!! she is the best bio professor for every class I've taken with her. Her expectations are clear and she provides so many resources to students. She's very easy to get in touch with and talking with her after class is so much fun! I will always recommend her. She's makes boring or challenging concepts fun to learn about :)

I love Professor Hoepfner. She is passionate about the material and teaches it well. The homework she assigns applies very well to exam material, and also provides mock exams as well as weekly review sessions with the TAs. For an introductory biology course, I enjoyed having her as my professor.

Amanda is amazing! She single-handedly changed my perspective on ecology and evolution. I went from almost changing my major to avoid the course to looking forward to it every day. She clearly outlines information for exams, while also presenting intellectually challenging material. This is one of the few classes, and professors, I would recommend!

I love Amanda so much, she is an incredible professor, an amazing person, she cares so much about teaching the material and of her students. She helped me on a personal level and honestly have never had a better professor in my life.
Amanda is definitely a tough nut to crack at times. She is not as warm as the other BIOL professors, but she's a great lecturer who cares about her students' success.

Her tests are very easy if you know the asnwers to all the learning objectives which she gives at the start of each lecture, there is really no reason to study anything but these as they are the only things on the exams. Some of the lectures for this course where a little repetative but for the most part it was interesting and well structured.

Great professor, but can easily get lost as Amanda moves quickly between slides. Very kind and provides many resources, including TA mock exams and review sessions that were essential to pass the exams. Weekly assignments on McGraw Hill and canvas, where mediocre advice would be given.

If you've never taken AP Bio or any type of bio class, this class is going to feel like you're being overloaded with information because Amanda reads off slides and moves quickly. She does a good job explaining topics and preparing you for the tests (if you pay attention). The TA's also hosted mock exams that were very similar to the midterms.
She is such a kind teacher. Not a lot of busy work. She wants her students to understand. Ngl she would also be a great pre school teacher
Dr. Hoepfner is amazing! She completely changed my outlook on Ecology. Clear lectures with expected learning outcomes highlighted. 10/10 would recommend!
Loved this class!! She always asks for understanding and will go over things if we don't completely understand what is happening. She seems to be very knowledgeable and cares about her students.

She's a great lecturer. She gets straight to the point and doesn't go on tangents. Her PowerPoints are amazing. Full of relevant info, objectives that tell you exactly what u need to know for exams could be a bit long at times. Love that she tells you exactly what u need to do to get a good grade. Clickers and quizzes are awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very nice but the class is super boring and every exam is "select all that apply" which makes them super hard. If you try really hard you can get an A but don't expect an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hoepfner was great during lectures but they are just boring and she sometimes treats her students like middle schoolers. The material is boring at times but all the information you learn is straight on the tests. Her weekly home-works are easy and the Friday quizzes are simple. Overall, she was decent but could have been more energetic.

Knowledgeable professor but it always seemed like she was talking down to the class and treating us like elementary students. Slides were very word heavy and lectures dragged on and got repetitive and boring. The material overall is a little dry. Exams were pretty fair and matched lecture material, but this is not a fun class to sit through

Amanda was a decent professor and her lectures were generally engaging and informative. However, she has unrealistic expectations of students out of class time, for example, assigning a Friday take home quiz even though class was not on Fridays. She is very condescending over email, and refuses to make any exceptions to due dates for any reason.

Professor Hoepfner is a really kind person. However, this class was extremely difficult and I don't feel that she helped. She takes a long time to respond to emails. She is very knowledgable but she often overloads her students with a ton of information during her lectures. Maybe it was just the way this class was set up, but it was a ton of work.

She is a very kind professor. She talks from a set of slides which if thats your learning style its very easy going. However the class has a work load for sure. I loved her as a professor, she may just not have everyones teaching style.

Great lectures with clear learning outcomes and relevant homework. I enjoyed her teaching style, even at 8 am she was always very prepared to teach. If you learn to take detailed notes and can connect overarching topics, you will ace her class.

Amanda is always willing to help people understand the material and never shames for the wrong answer. However, I took this class at 8 am and cannot tell you how many times I fell asleep while she was lecturing. They're boring and rudimentary. Exams are often "choose all that apply" with very similar answer options and have short answer portions.
A little too much information in the slides regarding content, but she was a great professor nonetheless

Amanda is great. She's super entertaining. My friends and I called her animal girl because we could never remember her last name. Anywho, she knows what she is talking about and it's rather impressive just how passionate she is. Would highly recommend taking all of her BIOL classes.
Great professor. She's open to and patient with questions and it's evident that she wants her students to understand the material. The lectures are content-heavy but very thorough.
Talks the entire time, does not check for understanding.
Easy dubs. Got 101% on the first exam. As long as you go to class every day, you should know all the content.

Dr. Hoepfner's knowledge was evident, but the lectures felt overwhelmingly dense with extraneous information. It seemed she was more focused on finishing the material than ensuring students' comprehension. The lack of responsiveness to student feedback was disappointing. Although pleasant, her teaching tactics and philosophy left much to be desired
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hoepfner's BIOL 1620 course showcased her expertise, but I found it to be lecture-heavy, and her presentation came across as condescending, implying the material was beyond undergraduates' grasp. While appreciating her kindness, her teaching tactics and philosophy didn't resonate with me.

Dr. Hoepfner clearly cares about ecology and evolution and it will definitely rub off on you! She shows how these topics apply to all life science careers (including medicine) which is definitely not something you find many bio profs showing you. Definitely go to lecture, it helps prep you for exams fairly well. I love Amanda! :)

This is a theoretical class and if you don't give an answer that she likes right or wrong you WILL get it wrong. She likes to put question on the test the are "select all that apply" and if get them all right but one you will miss it. She also says "give the best" answer and best is her opinion. even if your answer is right, it has to be her answer
Wonderful professor and human. She is super clear with expectations. This course is fun.

She makes an effort to know her students and is open to meeting with them outside of class. She cares about the material and making sure her students understand it. Clear learning objectives and engaging lectures.
There is clear stated objectives so you know exactly what you need to take away from the lectures. She is very open, and encouraging of, questions.

The most frustrating part of this class was the Clickers. Everything she taught us in class, I could teach myself at home. She's very kind and passionate, but she basically reads off the slides. Class time felt like a chore and a waste. The pre-class problems during the ecology section are impossible without the textbook, despite it not being req'd

Amanda is a great professor and passionate about the stuff she teaches. I took her for BIOL 1620 and 3410 and both classes were really fun and engaging. She uses lots of different tools to engage you (iClicker, quizzes, preclass work, exams, etc.) No extra credit! I wish she taught on her own because the professors she taught with weren't great.

A great lecturer, she gets straight to the point without any additional non-needed information. She explains things pretty well, and her expectations are clear. Tests and quizzes are confusing, she uses specific words and terms which hide the real answer. The class isn't too hard if you participate and do assignments. Lectures may get monotone.

Dr. Hoepfner was an amazing professor! 1620 is a lowkey class where you try, but effort gets you most of the way there. She would answer lots of questions related to the topic (even if it wasn't planned to be taught), so bring your curiosity with you and don't be afraid to ask her questions! :) Try (and not even that hard) and you'll do great!

This class was a breeze; I genuinely don't think they could make this class easier without just giving people A's. Lots of HW, but easy and most of it is just participation (only graded on if you tried it or not). Barely studied for any of the tests and always got +80%. Her attitude is good, ignore other reviews. She obviously wants you to succeed.

Amanda was a good professor and made the expectations for the course clear from the start. Exams and quizzes were doable if you studied the lectures. Reading the book helps as well. Don't fall behind on your work load and you will do well in the class!
Overall, pretty good. The class could be a bit boring at times and the clicker questions were confusing. Don't buy the textbook. The class overall wasn't terrible and didn't require too much work.

Amanda is a nice enough person, but frustrating when it comes to grading. She likes to trip you up with specific wording on quizzes and exams. She can be a little monotonous, which isn't ideal for 8 am classes. She's about as average as average can get. Not horrible, not great.

Amanda is much better at teaching than James. She doesn't rant and rave about random subjects and gets right to the point which I really liked. this is a bio class, get ready to work for your grade. I found the subjects easy to learn but you do have to study. Amanda does a good job leading you in the right direction for the tests. James does not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Did not support students at all!!! No reviews for exams or quizzes. Quizzes never had enough time and exams were way too long. Lecture was very very boring. Attendance was required with clicker questions and forced group assignments in class which were also part of attendance. Unfortunate that she was the only professor for bio 1620.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She does not help support students at all (does not have review sessions, quizzes don't prep for test, discussions don't help and even has assignments that she expects you to turn in and doesn't put them as an assignment on canvas). Her quizzes have TOO MANY questions that have multiple parts and NOT enough time. Material not clearly conveyed.

BIOL 2870 is probably the easiest class Ive taken so far. You are graded on attendance (5pts each class) and summaries of the lectures each class (5pts each class). Just show up to the 50 minute class once a week and just summarize what the lecturers say. Easy A. Also, if you miss a class you can submit an extra credit assignment for 10pts.

Expectations for exams were not clear. There hasn't been a 100% on exams by anyone this semester. Also claimed that she was not trying to "trick" us on exams and then proceeded to give us many trick questions. Would go off topic to ramble about how we should take 1620. Wouldn't show up to review sessions or discussions while the other professor did

Clicker attendance is mandatory; 6 quizzes, lowest is dropped; I would make sure to enjoy the material, its vocab based and easy; work in study groups!; If given the opportunity to retake this course again, I would just keep up with the topics and do the study guides at the end of each chapter; great professor and not too bad.

I've really enjoyed Dr. Hoepfner's class. Quizzes are hard but the exams test exactly what is outlined in the study guides at the end of each lecture. Coming from 1610, this class is a walk in the park. This class makes it clear what you need to understand and everything is very organized. Discussion is pointless though. Good class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice person but very tough grader. She is very unclear about what to study, so the tests are always a surprise. Her voice is tough to listen to over zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was an okay lecturer. She got her point across, but it was often hard to tell what was most important for us to study. She expected us to put in a lot of time and effort outside of class. She was big on group discussion. Exams and quizzes were both very hard, and no outside help was allowed. I probably spent about 15 hours a week on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: not supportive
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: When Amanda assigns tests/quizzes, she does not give you enough time especially when she has a lot of short answers. If you do not use the specific wordings that she uses, you will simply not get credit. Overall, she is a pretty tough grader and really doesn't seem to care about her students.

Bad reviews are mainly in response to the class as a whole. Amanda does a good job of communicating grading criteria as well as subjects covered in exams. TONS of dropped assignments, effective teaching. Took off a point because she's mean to the other professor who teaches the second half of this course. You disrespect Donald, you disrespect me.

She is very well-spoken and I really enjoyed her lectures! I think most people complaining probably didn't do a lot of the work because Prof. Hoepfner has a system built in for students who are unable to make some classes, miss assignments/quizzes. She drops a lot of your lowest scores, so people probably just used all of theirs and needed more.

Most people on here are just whining because Amanda didn't change her class structure to accommodate students who didn't do the bare minimum. She is an interesting and knowledgeable professor. 1620 is rather easy; go to class and study the quizzes/exam objectives provided and you'll do very well. The videos she provides and the lectures are great.

Amanda should not be teaching. I took her course this semester which was online due to COVID. Amanda could really care less about her students though. When asked if she could drop one of the quizzes (asked by multiple students throughout the semester) she promptly refused without giving any reason, which contributed to my grade in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really interesting class. Lots of homework, in-class activities, clicker questions (doesn't require much effort though). Quizzes were fairly in line with the material learned. Professor cares a lot about this subject so expect a somewhat passionate lecture tone.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Hoepfner is an organized and straight-forward teacher. If you do the pre-class quizzes (3 tries & super easy), post-class assignments (graded easily!), and quizzes you will do fine. She drops so many assignments and attendance, so there's definite leniency for students. TL;DR - go to class, learn content, succeed -quizzes are basic knowledge
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She makes no effort to accommodate for or help out students undergoing extenuating circumstances, ESPECIALLY with COVID going on and with students needing more leniency and flexibility with their classes. Even after reaching out several times for extra help or resources, or even a little flexibility, she is very condescending and hard to work with.

Really hope no one else has to take multiple classes from Amanda. Honestly ruins the biology department. She tries to teach learning habits to college kids like they are toddlers. Ex. 12 clickers a class to make sure you show up when the lectures are recorded anyways. Incredibly inefficient and thinks she's more important than everything else. Run
Terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: When you listen to her lectures she seems like a good professor, however, she does not care about what is going on in your life, all she cares about is if you turn is homework on time, no exceptions. NONE. She is too preachy and is really a stick in the mud when you need some wiggle room. Doesn't care if you're affected by COVID-19. NOT ONE BIT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hoepfner made the class full of interesting material incredibly boring and tedious. She gave multiple assignments a week (2 pre-class quizzes, 2 worksheets, 2 drawing assignments, and a post-class quiz, plus clicker quizzes through the videos). She was also not an understanding professor at all. I would not take from her ever again.

It's the absolute worst how professors in intro classes feel the need to make their classes as hard as possible not realizing we have other classes too. I ended up missing an assignment because of some medical issues, and she refused to accept my late homework. I learned more teaching myself than I did from Professor Hoepfner.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She seems passionate about her work and that is a good thing, however, she lacks the professional nature of professors. She stated that we were not allowed to submit regrades because we had abused them. If she was more professional and understanding she would be a world class professor. I hope she becomes more understanding of grades and situations
Good professor, but tests are a bit difficult, where the wording of the problem messes you up, and TA's and LA's dont know much about the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hoepfner was the best of the three professors teaching BIO 1620. Colin was terrible, and Don was okay, but it was like this was their first semester ever teaching a university class. Amanda, on the other hand was organized, and delivered the material in a way that was understandable. Definitely the best out of the 3 profs teaching bio 120

Avoid if you can. Dr. Hoepfner is nice enough but takes up a lot of class time with random assignments that feel like junior high busywork. There are 2+ quizzes and 2+ weird homework drawings due every week. This class isn't hard, but the routine of it is exhausting. It's a shame that such exciting material is handled in such an ineffective way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was very nervous going into this class having little background in biology. She made it very clear on the first day that she wants you to succeed and that your effort is the only thing that will allow you to do that. She loves what she teaches and she makes you love and live it. AMAZING CLASS, BETTER PROFESSOR!
She goes through the material quite fast but the homework is helpful and taking notes is a must. I enjoyed this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All of the lecture notes are posted online, but Amanda's lectures provide better ways to retain the information. Hold onto exams because they make it easier to study for the final exam. I got by with only studying for a few hours for each exam. There were always a few questions in the exams that we were never taught, so using the textbook is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a really nice teacher with pretty clear standards. You won't even need the book, just re read her slides. Prepare to do bad on the first exam, but it gets a lot easier from there. The exams are a lot simpler than you think they're going to be. Just pay attention and do the homework and you'll be just fine.

She goes through PowerPoints super quick in class, but all her notes and slides are posted online. I would recommend printing off the slides before class and taking notes of additional things she says on those notes. You really don't need the textbook. It might be a good study resource but DON'T BUY IT! If anything just check it out at library.

There is a lot of material covered in a short amount of time and there is a lot of homework, but it honestly is not hard if you stay on top of it. Best resource for this class: YOUR TA's!!!! Most of them hold weekly study sessions & discussions. They help a ton for studying for exams. Another tip: work on MasteringBio in groups so you can collab.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria
