reviews.comment: Spent very little time incorporating students into lectures. She is more interested in showing students how much she knows rather than teaching the subject itself. I would never recommend her as a Biology Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is my second time taking biology. I took it from another professor and failed miserably. I wanted to retake biology because I love the subject and Amanda is the BEST biology professor you will find! Her lectures are interesting and you can download them at home and study them. Mastering Bio isnt even that hard. I highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No makeup exams, which isn't atypical, but there are 3 possible points of extra credit throughout the ENTIRE semester so don't miss any. She constantly mispronounced important biological terms like nucleus & Drosophila, which was disconcerting. She seemed to be bad at keeping students' attention (but it was a big class, so I'll cut her some slack).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Be prepared to do a bunch of Mastering Biology homework. She makes 5 or so modules due on mondays, yet you won't get a good grade on them if you do them before monday. Each module has about 20-30 questions each, and can take a lot of time to get through. She also breezes through the powerpoints and expects you can write down everything in 30 sec
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Unreasonably fast-paced course, blazing through 3-5 chapters/week. Majority of grade is from exams, which are fairly difficult and graded incredibly slowly. She's not a very good public speaker, often conflating terms (homozygous vs heterozygous, etc) which can be confusing. Take with a different professor, if you can.

This is obviously a more difficult course, but she is a very good instructor, always positive and wants students to succeed. The only thing is the tests are written very hard (as it is a "weed out" class) but she is a good professor, you just need to keep up because she moves fast and work hard outside of class.

Gives way too much information on slides and expects you to write everything you can down in the 30 seconds you have to look at the slides. The only thing you'll be graded on is tests, homework never gets graded. She also went through 7 chapters in two weeks then had a test, while every other class is 10+ chapters behind.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty good for beginning bio. Only complaint is she goes through the lectures really fast, and if you distracted for a second, you are doomed. Syllabus isn't accurate at all, and a little test heavy. But she posts the lecture slides on canvas before the lecture so you can follow along. She sounds like she really likes her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Hoepfner is an amazing instructor. She really makes sure the class understands the material. Her lectures are very well organized and her PowerPoints are very helpful. Definitely one of the best professors I've had!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Exams are huge portion of your grade. Not very clear as to what are on the exams. Shes nice just a little bit overloading on info.

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. I love learning from people who are clearly passionate about their subject and about helping you learn more about it, which describes her. She's not the most polished lecturer, but she knows her stuff very well. If you study her slides and genuinely try to understand the concepts you'll do well in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Hoepfner is very enthusiastic about what she's teaching, but with a huge lecture hall, it's sometimes difficult to keep up. She goes through slides fast but does provide them online to view. Her tests aren't the easiest but if you study well you'll be fine. She also gives quite a bit of work outside of class. This is not a class to slack off in.

I took this class fall semester of my freshmen year and reading the reviews on here were definitely very scary, but I do have to say she is a really great professor you defiantly do have to work, but if you manage your time and make sure you study for an hour each day its possible to do super good, you just have to try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amanda is a new teacher. Just a couple years ago she was my cell bio TA. As a fresh PhD, it wasn't the best lecture class, but she really cares and tries. She's enthusiastic about the material, and her own orangutan research is cool. I know she'll improve with each class she teaches, so don't write her off yet. Lots of slides & clickers.

reviews.comment: She was a great professor! Graded by exams and clicker questions. Her lectures were clear and she only tests you on what she has on her slides. Her slides are available to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A majority of the time I had no idea what was going on in this course because of her poor teaching style. It's hard to remain engaged in this class because her power points are extremely boring and useless. I did well because I am dedicated to biology, but otherwise I would've failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amanda is not my favorite teacher by any means, her lectures were confusing and she would fly through 80 slides in a 50 minute class. I got B's on all of the tests, so it is possible to do well but takes dedication. I don't highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amanda was a fine professor, seemed to really care about what she was teaching and wanted students to learn. My only complaint is some of the questions on her tests aren't quite clear, but if you study diligently you should do fine in spite of this.

Look, this seemed hard when youre taking it but if you go to class, put in the effort to study and do the quizzes twice, you should be ok. The class averages were always around 60 for the test. She has anywhere between 60-110 slides per-lecture so dont even take notes, just print the slides off and study those. If youre a pre-med, take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amanda was honestly one of the worst professors I have encountered in my educational journey. to put it plainly she is there to do research, not to teach and she really does not care whether you understand the material or do well in class at all. She talks extremely fast during lecture and explains things extremely poorly. Do not recommend at all.

This class was great! A lot of reading, but if you keep up with it is definitely doable. Exams are open note so make sure to organize all your notes and things well! Attendance isn't mandatory but going to lecture really helps. You can also participate in studies for extra credit which is so worth it and a cool experience!
Terribly hard tests, goes so fast you have no idea what he's talking about.
Lecture videos are available online, tests are open note, book is helpful to read, he's responsive and a great professor. Highly recommend. Great interactive classes with guests once in a while.
Super easy class. He isn't the most engaging when it comes to lectures, so I skipped most of them and got an easy A. You can also look at your notes on exams which was super helpful.

Amazing lectures, goes a little fast but once you get used to it it becomes super clear. Quizzes and assignments out of class helped me a lot to understand what I missed, and the slides are so clear with material. Exams are open note and timed, but Dr. Inman makes class easy to learn material while also getting a good grade. Will be taking again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Inman is an excellent professor who truly cares for his students. He is always willing to talk with you after class and even goes as far as scheduling Zoom meetings for any questions. Overall a super smart professor who comprehensively covers a lot of essential topics. Tests are hard; take good notes and study hard.

Prof Inman is a great, flexible, and passionate instructor who definitely wants everyone in the class to succeed. However, if you are not a psych major, I would urge you to be aware that this course covers a TON of science/anatomy heavy material in an extremely short window of time. No breaks. Open note tests yes, timed, also yes. Difficult/fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very knowledgable professor, always willing to help. I learned so much in this class and looking back it was one of my favorite classes. Tests are weighted heavily. They are open book but there is so much material that you will need to spend a lot of time studying. Writing project, but you only write a few paragraphs a week.

Dr. Inman comes across as passionate about the material , as well as caring of his students. Dr. Inman and his TA were responsive, accommodating throughout the semester, and fostered a safe learning environment. Beware: this is an exam heavy course, your knowledge will be truly tested and can greatly impact your grade. Overall, good experience!

Good Professor! Inman is very knowledgeable about the course, and I ended up learning more in this class compared to others of this level. Be warned that this class is one of the most difficult courses the psychology major offers, at a 2000 level class. Don't be fooled by the open-book exams and weekly papers, be prepared to spend hours studying.

I took 3210 from Dr. Ibarra last spring and I will always stand by the idea that he is the best professor the department has! He is passionate but never overbearing and always treats students with respect and also knows how to have fun. Handouts are great and we were allowed to use them and the codebook for exams. Steel is a good design elective.

He tends to get distracted sometimes during lectures, which can be a waste of time and frustrating. However he is not a boring teacher, which is beneficial. Gives resources for tests that arent too difficult. Not much homework.

He is a decent teacher. I like the handouts he gives, which make it very easy to follow complex topics in class. Homework was difficult but the exams were straightforward and always related to the homework.
Great professor. Challenging in a good way and very knowledgable and enthusiastic.

Probably my favorite professor i've had at the U. I had him for 3210 as well. Super nice and entertaining, he provides hand outs that make notes and class really easy to understand. Tests are very similar to homework and are open note, open book. Only downside is if you miss class he usually doesn't post notes or material from class

At the time of this review, I don't have my final grade yet. But I do fear that I will have to retake the class again. I wish Luis taught the class in the spring because he is such a great professor! He was very witty in class and tried his best to pass most of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very good teacher, the handouts are super valuable to the class. given my current grade I run the risk of needing to retake the class but I would happily do it with this professor again. The tests matter to your grade more than anything and if you miss class you need to make an effort to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took structural analysis with him and loved him, was happy I could take steel as well the following semester. I love the way he presents, he provides you with handouts that make note taking much, much easier and provide you with everything you need for exams and homework. Exams follow the homework and what you learn in class. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rich is the GOAT. If you are taking Physics II at the U, take it from him, especially if you are a pre-health student. He is one of the nicest and funniest guys you will ever meet. He does everything he can to help you feel confident in your ability to do well in physics and succeed in your career.

Rich is so kind and genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. However, his lectures are not very applicable to the homework or exams. You will spend a lot of time studying certain topics just for them to not appear on the exams, and vice versa. This class was frustrating but the curve made it doable.

Physics is daunting as a pre-health student who needs a good grade, but Rich makes it very digestible and easy to do well. His lectures are funny, and most of the actual learning and problem solving happens during the discussions. Just make sure to study for the exams, even if you do just alright, you'll earn an A in the end.

Good teacher, makes the subject material fun with demonstrations and the like.
Make sure you study for the tests and you'll do perfectly well.

Rich is a great guy, built the grading so there is a low chance you even fail with missing a few assignments. Class was built for a pre med student because all the questions were all retired mcat questions.

Rich seems like a nice guy. Often times his personability got in the way of his teaching, making his lectures pretty meaningless. Most of what I learned was from the discussion sections. The class was trivially easy, tho. I missed like 10 discussions and 4 assignments and still squeaked by with an A-. If you want an easy A, take physics with Rich.

Rich was amazing for physics. His lectures were engaging and funny, and he gave in class quizzes which were super simple and easy. Discussions were where most of the physics was learned, led by the TAs. Attend class class and discussion most of the time and you will end with an A. The exams are hard, but curved heavily. There was also no final exam

Super easy for physics. Sweet man. He is not a great lecturer and goes on side tangents a lot but go to discussion and you'll be fine. Attendance is mandatory because most days there are quizzes but they total to 2% of your grade. Class is curved heavy because exams are hard. No final which is nice.

Rich was my favorite professor of this semester. He was so funny, caring, personable, and just knew a lot of what he taught. You can tell he really cares about this, and his patients. You should definitely take a class with him.

Best prof ever. To be completely honest, he doesn't really teach that much. Discussion is where you learn everything you need in the class, and the only reason to go to the lecture is to get the code for the lecture quiz and listen to his jokes. He has a textbook, but you don't have to read it; it can help with studying, however.

Rich is such a good professor. He respects all his students as equals to him, and can recognize when it's time to take a short break from a long lecture. He will do everything in his power to help you understand the material, and the grading curve is very forgiving.

Rich is a very funny man who has great stories. He can get distracted and go off on tangents but, I found it helpful as it kept me engaged. He actually wants his students to succeed and get an A. Physics is a hard topic so its not gonna be easy but Rich makes it manageable.

this guy was amazing, genuinly my favorite professor. he made the daily quizzes pretty simple, but i had to understand a lot of the material on my own. the only thing was each exam (3 in total) were mcat questions, but you get a cheat sheet. there is also no final.

Dr. Ingebretsen is a really chill professor. He really wants ALL of his students to succeed, and gives around 3 attempts on each quiz and allows unlimited retakes on exams (provided that you reach out to the TA.) Honestly, a very informative and interesting class, even though I took it for the credits. He also hands out random extra credit!
One of the best professors you could ever take, especially if you are pre-healthcare or fitness oriented and want to learn phycics through the lens of the human body

Rich is a great guy.  The lectures are 80 minutes long, and there is a small attendance quiz at the end of every class.  Those things are wicked easy if you're awake and have a pulse.  The exams are curved heavily.  They're taking questions from retired MCATs and applying physics properties to them.

Everyone should take intro to wilderness med. I learned so many interesting and valuable things about outdoor topics including water purification, injury treatment, proper clothing and footwear, so much more. Anyone who loves being outdoors should take this. He has great stories and is always so accomodating! Thank you Rich!!!!

He thinks he is funny but can't teach well. He should go into the stand-up comedy industry rather than school. His course involves tons of medical school content, extremely hard for international students to understand those terms, but the physics part is super easy, just middle school level.

Professor Rich makes this class super engaging. Lectures are captivating, no need to attend if you have the zoom link. Exams are a breeze with practice tests - unstuckstudy was a lifesaver too. Easy A, would 100% recommend this class!

Rich is a nice professor, but he is here just to hear himself talk. He has never done a complete practice problem in class- only jokes and talks conceptually about physics. The exams are retired MCAT questions so they are hard, and Rich will NOT prepare you. You have to learn everything on your own or in discussion. But at least he curves!
rich has super fun and has entertaining lectures and was very kind and accommodating of any circumstances that may arise.

Few professors I have met who care a lot about their students like Rich. I felt like I rarely had to rely on outside material and learned a lot from his class. You just have to attend. Don't miss lecture, and don't miss the discussions and you will get an A.

Professor Rich is a good professor. He is patient and has a sense of humor. However, he can not deeply explain the physics concepts and formulas. And, the exam emphasizes the conceptualization of physics. So, if you need to take this course and get a good grades, you need to learn more after class. Finally, I grade scale is reasonable.

Rich is a nice professor who will teach you physics and tell lots of stories. Lectures aren't mandatory, but discussions were with two graded quizzes (one individual and one group) twice per week. "Hard" exams since most don't attend lectures, but no problem if you pay attention and do practice quizzes. The course gets curved, so most get A grades.

Rich was one of the best professors I've had. He made lectures very interesting to listen to and showed genuine care for students both in and out of class. Rich has a very clear passion for what he teaches that is infectious. If you're thinking about taking this course, do it!
Reviews talking about his teaching style are likely students who didn't attend lecture. It was not mandatory, but as someone who went I relied very little on outside material

Amazing guy. Most of the reviews talking about a "disorganized" teaching style are likely students who did not attend lecture (it was not mandatory). But as someone who did show up, there was very minimal outside material i needed to use.

I'm cheating a little bit. I'm still taking the class, but this is the first time I've taken from a professor at the U and felt strongly enough to write a positive review for a professor. Most of the time, I want to get on here and talk about how bad someone is. Rich is amazing. He's humble and funny. His lectures are great, in my opinion.

Would 1000000% recommend taking this class with Dr. Rich! Such a laid back professor with interesting lectures. Don't need to attend class, he has a zoom link for every class, just need to show up for exams. Exams are easy, he gives you practice tests and that's all you need to pass. One short paper that can be written on any topic you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you spend ANY time outdoors, especially in the mountains, you need to take this class. We learned so much about backcountry safety. With the amount of outdoorsy folks at the U, this class will save lives and Rich is one of the best professors I've ever had. He makes an effort to get to know you and his lectures/stories are always fascinating.

Richard was visually a very knowledgeable and passionate guy. He made every class a welcoming setting and he made sure to invest time in his students. He ensured I kept a good grade on sick leave for 3 weeks. He made an amazing and beneficial textbook/website for this class, that I found extremely helpful and interactive.

Rich is an incredible teacher. His lectures were funny and informative. The demonstrations were helpful and anything unclear could be found in the textbook. We had one paper but it was only one page long and we could use AI. The exams were easy if you had paid attention. Great class if you are looking for an easy and fun GedEd.
Rich is great! I would recommend this course, especially if you are premed.

Each day I went to class hoping to learn and left disappointed. He spent class time going on tangents and talking about his personal life, and he spoke insensitively about social issues. He wrote the textbook and it's very disjointed, but if you memorize what it says you can get his ambiguous test questions right for a good grade. Avoid his class.

Rich is a super nice guy. He really talks to you like you are a real human being instead of a robot student. That said, his class drove me nuts. I never really knew what I was supposed to be learning. He curves heavily to account for this, so don't fear. You can score high fairly easily, but you won't master much physics for future endeavors.

Rich is such a kind and caring person, but his class drove me crazy. I woke up early to get to his 8am lecture, but then we never actually learned physics. He mostly taught about anatomy. I had to teach myself the entire class. There are absolutely NO assignments besides tests and quizzes. We also never knew the grading scale until after the final.

Rich is such a nice guy, but it's hard to defend his lectures/tests/teaching style. So scatterbrained, off topic, learned a lot about wilderness medicine but it is a college physics class. Grading scale is easy but be prepared to relearn all of physics when taking the MCAT or other tests

Incredible professor with so much experience. His lectures are fascinating and allows the students to be extremely engaged in wilderness medicine. There are 4 exams throughout the semester and one paper, that is literally all you have to do for this course. Would 100% take this class & this professor if you can!

Very easy, but a very disorganized/useless class.  In terms of tests, they aren't' even that bad- an (A) cutoff is a 75% and you can easily score above 85% on all exams, even though he "claims" they are MCATquestions. Don't even bother showing up to lectures if you need to take this class- just read the textbook, go to discussions, you'll be set!

DO NOT TAKE PHYSICS WITH RICH. He is incredibly unclear on what materials will be on the exams and states the last one isn't cumulative until four days before the exam is scheduled he says it is on previous material too. His exams are retired MCAT questions, but HELLO not everyone is going to med school. Never lectures about physics (only running)
Great teacher

Rich is a super nice guy, and his class is structured to reflect his desire for the success of his students. I took this over the summer, so it was fast-paced and hard to retain info. The exams are hard, but he grades on an MCAT grading scale where 50% is good. He doesn't teach super well. Had to rely on TAs and Khan Academy to save my grade.

An amazing professor! He is my favorite instructor so far at the University of Utah. Extremely knowledgeable incorporating a lot of fun demonstrations that you'll remember. The text is easy to read and engaging. Quizzes and quick assignments on each chapter. No final. One paper. Dr. Ingebretsen is the best!

Rich is such a homie and one of the coolest people ever! He has many important responsibilities outside of this class, but he still cares a ton about this class and will do anything to help people succeed. I appreciated how he gave us the opportunity to learn in the way that works best for us, while also giving us lots of good resources.
He is really funny! I would defiently reccomend this class.

He's a nice guy, but that doesn't make up for him being a lousy professor. If you want to actually learn physics, do not take 2010 with him. He doesn't teach, and you're left scrambling to learn from the TAs during the discussion section. Exams were based off of old MCAT questions, but I certainly do not feel prepared for the MCAT.

Lectures are pointless. The TA's teach all the information. Everyone gets a good grade, but your performance on exams is totally up to luck. They are MCAT questions, but it is totally randomized so some people get really easy exams and other people get stuff we never learned.
Rich was one of my favorite professors. Bro was comedy and his lectures were fantastic. One of my favorite classes to attend.

The only thing I did in this class was try to think of ways I could kill myself using the concepts being taught. much like the "ball rolling off the cliff", I wanted to fall off of something tall and reach Vmax before impact.

He doesn't have a clear grading scheme and his lectures are all over the place. If you need an A you just hope. Hardest exams ever. He will tell you not to attend lecture at the beginning of class but you MUST in order to do well on the quizes. If you want an easy pass, take this class but if you want to learn something this isn't the way to go.

Take the class. Rich is amazing, and is one of the only professors that has offered to write me a letter of RECC. I have taken two classes from him, and both have been incredible. He's literally the bomb .com, I would highly recommend taking any of his classes.

Dr. Ingebretsen is the definition of a good guy. That being said, it is the easiest class with the least application. Most information was common sense, and I felt weirdly guilty for waisting so much tuition money on the class. Fun experience if you're looking for an easy A with friends!
BEST PROFESSOR EVER. Easiest class, super funny guy. You can tell he really cares about his students. 10/10 would recommend.

Rich is a gifted storyteller and clearly passionate about what he teaches. However, TA's run the Canvas course and the quizzes rarely match up with the content in class. He avoided me when I would bring up my grade, but thanks to consistently confronting him throughout the semester he finally helped me. Great guy, I just wish the Canvas was better.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rich does care about students but the class was tailored toward medical majors. Tests were retired MCAT questions, and the majority of the class got 50% on them. The lectures were wasted talking about random things and I essentially had to go to YouTube to understand concepts. He says everyone gets an A or B so it seems redundant to try hard.

This class was tough but that might be because I am not a fan of physics. Rich made this class very enjoyable and fun! he did many in class demonstrations which made concepts easier to learn. He was very accommodating and offered lecture in person as well as over zoom. He is such a caring professor and always wants to get to know his students!
He's super caring and wants you to learn physics instead of stressing about your grade. Personally, I didn't attend many lectures and found it more useful to self-study.

Rich is a really good person but his class was way harder than an introductory physics course should be. Class averages on tests were 50% usually. The homework covered stuff that we never talked about in class or what we looked over in class taken to the extreme. Also we never reviewed any material leading up to tests, covered new stuff day before.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The nicest guy ever, and he really cares about all of his students.

Rich is literally the coolest person alive. From his medical career, to his outdoor advocacy, to all the stories he tells in class you will want to be his best friend. Honestly he wants to be your best friend, too. He knows his stuff, he understands, he cares. Its an easy A and you learn so much. If you spend time outdoors, take this class.

Literally the coolest guy ever. Always tries to be engaged with students. Most of the class is him going off the topic of the lecture and sharing his own experiences as a doctor/person in the wilderness, but it's actually very interesting and still educational. A good class to take if you love the outdoors, and want an easy A.

I'm a freshman this year and I was worried about how I'd be able to handle classes. This professor is very understanding, caring, and is always encouraging students to come up to him after class to talk about anything you're struggling IN or OUTSIDE of class. His lectures are easy to follow, taking light notes and attending his fun demonstrations.
Rich attempts to get to know each and every one of his students, he's laid back and overall a good professor! Quizzes and Exams are super easy as long as you read the textbook!

Subjective: quizzes are based on what he says entirely and have nothing to do with the material that was intended for each particular quiz. Talks about himself all the time, so if you listen + take notes, the quizzes do not match. He draws the bones instead of showing anatomy, completely incompetent doctor. Do not be fooled by his self-promotion!

Rich had to be my favorite professor this year. He is very understanding of students, especially student athletes. He said that no one has gotten lower than a B in his class in the last 20 years! The lectures were always interesting, and this felt more like a sports med class rather than physics if anything.

Just an amazing professor. Very well respected due to his easy going nature, kindness, and knowledge. I accidentally missed an online quiz and instead of giving me zero, he simply used my previous quiz score. Highly recommend taking a class with him at least once!

Rich is a super cool guy!! I took this class as a general education credit and I would definitely take another class with him again. Super funny and laid back professor who genuinely cares about each and every student of his. We need more professors like Rich!

Rich, is a classy dude. He encouraged our class to send him a biography about ourselves. He did a great job of navigating this class as we were required to take it online. I have to say he's probably one of my favorite professors. He understands that you have other commitments but in the summer it does go double speed. His TA's were a huge asset.

Rich is one of my favorite professors. His class is extremely interesting. He does his best to make learning fun. Gives great lectures and tells stories, that are applicable to the course. Truly cares about his students. Rich is always happy to help and guide his students. Assignments/quizzes are fairly easy.

Rich is an amazing guy. He loves what he does and loves his students. His class is ridiculously easy and he pretty much tries to give all his students an A. His lectures are funny and interesting and he brings in lots of guests. Rich is probably my favorite professor i've taken at the U and I would take his class again in a heartbeat.

Rich is easily one of the best professors i've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and their success. He is very considerate and knows that his class is not the only class you are taking. He keeps homework at a minimum and truly cares that you are learning and understanding concepts. Ten thumbs up for this guy.

Rich is the man! Physics can be a very tough subject, but he cares about you as an individual and he wants you to pass. I don't think we failed anybody in either 2010/2020 this semester I took it. He works with you and your grade is based of how everyone is doing in the class, not a black and white cut off line for each grade. Take from him!

Really funny and kind guy, but he was pretty disorganized and seemed to burn out a bit at the end of the class. He talked a lot about medical applications for the physics concepts, which is probably great if you're a premed student. I'd recommend him, but only if you're able to learn from textbooks and not just lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Rich is an amazing person, and I absolutely loved his lectures because they were entertaining and interesting. However, I didn't enjoy his style of teaching at all. He is very disorganized and goes on major tangents every 10 minutes. The tests were difficult because Rich doesn't write them. Its an easy A because everything is curved.

Rich has to be one of the best professors at the university. He has the most amazing stories to tell and is very good at breaking down difficult concepts. He cares about every student and wants them to succeed. If you have the chance tot are a class form him, do it! You wont regret it.
Super kind, really cares about his students. He has amazing stories and makes classes entertaining. He doesn't teach what you don't need to know, and is clear with what he will test on.

This is the perfect class to fulfill a science gen ed! It's all useful stuff about the body. Lots of cool in-class demonstrations. Quizzes and tests online except for the final. There are usually a few test questions that only come from the class lectures so try to be there.

Rich is incredible and his class is actually entertaining. The assignments and quizzes can be a little tricky at times but they are all take home and you can use the book (and friends). This was a great first college course. I learned a lot, there were a lot of fun science demos, and honestly just take this class because Rich is a teddy bear.

I love Rich. Nicest professor, and he truly cares about his students. He knows his stuff (PhD in physics and also a medical doctor) and the demonstrations were excellent. I think this is the best professor I've had thus far. I don't usually enjoy physics, but everything learned can be reflected in normal life, so it was well worth it.

I do not have interest in the medical field, so I took Ingebretsen's course as a general elective. Long story short, if I had to take any general elective, I would want a professor like Ingebretsen. The lectures were enjoyable and he does a great job of making the material fun to learn. Seriously, he is an incredible professor.

I took this class for a GE requirement that fulfills my "Physics" credit, and I'm so glad I took it instead of an actual physics class. It helped relate more to my major. HW is super easy. Rich is a gem. He tells you exactly what will be on the exam. Exams are super easy. If you need help during exams, he doesn't hesitate to help. Great class.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had! You learn so much from him, not just about the subject but about life. He is so nice and funny and is the kind of person you want to be around. He cares about his students and will do so much for them. Even though the class is easy, I have learned more from his class than the last 4yrs in engineering.

Rich is the next Bill Nye. He just cares that you learn and he will do whatever needed to make sure you to well in his class. He is the funniest teacher and always entertaining. The class is super easy.

Rich is a real sport. He's hilarious, has funny stories to tell, and generally has really fun classes. He tries really hard to make sure all of his students do their best, learn what they can, and have a really good time. He's the real MVP.
So nice
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected

reviews.comment: Rich is super freaking awesome. His class is interesting, his lectures are precise, and he is entertaining, which really helps keep focus. He is passionate about medicine and physics, and is a great professor.  Go out of your way to take physics from him. You will not regret taking it over the summer, and you will have an excellent professor.

Rich is easily the best professor I have had during my time at college. He truly cares about his students and does everything he can to help students learn and be successful. He uses demonstrations and videos to keep his lectures interesting. You will not regret taking a class from Dr Ingebretsen.

Rich is probably one of the coolest professors I have had my entire college career. Truly a awesome guy! He teaches an interesting class, and makes it super easy to understand. I thoroughly enjoyed this class -- and I highly recommend it to anyone and everyone!

Rich was a very entertaining professor and the class certainly has some educational value, but around test time it can be difficult to grasp what his expects you to know. He was also tough to get a hold of outside of class, as he can be disorganized, so his canvas is confusing. Otherwise, Rich does a great job.
Dr. Ingebretsen is hilarious and an all-around awesome guy.  Plus, the class is an easy A.

Rich is an amazing person and professor. Though I do wish he were a tad bit more organized, the pros cancel out that one con. He knows what he's talking about both in medicine and in outdoor recreation, and he's a super fun and hilarious guy. I learned so much in this class and you should absolutely take it hands down.

Rich is dope!! Such a good teacher! Really cares about the students and them succeeding. Gives you every opportunity possible to succeed. Easier class to take to fulfill a Gen-Ed requirement. Helps out all the time and likes to get to know you. Lots of demonstrations that are awesome. Also pretty funny.

Awesome professor. I highly encourage that you take this class, it's incredibly interesting and he makes lectures fun. Tests are easy enough if you study for them. Definitely go to class and take notes on the lecture. Wildly helpful on the study guides and tests. TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOURE INTERESTED IN STUDYING MEDICINE OR DO A LOT OF OUTDOORS THING

I highly recommend avoiding this class in the summer. I thought I would just get it over with but it bit me. So condensed and Shawn, the course marshall, is extremely hard. They gave out six A's out of 100ish students. Take it another time.
super cool professor
LOVED HIM! Funny and a very nice professor and at the end of the day he just wants us all to succeed in the class.

Funny teacher, very laid back on grading, which I appreciated.  Organization could have been a little better, but since I was coming straight from an overlapping class, it actually helped me not miss much of the lecture, so worked out in my favor.  ;)
Great teacher! Great demonstrations and funny. I would defiantly suggest taking physics over the summer with Richard. Its a lot of work for the summer but defiantly worth him as a teacher.

Got a 75 in physics this summer and got an A in both 1 and 2. The tests are very hard, his TA who doesn't come to class writes them so it is very hard to study for, but If you're dreading physics, take his summer classes, you get them both over with and it is relatively painless.

Rich hands out good grades to everyone. If you get in the 90s on every test, it doesn't matter because people that didn't work as hard will also get an "A". His lectures weren't organized, it seemed that he was unaware of what  he had to cover that day.  I learned all of the physics from the book and from the TAs. He also doesn't write the tests.

His lecture is not organized. So sometimes assignment and lecture are not related each other. Moreover, he does not make test. But TA who makes Test problem does not come to class. So I do not recommand this class.
Rich is awesome! He is one of the nicest professors you will ever meet and would do anything for his students. The class isn't hard and he didn't fail a single person this summer!

I don't know if this rating should go here. He was listed as the professor for this class but I only met him once. It's an MCAT prep class with a new teacher each week.  The class is super easy, show up, take the quizzes, get an A. It wasn't all that useful though. It helps for a quick overview and to stress you into studying.

He is one of my favorite professors/people in my entire college career (if not my VERY favorite). He's hilarious, so knowledgable & makes the class SO much more interesting than a simple lecture! He makes the class and material fun and it's things that you'll actually be able to use in your life. I'd recommend this class & this professor to anyone!
He is my FAVORITE professor. EVER. TAKE HIS CLASS. doesn't even matter which one. PHY3110 was awesome.
Best professor ever

Rich is such a nice relatable guy. He doesn't really care about grades, he is just out to teach and for you to actually learn! Great information taught! I would definitely recommend taking this class! The demonstrations and guest lectures are awesome! Attendance is not required, but I never wanted to miss a day! :)

Rich is an amazing teacher.  He cares a lot about making sure you understand the topics.  It is a very easy class if you have taken or are in hard classes like anatomy, physiology, etc.  He's amazing!

Rich is by far, the most awesome professor I have had at the U. He is very funny, incredibly nice, and very passionate about what he is teaching. I have taken two courses literally only because of the fact he is teaching them. I would HIGHLY recommend  him to anyone.

Rich is an amazing professor.  His classes are fun and interesting, he wants everyone to do well, and he really cares about his students. Also, I asked him for a letter of recommendation and he submitted it the very next day.  Great guy.
This guy is the man. Who would complain about an easy yet good and interesting Physics class. I haven't ever commented on here but will for this guy. Great and easy class.

SUMMER PHYSICS I&II: Very challenging.  Have your TAs setup ALL the online HW every day before you go home and don't fall behind.  Lecture not very helpful. PHYSICS OF THE HUMAN BODY and WILDERNESS MEDICINE: super easy upper level classes for the semester when you are also taking hard classes like Organic Chem, Anatomy, Physiology, etc. (his words)
I loved to going to this class. Rich is the coolest Professor. I am so glad I took this  class.

Richard is one of the best teachers and mentors on campus.  The class is easy, but he is more concernd about you learning and enjoying the topics he lectures on.  Take advantage of his wisdom and knowledge and friendship.  I absolutely love this man and he goes above and beyond for his students to help them in whatever they need. He is the man!
Rich is the best prof. I have had, even though I haven't taken any classes from him for several semesters he still remembers my name.  He really cares about the success of his students.
No Comments
Rich is the most friendly, down to earth professor at the school
best professor in the department
Rich is rare in respecting pre-professional students as a professor. He is funny and clear, and is not scraed of giving A when earned. Truly one of the best around.
Funny, very smart, very clear and helpfull. I loved the class and got my best grades ever.

Taking his class online right now, its very easy but ive never had a teacher slower to grade, the final is due in 2 days and he still hasn't graded anything in over 2 months. Taking it online is an easy A, Im pretty sure he doesn't check for AI. I have gotten 100% on every single assignment with minimal effort.

While the class was fairly easy, it did not help my writing skills at all. The concepts taught were very fundamental, and feedback was very robotic and did not add anything to my writing. Class time felt pointless as when there were topics taught they were not concise and were reiterated multiple times due to the professor's lack of clear english.

He graded papers extremely late, giving feedback on first drafts a day before the due date of the final draft, making it difficult to revise or predict our grade. Some feedback was very inconsistent with my paper, like ChatGPT wrote it. ChatGPT likely graded the papers too. Attendance is mandatory; class is unenjoyable and useless.
The class is incredibly boring, he grades with AI and his feedback is also blatantly AI. This would not be an issue if there weren't participation points. The class is an easy A though.

Genuinely a waste of time. I don't know why I pay thousands of dollars for a class like this. Grading is based off of YOU teaching the class, 3 writing assignments, and a final. Asked about how the final will look like a week before because we learned nothing, and she had no idea what it was going to be and said to just "study all the material".

This is one of the worst Comm classes. The structure of the class is a disaster. Majority of the teaching is pushed onto the students having to do presentations every Monday for the whole duration of the class. Your entire grade is based off your presentation, 3 writing assignments, and a final exam. I haven't learned anything all semester.

This class is poorly structured, with about 80% of teaching pushed onto students through presentations and group work. The professor rarely lectures, making it hard to stay engaged or learn. Paired with excessive reading and low-effort instruction, it feels like a waste of time. As a senior, this is the worst class I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: All I can say is nope.

Just don't. She has the students teach half of the lessons within the semester, so I'm really not sure what my tuition is going toward here. Boring lectures, unclear instructions on assignments, no rubric/examples provided, hosts class discussions but shoots down every opinion other than her own, and uses her own writings as required texts. Run.

I am three weeks into this class, and my word of advice is pray. She is very strict on the tiniest details and no grace. She does not offer any help when presented with a question.The coursework is interesting, but the way she teaches takes the joy out of what I'm learning. She isn't passionate about anything and is very transactional when teaching

She doesn't care about students learning. Her teaching and lectures will put you to sleep and she sucks at teaching. If you need help in this class, DON'T GO TO HER. She doesn't teach well. She's extremely strict on cheating and late work. In all four years I've never had someone so strict about late work even if there were a family emergency, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seemed like a really nice woman but man this was my least favorite class I have ever taken at the U. Profoundly boring. If it is a required class find a different professor. It is an easy A if you do the assignments on time but its not worth it. She did not seem like she wanted to be teaching. I hope she figures it out.

If I could do it again, I'd wait for a different professor. She said she was doing one thing for the final exam then changed it completely last minute on the last week. The final exam study presentation was not helpful at all. Never take this class if its not a requirement. Absolute BS. I dont know how they do it in Germany but this was not it.

It doesn't seem like she wants students to succeed. It was nearly impossible to get her to make necessary course adjustments for students to do well. She is so paranoid about cheating that it inhibits learning and overall doesn't work with students. I would wait until there is a different professor. TA's were great and they even struggled with her
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor reads directly off the slides and provides very little information beyond that. The quizzes were too short to test students' knowledge and this issue was tweaked a little by making the questions easier. The labs were not based on the lectures and attendance was mandatory to maintain a good grade. This class did not feel engaging.

Not a clear or precise lecturer, lots of filler words. Attendance was valued over learning. This class did not feel very valuable. It had the chance to provide cool opportunities to research, but instead we just had weekly quizzes and a final. The TA's were nice, but the labs also only rewarded attendance. Overall, it was boring, disengaging, easy.

Uses tons of filler words, hard to follow through with lectures. 
We had to convince her to change her 5min/10q quiz, was not realistic with graphs and Q's being paragraphs. She changed it to short answers but same time and 10 Q's. Was at least doable. 
Had to go to class for quiz code in order to get points for participation.
The TA was great.

She definitely isn't a teacher I would choose to take a class with, but she wasn't bad. She is passionate about what she teaches, she isn't a harsh grader, and she can be pleasant to talk to. She has a problem with students leaving lectures to go to the bathroom, and she doesn't accept late work. Tell her what she wants to hear and you'll pass.

This course offers a severe lack of professionalism. I am a believer in respecting my professors, but that same respect was not granted back. Any questions, even for clarification, were taken as direct attacks of her abilities. This became a hostile environment where I learned nothing and was attacked for being outspoken. Would not recommend.

*TOOK HER INDIGENOUS RIGHTS CLASS FOR BUSINESS CREDITS* Hands down one of the worst teachers I have ever had. She was so disrespectful and rude towards her students and just should not be a teacher what so ever. Told a kid in front of the class that she wouldn't go anywhere in life and made him cry! So disappointed to waste money on this class!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Singled people out. She would make people act out the readings we did in class. It's a Spanish class, not an acting class so I'm not sure why it wasn't extra cred. No office hours. She didn't show much understanding for my circumstances and when people would ask questions or email she would very often shrug it off or respond with something snarky.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had her for BUS 3940. This teacher was disorganized and had priorities out of line. It's almost like she enjoyed seeing students suffer over succeeding. Test formats are not traditional and deadlines are strict but not clearly communicated. Be prepared to be given no leeway for human mistakes as a result of her lack of communicating expectations.

WOW... Never had a professor this disorganized ever. I took her for BUS 3940 and dropped after the first week because I know her class was going to be a waste of time. She assigned quizzes that had like 8 questions but would take hours because you're trying to navigate an outdated website which made it difficult to find the answers.

BUS3940. Class wasn't too hard. Lots of writing homework's, not that bad, but time consuming. 2 exams. A big group presentation. Just make sure you remember what's on the quizzes. Every test/quiz was taken at home (even final). You can't really have an opinion that differs from hers. Tell her what she wants to hear and you will get good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took her BUS 3940 class and she is one of the worst professors I have ever had. She grades assignments like its a PHD program and will mark off points if you forget to copy and paste the question. Doesn't even allow you to leave during class even if you have to use the bathroom. DO NOT TAKE HER

She is a fairly average teacher. The course was poorly designed to have the homework on a given topic due before the topic was covered. She also did a very poor job explaining assignments/quizzes/tests and most instructions were hard to follow since the Spanish grammar was not correct. Very kind and understanding, needs to improve course structure.

I had to take this class online because of the pandemic. She did a really good job organizing her Canvas page and assignments were fairly easy to complete, but they did take some time. She requires a lot of participation in class and isn't afraid to call you out. She is a relatively generous grader.

Really bad. Classroom environment is not respectful. She will call people out during class if they get up and leave. Assignments are just busy work with no obvious effort/creativity on her part. Extremely unorganized and assignment instructions are often confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got an A but easily could have received a C if I had been in a bad group. You can do great on everything in the course but if members in your group for the group essay and participation don't do their part, it can hurt your grade big time. Prof was very unorganized, her instructions were bad and full of spelling errors. Terrible online course.

This professor makes no sense. She sent out emails to my classmates and I stating our project's draft was great. Then she grade is the lowest of the class. My peers and I did not complaint because we were afraid that if we did it would affect our grades negatively.

Ashley may be spirited at times, but she truly challenges her students to put their best foot forward. Despite running at a fast pace, she's willing to work with you, given earnest effort, communication, and sincerity.

For our final presentation, she had us display our projects at a museum, adding excitement to the thought of joining the pro world

Received no grades til four days after semester's end. Projects were graded solely on InDesign/Photoshop presentation, despite only receiving feedback on our drawings during the semester, and few software lectures. No feedback was given on presentations, only heard critiques about our drawings, the quality of the drawing didn't go toward the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I initially thought the professor would be chill, but she was harsh, passive-aggressive, and intolerant. Projects that weren't her style were overly criticised. No creative freedom. She rarely responds to emails. Grades randomly fluctuated after months of no change. The syllabus/grading policy was extremely vague, but weaponized against students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking GEOG 1300 online through her. She's not good at providing pre-quiz and exam material to study for, and everything is timed, which is the issue. Waste of my time and effort, and not a subject that needs to be this hard, nor is it important for future business leaders.
I wish she was my aunt

Ingrid was an incredible professor. Took me a min to warm up to her but she's really hilarious and willing to help you. This class was phenomenal, I learned about environmental topics I haven't learned in any other enviro. class. Field trips are fascinating, I'm still grieving over the one I missed to the water treatment facility. Please take this!
Really amazing professor and class, wish I could take the class all over again.

Go to class and pay attention and you will do fine on all the exams and assignments. The classes are mostly group discussions, otherswise it is fieldtrips, guest lectures, or very few traditional lectures. There is not very much work outside of class and the few outside class assignemnts were pretty fun. She is very funny and personable.

W INGRID bro i actually looooved my class with her. she is so chill and extremely funny but won't hesitate to lecture you like ur mom if you don't turn your stuff in. she leaves it up to you to succeed and wants you to learn a lot but won't hold ur hand through the class if that's something you need. HIGHLY recommend! lots of laughs with ingrid.

Absolutely wonderful professor. I learned so much in her class and enjoyed myself doing it, assignments are flexible and engaging. She is strict on deadlines but gives you plenty of time to work on things. Lots of reading, I found that audiobooks were my friend for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There was a lot of material in this class and the only way to succeed is to show up every day. Ingrid was very funny and personable and made the lectures interesting. You aren't graded on very many things, just a couple quizzes & exams so just study and do every assignment.

I LOVE INGRID she is so so funny and really cares about getting to know her students' lives outside of the class. She started every class by asking us what was trending and what we'd been watching on TikTok and seeing on Instagram. Even though this class can be a little boring she provides great info and is an awesome lecturer.

This class had a lecture and a lab component. Ingrid always ensured we had enough time to do the assignments and her TA was super helpful during lab. We did coding using R with specific instructions so it wasn't hard and Ingrid made it clear what was on the final exam. We had a field trip, a guest speaker, and other units that were on the test.

attendance isn't mandatory but is highly recommended as the material is only available during lecture. the exams were difficult because it required a lot of note taking during lecture. you have readings and class discussions weekly and one group project. very little assignments but were easy to do. a great class but lectures were boring at times
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She is a great professor who cares about students in the class. If you skip, you're grade will likely suffer, especially if you skip field trips (which are fascinating, so don't skip them!)

Every class had a unique discussion topic, and participation in the discussions helps on the tests. Also, make sure to do the reading, it'll help you a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome professor hands down. Super funny and cares about her students, and the tests are shockingly easy (gives you a full notecard to take to the exam). She takes the class on fieldtrips, and brings in guest lecturers which are super interesting. Although attendance is not mandatory, not showing up to class will hurt your grade.

An easy A if you put in any effort at all. As long as you pay attention in class (definitely show up) and do the readings assigned for the units, you'll do great. Ingrid is super cool and leads some super interesting class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Reading material - bought my own books for this class but was only required to read a few select chapters within each book
Lots of in-class discussions and PowerPoint lectures only a few times
Tests are on paper and handwritten

I made an account just to write this review. Professor Weinbauer may be my favorite professor of all time. The workload in this course is very manageable and she is conscious of students' lives and other classes students are taking. I can't say the same about other GEOG professors at the U. She is very down to Earth and makes ENVST a pleasure.

Ingrid is amazing. Her lectures are engaging and she is really funny! Many field trips and readings. She is a sweetheart and willing to help. Make sure you do the work on time, no late work! I truly loved the content of this class and Ingrid made it 10x better. If you have to take this class, don't be stressed. A note card can be used on the exam.

Weinbauer is a really nice teacher. Tests are very lecture specific so it is important to pay close attention to the details of her lecture. If you need help, she is always willing to meet with you and help you. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, and while the lectures can be somewhat boring, she tries to help by adding discussion about interesting topics. Austrian accent, but easy to understand. Because of COVID-19, she let us choose to opt out of the final research paper, and the final was easy. Great teacher overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class a few years ago came back just to leave this comment. This was definitely my most favorite class in all my college years. If you're looking to fulfill some Gen Ed requirements, look no further than this class. Ingrid is very understanding and the class is a breeze to get through if you put some effort and is very educational.

Super great professor. She's great at teaching and covering the material. She's humorous and very knowledgeable about what the material. Creates a welcoming and friendly environment and created a classroom atmosphere that I wanted to come to everyday. The books she uses are super interesting and give good insights.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I loved Ingrid! Take her class! You need to show up to class and take notes, she won't put the notes online. You need to be ready to work, but I think that is what is so helpful because by the time the test roles around you are prepared! I learned so much! She made the class very fun and enjoyable. One of the best professors I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's got funny wit and is engaging. Class lectures were interesting imo. Has a German accent, but completely coherent to me. Tests are EASY; gave us sheets of questions beforehand. Really just an essay. She made them take-home tests. One end of semester 10 min. partner project presentation. Did it on bees. Easy A. Would def take professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's nice and has a slight German accent, but coherent. Her classes are just lectures, which might get boring after a while, but she can be funny. There's also labs, which includes coding (it's not hard, there's detailed instructions) and the TA is helpful. Both are accessible. There was one partner project at the end and the tests are EASY.

She is German so very strict. She does not have compassion and treats everyone the same but she is available for consultation to discuss how you can do better. As the semester went on, the class became less intense. She became chill and fun. Stick it out with her, she really knows her stuff. I took this class for a GEN ED.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: -Gives good feedback -Participation matters -Dont skip class -Lots of homework -Accessible outside class -Clear grading criteria -Hilarious -Test heavy -Extra Credit -Group projects -Lecture heavy --I really enjoyed taking her class. She was a very entertaining professor who loves teaching. I took her GEOG 3330-01 class, and I would recommend it!

Ingrid is very passionate about geography and you can see that in the way she teaches. The class is a lecture with a documentary every so often. If you want to learn about human geography this is the class to take.

Ingrid is great and I wish she taught more classes in the GEOG major. Lots of field trips and guest speakers. You read two fantastic books and she assigns three projects. She's a fair grader and she has a great sense of humor.

Professor Weinbauer is an amazing teacher who knows what she is talking about. Really knowledgeable about the subject she teaches. You never walk out of her class without learning a handful of new things/issues/ideas. She engages with the students to make classroom learning fun and enjoyable. I would definitely recommend taking a class from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was unorganized in the sense that she expected you to do a LOT of outside studying, but wouldn't really talk about the expectations for tests and quizzes. I was very lost in this class as far as what I needed to do to get an A. I never missed class, and did all the assignments and took notes, and never did well on tests, even with tutor.

Ingrid loves teaching geography and this is a class that you will gain so much knowledge from if you're willing to put in the work. It's a very interesting class if you go to class do the homework and study hard for the tests.

Ingrid is an excellent instructor. I often times disagreed with her point of view and I was still respected by her. She is demanding but fair. You will learn a lot from her regardless of the class you take from her. Highly Recommended.
Wonderful teacher, take home tests helped a lot! Attendance is needed, but well worth it. Loved this class considering taking more geology classes because of this one!

Attendance is not required, but highly recommended because tests are based solely/primarily on notes taken in class. She knows her stuff and also knows that it's only a 1000 level class, so she's not terribly concerned with you knowing specific details. Tests can be hard but overall, great teacher.
Good class, sometimes hands out too much work. she like group work.

Math 1090: I was nervous about this class since I hadn't done math in over four years, but Irina was amazing! She's so kind, helpful, and truly cares about her students. It's not an easy class, but with effort, you'll do well. Highly recommend her!

Math 1090: Honestly, she's a very nice professor. If you ever have concerns, she'll let you know what's going to be on the quizzes. Although she goes really fast during lectures and has a strong accent, I can tell she wants her students to succeed and gives you everything you need. She emphasizes the important things to study. Very straightforward.

Though her accent is thick, her work is very clear. She is a very nice lady, willing to help you succeed. Class is incredibly easy, most course content should've been taught in basic high school math. Tests are heavily weighted. She drops your couple lowest tests and quiz's making it easy even if you don't understand a couple concepts.

The teaching is rough and unclear, she does not go over notes very well and likes to skip ahead before anyone has written down the notes or solved the problem. Her Accent is strong making it hard to understand what she Is teaching most of the time, I tend to go home and watch YouTube videos to learn what was being "taught" in class.
Great course and amazing instructor.

The professor was great and kind. Deadlines weren't strict, and she was lenient, which I really appreciated. The class has a final project, so just be prepared for that,it could be the toughest part of the course.

Robotics with Dr. Simpson was an amazing and fun class! It is a lecture/lab, so you listen to her lecture for a bit, and then do some enjoyable labs that teach you about robotics. The labs are done in MATLAB and uploaded to an Arduino. Once you finish the lab, you get checked off, and that's it for the day! Some of the lab parts could be better.

A strict and rigorous curriculum (2 HW/Week, 4 Exams, Final Project). Very beneficial in understanding the material. Lectures may not be exciting, but are efficient leaving time for her to offer homework help. Homework doesn't take long, exams can be mostly straightforward except for 1 or 2 problems. She offers help on the final project. Very Kind.
The homework and exams were so difficult; I feel like I got PTSD from this class, LOL. Definitely don't take it if you have a choice!

I originally came at the start of the semester and gave her a poor rating. I should have just given it time. It's true she's not the most exciting lecturer ever but she is so kind and will give you every opportunity humanly possible to get an A in the class. I also really appreciate how efficient every lecture is. 1.5 hour lecture always is 45 mins
please do not take this class, come back and thanks me later

She seems incredibly unprepared whenever she is teaching the class. It seems like each time she does a problem on the board it's her first time seeing it and when you ask her about homework she second guessed herself ten times and gets the answer wrong. The only redeeming part is the class is so easy you don't need to show up. She seems confused.

This was the easiest class I've taken because most topics are covered in physics 2. Around 60% of her homework final answers had at least one wrong answer, and I'd have to email her to get them changed. Tests and homework are extremely simple, except for the final project, which is way too time consuming (preparing a 20 minute lecture > 2000 words)

Pretty good professor, but don't use your phone or talk in her lectures. Her exams are fair and reasonable. Study the homework solutions and you'll do good on the exams. Exams have rewrites as well; has 4 midterms and no final. Pretty accessible outside of class, which I appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Be respectful in class and she'll respect you. 4 exams but you can get half points back that you missed. Homework for every lecture but they are short. Responds quickly outside of class. Learning curve at the beginning but overall she's a great professor. Don't be afraid to reach out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Just don't talk in her class or she will confront you. Tests and homework are easy and very little reading.

Dr. Zhu was given a bad hand with the course's outdated textbook and tried hard to teach us the content in ways that made sense. Weekly quizzes were often difficult, but several were dropped and were only 10% of the grade. Homework is reasonable and good practice. All 3 exams accurately covered content discussed in class and were graded kindly.

Dr. Zhu has more regular weekly office hours than any of my other professors, which is convenient for homework questions. The actual exams were based on practice exams, and he went over the practice exam solutions in extra sessions after class time. Quizzes asked conceptual questions, but the rest of the class was mostly computational.

Very cool, nice and understanding with extensions, cares about students. One thing, really unhelpful lectures, only goes over really dense theory and doesn't do examples, tends to go on tangents. Quizzes every week that you only get 10 minutes to do.

The professor was great. I had him for ODEs and he did a good job of teaching the content and making it easy to follow. He does not ramble on, and he genuinely cares about students. The grading scale was not harsh. It was also homework heavy, graded leniently. He assigned projects about the ODEs taught in class which was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He lectures about the course and then decides to make the tests not similar to what he is teaching. Alot of self-studying, and preparing yourself. His lectures are also very boring and not fun to attend. I would not recommend this professor. The class itself is not difficult, but the professor made the content difficult.

I took MATH2280 with him. His lectures are not very good, and they give you the bare minimum required to do homework expect to have to read a little bit of the textbook while doing homework. He assigns 2 projects which are structured very poorly, and require previous coding experience. The homeworks are pretty long but that is to be expected in DEs

Not a good lecturer. Teaches from slides, and continuously scrolls back and forth, so no time for notes. Makes no sense, rambles, and constantly asks us if he's correct. Will not do examples in class because they "take too long". Assigns quizzes you must do on weekends, and projects over breaks. Weekly homework assignments that take >3 hours. 2280

3140 is a tough course, and I think Jingyi understands this and does his best to make it bearable. The lectures near the beginning were difficult to follow, but he responded well to feedback and made improvements throughout the semester. If you take the time to learn the material, you'll pass with flying colors and gain a new appreciation for DEs.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I highly dislike the teaching style of this professor. I learn best from doing example problems, but he almost never showed us any examples, which made this class extremely difficult for me. The notes I take for this class are basically useless, I had to teach myself the topics through the textbook because there's actually examples there.

Assigned projects right before & over breaks (due right after break), rambled about inconsequential stuff that never applied to the homework- answered emails days later when it was too late, never had examples, talked a lot with little substance, never had a midterm so the final was 70% of our grade (even though he taught absolutely nothing)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Zhu obviously knows his stuff, but teaching a PDE class for engineers and not doing any examples at all isn't doing anyone any favors. Weekly quizzes

reviews.comment: He prepares well for each class, with all the right materials instead of winging it. I've had 2 classes with him. I've had trouble understanding the point he tries to get across, but not because of an accent.

reviews.comment: The tests and "super-quizzes" are simple if you already know the material but Professor Zhu takes a subject that should be straightforward and makes it incomprehensible.
