reviews.comment: Homework is 50% of the grade. Takes forever grading it, assigns homework based on previous assignments, so you don't know for sure if you're doing it correctly. Lectures hard to jive to homework. If you want to learn about finance, save yourself the trouble, take a diff math elective, and take finance from the school of business.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Knows his finance and works hard to impart it to his students. Homeworks are long and hard and weekly, 2 projects due throughout semester, and 1 final exam. Need to know or be ready to learn Excel. Math part is easy, but the finance concepts come less naturally. You need to understand the concepts more so than the math. Effective class and prof!
Mrs. Louie would go on many tangents during her lectures, but you could tell she is passionate about the topic. Go to TA office hours and focus during lectures and you should get an A.

Lectures were unimportant and rarely got through anything important. Went on FAR too many tangents that were unrelated to what we were learning. She relied too heavily on us learning from the TAs, which wouldn't be an issue if you didn't have a rigorous schedule and could attend office hours. Overall, I would recommend not taking this class.

Lectures weren't very informative and just went through a lot of slides without actually giving us any practice. She is very nice but I did better on tests when I utilized the TA's and SI sessions. I learned all of the content outside of the lectures.

i don't understand why so many people don't like her. she's a really good professor, her lectures are easy to understand and tests are easy if you put in effort, only bad side is no calculator but she's fair with the math.never read the text book or went to office hours, her class was enough to pass, lab is mandatory to attend but it's easy

Do not take this professors classes! She is very nice and takes time to help students outside of class an TA hours.  However, the avg scores on exams were around 20-40% on exams. Ochem is hard with whoever you take it with but I have friends who said it was very manageable with other profs.  The textbook is also very confusing.

Do not take this course. The class average on almost every test was a 10/50, and on the second midterm the highest grade was a D. Not once did she ever reply to any of my emails until at the very end the day before the final. This course is fully self taught, and you are given only the textbook and some short two minute videos to go off of.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is totally awful, I don't believe anyone can get an A. Her exams are unreasonably hard(particularly exam 2&3), you only have 30mins on part B, but she expects you to go through some extremely complicated reasoning. I heard about the Ochem class at Utah State University, it's easier. Run, it's impossible to get A at the U for this class.

Prof Louie is passionate and helpful when you ask questions, but much of the learning comes from the TAs and SI sessions. If you don't seek extra help, you may struggle. I wish lectures included more practice problems instead of so many slides. practice problem answers are given at SI but, for those who can't attend SI due to life, don't get them.

she relies on her TA's and SI to teach us rather than herself. It is impossible to be taught everything you need to know if you have a stacked schedule and cant attend office hours provided by the TAs

This professor definitely minored in theater. The TA's saved the class, without Elyse I would have failed. No calculators on exams, 4 exams for the entire semester, no final, the only extra credit provided is ON exams, they are worth 10 points and have been relatively easy if you understand the course material may the odds be ever in your favor

Professor Louie is clearly very passionate about her job and chemistry. her lectures were entertaining, but she could sometimes explain things in a confusing manner. She also does not allow calculators on her tests so brush up on your long division. I would reccomend utilizing the TA's for this course bevause there is a lot of material.

super sweet lady, loves her job, but not a good teacher, she doesn't actually TEACH anything, the only reason im doing okay is because of the TA's and YouTube. she doesn't explain things well at all, I think the class would actually be easier but she explains everything in a way that makes it 100X more confusing and will rush through everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Louie! She has a unique teaching style but if you ask questions when needed, she is super willing to slow down and re-explain things if needed. She's really passionate about her job and chemistry and it helps make the class fun and go by fast. 10/10 recommend. Also I would stay on top of reading. It's not too much but very helpful

I really loved professor Louie. She was very funny and enthusiastic during lectures. Her notes are also posted online. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but I would recommend trying to come. TAs were super helpful and provided many resources, even a group chat to ask questions. Class content got pretty difficult but still manageable.

Louie's teaching style was super confusing and every class was her reading off of lecture slides. She refused to let us use calculators on exams when that is not normal for this specific chemistry class. The only reason I passed this class was because of how helpful the TA's were. The SI sessions saved me so take advantage of those!!

Professor Louie is clearly enthusiastic about her job and her love for chemistry, but she is a terrible professor with a fundamentally flawed course. Her lectures are very confusing and pointless, and I learned absolutely nothing from her. Take full advantage of the Ta's and their Si sessions, I completely accredit my A to them.

Lectures were engaging and helpful! I relied on the textbook for all my learning and studying. Lots of outside of class studying. I think the best tactic is to read the chapters prior to the lecture. Lots of TA and office hour help when you are confused. 10 point extra credit question on every exam. I got 100's or more on every exam.

Professor Louie's lectures were very helpful at all. She seemed confused and used too many analogies to simplify the material, but didn't teach us the difficult parts and we had to learn it on our own. Her exams have a 10% extra credit question which is great but I don't think I actually learned that much. Prepare to study a lot on your own.

Professor Louie did a great job teaching Chem 1130! Her lectures were clear and she had such a fun personality throughout it keeping us engaged through the lesson. Her and the TAs are available most of the time to help if there is confusion after a lesson. Also be prepared for No Calculators on exams she will not let you use them!

Professor Louie did a great job teaching Chem 1130! Her lectures were clear and she had such a fun personality throughout it keeping us engaged through the lesson. Her and the TAs are available most of the time to help if there is confusion after a lesson. Also be prepared for No Calculators on exams she will not let you use them!
Professor DOES NOT GIVE FEEDBACK. You got that wrong and want to know why? Too bad. Solve more problems until you figure it out yourself.

Need to spend time doing practice problems in this class. Read the Klein 4th version textbook(easiest textbook to read ever), take notes for each week's chapter(s), do the practice problems at the end of every section, do the weekly homework and you'll get an easy A. Louie's course structure makes it VERY clear what you need to know for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her Lectures are all over the place and the homework is nothing at all like her test, but the homework is very difficult and takes up a lot of time. If you don't do well on the homework and her tests you wont pass the class. I highly suggest taking this class from a different professor. Someone that makes sense and their HW will prep you for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Janis is a caring, extraordinary person and a terrible professor. To succeed: go to as many office hours as possible, read and understand the book every week, never miss any "small" assignments, and understand the concepts on the practice exams forwards and backward. You'll have to teach yourself most of the material, but it's possible.

Though Prof Louie is a caring, gregarious, likable person, I found her teaching style to not mesh well with my or many of my classmates learning styles. Also, the time management of her lectures was a little subpar, ending up rushing through a lot of material near the end pretty often. Also, I found a lot of her chem analogies to be pretty obtuse

Every question on the exam is a trick question meant to confuse you. exams are 60% of the grade and the questions are difficult, the average on exams is 40 in a class of 170 students. she tells you upfront that the average will be 40. you won't learn anything from lectures

Lectures are not worth the time to attend imo, online videos and O Chem as a Second Language were better uses of time. Make sure to do the activity sheets and hw. TA's give good tips on the exams. Make sure to study a lot and hard, every little thing could be tested upon including stuff not directly mentioned in class but 'could' be ascertained.

This class is not for the weak. It broke me. There are only so many times you can reread the book or rewatch the lecture videos, there are only so many resources outside of class... I wouldn't recommend the online course to anybody for any reason. This class is no joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good, challenging organic chemistry class. You get what you put in to this class, that being said, Professor Louie has so many opportunities for you to recover your grade especially at the end. I normally crammed all the reading the day before the homework is due, failed 2 exams, but still ended with an A due to her final improvement policy.

This is a super challenging class though theres lots of opportunities to improve throughout the semester. Make sure to go office hours regularly bc participation is really important and dont slack on the lectures. Only con is the TAs canceled office hours a lot with super little notice and I already couldnt attend very many bc of my work schedule.
You were guaranteed to pass the class if you read the textbook and take advantage of the final improvement grade. She was interesting, fun and would answer all my Chemistry-related questions.
Youre going to have to teach yourself and practically read the entire textbook. Took way too long to answer emails and you can tell shes not very interested in teaching.

She never responds to student emails. Emailed her at least 10 times throughout the semester (given the class was online) and she did not respond to a single one. It was useless to email her. She was also super unclear about the entire class work and what was going. She randomly assigned exams and gave us NO information regarding it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She wasn't an amazing teacher in person, and you for sure had to put the hours into watching her content and explanations to pass the class, but she was very generous in grading the tests and in the content she gave on them. The main issue is you need to study 15+ hours per test, but that's to be expected for the class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't understand. She puts up so little inside of the lecture videos, leaves us to read the textbook to do the assignments, and puts like half of the concepts taught from either on the actual tests. I learned a lot from the textbook she used, but when it comes to actually teaching the subject, this professor is lacking. Take from anybody else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about the students. Passionate about her research and had interesting lectures to back it up. Pretty relaxed advanced lab too, and good for research lab experience!
Her class is tough, but it's definitely possible to pass with a good grade if you practice and ask questions at office hours.
Teaches ochem fully online (asynchronous) and does not respond to emails. That's all.

Professor Louie taught ochem 1 really well, especially considering the circumstances with covid. Go to office hours, ask the TAs for help, and read the book and you should be fine. Shes very personable and graded and made the assignments fairly.

She honestly seems like a really caring and nice person but her online lectures left much to be desired. She really only taught the very basic stuff and left us to figure out trickier problems with little guidance. Also, I'm in ochem 2 now and there is a BUNCH of stuff they expect us to know that she never went over or even mentioned.
Get ready for curve balls.

Gave vague assignment descriptions and then graded papers with incredibly specific unposted rubrics with over 45 criteria. Janis skirts direct assignment questions from students by making useless, patronizing analogies. Repeatedly gave F's on papers without teaching anything. Did not seem to care about students.

Recklessly unorganized. Its called "Adv Organic chem lab", but all I learned was how to perfectly format a paper. The whole grade is based on a few papers, so we spent 10 hours a week in lab for no reason. Avg grade on assignments was an F, and in lecture we were told she failed us 'so that we learn'. I feel disrespected having taken this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are no in-lab points, everything is based on papers and a poster presentation. Extremely vague assignments, and a lack of quality feedback ("feedback" was often just a single word circled with a ? next to it), made this class a nightmare. Her grading system was iffy too, it didnt seem like many papers were thoroughly read before grading. 0/5
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: 10 hours worth of research based lab time -which was great to a point but very repetitive and I feel like I didn't learn anything- and 2, 50 min lectures and the entire class was graded on writing alone. VERY vague assignments, never really answered questions about it, and the average for every paper was about 40%, NEVER responds to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: O-chem is a hard class but Louie makes it as achievable as possible to get a good grade. Her tests are fair. The TAs are there to help you out. You can for SURE get an A if you put in the time. Louie tells it straight so when you go to office hours and she mentions that you need to spend some time doing more practice problems - do it.

reviews.comment: She is wonderful at creating a great classroom community. I've never been in a class where i enjoyed and trusted my fellow students quite so much. Mostly because she makes it very clear that there is no competitive advantage to not helping each other out.

Professor Louie is super smart and wants everyone to get an A. This is completely achievable if you study, ask questions, read ahead, and utilize the TAs. To everyone complaining about having quizzes on uncovered material; that is reasonable, and that is college. College is not for everyone. Best prof ever.
She is an incredible instructor.  The class is the hardest class I've ever taken. Work hard in this class and Ochem 2 is much easier.

No homework, only practice problems. She never gives you the answers to the discussion sets. problems from discussion sets not on exams. Previous exams are not good study material, they only show the structure. she moves really fast during lecture and expects you to study the material before learning in lecture. only offers 5 points extra credit.

Janis was fantastic, I took her for Honors Ochem 1. She had very high expectations of her students but after all it was honors. She does go through material quickly but is very clear in doing so. There no doubt that she knows what she is talking about. Super helpful outside of class where she will explain anything in detail.

Difficult class, but totally do-able. Get to know the TAs. Attend office hours. Learn the material as you go - it's difficult to catch up at the very end. Professor Louie is a good human and will help you if you need it!

I really enjoyed her O Chem 1 class.  It made me really debate switching to a Chem major.  She does good demonstrations to illustrate concepts, and was always willing to go over mechanisms or problems.
Louie ran through all the material at a sprint, if you are not very interested in majoring in chemistry I would not suggest her. She will help you though if you actually ask outside of class.

Worst professor I have met. I was on dean's list until this course. She flies through the chapters too fast and expects us to know too much beyond the class. She would let 1/3 of students fail. She gave Harvard advanced o-chem exercises to us as material rather than the book. Do not take her class unless you are EXTREMELY familiar with o-chem.

The worst teacher I've had. She runs through the material too fast and even tells us that she expects us to know graduate level stuff she mentions in passing because "this is an Honors class". Since there's no homework, you don't know if you actually know the stuff. Grades depend only on the 4 tests. She has problem sets online, but no answers.

Professor Louie was the worst professor I've had in college. The lectures were unclear and the exams were awful. She seemed proud that the averages were so low on the exams, and blamed the students for not being prepared enough. I think that if the average on an exam is 35% in a class of 200, that's indicative of a really poorly written exam.

Difficult but fair. Forget all of these idiot complaining about  how she is "show offy". She has the same grade distribution that all other chem professors have. Read the book, do the problems and go to her office hours. She is very approachable and willing to help. I recommend her to everyone.

Louie is an okay teacher, a great person though (be sure to visit her office hours). Read/understand the textbook and going through the problems is helpful. The tests weren't too bad, pretty easy if you understand what you've read/gone over in class.

Professor Louie is a professional and treats her students the same way. She is creative in teaching her methods in chemistry and if you visit her office hours your life will become a lot easier. I'm proud to have had her as a teacher.Overall an amazing person and teacher.

I took her for O Chem 1. I did all suggested problems and it helped a lot. People on here complain, but they just don't like working hard I think. She is always available during office hours if you have any questions. She gives quizzes before lecturing material to get students to read before she teaches it, but you get unlimited chances to take it.

Wow, she is the worst professor I've EVER had.  I feel bad to say it because she was "nice", but it's true.  She doesn't follow the book, she tries to makes jokes all class long and never covers the material, and her tests are WAY too hard.  Her averages on the tests were between 20-35%...and she bragged about that.  Find another Prof if possible.
Bad, unclear, not very helpful. No homework given. Exams were poor.

Prof. Louie is an enthusiastic teacher, who has clever methods of introducing material; however, she lectures a little too fast to completely understand a subject, and requires too much from OChem I undergrads. I really liked her personality and teaching style, but she needs to cover topics better in class to prepare students more for the exams.

She talked way too fast and taught in a way that was almost show offy, like "look what I can do".... She did a review for her first test that was extremely helpful, but didn't for her other tests. Nice person, awful teacher.

She rushes through the class way too fast. Her tests are so hard, she expects you to know things that are way too advanced. Her testing is not fair at all. Shes a nice person but her teaching skills are aweful. Dont take the class from her. Wait a semester if you have to.

DO NOT TAKE O-CHEM with her. She literally spends 25% of the class doing pointless mimes, then speeds through the important material. Absolutely incomprehensible. Take my word for it: Unless you are a chemist, you will be VERY hard pressed to succeed. Her tests are extremely difficult, unrepresentative.All in all a horrible teacher
She's brilliant, beautiful, well-spoken, and a great teacher. But don't take classes from her unless you plan on studying 3 hours a night.
Very difficult exams, pointless online quizzes. Flies through the lecture material nonstop.

i know that most people hate Louie but i had so much fun and learned so much in her class. if you just want to pass  o chem don't take it from her but if you actually want to learn something (god forbid!) then she is the teacher you want.

She goes through the material so fast that she needs to catch her breath after each sentence. She gives test questions on material that she flew through in class. Prof Judd was great. He explained concepts throughly, and did a good job at answering questions. The courses' content is hard, and the class is based around the tests. He is well paced and thrives off class engagement. Would recommend!

Professor Judd is an amazing person. His class was alway engaging, while the homework and projects were long they get you ready for the exams. Professor Judd is the best. Best in the whole world.

Not an interesting class. Not a lot of effort in lesson plans.

Great guy, professionally and personally. Really appreciates student participation and is well versed in accounting both as a professional and academic.

Professor Judd is AMAZING!

Not only does he know what he's talking about when it comes to the course material, but he also shows a deep care for his students. He has worked with me on rescheduling an assignment and missing a few classes for traveling. 
Professor Judd makes accounting enjoyable and has been a pleasure to learn from.

Professor Judd clearly cares a lot about Accounting. He makes it feel a normally boring topic feel interesting. Lectures were fun to attend and the homework wasn't too bad. I do think the tests were quite difficult but I did appreciate the measures he took to minimize cheating.
One of the most down to earth and funniest professors I have met - though the class may be difficult, the professor makes it worth going.

Ken can really explain things clearly and arouse your passion in science. His class is well-organised and clearly-structured. I really learned a lot! Besides, he is enthusiastic about research himself, and is so inspirational, talented! It is great to work with him:)

The teacher overall was good, every time I had a question i'd post and get a full detailed response.
