Jeff is the best.  Made a three hour lecture fly by all semester.  Be prepared in advance of class, he will call on you and participation points are a big part of the grade.

Jeff is one of my favorite teachers at the U, he really cares about the success of his students and his lectures are always very interesting and engaging. Do the reading or he will absolutely crucify you in front of the class. It's awkward and uncomfortable for everyone. Keep up on attendance and reading and you will be just fine!
Jeff is the best teacher at the U. I genuinely looked forward to each class period. He is funny and intelligent. Lectures are very interesting. DO THE READING! If you don't he will embarrass you.

Jeff was the best professor I had in college. He is passionate about the law and teaching. Most interesting lectures I ever attended. I had 100% attendance not because my grade would be affected, but because I WANTED to attend. He took a subject as dry as the law and made me love it. Once again, best professor I've ever had.

Jeff is an incredible professor. I didn't know what to expect walking in, but am so thrilled I got to be a part of his class.  Jeff is an incredible orator and professor and is the only one that thanked each student individually for their participation in his class. In addition, the only one I have seen receive a standing ovation from his students.

Knows his stuff very well, and teaches you law in a way that you will understand. Attend class and read the book and you will be fine. Its not an easy class because of its subject but Jeff does a fantastic job. He cares that you understand, and will be willing to help if you do not understand something. Best professor I have had while at Utah.

HANDS DOWN BEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN!! In my senior year and best professor at the U for sure! Clearly cares about his students.  The dude knows his stuff and loves teaching it. Tests are hilarious but difficult. Participation is HUGE. You will not pass if you don't. I wish there were more teachers like him!
Amazing speaker, clearly cares about his students, only a midterm and a final + participation

Jeff is a good guy and an even better orator. This is why students fall in love with him, he is a very inspirational person because he knows how to present. His class was interesting, but the whole grade is based 2 tests which are unreasonably difficult. If I could have, I would have taken it from LDS bus college and transferred the credit over.

I have been to 3 different universities and am on my senior year. I don't even like law and he was still the best professor I have had. His closing speech made me tear up. He's definetly one to look up to
He is very passionate about his job. He loves to teach and give clear examples based on the theory we had. He is also a good inspiration. Don't miss a class or you wont pass!

Jeff definitely knows his material. His lectures are very fun. I thought his tests were EASY PEASY!! Foreign exchange students fail in this class :) One downfall of having him, is he is very rude. He requires you to participate in class, but every time I tried to participate he seemed to hate the questions I asked. Very unprofessional in that sense

Jeff is awesome. Easily the best professor I had during college. I was not excited about business law, after my first class with Jeff, that was changed dramatically. I looked forward to going and it was such an awesome class. I was also lucky enough to have Jeff in my line at graduation, so I got to shake his hand.

This is my last year of college and hands down Jeff Nielsen is the best professor I have ever had. He cares so much about his job and his students. It feels so good to finally find a professor that really cares. I was challenged, inspired, and motivated. I feel lucky to have the opportunity to take a class from Jeff.

Jeff is an amazing teacher. You will want to attend every class, not only so you do well on the exams, but because the lectures are so fascinating. Keep up on reading, participate in lectures and the Facebook group he creates. Include yourself and really listen. Jeff makes this class worth your money even though you HAVE to take it. Favorite class!

Jeff is the ideal teacher.  He is relatively young and really understands how students learn.  You will be talking about the interesting things you learn in his class to all your friends (yeah...business law!)  He gave the most inspiring speech on the last day of class and half of the students were crying.  TAKE HIS CLASS.

Jeff is probably one of the funniest professors at the U. He is always willing to answer questions at the end of class and knows how to make the class interesting. Don't miss out on this experience with him. He is so knowledgeable.
Jeff is one of the best professors I have had at the U. You must take this class from him if you have the opportunity
He is one the best professors ever. Hard class but worth your time to go to. Highly recommended.

Jeff is by far the best professors I've ever had. He takes a terribly dull subject and makes it surprisingly fascinating. His tests are NOT as difficult as people say, but recording his lectures (and listening to them) is what made a huge difference for me. The way he teaches inspires you to WANT to learn. I've never had a class I enjoyed more.
Jeff is an awesome guy. He is one of the best teachers at the U. His class are very entertaining and you learned tons  Exams are not easy, questions are too long and confusing. Be aware.
Final is way more difficult than the midterm.  As long as you attend class, you'll be fine on the exams.  He also cold calls to make sure you've done the readings.

Jeff is an awesome teacher and I highly recommend him. There are 2 tests and participation and that's it so you have to pay attention! Don't buy the book required, you can find a cheaper version online. But take Jeff, he is engaging, funny and hip.

What more can I say? This class is not easy, and Jeff won't babysit you. He doesn't care if you go to class or sleep while you're there. If you put in the effort, you will get a good grade. Jeff is organized, helpful, clear, and entertaining. Easily the best experience I've had in any course

Jeff is one of the most educated people I know but is down to earth and relates to students. He loves to teach and keeps the class exciting. The final exam was harder than expected so beware but class is not too difficult, he teaches all the business law classes, acct majors have another option but I would recommend this one.

Jeff is a baller.  I loved his class and thought he was one of the funniest, coolest guys on campus.  You have to read, participate and pay close attention to do well but you will absolutely love this class.

Professor Nielsen was my favorite teacher at the U so far.  He is really funny and makes class a lot of fun.  Grade is based on participation and two exams, all multiple choice (not an easy multiple choice, though - he gives you four answer options and more than one fits, so you have to pick the BEST answer).  Overall, great class.

Jeff was one of the best professors I've had! He knows the material very well but is very humble and approachable. If you put forth the effort in studying the exams, meeting with him (which he is very easy going!) to go over questions, and participate in class discussions, you'll do just fine. You wont regret it!

I had no interest in taking business law and put it off until my last semester to avoid it, but professor Nielsen made it one of my favorite classes at the U. He is really funny and he really knows his stuff. There is a lot of material and the exams are harder than you expect, but he is always willing to meet with you to help you understand it all.

I took his in person MATH 1050 course and never felt rushed or lost during the class. He was very flexible if you had extenuating circumstances when you could not come to take a quiz. Always made sure that we understood the content by asking us questions in class. Definitely wish he taught higher level math so I could learn again with him!

Dr. Lam is a stellar professor! His genuine passion for mathematics made me the most engaged I've ever been in a math class. He goes the extra mile to support his students' understanding of the material. Dr. Lam for president!!!

I also took MATH 1030 with him. This professor wants you to pass. If you put yourself into it then you will pass. He tries his best so everyone understands the course. Try to get him as your Math Professor!
Professor breaks down everything when it comes to solving, so we understand better. He is available during hours to meet in person or on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the easiest class I have ever taken. I went only on Mondays (to turn in the homework) and on days where we had a quiz and finished with a 98% in the class. His teaching methods aren't super clear, and I found it much easier to just read the chapter in my own time because the subjects are so easy to understand.

Nice guy. Eccentric, dorky. Despite being in a class of 70+ students, he pays attention to individual students (he even remembered my name and said hi about 2 semesters later!) His lectures are sometimes confusing, but he really does his best to help you out. Great with individual help. Gets super angry about cheaters--he's very observant about it.

I took a Math 1050 class from HongLu Fan and he was the worst teacher I've ever had. Tony had a Math 1050 class during the break in my schedule and he not only let me sit in on his lectures but learned my name and let me take his quizzes and tests for practice. Without him and his incredibly clear way of presenting material, I wouldn't have passed.
Great teacher.  Very clear with what he expects from students, he grades very fairly.  Keep up on homework and you will be fine.  I never enjoyed a math class until I took this class from Tony.

Nice guy. He's kind of dorky. Very helpful, though he can be confusing at times; he speaks really fast and sounds sort of "textbooky". He takes math seriously though, and expects you to do the same. He tries to make everything fair for the class.

Tony is a nice guy. He is pretty good at teaching and explaining things clearly. He is always willing to help. The homework load wasn't too bad and there was no surprises or trick questions on the test. Good class to take!

Tony lam is a phenomenal professor and very knowledgable of statistics. This is by no means a blow off class and requires dedication to do well in the class. Tony is easily approachable and extremely willing to help. If you need to take this class and want to learn the subject, I would highly suggest Tony. A+ Teacher.
He's ok, he can be confusing when explaining some topics. Pretty good, not so bad
GREAT PROFESSOR. Take this class it will be worth it.

Overall this class was mainly saved by ta. Sarah as a professor is not as bad as the reviews make it seem however chem 1130 was not a class I think she should be teaching. Instead she would be better for higher level stuff. Not a hard class if you put in the effort. Also a lot of help such as dropping assignments/tests which will save poor grade.

For an "introductory" course to chemistry, it does a bad job. Steer clear if you have never taken chemistry before, or prepare to teach everything to yourself. Attendance is mandatory, but lectures stuff too much information in a short period of time and don't teach much. Homework is tedious and the 3 exams are tough, but curved.

I think Lefave just did poorly with our class. She did not like us that much and we really did not like her. My issue is she had a lot of disorganized moments throughout the semester which you can't afford in a major class like this. Hopefully in the future it will be better. This class is hard and if you don't utilize the TAs you will get lost.

Did not love how she explained things, I felt like concepts were overcomplicated. Definitely will need to put in a good amount of study time outside of class. Tests were pretty hard and always took material a few steps farther. She loved pulling material from diagrams shown in lecture. Gives a curve to exams with a low average.
Sarah was a great teacher! I took 1130 from her and passed with an A. I would say it takes a lot of study time, but the TAs provide mock exams. She is very kind and responds to emails quickly.

Her lectures were boring and rarely helpful. She claimed our hw was harder than exams then blamed us when we performed poorly. I studied for days on material, and it would not be on the exam. She gave over 100 practice problems, expecting us to know stuff we didn't review/ have hw on. Exams never had enough time, not even TAs knew what to expect.

She yelled at me in front of my peers and made me sob in front of my peers at the end of an exam. I was not given enough time to complete my test because of the CDA not having available appointments but the teachers were aware of this with an in person talk and email. I would refuse to take her because of her lack of empathy with disabilities.

Somehow learned less in this class than I did in high school chemistry. Mandatory attendance for PowerPoint lectures proved a waste of time. Lefave frequently lied about what material would appear on the quizzes/exams then blamed student use of AI for poor performance. Unnecessarily convoluted way to teach an introductory class.

I do not think this woman should be a professor. She would get frustrated at how students were doing in the course but she herself often provided incorrect material. Avoid taking this course with her. She does not care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS PROFESSOR!!! She does not respect students; you will be treated as if you are in middle school. She appears unprepared for tests and doesn't teach; she reads from lecture slides that aren't posted on Canvas. I have had professors whose teaching style I didn't like, but she is unfit to manage and teach a class, and will not prepare you.

Never gave out an Exam "Practice" document, expect to over study for this class, Recc to study a couple weeks ahead. When everyone did bad on first exam, she blamed us and said to use our resources...but never questioned her teaching style... Very confusing teaching and wants to rush and solve everything 5 mins before class ends?

Very confusing teaching style,Prof Lefave expects you to know the material before lecture if you wanna know whats going on in class. Always skipping practice problems in lec, if she does practice problems, she wont go in depth of solving it.If I could go back to registering,I wouldn't have chosen to take this class with her. Save yourself and GPA.
she's better than carter but wow. do not expect to learn in class. she does not provide tangible study material for exams and is often wrong on practice problems. if u can take this online, do it.

This Professor is a GREAT person, but NOT a GREAT teacher for Gen Chem 1. The way she teaches is absolutely ATROCIOUSLY confusing. I taught myself better. I would go to her lectures, write whatever she jots down with a blank mind. Exams were also horrid, and new concepts would show up. Not a bad class if you can teach yourself :D...

I took college Chem in high school and this class made unlearn all that I did learn. The prof. frequently over explained simple topics and spent 2 seconds on the actually complex ones. Our grades were hidden for half the semester and only revealed right before the final. The final was bad, covering things we didn't learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have to take Gen Chem 1... drop out of school. This class tested my mind, my mettle, and my might. You'd think it's her first time teaching anything the way her lectures are overly complicated for the simplest things. We spent weeks learning how to convert units and some people were still confused. I'm out of characters, but I could go on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took AP Chem in high school and had to correct the way she would teach certain topics because she made everything so much more confusing than it needed to be. I don't think I paid attention in a single lecture because it was not worth my time, and she is just bad at teaching. I would have done bad if I had not taken chemistry before this

chem 1.She doesn't give anything to prep for the tests.she gave an 18pg set of problems & said “this will not be covered on the exam”.She is often wrong in calculations & homework missed cannot make up.often late to lectures & blames bad test aves on students.She expects learn everything outside independently and doesn't cover most of the material.

The Professor and the TAs are never on the same page, the homework is hard, and the course is not structured well. Then the test that is worth half of your grade is on all of the things you didn't go over during class
Chemistry is a difficult subject, but the professor made it understandable. Honestly, as long as you go into this class expecting to put in some effort, you'll be fine.

Lectures are hard to follow, exams are pretty difficult, the only thing that helps for practice problems is the homework but even then the tests are worded weirdly. The only thing going for you is the TA's, the "End of Chapter Questions" and the SI problems. Self-teaching is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take chemistry from her! I was taking biology along with this course and  had taken chemistry before but she made me understand science less. Her lectures are too short for what we go over, there are no quizzes to check your knowledge before exams, TAs and google are your best friend. You'll have to teach yourself a lot. Good luck!

Such an unorganized course. She's a bad lecturer overall speeding through information thats heavily tested on, skips over information and you'll have to teach yourself a lot of material.If you don't go to SI sessions or office hours its hard to do well. No quizzes so homework and exams are the only way to test you knowledge. Good Luck!

I actually found the lectures helpful, and the LAs for the class are wonderful. The homework and weekly quizzes cover what we learned well, and it's not too much. The issue is the exams.  She gave us an 18-page practice set for the final, but said that it won't cover everything. The exams are also very poorly worded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is one of the most unorganized classes I have ever taken. They are extremely unclear about the topics you are supposed to know (anything is liable to be on the exam). The mandatory lectures are extremely boring and unhelpful. If you confront her about her subpar management of the class, she insists it's your fault and problem. 0/10.
Her lectures are a complete and utter waste of time. Better to learn the material on your own and hope you do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took AP Chem in high school, did great got a 4, but had to take this class anyways for premed. Paying attention to this professor made me not understand topics I already knew very well. I got an A in the class but absolutely none of that came from the professor. She was also very unclear with her assignment scheduling.

Do not take from this professor!! I unlearned everything I knew by actually listening to her. Ended up just going to class for attendance. Homework and quiz schedule is also super confusing and assignments are often posted last minute. TAs are the only reason anyone survived this class.

This class is not that hard. Those who struggle are sorority girls who think being a nurse will come easily without studying. This is a chemistry class; you need to study. Do that, and you will be fine. I would take this class again.

Sarah could improve some aspects of her class, but overall, it's not as bad. If you apply yourself, you will do fine. Too many of the reviews come from those who talk over Sarah in lectures and don't pay attention.

Chem 1210, she was not as bad as most make her out to be. There is some room for improvement but the students themselves are more than half the problem. If people would shut up and listen instead of talking all class they might actually gain more understanding. Don't be disruptive all class and be surprised when things don't make sense.

Sarah is a new professor, I definitely see how she could improve in some areas. But she still does a great job. I think people are being way too harsh. Definitely one of the better professors. TAs did a great job too.

Any good reviews on here are likely from students who already understand chemistry and are not the average student. For the average student, Sarah Lefave's methods are lacking, and you won't learn much just from lectures. However, the TAs are amazing at picking up her slack, and if you can attend enough office hours, you will be okay.

Sarah is an awesome professor. She builds a good base by starting with simple concepts & gives us examples to go through during class. There were lots of opportunities to earn back points that I missed on homework. The exam drop & hw/lab drops were so nice. The TAs went above & beyond to make sure we were prepared for exams. Study & you'll do fine.

Ignore the reviews of students who don't know how to do any work without Chat GPT. Sarah is the most fair and kind professor in the Chemistry Department. It's sad to see her bad reviews due to the fact she teaches an intro course with unmotivated students. She is great. If you try, you will get an A. She wants to help students.

Professor Lefave is nice, but her lectures are bland, and we don't spend adequate amounts of time on challenging subjects. Often, we'll run out of time and she'll tell us to go to office hours to learn how to solve a problem. However, there are ways to get your grade up, and we get a test drop and lab drops. Lab is very easy and a grade boost.

I don't agree with a lot of the reviews here at all. Class is challenging... because chem is hard. I think Prof. Lefave does a great job teaching the content. Understanding homework is key as it is similar to the exams. Put in the effort, and you'll do fine. Also the TAs are SO helpful... There are endless resources available for this class.
I'm only taking it because it's required, and I'm barely getting by.

Sarah is a great person, however all of the TAs are on a different page. Some of them don't even know the material and all say different things. You will ONLY pass this class if you can make it to every outside of class extra help option. The TAs and professor show up to class extremely unprepared.

Sarah is very nice, however if you want to stay sane do not take this class. Important subjects were lightly touched on. She spends that majority of class talking about subjects that were rarely on the tests. The tests always included complex math problems we were never taught. The TA's are expected to do everything.

Be prepared to test on things she mentioned once in passing and questions 10x more difficult then they were in lab. Practice questions and topics are skipped in lectures. We are treated like toddlers in class, threatened with extra material in exams bc of some ppls chatter, while blatantly not caring about the quality of education we are given.

She rushes through important subjects and takes her time on ones that never show up on tests. Very unorganized. The TAs did the majority of teaching outside of class time, if you can not make their office hours good luck. Tests are brutal. Was not able to hand out exams on time and required students to stay after class hours to take it.

I've never had good experience with chemistry prior to this class so I was expecting it to be difficult but it was worse than I imagined. In short she doesn't teach. I haven't gotten my final grade back but I am expecting to have to retake the whole class, but not because of a lack of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nothing truer has ever been said by all these other ratings; they cover what's on my & likely many others' minds. If you don't have any prior chem experience, keep far away. It's not just her; it's a total systematic failure, with harsh grade distribution & far too short lectures. Save your sanity, time & MONEY by avoiding by any means. A sad scam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Being a nice person DOESN'T mean you're good at your job. I ditto the other ratings talking about her lectures and problems. I sit in the front EVERY lecture, take notes, do everything, and have a worse grade here than in ANATOMY. (I have a 4.0 partially through my junior year for reference) Worst course I've ever taken, hands down.

The material isn't hard, but the lack of organization and communication is so frustrating. She explains simple concepts all class, then last second briefly covers a hard topic, mistakes are in her slides and hw/mock exam keys, TAs have conflicting info about questions, our first test asked what a cation was, which we were then taught the day after.
be prepared to learn NOTHING from the MANDATORY LECTURES and then be completely screwed for test day! Her chemistry course is planned terribly and the students suffer accordingly. Be warned.
Sarah is good, eveyone who says she isnt dosent put effort twords the class to learn some matierials outside of class and going to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking chemistry with Prof. Lefave. She crams most of the learning into the last week before the test so the students are unprepared and there will be concepts on the test that she doesn't teach; you just have to learn by yourself. Relies on her TAs to basically teach the students for her. The material is easy enough to learn.

*chem 1210: I think she is a great professor, but easily gets frustrated when students aren't performing well. I think rather than Professor Lefave being subpar, it's a problem with the department. Lectures don't go over as much as I'd like. Exams are 50% of your grade, exams feel impossible, and material that wasn't mumbled appeared on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lefave is great at answering questions one on one however when teaching an intro Chemistry class is less helpful. She lectures like you already know the concepts and doesn't show where she gets the numbers. She also covers topics on the test that have not been covered in lecture, but blames class for failing.

I don't think I've ever taken such a disorganized course. She has poor communication and relies on her TAs to relay all important information to us, and the information relayed is often incorrect. A few topics on exams won't be covered in class; you just have to learn yourself. Sometimes contradicts her own teaching and makes it very hard to follow

I had Dr. Lefave for Ochem I & then intentionally took Biochem I with her. She's exactly what a great professor should be for these rigorous STEM classes. Has a simple Canvas setup, clear video lectures, no busywork, plenty of study material, quick email replies (even weekends), & very fair/helpful with grading & conceptual questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lefave seemed like a pretty chill professor, and she definitely knew the topic well. There were a couple things that got put on a test after she said that they wouldn't, but it wasn't anything you couldn't figure out if you had studied hard. There were also some things we probably should have covered that we didn't end up getting to.

Sarah is super chill and makes it very clear what material will be covered on the exams. The exams are similar in difficulty to the discussion worksheets, some questions can be a bit wild, but most are not bad at all. The course isn't difficult with her and she is cool.

Class is graded by 1 weekly online assignment, discussion, and exams. Lefave is probably the professor for you if you just want an A in biochem. She doesn‘t teach a hard class, just includes a lot of extra material in her lectures that you‘ll never see again. We barely got to the CAC and covered maybe half of what‘s covered by another prof.

Fluffs up lecture slides with stuff you won't need to know on the test, puts very easy questions on the study material, then asks insanely hard questions on the tests that were nowhere to be found on the study material
she is easily one of the most passionate, caring, and intelligent professors in the University of Utah, Department of Chemistry

Docks a lot of points for partial credit. Even if you only make one tiny mistake you'll probably lose 3-4 points on a problem. Doesn't explain concepts very well, and then gets irritated when students continue to not understand concepts. Unless you can afford lots of private tutoring, I would avoid at all costs.

I liked Sarah she's a good teacher. My one complaint is she kind of rushes out at the end of lectures, so you cant ask her questions, Im sure theres a reason for it. Do the homework and discussions and especially prepare for lecture, helps with understanding new concepts. Ochem is just a hard class you'll struggle but theres resources to use.

This was a hard, fast-paced class. The professor was very helpful, and even though she moved through her lectures quickly, she explained everything we needed to know if we ever had a question. There is homework each week, and occasionally we also did a report on an article. There were even opportunities to get more points on the midterms.

This professor was a really good professor! When ever someone had a question, she would answer it without making anyone feel stupid. Yes, this class was difficult but I think she made it easier to understand and taught in a very good way.

This class was HARD. She moves incredibly quick and it feels like she teaches way above the curriculum. Our unit of O chem felt way too advanced for an elementary chem class. She gives out a huge study guide 2 days before an exam, leaving you no time to study. I will say she is helpful if you ever have questions, but this course was extremely tough

I really enjoyed this class. VERY generous grading scale. Tests were fairly difficult but that's kind of to be expected for a chem class. My average on most tests was a 75, but the overall average grade for tests were way below that. Professor Lefave is awesome! Small nitpick, but the tests did have questions on things we did not go over in class.

She is very generous with grades that she drops and the extra credit. Her exams are VERY hard. I scored on average 60's on the exams but somehow still got an A in the class because I did all of my homework and the extra credit. I am NOT one who is good at chemistry but I applied myself a lot therefore I was able to get a good grade.

Awful Prof! Doesn't care about students and loves to waste time. Gives assignments/lectures over campus breaks and disregards student's time. VERY test and lecture heavy. Hard and awful tests that she doesn't help with prep for. Incredibly unhelpful and not understanding at all!! Would never take again!

By far the best professor I've ever had! He has a gift of making math make sense! He is super caring and very easy to talk to. He frequently asks how he can support his students and what he can improve on. The class was graded 100% on exams but he gives great practice exams and resources that make tests very doable if you put in the work!

Professor Wortman really cares about his students. He is very lenient and takes a lo of care in helping students actually understand the material rather than just getting through each section quickly. He takes his time and lets everyone catch up. Great professor.
Best math teacher i have ever had.

This was his first time teaching Math 1105, and he was amazing. He always goes through topics well enough for you to understand and do great on the weekly one-question quizzes. He helps with ANY problem and actually cares about his students. His exams are always true to what we learn, and he will help answer your questions.

Kevin is honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. His teaching style is really relaxed but he takes his time to engrain core concepts from classes. When people do poorly on a concept in an exam or quiz, he goes over it until everyone feels confident.

This guy was great, wish I could have him for the rest of calculus. He's really good at introducing concepts like limits/derivatives/etc. in a "common sense" kind of way that's good for someone who's hearing it for the first time. The class is entirely based on test grades though, I know some people struggle with that, but they're not too bad.

Man Kevin Wortman is amazing! He gives great explanations and is very clear on the expectations on exams. I though he was hilarious and I was excited to go to class each morning. I would gladly take a course from him again.
Very willing to help. Even the dumbest of questions are met with respect and understanding. Wish he taught calc 2 and 3 so I could take his class again!

the only grades were exams, while this is an easy class for people who are good at math it was pretty difficult for me. the lectures are great and he gives test prep thats almost always like the test, the only downside was that the textbook and papers given out were the only real resources, especially since this is a class only offered at the u.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The man, the myth, the legend. I would give up my first newborn for this man. Best Calc professor by FAR. take him if you can. only downside is that only things graded is exams so just make sure to study his practice exams and you should be good. very caring man and a even better professor.

Professor Wortman is one of the best professors at the U. He is very sweet and has a good sense of humour. He would give us paper copies of chapter summaries every day. Homework is not graded, but it is highly encouraged to do. The Entire class was 4 midterms and a final, but he gives practice exams that are really similar to the actual exam.

he is one of the best professors I ever had in U of U, clear lecture and perfect reviews for exams. HW is optional for his class, and your entire grade depends on how do on exam. this class have four midterms and 1 final exam.

Best math teacher Ive ever had! Lectures are well written, and he explains everything super well. I almost failed ap calc in hs but breezed through this class. He posts the lecture slides and pdfs from each chapter. There is optional hw that is easy and helpful. Exams are just like the study guides, and he has helpful review lectures before exams.

THE best professor! This class helped me learn the most with the least amount of effort and get a good foundation for other math. Going to class makes it 10x easier to learn the material, and he is always happy to explain any questions in/outside of class. Grade is 4 midterms + final, but the practice exams make it super clear and easy to prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wortman is seriously the best. I hate math but I've loved it because his lectures are so good. His presentations are clear and he really cares that the class is learning. Grades are based only on exams, but he provides really good prep work. Practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams.

THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!! If you're scared about math, take it with him. He's funny, a quick grader, and wonderful at explaining things in multiple different ways. Attendance isn't mandatory, but as long as you do the non-graded homeworks you'll be fine. Before every midterm, you get a practice review guide which is exactly like the actual midterm.

Overall Great class. He allowed Calculus to be so much easier with his way of explaining anyone could understand it quickly. Grade is only like 4 midterms and 1 final test, but the lectures allow us to be plenty prepared before it. Also unironically funny all the time.
Top tier. Top tier professor in general, and for this class. HIGHLY recommend taking it with him. Will greatly prepare you for math 3210 and 3220.

Optional homework, and no mandatory attendance. Nice and personal. Course material is easy to pick up, you may not even have to go to lecture. Weekly quizzes that can serve as your practice. No note sheets, however the tests are exactly the same as the practice test. Study the practice test, and you will be golden.

Our class was comprised of only homework assignments and no tests. None of these assignments felt outrageously difficult either. In lecture, he did a great job of outlining exactly what we would need to know to complete the homework. Attendance was mandatory, and you could miss three before losing points. I would recommend taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. Everything was super clear. No required homework but the labs are good at checking how prepared you are for the final. Great at answering questions. Great at grading exams on time. Would recommend 100%.
Wortman's class was amazing. He was clear in lectures, and made the class very accessible. I really enjoyed having him, and wish he taught more at the U.
Perfect! Would highly recommend. His lectures are great and would follow along with HW perfectly, exams were great as well. No complaints!

Professor Wortman is an amazing professor. His lecture style is very clear and easy to follow. The class did not have graded homework, but you are still expected to do the homework problems for practice. Would highly recommend Prof. Wortmans class!

Professor Wortman is AMAZING! He makes everything clear. Every practice exam he gave us before a midterm is just like the midterm. He is always willing to help every student who asks for it and is just an amazing guy. Never met a professor who loves the subject and his students as much as this guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Wortman is the best teacher I have ever had. He explains things very clearly and makes lectures interesting, note taking reccomended. The textbook was free and easy to use. The exams are just like the practice exams and he does in class reviews. I recommend doing the homework problems because they are very similar to the exams.

I loved him!! Calc was so nice with him! he is very clear with math and his notes are easy to follow. He repeats himself and all the tests have practice exams before them which are similar to the actual exam. I HIGHLY recommend him for anyone taking a calc course.

Calc 3 is definitely not easy so this class does require a lot of studying. His exams are worth 85% of your grade, and weekly quizzes worth 15%. The final replaces the lowest midterm score. His exams are just like his practice exams, so if you study and do the optional homework problems you should be good to pass his class with a high B or an A.

Professor Wortman was amazing. You didn't have to study heavily for his class, only midterms and the final contributed to your grade. His expectations for the exams were clear, and he provided a practice exam that closely resembled the actual one. I would definitely recommend his class and would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I have taken purely because of this professor. He hand writes his notes for lectures and all of the exams have practice exams before them that look very similar to the tests. Great professor!!

Professor Wortman teaches the same way "The Organic Chemistry Tutor" on YouTube teaches. He uses a tablet to project how to solve problems in real time. He mentions basics every day to refresh our memory, which is very helpful. Homework is not graded, though it's very helpful for success in exams. real time
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You can tell he really loves his job and wants his students to succeed. He provides practice exams that are almost identical to actual exam about 5 days before the test (Calculus 1)

Wortman was phenominal. His hand drawn lectures clearly shows his dedication to mathematics. He focuses on learning things that matter to the course. He never gets sidetracked and is always willing to answer students' quesions. He clearly presents concepts. If you need a professor that will help you understand math well then this is the one.
Just an outstanding professor. He really really cares about his students.
a really good professor
Phenomenal. I am no longer afraid of calculus because of Prof. Wortman. I would highly recommend his classes to anyone.
The lectures were amazing. Listened to us students and gave out exam preps which helped a lot. Cared a lot about us and replied to emails fast. WOULD RECOMMEND. Knows how to teach

Phenomenal professor. Professor Wortman is incredibly organized, and his lectures were very easy to follow. He is very kind and grades very fairly; it is quite obvious that your success is his number one priority. Reviews were also highly representative of exam content.
AMAZING! Best math teacher I have ever had. I absolutely loved him!!
If you have the option to take his class do it! Love Kevin!

Professor Wortman is simply an amazing professor. He was always perfectly clear about what he expects from you and makes Calc 3 easy and even enjoyable. The class material is hard, but his tests reflect exactly what he teaches and he is always willing to help you out!

Professor Wortman proved his understanding and credibility as a professor by adapting very well to the ongoing pandemic. He answers emails quickly and is open to talking to students about anything. As long as you ask questions and do the homework, you won't regret taking his class.

If you need to take Calculus and Kevin is an option, SIGN UP FOR IT! I hated Calc I and II but Kevin really knows how to teach math. He will get straight to the point and tell you how to do the problems. Exams were open note, super short, nothing sneaky. Take his 5/5 rating as a sign. Take his class. If you dread taking Calc, take. his. class.

This was the best calculus class I've ever taken. He explains concepts very clearly and simply, homework generally isn't too difficult/time consuming, and tests are short and just like the lecture/homework problems. Also, tests are more frequent so the material is fresh. Do yourself a favor and take Calc III with him.

Professor Wortman is one of the best rated professors for a reason. He made Calculus III a class I looked forward to during this hellish semester (a la pandemic). He explains things clearly, cares about his student's success, and is very flexible. Not sure what more you could ask for. Highly recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance!

Honestly, he is the best professor I've ever had. Very generous when grading homework and exams, and provides extremely helpful reference materials such as lecture summaries and in-depth problem solutions online. Once, I emailed him to ask about a homework problem, and next class he gave me a handwritten step-by-step solution! Best teacher ever!

Kevin is an excellent professor and perhaps the best I've had so far. He is understanding and very patient when teaching material--even topics that can seem simple--and has a very organized way of teaching. If you ever have the opportunity to take a class from Kevin, don't hesitate!

This was one of the best math classes I've ever taken. Wortman makes difficult subjects easy to understand, and he clearly cares a great deal about teaching. He is knowledgeable about the subject and willing to answer questions in and outside of class. He cares more about learning than grades, and is willing to work with you to help you learn.

Overall such a nice guy, and an even better professor. If I could I would take all my classes from Kevin. He clearly explains what will be on the exams, so as long as you study his practice exams you will pass with an A.
A really awesome, organized professor. Really good at teaching content and helping the students succeed.
So good! Best math class Ive ever taken.

Every single person that knows, or has taken a class from Kevin has nothing short of spectacular things to say about him. He is able to teach very difficult subjects in a manner that anyone can comprehend. I hope that someday I can take another class from Kevin since I was very pleased with how he taught Calculus 3. I highly recommend him.
Awesome teacher, very clear expectations on tests. He gives a review sheet with the exact type of problems that appear on the test, making it easy to ace as long as you put 1-2 hours into studying.

Best math class I've ever taken. He as a person is just awesome and truly cares about students. He tests for understanding, not to see if you can solve some godforsaken equation that takes computers for a spin. Meaning, if you understand the subject and know how to plug numbers into variables, you can ace the tests.

If you have the opportunity of taking a math class with Professor Wortman you'd be stupid not to take it. Unlike most professors, he takes the time to connect with his students and it's clear that he wants every student to succeed. The U of U is lucky to have him. Do whatever it takes to get in his class!
I'm a senior here. Kevin is easily the best professor I've had. Not a contest.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: hes the best honestly hes really nice and his lessons are so easy to pass and understand i recomend him!!!!!! have fun
Best math class I've ever Taken! He's so cute too!!

Kevin is by far the best Math teacher I have ever had. If you ever need him he has office hours and is always good to respond back to your emails. You have a weekly quiz every Friday but the lecture before he tells you what it is going to be on and practically gives you the answers. He also gives reviews that are pretty much the tests. TAKE HIM!

Best math teacher ever. He was always there to help students via email and appointment. He is very clear on his expectations and what you will be tested on. There is absolutely no reason not to get an A in this class if you put in some work. I'd take the rest of my classes from him if I could.

Professor Wortman is great.  He wrote his own textbook for Math 1060 and it is easily the most clear math textbook I've ever used.  He assists students often via meetings or email.  The homework prepares very well for the tests, and the practice tests look exactly like the exams. I wish Professor Wortman taught higher level classes, too!
Kevin is a terrific professor. Practice exams are exactly like tests. He has weekly quizzes but he will tell you what's on them the class before.

Kevin is the best math teacher I have ever had. He is very clear in how he explains concepts; and he puts the class notes online so we can print and bring them to class for notes. He has office hours and will answer additional Qs after class. There is a lot of homework and a weekly quiz. If you ask questions and be engaged, you'll do very well.

Hey folks.  Math is my least favorite subject and I made it through this class.  This man is smart, fair, and he  cares. He is hands down one of the best teachers.  Don't be a fool.  Sign up for his class ASAP.

Awesome professor! He is a very funny and nice guy who is always willing to help. He explains things so it's easy to understand and he gives you tons of reviews so that you're well prepared for the class. The homework isn't hard and you dont have to buy a book for his class either. Great professor!
Great Math teacher! No textbook to purchase and he keeps class interesting. Do the practice exams and you will be fine on the tests.
Best math teacher EVER! attend class, do the homework, and practice exams and you'll do fine. Really friendly and easy to talk to in case you need any help.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Like others said, if you go to class, do the homework (which is very easy), and go over the practice test, you will do great on the tests! He REALLY knows what he is talking about and will help you out if you don't fully understand the material. Attendance is mandatory but his class flies by as he makes it really interesting.
GREAT GREAT professor.  He was the best math teacher. easily.  attend class, study the practice exam.  you will do just fine.

Prof. Wortman is a great math teacher! His lectures make complicated math easy and the homework load isn't bad at all. If you do the practice test then the actual test isn't hard at all. He's very funny, helpful, relatable, and easy to understand. I would take all my required math from him if he taught any more classes.
Great Teacher.  Practice exams just like actual exams.  You do not need to buy a text book.

This class was great! He is such a great teacher and made everything so much easier. I am terrible at math and now he made things make sense. DO take math from him. You will have such a great semester! No textbook either and he gives practice exams JUST like his real exams.

Wortman is a great teacher.  The only people who complain about Wortman are those who do poorly in his class because they don't attend lectures.  Show up to class, keep up on the homework (easy),  and study the practice exams for a good grade.  Definitely my favorite math teacher.

He is pretty easy and makes sure that everyone understands what he is teaching. He is very open to questions and willing to help outside of class. He doesn't use a text book just his notes. If you look at the text book he only gets through the first couple chapters. EASY!

He doesn't dumb down the content but is still able to get the content across to almost every level of student.  He is extremely fair with test, with practice test that largely mimic the actual test.  If you attend lectures you will do well in this class.

Professor Wortman is great! He explains things clearly, and actually cares if you learn it or not. He is also pretty easy going and will answer any questions you have. Probably the best math teach I've ever had! Also puts all his text and homework on the internet, and is very reasonable when it comes to workload.

He is absolutely awesome! Makes sure everyone understands what he's talking about and gives us multiple examples both everyday and mathematical to appeal to most learning styles. Oh, and you don't need to buy a textbook because he writes his own and posts it online!
Attend class, he makes sure everyone understands. The work is easy. Show up, do the optional homework, A.

Wortman is a stud! first time i took math 1050 i had a D-.with wortman i pulled off a B+.pretty easy class.makes it easier to learn.doesn't expect as much as other professors might.don't need to buy the textbook.all the homework is online and pretty easy.exams are fine too.practice exams cover evrything you need to know to be prepared.take Wortman!

I hate math and I LOVED this class.  He is more concerned with making sure everyone understands the fundamentals than flying through material so fast you can't keep up like other math teachers I've had. He honestly wants everyone to do well and makes getting an A very doable.  He's just a big math nerd with funny lectures and a great lecture style!

Wortman is an awesome teacher.  At the beginning of the semester I was a little confused.  However, as time progressed, everything made sense.  He really cares about his students.  You don't even have to buy the text book.  Awesome dude, easy to talk to.

Make sure to do every assignment and try to go to every lab, so you can get a good buffer for the final. The labs and assignments were all very easy, so the lab final was the hardest part of the class. The labs and reports are much longer than CHEM 1215, and the final is basically a mini CHEM 1220 final with a bit of lab procedure.

I never interacted with the professor because the TA did almost everything. That being said, the lab was organized poorly with an outdated, poorly written lab manual. For about half of the class we did labs before we learned the content in lecture, with the last lab being almost a full month before learning the content. The final was also difficult
Final was very easy and we were told exactly what to study. You get 100 points dropped and TA basically does everything outside final exam stuff.
She is very unresponsive to emails, and pretty accommodating to students. Lab itself is fine because a TA runs it but she makes the final and it is unreasonably hard. Avoid if possible.

She is nice and the course is like any regular lab. However, the final was ridiculous. Way too hard for a 1 credit course. My rating would be higher if she didn't make the lab final so hard. It was all open ended/ no multiple choice. I hope she changes the final after seeing how bad we all did.

Stay away if you can. Shes a nice person, I bet, but I have seen how she snaps at students when she walks around different labs. The final has been changed so many times, and to figure out what the final is about, you have to dig through 10 emails she sends weekly instead of posting about it on Canvas. No lab final should be as hard
not a good professor
Completely changed how finals were done to make it much more difficult and load-bearing for students. Unclear with expectations and how things are done. Leaves everything up to the TAs.
Took this teacher for a lab and never met her but the class set up was great and when I did need to email her about things she was responsive and very helpful with very lenient grading.

I did not interact with her ever. I really only interacted with my TA. She did send out lots of announcements and she made the final. She changed the final to be a paper final instead of a lab final which I did not like, but I got an A in the class because I did good on the labs and lab reports. She changed the reports so be aware of what she says.

Her tests are made up of only homework problems and you are given the answers to the homework problems two days before the tests. She is not very good at using Canvas, very slow to put in grades, and is pretty unresponsive to emails. The class had to be curved significantly at the end. There were two classes where attendance was taken and graded.

The more she gets to know you, the more likely you are to get a better grade. If you go to her office hours, participate regularly in class you'll probably do better just because she recognizes you. If you miss class, even for medical issues, she will be very slow to answer emails and takes a very passive approach to helping during office hours.

She claims that she loves to teach but she puts very little effort into her teaching. Most of the material she uses comes from the lecture notes of other professors. Occasionally she turned to a slide and say "I have no idea why this is here" showing that she hadn't prepared for the lecture properly. Her main focus is on her research not teaching.

Luisa is a great professor that keeps her students in mind. Her lectures are tough and fast paced. She doesn't take attendance, but it matters - curving grades significantly if a student doesn't miss. Finish all the homework and assignments on time; she'll notice. Software used to complete homework gives you two attempts per assignment, use both!

Luisa is the best! She is always available through email and is quick to respond (including weekends and unusual hours). Go to her office hours and ask lots of questions. For the class in general, if you read the textbook and do all the homework you'll be fine.
I will disagree with the previous post. The exams are taken straight from the discussion assignments and the homework. The lectures could be better but the class is straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Compared to Steele's class, Luisa is a bit of a let-down. Her lectures are unorganized and difficult to understand. Only 5 Homework assignments which are easy. Tests are significantly more difficult. No extra credit, so plan ahead. She uses phrases like "I don't know" and Whatever" frequently. Do review problems in textbook and study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Luisa is very caring with her students and tries to engage on a personal level with everybody. She is an extremely smart person, and really wants you to do good! Although her lectures aren't completely well organized, she tries to make it so that you get a good grade. Tests are easy, and she is very helpful during office hours.
Whittaker-Brooks was very helpful during office hours and was always happy to explain things numerous times to me. Made a difficult subject easy to digest.

Advice for this class is to ask questions and go to Luisa outside of class. It will be time consuming with work and studying because there's a lot of material. Luisa is best one-on-one and is more than happy to help her students understand the material anytime. Not the best lecturer, but she wants you to succeed and is reasonable with grading.

reviews.comment: She would take something completely out of the class
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Luisa really grew on me as a prof. She's entertaining, and she interacts with her students. Online Mastering Chem assignments often have errors, but she's willing to fix your score. Her tests aren't impossible, but definitely study! I'd read the book, especially for Mastering Chem, and go to class. On 3 random days, we got points for attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Luisa is hilarious. She has such a quirky personality and truly is passionate about chemistry. I definitely had to put time in to practice but if you do the discussion sections you can expect a good grade on the tests. Luisa is always available to help and I truly found a friend in her. She is fantastic and I highly recommend her!

Luisa is very relaxed and lenient, but she also really pushes your understanding. Her tests are challenging but not unreasonable. Her lectures can be a bit confusing, but if you put in the work to learn the material with the pacing of the class, you'll get an A.

Her lectures are convoluted. While she is a very nice person, she puts forth the bare minimal effort to help students succeed. Complete disconnect between homework and tests because she just gets everything online. She barely gives partial credit on tests and expect to get 70% just because you made a few dumb mistakes. Take non-honors instead.

Luisa was a pretty great teacher, especially compared to the other Gen Chem professors at the U. She actually tries to teach you and does have some passion for some of the topics. Liked her stories and the perspective her research gave some of the topics. If you haven't taken AP, you'll have to work, but otherwise its a piece of cake.

She is a wonderful person and really is willing to help her students outside of the classroom. However, my friends and I believe that her heart is in her research rather than teaching. If you haven't taken AP chem, you're going to have to work twice as hard as most of your peers. Tests are tricky to figure out, but not unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: good professor. funny

Luisa is a very funny and blunt. She is not afraid to say exactly what she means. She knows chemistry pretty well and is willing to help. She also gives practice problems for tests and quizzes with almost identical problems from the tests, which helps getting a good grade majorly.

Luisa was funny and relaxed. Her favorite thing to say was "I don't know the periodic table!" She really cared about the students, she really knew her chemistry, and she really enjoys teaching. Her tests didn't seem too bad to me, but I had heard that many people studied hard for them. Go talk to her before the tests and she gives major hints.

Dr. Whittaker-Brooks is the best teacher I have ever had.   She makes lecture very fun and interesting.  She has a bunch of funny anecdotes related to her experiences in science.  I will highly recommend her.
This class was easy as long as you studied the material. The exams and quizzes weren't too hard if you spaced out your studying. If you don't, it can feel overwhelming in a short amount of time.

GREAT!! at getting point across via recorded lectures. Per lecture, 5 q. assgnmt that you can retake infinitely (not worth much, grade is heavily quizzes and exams). You take a quiz based on 2-3 assgnmt, (you can take 2x). 2-3 assgmnt per quiz, 2-3 quizzes per exam. Clear instructions walk you through solving each problem, which translate to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 4 Exams, one of which is a cumulative final. Also multiple quizzes, all timed (2 attempts). The online class is also very lecture-heavy and has a textbook (didn't really use the textbook). This class did take time and was, at times, hard b/c of the teacher's wording on certain problems or explanations, but with a little effort, it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The quizzes and assignments are super easy. There were 4 exams through the semester and all the modules for each exam are due the night before the exam, and then the exam was open for a week. However even if you get 100% on assignments and high scores on quizzes, the exams are difficult all 4 of them combined are worth almost 50% of your grade.
Instructions and grading criteria for assignments and tests were vague. There was also not much feedback given. Lectures and readings were very interesting though.
Did not give good feedback for assignments/tests. I also did not feel like the readings were valuable given their substance to length ratios.

I would not recommend, online organization was really poor. No modules tab to organize information and lectures, video lectures and assignments only posted through announcements. Content was interesting but be prepared to struggle to figure out where and when things must be submitted.
Probably my favorite professor at the U.
It was very difficult to get feedback/find out what to work on. Most of the grade was based on open-question tests. Spends a lot of lecture time in ways that made it hard to get the point.

It was the easiest class ever. There's a 2 homework about textbook problem, 2 homework about write 300 word for essay after watching Youtube. For the exam, just watch the exam review video. It exactly almost same as review. Easy, less homework. I didnt even watch lecture video but I got A+ . Trust me guys this guy is the best.
This course will be pretty easy if you have a basic understanding of math. The professor provides great example problems which help greatly during an exam. Exams are open note.
Posts so many lecture videos and talks very fast so the information is always unclear. Gives no heads up on upcoming tests till the day before. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have taken 3 classes from Professor Li. The reason I like him so much is he is so clear on his grading criteria. You know exactly what you have to do in the class and he sticks to his syllabus. The midterm and final combined are worth 70% of your grade, but he gives you the pages to study & the tests reflect what he gives you as the test prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had him for Econ 5420 China and the Global Economy. Overall, the class is fairly easy. The lectures are interesting and on the shorter side. I took the class online which did not impact studying the course material. The class is more history heavy than economics heavy. Overall, a low stress, high reward class which I would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He makes simple topic seem really hard and complex. Goes really fast and does not explain himself well at all. In fact he doesn't really explain things at all.

China and the Global Economy by Professor Li is a pretty easy class. One presentation throughout the semester on an article he gives you, and two exams. The exams are written in class by hand. Before the exams, he gives you around 10 to 20 pages to read. Study those readings and you should do fine. Really nice guy.
Prof Li is very knowledgeable about his field and his passion for it shows in his lectures. His exams are pretty straight forward and easy as long as you do the required readings for it.

I really enjoyed this class. The setup was two exams from readings, a presentation, and one homework. The lectures were interesting, but not mandatory. With this style of class, you really get out of it what you put into it. Li is very versed on the subject and selects great readings.

I have taken Professor Li for two Classes, and I am taking him for a third. His tests are exactly what he assigns for reading. But it is assigned a week before the exam, but still more than enough time to read them. They are 2 essays 3 if graduate student. So make sure you understand the readings he assigns. Very good professor highly recommend.

Only times you need to study are when he gives you the reading for the exams a week before. Overall doesnt ask much of you. Only 2 assignments and 2 tests and one power point. The assignments are really easy and so is the powerpoint. Just need to study for the exams the week before

Dr. Minor is very enthusiastic and makes lectures enjoyable. However, homework can sometimes take close to 8 hours and are graded rather harshly. Exams were weighted very heavily at 85%, but small cheat sheets were allowed. He did generously curve the class so that the overall grade distribution was fair after the final average was very low.

Worst class I've taken. Minor is unorganized & writes the project as he goes. He makes up a new one every semester, so constant changes to criteria & rules, broken sample code, etc. Took more time than the rest of my classes put together (including heat transfer). Our robot barely worked and we got 3rd place. Take from Mascaro if AT ALL POSSIBLE

Truly an awful experience. I've chosen to go into mechatronics, and I HATED this course. Minor is a nice guy, but didn't have realistic expectations. Choosing our groups for us, 40hr/week  workloads, giving sample code that didn't work, and just about everything else made this course brutal. Good luck.

Possibly the most time-consuming class I have ever taken. Prof. Minor does an average job in lectures, but his expectations and implementation of this course is awful. Minor is nice, but totally oblivious to the realities of his student's lives and how his course is structured. Turned an otherwise interesting topic into a nightmare.

As many have said, this class is the most time-consuming course by a huge margin. Don't overload your schedule when taking this class, you will easily spend a full-time job's worth of time on this class. Two large weekly assignments, weekly quizzes, weekly labs that take 3 hours, a weekly team presentation, and a massive team project on top.

Minor is a good guy that cares a lot but he also expects a LOT. I took him during a covid semester and I think him making the decision to have everyone build there own individual robot was a bit of a disaster. In past classes teams usually had to make one robot. We had four robots so four times the problems. This class is a full time job.

Professor Minor is a great guy and did a fine job teaching considering Covid. This class was difficult not because of him, but because of the departmentally mandated curriculum. Mechatronics requires an unbelievable amount of work. Minor was quite forgiving in extending deadlines when people struggled and provided help when asked.

Don't expect to have a life outside mechatronics if you take it with Minor. 3-4 hefty assignments every week, a quiz, a lab, and of course the semester long project make this the most demanding course I have ever taken by FAR. Full time job was an understatement. Avoid at all costs.

Granted, my experience is colored by the pandemic, but my class with professor Minor was one of the most stressful, irritating, and down right upsetting experiences I've had in university. Constantly changing the rules of the class project, lectures that had little worth to said project, and a workload that took up 80% of my time this semester

Aweful at lecturing. Assumes that you know things in super detail that he's never mentioned or may have been mentioned for 5 seconds in a class 2 years ago. Often got docked on labs for missing items that we were never told needed to be included. His quizzes and tests are full of trick questions that you need knowledge he didn't teach you to solve

This class was the most time-consuming class I've ever taken in the Mechanical Engineering program. There's a very large semester long group project to design and build a robot from scratch. There are also labs which are time consuming and difficult because there are pre and post labs. There are also quizzes every week (need 60% avg to pass).

Mark Minor is one of the most demanding professors I've had. You are required to get a minimum grade on all quizzes to meet "passing criteria" and solve even his most challenging homework problems in less than ten minutes (same timing on exams). But his class is fair; do what he says, solve HW as he says to, study hard, you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The professor will stand in front of the class and write notes on his computer and project them onto the screen. This would be okay if his handwritting was legible. He is not very knowledable about the subject and had to be corrected several times during lecture on different subjects. His TAs are harsh graders and make life a freakin nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I don't like him at all. His lectures consist of him sitting at the front talking to himself and working example problems without telling us what the example is until we are done. His tests are simply a race remember what you can, and race through the test, but don't try to think critically about anything or you will run out of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is a really good guy and is super understanding and helpful in a one on one environment.   That said though his head is in the clouds about the expectations for the class.    The amount of material on his tests makes it impossible to do good engineering work on the problems if you plan on finishing and the project will take up all of your time.

Really cool guy.  He puts all of his handwritten notes online for students.  He is a really good teacher and honestly cares about his students.  He was my project advisor for our senior project and he was amazing.  He will go out of his way to help you out not to mention he is the kind of professor you wouldn't mind hanging out with just for fun.

THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE HAD IN 3 YEARS OF ATTENDING THE UNIVERSITY'S MECHANICAL ENGINEERING PROGRAM. THE BEST! I had him for Mech II in spring of 2008 and my only regret is that he didn't teach Mech I or advanced controls the next semester. It's too bad the previous reviewer had a bad experience with him.
His teaching sucks and he is a mean guy. Very partial and highly unpredictable.
No complaints whatsoever. Got in, did the work, got out. Easy
Dr. Loewen is the best professor I have ever met in UoU. Attendance is not mandatory and exams are super easy to get over 95%. If you want to get easy A in UoU, just choose him!

Easiest class I've taken.
HW and Exams are all online, with open-note. Very easy to pass - hard to fail.
I never went to class and was able to catch up by the notes Loewen uploaded to Canvas.
Great Gen Ed course.
Extra credit for visiting the museum on campus during Dino events.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Loewen is a knowledgeable professor. He's very competent and goes over a lot of info. This class is a relatively easy A, but it requires doing a TON of homework, many of which are papers (short, but still). The grading is not harsh - as long as you submit it, you'll likely get an A. Attendance is not mandatory and all the lectures are recorded.
For an online GenEd, there is a surprising amount of work. I wouldn't recommend the class if you are taking other intense classes at the same time. Very nice and very funny professor though.

Professor Lowen one of my favorites, was very funny/entertaining. Class included zoom lectures that were easy to understand/fun. grade consisted of two short quizzes and two assignments each week (one for the topic that week, one for movie that week) that were pretty easy. Overall loved his class, excited to take another class of his next semester.

Loewen was a great professor and even while being over Zoom he makes his lectures so fun. He begins every class by watching Jurassic Park and he is a very fun and goofy professor. He has helped with many displays and findings at the history museum on campus so it's cool to hear his stories. If you miss a class his lectures are very easy to review.
Easy A! The content was super interesting and enjoyable. Zoom's are not mandatory and the course work is straightforward. I highly recommend taking Dr. Loewen's class if you can!

Loved this class! Learning from an expert in paleontology, what a wonderful experience. Online quizzes/exams were easy. All material is covered to prepare you for assignments. I'm taking another class from him in the future!

I took both GEO 1000 and 1040, and they were great! I was worried about fulfilling my gen ed requirements since I don't really enjoy learning about science, but these classes were easy. I didn't attend the Zoom meetings, just completed the assignments. Very easy classes—at times there can be quite a few assignments, but it honestly is not that bad.
He was AWESOME, wish that there was an option for in person!
did not join the zoom a single time. everything is online. amazingly easy class. highly recommend.

Easy class with fun professor. No textbook but you're expected to rent the week's movie online and watch it as homework. His online lectures weren't super helpful but I had no trouble passing the class whatsoever. If you look at the notes he posts, watch the movie, and do the assignments, this class is a super easy A.

Fun class with a professor who obviously and infectiously cares about the subject matter. Would absolutely recommend world of dino to anyone who is looking to fulfill a general credit, or who just wants a fun and interesting class. Mark makes it easy to do well and offers a lot of extra credit/field trip opportunities. Homework/quizzes are easy.
Coolest Professor I have had at the U. Easiest class I've taken yet most interesting. If you do not take this guy at least once during your college career, you are doing yourself a disservice.

Very easy class, I barely attended the zoom meetings and still passed. You get daily quizzes and movie/ homework assignments that were quick to do. Easy grading criteria, if you got a question wrong he will leave a comment on which one it is. Exams were mostly based off the quizzes. Drops your lowest quizzes and homework to boost your grade
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Nothing but good things to say. Dr. Loewen is very knowledgeable about the topics, explains them well, is engaging, and to top it off, offers (free!) field trips, which I highly recommend, as he's the most informed tour guide you'll ever have when it comes to dinosaurs. Super fun class, super fun professor.

Two homework and two quizzes each week, everything can be found on quizlet tho. Loved this professor, this is my second class I'm taking from him. he lets you turn in assignments late up until the exams. It's great being able to take easy classes when you're taking hard ones.
in lectures he plays with dinosaurs. we watched Jurassic Park. very cool.
Professor makes the material something we actually want to learn about. Lots of homework but is definitely manageable. Overall I would recommend him and this class.

This is my second time taking a course from him, Classes are fast-moving but well structured with a focus on fun, He has a really open teaching style, and just wants you to get interested in the material. Great guy, super chill, super experienced, and just wants to talk about dinosaurs.

Mark is an awesome professor. He loves lecturing about the ongoing discovery of dinosaur fossils. Despite his lectures being on Zoom, he ensures interaction is constantly present. There are two quizzes, one activity, and one project due every week; however, they're easy. He has field trips too! Overall, Mark is a great guy, and he's very engaging.

He's so passionate about his subject, the class covers some really interesting things. I know it's tempting to skip an online class, but it's great stress relief and basically does your homework for you if you show up. The dinosaur unit was a blast and I ended up learning way more than I expected. Sometimes answers and grades are unclear though.

I took both GEO1000 & GEO1040 from Mark and I highly recommend 1000 over 1040 if you're looking for an easy science credit. Be prepared to have to memorize a lot of bones, and beware biweekly quizzes and weekly projects & essays that are due THE DAY OF CLASS. He's chill about late work though. There are also several cool extra credit field trips!
The GOAT. A lot of busy work, but he's still the GOAT.
My all-time favorite professor!!!! He's so funny and the homework/quizzes are really easy

This class was super fun and super easy. There's a lot to do each week but its all so easy. You basically watch movies each week and answer worksheets about them. The midterm and final tests are really long but yet again they are VERY easy. Mark is a great teacher and seems to really care about the subject. Definitely take any of his classes!

This class was the easiest and most fun science credit of my entire academic career, and I'm looking forward to taking another class with him this upcoming semester! Mark doesn't tolerate disrespectful/annoying students. Sometimes it felt like things were under explained in the lectures, but the content is easy enough to figure out on your own.
