reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong he is a smart man but he does not know how to convey anything in a meaningful way to the students. His lecture notes were atrocious just a jumble of random scribblings. Expect 50+ hours of homework with no extensions, and no replies to emails. Don't forget about the lab section HW which adds another 15 hours. Have fun test-taking
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I will say that he seemed to care about students understanding during lecture and would take time to answer questions that you ask. Being someone who was not confident enough to speak up and ask questions during lecture, I had some trouble understanding the material. Instead, I emailed him for further help a couple times... he never answered me.

I would give the professor a 0 if I can. His lecture style remains the same online, which is unclear, riddled with junk and lack of examples during class time. Lots of hw is an understatement even for a 1 credit class. doesn't provide a lot of review for the exam. Expect to self teach yourself and cooperate with others to get through this classes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Nesse teaches a difficult class but he does it pretty well. You should attend lectures as he is quite good at answering questions and trying to look at just the notes can be difficult. There is a ridiculous amount of homework as well, so don't start it the night of. His teaching can be all over the place, but using the book can help immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nesse is a very smart guy and seems to genuinely want to help students learn. If you have a question during the lecture, he'll do his best to find a satisfactory answer. Homework is long, straight from the textbook, but helps solidify the knowledge he teaches in the lecture. Tests are only a few difficult questions, but they are very strictly timed
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are an absolute mess, his notes are messing and hard to decipher if you weren't there. The homework was a nightmare, expect about 50+ problems a week each problem with multiple parts with many steps!!! Oh, don't forget about the math lab problems. Do expect him to give extensions too, he expects that this is your only class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A very poor teacher who doesn't care that students aren't understanding. He does not care about his students, so his lectures are messy and incomprehensible.

A lot of homework is an understatement. He might ask you to code in the weekly math labs. His lectures are dry and filled with metaphors. Midterms are challenging. He does not prepare students enough for the test, which only happens during the week when the midterm is on Friday. You are better off with someone else or self-taught in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you learn by being taught, Nesse is not the Prof for you. Nesse is an incredibly smart man, but he has no idea how to communicate with his students. Be prepared to spend at least 10 hr per homework assignment and another 3-4 on the labs (on top of normal lab time). His tests are a toss up on the difficulty, but the finals tend to be brutal.

Teaches by metaphor. Hilarious comparisons that will stick in your brain. Does a fairly decent job of keeping Canvas updated. Beware unpredictable weekly hw. Longest so far took me 25hrs to complete, shortest was about 6hrs. No feedback from hw. Frankly I prefer Alfelds method of doing online homework with instant feedback and unlimited attempts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nesse was quite possibly one of the worst teachers I've had ever. When the class failed the first midterm, he didn't see that as an issue with teaching and instead shifted blame to the students themselves. The homework was also far too much work with some assignments reaching 70 problems. He did help more preparing for the final but he's still bad

Spends way too much time in class going over irrelevant topics. He's a super smart, passionate guy, but when we spend an entire class going over how calculus relates to image processing...? It just makes no sense and leaves so many people confused and unprepared for tests. I hope he can improve in the future, but I wouldn't take him ever again.

Do not take a class from Nesse. This is your final warning. Do everything you possible can to avoid his class. He is extremely unclear in his lectures. Im often more confused coming out of his lectures than going into them. He skips so many steps. His tests are IMPOSSIBLE. He does test on what he teaches. If you can even call what he does teaching.

If you're the kind of person who learns math through being taught (can't just read the textbook) good luck. His lectures are confusing, slow, and unrelated to what you really need to know. Homework is extremely long and different from the test content which are extremely difficult. Not willing to work with you or give quality feedback.

Nesse is a hilarious guy, but gives out way too much homework. I and my classmates spend 6+ hours outside of class working on problems that often don't even feel relevant. I'm talking homework assignments with 60 or 70 problems due Fridays with material we haven't covered completely until Thursdays. It's ridiculous and just not worth it.

Has passion and knowledge for what he teaches. But is not a good teacher. He fails to grasp that not everyone who takes this class is an engineering major. He gave a programming lab to people with no experience. His tests are reasonable. The class is super hw heavy. It is rare to not spend 6-8 hours a week on it. He is condescending as well. Don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Nesse will grade you on your understanding of the subject. The homework assignments are thorough and the labs are very effective. The tests are very representative of what was taught and he gives clear study guides. Overall, you will get a grade according to your understanding of the topics. He is a funny, quirky guy and I enjoyed lecture

This class is hard, if you haven't seen the material before, especially once you get into the PDE material. However, He is a very generous grader.  One reason why the PDE stuff is hard is because you switch to his own textbook (it's free) But to be honest, I didn't find the text book very helpful.  Easy  tests curves a lot. Averages were B plus
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Not a very good professor in my opinion. Homework is ridiculous, especially when it's problems from his book. Exams are easy, but He makes up for it in projects and labs. I had a hard time following his lectures once we started subjects from his book. His handwriting is not the best and He seems to never fully erase the chalk board. He is chill tho

Easy exams, difficult homework, knows his stuff.  Nesse is a great professor he cares about people understanding the concepts behind the math. If you enjoy math you'll love this class. On a side note he is has an awesome personality, super outdoorsy, climbs and so forth!

Homework is terribly hard and long. Put the time into it though - it's the only way you'll really learn. Tests are FAR easier than the homework. It can be done. Group projects are hella hard, so start early. He has his own book which is frustrating. Don't purchase a book, you'll barely use it. GOOD LUCK!

I found his lectures very helpful when I went and paid attention, though he did get  behind.(but the homework was still due on the material he didn't cover) The class was at 8:30 am, so I ended up just reading the book. I found the Homework very very long, but overall I thought the class was fair.

He is a nice fun guy but the worst teacher in the world.  You have labs every week that are really hard and do not help you understand the topic at all. We had a review session for one of our midterms and the only thing he did was pass out a practice midterm and did not help us go through it.

Although hes knowledgable, Lectures were confusing and I was always lost. I stopped going to lectures because I got more out of sitting and reading the book and working on the hw than I ever did in class. He fell behind in lectures and still expected Hw that were never covered to be turned in on their due dates. Expect maybe 10-15 hrs a week of hw

Never replies to emails. Lectures weren't helpful. Homeworks were made by him so you can't find examples in book that will help. He also doesn't believe in posting solutions to hw, tests, etc. The only plus is his tests aren't too hard.

His tests were passable but his homeworks were kinda rough. He makes up his own homework questions so there's no way to find book questions to see if you're doing it right.  He also doesn't post solutions to hw or midterms because he's against it. You won't know what you got right or wrong. He's also terrible at emailing back. Lectures were boring

Even as a second Bachelors student, I never had such a genuinely terrible professor until Dr. Nesse. He puts very little effort into teaching the class, rarely responds to emails, is often unwilling to meet outside of lecture, and is surprisingly rude. He did not return many assignments, even after months of waiting. Just awful.

Quite possibly the worst instructor I've ever had the displeasure of taking a class with. From the looks of it, nobody in class had a clue as what was going on. Your best bet is to memorize his practice tests word by word, as he won't bother put any effort on the actual tests, and you'll get plenty of points just writing down what you memorized.

I took Calculus I online during the summer semester. As noted before, all that the professor does is open the homework. Grades are not recorded for weeks, response to questions take days, and he cancelled the help sessions as well. Took the final yesterday, won't know the score or my final grade for two more weeks. Avoid him.

Online Calc 3. Professor did nothing but open webworks and record grades. Book did not cover material required for webworks or exams. Practice exams had wrong answers. Professor did not answer questions in Canvas. Did not set up office hours until April. Took painfully long to grade exams. Avoid at all costs.

Took online class, teacher put up webwork assignments and that's about it. Practice Tests were not very useful, solutions to these practice tests were rushed and incomplete. Didn't give suggested problems/sections from book... Very useless.
Dr. Durbach is awesome. Very much invested in seeing her students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not only was Professor Durbach a good teacher, she was a good person. Her classes are engaging, her readings are interesting and never excessive, her grading policy is fair and consistent. I've never written a review on this site, and I rarely fill out course feedback forms, but I was motivated to do so for her. That should tell u something.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nadja is caring, positive, and enjoys hearing from students. She is a tough grader but is invested in you having a successful thesis proposal. Use Grammarly and the Writing Center for essays. Pop Quizzes make attendance necessary and missing them kills your grade. 2% extra credit optional lecture and grade round up to the highest next percentage.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is fantastic! She is a very tough grader but also willing to discuss and help you grow based on feedback. I always felt like she cared for my success and comprehension of material. I will say that some of her essay assignments are open ended but I think she likes to see the directions a student goes! I would take the course all over again!

I had Professor Durbach for 3 different classes during my time at the U of U. HIST 1500, 3100 and 3140. She is an amazing professor and really cares about students success. By far my most favorite professor I had while at the U. She has amazing lectures, and is very well organized. Would recommend her to anyone.

If you want to go into history and don't like reading, then choose a different major. This class is no exception, TONS of reading involved. It may be different for others but the final exam was the toughest OF MY LIFE (3 full essays in 2 hours) but I'm glad I did it (and you can too!!!)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She was one of the toughest professors I had. The class is very time consuming with 1-2 Chapter of reading each week. The quizzes are difficult and the class average on them is below 50% for all the quizzes. She made me feel like I was a terrible writer. I thought I was gonna fail this course till the very last week of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Durbach is awesome and this class is really interesting. She grades tough but fairly. If you are a decent writer you can score around 90% on all the essays. Her quizzes are short and simple. Just be prepared to read a lot each week. It's interesting stuff though!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Durbach is a very effective instructor and she is super approachable and will offer any clarification. Do the readings, plan your essays carefully and you will do fine.

I feet like Durbach enjoys being "tough." Truthfully, I felt victimized by her. She causes her students a great deal of stress. I left her class feeling less confident about my abilities than when I began. There are plenty of great professors in that department. She is not one of them.

Dr. Durbach makes learning fun, and she makes you think about what you're learning. She is an expert on 19th Century Britain, and probably on 20th Century Britain. I'd go back just to sit in on her classes. Pretty tough grader, so don't take her if you don't want to pay attention and work hard in class.

I have taken a few courses from this professor and I have enjoyed them all. This course includes several "chapters" each includes several readings, video lectures, and discussion/review questions. There are three papers throughout the course and a final. The papers are challenging, but provide an excellent learning experience. Highly Recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Durbach is a great professor but she is a tough grader. She offers extra credit (at least in HIST4080) that is worth 5 percentage points on your grade. You have to work for it though. Very informative and knowledgeable.

The analysis papers are graded HARD and the topics are vague. She also told the class that there is a final exam the last month of the semester (no mention in the syllabus) and that she has the review sheet ready, BUT she won't post it until like a week before the actual exam (WHY?!) Do not take this class. I hope she curves her grades...

She grades on things she hasn't put into the instructions. She doesn't follow a proper grading rubric. The first paper I spent maybe 5 hours on and didn't have it reviewed by the Writing Center; the second paper I spent about 16 hours plus had several second opinions saying it was a really strong paper. Both got an 80%.....        :(

Make sure you know how to do a medical analysis or you will not get a good grade on the papers. She is a really tough grader but doesnt have a lot of assignments throughout the class. Take this if you are looking for easy quizzes and super hard analysis papers basically.
Puts too much emphasis on discussion participation.

Professor Durbach is a great teacher. Her lectures are very organized and the lessons are open for any question or discussion. Its sort of hard because there are only 3 papers and 1 final. The papers were hard but if you go to class you will do fine on the final. She is very friendly and always seems to be in a good mood.

Professor Durbach was great.  She is very knowledgeable on the subject she teaches and makes everything interesting.  She is also open to questions whenever you needed her.  I often emailed her and would get a response in less than twenty four hours.  Great class.

I was in her 20th Century Britain class the first year she taught it. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and she was a really fun teacher. It was pretty hard because its only one 3 page essay, one 10 paper, and a final  exam, (which I havent taken yet, wish me luck!!!) but overall I really enjoyed this class. Ton's of fun every day!

I took her for Victorian Britain and she was great--extremely accessible and friendly. Each lecture was well outlined and very organized. Readings assigned per week for discussion class on Fridays. Three papers and one final take-home exam.
Not a good class.

Teaches british history and Medical History.  An amazing professor who is willing to help and desires her students to learn what they are interested in.  One of the best teachers I have had in the department.  I wish i had taken her classes prior to having her for my Senior Seminar.

I honestly don't understand the dislike. Her lectures were pretty average but her homeworks weren't that difficult if you paid attention in class. People's main complaints for her were her tests, but she would mostly take all of the test questions from example problems, so they were super easy if you studied for them.

You walk into the class and leave feeling more confused than when you arrived. She doesn't explain new ideas clearly or even try to keep students interested, its actually the opposite. I asked questions, but the answers didn't really help, so I gave up. The only way to do well in this class with her is to study the WHOLE thing on your own.

The class was pretty simple, and the concepts were easy to understand. Pania does a good job at making sure that every concept is as confusing as possible. All of the examples she did in class had multiple mistakes, which her students would have to correct. She would get visibly angry at students who asked her questions during her lecture.

For a class that shouldn't be too difficult, she made the concepts much harder to understand than they needed to. Lectures were terrible, with the professor bouncing from topic to topic with very little explanation behind them. I'd leave lecture with more questions than answers. Overall, the professor is terrible at explaining the concepts

She doesn't know how to teach the subject. She clearly lacks teaching skills and invests energy in things that are not important for the learning process. If you really want to learn, consider taking another professor.

Prof. Newell seems to care how her students do in the class, but she clearly does not have a teachable understanding of mechanics of materials.  If anyone asks a question that slightly deviates from her lesson plan, she becomes distraught and answers a question that is not close to the one asked—better off learning directly from the textbook.
DO NOT TAKE MECHANICS OF MATERIALS FROM HER

Pania gets such a bad rap on here. I absolutely LOVED her. She gives clear expectations and her tests are EXACTLY like the hw/examples. Sometimes the exact same problems with other numbers. Class is demanding but if you do the hw you have an A easy. The final was optional which was awesome. Lectures were online and recorded. 10/10 would recommend

Worst test writer ever and she fully admitted she writes them the night before. Her online lectures were quite lackluster and we mostly composed of prewritten solutions to problems that she would poorly attempt to annotate with her mouse. Didn't record anything so if you missed a class you were screwed. Also did pop quizzes which just always suck.

While Prof Newell may be getting a bad rap she is a very caring person. Her lecturing ability is alittle rough and often times her lectures need revision. Tests are generally problems from HW or lecture so they aren't terrible. Solutions are just very inconsistently correct. That being said, she is so nice and is always encouraging the best.

She is a caring professor and genuinely wants all her students to succeed, but you have to work hard in her class. She emphasizes on understanding the fundamentals a lot and be ready to be tested on concept in her exams.

One of the worst professors I have ever seen. She humiliates students for not answering her questions that she has not done a good job teaching them. She is not useful in office hours. I suggest that she sits in other engineering classes at least for 4 years to learn basic teaching techniques. She does not belong to University of Utah.

Homework was very tricky and time consuming. She expects exceptionally high level of performance from all the students in the class. Closed book and closed notes exams and they were very tough. They were too lengthy to finish. Sometimes questions were unclear too. You also need to solve the problem the way it has been solved in class.

All tests and quizzes except for the final are no notes and closed book. I solved the problems a different way on the test and got the right answer, but got docked points because it was not done how she did it in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Newell has a complete lack of respect for the students she teaches. She will choose to belittle and embarrass most students in her class because she can. All you can do is work to understand the homework and try to make it through her poorly written tests and quizzes. She'll get better, but just hang in there and stay above the class average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Babu for 2140 Strength of Materials. Lectures were good, sometimes confusing at times. Office hours are very helpful. This is a difficult class but Dr. Babu provides more than enough resources to help you succeed if you take advantage of them. Exams are long and hard so make sure to study

Dr. Markovic is easily the laziest professor I have had the misfortune of taking a class from. He has created a system with these AI narrated videos that will allow him to “teach” this course until the day he retires with little to no effort while receiving the same pay that other professors are receiving for “the same work.” Group project blows.
All lectures were online videos. Homework was very simple if you watched the videos. Exams were identical to the homework which was very nice

The man. Unfortunately since it's transportation, not many students engage during his lectures. But, he is always super eager to answer any questions and go into more depth if needed. Homework and exams are super straightforward and doable.

Went above and beyond by answering questions and addressing concerns even on non-working days, such as Sundays. He exhibited a genuine eagerness to help clarify any doubts. Additionally, their lectures were well-structured, clear, and informative, which greatly contributed to a positive learning experience in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great instructor. Great content

he is very straightforward and accommodating. lectures are up to 2 hours long but the course was asynchronous. plenty of time to do assignments and exams (which is based on the homework). if you need help don't be afraid to ask.

very knowledgeable and reasonable, he is available outside of class to help. the homework and tests and quizzes were fair and reasonable. the biggest thing is there is so much busywork. expect to dedicate at least 9 hours a week to statistics. you will learn quickly. it might be rough if your not even slightly interested in statistics
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class for physics students
This was a tough course, but I learned a lot about PDEs. Lectures complimented the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't amazing. Didn't particularly care about your success. Office hours were limited. Homework problems were very difficult if you didn't have a very good grasp and 2+ years of continued practice in vector calc and linear algebra proofs. Advice: Review 3 proofs, 7 difficult computations for each subject of both fields. Pre-read the book
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Osting is really great at making sure concepts are clear. He gave us a well-defined outline of where we should be in our understanding of the subject. Also, if you get to take a 6000-level course with him, there is a great possibility of having a pizza party outside of class to prove a theorem not covered in class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Osting cares very much that you learn. Some assignments were a bit long, but he is very good about helping you if you get stuck. I would definitely recommend to anyone to take his class.

This was a great class - we covered many different topics, but I think we spent the right amount of time with each. Definitely take this course if you want to learn more about specific ways in which math is used to model phenomenon. The professor was very clear in lectures and lecture notes and was always there to help if you had any questions.

If you're into advanced applied math -- this is a great class to take.  You'll do a good amount of work but nothing unusual as compared to other upper division electives in sciences.  I enjoyed this course a lot !    The subject requires fluid multivariate calculus and linear algebra skills -- like almost all applied mathphysics classes.

He is trying to teach this class at a graduate level however this is a Hybrid undergraduate class. He doesn't acknowledge that you may have other class work or responsibilities which may not allow you to spend 4 hours a day on his class. He also has no clue how to teach younger students he only wants to do his research and teach grad students

Professor Symko is kind and caring, and a pretty average lecturer. Everything is handwritten, &slides are not available on Canvas. The homework was worth 25% of the grade, so the class was pretty test heavy. MEMORIZE THE STUDY GUIDES!!! Many of the answers for the exam will be on them! My final grade was curved from a C- to a B+ take that as u will
He has so much excitement for physics and his study guides for tests are very helpful, most questions come from the study guide. Minimal homework.

Professor Symko is one of the best instructors I have ever had. He is passionate about the material, the style of his lectures make concepts very easy to grasp, and he uses lots of demonstrations which helps solidify everything. The assignments and exams are multiple choice, it is not a difficult course. I wish I had him for every physics class.

He has been teaching for 40+ years and is very knowledgeable about physics, communication and audio. He's very nice and plays music before class starts to engage students from the beginning. Attend test reviews and take advantage of tutor hours.

Wouldn't take this class from him ever again. It could be really interesting, but he just sits there and reads off his lecture PDFs that don't correspond w/ the textbook. Really bad outside communication. Tests/homework don't reflect the lectures. Class is graded on 2 assignments, 3 tests alone. No office hours, no TA that we know of. STAY AWAY!

Professor Symko is very passionate about what he teaches. He works with students to make sure everyone understands the lectures and goes through all the homework and quizzes to further help. Make sure you don't have a class right after his class though, he doesn't really pay attention to the clock and keeps my class about 15 minutes late each class

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!! Your grade is based on homework and his exams. His lectures don't match the homework. His exams don't reflect what was taught in his lectures or his homework. Test averages were 58%. The only thing that helped me get an average score on his exams was going to his test reviews and then writing practice problems on a note card.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class I've ever taken. I was told this should be harder than chem, chem is so easy and makes so much sense. I have spent 12+ hours a week doing homework with tutors and I have learned nothing. If you want to take this class be sure you already know physics.

Difficulty of tests is dramatically higher than the lectures given. Hard to read his handwriting on lectures and answer keys for midterm exams. Discussion system is not helpful. Would NOT take any class from him again.

Professor Symko did a good job at explaining the basics of physics, but when it came time to take the test, I felt that what had learned didn't match the level of difficulty of the test; meaning the test was harder.
Tests are very hard, unlike any other bio class.
like everyone said he mostly just reads off the slides. his exams are really difficult

Lectures were ok, mostly based on slides. But neither the lectures nor the book prepares you for the exams. The questions were nearly incomprehensible. It's very easy to misinterpret despite understanding the content. But the final was better, so hopefully he realized exams were not accurately testing knowledge.

The exam is obscure and difficult to understand, and the material you've reviewed may not be covered at all… Meanwhile, topics that came up repeatedly during your review might not appear at all on the exam.

The lectures were redundant due to the fact that he read off the slides the entire time. The exams were unnecessarily difficult, and this is coming from someone who started studying a week before each exam. I used to be a cell biology major, and this class made me change my major because of how much I hated this class.

Rog's lectures felt like him just reading off of the powerpoint slides. Also, his tests were so difficult and felt like they didn't connect to the material covered in lecture. The questions are very convoluted and are written in a way that people who have a background in bio have a significant advantage, but not if you don't take a lot of bio.

He straight up cannot write a test that is decent and actually test your knowledge about any of the pathways or processes. He always has to test you on intricacy within something you may or may not have talked about and then you can have a whole lecture worth of material that won't even get tested.

Professor Rog is fine, but the disconnect between lecture content and tests is insane. The lectures do not prepare you for the exam. Even if you know the material, the wording of the questions is so convoluted that you could get it wrong. Everything except for the tests is fine, but wow do these tests suck.

Dr. Rog's class is definitely difficult, but not necessarily because designs it that way, but more because you have to grasp with scientific literature and abstract cell/molecular concepts that are hard to visualize. He values inclusivity and the power that comes from making mistakes and learning from them. Exams are tough, prepare ahead of time.

Professor Rog is challenging, but well within reason. His lectures are great and always had a quiz at the end. He is also very nice and encourages students to talk in class even if they might be wrong. The exams were quite tough, so make sure to study well for those.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR unless you have unlimited free time and no social life. She will give due dates at 9am and not specify its not due at midnight. only get 2 exused absences. attendance worth like 25%. she is a harsh grader. shes not very friendly. If you need WRTG 2 TAKE ANY OTHER PROFESSOR OR THIS WILL HURT YOUR GPA.

The majority of the class was talking amongst each other, but Kasimma guided the conversation well when we needed it. Gave long, detailed, and respectful feedback, and encouraged the same for all of us; really just a fantastic professor (just keep your phone away and participate in class). Also always says hi when we see each other on campus :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kasimma is a great instructor! She is funny and real during class discussions and creates a relaxed environment. Sometimes there can be misunderstandings because I believe English is not her first language, but that was never a real problem. There are 2 short story assignments throughout the semester and at least two writing assignments per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you value clear and concise assignments and a professor who can articulate instructions well, then choose a different professor. Kasimma was more interested in inflating her own published works and implementing coercive ideologies about race than providing a quality class about writing and rhetoric.

It felt like a high school class, you could not use your phone, laptop, or iPad, (all notes on paper), or you automatically lost participation/attendance credit. She is VERY attendance-heavy. The grades were unclear. She would take off points from assignments, but not say what was wrong. 2 essays (350 words) due every week. No drops with ANYTHING.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lots of content to cover and graded harshly in my opinion

While I do believe that Professor Okani knows her stuff, I fully believe that she grades too harshly and can be unfair at times. You are not allowed to turn in assignments late, you are not allowed to make up any assignments (drs note allowed), and you get little to no extra credit. Honestly, don't take her class if you struggle with writing.

Very funny and caring. The TA is her dog. She doesn't take herself too, seriously, so the environment in the classroom is a good vibe. Exams can be hard, but overall the class is extremely easy to pass. She also knows names pretty well by the first week.

acts like the nice nice teacher, seems supportive at first but if something happens, you r excuse is not good enough for her and your grade will suffer along side you. I had some serious personal issues over the semester, and when vocalizing this Stacey did not seem concerned and did not find that as a viable reason for missing an assignment.
Loved her class!
Great prof.
Loved her class! Dr. Overholt is smart, interesting, and has a perfect dog.
Fantastic professor!
She cares a ton about you and her job (probably too much)
Dr. Overholt is the best professor I've ever had! If you want a good time, ask her about her dog or her least favorite billionaires.
She cares a lot about her students and is super nice. The course itself was pretty easy and not a lot of heavy business material but I would say it's still helpful for public speaking.
Liked how this class was done, and loved that Stacey helped in every way she could. Makes herself available outside of class, and is always willing to help in any way she possibly can.

reviews.comment: Stacey's class was very useful to take during the last semester of my undergrad. I'm not a business major but the things we worked on: resumes, interviews, cover letters, etc, apply to any field. Loved her energy to make boring topics fun. As long as you show up to class it's a pretty easy and useful course.

I don't know how she has bad reviews. Stacey is the most welcoming professor I have ever had. I never felt like a COMM class was important, but I was wrong. She prepared us for interviews, resumes, and so much more that we would use in the real world. The bad reviews are from those who missed class or didn't apply themselves. There are NO EXAMS!

Professor Overholt is a great person and does her best for her students. That said, I wouldn't recommend this class for most people. There are multiple final projects and none of the work is really hard, but there is so much of it that I really struggled. The lessons are really good but it's really for MGT or BUIS students only.

This class was super helpful in preparing me for graduating and helping me prepare for the real world. Stacey offered great feedback and helped in any way possible. She was engaging, funny, and charismatic. I enjoyed this class.
One of the coolest teachers I've had so far in college. Her classwork is simple and her grading scale is clear. she is a swiftie and we love her for that

Stacey is an amazing professor. She knows her material and she teaches it well. The topics she covers arent exciting but hey someone has to do it, right? This class is the first of its kind at the U and I really enjoyed it 4 my last semester. There is an assignment due each week but it's worth it if you want laid-back assignments and an easy grade.

reviews.comment: MGT3810 was a pretty dull class but Stacey always had lots of energy and enthusiasm which made things better. She's willing to work with students and help you succeed. She grades very tough on grammar so triple check your writing assignments.

I dont know why Staceys rating is so low. She is so willing to work with students and genuinely wants to see her students do well. Her assignments have very detailed rubrics attached and the concepts are applicable to real life.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was a waste of 3 credits. If you don't care and you're here to pass and get through school, this class is for you. If you care about your education and have a desire to learn new skills that will benefit you in your career - do not register for this course.

Im sick of communications teachers thinking they are important. Nothing you have ever done is important, you are a communications teacher. Realize everyone in your class just wants an easy A. Period, nothing else. No one has any "goals for class", who actually does that. "I want to be a great communicator, let's do communications" said no one ever

All I can say is boo. All that is assigned in this class makes me feel like I'm in 10th grade, not a 6000 level masters course. I was so disappointed with this course. No interesting assignments. Get ready to record an introduction video of yourself then comment on 4 other people's videos. Seriously? Im not 10, and don't care about my classmates

reviews.comment: Stacey is a great professor. The class itself isn't the best but she makes up for the day material through her fun personality and great lectures.

reviews.comment: Not the most exciting class but stacey made it fun. She is very into pop culture and makes her lectures interesting. Super easy to get ahold of via email. Gives extra credit if you go to the writing center (DO IT). Gives extremely detailed outlines for papers and makes it very easy to do well. Do what is expected and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Stacey is a good professor. She gives really good feedback and is really funny. She co taught with 2 other teachers for media and pop culture, and they were all best friends.
Stacey is very funny and keeps class interesting and entertaining.
Amazing class

Lovely person and a great teacher! Not a hard class at all. Just show up, put yourself out there and she will guide you to your best. She really cares for her students and know how to make everyday activities fun, engaging, and educational.

Professor Webster is an amazing teacher, and she uses a lot of examples and activities that aid learning. Her class is never boring! She expects you to do well, but is also willing to do things to help you succeed.

Olivia is the best! She made the course material fun and interesting to learn. Her expectations were very clear, and she gave really helpful feedback. She really wanted everyone to succeed! She's very kind, caring, and easy to talk to. I would hands down take another class from her or recommend this class to anyone thinking about taking it!
Olivia is amazing. She is super fun and extremely caring. She has clear grading criteria, gives phenomenal feedback, and makes every class a joy to attend. Can not recommend enough!!

reviews.comment: Amazing professor but grades tough. Very knowledgeable about topics discussed in class and brought in guest speakers.

reviews.comment: Rebecca is so fab. I've taken a few of her classes and I just love her. She is very clear about her expectations and as long as you pay attention to that and follow her guidelines, it is not hard to get a good grade in her classes. Her content is engaging and interesting.

I LOVE this professor! She gives a lot of reading/writing assignments, but they really help you understand the lectures. Lectures are easy to follow and have all the material that will be on exams. It shows how much she wants students to succeed. Take her classes!!

This class overwhelmed me, I was hearing from other students how specific she is about grading and papers. Tbh having to read so many books, articles etc was very overwhelming. For those who have to work full time and are doing  4-5 classes this will be rough. I wanted to sleep forever and never wake up bc of this class

For an online class, Dr. Owen was amazing. She's super passionate about what she teaches and goes above and beyond to make sure she's getting the most important points across. She gives great feedback and has very clear expectations. Easy homework and great lectures, tests are easy. Definitely recommend her!

OMG! I got SO overwhelmed with the amount of videos and reading, especially in the second half of the semester! While Prof. Owens does a good job with the videos and making the information interesting, there is just SO MUCH. There is usually an assignment and a quiz every week, sometimes more. This class wasn't awful, just a lot to do each week.

Save your time and don't take this class. She is a really hard grader, and if you follow the rubric, she'll find a way to go around the rubric and still grade you poorly. Attendance is HEAVILY weighted, and she does is not understanding about missing. She has unreal expectations of what students can balance along with other classes.

Prof. Owen is kind and cares about her students' success. She does give a lot of feedback on assignments, but that is because she genuinely wants us to do better. She genuinely made my project and my group better with the feedback and assistance she gave. Highly recommend.

I took Dr. Owen's police and society class and enjoyed it a lot. The material was very interesting and we always had in class activities that were equally as interesting and very engaging. It was always very clear what was expected of us, and what was due in the class. Attendance is mandatory though, in-class assignments are graded and on paper.

Review is for Capstone 5000 
Professor Owen is a very sweet and caring professor. She is approachable and easy to talk to. She's a bit of a tough grader but if you do all your assignments and try your best you'll do a good job in the class.

I took this class online, it was amazing and I learned a lot. We had to read 2 books, and they were very intense but interesting. The exams were hard if you don't pay good attention to the online lectures. I highly recommend this class, it can just be heavy since it's about children.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Owen's lectures were engaging and informative. If you take notes on the lectures she allows you to use them on the quizzes and it makes them super easy. The material was super interesting and when readings were assigned they were relevant to the class and engaging. The weekly assignments never took me too long and were interesting too.

Sociology of Law: This class and professor was an amazing experience! I love how Professor Owen structure's her online courses. She responds pretty quickly to any emails and makes sure no one falls behind. She splits her lecture videos so it's easier to follow along. I strongly recommend this professor for any of her classes! I've taken a few

Online HSP5000: This class was a frustrating experience. Constant deductions for minor issues made it challenging to do well. Some delayed grading and excessive busywork overshadowed any potential benefits. Disappointingly, the course lacked substance, filled with tedious discussion replies & excessive reading, not the ideal capstone experience.

Pros: Taking notes is a must. Tests are not surprising or unclear. Good explanations of material, and gives good analysis of material and homework.

Cons: Weekly papers where you mostly regurgitate readings.

reviews.comment: *3563 Dr. Owen is incredible. She really knows what she is talking about and the classes never feel long or boring, she has so much interesting and engaging info. Two tests but they are based on the lectures, no textbook. There is a group project, but there is plenty of time to work on it and it wasn't bad at all. I highly recommend this class.

Rebecca is a great professor that is passionate about what she teaches. Her attendance is mandatory but most classes are just taking notes that are used for tests (2 tests per semester). There are 2 page writing assignments each week but she makes them engaging and easy to do. There is not textbook which is nice. I definitely recommend this class!

She is a nice human, however she should not be teaching this class. It is a class about gangs and it is obvious that she knows nothing. If you like articles then maybe take this class but I would not recommend

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Professor Owen as my teacher this semester. I have never learned so well from lectures before, but she is an incredible teacher and makes things really stick. reviews.comment: Shes a great professor! Although be ready for a lot of discussion posts and papers. If you read the articles you will do fine on the papers. Shes a fair grader and lets you make up if you dont do too good on a paper.

reviews.comment: His accent was incredibly hard to understand. I had to reteach myself everything from this class because I simply couldn't follow along with what he was teaching. He told us the first day of class that he wasn't even a chemistry teacher so we were going to learn together.
His teaching is just ok, reads off slides you can just get outside of class. accent isnt terribly hard to understand, but if you're higher up, it might be bad.
Me and my friend took his class. God he is very intelligent. If you don't understand him it's because this guy is at a different level of thinking. Very smart guy and 100% worth taking his class.

If your goal is to pay your tuition, easily pass the course, and get your diploma, then don't take Ozkanlar's class. Ozkanlar is a very intelligent person! If your goal is to understand chemistry rather than just knowing it, then he is the best professor.

Ozkanlar is not a good professor . He does not care for students and makes that very obvious. I once tried asking him a question over email and he told me to just “look it up”. The only reason I got the grade I did was due to switching to Statler's lectures.

His lectures are so diabolically bad that I had to start attending Professor Statler's lectures in order to actually understand anything while also attending his for mandatory attendance. The content of the lectures is different than the exams and quizzes, so you have to just hope you studied the right thing. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In all my years of being a student I have never had a teacher or professor this profoundly awful. I went into this class with a decent understanding of the topics already, but as soon as he started explaining those same topics, I felt my understanding decrease. I ended this class knowing less about chemistry than when I first enrolled.

At the beginning of the semester he was very hard to understand, but it got better over time.
To be honest, you should be fine with him, just read the textbook and rely on the material from other professors. Lectures have mandatory attendance, so tbh just do homework from other classes or talk to the other professors about sitting in theres.

He is THE BEST. His classes are very entertaining. Our professor is very intelligent, which can make it a little difficult for me to understand, but that's my problem, not his. His classes are quite enjoyable because he engages me in his lectures with an impressive showman-like demeanor. Trust me and take his class. You won't regret it;)

This guy genuinely cannot teach. He could not explain any of the material in a sensible manner. I was extremely confused on many topics till I realized that he was explaining them poorly or in a incomprehensible way. You will have to rely on the textbook heavily. I don't think he knows what he's even teaching half the time!

good man, bad teacher, only read off the ebook never actually explained the process behind stuff, his materials were insupplemental, go to prof statler if you want exam review sutff, exams are nothing like the homeworks, try to learn both math and concepts for the exams both show up in weird ways, AVOID AT ALL COSTS, hides grades aswell

reviews.comment: He has a very strong accent and is extremely difficult to understand. On top of this he does not walk through any of the content with you and just reads off the slides. Makes it so hard to understand what he is talking about and teaching, so you basically have to teach yourself everything.
He is an awful professor he doesn't know how to explain the subject. It doesn't make sense at all. I would never take his class again.

Not a good professor, made all the concepts as confusing as possible. He was 1 of 3 chem professors for 1210 and anyone I talked to in his class was struggling. Thick accent which is normally okay but he mumbles which makes it even harder. Reads off a slideshow and did barely any practice problems to help us.

He is an amazing guy outside of the classroom but I thought I was learning Physics instead of Chemistry during the semester. Yes, he was a Physics teacher before but that is not the subject I'm taking the class of. Exam and HWs are also pretty irrelevant to the lecture and I learn stuff only on the discussions and HWs.

It was very hard to understand what he was teaching; his English had a very thick accent. The quizzes, exams, and homework were not correlated with what Ozkanlar was teaching in class. I ended up having to learn all the content on my own. He did not answer questions asked in class, and he went over almost every lecture by several minutes.

Do not take Prof. Ozkanlar. The University needs to fire him. Impossible to understand accent, disorganized class, and worst of all does not care about his students whatsoever. He is only here to do research at the University. He is unhelpful and unresponsive. Homework is due 8pm every Saturday, no exceptions, No late submissions. 0/10 DO NOT TAKE

Ozkanlar is a knowledgeable professor and cares about his students. The accent/language barrier is there, but if you pay attention it's not that bad. Ask for his help, or help from the TAs and you'll get it. Review lecture slides for exams, do the homework, go to discussion to prep for quizzes, and you'll be fine. Office hours are your best friend.

Not a bad person but the lectures, homework, quizzes and exams all cover completely different content. Attendance is mandatory but he doesn't show the qr code till the end and will often go several minutes past the end of class. The only time I learned anything was from the TAs and LAs in the discussion.

He reads off of his slides and has a very tough accent. Sometimes misses a lot of information that needs to be cleared by the LA/TA. Wouldn't recommend if you are not ready to rot learn chemistry rather than understanding it well enough.

He used to be a physics professor, so he teaches the physics behind chemistry, not the actual chemistry. He also doesn't teach the same thing as the other professor (who writes the exams) so often times you're learning the wrong things. He's also incredibly hard to understand.
He's honestly not that bad. Just pay attention and remember that there is no such thing as a good chemistry class/ teacher.

Worst professor and reads the slides like he is seeing them for the first time. I also cannot understand what he is saying as his English is very poor. I teach myself everything. TA's are very helpful as I learn my stuff from the one discussion a week.

I've never had a professor who avoids eye contact with the class until this one. He reads straight from his slides the entire time, never noticing raised hands. On top of that, he's incredibly hard to understand, he simply doesn't know how to teach. His lectures sound robotic, and the information is confusing. Don't recommended at all.

He is impossible to understand. He doesn't even write his exams so he has no clue what was on them. Clark runs the whole class and he is just there to lecture/geek out about material that is far beyond the scope of this class. All his lectures are concept-based and show no examples of how to do calculations (which quizzes are only calculations)

Very difficult to understand with accent. I don't doubt he's a smart guy but he reads off his slides. My chem notes are just topics he goes over so I can go back home and research on my own. LA/TA are very helpful clearing up missing information (Which there is a lot of). Likely won't take him again. Lecture always goes past class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand, lectures from start to after class is over and keeps students late every day in order to get attendance points. Attendance is graded 5 days a week. Lectures do not translate to homework or quizzes and are hard to follow. Get ready to teach yourself the entire material while still going to mandatory lectures.

Good professor, the lectures get a bit confusing, and it's easy to get lost, but admittedly, I should have been a little more focused. I think the exams were very clear and matched the material he would practice with in class. Has this Google form thing for you to ask questions instead of raising your hand, and that's honestly really nice.

I took Pecsok for both OSC 2030 and 3440. His 2030 class was very boring and hard to follow, but he greatly improved for 3440. He made sure to go over plenty of examples in class and ensured we understood. I would recommend taking him for 3440, not 2030. The class was easier than 2030 because we could use Excel, and it was open-book.

Had him for OSC 2030. The majority of the grade is made up of 2 tests that are worth 34% of the grade each. He does curve strongly, but if you don't do well after the curve, it is very hard to do well in the class. Attendance is mandatory although he does allow you to get credit if you are sick. Main issue was he was really boring in class.
Super monotone

Does NOT teach well. His lectures are so hard to follow - I reteach myself most of the class for homework. The work outside of class is strenuious, there are no study guides, and again, the class is very boring. He has a question form but doesn't end up answering questions, but leaves us so confused that it's hard to answer questions.

Professor Pecsok's class was rewarding, but hard to follow at times. His lectures were direct, and I didn't pay attention it would be easy to fall behind. There were weekly homework assignment and just 2 test that were 70% of the grade. Overall, I'd say that this was a challenging but doable if you can put in the work.

i understand the more negative things people have said about this class but matt is actually very kind and helpful if you reach out to him for help. i think this was the first time he had taught this material and when he received feedback that it was wayy too lecture heavy, he immediately implemented changes to help us. i would take him again!  :)

I truly believe professor Pecsok is one of the best professors I had at the University of Utah. He is incredibly smart, willing to go over material until you no longer have questions and provide you with any help you need whether its coding help or material help. His class can be tough but he truly cares about his students and what he teaches.

Professor Pecsok is a wonderful professor who wants his students to succeed. The class is tough but he is willing to help on whatever you need help with and will help as long as necessary. He is able to take very complex topics and make them easy to understand. I feel like I could take what I have learned and apply it to a job on day one!

He cares but doesn't teach well. We use Excel in class, but not on exams, he also refuses to teach us manually. He says all sections do this...not true! Very monotone and teaches fast. You're required to attend, but end up teaching yourself. Don't do this to yourself.

Matt is super nice. He is definitely knowledgeable in his field cuz he never reads slides. Make sure you know the materials inside and out, cuz midterm's difficulty is ten levels above quiz. I recommend finish IS4420,4440,4485 before taking this class.The gourp project is hard.Start on that before midterm. Slides are organized and clear to read.

He is a nice guy, but he does not account for the fact that we have other classes. He tells you to review for the exams by studying every single slide and homework from the past, and refuses to give a study guide.

I enjoyed this class. Professor Pecsok does a good job at explaining difficult topics. Like the other reviews said, he does teach a lot through excel, and then does not allow excel on exams. Otherwise, he is a great teacher. Showing up to every class (attendance is mandatory) will give you the knowledge you need to pass the exams with ease.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's good at teaching the material, but I don't understand why you would teach a students to use certain tools and then not allow them to use it on the actual exam...at that point, he should have just taught us how do everything manually!

Attendance is mandatory and recommended. He teaches us how to do the material in Excel, has the HW based partly on Excel, and then doesn't allow Excel at all on tests. Lectures are very heavy and do not fully explain topics well enough to even be able to ask questions. However, he is a nice professor and responds to emails. The class isn't curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very boring class. Professor is mundane and makes this class way more difficult than it should be. Pace of teaching was TOO slow that it was hard to follow. No study guides & says "redo all the homework and problems on the slides". Mind you I got an A in bus calc w/ a professor with a horrible rating, and I am finding this class more difficult.
He doesn't actually teach the information which is really frustrating .

Matthew Pecsok really cares about his students and will be willing to help you with almost anything. He even gives you extra credit for just meeting with him so he can get to know you better. He does labs with you in class, and I have no doubt that he would be willing to sit with you for all his office hours to help you if you are struggling.
enthusiastic professor

While this class can be dry and be filled with a lot of busy work it does not draw an accurate picture of Prof. Pecsok. He cares so much and does his absolute best in making sure that his students understand the material. While this year's curriculum had its flaws, he took notes and is working on improving the curriculum. Highly recommended!

My brain turns to mush in this class. So insanely boring and dry. He doesn't even know his own course that well and outsources the lecture material and lab videos to our lord and savior CHONG OH who I hate even more. It's a dictionary filler class that you'll learn absolutely nothing in, which is a shame because it really seems legit but it's not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's not good at lecturing and would often just throw up the textbook (which had many mistakes btw) and scribble equations from it for the entirety of the lecture, yet attendance was required? On the other hand, the exams were easy as long as you study the homework and practice exams.
Hired for research not to be a good professor.
Very unhelpful and a tough grader. I won't take any course with him ever.

He is incredibly engaging and funny during his lectures, and the class itself is fairly easy. Just be prepared for some time consuming busy work at home. Otherwise, I would highly recommend this course.

his lectures are not helpful, half the time he doesn't know what is going on. he does not answer, i just started talking to his TA if i needed something. kind've an annoying amount of work outside of class considering its a required business class and not a major specific class.

Professor Oh is caring, but wasn't really efficient at lecturing for my class. I was pretty much using AI / Gemini the entire semester to just complete the 2 Python HW assignments every week. He's super accessible outside of class and offers extra credit. But overall, I didn't really learn that much from his class, but he's a great person.

I took IS4487, which was not on the list. There was a LOT of reading and an intensive group project at the end. I agree with the review about AI. The majority of the labs you would complete with AI, which seemed to defeat the purpose of learning the material. Professor Oh has an accent that was hard to understand at times during his lectures.

reviews.comment: Prof Oh is so sweet. He gives extensions on anything you ask for & extra credit. His assignments are busy work, but honestly not too bad. He is super passionate about IS and emails back fast, but he uses AI too much. He literally sent us an AI podcast explaining the concepts as study material for our exam. I love him but this AI slop needs to stop

One of the better professors I've had. Accessible outside of class during non-designated office hours. Seemed happy to help whenever I had questions. Extremely nice and helpful. Very passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Chong is very caring and really cares about what he teaches. The class is very content and homework heavy. There are is a quiz, lab and roleplay every week so you have to put a lot of time towards this class. The exams can be pretty difficult.

I have no idea why Prof Oh has 1 stars from students. He is so awesome and sweet. He replies to emails fast, gives extensions on anything you ask for, and extra credit. Yes, his course has a bunch of busy work, but it's honestly not even that much. He's so funny and happy to teach. He's one of the best teachers. Y'all kinda trippin if you hate him.

Ridiculous workload. Insanely long labs and homework. This is an introduction to IS class and a BRIDGE course for me, it's insane how much information is expected to be retained. This isn't my career, this won't come up in 99% of business classes.

The Professor is using AI and all of his labs are built on outdated systems. Everything that's layed out in the course is hard for the wrong reasons. It's confusing and lazy, and feels unacceptable with how expensive the business school is.
Waste of time. You learn nothing from his class, you have to learn by teaching yourself. And he's always using outdated material and AI. Probably too lazy to work on his own notes and lectures.

Professor Oh is an amazing teacher and you should take him if you can. He teaches the content well and prepares you for your exams and group projects well. He is funny and keeps the classes entertaining.
very nice and funny. very good at explaining the material.

usually a quiz and a lab a week, both fairly easy and can do from home (with the codes for the quizzes). he does not teach very well though and half the time the TA has to teach him how to do something. also takes forever to grade and reply to students.. I just started going to the TA instead and he was great!
This class was interesting because it was very code-heavy, however you just learn via copying what the professor does. I think this class lacks any real learning and rather teaches replication.

You will have a couple assignments per week that can add up but they're typically easy to complete if you pay attention in class. He is super forgiving on grades/ late work if you talk to him face to face.

Professor Chong is not good at teacher IS. He has no idea what he is doing a lot of the time and when we walk through the guided projects in class, students frequently correct him on his mistakes and the TA often has to show him how to do stuff. He is terrible at responding to emails and comes off rude in them when you just need help.

Chong's class was decently difficult. He is a very kind and funny professor, but in a short time period, he does not teach coding very well. You have a big group project to make a website and your homework builds up to it. However, he doesn't directly teach you in class how to do the things he asks for in assignments

I expected more from his class, but it wasn't bad. Long lectures and assignments are required that have no relation to web apps. TA grades pretty easy which is nice. There is a big group project due at the end but as long as you have a good group it's not bad. Keep the project simple and as long as you fulfill all the requirements you'll do well.
Professor Oh is funny, very intelligent, and a great professor. This class is challenging and the group project is a LOT of work, but you will learn so much from this class it's worth it.

Professor Oh is a very entertaining professor. His lectures can sometimes get a little repetitive with the videos he posts ahead of time, but other than that, the material was really straightforward and he keeps his class lighthearted. There are group projects, but halfway through the semester he made them individual projects instead.

Took his IS 4460 course as part of the IS Minor Summer Program abroad. The class was heavily focused on a difficult Group Project that focused on the functions of PHP and HTML primarily. He was readily available for help, but it was a lot of work for a 10 day timespan. However, I learned a lot and although his lectures can be rough, he teaches alot
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: A great credible professor, he knows what he's doing and talking about. Just do the assignments and you'll get an easy A. He is super nice and friendly, he fills his lectures with humor. If you take the class, especially take it with him. Just beware, there are some group projects and they may suck cuz of sucky team members, but still a good class.
Chong was a great professor. Keept me intrested and is a fast responder to emails. Take this class with him!

One of the nicest professors you will ever encounter. Really enjoys teaching and tries his best to make things fun. Most of the people in class enjoy his enthusiasm and his comedy throughout lectures.

This was an alright class, there are a lot of lectures and labs but they are pretty straightforward. It wasn't my favorite and was difficult at times but you learn a lot. Make sure you and your group are on the same page with everything and KEEP it simple. Web page design is a slippery slope and you could be making more work.

Amazing professor! Weekly assignments due every Sunday with labs and case studies to accompany lectures. Chapter quizzes and 2 Exams. Large group research paper at the end of the class and a presentation.

Such a caring guy! Really great professor and he really wants to see you succeed. There is a final group project that's a little tricky but other than that, if you do the homework and pay attention in lectures, it's a pretty easy A.

Ching is an awesome professor that is super passionate about what he teaches and really cares about his students success! Always positive and tries to have fun. His assignments are things that relate to real world problems that help better understand what you are willing. Also learn good basic excel functions.

I really loved BCOR2020. Ching is such an amazing professor, he is so funny and all of his lectures are straight to the point, easy to understand and informative. He is also amazing at responding, I get many responses back on canvas within 30min to 1 hour. Highly recommend.

Chong Oh is so awesome. Absolutely hilarious and enjoyable professor. His lectures were great and even though I couldn't go to a lot of them, they were always a treat. The class does get to be a lot of work but it is so worth it in the end because of how great of a professor he is and the genuine appreciation he has for his students.

This class hits on so many different aspects of web page design. So if you aren't paying attention to the labs or have a bad team, you'll be lost. Chong goes way to fast for you to learn anything and there are so many errors that one could experience.

Professor Oh is a nice guy, but don't take any classes from him if you can. He doesn't prepare you for industry at all. He loves to have your write papers, even though the class is a coding class. Very vague instructions on projects and will grade ruthlessly.

Prof. Oh tried but it just isnt his scene. If you choose to take his class, be ready to be bombarded with labs, quizzes and homework almost every week, on top of a not well-explained group project. Be ready to have your grades oddly regraded at any point. Youll have to learn 80% by yourself if you need a good grade.

This professor genuinely cares about his student's success. Obviously knew what he was talking about and was solid in preparing his students for business and especially good for those who want computer oriented degrees.

He is teaching outdated language and saying that it is widely used. He himself does not know what is widely being used. Also, he is using the same old materials from the past six years. He will give you 3 tasks to complete each week: project, homework, and lab. Almost 90% of the class, you need to teach yourself.

Chong is a great outside class but as a prof I was disappointed in him. His lectures do not teach but show. He doesnt explain the concept hes using to code he assumes you know what hes talking about . The group project is a mess because its an online class. Files are not organized. The group project description was a maze of links. Tests were hard.

reviews.comment: Professor Oh is a great online professor. There is busy work every week, but it isn't too bad. Weekly assignments and quizzes, two exams and a group project. He is a very nice guy and spends a lot of time getting to know his students.

Chong is not a good teacher. He does not care for his students, you sit there and watch him code for 3 straight hours and then he expects you to go home and do hours worth of homework that is 10x more complex and difficult .

It's classes like this that make me want to protest America's current educational system. This class was nothing but worthless busy work, didn't learn a thing. To give you an idea of the type of assignments he gives, remember "current events" in elementary school? Where you summarized a news article? Yeah, we did that weekly in this COLLEGE class.

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and the tests were very ambiguous. I would not take this class again. But I think maybe that is just the subject. Walked away feeling like I learned nothing and wasted money on tuition but the class is required for my major.

Professor Oh was a perfect online professor. Frequent feedback with tangible lectures and consistent opportunity to learn. There was A LOT of busy work... but it was all easy and fairly applicable to course topics. For a required class, he made it worth wile. Lab/Current-Events/Easy Assignment/Quiz due every Sunday.

reviews.comment: This class has been nice because it has been online! Chong Oh is super nice and willing to help you succeed. Sometimes his online homework directions were confusing and hard to follow but in the end it was an easy A.

This has just been one glorified high school class, which is extremely frustrating since it's supposed to be a 4000 level class. The lectures are straight from the book and offer little if any additional information on the chapters. He then decides to give absurd assignments, forcing you to comment on two other people's assignments. worthless class.
This class has been nonstop busy work. Weekly assignments include current events, quizzes, and meaningless "in-class exercises". This has been the most frustrating class I have ever taken.

Just a really cool person. I ended up with a B in his class, but I could've easily gotten an A if it weren't for my negligence. Oh, is willing to work with you to help you succeed. I had a business trip the week of finals and we organized an assignment to make up for my presentation. I would recommend him to anyone. AWESOME PERSON.

Professor Chong Oh is very good. Every homework assignment is hands on and he is always willing to make sure you understand. reviews.comment: If you show up and do your homework you should pass.  Don't waste money on a book because you go over the chapter for an hour before every quiz (more than enough time to absorb all the material).

The group project for this class was a great experience and incorporated many of the things we learned in class. Heavy textbook use, but it's really useful as many of the HW projects can be completed if you read the text.  Quiz at the beginning of each class.
I took his Web-Application masters class. It was hard subject. I wish he taught us more with real world example than just follow the examples in the text book.

reviews.comment: He really structures the class well. There are no surprises, which is nice. We covered a lot of interesting material, though it was hard to relate with a lot of it because I'm not an IS major. Still liked the class. Good professor.
This course had many languages to be taught in 10 classes. The professor did a very good job in balancing out and focusing on what was important and what could be self-taught.
Smart, nice, approachable, fair grader.
