He also never answers questions in a way that makes sense, and is kind of condescending to students who are asking questions. His canvas is very disorganized which caused a lot of confusion for students.

I took this class in Fall of 2021. It was a mix of both in-person and online. Prof Vikram is awesome. He really makes you fall in love with thermo and stat mech. He cares about the students and is happy to work with them. His hw and test are just at the right level to help the students learn. I am sure you will enjoy his class.

He is too concerned with having a perfect bell curve with grades. He doesnt care about the students doing well or not, all he wants is the average to be a C. He was upset when a lot of students got As on a test. He also is very heavy on readings. Make sure you have plenty of time to read the textbook (which is pretty good actually).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I just transferred, and Dr. Desphande is one of my favorite professors at the U so far. He keeps himself busy with his research and dedicating time to the department, but also makes you feel important and capable as a student. Tests and grading are as expected for an upper div. PHYS class. Can't wait to take 5510 from him this fall!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Victoria made this math class super manageable. Her lectures were easy to follow, homework was similar to lecture examples,  exams were VERY similar to practice exam/review, and she provides a ton of extra credit opportunities!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her class notes are based off of the textbook, but she teaches it nicely enough that I did not personally had to access the textbook myself. She posts everything online and it's very easy to access almost everything on canvas. She provides many extra credits, even on tests. As long as you do the material she provides, its pretty easy to pass!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lovely lovely professor, highly recommend.

Maybe the best professor I've had the opportunity to learn from at the University of Utah. It is clear that Professor Kala is very knowledgeable on the subject matter and enjoys teaching. Lectures are direct to the point and incredibly informative. Very caring and accessible outside of class, and understanding when I missed the final (my fault).

Can't recommend her enough! She does such a great job breaking down potentially confusing problems and providing step by step guidance for solving equations. Her exams are incredibly straightforward and fair, and she provides tons of practice material to prepare. She even offers extra credit! She makes 2280 a breeze, but you still learn a ton!

Professor Kala is amazing! She explains clearly, does lots of examples, and her homework and tests match perfectly—no surprises. And the hw isn't too heavy either. She offers extra credit, drops low scores, and is super helpful in office hours. Gives great calc refreshers too. Don't take 2280 from anyone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are well structured and very easy to follow. Her notes are clear, and I never have to read the textbook to do well in the class. Her grading rubric is clear, and there are many opportunities for extra credit. She's tied with Sean Groathouse for the best math professor I've had at the University of Utah. This has been my favorite class.

I took his Theories of Culture class last fall, and absolutely loved it. Pecora is an outstanding lecturer; he moves at a pretty quick pace through difficult material, so I would recommend taking good notes for the exams. Super funny, nice, and intelligent. Definitely would recommend -- just be sure to sink in the very comprehensive lectures.

Grade based on 3 exams alone, but Pecora is a kind, intelligent guy. No hand outs, but if you go to office hours you can "debate" for a few extra missed points. Sometimes studying is difficult. so much reading, but I found lectures intresting. Overall, I learned a ton, and though it was hard I have no regrets.

I like Pecora, but he grades rather subjectively on grammar. I asked for help from the writing center on it and he'd still mark a lot as grammatically incorrect. Pick up on what style of writing he wants and that will help you more. He is engaging and knowledgeable, but sometimes his lectures can border on meandering. Engage and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SO SMART?? The other reviews are right; Pecora has such an incredible grasp on the philosophers you study and moves fairly fast, so be ready to pay attention. As long as you take notes (I basically wrote down every sentence he said), he'll really be able to pull you into a fantastic essay-writing mode. Really a thoughtful, insightful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pecora navigates deftly through the minefields of Hegel, Marx, and Nietzsche as if it were nothing. Pay close attention to EVERYTHING he says because it's all critical to understand what is going on. He was very open about office hours and very responsive with questions via email, etc. I wish he taught more classes so I could take them.

Professor Pecora is a nice guy but he can tend to talk a lot and when he asks questions he seems to only be looking for very specific answers. The same is true for his grading, there usually wasn't any rubric for papers and he was a tough grader but he usually gives enough feedback to revise for a better grade. Lots of reading, but good discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pecora's lectures are interesting & insightful.  He is a strict grader when it comes to essays. Study the prompts, give yourself 2 days to write a draft, visit the writing center, & pay attention to grammar. If you complete the assigned readings, attend class, & listen & take notes, you'll do fine on the tests. He's a wonderful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting to listen to and clearly has passion for the subject, though lectures don't necessarily prepare you for tests.  Has a thing against e-books and online versions to the point where he requires you bring the textbook to class, despite the fact that much of the material covered is public domain.  Nice guy, though an exacting grader.

He is too condescending and arrogant to be a good professor. He created a hostile environment in the classroom, and his jokes about women were very unappreciated. Comments on papers showed he didn't actually read them. Very confusing. Only accepted his own opinion. I seriously recommend that you not take a course from him.
Taken for Theories of Culture. Knows his stuff, though sometimes it was difficult to pin down what we were supposed to be taking from it. Essay prompts were somewhat open-ended. Grammar matters.

Pecora seems to have a deep knowledge of the subject matter, but isn't very gifted at making his classes engaging. Show up if you want, but he doesn't take roll and staying awake is a challenge. He seems to be accommodating and helpful, but you've got to ask for it. Not a bad professor overall.

I was not able to get ahold of this professor throughout the entirety of the course. I felt that she graded me harsher because I was at times not able to come to class due to health reasons. When I asked her about it, I was brushed off. I do not recommend her as as in person class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Wei with all my heart. She was AMAZING. She was so caring and understanding. She took the time to get to know her students. I had technical difficulties during a participation discussion and she reached out to me directly before I could, and let me make it up. Her lectures are easy to follow, not much work other than quizzes and the exams

She's great! Was really understanding and lenient with everything. I didn't read the textbook and did fine. Attendance isn't mandatory, but would recommend going because she gives all of the answers to the quizzes and exams in the powerpoints and while lecturing.

While lectures were disorganized and difficult to follow (kind of scribbles on a chalk board), Professor He allowed students to get extra credit on well-done projects & graded our very easy exams forgivingly. Great online lecture notes as a textbook alternative. Potential to be successful without even going to class? Perhaps.

Hope he improves for future students. His lectures consist of mainly derivations without many examples to see it applied. You must memorize equations exactly as he writes and no review guide. He does the minimum unfortunately. For a complex subject, look for another prof as this one doesnt understand what learning Fluids for the first time is like.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor He. I think his lectures can be pretty dense with math and formulas but I rarely left not understanding what he was teaching. His lectures also follow a textbook that he wrote so it is easy to increase understanding. His homework is great for preparing for exams as well.

Dr. He has taken measures to improve the quality of his course, and genuinely seems to want students to succeed. As others have mentioned, the lectures are primarily used for derivations, however the exams are very reflective of the homework assignments and Dr. He is very transparent in what he expects students to know for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's clear that Dr. He has improved since the last time he taught 3710. Homework was graded on completion, the 2 projects were straight-forward, and both exams were representative of the material learned in class. Lectures are derivation-heavy and he can be very monotone, but he does explain certain concepts very well. Very fair professor.

Lectures are only HW solutions or incredibly long and tedious derivations of obvious facts., not once did lectures explain how to solve problems or apply concepts from this class.He has custom notation for math that makes following anything going on the board impossible, expect to read his own textbook constantly constantly to know what's going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Xiaowei He is the worst teacher I've ever had. I did good in this class, but that's because I didn't listen to a single thing he said. I had to get help from other professors at the university. 

Note to future students: Do NOT take ANY course from Xiaowei He!

If you are already a professional fluid dynamicist, you will survive. You will never know what was incorrect on the exams, since he doesn't release the solutions. He expects that you have a PhD in the subject already and always talks about problems that are meant for PhD students passing their final exam. Save your money, time, and sanity.
this teacher is very hard to understand

Please, save yourself the headache and avoid taking fluids with this professor. Fluid Mechanics is a very difficult subject to learn and it requires a passionate professor who has a good teaching style and class structure to succeed in it. That was not the case in this class.
This teacher doesn't know know how to teach.

Lectures were very confusing, and when questions were asked, they often got ignored or not answered in any meaningful manner. Tests are essentially pass fail as there is very little to no partial credit if questions are not answered in the format expected. The course is extremely derivation-heavy, heavy essentially no help on Canvas.

Fluids is already difficult but he makes it impossible.  HW is nothing like in class examples and posted HW solutions have errors everywhere.  Barely any review material for exams, 10 min Q&A in lecture before, only HW solutions that have errors everywhere.  I would highly advise against taking class with him if you can.

You basically have to read his mind on how he wants you to answer the test/homework questions. He doesn't do anything in class besides mumble derivations for the hour we have lecture. He doesn't give any study material/lecture notes besides the homework that you're assigned. This teacher makes me regret transferring to The University of Utah.

Worst teacher I've taken a class from. In a class of 100 students, the average was a 40% and he says has no idea why. He is very hard to understand and doesn't explain anything very well. When someone asks why something is a certain way he says “I've been doing fluid mechanics for 10 years so I think I know what I'm talking about”. Bad teacher.
40% average on the midterm and then pretends that it is the classes problem for not paying attention.
Hard homework with minimum feedback and barely posts anything to the class. Your grade relies on homework and exams only. Might as well buy the textbook and skip taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rubric is 40% homework and 30% on Midterms and final. Homework is everything in this class that means it's the only material you get for the exams. No review and we had to beg him to make a equation sheet for the class. Lectures are just going through derivations with no examples of actual problems. Homework needs to be done the way he does it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Molinero is very intelligent, funny, and cares a lot about her work and her students. But she was not my favorite professor. She relied very heavily on ChatGPT for exams, course content, and even in her explanations. She was also quite disorganized. Homework was MUCH harder than exams and class content, so it was not helpful at all.

Molinero is a great person. However, she relies on Chat GPT to create her discussions, lectures, exams, and keys. The exams have tons of extra credit, and homework is graded on participation, so basically everyone passes. She's very scatterbrained. If you have to take it from her, I recommend the YouTube channel Physical Chemistry.

Prof. Molinero was very hard to understand. She's very knowledgeable, but her lectures were hard to follow. Every test taken had an average grade of 65% which really hurt a lot of students grades, plus there was no curving done whatsoever. Would not recommend.

Professor Molinero is a hard-working, very knowledgeable, and caring professor. I just simply cannot understand her. I'm typically a student that can stay focused, but she's just really hard to follow. Her teaching skills are pretty bad. I wouldn't recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Molinero is a great teacher. Yes, her speech can be difficult to understand, but in my class of 80, 60 sat in the back (often on their phone), and 3 people asked questions. She has an enormous amount of knowledge and passion. I'm so thankful I took from her, because while I used to vehemently hate every part of chemistry, I now love it.

I loved Prof. Molinero! She was so knowledgeable and her lectures were fun to attend. She is funny and gets to know the people who show up. However, she teaches 1220 in tandem with Prof. Statler, who definitely takes over the class structure. Also the lectures are more for problem solving, so stay caught up with online modules to not fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She tries for what it's worth. She is smart and treats students as such but we don't know what she knows. Her heavy accent, rather poor handwriting, and sometimes mixing words up is a rough combo as sometimes I end up second guessing what she said and wrote down so I question my notes at times. A pro would be the great random knowledge she tells.

Would rather talk than listen to students or answer questions. Assigned questions on exams that weren't taught for another week in lecture. Regularly assigns homework at 8am on a random day without warning that will be made due less than a day later.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Molinero was a terrible teacher and an even worse human being. She lacked empathy completely. In better terms, shes a Karen. She would not answer questions and didnt seem interested in actually teaching. She has a very think accent too. I honestly hope she is fired so no one else has to suffer. Thank god for the underpaid TAs who actually taught.

Using clickers which means you must go to class in order to get points.  Difficult to understand her. Go to discussions because you will learn much more from your TAs and from the lecture videos. The only reason you need to go to class is to earn your participation points. Exams are ok but you really need to study.

This is the most poorly structured class I have ever taken. Nothing is taught in either lecture or discussion. There is absolutely no reason to go to class but you are required to attend in order to answer an absurd amount of clicker questions. If you don't understand a clicker question there will be no follow up by the professor to explain it.

The format of Molinero's lecture best suits those who prefer self-studying. She's not a great lecturer, but the course (designed by a great TA, Brock) is very straightforward. If you do the homework, practice tests, and put in effort outside of class to learn the material, you will succeed.

Terrible professor with even worse english. She refuses to answer questions and just tells you to ask your peers for help. Lectures are extremely unorganized. If you look around the room, not a single person is taking notes because there is no information presented in class. Flipped lecture is the worst idea ever.

Horrible professor.  The chemistry department at the U is terrible in general. They have abandoned the tried and true method of professors actually teaching the students, and instead have created a "flipped lecture" where the students just answer dozens of clicker questions each class. The professor doesn't teach and just asks questions.

She is very excited about chemistry, but it is poorly taught. The language barrier makes it more difficult to understand her. There are clicker points every lecture and discussion and the tests are pretty difficult.

Professor Molinero is tough. You can't understand her as her English isn't so good, but even if you can get over that, the lecture is all over the place. The material doesn't match the homework, and the conceptual final is very difficult as she only teaches the math. If you're gonna learn something, you're going to learn it in discussion.

The absolute worst professor I've ever had. She didn't speak the English language well enough to teach. Lectures were extremely disorganized, confusing, and didn't match the homework. When 90 students got below a 50% on the test, she spent a whole class telling us how it our fault. Get ready to teach yourself, because she doesn't know the material.

The only reason you go to class is for clicker participation points, her lectures are unclear and unorganized. You basically have to teach yourself because the material on the homework is not covered before it is due. English is not the professors first language, its reflected by poorly written slides and questions in class.
Might as well be teaching yourself, attendance is mandatory and the lectures are awful; it is exceptionally hard to understand what she is trying to teach. As a Chem E major,  she makes me hate chem
Can't understand a word she says. Flips back and fort . Might as well teach yourself. Calls students out for no reason . Worst professor ever.

Very hard subject but they teach it well, and it is graded with the knowledge that the the subject is quite difficult.  I found them helpful at explaining a inherently tough subject.  If you put in the work then you will do well.  After all quantum chemistry is not really easy, and it is the first course I ever had in the subject.
hard to understand, homework takes a very long time to do and doesnt help with the tests. not a very good professor
She is extremely hard to understand.  Homework has nothing to do with what is done in class or the exam.  Activities are like second homework set.
Best professor I have ever had! Final is worth 40 percent, which was hard, but still a great class to take!

Professor Zhu was a great teacher who covered content at a good pace. It was easy to reach him in office hours. The tests were very similar to the content covered in class and made it feel like studying actually helped. Overall, a great professor and class.

Amazing teacher. Plenty of examples and he really cares about the class. His office hours are super accessible and really helpful. Make sure to study hard for the final. The textbook has most of the homework answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Peter has been my favorite professor by far at the U. He went through examples in class and always showed each step. Super easy to follow. The final was worth 50% of the grade, but I understand his reasoning. All he is looking for is that you understand the basic concepts of statics since it is the foundation for lots of other classes.

I loved having Peter for statics. He was always able to explain things in a way that I could understand. All of the homework was fully graded so you know what you did wrong. Super nice, and you can tell he's happy to be teaching

Great professor, cares about teaching. Statics is a filter class, so not really his fault for the new concepts being hard to understand at first. Pay attention really well in class, take the time to understand concepts intuitively and you'll do great. Final was weighted heavily but as long as you do the above, it'll be an easy test.

I really enjoyed Peter as a professor. He's pretty funny and teaches the material clearly. Nevertheless, it was a fairly difficult class with some tricky-to-understand concepts. There are plenty of quizzes and you have to really understand the material to do well on the exams. Having friends in the class to check homework with is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Legitimately phenomenal professor. Taught purely from the blackboard and really knew his stuff. Probably the best lecturer I've had in engineering so far. Really hammered in the conceptual points of the content, but also did plenty of examples. Exams were reasonable and if you prepare for them you should do just fine.

Professor Xiang is a nice guy. I wouldn't put that past him. He tries hard to teach but I felt like there was a real lack of resources given to succeed in this class. As someone who had never taken a statistics class before, I found it difficult to find motivation to learn because I couldn't fully understand why we learned the concepts we did.

Prof Xiang tries plenty hard to teach you, but I just didn't find his lectures effective at all. I've taken 8 straight semesters of college math at this point, and this was by far the hardest time I've ever had trying to learn from a professor. Be ready to seek additional help, and do the practice tests. You've been warned.

3 days to complete quizzes, and a full week and a half to complete homework. He fully understands the difficulty of the course material and give enough time to go to office hours and to work at your own pace. Exams are difficult but he gives great resources to practice for exams, id say i wouln't have passed if it weren't for the practice material.

He explains the mathematics very well and has notes from a previous class on Canvas. Intuitively he wasn't the best at explaining things. Doesn't record lectures and are very important for success in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Xiang was often difficult to understand and doesn't understand students' questions a lot of the time. His homework wasn't bad, and he provides all of the solutions before hand. His exams, however, are brutal and worth the majority of your grade.

Similar to what's been said. Actively tries to get feedback from students and many chances to succeed (Answer key is given for every assignment before due date. Only 3 exams are graded meaning if you ace all 3 you don't need to take the final). Has a bit of an accent but still was understandable. I wish he had more time to answer questions in class

He's just ok, reads off of slides, and seems like he's teaching someone else's class. It's an easy class as long as you show up to class or keep a steady studying habit. Other than that he's just alright.

Posts recorded lectures on Canvas, attendance not mandatory. Not the greatest lecturer ever but seems nice. There are 11 homeworks and he drops one. Three midterms and a final but you can also drop one of those. I didn't go to lecture except on the exam days and I did just fine.
Great tutor!

Professor Lingyao is an exceptional educator who truly stands out in the academic world. Their dedication to teaching and passion for their subject are evident in every lecture, discussion, and interaction. What makes Professor Lingyao a great professor is their ability to make complex concepts accessible and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fantastic Professor!
Fantastic instructor! I will definitely take again.

He moves somewhat quickly through lessons, so don't look away or zone out. He expects you to understand calculus 1 and when he applies it in his lessons, he hurries through the steps which could make it difficult to understand. Slow grader. Exams are fairly easy as long as you update your formula sheet, pay attention in class, and do the homework.

You're better off watching YouTube videos than this professor. He skips steps. The solutions, or parts of the problems seem to be pulled from thin air. His supplied notes, have no meaningful order and just written everywhere so good luck trying to follow. Everyone so confused, they didn't know what to ask, when asked if there were questions.

All he does in class is go over problems and it's so understand what he's doing because he just skips over steps. Its impossible to learn from him and the homework is always super long and really hard to do. Takes 15 to 20 hours a week.

His lectures are very unclear and he does not explain things fully. Some content you have to learn outside of class because he does not explain it well enough, but the tests and quizzes are easy enough. Easy A if you can teach yourself and review some stuff on your own.
Lectures are hard to follow but homework is light and attendance is not mandatory. The tests and quizzes arent too hard either.

Professor Xie is very new and his teaching style is hard to follow. While lectures are frequent, they are moved through too quickly and with little explanation, leaving students to fend for themselves and learn from outside sources. The actual course taught me very little, I was only able to do the exams and homework using other learning material.

The lectures were disorganized and hard to follow. Basically a teach yourself class. He grades nicely though, so if you attempt an exam problem and get it wrong, you could still get most of the points. If you have a strong knowledge of algebra 2 then this class won't be too bad. If not, choose another instructor.
Disorganized and hard to follow his course structure.

Xie Lingyao is a new teacher which may make him difficult to follow. However, all lectures are recorded and posted, and are taken from the Math department where you can watch the same lectures. Homeworks are open most of the semester with no set dates. Quizzes about every 2-3 weeks. 4 exams. He is merciful in grading, and drops lowest exam scores.

The material is semi-difficult, but the worst part is that Mr. Xie's lectures and notes are insanely hard to follow. I've so far taught myself all of the material using the online classes lecture videos. As of Fall 2020 Lingyao is a first-year instructor, keep in mind, so lots will improve in the future.

The content within this course is SO boring, I don't think she is the problem with this course. She was really nice and cares about how you are doing. If you do reach out, she will respond in a timely manner. The lectures do get boring so be prepared. The course is heavily graded by Exams. Learn the formulas, the formula sheet sucks.

Meh. Neither good nor bad. She's alright at explaining things, I honestly think it's just the content of the course that is super bland. And that's not her, the accounting department is crazy with their course content and exams!
She was a pretty good professor. The classes were straightfoward and she provided very helpful practice study guides for midterms and finals.

Such a genuinely sweet lady and professor. Very concerned about the well-being of her students and truly wishes success upon you. Class is not a breeze by any means; however, she makes herself available when needed and provides students with study materials, slides, and practice worksheets. I recommend.
One of the best professors ive had! if you fail this class you dumb
Doesnt give the necessary formulas in the tests. Makes us memorize tons of formulas even though she gives us a formula sheet?
This is actually the worst class I have ever taken at the university. It is hard to follow and the class makes no sense overall. I would never recommend this class to anyone at the university.

One of the least interesting professors I've ever had. Lectures in a very confusing and out of order way that helps you learn nothing. The exams are the majority of your grade and she does not help you feel prepared at all. Would not take her again
She is hard to understand and the class is hard, I went too acctg hours every week to learn it.
made the lectures really confusing, tests made no sense and did not have any formula sheet/notes and hard to understand what shes talking about.

ACCTG 3100 is a very difficult class. The accounting department is terrible, they make one exam for all sections, and sections teach different styles. Sasha's teaching ability is amazing and I would certainly take her again, but the accounting department needs some major improvements. Exams are too hard.

Not engaging, difficult to understand, overcomplicates all the steps in her problems, lowk horrible professor. Our class had the lowest test averages in the accounting department probably because of her . Other professors explained concepts completely differently than she did. Had her for ACCTG 3100

Professor Peng is a fabulous person and she really knows what she is talking about. As someone who is NOT an accounting major and has absolutely no interest in accounting, this class has been very tough for me. Your grade will be based on how you do on the exams. Memorizing 30+ formulas is not my strong suit (no formula sheets on exams).

Very effective and knowledgable teacher who can answer any question you might have. My only complaint would be that she spends too much time going step-by-step through each problem and not enough time explaining conceptual frameworks.

Great professor. Time consuming material. Midterm and final exams are each broken into 4 different parts that each take about an hour and a half to two hours. Multiple graded case studies that are exponentially harder than the lecture and self study cases. 3 Problem sets that are easy if you did the self study cases for each lecture.

Peng was alright. I wish I would've had a different professor for this challenging class, but she was sufficient. She knows what she is talking about and is very knowledgeable. She wasn't much help when it came to the daunting group project and there wasn't TA help either. Her lectures are long, but engaging and keeps you on your toes. She is kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was challenging. The group project was large and tedious but a good learning experience (ALL 3600 classes have to do this project). Her quizzes were not hard if you prepared for them, and there was no homework. The final was exhausting for me, but there was nothing surprising on it. Overall she did a great job and was willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Sasha is an amazing professor who really knows her stuff. She is organized and presents the material in a structured way which makes reviewing for the quizzes easy. The group project is a beast, but Sasha is willing to help answer questions--as long as you put in the work. If you want to do well, be prepared to study the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Accounting 3600 is rough, and the project really sucks, but every 3600 class has to do it. As for teaching, Peng does a great job at explaining things. She's organized and her slides and handouts are literally how I will hopefully pass. Tests are extremely difficult if accounting doesn't come naturally to you.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is amazing at explaining things. She explained all of 2600 in one 3 hour class when it took 3 months for me to barely understand it. Seriously, if you're taking 3600 and aren't confident about your understandings take her class. On top of that, she posts the slides to canvas, so just take notes power point and you'll pass the class easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Peng gets a bad rap. She is a little difficult to understand because of her accent. However, she was also extremely helpful when I asked her questions. When it came to the group project, I felt more than comfortable asking her questions.
She was very clear about what material you need to know for tests.  Also, make sure you get a good group or you won't get a good grade.

She is not very engaged in the class; granted, being a professor is not her primary job (she is a researcher, and teacher on the side). Her tests are tough: no formulas provided and no multiple choice questions. Professor Peng's lectures are straight from slides, with some practice problems that can be helpful. I would recommend another professor.
STEER CLEAR AT ALL COSTS! Beginning Fall 2015, she only gives out SHORT-ANSWER quizzes and exams. You read that right - no multiple choice. Reads power point slides, not engaging at all.

I thought she was an amazing teacher! She was very clear and what she taught in class was consistent with what was expected on the exams. Overall structure was nice. I liked taking quizzes after each chapter because it kept me engaged. She was clear and gave great examples!

She just reads the slides off the screen. Attendance isn't mandatory. Group project is somewhat descent representation of real world life, but a GROUP project in accounting is ridiculous (I work at an accounting firm and even the CPA's thought it was ridiculous). Homework is average. Overall, Xiaoxia puts little effort into the class.

She is a really nice teacher, willing to meet with you and answer any questions. The worst thing is that she basically reads the power point slides, and the examples she hands out is straight from the book.
Not a good teacher at all.  Reads all slides. very soft spoken and makes no practical application of material. Might as well teach yourself. That said she is very responsive and available to help.

Xi might be my favorite prof I've had; he is so caring about every student no matter their skill level and always gives feedback. He frequently purchased materials for students to use, and he is the reason why I have pursued painting. The only negative thing I can think of is that he can get carried away with his lectures at times, but no biggie

Xi is not only one of the kindest teachers but kindest people ever. I have never heard anyone say anything negative about him. He gives you great feedback and resources through helpful lectures. Xi gives you a lot of time to work & checks on you individually. He is so encouraging!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xi is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is so considerate of his students' time, money, opinions, etc. He gives helpful feedback and suggestions and he works with students to help them get the most out of an assignment. I'll definitely take another class with him if I get the chance.

I love Xi so much! If I had the chance to take his class again, I would. He is honestly so adorable and is so passionate in his work. He's also really funny and kind, and won't hesitate to answer ANY questions you have. He will help you with your art! He doesn't have a mean bone in his body. Plus his accent is so cute!

Amazing professor that seems to really enjoy his field of study. Extremely helpful and accommodating, lectures were entertaining and educational, and doing the assignments very much helped me learn in an exciting manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Goes into good details in the lectures. Records setup for the 4 assignments throughout the semester, so they aren't too bad.

Great at detailing the steps needed to carry out different exploits and attacks, as well as their various defenses. Was very approachable, taking mid-semester feedback seriously (changing teaching style, adding breaks), and did a great job at answering questions on Piazza. A very project heavy course, but lots of help was available.

Jun Xu taught in a very engaging and homework-oriented manner. In all 4 projects for CS4440, the framework and basic code structure was given to us, leaving us to solve the actual learning objective. His TA's were a little hit or miss, but his lectures were very relevant and the concepts made clear sense. Would 100% take again.

Attending lectures and actively taking notes is a must if you want to do well. The projects were challenging but if you attended lecture he gave the steps needed to complete them. Office hours and piazza were very active. This class was the fastest graded CS course I've taken, which I really appreciated.

Jun is a nice guy but he is not great at conveying the material clearly. Often, questions asked in lectures, on piazza, or in office hours are not answered well. The assignments are difficult and many are just black box hacks where you have no idea how close you are to a correct solution and he doesn't offer much help.

JX has been one of the most caring professors I have had. He reviews topics multiple times, making sure everyone understands. He is very knowledgeable about the realm of computer security. There are 4 projects, but if you go to class he basically tells you how to solve them. Definitely take this class with him! I learned so much.

Jun Xu is an enthusiastic, caring lecturer who clearly loves what he teaches. The lecture material and 4 major projects throughout the semester are fun, interesting, and high quality. Overall this course is completely reasonable in workload and difficulty, even alongside other difficult CS courses. I highly recommend this course and professor.

The lecture material is great and very well crafted. I don't think Xu made it but he uses it. The assignments are genuinely interesting. Lectures can be a little difficult to understand but overall I recommend him as a teacher. He also takes on undergrads as research assistants which is cool. 4 large assignments with about a month each to complete.

This is for MATH3070. The lectures were pretty straightforward, he is good at relating the information you need to know. Only 5 homeworks the whole semester, all quite easy. Very accessible through email and outside of class to answer questions. Exams were 3 questions each and came straight from homework/practice test. No cumulative final.

At times lectures were hard to follow. However, Professor Shen was easily accessible outside of class to assist in homework or questions from lecture. During the first week, he even set up homework groups to allow us to work together throughout the semester. The tests are not overly difficult and neither is the homework.
This is for MATH3070. Xiao is a great professor! His lectures were thorough, and the homework and exams are very fair.

I felt like often I was learning more from YouTube and independent study than I was from him. His lectures were tough to follow, he wouldn't help with homework during office hours, and if you mess up one test you are not getting a good grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great teacher
Xi is the nicest and most kind professor I have ever had. I loved every minute of his class and getting to know him makes class so much better. Would highly recommend :)

Honestly he is the best art professor I've ever had in Undergraduate. He takes the time to get to know each person and their artistic abilities. He encourages everyone while also giving suggestions that feel personal to each artist. He is also kinda goofy which makes him super approachable.
Xi is very helpful and clearly cares about his students. He does spend quite a bit of studio class time on lecture, but doesn't mind if you work while he talks.

I would HEAVILY reccomend having Xi for a painting class, and maybe even try to get his foundation class as early as possible if you have to take the Art Foundation courses. He has a meticulous teaching style and very philosophical when it comes to teaching about the elements of art. He is so responsive in and out of class and gives great feedback
Xi really helped me develop my own style of drawing instead of copying his style, which several professors do. He takes time to work with you individually instead of solve problems as a class.
This is the best professor
Yuchen is the man.
please change profs, save yourself
Yuchen is the man

The professor is a very nice and kind person. However his material and the way he teaches is far too quick and leaves you wondering about things at certain times. If you have time to study on your own then this class is nice, however do not expect to learn concepts by only reading the book and going to lecture. Needs to work on his pace.

If I'm being honest, there were times when I didn't understand some things and had to go on YouTube and teach myself. If you have time to do your own studying, then you'll definitely pass with an A because his grading is too generous. Yibo is one of the most caring professors I've met.

A very nice person but the lecturing is hard to follow. Complicated concepts are breezed through fast, some steps are skipped and not written which make it confusing. Youtube videos are great help for self-teaching, but even then- the quizzes and tests are often slightly more complicated. The good thing is that he is very generous with grading.

Do not take this professor on everything dont do it, he may be really kind and caring, but his lectures aren't helpful at all, you have to basically learn everything by yourself, he wants you to basically memorize every formula, and he gives textbook homework. He doesn't explain things well, goes over concepts way to quickly, don't do it

He is a nice guy, but I was getting better grades not even going to the lectures and learning it myself through YouTube videos.  He's just not my teaching style. I feel like he jumps through complicated stuff fast and other stuff that is well known really slowly
There will be four more exams, one of the lowest grades will be cancelled, and the syllabus will be graded benevolently
Not the best at teaching but really caring. He's not strict on deadlines and wants to help you. He's really accommodating on all fronts
Not too bad
Although Calculus I was a little difficult, Yibo's careful responsibility allowed me to get over it
Yibo's courses are very interesting, the teaching ideas are very clear, the exam questions are kind, she cares about and interacts with students, and answers questions accurately.
Amazing.Easy.

Dr. Yoon is probably the single most caring professor I've dealt with at the U. She is super sweet and will do everything she can to see you succeed. Her homework can be a little hard, but the TAs and Dr. Yoon are very good at helping. She also does a lot to emphasize what will be on the midterms/final as long as you come to class.

Dr. Yoon is an incredibly kind professor. Her lectures on semiconductor physics are really engaging and she makes what you need to know very clear in the lectures. The homework was the most difficult part of the class, but if you make sure you understand it, youll do very well on the exams as long as you go to her lectures too.

Dr. Yoon is seriously the best professor I've ever had in college! She is an amazing lecturer and really cares about her students. She gives occasional quizzes, but if you pay attention in lecture you will do fine. The homeworks were the toughest part, but Dr. Yoon is super accessible and she also has a TA to help. I would take her class again!

I think the professor is a good person, very kind and funny. However, when it comes to actually teaching, the lectures can become confusing and it's not clear what will exactly be on exams. Calc II is hard, and I think he made it harder. Try to get a different professor, but if you don't, you'll be okay. He curves the final grade a LOT.

Yi Luo was the best math professor I have ever had. Usually in math classes, I feel confused. However, with Yi Luo, he ensures that lectures include many very clear examples of each question type. His tests are straight forward, you get a reference sheet, and there are no tricky questions. However, beware of pop quizzes...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures do not include examples. Does not actually show you how to do anything. Youre going to mostly self teach. He even suggested we find other teachers himself because he was aware of his teaching style and reviews...

Unless you're great at self-teaching, I don't recommend this professor. Lectures are very dry and often gives rude responses to questions. Exams are 75% of your grade and 25% is HW (no extra credit offered). Exams have a lot of true/false questions, and he doesn't give any partial credit for any work shown on them, which can really hurt your score.

This was a challenging class because the course material was difficult. I think this professor wasn't the best lecturer, but he outlined exams well and made it clear how he graded. He does have a bit of an accent, but I didn't actually find it hard to understand him. The midterms were hard, but he does let you drop your worst one.

One of the worst professors I have ever taken a class from. His English is not great, and that was especially obvious when I or my class mates would ask questions. He very obviously does not prepare his lectures. Topics seemed to be taught out of order, and it was often the case that the material on quizzes would be unrelated to the lectures.

This professor was very difficult to work with. Extremely lecture heavy, however these lectures were very hard to understand, using rigorous math language, assuming his class was able to understand, all while not speaking great English. He was often unclear about grading policy and was hard to get help with very limited office hours.
His lectures where not the easiest to understand but gave good prep for the exams and the heavy shift of grades at the end was okay

I liked how it was clear what we were supposed to know for exams with plenty of resources to learn the material. I wasn't the best student and think an A would have been achievable, as long as you stayed on top of homework and content. His lectures were pretty straight-forward, working through problems/answering questions. He was pretty funny too.

This is one of the worst professors I have ever had. He makes absolutely no sense during his lectures and speeds through everything. He claims the practice exams will be harder than the exam when its the exact opposite. He is so horrible he had to bring an A down to an 85 and then curve the grade so 35% of us could get to an 85.
VERY GOOD! REALLY, TRUST ME
if you can study carefully, everything will be good
actually, not bad

this guys ridiculous. avoid at all costs. Doesnt give examples, youre not sure what youre supposed to be learning when hes lecturing, its a mess. Hes brand new at teaching and is not really understanding of american culture at all. He tries to mog constantly. hes young, just got his phd. seriously, get someone else if you want to do good.

He is not a good professor, he is clearly new to teaching and essentially just does math on the board and expects you to follow. He also moves extremely fast in lecture yet still we have somehow been behind other sections of 1220 all semester. There are 3 midterms (20%, lowest one dropped) and a final (40%) which are essentially your entire grade.

He just isn't a good teacher. All the midterms had a 50% average with zero curve. Hard to understand both due to a language barrier and lack of preparation for lectures. He even recommended students swap out of his section at the beginning of the semester (I wasn't lucky enough for this to be an option). Avoid at ALL costs.
Ehhhh…. Not that great of a teacher, not very engaging, and has difficult lectures. He could be worse , though.
Grades harshly despite poor lectures
I don't like him, he's very hard to understand
If you can just know what is math, it will be easy to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I haven't enjoyed his class so far, I find him difficult to understand.
There will be four more exams, one of the lowest grades will be cancelled, and the syllabus will be graded benevolently
The teacher's teaching method is very good, the teaching knowledge is very broad, the knowledge point is very clear, a very good teacher.

He is a very bad professor when it comes to explaining contents and he is not comprehensive at all with deadlines, he does not accept feedback and can be very loud if you try to contest something. Take the class with someone else, it is better for your health.

Prof. Yang is very helpful. Attend lectures often, study the slides (he posts them before every lecture), do the homework. Every office hour I attended had a direct positive correlation to my grade. I believe many students rate poorly because they expect to understand everything during lecture. Study and you will be ok! This is a harder concept.

Prof. Yang undoubtedly lives up to the concept he was named after. He brings balance to the Computer Science department, counteracting every good professor with his lousy teaching abilities. The subjects are easy enough to just teach yourself online and still do well, which I would recommend. Yang makes it clear he doesn't want to be there.

The exam and homework problems are reasonable but its obvious he does not care about the class. He puts in the bare minimum effort. He uses other professors lecture slides, and he doesn't do exam review or make practice exams. He's also condescending to students who ask questions. The TA's are way more helpful. Would avoid if possible.

On one hand the material is incredibly simple, mostly reiterating basic high school math. On the other hand, Yang doesn't want to be here, which he's said himself. If you're even slightly familiar with the course's syllabus and think it sounds easy, take this class. If you think you'll need help, maybe try a different professor.

This is the only professor at this university I've felt my time and money were wasted. I'm someone with experience in math getting a 5 on the calc BC test in high school and an A in the required Linear Algebra class, but this guy does not know how to teach so you will have to teach yourself and question why you're even spending money on a degree.

This is the first class I've taken at the U that felt like money wasted. He gave 6 homework assignments and 4 exams where each was graded on by anywhere from 3-5 questions (sub questions on occasion). One exam (3 questions) didn't even offer partial credit? Lectures were useless. He seems to know his stuff but office hours weren't even helpful. 👎
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE. the first test averaged 65%, the second test averaged 80%, and the third test averaged 60%, with No curve or anything. He genuinely seems like he couldn't care less. More than half the class BARELY passes. He doesn't even know whats on his tests. Tests are 3 problems.

A really terrible professor. His lectures are really bad, and he can't teach the subject. The TAs do everything for him, and they are also not great. Very little room for error. No feedback on Exams (Check if they graded yours correctly since they often make mistakes. questions are about 20 points). I genuinely want a refund. Joke of a class

One of the worst professors I've had. Very passive agressive and it's clear he doesn't enjoy teaching this class. The TAs do all of the work, and even then they aren't consistent with grading. Only thing that determines your grade is like 6 homeworks and 4 exams. The exams are about 3 questions, missing one nearly drops you to an F.

Had him for CS 2100. Worst teacher I have had by far. Doesnt want to put in any effort, TAs do everything. The first test average was 65% and he doesn't curve... Gives zero help options, and the practice before exams was absolutely nothing like an exam. Doesn't review at all in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So this is Intro to Graphics. INTRO. Yet the class is on a flipped model, meaning that all the lectures are online via pre-recorded videos and the in-class lectures are "Q&A" sessions that last like 12 minutes out of the scheduled 80. There are so many problems with this class that 350 characters is too short. Just skip it entirely and save money.

One of the worst professors I've taken. He uses all of the last professors online lectures, does 0 lecturing himself. He says its flipped classroom but gives important info only in person. Also there is 0 guidance on how to do the coding. Every lecture is theory based but you need to somehow figure out how to use webGL on your own. Avoid this class

One of the best in the department. I understood what was expected and did what was required. The class was oriented to learning the material before anything else, which was great. I found his class to be at the right difficulty. Material can be hard to grasp, but not too hard. Tests were, in my opinion, easy, but worksheets are important for tests
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yao is the best professor I've ever had at the U. He's truly so amazing. I would 100% recommend any class if he's teaching it

Yao-Yuan Mao is probably the best astrophysics professor I've had. He teaches in a very caring way and does not emphasize grades. I am not stressed out by his class but I still learn a lot. He is always looking for ways to improve and I respect him a lot. Highly recommend.

He is a great teacher and clearly cares about students. His Calc 3 class goes at a very fast pace and he stays on-topic throughout all of the lecture time. Even though his tests often feel somewhat rushed on time, if you study the practice exam it is so similar that you should be all but guaranteed to get an A.

I love Yi-Heng! The first professor I did not get angry in class with lol. Usually they skip stuff or aren't really "there" and just doing a job, but Yi-Heng is fully 100% present. Bit of an accent and moved a lil fast but doable, super chill and wonderful caring teacher. Impressive math skills too. Vector calculus was kind of fun with him.
Very nice professor. Was way more than willing to help. His accent can be heavy at times during lectures, but he always will explain things again.
Explains things very well. Answers all questions clearly. Very genuine and sweet guy. Lectures are clear and very easy to understand.

The professor's teaching was not the greatest. He is a very nice guy, but his teaching style is ineffective. His energy levels were inconsistent from class-to-class. The class however is fairly easy as long as you study and complete the homework. The exams are easy, also being identical to the practice ones - no real tricks.

This guy doesn't really seem to know what he's teaching. I always came out of the lectures more confused than when I entered them. I stopped going to lectures about halfway through the semester and just learned stuff from YouTube. I got an A only cause his practice tests were same as the real tests. This guy is nothing to me, would take again tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ZJ is a good teacher if you actually go to class and pay attention. You may need a little bit of help outside of class because there's a lot to cover in these advanced classes. He is able to go over everything in a timely manner and answer questions until you understand what is going on. His tests are reasonably difficulty and he is a chill grader.
His biggest detriment is his lack of confidence. Most of the time it seemed like he was learning the material along with me while teaching.
Not a hard class if you have a good foundation in math, but lectures were fairly boring and hard to follow.
Has a hard accent that is difficult to understand and has a very weird way of teaching

Sweet professor, terrible at teaching. 
He does not explain a single problem/equation all the way through. He substitutes most of the equation when showing his work and it is extremely difficult to follow his explanations. However, he is very understanding but one of the worst math teachers I have ever had.
8 pages of midterm test in 90 minutes.

Dr. Aksamija is amazing. For a class that gets intensive in the second half, he does a great job balancing the exam difficulty and homework difficulty. All his problem sets do a fantastic job of helping to understand and retain the material learned. And he is a very nice person who is willing to help at any step along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is a super chill guy. His lectures were pretty hard for me to pay attention in, and there was a fair bit of busy work in this class, but his policies are great. The final wasn't cumulative, which was amazing. I'd recommend.

No notes, this guy is awesome. Cares about student success and it shows. I took the first two exams without studying on my own, just completing what he assigns (HW corrections and chapter summaries). I breezed through the first half but the last half gets much harder. Z knows that and does a great job accommodating students. Final not cumulative.

Dr. Z is great, his lectures and notes are super helpful. The problem sets are super helpful for preparing for exams and actually understanding concepts. I would take Dr. Z for every class if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: suuuuuch a cool guy, i love his wit and personality. Dad jokes lol... The course he teaches is designed to be difficult. You get incomplete information in lectures and expected to go to office hours to get the rest of the information. The class seems to be designed to weed out students. But as far as Z himself? one of the greatest personalities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This guy is fantastic. Funny, casual, cool, loveable sarcasm and wit. amazing guy. super available after hours and always interested in student outcomes. The teacher is fantastic, however if youre taking MSE 2160 god help your soul. I would joke with him that "for teaching such a difficult class, hes such a reasonable and likeable person".....

The course content is very challenging and content is covered very quickly, but he does a great job of accommodating this with the rest of the workload. Lot of your grade comes from just showing up, homework can be corrected to full credit before exams, and you can choose 4 out of the 5 subjects on an exam you feel most comfortable with.

Zlatan is already my favorite teacher, he is super interactive with students and makes lectures interesting. He is very fair with grading and gives many extra credit opportunities(can get full points on all homework's, skip 1 question on exam). Material can be challenging but I'll refer anyone taking MSE to take it with Zlatan!

He gives lots of chances to earn back credit in the class and I felt like I understood the material. His exams are tough but he lets you skip one question which really helps. He also requires you to read and summarize the textbook which is time-consuming but useful for understanding the material. I recommend everyone take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked her as a professor even though I took the class online. I found that she gave really great feedback which made me a better writer. The writing assignments and her curriculum work well together and you really gain a lot of new perspectives while taking the course.

Professor Zhu is a very participation heavy and lecture heavy professor. Every class you will probably have to answer questions or have discussions with your peers.

In my opinion, she is a supportive and helpful professor. At the end of classes, she would always stay late to answer any questions or give feedback.

Good professor with extensive knowledge about the course and topics. However, very heavy reading and homework. Also if you don't like to come to class and be lectured the whole time this is not the professor for you.  I never had a class that wasn't lectured the whole period.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I will be honest, this professor is definitely tough on grading. But honestly, I feel that this class really helped me become a better writer. If you are looking for a writing class just to take for credit and get an easy A I wouldn't recommend this class, but if you are looking for a class to improve then take this class.
Great and caring teacher. Really helpful teachings. Class will change your outlook in writing in a good way

Her lectures are well thought out and engaging. She is very knowledgeable in her material, and cares about her students. Engagement is key to success in her classes, so make sure to participate in discussions. Class is graded on papers, but you're given ample time to work on them. She's responsive and gives good feedback on your writing skills.

KING! This is my second time taking 3210 and I'm so glad Keyvan was teaching it this semester! This class is hard but Keyvan makes is manageable with the way he formats the class. He had lecture notes posted on canvas, weekly GROUP quizzes, a couple HW/Quiz drops, and extra credit opportunities. He cares a lot for his students success.
Great professor imo. Has an accent but his teaching style makes sense. Understanding TA's as well.

Keyvan is amazing! His lectures are so clear and precise and the notes are phenomenal. Also the entire course including all of the notes are available on Canvas the moment the course starts. He gives the right amount of homework and is very willing to help you succeed. I would take every math class with him if I could!!

I've taken this professor twice and really enjoy his teaching style and organization. He gives fair partial credit on exams. Labs were harder than expected. Sadly, corrections aren't allowed anymore due to the math department. Overall, a great professor. My "C+" was due to an outside emergency on the day of the midterm, so don't let that scare you!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Keyvan is an outstanding professor. He is clear in his expectations and is a very easy grader. His homework does take a bit of time, but compared to other professors I have had, it was quite a bit less. I would recommend him to anyone who asks.

I came into the class having a rough understanding of ODEs and left with a confident understanding of PDEs. He is an awesome teacher you can't go wrong with. I had the option to take another professor later in the day or Keyvan in early in the morning. I am very glad I chose him even if it was early in the morning. You really can't go wrong.

Absolutely amazing professor I cannot recommend him enough. I have NEVER felt as confident in a courses material than I have for this class. He gives so much partial credit on tests, the homeworks are very applicable, the lab sessions are extremely well organized. I'm limited by the word count but I can rave about him forever he is a fantastic prof
The lectures are very thorough and he goes over a lot of examples from the textbook.

All his notes are posted and extremely clear and concise. Everything that needs to be done is extremely well explained and clear. His test are kind of difficult sometimes but he is very forgiving with grading. If you put any effort in you will do well.

Keyvan explains course concepts very clearly and the lecture slides are readily available and informative. He does many examples in class and makes sure everyone understands the course content, rather than whether they can answer the questions right. I highly recommend him.

Keyvan gives really good, structured lectures. His handwriting is very neat, and he does everything very clearly. He understands what he's teaching, and is one of the few math professors at the University of Utah I would recommend.

Keyvan (K1) was perfect for Number Theory this semester. Class was a breeze when attending lectures. Some of the proof-based homework problems were more difficult, but questions on the midterms always felt within my abilities. Always available outside of class and was willing to work with me. Weekly quizzes are group work and reflected the tests.

Keyvan was a great professor with a laidback but very effective teaching style. The lectures were informative and presented several examples that were present on the homework and exams. Ample resources on canvas such as practice exams and lecture notes made exams less stressful. Overall Keyvan was a caring and thoughtful calculus professor.
I HATED 2200 but Keyvan made it very manageable and gave us chances to increase our grades with test corrections. His lectures were clear and helpful. Would take a class from him again 10/10

K1 is one of the best math professors at the U. His lectures were clear, and his handwriting is legible. His examples in class directly lined up with the homework, and he was clear on the steps. Open to questions. Had midterm corrections to make up lost points. Clear review criteria and helpful in office hours. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

He was a great professor. His lectures had a lot of examples so it was helpful to go to class even though attendance wasn't required. The homework was from textbook and pretty easy. We could take quizzes as a group but they were way harder than exams. He also gave extra credit for each midterm. Highly recommended!!

Up until this point I have struggled in every math class but for once, I understand things bc Keyvan is such an amazing professor. His lectures help so much bc he goes over examples clearly and makes everything make sense. Group quizzes in class aren't that bad, u can bring a mini formula sheet on tests. HW is from textbook, Tests are very fair!!!

Easily one of if not the best math instructors at the entire campus. Very neat and easily followed lectures, extremely patient when answering questions, and a clear love and passion for what he's teaching. You could not get better than K1

Such a great teacher. He lets you do midterm corrections to get 1/4 points back and gives you a cheat sheet on exams. He has group quizzes each week which help you learn the material. Exams were not tough. I would definitely take a class from him again.

This was a very good class and I had a great time learning the material. There were times that I needed to learn certain topics on my own because they weren't covered in class very well. Other than that, great professor and class.

Keyvan was a very forgiving grader, and he frequently paused for questions during lectures. If you want to take MATH 2271, I would highly recommend him. I would warn you that the homework problems from Gilbert Strang's textbook were often difficult, so it is wise to go to the math tutoring center or office hours.

Amazing and kind instructor. Clear assignment, quiz, exam details. Provides optional practice problems for every homework assignment (great for pre-exam practice) and has informative lectures. Personally some of the topics were easier to learn on my own but his lecture style is informative and he always willing to change to better fit the class.
keyvan was the GOAT. great lectures. we all adored him

Keyvan is a fantastic teacher. He is somewhat quiet, but that poses absolutely no problems. His lectures are clear, he is very open on what assignments are due, when quizzes and tests are, and overall my favorite teacher this semester.

You will forget he even has an accent. His lectures are mainly examples, so its best to write them down for later. He can elaborate, but tests are mainly just your ability to do certain problems. If you've seen it once, you can do it again. Simple guy with a sense of humor. Strangely quizzes are hard and tests are easy. Homework is practice.

Truly a very kind professor, more times than not he went out of his way to make our courses more intuitive: He kept really organized notes, kept everything online in case you missed something, gave optional homework assignments that you could use for review, and was really patient with students questions. You can tell he wants you to pass
Kev is the goat.

His lectures are just the textbook. By the end of the semester, nobody shows up to class because his lectures are terrible. He's a very nice and funny dude but he has a very quite voice and a hard accent to understand.

Keyvan is a great professor! He is super organized. Every assignment, note, and module is posted more than a month in advance. He even posts the keys for quizzes and test. He provides all the resources he possible can. It isn't easy content, but if you rework and thoroughly understand all the examples worked in lecture, you'll be in good shape.
Very very very nice, great math teacher the concept just didn't click for me, but he is very patient and a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Keyvan was a really good lecturer, and made every confusing calc topic seem simple. He was super understanding of late assignments within reason and I would definitely take another class with him.

Good professor, but his teachings are basically reciting a simplified version of the textbook. He also posts notes online, so only 1/3rd of the class attended lectures by the end of the semester. The tests weren't too bad, but they're worth a very significant portion of your grade.

His lectures are extremely structured, and follow very closely to the textbook (which I highly recommend as a resource). Quizzes can be challenging at times, but not out of scope of what you learn. Exams are really reasonable and not crazy hard. My personal favorite math teacher, highly recommend!
Great prof. who cares about students and makes going to class enjoyable everyday without fail.

Prof Yaghmayi is a very helpful and accommodating professor. His lectures are clear, thorough, and organized to make note-taking and understanding the material easier. Exams and quizzes are fair and his feedback on missed problems is very helpful. I would highly recommend taking a math course from him!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Yaghmayi was really great! He is very knowledgable, kind, funny, and makes concepts easy to understand. I do agree with some other ratings that say that he talks a bit quiet and sometimes doesn't answer the question asked. Overall, the class was straightforward, organized, and I learned a lot. I really enjoyed this class and professor.

Not much I can say about Keyvan that hasn't been said. He doesn't do anything special, he just does everything right. Great at explaining concepts, amazing use of examples, one of the best experiences I have had with a class at this school. I was deathly afraid of Calc 2 after hearing horror stories, keyvan made it not scary.

While Professor Yaghmayi is a really nice person, he does not really know how to teach. His lectures are verbatim to the textbook and talks in a very slow and quiet voice. His homework assignments were extremely long and exams were brutally made and graded. Honestly, I learned everything from youtube and google.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Keyvan's Differential Equations and Linear Algebra class was insanely difficult and homework-heavy.

Pros:
1. Every lecture is recorded, over half the class will just be watching from home

Cons:
1. Keyvan teaches very slowly and sometimes quietly
2. Teaches through massive homework assignments
3. Brutal Exams that are a massive chunk of your grade

Amazing professor! I failed Calc II (in the form of AP Calc BC) twice before but managed to pass his class with an A, not because he made it too easy, but because he was a great professor with enjoyable and entertaining lectures.

I loved taking calc2 from K1! He teaches concepts very well and is also very helpful in office hours. I always looked forward to class because his love for math is very infectious. He also seems like a genuinely funny person which was fun. "Let's say your worst enemy asks you to solve this integral..." hahaha got me every time! Highly recommend.

Keyvan was an amazing professor. There was a moderate amount of homework, and the practice quizzes he gave were very similar in format and difficulty to the actual midterms and finals. The tests were very fair and graded very punctually. He has a rather heavy accent but the lectures are very easy to understand regardless. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall really great professor. He explains everything very well and his handwriting is really neat. His midterms and final exam mimic the practice exams so if you study the practice exam thoroughly you should be good. Homework could be heavy some weeks though...

Keyvan is a great professor! Not only does he do his best to make sure you understand, but he is also sweet! It is a math class so obviously it can be hard but if you put in the work, you can definitely pass.

The material was difficult for this class but he always gave opportunities to ask questions and he was really really really helpful in office hours. He's super encouraging and did an excellent job of keeping up with canvas/posting lecture videos.

He's a cool guy. Doesn't beat around the bush. He's obviously not there to teach a freshman algebra class but he does a good job of teaching the material. Good luck getting a hold of him outside of class. If you have a good foundation of algebra already, you'll be fine.

Dr. Yaghmayi is the best professor I have had in the math department. MATH3210 is absolutely brutal but he made it a very enjoyable experience. He is extremely organized, the expectations are very clear, his explanations are clear, and it was a well done class. If you have the chance to take him, you need to!
You are guaranteed to pass the class if you put in the work. Tests were very fair and graded leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor gave us a lot of opportunities to do well. We could do test corrections which boosted my grade a ton and I really appreciated it. For tests, I'd really study the reviews. The test reviews reflected the actual tests heavily, granted the test would be slightly harder. If you do the homework and quizzes, you're golden.
Keyvan was a good teacher with interesting lectures. Tests were difficult but I would definitely take another class with him.

Keyvan is a great professor. However, if english is not your first language I would recommend taking this course from a different professor. He can be kind of hard to understand. He certainly knows the material very well. He gave us points back on our midterms for doing corrections. The class is challenging so you do have to work hard to do well.

The best math professor I've ever had. The way he explains things are very clear, and his notes are easily readable/understandable. He'll stay after class however long you need, and will respond emails late into the night. His tests mimick his reviews, though the test is a bit harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: K1 is awesome. 2250 was moderately difficult - weekly lab, take home quiz, and homework. The homework assignments were (mostly) easy. The take home quizzes are too. Labs can be hard, but that's sort of the point. Lectures are a bit long and slightly boring, but that's not K1's fault, it's the material.

K1 is by far the best professor I have had. His understanding of the lecture material is unmatched, and if you don't understand he will explain it to you ten different ways until you do. His notes are immaculate and he is a super fair grader. I took linear algebra and ODE's with him over the summer and loved him enough to justify 7:30 am 5 days/wk

Hands down the best math professor in the math department. The textbook that was used was absolute trash but Keyvan broke it down into simple easy to follow steps. His lectures were super organized and uploaded onto canvas afterward. He is super caring and is accessible outside of class. Quizzes Fridays were great practice for the test.

Keyvan is hands down the best professor ever. He puts in extra time to make sure that you understand the concepts and is good at explaining it in a way that makes sense to you. Overall a super fun guy, made my first semester of college so much easier!
