One of the best teachers I've had in my school career. Was an excellent PDE's professor and I would highly recommend. UofU upgrade this guy's office, he deserves it.

Keyvan is the type of professor that is an awesome person but not an awesome teacher. He is very kind and will answer any questions. He sometimes doesn't answer questions in the best way and some of the homework questions are completely unrelated (stuff we didn't learn). Other than that, he gives pretty good lectures, but beware, it can be a lot.

This is by far my most favorite teacher and is an amazing teacher. Everything he taught clicked instantly and was extremely clear to understand and comprehend. This class was made easy because of Keyvan's amazing teachings. He is always understanding and helpful. He is also very caring and willing to help no matter what. TAKE THIS TEACHER!!!!

THIS MAN IS THE BEST DAMN PROFESSOR IN THE MATHEMATICS DEPARTMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF UTAH! HE INSPIRED ME TO LOVE MATH AND IS ONE OF THE FUNNIEST PROFESSORS I HAVE EVER TAKEN. GIVE THIS MAN A BIGGER OFFICE.

Keyvan is a great professor. He makes us chuckle every once in a while, is very good at answering emails, and keeps the class relatively fast paced. Some homework questions are a little unrelated to what we learned in class but it's nothing impossible to do. About 2-3, 20 problems each- it's not as bad as it may seem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: class notes on the canvas. easy to follow his nots. quiz not bad at all.

Hes been my favorite professor, he is really nice and his lectures are really clear and he makes sure you understand. Homework is easy and quizzes are done in groups. Midterms can have one notecard and are short.
Super cool guy.

He's nice and is pretty funny, but he doesn't answer questions and if he does, its not really the question that was asked. He doesn't teach lectures every well and everyone is left on their own. We've had ridiculous math problems that would need a calculator but we can't use them for this class (1050). Best advice if you take him, go to tutoring.

A difficult class, more so in the summer semester. Keyvan has beautiful lecture notes and the innate ability to help students understand difficult concepts. A lot of the concepts build off of previous material discussed. An excellent prof, generous test correction policies, and accessible outside of class. No excuse not to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had K1 for calc 2 and was absolutely blown away. Everyone I have ever talked to has said calc 2 was the hardest math around but he made it easy to understand and he was very thorough with his explanations. His lecture notes are the most organized notes I have seen, making review easy. Also, our tests were open-note. I can't recommend him enough.

Was good except the tests were too difficult, 2 midterms and a final each worth 20% of the final grade. The test averages were all 67%. He gave midterm corrections and said he would curve the final grade but didn't actually do that. I got screwed over because only midterms had corrections and I did better on those. Didn't round my very close grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: K1 really cares for his students' success and is willing to help them with any questions they have. Class notes won't always be able to help with figuring out some of the harder homework questions, but they give a good general base of what you need to know. Let's you do midterm corrections for 40% points back which is super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Stern but fair. You can teach yourself with the textbook, but expect to attend lectures. He allows you to be self sufficient, but you'll have to put lots of work. He won't fail you as long as you demonstrate that you know what you're doing on tests and homework. Flexible course structure that advocates all kinds of learning. An excellent Professor!

This semester was very tough due to it being an online class but Keyvan did his best to make sure his students do well. Unfortunately,, the whole math department voted to make assessments harder so his tests were near impossible but he is very generous with test corrections. the homework quizzes can also be worked on in groups which I appreciate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. I was terrified by this class, but K1 did an incredible job of explaining concepts and going through detailed examples. Put in a bit of effort outside of lectures to understand what was taught and you will be more than fine. I actually had fun in this class!

I'm taking professor Yaghmayi's calc 2 class right now via zoom. Professor Yaghmayi is an amazing teacher. His lectures are clear and easy to follow and his lecture notes are the neatest notes I've ever seen. If you have a question he is happy to answer. Today I needed help on a homework problem and he stayed 40 minutes after class to help me.

Fantastic professor, lecture notes are otherworldly. Really talented at teaching complex mathematics and calculus over the internet. Just show up and try, you'll 100% pass. The lecture notes are so easy to read and organized, if you miss a class it's so easy to catch yourself up.

He's good at teaching calculus and clearly cares about his students. Generally, if you put the work in you'll be able to pass, but don't expect to get an A without a fair bit of work. The homework and quizzes weren't terrible considering it was calc, but the midterms were pretty killer; I'd just study for those as it mirrors the hw pretty closely.

Keyvan was a great math teacher for business calc, which my friends have complained in the past how horrible their profs were. There is weekly hw and quizzes, which you can work on groups and get a few extenstions on. My only gripe was sometimes picky on grading and slightly tough exams (open note). Would recommend taking calc from him.

The worst prof I've had at the U by far. Might be good for a calc class, but I was expecting more from a DE class for math majors. All we learned was algorithms and NO theory. Gave few proofs. His homework took 10+ hours some weeks + 2 hours for a quiz and it was very repetitious. Take from a different prof if you actually want to learn anything

I took his class during COVID, and he adapted well to the online format. Ive noticed hes very good at specifically answering the questions that students ask, rather than repeating something he said or talking around it like some teachers do. He has good handwriting, is nice, and loves what he does. (his name is pronounced like K 1)

Keyvan is awesome! He teaches very clearly and is willing to work with his students to address their needs. He expects you to do your work, but also provides opportunities like group quizzes or test corrections to make everything a bit more managable. Would definitely recommend him as a teacher!

Keyvan is awesome. He explains material well and he doesn't go too fast. I haven't taken math in over a year, and his class was very easy. He does group quizzes which is great and the exams are all problems you've done before, either in homework or class examples. If you need a great Math prof keyvan is your guy.

The lab books are filled with info, but he doesn't quiz/test on anything too difficult. Easy A and reviews before all tests!! There was a ton of extra credit, which helped if you skip a lab or messed up on a quiz!

He ran my Calc 1 lab and it was the WORST. He never collaborated with the professor and so the assignments in lab were often much harder than anything we did in class or for homework. Graded things really harshly and none it was ever returned. Also when asked questions he gives indirect answers and never explains how to do something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Keyvan was way nice, patient, and always helpful. Quizzes and exams were taken from examples and homework. Grading was very fair, and there was extra credit. Also, the notes were printed so you could just pay attention. Lectures were sometimes slow, but this was generally due to Keyvan thoroughly explaining concepts and answering questions.

Keyvan is very nice and caring. Sit in the front of the class and get involved if you want to do well; he's pretty quiet. Homework and (easy) group quizzes every week.  ALSO, he hands out awesome notes to follow along with. Final's worth a huge chunk of the overall grade, so do well. He curved the whole class at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: The solutions of the homework and quizzes are all on the web and he is willing to help us when we have question.  I expected Keyvan involve the class a little more during lectures. All in all it was good.

I absolutely liked the layout of the class and the way the lectures was set up.  He wanted to help students learn math! I did NOT like the WebAssign homework because it just consider the final answer not the whole solution.  Overall a great teacher.

I took professor Yaghmayi's class in the summer, which might be part of the reason the class was so horrible. Everything was very rushed, I felt like he went through a lot of information quickly without allotting time to understand the principle. I've done very well at math before this point, but this class was impossible.

She is very kind, however her lectures are difficult to understand at some points. Only assigns weekly quizzes, and attendance is taken through in class activities. Open note on exams, and final exam was made to improve the midterm grade.

I genuinely would do anything to drop this class. Lectures are just reused videos from another professor and content is mind numbingly boring. Assignments are easy but have extremely specific submission criteria so make sure you read every word of the instructions, and don't even think about using chat. Worst TA I've ever had.

This was the worst professor I've had at the U. Overall, it was a waste of money and time.  So unfortunate that she teaches so many classes; I've had to avoid taking another class from her.  Lectures are hard to understand, she takes forever to grade, and when she does, there is no feedback.  The syllabus and expectations are very unclear.

She is a very nice person, but not a good teacher. Luckily, the class is super easy, so I didn't mind. The group project kinda sucked, but it wasn't too much work. She told us on the day of the final exam that it wouldn't count toward our grade and was only to improve our midterm score.

AVIOD! Every assignment is exactly the same and un-engaging. Lectures are bad, they take a month plus to grade anything and then you get bad feedback if you're docked points. Don't ask for extensions if you're not in the hospital but if you turn in anything late it's a 0. Taking this class from a squirrel would be more effective

Professor really doesn't know the material very proficiently and struggles as a lecturer. Normally the type of class I'd skip and study on my own, but attendance affects a large percentage of your grade, and little leeway is given. Overall, one of the more frustrating classes I've had to take.
Easy online class for 2010
She was nice and her lectures were interesting.

She's a very nice and understanding person. Class was very easy but there are not a lot of grades in the class, it is a little hard to learn through her lectures but if you want to learn the material you can just put a little more effort into listening to the lectures otherwise you can also just not show up and easily get an A.

She is a nice person but is incredibly disorganized and her lectures are impossible to follow. She often asks weird questions and doesn't put enough details on the slides so you have to take notes off what she says but she rambles a lot. Easy enough class though
Helped a lot to pass and class was interesting, was flexible

Her lectures are hard to follow, but absolutely mandatory, the quizzes in the course claim to relate to those that they teach, but they rarely do. Communication throughout the course is terrible. The only thing that I learned from this class came from the optional textbook. If you can take a course done by ANYONE outside of her, DO IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are terrible

This was not a hard course. However, it wasn't easy to follow along with her lectures. She sometimes asks questions, but they often sound like statements, and she gets frustrated that nobody raises their hand to participate. There aren't many detailed slides, so it's hard to stay on track.  She seems like a very kind person, but I don't recommend.

Had a really hard time learning in this class. Nothing was ever thoroughly explained, and when a question was asked, it seemed like she didn't know the answer. Super unorganized, and never really prepared to lecture a whole class. Extremely easy class though, if you're looking for an easy A. Would not take again though.

This teacher just posted lecture videos from another professor and had the TAs grade everything, so there was no actual interaction. Class is SUPER EASY if you have taken psy1010. There are no exams and the quizzes/assignments are not hard, I spent no more than 1hr a week working on this class.

She can be difficult to understand, but after a few classes I got used to it. If you always come to class and listen attentively and take notes, you'll do well. I ended up learning a lot and actually enjoyed this class, especially compared to profs who just read off slides. She is also reasonably understanding if you make an effort.
Bad speaking skills. She can be quite confusing at times. Not the best option if you're actually trying to learn. If you want an easy A, then take the class.

Professor Zhang is caring and understanding, but also carries a lack of organization in her classroom. The grading is composed of a group project worked on throughout the semester and 2 exams -- which are the most difficult part of the class. Do well on the group project and try hard on the exams and you should be just fine.

Professor Zhang is a very kind instructor. However, her lack of organization and clear instruction create unnecessary difficulty and frustration in what should be an easy course. Most of the class is based around a simple group project that you work on throughout the semester, but it is graded easy and can be a big boost to your grade.

Very easy class. The only difficult portion of the class are the exams, which even then are open note and are often only difficult because of confusing wording. The group projects were useful but only take up two weeks of the entire class, and there's no incentive to engage with the other projects. Sometimes her lectures are confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful person, but seemed a bit new to teaching, so some aspects of the class were a bit unorganized. Attendance was marked at random. Easy grader on projects but tests can be a bit more difficult. Be prepared for group projects.

Amazing professor. 10/10 hands down. weekly quizzes are very easy. her exams are a little bit tricky but completely manageable. group project is easy and boost your grade so much. WILL TAKE HER AGAIN!!

Claims that there is no “right answer” to entrepreneurship but most of ur grade is exams and the questions are based on random opinions she gives in lecture. Does not really care about students or their success and just gives the bare minimum. No review guides or materials to help study. Makes snarky comments at students and is kinda mean.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tina was nice but some times impatient. She tries to be funny but isn't really. At least she makes the video lectures more light hearted, which is appreciated. I contacted her for extending an assignment and she kindly allowed it and even helped me move the date for the midterm a few days after so I could catch a break during my flight home.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This prof is really unlikeable, she has a bad temper if the class isn't participating and would yell when frustrated, just reminded me of middle school teachers tbh, super millennial and bad vibes overall. All the exam questions were super niche to material referenced in class only and she had no review or prep for exams at all. Overall, an L prof.

Taking her course was sometimes frustrating because it was not clear what to learn or what was expected on assignments. Lectures were engaging, and you could tell she had genuine passion about the subject.

She wants to seem like she's chill but she isn't. She is also SO vague on what you should study for the exams and doesn't set clear expectations. Make sure to attend as she tends to ask very specific questions on the exams about examples and activities she covered. I would not take her again, she is just meh, not nice but also not rude.

She did all right making class not so boring even though the content was completely useless pretty much but she herself does have a temper and is strangely subjective on random things. Super vague on what she wants but tells you not to be vague for assignments overall easy class just an L teacher. Easy grade just feels like a complete waste of time

Tina Ziemek has a temper and doesn't care much about her students at all. I went to talk to her after class to try and get credit for an assignment since I was unable to attend that week, and she flat out accused me of lying and swore at me. She said she would never open an assignment for any reason unless the Dean of students was involved.

I have had Tina for ENTP 1020 and Foundry and she is amazing. I don't get the bad reviews tbh. She is a hard grader but she gives you the information to do well, most people are just lazy. She is always available to answer questions, clarify, give feedback, bounce ideas, etc. Honestly an all-around great person and such a fun professor to be around

Don't get the bad reviews—she's super nice, approachable, and makes lectures entertaining enough(still a lecture). Teaches from slides, gives clear exam reviews. Attendance isn't graded, but quizzes rely on showing up (which is fair). My 3-hour class always ended an hour early. Tests are straightforward if you attend. Overall, very easy class.

If I could give you any good advise, do not take her class. Rude, tough grader, and subjective in the worst ways. She is not a kind person. She started her class by saying "you should drop this class if you don't like me or my way of doing things", she was right. Also, she says attendance isn't mandatory, but that's just a test.

Tina is a nice person, however she's never clear on what she wants. She says don't be vague, but she herself is not clear on the specifics that she wants. Even though her instructions are usually not clear, she still grades pretty harshly. The average on every assignment is usually a low B. Overall, she's a good person, just not a good professor.

Tina really has a hard time communicating to students about what she wants out of the class. But, the biggest offender is stating that attendance isn't mandatory, but then constantly harassing students about not coming to class. This professor weirdly had a hard stance on not asking questions for her tests, even tho her tests are full of curveballs
This professor is unnecessarily rude and demeaning in class as well as when asked questions outside of class.

Tina is an oratory teacher. There is no textbook. she is not clear at communicating what she wants in the assignments, and even states she will give you a vague responses if she "feels" like you should have understood the material. Would not recommend taking this class.
Nice professor and all, class wasnt too hard however professor made the midterm and final extremely hard as if we were all entrepreneur majors, uneccessarily difficult exams

Tina has been one of my favorite professors so far. If you show up to class she will recognize you and eventually become familiar with you. She is easy to talk to and always made class pretty fun. There aren't many professors that get breakfast burritos for the entire class :)

Tina is very proud of her teaching style, she is easy going but expects participation through assignments. I loved her ideas and lectures. My only complaint about this class would be that her midterm and final were very confusing. One of the major questions on the midterm was highly controversial as the correct answer was "google it". Overall good!

Tina is awesome! She gives super critical harsh feedback, but it comes from a place of love. She doesn't care about the class but wants you to apply it to the real world to start to make money and be entrepreneurial right now. She truly cares about her students, enough to learn everyones names. If you have an entrepreneurial spirit Tina is for you!

This professor is a fun teacher. Although not required, she makes lectures very interactive and more interesting than it actually is. The subject matter is easy to understand, so as long you do all the assignments you should pass with an easy A. There are some assignments where you have to interact with strangers, so be prepared for that.

Professor Ziemek does an okay job at teaching the material and keeps class not terribly boring. Grading is tough, especially for exams and the path to value assignment. Midterm and final exam questions felt too vague and confusing. Material is ambiguous and repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was unfortunate. These issues have to do both with the course itself and partly the professor. Assignments, even multiple choice quizzes, took weeks to grade. The material is extremely repetitive & poorly designed. I'm honestly surprised it is taught in this school. It was incredibly ineffective and did not accomplish its goals.

Tina was almost two months behind on grading assignments and quizzes making it very hard to understand how well you were doing in the class. Grading is tough as well. didnt understand the importance of this class. I would take 2040 from another teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's probably one of the more inspirational professors I have had. She really values engagement which is hard over Zoom, but she did the best job of any of my professors this semester. Super engaging class and teaches you stuff that is applicable in any type of future job field.

Overall, I thought this class to be unnecessary. It was like a wannabe course that wanted to legitimize itself into the university but didn't really have a whole lot to offer when it comes to course content and assignments. Kind of a waste of time and the professor made up for that by trying to pack in as much as possible

Professor is about 2 months behind on grading making it impossible to know what grade you have in the class. Also for quizzes it takes about a month to know what score you got. she is very unclear and harsh about grading. i would not recommend taking 2040 from this professor.

I really like Tina! If you participate in the class and find a project you like you will really enjoy the class. She is always willing to and likes to help when you need her to. She really cares for her students and wants you to succeed. I highly recommend you take her class even if you are not a business major.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She truly cares about your success as a student and as an entrepreneur. Really inspiring. Be prepared to participate. This is a great class for business and non-business majors.

Likes to make jokes about peoples projects and ideas in front of the class. Lectures are extremely vague. Posts the power points to study from but there's hardly any info on them just a lot of photos/media. If you skip a class you'll have absolutely no idea what that lecture you missed was about because of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tina is an easygoing teacher. She knows this class isn't our priority and our elective. So she treats it that way : Easy going, a few papers, and trys to inspire you more than just having you as a student. Great teacher, knows her class even though it was her first semester teaching it.
Not good. Very not good. In fact bad. Very bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The course content is brand new, so I get that's part of it, but she still made it pretty difficult to understand everything that was going on or why we were doing things. Can't tell if the material or the actual professor are more to blame, but either way it's not a great class.

Long homework, weekly quizzes, and an optional final. The Prof is nice and caring, trying her best to make a hard subject easy. The class is hard, but there are plenty of resources on her canvas. Work with others on homework to cut time. Quizzes and exams are the same as problems on homework. Challenging, but fair.

The class is very difficult but she definitely cares about the students and their success. She has a lot of resources available on canvas to help you learn and is very clear about grading so you know what you're doing wrong. Definitely one of my hardest classes but she does a good job teaching it.

I see plenty of complaints about prof Acevado but she really isn't that bad. These complaints obviously come from students that don't have much experience taking engineering classes, nature of it being an early requirement for the major. Prof Acevado does a fine job and can be extremely helpful and forgiving of mistake if you talk with her. Study

Statics is inherently pretty boring, and when I took it I had two 80 minute long classes a week, so I think Prof. Acevedo did pretty good considering that. A lot of the other review said it was hard to hear her or see her writing on the blackboard, but that's true of any big lecture class. I sat in the front and was fine.

Did not enjoy this class at all. You have to sit close to the front to see what she writes on the board. Her examples of the lectures are way simpler than that of the homework. I passed the class because I started reading the textbook instead of listening to the lecture. She will not answer your email for days. Even if it's urgent.

Statics in general is pretty hard, but she does a good job of going through the material. She stops for questions and elaborates when asked. Definitely utilize the tutoring center for help with the homework, it can get pretty tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She would always show up to class late, then hold us after late. If you can sit through a 80 minute lecture with little interaction, this could be for you. Personally, I prefer a more interactive class, and can get bored easily when being talked at for so long. Homework is long, but the feedback (from the TAs) is good. Quizzes every week too.
She gives very time consuming homework and her lectures suck. She's very quiet and writes very small so it is hard to see her example problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor is one of the few I've had who made me want to learn the material. She lectured pretty clearly, with her accent you might want to sit close to the front to hear better. Homework grading was fair, and there was a chance to opt out of the final which was nice. There were weekly quizzes, but she was clear about what would be on them
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was not available At ALL for students. I emailed her several times with absolutely no response. I asked my TA to tell her that I needed to talk to her, he passed along the message but she never got back to me. She doesn't care about her students and ignored the class's request to speak louder so we could hear the lecture.

Lectures are difficult to follow. It's almost easier to just watch some youtube videos about the topics on your own time and you'll understand more. HW isn't difficult and exams have a lot of practice and review material provided to study with.

This class does not have the hardest content, but be prepared to learn it all in your own time. Lectures are a waste of time as you cannot hear her soft voice or see her little writing on the board. Practice problems made the test okay and homework isn't bad, but only if you already understand the concepts or take your own time to watch videos.

Professor has a slight accent, however paired with the fact that she speaks very softly and mumbles towards the board while lecturing, it was very hard to hear and understand her. She ignored multiple requests to speak louder, write larger on the board, or make any effort to allow us to hear her better.

She really hated doing lecture. She looks like copy and paste lecture contents from somewhere. About 6 lecture notes among 24 are totally same. I suspect she understand continuum mechanics or not. In addition, I dont understand why I need do a project. If you take her lecture later, you can feel she always do her best not to do lecture.

Clear lectures that make things very understandable. She is lowkey on a power trip sometimes but overall she's great, you can tell she cares. Attendance isn't mandatory but idk how you can learn math without showing up. Group project sucks but start it early and you're fine. Weekly quizzes + 4 exams, BUT she drops the lowest of each! Take her class

She tries to reach out to students in every way. Participation doesn't matter that much. It only matters like 3% of grade. Quizes are frequent but she encourages students to share ideas. Homework is not heavy. You only have to take online quiz 2 or 3 times a week. Online quiz is unlimited try so it is really helpful to understand the class.
Prof. Aceves is a great teacher. She makes everything easy to understand and learn.

I took 1080 because I failed it in HS and I was TERRIFIED to take it. Prof. Aceves made it so much fun for me and I actually learned to love math again. She gave a lot of opportunity to improve and lots of prep material for exams. She was also super accessible during office hours and those saved my life. Notes allowed on tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very hard teacher for sure but is one of my favorites. Her lectures do move fast but she allows a lot of time for questions and gives worksheets to work on at the end of class. Her slides are amazing for studying or reviewing and she is very organized. If you actually try to learn, go to class, and do the worksheets, you will do good.

She was one of the most condescending teachers I've ever had. I usually get along very well with professors, but she was bound and determined to dislike all of us. I'm usually an A/B student, but I got one of the worst grades in this class. She did not explain the large 10 page paper and had derisive comments toward everyone. I would never go back.
Prof. Aceves made learning the material very easy, and everything was on canvas so if you missed class, it was easy to get caught up.

She was a nice professor, but she has a group project at the very end that is an 8-page paper that she grades very tough on and doesn't give as clear of instructions as you would think after the grades are given out. She moves fast and mostly only has online office hours.

She didn't teach me Calc 2. I taught myself. She introduces the information during lecture, and gives time to do the worksheet in class for extra practice. She moves quickly, so if you have not taken Calc 2 or Calc BC before, you will fall behind and have to teach yourself. She is condescending when answering questions. Worst math class I've taken.

Hands down the best calculus professor I have had. She does grade hard but she tells you exactly what she wants to see on tests/quizzes. Quizzes are once a week on Wednesday and homework assignments are due Friday. She is a really great professor who knows what she's talking about. I hate calc but if i had to take it again, id take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He walks through assignments during lectures, and makes things easy to understand. He was always helpful, humble, and approachable. The first 6 assignments consistently took 8-12 hours per week. I spent an average of 5 hours per week working on the last four assignments, which were group assignments.

His lectures are engaging and strongly connected to assignments, so ATTEND THEM. The workload is significant and challenging (8-15hrs per week can be expected). It's difficult to recover your grade if you miss assignments, so make sure to stay on top of them. Prof. Ahmad and the TAs are easily contacted through a Q&A platform (Piazza).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really appreciate the way he lectures. He asks questions and gets people involved. Assignments were released in the same format at the same time every week, which made it easier to succeed. He made all of the guidelines clear as well, which took away a lot of ambiguity and stress out of the class.
I really appreciate how he does things. He's kind to his students, not particularly strict, very thorough, good sense of humor. I hope I can take another one of his classes!
Professor Alsaleem is great, his lectures are easy to understand and he makes things comprehensible. He's also very quick at responding to emails and friendly. 10/10 would recommend.

He is a very good professor. I would say his class is on a busy work side. He is a tough grader, but he allows different ways to get our points back. He is also lecture-heavy, but I can't advocate for others, but I really like his lectures. He is understanding and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Zach expected everyone to be an amazing writer and graded very harshly. When I came to him to see how I could improve my grade he was insensitive and patronizing about me asking what I was missing and how I could do better. I wouldn't take a class with him again since frankly he's rude and thinks his class is way more important than it really is.

A lot of the weekly assignments feel like busywork but they aren't too difficult. There are a few big projects, but he assigns them in chunks so they're less intimidating. Some assignments have peer reviews but he doesn't look at them until the final submission, so ask him for help beforehand if you want to make sure you're on the right track.

He cares greatly about the quality of the work you turn in and is willing to work with you regarding the deadline. 

I was also going through a tough time, mentally, when taking this course, and he was the only professor who noticed and was willing to help me both mentally and academically to pass the course. 

A very respectable person.

Zach is a great professor who truly cares about his students. I would recommend taking this class if you are willing to work hard for your grade and want to become a better writer. His class has significantly improved my writing and research skills. This class helped me stand out in my field of work. Would recommend to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Zac is a very fair grader and the homework load is not too bad - the class and content is exactly what you would expect for writing 1010. The class was super lecture-heavy, but I think part of that was because of the lack of participation in my class.

Most of his assignments are 200-word responses 1-2 times a week which usually take about 30min to an hour to complete. His essay assignments do take a bit of effort but he helps you a lot along the way so they aren't very hard.

Great teacher, though his grading was very reasonable. He is a really nice guy and you read very interesting things in his class. If you reach out he will get back to you because he really cares about you as a student. His lectures were short but also entertaining. Great teacher!

He was the hardest grader I've ever had. I had lots of people review and edit my papers before I turned them in. They did well in their writing classes and they all said my papers were good after a few fixes and changes. Then I would turn them in and get a horrible grade. He would only say what was wrong but not how to fix them. Worst teacher ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I highly recommend him. He's the kind of instructor where as long as you do the work and go to class, you'll pass. His grading and assignments are very fair and reasonable. One minor complaint is for the final paper, he asked you to run to his office and turn it in rather than just turning it in online which would've been lot easier.

He is amazingly lenient for paper due dates. He will ensure you have enough time to complete assignments. His lectures are mandatory, but they are amazing and thorough. All questions will be answered. He is also a real character and goes on tangents that are enjoyable. I really get the vibe that he wants his students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Chatterley is one of the best teachers i've ever had! He clearly explained the course goals and he was always open to helping anyone that needed it. I never really thought I was good at writing until I took this class. Definitely would recommend him!

I met Mr. Chatterley a long time ago in a writing refresher and he was an amazing professor. He managed to inspire me enough to stay the UofU and though I didn't finish I managed to stay long enough to find a subject I loved.  I still think of his words often and thank him for the feedback he gave on a paper I wrote that convinced that I can write.

He is extremely tough but at the same time, encouraging in a way that makes you want to do better and makes you feel like you can, and should, do better.  It seems so natural for Zach, the mix of hard, but inspiring, and too many professors lack this ability.  Zach pushes in a positive way and it is an incredible experience.

I loved this professor. He is very intelligent and is good man.  It's more or less a typically writing class so be prepared to spend time researching and writing. 3 Major projects: Standard Operating Procedure, IMRAD report, and a Literature Review.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: There was a decent amount of work in this class but it was never overwhelming. The class discussions were very fun and he was very clear about what he expected on papers. Overall a very good and useful class.

Chatterley is an incredible prof, and I learned a ton from this class. Take it when you have some time to dedicate to it, you'll want to get all you can out of it. If you're looking into research as a career TAKE THIS CLASS, you learn a lot about reporting research and the sci community. Chatterley is really on your side, he wants you to do well.
He is a very good teacher. He talks the entire class period which makes it pretty boring. He is there to help you succeed

I took Zach's writing 1010 class in the spring semester 2013 and I loved it.  I learned more about writing in the first two weeks of class than i had learned up to that point.  My writing improved greatly in his class, and several of my professors since have complemented me on my writing ability.  I credit that to Zach's class.
I really liked Zach. I took scientific writing with him, and he taught me a lot. He was very helpful, and took time to explain things. Ask for extra help and he will give it.

Zach has good intentions for his students, but comes at in a very skidish and scattered manner. Topics for classes are often repeated from day to day, and the required readings for the next class session are always read and discussed without much quiz or test to see if students had read them. Very opinionated and at times cocky. Somewhat easy class

I took this class in spring 2012. He's not perfect with timing and clarity, but I was really impressed with the passion he had for the subject and the time he took to comment on papers and assist with content and writing. He's been the best writing professor I've had.

Awesome professor. The class was confusing at times, but Zac is very willing to help his students and wants them to do well. He will give you extra time on an assignment if you need it. I thought this class was very helpful for those going into the sciences. I would recommend Zac Chatterley for this class.

Awesome professor. The class was very confusing at times but he is very willing to help his students and wants them to succeed. He is understanding and will give you extra time on assignments when needed. I thought the class was very helpful for those going into the sciences, and I would recommend taking it from Zac Chatterley
Very rude and condescending.
This guy was very nice and smart. He helped work with you if you were struggling and generally cared about his students

Mr. Chatterley is an outstanding teacher. His class teaches you some very helpful fundamentals in writing that a student will be able to use in the future. As long as you do the assigned reading and ask questions when you're confused, getting an A in the class shouldn't be too difficult. He is very easy to talk to and will help you anytime you need

I enjoyed this class because of his teaching. The assigned readings are actually useful. He helps you learn how to do scientific writing, very different from WRTG 2010. The assignments are geared to give you experience and they do. He wants you to succeed, you can always go to him for answers. Responds quickly to emails. Great teacher, good class.
a very helpful and friendly professor.  Never wanted us to fail.
Wasn't very clear on what he expected from us.
Very opinionated. Tells you to do one thing on a paper then tells you to do something else that completely disagrees with the first thing. Almost impossible to do what he wants.
Incredibly helpful, but challenging. He really has your interests in mind-> the things I learned his class have helped me  though out my entire college career.
Very helpful always willing to help anyone that seeks help. Teaches you a lot of important information that you will want to know for the future.
I actually learned something about writing. Best writing 1010 professor.
I actually learned something about writing from him. Lots of reading but the reading defintely helps with writing essays and makes his expectations for papers clear.
He was awesome. I really enjoyed how he taught and he made it interesting.
Great teacher, he was very concise in his teaching style, and very well organized with his lectures.  Taking this class from him helped me fix a ton of my writing problems.
changes his mind three times before he tells us what to do for an assignment. We never know what he wants.
Good professor. There is a lot of reading, however all of the assigned reading is helpful in completing assignments.
No Comments
Very helpful, explained everything very well. Learned ALOT! Great class!
Took at uci. I find it funny how he never had office hours for his students. He never was accessible to his students. I would consider his course as a course to teach yourself.

An easy going, lenient professor. He is knowledgable regarding the material along with providing helpful and encouraging feedback. Just make sure to look over lecture slides and readings prior to quizzes/exams as his tend to be quite specific. Overall, great teacher and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Most quizzes questions are based on small details or facts so be sure to read questions carefully. He relies on student participation in discussions in each unit. I didn't use the textbook too much. The grading and layout of the class make it easy to understand what you need to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He relies on student participation to make the class more interesting. So try your best to respond and perhaps connect the topics to your own stories, he really loves and encourages that. Test wise, they are fairly difficult because of questions that focus on small facts about the power points so rigorously go through those. Test 2 was the hardest.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ryan really knows his stuff. Most of your grade is based on a few group projects, and the two exams. He really tries to make the material fun and interesting. I would 100% take a class from him again!

Ryan doesn't lecture very much. He has two guest lecturers and there are four presentations throughout the semester. The exams are heavily curved which is nice but I feel like I could have learned a lot more in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class this semester. Ryan's lectures are content heavy but you don't really need to retain everything he says to do well on the tests. They are heavily curved and on the test review he will go through the actual test and tell you want you need to know. Group projects are fun and relevant. Final project requires lots of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Ahlstrom is a good guy, very down to earth and easy to relate to, but this class was rough. There are 3 group projects, 1 individual project and 2 100 question tests (curved). The final group project is really hard and he does not give very clear instruction. He teaches his opinions but tests on what is in the book.

Ryan was a good professor. He provides feedback on assignments and is always available if you need help. Only peeve was that he spends minimal (I'm talking seconds) time on each slide, so it is extremely hard to keep up. He also doesn't post slides on Canvas until after the lecture, so it's difficult to match your notes with the slides later.

This was an easy class, show up and do the few assignments. There are two tests (that he allows you to grade on your own) and 4 presentations (3 group). He lectures too fast and doesn't give too many details into what he is doing. Overall, not too bad of a class if you don't want to learn and want an A grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff.  i took the money and banking class from Ahmad.  He pushes you to participate and answer questions, even if you're wrong or think you know, he wants you to try and answer and will help you understand if you're wrong.  This class is awesome if you don't understand how banking works.   show up to receive the occasional Extra cred.

Ahmad is certainly one of my favorite professors! I have taken 3 of his classes. He gives you detailed information about his exams about a week before the test and gives up to 10% extra credit for participation. Very willing to help out students who do not understand the material.
Great lectures, encourages participation. Actually knows material and is good at teaching it. Easy on tests, and homework.
Good lectures, has class participate, you don't have to attend class but you do get participation points for being there. Easy on homework,sand test great professor.
Rebecca Aho is one of the best instructors I have ever seen.
Great teacher. Easy to understand. She let us study things that we were interested in. The only thing that we had to do that was time consuming was a Spanish glossary.
Conversation class so attendance is required. No writing assignments, but a few largish projects. Consistent reading/online homework. Sra. Aho is a very nice teacher and I would take from her again

Rebecca knows Spanish well, but I don't feel that she's empathetic enough with her students. She's a bit rude. The classes consist of going through the chapters in the book. Overall, well organized course, but Rebecca needs to improve her communicative skills.
She was a really good teacher!  She was super helpful and followed through on her promises.  I loved going to class because she always made it interesting.  I totally recommend this professor.

Not a very good teacher. Unclear on expectations and inconsistent with method of grading. Forgot about a scheduled appointment with me and was annoyed the two times I asked for help. I recommend taking from a different teacher.

Not a very good teacher.She isn't very clear about what she expects from the students and isn't consistent with how she grades. She forgot about a meeting I scheduled with her and was clearly annoyed when I asked questions looking for help. I would recommend taking from a different teacher.
worst spanish teacher of my entire life
Like most labs, this class was ran by TAs. There are some more difficult pre-class assignments that you might want help on if you havent taken a lot of labs, but the TAs were very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TAs carry this class. It was quite easy, especially if you took 1615. Group work can be challenging, but overall I really liked it.

Adam was mostly uninvolved with the lab; I probably only saw him two or three times, it is mostly ran by TAs. Despite that, the lab ran well, and I wouldn't expect him to be too involved, so I had a good experience with him.

Adam is a super fun guy! While the lab is mainly run by TAs, Adam will pop in occasionally to provide support and see the progress you are making. He is always willing to give you individual support if you ask. Not a hard class at all.

Coletta created a very engaging class out of very difficult material. The quizes were retakable so you could take them without worrying about your grade to see what you actually knew. that was very helpful for learning without stressing. The exams were very well matched with the difficulty of the class and it didnt feel like anything was unfair.

Dr. Coletta is one of the best professors I have ever had. She always makes class very engaging and she is very knowledgeable. I would definitely take a class from her again and an A is very achievable.

She would say that the answers to study were in her lectures or the book and when you selected those answers she would say it was wrong or add a random answer. grading did not make sense at all, when she got several emails from students complaining about it she just stopped responding to everyone all together. Definitely not retaking it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Coletta is caring and very quick to respond to emails. But when you ask questions she gives a very surface level answer. Instead of explaining the right answer, she just states an irrelevant fact from the textbook. Her lecture videos are just her reading the textbook word for word. She puts info on the tests that were never in lecture or text.

This is definitely a hard course but Dr. Coletta makes it very bearable. You definitely have to work for your grade and the textbook will be your best friend. Dr. Coletta genuinely wants you to succeed, she provides a lot of feedback on exams and weekly quizzes. She is clear on what is expected of you and is very quick with responding to emails.

This is a tough course, but Dr. Coletta was very well at helping students with questions they had. Dr. Coletta also provided good videos that highlighted key points, but I would recommend reading the book as well. She provides a lot of time for exams and allows for note use. As long as you take good notes, you will be fine!

Adriana Coletta is very kind and knowledgeable, but not a very good professor. The only things on your grade are quizzes/exams and weekly mandatory review sessions. She does not have any homework or preparation aside from "recitation hours" for quizzes/exams so it's hard to know what to focus on. Highly recommend taking a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pros: HW is 50 percent of grade Cons:Was late to every lecture. Refused to provide answer key for practice problems he wrote for quizzes. Vital info for the quizzes (and final) was often not released until late the night before. Didn't release important resources until being informed they didn't exist. Wasn't communicative outside of class.

Huge disconnect between the lectures and the quizzes/final exam - topics he never taught popped up a lot in the assignments. Refuses to provide answer keys to practice problems. Course grading system was broken the whole semester despite having 4 TAs. I could not tell you what of value I have learned from this class.

Just not a very good lecturer. Stutters a lot, and doesn't engage the class very well. Learning through the (recommended but not required) textbook is viable. I will say that he's quite accessible outside of class, and actively responds to students online. There are bi-weekly quizzes, so make sure to keep up with the material.

If you genuinely want to study algorithms, take his class. Most reviewers here dont know who he actually is. Just know, when it comes to algorithms, it doesnt get any better than this. He is on the top of the chain.

"Leetcode" the class. Has programming assignments akin to leetcode questions, and theory assignments that are more in line with his lectures. Lectures can be boring and honestly unnecessary, you usually learn while doing homework. Theory heavy class with some helpful practical examples. Nice and funny, but his curriculum can be disorganized.

Very bad at teaching. His lectures made no sense and he was practically winging it every day. I went to the TA's for help one day and even he wasn't sure how to solve the theory problem. The only assignments that made sense were the programming assignments. Everything else was unorganized and confusing.
His exams are reasonable, but the course is boring. The TA is very helpful. Will give exams curve. Overall good

His TAs literally taught me any and all meaningful information this semester. Presentations come off as if he's just winging it every day; hard to take good notes. He decided to change the grade thresholds without warning before submitting final grades, which resulted in me dropping a letter grade.

This professor teaches via 'unorganized yapping'. Every lecture, it feels like he's playing catchup with himself from last time and then ends the lecture by saying something along the lines of "ya know?". The one good thing is that he curves the tests pretty hard (original average for the midterm was 32.7/50, then after the curve was 41.37/50).
The only teaching and communicating done in this class was through the TA's.

Lectures are super rough and the examples he gives in class are shockingly convoluted. Often skims over the parts of algorithms I have the biggest questions about in the name of concise pseudocode. I'm told he does much better in office hours but I've found that I do better in this course just watching youtube tutorials.

Get this man out of here. He confuses even himself. You will learn more about algorithms by googling random DSA buzzwords on your 15 minute bus commute to class than you will in his lectures. You will comprehend more if you choose to sleep outside the lecture hall. He cannot teach.

Not sure who gave him permission to lecture he shouldn't even be TA. 

Bad speaker, bad handwriting, bad slides, ambiguous assignments/questions, punishment for handwritten assignments (despite handwritten tests), and he spams assignments. 

I wouldn't recommend unless you have no life outside school and enjoy spending money just to teach yourself.

One of the most incompetent professors at the U. His lectures are wildly unhelpful and confusing - he takes way too long to (improperly) teach the basic parts of a new concept, and suddenly expects you to be an expert when you get to the theory homework and exams. I had to go to his TA and the internet to learn anything in this class. Total mess.

He knows how algorithms work, but he knows nothing about being a professor. The lectures are not helpful at all because he explains everything with poorly drawn diagrams. Often assigns 2 difficult assignments that are due within 2 days of eachother. Overall his knowledge of algorithms isn't worth enduring his class because he cannot explain it well

Very boring lectures and examples in class are at a high level while the homework dives much deeper without a firm foundation. I get confused all the time on how we apply what we did in class to the actual theory homework.

Lectures were slow and it was hard to keep interest at times. Where this professor really shines is when talking with him in person. He was very accessible and his office hours were a fantastic resource. He is always interested in student feedback on how he could improve things and I think the course was overall easier than in previous semesters.

Comparing to previous algorithm classes, we definitely had it easier. Although his lectures could be a bit slow moving, his assignments were relatively straightforward, and usually graded leniently. Exams were a bit tough, but he curved them. The grade distribution was quite a bit higher than previous years as well. Really nice guy, okay lectures.

late on publishing hw, or curving policies. Promised to give post final exams, but never did. Seems pre-occupied doing something else the whole semester. He is nice enough to curve both exams, but doesn't care teaching too much.

The lectures are extremely boring and slow. It is hard to focus and learn because of this. His slides are always a mess so it is tough to review. Exams and hw were fair but I only did well on them because of work I did outside of lectures. He is a nice guy who curved exams but not a good professor.

Professor would often disregard explanations or examples by telling us it was 'intuitive' or straightforward, even if it was a topic we had just barely started covering. Professor also told us we'd get a practice final, and waited until 2 days before the exam to inform us we wouldn't be getting one, while provided 0 other practice material.

the content is hard, the way he explains things is even harder to understand, ironically a logic class should be explained logicically, but his lecture notes are really confusing. If you ever had a class with kopta, you'll see his slides are understandable and organized step by step. Prof bhaskara makes it looks like we're studying law school

With his strong math skills.He has amazing habit of what ever he teach that will be thought with utmost clarity. Each and every line of proof in class will be cleanly derived from math. So he may not teach lot of stuff and make hard for student. Instead he teaches less content with more clarity. Sometimes his classes may be bit sleeply.

His lectures were dry & slow-paced. This combined with his accent made it challenging for me to stay awake in this course. The assignments were generally pretty easy, but it seems somehow wrong to have a 10 question multiple choice canvas quiz for the final. If you want the credit for stats I'd recommend him, if you want to learn stats steer clear.

I enjoyed Prof. Bhaskara. He moves at a pretty slow pace, but I can appreciate that because I struggled on this topic. He is accommodating, and his assignments are pretty easy for the most part. He is a good choice for this course.

Pretty relaxed class if you have a reasonable math/algorithms/data structures background. The professor doesn't usually explain trivial things so students need to be prepared or read a lot sometimes. Good homework problems. Exams can be a bit tough for the given time.
Clearly a brilliant guy with a sunny disposition. Enjoyed the course, highly recommend taking him.

Mathematical arguments lack rigor and maturity. Specified homework problems are often vague leaving in many ambiguities. Material is terrible. Powerpoint slides (in addition to being an non-portable format) should only be seen as supporting material for lectures, however they're used by the professor as primary reference material.

The professor gives a ton of work. His instructions are confusing, he is condescending when you email him with questions, and his grading makes no sense. You have a group project that is so unclear and there are a million assignments for it all semester. You can turn everything in on time and read all the materials but you probably won't get an A.
Such a good teacher and will always answer any questions you have.
Condescending and doesn't have good communication with students. The group work is miserable if you are unlucky and get paired with unresponsive people

Prepare to read, however if you attend class things make more sense. Professor Adua responds to questions in a very clear matter. I enjoyed seeing the correlation between concepts that he was well educated on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is a tough professor, and gives irritating group work. He is not cooperative at resolving issues, or answering questions. Be prepared for readings, and essay assignments. The assignments are confusing, and the grading is unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pretty cool. A little tough on grading papers.

He is a good person, but his class was very frustrating. There is an astronomic amount of reading. The quizzes are oddly specific and nitpicky; feedback on papers was minimal. There is a final group project. Be prepared to be miserable if you don't have good teammates. The class was interesting, but I was too stressed to enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class in and of itself was interesting (environmental sociology), and you could tell he knew what he was talking about. But he gave us a group research project, which was extremely difficult in an online class, and I was never able to contact him for any help. Overall the class wasn't difficult, the main project was just extremely frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I hated this class. Not because of the professor but what the course was. The group project was the goofiest thing ever. It was not clear at all what we were supposed to do & he graded it harshly. Then out of nowhere, an exam was added on and it was worth 30% of our grade?!?! It was just not a clear class & not very fun at all. I would not suggest
Really great guy! Has amazing lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I can't really rate him on the content because he follows the departmental course outline. As a person, he cares about his students and is knowledgable. He can be slow on the grading which is a problem because the course content requires he gives you approval and feedback to move on with the course. Huge group research project. Very time consuming

Quizzes are extremely specific. The class is more of a game to find nit-picky answers throughout the textbook. Wouldn't take this class if you value learning over playing the game in order to get an A.

The class follows a pretty strict weekly schedule of assignments. Easy if you keep up on your work. Would not recommend if you struggle to keep up. Weekly quizzes are super easy and open book. Assignments are not hard just time-consuming. The final is a research paper - super easy if you have done all the other assignments.

Extremely dense reading - get prepared to read several chapters and studies every week and take very specific quizzes on them. Luckily it's an online class so you have plenty of time to get it done. A few papers and discussions but not bad. Dr. Adua's commentated PowerPoints were very helpful in concisely and accurately conveying class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Adua seems really nice. His quizzes aren't great and his provided reading material is extremely dense, but overall I like the way his online class is set up. I think he's new to the University because he doesn't have any reviews but I think taking into consideration a few student suggestions will make his teaching style great.
Not a Bad Professor, not really a flexible teacher.

I wanted to like him because of all his good reviews, but I found my time in his class to be very difficult. Not only did he struggle to stay on an organized train of thought, but he also repeatedly made inappropriate jokes. It became so tiring that I gave up attending class for the rest of the semester and instead learned the material online.
Goat professor

Loved this class—would honestly consider minoring in IS if he taught all of them. He's funny and engaging, even for a 6–9pm class. He takes quizzes with the class and explains the reasoning. Exams are fair with a full page of notes. One major paper/presentation project.
He's caring and truly want us to succeed. He was creating the study guide based on the final exam so no one can fail his exam. I would take his class again
Super caring and kind, who truly wants his students to succeed. Very passionate about IS.

I was worried about this class cause it was pretty conceptual, but honestly, the exams were easy. He was a little weird, but funny most times. You have weekly quizzes, but they aren't hard. I took a lot of classes last sem and this was a nice breather class since Adam was so chill.
He is the best professor you will ever take from!! You can tell he really cares about the subject and makes it fun to learn about. He really helps and cares about his students it is really awesome.

100/10 professor. Cares about his students' overall well-being, is very knowledgeable, and funny. Lectures are interesting, and he always has a positive attitude. If I could have him as my professor in every class, I would.
he is such a king I loved having his class, he is super funny, awesome, cool and a good professor overall!!!!
Interesting subject matter. Could have been presented much better.
Nor really accessible after hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Adam is the best professor I've had so far. His class is well structured, and he really cares about his students' success. He encourages us to stay in touch (through LinkedIn) and will help us in our career pursuits. I actually got a job because he was connected to someone at the place I applied!

Adam makes the dry topic of IS entertaining by using humorous examples in class. Adam is not the typical professor where he reads off the slides, instead, he turns off the screens and uses the whiteboard to draw the concepts on the board, which helps. You can tell Adam has been in industry and won't waste your time explaining redundant concepts.

Adam was a great professor. He really cares about the material he teaches and cares about his students. He is very respectful to students and their time and makes the learning environment pleasant. Overall awesome guy.

Great class and teacher! I learned a lot during this class and I thought it was very interesting! None of the material is super hard, the labs are informative and easy if you follow instructions, and exams are VERY fair! Adam himself is super nice and caring, and does a GREAT job teaching! Both the class and teacher are A++! I highly recommend it!

Online class with really good videos, lots of labs on the main three cloud services, and the reading assignments were relevant to the topics of each lesson (there were only one or two that were really technical).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are looking for a professor to take IS from Adam Frisbee is your guy. He is passionate about his course content and students. He is a professor that really cares about the success of his students. Be ready to laugh in class and learn a lot of valuable information!

I took this class from this professor after reading all of his reviews on here. I have to say, all the reviews are accurate. He is such a great teacher and you can tell he really cares about the class and the material. I 100% recommend taking this class from Adam Frisbee.
Excellent professor. Enthusiastic about course content. Incredibly knowledgeable. Injected lots of humor into class.

Professor Frisbee is honestly the best professor that I have had in my educational career. He makes his lectures interesting and is very helpful when you have questions. He really wants his students to succeed and is always available to help you understand if you are stuck or if you have a question. He is fair and provides all the tools to get an A

Adam is an exceptional person and professor. He is passionate about IS and that shines through when he teaches. He genuinely cares about students and their success. His lectures are enthusiastic, informative and he made learning fun. I don't come from an IS background but he made it easy to learn. I would highly recommend taking a class from him.
Frisbee is one of the greats at the u... i hope to take more classes from him in the future. If you have the chance, take a class from this dude!
Prof. Frisbee was amazing as a lecturer. He knows his stuff, and he wants you to know it, too. He is willing to help you through anything; you just have to ask.

I have been through about 7 years of higher education and I can honestly say he was the worst teacher I have ever had. He would aimlessly wander during his lectures making it impossible to know what is important information and what is garbage. He does not provide slides or study materials. you wanna pass? READ! (also it wont let me rate 0)

Adam is a caring, compassionate teacher who genuinely wants you to succeed. He teaches without PowerPoint, which allows him to dynamically engage with students and avoid the boring reading from slides. This probably makes one or two students upset because it means they have to actually show up to take notes and participate. Highly recommend.

I really like Professor Frisbee as a person, but as a professor he makes it incredibly hard. His tests aren't anything like what he goes over class, and his quizzes aren't consistent to which chapters he is teaching currently. It may be just a hard semester given that the lab person quit making this course a little bit chaotic.

Adam is a really funny guy. His lectures are informative yet fun. He gets the class involved. There are weekly assignments, but the instructions for them make them fairly easy. The e-textbook came with the class, so I opened it up and read it. Its a well-written book, but not required to pass the class.

Adam is a great professor and he's hilarious which is a bonus. You can tell he is very passionate about the subject and he will make learning about Information Systems a breeze! Only thing I found irritable throughout the semester was how long it took to get a response from Adam or the TA, but nothing major. Great course overall and would recommend

Is straight to the point in his lectures. Will go over things that could be difficult over and over until students understand. Made me enjoy and consider IS as a major/minor. It was interesting with the labs and readings that he gave us.
Best Professor out there. Strongly recommend. I took this class with barely any knowledge, have learned SO much, and have enjoyed every minute of it. 10/10
Professor knows his stuff. You learn a lot and need to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took 4440 from Adam, he was really helpful if you needed it. Lectures were pretty good. He doe likes to go off on tangents, but they are interesting bits of information. Class is fairly easy, labs can be a bit difficult, but make sure to get help early before the lab is due.
Frisbee is the man! Will let you out of class early because he teaches in a clear and concise manner. Super funny and nice. Just make sure you schedule your labs early!

IS 4410 is a easy class if you keep up with all the weekly assignments. I thought the midterm and final were hard but Adam does curve your grades so it's not too bad. The labs are easy too but kinda time consuming so don't wait until the last day.

Get ready to learn from this course! Make sure to do all the labs for a good chance to get a good grade. Adam Frisbee wants you to learn and to see the potential Information Systems can do for your career. It was a great course made by a great teacher.
Very intelligent professor. Textbook is not required but crucial if you want an A. Labs are fairly easy and lectures are always interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good professor. He knows his stuff and shares what he has learned. I love that he was open and honest with his students, "you wont use this" or "this is important in this line of work." He is very funny and connects with students well.

Very prepared professor. Very intelligent and has a good amount of industry experience which makes for amazing lectures. Do not skip class (you probably won't even want to) because there is a lot of work done in class. He articulates his lectures well, is very energetic, and provides for a great educational experience.

his Cloud Computing Class at U of Utah was just 1-3 readings each week outside of class (super easy readings, only 1-5 pages each). Then a quiz at the beginning of class on these readings. Then 2 in-class hands-on labs which were actually fun and super easy. I was the only non-MSIS student in class (I am MBA) and it was still easy and also fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Adam Frisbee is a wonderful teacher. He is funny and really cares about his students. His lectures are easy to follow and he loves to make people laugh. If you paid attention to the lectures you do well on the quizzes, midterm, and final.

Frisbee is the funniest professor I've ever had. He's very clear about what's expected, you'd better be in class to make sure you are there for the labs and quizzes... He has a lot of real world experience and is knowledgeable about the industry and where it is going.

The G.O.A.T. The man is by far the best professor for IS 4410. I had some difficulty always understanding some things but because of Frisbee I was able to eventually understand everything and get an A in the class.

This was an awesome class. You might be able to get away by not attending class, but I always loved to go to class to listen to his lectures. I highly suggest you take this class from him even if the only time to take it is at night.
awesome class. The teacher is super excited to teach.

Adam was a great teacher. He was realistic and knew what he was talking about. He made a subject like IS manageable and I enjoyed coming to class! The homework assignments were interesting and applicable.

Adam was a great professor who made the course very entertaining. Kept lectures short and to the point with all the info you needed for the homework. Great review sessions where he told you exactly what to expect on the test. There were 5 sections of the class with one homework, one quiz and one discussion. Easy, but learned a ton.

Frisbee is one of the more engaging professors on the University of Utah campus. He has a deep background in tech and can explain difficult concepts in easy to understand ways. He is also hilarious and I will take a class from him again if I have the opportunity.

Adam Frisbee was a great lecturer and really funny! I waited until my senior year to take IS 4410 because I couldn't get into his class until now. He provides clear instruction and his exams clearly relate to what you are learning in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Frisbee is one of the best professors ever! He truly cares about his students and genuinely wants them to do well. Take his classes if you can! He's awesome and you won't regret it!

Adam is passionate about teaching and it clearly shows that he cares about his students. I loved coming to his lectures (very animated). Although I struggled with some aspects in this class, Adam was very responsive to my questions.

Adam is passionate about teaching and it clearly shows that he cares about his students. I loved coming to his lectures (very animated). Although I struggled with some of the material in this class, Adam was very responsive to my questions.
Awesome professor

Frisbee is the funniest, caring, most entertaining professor I've had at the U. As this is a required core course, it was great to take it from Frisbee as the work load was minimum, and as the course was easy for a non-IS major like myself. With that being said, I also learned a ton about IS, and was thankful that I took the course from Frisbee.
Pretty easy, but informative.

Has a good ability to mix the academics and real-world concepts to help foster understanding of a sometimes boring topic. The concepts in this class are really important to understand and implement in whatever organization you end up with.

Adam was an awesome instructor! I took him for IS 4410 - He made IS fun. He's very enthusiastic and it makes it that much more easy and interesting to sit through lectures. With no interest in IS beforehand, I looked forward to going to class. He has very clear grading criteria and the article readings, quizzes, and projects are easy and enjoyable.

As a business minor, I felt Professor Frisbee was a great teacher and was able to deliver the content in a simple way and made easy to understand. He seems to genuinely care about the students and their future.
He is an awesome professor.  His assignments make sense, and add to the course content.  I loved his class, and would definitely take something from him again.

Adam is an energetic and funny guy. His classes are rarely ever boring, and he brings in some interesting guest speakers. The work load was very light, and his tests are really easy. You have to build a website as a final project, but he walks you through most of it in class. Easy A.
Overall great professor, I personally wasn't particularly fond of the class on its own merits but since its required for many, if you're going to take it, take it from Frisbee.
