this professor really has a holier than thou attitude, never was much help, almost always demeaning. he acts much smarter than he is. when questioning him on simple subjects, it was like talking to a child with little to no communication skills.
I took this class because it was required. Being an online class Beasley can seem distant and a tough grader. That said he was willing to meet by zoom and gave good helpful advice about my writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every time I would get feedback from him, it was very demeaning. I felt like he was talking down to me always and didn't give feedback that was helpful. He would always make very rude and passive aggressive comments that were meant to tear me down. Absolutely would not recommend this class or this professor.

Part 2/2 Whenever I would receive an assignment back he would just tell me to look back to the grading criteria and never tell me what was actually wrong. I went to multiple tutoring sessions at the writing center to get help and even they were confused with his rubric style and cryptic comments under submissions. I DONT recommend this professor!

This professor is never clear about his grading criteria. I reached out to him multiple times over the semester via canvas to clarify the terms of multiple assignments.  The response I received was never helpful and he would never directly answer my questions. Part 1/2

Prof Beasley is an amazing professor for honors writing. His classes go deep and intellectual, prepare yourself for deep dives into niche philosophical ideas involving critical thinking. Put thought and effort into your essays and participate in class and you'll be good. Great class for WR2 requirement. Would recommend to anyone in honors

Beasley is a pretty easy grader, which is good because my biggest issue with him is that he does not make his grading criteria clear at all. He picks and chooses when to give you feedback on major assignments; most of the time, the feedback isn't helpful. Students need to know why they lost points on any assignment, especially major projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is clearly very intelligent and knows his stuff. He likes having deep conversations, but getting there in class sometimes can be tedious. Overall, I would recommend the class.

I took Beasley's Evil class. Definitely wasn't hard to pass. Some of the readings were hard to stomach but then the class is literally called "evil". The lecture and discussions went kind of all over the place. Caring guy, easy grader. Maybe not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Aaron Beasley is a very intelligent guy, but in the semester I took him (Spring 2023) he did not seem to know how to be a good professor. He didn't learn anyone's name and did not have good discussion questions prepared, which led to an overall stagnant and awkward class environment. He is a very easy grader, though.

While Beasley definitely knows much of what he's talking about, it feels like the information that he wants students to retain and remember is not very clear. He's not a tough grader at all, but has a very dull way of speaking. Attempt to understand what he's trying to communicate, and look at his comments, and you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the Honors IT Evil class and not only was the instructor terrible at letting the students lead discussions, he talked the entire time about his own opinions and we had quizzes everyday about insignificant information in the readings like "What animal showed up the most during this reading?". The class was a snooze fest.

I took Beasley in order to have an online class. He's super caring, even letting me redo an assignment when I very much shouldn't have been allowed to. But I seriously struggled when it came to the readings he used and feel like I didn't learn as much as I could have.
I really enjoyed his classes! I also took an honors specific course called Evil 2210 and i really enjoyed it. He can be a tough grader but i really enjoyed his discussions and highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Beasley's voice can be dull and even grating, but when no one in the class participates in discussion its not entirely his fault. The class content is as interesting or boring as people want it to be. Homework is a lot of reading and documentaries. Beasley is very accessible and gives good writing advice when asked for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Beasley's class was discussion-based, all surrounding the concept that AI is going to ruin everything. I would never describe this as a writing class. For someone obsessed with technology, Beasley makes his canvas confusing by not listing things as assignments. He is almost impossible to contact outside of class.

Everyone hates on him because the class is boring, but overall he is a good professor. He doesn't grade hard and switches up what we do in class every day. The workload for this class is actually fairly easy- for a writing class you only write like 3 essays. There is a video and a response due every week but they are fairly easy.

While Beasley is a caring man, he is very dull. His lectures weren't stimulating and the reading content wasn't either making this class very difficult. It is paper based (2 papers total) and while he does grade easy, the papers are intimidating in content and length.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Beasley was thrown in to this class in the middle of the semester, which made his teaching even more impressive. He wasn't a particularly tough grader, but he did give great feedback on essays. My favorite thing about him was how willing he was to let us take weird, different paths in our essays and readings of the texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beasley is knowledgable but not direct with his lectures. He seems uncomfortable lecturing. This class was extremely boring as well. There was no consistency. Sometimes he went over the readings, other times we just watched videos related to the idea of the reading. It felt like a waste of time to spend so much time reading and the not discuss it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Beasley didn't teach about the writing skills that I remember being taught in my English 1010 class in high school. Our topic that he dwelled on the entire semester was technology, and most of our "discussion" consisted of him speaking about academic works that none of us understood nor were interested in. Nice teacher, but a boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There's reading homework every day and a weekly response at the end of the week. I think it's really great because you get a chance to reflect on the pieces. The class doesn't require much from you. You just have to attend and do the (relatively easy) assignments. He tries really hard to make the classes engaging with partner work and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I am a first year student, so I wanted to take this class to become a better writer. I thought it would be good at first, small class size, nice teacher. But there are strange lectures and lots of heavy readings that didn't correlate with writing, or writing skills at all. If you WANT to learn about the controversy of AI, this class is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are actually interesting and relevant to the assignments if you are listening and comprehending them. He clearly knowledgeable on his teachings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: While he obviously understood English as a study, he used a class intended to teach argumentative writing to have us read non-traditional writing styles, like those of Gertrude Stein. It felt out of place and didn't give assistance in our actual assignments. He was being too cerebral in a practical class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Beasley was a really attentive prof and he clearly knew almost everything about the material. I liked the class and I like writing, if you don't actually like reading or writing you probably will not like the class...

Beasley is the most boring teacher I have ever had. He has long papers due all the time and to top it all off, he makes us read things that do not make sense (AKA French/Portuguese/Italian... anything that isn't english). Honestly, I changed my major from English to Communications because of this class. Don't take it, it is a complete waste of time

Although he is very nice and obviously smart the literature he chooses to give the class has NO purpose. We do the exact same thing every damn day and it is to the point where no one pays attention. He needs to figure out a lesson plan for each week because simply discussing what we found in the readings is not cutting it. Waste of my time!!

Class is graded by: weekly summaries, mandatory attendance,  two arguments, one repurpose of one of the arguments, and then a final portfolio. Grades easy, but his lectures are confusing, and his rubrics and be confusing too. Only time class was really NECESSARY to attend was when he handed out rubrics. Other than that, it was a waste of time.

Beasley is an amateur at absolute best. All aspects of 2010 he talks about are covered in a 1010 course or AP High School Senior class. Absolute snoozer of a class, if attendance wasn't mandatory (10% of the grade) I wouldn't come, it's not worth it. Grades papers incredibly lightly - treats you if you're graced by God to be in his presence.

My favorite professor in the Ling department so far. His lectures are actually entertaining and he does a great job of connecting the dots so nothing new seems like a far leap. I was super busy this semester and I learned a lot in this class but it also felt like a cakewalk which I appreciated. Highly reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Kaplan is a great professor who is very knowledgeable in his field and always willing to help you if you are struggling. The material in this course is very difficult and I would not recommend it to those who aren't very passionate about linguistics. Attendance is not required, but you will have a very difficult time if you do not show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Kaplan was great and clearly knows a lot about the field, but his lectures are very long and boring. The grading is calculated via "skills," so once you master something you can move on from it and only focus on things you need to improve on. Homework is weekly and attending class is highly encouraged in order to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a really good professor, but his class is SO LONG. His lectures are really boring if you're not into it, and he has a super weird grading system with a spreadsheet to calculate your grade. However, he is super willing to work with you, and give you credit if you're willing to try. He's a great professor, but it's a rough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kaplan is an amazing professor!! I learned so much in this class and it was so interesting. There were a lot of lectures where I couldn't stop taking notes because I wanted to remember all of the content because it was SO COOL! I never really talked to him outside of class but you can tell how much he cares about the course and his students.

Hands down the best class I have ever taken. I came into this class having a small interest in linguistics, by the end of the semester I had switched to a linguistics major and enrolled in two more of his courses. The class is very lecture heavy, but the material is fascinating and easy to follow. Attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended.

I had to retake this class for the third time because it really matters the professor you have for it!! Professor Kaplan made the material much more understandable than the other professor I took the class from the previous semester. He ensured that we understood the material and in my opinion set everyone in the class up for success. Thanks!

Easily the best professor I've ever encountered. His lectures are fascinating & engaging. The course is well organized and assignments are graded quickly. He grades fairly & gives plenty of feedback. The coursework is challenging enough to feel worth your time but not so difficult you can't get through it. Excellent professor & course all around.
Prof Kaplan is so sweet and makes linguistics really accessible to those of us who are not terribly familiar with it! I'd definitely take another class from him!

Language Myths is a good intensive class to take. The lectures were long and he sometimes didnt give clear instructions, however he is a lenient grader and works with the students. I wished hed be a little more strict with due dates though so some were not wiating on others to finish. Good choice for gen ed credit though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Smart and interesting. Class can be boring if you don't stay interested, but that is on you to stay engaged. Assignments are completely do-able, and he is so understanding of other obligations/life issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely boring and the homework is very hard and it is weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was a good professor. Sometimes the material can be hard to learn. But this is a good class to take to fill up one of those humanities credits. He really likes what he teaches and wants us to like it, as well. Exams weren't too bad, just study up.

Best professor I have ever had (and I am a Senior).  It was the most interesting class thanks to him, his teaching style and his passion for it. He is very clear and explains everything amazingly well! Loved this inspiring, interesting class and was thirsty for more after it.
This was seriously the best class I've ever taken.  So interesting! He's nerdy and awkward and it's just so great.

He's an adorable, slightly awkward man who really loves his field. His lectures are long but comprehensive, clear, and interesting. He is always willing to meet outside of class and answer questions. You really need to go to class to pass. Everything is in class, and there are no notes online.

He is very knowledgable and explains in a simple matter but he doesn't respond to emails which can get annoying especially when you need help. There is way too much homework in my opinion and it takes too much of your time. Quizzes are nice as you get to work with others on it. However, he is the only professor available for this course in spring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's a good course

Uses IVC lectures and notes, but they are a little dense, easy to fall behind if you miss lectures. Lots of homework questions every week, try not to wait till they're due. Exams were reasonable and tested on a curve. Lots of DE systems on final. Textbook was meh. Don't fall behind. Didn't love it but didn't hate it. He cares though. Quizzes.

Aaron Fogelson is one of the worst Professors I've had the absolute displeasure of learning from. His teaching relies HEAVILY on handwritten notes that are virtually illegible. This coupled with his dislike of answering clarification questions and yelling at students for doing so leads to an impossible situation. Avoid this man like the plague.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Currently approaching the final for this course and I'm not prepared. As a consequence of his disorganized class schedule, poor teaching ability, and lack of respect or care for students, this class alone has been more work than my other 12 credits combined. Another negative review at the end of 3/21 had a lot of accurate things to say. AVOID HIM!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gets irritated when students ask questions, in addition to getting frustrated when a student doesn't know the answer to a question asked in class. The material he lectures on and what the homework is on is significantly different from what is actually tested on, in terms of difficulty to the point where it isn't doable in the time given.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fogelson was very receptive to what was and wasn't working in terms of how he taught. If we had issues with anything he was always open to hearing them and changing how he did things. A little all over the place and not super clear in his lectures sometimes, but he was pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Protect this man at all costs.
Yeah so, he's my coworker which means the workload was very light. Big Swiftie and you should ask about his stickers. You won't regret it. Tip: want extra credit? Get him sour gummies.
He was very sweet and cheered me on with my final project.  i liked having him but wished he taught during day time and had more sections offered.

I had Aaron for a design class and loved how easy going he is.  He really pushed my work to be more professional and cared about me as an artist.  If you have a unique style, he will likely get excited and nerd out.  Very supportive guy.

I had Codden for Design Concepts and it was a fun class. Attendance really affects your grade but if you attend class, you get a lot of work done on the projects. I never had too much homework in this class except for chapter readings and some quizzes due before class. He was a funny teacher and very respectful about everyone's style of art.

Professor Agogo cares about what he is teaching, but he is not the best teacher. His lectures are hard to follow and often don't make sense. He is not the easiest to reach outside of class, but shout of the TA, she was great and always willing to help. I have not had the best experiences with the OSC department at the U overall.
Pretty all over the place and hard to follow.
Excel heavy but great professor overall. If you miss class he provides videos for you to watch but they're from a previous semester's class so it's difficult to get the concept at times.

Attendance isn't mandatory; most students stopped coming after the first couple of weeks. The lectures were boring, unproductive, and unrelated to the homework. Everything I learned was on my own, watching other professors' lecture videos. He's kind, and he tried, but teaching Excel by passing out papers in class isn't very effective.

Great teacher and knows a lot. I love that his class was 1 assignment a week and then a final. Usually the 1 assignment was a lab but you learned a lot from it. Lectures were always good. A lot of guest speakers. Like any class how much effort you put in is how much you will get out. Would take again and hope to take more of his classes.

I preferred just to use the textbook because his lectures were hard to follow. He often would go on side caveats, and his lecture structure/objectives were not clear. Most of his content can be learned through reading and doing assignments, so attendance in his course felt unnecessary at times. Easy course if you have some stats experience.

Professor Agogo was a great professor for OSC. I hate excel and osc topics but he broke down the material in a way that made it very understandable. No attendance grade as well which was nice! would recommend.

Professor Agogo is very intelligent and passionate about IS. He gives really clear and intriguing lectures on the subjects of IS and does a good job at connecting them to the real world and history. There were lots of HW assignments and quizzes in his class, but he does offer students a few opportunities for extra credit.
I took IS 3060 ( wasn't an option when I went to rate) but he's a very passionate professor. There are in class quizzes every week but open note, the exams are not open note. Overall good professor.
knowledgeable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I learned a lot from coding along with Prof. Aggarwal. It was a bit overwhelming in the first couple of classes, but then I got hang of it. The best part is that he educated us on how to manage our careers.

The subject matter is very specific and Rohit does know his stuff. However, teaching is not his forte. He has trouble explaining things in terms suitable for people who haven't been data analysts for years. It says something when the teacher has to attend TA hours because there are too many people for the TA to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just awesome
Excellent professor.

He is awesome. Most inspirational. Even though he is not bound to connect students to the industry, he gets people and arrange guest lectures. Stuck at some point in the assignment? mail him even at 1:00 AM on a Saturday night. you will get immediate reply. If you have right skill, he will try to help you with the job as well! Very knowledgable

The class is so poorly designed it makes it nearly impossible to retain any information. Sure he's helpful in his office and a nice guy, but I didn't learn a single thing in his poorly designed lectures. I got by solely by copying and pasting the code that he wrote in class. He's the worse IS professor at the U in my opinion. Sorry, Rohit.
This guy is a machine. He'll reply to your emails really quick. Very helpful. Cares about your understanding.

I'm going to be straight to the point-- he knows his stuff. However, I really struggled to understand his accent. He refuses to learn andor use Canvas (educationcommunication software). No quizzes, just three massive exams and a group project, so if you do poorly on one exam, you'll spend the rest of the semester worrying about failing the class.

Very knowledgeable prof, but doesn't know how to teach. Heavy accent doesn't make it easier. Most quizzes are from the book, but the book is not designed for the into class like this one. Quizzes are worth 70% of the grade. Group project is useless, but not too complicated.
He is friendly and approachable, but expects a lot. Quizes are tough. He brings in successful VCs and CEOs to campus all the time.
He is one of those professors who is really really smart but unfortunately can't teach ! I recommend reading the book to pass the quizzes. The text though is the wrong one for a beginners PHP course.

This guy never sleeps. I sent him email on Friday evening for help. I thought I would hear back on Monday. But within 2 minutes of my mail, he asked me to come on Teamviewer and helped me with my project remotely. It was 11.35PM in the night. Awesome!
Knowledgeable but covers a lot of material in the class. Very prompt and helpful. Has helped me even at 1AM. No kidding! Gives good grades. I wish if I had asked more questions in the class.

Is always willing to answer questions but someone has to be brave enough to ask.  No constand assignments or big tests and NO FINAL.  Has 7 in class quizzes that decide most of your grade.  Gives good grades on group project as long as you follow material assigned.  Very willing to help students with questions and the final group project.

Very hard to understand.  Goes way too fast--after one class I would have 25 pages of notes that made no sense.  Acted helpful, but going to him didn't help at all.  Too much required and not enough adequate instruction to complete required project.  Take this from Dr. McDonald.

Frankly, I was incredibly disinterested in the subject material, but despite that the class was fine. It was always clear what was expected of me and my project-mates, and the grading was VERY lenient. If you do all of the work you will almost definitely get an A. His lectures were good, and he was very personable w/ the students.
Really great class, even in a pandemic. Easy & digestible lectures, overall really cool guy. Would recommend to anyone
Prof. Agutter is completely enamored with his subject and he passes that passion on to his students. DES 2615 is a very unique, outside-of-the-box, and wonderful course. Definitely worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was interesting and they were clear on everything. He was a great professor and an interesting person, and he kept the class fun. There were random attendance checks throughout the semester also. There were many opportunities for feedback on projects throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jim was really helpful, there was three main projects to work on and they were all relatively simple. Just be prepared to work with a group
he is actually a really cool person he's not like all of the other teachers around the U but i really enjoy his class

Really great guy who is very involved. His teaching style is half lecture-based and half hands-on/critique of projects. He doesn't grade harshly if you put it a full effort. He is very easy to communicate with.

Great professor. Class was so interesting. As long as you participate and do your best, you will love the class. A great intro into Design. He really makes you love or at least appreciate Design. And we get a lot of guest speakers who talk about the different design fields. One of my favorite classes!

Lupe is a really sweet person. She's really good about accommodations, working with you, and giving extra time if you need it. But overall this class sucks. So boring, super hard, and VERY difficult online! Please take it in person! I cannot stress that enough. This is a class where you NEED irl lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: *NOTE* I am currently taking this class (online). Lupe is a good teacher, she is responsive to emails and makes herself fairly available. TEST HEAVY -- lots of material is covered on each exam. Homework and lab assignments are straight forward. Power point lectures are helpful and uploaded online. TOUGH CLASS, GOOD PROFESSOR.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is not a class I would recommend taking online. It's pretty challenging and if you take this from Lupe you will definitely be teaching yourself. She does video conferences to help you prepare for the tests which consist of her reading the slides word for word and not actually teaching you anything. It's doable on your own but not easy.

If you're terrible at math, don't take an online class. If you have no choice, she has TAs you can meet with on campus 1 day of the week if you need help. She also offers as much help as possible through e-mails. The 2nd part of the class is the hardest! I suggest doing the homework and labs at the start of the week so you can get help if needed.

She is a easy grader on homework and labs. Study guides seemed to align with the tests. No finals or midterms just three section exams. The course material she has chosen is very understandable reading. If you've take Stats before this should be an easy class, if you haven't the only way I'd see you doing bad in this class is due to your own fault

Basically you read the text book and take tests.   She's not very involved at all.  The homework and labs were easy, but the exams were very difficult.  Don't bother looking at the exam review sheets--very little of what is on there is actually on the test.  Tests on subjects and content much more harshly than homework/labs.

Professor Goel is everything that you would want in a professor. Clear, concise, great lectures, accommodating, funny, straight forward, great advice, good speaker. The only complaint is that he would give out prep exams that were a lot easier than the actual exams, leading me to believe some of the exams would be easier than thought. Amazing Prof!

Abhay was good for the most part but the homework style feels unhelpful. It's based on exposition not accuracy and we rarely work with real numbers. The only time we did work with real numbers was in the online "Webwork" and they were due after the associated exam. I just feel that I didn't get appropriate practice for the test. They are very kind.

Abhay Goel Is very intelligent- both in mathematics and teaching. They care about their students on a personal level- super accessible and responsive to questions. The only downside is how quickly they tend to explain everything- But they are definetly willing to slow down on a certain step upon request. Definetly would take again!

He's very smart and know how to adjust the difficulty of his exams based on the progress of the class. You should attend his classes to be able to do the homework and tests. His speed might be quite fast, but it is how the curriculum is. Finally, he is a good grader, and a smart professor you can feel comfortable with questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. He genuinely cares about making sure that you understand the content. Highly recommend.

He's a good person and he's friendly and caring, however, he's kinda too smart. He goes really fast and expects you to know how he's thinking about the problem. He doesn't really break down the steps all to well he'll just do something.

Awesome instructor! Really - he's super knowledgeable and he's super interested in making sure everybody gets it. Fair warning, you've gotta give him something to work with - the class has to engage and participate or you're not going to get the platinum experience. Don't be afraid to ask questions.

Probably the best math professor I had at the U!. Lectures were very clear, and the 3-4 tests were much like the homework and not very hard considering the subject. He's extremely smart even for a math professor but clearly he made an effort to be understandable. From what I remember he was chill and easy to reach outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Prof. Goel is a great professor, teaching concepts of Calc 3 very concisely and in a way that non-math majors can actually make sense of. Lectures are engaging and useful. Weekly quizzes are fair as are homework. Exams, however, are not. 4/4 exams had too much material for the time period and had to be curved.

Great professor, bad exam maker.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Best math professor I've had at the U so far. His lectures are awesome, he does problems that are directly reflected in homework, quizzes, and exams. If you have the opportunity, take him!
Super kind, willing to work with students

Abbott was great. She is very kind and very clear on what you need to know. She is always happy to help. A group assignment at the end is a decent amount of your grade as well as a cumulative final and weekly quizzes on the readings. Overall chill class.
Honestly loved this class, professor Abbott is an incredibly knowledgeable person and taught the class so well. Although the class is lecture based, it's pretty engaging and I learned a lot!
Love the class and professor was great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting. I heard some warning about tests but it was all super straight forward and pretty easy if you study. She gives very clear study guides before every exam. She never put anything on the exams that wasn't on the study guide. Easy to communicate with outside of class and almost always let us out early.

I loved Sydney! She is easy to connect with and wants students to succeed. There was a lot of weekly reading with a quiz at the beginning of each lecture. The reading is time consuming but not difficult. We also had to write an essay on a book and complete a group presentation project. The cooking labs were so fun. Take this if you love nutrition!

Sydney is a great professor! I have taken both 1020 and 3620 from her. There is a lot of material in 1020, but Sydney presents in a very structured approach and makes clear what we need to know for exams. She inspired me to do a nutrition minor!
Great professor! Pay attention to lecture and lecture slides and you'll be fine.

Sydney is by far my favorite professor I've had and inspired me to be a nutrition minor. She is incredibly knowledgeable and an amazing lecturer. She's very kind and understanding and wants students to succeed. The material was challenging at times but her test reviews tell you everything you need to know and if you go to class you will do good.

Sydney was incredible! Her lectures are super interesting and she teaches well. She offers lots of help if needed and has a super organized and clear class. I'm not a great test taker but still got a great grade because of her excellent teaching!

Amazing professor, so knowledgable and the course is outlined very clearly. Exams are pretty easy if you pay attention in class and study the night before. Would definitely take again! Not many assignments
This was a very enjoyable class. Professor Abbott is warm, engaging, and articulate. The information is interesting. The labs are fun. I highly recommend this class for the international requirement!

Sydney was amazing, I really enjoyed her class. It is vital to attend the lectures and stay engaged. As long as you pay attention, ask questions when needed, and dedicate time to knowing the material- you will do fine in this course.

Sydney is a great professor. She really is passionate about nutrition, but also spreads that to her students which makes the class a good learning environment. Her lectures are insightful, not boring, and helpful for the exams. She is very easy to contact out of class and will help you with whatever questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was a very organized professor. I thought she was very fair in grading and expectations. There is not a lot of room for missing class though. You need to be in attendance to do well. I loved all the course material; it was very interesting. She made the long classes not so bad because we did different activities like cooking labs and groups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was not very hard itself, the only problem being the workload. The reading took about 6 hours per weeks, which can be forgotten when other classes are taken. She also still has not graded assignments from 2 months ago. She does a good job at conveying material but watching lectures at faster speeds makes her voice very annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were extremely boring, and you had to sit in class for 3 hours! It was an insane about of time spent on a boring lecture that was never engaging. She also just read off her slides and most of the homework was busy work. She was never clear on the group project rubric which made it hard because she wouldn't answer questions either

3-hour lecture where she just straight read off her PowerPoint. So boring, definitely would not recommend it for a gen ed credit. Her grading style and requirements for the course reminded me of high school. Get ready for long readings/busy work as well that don't seem to have a point.

Sydney was so nice and willing to work with students. The assignments included a group presentation, food labs, and a critical book analysis. It was an interesting and engaging class that I'd recommend.

Sydney was a great professor. She wants her students to succeed and is very understanding. Lectures are pretty heavy and packed with a lot of info. I dont recommend skipping a lot because you miss a lot. As long as you do the work its an easy A. Tests are a little tough but she gets you prepared well! Would take again!

Loved this class!! Make sure you go to class because that's where you learn basically all of the material...& make sure you take notes every lecture so that you can do good on the final!! Honestly, as long as you go to lectures and do the couple assignments outside of class, you will get a good grade. Sydney is really nice and understanding!!

This class seemed to be more of a food and SUSTAINABILITY class, not a food and CULTURE class. I was expecting to learn more about the food cultures around the world, not about sustainable food tactics. There's too much to read outside of class and the labs were done at home, which caused issues. Overall, very misleading and disappointing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Abbott is super kind and willing to work with you and help you, it is a very heavy lecture and I wouldnt recommend skipping class, overall she is a great professor!

Prof. Abbott did an excellent job teaching online. She is very quick to respond to emails. Lectures and reading take more time than you would expect and while homework can be time consuming, it isn't very difficult. The tests are harder than you would expect- especially study for exam 2 (this is by far the hardest). Overall, pretty solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is well organized and you know expectations up front. Her format/class worked well for online/hybrid due to COVID19. An A is reasonable if you do the work and study. Test are a tad harder then you would think. Do a work upfront as it may take longer to read or watch the videos then you think. There is some extra credit. Only buy online book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a very tough grader. There are a ton of weekly readings not only in the textbook but outside sources as well. She took forever to grade assignments so it was hard to know what grade you had. She has a group project and doing it online is a living nightmare and she isn't very understanding about it, and she grades super hard on the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sydney Abbott does a ok job. There is a lot of stupid reading and you have to do the reading. You are testing on all the reading and it a way that makes it hard to fake it. The labs are super fun and make the class go by really fast. There are even 2 meeting where there is no class. You work with a group the whole time, and you have a few projects
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dont buy the textbook. There are a TON of readings, all available online. I got through them by downloading to my phone and listening text-to-speech. This class is easy, but my friend was in the same class/diff prof, and I realized Sydney graded way tougher and made it way more serious than the other profs. Its good/easy, but just tougher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sydney is such a great teacher. The structure of the class was great, you get assigned into groups and are either in lab, lecture or no class every week depending on your group number. Labs were fun and we made lots of great food. Lectures were slow but she keeps it interesting.

Sydney is a great professor. The material would get boring at times. The class was pretty lengthy so sitting watching PowerPoint slides was tough to stay focused. The part I loved the most about this class is the groups we were placed in for the entire semester. I got so close to my group and it made class fun!
Great prof. Don't expect an easy A, but don't expect a crazy grind.

A little more work than i expected, but overall i really enjoyed this class. A hand full of cooking labs, a group project, a few papers, and participation in class. I felt like she was a fair grader too, not too light or harsh. I would definitely take this class again and do recommend taking it

Professor Abbott rocks! Probably one of the best classes out there for an IR credit and inspired me to consider a minor in nutrition. Projects, papers, and group work. No. Tests. Abbott knows the material well and I loved hearing her bring in information from her experience as a dietician. Gives great feedback on graded assignments.
She's a young professor and still coming into her own. Relatively easy A if you do the work. Lots of writing and reading to do, but she outlines very specifically what she wants and sticks to it.

Most negative reviews hit the mark, no partial credit, very theory heavy lectures, acts very passive aggressive/condescending. Really just not fit to be a teacher. Make sure to not dare talk in his class, also I don't recommend asking questions as his answers to students would be something along the lines of read the book again to understand it.
Disjointed lectures, good reviews were written by him.

Clear passion for his subject during lectures. His exams were quite similar, if not identical, to the review material. I think he has bad reviews because he can be a little intense and will call you out if you talk in his class. But as long as you pay attention in lectures and learn from your mistakes he points out in your hw then you'll be fine

Dr. Abbott was a great professor. When you don't talk in his class and actually listen, you quickly find out the class is relatively easy, especially if you talk after class. All of his material comes straight from his mind, but all of the topics have strong correlations with each other. Study his previous exams and you'll be perfectly fine.

Throws in interesting bits of information but somewhat incoherent lectures and does a poor job helping to prepare the individual for exams with his lectures. Offers few resources compared to most other professors.

This class is tough and Abbott can be a tough guy to learn from if you don't put in the work. Exams are a big part of your grade, but study the provided past exams and you'll do fine. Don't be afraid to ask him questions during lecture, talk to him after, or go to office hours. He is passionate about the subject and willing to help if you ask.

This is a class with difficult material when that is paired with a professor with a different teaching style than what students are used to it gets substantially harder. His lectures are needed to keep up. Hw is hard but doable. Exams are the majority of your grade and make you think outside of the scope of study materials. Have good note cards.

Nothing in the homeworks were covered in class. Grading is pretty unclear for homework. The two midterms weren't terrible, but the final was brutal and so far outside of anything we had gone over. I genuinely had no idea what was going on for most of the semester.

Jake Abbott doesnt care about his students. He only cares about his research and makes up lecture content as he goes. No slides,Exams dont relate to lecture or HW. He said to me "dont read textbook" then when I got confused on an exam question "you should know its in your textbook". Exams worth 75% of your grade and its on content he's never taught

Probably the most frustrated I've been by a class so far. He acts like teaching is an inconvenience/distraction from his research. Lectures aren't mandatory but he doesn't post slides or notes, and refused to provide more study material for tests when people asked. Lectures seem to be made up as he goes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are just him talking about subjects off the top of his head. Writes all over multiple whiteboards and disorganized. Grades very harsh, exams are your whole grade basically, and you need 67% minimum in every grading category to not get auto failed. Exams are graded basically credit or no credit and not many resources to assist learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have had. The worst part is he thinks he's doing a good job, a very vague style. HW has little to do with tests. He feels he's smart and will try to prove it to students in the most awkward ways. Find online videos and you'll be OK, just make sure to go over previous exams. Grading is all or nothing with no sympathy.

Prepare for the absolute worst professor (if you would even call him that) you'll ever take. Abbott is test heavy where they are weighted at 75% and HW 25%. If you have an average of 67% in either category. You fail no matter what. He does not use slides, does not follow the book, and the homework does not reflect any of the tests.

Abbott is a difficult professor to work with. It seems like it upsets him when the class does well, and purposefully makes his final harder when people do well on midterms. Homework is long and unreasonable, since a lot of it is Matlab which won't be on exams. Not flexible at all when it comes to due dates. Not a good class environment.

Dr. Abbott is not particularly helpful as an instructor. He doesn't elaborate much when questions are asked and occasionally gets combative with students who ask clarifying questions. The classroom atmosphere is not particularly positive, and Dr. Abbott gets frustrated when students don't understand the content.

Provides absolutely no material so helping yourself or studying is very difficult. No lecture slides, no practice exams, and the textbook is very unhelpful and not in line with the class .If you miss even a single lecture you're screwed. He gives great real-world examples but completely skips over the basics so trying to keep up is very difficult.

Good teacher. Homeworks are on the longer side, but they prep you for the tests really well- which is good because he doesn't release study guides, past exams, or other study materials. Also doesn't curve exam scores, so you get what you get. Attendance isn't mandatory, but pretty important for this class if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really not happy with this class. Seems to be pissed off at students regularly, especially those who speak up. Minimal help, more expectation of understanding. Only goes into crucial detail if your brave enough to ask. Attending office hours doesn't make you want to do it again. Haven't had a worse teacher at the U.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I dont know if I have had a worse professor. Maybe it was subject-based and stats isn't his thing but I was really looking forward to this class and it is now miserable. The difficulty isn't terrible but you much learn yourself. Also, just a jerk of a teacher, disrespects the class as a whole if certain questions he expects us to know isnt answere

learned everything from the textbook. Abbott is fun to watch lecture -he will not hesitate to call you out if you're talking. grading is unclear and pretty hit or miss. he seemed pretty unprepared, it was like he was seeing the slides for the first time in front of the class. He is a nice guy, use the book and you're fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Abbott is a fantastic lecturer and very respected man. Homeworks aren't too bad but reading the book, listening in lecture, and doing every homework thoroughly is key to getting a good grade in Dr. Abbott's class as he does not give any partial credit on exams. Any gaps in your knowledge and he is sure to make your regret it!

He tries his best to make sure that you understand the topics covered in class and gives ample opportunity to ask questions if you don't understand. With that said, he doesn't give partial credit on his tests and you do not have many opportunities to bring your grade up from those. All told, he's a decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took the second semester of Mechatronics from Professor Abbott.  The class was difficult  and he expects you to keep pace. His lectures are clear and well organized. He also provides ample opportunity to ask questions. He is good at giving practical examples of discussion topics. He is a helpful teacher though not receptive to excuses. Long HMW

Complicated material, difficult homework, very stressful tests. He wants you to be able to focus on the basics and look at the core principles from every angle. He is a decent teacher and pretty good at explaining stuff, but he expects a lot.

Worst professor I have ever had. Test did not reflect homework or lecture material. You must read every word in the textbook to get good test scores. He does not give you a good idea on what will be covered on exams. Anytime you go to his office hours he just answers you question with another question which in the ends never helps you.

Dr. Abbott is an exceptional professor. He is a really visual teacher and gets his whole body and props into illustrating the concepts. He's a fair grader and it's easy to score high on the overall homework grade, but most distinguishing of all is the quality of his lectures and how he makes learning simple for the student.

This was a somewhat difficult class. Dr. Abbott attempts to be fair in grading though. He does come off as intimidating, and definitely have questions prepared before coming to office hours and don't expect him to supply excess information. Be ready to learn and actually pay attention in class and you'll do fine.

Difficult class made even more difficult by the overly comprehensive lectures.  Way too much superfluous information in lectures that ends up making everything convoluted and confusing.   No structured review session for tests, just Q&A.  Since he is so non-specific with what is on tests, it makes it difficult to do well.

This class is befuddling. Why is a electrical engineering control theory class about lapace transforms and state space variables being taught as a required upper division class? Mechatronics is hard, but it could be made easier with a decent teacher. I might as well do the class in Chinese with the way it is being taught.
The hardest part of this class was the lab. If you go to class and take good notes, you should do fine on the tests (mostly multiple choice) and the homework. His grading is really fair.

She is an extremely difficult professor to deal with. She wants homework assignments printed out on her desk before class begins. If students are 1 minute late, she doesn't accept the submission and deducts score.

She comes off very cold and when we went virtual she was very unclear about communicating expectations. Nice to work with for your stimulation but any individual questions you ask her may lead to extremely blunt and sometimes rude replies. Not the most understanding teacher and doesn't attempt to relate to students much at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff like no one else. She's overly blunt and comes off as cold, but a really good teacher if you did all your work and have genuine questions. Use her office hours for the group project or else you won't get it at all. Use every single one of your resource to understand the course or you'll be mercilessly left behind.

Abbie knows her stuff. She is not easy on you, and expects you to put in the time and effort. It's a hard earned A, but achievable if you participate, try hard, and do the homework. Dont do any of these and you get a C.

The weekly group projects are hard, unless your team works together. Remember that whether you are submitting or not, your team evaluation at the end of the semester will tell if you were coasting or being an asset. Abbie is a tough grader, but a quality professor who only asks you to work for your grade and participate. An intro to the real world!

For all of you that are lazy and just want to get by, Abbie will rip you apart. However, she cares because you are supposed to be learning and she will punish you if you don't show up prepared and ready to discuss and learn. This class has a lot to offer and if you really try this will be one of the best classes you ever take.

Abbie is tough. However, she is willing to help and you can do well if you put the time in and be incredibly involved and attentive. The simulation is hard and time consuming but you will learn alot in this class.

She is intimidating for sure, BUT she's not all that bad if you just do what's expected of you in class--participate, clearly answer the prompts for the cases, and listen to her tips about the group project. What you're graded on is very black and white and it is extremely easy to pass her class if you just listen to what she wants from you.

Abbie is a tough grader. If you don't clearly label what she's asking for in the assignments so she can see it at a glance, you lose points. Also, the simulation is 50% of your grade but there is almost no discussion on it in class. My suggestion: read the 150-page case manual and frequently meet with her if you're struggling. Learned a lot though.

Get ready for the most time consuming class of your first year MBA requirements where you will have no clue what you are supposed to be learning. Just remember her grading is random, participation is based on how much she likes you, and no matter what she is always right. This professor could really use a read of "Ego is the Enemy."

The lectures were interesting and she is definitely knowledgeable. However, there's little to no guidance on assignments. You're basically graded on your ability to teach yourself marketing. The group simulation was a nightmare because your grade suffers if the rest of the group doesn't see eye to eye.
A great class.  This is College people if it is not hard your wasting your money.  She was funny and your not going to find another professor with her knowledge.

Abbie is tough, but her door is always open to students. This was my first marketing class and I learned so much. Just try, show up to class, turn in thoughtful responses for the cases, and not only you will be fine grade wise, but you'll learn so much.
It's all about the class participation and ppts in Abbie's class. The lecture comprises of a 100 page ppt that she'll skim through. The more you talk in her class, the more grades you get.
Abbie's syllabus alone made her sound like an arrogant ruthless Beast or Dragon. In person, she was exactly that. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!
Amazing!

It is easy to see Abby's love of teaching in her class. She is extremely helpful and gives attention to every student in the class. She wants to help each student improve and recognizes their accomplishments. She is a happy, caring, person who is also extremely organized and put together. She is undeniably one of my favorite teachers.
Abby is one of my favorite teachers of all time- kind, open, encouraging, and genuinely invested in you as a person. Great classes, great professor.
She is a great teacher and has a fast resource of knowledge that she is able to give to you. She always answered my many questions and has a love of live that is unmatchable!
Unless you were a professional at understanding contradicting views of yourself there is not a chance you would pass

Professor McDougall was extremely delayed in grading assignments, and I didn't really know what my grade was throughout the semester. Halfway through the semester she stopped giving feedback altogether because she was so behind with grading. This course had some vaguely interesting concepts, but the material all felt repetitive and unproductive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sure the course is tough but man it is college. If you can't handle reading a book every two weeks this isn't the route for you. She is a total gem. Kind, relatable, and flexible. If you reach out and create a relationship she will take care of you. She is awesome, if you do the work you will likely get an A. Cannot stress enough 10/10 person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this professor. She is super kind and reasonable and cares about her students. However, you have to come to class and there is a LOT of reading and writing. But she gives great feedback and I found her to be a reasonable grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. McDougall was an amazing professor especially to have my first semester of college. The class itself I found really hard and you have to read a lot every week. Then there's a lot of papers and short response (still 500-700) word things due but if you go to her in office hours she will help you out a ton and give an extension if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Excellent class overall. Course was organized nicely and I never felt that there was too much work each week considering this is a 5000 level class. There is a relatively large research paper that is worth a decent portion of your grade, however she does offer extra credit! Aimee was quick to remedy any problems and will meet with you if needed.

This was one of the best classes I have ever taken online. Aimee is a great teacher and makes the course easy to follow along with. I highly recommend this class. I would take it again in a heartbeat. Super easy!
Her online class was great. Super simple and easy to get a good grade if you stay on top of the assignments due every week and have a basic understanding of the topics/readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy! Weekly assignments and a couple of exams but I got 100% in this class and it was by far my easiest class this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm in her class right now. She has 13 quizzes, discussion and a research paper. This class is pretty easy, just a little too much. Each chapter is very lengthy and you have other assigned readings too. It's a lot of work, but it's possible to get a A if you do everything. It's basically tons of busy work; which could of been condensed.

She was a good professor, but the class was redundant and a bit too in depth to the point of over-obviousness. I never really felt challenged, and passed both tests (90%+) without much effort at all. She was helpful and knew a lot about the subject.
It is clear what is expected of you, you have to try and as long as you do that you should survive. He is extremely friendly and will surely help if asked.

The only reason I passed this class is because of the TA. Professor Ailion would give lectures on proving the mathematical theories but never explains how to apply them. The he gives you incredibly difficult quizzes that are worth 40% of the final grade. Avg class score 410. Expect to work very, very hard.

A very old school professor who believes that the lecture/exam class format is the only way to learn.  His lectures were basically carbon copies of the book (which means useless).  Couldn't understand why his lectures were poorly attended.
his lecture are useless and the homework is totally different form his exams. Do not take a this class from this guy!
TA's were way more informative than the lectures. Class average for midterms were usually below 50%.  I would suggest taking from another teacher.
Terrible professor. Lectures in class have nothing to do with what he expects you to know for the exams.

Not only one of the worst teachers/professors I've ever had but probably the worst instructor of anything, ever. Lectures are counterproductive, materials given are essentially useless, and then gives very challenging homework questions and tests.

The class average for exams was 40% at the end of the semester, there was a clear disconnect between the professor and students. I tried extremely hard to understand and somehow managed to get a "C", but left the class feeling extremely confused. Would NOT recommend this class/professor combination!
Hard class, good professor.
Good professor, loves the subject. Very helpful and accommodating, the subject is difficult and so is the course but a good grade is possible.

Course is difficult, but graded on a curve.  Very helpful out of class and interested in the progress of students.  Overall a good professor who gets a bad rap because the subject is difficult, everyone forgets that its difficult for everyone and therefore has a big curve.

Tests were difficult, but graded on a pretty steep curve. He was often around 5 minutes late to class then wouldn't have enough time to cover all the material he wanted to. Overall a pretty "meh" teacher.

Honestly this guy needs to hurry up and retire.  For an introductory class this class was way too hard, spent a ton more time in this then I did in ochem.  When I brought a legitimate concern to him about my grade he replied "I don't have time for this, please don't email me again."  The U needs to replace their physics department

By far the worst science or math professor that I have ever had, and that rivals a Russian lady I had back a few years ago for Calc III. His lectures are useless and he doesn't care what the class average is. His tests have nothing to do with what he talks about in class. In my opinion, this guy is smart, but a horrible professor.
Hard to read his handwriting, hard to understand what he is trying to explain.  He is an okay guy. Just not one I would recommend learning physics from.
Very hard class, but is somewhat effective in teaching the basics. If you have a moderate background in physics, you won't learn anything in class.
I didn't go to class that often, just read the book and worked a lot of problems.  Tests are fair.

Professor Ailion's class is by far the hardest I've ever taken. I enjoyed his lectures and examples in class very much, but they were nearly useless for helping you with homework (which is VERY hard). I relied HEAVILY on the TA's, the book, and the tutors in the math center to pass this class, which I've never had to do for any other class.

Ailion is clear on what is  expected; he spends one day going over the entire syllabus. Lecture is helpful; he derives equations and explains how to use them. Homework and tests are challenging--you NEED to understand concepts to do well; you can NOT memorize how to do a problem and expect to do well.  Ailion gives extra help at request. Good Luck

He's funny and nice but the lectures are indeed totally useless.  What you learn in class is really not helpful for solving the homework (which is generally pretty hard).  The textbook was the only reason I did well (or even passed) in this class.

Ailion is very intelligent.  He teaches how to derive everything algebraically which is a very valuable way to learn physics.  The hard part is there is a disjunct between the easy problems he shows you how to solve and the homework and exam problems which mainly try to trick you.  To succeed you just really have to do as many problems possible

He is absolutely terrible.  Of course he is intelligent and knowledgeable, but that doesn't mean he knows how to teach effectively.  I had to withdraw from this class.  I re-took it with Pantziris who is the best teacher.

Lectures focus on derivation of equations. Ailion is a good researcher, but poor teacher. He lectures right off his lecture notes and gets confused if he strays. Homework problems as from book. Tests are tricky and test scores average are usually around 50% Read the textbook. Use the TA sessions for help. Best to take from a different teacher.

He's by far the worst teacher I've ever had. All he does is teach the basics and then puts hard and "trick" questions on the HW and tests. He's also very proud and takes typical questions asked in class as attacks on his teaching methods. Do not take his class if you can avoid it. If you do have to take it, use the TA's to get help.

This prof. was very nice, however he did not teach the class with any structure.  I am all for a hard class, however the lectures were a waste of my time.  He really knows his stuff, but that is useless if unable to convey it to a group of people new to the subject matter.

I feel i have to defend him a bit, i like him.
