Not once in this class did I see her kick a student out of class or yell at any of them either.  This is a pretty heavy course, but I'd recommend taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anna is very sweet and she does teach well. She is a little awkward though, and the precalculus course is overwhelming, having her everyday and with so much homework. Although it was a lot, she was a good teacher and I appreciate her hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anna was not a very entertaining lecturer. The class dragged on and everyone including me dreaded it. I'm so happy this class is over. I understood everything until the end of the course. She wasn't clear on certain subjects and it just felt super rushed. RUN DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Anna was positively in the top worst teachers I have ever had. She is extremely moody, yells at students for everything and anything, including asking simple questions. reviews.comment: Kicks students out of class regularly. Does not explain half of the content on the homework. You cannot have your phone out in class, although you are paying thousands of dollars to be there.

Anna is very strict and treats her students as if they are in high school. She doesn't have an patience and is not a good teacher. She spends more time saying "Um" than she does actually teaching the material. When she does teach the material she is not thorough. I would not take this class again.

She's an interesting teacher. She has an usual enthusiasm that is almost awkward, but is funny and gets us to laugh early in the morning. The lowest of 3 midterms is only 10% of grade, quizzes  & 5 hours of hw weekly.

reviews.comment: She is terrible at teaching the material and will yell at a student in front of the entire class (150 people) even if you are WHISPERING to the person next to you. After she yells at you, she will then kick you out of her class. (Kicks out at least two people a week). Easily the WORST professor I have ever had. If you have the choice, STAY AWAY.

Anna overall is a very caring and sweet woman. However, her teaching can be lackluster at times. Since it's a big lecture, you must be prepared to teach yourself most of the material. The homework does not match the lectures. She over-complicates how to solve problems, TA's will be your best friends! Very sweet person, but you're your best teacher.

in a small class environment she great goes in depth with questions and tries to explain things in different ways so the students get it. However i could see (and have heard) she doe snot do well in a large class environment with controlling the class  with students who don't care to be respectful.

Worst math teacher on the planet. Gets annoyed when you ask simple questions, and will not work with you when you don't understand. Horrible teacher, and the homework does not match the material. She is not willing to help at all. And instead of helping the class, she rushed through more material. Stear clear away from this horrid teacher.

This class was okay. I still learned quite a bit but as others have stated her homework has almost nothing to do with lecture. Out of the five written homework that we had one of them was straight forward with what we were doing in class and the rest were just plain confusing and most people I talked to in the class said the same thing.
She's not very clear when she teaches, she also repeats herself a lot.  She teaches like she's teaching 5 year olds.  Overall it's an easy class though.

Anna is a great professor for MATH 1060.  She explains each example thoroughly to do well on the weekly quizzes, homework, and the final.  She is willing to help any student who has questions about the lessons or has concerns about passing the class.  She is also a relaxed professor who is not so much of a harsh professor. Great class.

the class lectures are completely irrelevant  to the online homework, all other work outside of class, and tests. the class has more than 100 students making it difficult to receive help in class so everything is done in groups. If taking this course plan to teach yourself!

I got the vibe that she was still trying to find her teaching groove, but she explained the material well enough and the exams were straightforward.  She didn't get me excited about the subject, but her teaching method was adequate.

Enrollment in this class started at a staggering 145 students which is a bit ridiculous for any learning environment - Lets be real! Clickers were used for participation. Great if in a group with a math whiz, horrible if you were in a group that was lost. No help ever! Assignments galore and in class lessons didn't relate to homework or exams.
I had her for calculus 1 and she was a great teacher. She understood how students learn and using the textbook so that the students had a clear addition to her own notes was great.
Pretty good teacher, but she's a spurs fan... Her homework was alright, but the textbook really sucks. It's a math class so there's not much to say about it.
really easy professor. very helpful and easy to understand. not accent! she required homework to be turned in. but no trick problems very good professor!

The professor was honestly great. So kind and generous, gave a class-wide bump to end of semester grades which was awesome. The weighting of the course was brutal. 80% tests and 20% homework. reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Hong. He is very accommodating towards students. There is extra credit given if you show up to class, so don't skip too often. The course is pretty easy. Only downside is that tests are 80 percent of your grade.

This is my first time leaving a review for a professor. He is a nice person I think, and he does care a lot about the subject he teaches, but his lectures are terribly convoluted and somehow manage to make even the most basic topics seem confusing. Assignments are vague. He will answer questions and somehow manage to leave you with more questions..

Absolutute worst professor I've had thus far in college. To start off, I was constantly confused by whatever he was trying to teach. The tests were on material he didn't cover and the first midterm has a class average around 50%. Ended up teaching myself for the rest of the semester. Lectures were pointless yet had mandatory attendance. RUN

Wholly unenjoyable class. Lectures were monotonous and it's hard not to fall asleep but attendance was mandatory. The projects given out were explained and laid out so poorly, and grading takes literally FOREVER. No time to fully research our final project, and then waits until Dec. 23rd to finish f*cking grading it. GPA got shafted last minute.
Dr. Hong is a kind person, but ultimately an ineffective professor. If he cared as much about our learning as he did about our attendance, we might have learned something in this course.

Avoid Andy Hong for your own sanity. Every lecture is mandatory and his teaching is very hard to understand or follow. I ended up learning the entire class from the textbook as well as other materials online, as Hong does not post ANYTHING on canvas other than grades. Curve is generous cuz no one understands anything but that's the only positive.
Disorganized professor. He seemed confused during lecture, and you end up teaching almost everything to yourself.
Required attendance to lectures, group labs every week. The work isn't terribly difficult, but his lectures are pretty boring. If you've taken high school stats, this course will be mostly review.

What a joke of a professor. I think the first time he saw any of our material was the same time as us during lecture, as he uses provided slides by the textbook company. This is the most ineffective professor the U has to offer. Stay away! I would have a better experience taking this class from Helen Keller.

He is a very kind person but his lectures were confusing and hard to understand. The assignments he assigned were also not explained very well and I was overall just very confused for most of the semester.

He is really, really bad at teaching economics. He doesn't explain anything, and he just reads slides. You can hardly hear him, and he doesn't define new terms that he uses. Homework was extremely difficult and covered topics that he doesn't explain. Tests were so short that each problem was worth like 25% of the test which is insane.

Very ineffective professor, He simply reads problems from the book in class, then expects everyone to know the answer already. Assigns too much homework and has his TA's grade everything, even though they barely know what's going on. The only redeeming factor is that he curves REALLY hard at the end of the semester, if he didn't no one would pass.

reviews.comment: His teaching was ineffective and he chose all the problems in the book that didn't have answers, so I couldn't tell if I was on the right track. I didn't like the textbook choice either- it had some errors and unclear wording. His exams are short and don't cover everything but they can be a little confusing. The grading was very generous though.

The class was called field studies in urban ecology. We did one field study throughout the entire semester and it lacked any kind of real information or learning opportunities. He never grades anything and the TAs rarely even knew what was going on. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES! I have never been so disappointed by a class at the U
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall great teacher. Understand if you let him know before hand. Everything you turn in is pretty easy to figure out and receive a good grade in. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The grade weight was skewed heavily towards tests, so make sure to study. The nice part was that the final was not comprehensive and only included material that had been covered since the last midterm. He is very reasonable and willing to work with your personal circumstances.

he prioritizes you learning the concepts over doing it right the first time by letting you resubmit homework and test corrections to make up points. he is terrible at keeping up to date on grades. textbook heavy (uses tables in the back a lot). encourages group discussion and participation for extra points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Roberts is an amazing professor. He genuinely cares so much about his students and is such an amazing role model. His lectures are very engaging, and his class structure is very organized. Dr. Roberts is an amazing mentor who truly wants you to succeed in your goals. I would highly recommend taking his class.

He is extremely organized, responsive, and kind. He goes out of his way to approach each student to see if they understand the material and he is very organized. All of his notes, worksheets, and keys are posted on canvas along with additional lectures. Through the worksheets, you see exactly what concepts he wants you to understand for the tests

Professor Roberts is the best chemistry professor I've had so far. He is incredibly knowledgeable about organic chemistry and incorporated tips about graduate school preparation into his lectures. He's very available and willing to help students. The discussion problem sets are very helpful for exam preparation.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really dislike and don't excel through online learning, but given the circumstances, Dr. Roberts has done a great job. He seems to care about and understand his students, which has made the course much more approachable.

reviews.comment: Dr. Roberts is very caring, his lectures are enjoyable, and you will learn a lot. Honors Ochem II is a hard class, but you will have a lot of help. reviews.comment: I have to say her forced participation is awkward and quite counterproductive.

Last day of school and first time writing a review of a professor. Anne is taking too much obscure and unclear her own judgement on bi-weekly quizzes and the feedback is highly opinioned if any real feedback. Student have to guess what she want
She is so opiniated. And She tried to advertise her classes whenever you found a chance. Very p a t h x etic.
A total disappointment. In philosophy, people supposed to be open-minded. But Anne, she appears to be, when you talked a little deeper, you will find she isn't.

The big problem I faced with Anne was never received a grade or feedback on the daily quizzes and biweekly mini-exams. Great lecturer, but seemingly not given enough resources.
Not recommended because of her inability to communicate
She is placing her heavy opinions on the content of the course. She is a failure of judgement.
Forced participation when what she talks does not interest you.
The best teacher you can have. look at a different lense

Really liked the class, super interesting and clear material. She leads really good discussions and provokes very good questions. reviews.comment: Professor Peterson is very knowledgeable about Ancient Greek Philosophy. She is very caring, understanding, and approachable. She makes expectations clear at the beginning of the semester. You do need books for this course. She wants every student to succeed and gave detailed feedback on writing assignments to help improve writing moving forward.

Professor Peterson is by far the best in the philosophy department. I have taken three classes from her by the time of this rating and I can just say that I have had some of the best discussions in my life with her. She is very understanding, witty, and open to new ideas. Would recommend for any class!

Prof. Peterson is a good teacher, but her lectures can feel disjointed and lack brevity. I also wasn't a big fan of her participation policy, as it forces people to talk even when they have nothing to say. Don't let my rating scare you away, though! I've learned a great deal in her class and have generally enjoyed it.

Only actually payed attention to like 5 zoom lectures but still got an A on all assignments. Pay attention to grading criteria on papers. Turn everything in even if it is late because she has a very lenient late policy even on papers. She responds to emails quickly and is understanding! Definitely the best humanities credit class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My main issue was that for a lower level class her grading was incredibly harsh. It was very slim that anyone in the class would get 100% on any assignment or paper. Even if you get all the correct answers you will still loose points if you did not "go the extra mile."  Also takes a very long time to grade anything.

Prof. Peterson is my absolute favorite professor. I have taken three classes with her now, and without a doubt her classes have some of the best and most generative discussions in the entire phil department. This is because Prof. Peterson knows how to listen to students and is supportive and caring, giving students the confidence to speak up.

I have only taken multiple classes from two different professors. One of them was Anne Peterson, whom I have had four times, and that wasn't an accident. That should say a lot. She is passionate and knowledgable. Her lecture slides are great, and her grading is very fair while pushing you just enough. One of the best professors I have ever had.

Professor Anne Peterson is a really nice and caring teacher. However, found myself lost frequently in class. Slideshows are close to impossible to take notes on as they have an absurd amount of content and the Professor flies through them rapidly. Be prepared to read a lot and struggle with the content being taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Peterson's PHIL 5110 class on Aristotle was a lot of fun. We read selections from Aristotle's corpus every week along with secondary readings and posted a 100-word online discussion response/question each week. There were three papers, a rewrite of our first paper, and then a final exam. The class was tough, but I recommend it unreservedly.

Attendance is a grade, but very easy to get and in class assignments are very simple. There are also a couple of group projects/presentations, but she grades lightly and gives good feedback. I believe there were 2 in class "quizzes" but they were full points as long as you were just there and turned something in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anita is very kind and understanding. I took the capstone course for HSP (not LEAP 1140), and she gave great feedback and was fun to be in class with. She was flexible and gave students the freedom to structure their group projects. Attendance was important, but communicating absences with her was no big deal.

This is for FCS3380
She is very kind and understanding, I had a couple issues during the semester and she made it easier for me to stay up to date with assignments at my own pace. The material was interesting and applicable to any pre-health students. I highly recommend this professor, she's amazing!
Anita was very kind and class was easy. However there was a clear disconnect and she made some projects on a whim.
A very nice professor who is very knowledgable about the topic and makes it interesting because she herself is interested. Flexible and communicative and keeps busy work to a minimum.

Prof Pascoe is so sweet and such a great professor. It's easy to tell she genuinely cares about each student. The class was well organized and easy to understand. She's very reachable if you have questions about anything. You do have to go to class if you want a good grade, but lectures are interesting. I'd definitely take a class from her again!

Anita was a great professor, her class starts with blasting music of a very helpful song for the subject. She is very understanding of pretty much everything, she is also willing to help you as many times as you ask. Quite honestly 10/10 professors, it does have a fair amount of assignments and they WILL take you at least 2-3 hours but super easy!

I took Anita's class online and it was a great experience. She provides pp lectures with audio and clearly explains every section where homework will be involved. If you are confused with something she responds within a day  via email. She definitely wants you to succeed in this class. 2 exams in the semester. If you do the HW you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I've had at the U of U. She truly wants every student to succeed and believes it is possible for all to do so.  Her lectures are participant based, so it is pertinent to complete the reading before class. While there is a lot of reading,  and "pop quizzes", there are only a few assignments which make it nice.

Anita is AMAZING! I took her two week intensive  course so the participation was a big part of class - but she was so great at relaying the important details that you needed to remember. I would highly recommend her as a professor for this, or any class, that you may need to take.

I haven't been back to school in over 10 years and it's a hybrid class. The professor is really helpful and I found all the lectures really interesting.   There's a little math involved and a lot of reading. Just go to class, do the work and if you don't understand ask her she is always willing to help you understand. i would reccomend this teacher

She is a fantastic teacher, I loved her lectures and truly enjoyed every minute of her class! As long as you come to class (attendance is part of your grade) and do the few assignments throughout the semester it is impossible to get less than an A. Loved her!!

I really enjoyed the class Population and Society by Professor Pascoe. She is a great teacher and makes the lectures very entertaining. She also lets you use a page of notes for every exam which is very nice. She also lets the students interacting in the lectures. She asks you questions that relate to all of us and she likes to hear our opinion.

Class was lightwork no reaction but incredibly dull. The topics you learn seem to be random and only loosely related in that a db is involved somehow. Overall not my cup of tea, but maybe people that are really into human centered development will appreciate this course, though I think AI has made most the solutions we covered irrelevant.

Human centered data management: Attendance not mandatory at all except for lectures. Homeworks were super easy, and there were only 2 of them. The quizzes were easy, especially using the Scribe notes posted on the syllabus.

I'm writing review for Deep Learning class. Lecture is well-organized and I learned a lot from the class. Homework is rough and you should be familiar with NumPy beforehand. But we can learn a lot from the homework, and a lot of extra credit opportunities.
Fun lectures and interesting if complicated homew

The class was super chill, attendance points counted as extra credit, and only had two homeworks and one midterm exam. She did her best to make sure every student succeeded and you could tell she is very passionate about data management. The TA's were super helpful and accessible and overall the class was super easy as long as you put in effort.

He is very understanding and willing to change due dates if you ask nicely. He's the best because he doesn't want to see any students fail—he will work with you if you encounter any obstacles. I can't say enough good things about him.  The only thing that i dont like is that there are a lot of reading assignments(not difficult, just time‑consuming.

This class is very easy and Russ is a very caring professor. I think reducing that busy work is something he could improve on, but the technical report and job packet develop very useful skills for an engineer to have. The flipped classroom style is a bit annoying but just focus on what he emphasizes in lecture and you'll be good.

If you do what he says, you WILL become a better writer. He gives a lot of readings and they are all worth it and interesting. He's flexible on deadlines if you communicate, and he's willing to take criticism and implement changes immediately.

Professor Askren is a very flexible and understanding professor. He is very laid back and does a great job at teaching relevant and useful material. Willing to extend due dates if other exams/projects in other courses come up. Provides meaningful feedback, and is fairly reasonable on grading. Prepare to WORK, a lot of writing. Nice guy overall.

Russ is a great professor, he's caring and is willing to push back deadlines to relieve some of our stress. He gives great feedback on assignments, too. This class was a lot more work than I was expecting it to be (not hard, just a lot of assignments). But he is passionate about what he teaches and has good resources online too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was hesitant to take him as a teacher due to the previous rating, but Russell completely surprised me. He would bend over backwards to make sure student's needs were met, and the grading was fair. The only criticism I can offer is that grading takes forever, which is understandable because most of the assignments are written essays/memos.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

Whole grade is 4 tests and if you struggle in his class, tough luck. He comes with a superiority complex and is completely unfocused on helping you learn. A real Gale Nolan type.

reviews.comment: this guy showed a prager u video in class and tried to claim that christopher columbus wasnt actually a bad guy at all. i feel like thats all you need to know

Classes are good. Sandomir really know what he is talking about. But exam are really long, few hours and many questions. Intense reading, specially if you decide to do this course on summer. It is a challenging course but a really nice class

Accounting, marketing, finance etc. Could have been dry but was a real intellectual experience. Professor Sandomir is excellent at explaining concepts and hes is fair in his grading but exams and quizzes are tough. They do include marketing strategy, accounting, and banking questions. You need to study but he gives you a lot of time.

Professor Sandomir is definitely an intelligent lecturer and he has a lot of information to share. His tests are really difficult, but if you study diligently you should do above average on them and there's also a curve. The textbook wasn't necessary in my opinion because most of the reading can be found online for free, save your money.

reviews.comment: This is way harder than I thought but way more interesting too. The exams are pretty hard but the quizzes are pretty easy. Sandomir is what makes this class. Hes incredibly knowledgeable about everything. And he puts it all in there in ways matching up with marketing you would never imagine. Still better study because hes all business.

This class is way more interesting than I thought it would be and not at all what I expected. Its kind of a mashup of marketing finance accounting and history and economics and things like that. If you came to college to find at least one professor you would remember Sandomir is the guy. His lectures are incredible and really interesting

Professor Sandomir is an excellent teacher for free-thinking students who only expect to get out as much as they put in. Students who feel entitled to only hearing opinions they agree with and receiving handout grades will not bode well with Sandomir. He is a much needed conservative voice in a school where applicable knowledge is mostly gone.

You will hear fabulous lectures that really open your eyes to marketing . Dr Sandomir teaches a lot of strategy and its one of the most interesting parts of the class. Exams are tough, but he provides helpful study questions. There are a lot of business articles to read. Hes an incredibly good professor. Keep up and youll learn the subject.

Flat out the best Professor I've had at the U. The lectures are brilliant and this he is very knowledgeable. The exams are difficult but the grading is fair. You need to really work in this class and if you don't you will probably not like Professor Sandomir very much. But if you do the work and listen attentively you'll love the guy.

Professor Sandomir is phenomenal! I have taken two classes from him, his lectures are well prepared and his teaching ability is outstanding. His tests are graded very fairly and he uses curving methods that heavily favor the students who put in fair study efforts. There is no mindless busywork and the text book you read is not to heavy.

Professor Sandomir has lectures in what he calls "coffee shop talks" where you just discuss concepts in a relaxed way. If you, and your classmates, take advantage of this and ask questions you will learn A LOT. Sandomir can answer just about any question on the subject. Tests are the HARDEST I have ever taken but thats by design and theyre curved.

Did not even try to accommodate to anyone for anything. Lectures and readings didnt align with tests or quizzes. You wont know your actual grade till the end of the semester. Would never take again and shouldve withdrew from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a very good class. Professor sandomir is a great lecturer and the material was very interesting. Be certain to do your packback articles every week. Don't wait till the end of the semester to read them. They're very interesting and worth the time. Use his study guide for the exams. They helped me immensely

Sandomir is an excellent speaker. In every other aspect of being a professor, he's awful. He shoves participation to online autograded sites, grades vaguely, offers no study resources or help aside from "read more", offers no guidelines for the project, and expects every student to dedicate everything to his (required) course. He's a lazy professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Without a doubt the best lecturing professor ever. The lectures are very deep and engaging, but they are also applicable and full of strategic thinking. Exams are tough but fair and he grades on a curve.

Sandomir is knowledgeable, but his 3000 class is a mess. The textbook is great, and his lectures are interesting, but there is a disconnect between the content in the book and the test. He tests you on application, not concepts, and uses the 'best answer' technique. Basically, there is no real way to study. Plus, he doesn't use Canvas grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Superb professor with tons of experience and enthusiasm. Emphasis on strategy. He brings in lots of economics and goes way beyond the text. Tough exams but fair grading. On top of everything. Do the reading and bring good questions to class. Extremely engaging speaker.

Sandomir is the one of the most impressive lecturers at the university of utah. He has tons of real world experience but knows all the academic studies and issues too. Its amazing to hear a guy who speaks in perfect sentences but is super interesting and finds ways to work every subject you can think of in to lectures about markets and economics.

What an amazing professor! There is a fair amount of reading, but I personally loved the readings, they are very interesting to read and discuss with professor Sandomir. Great content provided in a meaningful way.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The problem with this class is the material is old, not relevant to 2020. He rambles for 2 hours straight, very hard to follow. The textbook is essentially useless for his exams, because he writes his own exam questions, they only make sense to him. You can study everything but won't get his questions. Very hard to follow. He is nice, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is a very practical class but filled with amazing strategy and tactic marketing g plays. Dr. Sandomir knows this stuff like a chess This is an excellent class. I took Professor Sandomir's Business 1050 course completely online and I learned a lot from this class! Professor Sandomir is highly knowledgable on all the required readings. Even though the readings can be tedious, if you pay attention in his lectures and take thorough notes on the readings key points, you will get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class. Excellent professor.

He will overwhelm you with his lectures. He crams too much info into lectures, talks too fast , and uses complicated vocabulary. It's very easy to get lost but he expects you to keep up. He does write some notes on the board but it's very messy. Just record him. Textbook is expensive and I could easily look up all the readings in it online.
Not good at making things clear to myself and the entire class. Asked repeatedly and he does not understand what is wrong with the teaching. Learn for yourself deal and attending classes do not help.

What an abysmal teacher!!! lectures have absolutely nothing to do with tests, the textbook is a must buy and is super expensive, you will never use it again, and if you ever ask for help he will actually make fun of you.
Horrid teacher, Gives unclear instructions with no second chances.
Heavy Grader , not very instructive, does not give any chance. also VERY unclear.
not good at teaching. his attendance policy for an online class is unrealistic. Would not recommend him to anyone.
Definitely not a good professor, one of the worst I've had at the university

reviews.comment: If you can take this class from anyone else, do it. Sandomir's lectures are long and confusing, and the readings are hard to understand. His grading technique is super confusing- I even didn't know what my grade was until I checked my transcript. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he tells you when quizzes, test and even the final is in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures don't line up with the textbook so be prepared for the tests to be an absolute mess. Ask for a definition? Be ready to not know if he wants his definition or the textbooks. Withdrawing from this class was the best decision I ever made. Especially since he randomly will curve stuff so sometimes your 50% becomes an A & sometimes not
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enormous amount of work, but if you really want the career, Sandomir is the guy. Super smart and way educated.. The project is nerve-wracking and presenting it to professionals is sooo hard! But it's the only way to learn the material. Grading is based whether plan can go to market immediately or not. Great class. Great professor.

An excellent class but challenging. Sandomir is a fabulous lecturer, the best I have heard at the U, but he is a no nonsense guy. He provides lots of preparation and is good about office hours, but you have to do the work. He doesnt have a lot of patience for losers. But he is so good at what he does, he is worth the work.

Sandomir is one of the best professors at the U. Maybe the best really. Not just blow your mind lectures, but a first rate mind that's totally original. Some challenging exams, but worth the study to hang out with the guy. Incredible jazz musician too, we saw him last weekend at a local spot. Take any class he teaches.

Sandomir has a big rep and it shows. His lectures cover the subject amazingly well but he brings this wealth of huge intellect and broad education to everything. We sit there stunned pretty often. Three exams, all pretty challenging and three quizzes, not toolbar. Totally worth your time.
Professor Sandomir's lectures and personality can come off extremely grating and unnecessarily fast-paced. From his class though, you learn an immense amount if you're willing to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sandomir is very competent and has an unbelievable mind. He covers an enormous amount of material so you have to keep up. He's probably the best lecturer you will ever hear, but you must listen super carefully. He's got a tough, traditional outside, but he's a pretty soft romantic on the inside.

Sandomirs lectures are outrageously brilliant.. Id go anywhere to hear this guy. You will want to research lots of marketing and finance topics after hearing him. Hes serious about education so dont take 1050 from him if youre not serious. Exams and quizzes are fair, but you need to be at all lectures and carefully read a load of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent professor! This class can be truly unique. If you apply yourself alongside Sandomir's guidance and lectures, you will gain a new perspective on business and the world around you. He is very traditional with required readings each class. Test and quiz heavy. If you love to learn, he is your professor to take for Bus 1050!!! Very fair!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent class and superb professor. Sandomir is very good at mixing the analytical and philosophical in financial, economic, and literary areas. Serious and engaging lectures. Learned a ton.

Professor Sandomir is very knowledgable about marketing. He gives lots of examples which helps to understand the concepts. He is opinionated about certain things, so sometimes you have to tune him out. There are 4 quizzes and 3 midterms, 1 of them is a take-home midterm. Show up on time and get extra credit 3 or 4 times throughout the semester.

Sandomir is just the most brilliant lecturing professor I have ever experienced. He is in complete command of the subject and other subjects too. I was inspired every class day. He is also much needed conservative counterpoint in the biz school where most students are liberals. Some resent him for destroying their positions so completely.

I really loved 1050! Sandomir introduced accounting, finance, marketing, and management in amazing lectures that tied classical readings to business concepts. He made balance sheets and income statements understandable. The exams and quizzes are tough, but fair. His book covers 2500 years of readings from Confucious and Sun Tzu and Milton Friedman

The lectures expand way beyond text but in very practical ways. Sandomir literally tells you what to study for three quizzes and he provides helpful study guides for three exams. Only text reading and no outside assignments. If you are lazy, take someone else.

I took Prof Sandomir for Bus 1050 and thought it was great, taking marketing 3010 was a different experience. Required lots reading, the tests were extremely difficult and the study guide he hands out were not very helpful. Classes are werer interesting but then he would ruin it with his political views and get side tracked. Take from someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A solid class. Interesting introduction to the business disciplines. The readings can be difficult, but Sandomir is expert at getting you through them.

Alan Sandomir is a great lecturer, but the class was not great. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but a lot of people weren't coming, so he started taking roll. He expects you to know a lot about the readings, so make sure you pay attention in class and do the readings beforehand. It wasn't the hardest class, but he makes it harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a very good class. Sandomir is very knowledgeable and flexible. He changed the date of a quiz for us because we were not prepared--very nice! There is a lot of complexity, but Sandomir is very helpful outside of class, too. Occasional political and economic issues, but he is open-minded about these things. Great lectures!

Sandomir is one of those professors who thinks he is far smarter than he actually is. He has a firm grasp on his own material, but enjoys lecturing students on his close minded political opinions and degrading students with different ideals. He is disorganized and will change quiz/test schedules the day of. My advice, take a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sandomir is really smart and is expert at making marketing, finance, and accounting understandable. He is the best lecturer Ive ever had. You will have to work to get a good grade, but hes really amazing and youll like the class if you are a serious student.

Dr. Sandomir is the quintessence of the academic challenger I had hoped I could experience in a university setting. I believe that Alan is absolutely committed to both the Socratic method of pedagogy and is an unyielding heterodoxical educator (spelling?). Although his class offerings are outside of my major, Ill take all his classes I can afford
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sandomir is one of the authors of the textbook used in this class, therefore this is his "language." He is a pro at the content of this class, however due to that he is unable to teach it in a way that students who come into this class with no prior knowledge understand the material, he's unable to "dumb it down" meaning make it easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most serious teacher I have ever had. If you are passionate about the foundations of business, this is the teacher for you. If you aren't, I would not recommend. Grade for whole class based off 4 quizzes/tests. He is not afraid to call out students in class that he thinks did not read the textbook, and seems to find a slight joy in it.

Professor Sandomir is by far the bets professor I have had during my college experience. He is one of the few professors at the U that I genuinely look forward to hearing his lectures. He also is rare in the sense of that he has a very capitalistic mindset which is a beautiful thing in a world where that is lacking, however he respects all opinoins

This class will open your mind to marketing, finance, and accounting, and help you to know the meaning of capitalism and socialism too. Professor Sandomir is an exciting and super amazing lecturer, fair and helpful outside of class. You wont be bored!

He is a very recognized professor in the business school. However, he is very closed minded and the class centers around his capitalist and conservative ideals. If you disagree, he doesn't welcome your ideas. It felt as though the students in the class were trying so hard to please him and his ideas instead of developing their own.

He knows what he is talking about, and can explain material wonderfully. He is very understanding. My group did a project without me and he gave me a 1 month extension to do it on my own. If you are: honest with him, go to his class, take good notes, ask questions you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The lectures consisted of the professor attempt at "Socratic teaching" but came off as self aggrandizing at best. This class blends philosophy, religious arguments, pro-capitalism and Americana in a way that boggles the mind. No exam/quiz dates were posted on syllabus as a way to encourage 'class attendance'. He uses vocab to intimidate freshman.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is challenging but Dr Sandomir is a brilliant and inspiring lecturer. Be serious and youll do well. He gives you all the tools. His reputation as the best lecturer at the university is totally deserved and he will help you if you ask for it. He spent an a lot of time with me explaining fed banking policy. Take the class seriously.

I don't mind work but way too much work than necessary. Tests felt like a 3000+ level class. Lectures are too fast paced and over detailed that you should just record the lectures than take notes. Very easy to miss lots of important stuff he says in his lectures. This class counts as a GenEd but don't take it if it's just for GenEd.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are mandatory for this class. The material is very complex and hard to understand at times. Lectures move very quickly if you blink you might miss something. reviews.comment: Definitely read the assignments and make notes. Take good notes and reference your notes to your readings. He's great
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Alan is a great guy. He knows his stuff and has a lot of experience in the field. Lectures are long but he keeps things interesting. Tests are long with a lot of reading. The book isn't necessary if you study the heck outta the power points and take good notes. I would take the honors version or a diff prof if you can cuz the group project STINKS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Sandomir is not like any biz professor you will ever have. He is knowledgeable beyond all others and is the not quite human who speaks in perfect sentences só big with inspiring ideas that marketing and finance sound like physics and astronomy. So amazing! He will change you for the better but dont fall behind.. that will kill your grade.

Such an amazing professor, he provided a clear understanding of the materials during his lectures. If you do not go to lecture you will fail miserably. Take copious amounts of notes and do your readings before class and you will be fine. The readings usually take about an hour to read through and understand. Will take another class from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Sandomir is an excellent lecturer, the most engaging I have had. I really like his style of teaching. Read the text and attend lectures and youll do well.
Fantastic lecturer! Professor Sandomir is by far the most engaging professor Ive ever had! I couldnt reccomend taking his class more!

Dr Sandomir is the professor I will remember 20 years from now. He converted me into becoming a business intellectual dedicated to marketing and finance. I recorded all but his first two lectures and they blow away everyone who hears them. Take the class seriously and ut will make you a better person and much much smarter.

One of my favorites. Great lecturer, interesting, passionate, easy to work with, and well educated. Take good notes in class and on readings! Tests/quizzes are multiple choice, T/F, essay, but you'll need to understand the concepts well in order to get a good grade on them. I had 2 quizzes and 2 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Favorite professor of all time. Incredibly knowledgeable, and it shows in his lectures. His orating skills are incredible and keep the class engaged the whole time. Probably the most respected professor at the U.

reviews.comment: For internationals , it is hard
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really knowledgeable professor. The type of teacher you want if you are really interested in the subject matter. Was not an easy A but easy enough to pass. I took his morning class and was easily able to stay awake because he was very engaging.

Pretty much your entire grade depends on three exams and an audit project. I thought the tests were really hard but Alan curves a lot. Many of the test questions came from his lectures so if you wanna do well on the tests you better go to class.

Sandomir is a very intelligent individual, but his teaching really depends on the individual. He unnecessarily uses difficult vocabulary which makes lectures difficult to comprehend, and while his lectures were decent he is very dismissive to students with views other than his.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wow. This class had perhaps some of the most inspirational, polarizing and mind-stretching lectures ever given. The ideas in this class will challenge you, change you and make you want to be better. All given by a superb professor that is both intense and eloquent. Grades are attendance based, no tests. Verrry recommended!

Dr Sandomir is strategy intensive and requires a very complete understanding of tactical responses to everything! Lectures are super intense but he's the best lecturer I've ever heard so it's all pretty incredible. There is one huge project. I love this guy because he's brilliant but knows how to bring us into his world. He's a great role model.

Sandomir is the best professor of my four years. His lectures are off the wall brilliant and very energetic.  He has an amazing way of piecing together technical material with everything from philosophy to psychology.  I am simply blown away by the intellect and it inspires me.  Beware. There is a project, but it very applicable.  Take this class!

Professor Sandomir is brilliant! His lectures aren't always the most engaging, and he can end up going on unrelated tangents sometimes, but Professor Sandomir will get you to think critically about business, and provide interesting perspectives! I would recommend taking any class that you can from Sandomir, even if you aren't a business major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you don't attend class you won't pass. Most of what is on the tests comes from lecture. Textbook is used but the tests are filled with logic/decision making questions that you would only be comfortable with if you come to class. Also offers marketing audit for credit. His lectures are amazing and really make you think. I really liked the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Does not give homework, only assigns chapters to read. Show up to lectures as he tests heavily on lecture slides and videos. Does not offer extra credit. Mandatory group audit project. Curves exam grades. Show up to class, study the lectures, take notes, complete the audit and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took 1050 from Sandomir last year.  Fact--he is the most brilliant and engaging lecturer you will find.  If you are a serious student you will never view finance, marketing, and accounting the same way again.  Ask students who are mature who spins their heads around!  It is Sandomir.  He won't be your friend, but he'll change you for the better.

Alan Sandomir is a quality professor. His class is heavily lecture based. His lectures are occasionally dull, but often thought-provoking in that they expanded my vocabulary and made me think about the world in different ways. That being said, he often gets overly political and is very impersonal (he didn't know my name after an entire semester).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sandomir is an incredibly bright professor. However, he is all over the place. The audit project is worth almost 25% of your grade, and he only spoke about it ONCE for 3 minutes. His tests cover material he doesn't cover in class AND is also not in the book. His tests are tricky, but he curves hard. Super nice guy, the class was just annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Sandomir puts a lot of heart into what he teaches, and expects his students to care a lot as well. Don't skip class, don't leave early (gives pop quizzes at end of lecture occasionally,) complete all assigned readings at least once, participate in class discussions, and this will be one of the most enjoyable and rewarding classes you'll take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's the end of the semester and still don't know my grade - he does not put in grades. Class is graded by 2 quizzes and 2 exams - both extremely difficult. Tests are around 100 questions. His lectures are horrible, I hardly know what he's talking about. Not a good teacher for an entry level class. Would not take him ever again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took BUS 2000 at the same time I took MKTG 3000.  This class really illuminated the other.  Professor Sandomir's lectures are famous across campus.  Power Basics is probably the must famous lecture series at the U.  I will only say this: utterly amazing!  Take this class from Sandomir.  It's the one class you'll never forget!

Professor Sandomir was by far my favorite professor in my four years. His lectures were brilliant and motivating.  He spent an hour with me explaining marginal analysis and break even and helped me through the final.  I never really thought of marketing and finance as intellectual subjects for "combat" as he said.  I loved his teaching style.

Professors Sandomir is obviously an expert in his field, but I often felt that his teaching style (long, emphatic lecture) did not enhance my mastery of the subject matter. Because I had so few opportunities to participate or discuss the topics covered, I often got distracted. My learning would've been enhanced by more interaction.

You have three tests and one marketing audit to do. He gives you almost all semester to work on the audit so don't wait until last minute! He brings real world examples into the mix and is so passionate about what he does. He made me consider marketing as a major

This class was hard to follow at times.  The focus was on business philosophy, I think.  The lectures were mostly rehash of the reading without adding very much depth, but the lectures are essential to being successful in the class. He occasionally offers extra credit for those who are on-time to class and can answer a few questions on the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Sandomir was very enjoyable. The lectures were very well done, and I always left super inspired. The reading load is tough, basically read the whole text book , which was written by him. Does express political views, and if you don't agree, I could see why it would irritate someone.  2 Exams, 2 quizzes, and some pop quizzes, graded on a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Sandomir is a great professor!  He is extremely passionate in his lectures and I would definitely take a class from him again.  That being said, if you struggle getting up and going to class then BUS2000 is not for you.  You are graded completely on attendance.  There's also some public speaking involved.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dude is cool

Seriously the most inspirational guy ive ever met. If you have the chance do take his class do it quick before he retires. the class was mostly lecture with a few discussion but he is not boring to listen to. makes you wanna do business for the greater good of people. so intelligent. only graded on 2 group papers, midterm, and a final.

I have had the privilege of having Sandomir in two different classes, now. His teaching style is fast-paced, but very in-depth, so you end up learning A TON. He implements history, literature, and philosophy into all of his lectures and captivates his students. His classes are tough, but very rewarding in knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Sandomir's lectures are brilliant.  I felt inspired after each lecture and it helped me to do pretty well.  He is great at bringing marketing and finance together with politics and economics.  Still, a word of warning.  He has no patience for student laziness.  I discovered that my first two weeks!

I hated this class. Sandomir knows that he is a genius and isn't afraid to make sure that everyone knows it. He goes out of his way to use the biggest, most complicated vocabulary possible not only in his lectures but also in his tests and quizzes. The lectures are quite honestly a huge bore and I really didn't even learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Sandomir is intelligent and cares about the subject.  Unfortunately, his lectures were all over the place.  He also got very political in many of his lectures, despite promising that he wouldn't which frequently frustrated me.  There are two very difficult tests and two long group papers.  Fortunately, he graded the tests on a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I loved his teaching so much, I plan to take a course of his in the future. There is a lot of reading, but I found it both interesting and applicable (to more than just business). And, although there are mostly lectures, I found them extremely intriguing and inspirational. His teaching always made it worthwhile to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Sandomir is an amazing teacher and it's great to listen to him lecture.

As an fall semester freshman, taking this class has been a very good transition from high school level reading to understanding how much it takes in college. Although there is a lot of reading, i highly recommend because of his interesting lectures.
3010 was one of the most valuable classes I took last year.  Lots of strategy and detal but well worth it.  Sandomirs lectures are gems.

Want to learn what plato or socrates thought of marketing? Look no further. Personally i thought his lectures were far too removed from marketing and it felt more like a philosophy course. I got about 60% on each test (3 of them) and got a B+.  I would take it from another professor who may focus on up-to-date marketing principles and concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor, very engaging and, even though it is very lecture-heavy, he is very interesting to listen to. BUS1050 requires an $80 book that he helped co-write, which you read multiple readings from every day. It's also mostly a philosophically-driven class, especially for Business. Highly recommend Sandomir in general, very interesting

It's imperative that you show up for the lectures, at the beginning of the year he stresses reading the book but if you go to the lectures you won't need to. Lectures are generally good, but he can be overly pedantic at times.  Not that difficult, his grading is really strange but he does grade at a curve. Study for the test and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sandomir is easily one of the best professors at the U. His lectures are extremely interesting and reflect what will be on the tests. Read the assigned chapters before class, it enhances his lectures tremendously. My only complaint is I wish he had a clearer grading criteria at the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I wasn't a fan of this class at first. The first half is mostly history/philosophy readings that relate to business. I'm not a fan of history or philosophy so it was tough for me to get through them. Grades are based on only a few quizzes, midterm and exam. They are very tough so study hard and know the details of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Brilliant professor with tons of real world marketing experience. His tests are really tough and if you aren't there for the lectures you probably won't do well. You'll have to work for it, but an A is very attainable if you put in a couple extra hours of study for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected by students--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Without a doubt, the best professor I had in any department.  I learned more in his 3010 than in any other business class I took.  And nobody gives more interesting lectures than Dr. Sandomir.  Even though I graduated this month, I will probably return to sit in on his Power Basics class.

this classmy most neglected and still got out with a passinggrade.  Format 3 tests 1 being the final & non cumulative. Tests formatted to where you need to know examples of definitions.  example: he'll give you a question and you need to identify what type of marketing this is.  smart informative professor. read & evaluate the chapters.

One of the most thought-provoking classes I have taken in my college career. He talks extremely fast, so I recommend recording every lecture. The tests are difficult but if you study hard and attend each class you will be fine. This class changed my life. Highly recommend! Will take as many classes from Sandomir as I can.

Sandomir, is truly a remarkable speaker, very wide ranged, intuitive, and pragmatic lectures that you can apply to your daily lives if you choose to. Lectures are great, if you have a great night sleep. Reading is easy, if you enjoy them. Tests are hard, if you didn't study.

I took BUS1051 from Prof. Sandomir, and was not a fan because of the reading load. I took this class from him due to lack of alternatives, and I am glad I did. His lectures were super interesting; I had no problem paying attention even though class was at 7:30am. Less reading, and more conceptual information that you can follow easily. Loved it.

Very hard class. Professor Sandomir is very well educated and teaches to prove how educated he is. Very nice man that will help you in any way possible. Lots of reading. Tests are very difficult. Whole grade based off of 2 quizes, a midterm and a exam. But does use a curve.

He is a great and entertaining lecturer.  He gives comprehensive study guides for his quizes and exams.  Two quizes.  Two exams.  If you do the readings and attend class you should have no problem doing well.

Alan Sandomir is the kind of teacher that you read about at great universities in ages past. I'm a graduating senior & looking back on my college experience, Alan Sandomir stands as the most intelligent, articulate, & thought-provoking professor I've had the pleasure to learn from. Challenging class, but among the most valuable you'll ever take.

His class is him lecturing the whole time.  You are assigned reading for each class and you are required to do some participation in class.  However, I found that doing the readings was not very necessary.  He explains how he wants you to interpret the text in class.  Just understand his study guides and you will do great on the tests.

He is a great lecturer. Use the study guided he provides and  you should be okay for the tests. It is best to do all the readings before class so the topics he covers in lecture will make more sense. Entertaining.

I would not suggest taking this class at 7:30 am. He is a great professor, knows what he is talking about. He is very specific in what he looks for in essays. DO THE READINGS and participate if you actually want to pass and learn something from the class. Don't be afraid to speak up in class, participation is part of your grade.

Sandomir is a great professor. He is probably the most well-read and intelligent man I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. Readings are mandatory (don't skip them!) and come to class  (EVERYDAY) prepared to listen & participate if you can. Tests are hard but if you really pay attention in class and get help when you need it, you will do fine!

He is a good professor with awesome lectures. It is very hard to keep up with his reading assignments though and his tests are very hard, however, he does curve them. Just don't skip class. And if you're not a morning person don't take the 7:30 class, even if its the only one open.

Probably the most interesting and sophisticated lectures I have ever heard. He has a way of linking everything from Freud and Nietzsche to balance sheets and market development strategies...a wild ride but that's what I was hoping for.  He gives shape to some pretty unwieldy subjects, but I can't say enough about the incredible quality of lectures.

This man is the coolest. He seriously is the most intelligent person. He plays this act like his class is going to be the hardest thing ever, but if you do the readings and try and learn a little background in economics you should be great. He co-wrote the textbook, so he knows his stuff.

A really good professor. He knows what he's talking about and sometimes I felt inspired, even though we were just talking about business. If you don't take the class seriously, it's hard, but if you're interested in business (and also philosophy) you'll love it.

Amazing professor, he is very intresting and teaches alot and talking class with him is a brain opener and makes you think in new ways and very differently and when your done with his class  you notice that you are much wiser and ready for whats coming your way !
Its a lot to take in during one semester, but Sandomir does a great job at keeping your attention and making it interesting.

He is a really amazing lecturer. He made a boring topic super exciting. Make sure that you go to class since that is where he tells you what to read, and when the quizzes and tests are. The only problem I had was that he was trying to push his vegetarianism onto the class. He would bring it up whenever he could. Other than that though he is amazing

Alan was great at making a not so entertaining subject somewhat entertaining. I personally enjoyed the lectures. The literature is difficult, if you don't read the chapters before class, you will be lost. He likes people who participate, be prepared to be called on if you sit in the front.  I cannot stress enough, READ THE BOOK.

Professor Sandomir is hard-core to say the least. His lectures are fantastic. You will never get bored if you are actually interested in business. I found the material very difficult. There is a lot of reading and his tests are super hard. However, he grades the 2 quizzes and 2 tests on a curve so you really only have to be better than your peers.

Amazing teacher, the best the U of U has to offer in terms of teaching and helping you intellectually grow. I would highly recommend this teacher as he pushes you to your limit but at the end you are satisfied with your self. NO STUDY, NO PASS LOOKING FOR AN EASY A THIS IS NOT THE CLASS.

Sandomir gives excellent lectures and really knows the material since he helped create the textbook. He doesn't grade attendance, but does notice who attends lectures and who doesn't. He doesn't give a syllabus so attendance is essential for knowing when quizzes and tests are given. Many test questions are also based on material covered in class.

Sandomir uses his own textbook which is just excerpts of philosophers. Class attendance (though not mandatory) is essential to passing. Get ready to take notes and a voice recorder. He can get confusing. He's pretty pompous, arrogant, and not very helpfulbut he knows the material and teaches it well. Exams are hard but curve is pretty generous.

Sandomir is a passionate, captivating, and intelligent lecturer.  He LOVES teaching this class, which makes it enjoyable.  No turn-in homework, just loads of reading from the book.  If you don't read, you're toast.  Tests are tricky, with answers feeling like they could go either way.  The class is basically reading comprehension and memorization.

One of the best professors at the University. Attend the lectures and keep detailed notes and you will do well on his tests. They are tough but he gives a generous curve. Makes sure to keep up with the assigned readings! Fantastic class overall.

Expect to spend every single day of the week working on your presentation towards the end of the semester. Sandomir changes ideas all the time. Know how to use photoshop and get ready to present to a bunch of judges. Lots of meetings outside of class about once a week.  *Sandomir is an amazing lecturer and a great person. Very hard class though

Sandomir knows his stuff. Can tell he has real world experience. he is difficult to follow. You need to pay attention to every word he says because he talks fast and uses a wide vocabulary. Test question can be confusing.

This class is a cross between philosophy and business ethics.  Mind blowing lectures and mind opening storiesexamples.  Sandomir is a brilliant dude but doesn't quite understand straightforward test questions.  His tests leave something to be desired but you are probably required to take the class.  Do the readings and try to know the material.
No assignments, only tests and quizzes No fixed schedule, attendance not mandatory but essential Textbooks essential

I have had Sandomir for other classes, mostly because I love his lectures.  Exams can be challenging but hey, this is college!  He is incredibly thorough in explaining complex issues. If there were any classes left that I could take from him I would.

Great teacher, long lectures and hard hard test. You have to keep on reading and be prepared to study hard for exams. Prof only weakness is the exams because he doesn't lecture the same way he gives exams. Best part is you only have exams and no papers! Don't let that fool you, record his lectures, sit up front, participate, ask questions and study

Sandomir is all about strategytáctics which he teaches like chess moves. He knows this stuff inside out.  His lectures will blow you away.  He is just as off the wall mind bending in Foundations.  If you really want to know the subject, Sandomir is your guy.  Really amazing!

I don't understand why this is a 1050 class, feels more like a 3000+ class. Also, it felt more like a philosophy class rather than a foundation class. We briefly covered the different branches of business and focused mainly on difficult readings from philosophers. Also, 30 minutes is not near enough time to take a quiz that has 50+ questions.

Professor Sandomir expects a lot, but he gives you a thousand times more. I have never heard lectures that motivated me like his.  He lectures to the top of the class.... If you are not interested in excellence, then you should find a different professor.

Sandomir may be the best lecturer in the entire state. You'll never be bored in his class. He's thought-provoking, and although he doesn't intend to offend anyone, he's not afraid to teach what he knows. Even though this class is easy (just attendance), it's worth so much more than an easy A. I would take it again and again.

Bus Foundations wasn't a class I thought it would be. It's more about philosophy and what people think about business. I'd recommend recording lectures and taking very detailed and thorough notes. Make sure you know the material inside and out for the tests. Don't do the readings - he talks about them in detail during lectures, but know the basics

Power Basics is the most intellectual business class ever.  Professor Sandomir is beyond brilliant.  We feel like we're taking a class at Oxford or some school like that.  Sandomir ties marketing and finance to big, crazy ideas about power in business and can pull facts and numbers and quotes from every thinker.  But don't miss more than 4 classes!
Incredible class. Teacher is full of charisma and seeks to inspire students. Take lots of notes on lectures as readings are not necessary. Scored highest on final and never opened book.

Alan Sandomir is the best professor I've ever had in my life. If you are in school to just pass by and get easy A's, don't bother coming to his class. If you are in school to learn to be the best you can be and be inspired by an insightful and brilliant man, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS FRON ANYONE ELSE BUT HIM. Take notes of the lectures!!!

I think I have taken every one of Professor Sandomir's classes.  His lectures are remarkable in so many ways--he can begin with some strategic issue, move to Tomas Aquinas and Thorsten Veblen, then some 20th century composer, and on to something about new product policy.  Amazing.  The exams stretch you, but he grades fairly.  Totally worth it.

He writes his tests on mostly his lectures, which are tend to long, confusing, and ambiguous.  He expects you to understand his point of view and that you will love all the readings just as much as he does.  You are usually assigned 30 pages every class, but more importantly is taking notes on "his" perspective of readings.

Smartest man that offers pre-business classes.  I left nearly every lecture thinking about business in a completely different way.  Class is rich and exams are very challenging. Pay attention, do your readings, and go to all the reviews and you'll come out with a decent grade.  He curves generously.

Pay attention in class. My biggest advice is to record his lectures and listen to them again before tests. I never touched the book and walked out with an A with this method. Very interesting man to talk to after class as well.
study all powerpoint slides and don't miss lectures.  a lot of strategy work but totally fascinating lectures and a way of seeing the subject intellectually.
This man is a genius.  Take every class you can from him.
GOOD CLASS, just for more Units

Incredible class. Enticing lectures and makes you think differently about life. 2 quizzes and 2 tests grading wise, and they are tough. GO TO CLASS, DO THE READINGS. My section made a global google doc for studying for each test and quiz, and it helped tremendously. Sandomir is hands down the best professor I've ever had.

Make sure you (1) attend the reviews, (2) complete the study guide, and (3) do the readings. This class is a lot of work. Lectures are intense. Two quizzes and two exams make up final grade. Hardest multiple choice test I've seen so far! But Sandomir is a brilliant guy, expert at the subject, generally helpful. WILL offend some of his students.

Sandomir is amazing. His lectures are not boring; attendance is mandatory; tests/quizzes are super difficult unless you study your brains out. I thought he would be very hard, but it is the material that can be confusing. Attend reviews and take A LOT of notes.

I think I have taken every class taught by Professor Sandomir.  He is an incredible lecturer--you will never be bored.  His exams are pretty tough, but they really to test you on the material he teaches.  His curves are fair. You would really be missing something special if you didn't hear at least one of his lectures.
Unclear in lectures and confusing. tests are terribly hard

Professor Sandomir is BRILLIANT. Took this my first semester at the U, and loved him. He can get off on tangents and talks fast and can be difficult to understand at times, but his lectures were phenomenal. His tests are pretty difficult, but his curve is very fair. As long as you go to class and do the readings, you shouldn't struggle.
Good class, kind of hard but  he curves well

I have taken most of Professor Sandomir's classes and they are all excellent.  As everyone here says, his lectures are really amazing--brilliant but kind of inspiring, too. I think I did better in 4020 because he mad us learn straategy. There is so much of it but listen carefully and study the slides!  I finally go it and it has helped so much.

I got the chance to take 1050 and 2000 with prof. What really needs to be said? 2000 should be mandatory. Lectures are absolutely incredible, and the topic should be on everyones mind moving forward into the business school. One heck of a guy and an absolutely excellent purveyor of knowledge. Take every class you can, but be prepared to work hard.
In my four years at the U, I have never heard a more spectacular lecturer.  Every time I attended this class, I left changed in a serious way.  I cannot say enough for this professor's skills.
Very well organized. Slides on Canvas. Gives good lectures and test reviews. You DO have to read the book.

Sandomir is very passionate about what he's teaching. If you really want to learn business then take this guy! You're getting what you pay for and that's a good education. Basically all you have to do is show up, take good notes, do the readings go to the reviews and you should get an A. Coming to class is not mandatory but he throws in pop quizzes

This was the third class I took with Sandomir. A lot more hands on and we worked with a real client with a real budget--almost $300,000. Fabulous class. Fabulous professor--knows the subject from every angle.

I have had Professor Sandomir for two other classes.  His lectures are so incredibly good--exactly what you would expect from a professor at a top notch school.  He justifies my choice of the U.  Just a fabulous profesoor

Great great great class. Incredibly enticing lectures with broad and interesting subject matter. You can tell prof absolutely loves teaching which is what makes the class so great. As for it being hard, if you actually do the readings (they aren't that long) the class is a breeze. I gave it a 4 on easiness simply because in a 5 I doubt you'd read.

Fabulous class.  Professor Sandomir is, I think, one the foremost authorities on the subject of power and commerce. His lectures are off the map stupendous. I will sit in on this class again and again.

Professor Sandomir is great, his test and quizzes are extremely difficult but study hard, go to every class, read every story, and you'll pass. Not you're typical level 1 class, more like 3 or 4. I would take that class toward the end of completing my pre-business classes.
Professor Sandomir is an excellent professor.  His  lectures are really fine and you always know he is pakcing in a lot of information with terrific insights.

Brilliant professor and very passionate about the topic! Class is tough to keep up with and the tests are really difficult but it is the best class I have had at college! His TA with the hat is super helpful for preparing for the exams and really hot!

I highly recommend professor Sandomir. He is an extremely intelligent professor who gives very interesting and worthwhile lectures. He is easy to talk to and willing to help when you do not understand the material. Take a class from this professor! You won't regret it.

Tests were really hard and almost impossible to study for, as they were mostly strategy based.  He lectures non-stop every single class period.  I HIGHLY recommend recording his lectures - there is too much information discussed not to.  Definitely not a typical 3000 level course.
Make sure you come to class and take intense notes and you will be set!
tough class, attend class and read the chapters. awesome teacher my favorite so far
Very tough class. Study hard... You have to more efforts in this course to even get B plus or A minus. He uses big words, but very knowledgable and informative!!Enjoy the class.
Awesome prof. Very knowledgeable . Tests are hard, but not impossible. I would recommend recording his lectures.
One of my favorites. Very passionate about what he teaches, and a very interesting way to approach business. Class was not biased (politically, religiously.. etc), which I loved.

I have sat in on Professor Sandomir's Foundations class several times.  It's hard to tell he had heart problems because his lectures are still so brilliant. Still, I am glad he is regaining his health because to lose him would be like losing a national treasure.  You will really likes his classes.  Even more, you will really like him.

The Class is interesting it is almost 100% based on readings his interpretations of them. Don't expect to learn anything useful about business in this class but review the study guides and go to the TA's review sessions and its pretty easy. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives tips and assignments in class only nothing in syllabus
Awesome teacher! He makes the class time fly by! Such an interesting guy

One of the University's sexiest professor's on campus! Not only is he dedicated to his classes, he is also deeply invested in the students growth. He challenges you to look beyond the text and has great experiences to back up his claims. His is a most know professor if you want to excel in the field of business.

Professor Sandomir is a great professor. He really gets into his lectures and captures your attention.
