Professor Bullough is a very nice person, she was really easy going and it helped me a lot with Stats homework because she will go through some of the questions during class. She also explains Stats in a very simple way which is nice as well.
Classes dragged on a lot but over she was great and pretty easy work load.
Great professor, and she makes everything easy to understand. I enjoyed the flipped classroom learning style where we focused on doing homework in class.

Aubrey Bullough is an incredible professor! I was nervous about this course because I had heard it was really difficult, but Professor Bullough made it easy. She explained all of the concepts really well and made sure we were prepared for all of the Exams and quizzes. I highly recommend this professor!!!

Professor Bullough was an exceptional professor. Her classroom is taught reversely, where you are supposed to go over the content in your own time and work on homework and hands-on assignments in class. This can be challenging but as long as you pay attention in class and seek to understand information you may find confusing, it won't be an issue.

She was an average professor that knew the topics that she needed to teach. Tests were kind of hard but not too bad. I would take a class from her again, because it was kind of easy, not because of how she taught. Material seemed easy when she taught it, but the homeworks were a little more complex.

Very patient with questions. Responsive to emails. If you attend class and do the homework, I can't understand how you wouldn't get a B+ or better. It's especially important to go to the test review, where she pretty much just does different versions of the test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bullough is a nice lady, but not the greatest professor. She had a hard time getting the attention of the class and would talk in circles and go on tangents instead of actually teaching what we need to know.

Bullough is a very nice person, but her lectures were boring. She was not very assertive with the students, and there was SO MUCH TALKING. She could not get their attention or for anyone to engage in class. Sometimes it was hard to hear her from the talking going on, even sitting towards the front.

Very nice professor, however, she struggles to keep the attention of the class. Everyone talks over her during lectures and it makes it difficult to pay attention. She spends most of the class going over homework I have already finished. The quizzes and homework are not too difficult, especially if you do them with friends. Basically a stats class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fall 2022 / Good Module

Bullough was so great! Any time I needed help, she was eager and willing to offer any assistance I needed. Her lectures weren't boring, and she went slow, taking time to answer questions. She did a fantastic job at providing resources for us to practice and get ready for the 3 tests throughout the year. I loved her!
She took forever to grade assignments so you never knew what needed to be worked on or not

Great teacher. Course work is very manageable. I would recommend either going to class (more preferred) or watching her videos. You will need to do one of the two to understand the excel questions. If you don't do one of the two, you will not to well in the class. Word problems on the tests/quizzes are a little confusing.

She cared about her students and was willing to go back and answer any questions in class. The material can be hard for some but if you go to the lectures and follow along she goes through how to do everything step by step. The quizzes and exams are all online and can be taken with friends; you will usually get the same questions just diff numbers

Aubrey was such a good professor! the material is not fun or very interesting but she walks you through it step by step and is easily approachable. as long as you show up to class or just go to office hours when needed you will easily get an A. Not very test heavy just do HW assignmets.

She's a really good professor. I personally don't really understand some of the concepts so going to her office hours helps a lot. For the most part it's a straightforward class. Only complaint is that there are a lot of slides and it can be hard to stay awake.

The material can be tough, but if you study enough, you'll be just fine. I got an A+ without ever going to class, so that gives you an idea. You'll rarely be stressed out by the amount of work you have to do in the class because there aren't that many assignments given per week. She's pretty nice and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Aubrey was an excellent introductory statistics teacher. It is obvious that she wants everything she teaches to be clear and understandable. She always made herself available for after-class help, and her lectures were given at a good pace. Took good notes and walked away with a fairly easy A.

Professor Bullough was the best professor i've ever in any sort of math/statistics class. She is sooo good. You can tell that she enjoys teaching and wants her students to succeed. Every lesson is super carefully thought out and explained in the most clear, understandable way possible. I'd recommend her to anyone. She makes statistics enjoyable.

The class is needed for a business degree. I would recommend not doing it online. She is a nice person and willing to meet but she will first expect you to use your resources before explaining material. The videos are super long and I wouldn't recommend the course, at least not online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were hard and the worse, the lecture were all over the place. She will teach you several ways and just make things confusing. Then in webinars will show her way (the easiest imo).

This was the best online class I have ever taken. I don't know what everyone below is complaining about. If you set aside time to watch her lectures carefully and do all the homework including the review, you'll get an A. Be proactive about creating a group with 5 people for the project as well. Awesome class, awesome professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The material itself for the class is tough, but Aubrey does a great job of explaining everything. If I had to retake this class I would take it from her. I recommend taking the class online, it's honestly not that hard as long as you stay on top of it. Amazing teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The online class is very easy, just make sure to set aside time to watch her lecture videos. Some are long and some are very fast. She really helps you understand the material in the lecture videos. The homework can be a little challenging but if you have the book for practice problems then the homework and tests are a piece of cake.

This class is rough,. You have one chance at each question on the assignments, the tests are extremely hard, and the group project doesn't really have clear grading criteria. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone.

She wasn't that great of a professor. Her lectures were all over the place, and her lecture just seemed to drag on. The homeworks were bothersoe because you only had one shot to do each question, where every other math class I've had the professors let you do it as many times as needed until you understood it.
Awful teacher, the only way I learned in this class is by doing the work by myself online. Doesn't know how to teach and will put you to sleep in the lectures.

Horrible professor. Doesn't apply a curve and she can't teach at all. And with teaching something like statistics, you better know how to teach and simplify it. Overall, just a bad professor, really quiet, so it's hard to hear her. I would recommend taking this from someone else as this grade is huge on getting into the Business School.
Useless. Probably the worst "Professor" I've ever had. Terrible at teaching. Just makes you do group work with other students who don't know anything as if you're going to learn anything that way.

Great professor, tried harder to help the class than any I've had thus far. Holds "webinars" every week that are underutilized and a great way to ask questions and get help. Statistics is an awful, boring subject in itself but Bullough tries her best to make it interesting. I did not take the online class, but I would consider it from this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A real gem!  Explains the material very clearly and points out what is most important to study for the exams. She does Everything in her power to help you.  Unfortunately I only had her for half the semester because she had to take over for my professor Jin Ming because everyone was failing. I would take again in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you need to take statistics, I totally recommend Aubrey! She breaks down everything and has a lot of access to extra practice if needed. You do need to go to class but overall great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Aubrey is a really, REALLY good teacher. She genuinely cares about her students and goes above and beyond with additional study sessions, video lectures, tutoring times and in class examples to make sure you know the content. The content is TOUGH, but Aubrey does a great job making a not so easy class much more understandable.

Aubrey taught my class in another professor's absence.  She did an incredible job and taught way better than Tariq Mugal.  She patiently and accurately answers any questions and gives you all the tools you need to pass the class.  This class only had 1 HW due every week and a midterm and a Final.  You should definitely take Statistics from her.

Aubrey was a great professor.  Very clear teacher and made the material simple.  She doesn't have that loud of a voice so if you didn't sit at the front of the class it was hard to hear.  Overall great professor though!

She reads off her slides all of class. Learned more from the lectures online from another teacher, then I do when I go to the actual class. Her review for the midterm doesn't help with the actual test.  She hasn't updated her syllabus even though the chapters changed on the midterm.
Tough class. She give pretty good lectures, nothing too special. Sometimes things weren't clear but she made up for it in one on one conferences.

An alright professor, can't contain rowdy students in class. Felt like a high school atmosphere. What she has on the review is not on the exam. So good luck to all. Does not apply a curve, even though at the beginning of the semester she said there would be a curve. Wonderful. Study everything on the chapters, not just her review.

Always willing to help out students. Her lectures aren't the best, but she is great during one on one sessions. If you don't understand the material make sure you go to TA hours and just get with Aubrey before the test to review and you will do just fine.
Very good professor. She makes the material easy to understand. I would definitely suggest you take OIS 2340 from her.

Aubrey isn't always the clearest in the classroom, but she makes up for it when you talk to her one-on-one. She's always willing to be over backward for you, and gives feedback on the Excel assignments and lets you resubmit them. She's incredibly sweet .
Her homeworks takes time to complete, and the exams are somewhat hard. She gives couple of random extra credits during class which you will get by being there.
Talented teacher, really makes sure you understand the principles, and does a great job conveying information.
She is young and kind of timid but she is really fair and a great teacher. The head of the department came and taught one class after that I was so glad I took her and not him.

Aubrey was super awesome! When I took her class, it was only her second semester teaching and she's already really good. She didn't have much say over our grades because the department head controlled them, but she was super helpful and made this class a lot of fun with constant examples of the material.
Lenient and understanding professor. Lecture videos were helpful and never a waste of time.
Aubrey's 1010 class had three major papers so the load wasn't that bad. Gave extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.
She really wants her students to pass. If you tell her you need extra time on something she will give you extra time. Very understanding

She was an awesome teacher and was respectful of her students! It was a chill environment, but get ready to present!!! I don't like speaking in front of class but she makes you do it, but its good experience though! We only did like 3 major papers, and they were challenging, but not as bad as others I have done.

Aubrey is a very relaxed professor and it's pretty easy to do well in her class. There will be pop quizzes, but that's the only way attendance is taken. They're not hard and basically just a review of the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really wants her students to pass and puts in a lot of effort to have students pass her classes

Christy is truly is knowledgeable about everything she teaches, passionate about the subjects in this class and she did an amazing job teaching it. She is kind, understanding and a fair professor. You know exactly what to expect in the class and as far as grading, it was all very clear.

She is one of my favorite professors at the University of Utah. She goes above and beyond to make sure students understand the material and are prepared for big assignments and exams. The lectures are short but they're filled with so much information and everything is explained so well. I wish she taught more classes in the education department.

Christy is such an amazing professor, and you can tell the passion and care she has for students! She really wants you to succeed in her class, and will do everything in her power to help you. Her lectures are extremely beneficial and you'll leave class with a plethora of new knowledge you can apply in real life
Christy is very knowledgeable and is passionate about her field. Her class is easy so long as you do the readings and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you are not willing to teach yourself. It is very hard to understand her accent and  she teaches in a little bit of a strange way that i never understood. I eventually stopped going to the lectures and started teaching myself the math with the homework.
Hard to understand, thick accent, illegible handwriting; I had to teach myself most of the material.

We're only given a cursory overview of the material, and I often have to find videos elsewhere to explain better. This is remedial math, we clearly need help. She's nice, but sometimes I feel like I'm teaching myself. Though in fairness the workload isn't high and she gives lots of things like late passes, chances for extra credit, etc.

Professor Jensen is impossible to understand. Her class is horrible, I show up every day but I haven't learned a thing. The entire time I spend trying to figure out what she is saying, I miss all the information critical to the math. Her handwriting is illegible, and she writes so fast. It's like a minion trying to teach hieroglyphics.

THICK ACCENT. Hard to understand. Handwriting is unclear, lectures are confusing. Attendance is not mandatory so honestly I would not go and teach yourself the material. Quizzes are short, only 1-3 questions, but weekly. Exams are not terrible, but the word problems can be difficult. Lots of homework, but it is not too bad, just keep up with it.

Her accent makes it really hard to understand. She gives only three exams and a final, with weekly quizzes. The tests are easy and short. Her lectures don't make much sense, so honestly, don't go to them and instead learn it yourself.

Aurora is an amazing professor but sometimes it was hard to understand her because of her accent but that didn't stop me from trying to learn in her class. The tests and quizzes were very easy and she did give us lots of review days, the only thing was that her lectures were hard to understand sometimes.

Professor Jensen was alright. Her accent can make it tough to understand her and she isn't very open to questions. Although, she drops a lot of quizzes and assignments and lets you use a 2 sided page of notes on midterms and the finals. If you can learn the info on your own, it's not to bad of a class.

She's a good person but a difficult teacher. Her accent can be hard to understand and her notes are and can get very messy and close to impossible to interpret especially online notes. She like to jump white board to white board and can also be a bit hard to hear she should definitely use the microphone.

She primarily does problems on the board. However, she also engages with students asking students to solve problems on the board with the class. She is very sweet and will work with you outside of class. If traditional lecture style of teaching is not your style she may not be a professor for you however, if it is she is a very good professor.

Her lectures usually consist of a few questions from the chapter that you probably won't ever see again. Very unhelpful lectures overall. The grading scale is pretty nice though, and you can use a double-sided sheet of notes on all the tests (which are your entire grade).
The tests are VERY SIMILAR to the review
DO THE HOMEWORK AND SKIP THE LECTURE

reviews.comment: This professor was very dull and unhelpful. I couldn't understand what she taught, and she often got mad when someone asked a question. She was late to class and blamed us for not being prepared. I would recommend using Khan Academy instead of her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The notes she gave was good, and she explained the concepts well. The homework assignments did take a while, but it helps you understand. The exam is pretty similar to her reviews, and aren't that difficult. She allows a page of notes too. Honestly if you just keep on top of the material, you should be fine.

I'd never taken calc before and her tests are just like the review plus you get a cheat sheet for each exam. She has a thick accent and it gets confusing sometimes but you have the discussions to help with that.
She is really nice and her lectures are great! We cover all of the testing material in class and can be supplemented by the text book.

She can be a bit hard to understand because of her accent. Overall, the class wasn't too bad if you show up constantly. There are weekly quizzes and homework. The material begins to get hard towards the end of the semester.

She's a great person and caring about her students but her teaching wasn't good. She would get confused very easily and it would take the whole class to do 2-3 problems. there is extra credit and she does allow a paper with you during tests which is helpful. the tests weren't hard but you need to learn by yourself a lot.
Nice person but will not admit to mistakes and teaching is very confusing. Has a heavy accent so it's harder to understand. Be prepared to teach yourself outside of class.

Aurora is a very nice person and she cares a lot. However, the class is just very hard due to messy handwriting and the pace of the class is very fast. The grading scale is very lenient however and it was honestly pretty fun persevering through this class with other students. Would take another Calc 1 professor but it's not the end of the world.

Sweet person, but not good as a professor. It was difficult to get help and she would confuse herself sometimes in lectures. If you haven't taken calc before this class will be very difficult, if you have it won't be as bad but still very confusing.

I really like Aurora Jensen, she worked around my accommodations (I had a baby in the middle of a semester) She was very nice about everything. I also thought she was a pretty good teacher, she does have a heavy accent but you can still understand her.

She is an extremely kind person; however, she was not a good teacher. Every subject we went through she would just put it on the board with little to no explanation. If students asked questions, she would either not answer them or get confused and move on. Her communication outside of the classroom was not the greatest and often times very delayed.

A heavy accent didn't help, but she often would race through topics and not give the clearest explanations of concepts. Many things that were on the exams she didn't tell us, and I had to ask questions to get the in formation out of her.

Jensen was definitely a rough professor. She has a very thick accent making it difficult to understand and when you ask questions in class she will make you feel stupid. I felt that homework amount was reasonable for a math class but some questions were ridiculous, use photomath. She drops 3 quizzes at the end, and final can replace 1/3 midterms.

She's a really like a kind person, but teaching is not her strong suit. She was very hard to communicate with because she would speed through questions and wouldn't thoroughly answers them. When you would try to ask questions, she would somehow make you even more confused. Which meant I had to basically teach myself everything.

Aurora Jensen was a very frustrating teacher, she expected the whole class to already know and understand the material, most the time I had to try and teach myself how to do it after class but that will only get you so far. On top of that, she wouldn't go over anyones questions in the class very well, mainly because she expects you to know it.

Terrible! Gives like 30 homework problems a week, each problem taking at the very least 30 minutes. quizzes every other class, goes overtime, is always at least 5 minutes late to class, doesn't explain necessary information. I had to teach myself everything. does allow cheat sheets on all tests tho. Other than that I absolutely despise her.

One of the worst things about this class (there are many) is how she grades your homework. She grades it on completion but then also chooses one random problem to grade individually. A lot of the time, there are many problems that she does not even teach in class.
She is terrible at teaching. The only way you can learn is by going to Math labs. There is a lot of homework so keep in mind you have to teach yourself how to do them
She is the worst, you have to teach yourself everything and she assigns so much homework
Don't bother on going to class she doesn't teach you anything and just gives you a load of homework. So just know you have to teach yourself
Terrible teacher, assigns so much homework within the first week and pretty much tells you to teach yourself.

She is actually the worst teacher I have ever had. She goes over math problems in class that have little to no correlation to the homework, she treats you like a child that doesn't know anything, and you have to teach yourself in order to pass this class. If you arent decent at math its going to be really hard because she doesnt teach anything.

Going to this class is pretty much pointless.  She does not teach anything well at all, is very rude, and if you ask questions gets angry at you. She has a very thick accent so it's pretty hard to understand what shes saying half the time. I have to teach myself everything
She is nice, but doesn't really know how to answer questions and people don't really get when she's joking.

She has an accent that is tough to understand at times. First Week of classes, she assigned over 250 math problems as homework. Her strategy for grading HW is that 50% credit for doing all the problems and the other 50% is ONE PROBLEM selected from the over 100 problems. She often skips material in class and you are required to teach yourself.

reviews.comment: Taking this class was at times very difficult. Simply because I had to teach myself all of the material. Additionally, going to class was pointless since she spent most of the class time explaining one or two problems. When she finally explained the problems, I still didn't feel I had learned anything.
terrible teacher. hard to understand. lectures are pointless. i taught myself the whole semester. final exam is the worst thing I've ever taken. she did not prepare us for any of the exams.

She has a thick accent so it can be hard to understand her at times. Sometimes she doesn't know what she's talking about or doesn't know how to answer student's questions. Having a solid foundation in Precalc is the only thing that got me through. Definitely read the book, often times she would leave out important formulas or other explanations.
Good

reviews.comment: If math is your strong suit, do not take this class. Jensen tells you how formulas work but not the why. If you're ok with memorizing formulas and just plugging them in mindlessly it will be an easy A. Although her teaching style isn't for everyone. She does want the best for her students. She understands the stresses of students and accommodates.

Aurora is a very kind person. With that being said, she does tend to get quite frustrated in class. Her lectures are often extremely confusing and I feel like she doesn't do well managing her time spent on each topic. There is not a lot of HW, and the tests are pretty simple. Unfortunately, I did most my learning from HW solutions and the textbook.

I was not impressed with Aurora this year. She is kind, but I really can't find any other positive qualities about her. Her lectures were unorganized and scattered. Most of the questions that I asked her were not answered clearly or not even answered at all. Trying to communicate with her over email is impossible. I taught myself the whole semester

reviews.comment: She is trying her best but is very difficult to understand her. Coursework was easy enough, but that said I taught all of it to myself.

reviews.comment: Difficult professor, not only because the course material is difficult, but also because she fails to teach you the things you need to know to be successful in this class. She is rude to her students. Shows up to class not knowing the material she is teaching. And gets upset when you ask questions. 0/10. DO NOT take this professor.

By far worst professor. Used other professors work, simply read the notes and didnt explain, get frustrated and low key puts you down when you call her out or ask qs. One day we had class and she was in a trailer. She then stopped teaching, got up, left for a while without explaining anything, and then came back and ended the zoom class. Fire her
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Aurora is by far the worst math professor at the University of Utah. She doesn't create her own lesson plan so when you do ask her a question about it she doesn't know how to solve it. She is also incredibly rude and yells at you during quizzes and tests. If you don't teach yourself in this class you will not pass. I DONT RECOMMEND!!!

semester isnt even over but there is no way she can redeem herself. she struggles to provide valuable information, and the only way youre going to possibly do well is if youre already a math god. she barely speaks cohesive english and half of her lectures are composed of being frustrated at the class for not knowing untaught material. run.
Uses other professors' presentations and is rude towards people who ask questions in class. Also very disorganized in class and will not respond to emails quickly, if at all.

Aurora tried teaching our class by using another professors slideshows. Most of the time she could barely explain the material herself. She struggled immensely with teaching remotely. Was very unorganized. Worst part about her is she is combative towards questions.
She's terrible

At times she just did not seem too knowledgeable. It was fairly common for her to make a mistake and not notice and she would continue on. However, the TA's are very included and will help a ton throughout the class if you have any questions.
I took this pre-covid and I struggled to understand Jensen. She got mad when people asked questions, and she just read off of slides.

I'm lucky the material was mostly stuff I had learned before. If I didn't already know it, I had to teach myself. She says everything is "common sense," and talks to you like you are stupid when you have a question or get something wrong. She doesn't let you finish your questions, either, and makes things needlessly confusing. I don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worst prof I've ever had. She won't answer your emails, her lectures are indecipherable and if you ask questions she talks to you like you're stupid. Everything I have learned from this class I've learned from youtube. Her accent is thick, and it makes her hard to understand. If you're good at math, you'll do okay, if you're not, pray.

This class was a waste of time. The material itself is easy but she just confuses everyone with her rambling. She blames you for not knowing things & everyone taking her online class is failing the quizzes because this is my easiest class but with the STRICTEST grading Ive ever seen. take this class online @ slcc& I guarantee itll be better.

While you may have a better experience in this class, it definitely was on my list of bad professors I've had. She made you feel like a kindergartener when you don't understand a problem, and it wasn't uncommon to leave class more confused than when you first arrived. It helps to never skip class, study, and ask detailed questions in class.

Professor Jensen is an extremely knowledgeable and a great instructor. There are 12 HW, 10 Quizzes, 2 Midterm, 1 Semester Project, and a final exam. There are 2 drop for quizzes and homework. She gives a clear idea what is going to be on exams and the lectures are extremely helpful. She is always available for help required to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stats is not an easy subject and Aurora did not make it any easier. Besides the fact that she has a very thick accent and it is extremely hard to understand her, she barely teaches. Her exams are hard and she does not prepare her students properly for them. Try to find a different professor for Math 1070.

She is very difficult to understand, especially when everything is switched online. When it was in-person, it was already hard to understand what she was teaching. Everything on Canvas was also very messy and disorganized. I mostly had to teach myself throughout the whole course. It gets harder to do so later on and you're left not understanding.
Worst professor. Absolutely choked with the switch to online classes, and when we weren't online she was impossible to understand.
She is nice woman, but you have to put the work in to receive a good grade.

She cares about her students and will go out of her way to help them with exams. The test are really straight forward and basically you just need to know how to use the equations of the chapter(which she gives you!) come to class, either take notes or participate when she asks and you'll get an A. quizzes are 75% group. She'll meet with students.

If you're good at math this class will be easy. Not because she's a great teacher but because most of this class involves simple algebra and all of the variables are given to you. She is not approachable. Her accent really isn't that bad, I've had worse at the U. Homework is graded on completion not correctness. Easy grader on tests and quizzes

She is very nice. But we never finish the lectures and terms are not explained at all. The grader is good. The 3 exams is what makes or breaks your grade. You have to study outside of class to understand what you are doing. Her accent is thick and it is hard to hear/understand her during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not an amazing teacher. She basically just reads to us from slides and then she will do one probably in class that's kinda hard to follow. She does have an accent but I don't find her that difficult to understand. She is not all that approachable. Will not post in class materials so she can prevent people who skip from having the in class stuff

I personally have never received such a poor grade. I am not that good at math but sheesh, it was difficult for me. I had to teach my self for the most part. I would recommend a different professor if you are not good at math.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a language barrier which makes it hard to understand her but it gets better as the semester goes. Also, She got a bit impatient with a couple of students in class that weren't understanding the material and I thought that was a bit unprofessional. She talks to you like you're an idiot if you don't understand it. The homework was confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor is not good at answering questions and gets very inpatient. She hates when students take a long time finishing a problem or a test. She is very uptight and not a very good math teacher. I am good at math but I always got so confused because she does not really know the content herself, which is weird because she is a math teacher.

Aurora is really sweet, at first it can be hard to understand her but other than that she really is a good teacher! TA's help a lot and the lab really helps clear things up from the lecture. If you do all your assignments, get help when you need it, show up to class (has multiple clicker points a day), and study the review you will do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took 1010 w Aurora, and I wouldn't recommend. She is very hard to understand because of her accent. Homework is unrelated to class material and tests can also be unrelated, a quiz every week but sometimes group quizzes. She a nice person but I wouldn't recommend this class.

To succeed in Dr. Jensen's class, you have to take detailed notes, attend the entire lecture (without leaving early) and apply the material. She provides all of the resources  office hours, practice tests, supplemental work  to do well. Her accent makes some things *slightly* difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Aurora is a nice person, but the language barrier can be an obstacle in the class. Ended up teaching myself most of the time. Homework can be completely unrelated to class material, but the tests are extremely easy. Overall I would probably recommend taking a different class, even though you can do well in this one.

Jensen was hard to understand at the beginning, but it got better. Also, her exams are probably the easiest exams I've ever taken. She gives you a study guide and copies those questions for exams, of course she'll change a number or two. Overall I just hated going to class, but it was an easy math class.

At the beginning it was hard to follow her, but with time I got used to it. You can tell that she is smart, and have her ways to solve problems. There is several quizzes( she takes out two), 3 exams, and the final. Attendance is calculated as clicker points. She is caring, smart, and will help no matter what, I would like to be her student again.
Professor Bauman is a great writing teacher, she gives lots of great feedback on work and discussions is very caring, and mainly looks for quality in your work. Would 100% recommend her.

Amazing professor! Took creative writing with her and learned many new things. She is easy to contact if you need help within her office hours, and she is understandable. Lots of discussion about different forms of writing. Her grading is more based off effort. Participation is important, you get the chance to do workshops and read others writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved having Audrey for WRTG 2010. She is very nice and accommodating on all assignments. I've had professors that just could not give an A on a paper. I don't think I ever received anything below an A from her. All she is looking for is the effort and time put into your work, not just the writing itself. In-class discussions were always fun.
Very entertaining to listen to and just wants you to learn. He expects you to put in the work but the work load is pretty light and totally doable with a busy schedule.

Great professor. It's obvious that he's passionate about the subject and cares about his students. Lots of reading, but not a ton of assignments. It's nice to learn how to write papers/resumes that will actually be useful as an engineer, and he has a lot of applicable experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Booth does a great job of teaching Professional Communications. He gives great lectures and gives fantastic feedback on the work you submit. This class was more work than I expected but it was worth it. Definitely take this class if you want to communicate more effectively as an engineer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Austin Booth is a great professor. He does an awesome job in his lectures and I found myself learning a lot in his class. Professor Booth emphasized critical thinking and applying critically thinking principles to your writing. The class also covered ethics in engineering. There were many good discussions. All the assignments are papers.
Worst class I have ever taken. She is not consistent or clear. Posted assignments randomly. Never responded or answered emails. Was a disaster.

Online class was confusing and very disorganized. The way the professor formatted the discussion groups made it very difficult to make all of the necessary responses by the due date. Tests were not extremely difficult as long as you followed the lectures each week.

Terrible as an online professor. She was unfamiliar with the online format, thus assignment due dates were frequently incorrect and discussion groups confusing. Test questions were NOT representative of the material, and included many "trick" questions that were worded poorly. Professor would not respond to e-mails either.

If you go to class and pay attention, you'll get an A. There was no final or midterm, just a final project that was easy enough if you've gone to class. The professor was passionate about the subject and ready to answer any questions. Overall, I would take this class again.
His grading rubric was fair and straight forward, he wants students to pass and succeed. Assignments can take a long time. Overall recommend over surveying 100p.

Dr. Nassar is extremely passionate about the topic of geomatics and is incredibly knowledgeable, which are normally desirable qualities in a professor. However, in this case, Dr. Nassar imposes said passion onto students and expects students to be as passionate as he is. Homework assignments are impossible to complete, as well as the final project.

Only a couple assignments, 1 midterm and a final. Assignments and midterm are fine if you go to lab. He tends to repeat himself a lot in lecture and you don't learn much, although attendance isn't mandatory. Learned pretty much everything in lab. The final project is super long and complicated so start early, he will help out if you need him to.
Lets you redo assignments. the term project is really bad and long, start early. easier than surveying.
Easy class, but Nassar is condescending and no one enjoys going to his class.

My favorite professor EVER! I came to class ready for a laugh and a fun fact every time. Lectures are recorded in case you can't make it or want to rewatch to prepare for exams. The exams are mostly multiple choice and the answers come straight from her lectures. She is extremely dedicated and genuinely wants you to enjoy and thrive in her class!
Attending class really matters. The comprehension checks she does at the beginning of class really help with understanding the class material. Overall a wonderful professor and an interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at the U! Comparative Physiology is a broad and complicated field, but she breaks it down into manageable pieces. She does iClicker questions before each class and throughout lecture to make sure everyone understands the material. Tests are fairly hard- she makes you think about how things work together. Do the readings!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ayako is awesome her lectures are amazing and she is pretty funny. The class itself is interesting but is hard, lectures are packed with a ton of information and can be a little overwhelming. Her exams are hard but she tries her best to give you all the resources you need to succeed. You're graded on 3 exams and 5 quizzes.

Professor Yamaguchi is an absolute treat to learn from. She is really invested in the topic of physiology and insanely knowledgeable in her field. She is also very understanding and helpful with questions. She really wants to see student success! Very test heavy class with hard material, but she gives plenty of resources. Highly recommend!
she's funny and easy going and her lectures aren't boring. make sure you study, by memorizing every single thing on the 90/lecture slides and you will do well. the textbook didn't really matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I LOVED Dr. Yamaguchi. She was such an advocate for the learning of all her students. She worked to involve everyone and even though she's a GENIUS in her field, she never came across as snooty or superior. I was worried about having a research professor teach my course as I've realized they often focus more on their research. Not the case here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking this class unless you have really good memory. Each lecture holds about 75 slides on it and you have about 9 lectures worth of slides to memorize for test. overall test score is based of the highest grade earned on the test which seems nice but if someone scores 100% on it doesn't really help you like she says.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very organized, very clear about what material she expects you to know for exams. The exams come from lectures, the book is not necessary (but it's helpful). DO NOT SKIP LECTURE. She posts slides, but 90% of the time the slide doesn't reflect what she wants you to know, and she goes very in depth on the figures. Overall, hard class but great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Comparative Physiology was an interesting class, however, two tests make up 80% of your grade. Third test will account for 10% and group quizzes are the other 10%. Beware of this class if you do not do well with massive amounts of memorization and difficult tests. If you attend class, do the reading, and ask lots of questions, you can survive.

Osama was an amazing professor. Calc 2 is a pretty difficult class but he makes it a whole lot easier. His tests are very similar to example problems done in class, but I recommend getting the textbook for extra practice. Amazing lecturer and explains complicated problems in a simple matter. He is also very helpful during office hours.
Prof. Khalil makes calc interesting and easy to understand. You can really tell that he cares about his students. He is a very fair grader and gives lots of partial credit.

Professor Khalil is a good professor who cares about students understanding of each topic provided the student cares as well. His lectures are helpful and the material provided in are a good representation of what will be on the test. His tests are easy to study for and a study guide is provided which represents what is on the test.

Professor Azenui was awesome! The class is a lot of work, so its important to stay on top of your assignments and not wait til the last minute, but I'd say it was what I expected from online econ. I didn't schedule an exam in the testing center in time and prof Azenui extended the due date for me, which made me like her a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you're considering taking the online course I would rethink it. The online homework load was strenuous and the textbook doesn't explain all the math which leaves you to figuring it out. It's a difficult online course and it takes a lot of time to understand it all. The homework sometimes feels like it will never end.

No assignments for the class; the class was completely based off of 3 exams. In her syllabus she even mentions that 60% of the people that take her class do not pass it. I would not recommend this at all. She also takes forever to grade the 3 assignments.
Encourages students. Provide great lectures and study material
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was very easy. Attendance is mandatory due to attendance quizzes, but paying attention isn't necessary.

Azuma sensei is a professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. He lays out what you need to know for the test and everything comes from the textbook. This class is kanji and reading heavy, so these are the things you should practice the most. He is also funny and will keep you entertained in class.

He is very knowledgeable in what he teaches. He covers content well, wants you to understand. He has a sense of humor and enjoys teaching. I thought his class was easy but that depends on your level of Japanese. Some people had a really hard time. Lots of Kanji, lots of reading. No textbook for this class.

Shoji just reads the book. If you're looking for structured, this is it. He tells you what the tests are on, and you just have to do a little before class prep, never more than like an hour, and you're golden. Tests are just the same. Put an hour or two into prep, and you get a good score.

I could buy the textbook and teach myself the class. The class is a bookclub to discuss the book and nothing but the book. Shoji is stil adamant about attendance, however. Very unhelpful for an upper division class.
Class wasn't too difficult if you memorized the bookwork. However, Shoji was Much too arrogant and self-serving. Worst teacher I've had so far at the U.

If you take this class, do not turn in pages from your workbook, unless you have made copies. Future assignments will be in her possession! I have never taken a class, I studied for, and still did poorly.

I've taken Azuma for both JPN 1010 and 1020 and she's one of the best professors I've ever had. There's a lot of homework but it's not difficult and can be finished fairly quickly. Her lectures are very structured and she guides you through all new material. Lectures are participation heavy and engaging. Overall, she's very sweet and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Excellent Japanese professor. She does a great job at teaching at a good pace where you feel like you learn a lot but are not overwhelmed at any time.
Professor Azuma is the best. She is really good at lecturing and is really funny. Super helpful and wants to see you do well.

She's genuinely my favorite teacher at the U. I love her and her classes so much that I structured my Junior year around being able to take them. If you want to learn Japanese, do it with her. She's understanding, upbeat, and funny. Being in class with her is a joy

Azuma sensei teaches Japanese really well. She explains it in ways that make sense. We used the textbook a lot and had lots of homework, but if you had questions she was very willing to help. She doesn't grade very harshly and is very nice.

Azuma Sensei is an amazing Japanese teacher and makes learning Japanese easier. She is very clear about her grading and uses the same format for all her classes. If you take Japanese, take it with Azuma Sensei.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Azuma-sensei is an amazing professor! I took her for 1010, 1020, 2010, and currently 2020. She is super sweet and easy to understand. You get homework daily, but you will still get full points as long as you complete it which is very admirable because you shouldn't be docked for mistakes when learning in my opinion.

Azuma sensei is great at teaching the language and has a clear passion for doing so. She is lighthearted and caring, ultimately making the lectures more enjoyable. The learning can be slow, though Japanese is not an easy language to learn for native English speakers so it might just be right for some people. Overall, I would highly recommend

She is a great professor! She does give a lot of homework but it is all pretty easy and can be finished quickly. I also felt that she was pretty lenient on grading for quizzes and exams. She gives study guides for mid term and finals that are essentially the exam. Would highly recommend.

Amazing professor! She really cares about your success, and her grading is very reasonable. She encourages participation and has daily homework, which is a huge help for those just learning the language.
Best professor Ive ever had. Such a caring person who for someone who isnt the greatest English speaker does an amazing job teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Azuma is an awesome teacher who is super funny. She is willingly to help out students who are having a harder time with the language and is very kind. In the classroom, she involves every student in the lecture so it is easier to memorize and learn how to speak Japanese. Would definitely recommend taking one of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is an amazing teacher! She explains things to you very well, and she explains things perfectly for beginners. She is a great teacher to take, she goes slow enough that you don't feel super overwhelmed, which is important for learning a new language. There is homework everyday, but it is totally necessary to keep practicing with this language!

Azuma-sensei is awesome! I took two classes from her. She speaks about 60%  Japanese during lectures. At the beginning of the year, it's a little disorienting and you're like "whaa" but she says crucial instructions in English. Her constant Japanese speaking really helps you get used to it. She doesn't dock points on homework if you made mistakes.
Great teacher!
Little hard, but she's very nice and understanding.

Azuma sensei is awesome. She is hilarious and always has a good attitude about things. Take as many classes from her as you can. You've got to be there & do your stuff. She really knows her stuff and presents it in a good easy to understand way, and if you're good, she's always up for inclass parties if they include Japanese food! Highly Recommend.
She is very nice and kind. It is very easy to get an A in this class. I like her teaching, except she covers materials too slowly.
Im going to miss Azuma sensei, she taught us a lot.
She's a pretty cool teacher.  I like her.
Good class! Kind of hard if you've never heard Japanese before at all, but otherwise okay.
The first day of class when she speaks purely in japanese you're like "whaaaa!" but you get use to it and shes okay, she makes snide/funny comments about how great Japan is.

While the classwork was easy, based almost entirely on discussions, the professor was often unavailable. She relied on other teachers' videos and gave confusing assignments. Though I never worried about the work or failing, this professor is not great at teaching. This class was manageable, but I wouldn't take a more challenging course with her!

This professor put almost no effort into this course. I didn't even know this professor's name until a month or so in because she used another professor's lectures. The lectures take about 3 hours to watch, with multiple readings and a discussion every week was way too much work, I struggled to keep up. She offered no assistance or guidance either.

I'm taking this course online but I barely know who the professor is because she use someone else's lectures. The discussions are harshly graded and the exams are stressful because you cannot go back to your previous questions.

This professor was the WORST professor I have ever had. She copied and pasted ANOTHER professor's in-person course into Canvas and labeled it as an online course. Her E-Mail replies are short and NOT helpful. She put no effort into this course which made it very hard to follow what was expected. Extremely disappointed with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Babu for 2140. Very good lectures, though some were a bit confusing at times. Office hours were very helpful and she is willing to work with you to understand the concepts. Exams are difficult, but doable
She always encourages students to ask for help and genuinely cares about their success. Her lectures were good, though sometimes hard to follow.

This class is not difficult, all material is posted online and quizzes after every class are open note.

The hardest part of this class will be working on the big semester project with your randomly assigned lab group. Tests can be mid but she allows a cheat sheet, invest some hours into studying and you'll get a good score
Awesome Professor! Computer tools is an easy class, but is just lots of busy work.

I took her 2010 statics class. The hardest parts of class were the centroid and moment of inertia questions so give yourself extra time, and you may want to review triangle and angle properties. She is really nice and supportive, met with me even though I had class/work during her office hours. She writes problems/solutions on the board clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class for statics 2010, great professor. Super nice and lectures were clear and easy to understand. Lots of materials available on canvas and she gave good review for tests. Available outside of class and will help out if you need her to. Overall, super nice and would definitely take her again.

I took Strength and Structures from Dr. Babu, and while her courses are not easy, she is enjoyable to work with and genuinely wants students to succeed. If she thought you were trying, she would happily grant extensions/work with you. Tests are tough but doable, homework and quizzes were fine. Project was also tough but she was eager to help

Said that the reason scores are low on Rate my Prof. was because the ratings are from students who did not attend class I attended EVERY ONE. Still bad teacher. Nice guy, but really doesn't care about teaching only cares about the University paying for his research. Reads from off his phone for lectures and solves problems wrong then just moves on.

Said that attendance was mandatory because he did not give announcements outside of class. There were assignments from February not graded until the end of April. Basically non existent Canvas course. No notes, no slides, no lecture recordings, no due dates, basically empty except for emailed announcements. Unavailable outside class

Made fun of a student (with special needs) for being loud and asking questions when the student wasn't there. Made a distasteful comment about how the student being absent made "the class so much quieter". Also did not stand up for said student when in class someone cussed at him. It was really hard to attend lecture after that.

Instructor would show up 5 or 10 minutes late every lecture and then make comments on how class was too short. Admitted to using Chat GPT to write some of his lectures or solve problems. Would frequently come to lectures unprepared or with no notes. He would try to do example problems without solving beforehand and then get confused or just move on

2 spectrums for profs. 1st: evil to kind. 2nd: attentive/organized to disorganized/unstructured. Prof is hella chill but disorganized. Will acively give you any points he can on any/everything. Hes trying to help your grade. Study consistently on your own, at least B or A. I didn't, hence D. always 5 min late to class. DID give study guides to us.
If you take him just learn by yourself with the textbook. He's rarely accessible, overcomplicates his lectures, and takes forever to grade. At least he admitted to only doing it for the postdoc.
Take this class from anyone else. He was learning calc while trying to teach us. No understanding of the class and taught from the textbook

super disorganized canvas, poor teaching, late to class everyday by at least 5 or so mins, seemed to barely know the content even, only just read out the textbook, very unaccessible communication and help outside of class.

The lectures were incredibly unproductive, and prof Bashwinger completely refused to provide any study materials for any exams. I don't remember a single time where he answered a question clearly and didn't go off on some random tangent. He also didn't follow the syllabus for the course at all.

He definitely knows a lot about the topic, and he's clearly a very good mathematician, but he sometimes gets bogged down in rigor and struggles to teach in a way that's helpful for the students. His course was not very organized at all, and he mostly left the administrative side to the course coordinator, but overall, I really liked him.

The course was poorly organized. The professor did not create the syllabus, and it was inaccurate. Lectures were unprepared and disorganized, with frequent errors in the example problems worked in class. No practice exams were provided for the midterm or final.

Not good at proctoring tests, sits on his phone for most of the test, and doesn't notice when people go on their phones to take pictures of tests/quizzes and upload them to AI, doesn't even notice the large amount of perfect scores. On top of that, his lectures are just him reading off his phone and are impossible to follow and stay awake during.

Although I attended to 90% of his lectures, I didn't learn anything from these, as he just talking on the board with his confusing notes. Unstructured class with no clear syllabus, no practice offered before exams, little extra credit offered, subjective grading rubric. I like his personalities, but he has NO intention on his students' success.

Do NOT take a class from this professor if you can help it. The course and syllabus was set up for him and he never stuck to it. Every lecture (once he showed up) was full of mistakes and frustration. Teaching was very obviously a side gig to his personal life.

Avoid Eli at all costs. He showed up ~5 minutes late everyday for a class that's only 50 minutes, would get problems and explanations wrong often and did not care about this class or his students. He only read from the textbook and as well openly admitted he didn't write his syllabus and even to the end it had many serious uncorrected errors.

The worst professor ever! He arrives late to his 50 minute lecture periods constantly, doesn't have any PPTs or even videos prepared, and teaches concepts on a whiteboard, in which he continuously makes arithmetic errors and has to back track. His canvas is the worst I have ever seen and you always have to request regrades on his test grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Reads from text book, acts as though he's teaching the material in a different way by bringing his own regurgitated version of the textbook in a piece of paper he wrote the night before. Canvas is unstructured, don't use the hw as a guide to the exam as its irrelevant, there is NO exam practice material be ready to fail. Save your money and time.

Expect a lot of very mathematical definitions that are worded very mathy, but precise, and kind of hard to understand at first. If you go to every lecture (which most did not do this semester) you'll understand all the material. Though, the syllabus is inaccurate and the canvas is unorganized (quizzes usually ended up under the files category).

Assigns quizzes every week that are 2 questions long and he doesn't tell you what the quiz is on until he decides to email you (usually at 10pm the day before). He just reads the math textbook on his phone and writes on the chalkboard all class. Very unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures consist of reading out of textbook, does not post due dates, syllabus very inaccurate (says there is 3 quizzes but one every week), provides no (NO) resources, shows a general lack of care. Average was 68% on the second test. You'll need to both teach yourself and go to class to know what you need to teach yourself.

This professor is one of those that does not care about teaching, he just cares about his career. So he is pretty disorganized with homework and quizzes. His classes are not very useful, his notations are very confusing and he is not very accessible outside class. Most of people are having hard time learning in his class.

I'm jazz pianist as a hobby but engineering major, so I thought this class would be amazing for a general. I learned a lot but only because I put extra time into learning because I'm passionate. The material is so cool but the class structure and their teaching made it so boring and such a slog. Easy A, but I wish it was as fun as it should be.
This was a great class to take over the summer! The half semester content moved at a great pace, with lectures, study guides, and the textbook being excellent resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Take this class for an easy A. I sometimes forgot I was in this class because of how minimal effort was needed to pass.

This class was really fun and low stress. There were lectures to watch every week that were a little lengthy but Professor Basinger was fun and passionate about her subject. The assignments were pretty easy and she gives really detailed study guides for the exams so its easy to get a good grade. Great class!

This class was a good class to to take over summer because of the light course-load. Was a great class to take if you're interested in music, you get to listen to lots of different jazz and learn about different musicians and the weekly quizzes are very easy if you look at the lectures.

This class had only a few assignments. She put out study guides for the midterm and final, and honestly if you fill them out, you'll have pretty much what you need for them; just be fast when taking the tests. The tests are also curved. The paper was graded kind of harshly, and it seemed unclear what exactly she was looking for.

If you need an art credit take this class. Super easy and honestly one of those classes you don't have to worry too much about. One quiz per week, can retake until you get 100 and 3 tests. She curves them HEAVY so don't stress. Took this over summer but forgot to review :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the easiest online classes I've taken at the U, in my opinion. The curve on the test is insanely generous. If you put in minimal effort (literally 3 hours per test based on the study guide), you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bettie Jo was a great teacher. I didn't interact with her very much since this was an online class. Use shazam for the tests. It is super easy, sometimes shazam wont give you the correct answer and wont pick up on the song.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not watch any lectures but still got an A because the professor was extremely clear in her grading criteria. If you just follow the rubric for the paper and the 2 study guides for the midterm and the final, you will get a 100% after curve. I did not learn anything in this class

TBH I dont remember the class, that was how uninvolved I was. Essays were kind of hard and the final exam was also hard. Im sure if you payed attention and did what you were supposed to it would have been easy. Long story short lots of work in order to prepare for exams and assignments, but it was all optional so I only did the bare minimum.

I personally did not watch any lectures or read a single page out of the book and got an A. This class does not require much of you until the midterm, final, and final paper. She does curve the final and midterm. The paper was graded pretty harshly so make sure you are on top of it. The final and midterm are hard, they are closed note.

This class was not very hard and it was online. There was about two lectures per week, listening quizzes, a paper, a midterm and a final. Professor Basinger outlined the paper page by page and even told us what information she would recommend we put in the paper. She also gave study guides for both exams that were very helpful.

You could pass this class w/ an A without listening to any of her pre-recorded lectures or reading the book. Recommend knowing the topic listed on her study guide rather than just what's listed. She was nice and generous to talk about what exactly to put on the paper, so just put what she said in essay format really. Exams were stressful for me tho
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were only 8 graded assignments, and 5 of them were open-note, unlimited-try quizzes. Dr. Basinger was a very fair grader, and the class was not very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super easy just a few quizzes all on quizlet. 1 hard essay. 2 finals that are kinda hard because they are proctored but thats it. Barely any work.

This class is very straightforward and not difficult at all. It is graded very fairly and honestly you could pass this class with minimal studying. I do recommend at least attending lectures if you want to get an A, but even that is optional. The most difficult part about the class is the paper, otherwise it's just memorization for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend taking this course online to cover your diversity and fine arts credit. There were 5 listening quizzes, 1 paper, and 2 tests (midterm and final). Super easy, even though the content was pretty boring. Professor also provides a study guide so you know exactly what is on the test. Not a class you need to be stressed about!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Survey of Jazz is an easy class and Bettie is very nice, easy-going teacher that recognizes it's a gen-ed. She can get longwinded but she also likes to make jokes sometimes so that's

Bettie Jo is a good professor and knows her stuff. She is a fair teacher. It's a relatively easy class to pass; requirements include 3 exams, one paper, and going to 3 jazz concerts throughout the semester. Her study guides are extremely useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The content of the course wasnt delivered in a particularly engaging way. I think the delivery of the material could use some TLC as the lectures tend to get a bit monotonous as the semester drags on. She is very knowledgeable about the subject matter, but itd be great if the course were more interactive. Its very, very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Basinger is the best professor one can hope for when you are one of the many students who take this class to fill credits. Very little busywork, extremely generous study guides for the midterms, and 15% of the grade is just going to a concert. Her voice is a little raspy but it's not like she can do much about it. 5/5
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: easy A without going to class, you can find most of  her test answers online, there is one essay required but its  easy, the concert attendances are also easy just go to sugar house coffee shop on Thursdays for credit. Boring teacher but good taste for jazz music! her TA made me want to kms  though haha.
I now understand the negative reviews.  I agree.

Great class that is washed out by her boring lectures.  Study the slides, and dont go to lectures until a week or 2 before an exam to catch some exam hints. Make time for concert attandance! Use flash cards with her study guides to study for the tests. The paper was the hardest, but still easy as she tells you what she expects. Easy A.
few graded assignments, then she let her ta grade the biggest one and she did an awful job. there are pop quizes once people stop showing up to class. extremely hard for a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The exams are tough with listening portions, but if you follow the study guide and know everything on it, you will be more than prepared. Didn't go to class all semester and pulled an A so its not very tough. One long paper, but she's not a tough grader.

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken. Three tests which the answers are basically a copy-and-paste from the slides (which she uploads), three concerts where you only need proof attendance, and ONE paper. The paper is probably the hardest part, but she give you all the materials and explains what she wants. Plus, I learned a lot about Jazz.

Great Professor and knows her Jazz! The most difficult part of the class is the required paper that is worth a large portion of your grade. She gives you a lot of time to work on it and if you attend class she might even give you some pointers! Tests are fairly straightforward. Great class to get your Fine Art and Diversity credit

Bettie Jo is a fine music professor. It is very easy to get an A, and the material can be interesting if you take the time to dive into it. If you need to get a gen ed out of the way, I would highly recommend this class.

This class is so boring. Dr. Basinger's lectures are long and boring and she posts all the slides on Canvas so you don't really need to go to class anyway. She only grades you on the midterm, final, paper and concert attendance. If you don't do the concert attendance, you won't pass the class. She also has an annoying voice. Good luck

Class is long and lectures get so boring. Attendance isn't mandatory therefore no one goes to class except for tests. It is very important to study for tests. The professor is kind and understanding and is great at communication. YOU MUST ATTENDS CONCERTS to pass.

Easy easy easy easy class. Show up to the two classes before the midterms so you can get the specific listening times for the listening portion of the tests. Her lectures are hard to listen to, so don't bother going.  Don't buy the book and if you ask around you can find the songs without buying them.

Easiest class i have taken. You dont need to go to class except test days. All the study guides for the tests are posted online a week before the test and are EXACTLY what the questions will be on the test. The hardest part is memorizing the songs/artists. The only reason to buy the book would be for the music otherwise you dont use it. Easy A.

Bettie has good intentions but, her attitude toward students with no interest in Jazz is just appalling. Even with this being an "intro" class Big Jo,(as requested) goes far more in-depth than I am sure she did in becoming Dr. Jazz. Her lectures are hurtful to the ear and the amount of times Jo brought food to class without sharing is upsetting:(

I heard this was an easy A, and while the course is easy the grading is really quite strict and it is not clear what is expected from the students. The teacher Bettie "Big Jo" Basinger seems to have no interest in actually teaching or captivating the students, the lectures are torture if Jazz isn't your favorite thing in the world.

This class was extremely easy and a good way to get in a diversity and fine arts credit. There are two midterms, one paper, and several concerts. She gives you an exact study guide of the test and test hints in class. There is no need to read either.

Lectures are really boring, don't bother going until the 3 classes before the test where she'll give the listening times for the test. Print out the study guide and use the lecture slides she posts online. Make sure and attend the concerts early.

The easiest Class ever.  Its a diversity and a fine arts credit so that is why i took it.  Only went on test days because all class lectures are online.  you should go to class the day before the test, she'll give you lots of hints, especially on the listening sections.  book is not necessary but the cd's are so chip in for 1 book as a group.

This class was such a boring class. Her speaking style is very spaced and she sometimes mumbles. ALL the answers to everything are online on her powerpoints. The hardest part was the listening portion on tests. If you have no interest in Jazz, don't expect to find it with Bettie Jo.

Using Gidden's Jazz text, Basinger creates an informative survey of jazz course. She is a high-energy lecturer who kept me attentive & entertained through her 500+ lecture slides. One written paper req. Three tests require memorizing the names and a characteristic of 20 to 35 songs each. Highly recommend for required fine arts diversity credits.

Very easy class, especially if you show up to class. She'll give you test answers, so even if you don't want to go to class (which isn't all that necessary), go for a few days before the tests and you'll ace them all. Only one assignment, which was nice, plus a few concerts out of class. Easy way to make the grade.

Professor Bakshi is super outgoing and makes his lectures very intriguing and applicable to the real world. He is really good at explaining the class topics in a simple way for students to learn. Just attend class, participate, and pay attention to his lectures, and you will be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor all around!

Very good professor. This class was an elective for my major and I didn't think it would be applicable to my field. I was wrong. He gives great practical examples of concepts that apply across various business settings, not just supply chain stuff. HW and exams were fairly easy as long as you pay attention in class and do a little bit of practice.

Super knowledgeable professor but there were only 2 homework assignments and 1 quiz and 1 exam for the whole course. Each of those would only have 15 questions each. There is so much content covered in such a short period of time and not a lot of practice problems to go with each thing learned. I was only told to review the slides as practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Bakshi! He is one of my favorite professors at the U. He goes slow to make sure that everyone understands the content and is such a kind and caring professor. He really cares for his students. Graded by a few things-- two homework and two tests. Overall, highly recommend!

He is THE BEST! He is very clear in lectures and genuinely wants students to succeed. He is super willing to answer questions to help students and remembers people's names so it is super personal. There is little homework, and the tests are not too difficult if you study and show up to class. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!

Professor Bakshi is great. The course material is complex, but he explains it in a way that is easy to understand. He wants his students to be able to grasp the ideas conceptually and he does a good job of that. He cares about his students and will know your name in a class of 50 students. As a bonus, class ended early, and there is no busy work.

Professor Bakshi had an amazing teaching style and was able to explain complex topics in easily-digestible and intuitive ways.  He was also immensely kind to his students and took the time to explain topics multiple times to ensure that students understood the concepts well.  One of the best professors I've had during my time at the University.

Professor Bakhsi made a complicated topic very simple to understand and as a result, the topic didn't seem that complicated. He uses excellent examples and even improvises some to adjust to different students' learning methods.

Bakshi is a phenomenal professor, one of my favorites in the entire University. His pacing and the way he presents information makes difficult information palatable and easy to understand. Great teacher, great guy, would 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Bakshi does care about his students and will not move onto until everyone understands. The material can be dry, while the class is fast paced. The homework answers can be found online. The tests are like the study guide, so make sure to practice that. Also, there is a cheat sheet! Make sure to put practice problems that are trick on there!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took the accelerated version of this class. The whole grade is two homework assignments, two exams, and participation. I'm not going to lie - this class is not easy. Nitin spent very little time on material before moving on to the next thing, which made it hard to keep up. However, he is always willing to meet with you outside of class if needed
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS
