reviews.comment: Nitin is a tremendous professor. He takes his time in class and makes sure everyone understands it. His enthusiasm leads to great, engaging lectures. He likes when people participate and are engaged. If you show some interest, which is very easy to do, he will do anything he can to help. I highly recommend this class!

Dr. Bakshi was probably my favorite professor I have had at the U. He knows the material very well and makes sure everyone in the class understands the material as well.  The class is very difficult so if you skip the lectures, you probably will not do well. Dr. Bakshi also adds in subtle humor which makes the class enjoyable. Amazing professor.

Nitin is not only a passionate, knowledgable professor but also just a great guy. He cares about his students' success and tailors his pace to meet students' needs. The subject material is difficult, but if you go to class and ask for help you'll do fine. Take OIS from Nitin!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ignore the grade, I flopped when I took this class lol. Petar was a great at lecturing, engaging and clearly cared about us doing well. However, because theres not a lot in the grade book if you do bad on one midterm its hard to come back. I'd say for this class, study the definitions early. Homework is graded on correctness so lock in
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had for math! His lectures are super engaging and easy to follow. His exams are very easy if you pay attention and are nearly identical to the reviews. Gives out a moderate, very doable amount of homework. Seriously the best, you'll be glad you took this class from him

One of the BEST professors I've ever had. He made the abstract concepts easier to understand and truly cares about student success. Very few homework assignments and his tests aren't hard if you've been paying attention in class.

Petar made this class really enjoyable because he really did care about his student's learning. He's very wise and willing to help students. He's also a funny guy! As a math major in their 3rd year he is one of the BEST math prof out there! 
We only have 5 hws which were 25% and exams were 75%. TRUST he is a rare gem of a professor! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Petar is the GOAT. His lectures are amazing. This was the first math class since HS that I actually felt like I was synthesizing the material and not just memorizing. He grades very fairly and answers in class questions intelligently. I'm genuinely sad that he will probably never teach a class of mine again lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Favorite math prof I've had! It's different from other math classes I've taken, a lot more abstract and goes into the whys of things, making lecutres a bit harder to understand but way cooler. Exams are graded kindly and arithmetic errors are easily forgiven if you understand the concepts. I definitely recommend!

He teaches everything so perfect. exams were easy if you understand and practice everything. Class average exams were like a B. We are graded by little things like 6 hw and 3 exams. Overall great guy will definitely take again. HES THE BEST!

Firstly, linear algebra is not your typical math class. Dr. Bakic's approach to teaching linear algebra is heavily theoretical. He explains everything via proofs, even though the tests are not proof-based. The tests are computational, which is precisely what they should be, with perhaps one small theory question thrown in. I'd take from him again.

His total grade is calculated in two parts, proof and daily homework. The exam is also divided into two parts, calculation and proof. You can easily score the calculations part, but you must attend classes on time to learn the proofs part. I missed a course before for some reasons, you may find that you cannot understand the latter part.
The lectures were very helpful and straightforward. The homework was easy after the lecture and there were no surprises on exams. Great professor and very fun class.

Professor Baik is very good at lecturing, he asks questions and asks people to go to the board to solve problems. Outside of class he is easy to reach and answered your question very well and detailed He can help you with studying and doing the homework a lot. His homework is fairly easy however be aware of not many assignments and no formula sheet
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
There was a 2 month period with no assignments, then a week before the midterm we were given an assignment. Same thing happened w/ the final. BC this is a math class it makes it easy to get lost. 

I've never said this before, but I wish there were more assignments.. 

His test reviews are great though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bakic was a godsend for 3220 (taken a while ago). It's really impressive how clearly he communicates the concepts during the lectures. They were a bit boring at times, but I think that was mainly due to the course being online with not a lot of interaction.

Very caring and understanding professor. Exams were worth the majority of your grade but the practice exams outlined exactly what you need to know! If you miss class its hard to catch back up because the only material is what he does in lecture. tough course but expectations are clear and reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: What made him so hard was the fact that he would just make up questions and solve them in front of us. The class was boring due to it being so low energy. Minimal homework which made it hard to really learn the stuff because you would do it once and that was that. His practice exams were GOLD though.

Petar is a great teacher that is clear and concise in his lectures and office hours. He's very caring and is willing to work with you always. His tests perfectly reflect all of the knowledge covered in the lectures and homework. I was worried that Calc 2 was going to be extremely difficult, as everyone says, but with Petar, I've never felt lost.

Nice guy but the class was very low energy. It was very hard to focus during the lectures because it seemed like he rolled out of bed with us. I just wish the lectures could be more engaging instead of information being spoken at us.

Seems to really care about his students and wants them to succeed. If you went to all the lectures and did all the homework I can't see why you would have any difficulty passing his class My one complaint would be that I'm not sure the class was hard enough. I think the rest of the MATH department can be brutal and this may not prepare you for that

Hope that Professor Beck is doing well despite a difficult time. She is good 1010 professor and not a harsh grader. There is a lot of writing that comes with this class, but even if you get behind you can turn things in for partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In our classroom, she's been very kind and understanding with everyone and it is easy to tell she cares about her students despite her personal hardships, but I felt the material at times could feel mundane since many asked "why" we were learning about some of the subjects other than how to write. A great professor, but an okay course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Grades papers at the end of the semester.

Professor Beck is great. Her lectures are very clear and easy to follow, and she always takes the time to make sure her students know what's expected of them. The material is interesting, and it's obvious that she cares. If you're sick, or if you have accommodations, then she is very understanding. I'd totally recommend her for writing 1010.
Easiest gen ed class to take. Discussion posts every week thats due on Wednesdays, and replying to 4 others due Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is one of the hardest graders I've ever had. You really on top of things if you want to get an A.There is a lot of reading on top of the normal lectures. There is also no extra credit. This class was also unbelievably hard for an intro class. If you want to take Art history and enjoy it, I would suggest having a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is great. If you don't like reading, then college isn't for you. Pretty simple, do the reading and everything else comes easy. This professor takes time to go beyond the lesson. If you want to pass her class just read; it isn't that hard if you read. Would recommend it to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: This professor has unbelievable grading standards and its a wonder anyone passes this class. Not at all what you would expect for a 1000 level intro course.

I did not like this class at all. It was nothing like I expected. One discussion post w 3 replies and one quiz a week. Though this doesn't sound like a lot. It was terrible. Discussion posts took me a minimum of 2 hours each week and the quizzes were quite difficult. She is a tough grader and doesn't provided sufficient feedback to correct mistakes

I took this 1000-level class as senior and this was the harshest grading Ive ever seen. I worked hard every week, but the vague criteria about careful looking was my downfall. Apparently careful looking doesnt mean mentioning and connecting details or even trying your best to. All this class teaches you is that your best isnt good enough.

I took this 1000 level course to discover more about the masters of art and I was sorely disappointed. This class had unclear guidelines and no examples of what kind of answers are expected. We're told to "compare and contrast" various artwork with little formal analysis examples provided. If you're not an art major, steer clear.

If you're not an art person, don't take this class. The "careful looking" she grades on each week is not intuitive unless you are artistically inclined. I found myself begging for help from my peers each week because I could not, no matter how hard I tried, understand and adhere to the expectations she has for the writing assignments.
Great professor! The course is clearly laid out with weekly discussions and a final project. I enjoyed the topics as they are open-ended and very creative! Would highly recommend this online course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Elizabeth is the kind of professor that all should strive to be. Respects your time, understands mistakes happen, and makes thoughtful material. 10/10 professor and easily the best online course ive taken.

I took Art 3010 & would recommend this class & this professor to anyone. Canvas is laid out very clearly, everything is straightforward, & as long as you do the assignments you'll get a good grade. Each week you do some reading, write a response to a prompt, & reply to 4 classmates. No quizzes or exams. Great class if you have a heavy schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy course, weekly canvas discussion. Don't need to buy the textbook as she uploads audio for each chapter when needed. Light course load and easy grading. Professor is kind and flexible. Interesting content.
EASY CLASS! She only posts one assignment (group discussion) weekly and one final but not complicated final project. I recommend her class.
This class is very easy as long as you complete all the assignments. However, I've noticed that the teacher isn't particularly responsive to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor that's very accommodating. This was the easiest course I have ever taken. Even easier than the 1000 level gen-eds. If you need a light gen-ed during a brutal semester, I can't recommend this enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you need an easy class in a heavy schedule this is the class for you. It's easy to do well if you budget a bit of time per week. The class was online but every time Prof Dewitte communicated with us she was kind and encouraging.

Dewitte is one of the kindest and most understanding teachers at the U. Her class is easy and the homework load is light. There are interesting concepts and ideas proposed in the class that can be very fun to engage with. There are no late penalties or deadlines for most of the coursework and the final project is very flexible

I took language of color online and it's an easy class. All you do is reply to 4 discussion posts and write one of your own. The assignments did take some thinking and time but nothing hard at all. If you need that credit for fine arts or something, this is a good choice.

Every week you have an online discussion. You have to submit at least 5 posts per discussion. At times, commenting 4 times can be somewhat maddening. These discussions completely make up your grade. You can work ahead if you want.
Easiest class I have ever taken. There is one canvas discussion each week and then one final project. Super easy and she is super chill about grading or things being late.

Took this online a year ago for an IR requirement. Literally the easiest thing ever. All the weekly readings were super interesting and the final project was completely up to you so long as it had SOMETHING to do with color (I did something with song lyrics). Elizabeth is very kind and super into creativity. Like 4 discussion posts a week.
literally the easiest class at the U. take 1010 for your art credit and 3010 for your IR credit and you'll thank me later. you write two paragraphs a week and respond to 4 discussion posts.

Color class? Was surprisingly interesting! It is an easy class which was nice. Assignments included online discussions and a final project/presentation. I basically took this class online even though it was in person because attendance was not mandatory. She is a very nice professor too, but don't expect her to answer any emails.
Easy A if you do the discussion posts. Don't buy the textbook because you can find everything online.
She is a fairly lenient grader, so getting an A is easy as long as you turn everything on time. The class was graded solely on weekly discussions and one final project on a topic of your choosing.

Great online class. She is really caring and understanding about deadlines which is nice since I am taking the course with the ongoing pandemic. Just lots of Canvas discussions you might scream sometimes. You have to comment like four times! I don't even talk to that many people in one day.

The class had many outdated example or subjects but it was really interesting to learn about a subject that we glance over everyday. The professor didn't communicate very often so didn't get to know them as a professor but enjoyed their class.

Overall I really like Elizabeth as an instructor. She did assign weekly discussion posts that made up most of your grade but they were fairly easy as long as you did the readings, which she uploaded to that week's assignment page on Canvas. She made an effort to include students in her lectures and promoted discussion in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: A mundane and soulless online Gen-Ed class that only requires participation for a 100% A+ grade. How many years it has been since she last updated this course, since 50% of the links in every module either has expired, doesn't work, or leads to some weird Russian site. Want some easy credits? Take this. Don't expect much tho. Don't buy the txtbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the easiest class I've every taken and one of the most lenient professors I've ever had. Her class was very interesting, and she was very passionate about the subject. The assignments are mostly online discussions and one group presentation, along with a final paper. She doesn't hesitate to answer questions or help a student out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! I took this class for an IR credit, and I'm glad I did. The homework was very easy, but still interesting and thought-provoking. She encourages student participation, but is understanding of those who aren't comfortable with speaking in front of the entire class.
ART 3010 is definitely one of the easiest classes I've ever taken at the U. Elizabeth was really lenient and extremely kind! If you still need an IR course, take ART 3010 with her.

This class is all writing. There are weekly online discussions, a midterm paper, and a final paper. She appreciates everyone's ideas. Got me thinking in a different way than usual (I'm not an art person, just needed a writing credit). The class is easy, but you'll need to remind yourself when the discussions are due or you can fall behind & take 0s
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Elizabeth is a sweet, caring professor. This class is an easy A if you do all the work. Weekly online discussion posts, as well as a presentation. She doesn't really lecture, the students each have to lecture one day. Does not take attendance or believe in tests. One final paper. This class is great for the IR credit.

Very easy to receive an A. Make weekly posts regarding the readings/artwork she posts for you to see, do a group presentation/or send her your notes on your part (if you don't want to present), write a final paper, and you're done.
I took this class online and it was very easy. Typical online class work which has you turn in something every week but other than that I would take again! Great way to fill  a general credit.

Dewitte's class was extremely easy. A few lectures were canceled, and not very many people show up. The lectures are pretty much entirely student led, which is the reason why I think many people skip out. Because the lectures are unrelated to the weekly assignments, it's easy to miss class and still get a good grade.

Elizabeth is a super nice lady. Her class was also pretty easy. Basically, the students will lead discussions, rather than her giving daily lectures, which I enjoyed. Art really isn't my thing, but if you're looking for an interesting class taught by someone who really enjoys the subject, Language of Color is a good one to take.

Take this class if you're only trying to get your general credits out of the way. Easy A, all you have to do is participate in group discussions, and write two papers! There are no tests. Would not recommend taking if you are planning on being an art major, though. I bought a book but didn't use it at all. Everything can be found online!
Does not teach

Prof Dewitte used the first few weeks of class purely for lecture without any kind of assignments, which set a specific tone for the class.  When she finally got things in order for class we had weekly readingassignmentsand discussions online, as well as student led discussions in class.  The students taught the majority of the class.

I would avoid this class. Scott is a very nice person but it's clear that he's slowed down. The lectures are a mess and have constant errors. Teaching yourself at home often doesn't work due to the same reason. No T/A felt like a slap in the face.
Scott is a great lecturer. There wasn't enough guidance for the quizzes/projects, often leaving you wondering what to study.

He often mis-speaks during his lectures so you have to be paying attention closely to make sure you don't get the wrong info. His slides are pretty bad for studying outside of class, they are mainly for his lectures so they are missing lots of key information. There are basically no other study resources so take notes for sure or you're in trouble.

Scott was okay. He is knowledgable about the material but he explains it all in a very confusing way. I usually had to go home and teach myself a different way. He will complain that no one comes to class, but his lectures aren't engaging and make things more confusing. His slides are all over the place and dont help to learn on your own.
I like his lectures even though they can get boring, funny guy. Lenient grader.
To state that this Professor is Self-Righteous would be an understatement. I feel for his family.
The Professor tries to teach kindness and empathy like our Lord and Savior yet he fails to realize he lives a prideful/boastful life.

Impressive that this Professor does two thing very well.  First, he gloats and brags about his prior job/position in the Bourgeoise industry. Second, he complains when students desire to show up to his gloat lectures are diminished. Please, if you read these ratings do not take this Professor. Stay Away!!!!!

Strongly advise against this professor, especially morning classes. Clear signs of cognitive difficulty; repeats himself constantly, mixes up his own sections, gives unclear assignment instructions, and provides disorganized, low-quality slides. No TA either. Genuinely nice person, but he should reduce his load. Drop immediately if there's no TA.

Curves grades across multiple class periods. Prof can understand that the 7:30 am class underperforms compared to his pm class. However, he cant comprehend that early am student are often busier with many additional responsibilities beyond that of a typical college student. Essentially, already disadvantaged students get a double hit!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof constantly preaches fairness. There is absolutely no allowance for missing class (not matter what!) and participation is graded. You'll miss vital communication, and he'll claim that the information was mentioned 3 classes in a row. When there is no allowance for life, you are grading people by privilege and luck. Life isnt fair btw, Becker.

Professor Becker is very knowledgeable and cares deeply about your success. He's there to help and gives good feedback. Given his background and experience, he's an excellent resource if you're curious about real-world application of the materials you're learning. You signed up to learn, so go to class and pay attention; you'll be fine. Recommend!

His slide decks are horrible. A disorganized mess that is extremely tough to understand if you miss a lecture. There is no step-by-step explanation to solving problems, only a clutter of numbers, arrows, signage, and other unclear labeling.

Becker is such a great professor, he is super clear with what he grades you on. If you go to class you will succeed. He is funny, engaging, and truly wants all of his students to do well in the class. Dont buy the text book for int acctg, I never read it and was kinda a waste. Study the lecture slides for quizzes and you will do fine.

lets say you don't go to class you are damned you cant pass his quizzes because he will give you the worst things on the quiz and as for the materials to study from he has these lecture ppts from which there will only be 15% on the quiz. When the class average lies around 60 percent i dont see a problem in the students but the professor.

He is extremely inaccessible outside of class. Also complained multiple times about the majority of students failing his confusing quizzes, but if more than half of the class is failing its def on him. Has trouble speaking succinctly and there were typos on everything. Tries to trick you on EVERY quiz, but the 2 exams are definitely easier.

passionate, gifted. i did horrible in philip jeff's Fin 2 so i was really scared to take Fin 3 but becker is AMAZING at breaking down each new concept logically, step by step, little by little, and gives lots of small quizzes that he goes through afterwards in class. SO HELPFUL. i hear his exams are really hard though and i havent had a midterm yet

I am obsessed with this man. Take as many of his classes as possible!!!! The material is really difficult but he is more than willing to help you and don't be afraid to ask questions, sometimes he gets ahead of himself so if you raise your hand and ask him to repeat or slow down he totally will. I wish I could have him as my prof for every class.

Excellent professor. He was able to teach complicated topics in simple and easy to understand ways. I would recommend taking this class. It definitely takes work but as long as you do what you're supposed to do you'll do well. He will help you succeed if you take initiative.

Scott is very uncoordinated and sloppy. The tests and quizzes frequently had typos and clarification issues. It was annoying to constantly interrupt our test-taking and have him explain the corrections we needed to make to a question. He also has trouble speaking succinctly and smoothly which made it hard to follow his thought process.

Scott Becker is amazing. He taught this class so well! His lectures are always engaging and helpful. The material covered in this class is definitely challenging, but so long as you attend the lectures and follow the suggested problems he gives, you can manage. He is eager to answer any questions his students have. I would absolutely recommend him.

Scott is a great professor. If you can, wait to take 5140 until 2024. He is still figuring out how to teach the course and it suffered a bit due to that. Everything we did in class all followed the exact same set of facts, but then the in class quizzes would be slightly different, which made me feel unprepared for them no matter how long I studied.

Scott is an incredible professor hands down.  His experience in the field is unmatched and it makes for some really interesting and engaging lectures.  He is entertaining and makes boring concepts interesting by tying them in with his past work experiences.  Although the material is difficult, he makes it easy to understand.

He is an awesome professor. He makes sure that you understand the material for this class. This is a hard class so you should be ready to spend time for doing the quizzes, homeworks and Mconnect. He is a fun professor and he is actively searching for feedback. You definitely should take this class even it is not mandatory at the U of U anymore.

Scott is one of the clearest and best instructing professors I have had at the DESB. He makes difficult concepts easy to understand and it's obvious he knows what he is talking about. I took this class as a summer accelerated course, which was a lot of work, but Scott made it much easier than it could have been.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was not as hard as you think. If you keep up with his lectures and study hard, you will pass this class! Fall2020 taught 100% online, lectures can be boring because no one participates, but Becker delivers. Exams aren't always clear on what to study or good examples of prep material but his slides hold the key. You must STUDY for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was an intro class for accounting but he didn't teach in a way that was easy to understand for someone who had never learned accounting before. He definitely knew what he was talking about during the lectures but he didn't simplify it down enough for the class to understand. Great guy and very charismatic, he expected attendance/participation.

Honestly, I didn't find the class that hard despite the rumors. His tests are extremely fair. If you do practice problems from his slides and the suggested book practice problems, you'll be completely fine. You definitely have to apply what you've learned, and his "CFO questions" make up a lot of your grade, but he doesn't test anything not taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Scott is a great guy as well as a great professor. The class itself is pretty hard and you will have to study a good amount regardless of which professor you have. If you take this class, Becker is the one to get.

This professor is not helpful with this course. He teaches the easiest material and tests on the absolute hardest material. It is impossible to prepare for his tests because you are going to see problems 10X harder than any practice problem he goes over.

Scott is the best professor I've ever had. The subject is HARD. But Scott does a great job teaching it. Treats you like an adult rather than a child. Will always make time to meet with you outside of class. He wants you to succeed and is a big encourager for continuing on to the MACC program. I would take any class Scott is teaching. Favorite one.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're an accounting major you basically cannot avoid this guy (yet) so here's some advice: 1. If I'm wrong and you can avoid him, do it. 2. His tests are nothing like his lectures, averages are always in the low 70s. Curves are always ridiculous, my B- got curved to an A. 3. He is completely inaccessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Scott is VERY knowledgeable when it comes to this subject. He has real life experience which is really appreciated from most students. The class is extremely tough, but Professor Becker does a good job.

Professor Becker is very versed on the language of accounting (he was the CFO at Qualcomm). He is caring and tries to learn everyone's name. The Accounting department makes all the quizzes and tests for all the ACCTG 2600 classes and he prepares you for all of them if you are willing to take advantage of office hours and are willing to go to class.

Scott Becker is one of the most charismatic people I've ever met, but he isn't an extraordinary professor. His quizzes are quite difficult and often feature questions concerning concepts he didn't teach. Becker has real-life experience, which is great, but his lectures didn't teach me anything that the textbook could not.

If you want an "A" in this class, then I highly suggest you read the chapters and take notes and do the homework before his lectures. The professor moves fast during his lectures and they help clarify accounting methods that you read about the night before. He will also call on you in class whether you know an answer or not. So be ready for that!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, really cares about his students, and wants them to succeed. He tries to learn everyones' names and creates an engaging learning environment. If you need help or are confused he will make time to to help you.  One of my favorite professors at the U.

If you've never taken accounting, and have no clue where to start professor Becker makes it easy. There are weekly quizzes, which are usually harder than the exams. I used the book to study for exams and quizzes which was helpful. He will always meet with you, and had a TA that was also very helpful. Great professor, he made accounting interesting.

One of my absolute favorite teachers I've ever had at the U. He was engaging, memorized everyone's name and made lectures really interesting. There was only about 1 thing of homework a night but it wasn't especially hard . Quizzes once a week but if you went to class and did the reading it was easy. Midterms and final were pretty hard.

Professor Becker is a great instructor. Lectures are great and he teaches well. However, he didn't prepare you for the quizzes and exams. Homework and in class examples were much easier than what was covered on quizzes and exams. Conceptual questions on exams were ambiguous. He taught the 2600 class as if it was a 5000 level course.

He is well-organized and his top priority is making sure everyone is in position to succeed. His mind can sometimes be all over the place during lectures and it might get confusing. He doesn't erase the board very well, which might be a pet peeve of some, but that's just nit-picking. There is definitely a lot to learn from Professor Becker.

Scott is a great teacher but a hard one. His tests are completely different from his lectures/in class problems and the average on them is in the low 70s. The good thing is the class is curved. Scott is a great lecturer I just didn't like the way he tested. It was confusing and completely opposite from the homework. It was the hardest B I ever got.

Prof Becker does a really good job of drilling in the basics. This class is mostly comprehensive and it's crucial you understand the first chapters. He constantly teaches you the basics and it makes the tough midterms and finals a lot easier.
Great professor I definitely recommand him. He's very clear on his lectures. He replies to your emails pretty quick. Take his class

Professor Becker is so great. He is laid back and is available to students when they need help. I emailed him and got response within the same day! He is also personable, very organized, and prepared for his lectures. He gives you a heads up on his tests and doesn't test you on anything he doesn't lecture on. He also drops  2 lowest quiz scores.
Insanely understanding professor and actually cares about his students.
Great professor! You can tell he cares about his students and gives great lectures. In it for love of the game, not a paycheck.
Ben is super awesome! He's a great guy and obviously cares about his students. 10/10 would recommend.
He had a chill vibe hes a cool dude and likes the course material even sometimes its a little boring. Tests weren't too hard and the labs you get guided through not much to worry about.
Super easy class and professor. He likes teaching this course and actually cares about the students. This class never stressed me out, but I still retained the material.

This professor really cares about the material and relies heavily on slides. Attending class is helpful and mandatory. Each class had an in-class activity, followed by a quiz next session. Labs were done in class but could be completed independently using the step-by-step Canvas videos.

Professor Repak is an amazing professor who geniunly care about his students and wants to see his students suceed. He cares that each student geniunly learns his content and know how to teach and get the point across while still being funny and bringing some light heardness to a class.
Honestly he's just such a nice dude. Always very willing to work with people if problems come up.
Great professor! He's very knowledgeable, funny, and personable. 10/10 would recommend
Labs can be tedious and sometimes not directly related to lecture material. Decent professor with good slides. Lectures can be a bit dry if you don't really care about the material.
Great  professor, helped me a lot.

Not a hard class, the only hard thing was the group project because of how long it is so make sure to start it ASAP. He also does give you a lot of opportunities to work on the project and get feedback on it which was helpful.
The class material itself is not difficult but the workload is very intensive. Make sure you don't fall behind in this class because he's not that nice about offering extensions on the labs

This class covers a lot of material and has a huge end-of-the-semester project that you start at the beginning of the semester. Make sure to start early so that you don't fall behind. It's not that bad of a class if you have a good group. The T.A. I had was a very harsh grader but helpful and supportive. But sometimes kind of mean.

Ben is amazing. I would encourage everyone to show up as much as possible. He's got a great sense of humor but is also extremely insightful. He's also very understanding and remembers what it's like to be a student so he doesn't make the class overwhelming. Easily the best IS prof, and one of my all time favorites. The TA (Leyna) was amazing too!!

By far one of the best professors of the School of Business. He is focused on making sure people learn from this class and other classes by creating a single, continuous feedback project where he and his TAs tell you what needs to be fixed and generally how. You will leave these classes having actually learned something, and that says a lot.

Prof Ben Repak is a kind and humble instructor with an outstanding teaching style. My experience in his class has been exceptional, as I gained valuable knowledge and practical skills through group projects and class activities. The final project is especially effective, helping build transferable skills.  10/10!
You got out of this class what you put into it. Some of the course info overlaps with other courses but it was a good refresher or a good stepping stone into those other more advanced classes.
This is the best professor I have ever had in university. Even though the course is very difficult.

Ben is an awesome professor! Easily my favorite in the IS department. He is such a genuine and down to earth guy, and he does his best to work with students. The subject matter wasn't my favorite but Ben is able to make lectures much more interesting and tolerable. 10/10!!!!
Ben is great. I would recommend his class. His class is fairly straightforward. The group project is fairly difficult, but he is more than willing to help you and give you lots of feedback.

Professor Repak was a great caring professor who laid out what was needed for the course.  As long as you are up to date with the group project throughout the semester, it is very manageable. Professor Repak overall is a very helpful, caring, and fun professor and I would take another class from him.

The class is exceptionally well-structured, making it a breeze to follow and learn from, especially as an online course. The effort and dedication to both the subject matter and students shines through, making the learning experience deeply enriching. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class, very reasonable workload and he professor is very understanding
He is a very competent professor, knows his classes and adjusts his homework and lectures each semester to promote original work. Very easy to talk to and responds quickly to students
Thorough and easy to learn from.
Ben is a great instructor. Although this was taken online I've also taken him in person, he makes things super easy to understand.

One of the most well-organized classes I have ever taken! Each week there are lecture videos to watch as well as clear outlines of what to accomplish and submit. Ben is always willing to meet if you have any questions about the labs or group project. Start early on the project and work on it throughout the semester or you'll regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ben CARES about his students. He truly puts in the time and effort to make us as successful as possible. Everything in his classes is straightforward, and even when you have a question, Ben is there for you. The best professor at the U by a landslide. YOU ROCK BEN! KEEP BEING AWESOME!!!!!!!!!!!

Ben is one of the best professors I've had at the U. Super accessible for office hours, willing to work with student's schedules, very flexible with different levels of understanding in his courses. His canvas courses are set up extremely well, so just attend class, pay attention, and GET THE GROUP PROJECT DONE EARLY.

Ben Repak is my favorite professor in the IS program so far, and he says the funniest tidbits in class! His class moves at a steady pace which allows you to learn SQL smoothly. He's always available for help outside of class hours when it comes to labs and the group project - utilize this! Make sure to get with a good group for the final project.
The course is well structured and given with a lot of enthusiasm. Always looked forward to his classes and learned a lot!

Ben is very supportive and is available and open to meet whenever you need. I utilized this often. However, you wouldn't have to meet so much if he actually explained how to do more of the technical requirements for the project (logical and physical ERDs and DFDs). Overall he is good, just difficult due to lack of technical instructional lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ben did a great job making tough material more interesting and easier to understand!
Great professor, cares a lot about his class and truly wants everyone to learn. Would highly recommend.
Ben is excellent at presenting the course material. He was always willing to listen and help his students be successful. He also adds a healthy dose of humor that made the class more fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ben teaches the most well put-together classes in the IS school. He goes at an excellent pace, and you'll leave feeling like you've learned a lot. He really takes time to make sure you understand what's going on. All the homework feels valid, no busy work. The labs/group project can take a long time but if you stay on top of them you'll be fine.
Ben is a great professor! gives great feedback and the lab actually helps in understanding the material and is useful.
Ben Repak was a great professor. He provided good hands on experience with SQL and kept class interesting and engaging. Good beginner class for database fundamentals. He can also be pretty funny

I took Professor Repak over a summer program in which he taught his IS 4420 class in only 10 days with 4 hours each day, and I was amazed. I learned many valuable lessons about database development and design and although there was a cram at the end to finish our group project, he worked with us a ton and was extremely helpful. Highly recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ben was one of the most engaging online professors I've had. COVID has made things rough and I appreciated Ben's engaging teaching style. He is eager to give feedback and provides ample opportunities to get your work checked. He engages with the students like he's one of us, like he's our friend and I really appreciated his effort in that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Repak is an excellent professor. You can tell that he put a lot of effort into the class to make it a great experience (it works). He provides excellent feedback and provides real-world/applicable experiences. He does not have unrealistic expectations of students, every grade was fair and lenient. One of the best professors that I've had

This was the second class I took from Ben and he is hands down the best IS professor at the U. Brings relevant and hands on knowledge into the classroom. Encourages students to reach out if they need help understanding any concepts. Breaks concepts into easy to understand lectures and PPTs. Highly recommend taking all the classes you can from him.

Ben is by far and away the best professor in the IS department. He makes tough concepts easy to understand and makes it very clear what he wants done on assignments. Would highly recommend taking his class.
My second class from Ben and just reinforces why i enjoyed his course the first time.

Ben is hands down the best IS professor I've had at the U. His lectures are interesting and he actually pulls real world experience into them. For being a three hour night class, these were easy to get through. A lot of homework but it isn't bad and actually helps you. The group project blows if you got bad people in your group, so get to work fast

Loved taking this class. It is kind of a challenging course since there is so much to learn. Ben really wants to have you succeed and understand WHY. He makes time for you if you need some extra help outside of class, which is much appreciated. :)
Ben is an excellent instructor. He's clear in his presentation of the material, and is very obviously knowledgeable about the subject. He also has real-world experience which is super helpful.

Instructor was Awesome. Course was online, but Instructor made sure we had as much help and information available for students to succeed. His response to emails or Canvas messages were very fast. Always kept class updated on what was going on in the Course. If you are really good at following directions, this course won't be too hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This teacher is really willing to work through any questions that you might have. He cares a lot about your success and will do everything in his power to help you do well! Would recommend him,  he is especially helpful when navigating an online computer class.
Sent constant messages to class and was always willing to provide information and help for class. Easy class, like 3 hours of homework due once a week.

I stopped going to class because he expected us to know everything before coming into the course. Nice guy, worst lecturer I've had in a while. Lectures were boring and examples were never done. I had to teach this class to myself using O-Chem Tutor and Khan Academy. Never knew how to answer questions in depth. Tests are similar to practice tests.

Steve was one of the worst teaching professors I have ever had. He clearly cared about what we were learning, but had unrealistic expectations about our prior understanding of the course for an entry-level class. He assigned a lot of homework and rarely answered questions during his bland, monotone lectures. Not a great professor, but a nice guy.
The worst optics professor in The U. Don't ever take his classes.
He's a very lay back teacher, but he knows a lot.  He cancels his classes a lot for minor issues like catching a cold.
Great guy, not a great teacher. Slides were all over the place and hard to follow. Tests were fair, as long as you put in a lot of work you should do fine in the class.

Questions on test are inconsistent with lecture content. Lectures are boring and he often goes sideways during his lectures. If you want to remain sane during your last year as a biology student DO NOT take this professor. If this class with David is required for you to graduate, I recommend either changing your emphasis or your degree.

Class completely forgets the premise of college. College should be for teaching concepts and ideas, opening the doors for further exploration and interest. This entire class is a training in rote memorization of unimportant, useless "quick facts". Too many papers. Too much useless information. Lectures are boring and class is very disorganized.

For biochem, Blair is great compared to Horvath (other instructor who co-teaches biochem). But Blair's hw sets didn't always reflect what was tested on. He is a nice, funny guy, but w/o an instructor who is savvy with teaching techniques, the course material is hard to digest. Most of his material involved memorization of cycles + structures (fyi).

Blair a wildly intelligent guy and very interested it what he teaches. Exams 100% require some studying. Problem Sets are time consuming but straight forward. If you just show up to class there are lots of free points and he'll subtly guide your studying. Class is fascinating if you're actually interested in biology. Probably very hard if not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a beast. Taught with horvath and they both are not great in different ways. Blair is a great guy, but his lectures are way too vague and far to dense to even know how/what to study for exams. Also why on earth do we have an exam a week before our cumulative final? someone put me out of my misery i beg of you

Colectured with Horvath in my semester - Know cycles for exam. He sometimes asks about name and sometimes not. First half of class was alot easier than the last half (about 3 times more content). His final was harder than I thought, giving us mean of 88/160. Does not give past exams like Horvath do. All I can say is study broad and not too deep.

If you don't need this class, DON'T TAKE IT. I've taken him twice, and his lecture style is disorganized. He either doesn't cover all of the slides, or runs through them so fast you can't keep up. All of the stuff will still be on the exam, though! You will have to read at least two research papers a week, and know them inside and out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Made me want to slam my head on the table. Exams are random trivia he mentions maybe once.When asked what will be on final, he says, "everything." Thanks David, that was really helpful :). Expected to know all information on slides AND every paper you have to possibly read in that class. TA for that class is absolutely useless and condescending
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is possibly the worst class I have EVER taken. You think the exams are hard? NO, wait until the final. He gives you NOTHING. No reviews, no guidance as to what is going to be on the exam, NOTHING, you are expected to know not only the 40+ lecture slides with 95% of information that he won't ask you, but also required to know 50+ papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm convinced that the point of this class is to show you that you know nothing. You have to read SO many papers. The homeworks take hours upon hours to complete. The exams made me want to pull my hair out. It's ridiculous that this class is required for all biology majors. Very hard with uninteresting lectures that just made me want to drop out.

The first half of his content was laid out clearly and expectations were very clear on what we were supposed to know. The second half was chaotic and he was very vague about how much we should know - and he didn't give many study materials. He's very laid back and his test questions are fair, but sometimes tested on concepts he mentioned in passing

Dr. Blair was really relaxed in lecture but he goes off on tangents. Loves to incorporate scientific papers into homework assignments which can be hard to read. A lot of his content is focused on memorization and I spent a LOT of time studying for his exams. He doesn't provide a lot of study guides so you are on your own to figure it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: David's a cool guy, cares about his students, and has interesting lectures. Studying for tests was difficult, he crams a lot into his lectures and picks random parts to test you on but hardly guides you on what to study. His tests are all from lectures, so pay attention to those. You read a lot of scientific papers.

Dr. Blair is very misleading and memorization-focused. He is generally kind, but he would often say "I don't care about structures" and then test you on exactly that. If he didn't explicitly say he didn't care about certain topics, I wouldn't say this at all, but it was genuinely frustrating to be directly mislead.

Highly recommend not taking this course.Professor Blair is understanding and caring of his students but his lectures are very dry, not engaging, and hard to get through. Professor Blair also gives little to no instruction of how to prepare for exams and therefore exams are very difficult due to unclarity of what will show up on the exam.

Take another course. Professor Blair is very friendly but his lectures are extremely dry and you end up having to self study. This course would be greatly improved if he recorded his lectures and didn't make attendance mandatory. The amount of reading for this class is unreal and you have to memorize multiple studies for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredibly dry. Frequently unclear what you're actually supposed to know. About 80% of the points on any given exam will be based on knowledge of random bits of trivia, recall of the papers he assigns, and visual memory of biochemical diagrams shown in class. Not understanding or accessible. Avoid if possible.

Prof. Blair is passionate about Microbio & it shows! Incorporates lots of papers into his lecture (skim over them at least). Recommend knowing your Chem/Biochem before taking this to understand the concepts. Textbook is optional but helps your understanding. Midterms are fair & based on lecture material. Lots of in class activities for easy credit.

Professor Blair is awesome! Besides exams there are many other ways to get points for his 3370 class. I liked that there were always class activities at the end reinforcing the concepts we had just learned.

Dave is a great professor. Super passionate about what he is teaching and really cares about his students. He makes an effort with every student in his class. Pay attention and you won't have trouble with the exams.
Dr. Blair is an absolute mad lad. Very knowledgeable about biochem and explained all my high school chemistry woes away. Definitely would take a class from him again. Funny and quirky.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible professor, did not learn a single from him, had to self teach for his exams. Don't take this class from this dude, quality of life goes down.

Dr. Blair is really passionate about microbial biology and does a great job teaching the subject and making it interesting. This is a class I enjoyed particularly because it took concepts I learned in other biology classes and made them easier to understand or put them into a new context. TAs are super and Dr. Blair is easy to approach as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I honestly loved Dr. Blair. I think his lectures are good and give all the information you need, even if sometimes it's a lot. He doesn't post any lectures or notes, so definitely utilize the TAs. Special shoutout to Justin because he's hilarious and the best. Dr. Blair is funny himself and enjoys a good time and being involved with his students.

Tough to rate this class, David is awesome, super funny and great guy, but the format of the class is difficult. No notes posted online, lots of reading, 4 exams, a final, and 3 problem sets. Wouldn't "recommend" it, but I've had worse classes. The TAs are your best resources here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really interesting class! I loved this teacher so much! I highly recommend taking this course if you're interested in microbes.  Requires you to read scientific papers weekly, which was the most important skill I've learned at the u. Once you get used to the class, you will understand what it takes to get an A and it is definitely doable!

This class requires so much reading. Several chapters a week plus one or two research papers (don't skip the chapter readings). He gets animated about things, and calls a lot of microbes "cute". It gets annoying. There are no lecture slides, be prepared to take everything by handtablet. It's difficult, 60-70% class average. A lot of work needed.
Interesting class uses primary literature.  Super cool guy.  Final exam weighted heavily on material that was taught right before the final.

Class was really hard. I studied my butt off and went to as many discussions as possible! Justin was my TA. He was smart, but was also taking the class the first time with us (which is funny because he did great!). If you read the chapters and study after each lecture, you will get an A! DO IT! or you will fail miserably.

Simon was a lovely instructor. He made an effort to engage with students and I felt cared for. His demonstrations on Illustrator and Photoshop are definitely fast paced, but if you request for him to slow down he will. I know the basics of the above Adobe applications, so he taught successfully! Plus he is a funny guy, made for an enjoyable course.

Simon is an amazing teacher, his lectures are fun and intersting, he helps with whatever you need and provides good feedback. His class was always intersting and all of the projects were fun and interesting.

Simon was my literal saving grace this term (1/2 Spring). I was having SUCH a hard time with my other classes and he was the only class I actually enjoyed going to. Very easy if you have prior experience with photoshop and illustrator. Honestly a very easy A-- however attendance is mandatory (1/3 grade drop EACH missed class) and can be tedious.

Simon is a fun professor. He will always have a great dad joke when you least expect it. He gives excellent feedback that helps with any final project. Don't get off of class earlier because you don't like to see Simon mad.

What a silly guy, honestly, with interesting lore. He is great at explaining things but he does go through demos/explanations quickly, so make sure to ask him to slow down if you need to. His feedback and one-on-one help is also great. Something to note is that his due dates are at very specific times. You will be docked points if late.

Wonderful professor; moves fast in class but gives help one on one if asked. Lots of assignments but they are not too difficult and go quick. Your work will be shown to the whole class for peer reviews, but the professor is kind and gives good feedback. Attendance is important, work isn't graded harshly, do your best and you're likely to succeed.

Really great professor and class. Very easy going and organized. All assignments/demos/projects are under canvas with video assistance. Assignments are fun and challenging, but not too difficult for beginners. Provides new perspective on business side of BFA. Talks fast during lectures but is aware - will slow down when informed.

The project load seemed overwhelming at first but most projects were easy enough to be completed in class alongside the demonstration for how to do them! Prof. Blundell was very good at explaining the programs in a way that made them understandable. 10/10 I DO recommend. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Blundell was really good. I took a beginning graphic design class with him and really enjoyed it. He helps each student when needed and gives good feedback. Only when he's demonstrating a new tool in Adobe he goes very fast and if you don't keep up you'll get completely lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you enjoy photography, then this is an amazing class to take. Professor Blundell gives amazing feedback on your work. He allows you to explore different types of photography and hone your skills in a specific area.
Goes really fast during demonstration, so don't space out , talk, or look at your phone during, or else you'll be very lost.
Simon is like a friend more than a professor, he is easy to talk to and really helps solve issues in your work. Sit in the front of the class, he moves fast.

Dr. Black is outstanding: brilliant, well-read, has very high standards, genuinely cares about his students.  Take a class from him if you came to the U to get a world class education.  Do the following: *Attend every class *Read the assigned materials closely *Make thoughtful comments in class *Meet with him one-one-one to get & give feedback

He's not arrogant, he just wants you to be able to defend your statements in class and in papers and he makes he you think critically on the spot more than any professor I've had. The assignments are easy, he lets the class spearhead the discussion and he guides it, it just requires students to participate. Don't take if you are lazy.

I took ENGL 3600.  You will have 3 papers in this class from about 5 - 7 pages.  You will have a fair amount of reading.  And some short writing assignments.  At first I didn't like Scott, but after a while he grew on me.  The thing Scott wants in his papers is a good close reading.  Close reading is the key.  He will improved your writing.

A plug for Scott.  I guess he could seem "arrogant" on first blush--he's a bit shy--but you'll find he's one of the kindest and most humble professors you could ever hope to meet at a big research university.  Also, I feel he deserves a "hot" pepper.

The comment about Skeet Shooting is kind of true, but Scott makes up for it with his friendly personality and willingness to help students learn.  Good grades aren't easy in Scott's class, but if you're willing to work for it, Scott gives his students as many opportunities as they want, so getting an "A" simply comes down to effort.

Although I wouldn't disagree with the comments about his class often seeming like an intellectual skeet shoot, or the a slight air of arrogance, I would also say that his course was one of the most intellectually stimulating, and that he has a genuine desire to help the students learn.  unlike some profs i've had at the U, scott was always willing

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. He would answer any questions you had without making you feel dumb at all. Some professors have a very hard time with this.

I have had him for two classes and he is a very good teacher. He's a funny guy and if you go to class you can get some extra credit and is very far. Stay for all of your tests.(may turn into a group test during the test)
He is hilarious, helpful and unpredictable. He is an organized person, would engage in any kind of discussion with his students. Generally, he is such a great professor for this course.

So far the best professor I have had. He cares about how well you do in the class and keeps your hopes after bad exam scores. Though the material is tough, there are A LOT of opportunities to raise up your grade if you are willing to put in the time. I got under 70% on the 2 midterms, but passed the final and finished with a B. Amazing professor

He is fun and a hilarious teacher. I did not think he was very approachable. His tests are very hard and he gives you a lot of homework. I didn't think it was a fair amount of work. dont take his class with a lot of other hard classes. It takes up a lot of time keeping up with this class.

He is excellent at teaching, his passion for math is evident in his lectures.  He works his sense of humor into lectures.  He is always available to help with material and patient and concise in his explanations.  A+, would take him again.

Excellent new teacher. Naturally talented guy. Keeps the class fun and airy and presents super complicated mathematical stuffs in very clear, very digestible terms. Has a good sense of humor and will use it to keep you on your toes. Course is not easy by any means, but if you must take it then take it with this guy; you won't find anyone better.

He is a very fair instructor and is always willing to help!  He holds extra review sessions and posts review problems prior to exams.  His exams sometimes are quite challenging but that's probably because of how much material was covered.  He seems to care about teaching and what's more, he is quite funny!  Engaging instructor.

Solid undergrad econometrics course. The material is dry by nature, so lectures are dry too. Professor Bhatachary clearly tries her best: slides are fine and grading is fair, just three exams.Uses Stata. For anyone going into consulting, the class will help. Not exciting, but effective. Recommended if you just want to get good at econometrics.

4651 was not a difficult class, but good lord was it difficult to get through.  There is virtually no engagement with students whatsoever, and your entire grade is based upon three tests out of 50 points each.  This is not a hard class, but my only advice is to USE TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She teaches the class in a purely Mathematical, proof-based matter. The slides will be hard (especially at the end of class) to follow if you are not a math major. The lectures are boring and hard to follow. 

However, the tests are easy, and she gives an easy template to follow to ace them all. 

Overall, take for an easy A.

This was an online course, so the lectures was recorded. She focuses a lot on theory. She is not super approachable. Assignments can be hard, especially in Stata, but if you work hard enough you will get good grades. Meet people in that class and work together. It made it easier for me and helped me find a nice squad. Ask and she'll help.

Absolutely the worst professor I've experienced during my time at this university. She clearly has no knowledge about teaching. All lectures are reused recorded classes from 2020, and she does not put any effort into quality teaching. I have no doubt that she could be a good lecturer if every student already knew everything about the subject.

She is not an unskilled professor but simply an unmotivated one. She teaches mostly through recorded videos that are incredibly low effort and difficult to follow. Found myself trying to learn through google searches instead of her curriculum.
prof bhattacharya was a professor i learned a lot from. her lectures were to the point, presented using slides and her exams and assignments were related to real world problems. take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you want a good grade and low time commitment for econ 3640 this professor is for you. Just keep in mind this was online for me it could be different if it's in-person in the future.

This is an Asian history class and Prof. Bhatacharya is teaching this for the first time. She did an amazing job. Learned so much about South Asia. Presentations, discussions, etc made this so interesting class. I highly recommend it.

reviews.comment: Very hard and interesting class. Bhatacharay is very clear and cares about the students. Take the class if you want to learn any statistics.

reviews.comment: Given that I plan to attend grad school, I have a new appreciation for what a valuable Prof. Bhattacharya is for this class. It is clear that she has lots of experience with the material. She can be a bit monotone in the delivery, but the subject is equally dry. She gives a solid foundation in metrics.
She is a great professor. While at times the content is a bit beyond dry, she brings with it a refreshing sense of relevance. I will encourage others to take the class.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bhattacharya's class is entirely lectures. There are lots of in-class assignments, and your grade is based on exams. Even though the subject can be dry, she does her best by providing examples that make things more interesting. She genuinely cares about her students and I'd recommend taking his class if you feel okay with statistics.
