reviews.comment: Read the text and skip lecture because Haimanti delivers lectures so infuriatingly boring and ineffectual that if you do attend, you'll wish you were sitting through a root canal instead. If I failed 4651, I would probably drop out of school because digging ditches for the rest of my life sounds much more fun than retaking this class.

Classes was extremely boring, professor didn't speak loud enough and I had a hard time understanding her accent. Exams were straight forward with assignments and review though. I felt going to class had little effect on me learning the course content.

Don't take this class from her if you can, she's an utter failure as a professor.  Lectures are dry, and you'll go into your tests not even knowing what they're about. I'll put it like this, she let us use our computers and anything else available to us in an introductory stats course(Not even mathematical stats) and most of the class still failed.

Prepare to study like you are about to fail, because you are. You are forced to guess what she expects of you, and she litteraly will get a huge smile on her face when she tells you that you are wrong. By far the worst teacher I have ever had!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She reads heavily from powerpoints and the expounds on the vague ideas in the powerpoint. If you go to class every time and take decent notes, the tests are no problem. Getting past the accent takes focus. She emphasis proper notation heavily, you can tell she is very passionate about it. The classes are lecture heavy, with virtually no homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took this Economic Stats class in Spring of 2016 to prepare for Econometrics. Easily one of the worst teachers ive ever had. Im not sure if it was her thick accent or the dry and boring lectures,I honestly didnt learn a thing in her class. It is easy to slide by with a passing grade because everyone bombs the tests which results in a strong curve

Professor bhatacharya taught behavioral economics. the class was fascinating partly due to the material and her clear explanations. the class is good for you if you know some basic mathematics and logic. go for it.

Haimanti took a potentially interesting subject, game theory, and made it really dry and boring. Lectures were long and not interesting. Would have preferred a text book, so I could clarify topics that i zoned out on. Would not recommend her as a professor.

She takes attendance so you need to go. Lectures are hard to pay attention to, not sure if its because of her accent or the depth that she goes into on the subject. She is very passionate about it, and wants students to succeed. Most assignments are group projects, and tests aren't too bad( even if you don't know that much).
I was not sure abt the class before. but after it ended i am glad i took it from her. it was a super class and i learned a lot...

Super smart with relevant experience that she shares in the classroom. She is old school with explanations and they can be lengthy but if you put in effort, you will get results. She is challenging but completely fair and there is no reason to get a disappointing grade from her. She is also quite arranged. Find out for yourself.
Hard to pay attention, might be my short attention span or it could be because shes hard to understand
Great prof, makes the material interesting.
If you put good effort in and actually study, you'll get guaranteed good grades. Unlike other profs, she actually goes over things slowly to make certain you understand and doesn't leave you going.

This is my first econometrix class. it is a dry subject but prof. bhatacharaya did a nice job. i am also now familiar with how to handle data in statistical packages. i am happy that i learned this from her. very nice.
Her class is just one of the best in the econ dept. Clear explanations, good material and alwahs helpful.

She was very hard to understand ans would jump around in the material so much that when the test came no one knew what to do.  I had a low score and asked her for help of which she replied that I would have to figure it out on my own. terrible
So nice and such an easy class! Love him so much!
sweetest professor ever, very understanding with conflicts, easy course and workload overall, and attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMERICAN GEM. I WOULD DO ANYTHING FOR KEVIN HE IS SO AMAZING. He is the kindest and sweetest man. The whole class is grades by one project and as long as you do not bomb it, you'll get an A. He is open to improving his class each semester and he makes the classroom fun even for introverts. Love this class.

This class is graded only on participation and one final group project. Throughout the semester, you work with a team to create a marketing campaign for a real-world client. This class was a lot of fun and as long as you show up and contribute to your project, you're guaranteed an A. Prof. Bischoff was always very helpful both in and out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took ENTP. I really like her; I thought she gave good lectures and provided real-world insights. She encouraged us to use personal experiences in weekly assignments, and always answered questions out of class. Exams were not hard, just do the practice tests and read and you will be fine. Would absolutely recommend her to anyone
She's caring and the class is easy. The lectures are boring but if you do all the work you'll be completely fine for the tests. Highly recommend. She wants to see you succeed.

Having taken two of Bing's classes, she is a decent and caring professor! She is easy to communicate with and very kind. Prepare to do reading, as her slides don't cover all the material. The workload can be heavy at times and feels like busy work. I do wish her slides were a bit clearer, as they sometimes do not align with questions on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are messy and hard to follow since she jumps around in the power points. There's weekly quizzes which are easy but the tests are much harder. There's a group presentation and final paper but you can choose your group, or be put in a random one.

This is my second time taking her class and I really enjoy listening to her lectures. She communicates very well and wants everyone to succeed. She gave very good feedback on our group presentations and is always available for questions.
She was a great professor that did a good job at teaching the material. I found the class relatively easy. Take her if you can

I don't want to be too hard on her, because for the most part she is fine. I had her for BCOR2040 as well as STRAT3700 and the classes are virtually identical. My big complaint is that her exams are lazily written. There are typos and the questions are written unclearly. It's clear that she doesn't review exam questions before publishing on canvas.

Bing was a really good professor. She has a talent to teach this beginner bcor class and make it manageable. All the work was due on one day, and in my opinion the work wasn't too hard. The class was 2 hours, but she always fit everything into 80 min which was very nice. I would very much recommend taking this class from her.

Bing Su was the best 2040 teacher I could've asked for. If you needed to talk to her about anything, she would be there for you before or after class. She was also a great communicator via email or canvas if you needed to reach out. I also really thought the TAs in this class were helpful and nice well rounded people.
Thought she was very helpful and understanding

Although I was barely even in class to begin with, she certainly didn't seem bad by any means. The class was pretty easy, but useless. Just show up for the midterm and final and you'll be fine. Don't bother showing up for lectures, especially when we pay money to watch... Throx, the cure for a missing sock? Yeah, I couldn't believe that either.
Her TAs grade very strict! She's a great professor though, her lectures are engaging.
Great lectures. She always makes sure that everyone understands a concept before moving on. The course work was never too difficult to manage.

I do not think I learned anything but still got an A-. Maybe If I tried a little harder I would've gotten A. Huge lecture hall so hard to stay engaged but it is possible if you sit in front. You do not have to go to class as the semester progresses but I'm sure if you do your grade will benefit.
Fall 2022 / No attendance check, and the test is done by Canvas through access code. I missed the exam, but she extended the exam period.

Professor Su was excellent, very organized, and passionate about business. No assignment was too hard, yet I feel as though I learned something every class. Class was huge (in an auditorium) so I didn't get to know her personally but she was good at making sure everyone understood before moving on. Weekly quizzes were easy and homework is helpful.

She is a very knowledgeable professor, but she seems to be teaching too low of a level given her qualifications and background. The lectures are long, and not the most engaging. You will pass the class just fine if you do the work. Everything is published online and attendance is not mandatory. However, go for the exam reviews.
Super caring professor and I highly recommend her. A little lecture heavy but it contains good information. Menti has a lot of questions on the tests so pay attention to those.

I loved Professor Su. She was very engaging in class and the class was structure was easy to understand. She is not the best at answering emails so I do recommend reaching out to the TAs. But other than that, she cared about her students and made sure they knew what was going on in regards to assignments and tests.

Bing is a really big fan of Elon, so I hope you enjoy that. Besides that, class was super easy and Bing was actually really helpful if you message her on Canvas. The only part about the class that sucked were the TAs who between sitting on their pile of bleached bones and being overly pedantic about assignments, were busy giving out asinine grades.

Professor Su is knowledgable on the subject and always responds to emails quickly. You don't need to attend the lectures, just read the slides she posts and do the homework and you'll be fine on all of the tests.
She is a great teacher and is very passionate. You can tell she knows the topic well. She is soft-spoken, so I would recommend sitting at the front of the class.

You can tell Professor Su is very well educated in the material she teaches! I found her lectures to be really interesting. Midterm and final exam are open note, similar to the questions we practice in class.

Bing Su is great! Her lectures were interesting and engaging and often did not take the whole two hours. She is soft-spoken but well respected and students know when it is time to listen. The lectures are also always posted in the modules along with supplemental readings and videos in case you miss a class!

There is no textbook for the class, so all of the reading assignments are given through canvas. She is really nice, approachable, and friendly. I'd advise taking pictures of the mentimeter questions, because similar questions are on the midterm. If you participate, review the slides before every classand take notes on the slides, you'll do fine.

Lectures and slides were very interesting and she has a great understanding of the topic and is professional. It can be easy to miss points on assignments if you do not pay attention to rubrics. Take screenshots of the Mentimeter questions because they will be on the tests. Also, take good notes because the tests are open note!

Professor Su is very nice and makes the class interesting with real life examples. Theres usually an assignment a week and it's never super hard, but sometimes the instruction is unclear and students aren't really sure what they are doing. The TA's grade everything and you can only communicate questions through the TA's.

The TA has more authority than the professor. The professor comes to the TA when she has a question. The microphone is always having technical difficulties, she doesnt speak up, and the material she shows is repetitive. The TA is also not very helpful. Shes also not very consistent with due dates, theyre very random.

I really enjoyed this class and thought the professor and TAs really cared about the students. The class was fun and participation was encouraged. Overall, pretty easy class as long as you pay attention.

reviews.comment: Bing Su has problems with her microphone every class. The lecture is 2 hours long and goes by so slow with her monotonous talking. I am not interested in entrepreneurship at all and I hate this class. However, I think if you were genuinely interested in entrepreneurship it would be helpful. A lot of homework and has all quiz grades muted.

reviews.comment: Really focused on providing real-life lessons for her students. If you don't attend the lecture then you will EASILY be lost in the sauce. Makes you work for it, but it's very interpersonal and not a difficult class- but an interesting one.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Lyda is a strong professor with a clear teaching style and an approachable way of presenting material. The course is well-structured and the case studies are reasonable in scope. Some challenges this semester may have stemmed from TA support rather than the course itself, which is worth keeping in mind when reading other reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Expectations were often unclear, making it hard to prepare. Feedback sometimes felt more critical than constructive. Some quiz questions were confusing or poorly worded, which made demonstrating understanding difficult. Overall, topics felt more complicated than necessary.

I didn't learn anything from this class. Grades tough on case studies, but only gives generic, AI generated feedback. She gets defensive from differing points of view that are logical but not the argument she wants to make.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Lyda is a great Professor if you are looking to push your critical thinking skills to the next level. She demands a lot in class participation, even though her lectures and slides were very vague and not helpful for the exams or case assignments. She will roast you in class if your group project did not cite any evidence from the case.

Lyda isnt a great professor. The biggest issue is her instructions, which are incredibly vague and hard to understand. Rubrics are vague and if you don't include something she wanted you get points off. Slides are terrible and do not have sufficient information on them to study with. She also loves Elon Musk. Beware of cold calls.

She offers poor guidelines on the main group project and then just tears apart any group that does it wrong. Her instructions regarding presentations are very different from what every other management professor teaches you. Her lectures are generally dull and not very useful.

Honestly I do not understand why people dislike her. she can be a little intense at times but the lectures are enjoyable, workloads not hard, she does grade a little on participation but its not difficult to participate in the discussions or answering simple questions. pay attention in class, do your work and you'll pass.

The worst professor I have taken at The U. Would not recommend and highly recommend avoiding any class taught by her. If you have a different opinion, she will shut it down. As someone else said, how is she employed by The U?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Would highly avoid. She takes pride in being a tough grader. Her tests are based on her opinions and what she says in class sprinkled in with text information. Doesnt seem to care about students as she picks favorites and lacks clarity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. How the university can keep someone with such a bad reputation is beyond me. She doesnt care about her students as much as she cares about Elon Musk. She is condescending and lacks any clarity in grading.

Exam questions are based on things said in class. Ensure that you fully master each concept; Not only just know it, but know what it is once it is turned the other way around. Read the textbook and readings provided, and take notes. Something frustrating about her is that exam questions are worded or phrased unnecessarily confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unpopular opinion, but I liked Lyda. She was always fun and engaging and knew what she was talking about. She will make you talk in class, has a lot of papers, and (her TA's) grade tough, which makes people not like her. However, I feel like I actually learned from her and retained the information. If you prepare for class she'll love you.

I would not recommend Lyda Bigelow in any capacity. For one, she is very condescending to students, unwilling to communicate like a professional, and is degrading to students who answer her questions incorrectly. Secondly, her lectures are all over the place and do not follow a coherent or reasonable path. Lyda should be fired from the University.

If I could give her a negative rating I would. This is the worst professor I have ever had. She is so rude, don't even bother asking her for help. She does not care about her students! She will call you out in front of class if you answer her question wrong and will be very upfront about it in a very rude way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the most conceited professors. She doesn't care about her students and will make you feel stupid for asking questions. On one of our first case studies, she forgot to post the instructions and rubric on canvas and then she got mad when we all got bad scores and blamed it on the class. If you can avoid this class then do.
It's all about attendance and participation. Read the case the morning of class, walk in, talk, walk out, and you'll get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall grade was earned through analyzing cases, a few discussions. Group project, presentation and paper were cancelled during move to online courses. Lyda is not patient with students. Not punctual in returning grades back to students. Final exam grades and final grades are not submitted yet. Power and control. Let us go! Dont recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Way too many group projects, papers and presentation requirements. Took forever on final grades. Disrespectful and condescending towards students. Refused student feedback and passive aggressive. Many case analysis of readings and concepts. Not open to questions from students. Thankful for coronavirus, she cancelled final project. Nightmare!

If I could submit a score of less than 0, I would. This class is a constant guessing game of "what does Lyda want?" She isn't clear on her expectations, and then gets visibly mad when you don't understand. She literally said, "If you answer correctly, but I don't feel like you actually understand the concept, I won't give you points."

I honestly wouldn't recommend taking Lyda ever. Shes totally all over the place with her lectures and her reasons or taking awake points incredibly arbitrary. Giving her the answer to a question isn't enough you have to show your understanding in with a paragraph of explanation even if she isn't asking for that. Very unclear.

The class itself wasn't super easy, but if you pay attention in class and study for quizzes/midterms you should be fine. She gives away a lot of answers to quizzes/tests during her class lectures so just pay close attention and try to engage yourself as much as possible. The most important thing to Lyda is to make sure her students understand.

Lyda is one of the best professors I've had in my college career. She cares about everyone in the class and just wants you to understand the material and do well. Participate in class, it will be helpful on the quizzes and exams, as well as your over all grade. If you have an opportunity to take a class taught by Lyda, TAKE IT!

Lyda constantly gives pop quizzes with vague questions, and wouldn't let me make one up even though I told her I would be missing a class several weeks in advance. She also doesn't post her class slides until after the class so you can't follow along on your own computer. Inflexible in office hours, and she doesn't check her uMail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lyda's a great teacher! She really cares about every students success. She's very enthusiastic and has a deap understanding of the material. To do well, read the chapters, read them again, and participate in class disscussions. Would recommend not asking questions that are answered in the syllabus. I hope to take more classes from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Lyda is one professor you either love or hate. Fortunately, I loved her. She did a great job teaching Strategic Management and she did her best to make the class interesting and relevant. You could tell she cared about the students and wanted us to succeed outside the classroom. Textbook is nice, but not necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took MGT 1030 & 1050 online with Prof Bishop and she is a good lecturer, and the workload is not bad. Sometimes on quizzes and exams, hyper specific questions were asked bordering on semantics, mostly in MGT 1030 which was really annoying. Personally I really enjoyed the content in MGT 1050 way more it was so fascinating and thought provoking.

The only reason I would not retake her is because of all of the group work we did. There were two formal graded group projects, but every class we were either being paired up or put in groups to talk about the required readings we had to do, or do some group activity, and then we would go over them as a class afterwards.
Class is pretty easy, the only stressful thing was a group project which was hard to get coordinated with people online but otherwise I enjoyed the class.

The professor for this class was good, it's a boring topic so that cannot be helped. My only issue with this class is the group project. It's worth so much of your grade and you are depending on other people to do their work, which we all know, won't happen. The only reason I got a bad grade was due to other people's laziness.

The content was boring, but she was a very fair grader and was clear with her expectations. The professor posts lecture slides that make the content significantly more comprehensible. The two essays were easy to write as long as you understand the basic concepts that each author focused on and wrote about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class as a requirement for my degree, and it was a great class with a fantastic professor. The homework and lectures are easy to understand and have clear instructions. The two essays were alright, and the quizzes were an easy A if you watched the lecture. I bought the book but only used it when citing for the essays.

1050 in general is a very boring class but it is not her fault. the weekly quizzes and discussions are super easy. the 2 essays are not that bad but the final is worth 300 points which is a ton compared to everything else-- and there are no other tests so you do not know what it is going to be like
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this professor. I had to take BUS 1050 for a gen ed requirement and this class was the best online class to take it. Lectures through video but she upload her powerpoint which was super helpful. Textbook was required for the class but I didn't buy it and still got an A. Final Exam is open book which was super helpful. Learned a lot!

There are a lot of readings from many different people. They're not long though. The textbook is required, so try to buy it used. The quizzes are really easy, and not hard. If you review the lecture slides, watch the lectures, and the readings, you do fine. There are 2 papers. One is in lieu of a midterm. Take this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: don't want take anymore

Long story short, this professor is EVIL. I haven't stopped smiling after realizing I will never see her again. If you feel like you haven't been through enough hardships in your life, take this class. Really brutal grader, and her feedback is nonexistent. The one thing the prof excels at is being on bull****. This is the prof equivalent of BYU.

To be completely honest, never take this class. The prof grades like she got a vendetta against me. I put out my best work and she dogged on it without actually teaching me how to improve. Was an easy A from busy work. POV take this class if you want to learn nothing. Skipping this class was the most blissful thing i've ever ever done.

reviews.comment:
This class is not hard, but Mrs. Bishop is terrible. She grades everything during her classes instead of teaching, and she gives no effort or feedback. Attendance matters for some reason, even though I had nothing to do in class. I have an acronym to describe this class for you:
Boring
Incompetent
Stuck up
Horrible
Outrageous
Pathetic

In terms of Ms. Bishop her class in general is not that bad. However she sucks. The lectures were clearly read from a script. She would grade everything during her class periods and seemed to have a lack of effort. also almost no feedback on drafts where she will take points off for not following her "feedback" 10/10 never taking her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are a writer who needs lots of guidance and feedback don't take this class. The grading rubric is confusing and sometimes contradictory, she gives little to no input on your drafts and often still takes points off. The homework can be confusing but is overall not too hard. I spent lots of time confused and having to resolve my own issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The homework is busy work, but overall easy. The essays, she gives no feedback on the drafts so youre going into the final blind. There's no clear requirements and criteria and when there is a rubric she doesn't even grade according to it. All of her lectures are repeating the things shes already said, but she canceled class alot so thats good

Doesn't give clear requirements for the assignments at all, so you basically go into each without any guidance. Doesn't give clear feedback at all, and then grades like she gave you every resource possible.

Easily the worst instructor I have had. Her lectures were boring/unproductive yet always mandatory. I didn't learn anything from the class. She was extremely rude--giving poor, unclear feedback, grading unfoundedly harsh, and not willing to work with students on explaining grades or fixing issues. I do not recommend this instructor.

She's a grad student, so it's reasonable that she has less experience in teaching. Her class is fairly easy and attendance matters. She will grade things without descriptive comments and the grade for each category will not be posted on Canvas as she grades in her paper. Staying engaged during class and submitting assignments on time will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class was fairly easy. However, she was one of the rudest professors I've ever had. She gave little to no feedback on rough drafts but still took points off the final with no explanation. She also got offended easily and sent out announcements saying that questioning her grading was disrespectful. Overall, just weird and unwelcoming vibes.

Bimstein is a great character to meet and has lots of fun stories and skills, but in terms of actually teaching he does very little. His reading and Think Piece responses are bland and often just him repeating what you said back to you and the reading assigned are repetitive and boring. But the workshops are fun and it's an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best teachers I've ever had. I took both of his classes and he is such an interesting/unique person that he draws you in. There is a lot of reading but if you engage thoughtfully with the material is goes a long way.

Prof Bimstein is one of the greatest people you will meet, and this class is one of the most unique and inspiring courses offered at the U. Learning about silence and expanding one's worldview on mindfulness is something I never thought I'd do, but I am grateful for doing it. The discussions are great, and it is not required that you speak in them.

Bimstein is such a sweet old man! Artfully Extended Mind was such a unique course and was very spontaneous. We met all over campus and had unique workshops. LOTS of reading/pre-class work. 3 papers total (gives through feedback... got an infinity A)! He serenades the class with songs inspired by students. Has funky style and brings stuffed animals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor and person. Super enthusiastic about what he teaches. Gives different opportunities for how you participate, and is super flexible with students. Most difficult aspect is the amount of reading, make sure you leave enough time. Really enjoyed my time in class, would take again.

I mainly took this course to get the FF credit, but I enjoyed it way more than I thought. Be prepared for a lot of reading assignments but it's pretty interesting stuff, and only had to write three short papers. Professor Bimstein is a super charismatic and quirky guy, and I wouldn't have enjoyed the class as much if he wasn't teaching it.

Professor Bimstein is the best professor I've had at the U. He is highly engaging and truly cares about all of his students. He gives wonderful feedback on papers. Along with that, he truly listens and engages with his students. He has such innovative experiences and brings in presenters to continue ideas. I give him an Infinity A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Fun and interesting guy! Most of the work involves reading, listening to musical pieces/videos, and the few easy-ish papers. The key to do well in this class is to just take the points/notes form the homework that interest you the most. If it feels like a lot of reading, skip to your favorite parts! Take this class for HONORS/FF.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Bimstein is such an interesting person who cares a lot about students' discussion and insights on material. He values effort and deep insight put into essays and comments, so as long as you put effort into participating in a deep way, you will be golden in his classes. I strongly recommend Prof. Bimstein!

Phil is an awesome guy. He gives really good feedback on all of the three papers you write during the semester. Class is almost always interesting, and the guests he brought in were awesome. You can tell he cares about his work and his students. I am taking Phil again next semester in his other class. I would highly recommend Phil as a professor.

Extremely kind and passionate about what he teaches. HONORS2850 was a joy; while some of the material may seem esoteric, if you engage with the ideas presented, you can learn a lot about both yourself and others after all, thats the goal! Id definitely recommend taking any courses Phillip teaches.

I never thought I'd enjoy anything about this course until Phillip taught it. He gives students the ability to get participation points in multiple ways, discusses interesting and relevant topics, and genuinely cares about his students. His feedback on participation and papers is very personal: he boosts your confidence and truly believes in you.

Phillip is a great professor! His courses and lectures are very interesting and engaging. In-class participation is important, but if you don't like speaking in class (like me), you can turn in written comments instead. There were no tests in my class, just short papers every few weeks. His grading seems a little inconsistent, but nothing too bad.
I took this class expecting to get an easy and a good discussion about philosophy however I was met with lots and lots of readings about tedious topics. Be prepared to read A LOT in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Bimstein is a fantastic professor! The class is an easy honor fine arts credit, but it's so enjoyable nonetheless. He is a passionate, quirky guy who connects music to communication and real life in so many interesting ways. The class also has numerous interesting guest presenters/speakers including live music and a drum circle!

A truly incredible professor and EVERYONE should take his class! He's so passionate about his work and class discussions are always fun, engaging, and entertaining. I took the class because I thought it would be an easy A (& it is), but I ended up being a lot more inspired and challenged than I thought. Class is 3 hours, once/week with 20 min break

By far the best class I've ever taken. He was so supportive and kind. I loved going to his class even though it was 3 hours long. Every class was inspiring. If your have the chance to take a class by him, definitely do. I recommend his classes to all my friends.

It is not often you find a professor in a creatively-based topic that can communicate abstract ideas in a grounded way without losing any of the original meaning. If you have the opportunity to take a class from Phillip, do so by all means. I left class everyday feeling inspired.

Great lecturer, last question of online quizzes was a free point to point out something you struggled with, which he would then cover in the next class. Weekly homework, but TAs help during discussion sections (not mandatory). Exams were moderately difficult, but exam corrections were available to get 50% of the points lost back. Would take again!
Great professor who genuinely cares about having his students succeed.
Definitely a fun and great lab, you can tell he definitely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.

TAKE THIS CLASS I cannot stress this enough. Probably the best class I have taken at the U. Bill is so fun and so intelligent and knows what he is talking about. Lectures are so fun and engaging and I always looked forward to going to this class

Bill is the best! Instead of textbooks he has other books you read that are easy and enjoyable. He can tell who puts effort in and who doesn't, and your grade reflects that. His lectures are fun and you will learn a lot about creative advertising in a fun, relaxed setting.

YOU NEED TO TAKE THIS CLASS WITH BILL. He is by far the best professor here at the U and would take this class over again. The class doesn't contain any test but you do have readings and a discussion assignment on it. You also have one big assignment but Bill is willing to help you and your group out when ever you want.
dope

Bill is easily one of the best professors at the U. Creativity isn't easy for everyone, but he finds a way for every single student to tap into their right brain. He does a fantastic job of bringing real-world examples into the class. He sets every student up for success while giving supportive feedback along the way. His credibility speaks volumes

BILL IS A WONDERFUL TEACHER. HE HAS SO MUCH EXPERIENCE AND WANTS YOU TO LEARN AND SUCCEED. HE REALLY DRIVES THE PURPOSE OF HIS CLASS HOME THROUGH THE READINGS AND HANDS ON GROUP PROJECTS. PARTICIPATION AND ATTENDANCE IS A LARGE PORTION OF YOUR GRADE, SO BE SURE TO ATTEND, YOU REALLY WILL BENEFIT AND ENJOY GOING.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Bill is a wonderful professor. He is so intelligent and passionate about creative advertising. He is also very high up and respected in the advertising world. TAKE HIS CLASS! He really engages everyone and inspires you to be more creative and pushes your boundaries to be more creative. He really cares about the success of all his students.

I was in PDE's and Vector Calc with Simon and he did a great job teaching it. The course content was very difficult, but he made this course very manageable. The tests were difficult, but I felt the grading was very fair and, in some cases, generous. He was my favorite math professor, and I would recommend him for any math course.

Simon was my favorite math professor that I've had all of college. I was in his 7:30 am math 3140 PDE and vector calc. the material is difficult as expected but Simon made the class feel very manageable. Grading of the tests felt very fair, even generous. It felt clear he wants his students to succeed in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is definitely a teacher who expects you to understand the basics of calculus before taking his class. He'll go through everything you need to know for the midterms/final, but often times it was hard to follow his train of thought after he defined and proofed everything and anything. Looks: 10/10
Although English is not his first language, his lectures are amazing. I love Professor Bohun.

Simon is a very personable professor. I struggled with calculus in high school and never thought I'd be able to pass it in college. I ended this class with an A and I'll be forever grateful for the insight and clear lectures he gave. If I had to take another math class for my major, I'd want to take another one from him.

If I could give someone a rating lower than a one. He doesn't give instruction because he doesn't believe in it. He doesn't give grading rubrics then gives you a mid grade on an essay purely because he didn't think it was good enough. You get zero information on what you are being graded on and when I asked his response is extremely patronizing.

His class was easy but there was a lot of reading, sometimes 90 pages due in 2 days. Most of the readings though are super interesting and create good discussions. I can never tell though if he is extremely sarcastic or passive aggressive all the time. He's constantly at that line and I can't tell.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Some people should not teach. Educational content was lacking, felt slapped together, random grading, boring lectures. Very educated guy and is not mean or malicious, but I got the feeling that Allan was there for a paycheck and not for the mentorship of his students. Took him for two separate classes and felt like I came up dry education wise.

This was actually for IT Health which is an Honors Integrated Minor specific course. Class was genuinely enjoyable and I looked forward to attending. Professor is funny and cares about his students. I would 100% take again.

I had professor Borst for HONOR2211 and I really enjoyed his class. It was definitely lecture heavy and required a lot of work outside of class. There was a lot of reading every week but as long as you came to class and did the assignments he was willing to work with you on grades and gave good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Some of his expectations are difficult to understand so it's hard to know what to do for assignments, but he gives good opportunities to work with peers to do well on the essays. Not the best teacher/lecturer but his material was engaging.

For HONOR 3200, I didn't interact with Allan very much because it was online. The class was pretty easy and consisted of five or six essays that were around 600-700 words each. He had the class grouped into small groups, and we were assigned peer reviews and discussions as well. The papers were pretty easy, and the class was well organized.

He is nice guy - checked in with us throughout the semester and was lenient on due dates. But like there were SO MANY ASSIGNMENTS. Papers, peer reviews, and discussions every week. Even though I genuinely tried my best, I still got meh grades on some essays and no feedback. I liked that it was entirely asynchonous, but this class is no easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A lot of reading and is very critical when grading your assignments. He reads all the assignments to make sure he can provide you with feedback, but sometimes it comes off as pretentious. Be careful of this class because it seems like it would be easy, but if he is this critical with everything he grades you could end up with a bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Allan wasn't too bad at all. He's a funny, relatable guy that I'm sure is pretty cool. The problem is that his class is boring. So boring. I left his classes half asleep because the course material was so bland. I survived though, and so will you, as this is a necessary course. Get ready for some homework, but they are usually easy assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is honestly my favorite professor I've ever taken. He's genuinely very kind, caring, and laidback. He was always very flexible with accommodations and grades and the course work was not heavy or difficult at all. It was easy to end this course with a 100%

This class is extremely tough and research based. The teacher assigns 2 30-40 page readings per week that are very complex and he does not cover them well. He does very little to properly prepare students for exams and often has quizzes at the end of every class on the material from the night before and will chastise you for being 30 seconds late.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bryan is awesome! MGT3600 was difficult, though having a good group is SUPER important; group work makes up 45% of your grade. Get ready to read long and scientific articles, but they have great application if you try your best. There are three cumulative tests (drop lowest) and quizzes every Wednesday on class material. Overall, it was enjoyable!!

Take the lectures seriously and make sure you show up to class on the first day and really focus on getting into a good group. Your group could make or break your experience in this class. Bonner is a good professor, very knowledgable about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible professor. Would kick you out for walking in one second late, and slides just seemed way too scientific for a BUSINESS course. Quizzes every week and if you didnt read the 30-40 page article it would not go well. I got good enough scores on all my exams to get an A but still got a C in the class because I missed too many classes

dont do it bro. This class was harder than my Business Law was by a long shot. 30-40+ page articles to read PER week and then SUMMARIZE on tests that we do not go over in class and the study guides for said tests hardly pertain to what's actually on it. Crazy how I'm a senior yet don't know what grade I will get. Hardest class I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am only writing this review because of the the guy who wrote Bryan is a "book worm nerd" in his review. The story behind that comment is the guy who wrote that was told to put his phone away after being rude for the whole semester. He was so mad that in a fit of rage he wrote that like a baby throwing a tantrum. We live in a society or something.

I do not recommend taking this professor to anyone. This guy is a book worm nerd who does nothing but site research that we will all forget. Does not connect his work to the real life and he will mark you off for participation if you are 30 seconds late. He quizzes you on class material the day of so you better memorize every little detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bryan is a great professor. He explains everything thoroughly in his lecture videos. You'll want to pay close attention to detail and take great notes, but he gives you all the information to succeed. His emails are rather dry, and he says it like it is. With that being said, however, he is more than happy to explain confusing topics. Not too hard

Bryan is a gem of a professor. You can tell he deeply cares about his students and making sure they succeed. During the pandemic, he was incredibly empathetic and accommodating. As a plus, he's hilarious. Never thought a Canvas notification could actually make me laugh, but here we are.

Great professor. Really knows his subject, and does everything he can to relate it in a way that students can understand. Don't try to meet with him outside of class, though--I scheduled three meetings, all three fell through.

Bryan is certainly among the top 3 professors I've had at the U. He is caring, passionate, and relatable. He expects much, but helps his students succeed.  He treats students as equals which is surprisingly rare among university faculty. I would recommend his class(es) to anyone I know.

Easily the best Professor I have ever had.  The tests and quizzes are quite tough, but this class is more about participation.  He rewards participation and effort more than performance on tests and quizzes.  You definitely need to attend class. I would say you could probably get away without the book.  Speak up in class and you will do well.
Bryan is a brilliant professor, not just someone who fell into his position.  He makes his lectures interesting and applicable.  You can tell he genuinely cares about his students.

He was hilarious, knew the subject matter well, and is an easy grader. He also treats his students as equals and will answer any question they have. Great guy. Would take another class from him. I'm a serial class-ditcher, but I never missed this class, because it was awesome.
He was awesome. He knew the subject so well. He has had tons of experience in the business world and always goes out of his way to make sure your questions are answered.

This is one of the best professors I have had here at the U. He was very enthusiastic about this class and he made a personal relationship with every person in our class. You need to put in effort and come to his class, but you will want to. I learned so much from him.

While Bryan is perhaps one of the more difficult professors i've have he is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Not only is he thoroughly knowledgeable about what he teaches, but he also tries to help his students as much as possible. You'll need to read the text but he makes you want to read in some ways.

Excellent teacher - one of the best at the U.  Can be a little difficult - you must attend class and read the chapters.  His lectures are great and he makes sure you really understand the concepts.  Highly Recommended.
No Comments

I started out not liking this professor much because he's kind of strict (wants people to be in their seats on time, etc) but I think that's just because he wants to make the most out of the class time. I learned a lot in his class. He's really willing to help if you're not getting something but doesn't care much for excuses (I tried that once).
This guy is about the best professor I've had. If you care about learning to be a better manager (and maybe even a better person), take his class. Don't expect it to be easy, though.
He is funny and fair, but has tests that are hard to study for. Must attend class everyday in order to score well on quizzes
No Comments
Nice guy. Good taste in shoes.
No Comments

Idk why this guy doesn't have a higher rating. His lectures are a little dull but he knows his stuff, cares about his students, and provides all of his slides + lecture information. No attendance required but he almost always ends lecture early. Def a safe option for ECE 2210 and much better than the professors some of my friends had.

Dr. Bodson is very kind, understanding, and easy to reach out to. Two relatively short homeworks each week and four midterms with the lowest dropped. Exams were very fair and much easier than his previous sections, averages were in the 80s. He sometimes doesn't explain enough of his work during lectures, but the course material wasn't too difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bodson is very flexible and understanding. Sometimes I wish he could be more concise with the information he gives; that way, it's easier for me to stay focused during his lectures. Overall, I appreciate how thoughtful and gentle he is with his lectures and students.

I showed up to the first few classes and realised he just slowly reads out his slides. Never showed up after that and used them to teach myself. I got lucky I understood it, class average on one test was an F and the others never above a C. The topics were a lot of fun, like puzzles to solve, but he made it awful. Labs were cool though!

Marc is a very nice person and is very passionate about what he does, but he should not be teaching an undergraduate level class. ECE 2210 should consist of fairly entry level material, but it was made unnecessarily difficult by Bodson. The exams were not based on any of the homeworks or lecture material and were graded really roughly. No curve.

Lectures are pretty bad, mostly reading from slides and then working problems that are far simpler from both the homework and the exam questions so workload doesn't feel properly explained. Homework is nice because solutions are provided prior to submission to double check, but content is not always explained in lecture before hand.

Dr. Bodson is very knowledgeable and very active to keep his materials up-to-date. His materials and methods may seem difficult or different at the beginning, but ultimately his process is the easiest and simpler. He is very eager to teach and available whenever we need him. I believe the credit hours should be increased from 3 to 4/4.5.

Dr. Bodson is very knowledgeable and organized this course well. The credit hours should probably be increased to 4-6 credit hours. The materials are carefully planned and the theories presented are up-to-date.

For a course titled "control of electric motors" I was disappointed to have never worked with a motor in the class or lab. 'Motor simulation' would be a more appropriate class name. Classroom engagement is low, Professor reads from slides, and not a single practice problem was worked during lecture. For a three credit course the workload is high.

The amount of time spent in this class is more than the entire rest of my schedule. Worst idea ever. Control of electric motors sounds cool but the workload is outrageous. The 3 credits you get from this class should be at least 6 for the amount of time the homework and labs take.

It is clear she doesn't trust students. I have never had an online course require in-person, proctored tests. I live out of state and it defeated the purpose of taking an online course. Her tests are hard, and I have had consistent As throughout my entire college career. I graduate in a month and she is the only B I will have received.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would have used the respected category too had it allow the fourth one. A teacher that help students learn more by being positively welcoming and passionate and caring but also clear with expectations to ensure healthy academic dynamic flows for everybody. Her syllabus is only a fraction of her enthusiastic urge to teach in categories described.

Dr. Bowen is one of the smartest professors I have had, and for that I greatly respect her and her passion to teach. However, this classes grades are majority quizzes and 2 exams, so if you feel you struggle in that area, I suggest taking a different class. Lectures can be confusing, and I felt as though they didn't always help my learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowen was great, would highly recommend. She had some personal health issues but pivoted really well and clearly communicated expectations/changes. If you go to the lectures (which are great), read, and study for exams you will do well in her class. Exams can be tricky but she gives a study guide. Will look for her classes in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is an in person class disguised as an online course. its flipped, so all of the lectures are online, making it hard to follow along and ask questions like a normal lecture. I can't learn from recorded videos and i assume a lot of other students cant either. In-person activities are kind of helpful though.

Such a kind person, and I loved this class! It is very test heavy, with 60% tests and 30% quizzes as of Spring 25. Going to lecture will be your biggest help, even though attendence is not mandatory, as the things on the exams are usually exactly what she teaches. There was no group project this semester and extra credit was limited but went far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bowen is an outstanding professor. This is my second course with her. She is very well spoken, making her lectures quite engaging and elaborate. She clearly defines the expectations of both herself and her students on Day 1, so you have a clear understanding of how to succeed. So far, she has been my favorite psych professor at the U.

I liked the material in this class but if you take it get ready to have your grade based full off quizzes. There is genuinely no other grades besides quizzes and tests. I think the tests are way harder than they need to be and the study guides are nothing like the tests. She is a good teacher though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I got an A in the class, I did not enjoy it. The material seems harder to grasp than it should be. I feel like it is the way she teaches it. The exams are long and are the main part of the grade. There is also a group project in the end which I think was useless. She does drop one exam of 3 and offers extra credit so that helps.
Comically easy course. Final exam was optional, only homework was a group project at the end of the semester that was pretty easy. Lots of drops, and ample extra credit available
Gets a little sidetracked during lectures. She really likes to talk.

Lot's of student complaints and I, unfortunately, was having problems too. Though I got an A, she is not easy and very unmovable even with extenuating circumstances. She was really bad with me concerning CDA accessibility and is not accommodating though she thinks she is on her own terms. Not a lot of assignments so points are heavily weighted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not great, but not bad either. Overall the class content was very interesting, but I found reading the book was a more informative than her slides/lectures. Maybe that was the point to get us to read the book, but made going to class some days a drag. She is very passionate about the subject though, so it's not a bad class by any means.

Kimberly was a great professor. Was very accommodating to the students. Incredibly organized and I never had any questions on assignments because they were so thoroughly explained. She takes a little bit to get things graded and back to you, and often in chunks. A great teacher, very cognizant of her students and overall, a pretty easy class
I loved this class! It's easy to get a good grade if you try and she gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and drops one of the exams/ other assignments with low scores.

Dr. Bowen is extremely knowledgable & passionate & likes questions. There are very few things graded: 3 exams (lowest score dropped), group project + presentation, short answers during class based on notes/reading. The study guides were extremely long and difficult which made preparing for exams hard. Not an easy class but does her best to help.

Bowen is an interesting teacher. Her class is very lecture heavy throughout the semester, but the second half was a lot of small group discussions. The exams were difficult and required a lot of attention while studying in order to feel prepared. Luckily, there are ample opportunities to receive extra credit on assignments or either of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
If you are novice of psychology course, I don't recommend to take this class with Dr. Bowen.
The exam questions are difficult... It is not easy class to get a satisfying grade

(CS major) This was probably the easiest class I've taken at the U. XC opportunities are so abundant that rn (before I've taken the final) I could get a 33/50 on the final and still get an A from all the easy XC. Exceptionally detailed syllabus, and she sticks strongly to those policies. Decent lecturer, leads thoughtful in-class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bowen has her plate full teaching a ton of classes but she still takes the time to speak with students who reach out. She makes disclaimers about response times to give context why she takes a long time to respond to emails. The course work was clear and easy to understand and the test material is straightforward. Overall a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take the class from anyone else. Her quizzes were full of trick questions some were even a bit of a stretch. I missed a few assignments and she was not willing to work with me whatsoever even though I hadn't missed any before and with everything going on, you'd expect a little more compassion especially when you have a legitimate reason. Do not rec
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gave very little assignments and was a very tough grader. Was awful at responding her emails. Lots of content but that is expected with psychology so its understandable. I took her class online and she made us do a group project which was difficult to manage. Overall, did not like her teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Found the class pretty interesting, attendance & note taking isnt required but I dont see how youll do good if you dont. Not a lot of graded material which can be both good & bad. No makeup nor extra credit available, textbook is required (sometimes theres multiple chapters due) workload: chapter (2pgs) papers 1x week & 3 heavily graded essays
Too much ambiguity and trick questions. The class is fairly unorganized and difficult to navigate. There are tons of trick questions and ambiguous instructions that lead to her grading harshly.

For an online class, this class required a lot of attention. Kimberly had an awful time managing canvas at the beginning of the semester, which caused a lot of frustration and chaos for our class. Make sure you refer to syllabus due dates and not canvas due dates. Workload is fair with 4 lengthy discussions, minimum reading, and frequent quizzes.
Average class. Very nice prof., friendly and helpful. The exams can be confusing because the answers are so alike, this was kind of frusterating. Overall not bad.

He is inexperienced and impossible to understand. His lectures involved doing problems on a projector and not explaining them which caused most students to not go to them. People's scores were so bad (avg 60% on tests) he gave out extra credit for just showing up which was the only reason I got a B. Would not recommend unless you want a B or lower.

Lectures are hard to understand. Questions are never answered with clarity. makes mistakes on his work, which I was fine with the first few times. But when it happens a lot it confuses me. Just solves problems in front of us, no explaining. not experienced with teaching; sometimes no lecture due to technical difficulties with his ipad.

Very poor teaching skills. Lectures were hard to understand and not very structured. Attendance was revealed to be mandatory and graded after the final exams, despite being told it was not at the beginning of the class. Would not recommend.

Minimal communication to students outside of announcements, not very engaging during lecture, difficult to understand in class, leaves zero makeups available regardless of your situation (e.g., I had to take his final with the flu or else I fail the class). Grade policy is forgiving, however the cons outweigh the pros 10-1.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were very difficult and unclear. Gave lots of homework, which was helpful, but hard to understand with no base understanding of the topic. Tests were hard, and reviews were not related to the tests. No extra credit unless nobody came to class and you happened to. Cannot request regrades.

He is a very nice person and is forgiving about exam dates if an emergency comes up. But his lectures just don't really stick. He is really hard to understand. When he is explaining something, he oftentimes goes back and erases the work he showed, which is not helpful in a math class. If you don't already know the content, I'd take someone else.
awful lectures, had to figure it all out myself with the textbooks and assignments.
So awful, had to withdrawal from his class because it was so bad.

Horrible lectures. Frequently makes mistakes in lectures and asks students if correct. Weekly quizzes that we didn't get back until the day before the midterm. Kabeer's grading felt purposefully harsh, like he was looking for small flaws to take large chunks of points off for.

Run - not walk - away from this class. If you struggle with something, you will be either mocked, ignored, or directed to the TAs, who at times are just as confused as you are. He says he doesn't want to make the class stressful. One of the most stressful classes ever. Run.

Some evolutionary psych topics can be uncomfortable, so if that's not your thing, maybe skip it. Lots of opportunity for extra credit and office hours. There are a lot of readings and if you want to get a good grade in this class you have to do the homework. Attendance is extremely mandatory. DO NOT TAKE CLASS IF YOU WANT AN EASY CLASS. Really interesting and intriguing content if you put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Currently, week 4 of the course, and in my 4 years of university, I have never met such a self-centered man. 1st lecture was quotes, AI-generated, from students praising him to the high heavens. Accuses you of using AI; we used lockdown browsers for everything, call you inadequate, and make fun of your physical characteristics. Grading is random.

Insanely harsh grader, the instructions are not specific enough to be grading this hard. His TA's to most of the grading, yet the grading seems to be random, it could be the same quality of work yet receive a complete opposite grade. This was an extremely frustrating class, and offered little help.

You will be reading ~40 pages of fine-print academic papers a week, and his army of TAs are insanely harsh graders. On the weekly assignments you may put in the same amount of effort for each, yet get a seemingly randomized grade, with some incredibly vague criticism such as "mmm, use more critical thinking!" Incredible harsh and frustrating class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellis is incredibly knowledgable about the topics he teaches on. However, this is by far the most fascinating course I've ever taken and it's definitely for you if you're interested in the knowledge.

i would say leave a semester of work behind and just dont take this clas

this teacher doesn't care about students if they are writing on the board for problems they won't even check if the students are finished writing and just moves on and just guesses that everyone got it on the first try there is a quiz every week and 5 homework's due every weekend and trying to balance this class with others is so terrible.
doesn't teach just writes stuff on the board

had hw almost every week even during exam week but useful to prepare exam

review exams useful & not same in exam - grade generous

Cool, Fun, Good teaching, Highly recommend

Dan was a pretty good teacher. He was always open to questions and was accessible outside of class. I personally struggled with the material, but I think it was more me than him. Exams were pretty difficult and homework assignments could be challenging.

Professor Bragg was good at explaining things, and the lectures were occasionally funny. The lectures were detailed but not too dry. The professor is newer and could use a little more enthusiasm, but that's a minor thing. Overall, it was a great class, with long, occasionally-hard homeworks but fairly 'easier' tests.

The class was an evening class, so the class structure was very simple, with no participation points or anything for lectures. There was weekly homework assignments that never took me super long to complete, two midterms, and a final. Instruction was super clear.
Dr. Sproul is highly respected and loved. He cares for all of his students, is reliable, and is so funny. Unfortunately, he seems mostly uninvolved and uninterested in rehearsals after band camp.
Dr Sproul is a great professor, he made marching band and music very enjoyable.

If you are on the fence about marching band this should be your sign to do it, one of the funniest and most chill professors. get ready for a good time, he will poke fun at you but you can always poke back!

Dr. Sproul is one of my favorite professors on campus, he leads a dang good marching band and he genuinely cares about all of his students.  Sproul has personally helped me through many hardships and has been a big part of my staying at the school. Definitely take marching band with him if you can, you won't regret it.  go utes
Marching band was great :)

Concert Attendance: It always depends on the TA how many convocations are scheduled. reviews.comment: Brian Sproul is a good guy. You need to pull your weight and do what you say you will, and things will be great. He honestly cares about his students and makes sure students love music and performing. Great teacher-take from him whenever you can.

If you want to be part of an amazing marching band take this class!! Sproul is very motivational and we do a lot of great things. obviously participation is a must and he will not be easy on you if you miss rehersal. He was a great teacher. He really helped the band. He knew when to come in and focus on something specific, but he also knew when to step back and let the section leaders take care of it. He was funny, kind, and caring. Pretty great.

I am completely in love with this class and plan on taking it every year until I graduate. Sproul's attitude, work ethic, and attention to detail are outstanding. He makes you want to work hard. Inspiring.
Probably my most favorite class on campus! It's a lot of work, but it is definitely worth it. Sproul is an amazing director! He's very funny, totally understanding, and extremely helpful.
Great person! Very accomodating and understanding. Very helpful as well.
Really great teacher, had so much fun in his class! Connected well with the students and created a great learning environment. I'm a better musician from the time I spent in this class!

He gives practice exams with 60-75% identical questions to the actual exam. Exams averaged mid-80s. He gives 3% extra credit. It's a 200-level course, but you need to read the textbook and put in effort to succeed. Final is cumulative but with questions from earlier exams. He teaches well and I learned a lot. A difficult but rewarding course.

I had a 69.4 in the class after doing everything and getting 100 on them. His tests were so hard and didn't curve. I emailed him to see if there was anything I could do to get a 70, he replied saying that he'd give me tips to help me study.

reviews.comment: Took PSY 1010 with him online. Great lecture videos that explained topics super well. If you take notes and pay attention to his lecture videos, it's a guaranteed A+

Professor grades harshly, but based on a rubric so be sure to read assignment instructions very closely. Exams are fairly difficult because they are so few points, but there are lots of opportunities for extra credit. Lectures are interesting and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very easy class to be successful in. Lectures are posted weekly, exams are based heavily on quiz question, and there are helpful resources posted for review. Lowest exam grade is dropped at the end of the semester.

This class should NOT be this hard. Exam averages were 68%, 72%, and 66%. (post 5 point adjustment). If you want to do a bunch of busy work, this will be great for you. Grading was very unclear and simply frustrating. Dr. Branch is very smart and his lectures are informative, but his TA's do all the grading and it's bad.

I loved this class and found it super interesting. The lecture videos could be long, and sometimes he talked more than the woman professor on the videos which was annoying, but still super interesting. Quizzes and exams are easy if you pay attention and take notes. Not a demanding class at all, just stay on top of your stuff.
Great professor! Interesting lectures and knows what he is talking about. Easy grading and extra credit opportunities. Would definitely take again!

Professor Branch is incredible. He can get information across easily and keep students engaged. Tests require studying but definitely not difficult. He's smart, accomplished, funny, and cares about his students. Information sticks in the brain well.
He was so good at lectures, like I actually got information from it. He was good at engaging the class, really great set up.

The best class! It's so much fun to learn, and I never thought I would say that about school! Amazing lectures and so considerate when it comes to grading and personal reasons! I would take this class over and over! I almost didn't take this class, but I'm so glad I did!

His class is super interesting and he himself is also really awesome! he is really engaging and provides good examples of concepts. His coursework itself is easy, the tests are easy too and he is easily accessible and helpful. He always answers questions and is helpful. A little bit of group discussion every now and again. overall 10/10
Such an amazing teacher, I would recommend him to everyone. His assignments are very clear and he's a very nice grader who will always answer your questions.

CogPsych with Dr. Branch was one of my favorite courses I've taken at the college level. He gives fantastic lectures and is eager to answer questions carefully and thoroughly. His exams were challenging, but they are well worded and very doable if you pay attention during lecture. I signed up for two more courses with him and I'd highly recommend!

Professor Branch is one of the best professors I've had. He is very organized and prepares you for exams. I took PSY 2100 with him and found it pretty easy as long as you do the reading and assignments. He also does practice quiz questions that are very useful. I currently have two more classes with him. I highly recommend taking Professor Branch!

While I never interacted with this professor, based on his announcements and responses in discussion posts, he seems like a nice person. The assignments and tests were very easy. The TA however was quite condescending, but it didn't make a big impact on the course as a whole.

I took his PSY 2100 class, and I loved it! Dr. Branch knows all of his material extremely well and is very organized in his lectures. He is very engaging during class and funny. I would highly recommend taking any class from him. He offered up to 5% extra credit for his class and it's all really easy to acquire. Amazing professor.

Professor Branch basically took over this course from the previous professor, but it's a pretty good course with easy to follow content and lectures. There's about 3-5 very easy assignments per week, and three open note exams + study guides. The lectures are very easy to learn from, and it's just basic psychology content. Amazing Canvas setup.

Professor Burbank is the best. I've taken 2 classes with him now, all with an extremely manageable workload. While it is reading-heavy, all political science classes tend to be. The lectures can be mundane, but he is passionate about what he teaches and is very knowledgeable about what he teaches.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor with a lot of passion for the subject. Class time can be a bit tedious. He has a great smile.

I had a really great time taking political parties with Professor Burbank! The professor is always very fair and unbars which can be difficult given the subject of the class. The discussion boards are always on really interesting topics. The quizzes and final are definitely doable if you study the quizzes and readings beforehand.

He is good at giving lectures but you may get bored easily. He is easy to make get sidetracked on different subjects to kill class time but the discussions can always be good. He has a lot of knowledge about what he teaches and passion which is all you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

However, the class is easy and he is genuinely a nice person that seems to care about students' succuess.

Professor Burbank is great. We would spend the first 20-30 minutes discussing current events and he always remained very neutral. There are a few easy online discussions and online quizzes. The final should be easy if you study the quizzes and read the assigned book. The essay is an easy A if you spend some time on it.

Professor Burbank is very caring; he is willing to help and give amazing feedback on the papers and assignments he gives so take advantage of it. Extremelly knowledgable.

Burgon is a tough grader, but it's due to her extremely tight timeline of useless papers/presentations. The assignments are impossible to understand what's needed to get a good grade. Burgon has no idea what she's doing. She says she hates busy work, yet assigns busy work every week with due dates 2 dates in between. As a person, she is very nice and seems to care about students. Not a great professor. Lectures were unhelpful, we did grammar worksheets made for third graders. Professor Burgon is the best professor I have ever had at this school. The only reason she has low ratings is because mechanical engineers hate writing and think it's her fault. Holli is a very tough grader. she somehow can be extremely specific with her rubric and still miss critical parts of the assignment that you will be penalized for. Tony is an great prof. & overall amazing human being, is always willing to help, and has entertaining lectures! Just keep in mind this 2 credit class has the workload of a typical 4 credit class. Exam averages in the 60s and 70s, but an A is well within reach after test corrections & curve.

Tony is such an amazing professor who cares about his students and the material he is teaching. He is super accessible outside of class and provides lots of ways to improve in his class.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE IF YOU SKIPPED CHEM1703!! I made this mistake and felt overwhelmed. Tony was so caring and I cried in his office with him. He has such a big heart once you get to know him. He cared for women in STEM, even when I was one of the only girls in the class.

Tony is awesome! Thanks to him, both 1703 and 1705 are some of the best classes I've taken. He is always accessible by email as well as texting and is eager to help with homework, projects & anything else you need. Go to office hours when you feel stuck. He does not tolerate bs, so work hard and you will do well.

Tony really cares and wants his students to succeed. The tests are very difficult with low averages (60-70%). Tony provides exams from previous years, so study those exams to do well. Coding in python is heavily involved in the class. Tony is also very available for help and so are the TAs. The class is curved at the end of the semester.

Tony is a really great professor teaching a very difficult class. Taking this class during a pandemic added a lot of stress, but Tony did the best he could to make it easier for us and be accessible. There is lot of content in a short period of time, and I would recommend getting a head start in learning how to code. Final grades are heavily curved
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Tony really makes himself available for you, which makes a huge difference. They have to pack 4 credits worth of material into just 2, but he does a great job making sure you know what is going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 1705 is a very different course from 1703. 1705 is less of a traditional classroom based course. There is a lecture which covers the lab of the week. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Tony is an amazing teacher with great lectures. Tony is accessible at almost any time because most of the time he is in the Meldrum Lab working.
