Very difficult class. The homework is hard, but it really preps you for tests. This is not a class you need a 90 in to get an A, ours went down into the 70s.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great professor and an amazing person. His attitude is so positive and funny it makes class worth while!

Tony is one of the best instructors in the department. There is a good deal of homework in this class along with group projects. He's always willing to help you out, but make sure you put in a good effort to work on the assignment too.

Tony is the kind of professor that every student wants; caring, crazy smart, makes time to help you one on one, funny, personable; the list goes on. Super easy DIV/FF credit. I averaged 82 on the midterms and ended up with an A after I got 92 on the final. Do the concert reports early.

Took an online diversity credit from her. Easy easy easy, which is great because it avoids the time-wasting on a class that I have no interest in, and History of Jazz is by for not-the-worst div credit you can take.

I'm on my last semester at the U, and I must say the material in this class is the hardest I've ever seen. And I have played piano my whole life. This was an online class and the material is borrowed from another program at GWU. The teacher is really helpful and fair as far as grading, if you don't have any background in music, don't take it!
A very enthusiastic teacher, extremely nice and helpful. Loved this class!
Best teacher ever she will work with you and her test isn't that hard.

This is a great class.  It is fun, entertaining, not too difficult if you apply yourself, and very manageable with a full schedule.  Dr. Clayton is extremely nice and knowledgeable! She goes out of her way to help students to get a good grade.  Going to class is not mandatory (except for 3 days) but is recommended if you want to get a good grade.

Great Teacher without a doubt no questions there.  Although the class is a general education class and so I wasn't that interested in the first place.  BUT she doesn't make it unnecessarily hard and quite contrary makes it easy to pass.  It seems that she understands that the MUSC3600 class is a gen ed and most people taking it aren't math majors.

Justin was a great professor. His grading was easy to understand and provided valuable feedback on assignments. If you are a games major, I would suggest taking this class as you would understand the material well. The number of games we have to play in a short amount of time can sometimes be stressful, but overall, it is a fairly easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content of this class was really interesting, I really liked the material we were taught and the games Carpenter had us study, but unfortunately his grading was outrageous. I would spend time on my papers and I would feel confident in my writing, but he would take off points for irrelevant things and not explain why.

Although certainly willing to give extensions to students on bigger papers, this was definitely a course that was more difficult than it had to be. Grading felt very abstract and confusing, with hard standards to reach what he expected from a paper. I took this class for fun and to play games, but it has left me feeling more stressed than necessary
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although obviously knowledgeable about the content, Professor Carpenter is not a great lecturer, the class concepts are already exceptionally abstract, and he doesn't make it much easier by having his lecture slides be paragraphs of text he rarely explains or discusses. With that being said, He provides ample time for assignments and extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Justin Carpenter I believe to be a kind and caring person. That being said I don't think that they should necessarily be a teacher within an online class. Criteria were almost impossible to figure out, within my class. The final project instructions were only 3 sentences, and we graded on criteria that we could not have known existed.

The professor was nice, but we weren't given chance to adjust based on the feedback. On the final assignment, he gave a 1 week extension, but he gave feedback on just the first assignment only three days before the extended due date. The feedback from all of the other assignments came back only after grades were finalized, so the class felt risky.

Every week we needed to watch a couple almost hour long lectures, play the game, read, write 2 discussion posts (500 words each), reply to 4 people, a journal entry (500 words), and a unit engagement (1000 words). Then he waited till the last minute to grade and give feedback.Took what should have been a fun class and made it draining.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's kinda bad at explaining things, and sometimes things are different than how Pearson expects you to do things. Make sure you know how to do the written homework problems, since those are what the exam tests on the most

I took this course online, so the grading might be different from his in-person class, but Professor Cecil was great. Most of the online lectures are from the Math Department, but he is easily accessible by email and provides supplemental material. Exam grades were very forgiving, too. If you try your best and ask for help, you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have taken this professor for math 1210 and now I am taking him for 1220. He isn't the worst professor ever but he does skip steps and goes through some examples too fast. I really don't like the way his exams are. The first couple questions are multiple choice so if you get a question wrong, that's 5 points gone.
Very lecture heavy. He's right handed and has pretty decent handwriting.

He is a good professor and seems like a chill guy. His office hours are helpful and his lectures are overall good. He does assign a lot of homework that can take a long time to complete. His tests are really difficult and you often aren't fully prepared for what is on them. His grading scale is nice though (an 88% is an A) but he doesn't curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very chill guy. Really knows his stuff. Great professor to go to and ask random calculus related questions and he is able to give you deep answers rather than just surface level things related to tests.

The curved grading scale ensures that if you put real effort into the class, you won't fail. However, if you're not willing to put every bit of free time into repetitively practicing problems, you'll end up with a bad grade. I got a 54% on the second midterm exam, yet studied with every bit of free time I had in the week leading up to the test.

He teaches pretty well in his lectures, and I feel he grades leniently on the tests, but that doesn't help the fact that he assigns so much homework. The week before finals, he assigned 5 different homework assignments. These aren't short assignments by any means and will typically take around an hour each, even with help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has an easy grading scale (88%=4.0) and thank God because his tests are brutal. Don't be fooled by the easy practice tests. A very knowledgeable professor but also ruthless. No homework following exams but the weeks following will have 4-5 assignments each taking 30-60 minutes each.
lectures are confusing
Throws math up on the board without thoroughly explaining it and wonders why whenever he asks a question, barely anybody answers

He spent the entire semester out because his "dad was in the hospital" then came back and gave everyone bad grades right before the final because nothing had been graded up until this point. He doesn't allow a formula sheet, unlike every other professor, and expects students to memorize 20+ formulas and know which to use based on word problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Cecil is nice, but not the easiest to follow. His lectures are on old recordings, you need to have a SOLID understanding of math. Don't expect him to teach you, he isn't there to teach but answer questions in a non understanding way. He does slide his grading to make decent grades easier, but for a reason. Curve grading on exams only not finl
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. He goes too fast to take notes from and can barely explain the math he's doing. He's a nice guy but going to his class is a waste of time. He just projects his iPad notes and talks through them but skips steps and assumes you know a lot of things and won't explain. if you take his class, tutoring and Youtube is your best friend

Pretty okay experience all things considered. The textbook's essentially mandatory to read if you take it online, as the lectures are really only beneficial for supplementing them. Matthew was responsive to my emails. Exams were a mix of multiple choice, with some handwritten questions. I don't think the practice exams prepare you quite enough.

He's a fine professor, but the tests are so difficult, I pulled 3 all-nighters studying for his exams this semester. He doesn't allow cheat sheets, and every other professor does. The homework is very difficult, and the tests are very hard, and you have to rush to complete them. His grade curve is nice, though.

I would not take calc 2 from him. He's nice, but he can go on tangents in lecture. You aren't allowed a cheat sheet on exams, his exams are very hard to finish on time, has a multiple choice section worth about 29% of your exam grade where no partial credit is possible. Made learning already difficult material much harder

Wasn't nice when I asked for help and was not super willing to work with me and help me understand, and he didn't use the textbook. All the homework is on webwork which I hated because It takes like three times longer than what it would normally take just because I will type it in wrong, or get one small thing wrong but webwork says its wrong.
Do not take calc 2 with him it was awful.

Matt is a great professor. 99% of the time he is very clear, concise, and informative. He is very respectful of questions, and often does a great job explaining things in further detail if requested. Occasionally he goes pretty fast, which can make keeping up difficult if you don't fully understand the content. Assignments are pretty manageable.

The average scores for our first exam was a 65% and the second was 56%. He curved these to save us and himself. Instead of seeing these scores as a reflection of his teaching style, he suggested that we "improve our study habits". I'm disappointed in the UofU of continuing to support teachers like passively teach. Quality has dropped since 2016.
Was really great explaining math concepts and listening to questions. Seemed like he really cared about how his students did in the course and wanted them to do well. Overall a good professor.

Overall good class, I recommend strongly to have experience in precalc completely as the course does move quickly, lectures can be very helpful but handwriting on blackboard can be hard to read I recommend to sit in the front and become familiar with midterm format early on
Cecil's class was fine. It's a pretty hard calc class but his grading scale is every 15% which makes it pretty easy to get a good grade. Homework and labs help cushion your grade too.

I'm not sure how his in-person lectures are, but I took Calc 3 online from him and his pre-recorded lectures are awful: low quality videos, bad handwriting, and overall I think he's just not a good lecturer. The homeworks and exams are fair, though. The class is fine as long as you can find another source to actually learn the material from :D

He puts questions on the exam that you have never covered in class. If you do go over it in class it is for 3 seconds max and you get one example. He makes learning calculus way more difficult than it has to be. He also has sloppy handwriting which is stressful. I will never take another math class taught by him again.

I like his class! It's difficult, but I think that's also just bc it's calc. He can go on some tangents, and some things feel a little rushed because of the amount of content, but overall a good professor. He also has pretty dry humor that pops out at random times, which is always enjoyable. Medium amt of weekly hw, but can help cushion the grade.

I took the class online and I found him very unhelpful. After our first exam he word for word sent an email out saying how he noticed a lot of students struggling with derivative rules and that we needed "to fix your problems as soon as possible" with no further help or suggestions for students to receive help. Do not take it online.

I learned what I needed to, but this professor was really boring and had really meandering lectures. The homework isn't too bad if you stay on top of it and understand the concepts, but if you don't, then it takes forever. Also, I didn't have any TA's, which made it difficult to get help on assignments.

Overall he was pretty good. The class was difficult but that's just calculus. He usually did a really good job of explaining the material, only problems are that there is a lot of material covered in a very short amount of time, but I guess that's not really his fault. Just try not to miss class or make up is gonna be really difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought his lectures were very informative, helpful, and entertaining. He is very explicit with what he expects from students even going so far as to tell us where he was getting questions for the final. He's always willing to go through the smaller steps even if it's something simple. Tests are also a large part of the grade

Don't recommend. There are 25+ difficult homework problems a week, and each type of problem is only gone over once in class, sometimes not at all.
His grading scale is generous, but it was extremely difficult to learn the math. I left lectures extremely confused, and I couldn't teach myself because the homework problems were nowhere online.

A little dull, but his grading scale is very generous. Letter grades are every 15% instead of 10%. So 85 is A-, 70 is B-, etc. I could've gotten a 0 on the final and still passed the class. Homework only took a couple of hours each week. Midterms weren't too bad. If all you care about his getting the credit, then take it from Cecil.

Professor Cecil uses a variety of resources to teach the content, including a lot of good lectures. His tests are very similar to the practice tests he gives. You know what is expected and if you put forth the effort you can easily get an A. He offers a generous curve/extra credit, I finished with 108%! I would definitely take his class again!
tests difficult, especially multiple choice section, but seems like he has been teaching the class for a long time so he knows what he is doing. The lectures were okay.

I found the pre-recorded lectures to be useful, only helpful on exam 1 and 2 though. Not enough examples to help much on the later material. Textbook = useless, looked at it ONCE the entire semester. Practice tests are helpful and mirror what's on the exams. Fair grader, gives significant partial credit. Study for the damn tests and you'll do well.

The prerecorded lectures were mostly useless so be prepared to do a lot of youtube searching for answers. This class is mostly graded based on tests, and he provided tons of test prep to use which was very helpful. Don't buy the textbook its mostly proofs and I never found it helpful.

Prof Cecil was a good professor, he just makes his tests really hard. Thorough in his lectures, but a really harsh grader, and takes points off tests for crazy things (not writing x to inf when doing L'Hopital's rule). Lots of homework, but if you put in the time and effort this is a good class. Practice exams are just like the actual test.

Mediocre at best. He may be alright online, but he rushes through the material in person and is terrible at answering questions. The tests are hard!!! Averages were around 50%, he doesn't curve. No notecards are allowed. Tests are basically speed tests rather than covering knowledge. I would avoid taking in-person classes with him if possible.
He was genuinely fine. He definitly cares about his students as people, but in an academic sense fine is the mouse accurate term.

Nice guy, but goes fast and doesn't go over everything. Not very good at teaching. Doesn't bother to re-write tests and quizzes even if we didn't learn the given topic yet. Quiz every single day. Don't take Calc 2 from Cecil.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took online class. Just use khan academy instead of recorded lectures. Weekly homeworks don't take too much time. 4 exams are 70% of the grade and the final was difficult, but they are very similar to his past exams which are online with answers to study. Generous grading scale and rounds grades. Put in the time on exam weeks and you'll do fine.
Honestly just didnt like his class it was heavy on self learning and watching videos he didnt explain anything

OMFG, he is insane. His tests are extremely short timed considering how much problems on the tests. Usually no one ever completes his tests. It is like speed test. Be prepared or you wont pass. And if I were you I wouldn't take it from him. The class average was 60%. But he has a generous curve. 10-15% bump on what you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took his 2210 course online, so all the lectures were recorded videos posted online. He has a very abrasive personality and makes you feel dumb if you ask any clarification questions.

The worst math professor I've ever had. Timed exams, where you have to complete 8 CALC problems in 25 minutes or less. I know the material, but my test anxiety is thru the roof in this class. He explains things in a way more complicated way than necessary. He gave me a 9/14 on a pre exam assignment, bc the angle of my camera was wrong. DONT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class by Dr. Cecil is the worst class I've been in. He gives me the feeling that he doesn't care about our class, and he never responds to students' discussions on canvas. His recorded lectures are very hard to understand; I have to google the topics myself. When it comes to exams, you won't have time to finish. Avoid this prof if you can.

This professor was terrible. He is lazy when it comes to teaching, the video lectures that he does have recorded make no sense so I ended up teaching myself most of the content off of the internet. Oftentimes the homework is very different from the lectures. Tests are also not allotted enough time to even finish large sections of work. Stay clear!!

I took an online 2210 class. He posts weekly videos about the subject, has online HW, and written HW. The tests are awful. They are about 70-60% of what you practice in the HW and reviews. The rest is just abstract questions or questions you hardly have touched. Avoid this prof if you want to learn and get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cecil gets through lectures efficiently and provides very good notes to be annotated in class. Exams are representative of homework and very fair. He teaches some things in a very confusing way, so your mileage may vary. He is a very big fan of proofs and you will have no doubt that what he is telling you is true.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Calc 1 from Cecil and he's okay. He gives out weekly homework and the section I was in also included a lab that was also graded. His class is graded on a generous curve with an 88 being an A. But his tests are crazy hard and you should study for them intensely. The average on my classes final was a 63%. Would not recommend

The online homework program used is called Derivita, there was one homework every week with about 23-25 problems. Now that sounds easy, but the Derivita program is such a pain to use with the case sensitive formatting. Don't take this class if you are taking other harder classes, because study time on top of homework will take up all your time

Good professor. His grading criteria are by 15 points instead of the usual 10. So an 85 is an A a 70 is a B and so on. Also, he has his previous tests available to study so that really helped me pass the tests. If you can't learn properly in lectures (like me) I suggest taking the class online. At least then you can rewind the videos

Matt has a monotone voice so if you tend to fall asleep easily to that then I would recommend to not take this class. His exams are pretty difficult and the practice tests are just extra problems for you to do, it doesn't reflect the actual exams. He is very generous on the grading curve, but the final exam average for my class was a 65% so :/
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took online Calc III class. Matt has a bunch of lecture videos for each section. The videos are pretty lengthy, but it has good content. The assignments are reasonably straightforward. The killer of this class is the exams, half multiple choice half written. Study religiously for exams. The final was one of the hardest tests I have ever taken.

Matt is a pretty good professor, despite teaching a difficult subject that not many people enjoy taking. He can fall into the "this math concept is easy because it's instinctive to me" trap but mostly explains everything thoroughly and in multiple ways. I'd recommend for Calc, for sure.
Study, study, study! Professor Cecils tests are very hard. If you have questions ask in class or during office hours. The proofs are confusing so pay attention to the math rather than the proofs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Matt did an 'ok' job for my calc 1 class. I ended up relying completely on the math department videos because his were lacking topics covered in the homework and tests. He came off as a little condescending and rude when I emailed him questions. The tests were killer and way harder than the homework problems. At least he offered some extra credit.
I took Calculus 1 before I went into this class, so I may be biased, but I felt like he made sense and explained the material well. He has a sarcastic sense of humor, so that's a perk.

Cecil is a quirky and fun professor. He'll teach you how to "play the game" of calculus. I had taken AP Calculus AB before taking this class, but he really dove in deep into some of the concepts. There are a lot of proofs in the lectures, so stay awake if you can. Definitely try a lot of practice problems before the test, they are historically hard
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Love this guy only one homework assignment a week. Really easy to understand and even had a little humor.

Cecil is a no nonsense guy. He doesn't waste time and gets through lectures effectively and quickly. I find his approach very refreshing. If you pay attention in class his explanations actually make a lot of sense and he doesn't skip over things that other math profs would. Homework is average, test content is similar to practice tests and homework

I loved Professor Cecil. His explanations  were detailed, and sometimes a bit too wordy, but they built a good foundation for the material. He does give a fair load of homework, but he grades pretty fairly, and it's really clear what's expected of you, but you have to be willing to show up, pay attention to lectures, and show ALL of your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I don't know why so many people have burned Professor Cecil in the reviews lately. He's a nice guy and he does a good job. I took Calc 1 and Calc II from him. If you take his physical class, his lectures are quite good. If you take his online class, his lecture videos are great supplements, but make sure to watch the math department videos as well.

Do not take online Calc III from this professor. You will hate your life. I got mostly A's on my homework assignments and struggled to pass his exams. His test averages hit 70%. His grading scale is generous, but it does not compensate. Doesn't check your work on exams like most math teachers, chooses the lazy route and has mostly multiple choice.

His tests are awful. Even if you do okay on the homework it won't help you much. Unless you are a math genius or have a lot of time Avoid this class! No calculators and no formulas on the test and no credit for multiple choice unless you get the right answer.  Good news is he lowered the grade needed to pass otherwise you would die.

Avoid Professor Cecil. In comparison to other teachers, he is the worst. Cecil is the only one who thinks it is ok to put questions on the test that are not even similar to HW or practice exams. If you are trying to get into a successful career, take it from someone else. He is rude and a harsh grader. You will like math if you take from another.

He has his own recorded lectures, in addition to the Math's department online lectures. I liked the Math department's lectures better, but watched all of Matthew's lectures as well. His lectures are very good supplements and he explains a few things differently which I found helpful. He also does weekly online office hours which he records.

Prof. Cecil was a really good teacher. I took his online class (which can be a risk with online math) but it went really well. Good steady pace with an assignment a week and 4 tests for the semester. Great class and a lot of resources if you need help. The tests are a bit hard, that's what got me with the B-
He does a great job teaching this class. He has note packets for every week and he makes it all the way through the material without rushing. Very good teacher.

I'll have to take it again, but I'd gladly take it from Cecil. He's helpful and will explain how to do any problem, but really with this class, it's about how much work YOU put in. You need to do the homework (there's a lot of it). You need to do the lab packets (They require outside assistance). He grades on a pretty generous curve (100-85 is A)

I've taken Calc 1 and Calc 2 from Matt and could not ask for a better professor. He's super clear when explaining things in his online office hours. His grading scale is wonderful and his online practice quizzes are very helpful when studying for exams. I would suggest him as a professor any day.

Every week he has an hour where you can ask him any questions from the assignment. He goes through each part step by step, which is very nice. The assignment do take a while to do though, but that was expected in an online class.  His videos were very informative, and they were enjoyable to watch.

Straightforward with his syllabus and teaching style, and has a good curve for the online course. Keep up with the homework and be prepared for a challenging second exam. Has online office hours that are worth attending if you need help.

This Professor is amazing! He is so wiling to work with you on anything and understands there is more than just his class going on in your life. He gives good feedback and is extremely responsive to emails. He has lecture videos that he posts for his calculus series in canvas and they are very helpful! I don't think I would've passed Calculus wout

His grading scale is made to let students pass. I think 89-90% is A or something. Unlimited attempts on homework. Do whatever it takes to get 100% on all the homework(google should help you, hint hint) and you are guaranteed with somewhere around B as long as you get passing grade for tests. He replies back promptly and office hours are useful.

Awesome professor.  It's pretty chill taking this class online.  You only have to worry about submitting one assignment a week and there's only two midterm tests and a final in addition to the homework that make up your grade.

Very good teacher. He makes his own videos and posts them online. He also posts previous tests and his exams are very similar to those. He was very helpful and responded to questions quickly. Weekly homework assignment, two midterms, and a final exam make up your grade.
She is overall a great teacher. I wish to have her as a teacher again
I highly recommend taking Mitizi's Writing 2010 class. She was a gracious and caring professor!

Amazing teacher! She gives us a lot of opportunities to get the grade that we want, and her classes are super easy. She also makes sure that this class isn't heavy with homework. There are times when the assignments are confusing, but eventually you will get it. If you are thinking about taking a WRTG 2010 class, this is the class for you!
would not recommend

Mitzi is very comprehensive and tolerant. Attendance is not mandatory and if you have some problem you should totally message her about an assignment or something that happened that you couldn`t finish it in time. Definetly th ebst writing teatcher I've ever had.

Mitzi is a very caring professor. I took the second-half course in the summer semester, so she cut down the syllabus in order not to make it intense for us. She is SUPER chilled with our assignments, she is always ready to help you with your assignment if you fall behind. Definitely choose her as an instructor for my writing class if I had a chance
I took it online and it was pretty easy. Lots of quizzes but only 2 essays and 4 exams.

Dr Clayton really cares about her students and is passionate about music. The class was overall easy, but exams are a LOT of memorization and niche knowledge. The hour review videos never cover everything on the test, and neither do the documents. There are no real lectures; videos are eclectic. Cheat sheets were LONG and still didn't cover it!
Cathryn is a good professor. The class itself isn't too hard besides the 3 exams.

This class is very easy. The tests are all memorization, but if you just do the reviews you should be able to to get above 90%. She's very generous grading papers so just do all of the assignments and an A is gaurenteed.

The class itself is really dry, but that's mainly the textbook's fault. For her part, her lecture videos were actually rather informative, and helped clarify the textbook content and boil things down to the important concepts. She's a really nice person, and she's passionate about the subject.

This class was very easy as someone who's played piano for most of my life. Literally did half the course in the first week. All you have to do is try your best and complete the participation stuff. The tests had unlimited retakes, except for the final, which was open note. Piece of cake and easy A, I never saw profs face the entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took intro to music theory online. Was simple enough, just about what I expected from an online course in that it was not too engaging or difficult.

The class was ok, but lectures were very repetitive and not super easy to understand. Kind of disorganized, and completely based on memorization. Study guides and exam prep was good though. Probably wouldn't take again, but wasn't bad.

Expectations are laid out clearly and tests are very memorization-heavy. Lectures are quite boring, Dr. Clayton tends to ramble, and due to the nature of the class and her teaching style, none of the topics within World Music are discussed in the depth they deserve.

(previously 3600) I ended up finding this class extremely interesting despite my initial hesitancy! Assignments included chapter quizzes, a couple papers, some discussion posts and 3 tests all of which were fairly easy if you show up to class.  Tests were a little difficult but very easy if you consistently go to class and prepare beforehand.

I took MUSC 1250 online, and the teacher is fantastic. The class was tough at first for a 1000-level course, with easy assignments but hard tests. After we gave her feedback during the semester, she posted review zoom recordings for the tests and made the last two tests easier. Overall, I'd recommend the class now that the difficulty was improved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, it is not a hard class, but just the tests are annoying. Closed book, proctored, which is frustrating but not too bad.

She is really sweet and accessible. The stuff I had the hardest times with were the tests, they were closed book and would rely on super-specific facts that are hard to recall off the top of your head. The weekly quizzes were tedious but you can retake them with no point reduction. The papers were fairly simple to, she is a very forgiving grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Ms. Clayton is not a bad professor by any means but also not a fantastic one. The class doesn't do her any favors as it is typically very dry but the material was a little boring, the teaching was a little boring, but the class wasn't hard.

Overall, the class isn't that bad, and there are far worse professors out there. Dr. Clayton is very nice, she's open to questions, etc. The class is just very dry. I don't know whether to fault her or the textbook, but the class treats world music like the questionable textbook in Dead Poets Society treats Shakespeare. It's an easy IR/FF gen tho.

Nice lady, class isn't that hard, but the workload is not entry level and it can get really time consuming if you let it. You'll have a minimum of 4 assignments a week, sometimes double that. They aren't hard but they also don't prepare you for the close-note exams. Not a gen-ed I would recommend trying to squeeze in during a heavier semester.

Prof. Clayton is a good and kind professor, I just do not find the material that interesting. Class is graded on a few < 30 minute discussion posts, 3 short papers, and 3 exams. Attendance is not mandatory and generally this class is super easy, just study for the test with the terms she provides and read the short textbook chapters. Easy class.

I think Prof. Clayton does a really good job at communicating very well with her students. If you end up missing a day, she'll zoom her lectures so you don't get behind on anything. She's also very flexible  at giving you a make up day if you miss an exam and will let you redo assignments if necessary.
Her classes are very boring and she thinks students taking the class are all music majors hence teaches that way but I think it would be better if she taught it in the way of a gen ed.

Got on the zooms maybe the first 3-ish weeks until I just stopped altogether- they were pretty boring to me so I kept falling asleep. Quiz answers can be found online so you only really need to read if there's a paper due, which are not very often and very easy to BS. Professor is very, very sweet tho and obviously passionate about the subject.

Dr. Clayton is very caring and enthusiastic about world music. Exams are 50 questions with mostly multiple choice questions. Her exam review guides will be the most important resource for an easy A. There are a few papers; however, they're easy to complete. Discussion and quizzes take 20 minutes max. Easy class for IR and FF requirements.
Professor Clayton was a decent professor. Her lectures and assignments were clear, but since this was an online class, it wasn't ideal to have proctored exams with such heavy content.

The online course allowed you to do assignments and quizzes as often as you wanted before the due date, so getting a 100% on everything is easy. The exams you can only take once, so it's best you understand the material before taking them, but they weren't too difficult.

Unit tests -heavily graded, proctored (3 x 100 pts each) comprehensive; small assignments (5-10 pts each). The instructor is knowledgeable, caring, but a little long-winded. We studied country by country rather than comparing instruments/music across the globe -  would have been more helpful. Study guides: time-consuming so do while reading text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy and the course does teach you some stuff about music theory. The program that they used for quizzes and assignments I did not like because you had to drag and drop.
Wouldn't recommend taking this class as an elective. If you don't have prior music experience, get ready to put in some real hours. Not the easy A I was expecting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easy class for those who have experience with musical instruments. Mostly self-taught, but her videos are very helpful. Fun composition projects as well. Would recommend it, especially if you play an instrument or are interested in composition.
Lengthy class with a dry textbook. Mostly a self-taught class, but structured in a way that's manageable for sure. Easy credit so long as you study a bit.

There are lots of quizzes but you have unlimited retakes so it's no stress. There are three exams, collectively worth half of your grade. There are study guides made for each of these with precisely what will be on the exam. There are also three short essays, two concert reports, and one term paper, all of which are very easy.

one of the best teachers ive had. though theres homework due each week u have unlimited attempts and can find answers easily. same each week so you know what to do. took two classes with this teacher and would recommend to anyone for gen eds. always willing to make accomodations if something happens in your life and is so understanding.

This class is fairly easy, but I have a background in music and wouldn't recommend it unless you do too. There's a lot of information you have to learn about music history so if you're just trying to get an easy credit I wouldn't take this class. Lots of quizzes every week plus inquisitive. Good for a summer course but not for fall or spring.

This professor is terrible. Like many people have said, a 1010 class should not be this hard, especially for a gen ed class. This is insane. There's so much homework and crazy expectations. I def do not recommend this class whatsoever.

Took this class online, and it was so easy. I never really interacted with the professor much at all. There are a few assignments to do every couple of weeks but they are really easy to complete. There are a few more effort-full assignments throughout the semester like a few short essays, but theyre not bad at all. Its hard to not do well.

Lots of weekly quizzes based off of reading. The assignments are pretty repetitive and there are a lot of them but they aren't too hard. The professor is very nice and willing to open tests early to accommodate schedule issues!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her exams are hard. I would not take this class. Quizzes and assignments does not correlate with the exam. I would take another easier gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was, without a doubt, the worst class I've taken. ALL the material on the midterms was not in any of the previous quizzes or assignments, and hardly anything counts in the final grade except for those midterms. On top of it all, the course material is utterly useless and unimportant.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has a ridiculous amount of work each week however you don't really have to do it all. Quizlet will be your friend and a lot of the assigned readings aren't graded. The tests are open internet so if you're good at utilizing that you don't need to study. Maybe this class is good in person but online it's just too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you already have a musical background, take this class it'll be an easy A . If not stay away. I could do all the assignments easily as I already knew it all but if I didn't I would've hated this class. The videos help with nothing and the quizzes are so frustrating. If you get one part of 20 wrong then no points for the whole question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course structure is simple. read the book chapters, take the short quizzes, and then do a final chapter quiz. midterm & final exams are not hard if you do the work. i didnt even study! she lets you turn in the assignments on your own time with flexible deadlines. responsive. gives her own lectures for difficult sections in the book!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Overall, she didn't do much aside from read from the textbooks in her lectures. You can almost entirely just use the canvas page and the textbook and never have to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Clayton is a solid professor she lays out the class well so that you know what to expect to receive the highest grade you want in the class. I took it online and there was a lot of weekly homework assignments. A lot of help can be found on quizlet for this. There are three midterms. If youre looking for an easy fine arts credit this is it.

Class is fairly easy, especially if you enjoy some aspect of music or want to learn. Its basically teach yourself which can be a downside but there are some lecture videos which are very helpful. If you work ahead you can finish the course really fast and get it done with. Learned a lot to add to my musical knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Maybe its the covid thing but it really doesnt seem like she cares... up to 4 quizzes per week and up to 40 questions in each quiz, all completely mind numbing. not really sure if there are even lecture videos to accompany the class, ive just been using the textbook. DO NOT take this class looking for an easy general, you will regret it.

No lectures or lecture videos to watch. Mostly all the work is just reading the textbook and taking chapter quizzes that have unlimited tries. We did have an open book midterm, but the professor found out that people post the contents of the exams to Quizlet, so we were forced to use ProctorU for the final which is such a sketchy browser extension.

There are weekly quizzes but they are based on the homework and on the chapter quizzes you are allowed unlimited attempts. If you don't like music you probably won't enjoy this class but passing it with an A will still come easy.

Horrible structure. Hours of videos and reading each week for this class. No lecture or any content from the professor themself. Class is based solely on reading out of a poorly written textbook and at least three or four hours of jazz videos each week. Tests are based on obscure, miniscule details that no one would remember. Very annoying class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Worst. Class. Ever. For an INTRODUCTION class, there's way too much homework. Over 10 quizzes a week. And most quizzes have the same questions. There's also essays you have to write, and she doesn't even read them. She will give you 100% for just writing something, but she'll also write "Great Report!" This entire class was just busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly if you have to take this class it sucks the tests were ridiculously hard. I took it online so in class will probably be a ton easier.

This class was taken for my international requirement, but it was a fantastic class to take, especially because I was interested in music. The textbook is a must when doing the assignments and quizzes, and the exams required a fair amount of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Every assignment is a quiz and you can do it over as much as you want until you get a good grade on them. Prof. Clayton was very nice, willing to work with you and answer questions. The material is very organized and presented well.

Professor Clayton's online class (MUSC 1460) was relatively easy for someone with a music background. If you have no musical experience, prepare for a lot of textbook reading and studying. Professor Clayton is always willing to help out if you ask. You have unlimited redos on all homework and quizzes, and the test questions come from the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Clayton was awesome. This course satisfied my International Requirement for the University of Utah. There is an online textbook for this course. It's really fascinating. If you study hard and read the book, you'll be just fine. Her class is structured well and quite reasonable. I highly recommend taking this class from her.

If you show up to her class and actually listen, you will pass. The tests are usually 50 questions and are multiple-choice. They probably take about 15min to take. There are only 4-6 homework disscussions and they're pretty easy. Dr. Clayton is very nice and quirky. She doesn't dock you points if you turn a discussion in late. Overall good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really easy class, especially if you already know a bit about music. The last part was tough for me because I didn't know any of the material, but I figured it out okay. You can retake all of the quizzes and homework until you get 100%, so you can get an A+ if you put in a little extra time.

Her lectures are great. She marks 100% on the homework as long as you finish them, and you can even turn them in late. So I thought this class was very easy until taking the tests. They are hard since you don't know what she expects, and you seem to have to know *every detail from class to do good. They also make up 3/4 of the final grade :(

Really sweet woman. Understands that her class is a "Gen Ed." class so makes it genuinely interesting and fun. Really good study guides that prepare for the test too. You can skip a good amount of classes but I liked the class enough that I actually wanted to go.

While this is just Intro to Music Theory, you can tell that Professor Clayton cares a lot about what she's teaching and who she's teaching. The textbook integration of the material is done well, and her supplemental online lectures are clear and easy to understand.

She's not a bad teacher, but she didn't really do much, then again it's an online class. She's available and has a TA and they explain things well. I have a music background so the class was extremely easy, but if you're completely new there are probably some topics that'll be iffy. The tests are scheduled and taken in person on paper.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was fun and interesting. Probably the best class you could take for the IR and Fine Arts requirement. She had fair tests if you at least cram an hour or two but if you didn't have the energy the extra credit or two will save the day.
Fantastic class, fantastic professor!!!

I took this class for my music minor thinking it would be an easy A class. It was for the most part; there were only a few assignments to work on at home, and attendance wasn't mandatory, but the tests really killed me! They are SO HARD! I got 100% on every assignment but I did terribly on the tests and even the extra credit didn't help a ton.

The tests for the class are easy if you put some time in to studying, follow the study guide and use the flashcards and you should be fine. There are quizzes for every chapter, but they're not hard. Only a few papers, not graded harshly. If you email her, it may take some time, but she'll get back to you with a good response.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good class. Lots of videos to watch. The technical stuff was hard for me to grasp. Workload wasn't too heavy. Grading was fast, which I appreciated.

The way Dr. Clayton taught her class was disorganized which made it difficult to take notes because you don't really know what to write. There are a couple papers and discussions, but she's an easy grader so as long as you do it you'll get full credit. She's also extremely lenient with late work which is a plus. Do well on the exams and you're set.

I took Music 1010 for the summer for a fine arts credit. No complaints. Fair grading, just make sure you study for the midterms. The class isn't too hard as long as you study. The study guides are useful for prepping for midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Clayton is AMAZING!!! Her classes are super organized, and pretty easy. There's one basic quiz and assignment each week. She will give you tons of help, and is EXTREMELY lenient. There's no penalty for turning things in late, so there's no stress about deadlines. Would totally recommend her as a professor.
This class is an easy A if you have done any music before.

This online class is very simple if you have a music background.  If not, you will have to put in some effort.  Once a week there is an assignment, but you only have to say you did it, and then a simple online quiz that can be taken as many times as needed.  She is very helpful and will answer whatever questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nice professor, is really passionate about music. I'm not a music major, so the class was sometimes boring for me. But she prepares you for exams.

I love her online courses! So organized, so I never have to guess what's coming up next. And I can always work ahead if I know I'm going to be busy. You get unlimited tries on quizzes. The papers are short and pretty straightforward. Just use her study guide for the exams and you'll do fine. Would recommend 1000% if you need a FF, DV, or IR credit.

Doctor Clayton is nice. She does a great job at making this class interesting. She brings in a few guest lecturers and instruments from around the world. Her tests are mainly multiple choice, a few listening, and a couple free response. If you attend the lecture before the test, she usually goes over everything that you need to know for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took online survey of jazz to fulfill the FF requirement. The class has weekly assignments and quizzes with three tests. Studying for these tests is a must! If you complete the quizzes, and the study guide she gives you, you'll do fine. Prof Clayton gives extra credit and was easy to reach with questions.

Cathryn is so adorable. She cares about her students and music. her class is so easy. just attend her review sessions a class time before the exam and she goes over her exam review materials. study off of that and you're solid. no need to attend class or read the textbook.

Class was Easy. You don't really have to show up to class, just study the study guides she provides for the 2 midterms and final and you will be fine. Do the other small assignments in class and don't miss the easy points.  Don't waste your money on the book, you won't use it. If you do attend class, she makes it fairly interesting

I took this class online and I loved it. Professor Clayton lines out exactly what you need to do and when you need to do it. Straightforward class. I learned new things even though I've been playing piano for 13 years. I would recommend this class to anyone who still needs to fulfill a GenEd requirement.
I loved Cathryn. She's very generous and lenient with due dates, and I truly enjoyed her lectures.
Professor Clayton is great! Although this subject was totally new to me, she made the class not so hard. I also had technical issues and she was so understanding. I would recommend.

Prof Clayton is great. I took her class online. She encourages questions and provides lots of practice. Definitely recommend. She uses this outdated online CD things as a textbook. IDK. It wasn't very compatible with my computer. The songs wouldn't play and some functions didn't work. BUT she provided enough instructional material it was fine.

I took the class online and there were discussion posts almost every week, but they were easy. Lots of quizzes, but they're all simple. Really easy grader- I got 100 on every assignment. However, the tests were really hard. I would study for 2 weeks in advance, yet the highest test grade I got was a 76. If you're a good test taker, its a good class

She assigns online discussions to participate but not very difficult. Just the difficult material. Some writing assignments and two concert reports. One 15 points worth extra credit concert report (DO IT!!!) Tests are tough but if you study, you will be fine.
Cathryn is the best professor you will encounter at the U. If you want an easy A take it with her. Listening portion on the exam was the only part i did not like in her exams.

Three tests total with a few assignments each week. Taking it online I thought was really easy and manageable. Clayton is great at laying out exactly what you're supposed to do. If you read the textbook, it actually helps even though it's bland. She gives you a review sheet for each midterm that is GOLD. Review those concepts and you're good to go.

She's the happiest professor I've ever met; always smiling and happy! Late-work policy is amazing, have it in by the end of the semester and you're good! She brings in musicians occasionally & tries to make class interesting. Tests are easy as long as you study the review. Hardly ever used the textbook, but you do need the CD's for listening.

Easy A. There were 3 essays assigned throughout the semester but, as long as you don't plagiarize and meet the minimum requirements, she'll give you 100%. Chapter quizzes every week but you can do them as many times as you need except for movie quizzes, but most of the answers are online.

Dr. Clayton is a wonderful, caring, and attentive teacher!  I learned much more than I expected about world cultures through taking MUSC 3600.  She explains concepts in a very clear, easy to understand/approach way.  Attendance is not mandatory, but I went every time because I got so much out of her lectures!  She is also easy to work with!!!

This class is a gem; go to class, pay attention, learn about the world, and get an A.  She brings musicians to class occasionally, which is fun.  She's the happiest professor I've ever had, always laughing and giggling; very pleasant.  Her late-work policy is outrageously flexible; basically, if it's in by the end of the semester, you're golden.

I was really not interested in the class, but Dr. Clayton made it at least bearable.  I would say the tests are pretty hard if you're not familiar with music. Lots of names of people but if you need clarification she is definitely there to give it to you. It was the first time it was taught, so it can only get better and she did a great job.
She is super cute and funny. She is super flexible and you can pass this class no problem as long as you do the work.

Tangs canvas page is very confusing and figuring what assignments are due at the end of the week was the hardest part of her class. otherwise the workload is very manageable. online lectures help and she will respond to questions via email.

The professor is extremely hard to understand and the directions are not clear whatsoever. The actual workload isn't overly insane, but I felt as though I was teaching myself with no guidance throughout the course, rather than the professor doing her job. Honestly, save yourself and do not take this class.

Professor Teng's class had an individual project for the first half of the semester and a group project for the second half. Most assignments/projects in this class didn't have clear instructions. Office hours were only by appointment but was available to talk after class since the class typically didn't last the full amount. Not what I expected.

Professor Teng is ok, I really liked the guest speakers she would bring in and her lectures were ok. Professor Teng doesn't really answer emails however. Once your grade drops it's hard to get it back up, I feel that this course requires too much effort for a gen ed requirement. Least favorite class of the semester to be honest.

Unclear instructions. Not that much work, but extremely confusing and vague. EXTREMELY hard to get in touch with the TAs and the professor. I have been trying to reach out for almost 4 weeks now with no resolution. Due dates are all messed up too and copy and pasted from the spring semester (due dates were in Feb when the semester ends in Dec).

Her Asian accent is sometimes hard to understand. Large class size with 4 TAs. We didn't do too much work in the class, but the assignments weren't always clearly explained, so I spent time trying to figure out what to do. She had some guest speakers come and would sometimes talk about her personal experiences with start-ups which was interesting

Took the online class it was unorganized and clearly a copy/past of her past course from canvas. Set deadlines over breaks the dates in the modules were wrong. (canvas module said it was due in Feb mind you this was a fall semester class) It's easy just useless work through some website. Overall it was lazy and disappointing due t0 lack of effort.
brawhehhhhhhh terrible, ooooof
Snooze Fest

Professor Teng is ok... not great lectures, not very clear what we were supposed to do on assignments, and generally I didn't feel like I learned anything from the class -- but it was a super easy A and activities were hands-on and done mainly in class. Just don't expect to get anything out of the class.

One assignment per week, and the last two were significantly more difficult. The course moves quickly, and most topics require reading beyond lecture material. Cem's textbook chapters were especially helpful for understanding the material. It can be hard to get help outside of lecture, and lecture went 10 or so minutes over time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Cem is one of the most knowledgeable people in the entire graphics field. With that being said, there are very few opportunities to actually see Cem, as the course is based entirely on prerecorded lecture videos and an in-person alternate professor who is not nearly as knowledgeable, and is the only person besides TA's who has office/help hours.

Fantastic. Professors like Cem are the reason the U is a top school (right next to Cornell and Stanford) for graphics. Recorded lectures are high quality, engaging, and give you a peek into upcoming trends in graphics tech that no other professor could shed light on because he and his colleagues are the ones advancing the industry.

There's no SHOT this professor doesn't have 5/5 average when I clicked this page. I've taken both classes he offers. Cem is a real one. There's no other way I would prefer to learn graphics. He's smart, funny, caring, etc. The only downside is you need to get creative when you run into bugs -- not a ton of help hours. Everything else is perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Cem is a very cool professor. His lecture videos are well put together, engaging, and informative. It did feel like the lectures do not directly help with the assignments, so make sure to go to TA hours for help. His exam review sessions are super helpful. Super generous late policy, which was a life saver for me. Fun and interesting class.
fun ass class cem is the big homie lectures are super engaging and online, on ur own time

Loves the subject and understands how complicated it can be so he keeps the pace slow. People complain that he does not do coding examples but he keeps the projects so simple that to provide coding examples would give away the solutions to the projects. I also learned a lot of linear algebra concepts that I struggled with in linear algebra class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Gave alot of skeleton code so u only focus on the material covered in lectures. It's very easy to get stuck if one line of code is off to make sure to find online resources to help u as very little TA hours leads to this class being all Piazza help. Very generous late policy. Really cool projects and he shows u the latest in CG as he does research.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cem is awesome. I took Intro to CG and Interactive CG but the latter was way harder as he didn't give us any skeleton code like the intro class. Projects/material are really cool but getting stuck on a bug for DAYS was common the whole semester which consumed alot of time. He always has less TA hours than he should so online resources are best.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: VERY generous late policy. Late hw only suffers a 5% penalty. Everyone gets 10 late days w/out penalty. Allows free hw submissions after deadlines if you showed a clear attempt the first try. However, such niceness comes at a cost- NO HELP HOURS, piazza only. Also, no coding demos or examples in lectures.

By far the worst class I've ever taken, time & money completely wasted. Expect to do all learning on your own. It would be helpful if he showed us HOW to use OpenGL (as a PROFESSOR should). He doesn't because there are "so many ways" to do it. Just some options of how would be nice, but NO. Expect NO help. Office hours are also a joke.

Cem was awesome! This has been one of my favorite classes at the University of Utah. The structure of the class is great. Your grade is based on assignments only. The assignments aren't terribly hard and a lot of fun. Make sure to pay attention during his lectures since that will be your main guide for the assignments.

If you have a chance to take a class with Cem, do it. Best lectures I had all semester by far, they were interesting and applied directly to the homework. The only work in the class was homework assignments, which were well designed and fun to work on. I couldn't say enough good things about Cem, I would suggest him and this class to anyone in CS.

I absolutely loved Anil; he was actually my professor for Math 1090. I was terrified to get back into math after not taking a math class for 2 whole years, but he was extremely helpful. He explains things in a way that makes sense & provides so many opportunities for students to get help. It never felt rushed & he truly cares about his students!

Anil is a great lecturer so make sure to attend and take notes. It's a hard subject in general, so my only real complaint with the class is that there are so few things graded and no extra credit, so any slight fumble on the two midterms/final drops your grade significantly. Homework/labs are graded pretty easily but they don't cushion your grade.

Anil is a great teacher. Although his lectures can be very conceptual, he explains things thoroughly and is very open to questions. I have never had an issue with getting help from him. The homework is not long, although some questions can be more difficult. The tests are very fair and designed to test the more general aspects of a unit.

Lectures are pretty bad, this is an applied engineering mathematics course primarily focusing on physics, but a lot of time was spent on proofs and derivations that simply don't matter, a lot of time felt wasted. Homework is a mess, graded very harshly and often doesn't resemble class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's honestly so hard to keep up with, learned almost nothing in class and was just so confused.

Anil is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about his students. He makes a concerted effort to assess how well students grasp the concepts he teaches and will dedicate as much time as needed to ensure everyone is up to speed before moving on. If you simply ask him questions, he will make sure to do everything he can to help you understand.

Anil is a great professor. He explains things in ways that are easy to understand. He understands the difficulty of the class and tries to accommodate the best he can. Midterms are very similar to practice midterms he provides, so it's clear what you're supposed to know. Very funny as well which makes the class enjoyable. Definitely take Anil.
Would not recommend at all. Super high standards, more than there should be for a class like this. One of the few classes I truly did not enjoy in my undergrad.

This class feels like a high school class. Attendance is mandatory, the professor wants to learn your name, she has a weird grading scale, and she just FEELS like a high school teacher. You can ignore the readings and a lot of the lecture stuff. For the assignments, there is very tough grading, spend a lot of time editing and perfecting your work.

Just don't take her for this class. Her grading scheme makes the class way too hard for what it is. The grading for each assignment is not lenient and even the smallest mistake can mean a 0 for that assignment. She makes the class much harder than it needs to be, and I've heard other professors make the class reasonable.
Don't take, not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It feels like putting in the work of a 10-credit course for just 3 credits. I spent 8 hours each week on homework, and the grading is so harsh that even one small mistake can mean a zero. Resubmissions aren't allowed unless you use a token. I would strongly discourage anyone from taking her class, as she makes everything unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course wasn't difficult, but she made it extremely hard to pass. Homework can only be submitted once, even before the due date, and any mistake means a zero. This grading policy made it nearly impossible to maintain good grades—I had always been a straight-A student until this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: First assignment. Write about a game. What? I don't play games. Drop.

Weirdest, unclear grading system I've ever seen, extremely heavy on criticism with harsh grading to match. There was an assignment at the end of the VERY FIRST CLASS during syllabus week. It's clear that because this is a remedial class for an engineering course she's completely jaded and thinks that all students hate her class, which they do.

This was an extremely intense course. There were tons of assignments and readings due every week, and it got very overwhelming. Dr. Paskett is nice and will help you where she can, but is a harsh grader and isn't always clear as to what she is looking for. A large part of your grade is a group project where she picks your group. Hope for a good one
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Paskett is a poor professor and I would advise against taking her. She grades very harshly and is often unclear in her critiques to your assignments. She'll often mark you down for not following the seven C's of technical writing, but won't elaborate on which C you were lacking in, which made it difficult to improve your writing.
The class was kind of tough, but she is helpful and I learned a lot. Apply the assignment feedback and you'll be good. I got a job thanks to the resume assignment!

Dr. Paskett is a very tough grader. For the record, this course ruined my 4.0 GPA as an electrical engineer. She gives lots of feedback, but she also expects you to figure out a lot of your writing issues on your own, which was frustrating. If you are worried about your grade coming into this course, take it with another professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cecile is a professional well mannered instructor. She controls the classroom well and paces her lectures so that they can be easily digested. BUT SHE ASSIGNS SO MUCH BUSY WORK. A REVISION AND REFLECTION ASSIGNMENT WORTH 20% OF OUR GRADE DUE ON FINALS WEEK? FOR ENGINEERS? NO ONE CARES ABOUT YOUR CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Every week you watch lecture videos then do surveys and discussions. I actually found this class pretty fun. Midterm paper and final paper are easy if you apply the feedback she gives you throughout the year.
do NOT take this class. her class is so harmful to GPA.

it's a hard class, but she was helpful

This was the worst class I have ever taken. This has been the most difficult class i have ever taken and i regret the day that i signed up for it.

This was the worst class and the worst teacher. Her lectures were confusing and so were the tests. She didn't give you a good study guide, and I didn't feel like anything I learned in class was on the exam. Terrible glass. Take it from someone else.
Absolutely ridiculous. Worst teacher I have ever had. Her tests aren't even based off of what you learn in class. Extremely strict and not helpful whatsoever. Stay away from her class if possible.
Way to hard to understand her wording. Not a lot of assignments/homework. Tests, once again hard to understand her wording which makes them not that easy to pass.

She's a grad student, knows her stuff.  Too theoretical for me.  It's an intro course, yet it was more difficult than my upper division courses.  She's willing to help and answer questions whenever needed though, she's a nice person.

Gaben cares a lot about your success, and he will chat with you to make sure you're both on the same page in regard to assignments. I recommend using office hours if you fall behind or just need to chat things out, he's very understanding.

My favorite professor I have had at the U so far! His lectures are filled with so much knowledge and inspiration, I would take a lot of notes. He also offers great advice. Gaben is a great teacher. He is funny and has a lot of information to give. His lectures are interactive and you are able to talk. He wants you to succeed and get an A. The 3 exams are easy if you pay attention and read the textbook. Overall and great Professor and class.

Professor Sanchez was one of the most inspirational professors I've ever had. He cares a great deal about his students and wants them all to actually learn. He gives great lectures, and is hilarious. He is extremely knowledgeable of the courses he teaches.

Cecilia is incredibly intelligent/kind/engaging, and this class is both interesting and stress free. Great professor. PSY3220 was not hard at all. There were 3-4 tests and a paper, but the combined effort to do those was not that hard.

This professor is the best lecturer I've ever had. So engaging! There were only three assessments the whole semester- two exams and an essay.

Dr. Wainryb was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, but fortunately taught in a way students could understand. She welcomed questions. reviews.comment: If you read the text and go to class everyday and somewhat pay attention in her lectures you will pass. She is so so intelligent. I would do the extra credit if you aren't the best test taker, because all that is on your grade is 2 tests a term paper and an extra credit option.

She is one of my favorite professors at the U. I learned so much from her class. It is definitely a class that you need to attend the lectures to do well. This class was phenomenal - I adored it. Chapman is a fantastic instructor, and made the not-too-easy concepts feel totally manageable. Plus the textbook is actually interesting!
Best teacher in the philosophy department!

Admittedly I am not good at advanced logic. But Chapman worked with me until I got what I needed to. He's exceptionally smart and kind. He gave genuine time in office hours and made sure I demonstrated what I needed to in order to pass the class. If you don't want to be left behind he won't leave you behind. A real gem in the department

Professor Waters has a particular knack for taking complex topics and creating palatable material that is easy for students to understand. Time Travel was anything but BS. Great applied logic course. He's funny, knowledgeable, and exciting. You will need to flex your brain to wrap your head around concepts, but his lectures make this doable. 10/10

I loved him! I took him for deductive logic, which is known to be one of the tougher philosophy classes. He made it really enjoyable and although I did end up getting an a- while striving for an a, I feel that I learned so much that I can apply in my math and cs major! Also the book he makes you buy is actually helpful and the tests r open book
Chapman has a mind for logic and is a great lecturer.

He is clear about expectations from the first day of class. Be ready to read, but fortunately all reading is online. No need to purchase books, etc. The stories and content is very interesting. The material is confusing at times, but Chapman is so approachable and makes lectures so fun and breaks things down to make it easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As someone who has taken two of Chapman's classes and plans on taking a third, I can confidently say that he is one of the best professors in the philosophy department. I really loved what I learned, but I felt that we were graded really harshly. Over the course of the semester, we took 5, 25 point quizzes. The average on all the quizzes was never above a 15/25.
Great professor for Inductive logic. Went at the classes pace, used good examples, funny guy. Would recommend for anyone taking philosophy courses or just interested in logic.

I love Chapman! I took many phil classes from him and really enjoyed learning from him. He cares a lot, so if you put in effort and show that you care, he will match the effort. I had many conversations with him outside of class and he really helped me improve my writing.

Was actually Phil 3210 Inductive Logic that but was not an option to select for this rating.

Great professor who is determined to make inductive logic fun and applicable.

This professor is very passionate about philosophy. His class is challenging in the best way possible. The lectures are super funny and interesting. Chapman is a real character. Entertaining and interesting class to explore new ideas. Somewhat difficult for a 1000 level class, but overall worth it.

No.... Do yourself (and him) a favor and do not go near this professor. I would write a more detailed review; however, I can't even begin to put into words how awful of an experience it is with Professor Waters.

Pure awesomeness.Friendly, knowledgeable and considerate. I'd take another class from her.
Extremely kind and caring professor.

One of the easiest class I've ever taken at the University of Utah. Very little assignments, just readings.
One of the best history professors I've had.

very very easy class. there are 5 modules you have to do the entire semester then you just have to log your steps each week. the final is a class survery. super easy

Horrible experience in class. Would not recommend.

reviews.comment: Daily quizzes (typically take-home due same day) count for a lot of your grade, but are basically an outline of the exam, just with different numbers. GO TO LECTURE. I have sucked at math my entire academic career, and this class was extremely easy to comprehend if you pay attention.

He's actually a great professor. He gives daily quizzes which are incredibly helpful and they don't take long to do! He's also always cracking jokes. Those who scored low probably didn't care enough to try on daily quizzes or pay attention but if you do that you'll do just fine!

Be prepared for a heavy workload, but the path to an A is very clear. While the weekly homework feels like busy work, the daily quizzes are actually the most important part of the class because they mirror the exams exactly. The lectures also align perfectly with the exams. If you show up every day and master the quizzes, you will pass easily.

If you attend lecture every day and do the quizzes, you'll easily pass. Teaches the material concisely with good examples. Exams are just the quizzes with different numbers. Hard to understand his English sometimes and doesn't answer questions well, so just look those up later. ATTENDANCE IS ESSENTIAL. Funny guy too, first time I've liked math.

Love this guy! Comes across a little rude at first but ends up being one of the best professors. Daily quizzes are a little annoying but super helpful in the long run since he bases exam questions off them. Makes tough concepts easy to understand through lots of example problems. Difficult course but very easy to succeed if you put in the work.

I only say lots of homework because he gives daily take home quizzes but they're always related to that day's lecture. His notes are great and the tests directly mirror the quizzes. Easy way to study and he wants you to pass.

Professor Choi was good, You have to go to class because of daily quizes, however these quizes are pretty easy and often are taken home. Exams are honestly easy and he gives plenty of resoruces. Prof choi is not terrible at teaching, hes just very hard to understand and he says that the language barrier isn't an issue and shouldn't be an excuse. Such a great professor, gives you points wherever he can (dropping lowest 6 quiz grades, lowest 3 hw assignments, and lowest midterm grade), and gives amazing notes for how to do things, however he does do a quiz every time you are in class. The quizzes are fairly easy as long as you paid attention in lecture.
Take any math class you can with him. You will not regret it

I got 102% and loved this class, it was so hard though. I think his class structure makes the workload unnecessarily excessive, however it helped me learn the material better than ever.
