Gives daily quizzes and he hasn't even graded half of them -- AND the semester's over. The quizzes near the end were COMPLETELY derailed of the content we learned in class. Take ANYONE else

Professor connects concepts well to previous knowledge to make it easier and faster to learn. He answers questions very thoroughly if you go up to him during break or after class. Homework can be a lot but exams are easy to study for.

Good lectures and use of daily quizzes hammers home the concepts. Provides extra credit on tests. My low rating comes from regularly leaving work ungraded for long periods of time, requiring attendance to be able to work on the quizzes, curving the class to be competitive, high work time ratio on tests, and HW is time intensive redundant busy work.

Took his summer Calc 3. Definitely a language barrier but he will answer all questions asked. Not a bad lecturer and he gives you up to 10 points of extra credit on every test so its pretty hard to fail... Exams are very similar to quizzes but the homework can be difficult at times.

I can usually understand teachers well, but when I am LITERALLY PAYING $3000 to take Multivariable Calculus and the instructor can't speak complete english sentences, I want to sue the university. How do these executives let people like this teach? He needs to work on his english and get a better mic and PLEASE take your job seriously. Do not take.

This professor loathes his students. He will berate anyone for questions and say they aren't paying attention, alienating his own class. Even after asking for questions. He's a 3/5 at explaining things at best. Daily quizzes to check attendance and the way he behaves I can best describe is a middle school professor having a midlife crisis. Avoid.
Choi is the goat, yes he gives you daily quizzes but they aren't hard especially if you do them right after class.

Sung Chan was good at pushing understanding of the material. He would take time in lectures to show some examples and push understanding. Beware of daily quizzes, which arent that difficult if you pay attention in class, as they make up a good chunk of your grade. Exams were easier than hw, which could be tedious. He offered extra credit in exams.

Vector Calculus and PDEs for engineers. The daily quizzes are annoying and time consuming, but they force you to learn. Basically it's a lot of content for one class, but he teaches it pretty well. Super organized guy.
He's a king. There are daily quizzes that you have to get in class, but they really help understand the material. The quizzes are like the tests and he genuinely wants you to understand. Love him!

while the material could be tough, sung choi was able to make it all so easy to understand

reviews.comment: I took his Calc 3 in the summer. He is an amazing and hilarious man, and he teaches you the important things.

Other than that, his teaching style is great and he explains the content in a very understandable and simple way. Exams are graded very leniently and are similar to the daily quizzes. Very funny and down-to-earth professor.

He gives out a daily quiz, which I suppose would be fine but he also gives out lengthy and difficult homework along with this quiz. It was hard to balance both and he makes us show up to receive the quiz, which is stupid that he polices attendance.
He gave us not on intensive homework, but a daily take home quiz. Balancing both was difficult. I would have been ok with one or the other, but this class just was burdensome.

His teaching style made complex mathematical concepts easy to understand. I really liked the class structure, and he genuinely cares about his students. He comes well-prepared for each session, and after taking his class, you can't help but grasp math better. Highly recommend!

He is good at teaching, but a VERY unfair grader. Spent 20+ hours a week on homework alone. 50 % of your homework grade was on completion, 50% was if you did 1 question (a question he chose a random) correctly. 
Did I learn well and a lot in his lectures? Yes.
Did I struggle finding the time to sleep with the amount of homework he gave?
Also yes.

reviews.comment: It can be really hard to understand him at times. Mr. Choi does give out daily quizzes, so attendance matters, that are due the next day, but most of the problems are pulled out from the lectures. Exams are very similar to the quizzes. Mr. Choi is a great professor though, just be weary by the quizzes, they can be challenging at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I learned a ton in this class. Prof. Choi was very clear and detailed in the way he explained things and was thorough about showing the steps to solve each problem. His quizzes and note sheets helped reinforce what we learned in class, the exams were always based directly off of them. He was always nice and pleasant to students. Highly recommend!

I did the best I ever have in any math class as Sung Choi as my 2250 teacher. He had daily quizes that helped a ton to get ready for the exams. Homework and a lab every week which also helped to get ready for the exams. He is hard to understand but if you go to the tutoring center, you will easliy get a good grade.

One of the best professors I have every had in math. Made things clear, lectures notes you can look back at are very well written out. Many example problems. We did have daily quizzes and a handful of homework but the quizzes are short and based on that day's problems. Honestly a very good way to practice, exams were similar difficulty to quizzes!

Took his class for Engi. Calc 2 and Diff Eq. He is an incredibly fair but tough teacher. He will never testor give you hw on something he hasn't taught you on. Attedance is mandatory but tbh his class is the only one I look forward to.

Daily quizzes are kind of a hassle but they don't take much time. Seems scary initially but is actually pretty nice. Exams are copies of his quizzes (90% avg). Straightforward and pretty easy, especially compared to other professors.

Daily quizzes but they truly help you learn. It's obvious he truly cares about his students' learning and he does his best to assist each student to help them succeed. He will make sure that everyone gets the concept before moving on. One of the only classes that I truly learned a lot and felt confident about. Definitely a top-tier professor.

Teaches well, short quizzes every lecture but they are due 11:59pm day of. Homework is a little lengthy, assigned once a week. He does care about his students, goes based off the textbook and never waste time.

Super funny
Does a lot of examples making it easy to learn.

3220 is a HARD class. Most topics will be confusing at some point. I took this class in Fall 2023. There were daily quizzes assigned every day of class, as well as homework every week/biweekly sometimes. As for exams, well the only reason I got a B is because how forgiving he grades exams. He speaks quietly and with an accent. Good lecture layouts.

Sung Chan is difficult to understand but his handwriting isn't illegible. He really wants to see his students succeed!! I went to his office hours every week and we formed a really good bond. I took this class a year ago and everytime I see him still, he still says hi and we chat. He wrote a good reference letter for me.

Being allowed to have a note sheet on the exams was the only thing that helped me pass. Calc 2 is hard to begin with, but taking it with Sung Chan is harder. He flies- like speeds- through the material and gives a quiz every class so attendance is mandatory.

Sung Chan is a very good professor and does genuinely do his best for his students. 5080 is notoriously difficult, a fact which isn't helped by the textbook. Sung Chan distilled this textbook into something more readable and essentially rewrote the textbook, correcting its flaws. Prepare for daily quizzes, homeworks require some time and thought.

Took eng calc 2 with him, hardest class I've taken with an insane amount of material to cover but he was a great teacher and really got me to work and learn a lot. If I would've taken this class under anyone else I likely would've failed

Daily quizzes were given in this class, but a review was done at the beginning that had the exact same format as the quiz, just with different numbers. Overall I had a decent learning experience with this professor, he may seem harsh at first but he can be accommodating and funny as you get more into the year.

This professor is a joke. He takes half the class reviewing for the daily quiz, and only 10-20 minutes teaching new material. Then he complains we are slow and behind. The exams are very difficult, and most of your grades are based on them. Also, DAILY QUIZZES are also difficult. The homework has no correlation to the lecture. Would not recommend

Sungchan is a wonderful professor and probably my favorite math professor I have had at the U. There is a quiz each class but he does a review that is nearly identical to the quiz each day at the start of class. He genuinely cares about his students and is always an open door for questions. Be respectful and responsible and you will do fine!

Well organized class. Lectures were easy to follow, he had very clear explanations on the subject. He has quizzes everyday but 8 drops so it's okay to miss a class then and there. As long as you do good on the quizzes and use them to study, you can pass his tests. In this class I was able to genuinely learn the material and do good on exams.

Professor Choi was a great teacher who had a very straightforward setup for the class. With quizzes every single class period, it's really important not to miss class as much as you can, but I can tell you right now those quizzes help so much. I did little studying for this course and relied mainly on the quizzes to learn, I highly recommend him.

The structure of this class is one of the best I've ever had. He had clear lecture notes that he followed along with daily quizzes and weekly homework. The daily quizzes were short and typically not too difficult and they truly reinforced what we were currently learning. The homework was not too much and help was available if needed.

Calc 2 is difficult for most students to begin with. Professor Choi is often difficult to understand, has nearly illegible handwriting, and quizzes every lecture was excessive. I had to teach myself this class in its entirety just to pass. The only thing that got me through was him allowing a notes sheet on midterms. Don't recommend for calc 2.
He takes ages to grade...like AGES. Also yells...everybody has bad days but to yell at students asking questions...yikes. Quizzes were helpful.

(There were no options to choose MATH 1220 on the source code so I had to select 1210). 
I took Calc 2 from him. He's a great, caring, and generous professor, and exams were primarily based on quizzes. I would definitely take other math courses with him next time. Just beware of attendance and daily quizzes.

Daily graded quizzes, but they are the exact problems you'll get on tests. His tests are also very easy. Amount of problems on weekly homework could be dialed down a bit, but otherwise a great teacher.
He is pretty relaxed and he tries to help the students hear him better with a mic.

An absolutely amazing professor. You might think that daily quizzes are rough, but they are not difficult and do wonders to reinforce the material. He walks you through a review sheet that is almost exactly the same at the beginning of class. He never takes it for granted you know something and reiterates a lot. Best math teacher I've ever had.

Incredibly caring and competent prof. He's so helpful in many ways:responds to emails quickly, available outside of class, takes extra time from his office hours to help if struggling. People think he is very strict, but he is very lenient. Despite having a language barrier, he works very hard and makes his material relevant and easy to understand.

Prof. Choi is a fantastic teacher. He really cares about his students and takes time our of his office hours and personal life to help his students with any help they need. He responds to emails even when it is very late. I think it is admirable that he is such a great teacher despite having a hard time speaking english.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher and really brilliant man! Knows a lot about economics! Very informative and I would highly recommend this course. Prof. Bilginsoy is not overly enthusiastic, but he is super smart and clear, he will help if you ask.

Professor Bilginsoy is extremely knowledgeable and, at least for ECON 3380, reasonable in terms of workload and overall difficulty(pretty easy A). I don't think you're likely to be inspired or otherwise blown away by his instruction (good but B+ overall), so if you're looking to get the most out of your education, look elsewhere.

Of the 13 different econ professors I have had at the U, he is hands down the hardest and most demanding.  If you're looking to coast go somewhere else, if you want to learn econ there is no one who can compare.  I highly, highly, recommend him and he ruined my 4.0.

He is full of information on the subject at hand. He is willing to talk about anything you do not quite get. Get ready to read and write essays though. The only assignments are essays and they can be quite tough.

This class is so full of information it is overwhelming. The professor is an economic genius however not the best teacher. It was hard to follow almost every day. Entire grade based on 2 midterms and 1 final all essay format requiring 4 essays within each midterm/final. I learned a lot but the stress level was out of the roof. Hardest class.

This is the worst class and worst teacher I've ever had. Grade based on 3 essay exams. There's no study guide and it's hard to understand his lectures. LOTS of reading. If you have a solid econ and finance knowledge you may do well, if you don't, you won't. Spent so much time studying for his exams, I wasn't able to focus much on my other classes.

I really enjoyed this class. Cihan expects you to understand the material but he provides a good base of understanding through his lectures. This isn't an easy class, but it's definitely worth the effort. Attend class, take good notes, do the prep-questions and you'll do fine.
This class is awful. I can't tell if it's his lecturing style or the subject material. He gives a lot of readings and no study guide. Take a different 3200 class. I wouldn't recommend the class.

He is a very smart guy and knows everything there is to know about the subject. The grade is based on three tests which are in essay format (the absolute worst) and extremely difficult. I worked very hard and didn't do very well on the tests but he still gave me a C.

I found his class to be quite easy and very low stress. he does grade based on 2 midterms and the final, but he gives a study guide. As long as you can answer the questions FULLY on the study guide, you should be fine. I got an A in the class and put a total of 15hrs studying. Don't do the required readings. Only study when he posts the guide.

This class was so hard. His grades came from 3 papers where he gave an outline but graded hard. Everyone in the class was confused on what he was looking for. Got his lectures off Wikipedia. Worked my butt off and got a C. Doesn't really help if you need it.

Cihan is excited about the subject, but don't expect him to work with you. Grades are based on three assignments. I did fine in the class, but he is a pretty dry lecturer. He always seemed eager to have class over. Not my favorite Econ elective credit.

Great class i really enjoyed it.  It is harder than most classes but worth it.  He requires that you get a pretty good understanding of what you will be tested on.  Yes you don't always know what to study but he gives a study guide which was enough to get me an A in the class.  I would recommend it for those who are ok working hard to learn a lot

Very fun professor. He is excited about his lectures and makes them enjoyable to listen to. He welcomes questions and will tell you when he doesn't know the answer which is nice. He is not too friendly to the Austrian school which isn't surprising because few professors are but like other professors hasn't spent much time learning what the Austrians really believe. Some things he said about them wasn't accurate. Overall very good class and professor.

I took his first class. Thought he did a great job, all things considered. He tests fairly and provides more than enough study material. Lectures are tough to make it through because this course is very dense. You will have to work hard to do well.

Bob is awesome! I had him for his first class and he was great! Lots of material, he tends to rush through it in class but will go in depth if you ask, i dont blame him since it is a lot of material to cover in one class. Go to class, take the quizzes, and read the textbook. I would definitely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Bob is such a great professor! I learned so much from him and the class is very interesting. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. Bob was a great teacher that truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. He provides good study material such as handouts and is a fair grader. If you read the material,show up to class, and study you will get a good grade.

Bob has a ton of energy in class which made it engaging. His tests were tough and required you to read the textbook along with coming to lecture. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

he's really helpful and i really liked the course pacing. he goes pretty fast, so that's nice because i hate it when profs go slow. he writes out really good examples on the board, and if you write those down you know what is on the exams. grading is really fair. enjoyed his class a lot.

I had Dan at mit. he's a great teacher. our whole entire recitation "fell in love" with him. I just realized that he's here now. all the best dan!!!! ooohhh...and I have to say this: "do come back to mit!!!"

I would retake a class from him.
Sometimes he'll lose you, as do all math Professors. But he's a really nice guy, and seems to care. His tests aren't too bad either. I'd take a class from him again.

Prof. Clavijo is as knowledgeable as he is funny. His lectures are clear and organized and he answers questions very well. Tests are difficult but not impossible. He takes feedback very well and it's clear he takes this part of his job very seriously.

Fluid Mechaniccs. He would typically cancel one (sometimes 2) of our 3 lectures a week because we were somehow "so ahead". His exams were very unpredictable with several curveballs (as he called them). Offered to write a letter of rec for any student who gave him a 5-star rating.

Dr. Clavijo made sure that everything made sense for studies and even had a day reserved for helping us on the homeworks. If you aren't a great test taker this might not be your cup of tea but if you understand the hw and the process of the problems then you'll be fine. He is the funniest professor at the U. Maybe even in the world. His lectures always are incredibly engaging. Tests can be a bit brutal but hey it's engineering.

Fluid Mechanics.

His classes might seem boring as a few students might say. I disagree. He tries his best to teach his students the concepts and it's great. Very sarcastic, makes the class interesting. Very organized  professor.

reviews.comment: Really funny and engaging guy. I never went to class and still got an A, but just because I don't care much about birds. If you study before the exams you'll be fine, super interesting and easy-to-grasp content.

How can u make the whole grade quizzes and exams and nothing else? Very dense PowerPoints with a lot to memorize. His exams are open ended making it much more difficult. do decent on exams u can't pass the class because you have to get a perfect scores to pass the class since its only exams and quizzes. Quizzes only open for a day and one attempt.

reviews.comment: Dr. Clayton is really one of the most engaged teachers I've ever received. He is invested in everything he teaches and definitely knows what he's doing. I love his class

VERY EASY 5000 level class. You don't have to go to lecture if you're willing to go over uploaded slides on your own before tests, but the lectures I did go to were always interesting and easy to follow. final is 30% of your total grade, but his exams are very fair. This strategy is hit-or-miss in general, but Dale executes it well. He makes a concerted effort of including every key point on the slides, and doesn't ask trick questions. Lectures were funny and engaging.

It wasn't an option, but I have him for 5350, Ornithology. He is FANTASTIC. Easily my favorite class that I've taken during undergrad. I had really low expectations for the class, as I was not much of a "bird lover," but his enthusiasm and interest is contagious. He cares about students, and reminds us that we're worth more than a letter grade.

reviews.comment: Tough class and some lectures were really about his research rather than useful material. Full of himself.

reviews.comment: I liked his half of the class better, found his teaching and slides a lot more simple, and he reuses questions for the final which was a bonus

He paces himself with his slides, so you don't HAVE to go to class, but it does help because he adds things. He knows his stuff. The class itself is a little hard because 95 is an A and the final is comprehensive, so you have to try. Textbook not used.

I think Dr. Clayton teaches just fine. I felt as though he was unapproachable though, in a sense the opposite of caring. The few times I reached out he seemed disrespectful in the emails. The class was test heavy and I think switching professors part way through makes this subject even less appealing. He knows what he is teaching.

Grading scale to get an A is higher than what is usually seen in classes. On exams they want you to use a very specific vocabulary. Make sure to go to class and do the reading for the best grade possible. Doesn't round up on grades even if it is 0.1%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dale is one of the most gifted lecturers I have had in my academic career. He presented the information in his class in an engaging, informative, and humorous way, all at the same time. It made it very easy to attend his lectures and get those clicker points. His class is test heavy and has a high lower bound for an A (95%), but he makes it easier.

Very first day of class he said its VERY difficult to get an A in my course, but it is possible. Simply put all you do is read, take exams and do clicker questions. He does a lot of name dropping to show how many people hes written papers with, just seems like he wants his students to think he is cool and smart. Not my fav
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great professor! Very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. The exams are tough due to specificity, but he is available outside of class to help you succeed and also goes over many questions in class in detail. Definitely one of my favorite biology professors. Ended up enjoying this class a lot more than expected and learned a lot
I enjoyed Dale's class. He was passionate about the material and I ended up learning a lot. All the exam questions were throughly discussed in lecture.
Tests weren't easy, but at the beginning of the semester, you're told to do the reading to get an A. You have to be there to get the clicker points.

Dale's field course was the BEST!! Desert ecology was my first field course and it was amazing. I had no previous birding experience but that didn't matter. Dale gave great help in identifying birds and teaching what to look for. At the end of the week we had to do a presentation and paper but it wasn't bad at all. LOVED IT AND LOVED HIM! FANTASTIC

He was a very knowledgable professor. Has done some great work in the field of evolutionary biology. Exams were difficult and I felt like the grading was much too strict, if you don't write exactly what is on the key then your answer is wrong even if you think that you can back it up with what was taught. Lectures were  mostly very interesting.

Prof. Dale is super hard to follow and he often contradicts himself.  Don't get me wrong- he's a really nice and likable guy.  Just a really hard professor.  Averages on exams were in the 50's and 60's.  Clearly, nobody really understood him. Thankfully, he reused his earlier questions on his portion of the final.

Great class! Very interesting material. Prof Clayton is a hard grader, he requires complete understanding of the material and you must answer things succinctly or he will dock you. You MUST do the reading and come to class every day and you will, at least, pass. I enjoyed this class thoroughly.
This class wasn't very interesting. He has theories about things and tries to state them as facts. I don't recommend this class. Too bad it's required.
Class was very well designed and I learned a lot about a variety of issues while working on a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sometimes it was hard to actually understand the whole concept while in lecture, but with practice problems it became easy to understand.

Had Prof De Grandi for PHYS2220 last semester, and she was one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are really fun and easy to follow, the grading system is clear, and she really cares about teaching.
Records and posts all her lectures and notes, provides lots of resources, and a relatively nice grader. Kind and understanding as well.

shes cool, teaching style is different. Moves pretty fast but makes the course very passable. Lots of resources and honestly I cant complain. She does record all her lectures which is helpful, to be honest she is very dedicated to student success.

You can tell Claudia genuinely wants all of her students to succeed and has a passion for what she does. She is clear about what is expected in the class and is very accessible outside of class despite having 400+ students to worry about. If you have to take Physics do it with her!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is amazing! Provides numerous opportunities to succeed in her class. Cares about her students and is always in the study hall trying to learn names and help students. 10/10 would recommend her.
Very caring and passionate about the subject. Provides countless opportunities for her students to succeed. Class is well structured.

She is a very good teacher and cares about her students. She goes beyond expectations to demonstrate the content in a way that is clear. My only complaint about the class is the amount of homework. While the majority can be done in a few minutes, there are 6 homework assignments each week, a few of which are only open for 1-2 days.
has lecture recondings!

Oh my gosh the best professor I've encountered at the u! She is so sweet, offers so many options to succeed in her class, personalizes every homework and lecture, and actually attends study halls and makes an effort to learn her students. She is a great teacher as well, definitely worth taking a class from her.Used to hate physics and now I love it

Lovely person, draws great pictures, gives so many opportunities to improve your grade (extra credit, exam resubmissions, grading policies) that it's basically impossible to do badly in this class if you're trying at all - probably is good at actually teaching the material but I couldn't tell you for sure, if she is that's a nice bonus.
Very inclusive lectures with great examples to get you involved and leave not confused.

Might just be the perfect Prof. Exams are a breeze and you will most likely finish early. Preps you with lots of practice from homework. Lectures are entertaining and easy to follow (also optional if you can learn from homework). Super nice, funny, and helpful. Plenty of resources if you have trouble. Take this class for a good experience.
Fantastic professor, one of the best I have ever had.

Claudia was very caring and clear in her instruction and expectations. She attended nearly every study hall and was very easy to reach outside of class. She had lots of fun demos in lecture. Homework could be difficult but attend study hall and you'll be just fine. The test prep materials were very useful and tests were fair. Fantastic professor!

Learned a lot & was really impressed with how well she presented difficult topics. She also takes the time to learn everyone's name despite the big class. Homework is spread out and due nearly every day of the week. For exams she lets you do a resubmission (for less points, but it still helps). GO TO STUDY HALL!

I never attended lecture, but I'd attend help hours for homework (highly recommend). Both the Professor and TA's were amazing, it truly felt like they cared. Homework can be challenging at times, but help you prepare for the exam/quizzes. I wish all my professors acted like Claudia!

I never ended up reading the textbook, I found the example problems most helpful,
the test prep materials were great for tests, she honestly made my day as a professor, and was the most caring professor I have ever had. 100% recommend.

Really great professor! Makes learning fun. REALLY wants to see her students succeed. Office hours are what SAVED me through this class; I really recommend to go. Don't feel embarrassed to go - literally EVERYONE does; it's hard to get a seat sometimes. This class is very fun and easy if you actually try

Really great professor! Physics is hard but she makes it fun. Lots of demonstrations and she is not afraid to go over things multiple times to make sure everyone gets it. Lectures are recorded. All exams are open note and open for a few days so you can take it at your own time. Weekly homework assignments with 2 parts -- office hours are v helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Protect her at all costs!

Professor De Grandi is one of my favorites I've had. She's so caring in and out of class, and I've found her lectures extremely straightforward and easy to understand, as well as her class notes so helpful. I've not taken physics before, so I'm glad that she was my introduction. Her canvas is well organized.

Amazing professor that showed how much she cared to put the needs of her students first by always having a plethora of resources for students. The way the class is conducted is very collaborative with high encouragement to work through problems with others. One of the best professors and most enjoyable courses I have ever taken.

Dr. De Grandi is an incredibly caring professor. Her lectures are fun and engaging and she does her best to make sure that she is as clear as possible. She is also the most feedback-accepting professor I've ever had. She actively listens and will adjust everything to aid in the learning of her students. Use her many resources and you will do fine

Get ready for this class to be your top priority, there's lots to do every day to stay on top of everything. Claudia is great and cares and does her best to make this difficult course accessible to all, she's always willing to listen. She memorized everybody's name that regularly came to lecture (the lecture hall was about 120 students max).

Excellent class. Best structured class I've ever taken period. Take-home exams. Homework imo harder than the exams. Never needed to interact with her one-on-one but she seemed rather nice and helpful. Very interesting material as well. Honestly wish she taught more/at a faster rate.

Claudia de Grandi is a great professor and full of personality. Lectures can be boring, but she usually switches them up with demonstrations and other activities. The workload may seem like a lot, but practice is important in physics. She knows it's hard to cheat on physics so the midterms are take home, allowing for less stress.

I took her for both Physics 1 and 2. She's great. Clear expectations and lots of mercy with extensions and omitted assignments. The two midterms are 10% of your grade each and the final is 12%. If you do better on the final than the midterms (which is totally possible) it's 32% of your grade. Gives lots of extra credit too. Do work, and get an A.

Claudia is a great lecturer and it's very apparent that she cares about her students. Her course is very well organized and pretty heavily structured - if you like to study entirely on your own terms it may not be for you - but I found that her consistent, approachable assignments made it so I never had to do any additional studying to understand.

Claudia was phenomenal! 

This was the best structured class I've taken! Exams were very doable and resembled the homework and reviews very closely.

Pre-class quizzes were short and insightful. The homework was fairly easy. All the formulas are provided, even during exams.

Claudia makes physics very approachable. I learned a lot in this class.

Dr. De Grandi has deeply planned every second of this class. If you are someone who likes self-studying and exploring your own learning pathways, you may end up feeling frustrated at times because De Grandi's lectures and 6-7 (small to medium sized) weekly assignments will likely take up all the time you have to study this courses content.She cares
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Claudia's the goat
Very well-structured class and allows several ways to get help.

Claudia has got this class down to a science. She has broken the learning process into bite size pieces. She also has Lecture Hall hours where a bunch of TA's and LA's hang out ready to help you with the homework. The exams are take-home and she gives you over 3 hours, which is far more than you'll need.

Deeply cares about her students' success. Was very accommodating to issues I had during the semester. All lectures are recorded and posted on Canvas. The amount of work needed is kind of a lot, but Claudia offers many drops for quizzes, homework, pre-classes, and discussions, so falling behind wasn't the end for my grade. Good support system.

Claudia is amazing. Her course material and grading criteria is clear. I'll admit that some lectures are boring (attendance isn't required), but it's usually just to lay the foundation of physics or help students. Average homework load and difficulty for the amount of credits. Fair (not too easy) Exams. Her and her teaching team made it doable.

Course is organized and accessible for many learning styles. Claudia is very caring and an amazing teacher and person.  I feel confident and capable of understanding and thinking of physics of things outside of the coursework and feel like I am able to really engage in the material. This is what real learning looks like! Take her class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. The class itself is pretty challenging, with a decent amount of homework, and you have to put in the effort to understand stuff, but Dr. De Grandi really makes it as easy as possible for such a complex concept. 100% recommended, tempted to take Phys 2 just because I enjoyed them as a professor so much.

Professor de Grandi taught Physics perfectly. Her content was very organized and all assignments/tests accurately reflected the material taught. She cares a lot about the success of her students and is always willing to help. Though there are a lot of assignments, all of them were carefully chosen so that the student can best learn the material.

She clearly loves to teach and in saying that sometimes she tries too hard which sometimes leads you not to learn a topic well. In saying that it also comes through in the HW as it is long and sometimes hard. TBH a bit excessive which means make time of suffer with your grade. Her grading is very nice though lots of partial credit.

I think the best word to describe Claudia is fair. I always felt like the grading was fair, the work load was fair, and the tests were fair. She is always asking the students for ways she can improve the class and it shows. The lectures are super boring but they are optional. Discussion section is what helped me the most in the class.

Physics is a challenging subject, and Claudia provides so many opportunities for students to learn according to their needs (study hall, discussions, homework, etc.) I am not a visual learner, but I found this class highly doable. Tests are open note and, in my experience, are graded fairly leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor De Grandi's class is very difficult and if you find yourself behind in the beginning, the rest of the semester is miserable. She responds to email quickly but does not make the best accommodations if something urgent comes up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Claudia pours her heart and soul into her teaching, but that is directly represented by how many assignments you are given. THERE'S A LOT OF THEM! None are particularly hard... but it's a lot! That said you can tell she cares and does a great job covering the material.

Claudia is a great person, very kind and willing to answer questions. As an instructor she moves very rapidly through content, you don't get much of a chance to understand the material as you take notes. Everything in the class had tons of different components (i.e. homeworks were two parts and exams were three parts). Discussion sections helpful!

If you expect to breeze through this class, you won't. Every time I finally understood what was going on, the subject would change to something new. That being said, Prof DeGrandi is probably one of the best professors I have ever had. You can tell that above all she wants her students to succeed.

Prof De Grandi is an excellent teacher. She surrounds herself with a sizable team of TAs and LAs to always have the capacity to help students as much as needed. During my semester she often would change the class structure in response to feedback from students. Her class is tough, but if you go to study halls when you are struggling, you'll be fine

Claudia really does care about her students. With everything online right now it's really hard to connect and she tries her best. Her study halls are a massive help and I don't think I would've passed this class without them. Her tests are three days long which is annoying but overall I love the way she teaches and I'll be taking 2220 with her.

Professor De Grandi is very good at teaching Physics, I love how she explains things. But she takes the class at a very high speed. I constantly felt like I was a lecture behind, even with re-watching the lectures, and reading the textbook.

Her caring attitude doesn't make up for every time she sets up an example needed for homework, then stops in the middle with an excuse about time, then tells us to just view her notes after class. This is in addition to the pre-class videos, discussions, 2-part homeworks, and extra modules she assigns. Tests last 3 days, with 3 parts. Enough said.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Claudia is super nice but tries too hard to make things work that it takes away from the learning experience. With the class being online, she has a hard time transitioning to technological situation. She uses a lot of time teaching us with one example and having heavy homework that goes much deeper than what is taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory but the material is worthless so enjoy wasting 4-5 hours a week learning nothing. Her practice material for tests does not actually prepare you for the test. Her online format for classes is insufferable as well. All I have is regret in taking her class. Do not under any circumstances take her class during COVID.

Claudia obviously wants to be a great teacher, and cares about the feelings of her students. It seems that for new physics students she might be good. But she also schedules excessive amounts of homework. Up to 12 a week. Most of these are busywork and many are thinly-veiled mandatory attendance requirements. Online instruction at its most chaotic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I took the physics lab taught by Claudia. Claudia herself is really nice and accessible and you can tell she tries to do a good job putting together the lab, but the labs just suck either way. They're tedious and I had to spend a lot of time outside of class working on them, instructions were vague. I'm glad I took it with her, but the class sucks

Before Claudia, I was not good at physics at all. A lot of the time I was very confused mostly because of the professor. Thanks to Claudia, I actually understand physics now. She is such an amazing professor. She cares so much, has a lot of study halls that are extremely helpful. She even messaged me to say good job after my midterm 2 score came.
Awesome professor! Claudia, cares about her students success. The study halls that she setup were very beneficial to my success in the class. Also, she is very open to student feedback.

I've never been good at physics. This class was definitely challenging for me, but I felt like Professor De Grandi taught this course more understanding to those who were not engineering or STEM majors!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Claudia is an amazing teacher with fantastic demos and a great lecture style. Don't be afraid to ask any question any time as she will answer it or look into answering it in a way you can understand. It's a wonderful class, but make sure you stay with the homework and use the discussion sections. She also brings pizza sticks to study hall so go!

She's the first professor I've known who is willing to drop the first 2 midterm scores in favor of the score on the finals as long as it proves we learned the material. The first thing in class we did was submit a self-introduction, typical snowflake move. But, the first time I went to study hall, she could name everyone there! That's dedication.

Claudia is SUCH an amazing professor. She is so sweet, super funny, and is the only professor whose lectures I have never skipped. She really cares about you and she grades really easily. Tests are 85% individual work, 15% 3-person group (or 100% if you did better than the group). 3 quizzes dropped, 4 assignments dropped, final can replace midterms
She'll bring cookies during study hall hours, and is always available to talk out of class
Great professor and gives students many opportunities for success. Discussion sections twice a week where attendance and participation are graded! Do not skip them!
Good class, good professor, I recommend going to office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her class; however, I found her lectures to be pretty unhelpful. While often interesting, I struggled to understand how to take the demos/deviations and apply them. Exams are graded very lightly and there's lots of opportunities to improve grades. She clearly wants her students to pass and do well beyond her class.
Gives you many resources to learn and incentivizes you to use them very well =) wonderful job
Professor Claudia, was alright her lectures were a little confusing and hard to digest. I wish she used more examples, and better explanations. Just read the textbook and you'll be fine.

Professor DeGrandi provided a helpful approach to teaching. She would work through ample examples that were directly applicable to hw. She recorded every lecture in case you missed class. The hw and discussions perfectly prepare you for the exams, which consisted of similar problems. Exams had limited numerical answers, relying on variable usage.

Dr. DeGrandi is a wonderful professor who cares about student learning and students themselves. Her class is set up to make learning very accessible. She very willing to work with students to help them learn even in a large class. She gives lots of space for students to ask and answer questions in lecture allowing them to check their understanding

A really smart professor who makes learning really accessible. Lots of extra credit is offered, though exams are tough. She remembers students names even in a giant lecture hall, which is commendable.

Claudia is the best! She wants everyone to get an A; she gives so much extra credit, which inflates your grade. Do the extra credit and go to study hall it's an easy A. She is also a great person. I can't say her lectures grabbed my attention every time, but they are easy to follow, and missing lectures here and there won't hurt she also records.

Loved her classes. Took her for PHYS 2210 and 2220, both were some of my easiest classes (As long as I did the HW assignments, attended discussion sections, and watched lectures) Study hall is available 3 times a week if anyone needs extra help, and lectures are recorded and uploaded within a couple of hours.
She is one of the most caring professors out there and clearly cares about the success of her students!

At first her class seemed really labor intensive with lots of work, but it really wasn't very bad. She actually is very well organized and clear in expectations, so if you do poorly that's on you. There are lots of assignments and grades in the class, so it's easy to make up for missed work and she will allow a few missed assignments w/o hurt grade
Daniel's class is sometimes run more like a conditioning class than a technique class.

Daniel is an awesome professor who is a great teacher, mentor, and person. He is always willing to help you/offer advice, and he is well versed in many different technical aspects. He truly cares about his students and his classes are always a blast to be in!
Daniel is intentional and genuine in his feedback. He sees people for who they are and gives guidance based off of what he feels you might want to focus on. I love Daniel! Best teacher ever

Daniel Clifton is perhaps the best contemporary/modern dance professor in north america. You will not find another prof who cares for students with half the sincerity that Clifton has. Yes, his freshman tech class is physically demanding, but such is dance, and such is life. Daniel is truly one of the best there is!
A little bit of a bore, but cant be intresting at moments. She is passionate. Exams are challenging but you can get an A on them. The rest of the class is free points besides exams.
She was a decent professors. The slides were often times hard to follow along. Her tests were not really too difficult, although the class average on them all was around 80%.

Her lectures are boring and repetitive. She's not very knowledgeable; you have to mostly study by yourself. She isn't super kind or particularly caring. But the class is easy with her. So I recommend!

Over the course of the semester I didn't take a single note. However, I kept track of something much more important. Over a total of 1,110 lecture minutes she said the words "Competitive Advantage" roughly 448 times resulting in a rate of 0.40 CA/min.

Colleen has never had a real job in the business world, and it shows. She strictly sticks to lecturing about the homework and offers no insight beyond the readings we do. Her test questions can be confusing. Everything she teaches is so elementary that it should be a 1000-level class for freshman students, not junior/senior business students.

Colleen is very passionate about what she teaches, and it shows. The class overall is more difficult than some, but if you do the required readings and complete assignments, you'll get some useful knowledge about management. Tests are pretty difficult, so stay on top of studying. Overall, great professor, but be ready to engage.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Highly recommend Colleen for STRAT 3700. The course is made up of quizzes, 3 exams, and 400 word case analysis papers. She is a great lecturer and does a great job explaining course concepts. I found the class and cases interesting and easy to complete. Go to class and try on the case studies and you will receive a good grade and learn something.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Colby was a great professor. His lectures were easy to understand, and he made sure we understood the content before moving on to another subject. Colby made his lectures entertaining instead of just lecturing. Attendance was not mandatory for my class, but of course, if you want to do well, I would suggest attending lectures and discussions.

Colby is a fun guy and definitely loves what he teaches. He was good at keeping us awake during our 8:35 AM class. The only problem I had was that he over-explained things a lot. But overall, he's great!

Professor Tanner was great at giving engaging lectures, while repeating the concepts ad nauseum in different ways to really help it sink in. He was also very funny, and I loved seeing all of the political commentary shirts he made throughout the semester. My only complaint would be that the readings and the lectures didn't always line up 1:1.

Professor Tanner is awesome. I took him Spring 2026 for BIOL 1610 and even though I slept in class way too often, I still learned everything because he teaches so clearly. He's super chill, fair, and willing to help if you show effort. Homework is real but doable, exams match quizzes, and the final is literally the exams reused and he's hilarious.

Colby is an amazing human. I had multiple instances where I got way behind on coursework, and it was looking like I was gonna fail the class. After like 2 emails and a 5 minute meeting, Colby said I could email him all my missing work for full credit. His lectures are also super engaging, and exams aren't too hard. Easy A if you put in the effort.

I had him my first semester at the U, and he is such an amazing professor. He is actually the best teacher I have had. Take good notes, and pay attention. He is actually the best professor I have ever had. He makes the lectures so entertaining, AND teaches the same concept in different ways for people to understand. STUDY THE QUIZZES!
Lectures can drag and there is a heavy busywork vibe to your assignments. Colby makes up for it by being a super chill professor who is helpful and the material is never insanely hard.

This course has way too many assignments. Colby is very nice and he clearly cares about students, but sometimes his lectures feel a little innacurate. I think he does a good job getting students engaged and interested in biology, but a poor job at actually teaching biology. Overall not my favorite course. Way too mcuh busy work. Takes a lot of time

I took BIOL1610 my first  ever semester. Colby's upbeat lectures and relatively easy content helped me get used to college. He definitely knows what he's teaching and seems to enjoy it (as long as he's had enough coffee). He's also a cool guy in general. I personally never got the courage to go up and talk to him but he liked Dr. Who, so I'm bias.

There is lots of homework, but it becomes manageable over the semester. Tests can be tough. You get 2 weeks' worth of drops, so messing up a few assignments isn't a big deal. The Draw to Learn's are very helpful, but unclear instructions make it hard to earn full credit. Discussions are pointless aside from counting towards attendance.

Colby is THE BEST! His tests are fair and not very hard. Study and review what he says to and you'll be good. Lot's of weekly assignments, do assignments and go to the lectures. Very fair class, just show up and work. He cares about students.

COLBY IS THE BEST! I can say for sure he is one/if not, the ONLY professor that truly cares about the success of his students. He is VERY accommodating and will work with you through any circumstance and provide support if a student is struggling. He loves honesty from students even if you hate the class! Such a chill guys and deserves a raise.

The professor is great and chill. Homework isn't too bad, about an hour each, due weekly but it really helps for exams. He clearly tells you what to focus on, so if you pay attention and do the work, this class can be an easy A.

He's very patient and willing to work with students regardless of situation; discussion meetings are mandatory and the lectures are not, but I would recommend going to the lectures anyway because he's funny and makes the material interesting. His class was the first that I didn't think the lectures were a waste of time.

He has to be one of the best professors in the entire university. He has this many 5 stars for a reason and they are well deserved. Seriously, do yourself a favor and take this class with Colby. If its full, pay someone to drop it so you can take their spot. And if you have to, pay them a good amount, it'll be the best decision you make.

If he was a woman, he would be disliked more than he is. I went to all office hours, did all of my assignments, did tutoring, and still got a 70% on the final. I had difficulty in the class with the quizzes and exams all semester. He explains like he expects you to know what he is talking about. The TA's are better. PREPARE FOR A LOT OF ASSIGNMENTS
Colby was great, Class is really not hard if you go to class and pay attention and do your homework. chiller

Colby is literally as great and easy of a professor as it gets. He really is as chill as they come, especially for the bio department cuz the other bio professors are lowkey garbage unless it's Naina Phadnis. Colby and Naina are the best in the business. The class is hard work but very much doable. I recommend Colby everytime.
interesting guy
Colby is a fantastic professor who does a great job conveying the information.

Amazing professor and TA's. This class im sure is easy if you've take AP bio i didnt and still did fine. Theres a lot of busy work but its all worth it to better understand material. Very easy guy to talk to and enjoys teaching. When you're in a discussion class and think you arent learning move to another PLEASE helped me a bunch.

Colby's class was the best part of my first semester. His class makes a lot of sense. There is quite a bit of homework, but they're short and mostly graded off of completion, so no stress if you get problems wrong. His exams are completely lecture based, and he doesn't try to trick you; in fact, he gives you the answers to the exams in class.
Super easy class if you pay attention and do the assignments!

hes a chiller. just do your assignments and youll be fine. the course builds on itself so dont get behind. dont use AI to do ur assignments for you. if you just actually do the assignments you lowk dont need to study. he gives you quizzes before the test that are similar to the test.

Colby is a great teacher especially as a freshman with this being my first big lecture hall class. He keeps lectures engaging and interesting and is very funny. The difficulty of tests is fair as long as you pay attention to lectures, and I barely needed to study to get an A. The assignments he has us do online are also really helpful.

I love Colby Tanner. His class was really interesting and he is a good speaker. He cares about his students and responds to emails extremely fast. As long as you come to class, participate in iClickers, do all the assignments, and study well enough for exams, you will get a guaranteed A.

Colby has been one of my favorite professors. I found his lectures generally pretty easy to follow, and he is always open to questions. He is very clear about what will be on a quiz or exam and he makes it really easy to earn points with assignments. As long as you show up and pay attention in lectures you should be fine.

Colby was a very fun and entertaining professor. He made long lectures engaging and made sure that you understood what he was teaching. He shows true passion for what he teaches and for his students to grow in their education.

This professor was extremely difficult to reach, even when I had other faculty reach out after I got a response, he was not reliable throughout the semester and did not respond well to asking for help. I would not take a class with this professor again.
Colby was seriously such a refresher coming into college. Great lectures, and the extra homework is honestly just helpful, so use it as a tool!

Seriously the best bio teacher out there. Yes, it's a lot of homework but that repetition just leads to understanding. Attendance is not mandatory but you should definitely go to every lecture, he makes biology so easy to learn and literally gives you answers to exam questions in lecture. Loved this class so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: funny and come to class or u wont understand the material

Colby is SUCH a good teacher. The way he lectures and tells the stories of basic biology is so accessible and makes things easy to understand and remember. Homework was never hard because I remembered things! He's really fun, super accessible and easy to get a hold of if you need something. Super super glad I took his class.
I really enjoyed the class I took with Colby Tanner. It was my first class in university and he made the process super easy and engaging. would highly recommend anyone to take his class.
Teaches it clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Even at 8 a.m., he was enthusiastic and engaging with his students and the material. If you commit to studying the material, attend mock exams, ask for help from teaching assistants, and actively participate in class, you should do well. While there is a substantial amount of material to cover and homework to complete, it is manageable.

I took this lab with Colby and he is really nice and chill. The lab is straightforward and you work on the projects each time with your group. Nothing was hard just sometimes time consuming. Overall he is the best to take for a lab credit. He understands that a 1 credit lab shouldn't be tough. I highly recommend his section.
Colby is so good at his job. Easy to understand if you pay attention in class. Make sure you show up to lectures and actively engage with his lessons. Easy A if you apply yourself.

Before I start, I want to mention that I was a senior with Biology major. I took this class to replace my AP credits. The things Colby teach in this class was a foundation for upper division classes. It is not too deep, but covers the wide area in biology. Even though this class has enormous amount of "homeworks", I think it's worth it. Easy exams.

Great professor. His lectures can sometimes be long winded. But the content is interesting. The assignments and quizzes line up very similarly to the tests. As long as you turn in your assignments and pay attention in class you will do well.

My absolute favorite professor I've had at the U so far. Insane aura, amazing lectures, and so so so compassionate and understanding. I would actually pay money to rate higher than 5 stars. If you're debating, this is your sign. Take from Colby!!!

Genuinely one of my favorite professors i've ever had. He made me excited to learn and want to go to class. 2nd time taking this class bc the 1st time the professor was the worst! 1000% take 1610 w/ Colby if u can! Aside from learning a lot, being around colby was always so refreshing as he was a good reminder to me to not take life too seriously.

If you take BIO1610, take it with Colby! I learned so much and the content was easy to digest in lectures and it was very clearly outlined what we needed to know. Also, he is the most whimsical person you will ever meet so lectures were always interesting.
colby is so amazing
Literally the best professor I've ever taken at the U. If you take Bio 1610 take Colby.

Amazing professor, great sense of humor and very intellectual as a person himself. Lectures are actually interesting. Do the homeworks and go to discussion they are valuable. Find friends to study with and you will do good. This class is very broad but gives you a great introduction to biology as a science. You can also do clickers in bed if u sick
Chiller. Talks fast though.

Colby is a great guy. His biggest strength is his ability to make you understand concepts you knew nothing about beforehand. To be fair, the class material is extremely easy. Sit in the front row! You will have a great time

Colby was a great professor all around, very chill and friendly! He made the concepts clear, but I give him a 4 because he went through some of the harder concepts a little fast for me. However, going to the discussions and office hours will help with understanding. He is very open to helping and often sits at the back of office hours/discussions.

Colby is awesome! He's so funny and approachable. I love how his lab actually felt like a 1-credit lab. The labs were easy and fun. It's a good supplement/review if you're taking the physiology lecture simultaneously. As someone who doesn't usually like group projects, I enjoyed the one at the end.
Colby is the best, legit one of the most engaging professors at the U and is super accessible if something comes up last minute. He is there for his students and it shows, everyone loves him.
He was super nice! One time i emailed him at 11 pm and he answered me by 12 literal LIFE SAVER. He was also super funny
Colby Tanner is a great professor. You can tell he cares for his students and he wants you to succeed. His class was super fun.
Awesome professor, I really enjoyed this class! Colby is super interesting, and you learn a lot from his lectures.

Colby is a cool guy but is an ineffective professor. Most first-year students like him because he treats them as 2-year-olds and dumbs concepts down to a 1+1=2 level. Anyone hoping to learn useful information will be disappointed, class is frequently a waste of time and unorganized. He seems more interested in being liked than promoting learning.

Colby was a great professor for BIOL 1610, he really made difficult concepts much easier to grasp. The PowerPoints in class are super helpful and be sure to take notes on those, and there were iClicker questions periodically in class for attendance points. He's such a nice and cool guy.

Lectures were well explained however sometimes were fast paced. Great professor and makes a very difficult class easier to succeed. There is a good amount of work every week, however most homework is completion points. Exams and quizzes were difficult but manageable. Take lots of notes and study weekly rather than just before exams.
Colby Tanner is my all time favorite professor. He cared about each student and his lectures were always helpful while being entertaining. If you really want to learn biology, take from him.

I chose Colby as my biology professor because his name sounded cool, and guess what? His name is cool, but so is he! Colby makes biology fun and engaging, breaking concepts down in a digestible way. While there's a lot of homework, he reminds us of deadlines and shares tips to help us succeed. He is just a chill guy.

Great teacher. I took the 8 am class in order to have him as my teacher and it was worth it. There are a lot of assignments with Magraw-Hill, but they aren't bad at all. He does take attendance as part of your grade and most learning happens in class, so go to class. If you do the assignments/reading and go to class you will do just fine.

Professor Tanner is by far one of my favorite professors. He is passionate about what he is teaching and gives SO many resources to be able to succeed. There are a lot of TA's to help in the class as well as review sessions and mock exams. There is a lot of homework but it is not time consuming and fairly straight forward.

Colby is a great teacher, he made the class very fun. Attendance is mandatory but you get 1 drop on your lecture grade and 2 on your discussion because he knows life happens.There are a lot of assignments but they're not too hard. Class can be bit boring but other times can be really engaging. Colby cares about the students and makes it fun.

Trust me, everyone. He's the professor you all need, Colby's fantastic. He will heavily emphasize the points you will be tested on and implore those to attend discussions, out-of-lecture resources, etc. He's more than willing to assist you when needed. I have nothing more to say, he's kind, funny, and the best professor I've had at the university.
This class would have been so much harder if I didn't have tanner. You will have about 5 assignments a week, but they are pretty easy. I recommend going to office hours one a week.

Biology can be tough to learn, but Colby makes it easier to understand through his lectures and help resources he provides which really helped me succeed in his class by getting an 80% average on quizzes and exams. He really does care about your learning. If you need this class, take it from him.

Great professor that understands what a 1 credit class should be and utilized information that was very applicable to class. I learned more essential information from this lab that was usable on the test than I did in class. Awesome teacher

Colby is an amazing professor! Biology is generally a hard class but he made it super easy to follow the lectures and understand. He also provides MANY opportunities to review and ask questions. This class is homework heavy but they are small assignments I found super helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The quizzes are similar to the tests. He is clear about what to study and there is plenty of help outside of class. For bio 1610, great course.
Colby is awesome! He's obviously very passionate about the subject he teaches and made everything very interesting and intuitive to learn.
Gives great lectures and understands the curriculum very well. He and his TA's are also very willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring and provides lots of resources.

Colby is an exceptional professor with a top-notch course design. You'll have to do consistent work throughout the semester, and the payoff is less cramming for tests. He teaches you how to be a better student. The variety of creative assignments translate to a deeper understanding of core concepts. One of the most gifted instructors out there.

Colby was the best teacher I have had through all of my education. He cares so much about his students and it really shows, he seems to do whatever it takes to make sure the class understands. He does a lot of drawing on the board and is not just about memorization, but actually understanding. I always looked forward to going to this class.

Colby is an awesome professor. It's clear he knows and has a passion for the material. He puts in effort to know his students, super understanding, and will help you get any grade you want. If you're taking BIOL, don't miss out on Colby. The comments mentioning lots of homework is true, but they're quick and easy so don't let that turn you away!
Colby is a fantastic teacher and mentor. Wish I could take more classes with him. If you show up every day and make an effort to study, you will be guaranteed a good grade.

Colby was a great professor! Despite attendance being mandatory, he made lectures interesting and fun. He didn't mind answering questions in the middle of lecture, this is where his knowledge and passion for biology really showed. Bio 1610 is a time consuming class, but if you're going to take it, take it with him!

If you have to take biology and you know you're going to have a difficult time, take Colby's class! This is a very difficult class with so many assignments, but Colby explains things in a way that's easy to understand. Read the provided text and get high scores on pre/post class and DTLs and worksheets because they add up.

Colby is the BEST. I cannot recommend him enough. He deeply cares about his students and wanted us to succeed. That's why our class fell a little behind, because he realized we weren't catching onto some of the topics. He spent extra time to go over them. I would say this class is achievable. Just aim for understanding rather than memorizing!

He is a great professor and is very passionate about what he teaches. Hes very funny and gets to know the students. This class has so many assignments. There are multiple quizzes, and other assignments due every week. attendance is mandatory since he has questions in class that count towards your grade. overall i recommend this professor.

This guy is amazing! He is so understanding and helpful and actually cares about his students. There is usually a small point quiz you take at home before and after class and a drawing assignment after every class too. About 6 real quizzes/exams throughout the actual class. Super great guy.

Colby Tanner is a really fun professor and is a good teacher but the sheer amount of assignments is absurd. We had 6 assignments due during finals week and had ~80 assignments throughout the year. The content was nowhere near hard enough to need so many things to do. This class would have been much better without so many assignments

what a great teacher! i was in the 8am class, but i made it to every single class because of how interesting it was.His class is super engaging and interesting, you can tell that he cares about his students. this is a very work heavy course, you will have a lot of homework but trust that its super helpful and genuinely strengthens your learning.

I definitely would recommend taking Colby for Biology if you need it. He cares for everyone to succeed and wants everyone to pass. The class can be hard if you're not very sciency, but he provides lots of outside resources for help. He's also willing to answer questions if you have them and is a very nice guy. I wish he taught more classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had here at the U! He genuinely cares about teaching the content and makes sure you not only understand the material but know how to apply it. He is a great person overall and I would definitely recommend taking a class from him!!

Colby is definitely one of the best professors I've ever had! His lectures are entertaining and he always ensures his students understand the material. You can tell he is truly passionate about his job and he cares about your success. I would 100% take this class again, it's my favorite!
Amazing professor, he has good lectures and easy makes them easy to understand, you will have to study a lot but he provides so many resources and prepares you for the criteria on exams

Colby is literally the best professor I have ever had. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and he is always willing to answer questions and help students fully understand the subject. He is very engaged with students in the class and cares about our education.

I loved Colby's class so much! His lectures were engaging and he really cares about his students. Every time someone would raise their hand he asked for their name, and it really made a good impression to a 300 person lecture that he tried to learn names. I would definitely take his class again, and I wish he taught every subject!

Yes, the hype is real. Colby has a passion for teaching. He is very goofy and casual, but I think that is why he is amazing; it doesn't feel like a task to listen to him. He is great at relaying expectations on quizzes and exams and explains why each thing we learned was important/relevant. Took him again for 1620, there was no question.
Colby is a great professor. He is kind of all over the place however, he cares about his students and tries to engage them in the lesson. If you are going to take biology choose Colby.

Professor Colby is the best! This was my second time taking bio 1610 and he was much better than Renee in my opinion. He does really care about his students and takes time to learn their name especially if they participate in class. He prioritizes making sure the class as a whole gets critical concepts within the course and wants everyone to pass.

Fantastic teacher! His lectures were so engaging and he really cares about students. He provides so many resources outside of class if you do not understand a concept (study halls, discussions, etc). In past biology classes, I felt like I was memorizing trivia, but in this class I learned the why behind everything we were learning.

This is a one credit lab and he treats it like one. Not too much work but the labs are interesting and he makes it engaging. He is also the nicest and open to questions and suggestions from students. So personable and easy to get along with him. If you need a bio lab credit take this!!

After 3 years at the U, I have finally had a positive experience with a professor in STEM. He is an AMAZING teacher! He makes the classroom a positive environment, is goofy, and genuinely cares about his students. I wish I was able to have him for more bio courses!

Colby has become one of my favorite professors. He cares about his students and ensures they understand the material so they do well in his class. He does not mind if you ask him questions; he is always happy to help. I would 100% recommend him for Bio!!!

Tanner is a great lecturer who cares about his students. The class itself is tough but he works hard to make sure his students are getting the help they need. Uses IClicker for attendance/participation. I believe Renee Dawson is the head of the course so Tanner didn't make any of the assignments himself, but he did a great job.

Colby was an assistant professor so to my knowledge he didn't create any assignments or tests. He was super caring and even gave out his personal number to students so they could text him with any questions. He always made time out side of class to help students who were struggling. Overall a 5/5
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Genuinely one of the best professors I have learned from. His lectures are fun and engaging and you can tell he really cares about his students and enjoys the material and his job. 
He's super chill and understanding and if you're real with him he'll be real with you.
10/10 would recommend him to anyone wanting to take 1610!!!
Very cool and understanding guy

Colby is amazing he showed up to class the first day wearing cargo pants and a t-shirt and my friend and I knew we'd like him. He's a good lecturer and has a great personality. The work isn't difficult. Just pay attention and do the pre and post test stuff. Would recommend.
Colby is amazing! Super easy to track with and understand. You can tell he truly cares about his students and what he's teaching. Highly recommend taking a Colby Tanner class!

really chill and humble guy, knows what he's talking about and always does his best to answer students' questions and clearly explain topics during lectures. He only taught parts of biol 1620, but I felt more engaged when he taught than the other prof.
Colby is a very chill and nice person. He cares about his students and answers his student's questions thoughtfully.
The way he encourage students to be curious is rare. I think that is what education is missing.

Colby is very caring to his student. He encourages questions and discussion from students. Every time students ask him question, he will be very patiently to answer them. If something he does not know, he would just honestly say "I don't know much about it".

For 1620. I liked Prof. Tanner, but the lectures were constantly, constantly interrupted by students. He would stop lecturing to answer questions, which often left students waiting to understand what we were actually supposed to learn/study/write down. This made the course confusing, and we fell really behind. Otherwise, he's very nice.

For 1620: Good teacher, may ramble a little but overall is concise on what you need to know and makes emphasizes tested content. Only teached for the second half of class but was good for the time being. Tests were generally easy if you studied all DTL and previous quizzes. Quizzes are every 2 weeks and are take home.

So chill and nice. He really wants you to succeed and understand why things work the way they do. If someone missed class, he reached out to keep you in the loop. During final project presentations, he gave good constructive criticism when he could have ripped some of the groups apart. 

Would take again in a heartbeat.

He only taught the second half of the semester. Tanner wants you to succeed. Everything on tests was in lectures or DTLs. Tells you what to expect for exams and quizzes if you go in during office hours. I was in a lecture hall with 100 people and he took the time to ask everyone their names. Really nice guy and very understanding if you talk to him
Amazing Professor, actually uses real life situations around campus to help give insight to the class. He really cares about the course as he helped make the course and helps everyone succeed.

Dr. Costa was a great professor, but his class was only graded on five tests, which were 100 questions long and almost opinion based. Attendance is definitely mandatory as he does not post any slides or lecture material online. His lectures are also very heavy and cover lots of material in a short amount of time. Overall, he is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: History of Rock & Roll is a very interesting subject! Prof. Costa is an entertaining lecturer. Your entire grade is based off of five 100 question quizzes throughout the semester, open note/book. No other assignments. He has a textbook that you can study from, but it can become tedious. TLDR: Entertaining content, poor method of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Costa is so passionate about what he teaches and really cares about his students. While the grades for this class only consist of 5 100-question tests, they aren't timed and are open-note/book. He's truly a nice guy and keeps lectures fun and interesting. While attendance isn't mandatory, I highly suggest sitting in on his Zoom lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things
