reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class! His lectures were very entertaining and he's a funny guy. The tests are quite challenging because a lot of the questions he doesn't even talk about in class, but you can use the textbook on tests.

I took this class online and it was so useless. I didn't learn anything. The entire class is graded on 5 100 question tests. The tests are so time consuming and everything is found in his book. If you're looking to get the gen ed requirement I'd recommend taking literally anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love this guy. He cares so deeply about what he is teaching and has done it so long. The most interesting class I've taken this semester I loved it. The only problem is the only thing he grades on is these long long tests that you take on your own. I wish he just did something better for grading

John Costa is probably very nice, but his class isnt. This class has no other work except for the test you take every few months, each test having 100+ questions. Every answer is in HIS book. Nothing online is correct, and it takes hours to take because of the horrible word search the book has. Easy A, but only if you put hours into all tests
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is click baiting you on the first lecture. He seems like a nice and funny guy which don't get me wrong he is. The lectures are very fun. Then you realize once you get to the test "HUH" I actually don't need to go to class. Why? Because he is pulling every answer from god knows where. Only way to pass is to spend hours going through the textbook.
I wasn't expecting to like this class much, was just taking it to get the credit out of the way. Ended up being one of my favorite classes. Would recommend.

All of his class is made up of midterm grades. The questions seem almost opinionated and if you use AI you usually get between 80-85% on the tests. They are not very well agreed upon answers if you look them up. As other reviewers have said it seems like he got offended his class was an easy A and started to deviate and purposely make test hard

This class had optional zoom lectures, I did not attend any but have heard they are enjoyable. The grade book consists of 5 exams that are very specific but easily found on quizlets. If you are looking for a low effort, no homework class, highly recommend.

Overall a very interesting class. There are 5 midterms and that is your entire grade. The tests are very trivial and often misleading. I think this guy was just trying to get away from the "easy A" allegations. The majority of what is on his tests is not talked about in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Costa clearly is passionate about music and it's history. It shows in his lectures. While they are zoom/recorded lectures, they're a lot of fun to learn from. The only thing that counts towards your grade is 5 tests throughout the semester, which aren't cumulative. Costa allows open notes and has plenty of resources for you to study with.
John Costa is a good professor and very engaging in class. However, his tests are difficult and usually include information that the internet doesn't even know.

Professor Costa's class was super easy. It was graded only on the tests so make sure to do good on them. He had three zoom lectures a week that covers each topic so he will be talking a lot. There is also assigned reading each week which is pretty easy to follow. Overall his class was not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Costa's lectures are engaging and rewarding if you put in the effort. The class revolves around 5 exams, so staying on top of the material is key. I found Unstuck ai and the free textbook helpful for study prep, along with attending class. Overall, an enjoyable and manageable course.
This class is very easy, grades are only from 5 online tests which you have 48 hours to do. Attendance is not required but I highly recommend going because it is interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Costa is passionate about the subject but not so much about his students' learning. He is not online savvy, so the fact that the class is online makes it difficult to understand.  The textbook used was written by him and is a bullet-pointed list of topics covered.

This class is a breeze. The tests take a really long time if you only use the textbook. Exams have 100 questions, most answers can be found online. The lectures are not mandatory, though they are very interesting. The professor is obviously passionate about the subject. He isn't super internet savvy, so the online students had some trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Costa is one of my favorite profs of all time. The guy loves Rock and Roll and it shows. His lectures are an absolute blast, and he always has dope stories to tell about all of the bands. The tests are a little arduous but they're absolutely worth it.

Rock on Dr. Costa!
Heartless man

Professor Costa was very excited about his class and made his lectures energetic and interesting. The class was based on 5 exams but they were all pretty relatable to the information from lectures. his lectures aren't mandatory but I recommend listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't enjoy this class. I didn't interact with the professor very much but I didn't like this class. Avoid taking it if you can. It seems like it would be simple but it is not. You have to pay attention and read.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the semester, I didn't pay too much attention during classes and I was always on my phone. But near the halfway point, I put the phone down and started attentively listening for his lectures and he was so incredible. If you put in the effort and actually show up to class, this can be the most rewarding class you will ever take.

There are few people who care about music as much as Professor Costa. And not only does he care, but he encourages his students to care and become involved. The only thing on your grade is 5 exams (no homework) so you just have to listen to lectures to do well on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a really easy class. There are five exams, and you can easily get an A or a B without much effort. Also, Costa's textbook is poorly made and doesn't help much with exams. It's more of a vast tome of loosely organized notes than anything. If you need an easy fine arts credit, take it, but avoid otherwise.

Entire class is based solely on five exams. If you miss a test though, he's not forgiving. Super easy class, ~20 people in the 200 person class would show up by the end of the semester. Textbook is not very helpful, as it's just 600 pages of the professor's notes, but you shouldn't really need it. Know when the exams are and the class is easy.

Dr. Costa was my favorite professor in my first semester of college. You could NEVER show up, and do the tests and end with an A. That is what over half the class does. Although, by doing this you are missing a major opportunity to learn and hear a wise mans story. He has lived the music scene his whole life. Amazing lectures. If you take, SHOW UP!

Professor Costa is definitely passionate about music and its history. He is very animated and loves putting on a show, but the class is definitely not hard in any way. You can not show up all year and still pass. If you want to learn from his class then go, but if you just want an A then don't. There are only 5 tests all year which are all online.

This professor openly admitted to doing LSD in his younger years.... it shows.... 5/5 stars!! I liked this professor. He was very animated and entertaining during class. The grade is based off of 5 tests that are easy. Its an easy A.

THE EASIEST CLASS AT THE U. Class is graded on 5 tests which are open book and online with a 24 hour time period to complete them. You could never show up to class and get an A+ in this class. However, if you do show up to class, he is quite funny and I actually enjoyed learning about the history of rock & roll. Would take again.

The 5 tests are a bit much, and the textbook is rather boring.

Nevertheless, Dr. Costa is engaging and hilarious in every lecture! I wish he would publish a book containing all of his funny sayings!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class hoping for something fun and educational, but I was disappointed. Costa clearly teaches this class just for the money, and would rather be writing music than doing this. His "textbook" is written by him, and is 82$ for what is literally bullet notes. It's an unreadable textbook in a clear cash grab class. I was sorely disappointed
N/A

Professor Costa is fantastic! His lectures are interesting, and he shows videos that help the time go by faster. He is also funny at some points and always seems very happy. The class is graded on five tests. Other than the five tests, I would definitely take this class again. Great class and professor!

The class was easy to get an A in, as there only are five 100-questioned exams to complete. One could feasibly get above a 90 without using the professor's textbook. The textbook is boring as it looks like someone wrote bulleted notes everywhere. One could never go to class and read the texture and still get an easy A. Take this class.
I didn't show up to a single class and I got >90% on all 5 of the exams. Sorta slow to respond to emails though.

His class is 100% graded by 5 tests on obscure music facts. I had a health emergency while on a trip and could not make it back in time to take his online test. He would not let me take it because I was "on vacation" and that was not a viable reason. I almost failed because of this. I thought professors would value my health and safety over a test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just use quizlet. Take it online. I had no interaction with him, I did not buy his textbook, and I did not watch a single lecture. I got an A, so if you want an A for a gen ed then this is your class. People say he is terrible but I am not really sure why. I mean it is an easy A so I am not sure why people are complaining as much as they do.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You get graded by 5 online test. 99% of the answers can be found online. If you want to pass this class you basically have to cheat because instead of lecturing he just sits there and rambles for hours. Doesn't matter if you take it online in person. Easy a but annoying if you want to actually learn about the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hated this professor, the class is mid. Graded on 5 exams that's it. If you miss it then there is no way you can retake it. Costa is very hard on the students. Overall, professor sucks, class is mid, but if you do take this class, TAKE IT ONLINE!!! Even thought that the syllabus says he'll post the lectures online he doesn't.
So easy. Only take 5 tests and that's it no other assignments. Don't need to study either because all of the answers are online.

There are no assignments in this class other than the 5 exams. They are 100 questions and will suck the life out of you, they are extremely hard but definitely passable. In the end I would not worry too much, I say this class is an easy A.
i did not go once after tuition was due (two weeks into the semester) because it is just based off of five tests... all which you can control f on either the textbook or quizlets to find the answers

Such an easy class. Graded by 5 tests where most answers are online or in the textbook. All tests were online. In the syllabus, it says attendance is recommended. His lectures can be entertaining but can also be used for like a study hall.

Your grade is based on 5 tests that are each worth 100 points. His "textbook" is a bunch of middle school bullet point notes. If you are looking for an easy A then I guess you could take this class.  However, if you think you might have unexpected, last minute emergencies, he will not care and will give you a 0 on the test.  Just keep it in mind.

cant speak about this class as someone who took it to actually learn the subject. took it online to fulfill fine arts credit, easy a. attendance not required online, and dont bother paying for the textbook. but he wont remind you of the exam dates so make sure youre on top of it. dont bother emailing him- you wont get a reply.

Haven't even finished his class but I know it's going to be so easy. He gives you 5 tests for the whole semester and since they are open note you can just use Quizlet. Don't even bother about going to class it doesn't matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class for GenEd credit. The class is based on 5 tests ONLY, and if you miss one, your grade tanks. I had a family member unexpectedly pass away during the last test in this class, and when I reached out to Dr. Costa, he threw his strict missing/late policy in my face, then proceeded to ghost me via email. No compassion, careless, 0/10!!

This prof has a low effort "textbook" he wrote thats just a bullet point list of notes. Theres only 5 tests, all of which with repeat questions, typos, and impossible questions without context. If you miss one online test you get a fail and he wont let you retake it no matter what. This prof is just riding off the money without even trying to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty mid professor and class. Interesting if you enjoy music, but the first couple weeks are a bit boring. Class relies on lectures and 5 tests you're graded on. Prof is a bit monotone in his lectures. Tests not too hard, since theyre open note and book. Overall, glad I took this class, and I learned a lot. Will I rememeber it all? Probably not.

Costa is a terrible professor. There are only 5 assignments (each 100 points) and if you miss even one, you end up with a failing grade. He has no compassion for students and won't give anyone a second chance unless there is documented proof that you were on your deathbed. Do not take this class.

The professor writes his own "textbook" every year and charges $80 for it so he can make money as well. The "textbook" is also nothing more than lecture notes for the professor. Your grade is based ONLY on 5, 100 question exams. The class is open note so use quizlet and you should be fine. Easy class, waste of time to go to lecture or use the book.

I took history of rock and roll with costa, if you're looking for an easy course for your ff credit and don't want any work basically.  The downside is that if you miss one of the 5 tests (these five tests are the only thing in the class all semester) you're screwed.  I did great on every test but missed one and got a D

Listen this class is easy given you do not have to really do anything besides the FIVE midterms. John's textbook is written like an MLA outline and is very hard to study given the high volume of facts.

I took this class because it sounded interesting and I like music. Due to a severe mental health issue, I was unable to take the first test. When I emailed him the day after, he responded rudely and then did not respond AT ALL to my follow up email. He wrote the textbook and it sucks, literally just a compilation of Cornell notes.
Not the best presentations, if you don't show up to class and memorize everything, don't expect a good grade on your tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: John is really passionate about what he teaches which is a good quality to have. His class is very lecture heavy with no slides, just him speaking and maybe some music/instrumental videos. Your grade if made up of 5 online exams, so it's important to do good. Exams aren't bad, you can usually find the answers by reading the textbook.

Awful scammy teacher. He makes you buy the textbook he wrote, but he requires the most recent version and just keeps releasing new versions so everyone fills his pockets. Also exceptionally bad at responding to emails but makes it the student's problem when he doesn't answer, and in the syllabus says that its on students to follow up.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easiest class ever! I did not attend class often and still got a good grade. Grades are only based on the tests and I never really used the textbook.
Easiest class I have ever taken. 10/10. I used the textbook for a bit, but you don't really need it. Exams were pretty easy and the prof was nice.

The worst class I have ever had. If you miss one of the 5 chapter tests you might not pass the class. He is very strict about retake policies, he would not make any exceptions even for illnesses (including covid-19). Every lecture is him reading directly from the textbook, word for word. He is a rude and uncaring person. No passion for teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a really great guy. This was an easy class and the lectures were super interesting and easy to listen to. He makes good jokes and keeps lectures entertaining. I'm not insanely smart and this was an easy and fun class to be apart of.

The class has 5, 100pt quizzes as the only assignments. The textbook is expensive and is nothing more than a loosely put-together collection of notes. Save yourself the money and peruse some infamous online sites instead of trying to read the textbook. The lectures are also just the prof reading straight from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't care about students and is very rude. If you miss one of his 5 tests you are screwed cause he won't let you retake it or anything.

I took his course pre-covid. He works by a standard where you cannot have your phone out in class or he will yell at you, so I have no idea how he functions doing it online. Although yes, the only thing you are graded on is 5 one-hundred point tests in his class, I genuinely found his lectures and personality really entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Yeah this prof sucks. I gave him a 2 because his dog was mildly entertaining. There may or may not be an online flashcard service which could have all the answers to his tests which I most certainly would not have used if it existed...

Took this class alongside a heavy science curriculum during the pandemic to have fun and learn about music because it is a passion of mine. Costa only responded to one of the 3 emails I sent him and caused me more stress then COVID. Would never take a class with him again and I wish profanity was allowed on this site just for him.

This is the type of class that you will get what you give. Since Rock and Roll really interests me, I actually put a lot of time into focusing on this class and reading the textbook and etc. Your grade is based on 5 tests taken throughout the semester however if you didn't pay attention you can find all of the answers online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are wordy and he requires a textbook which he wrote. Except it isn't a textbook, it's more of a long set of unorganized notes which are sometimes inaccurate, and seem to just be based on his opinion. Easy class if you are just looking to fill a general because the tests are all on quizlet. He is difficult and seldom replies to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is perhaps the most ridiculous class I have ever taken. There are only 5 grades (all tests) that determine your final grade. People claim the test is online but you will not find all of the answers there. Nor will you find answers in his lectures! His tests set you up for a B+. Costa you are hurting students. Retire.

As most people say he's pretty bad at communicating and basically reads straight off of the textbook making his lectures seem boring and long. It's really conflicting on whether or not I would recommend this class. If you are online and can use CTRL+F then its not a bad choice, without it this class would have been a lot harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly he lacks communication, but it's hard with online to have good communication. He's really fun and laid back and his zoom classes are fairly entertaining. Overall easy class, THE ONLY THINGS GRADED ARE THE 4 TESTS you take. If you miss a test, you don't get another chance to take it. Overall good, simple, laidback class.
This professor will not communicate and cooperate with students, will ignore students' requests! Nothing can be discussed. Also, it's an online course.

Possibly the easiest Gen Ed you could take. I showed up only the first few lectures & ended with an A. The one thing that irked me is that his lectures are very interesting and informational, but the info in the lectures is not the same as the 5, 100 question tests. Where can you find that info? In HIS book which you must purchase to do well.

I attended some lectures thinking I would be able to learn and do well on the tests, but that was not true at all. I was able to get about 3-5 questions (out of 100) on the test from the lectures and I was paying attention during the whole 2 hours. You basically have to look in the book for help and even that didnt help. Plus, tests are on saturday
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are an actual fan of Rock & Roll then DO NOT, and I repeat DO NOT take this class. It is frustrating beyond description and the entire coursework is based upon his personal opinion. His text is riddled with inaccuracies that a simple google search will simply prove wrong. The tests are long, scrupulous, and frustrating. Wish I could type mor

John is very opinionated about certain things and makes that clear the first day. Final grade is based off of 5 tests. You do not have to go to class, just know the dates of the tests and take them online.

The lectures always inevitably turn into rants. Passionate about what he is teaching but forces his own agenda. Feels like a class that doesn't need to be as political as he makes it. I stopped showing up about half way through the semester because the tests were so easy. Also has a weird vendetta against phones and will yell if he sees one

Costa is an extremely boring professor. The class isn't very exciting, and the only assignments he has are 5 tests. That's it. The best/worst part is that all of the tests are online, but he caught onto it and caught a few students cheating. All in all, not very exciting class, not very exciting subject, but easy enough if you want to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Costa has clear passion for what he does, and he has very extensive knowledge of the material, but his class was surprisingly difficult. Cheating is an extreme issue in this course as the only graded material is 5 online tests; I came to class every single day and took extensive notes and still did not score higher than a 90 on the online tests.

Very interesting class if you are a fan of music and want to get a fine arts credit out of the way. The lectures were very interesting and fairly easy to follow, considering he almost recites the textbook word for word. Really cool guy with some great stories.
"Show up & pass"? This class is more like "Not show up & get A." Take it when you need a Fine-art and have a tight schedule. It's just that simple.

Make a friend that's taken this class before- they'll tell you everything you need to know. Only graded assignments are 5 tests. Answers come from his textbook, but his lectures are really fun to listen to and he really loves what he teaches. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, I'd go to his class just to listen.

This class CAN be the easy A that everyone thinks it is, but don't be fooled. The tests are long and if you miss EVEN ONE you can come close to failing the class. He will not remind you that the tests are coming up, and if you ask him to reopen it for you he will get angry with you. His lectures were entertaining, but you don't need to go to class.

Only showed up to class on the first day. Only 5 tests online that you can find all the answers for on quizlet or in the textbook. Tests take a long time but average is always a high A. Got 3 credit hours for never showing up to class so I'm satisfied. Take this class if you don't want to learn or have a busy schedule!

This class was very easy. There are five exams throughout the semester, all online and without a time limit. You can find all the answers in the textbook but get ready to spend a couple hours on each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Grade is based off of 5 online tests. Lectures can be long and most of the class does not attend. It is an easy class but not very engaging. Don't have your phone out in class.
Super interesting class. Lecture based with 5 tests, which are online. He hates cell phone use in class.

Costa's a very laid back and easy going guy. Hates having phones out and has quite a few catchphrases. History of Rock and Roll with him was easy and it was fun to listen to music and hear him talk about different artists. The vast majority of the class is him lecturing, with occasional breaks to listen to songs. Very passionate about the subject.

A great class to knock out a fine arts credit since you don't even have to show up. Costa has great lectures if you do decide to roll into class though. Definitely a class to take if you're a STEM major and need a break since there are only five tests which are open book and you can take it online anywhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Costas History of Rock n Roll class is probably the easiest class at the U. The class had 150+ students, but on a good day, only 10-12 students showed up. Tests are open book and online, so you can do them at home. The tests do take a very long time to complete, sometimes 3+ hours. There are quizlets online, use those, not the book.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was by far the best class i've ever taken. I love music and this class was perfect for me. I was one of 3 students that attended lecture each class, but it was worth it. I've learned so many interesting things and this class does come in handy for interesting topics of conversation.

Easiest fine art credit ever. I never went to class and ended with a solid A. You just take 5 online open note tests and that's it. Would recommend to anyone who doesn't actually like taking arts classes.

He knows his stuff and you can tell he loves teaching the subject. If you're an audio learner, this class is perfect. Personally, I wish there was a visual aspect to the class, such as powerpoint or music videos. Make sure to buy the textbook! His exams are long but they're open note, online and not timed. 5 exams, 100 q's each, multi. choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took History of Rock and Roll from Dr. Costa and it was the worst. The only thing on your grade is 5 open book tests that are online and you have 24 hours to take. His lectures are awful, he's monotone and there are no powerpoints or anything. He just stands on a stage and talks. It's very boring and there's no reason to go. Easy A but awful.
Class lectures were very long and boring. Tests are long and tedious but very easy since they are open book.

History of Rock and Roll is the easiest class ever I probably went to class less than 5 times and got a 97% in the class. No homework, no quizzes just 5 tests, those 5 tests are done online at home so if you work with people on the test you'll be totally fine. Such an easy Fine Art credit. I recommend for all.

He is quite opinionated, and will go off on tangents about the Velvet Underground or how the internet ruined music. I stopped showing 2/3 of the way through the semester because attending the lectures was totally unnecessary and boring. If you want and easy A for your FF credit this class is fine, just don't expect a whole lot for your money.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: he seems very passionate about what he's talking about and it can be interesting at times but this class bored me to sleep. and only 1/4 of the students actually show up which is disappointing. overall this class is an easy A.
I love everything about this class. John Costa is phenomenal!

A fun class that allows you to learn more about music and even find new genres you may enjoy. This class is very easy, the final grade comes only from 5 tests averaged out. Tests were online, open for 24 hrs, and open book. Every answer is in the textbook, or in somebody's flash cards online. Showing up is optional but the lectures are worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class!  Interesting, easy art credit.

This guy is super cool, laid back, and a hilarious dude. You really don't need to go to class since all the test are online and untimed. A major bummer for at least the first half summer session, was that you had to do the tests on Saturdays. You should at least look at the syllabus and go to class the days when he talks about a topic you like.

This is an easy A class to take care of your Fine Arts credit.  Your grade is based on five online tests that have no time limit, so you can look up all the answers in the book that he wrote himself.  There is no need to go to class, but you might as well because he plays music from and talks about some way cool artists!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easiest FF gen ed credit so i highly recommend it! You need to take 5 tests online open book that is all.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is the best class to take if you want an easy GenEd fine arts course. After the first week, only about half the students enrolled actually showed up to class. John Costa is an awesome professor and knows his stuff! MAKE SURE TO DO THE TESTS ON TIME! He doesn't usually cut you a break. Overall, such a chill class!

Easy class, grade based entirely on 5 online, open book tests. I really enjoyed going to lecture, but it definitely isn't mandatory. Get the textbook and do the review questions at the end and it'll save you a ton of time on the tests.

MUSC 2100 is probably the easiest FF credit you can take. The only grades are five open-book, online tests throughout the semester. Attendance is absolutely optional (there were 200 students in my class, maybe 30 showed up). Buy the textbook, it's worth it to have it for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: An easy A with 5 open note tests and non-mandatory attendance. If you need an FF credit and don't care how you get it, take this course. All you really need is the textbook.
I couldn't stand him. Attendance isn't necessary.  Tests took me about 6 hours to complete. Open book tests answers on are online. Easy A.
If you need a FF credit and want to bump up your GPA--take MUSC 2100. Tests are long (100 questions) but it's open book and quite easy.

If you want to get an a and an FF credit, take this class.  If you want to actually get something from your education, DO NOT take this class.  I didn't learn anything.  Class based on 5 open-book online tests which you can get all answers easily from book or other sources. My recommendation - take another class and actually learn something.
The entire grade is based on 5 open book tests which are online and have no time limit. Answers are not hard to find
You have 5 tests, but they are online and there isn't a time limit. If you do the chapter reviews from the textbook, then you should be golden. The textbook is they KEY TO SUCCESS IN THIS CLASS!!

If you happen to miss a test for what ever reason it completely ruins your chance of getting a high grade in the class. Not very willing to let students retake test. The grade is made up of 5 test that are each open for 24 hours. Your grade is based on your average score of these 5 test. Easy class just make sure you set a reminder for test dates.

This class was super easy and even though he may not look it the professor is super chill. Participation is not important at all you don't even have to show up grade is based on 5 online, open book, take at home, test. The class is interesting and he makes it fun but if you just need the credit/easy A definitely choose this one.

Dr. Coleman has very long, boring lectures that make you want to fall asleep. The TAs for this class were also very picky about grading and harsh about the smallest things. There are online quizzes almost every week about the readings, some with trick questions. Attendance is mandatory and is part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Coleman is definitely passionate about what he teaches but he's not the right person for it. I'm not sure if he actually reads the essays that we submit or if he just glances at them and assigns a grade based on how he's feeling and whether he likes the student. Useful feedback is a rarity from him and sometimes your grade feels like roulette.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though the class is lecture heavy, he does a good job making it interesting and covers subjects not often discussed in american history. He is very respectful to students and their questions. The grading system is well balanced, though you have to stay on top of the quizzes and attendance.

Based on weekly quizzes, 2 exams, and 2 book reports. Almost no guidance, and canvas is unorganized. Professor is nice, and willing to help, but for the most part attend lectures and your on your own. Make sure you check the syllabus, because he gives very short notice for things that have huge impacts on your grade.

This class is very lecture heavy. Every class is a lecture, nothing different. He goes through the slides fairly fast, lots of notetaking. Attendance is mandatory at the end of class. Your grade is based off of a few things. There's two exams and two book reviews, there is a weekly quiz based off the weekly readings. The readings are very tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is based on two book reviews and two tests. The professor briefly mentions the reviews early on, then not again until right before they're due, with no guidance despite them being nearly half your grade. Study guides cover little of what's on tests, which often include obscure lecture details. Take a different class.
He is terrible at grading and very unorganized.

Graded by a few tests and quizzes, attendance taken. Only so much can be done to make a 300-person American History lecture not super boring. Dr. Coleman essentially just followed PowerPoints with bullet points for lectures, but did a very good job explaining why things happened and how different historical events tie in together.
Attendance was required. His lectures mostly consisted of just reading the PowerPoints he provided. Easy two tests and two essays. Pretty easy gen ed

There were some weekly quizzes, but your grade is determined by 2 essays and 2 tests. The tests were easy, and the essays were also easy if you knew where to pull information from. The lectures were him reading the slides aloud, so if they don't take attendance, you don't need to show up. Overall, an easy gen-ed class.

Dr. Coleman's lectures were easy to access on canvas, but were often long presentations and copying down the slides verbatim each class; majority of things said in class you will be tested on. Two major 1,000 word essays, 2 tests (midterms and finals) that Dr. Coleman provided study guides for one week before the exams.

Professor Coleman is fantastic! Their history class is both doable and manageable, with clear lectures that make complex topics easy to grasp. They are always available to help and provide helpful feedback. Exams and assignments are fair. Highly recommend taking this class!

Where should I start, he's just a great dude. His lectures are engaging and informative. The class is manageable, with success largely depending on two essays and the midterm and final, which are fair and not overly difficult.

This class isn't easy, but Prof. Csirmaz is wonderful and always incredibly helpful. She has worked with me multiple times to make sure I understand all of the material, even if it takes a while. She has reached out to me personally to see if I needed help in class. The work is hard, but if you try and put in the effort, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice person and gives amazing, extremely detailed feedback (like, I've never seen anything like it). I feel like her lectures were kind of confusing at times, but I still managed to follow them. I'm not sure that I would recommend the class because the subject matter ended up being kind of boring, but I'd still recommend Aniko as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Online. Summer. Covid-19. She graded based on completion. Not stressful. Had times when my brain hurt from all the readings. If you show effort & do your work then you'll pass with flying colors. Some of the papers were hard reads, BUT Aniko truly wants students to understand difficult concepts & gives great feedback to help when you don't get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I usually have a very easy time in my Linguistics classes, but Syntax with Aniko was difficult. There were a lot of times that I felt she was making things a lot more difficult than they needed to be. She's also a very tough grader and takes points off for anything. Just make sure you actually read the textbook and stay caught up, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The rest of of the reviews about Aniko are really bad, but I actually like her as a professor. I was in  Introduction to Syntax last semester with another professor and I ended up dropping the course because I was totally lost. Aniko has structure in her class and she won't move on until the material is clear. She is always willing to help.

Even though there aren't many tests, there are tons of HW Assignments. And there's a disconnect between the HW and the test. On the Midterm, 60% of the class failed and she refused to curve it. Very difficult class for such an interesting subject.
With the class average for the midterm being 50% you should seriously reconsider taking this class if you care at all about your GPA.
Nice woman but terrible at teaching. Linguistics 1200 is a general and she treated it like a class meant for linguistics majors. It was awful

Aniko is a great person - her teaching is not. She does not understand the concept of "curving." If you fail the midterm (which most of my class did), better withdraw or else you will have to get 100% on every assignment and final then assigned after that. If you aren't interested in Linguistics, do not take this class.
Nice person, bad at teaching.
we love dworkin
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Craig is a really thoughtful and knowledgeable professor. Definitely a laissez-faire classroom (your final grade is up to you and discussions are largely student-driven.) But Craig still obviously cares about students and forms a relationship with the class. Discussions were always fun and interesting -- new and weird ideas always welcomed.
He is very kind. He does not give exams and quizzes. Yes, his grading is subjective. Thus, give him a good impression! Read the stuff and write some random thoughts then you get an A. Why not?

As long as you do the readings and give the writings "the good college try" you'll be absolutely fine. Professor wants to help everybody learn and that is what he does. No exams or homework assignments, but just be sure to attend class, do the readings and post your writings on Canvas. If you do that you'll get an A no problem.

Solely based on weekly discussion posts. SO much writing, and it felt a lot like busy work. Really not a lot of requirements, not a real rubric involved, just a lot of talking about women writers. Completely student-driven, so I didn't get to know him very well. Didn't really serve my knowledge or pique interest, but a good selection of readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved him, as a person he was extremely smart, caring and enthusiastic about what he taught.  The course is a little strangely structured and the only grade is your final grade (which you get to suggest) but it made me think a lot and the content was interesting.

As long as you read, participate in discussion and keep up with your posts + 1 presentation- you will make an A. Professor Dworkin is REALLY into avant-garde poetry. The thing is avant-garde poetry is super weird and makes little to no sense. So good luck with that! But his enthusiasm makes up for it! Just give your opinion in class and your good.

Craig is one of the kindest, most caring professors I've had at the U. Although the content of what he thought was a little obscure (language poetry), he's extremely knowledgeable about it, works with you on it, and, as long as you show up regularly and show him that you care about doing well in the class, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: This has to be the weirdest guy I know. He never taught the entire semester. This course was the biggest waste of time and taught me absolutely nothing. All grades are completely subjective and are not judged based on correctness or any sort of Rubric. Worst class and professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Craig is very smart and he is amazing I think he really cares about his students and he tries to find ways to help. This class is FOR SURE different. Expect a LOT of reading, a LOT of weird hypothesis, a lot of poetry, and abstract thinking... so if you are not into the whole concept of "read between the lines" this class is not for u

The entire course consisted of coming up with thesis' of obscure PDF documents.  It was clear he never prepared anything for the class and the entire class was a discussion of these documents.  You need to constantly BS everything for participation.  This was a class where the only thing you learned was to check this site before enrolling in it.

- Politics of Media - No textbook required (but PDFs galore via Canvas) - Tons of theory reading, most it comprehensible  - No tests or essays  - 50% of grade was in class participation, 25% of grade was from weekly online Canvas postings, and the last 25% was a presentation (you sign-up for a day to initiate the class discussion; simple).

I did sometimes struggle to stay awake but I loved the open floor discussions where everyone was encouraged to share. He's a published author and a wise professor who guided us through this very complex and abstract language poetry. I learned a lot and he was an easy grader. I'd take a class from him again.

So frustrating! Dworkin originally gave me a B (only one received EVER) and finally changed it to an A- after I went and consulted with him. Class "requirements" were not made clear, there was no grading scale, and the worst was that out of the weekly and final papers we wrote (12+) students did not receive a SINGLE ONE with feedback. Grr.

Ineffective professor. I asked for help a couple of times but eventually stopped when professor told me my guess was as good as his. Professor never offered feedback; we received no grades except the final grade. Professor was a little too hands off during class; I often wondered if he'd prepared at all. Very disappointing.

I didn't care for him, but I know he has his fans--the class just didn't have enough structure to work for me. He's a smart guy, but I ended up learning a lot more from other students in the class than from him. However, whether you understand what he's saying or not it's fairly easy to do well in the class. A little BS goes a long way.

Great teacher! He really made the conversation interesting and was always interested in hearing what anyone had to say regardless of it being right or wrong. He wasn't to tough on grading, but I think it was because he wanted to see if you understood a concept rather than seeing if you could write a sentence that met his standards. Really nice guy.
i knew this prof from princeton-- and wanted to remark that he is the COOLEST most wonderful professor ever. Utah is a lucky school...
especially for the avant-garde at heart.

Good class discussions, but he never returned any weekly papers so many were unsure of their progress in the class.  He did hold individual meetings to discuss midterms.  From what I understand, the topics discussed are not typical 2600 topics.  I didn't learn anything about literary forms, but I learned a lot about deep analysis

Studies in Modernism...no one in the class really knew what was going on...at the start of the class he said we'd do weekly writings, but he only assigned two.    His class was really tough, mainly because the stuff we were reading was tough...any time you do Pound, Zukofsky, Neidecker, etc it's going to be hard.  He'll help if you go talk to him.
Craig is amazing, brilliant, and in the know.
No Comments
No Comments
A really great class so far, interesting reading, good discussions.  He brings up stuff that really makes you think.  Humorous and not boring.
no one in the class ever had any idea what it was about or what the assignments were, or how we were doing in it.  easy and fun though.

Crawford grades so difficult! You have to read the complicated instructions very carefully to be able to get a good grade, and if you make one slight mistake on the assignments, then he chops your grade in half, with little chances of being able to redo it. Would not recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was very laid back, and the lectures were actually interesting. For a writing class, there are only 3 main assignments, and you really only have to actually write something for the last one. I would definitely recommend this class for anyone needing to take an upper-division course.

Lewis seems strict and sort of mean at first, but he's a grade-A chiller. Lectures are super interesting, as are the larger assignments. There isn't that much writing for a writing class. Lewis knows a ton about tech and the arts and he's got some cool lore, too. He used to DJ and I think he owned a record store.
This professor used classtime to constantly talk about his health problems. He was petty, mean, condescending, and openly gossiped about colleagues and students.

This class was pretty fun for a CW requirement and ARTX elective. We had 3 major individual projects with smaller things in between. The projects were on programs like Indesign which he taught you how to use. It's a unique writing class and you can tell he likes to teach it, so he tries to make the class easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
ARTX3600
I enjoyed the class. It felt like there wasn't a lot of writing happening even though it was a writing class. Most of the assignments were on the shorter side, with one big writing assignment.. But, you can tell he genuinely loves the subject and was always open to answering questions.

Very chill professor. The class was mainly project-based, with three individual projects and two group projects. These projects were extremely open-ended; as long as you stuck to the theme (which was based on 'passions' you chose at the beginning of the year) and included some required elements you could pretty much make anything. Very cool class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is the rudest, most disrespectful, and downright mean teacher I think I have ever had. He frequently, and literally, shouts at students if he has to repeat himself, or if they are working to complete something that is due that class (which everyone does once and awhile), he is not encouraging, he does not want to help you and grades super harsh.

Prof. Crawford has one of the best methods for homework that I've ever seen. He has you write down three of your major interests at the beginning of the semester and then has you complete assignments based on those interests while applying the information you've learned.

He can be a real jerk sometimes but not very often, usually he is pretty cool. you have a lot of projects and one group projects at the end. no final and a couple of quizzes online. he grades tough though.

Prof. Cotter clearly enjoys making non-traditional exams with curveballs, but they are generally fair. His lectures are certainly more harmful than helpful, though, so I would rely on outside resources to prepare. He is funny and kind but unfortunately, less so when the class average for an exam is a failing grade. He does not curve. Study early.

Just like everyone says, his lectures are not helpful. However, he was always willing to help after class and even stays longer to help. As a tip, study more on how he does thing that just the concepts. This class concept did depend on the past units, so don't think you can just move on if you didn't understand the past material.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My mother has been dealing with breast cancer and surgeries and everything that comes with breast cancer, and cotter has not been compassionate towards the situation at all. She was in the ICU for a stretch during an exam period, and he said that is why one exam grade is dropped and cannot be made up. Will not compromise/accommodate personal issues

For the very base introduction to circuits Lab, Neil Cotter was pretty good. For the very top level stuff with circuits he does a good job at teaching the topics alongside the TA who helps explain in class as well. During lecture he sometimes just goes off on random tangents but its honestly kinda fun. Not a hard course by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was extremely difficult to pay attention in class past the first couple weeks. He constantly made mistakes in his overbearing and overcomplicated examples, and taught as if all of us already knew every intricate detail of the material. Angela Rasmussen's YouTube videos will get you through this course. This was just a bad experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The whole class is pretty much determined by the exams. During his lectures, he just mumbles and it's impossible to hear him. Also, he'll just ramble on about other stuff and its super difficult to follow along. Just watch Rasmussen's videos they're a million times better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He just didn't want to teach this class and made it very obvious on several occasions. Tests are 80% of your grade, and we got barely any actual study material. For one of his exams, he gave us two practice examples where we found 10+ errors. His response? The "correct" solutions 10 pm the night before the exam. No credit, no recognition. Awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very fast paced, often quoted by others "not worth going". He's very smart but enjoys overcomplicating concepts and techniques. There is no correalation between his lecture and materials to real 50 minutes exam, where he makes sure to present you with something you have never encountered before. No curves No extra credit.

Lectures are terrible, you dont learn much of anything. The canvas page did have lots of learning material, which was about the only good thing about the whole course. Tests are super hard, so study up and good luck. would not recommend.

Your grade is almost entirely dependent on the exams. The only reason I did well on the exams was because of Angela Rasmussen since Cotter just uses her quizzes and learning materials. I attended EVERY lecture, but I genuinely believe that attending his lectures is only detrimental to your own understanding of the material they are so disjointed.

A very, VERY poor lecturer. The lectures don't match the homework. He gives very little examples. His exams don't match the homework. His exam reviews don't match his exams.

By far one of the worst experiences I've had in university. Please don't think it'll be different with you, it won't.

I hate giving him a bad review since he was a delight to talk with, but this was such a disjointed class. Cotter is a mathematician who went into electrical engineering, the class is very difficult as Cotter didn't explain material or give many examples. Avoid at all costs

Cotter is a good guy, his lectures are dry. He will go on confusing tangents in the middle of a thought.
He talks in a monotone level, records all lectures, and works though problems in class. Highly rec going to the lectures.
The grade was 75% exams, the rest trickled into assignments. TA and working though labs saved my grade.

Absolutely terrible professor with his style of teaching being more akin to an excuse for him to brag about how much smarter he is than you. Lecture's don't help with him skipping steps for topics you haven't even covered yet. Tests are the only thing that matters in that class and even with thoughts he will change your score when he pleases.

Dr. Cotter's exams are challenging but not ridiculous and he loves to throw in a curveball. However, if you attend lectures you will always have a clear understanding of what is required to do well on the exams. Also, he is always in his office and will stop whatever he is doing to help you out with any problems. No homework grade.

Professor is of no help. Some homework problems do not reflect the actual material learned in class. Not to mention his work is unbelievably hard to follow. I would've preferred a different professor teaching. Use the textbook, you'll learn more from the textbook than from him.

Professor Cotter's lectures are pretty much zero help, and he doesn't give homework to reinforce concepts. I've pretty much learned the material in this course from looking at past exams and the solutions to the assessments he gives us. I feel like my understanding of fundamental EE concepts is rudimentary at best due to Professor Cotter.

Never in my life have I had a teacher like Cotter. Without fail, every single time I watch a lecture video, I end up more confused than before. Attempting to learn from him is a joke. I understand the material learning independently, and do great on tests and quizzes... but that is all learning from outside resources. Avoid at all costs.

I felt like I had to teach myself most of the subject, However he does have homework solutions and past exams posted. I would recommend for the start of a unit to just look at the past exams see what concepts are commonly tested on and start teaching yourself those concepts over the weekend and you will be fine.
Last week of school he gave us a Midterm, a final, a lab final, and a quiz. All during finals week.
Best Professor in the world

Worst Professor I've ever taken. Rude, arrogant, and purposefully made the course extra difficult presumably to weed out students. The content itself was pretty easy but he spent most of class going through ridiculously complicated problems that he'd not always get through, instead of teaching us. Tests were awful too and had things we'd never seen

His lectures have too many cluttered notes and disorganized materials. His tests are short but go by fast and you're bound to make mistakes. If you can take a different prof, do it. Otherwise, form good study groups and go to his office hours. I honestly think if his exam periods are longer, I might get a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Picture a happy grandpa & you'll have Prof. Cotter! He is passionate about ECE & his student's success. He made class entertaining and engaged everyone. He provides lots of resources to help you learn the content in addition to his recorded lectures and notes. There wasn't a lot of homework, but it wasn't spaced out very well so it felt like a lot.

Nice Guy and all, but his lectures are ridiculously hard to follow due to his rambling and inability to focus and engage with his students. His tests would likely be far easier and reasonable given the limited time frame if he could effectively teach. If you are not confident in your ability to learn on your own, do not take this from Cotter.

Professor Cotter is easily one of the worst professors you will ever have. I took his 1240 class twice and couldn't make sense of it. If you're considering ECE here's a tip... Don't. This man is too unorganized to be teaching and, unfortunately, he teaches the next 3 levels in ECE. I can not believe this man has a PhD.

Professor Cotter is a nice guy, but he should not be teaching. His lectures are just him rambling about nothing you need to know. Showing up to lecture is a waste of time. The class is easy to pass, as almost all the grade is exams which are based off of the previous years. Do not take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Neil Cotter tends to go on tangents all the time during lectures, so I didn't find attending very helpful. He provides the answers to the homework, which is helpful, but can also very easily be abused. I found tests to be very difficult. He provides old classes' notes/material, but there is so much of it that it's unclear where to study from.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is set up so that you watch lectures at home and then come to class and ask questions and get extra information. He gives lots of useful handouts that you can take notes on and have during exams
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not teach the meaning behind the concepts, only walks through using the formulas. I eventually stopped going to class and just read the textbook and watched youtube videos to learn the material. He does have a nice course layout though. He dropped the lowest test, gave extra credit, and offered previous exams and homework answers.

Highly recommended not to take this professor. He loves to joke but I wished he had teaching skills instead of pun skills. He literally asks very very vague questions on exams which are ridiculous to even understand let alone solve them. His classes are super boring. He teaches 1+1 and asks about 1/0?

Cotter gives difficult exams but prepares you for them very well. His tests reflect the homework, and the homework reflects the lectures. If you take good notes and pay attention in class you are set. His homework comes with solutions and he is happy to help outside of class. He gives solutions to past exams so you have can prepare for the exams.

Professor Cotter is literally the best professor you can get, he is always trying to make sure everyone is on the same page and always makes himself available for help although his labs suck he's great! He will always make jokes while lecturing which is very delightful and he is great at spacing things out so you don't feel overloaded

Nice guy, cracks a lot of jokes... But I learn absolutely nothing in his lectures. He never gives any type of explanation of the simple, basic, necessary knowledges and goes into unnecessary tangents of deep proofs because I think he's bored of teaching the same material. Unfortunately, this does not make for a great experience for students.

Super outgoing and easy to talk to. His lectures are pretty boring and the notes are all on canvas. To be completely honest, watch Professor Leonard's statistics playlist on YouTube as it mirrors the class very closely and its a huge benefit. Tests are straightforward and mirror what he posts for examples but he will mix up things to trick you.

Cotter is overall a solid prof for the subject matter. This class is not extremely difficult while introducing you to the concepts for the first time. Overall I liked his teaching style and everything clicked. Also his dad jokes can sometimes be pretty funny
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives you all of the answers to the HW, and offers extra credit opportunities. However, his tests are difficult and most of the questions on the tests are difficult/different than the HW or lecture examples. He does drop the lowest 2 HWs and lowest exam. Biggest tip would be to look at his lecture notes and only study from his previous exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives LOTS of references (almost too many) and completed homework solutions with work for each homework (VERY helpful). Tests were harder than any prior material or references, but he drops the lowest of your 4 test scores (3 tests make up 75% of your grade). All in all not awful, but take a different prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A lot of people complained about his lectures but I think the lectures are a result the way the class is structured. They call it a "flipped classroom" so you're supposed to get the concepts from watching lecture videos before class and then class time is dedicated to working on examples. Overall a good professor if you can get past his jokes.

ECE 1250 is a tough class in general no matter who you take it from, mostly just a lot of lab work and the tests have only 3 or 4 questions. However, there are so many practice exams you will get a good grade on tests if you practice all of them! He passes out notes to help you and you can use them with exams.

Cotter may ramble occasionally when lecturing, but the lectures still give a great introduction. His homeworks are great for the starting EE or CE classes as they teach a lot, but are not impossibly difficult. (The solutions are posted!) The tests are  challenging, but always reasonable if you have done the homeworks.

Dr. Cotter is a really nice and funny guy but his lectures are confusing and doesn't explain things well and doesn't stop to check for understanding. As long as one person (always that really smart kid in the class) answers his questions he thinks the whole class is up to that understanding. He is available in office hours to help though.

Awesome professor. The homework helps for the Exams. (Almost) all of the HW solutions are available prior to the due date. 3 exams, during the final you can retake any or all of the exams. He allows notes for exams. Very generous grader.

Every class i have taken from him has made me hate the subject he is teaching. Took 1250 and 2240 from him and retook 2240 if i remember correctly. I urge you to stay away from him. Really smart guy and very nice, but unfortunately he cannot teach 3530 either. He makes things much more difficult than they need to be and his tests are very tough.

Dr. Cotter is a very fair teacher. I felt like his class was well balanced and if he taught more classes on my track I would definitely take another class from him. Very helpful and always willing to work with students who come to office hours. His tests are reasonable and he provides adequate material beforehand to study.

For sure the worst professor ever.  Took this class as a retake for better grade will definitely be avoiding him for the rest of my time in collage.  His classes consist of him doing problems wrong on the board then telling you to go home and figure it out and he will post the solution when he has time to go home and work through it.  Ridiculous!!!

If youre just starting CE or EE this class will get you pumped. All you do is get points for attending and learn about your future career and build some easy circuits. All these other reviews seem bad but that's because everyone except cotter teaches in this class. He did however spend an extra 1/2 hour of his time helping me with my power supply.

Probably the worst professor/teacher I have had. Assigns too much work for only 4 units and I do not think he realizes the workload he assigns. Rants the whole 1 hour and 50 minutes. His class has made my life much more stressful this semester.
Test's were open note. Pretty easy class in my opinion and Cotter is a pretty easy going guy. Very easy to talk to and get help.

The class, or seminar rather, is very relaxed.  Sometimes we build electric circuits and Mr. Cotter is willing to help students who struggle or have no experience in electric circuits.  He loves what he does and is always asking questions when guest speakers come and talk to the class about what they do and how students can get involved.

He basically just stands in front of the class and talks almost the entire class time. Homework is a whole lot of writing and a whole lot of reading. Make sure you pay attention or you will easily get lost.
Worst professor I've had. He expects to much for the units taken, doesn't know how to explain or help people with questions. Pretty sure there is something wrong about him
One of the worst professors I've ever had.

Not a good teacher. Had him for 1250 and 2240. Currently in 2240 and doing horrible. He does not stick to text book and basically does not teach you. All class he just does really complicated circuits when im sure half the class doesnt know whats going on. Nice guy and tries to help but he needs to work on teaching students who dont know everything
Dr Cotter enjoys working with students in his office and is more than willing to work around individual schedules to help out his students.

The average test scores on 3 out of 4 of his tests were 64% or below. He spends whole class periods working on one circuit and it's never anything like the circuits he gives on the tests. Teaches complex methods of performing simple circuit analysis rather then straight forward methods. Smart, but not good at teaching.
Honestly, he doesn't know how to interact with students but when he speaks; he speaks with some sense of humor...

Fairly good teacher.  Is always willing to help so just stop by his office or send him an email and he will respond quickly.  Nice thing is that he gives you the answers to homework problems so you can double check your work.  Tests are quite hard though.
Least helpful, worst teacher I have ever had to endure. Plays favorites. Rewards students, that do not work hard, for agreeing with him. All learning is done outside class.
REEEEEEEEALLLLLLLLLLLLLLYYYYYYYYYY?

Cotter is a good professor and he cares about the students doing well. I think he needs to work on focusing his lectures and not getting sidetracked as much. He is a talker. If you ever go to your office prepare to be there for a while it is hard to escape. Overall a good teacher but class and tests can be tough. Prepare to spend a lot of time.
Very bias to students.

class was literally useless. i dont think i walked away with any additional intellect after this semester. doesnt really teach. just talks. 'u know what i mean' is his catch-phrase. boring class. the atmosphere of the class atleast for me was comparable to a really comfortable bed. i acted accordingly.
Very bias. says "you know what i mean" all of the time. I dread this class. you have to participate and read, he will call on you.
Disorganized and Very Bias to Students. Easy to B.S. work in class.

Tends to disagree with students opinions different from his. ALWAYS goes off on a tangent which can literally take up the whole class time. He is extremely picky on how assignments are done. Tends to cancel class last minute (ex. 2 hrs BEFORE class) Do not take him. Try to get a different teacher if you can.

Its an engineering class and kinda tuff. Overall a good teacher, He knows his stuff. I do not understand all the harsh comments. The one thing i dont like about him is the tech. Comm. Awful class, but forced to take it. He is teaching an abstract subject to students who most likely haven't seen the material, which can be frustrating to both partys

Dr. Cotter is a pretty good teacher. Makes himself available for questions. Tests are extremely difficult and take a long time; class average was around 60. He does grade on a curve, which lifts everyone up at the end. Find the smart kids in class and form a study group with them; that's how I survived.
Not a bad teacher, good at keeping a boring subject interesting
BAD.... I am literally less intelligent because I attended this class

He is Hilarious. Me and my friends make fun of him. Boring class. But now is a much easier than the previous semester that I had him. Way less work and you can most of the time B.S. your work in class. Just do your work and attend class and participate you will be find
Ok teacher, Hartnell College
Great teacher, very clear with instructions. Lots of reading though, he encourages class discussions.
HE IS HARD HEADED. Cannot convince the guy!!! Boring and unclear. Failed the class cause i did not attend but if you do your part: assignments, read, etc. you will pass the class like nothing
By far, the worst instructor I've ever had.  I learned nothing in his class.  Avoid at all costs.

Unclear, Unhelpful, Way Bias(left), unsupportive of individual thoughts/opinions, discussions or debates occur mostly between students and Juan (as opposed to the entire class or other students), class goes way off topic really quickly and discussions tend to become pointless.  Juan talks A LOT about his own views opinions.
This man should not be teaching at all. Avoid this class as much as possible.

Poor instructor. Spends less time explaining concepts than he does making jokes and offering shortcuts. Tries to offer insight into problems by using graphical methods that are more confusing than helpful. I learned just about everything on my own from the text. Exams are intentionally too long and difficult...don't expect to finish them.

Quality very low, cancelled two sessions one day prior to class. Repeatedly ends sessions early out of laziness. Condescending to students, disrespectful of opinions, disruptive to the flow of class, can't keep his head together to maintain structure. Prof. Oliverez, perhaps a Jr. High School level Civics would better fit your unprofessionalism.

Horrible teacher. Not flexible at all unless it benefits him. Grading is EXTREMELY bias. If your point of view differs from his, you are automatically wrong. Not clear on instructions at all. DO NOT take unless you have to!
This professor is the worst ever!
No Comments
No Comments
SUCKS
One would almost suspect that he is trying to do a terrible job - can anyone teach this poorly without trying?
No Comments

Really? HAHAHA! Thats all I could do is laugh. This professor is ridicoulous! Our sylibi wasn't ready until 3 1/2 weeks into the course, he expected us to catch up. Not very fair in organizing what he expected us to do. NEVER organized. I appriciate his opinions and his cultural identity and what he brings to the table. I could see how other students consider him ****, but I only see him as looking through his identity and implementing that on his students. He's a nice guy!
This class was the biggest waste of time and I learned nothing but still got an A in the class. The class satisfied two ULR's but it was such a waste of time. He is soooo boring. Never shuts up.
arriva zapata putos
He's more concerned with his stupid games and computer programming projects then teaching stats.
The project has nothing to do with the class.  In fact it is a pile of crap.

He is not helpful at all. He doesn't allow other people to give there opinions and if they do they are wrong. The assignments are easy but it takes forever for him to explain what he wants from it. You cannot contact him and he is unorganized.

He's a nice teacher, but sometimes he lectures too much of his own opinions, which is okay to learn from but he does not give a chance to listen to students output. If you like politics and sitting for 2 hrs of lecturing then this is the class.
This is the worst class!!! It is so boring, but it is super easy if you understand the assignments. He is not clear or helpful with assignments, I dread going everyday!
No Comments
Its the course content thats controversial
funny and sarcastic

Class was 3600, not 2600. Branden is great! He knows what he's doing and is able to explain things very clearly. The only bad part of this class is that I think we didn't get as far as he wanted because he kept having to stop and re-explain things or help individuals with specific issues. He never got upset about it, though. Great professor.
Super helpful when learning, takes the time to explain everything thoroughly as much as needed.

Although I got off to an unsteady start in his class, Branden was an incredible help, he's incredibly knowledgeable and actively works within the field. He is one of the few professors in the program I would say is an expert in Zbrush and Maya. He moves quickly, but with purpose, communicate, and you'll do well.

I learned nothing from this course. The stuff that was taught pertained to nothing with animation most times. With the quizzes, he would take quotes directly from the many videos provided, but then change but the answer slightly with a few different variations. The test was just questions from the quiz and if you didn't take notes, you would fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're thinking about taking this for a credit, DO NOT. It's so poorly structed (I don't think he's updated the curriculum since covid) and the final is impossible. There's so little to get graded on that if you don't get 100% on every quiz, you're not getting an A. Doesn't offer extra credit. I'd say more if there wasn't a character limit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While I did really enjoy this class... It was ROUGH. Definitely *thee* most time consuming online class I've ever taken in my life. I've always done super well in online classes but this one was so lecture/time consuming it was difficult. Make sure you take notes and genuinely watch the videos provided.

Would be a better class if I would have taken it in person. It is very repetitive when it is an online course because of the amount of small clips you have to watch. There is usually around 20 clips a week with multiple questions to answer with weekly quizzes. He is cool and gives great feedback but better to take it in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not too bad. Better than some. Randomized test questions from a large bank, final exam draws from questions across the semester, so take notes from EVERY quiz, as well as the lectures. Not a lot of active learning, but I enjoyed the content. Pretty easy if you can look past 1-2 oddly worded quiz Q's and devote 2-4 hours a week to lectures. 6.5/10.

Chill class, takes a very long time to get through the lectures (typically 3-6 hours for me), and you take one quiz every week based on that lecture. Have to take very in depth notes as literally anything could be on the quizzes, and bc the only thing you're graded on is a weekly quiz and tests, bombing one quiz can cost you your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor almost seems hesitant to give his own knowledge to students, solely providing curated video playlists made by other people with some vague questions about minute details in each video. With the passive aggressive communication to literally zero instructional value, I could've got the same education with 10 hours of YouTube.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Poorly written questions.

This was an easy and interesting class. Each week you have a list of videos to watch with questions for each. He provides the timestamp for the answers. Be sure you answer those questions and save them because they'll be the answers for your weekly quiz and your final. Be sure to use your 2 attempts on your quizzes and also write those answers.

Fine class, I prefer this method of online classes to be honest. It's on a weekly basis so as long as you take the quiz by the end of the week, you don't have to stress too hard. Just take notes on the questions of the videos and you'll be fine and might learn some cool things if you're interested.

It was an overall okay class, it was more just a "remember this obscure moment in this part of the film" than anything else. Its not a hard class whatsoever and he seems like a good professor but the curriculum needs to updating

This professor hasn't updated the course since COVID-19, The professor is obviously knowledgeable, but it feels like he doesn't want to teach which can make him feel rather pretentious the few times you actually see him. The class is asynchronous so beware. Your entire grade is determined through weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Average online class; it was generally a little boring and tedious. Every few weeks we would talk about a film I enjoy and those parts of the class were fun.
