Craig is really passionate about what he does and it shows through his lectures. The entire class is comprised out of videos about the film industry. As long as you take good notes, you'll do fine in the class. Quizzes are open note.

Honestly, terrible professor. Grade based on cumulative small clips you view and remembering pointless details about " what gesture did the wave make in the movie Moana?". I received a C+ because the final was composed of answers that were 2 seconds of a 1 hour-long clip. Not to mention he flags every Quizlet so good luck!

The class easy if you take good notes from lectures. I would say though that sometimes it was too much and it was very tiring. Take this class if you can keep up with the week notes which help a lot for the final exam.

Each week two classes are posted, each have about 15 videos that you need to take notes on and those notes can then be used on that week's quiz. Interesting material and fun class, but make sure that you watch all of the videos and take thorough notes! The professor is very accommodating and is open to feedback and concerns!

Each class consists of around 30 short videos taken from youtube + quizzes graded on random information from the clips, testing less your understanding of concepts and more "can you remember the joke Brad Bird made in this interview." The professor's commentary on the clips is surface-level or actively unhelpful. Not hard, but you won't learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All online class with lectures being a mix of few readings and short-curated videos that explain concepts with questions to answer afterwards. Very straightforward and interesting course. Responds to questions and messages.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This professor has got to be one of the laziest. Everything is done online and he doesn't even do his own lectures. He finds videos for you to watch and then gives you regular quizzes that are graded by a machine. He leaves you no feedback nor does he take any concern or care for individual students.
I learned a lot. Also not boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall, a really easy class as long as you go through each week's material and take notes. There is a lot of information to go through so don't fall behind. Lectures were very intriguing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is completely online and you will never have any interaction with the professor, although he seems nice through his weekly reminder emails. This class consists of watching around 20-30 short clips each week and taking notes then taking a quiz each Sunday. Not exactly hard work, but does get boring and a little annoying after a while.

Great class and professor. It's very easy to pass you just view the material every week and answer a quiz at the end. Most of the material is in video form and it was genuinely interesting 90% of the time. The class is all online so there wasn't a ton of interaction but the professor was always available if help was needed.
Film 1600 was an easy A class. There are weekly quizzes and a final test, the test is based on the questions from each weeks quiz! Take notes on all of the lectures and you will pass!
Great lectures but the quizzes are 70% questions that are unrelated and niche aspects of lectures. Quizzes feel like they aren't checking intelligence but how much busy work you can do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I thought this class was very simple! The course mostly relied on videos and readings. At the end of the week, there was a quiz relying on those videos and readings. However, I would have liked there to be more of an emphasis on critical thinking. Many of the quizzes relied on specific information. Overall though, I enjoyed the class!

A very easy fine arts general ed to take. Your grade is entirely based on quizzes and the final. It was quite time-consuming to watch the lectures each week and then take the quiz (took me 3-4 hours a week). The quiz questions are very specific from the lectures. As long as you make time for this class and take good notes, you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This wasn't the easy peasy class that I was led to believe it is, but not too bad. There were a lot of lectures to watch but they could be watched at any time, so you could get weeks ahead in class.

Overall, he was a good professor. There was a ton of lecture work and the lectures had you answer questions about a video you watch, I wish he would have been more straight forward so I knew the answers before the quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Caldwell's class was overall very good. very material heavy. there were a lot of information, but if you watch the lectures, a lot of the questions on the quizzes and tests are very easy. There are two tests, midterm and a final. Unfortunately, there are no extra credit options but if you study and watch the lectures every week it's pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's straightforward, there's a quiz every week with a final at the end of the semester. The lectures are just a bunch of videos, and they're actually entertaining. I enjoyed watching the videos, but the quizzes are a little difficult. The questions are vague, but the final questions are the quiz questions, so take good notes on the answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Online course, material is inspirational & fun. Communication is somewhat passive aggressive when he was warned that not all the weekly quiz questions correlate with his questions under each video. BEWARE! Watch the majority of the clips, because even if he says to skip around, that material DOES show up on the quiz. Easy A if you do your work!

The class, while pretty easy and overall enjoyable, I don't feel it's presented in a way that will help you to absorb and learn the course material. Weekly quizzes will often consist of specific details from the course content with you focusing more on finding the answers to these questions rather than understanding core concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class has a lot to go into it during each module. There are like 6 components to each week, so it's a pretty time consuming class. He is very strict on his due dates, and that is a really easy way to get behind. Also, take each quiz twice and get really familiar with those: that's all the final is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In film 1600 all the lectures are pre-recorded and the grade is based entirely off weekly quizzes and a final exam. It takes a lot of time but isn't hard work. No critical thinking involved and you don't learn that much because the quizzes and final all focus on super specific/random facts. Wouldn't recommend this class.

Easiest class I've taken since middle school. It's like watching YouTube but for credit. You basically watch behind the scenes videos from Blu Rays and take open book quizzes that you can take again if you mess up!

I took this class as a gen ed and found it very fascinating! I'm not majoring in anything related to Animation, but as someone who loves film and television this was a really interesting class. You will have lessons each week (all videos) that take a few hours, and one 15 question quiz due every Sunday.

As an online class, it is sort of a YouTube class. There are readings but mostly short videos of animations, lectures, how animation is made. There are quizzes every week, which was a pain at first but kept me from falling behind. No midterm, and the final is open notes. Well organized. There are questions with the videos that cover most quizzes.

It was not what I expected. You don't watch movies; you learn more about the people who make them and often watch them making the animation. Got to view the lectures but the professor provides the questions that are used in the quizzes. If you have to take a Gen Ed I would recommend it.

You will see lots of animations with the animators explaining how they did it. I learned a lot. Not hard, but had to stay on top of it every week. The organization made it straight forward. My roommate had Rock & Roll but often she would be looking over my shoulder. There was much I hadn't seen before. Definitely check it out.
The class is well organized and the clips are are interesting. Quizzes are due every week but allowed to work ahead. I learned a lot about how animation works.
Being organized and going through the material, it is straight forward to get an A. Well actually an A-. He lets you take all the quizzes twice which helps.

This is a great option for a GenEd Fine Arts credit. The course is very well organized and structured. There's no homework, but every week a quiz is due based on videos and a weekly reading. It's fairly easy to get through and quite interesting.

I took the online Animation class and loved it. It is a perfect easy elective. Weekly quizzes based on short video clips. I knew nothing on the subject, but it was very interesting. I was able to work ahead and finished the whole class a month early.

Everything in the class material is supplemented with fantastic examples of the principles in animation that are needing to be covered. The fact that the material is updated every semester by him shows how much he cares, and how knowledgeable he is on the subject matter. The quizzes are sometimes oddly specific, but otherwise great.

Real easy class with a small workload. You do learn a lot from the "lectures", a few short videos about different things. Quizzes each week that are open material, which make them very easy. No other assignments. Final is based on every quiz and is open material. Very easy class, some questions I couldn't find the answer to, but easy A.

I was able to finish the class 4 weeks before the end of the semester. The class is primarily short clips of animation and the creators talking about how they did it. Each week is a different focus. Learned alot. The professor has inserts as he makes points. It is great that he actually worked in the industry and you get those insights .

His storyboarding class was the best class I've taken so far. The work load is quite a lot, with a 50-60 image length storyboard and pitch being due every other week. But the class is so much fun and he gives great feedback both in person and when he grades your assignments. Couldn't recommend him higher!

Learned alot. The class is straightforward. Video clips of professionals, questions and quizzes and final based on those questions. You can get an A if you just go through the material. I dreaded having to take another fine arts general education course but this one was good.

I took the online version of the course. Grades are quizzes and final based on quizzes. The professor uses extensive movie/animation clips combined with specific written reference to clips. The weekly quizzes come directly from the online material. Each week is structured the same with something new about how animation is created. Straight forward.

This was a hybrid course, and honestly you could never go to class and get an 100%. The lectures just cover what he puts on his website (he is passionate, but the material can be a bit boring), and the only stuff that gets graded are the quizzes and the final exam, which are all online and open note. Super easy Gen Ed.
This man loves animation and his passion for it is contagious. Really easy going but he rambles a lot. Classes are easy.

1/2 of class is online. Most of class is watching film clips and listening to the teacher explain techniques of animation. Like comment above,test Q's are hard to study 4 even with an "open notes" policy. Although if you study well you should be able to do good. Pretty much have to print off everything you can and know where everything is at or...

This was a hybrid class so much of the things were online. There wasn't a textbook to the class and all he did was show us clips from dvd extras of movies. I learned a little bit about animation, but at first it was really boring. Honestly I wish I would have taken a different class for a fine art credit unless you are a movie buff.
LOVED HIM, such a great professor, I had so much fun and learnt so much from his class, and he is easy on the eyes as well, ( no disrespect) but was a pleasure learning from him.

His lectures were fun and concise. Since this is a hybrid class, half of the work is online. His online class was organized for the most part and his tests were open note and relatively easy. I recommend this class for someone who wants to get their fine arts credit.
Do not take any course with this professor. She does not give good grades and her instructions and grading policies are beyond unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take any course with this professor. She will give assignments with little instructions and no rubric. She will NEVER give 100% even if you did everything right based on the limited instructions. She is an unfair grader and it truly feels like she wants you to fail in her class. I truly have never had a worse professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is very lecture heavy and the only grades that go into the gradebook are 4 papers. When Professor Crumley lectures, she reads straight from a paper. You have to read articles for homework and some of them are very long - up to 70 pages. She is flexible with deadlines and will give feedback on papers before submitting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Crumley is super educational and fun to be around. Her class consisted of powerpoints but she would go very into depth about her topics. Her class is participation heavy as she will ask us questions then have us discuss our answers. Very few assignments but they were easy and had clear expectations. Would rake a class of hers again.

I actually did not take PSY 3140 from professor Creem-Regehr but her lecture videos were the ones that were listed for this course and I loved her. She was very clear, calm, and engaging. I really loved this class and would take it again if I could. If you do not enjoy neuropsych, it may be difficult but I thought it was interesting and challenging

Sensation and perception is one of the most interesting courses and Dr. Creem-Regehr's lectures are very thorough. I really enjoyed this class and think that she was a great professor to take it with.

I liked Dr. Creem-Regehr. I will say she is a little bit of a serious woman, but she is a very credible researcher at the U and I'm sure she's busy doing important work. Overall this course was somewhat challenging but her lectures are thorough and she is very qualified! I respect her!

I took this summer taught by someone else but with all of this prof's materials. Complicated concepts were explained in a way that was straightforward and easy to understand. The lectures were interesting too. The exams were honestly pretty easy if you take good notes. 10/10

Professor teaches great & can explain concepts clear in her lectures however I just ended up not liking the class. I expected more & quickly found myself uninterested. Exams are 7.5/10 on difficultly levelnot at all like practice quizzes we have each week so studying is a must! Exams are worth 72% of your overall grade (drops your lowest).
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and even better class. She was an awesome instructor to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is one of my favorite professors ever. She is very knowledgeable and a fantastic teacher. She explains very difficult and technical topics in ways that are easy to understand, and that I probably wouldn't have understood from another professor. She gives great feedback, study guides, and really sets you up to succeed. Amazing class & professor.

Good course. Professor highly knowledgeable. Her lectures are informative. Tests difficult, study up before taking. She does reviews, but they are led by student questions, which only helps with confusing points, not with a sense of what to study for. Study for everything, is my advice.

This was my favorite course so far, and I'm in my third year! The professor is so knowledgeable, and the content is very clear. If you know the study guide answers, you'll do great on the exams. No reading, it's just video lectures that are 10-20 minutes long, and interesting!! HW is just 1/2 page paper per week on the lectures. I learned so much!

Very interesting class! Make sure you show up to class every time, review the weekly questions (optional), go over notes, and attend review sessions to do well on exams. Sarah tests heavily on comprehension, so you have some writing to do for tests, but they're not too tough. Her voice made me sleepy, but she was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sarah is a good professor and she had interesting lectures. I enjoyed her class a lot! The class had a lot of material and I wouldn't consider it "easy", but before each test she had an option review session which made the tests pretty simple. I'm not a good student and I got an A.
Such a great class!

She is easily the WORST professor I have had at the U. In the online course she just posts the recorded lectures from her "in class" sections. You listen to a 2 hr lecture for what ends up being about 20 minutes of actual useful information, the rest is her saying "um", and people asking questions... which you can't hear... WORST CLASS EVER.

She records the lectures and is very easy to follow and understand.  You do not need this textbook.  There are ten very easy mini-assignments and if you do the study guides you will do well on the tests.  Her tests are not multiple choice, they are comprehensive but if you review they are pretty easy.

If you attend/watch the lectures and complete the review questions, you'll do fine on the tests and in the class. Weekly 1/2 page papers due and 4 tests throughout the semester. I would recommend taking this class from Professor CR.

Very interesting class. Didn't really need to come to class because she recorded the sessions for the online class, which we got access to anyway. The tests are hard, but not impossible. The lectures have everything you need. The book isn't needed. She's a great teacher. :)

One of the hardest classes I have ever taken in Psychology.  She knows her stuff!  Be prepared for brilliance and difficult tests.  Se does not test memorization, she tests for comprehension.  She's very approachable and amazing at what she does.
great prof who really helped alot in this class. asks good questions and usually prepared for class

Attendence optional, she provides you with the complete lecture notes, and hands out review sheets before each exam. The problem is that the exams are extremely difficult, requiring you to know your stuff backwards and forwards (not just the answers to the questions on the review sheet).

Do not take Ms. Crawford for math 1090. She grades extremely tough and only relies on online lectures that aren't even taught by her. When you get back to class you barely practice the work. You have to use YouTube to teach yourself. If you have her, drop the class and switch to another teacher.

Ms. Crawford may of been the worst teacher I have ever had in my whole life. She, as a person, is not the problem, but rather her way of teaching. Her method of teaching was horrendous; the lectures were speed runs of copying the notes key to the white board. In this class, there were countless times where students had to make multiple corrections.

Extremely hard to follow her "lectures" and when she did try to teach, more than half the time she was corrected by students. In a whole semester of this class I learned more watching YouTube videos. She is also very hard to get in contact with and will not be responsive to emails. Lastly she often talked and responded in a condescending manner.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS! In all my years of school, I have never had a worse "teacher" then her. You are better off never coming to class and learning all the concepts on YouTube. She once had the problem 2030-2009 and had to use a calculator to solve it. Then said "Oops, I am not great at adding or subtracting". You will regret ever taken her class.

The lectures were awful in this class. She was very hard to follow and never really knows what she is talking about. She takes all the problems out of the book and it is easier to just teach yourself outside of class. I would not take this professor again.
I would give her a zero star if that was possible. She only follows the textbook number by number and I'm convinced she doesn't know how to do the math. Lectures also make no sense.

Lectures in this class were pointless. You are better off spending class time teaching it yourself than going to her class. She never comes prepared, often looks at phone and notes, and gets no where in lectures. She struggles to teach at a good pace, she struggles with concepts and you leave class finishing one problem which she stubbles over.

Her lectures were very confusing and hard to follow, even if you understand the material. You have a quiz most days of the week, and she luckily dropped the three lowest quizes. She was always friendly, but not the best at explaining. Her calender was also never updated which made it hard to see what assignments were due when.
Awful lectures.

She teaches way too fast, does not teach the material well or clearly at all, and will assign extra homework last minute. And me and other students got all of the answers right on the recent quiz, and she gave us awful scores.
Does not explain half the material. Moves on when no one in the class has any understanding of the concepts she is teaching.
I felt that there was a lack of actually teaching. Myself as well as others thought that she was more just talking as well as making things much harder than they needed to be.

This professor was terrible. Did not teach a single lesson without checking her phone for the answers. The most basic concepts were taught in a way which made them impossible to learn efficiently. I had a hard time showing up to class after the first couple of weeks because watching youtube would be far more effective. Do not take this professor.

Professor Rudds is great. This is a higher class so she won't tolerate minimal effort but respects passion. We decided our due dates as a class for our papers and extra credit is offered. The topic for the seminar is decided by her and can change. Grading is a bit difficult and attending the seminar is the best way to get info on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super interesting lectures, expands on a genre I didn't know had so much literature on. Exposed to great media during the class, wonderful teacher who really cares about you grasping the material. Lowkey played Wizard 101 during some lectures, but I never missed a beat and the themes covered were great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have one strong regret about taking a class from Professor Rudds, and that is that its my final semester and I didnt get the chance to take another one. She is the best!
Professor Rudds is great. Well organized and passionate about what she's teaching. Kind of a hardass when it comes to feedback but a forgiving grader, which is a great combo in my book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A good professor makes students want to learn more about their field, which this class did for me, now I want to learn more about data analysis. Prof. Curry is helpful and will go out of her way to help if you ask for it. Grading was clear, and you can submit the final in parts before due date (and she will give you feedback! I got 100% on mine.)

Very good at making complex and abstract material accessible and understandable, her expectations for assignments are always clear and consistent with how they're graded, and she's very approachable and reasonable about troubleshooting with the coding software and other issues a student may run up against.

Dr. Curry is truly invested in her students. She is especially good at helping you troubleshoot problems with the RStudio coding software. In everything, she is down to earth, approachable, and the kind of professor you'd want your friends or siblings to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Curry was very caring and kind. She gives lots of chances to get a better grade and will work with you to succeed in the class. She's a pretty lenient grader and as long as you try in the class you will pass. Lectures can be boring and attendance is mandatory to pass. I found her to be a very delightful professor.
She is a tough grader. Sometime, she can be very nice, sometime, she can be very mean. I am kind of hard to reach her mind.

She is a strict grader and an uninteresting teacher. She is very by-the-book, which I suppose is due to the subject matter, political analysis. The actual subject matter is useful, but she doesn't make it terribly exciting. Interesting subject, but poor teacher.

Prof Curry is a very good teacher. She does assign extensive amounts of reading, which is repetitive and annoying . However, she is a good communicator and all of the things that she goes over in class is really understandable. She is a harsh grader so make sure you understand what it is she is looking for to grade.

ENGL 3850! Dr. Culver was my favorite professor this semester. He was engaging, kind, and very intelligent. Prepare to do readings bi-weekly and 5 papers (3 are at least 3 pgs and 2 are at least 5 pgs). No exams or any quizzes, but you must participate in the in-class discussions. Overall, the class was fun and inspired a love for reading.

A 2-3 page paper everyother week, didn't use canvas so you had no way to access your grade, graded the papers but said they were "estimations" that would change based on the final essay, chose a lot of abolitionist literature for class but also used the n word. Wants his essays printed. Knowledgeable but proceed w/caution. Wasn't a good fit for me.

I had to read 10 books for this class. They were hard to read and boring. Culver however, is very passionate and tries to make the class as interesting as he can. There were no activities, just him giving lectures. There were 5 response papers and he grades them in depth. Wouldn't recommend the class but Culver is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really liked the way he presented material on the rare occasions he lectured (most of the class was discussion). He has a fantastic speaking voice and is really fun to listen to. On papers, he gave the best grades for creativity. Don't be afraid to have an original take on assignment--within reason.

Culver is extremely intelligent, but also very approachable. He wants you to do well on your writing assignments and is willing to take time with you outside of class (or via email) to do this. He holds really interesting discussions and is always very respectful. I would definitely take another class from him.

Interesting lecturer but it felt more like a writing class than a business class. read a billion novels, wrote 4 papers which are very. harshly. graded., 2 exams on the novels w q's he mentioned once during the semester, and thats it. if u show up to every class and listenwrite down Everything He Says + read a novel a week then take it.

There is a good amount of reading you have to do and you have to be on top of it or you will start to fall behind.  Luckily he doesn't grade that tough and provides really good criticism.  Also if you go to class every time you will be ready for the tests for sure.

Excellent. Facilitates great discussion. Lectures are interesting, on-topic, very insightful. My writing became better and more clear because of this professor. Because of his class, I was able to read the Epic of Gilgamesh and love it. Couldn't have done that on my own.

Honestly one of the best, if not the best, professor I have ever had. Makes the subject matter both interesting and understandable. He is also very interesting in improving the papers you turn in, so when you get it back you can become a much better writer. Take as many classes from him as you can.

Culver is the best. I am going to wait and take another IT course from him next year. It was so easy. There is a lot of reading, but you can get by just skimming and taking decent notes on what he talks about. Four 2-3 page papers, four one page quizzes, NO FINAL, participation and attendance factor into grade. I felt enlightened after his course.

Explained critical theory well and thoroughly and was actually a lot more fun than I thought it would be. Readings are hard, but they're hard with everyone in 3600. Actively participating and asking questions really helps in understanding. He's willing to work with students' schedules for papers and tests.
Professor is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about his topic.  He is very invested in helping the students succeed.

This guy is so awesome. The texts for this class are kind of boring, but you can't escape that no matter who you take IT from. However, I was legitimately excited to go to class everyday because he makes it so interesting.

He is Epic. He really knows how to teach, and he makes every book comprehensible. He can make a typically boring class a lot more enjoyable and interesting. He helped me enjoy english and enjoy my experience at the University of Utah. He completely knows what he is doing like he is a natural. He can also relate his experiences into the class. Great
Really good professor, especially when compared to the other Honors IT course teachers.

Some classmates and I were talking about how great this guy is the other day. The reading is nightmarish, but he makes it comprehensible. He's intelligent, funny, and genuine. Probably the best professor in the English Department. Go for it if you're up for a challenge!

He is one of the most intelligent professors I have had at the University. He is easy to approach and offers excellent lecture on the rather difficult material we are covering. He takes roll daily and communicates back very well on essays.

He’s really approachable and really wants his students to have a firm understanding of the material covered in class.  My class was structured into seven-eight different topics and there was a short 1-3 page essay on each.  He’s fair on grading.  Not only does he grade his student’s analysis but also their grammar.

Culver is very bright and also extremely approachable...One of few professors that actually encourages students stopping by if confused about materials covered in class. Be sure to stay on top of the reading before lecture, there  is LOTS of reading. But to be expected in an Honors IT class. Also close textual reading is a must to understand text
Very dry, texts are so so, doesn't take attendance, and only a few papers.

He's really knowledgeable about what he's teaching, you can tell he's genuinely interested in his subject. Lots of reading but it was alright. Fair on essays, flexible with due dates and works with you. Good class :)

Curry was an amazing professor who broke down concepts very easily. His lectures were both entertaining and informative, and it wasn't a hard class either. Highly recommend this class and this professor.

great prof, and engaging lectures. he is super funny and cares about engaging with the audience. My class was big, roughly 350 people but the lectures always felt personal. Great guy, and a former lobbyist and knows what he is talking about!
Great professor, never afraid to ask questions or get help. Always was happy to attend his class.

I LOVE this guy. He is the best and really chill and funny and cancels class a fair amount. He only does one chapter, chapter quiz, and two lectures a week. There are two exams (open note all answers on quizlet) and two writing papers which he clearly outlines and basically provides everything for you. he is the BEST!

Good lecturer. You will rarely interface with Prof. Curry as anything to do with grading is through your TA. You can get by with doing reading quizzes with readings open and CTRL+F ing the page. Papers can be annoying but if you are passionate about the topic of choice it's easy. Its hard to get below a B in my opinion.

I'm not super interested in government, but overall I enjoyed the class! Professor Curry is very knowledgeable about the subject, and he was good at explaining concepts. He would incorporate polls in his lectures as a way of engaging the class and having people share their opinions. He's also pretty funny and knows how to relate to students.

An amazing person + lecturer, he really knows his stuff and is passionate. Loved this class but I'm biased- lots of reading and quizzes outside of class but it's doable, besides that just 2 papers & 2 exams. Explains things in a really good way, and talks about things like a human, he's funny. Enjoyed this class and hope to take more with him!

Hes a funny teacher. He knows his stuff. The class is boring a lot of the times, but what can you expect from an entry level politics class. 2 major writing assignments that are pretty easy. There are reading quizzes every week that make up a large chunk of the grade. just dont forget to do those, show up to class and youll get an easy A.

Pro. Curry was great and his class was easy. The topic is boring but hey what can you do its American Government. But if you are into that then his class is amazing. Lots of reading so be ready and there are 15 question quizzes on the reading every week.
love this guy, funny and super easy but lots of lectures and textbooks

Deeply knowledgeable about what he teaches. Lots of nuance and data-driven material. Prepares really thorough lectures and is extremely clear when speaking. Reserves ample time for questions and answers them comprehensively. He has an attendance grade but I don't think he's very strict on it. I learned a lot in his class. Very funny DRY humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Curry is a nice and funny guy who genuinely loves teaching. The workload wasn't bad and he hardly took attendance. The only complaint I have is that he is a shockingly tough grader (I would give 4.5 stars if I could), especially compared to other POLS professors I've had. I eeked out an A in the end, but it took a lot of effort and a curve.

Curry is very knowledgeable and passionate about his classes. Given his research interests are on Congress, he has a lot to say and he does it in through well-tailored lectures. Class consisted of lectures, semester-long group project that's not too hard if you get a good group together. He's a critical grader, so don't expect an easy A.

Prof Curry is overall a great professor who understands the topic he teaches. If you like the subject the lectures are fairly entertaining and funny. If you don't, then you could find some of them pretty boring. Quizzes and tests are fairly easy overall, and the two essays have very clear and specific guidelines that make them fairly easy.

Lectures are boring, but the class is easy if you are taking it for a Gen Ed. All quizzes and exams are online through canvas. Clicker questions to get credit for participation and then two research essays. The essays are great, he gives very clear outlines and resources for what he wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Curry is very good at lectures, but they are super boring. Go to class for the participation points. There are huge reading assignments weekly, and you should read it if you want to do well on the test. There are only two writing assignments. Overall I didn't enjoy this class very much, and would not re-take.
Loved Professor Curry! He is passionate and makes this class interesting. He is funny, too! He provides clear grading criteria and there are only two tests- a midterm and final. Would take again!
Excellent instructor. Curry lays out very clear grading criteria in the syllabus and provides great study guides for each test. His lectures are interactive, informative, and even humorous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took this class for the AI requirement. Curry's humor made the lectures better. Take good notes and the tests shouldn't be too hard. Weekly reading and quizzes

Show up and you'll get a B, apply yourself and get an A. Textbooks not needed and test material is found in the lecture slides he posts online. Curry is a funny guy and his lectures are engaging as long as you are engaged. Uses a polling tool in class to take attendance. Either show up or get the access code of the day from a friend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Curry was great, he had amazing lectures. You basically just needed to listen in class to do well. I took AP GOV. in high school so I was basically relearning the material. You had to purchase textbooks for the class but I never opened a page of the readings. 2 easy papers and 2 exams both online. I had a C in participation and got a A-.

I'm not a political science major and this was super boring to me, I had to try really hard to get an A not because it was hard but because this was my last general credit course and I was so done with them.
Really great and interesting lectures. Don't have to read in the class to pass.
Has a way to take attendance, so it matters and will count against you if you miss. Lectures a ton. Pretty boring
Everything is multiple choice and only two papers the entire semester.

Being a stem major, I didn't pay much attention in this class. Not that I don't care for national gov, but he is a boring lecturer. If you show up to class to get clicker points, do the weekly online quizzes, do two fairly easy 3 pg min writing assignments, and take midterm and final online, this class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took this class for the AI requirement and don't regret that choice. He's a great prof, lectures can be a little boring if you're not interested in the subject matter. LOTS of reading, but the tests/quizzes are all done online so they're open-book which is super nice. There are also two papers you'll write, but easy enough if you put in the effort.

Curry is the best professor at the U.  Take every class you can from him.  He is fair in his grading and understands that students have a life outside of school.  I took three classes from him and want to take more.

Professor Curry is an engaging, personable, and intelligent instructor. He's really chill and facilitated discussion really well. He obviously knows a lot about what he teaches and he really cares about his students. I would definitely recommend his classes to anyone interested in politics.
Tests are a little hard. Get ready to scramble.

Let me tell you something about James CURRY, this guy is spicy. He brought the heat to nearly every single class I went to. I can only count on my hands the amount of times he didn't bring the heat. Curry gets fired up for politics. Tests were not as hot but more of a simmering heat . If you can get spicy for politics take this class.
He is a very smart professor and you can tell that he has a passion for congress and the presidency.
Able to make learning about the American Presidency the best class you have ever taken. Lets you bring a full page of notes for midterm and final and provides you with a blue book

Great professor. Very passionate about the topic. Very helpful when you ask. Makes jokes about current politics. Took a whole semester from him and I still cannot tell what his partisanship is. Let's you have a sheet of notes for the tests.

David Curtis was a good professor. His lectures were informative, but sometimes boring and lacking feeling. However, he got the job done and I felt that I learned the material fairly well. Overall, a good teacher and I would take him again.

His lectures weren't super exciting, but I didn't hate the class. The class was pretty easy. 80% of the class is common-sense & basic biology. All the quizzes and tests are based on the lectures, so I didn't find reading the textbook helpful. I did do some studying before the tests and his study guides were helpful. He's nice and caring.
Very straightforward class. As long as you attend lectures and pay attention you will be fine. His expectations are clear and the class is easy to manage.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis's classes are fairly easy as long as you go as he will sometimes spring assignments that can only be done in class. Material is kind of boring, but it can be interesting. Tests are incredibly easy. Overall, I'd consider this class an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While attendance isn't mandatory, going to class makes a huge difference in how you do on tests. This class is definitely easy but is also very easy to get behind in. Curtis is easy to reach outside of class and is willing to work with you when life gets crazy. Great introduction course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis is amazing! He has 3 exams that aren't cumulative and a few homework assignments that are not very difficult. There are pop quizzes, but they are REALLY easy if you listen to his lectures. A lot of the quiz questions were based on participation. He also offers a couple extra credit opportunities which really boost your grade.

Professor Curtis was amazing. His class was very easy as long as you do the readings, fill out the study guide, and pay attention in class. He is very kind and willing to work with you and the topics are interesting. 3 non-cumulative tests and very few assignments. 10/10, loved this class

I really enjoy Proffessor Curtis. There are few homework assignments and are on interesting topics and easy to do well. There are three exams over the course of the semester and none are cumulative! There are also bonus questions which help you earn a better grade! He is a very nice teacher and his lectures are very easy to follow.

Success in this class relies on the readings. Professor Curtis is very knowledgeable about the course content and he makes lectures exciting and easy to follow. Your grade depends heavily on the quizzes and exams in this class, but there are opportunities for extra credit. Professor Curtis was easy to contact and was always flexible and adaptive!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, definetly recommend this class. Easy A, show up, do your homework, prepare for pop quizzes. Only has 2 exams, one midterm and final which are very easy. I'd take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy if you do the homework (txtbk/news/journal article. Journals can be long, but the reading is usually short.) You will learn the material. Don't sweat the pop quizzes if you do hw. Every Friday you read one or two relevant articles and write a post about them. Those take some effort, but it's not bad. Do the homework and participate in class.
Would not recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was easy and also very interesting. There aren't many assignments, reading the textbook is important, and he does do pop quizzes. He is a great professor that wants students to succeed and is available outside of class. Extra credit was offered and as long as you attended classes and do the readings the exams are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Jennifer is a very smart and nice professor, but this class was pretty disorganized and pointless at times. The readings can be tedious and you can get cold called in class, but the material was just not interesting enough for me to be truly engaged. It felt like common sense at times. Overall an easy A. Exams are common sense+light studying

Dr. Cummings is the best professor at the U. Dr. Cummings cares about her students, lets everyone have a voice, and gives amazing lectures that make you think a lot about how you communicate and approach conflict in your personal life. Out of all the classes I have taken at the U, this one is by far the most interesting and worth taking.

She as a professor is great, definitely knows her material and is very smart. However, the way she runs her classroom is a waste of time. I took MGT 4860, and people in class use it as a time to complain about their lives. 75% of the class is people whining about their boring lives and she encourages it. If you like oversharers, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Cummings is a great professor. Her lectures are really interesting, but the material she covers is basically what she makes you watch. She's kind of a tough grader. The other professors for the same class are more lenient. This is a public speaking class, so if you're good at it, take it with her, if not, choose a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jennifer is AMAZING! One of the best professors I have had at the U. She really cares about her students. There are not many assignments so you do have to do well on them. She is really clear about the criteria so it isn't too difficult. The tests are pretty easy as long as you watch the lecture videos. I learned a lot of stuff I still use!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is mandatory, but I wouldn't take it. Pointless, walk away with absolutely nothing constructive. There are grammar quizzes, lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Cummings is one of my favorite professors at the U! You have to read two books for this class but they're both some of the best books I've ever read and I really enjoyed them. You have to be invested in this class, it's not just an easy A that you don't have to show up to. But if you show up and listen in class you will get an A.

Dr. Cummings is wonderful. She makes it clear what is expected to earn your grade. If you do the work, you'll get a good grade. I didn't really use the textbook, but there are lecture videos that you need to watch. Be ready to give presentations to the class.

Prof Cummings is solid. Class was somewhat easy. Lots of group projects but as long as you have a good group you are fine. No assignments over the top at all. Seemed to be quite an easy class. But the teacher is super nice and relaxed! Flexible with your schedule too.

Jennifer was AMAZING! I was seriously dreading this class. She made the classroom a safe place which made it less intimidating. She is a fair grader. Lots of busy work, but nothing to hard! I would definitely choose her over the other professors.

Jennifer co taught this class with Kate Canas. She does a good job with lectures and in class exercises. Doesn't grade all that tough. Her assignments aren't difficult but also aren't meaningless busy work. She's good if you need a comms class.

Jennifer is great. I was dreading this class but she makes it as fun as a business communication class can be. She seems rigid at first but is really engaging once the course gets rolling. I also liked that her grading is fair and accurate, and she lets you know exactly where you need to improve.
Jennifer is awesome, she brings real life content into the class and makes class enjoyable.

Tough class! Grading was somewhat subjective and tough. Be prepared for surprise reading quizzes. Doing poorly on an assignment can really hurt your grade as there was no extra credit. Dr. Cummings is extremely friendly, professional, and there to help when asked. Great instructor.
There is an attendance and participation grade for the class, so be there. While there are not many tests, there are three public presentations; one in a group.

For a communications class, you wouldn't expect anything less than a clear and concise professor. Jennifer's teaching is very retainable and clear. Lots of group activitiesprojects, a couple tests (if you do the reading, you will pass). She helps her students hone their communication skills to best help them in real-life professional situations.

Ms. Cummings and her class have been my all time favorite! The way she teaches is great, she lets the class lead and she asks a lot of thought provoking questions. There's no textbook since she picks and chooses chapter from different book. She wants you to explore comm. and relationships and the assignments reflect that. The content is relatable.

Loved this teacher!  I had her for COMM 3040 and COMM 2110 and absolutely loved the course material.  Teacher was very interesting and engaging.  2 tests, 1 paper, group discussions, presentation.  Tests were fairly easy if you completed the study guide she prepares.  NO TEXTBOOK for my section which was great.  Definitely recommend her!

I absolutely hated this class! 1. First the tests were difficult and vague.2 Course Content was uninteresting, especially as a senior in communication, it felt like a repeat. 3.Assignments( especially the online discussions)felt like busy work. 4. Class was a group therapy session for the five people who apparently had serious life issues.

I loved her class.  She is a very interesting teacher who knows her stuff. Her 3040 class consisted of three exams, final 8-10 page paper, group project and journals. I would definitely recommend her.

She is very nice, easy and knows the material. I was so excited for this class but was honestly disappointed. The book that you read is very boring plus it is discussed in class for an entire week. The material outside of this book was interesting though. I got really tired of reading and then having class discussions day after day.
New graduated phd professor. You can tell she has a very vast understanding of family communication. The text chosen to read was very good.

Dr. Berg was an exceptional professor. Her lectures were engaging, assignments were meaningful, and class discussions were welcoming—even at 9 a.m. She was always approachable and supportive of students. I couldn't recommend her more highly.
Unclear grading criteria, heavy-weighted quizzes, in-class participations assignments.

Professor Berg is caring and knows her material very well. She does participation activities during class, so you have to be there. You are allowed one late pass and are able to do one of the participation activities online. If you have questions, then Professor Berg and her TA are always available and willing to talk with you.

Professor Berg is a great professor. She is caring and works well with you. There is a couple of tests for this course. She doesn't take attendance everyday (she def wants you there every class) she takes attendance with questions once a week every other week that is used and so she can make sure you are retaining the information.

Best professor Ive ever had. Pioneer in her field. Does amazing research. Has her own company. Super humble, you wouldn't know any of this. PASSIONATE about the material. You watch lectures, then come to class. Easy to do well if you keep up. Just watch out, canvas doesn't show the grade you'll get. Canvas showed me a 96%. But I ended up with a 92%
amazing lectures. the work you have to put is alot, but you will never get bad scores because tests are easy and many extra credits

Dr. Furse does an amazing job answering as many questions as possible. She uses the flipped classroom method, so you'll watch videos on the material the night before and then work through the homework with her in class. Her tests are reasonable and you can retake any number of them at the end of the course. Do well enough and you can skip the final
Great professor. Would take again
I love professor Cynthia. She is caring and a great communicator. She'll do everything she could for your success. Even complex materials become simple with her teaching.

Great professor for starting your ECE program. She taught the material well but you need to put in the effort to succeed as usual. Tests are open notes worth 88% of your grade (22% in 4 exams). Her canvas is a bit of a learning curve so focus on cookbooks and lecture videos. HW/Labs aren't due till the end but try to stay on schedule.
Tests are worth 88% of your grade, this professor is a little too easygoing for the material, but if you are driven enough to stay on top of your own work, you will succeed.

This is a professor who not only cares about getting students to learn, but also recognizing the importance of GPA for securing jobs/internships. Zero ego, incredible passion, effective communication, ample extra credit, ability to retake tests for the final. I came, I saw, I learned. 10/10 would take again.
Amazing professor. She will explain things very easily and is very helpful if you go to her office hours.

Incredible communicator. I don't go to my class anymore because I can find all the information necessary and save 45 minutes of my life. Every professor in ECE should teach the 5 minute-lesson challenge at this level.

Very good professor!!! Her lectures were fun and kept me interested, the homework helped me understand, and the tests were open notes. I would recommend this class to anyone starting in the ECE program at the U.

Large class, very confusing teaching style. She shows to many examples of what people are doing with their Phd and forgets to teach the class.  She is very nice and is willing to help but good luck getting 5 minutes, as she is extremely busy with other University projects.
The best professor in ECE Department !!!

Dr. Furse is an incredibly caring professor.  She is always trying to find ways to improve course work so she can teach more effectively.  She also gave us many chances to make up lab and homework points we missed.  I learned a lot in this class but I did have to work for it.
Awesome professor!
Has excellent videos to watch before coming to class.  Spends more time on examples than most teachers
Very enthusastic, good homework and clear description. Kinda unorganized, Has some good youtube videos. Excpect alot of work. Prelabs take forever, look at them at least 3 days before lab.

Pro:  Good, smart instructor who's very willing to help you learn. Enthusiastic about the material!  She gives lots of partial credit.  Con:  Lectures are unorganized and hard to follow. Labs are horrible and don't supplement the class material.
The best that among who have taught me

If you go to class and pay attention it's a pretty easy class. She gives out the test questions out a week before the test so just memorize the answers. The essays aren't bad if you attend the lectures and read the handouts. I never read any of the material, everything needed is in her handouts. Go to the office hours if you need help, she's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She focuses on morals and ethics which is not the topic I am interested in, but she gives good feedback on the paper. As long as you write as her request you will pass the class.

This class was awful. Professor stark is a very tough grader, and she is very unclear of what she expects from students with their papers. Also, the only assignments for this class is papers and the final exam. Thankfully, she does allow re-writes on your papers if you want a better grade, but it is very difficult to get the grades up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's a harsh grader and is difficult to work with. GO TO CLASS. Attendance is key to getting an A because of her grading system in which attendance can boost a paper's grade. If you do not like reading or writing, do not take this course. She is unclear about what she expects from students so meet with her for clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Weekly phil. readings with accompanying news articles that have a corresponding quiz. 3 papers summarizing the paper's argument and finding a critique. Quizzes are easy but the papers can be difficult as critiques can be difficult to come up with it. Meet with her to discuss your critiques! She will tell you if they're good or bad critiques.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She gives off a blasé vibe to me, as if she'd rather be elsewhere, which she often confirms verbally. Regular unrelated tangents. She doesn't prepare well for lectures. If you do well in the class, you will have improved your ability to memorize. The class content was intriguing. She prepares good outlines which are helpful in seeing the arguments.

Solid class, focused on race specifically. The class is listed as political philosophy though so if you are looking for something with a more broad focus look for a different professor. I respect her reasoning for doing a race specific class-but if you pay close attention to race issues in America and have studied it at all seek another class.

Unfortunately I misunderstood the prompt on the first essay in this class (making it impossible to get an A). Handouts are very helpful for the 3 essays and exams. Exams are essay format and difficult, but she gives you the questions ahead of time. This class is taught as if you already have a good understanding of philosophy. Readings are hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Best class Ive had thus far. She is a great professor and really covers the material. She hands out break downs of all the reading and grades anonymously. Over all there is a lot of reading but super interesting. Attendance isnt mandatory but you do need to go or youll be lost. 3 papers and an optional 3 tests
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There are 4 papers and 2 exams, as long as you attend class and do the readings youll be okay. You are not required to go to class however it is very helpful in order to do the papers! Lectures most classes & you do watch some films. Cynthia is a good professor, she was available outside of class if you needed extra help! Ask for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: 40% of your grade is determined by the cumulative final exam, which you get a study guide for the week before. There were four papers, with one optional paper to replace your lowest grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Cynthia is awesome! She lectures really well and keeps you very entertained. Attendance isn't mandatory except for on days when you have to turn in things. 4 papers, 2 tests- all questions given in advance. Assignments are easy and based on completion not quality. Several days where you just watch movies and answer questions. hardly use book at all
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is really a philosophy class so their are some difficult readings but she does her best to explain the material in a comprehensive way. her grading is straight forward and can be harsh. Sometimes she assigns papers on Tuesday that are due on Thursday with a long reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Does not respond to emails. Did not grade anything until halfway in the semester. Pushes her ideas onto students and then expects them to deliver quality work. Terrible.
She is an inspiration. I've learned a great deal from her. We need more teachers like her! I loved the readings that were assigned and our discussions. I really appreciate her stories and wisdoms.

Dr Benally tries to run her lectures like a high school classroom, while continually harping on her experience and doctoral learning. She's the least approachable and helpful professor I've ever had, she will never give you a straight answer on any question you ask, and will happily cut students off to talk about her experience. Avoid at all costs.

Dr. Benally is one of the worst professors I have ever had. I took her class my last semester of undergrad, and it was the most infuriating experience Ive ever had. This class is a multicultural education class, but she only focuses on her culture, for the whole time. She is a horrible educator who has no business teaching others about diversity.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Randomly gives homework 0's and enters scores incorrectly. Rants about irrelevant material. Take anyone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor is very slow to respond to students. When asking for help with scheduled times and exams don't even ask for help you'll just get your hopes up. Grading is fair but it is obvious the professor is not interested in helping students.

She is very unorganized and unresponsive to student needs. Her grading time and feedback takes way too long. Most importantly she is very unresponsive to making improvements. You are on your own in her classes. I do not recommend this instructor.

I was thoroughly disappointed in this instructor. I didn't feel like there was any investment in students' success. The online instruction is horrible, which doesn't help. If you do well learning completely on your own, then you'll probably be fine but I wouldn't recommend her.
I took her online class. She is slow to respond to emails, slow to grade tests, and slow to enter grades. Not very helpful at all, you're basically on your own.

This class was super easy. Just go to class and do the occasional online quiz that she allows you to retake if you do poorly.  She's super nice and very understanding (not to mention she's easy on the eyes).  If for any reason you need to take an upper division psych class, do take it.  Easy A.

I had Danielle as an instructor for Psychology of Gender. She is by far the coolest grad student teacher I have ever had. She's knowledgeable, cares about what she's teaching, she's engaging, and she makes class interesting. She's a really cool person, and she's also really funny. I would recommend taking a class from her.
I had her for abnormal child development. She's a clear lecturer and very reasonable. I liked her and would take another class from her if I got the chance.
Very interesting lecturer. I looked forward to class.
He doesn't upload his notes so its very important to head to lecture. His tests are pretty hard but if you do well on the 3 midterms he lets you skip the final.

Dr C. is an awesome professor and even jokes around in lectures. He can grade tough, especially on free body diagrams and calculating the right inertia, but in a way that I think is very fair and constructive. It's a hard class afterall. Skipping lectures is not the best option for this class even if attendance is not mandatory!

Dr. Czabaj explained concepts well in lecture and did plenty of example problems. Homework length was reasonable and weekly quizzes were mostly easy. Exams were on the harder side but were similar to homework problems but in greater detail. Final exam is optional. I thought the material was relatively easy and he taught the class well.
Is a good professor until you need help on something. Then it is better to figure out another way to get help. He will not help with anything covered in lecture even if you do not understand it.
Seems like a chill guy. Grades like I'm in Germany in the 1940's. Better get ur calculations right
Lectures are amazing, and grading is fair. However, the professor is often rude and seems indifferent to student concerns

I wrote the review about comparing this professor to Amy Verkler and Hunter Simper. After consideration, I've realized he's not so bad. The subject is pretty simple; however, he lacks clarity in his lectures, but maybe this is due to such large class sizes. He can be a little rude at times, but overall a good professor. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Favorite professor I've ever had. Tests are very fair, if you do the homework you'll be just fine. Barely had to study because of how good his lectures are. Perfect mix of examples and new information. Extremely helpful if you go to office hours. If you ignore the class, its easy to get lost, but if you go to class, there's nothing to worry about.

Honestly I had no trouble in this class. His lectures were clear, and he would go over things that were confusing(Sometimes too smart for his own good). Homework can be difficult as he does not give the final answers. Office hours for homework and understanding of material. Became so intuitive I barely had to study for the exams. Quizzes on Thurs.
I disagree with the comment about him being worse than Amy Verkler and Hunter Simper. He is a good prof and cares but is a VERY tough grader

The class was hard but the professor is great. Lectures covered the homework topics well and the tests pretty much followed the homework. He went over lots of examples in class and had the lecture slides posted on Canvas as well. He went over confusing topics again right before exams to help us prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Czabaj is a smart guy who can come off kinda harsh. The homeworks were much harder than exams and often differed from the lectures. If you can study the homeworks and understand them you'll do fine on the exams. In class quizzes are not hard but are given frequently. Make sure you show up to take them or they will tank your grade.

Great professor, homework is manageable, tests are super easy. The final project is well explained and he does an example as well. I wish he did more examples, but learning the material takes up most of the time.

He is very knowledgeable in the subject and his lectures are good. The test are heavy graded and is really easy to drop your grade with little mistakes. Lectures and homework prepare you for the exams but he will make it more difficult.

Does a good job lecturing. The homework will prepare you for the test. But he is a tough grader. If you miss one concept, or make one wrong assumption that will take off at least 10% of your exam grade.

Homework is long and tedious, but not hard. Exams had combinations of problems or twists that weren't taught in lecture, the textbook, or on homework. Not all of the lecture materials are posted online, including some important equations.

Dr. Czabaj ("chah-bye") is an excellent professor.  He is open to feedback and questions during lectures. His homework is fair though sometimes lengthy. Lab reports are straightforward. Tests are fair and straightforward if you understand the homework.

Worked examples in lecture frequently had basic arithmetic & conceptual errors. Exams had too many questions for the amount of time given. A steam table needed for the final was only handed out halfway through the exam. There were typos on multiple formula sheets & final exam questions. Attendance is mandatory for pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She means well but her classes are a disaster. She consistently explains important concepts wrong and makes errors in grading. She changed the grade scale 2 months in, making it harder than in the syllabus, then said the grade scale on the syllabus was a “typo” and that what she meant to write is more important that what she actually wrote.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lectures are a mess (she doesn't seem to understand her own material, and is very unorganized in it). Turns out you can get a 0% on surveys, don't ask me how.
She cannot keep a coherent train of thought.

In general, attendance is mandatory, but you'll need to teach yourself.

Ifeel bad writing this because Deisy is a super nice person, but this class was rough. Many assignments weren't graded until after the final, leaving everyone completely clueless of their grades. Answer keys for assignments and practice exams were frequently wrong, making online resources more helpful for learning than the actual class.

Overall bad experience in all aspects. She updates the test during the test. It would be changing numbers and other essential parts to problems. The lectures are mandatory attendance for random quizes. But many of the lectures would be her wanted us to solve problems that we havent seen before and she wouldnt speak for the majority of the class.

Undoubtedly one of the worst professors I've had. Grading is untimely and ambiguous, often incorrect, and exams are being updated halfway through. Content is a complete mess, just read the textbook atp. Attendance is mandatory with pop quizzes. It's hard to contact her, even though you have to do that often to clear up grading issues/circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unorganized, difficult to contact, and made her tests too long for the amount of time given. We didn't know our grades for half the semester, and she makes tests worth a huge percentage of our grade. Her handwriting is bad, and she doesn't offer many resources to study. She was changing the questions on the final exam WHILE we were taking it.

This is the worst class I have ever taken in engineering, mainly due to the professor. However, she is a nice person overall. The grade letter breakdown is still unknown even after the semester is over. She was late to the final exam to hand out tests. The final project and final exam were also a disaster and were insanely hard compared to HW.

Deisy is super nice and is very willing to help students with assignments. Despite her being willing to help, her advice is sometimes not the most useful. The final grades for the course were incorrect and didn't get fixed until well into the next semester.

Professor Dentinger is awesome! I genuinely felt her and her TA wanted me to succeed. They give timely feedback, great expansion of material in class, and extra credit opportunities! I cannot recommend this class enough. I looked forward to class every single day. If you take notes, read the textbook, and attend class you are bound for success!

Dentinger is super charismatic and has great lectures! She really cares about her students' thoughts in discussion. For this class specifically since it's so broad, be ready to read!!! For a fun history elective I wouldn't recommend based on the amount of work but for majors 10/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor yet. I remember walking into her class on the first day feeling so depressed and sad after moving away from home and being away from what I knew so well. Her bright demeanor lit up the room and made my day. She is an understanding teacher and works well with students' needs. I took her Great Books and History of Medicine course.

I loved this class w Rachel. She was so sweet and obviously passionate about the course material. We did have to do two papers, but she gave extensions freely and didnt grade too harshly. For our final, we did a debate, and it was such a fun way to apply what we had been learning all semester. Absolutely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Dentinger is very helpful and knowledgeable. The class is based on real learning, not regurgitation of memorized facts. You have to really understand the abstract concepts being talked about so you can write about them and participate in discussion. The class was interesting and thought provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rachel, with Ann, is a really kind and passionate professor. With the online format proper class participation is tough but they did the best they could. Rachel is also very nice and considerate. The papers are graded fairly harsh so give them time and try to get pre-submission feedback from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Fun class, but I ended up getting an 88 in the class for one of the 2 semesters, for the amount of work I put in it should have been an A. If you have conservative viewpoints don't express that in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rachel is a great professor. She is very caring for her students and will go out of her way to help them and give them either constructive feedback or recognition for how well you did.

Rachel is so sweet and so interesting. Her passion for her subjects are so clear, and it makes the class so much more interesting. I had her for an IT and readings were assigned every class. The class took a lot of energy and time, but it was super fun and I learned a lot.
Her class is really interesting but she makes you write a couple really big papers that dont have super clear directions. she grades tough but gives great feedback. Not a class for Pre-Med students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I am shocked the university still employs this professor. This is not the line of work he should be in. He does not communicate clear deadlines. He doesn't grade things himself and won't fix when Canvas grades incorrectly. His lectures are incoherent monologues. No learning happened in this class. Everyone wasted their time for the 3 credits.

Stupidly easy but I felt like I learned more in this class than I did in all of my other classes combined. Makes me want to switch out of stem. The guy is very smart and his lectures are indeed rambley but that was the best part. I actually showed up to the lectures out of my own free will and not because I had to.

Online class COMM 5640. Extremely boring having to listen to his prerecorded pptx in slow motion. His slurring and incomplete thoughts were so frustrating. There's like 7 different books  you have to source on your own, some of which are available from the marriott library, others you have to pay for. Weekly quizzes and huge paper at the end. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took two courses from him. In both, he spent much of his curriculum and lectures complaining about modern technology and modern youth culture + going off on tangents. While I agree aspects of social media are bad and need to change, his slow lectures feel like boomer sermons. Also: he's *really* not tech savvy and it negatively affects grading.

What is taught in the media and pop culture class has nothing to do with media and pop culture. It is entirely a change for the professor to talk about everything he views as wrong with how younger generations interact with technology. The assigned readings are ableist and there is zero chance to talk to him about it or discuss the readings.

Nice guy, but good lord the work load is not worth it. Instead of tests and quizzes he'll often replace them with tedious and time consuming projects. Most of the homework too relies on having to meet with people outside of class and the assignments are weighted really bad. Something that takes a lot of time ends up being less than other assignment
This professor is honestly the best. He has made Korean fun, interactive, and explains in a way that helps you understand really well. I couldn't recommend this professor enough.
Super nice and makes it really easy to learn.

Everything about this professor is amazing. He helps me understand and makes learning Korean fun. He is making me want to come to class every week and continue to learn Korean. Best professor I've ever had
Great professor! He is very patient and makes sure everyone is understanding the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ive never felt more comfortable and taken care of in any class before this one. Professor Driggs was extremely attentive and caring and did whatever he could to help each student feel like they could succeed in the class. It was such welcoming environment and I learned so much in these classes. Thank you!

Professor Derek Driggs is amazing--very funny, caring, and flexible. Textbook assignments are graded based on completion & there is extra credit offered, though the exams can be difficult. Study and work hard and you'll do well in his class. He made learning Korean fun :).

Korean is a really tough class, and has a load of homework. Working in class is just as strenuous. However, Derek is very relaxed and always so patient while students learn new vocabulary. He is approachable, easy to get along with, and helpful. Only downside is that sometimes he is absent from class, so we have more work in the following class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Driggs was truly an amazing Korean teacher, he ensures to solidify many different forms, endings, concepts, and grammar, repeating some areas if he finds students' are struggling. Driggs' grading is a bit harsher than other Korean professors at the U, but I find that helps to pinpoint the areas the student may be lacking in.
