This is my third semester taking classes with Dr. Driggs. He is incredibly kind and thoughtful. His lectures are engaging and he is able to explain things in such an interesting way. Because he's a linguist he actually understands why Korean grammar is the way it is. You can tell that he really enjoys what he does.

Derek is so good at explaining things and he provides interesting context to coursework so you can see the bigger picture. Coursework is not too strenuous, but you need to take time outside of class to solidify concepts and practice. He also assigns creative assignments that make doing coursework more fun. I recommend taking his class!
I've taken Derek for Korean 1020 and 2010 so far, and I love him! Super helpful and understanding.

Truly a great professor. I can honestly say the best professor I have had. He is super personable and funny. I always look forward to attending class. He sets clear & reasonable expectations, but is also willing to work with you if needed. He is incredibly knowledgeable and keeps classes engaging and relevant. Hope to take more classes from him.

He is incredibly intelligent and has a lot of experience to share and his lectures are easy to understand. If there is anything you don't understand he is always willing to go over it with you. He creates a fun and inclusive environment that allows for the best learning experience. I have never enjoyed learning as much as I do in his class.

It is evident that Professor Driggs is very passionate about what he teaches and is very well-informed. He makes his students feel comfortable in class, pushes them to do their best, and supports them in their efforts. It's a heavy class with lots of things to learn, but he keeps class engaging and fun, as well as applicable to real life.

Professor Diamond is so fun! Her lectures are mandatory but she's very entertaining. Take notes for extra credit (super easy). Don't fall behind on assignment and make sure you always go to class and discussion! Also, pick option three for the final project it's fun! There also is no final exam so just keep up with assignments and read the rubric.

Lisa Diamond is an amazing, eminent researcher with a long history in the field and a decorated resume, but she's also a one-of-a-kind person who will change the way you see the world. Her courses are up-to-date and modern and she always adapts to new technology rather than decrying it. She's so good people actually come to her 8AM class.

I think Dr. Diamond's teaching style is great and I loved her lectures! But everything is graded by TAs and while attendance is mandatory/ is taken with an assignment each day, it can be done outside of class. She is a bit hard to get ahold of and if your TA is also hard to get ahold of it can be hard to get answers in a timely matter, or at all.

To those who oppose generative AI like ChatGPT, Diamond is now requiring it for 20% of the grade in this class. This is something that I personally oppose to because of the environmental impacts and the anti-intellectualism in humans that it promotes because it "does the thinking". When I discussed my opposition, she said treat it like a human :/

All grading is handled by the TAs, and about 90% of it is simply for completion. Half of the class is student led, so attendance isn't actually mandatory. If you are genuinely interested in the course content, you would likely be better off taking it with another professor.
Her TAs grade everything. Didn't go to that class for 2 months and still passed with 100%.

Loved this class! Supper fun and enthusiastic professor. The class time was early in the morning so that part sucked, but the class itself is really easy and fun to be in. Attendance does matter because she does an attendance word each day and if you miss that it will lower your grade. But overall, none of that is much of a problem.

Lisa is the most energetic, fun, and funny professor I've ever had. Despite the class being at 8 AM she never failed to bring positivity to our lectures. She also explained the material so clearly and in such an entertaining matter that she never failed to be engage our class.
Prof. Diamond was awesome! She is passionate and fun to listen to.

Lisa Diamond is an amazing professor! She makes her lectures so interesting! She is kind and so supportive especially to women and LGBT-Q+ individuals and others who are generally not supported as much. She is so inspirational and fun, and she's not afraid to be herself even if it means being a little wacky sometimes. She's so tech-savvy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Diamond is an incredible professor and very talented lecturer. The material was very engaging and she made it even more so. Her expectation for us were clear and I felt like I breezed through the class, not because it was easy but because Dr. Diamond made it straightforward. Overall, wonderful class and professor!

Excellent professor and class. Lectures were straightforward and easy to follow, and the content was enjoyable and relevant. Professor Diamond is charismatic, hilarious, and kind. She had a group of TA's who took care of grading/emails, all gave quick responses and graded fairly. Lots of opportunities for extra credit, and lectures are recorded.

Prof D was awesome! Her lectures were easy to comprehend, follow, and very entertaining. Prof. D's lectures were a bit early, so I missed a few, but the attendance on lectures was not looked at. She also posts the lectures online so you can watch them prior to the discussion session on Wednesdays. The TA's and discussion are the most important.

Lisa Diamond is super engaging and the PSY 1080 class (Love & Relationships) is very straightforward. The lectures are easy to follow and notes are extra credit! TAs grade most (if not all) of your assignments, so make sure to create a good relationship with whoever yours ends up being.
I loved Dr. Diamond's class! The lectures were fun and the homework wasn't hard or time-consuming. Plus the material is applicable to everyday life :)
The lectures were super interesting, homework assignments were easy, and overall it was a super fun but easy class. Highly recommend.
Dr. Diamond Is an amazing teacher. Psych 1080 was such an exciting and enjoyable class.
Lectures were great and she had zoom recordings.

She was nothing short of amazing! She expects you to do your best but gives you the needed things to do well in this class. She wants to see you do good! She is so good at responding to emails! She is always willing to answer questions and to help. If you miss a class she provides the resources to catch up as well! I LOVED LISA AS A PROFESSOR!

*GNDR 5770*
Absolutely my favorite teacher I have ever had. She is unbelievably kind, caring, generous, intelligent, hardworking, and funny. She spent half of the class lecturing and the other was spent as a class discussion. Her final paper was long, but she seemed to grade pretty easy. Dr. Diamond can also be a bit scattered, which I don't mind.

Literally one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so passionate and knowledgeable. I have recommended this course to all of my friends. No tests and very very little homework. The lectures are fun and fascinating to go to. TAKE THIS CLASS ASAP

If you dont show up to class, you lose a massive amount of points. Lisa is super nice and I really respect her, but the structure of the class really sucked. I thought this would be a fun class (love and relationships is a cool subject), but I only ended up becoming apathetic towards anything related to the material because of all the busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I would absolutely recommend this class. This isn't the typical course determined by quizzes and exams. In fact there are NO EXAMS or quizzes! She expects you to learn through applying the material IRL. There are small weekly assignments and SO MANY extra credit opportunities. So many opportunities to get a good grade and you learn so much.

On one hand, Lisa is a very caring and understanding professor who teaches really interesting material and offers tons of extra credit and makeup. On the other hand, this class has the MOST BUSYWORK I have EVER had in my 3 years in college. I took this class for fun, but ended up spending more time on it than any of my 4000 level classes.

Absolutely loved this class no exams or quizzes but in turn theres a lot of small busy work thats due every week. Almost all of it has a grace period though so it can be turned in late with few to no penalty. Note taking is a must since it is part of your grade at the end. Book is also a must since theres an assignment for every chapter covered

Dr Diamond is easily my favourite professor at the U. There are no tests in this class which is fantastic. I have learned more from this class than any other class I've ever taken. Her lectures are interesting and she's very funny and fun to listen to. Would recommend!!

I just really love this woman. She is clear, funny, and passionate. I took her Psychology/History of the Gay Family class and I highly suggest everyone do the same. She's slightly unorganized but not to the point where it effects the class.

Lisa is one of my favorite teachers i've ever had. Her lectures were very interesting and she is clearly passionate about what she teaches. Her student aid was absolutely amazing and I alway got quick emails back from both of them. Highly recommend this class and professor.

This class is passable if you do your readings (and there's a lot of it). The sucky thing is one of the readings requires you to get a book (titled: Psychology of Love) that costs like $100++ and it's her book. I do find her lectures to be a tad bit boring though. But don't worry, you'll pass if you just do the discussions and paper.

This class was extremely easy. There are weekly assignments, but they're small. The tests are super easy and there is one paper. Not hard at all. The lectures are fairly long and can be a bit boring since a lot of the info in them is common knowledge, but still a good class over all.

I have never been to such a pointless class. I read, did the homework and her lovely student aids (who grade and do all the work btw) gave me a terrible grade on my well researched final paper. They did not give feedback on what was wrong with it. I suppose there were not enough of Lisa Diamond's theories in it. If you can avoid her, please do.
She really knows her field and is an excellent presenter.  She grades hard and pushes students.  I loved the class and her style

Took this class last semester and wanted to drop it within the first month, primarily because this professor is extremely rude. The material is interesting, but it makes it difficult to strive to do well when your professor makes nasty comments at any questions asked. Sorry, I guess I thought that was your job--my mistake.

This class was ridiculous. More work and reading than even my graduate level classes. The weekly questions were boring and a hassle. I can't really say I learned much. She and her TA were both pretty rude and demeaning. I was excited to take this class and tried hard to like it, but it was awful. I don't recommend this class or this teacher.

Compared to all of my other 5000 level classes, this 2800 level class had BY FAR more work.  The readings were excessive and a lot of the time, boring.  The online version of the class had many technical difficulties, making the learning environment stressful.  Grades were entered VERY VERY late (months, sometimes), if they were entered at all.

I took the online version of this class. We had to buy her book which was over $100 and another book which was $60 just to rent. The lectures weren't put online for a couple of weeks after school started so everyone online was WAY behind.Most of the recorded lectures had problems too.

This class was fun. It was a really interesting subject (love) and I learned a lot from her. She knows a lot of stuff! She is very smart and always funny and enthusiastic during her lectures. Tests were pretty easy. You have to do weekly reading questions which sucked. And a 1,500 word paper that was hard because she wasn't very clear about it.

Seemed like a great professor. Really enthusiastic & TONS of info. But when I started having personal issues & contacted her about meeting to discuss my grade & I was really having a hard time, she totally shut me down. COMPLETELY apathetic to students. For someone who teaches Psychology, you would think she could muster up a little understanding.
Difficult subject but she is absolutely hilarious and tried very hard to get the students deeply interested in what she is teaching. She was a great teacher.
Stand-up comic for a teacher.  She's really smart and really funny.  Her tests weren't too bad either.  You learn alot that can be applied to real life which is always helpful
Dr. Diamond is so much fun during her lectures. The only down side to her class is a long paper due towards the end of the semester.
No Comments
No Comments
Amazing class one of my faves.
No Comments

She is so funny to watch! She really gets into her lectures. Her tests aren't so bad either, if you do the work and the reading then you will do fine in this class. I love her personality. It's nice to see a professor who actually has teaching skills!!!!

Very chill class and professor. Easy to ask questions and advice on CAD or your pump. Rope pumps are meta for winning but not applicable in real life scenarios so do what you want with that info. Very fun project. Pass the CSWA exam for a good grade in the class.

This class was quite easy and he was not that strict, did a lot of awesome CAD, but you need to pass a CAD exam to pass the class. Later we built a water pump and that was fun. He's pretty easy going and helpful.

M was amazing. They were very straightforward with what was expected and they made sure everyone had the resources to succeed. This is likely one of the more stressful classes to teach, but they never let it show, and if you put forth any effort in this class it was rewarded.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor M is literally so kind. They want you to succeed. The class isn't hard at all, and you honestly get what you put into it. If you don't want to learn, you won't be forced to, but you have the opportunity to learn a ton in this class. If you don't have background in CADD that might be your only struggle. Easy class, M is very helpful.

Prof M is great. He/They is super caring about you learning and is a great prof. All I have to say is make sure you learn best practices for Solidworks, as the CSWA exam kicked me in the rear the first time I took it. Water pump at the end of the year is super fun. (Make sure to do rope pump 3 inch pvc if you want to win)

I will start by saying they began as a great professor. Kinda cold sometimes, can be very condescending. Later on, they seemed not to care as much. Ignoring emails, not being helpful during labs, and overall, a difficult professor to deal with. When I had problems with my group for the water pump project, they did not help, and rather shunned me.

Professor Dillon's intro to mechanical engineering was a great class. Lectures were very informative and directly correlated to the final project water pump. He was also present in the labs and helped us better improve our projects.
This class is a very fun intro to mechanical engineering.

Amazing Professor! Their only wish from you in this class is to succeed. They are also trying their best to get your water pump working and help out students who struggles with low grades. TAs are also pretty helpful for SW.
Prof M is awesome they are super caring and just want you to succeed in your water pump. They want all of their student to succeed and will go out of their way for you.

Really don't have any negative feedback to give. Homework load was extremely manageable, one assignment per week that labs gave 3 hours to work on. Second half of the semester is a single group project, they're there to help if you have questions, but much of the time is spent working with TAs in labs.

I was so worried about engineering, but prof M made it so easy and enjoyable. The labs are insanely loaded with homework, but proved so helpful when studying for the SW exam. They always gave clear feedback on our water pump and encouraged our team. The canvas page is a bit hard to navigate, so stay on top of your assignments! Participate! Have fun

don't let these people steer you away from taking a class from Justin. if you show up and work hard that's all you need to pass his classes! he is very caring and does take notice to if you're actually putting your best effort into what you're creating. if you slack off it will be reflected within your grade!! justin is the dawg

The reviews on Justin made me so nervous to take his class, but he was so accommodating and kind. I can't imagine him having an issue with a student unless the student themselves were difficult or arrogant. He's willing to help and doesn't require attendance most days of the semester, which gives us time to work on projects on our own time.

You need to get to know Justin and understand that he will just never give you a nice compliment on your work. Its usually criticism coupled with a quick "looks good" but once you get past the fact you wont get reassurance he is a really good teacher. He knows all the ins and outs of printmaking, and you'd respect him a lot!

Justin cares more about getting narcissistic supply than helping his students. He talks at you, not to you. If you get on his good side, he is ok, but the second you don't give him 100% control, he freaks out. He is super passive aggressive, and the whole classroom has a deeply toxic environment to it because of him. Avoid.

If you are an eager student that wants to learn how to do printmaking, Diggle is your sensei.
He is an amazing printmaker and artist, who will push you to make the best prints of your work.
He doesn't like slackers, or people just trying to skate through, so I would avoid his class if you're looking for something easy. Make sure to clean up well!

Very patronizing, and often quite rude to students, as well as student teachers, and faculty members. Makes the print studio a sad environment filled with anxiety, rather than the relaxed, fun, creative energy many of the painting and drawing classes have.
Was not a fan

I don't understand the negative reviews- I'm assuming they're from freshman who don't want to put in effort. Fun assignments with great demonstrations, be prepared to put in work to succeed (like in any class). Super fun guy, one of the best art teachers I've ever had. He is very knowledgeable about the subject he teaches and is very helpful.
Had to take this class for my major.
I would not recommend. Not pleasant
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am a painting and drawing major, but took this class to fulfill my printmaking requirement.  I easily jumped right in to the process thanks to the great direction from Prof Diggle and he definitely cared a great deal about how everyone was performing in the class. We had a collaborative assignment in his class which I thought was unique and fun.
Best Professor ever!

Great professor, explains things in easy and digestible parts. Homeworks are long but mostly doable. Exams are hard but there's opportunities to improve your grades. Labs are basically impossible without showing up to office hours. However he is very easy to work with. You can tell he wants to help you succeed if you're willing to put the effort in

Dimas is not a proffeser by title, but he has a lot of math knowledge. His tests don't allow equation sheets, but parts of questions build on eachother, so one part will help you answer the next part (don't worry, he will still give points if your later answers are correct based on earlier incorrect work). He really wants his students to succeed.

Expect a high-intensity environment. The grading criteria are quite rigid, often resulting in 100% or 0% without much nuance. You'll need to dive deep into the texts to satisfy the  requirement for 'deep meaning.' However, implementing feedback is tough as the comments aren't always actionable. Hes very strict with "AI"? make sure your voice ig

Incredibly hard grader. You either receive a 0% or 100% on assignments; if one part of the assignment is incorrect, you'll receive a 0 for that entire grade. Very hard to get in touch with and doesn't provide actual advice as to what you can do better for the next assignments, but says it's not personal enough and immediately assumes you use AI.

He knows his stuff, and the content is easy to understand. However, he is incredibly strict with grading (MAKE SURE YOU READ THE SYLLABUS), and it's difficult to manage if you have a heavy class load or can't grasp the implied angle he wants from you. Be aware.

For a 2000 level class, it was taken to seriously and graded too harshly. Our first assignment's average was a 45/75. That was the average. There is some kind of miscommunication going on for expectations, and grades were far too harsh for the work submitted.

I had to reach out to this professor several times over the course of the semester because he wasn't submitting any of my grades for 5-7 weeks on average after the due dates. Because of that, I had no feedback going into the next large assignment. He didn't do well in an online class because he didn't explain any of the concepts; just had us read.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: worst professor ever does not want students to succeed and will not work with you to pass the class. trust me dont get stuck w him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So behind on grading. I didn't get a single assignment graded until halfway through the semester and I didn't get my midterm score back until a week before the final. How do you expect to understand the material if I don't receive any feedback, especially since this is an online course? I would not recommend this professor to anyone.

I absolutely LOVE this professor, he is very personal, and he's very friendly with the students. He takes his time to get to know every one of you and also is super kind. The readings are a lot, but it's worth it as the readings are lowkey fun and important to the fun class discussions we have the next day. Would recommend 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dominic was awesome. You can tell he was passionate about the materials we covered, and he also shared his own work with the class (it was brilliant). If you do the readings, this class won't be too difficult.

Dominic was great! I took COMM 1020 (public speaking) from him, but RMP isn't letting me select that class. It's a little heavy on lectures, but there are no tests and very few assignments. The main things we were graded on were our speeches, and it was easy to get a high grade on those if you came prepared. Dominic was a fun guy, very friendly.

Prof. Walker-Pecoraro's class was very interesting and I learned a lot. He's very knowledgeable in the field and gives great feedback. The class had no tests, but there was homework and a few projects. There is one big individual project and one big team project. The work wasn't difficult, but you need to pay attention to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dominic is a fantastic professor, and is always happy to help all of his students. You will have to write a lot of papers in this class, but you are allowed to write about topics you find interesting which made the class really fun.

there are (almost always) readings to complete before every class. Participation matters, both in attendance and in the discussions! it's a difficult class, but he makes it feel more manageable and is always there for feedback or help when you need it.

Kopta is a great instructor all around. This class especially is known to be difficult, but with Kopta it is not so bad. Attendance is graded unfortunately. On every assignment you are given grading tests, so you have no excuse for doing bad on those. The new test structure this semester made it easier imo, much easier to get good scores on these.

Daniel Copta is a great instructor, and I've had positive experiences with him before. I would take him again, just not for this class. The exams focused too much on memorizing assignment details rather than understanding, and with tests heavily weighted, one exam could significantly impact your overall grade. This made grading feel unfair overall.

I was a big fan of Kopta, and he's a great professor, but honestly I think this semester he tried inflating the difficulty for this class way too much. I think basing 50% of your grades on tests with a small question bank was a bad idea. Even though I did the assignments, taking each of them was an immense amount of stress.

Wouldn't let me take a syllabus quiz I missed in the first week which was due before I was even added to the Canvas or enrolled in the class (because I'm going to cheat with my peers on a Syllabus quiz???) 

Not very accommodating to CDA either.

He breaks down each topic in a clear and granular way that makes everything feel obvious. Homework takes a long time, but is mostly very interesting. From talking to other students it seems that he has toned down some of the tedious nature of the homework, while still helping you get experience implementing class concepts.

Having taken this class twice, and finally passing (a B- is passing), I had a much nicer time with this professor. He properly teaches, he knows what he's doing and he wants students to succeed. The course itself is just really difficult.
Best CS professor at the u
Kopta is so amazing! I love his classes so much! His teaching style is really clear and he makes resources really accessible will definitely take more classes with him.

I would say that Kopta has been the best professor I've had at the U. He's very knowledgeable and I'm happy I that he's the one teaching 3810. If it would be anyone else the class would be magnitudes more difficult. His lectures go into detail and he makes sure that you are understanding the material.

Everything everyone says is true. He is super smart and knowledgeable on the subjects he teaches. I studied so much for his exams and didn't get the scores I wanted, but that doesn't change the fact he's a great professor. Highly recommend, but definitely requires hard work.

I've had this professor for three classes and his classes are pretty test heavy, but he is really accessible outside of class and he explains concepts extremely well! 
Cheat sheet must-haves:
1. QUIZZES
2. Broad concepts he mainly talks through
3. Homework examples
This has helped me get As before but I was not locked in this semester.

Overall an amazing teacher. Really cares about students success in the course. The assignments were clear and he would give you a direction to go in during each lecture. The course was overall not hard, but it does take time to do the assignments and projects. Start them early

Professor Kopta has some of the best lectures I've ever attended. He presents the material in a straightforward way with very detailed explanations of concepts. Homework is time consuming but relevant. He expects a lot from his students, and has quite challenging exams. You will learn a TON in this class.

Professor Kopta's teaching style is absolutely stellar; his slides make difficult concepts actually digestible.

One thing I love about his classes is that he uploads his lectures as videos onto Canvas after class; if I miss class, I can go back and take notes, which I appreciate. 

He is also often active on Piazza, giving lots of help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor. However, this guy has a twisted sense of morality. He keeps solutions from the past 5-10 years to make sure you'll be caught cheating. He will hide HTML in the canvas page's instructions to entrap students who use AI. He will advise you to use AI and then penalize you for it. He will even (try) pursue action once you're graduated.
Dr. Kopta is an excellent professor. His lectures are engaging and fun and I learned a lot in his class. His assignments are well made and I enjoyed doing them. Overall, excellent professor.

Took several courses with Kopta—outstanding. Yes, his exams and assignments can be difficult, but they're always fair and well-aligned with the material. He has a rare talent for teaching complex concepts clearly and effectively

He's easily the best CS professor in the department—and arguably one of the best instructors at the entire university

I honestly found Kopta to be overhyped. Lectures were fine but nothing spectacular. HW schedule was weird, there was no HW covering the last 3-4 weeks of lecture. I found grading to be strict, and think my grade suffered because I didn't cheat on the midterm while many of my peers probably did. Not sure why it wasn't proctored/at lib testing center

The class sprints in the beginning, leaving most students behind. PLEASE lay out a solid foundation first, going over high level concepts, then deep dive certain sections. MUCH preferable to the bottom up approach that Kopta loves to take. Outdated teaching techniques, and poor learning outcomes.

Signed, a now Senior Database System Engineer

The lectures were so long along witht the weekly assignments this class took so much time. Kopta over complicates everything. I had 3500 with him too and every who took it prior said he complicats it so much.

This professor hides hidden prompts in his instructions in HTML and then he tries to catch students using generative AI. He includes a clause in his academic misconduct policy that states that inputting any details of specifications into generative AI counts as academic misconduct. So be careful when taking classes with him or Travis Martin.

He is a great professor and one of the best at the university, for databases he is the guy for you and his lectures are going to be easy to understand, I just wish the office hours for this course were offline but otherwise great.

Kopta is a stellar professor who makes learning Database Systems a breeze. His lectures are clear, and he's always responsive on Piazza. Quizzes and exams are challenging but fair. Definitely try unstuckstudy for extra practice!

I regret the lack of effort I put into this class. I was so hyper focused on 3500 that I neglected this class a little bit and with the difficulty of the tests, did not do as well as I would have liked to. Prof Kopta taught a great class though, I would recommend him to anyone. I just think for me, 3500 and 3810 in the same semester was too much.

I love Kopta! He is super knowledgeable and this is the class where I feel like I have learned the most about coding so far. His assignments are difficult but well documented(mostly) and he is super active on Piazza to answer questions. He has hands down the best slides in the department. I would take Kopta for every class if I could

Seriously one of the best classes I have ever taken. It is hard, but the lectures are so interesting that I never felt an urge to skip. The course material is fascinating. The assembly assignments are loads of fun, and the assignments really test your understanding of the material. This class is like treading water. Don't let yourself fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: CS3500 is a tough class because of assignments. However, this class doesn't feel like the tedious CS2420. Plus, Kopta is open, caring, down to earth, and a great lecturer. Just stay on top of assignments and get a good partner. You'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm about to graduate. Professor Kopta is the best professor I've had within CS here at the U. His classes are hard, and his tests are difficult. But I haven't had a lecturer that is as thorough and articulate as Professor Kopta. His lectures and slides are so clear. I've learned the most from Professor Kopta. Bravo to him.
His tests are difficult but if you prepare enough, you'll get a lot out of his classes. His lectures are organized and well articulated. I still remember everything I learned from his classes.

He's just a really really smart guy, and kind of expects the students to be on the same page as him. It's just so fast paced cuz we have assignments due every single week, and so we barely get time to understand the material. He's a good professor, and teaches well, but he has really difficult exams and hard grading criteria.
My favorite programming class at the U so far, professor kopta's lectures are the best and his explanation is very clear

Systems is just hard, so Kopta is a difficulty 3 compared to how I imagine any other professor. It's tedious and technical material, but he does a fantastic job of thoroughly and cleanly explaining every concept. The assignments all take many hours, but I never felt like I lacked any of the knowledge I needed to complete them. Top quality lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Danny continues to be one of the best professors in the department. The online format does present challenges, but his slides and explanations are all very clear and well thought out. Expectations for assignments are very clearly communicated, and any questions about gray areas are quickly cleared up by the TAs, if he doesn't answer them first.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kopta has to be the best lecturer in the CS department. His lectures make learning easy, although there is a lot of information that you are expected to know. Both the midterm and the final are open note. There is also a lot of group work for this class. Overall, definitely take this class from Kopta if you can!

Professor Kopta is amazing. He does a great job teaching Database Systems. The only downside to this class were the somewhat annoying quizzes and his very difficult exams. If you study and keep up with the homework though, you'll do fine. The class does get easier after the first exam and project is worthwhile and fun! Find a good partner though!

This class was harder than I was expecting. Quizzes are difficult, some TAs would check them over for you before you submit which was nice. The exams were difficult, but I expected that from Kopta. Second half of the semester is partner work, find someone good to work with early on.

He does good lectures however the quiz for each lecture requires too much time to do, and quizzes accounted for 10%. I know he's the type "you gotta work to earn it" but making quizzes that hard is a bit waste of time

Lectures were clear and informative, but he also boring and monotone. You kind of get the vibe he would rather be teaching higher level classes which I totally understand. Assignments were extremely easy, and the tests were also pretty chill if you pay attention to the lectures and do the practice exams.

Prof Kopta was a great first teacher into the world of programming. The homework got progressively harder so it's helpful to go to TA's for help. If coding is a new skill for you, be prepared to spend lots of time on the class. The tests were on paper which was a learning curve but topics were fair. He completely gets rid of 'imposter syndrome.'
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are dense with material so show up to them. Lots of extra credit opportunities to boost assignment scores. Assignment requirements are straightforward so if you follow them you'll get 100%. Tests require good knowledge of the topics and were fair. I would recommend him.

Dany is an interesting lecturer, and every lecture critically matters/is dense because of it.
HOWEVER - if you are the type of student who doesn't do well with lectures, he is your worst pick by far. His exams are known to be more difficult than other professors, and he expects much out of his students.
TLDR; Recommended for non-ADHD students.

Kopta is an awesome professor hands down. With all the bad teachers you can get for classes, if he is teaching a class you need to take it is a no-brainer to take it with him. Explains things very well, is extremely fair, and really wants you to learn and get a lot out of your degree.

He's not bad, but not good. Need more free days for attendance.

EXAMS ARE INCREDIBLY HARD

His lectures are very informative. Good instructor but not a good people person. I get very frustrated when I go to him for help.

Labs are useless. Learn nothing. Waste of time.

Grading is way too strict imo. It's very black and white, no leniency anywhere

Kopta is great, and honestly I didn't think that he was too difficult. His lectures are great, clear and informative, even if a little boring sometimes. Assignments aren't too hard but are graded harshly I think. Tests are hard but seem fair enough.

His lectures cover the content in an easy to understand measure. His assignments can be difficult, but I always finish them with a far better understanding of the material. His tests are on the more difficult side and are honestly weighted too heavily for what they are. He can be a really hard professor but if you pay attention you'll learn a lot.

If you take 5530 at the U, you'll almost certainly have Kopta. That's not a bad thing, as he is one of the best lecturers the program has, he is very attentive to class questions on Piazza, and gives very well-crafted assignments to help you master the subject. His exams are notoriously difficult yet fair, so be sure to study up for those.

He's the GOAT. Lectures and slides are god-tier! Everything was so organized, and the piazza was extremely well monitored by him. Though exams are on the difficult side, rest assured he gives you all the resources you'll need to succeed. If you ever have an opportunity to take class with Kopta, do it!!! You will learn so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Videos are separated into topics, 3-10 minutes. Quizzes are 10 questions or shorter. Use visual studio C#.
Tests are not not easy A but fair enough, open book but no time to look at any notes.
Piazza is always active.

This class has a reputation for being hard, but I didn't think it was too bad. Sometimes the programming assignments are challenging, but I think Kopta's lectures are straightforward. Don't hesitate to go to TA hours. Make sure you really understand everything and study for the exams because those are tough and they are graded kind of harshly.
He did his job well, I never struggled to understand the topics he explained, and he posts all lectures and slides.
No complaints from me. Danny's a funny guy, he lectures very practically and explains concepts well, and is active on Piazza. I'd absolutely take another class from him.

He is very experienced in CS and was an excellent instructor. He introduces new content in a constructive and easy-to-understand way. I learned a lot in his class and his group assignments follow closely along with the lectures

Taught alongside Travis Martin. Professors were good with lectures and answering questions during them. Very respondant outside of class on Piazza or Canvas. Assignments were time-consuming, but grading criteria were always clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 4cr courses like this shouldn't take more than 12 hours per week. It took too much time for me and was hard to keep up with. I've noticed thousands of questions on the piazza and TAs were almost always busy. Those indicate things weren't clear to students. Normally, students should be able to make it without seeking additional help.

Assignments and analysis papers take ~ 20 h/week. Plus, you see TAs, utilize piazza, weekly quizzes(6%), attend labs(8%), and classes. Participation (6% of total grade). Grading is not elder-friendly:late work is penalized by 10%/day. Think spending ~25 h/week min for this class and being a full-time student. B is difficult to get.

2420 is naturally a hard class, but Kopta taught it extremely well. Through Piazza and office hours, help was extremely accessible. My sole complaint is that some assignment specifications were illogical or confusing, but that was mostly a semantic thing and did not impact the difficulty. Get a good partner, the entire class is pair programming.
He is a great professor and have a great knowledge of what he's teaching but he thinks every student naturally knows every thing about programming.

Simply Awful! You won't know the assignments' rubric. No tolerance. Late work is 10% ducked off for a day. Submitting not finished work is better than a full late work. He seems doesn't care. It's not a difficult class, it's just confusing about how he teaches and what he expects in the answers on the exam. Teaching and grading could be better

I really enjoyed his class and his lectures were beneficial. He has many slides on his PowerPoint, making it easy to review the past material. Personally, I think he's excellent and I didn't have any issues with him. If the lectures are boring, maybe CS isn't for you. The only issue I had is it took forever for him to grade. Very clear grader.

Kopta's teachings are confusing. You'll constantly question yourself, let alone be proud of pursuing the cs major. Great TAs though! I spent too much time studying, but still, the expected final grades are a B+ or A-. I don't recommend Kopta's class to any student. He takes trivial things that don't add anything to your knowledge too seriously.

2420 is a difficult class. Kopta helps make it manageable and working with TA's helps with getting started on projects and studying for exams. I do wish though that there was a textbook that you could read for additional information to help study for exams.

Professor Kopta seems like a nice guy and he is available to ask questions, if that is important to you. His lectures bored me to tears, it made me question if I wanted to major in CS. Also he doesn't give you any learning resources other then lecture slides and class recordings so it was sometimes hard to know where to start on assignments.
Very detailed lecturer with mostly well-made assignments. Very good at providing help if you need it.

I wouldn't recommend taking his class. He is very lecture heavy and teaches as if the students have had years of experience in the class when most, if not all, are fairly new. The assignment details are always unclear and he isn't very good at answering questions on Piazza because the answers are always vague. Expect to teach yourself honestly.

This class was very difficult but I could've done better if I had a professor that could actually answer my questions. I'm not saying he doesn't know the material. I'm saying that he is always INCREDIBLY vague with his answers. I never felt like asking him for help really helped. My partner and I always felt like we were on our own to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kopta's great. He's really funny in lectures, his assignments are very well-explained, he's active on Piazza. Would take again.

Professor Kopta is great. His lectures were always very helpful and quite interesting and entertaining. Assignments were a little bit vague on the specific requirements but Kopta was always available on Piazza for clarifying questions or just help in general.

Kopta definitely is a good lecturer. He does a lot of teaching by examples. My one major complaint is that he crams a lot into his lectures, a little too much for you to absorb. His lectures often contain one hundred slides but sometimes even more. You do get six pages of notes for his exams though.

Kopta is very strict but extremely good at explaining things. This class is my best class so far. I learned A TON, and I wish we had more similar practical class taught by him. 

Prof is very diligent on answering questions on Piazza. And the atmosphere of his class is very good. Students help each other on Piazza as well.

Kopta leans on in class lecture quizzes and weekly quizzes which account for nearly an entire letter grade to ensure students attend his lengthy, circular lectures. Expect quizzes and labs to be poorly worded and confusing. The concepts in this class are not difficult but feel like a grind because of the ineptitude of the CS department.
One of the best instructors I have ever had. Extremely well thought out class structure and lectures. Super clear grading. Welcoming environment.

Danny is great at explaining difficult concepts is an understandable way, and he seems to care about the students.  He would extend the deadline on assignments if it seemed like it was necessary, and his exams weren't terribly difficult.  This class has been my favorite CS elective so far, and I highly recommend it.

This professor will not give partial credit when credit is due, late on replies to emails, and little to no compassion when help is needed. Requires a textbook that wasn't needed (waste of $). One of the worst classes at my time at the U.

Great professor. He is very good at explaining his lectures. I never found myself confused for more than a few minutes. The assignments aren't too challenging. If you have trouble outside of class, he always responded very timely to Piazza. There were three exams that weren't very hard. Two pages of notes were allowed.

Professor Kopta has always been respected in our university. This class is online and is very lecture/quiz heavy. Every single topic was explained thoroughly and very well. The midterm and final were tough, but also fair. The homework and projects are relatively easy as long as you understand the topics taught. Take this class!

Kopta knows what he is teaching. This was my first programming class and I understood it very well because of him. Goes over concepts and explains them in ways that make sense, and provides many resources like slides and recorded lectures. Homework is enjoyable and challenging, so put in enough time to learn. Long lecture but provides small breaks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely good lecturer, I was able to learn very difficult concepts with ease. As long as you start assignments early and take advantage of TA hours, you will do great.

Prof. Kopta is the best CS professor here. You can tell he really knows what he's talking about, but he makes even the most complex concepts seem approachable and does this without "dumbing it down". He seems really down-to-earth and doesn't have an inflated ego like other CS professors.

I took Professor Kopta's class during the Pandemic and his lectures were great for explaining the material. Most of the grade is based on homework and the grading criteria is very clear. He is a great professor.

Kopta is pretty cool. He wants you to succeed. If you ask for extra help, he will give it to you. Sometimes tho it's a bit hard for him to understand something you ask him. He gave fair tests, and fair assignments. The assignments were more time consuming than tough. Start early! I felt like I had to work on them ALL THE TIME to get it done.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kopta is a good dude. He definitely wants his students to succeed. Also his lectures were engaging and sometimes funny.

Good professor however difficult class, only issue I had with the professor is on the final he kept saying we wouldn't need to memorize a certain thing for the test but he threw it onto the test anyways, as others have said, make sure you find a good programming partner it'll make a big difference, weekly prog. assignments b sure to start early

You cant beat Danny. So helpful and the lectures are in depth but not lengthy. Always gave breaks in class and gave class extensions on 3 assignments. Assignments are significantly tougher than 2420 ime. Spent more hours so prep for that! Hes available every day for oo and always answers questions after class and via piazza. Great guy.
Great Prof, would take any CS class from him.

To echo a bunch of other reviews, make sure you get a good programming partner. You will do most of the homework assignments in pairs and you only get to switch partners once. Prof. Kopta has such smooth lectures that I didn't notice it until he invited a guest lecturer in. Suddenly I had to ask a load of questions to understand the guest speaker

Daniel was a great professor, you have to keep into account that this class is HARD. The material is HARD. Overall, doable. Make sure you find a good coding partner, it really can make or break your overall experience in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Kopta is probably my favorite CS professor at the U so far. Highly proficient in conveying new concepts to students, the lectures he gives are awesome. The workload for this course is heavy (as are all 4-credit CS courses), but fair. Great at explaining concepts and providing good reasons why students should care about them. Highly recommended!
The course is super easy. *Too* easy. He practically does the homework for us. Some lectures are entirely devoted to review for exams. Tests are open-note.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kopta is a great lecturer and taught the course content in a clear and understandable way. My only frustration was with the use of partner projects in an online class. Piazza is not a great way to find a partner because you don't really know the person, only their schedule. The pair project impacts your grade a lot, so you want to like your partner

He is one of the best instructors I have had at the U. Very knowledgeable in what he's teaching and willing to help students whenever they struggle. You have to work hard, but he provides everything you need to succeed. In CS5530 you need to have good habits to study on your own and go through all the work since there is no set time block for it.

Professor Kopta is the real deal. Take any class from him and you'll be guaranteed to learn a lot and know that every assignment/test will be fair. That said, his assignments can be challenging, though never overly difficult. Honestly there are few on his level.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Kopta's class. He is very knowledgeable about coding and is always willing to answer student questions (in class, online, office hours, etc). His lectures aren't too long or boring. Assignment instructions are very clear, and if there is any confusion, he is quick to clear it up. Overall, really good professor.

One of the few Professors in the CS department that can actually teach effectively. This is a very hard class, but I honestly learned so much. Assignments take up a significant amount of time and tests are challenging to say the least, but not to the point where it is discouraging. I can't recommend this Professor enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor Ive ever had for a class. Hes just too good at teaching the class material, and you can tell he cares about how you do in the class. The downside was that the class was pretty difficult, and assignments required a lot of effort. But, I learned a ton and I cannot wait until I take databases with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He will overwhelm you with how much he expects you to learn. The PowerPoints for his lectures average to a hundred slides. On his exams, he expects you to know as much as he crams in his lectures. You get to use six pages of notes for his exams but it can still be a lot to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Danny is one of the greatest CS professors here. He is funny, is always happy to help, and really knows his stuff. The amount of work in this class is heavy but it isn't particularly difficult. The first half of the class is kind of boring, but hang on. The second half of the class gets much more interesting.
Kopta is an all around solid professor. Slides were excellent to review from and everything is recorded.

Kopta's lectures are always well organized and for the most part super interesting. He also does a great job at accommodating assignments and office hours for the class. The tests were kind of unfair though with the weights of the questions and the material.

Dr. Kopta is really smart and really kind. He would quickly answer our questions online and would help us in real life too. This made the class a lot better because I felt like he really wanted us to succeed. He's very intelligent and he gave me a few "gems" about software engineering that really stuck in my head because they're so useful.

This class is difficult, I wont sugar coat it. The last couple assignments took us about 20 hours each and the others averaged between 8-12. Danny is a great professor though and teaches the concepts really well. He also helps with TA hours which get really clogged up during the hard assignments. Tests were easier than homework, to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wish I could have Professor Kopta for all my CS classes as he's my favorite I've had so far. The class was insanely hard but I definitely learned a ton. The negative is the assignments were so difficult that the TA help sessions were slammed and help was often not accessable and the TA's were often not helpful. If you can go to his office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The lectures were fine, not the best, not the worst. Assignments were fine, final project was partner, which was unnecessary. Overall 3.9, but like Kopta, no rounding.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kopta's 4400 class is extremely hard, but he is empathetic and does everything he can to help you learn and succeed. He mentions that you have to get above a 65% average on the exams to pass, but I know numerous people who didn't quite make the mark and he saw how hard they worked and they left the class with a B. Nice guy. Has my respect

I have trouble staying interested in Danny's classes. He seems like he's always passively angry at the class, and that he doesn't enjoy his job. His lectures move really fast and he doesn't give many opportunities to ask questions.
Dr. Kopta is an amazing professor! It doesn't get better than him at the U.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Danny was a great professor. His lectures are relevant and topics are very helpful with the current assignment. He does a pretty good job answering questions and explaining pros and cons of different ways to solve problems. He's also pretty funny. The assignment specs are a lot to take in but give good information.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Kopta is a great professor. He is a great lecturer and will answer any questions asked. Expect a lot of homework. Depending on skill it can take 4-14 hours, personally most of my time was on analysis. You must have a partner for every assignment or it is an automatic 15% off your grade. Would take a class from this professor again.

Very good about explaining concepts. Also a generous god as he gives you a fair portion of code and help on projects in class. He is very good about answering questions on Piazza and definitely knows what he's talking about. A solid prof.

Daniel is my favorite CS prof at the U. His lectures are clear and easy to follow. His assignments are clear in their requirements. And he is very approachable and easy to come to for help. Had him both for 3500 and 4400 and he was great in both of them. His tests are tough but fair. If you have a chance take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Kopta is dedicated to constantly improving the courses he teaches, seeking feedback from students about the course and creating new content to increase student engagement and learning. His commitment to leave the course better than he found it is a quality I admire and will strive to emulate in my own pursuits in industry and academia.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Danny is one of the rare professors that are both extremely knowledgeable in their subject area and able to teach extremely well. He really knows the subject matter for CS4400 and is able to convey it in a meaningful way. Easily one of the best professors I've had at the U. I wish i had the opportunity to take another class from him.
Prof. Kopta is an excellent lecturer and teacher.
I had both CS4400 and CS3500 with Prof. Kopta. Really enjoyed his lecture. The review quiz after each class is really helpful for going through what we have covered. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, one of the best in the U. If he's teaching a class you're wanting to take, you can't go wrong. CS 3500 with him was great. Tough, but fun assignments. Reasonable tests. Good teaching style amd lecture material. No complaints!

Professor Kopta does a great job of lecturing on material that is useful in the software engineering process. Most assignments take a while to complete but he makes sure to schedule TA and office hours at convenient times. He also touches on various aspects of the assignments in class to provide a better understanding for the students. 10/10.

First, I love Prof. Kopta and could not wait to start CS4400 with him next semester. CS3500, however, is not my type of tea and did not really enjoy the course as I would enjoy most other CS classes. I learned something about SE but I think I am more into new and exciting knowledge like OS, algoriths and networking.

Amazing teacher. Has nice ways of tying subjects together and I feel like I learned a lot of useful information that's applicable to work. Mixes up lectures between demos and Powerpoints which allows us to see what is happening in certain programs. The assignments take time and build off of each other and tests are fairly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A great CS professor. I highly recommend him for CS3500 or any other CS course. Towards the end of the semester, weekly assignments are done as pair programming (as is customary for CS3500). Quite a bit of work outside of class, but much less than that of CS2420.

CS professors should be more like Kopta. Very involved. Very relatable. And a heck of a good lecturer who knows how to explain difficult software engineering concepts. Assignments and tests are appropriately difficult. TA choices are great too. He's a gem of a professor, take a class from him.
It's very obvious that Kopta knows what he's talking about and is comfortable teaching the information. He's a solid instructor and I would recommend him to anyone.

Daniel's a fantastic professor. I learned so much in this class! He's very good at teaching difficult concepts and uses good examples to demonstrate with.  This class was challenging - if you slack you will fall behind quickly. Tests are appropriately difficult. TAs were great as well, but I think this is in part because of Daniel's involvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Laid-back, easy-going class.  Lectures could get a little slow-moving at times but instructor worked on fixing that.  I learned a lot in this class and the instructor was effective at teaching the material.

by far the worst professor I've had my entire time at the U. I have had no idea what my grade is the entire semester and he makes no attempts to convey that information to the class. He doesn't post assignments or announcements on canvas and quite frankly I don't think he even knows how to use the website in the slightest.

Syllabus is wildly inaccurate, and he makes no attempt to update it. Readings were not posted several weeks in a row. If you miss class, you'll have no idea when quizzes are: there is nothing on Canvas to tell you. Lectures are stream-of-consciousness rants where you'll have no idea what's relevant until you're looking at exam questions. Nightmare.
Really nice teacher, but you have to read a lot for the weekly quizzes. None of his grades are posted on Canvas because everything is on paper, but he's very nice and open to suggestions.
Just don't take it. Lecture is unorganized, ppt is there but doesn't help with studying, exams are unclear and the rubric for the anything in the course is not there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AWFUL. I have no idea what my grade is, and he couldn't provide an exact answer when I asked mid-semester. Rude and dismissive toward students who have a comment or concern. EXTREMELY socially awkward and difficult to talk to. Terrible. Disrespected me when I asked for help and made me cry when I didn't understand what a question was asking. AWFUL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot recommend Prof Jones to any friend, nor foe. His syllabus is incredibly unclear. ZERO grades were entered into canvas all semester. HE LOST 2/3 of my exam scores, I had no idea until I saw my final grade posted as an F. Lectures are boring and REPETITIVE. Attendance and reading is necessary. He is unhelpful and unbothered. Steer clear y'all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst teacher of my adult life... and I've been in school a long time. He is extremely unkind, unhelpful, and entirely unclear with his expectations. The tests are based off of information from FIVE DIFFERENT TEXTS. There is no way of knowing how to study from the texts. When you ask for help, he is unwilling. Lectures are unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: prof jones is an absolute sweetheart, but i'm going to be honest with you, i went to like maybe five lectures max. it was hard with covid and everything, and he rambled on a lot and it was hard to keep up with him and take notes. i ended up getting a B+ somehow anyway, so idk. i wouldn't take him, but he's very sweet!

3 exams; 2 are given in last 4 weeks ; biweekly "discussions" are actually essays. highly lecture, not organized; he repeats himself constantly. lectures don't correlate with readings. Tests are on lecture material; No feedback on essays or test, you never know how you are doing in class. total of 13 graded items.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny guy and chill

Lectures for this class can be useless and very boring. Lots of group papers so take this class with people you know. He grades the cases kind of hard so just put some thought into them and refer to his outline and you'll be fine. Sometimes he says kind of problematic stuff and it's so funny, he's very entertaining.

Easy grader. Readings in chapter were given for extra credit, weekly lectures were about 30mins-1hr and you could play them on 2x speed which made them even shorter. There's a few weekly assignments but they are small and easy to do well in, discussion post, 5 question quizzes (you can typically find the answer by searching the online textbook).

Paul Dowling has a great sense of humor and tries to make his classes fun and engaging. That said, I didn't actually learn much taking from him. Tests are straight forward, as are the assignments. Read the assigned text if you really want to learn.

1) learn the sim from the get go; it will save you pain/frustration later. 2) Plan on 3-4 hours of study before each test; use slide shows and READ the book. 3) Don't sweat in-class quizzes, just briefly read the articles. 4) Use the search feature in the e-book to locate answers faster for online quizzes. 5) overall moderate, but doable, workload.

Paul was very helpful. Always willing to review a paper before it was turned in. Easy to reach him if you'd like.  lectures can be long and boring and he admits the material isn't that great. Tries to spice it up a bit with some stuff from his marketing class. The tests are hard. Harder than they should be. But he grades easy on other stuff.

The outline in the syllabus does not make since. You think you understand how the course works and what is expected then you take an exam that makes no since. The exams are 60% of your grade, and the study guides dont help you at all. (AND ANYTHING COULD BE ON IT!) Homework assignements are easy and tedious. But they do not out way the exams, and if you dont do well on them you cant catch up no matter how hard you work.  Poor class structure.
Hard class. Could never figure out when lecture started and when he was done talking about all the 'interesting' things he found in the Economist that weekend.

One of the best marketing professors! His lectures were always interesting and engaging. He does a great job at keeping the class organized and easy to follow. He cares about his students and is always willing to help. Be prepared to participate during discussions if you want a good grade. Definitely recommend Professor Dolifka for this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Dolifka was an amazing professor for this being only his 2nd semester teaching here. His lectures were interesting and engaging. The assignments were straightforward, 4 MBA case preps, 1 quiz, a simulation and a group project. However, participation matters when it comes to discussing the cases, and attendance isn't mandatory but encouraged.

David is an incredible professor and really cares about his students. Every class felt engaging with discussions, and the lectures were very interesting to listen to. Participation is a big part of the grade, so make sure to participate! I highly recommend taking this class overall.

I am not one to write reviews, but David absolutely deserves one. He is amazing! It's so apparent he cares about his students. He loves what he does, and you can tell through the way he teaches. My only advice is to read the syllabus!! If you don't, you will be lost. Attend class, his lectures (and your grade) are worth it.

Professor Dolifka was amazing! He was very generous with the case studies and very thoughouly explained them. His lectures are very easy to follow and the discussions in class are lead by him and fun to talk about with the class. The simulation project at the end of the semester was super engaging and the competition aspect was awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: David is one of the more engaging professors I have come across. Often times I dread going to class, but I always pushed to make it to his class. He is young and understands his students and their ways of learning.

Professor Dolifka is truly one of my favorite professors I've ever had (hence me adding him to rate my professor.) He's so smart and engaging and you can tell he really cares about his students and what he teaches. He also connects everything to current topics and things that are going on in the world, and he's just a rly cool guy. Thank you Prof!

THE CLASS WAS ECE 1240! 10/10. He makes difficult content easily digestible. He accepts work no matter how late it is. He's also very nice and easy to work with, super lenient. He recognizes us for our skills and makes us feel seen. Easily the best professor I've had so far. If I could take every engineering class with him I would. Highly recommend
I loved him. He was so funny and he actually seemed to enjoy teaching. I would take his lab again.

He taught the lab portion of BME-2100. The lab portion is fantastic in my opinion. The activities are fun and helpful for the class. My lab TA was awesome and was also very helpful. Dr. Christensen is incredibly nice and involved in the lab.

He was extremely nice in lab. Pretty much all you could hope for, he is very willing to help his students however he can, and is very good at explaining concepts. His grading is pretty lienent as long as you clearly demonstrate that you know what is going on.

He is a super nice and is always present in the lab section of this class. His TA's are the one leading the lab (which are really straightforward) but he is available to come in if someone needs help, he is super nice and knowledgeable and knows how to teach. I would take a lab from him again. The lab grade raises your grade at the end too!

Dr. Christensen is an amazing teacher. He teaches with Dr. Macleod (who loves to hear himself speak), but go to Christensen for any questions, he will help you understand so much better. He in incredibly knowledgeable, and loves to help you learn. For Fund 2, READ THE BOOK, reading quizzes expect you to have thoroughly read the chapter.

Dr. Christensen is fantastic. He's really friendly and an amazing teacher. I learned so much from him because he actually put in the time to teach each student one to one. He taught with Rob MacLeod for this class, but Dr. Christensen was better at teaching. I also had him for lab and he never made me feel like I was stupid. I absolutely loved him.

Lecture videos are outdated, some being 4+ yrs old. There is no study guide for the exams, and while readings are presented as optional or extra credit, a significant portion of the exam material is based on the textbook. The exams were hard due to the specificity of the questions and the lack of a study sheet. Felt very unorganized

overall he is very okay. he will absolutely make some sort of HR violating comment towards you, but i think its more in a way of trying to connect with "gen z". very lecture heavy but content isnt hard. sometimes annoying busy work but nothing too bad. tests are kinda hard because a lot of it is irrelevant stuff usually.

Chill guy, but he makes certain comments every now and again that leave you going ??? He gives the vibes of being older but trying to keep up with Gen Z trends. He's a good professor and knowledgeable but his lectures were all over the place. His study guide was also very broad and not really helpful, and still confused on what to study for.

He rambles a lot and gets off topic. Don't go to his lectures. You won't learn anything. My only pro is that he does seem caring, though, besides the offensive comments he makes every once in a while. Those can be off-putting. His tests are also filled with questions and concepts he doesn't really teach about. Very group project-based.

This course is just MKTG 3040, but if you said the word "international" once in a while.  Anything new I learned was from reading the textbook, which he never used or referenced. The professor often used outdated content. Tests were on his rambling lectures. Easy class, funny guy, but this didn't make up for the lack of content or class structure.

Paul is great. He is very caring and loves to talk about his family. He rambles a little but it's from a place of interest and wanting to share. Smart book assignments suck. He gives super clear criteria on the group papers and its easy to do well on them, especially because he will mark up a draft for you if you just ask.

Paul is a cool and funny guy, but he can ramble on during lectures sometimes. His way of teaching won't be for everyone, but overall, as long as you do the group papers and assignments, you'll do fine. He offers good extra credit opportunities and gives good feedback. It's hard to pay attention in his class sometimes, but is also interesting.

This class requires students to participate proactively in order to succeed. The exams are hard, but as long as you pay attention in class and do all the readings, you will be good. The group projects are what really matter, which have higher proportion in grading. He is a humorous lecturer and an easy-going person as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Paul is a good guy but terrible professor. He would ramble on and on about things that didn't matter very much. I stopped going a month into the semester. I reviewed the content he posted because lecture was worthless. Easy class for the international credit but don't expect to learn anything worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Spends half of each class talking about nonsense. Rambles about personal experiences more than course material. Group projects are assigned without any instruction, and are graded as if we are supposed to know everything. Really disappointing, a nice guy but a bad professor. Would not recommend

This class was good. The grading criteria was very clear. The three papers are described well and easy to get a good grade when following the example documents. The midterm and final were difficult because they ask questions like "what did the professor think was the most important _" and the options were all things we talked about being important.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Paul is unironically funny at times and he goes on long tangents but he is very enthusiastic about what he teaches. Pick a good group for the group papers because they are long but not difficult if everyone does their part. Mostly graded on group papers with 2 exams and a couple easy assignments per week. Pretty easy A if you just do the homework

Paul is a great guy and I liked his class - he can get a bit off topic during lectures, but he keeps class mostly entertaining with his funny remarks. Choose a good group as you have to write multiple papers. Exams aren't hard as long as you read through the study guide and pay attention in class as he'll point out exam questions.

Professor Dowling is entertaining and wants everyone to learn. He can be all over the place in his lectures, so sometimes reviewing the information yourself can be useful in the long run. You must do group case studies so pick a good group. Otherwise, the class is fun and fairly straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I'll admit the lectures drag because sometimes the professor can get off-topic, but all the test questions are in his lectures. He doesn't use the textbook for questions so really, just show up and listen/take notes and you'll do fine on the tests. His study guide also has everything you need to know to get a good grade on the test.

His course as mediocre. In college, you'll have to go through some mediocre classes along the way which is fine. But the part that infuriated me about his course was that there is content on each exam that you in no way, shape, or form went over in the lectures or readings. So even if you put in work your grade still might suffer.

Professor Dowling is one of the nicest and encouraging professors I've had at the University of Utah. I would definitely recommend taking his online MKTG 5000 course . I can't judge the in-person course since I didn't take that but overall, the professor is just great and nice. The discussions are engaging and the course simulation is really fun!

This professor loves to be difficult. His grading is tough and he has strict requirements when completing assignments. The tests are difficult and lectures are painful. One of the worst professors I've had as he talks about nonsense every lecture. I would recommend taking a different class is possible.

Discussion and Quizzes are easy, but the 2 exams are tough. He doesn't have a study guide for his exams which sucks because there are ?'s on the exams that were never covered. There is also a very annoying game u have to play that's worth a lot of your grade. If you get anything less than 10/10, it hurts your grade quite a bit. Ok class at best.

Paul is very funny, he comes off as 'grandfatherly'. I really enjoy his morning calss and I will be taking advanced marketing classes from him next semester. I really enjoy his teaching style. He will clearly tell you what parts of the chapters in the book to read and what will be on the test. The DESB is hard, so don't expect anything less.

Paul knows a lot about international marketing. The problem is, he doesn't teach it to you. His "lectures" consist of showing international ads just for fun, or going through each chapter in the book and telling you what pages to read and what pages to skip for the test. There are also group papers, but it's an easy grade if you show up and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Not a bad class. He doesn't even read your papers or discussion posts. Pretty much just gives full credit for everything. Super easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Very lazy and unorganized professor. Very dumb, you don't see your grade all semester, he doesn't upload it to canvas. Cry baby, just bashes Trump and Republicans for a good 15-20 min. every class. Get over it, he won. Doesn't teach, just reads from the book of what he wants you to know. Fun subject, but he doesn't teach it to you.

Very, very, VERY unorganized professor. He will have things on the exam that you didn't cover, so prepare for that. His online lecture videos are outdated, he says he has a study guide on them but in all actuality there is no study guide.  Oh and that stupid marketing game is worth a lot of points, each point is like 1%-2%, and the game is trash.

He was an amazing professor. You do have to do a lot of studying to pass his tests but I learned so much. He's definitely one of the professors I have learned the most from. He clearly follows the textbook and tells you what stuff to ignore in the textbook if it's not important. He applies real world examples to all concepts and is extremely clear.
