Professor Dowling is always giving us examples on the principles we learned in class, and he gives us spaces to imagine an international business development. However, not all of his slides shown in class are posted on online learning system for us to review, and he does not give us times and teaching assistants to review after class.

He is a nice guy but he is not good in teaching , first he makes the class very very hard what he explaines in his lecturs are different from the text book, you have to attend his class and the worst ever thing is he is the only professor who is teaching BUS 2900 , DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM, plus he does not help when you ask him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great professor with interesting lecture components. For the most part the lectures were him just skimming the book and telling you what not to read, which was cool. Don't screw around with bad groups for the group project though, you will be stuck with them for the whole semester even if he is forgiving about bad partners.

His class is pretty interesting, but course load somewhat demanding. Tests are hard,  and alot of questions come from his lectures. (the professor said in class that __) Business plan is not too bad if you have a good group otherwise its a nightmare  Just sucks its  at 7:30am and he is the only option.

Surprisingly this class was a breeze. Material is very straight forward. His "study guides" are rubbish. It's no study guide at all, but you really don't need it. Lectures can be long and hard to pay attention for. He is helpful and will meet out of class to give good feedback.

Paul is a really nice guy. Makes himself very available to help out. Will proofread your papers to ensure you get 100%. Tries to make the subject matter more interesting. All that being said, class is a bit dry and tests are harder than you'd expect for a 2000 level class.

Paul is a good professor. Sometimes I felt like his class lectures were wasting time (for the first 2 months of class he still took about 10-15 minutes to ask questions about the syllabus, and if no one responded we would just wait). He is always there to help! He wants his students to be successful and there are great bits of info in his classes.

He was a great professor! He was enthusiastic, available to consult, and had a strong knowledge of course material. However, he had a tendency to go on tangents and get off topic, which made it difficult to take lecture notes. His course is based on many points, so assignments and tests are important
The class is boring. The only exciting thing is the trade show. Don't take it if you don't have to...If you have a choice, take a different class. The class is extremely outdated.

The class is semi interesting, but if you're going to take it then take it from him. Course load isn't too demanding. Tests are hard, but if you come to class and study like a normal college person does then you should be good. Business plan is easy make sure you get a good group. Prof is interesting and knows a ton about the stuff.
Long lectures from the text book.

Dowling is very helpful!  The tests are difficult, but if you study hard you can get an A.  The business plan was difficult, but really helpful in learning the subject.  If you have any questions, he will help you out.  He is also a wonderful resource for internships and writes wonderful letters of recommendation.

Paul was a great professor. His lectures were fun and interesting. His assignments and business plan were pretty simple and he lines out the resources to do good on them. He also pre-grades them so I would take advantage of that if you want an A. His tests can be tough, but if you take good notes in class and study then you'll do fine.

Paul is an interesting professor.  He uses a computer simulation that you do in groups as a huge portion of your grade, but tests aren't worth as much as in a normal class.  He definitely likes the subject, but be aware this class is like a continuation of MKTG 3010, think of it as an applied marketing class and you'll be better prepared for it.

Dowling is awesome!  He helped me a ton and is pretty lenient on the business plan as long as you show you put in some effort.  The tests are hard, but he goes over them with you if you go to office hours and he really wants his students to do well.  Definitely attend class, most test questions come from lectures.  Worth getting to know.

I received an A- I believe largely to my participation. I was always outgoing in class and contributed. I did decent on quizzes and tests, and good on assignments, but definitely be sure and participate.

I thought Pro Dowling was really easy to work with. I had some issues with my group for the business proposal and he helped me out a lot.  The business proposal seems like a lot of work but it is really easy to get a good grade on and he doesn't expect very much and you can turn it in early and he will go over it to guarantee an A. Clear tests

This class is awful! Lectures are a repeat of what you read in the book with little new info to contribute. Worse, the tests are poorly written with questions drawing from minute facts, they don't test understanding, just reading retention.Total class test avg: D! The business plan isn't bad, just inane. Get an A on it, you'll need the points!

Would have liked a better teacher.  He rambles on sometimes.  His tests are ridiculous, not necessarily difficult, but there are a lot of ambiguous answers.  Does not curve. His lectures are very powerpoint intensive.  All in all, find another professor.
no comment

The guy's class was interesting but a third of the class was close to failing, and it was near impossible to get an A.  Tests in the class were a huge joke and were full of questions that make you guess. In addition to his lovely test writing skills,  he makes you complete this intricate intl. business plan that's a total waste of time.

Makes you complete a massive research project that takes forever. He will not work with you at all for make-up exams and is not willing to negotiate with students for a change in the test dates. Assigns tests close to holidays so you have to pull an all nighter the day you get back from a holiday weekend. Makes it difficult to arrange to leave town
Dowling was nice but not as much passion and experience as the last guy (kaplan), we can do better but it's an easy A.
Paul is a good teacher he does anything he can to make the class as interesting as possible, funny guy to.
I had Paul for Mktg 3010 too and he is such an awesome professor.  His class in interesting and informing and he conducts it in a way to is fun for all.

Very good instructor! His lectures taught a lot of relevant and practical information. If you want to do well in his class make sure you know the vocabulary terms for the chapters, attend classes and especially attend the video & guest-speaker ones. If I had to take another marketing class I'd definately take it from this guy.
Easily the greatest course and professor I've had during my four years at the university. Drager is extremely humble, honest, and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lindsey is one of the best professors at this school. Universally beloved, and always available to give feedback and advice.

Passionate, funny, clearly knows her stuff. Got me way more interested in narrative theory than I ever thought I'd be. Texts were really interesting, reasonable amount of reading. Loved the class discussions. Basically, do the work and participate and you'll get an A. Definitely take her class if you're a writer or even if you just love books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor. Very willing to work with anybody on their grade. Accepts late work and works hard to create a supportive community of writers within her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She is amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Drager was very resourceful and knowledgeable with the content.  She encourages & mainly let the students run most of the class through discussions.  Her assignments (discussion posts) were easy & the feedback she gives is very detailed & thorough.  Her final is also easy as you analyze a horror story or write one.

Genuinely my favorite professor I've taken from in my college career. The short stories and books in her curriculum are fascinating and interesting. Outside and inside of class, she shows great concern for her students mental health and well being. Her feedback is extensive and extremely helpful. She is so down to earth and funny. Take Drager!

Drager is EXTREMELY sharp. She'll take what any student says during class discussion, and then she'll run it through the lens of narrative theory. This is effective in getting the students to see the same aspects of narrative theory applied from different points of view. By the end of the class, it's almost impossible to not just "get it."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Drager is absolutely fantastic.  She gives amazing lectures and is very encouraging during discussions.  During the first half of the semester, you read a few short stories each week and write a weekly 500-word response to them.  During the second half, you read a new novel every other week and write responses.  The responses are very easy.

Lindsey Drager is my favorite professor at the U. Never enjoyed writing and reading so much. The best thing about her is her feedback. She is good at giving really great constructive feedback and I know I am a better writer because of it. Most importantly she cares about what she is teaching and that is super evident from her teaching methods.
Amazing professor who always makes sure you get good feedback and feel heard in class. No complaints.
Trolls get out of here Professor Drager is a star! Highly recommend!!!

Lindsey Drager is an amazing professor who crafts extremely effective lectures. The discussions are enjoyable and I always left class feeling like I learned something new. I highly recommend taking a course with her.

Drager was a great professor! Graded weekly responses that weren't difficult at all, she provided helpful and encouraging feedback on every single response. The final project is super simple, an analysis on a horror book of your choosing or creating your own horror story. Loved this class.

Ok teacher. Taken via video during covid time. Hybrid. Ok at out of class communication. Ok at assignments and communicating with students. Kinda fun. Not the most personable. Good connection if you are going into the play business or theatre business. I thought I was, and she gave me good resources and websites and people and colleges.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The only thing I really would have wanted was to hear more of her lecturing, as the class was heavily dealing in class discussion, because she's brilliant! Drager (as she lets students call her) truly reads anything she makes you write, enough to bring them up weeks later and get the right student. Incredible teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Took one class from her, liked her so much I took another the next semester. I'd take another if I had the option. She's kind, smart, funny, and gives incredibly good feedback on work. I wish all my professors were like her.
Spent most of the semester frustrated. It took weeks to get feedback. Didn't feel heard or seen as a student by the professor, both in the class content and in interactions with her.

Great if you don't care much about writing, not so great if you do. I was coddled. Didn't get great feedback. I didn't really learn anything, and I hadn't even thought about playwriting before this class. Overall just super frustrating.

I took Drager's class twice. Both times I took her class were great. She cares so much about her students and is willing to work with you as much as possible. She's very understanding and caring. She's a professor that will always make sure you're learning someone new. Usually 2-3 writing workshops and reading. Easy class. 10/10, HIGHLY recommend.

Professor McNutt taught well but I found his class fairly hard for an entry level course. The tests are very difficult and count for a lot of your final grade. However, if you went to office hours to discuss your test grade you could receive three points of extra credit, which was very helpful.

Wasn't the best professor. The grading was fairly harsh, simple mistakes resulted in a whole point taken off. The tests themselves also were very vague and often asked questions that required extra practice on those problems that we didn't have access to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were fine, however there was little you do to practice the material outside of class when he did poorly. This professor was very vague on what you need to know for Paper Tests, which counted for 56% of your grade. Literally gave a "list of topics" before tests. I think I only did okay because of prior experience with Python.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mcnutt is an excellent professor. His courses sparked my interest in programming. He has a humorous teaching style, and explains concepts thoroughly in an easy-to-understand way. He also offers extra credit for attending office hours.

Professor Shephard absolutely knows the material and how to make it engaging. There is a lot of reading every week, but it's quite enjoyable, and the class is best when you participate in the discussion. Be prepared for him to go on a lot of tangents, but they are usually related to the overall discussion and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very fun and informative. Professor Shephard was a very interesting and knowledgeable lecturer. This class was very reading heavy and only had a few assignments. We had a discussion once a week and two papers worth a big portion of the grade. Overall, I really enjoyed this class and would recommend it to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Goes on many tangents that are unrelated to the course material or the required readings. Unclear in his speaking and uses a lot of filler words.

To the three people who gave poor reviews, I want you to know that commenting about the way someone speaks is not only an ad hominem attack, but it's also downright mfn rude. Also, read the course description and syllabus when enrolling so you know what the class is going to cover? Do you NOT do that? READING about the class EXPLAINS the class.

Professor Shepard made me think about different forms of literature in ways that I've never truly thought of before. He engages the class in a very charming and humorous way, and I personally have had long conversations with him outside of class about the materials in the class. He's genuinely passionate, about what he teaches. Highly recommend.

As long as you bring passion and care with you into the classroom, Dr. Shephard's courses are the most ardent and enjoyable classes that anyone can partake in. I have had 2 classes with him, and both courses taught me so much about English Academia and its way of thought.

He taught us ONLY about steampunk in an African American Literature course. We read around 12 books, all written by white authors until the last two weeks of the semester. Terrifyingly boring lectures that go nowhere, terrible at communicating, and he takes months to grade short papers. Genuinely recommend taking any other class.
Absolutely horrible and rude. When I tried to get extra help outside of class, he said "umm" every sentence and provided no foundational feedback on how to improve my essays. I would not recommend.

This professor is very kind and inclusive. I learned a lot of interesting things in this course. There are a few papers and discussion responses. It is an English class so there is a lot of reading. Overall, this class and this professor were good. I strongly recommend.

Wonderful class! He teaches with passion and you can really tell he cares about the subject matter! He's super involved and treats you as people. I couldn't recommend a teacher enough. He has a tendency to say "so basically um" every beginning of his sentences. I wish I had not taken this class. The material was not bad, but how we were tested made no sense. Avoid this professor at all costs. Just posts video lectures from 3 years ago, and doesn't even organize them in a way that is easy for you to access and follow. I emailed him once about my term paper, but I still haven't received a response. Do not take him, at all costs.

Linke's class was difficult and sometimes a little dry, but it's population geography and demographic studies. Just write what you know/earned and you'll get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, and I did not find the lectures very helpful or engaging. In fact I found them hard to follow and confusing. I attended every class, yet I can't say I learned anything meaningful besides some definitions and how to use the library resources for the research paper.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Sweetheart. Gracious grader, will work with you, and adores his subject material. He cultivated a safe classroom atmosphere; although it could get boring at times. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I took his Austen lecture and it was my ALL-TIME FAVORITE class. We had to read all 6 novels, the class is lecture heavy and he does speak for the majority of it but he is very funny and the classes pass by quickly. 2 essays for the Midterm and 3 for the Final, sounds overwhelming but the essays are quite short. TAKE HIS CLASS.

I really really loved Professor Franta, and I would highly recommend taking any class you can from him. He gave me great feedback on my essays, and I got a better grade every time which showed how much that feedback helped me improve my writing.

reviews.comment: Professor Franta is a really good lecturer and his classes are always fun. He really cares about his students. There isnt too much homework besides reading, and he goes over everything essential in class.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Nice guy who knows his stuff but the dude likes to talk. I'm cool with lecture-based classes but sometimes he'd go off on a tangent.
Really long, dry lectures. Occasional pop quizzes, but he doesn't care TOO much about actual class participation. I've watched a lot of Netflix in there.

He enjoys the subject but doesn't make it accessible to students. Doesn't know how to handle participation, so he doesn't encourage it. The class 70% lengthy lecture, 20% in-class reading, 10% small group discussion. Doesn't know how to view a text from standpoints other than his own.

Franta is intelligent and witty. His lectures are casual and interesting. If you are in class, you get credit for the pop quizzes. The midterms, essays and finals are relatively easy as long as you've been to class and paid attention. He offers re-writes on all assignments and is always willing to meet with you and help. Every chance to succeed.

Professor Franta is a great guy. He's intelligent, super willing to work with students (yes, even with extensions), and I highly recommend taking a class from him if you don't mind a lot of lecture. He clearly knows his stuff, but he does sometimes ramble on.

Franta is a fairly good teacher. If you don't like the material to begin with, you will probably hate this class. He's VERY dry and LOVES to hear himself talk. That being said, he grades really easily. Don't come tired, you WILL fall asleep. He's a fairly good looking older man though.

He's a good professor he knows his stuff.  However, his teaching style is very dry.  Very little class participation.  If you come to class you'll know exactly what's on the tests.  Pretty easy A for me.
Really enjoyed the class, and would recommend anyone to take the class from Franta.
I loved the literature we read and Franta made the lectures very interesting.  He is funny and intelligent.  I would take another class from him.

I'm pretty sure I already left something (has it been removed?).  Andy Franta is against censorship.  He would want my comments about him to be open to the world.  May Andy live on victorious and with plenty.
Loved the way the material was presented and tested on -- coincided perfectly.   Have taken multiple courses from this professor and have been consistently impressed.
Knowledgeable, helpful, and nice to look at too.
Tests and quizzes are easy if you go to class. Discussions are usually stimulating and fun. He's a great, young, hip teacher and I'd take another class from him.

Should 100% be 5 credits (4 minimum)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Horrible professor! The class was fun and interesting but Professor Dryer is extremely demeaning if you are not interested in going to law school. Prof. Dryer is the best professor I've ever had. The class itself was great but he made it that much better. He really knows what he's talking about and explains it clearly. It's intimidating to talk aloud because you have to stand strong on your point. The class is great and fun and so is Prof. Dryer

Professor Dryer is incredibly smart.  Classes are fun and he gets you thinking like not many other teachers can do.  THe only drawback is that since he's a lawyer, he talks like a lawyer, so if you have a point to make you have to hold it for a long time.  It's my favorite class though, i HIGHLY recommend Dryer!
Duncan is a phenomenal professor, I loved this class and learned a lot. He is super understanding and clear with his expectations, and gives great feedback on essays

He was awesome. He is a very young and knowledgeable about the workload of students, so he is understanding. The lectures were highly engaging and he lets the students guide how the class goes. Participation is very important, and he values and incorporates feedback well. I would definitely recommend. Not too much Homework.

Duncan was very thorough with his expectations of the class. He would let the students pick the topic of each lecture and would go off with what the students would talk about. He is very knowledgeable with is coursework and was always there to help students out. 100% recommend

This class is very simple and the teacher is extremely chill, he is super understanding and attendance is not mandatory. I would definitely would recommend to take this class if you are planning to be a communication major.

No official book for Comm. 3030 Social Responsibility. Though readings are provided from different research articles. Duncan went with whatever topics the class voted on at the beginning of the semester. He knows his stuff and is very intelligent. Concepts are well thought out and presented. Not to mention he's a hot/ hansome student professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor I have ever had!! She teaches so well and doesn't just read of the slides. She takes time to know her students and is genuinely so sweet. I took her QAMO 2010 class and I understood the material very well and she also gave practice tests for exams. I would 100% recommend taking her class she's amazing!

She's always ready to answer all the questions I have. No need to purchase textbook because her lecture videos are very helpful to understand the material. She always gives good feedback and very easy going. Highly recommend her class and she makes such difficult topics so much easier!!
Cares alot, i found the material relativley easy. Grading is clear, you get 2 chances on all the quizzes. Problems sets due every couple weeks but they are only like 5 questions with 1-3 parts each.
Best professor in the Economics department when it comes to teaching. Amazing lectures and cares about the students. Makes even the most difficult topics easy to understand.

Very easy grader but also very good instructor. Best instructor I have had in college very clear and makes any complex idea easy to understand. Also very easy grader so you not only come out with an A but also understand the material very well.

Gives great lectures and was flexible with me during exam time. She goes over everything in the lectures and does plenty of examples so your not having too much trouble when it comes to projects and exams. The reading is recommended but I feel her lectures do a good enough job at covering everything. I heavily recommend her class.
I actually took POLS 2100 but he was amazing! Only have three assignments a week of a discussion, short writing assignment, and a video journal. Pretty easy and would highly recommend!

Professor Dunne makes a three hour lecture very interesting. There are weekly quizzes and writing assignments that are very clear and easy. reviews.comment: I took POLS 5750 online, and I really enjoyed it. Each week had 3 assignments (a quiz, a discussion post, and a reading summary) that were easy and not time-consuming. reviews.comment: One of the easiest professors I have had at the U. He's very easy when grading and always answers my questions. I took his ESL class at SLCC and now his business class at the U. Definitely recommend his class. Very easy and caring professor!

Gordon Dunne is a great professor, and I learned so much from his class. There is a lot of reading, and there is a quiz and discussion each week about what was covered in the reading. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dunne was a great professor and I could tell he cared about what he was teaching. Each module consists of a reading, discussion, and quiz. Professor Dunne was one of the best professors I have had in my time at the U. While it was a three hour class, the lectures were engaging to make them doable. His grading policy is very clear and he allows some leniency with your schedule. Overall he was an amazing professor who clearly cared about his students.

Awesome professor and very responsive to emails given other online courses I've taken. Super lenient when it came to due dates. Two term papers, weekly quizzes and a final. So glad I took Mr. Dunne's class. Often Politica Science can be dry and dense subject, and yet, Mr. Dunne manage to keep our lectures dynamic, engaging, thought and discussion provoking. Higly recommend.

reviews.comment: Very smart and lectures well. Would definitely reccomend his EU class

Prof Dunne is very knowledgeable and makes this class very palatable even for those who don't know much about the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Dunne is really great and this class is super interesting. He cares and understands that we all have lives outside of school, too. Love this class.

I really enjoyed taking this course from Professor Dunne. He accepted late work, was lenient, and was very understanding about it as well. Because he had a clear grading criteria (a reading quiz and discussion weekly, 2 papers, and a final paper) and cared about us as students, I made the extra effort to gain knowledge from the course material.
Easy grader. Accepts late work even. There's just a lot of reading, and a decent amount of writing.

reviews.comment: Prof. Dunne is one of the greatest teachers I have had at the U. He is clearly very knowledgeable about his field, and passionate about teaching. Prof Dunne was honestly one of the best professors I have come by at the U so far. Super caring & understanding & really made sure we were learning the material & not suffering through it. reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dugar is awesome! Highly recommend him for microeconomics. He communicates very clearly with students and wants them to succeed in his class. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He goes by Suhb. Fantastic teacher and knows his stuff very well. This is a tough tough class and uses lots of analytical reasoning. I worked so much in this course than in any other classes. Now I think I know how to think strategically. Go for it!

reviews.comment: Professor was entertaining and very knowledgable about the content presented in class. Sometimes I felt overloaded with classes but exams reflected this course's content covered in class. It was a challenging class but you'd generally learn a big deal out of it.

Film 2110, so much studying is required to do well on his exams, a good portion of what was tested are things not covered in his slide decks, but mentioned during his very long spiels in class. Every day I wake up and pray to god that I am sick so I don't have to go to this class. It is the biggest waste of time I have ever been a part of and the incessant rambling of the professor is so mind-numbing that I fall asleep every class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CARE ABOUT YOUR GPA.

reviews.comment: Sam is great, he's very personal.  There is not much homework, our grade was determined by in class participation, and tests.  He would show movies in class, and if you weren't there to watch them you weren't keeping up with the class.  He's very knowledgeable and loves Tolkien.  As for textbooks, you could easily get them from the library.

This class was absolutely fantastic.  Sam knows his stuff and obviously loves the material (this was a horror film class).  You can't breeze through and get an easy A, but if you put in the work you will do well.  He will work with you if you need to make sure you make it.  I cannot recommend him highly enough.

Sam is, without a doubt, my favorite professor that I've had at this school. He is crazy knowledgable about anything film theory, or film history. He also works very hard to make sure students understand the material. I met with him multiple times to get extra help, and he was happy to do it. He gives great handouts on lectures too. Fantastic prof.
He makes an effort and expects his students to as well. He knows what he is talking about and pays attention to his students.

Fantastic professor. I'm a huge film nerd so I loved every second of his class. If you care about analysis you could be very bored in his class. But if you're even slightly interested in film analysis, he is insanely knowledgable and can teach you a lot. He's very passionate and fun. You have to work. He's always willing to help you on your papers.

Sam seems like a pretty nice guy. The subject he teaches (film history) can be boring at times, but he pauses lecturing to answer any questions, and he can e-mail you lecture notes if you miss class. Tests are hard, so watch the movies carefully and take good notes.  Also, the book is totally unnecessary.

Attendance isnt required everyday, but there are a couple classes that she does in class participation activities without telling the class.

Don't take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She was a great professor! You have to write many papers, review articles, and a couple of group and individual presentations; so be prepared for that. There is a lot of busy work and assignments, but you learn a lot and the material is interesting to learn. At times, the lectures can get a little wordy with the length of the PowerPoints

I learned a lot in this class. Definitely needed the book with me to give me the detailed information she leaves out in the lectures. Doing the study guides helps a ton and she lets you turn in assignments 1 week prior for feedback-definitely recommend that. I could've gotten a better grade if I tried harder.

You can tell she really knows her stuff and it is an important subject. Beats you to death with PPt slides. As long as you go through the practice problems on the online tool a ton before the test you should do okay on it. There is a lot of memorization. Group projects are involved.
Canvas was a complete mess. Many assignments' due dates were changed.

She was very helpful if you ever needed anything and we got like one assignment a month. The class overall was easy, but it is hard to remember all the notes that she gives (it's A LOT); therefore, making it hard to get a good score on tests.

She makes this class very difficult to succeed in. I would recommend taking nutrition from a different professor. I had pages of notes every class because she does not post power points online. Class average for the first test was 62%. Lots of busy work.

Assignments and online quizzes were easy. You have to go to class to get because she does not provide PPT online. I would say around 25% of test material comes from in class and can't really be found in book. She's very nice and I like her style of teaching.
She changed PPT too fast!

Dr. Klure is a fantastic teacher whom I highly recommend. He made the class fun and interesting. Beware of a semester-long group project- it's pretty easy but annoying if you get bad partners. His tests were difficult (all short answer), so you have to study hard for them. If you memorize everything on the slides you should be good. Lots of EC.
Great professor, you can tell he cares. He is a good lecturer and class is engaging.

He's overall pretty cool. If you try to access extra help or need time for assignments he's like 50/50 willing to help you—definitely don't come in begging for a grade drop or retake without good reason though. Spectacularly terrible teacher. Test material is easy, but he will CONSTANTLY include double answers, and try to trip you up on semantics/insignificant discrepancies. Docks large amounts of points on written assignments for seemingly no reason, and it's an online class, so he could care less about responding to grading questions. Avoid this man.

It's such a great class! Only two exams, a two page essay and a four page essay. They're both conveniently easy.  You are put into a posse and the people in that group engage and discuss specific topics. I would highly recommend this class for an easy credit!

Bad teacher. At first you may like him, but he is extremel unhelpful. No sympathy for his students. This is an online course, so you would expect some lean way. But no. I don't understand professors like this one. He acts as though he is soo involved with the students, but when trying to email him I received annoyed emails back with little words.

Eggert's class was very dry. He gave assignment all worth 1 or 2 points for the most part and then 2- 100 point exams in which he graded unfairly and extremely harshly. His TA was also very harsh, almost over the top. This class is not necessarily hard, but you pretty much have to be able to write PhD. level papers to receive a good grade.

Eggert was extremely absent. He was not helpful when I e-mailed him with questions or concerns. For such a fun titled class the content was dry. He only grades two things all semester, which is nice that you have lots of single participation points but when he grades your two tests, it slaughters your grade. No help. Not available or receptive.

Its an easy class. If you need a gen credit take this class. Its online. All you have to do is participate. Hes harsh when he grades your essays, but you only have 2 the entire semester. No exams, but weekly quizzes.

I took this class online. Take it if you need a Gen Ed credit and have no time. 30 minutes of effort per week. It is very participation based. You get full credit for trying. There were 2 papers that were 3 pages each. No tests. He's not a harsh grader on the papers and gives good personal feedback. Communicates really well for an online professor.

Pretty chill class, the final wasn't super consistent with the rest of the tests and materials but if yu go to class and take it seriously you will do fine.  He is pretty cool and posts all powerpoints online.
This class, despite its name, is so boring. I basically didn't go to class the last half of the semester...
Over all he is a pretty cool dude once some rapport has been established. His classes are lecture based, and yes, are open to questions. Very helpful and understanding.

He just goes over the reading in class so if you get it you don't need to come. He's fun because he's so interested in ling. Definitely willing to help and will answer all questions in class. I recommend getting a group together for test though.
Interesting topics for his Bad Words and Taboo Terms course, particularly for anyone working in psychology or anthropology.

This class is super boring!! all we do is lecture every single day.  If you take it drink lots of caffeine prior to class.  It's so hard to make myself come.  Also, the only thing we are graded on is 2 six page papers. it sucks

My homegirl. She was always willing to be flexible and meet with students. She knew her stuff but you can tell that she's just beginning to teach, so she still has a long way to go. She was big on trying things on our own and then going over it together during lecture, which I liked. Grading was kind of weird, but she was always fair. Looots of HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Eichberg is great, she cares a lot for her students and is very approachable. I would definitely take more classes with her. Very clear in lectures and if you do the homework, the exams are easy; whenever you cannot do the homework problems, she would make the time to make sure you understand. She is great!
She was ok she lectures to fast in class and would lecture about theorems that were not worth class time. She was weird about grading with particular things

Not a great lecturer, she would go way too fast half the class and then go off on a tangent explaining a theorem only 1/4 of the class would understand. Nice and accessible outside of class though. Don't be stupid like me - if you go to all the classes and start the homework before the day it's due, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not a great prof. Too much hw, weird about grading, and not great at teaching math. Goes wayyy to fast in class. Be prepared to teach yourself if you have to take her class.
Not a great prof. Cares more about what her students think about her than what they actually learn. Weirdly tough grader about dumb things. Doesnt give formula sheets. Over grades exams.

Rebekah is a phenomenal teacher that is very kind and understanding, she just wants her students to learn and succeed. She is always available to help and always goes the extra mile. Use her daily activity note sheets, take her practice exams, and finish all your homework and the class will be quite easy. She is super chill and relatable.

Like everyone said, shes super chill and teaches semi-good. However, her biggest flaw is the sass and attitude she has when students ask a question. Not all of us have a doctorate in mathematics and we're in class because we have to be not because we actually enjoy calculus. She has the tendency to make us feel dumb. Shes an easy grader though!
She is amazing. Genuinely loves math and is awesome at teaching it. I genuinely just liked her as a person and loved the comments and stories she had. Super willing to help and made calc 1 easy.

Rebekah is a super chill professor and cares greatly about her students and them learning the material. The information in calculus two is hard but she makes it fun to learn about and is super organized. If you get the chance definitely take the class from her.

Dr. Eisenmen requires a lot from you and she expects you to show up and give her your best. If you cant do that then dont waste yours or her time, but if you can then her classes and material will impact, influence, and guide you for many years to come!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very hard with high expectations and little to no guidance.  She was also my adviser.  Never in her office, doesn't return voice mails or emails, constantly losing documents sent to her.  What a joke

By 1995 they were printing T-shirts that said "I survived Eisenman" - THAT IS HOW HARD SHE IS.  She expects perfection.  She is one of hardest professors. She comes off - standoffish..but make appts w her & get to know her. It will help BIG TIME!  you MUST put a LOT of study time into her classes PERIOD.

This was by far the hardest class I had to take for my ESS degree. Dr. Eisenman is tough. Don't miss any of her study sessions. But if you do attend them, make sure you have questions for her. She's more willing to help you understand things and takes the time to explain it. Her tests are very difficult.

This prof was absolutely horrible.  Expectations were not clear and nor were her teaching methods.  I had friends in the same course with another instructor and it was clear who ended up much happier at the end of the semester.  Definately avoid this prof at all cost.

The format of the class is completely unfair for the students enrolled. Read, present, and write a paper based on everyone's presentations and yours. Isnt a teacher supposed to teach? Felt like I was doing busy work the entire time and didnt have time to work. Knowledge is dependent on other people. She's lazy, waste of time and money.
very tough teacher and not very nice.
No Comments
No Comments

Took paleobiology. Tony (Ekdale) is a great teacher. If you attend class and lab and memorize like hell, then you'll be fine. You'll do LOTS of drawing of extinct animals. The field trips rock! Time consuming but great class. Tony knows fossils!

Great professor! The class isn't necessarily easy, but I wouldn't say it's hard. The first exam is the hardest, and the first 6 lectures are the most uninteresting, but after that the class is interesting! He always has a handout, so make sure you get one! All the test questions are in bold on the handouts or he tells you. Great class

Great professor, and great person. Extremely knowledgeable about the subjects he talks about and is always willing to work with students and help them in anyway. Tests are pretty hard, study everything he gives you and talks about in lectures, even the little seemingly unimportant things. Creates a fun environment and teaches an awesome class
Professor Ekdale is amazing!  I absolutely loved his class.  He is a great professor, very passionate and interesting.  I would recommend this class to anyone interested in fossils and geology.
This class sucks.  It's suprisingly hard and Ekdale is a pretty average teacher.  He's not much of a speaker and is prone to overusing exclamation points in his handouts.  Man, I hate that.

Coach Emilie is great and puts effort into the class. The material is useful for preparing for internships and interviews but, I felt the workload was heavy for a 1-credit course. Since many take it early in college, some wont appreciate the career prep until later. Overall, helpful class but the assignments could be made to match the credit value.
Worst teacher of all time. Way to many assignments for this one credit class. Stingy and very strict on grading. Never take her. I was forced to.

WAY TOO MUCH WORK FOR A SINGLE CREDIT/NON CREDIT CLASS. it's all easy, but i kid you not it is about 5 assignments a day that all take you way too much time for very little points. like when you spend two hours on an assignment worth 5 points and she docks you 3 of those points because you missed one sentence, it is not ideal. its just annoying tbh

I really loved this class, and I am going to miss her lectures. Attendance does matter, but you will want to go to class because she gives really amazing lectures. Homework and group projects are manageable and reasonable. You can tell she's really passionate about what she does and cares about her students. Take her class!!!

Elle is my favorite professor at the U! Her class is welcoming, and she's very understanding when things come up. She's a true girlboss who knows her stuff, and her stories and opinions are always engaging. Highly recommend!

I took a 3-hour-long discussion-based course and it became my favorite course. Elle is an amazing professor who knows so much and cares so much. Class is not challenging, show up (you'll enjoy it too) and do weekly reflections (just graded on completion not substance), and then do a few group assignments (she gives class time to work on it). LOVED

I love Elle. I took this class with her in Spring of 2023, and I have still not forgotten the sense of peace I felt while being in her class. I loved learning about this subject, and I feel Elle was a great professor/role model to learn from. The college of Social Work at the U needs more instructors like Elle, she is so positively impactful.

Elle was amazing! You have an assignment each week and a group project throughout the semester. Her lectures are absolutely amazing and she really talks about such hard things like child abuse in such a caring way. She has so much experience in the field

Ellie has fantastic lectures that are full of information about her experience working with CPS and the foster care system. The class is easy and Ellie provides great feedback. There is a group project but it is simple to split up. Ellie is a great professor who created a safe environment for each student to share and discuss hard topics.
Nah this was the goat take my boy Emre easiest class in existence i love this guy.

He's a super sweet guy. Class is so boring but he does his best with the lectures. As long as you do the practice test, the exams are exactly like that and you'll be fine. Wants you to succeed and is willing to work with you.
Study Materials are very similar to exams. Cares about your learning and less so about grades. Would highly recommend.

I really liked this guy. He's kind & cares about his students and makes sure they learn what they need. If you're not an OSC major you will find this class boring. I'm in ENTP and found some of this material useful to learn from a business standpoint. He goes deep into material so just make sure to know how to do the hw and you will ace the test.
Really Nice professor. He takes feedback and cares about your learning more than grades.
Very caring but a little disorganized. He accepts feedback from students and tries to get students engaged in class. Makes a lot of practice problems which I enjoyed.

He is such a sweet professor. He really does everything to help you succeed in his class. He tends to overexplain in his lectures and will fill the whole class time, but the lectures are really helpful. The extra explanations really explain the concepts and make it easier to understand. 100% recommend.
Super sweet professor, practice exams are exactly like the test, and attendance isn't mandatory. He genuinely wants his students to succeed.

Professor Ertan is a good teacher; he's just disorganized. It's clear Emre wants students to succeed. He tries his best to really explain why things are done the way they are. If you make the effort to come to class and listen, you'll get something out of it and do well on the six homeworks, two tests, and project paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he actually wants to help students understand the concept unlike other teachers

He is a very kind and caring professor. However, his accent can be hard to understand, and he sometimes overexplains and overcomplicates topics. 2 Exams are 60% of your grade BUT his exam reviews are superrr if not almost exactly like the real exams. It can be a bit hard to listen to him; everyone dozes off in class. Not a bad prof overall

Prof. Ertan was a good professor. The concepts he covered tended to go from being pretty simple to really complex but he was always happy to go over what students needed. You could really tell he cared about his students understanding and put a lot of care into his work.

I had Emilie back in Fall 2023. I LOVED her. The business school is to blame for the amount of homework needed for the class. She is required to assign a lot of homework. The business school has changed almost everything in the curriculum, and made the class farrr more demanding than it was when I took it. She is so nice. Dont blame her for the hw

I think she genuinely wants you to do well which is so important. I will say lectures were boring at times and she tends to get irritated with the students easily which I dont think is the way to go, overall good though.

Proffesor was alright, but there is SO MUCH WORK in this class for it to be a credit/noncredit. It was kind of insane. Not sure if that is Emilie's doing or just what she's required to do but It felt like a waste of time and money. Definitely could have got all of this information in one or two required meetings with my career coach or something.

This class was NOT fun to take. If you meet with your career coach at all, then everything in this class will be information you have already learned. Soooo many assignments for a C/NC class. They can be very time consuming as well. The professor was quite rude sometimes. That being said, this class is an easy credit class.

Not even a bad professor, more just a JOKE of a class. Nothing in this class was necessary, and I dreaded the work in this class more than my actual hard classes. Be prepared to tweak your resume 4 different niche ways for no reason. Such a waste of time. The potential for the curriculum in this class is there; however, executed horribly.

For a pass/fail class, the workload is insane. I have more homework in this class than I have in any other class. She gives so many nonsense assignments that just take up way too much time. Straight up worst class I have ever taken. Genuinely worst teacher I've ever had. She really sucks. Do not take her at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A one-credit class but has three assignments due almost every day?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Emilie is hands down the nicest professor. I can really tell she cares about her students. She was very accessible and would answer any questions during and after the class. This class does have busy work, but it is easy. I learned a lot from her and would 100% take a class from her again. 10/10 would recommend taking this class from her!

The material in this class isn't hard it's offensively easy, the problem lies in the INSANE amount of work required for this class, this professor has no respect for your time and you will be doing 30+ completely meaningless assignments a week. Let me be clear, this class holds absolutely zero value in any way and is only here to waste your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I felt this was a lot of work for a pass or fail, but nothing hard. It was explained during class on why its helpful.

Way too much homework for pass/fail class. None of my classes have the amount of work that this class has and those ones are for an actual grade. You give a liberal professor like her a tiny bit of power and they turn into hitler. Very inconsiderate about anything that adds anything to her workload and has a doesn't GAF about you attitude. Avoid.

SO MANY ASSIGNMENTS. they are all easy, but they take forever and are very pointless. she is very nice, and you can tell she really does care about her students. I took this class in the summer, and I had more assignments in this class by itself then i do while taking 15 credits right now in the fall.
IT IS A ONE CREDIT PASS/FAIL CLASS. ACT LIKE IT. 20+ *time consuming* assignments a week is not acting like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's kind of a pushover I will agree.. She gave us a lot of homework, and you're expected to come to the studio after hours, which was tough as a commuter. Also quite nitpicky on things.

Nice as a person, not a great professor. She spends most of her class lecturing, and we often go overtime in class because she is talking so much and leaves us no work time. Most work and projects are homework assignments, which makes it difficult when you're a commuter student. She is also a pushover when it comes to boundaries.
10/10. Knows and loves her stuff. She and Amy Thompson made the classroom so welcoming and non-judgmental. I would take a class from her again any day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unfair toxic workplace, poor communication and lack of transparency. Your choice to highly damage your self-esteem, and buy a handful of stress. Paid and non-paid students subject to the same work participation. Was said "earn the better treatment". Values competition over collaboration. PhD is no no cause you sign up for all these for a long term.

Dr. Gaillardon is an incredibly knowledgeable professor. He was capable of answering just about any complex question that was thrown his way. My only major complaint is that his grading is very harsh. Otherwise there is a major chip project that is hard, but feels very rewarding.

He has good knowledge in the field. I wish we could have small tasks with correct solutions in canvas that split the grading into pieces. Group projects are graded harshly. Missing page numbers lost 10 overall points which was not indicated in the rubrics. He has a happy personality though.

He's a really great guy, but he doesn't teach particularly well. He flies through examples really quickly, and the majority of the homework questions are things that we never really touch on in class. A lot of the time I struggle to figure out where to even start. 

That said, I do think he's improving as the semester goes on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst teacher I have ever had, lectures are awful and confusing and way too much homework. He's nice but does not need to be a teacher at all.

He is a great guy and respects his students, but is not a good teacher. His lectures are confusing, and he often gets lost and doesn't know how to solve the problems he is trying to teach. His practice exam tests are AI-generated and are not like the tests at all. He requires attendance even though he goes solely off the textbook.

Well, if you have any other options besides this prof, just pick anyone else.
I'm pretty sure anyone who teaches Calc 3 would be better than him.
I thought it wouldn't be a big deal to take a class from a prof with zero reviews and yeah, that was the one and only mistake I made.

He's a nice person but he makes up his in-class examples on the fly. It's hard to learn from his lectures because half of the time he can't figure out or has to redo a problem. Also refused to review for any tests in class and gave us chatGPT generated practice exams that were nothing like the test. You can pass but I'd recommend any other teacher.

This guy is not worth anyone's time. His lectures confuse you more than they teach you, all the homework problems come from the textbook, he doesn't provide a review before the midterm, his practice exams are written by AI, he fails to get anyone's engagement because his own lecture notes confuse him. You are better off not showing up.

This class was pretty boring. It was basically music history and the beginning was really weird. The professor was nice and the class was relatively easy. Wouldn't recommend for a general fine arts credit though.

Dr. Nelson is a super engaging and caring professor. Coming in I wasn't the most interested in classical music, but I've been pleasantly surprised how much I've enjoyed the class because of her engaging lectures and small class projects. She really cares for your success and is always wanting to help.

She is the best teacher I have had so far at the U. She cares so much about what she teaches, she is hilarious, and she inspired me to learn the curriculum. If you need to get you fine arts credit, you shouldn't take any other class or teacher. She uses videos and music, so you can visualize what you are listening. She is the best!

She was such a great professor, she truly cared about what she was teaching and made class interesting. You can use notes on all the tests! All assignments are fairly easy. Her PA was a little rough on grading sometimes. Overall great class!

I took the week long intensive of this course and she did an amazing job teaching it. She also offers a lot of extra credit options so as long as you pay attention and try it's almost impossible to not get an A. She seems to really enjoy teaching this class and is very open and willing to admit when she doesn't know something for sure.

Took MUSC 3600 as an intensive course and she was really sweet about the material and taught in a great sense. There is a individual and a collaborative quiz which are open note. She is nice about grading and is open towards extra credit.
She does a lot of silly activities to help us learn. You can tell she puts effort into her lessons.

Dr. Nelson was one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. Her Survey of Jazz class covers a lot of touchy subjects, but she is very thoughtful and respectful. There is a quiz every week, usually 5 questions that are just there to specify what was important (Super easy). There are a few projects and papers and readings, but nothing too difficult

Dr. Nelson's class is very informative. She makes lectures engaging and cares that students understand the subject matter. She is also very responsive through media like the Canvas email system. Overall she has everything you could ask for from a professor.

Professor Nelson was knowledgeable about the topics discussed in class. I have a music background, but if I didn't I think some of the concepts would've been a little more difficult to understand but not impossible. It was nice to be able to attend class via zoom and view lectures later if needed if I could not attend that day for whatever reason.

Every assignment was clear and straightforward, and between recorded lectures and the textbook there was not any information I could not understand. This is a great class for incoming freshmen who will need the FF/DV credit, but also want to get eased into college-level expectations. Every paper was short and easy, with a clear rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Emily was genuinely a caring person. The homework matters a lot, but the grading isn't too bad at all. Quizzes are in person, so definitely go to those. She uploaded her lectures to zoom, so if you had to miss, you could stay caught up. Lots of reminders for homework and exams. Can't recommend her enough!

Such a great professor! Her class was so interesting, but low-pressure at the same time so I felt like I could focus on learning without memorizing. Tests and quizzes are open notes, and her lectures are very fun to listen to! I loved how inclusive she made the class, and how she would consistently play musical examples of what we were learning.

I'm not a music major and Dr Nelson made this class easy to understand. I took this class on a whim but I'm glad I did. Dr Nelson is super understanding and wants the best for her students. As long as you show up and do the work you're fine. We do reviews before all the tests and she gives great study guides.

I enjoyed attending Dr. Nelson's intensive world music class between Spring and Summer semester. You can tell that she loves teaching and really wants her students to understand the concepts. The class isn't difficult as the quizzes and exams are open note, just remember it's a lot of material to go over in a week. By the end, you'll be exhausted!!

Introduction to Music - Fall 2021.
Dr Nelson is a pretty quirky person, but that's a lot better than a boring person. She's very nerdily excited about everything she talks about, which is honestly perfect for a music class. Personally, I think this class should be called Introduction to Music History, but it was still really interesting.

Dr. Nelson is an amazing professor. I absolutely enjoyed learning from her this semester. She allowed for notes to be used on all quizzes and exams. Make sure to attend the review sessions as going to them almost guarantees an A for the exam. I learned a lot while not having to stress about the final paper / exams. Great professor!

I took the week long intensive and I absolutely loved it! It was so easy to get everything done in a week and I didn't even need to do the final assignment due about a month after the physical course was complete while still getting an A. There's quizzes (both a group and individual) at the end of each class about the coursework learned that day.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really nice and fair about assignments.

Professor Nelson teaches an interesting class. I'm not big on history but her lectures were clear about what you needed to know and moved at a good pace. Attendance was mandatory, but she worked with students who couldn't come to class. If you try in her class, you can easily get an A.

I took prof. Nelson's flex course at sandy campus and she was wonders. For this kind of course attendance is necessary as you're there from 8-5 for the whole week. She is a wonderful teacher who loves anything with music. She is also very attentive with her students and pops jokes. Be prepared to listen to lecture, watch videos and work w others

Dr. N is an amazing professor. I'm not super fascinated with the history behind music and composers but she made learning not only tolerable but also enjoyable. There are 2-3 short papers due throughout the semester as well as occasional homework however, they aren't very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is a wonderful professor who really cares about you and tries her best to make class interesting and enjoyable. Textbook was hardly used but there are some readings that are important. Overall, I would definitely recommend her.
Professor Nelson is fun. Her lectures are really interesting and the assignments are doable but not so easy that they're boring. She is also funny and has lots of jokes.
Professor Nelson is fun. Her lectures are really interesting and the assignments are doable but not so easy that they're boring. She also has lots of jokes.

She was a very nice teacher and very understanding of basically any circumstance possible. All of her lectures were entertaining and worth going to, and due to her tests, it was an easy to pass class as well as a fun one where you could focus more on the content and enjoying it as opposed to just memorizing information.

It's obvious that Professor Nelson cares and wants you to succeed in her class. She is so energetic and enthusiastic during lectures, and her humorous quips make the class fun. She tells you exactly what you have to do, so if you show up to class and do what is expected, you'll pass with an easy A.

Emily is really a great professor! If you are needing to take this class for a requirement, take this one. You have a 5 point quiz at the end of each class on the materials you just learned. If you show up and mildly participate it is an easy A. She is not boring when lecturing plus who doesn't love music? Easy class overall.

Taking survey of Jazz with Emily was my best decision this semester. Forget the fact that this class fulfills both a diversity and fine arts credit, the TA would improvise on his saxophone nearly every week! This class was so fun and easy, as long as you took good notes and showed up for the easy weekly quizzes.

All of the tests and quizzes were open notes and she gives very detailed note sheets and outlines which really helped. Attendance is a small part of the grade, but it would definitely hurt to skip often.
Professor Nelson is such a nice professor. Really cares about what she teaches and is super accessible outside of class. Would definitely recommend.

Emily Nelson's lectures are fun bc she's enthusiastic and the workload in the class is pretty easy. There's a lot to do, but it's all easy busywork. Exams are easy, and most of the final exam reuses the same questions in midterm 1 and 2. I never studied for the exams and got an A- in the class. There are 2 extra credit homework, 10 pts each.
Professor Nelson is one of those professors that you will always remember. She is dedicated to helping students succeed.

I took the week-long intensive course. She understands how to break up the monotony of 8-hour days with group assignments, videos, and lots of participation to keep you involved. Best professor for this class.

Really good teacher. It's obvious she loves music and sharing it. A decent amount of reading. There are IN-class group assignments, but thankfully no OUTSIDE-class group projects. Attend class, do assignments and halfway participate and it's an A, and interesting as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took as intensive class; much easier than expected. Emily is SO nice and very fun!! I absolutely loved this class and I learned a ton in a short time. 5 exams covering the material learned that day, 1 is dropped. 2 papers, with a month to do them. 1 fun group presentation. LOTS of extra credit! Emily goes out of her way to make lectures exciting :)

I took this class as a half semester intensive class. Very well worth the shortened semester especially since it was during summer. I wouldn't say it was an easy class, but getting an A is very obtainable. Emily knows her stuff and she expects you to take detailed notes to be able to pass the quizzes. I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took the class as an intensive course over the course of one week. She really is a great teacher and makes you think about the differences between cultures. It was a really fun and easy class to take.

I took this class as an intensive course and i loved it she was very informative and kind. She did her best to answer all questions and gave extra credit by far was the best choice I've made for getting FF & DV credit in one week!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Emily was so informative and enthusiastic. If you pay attention, you will pass the tests without a problem. She is very straightforward about her expectations and with her questions. I fully recommend the class for anyone, even if it is just for a graduation requirement.

She always seems to second guess herself and makes the material sound boring. I feel as if she's timid and for me it didn't keep my attention because I'd have to go look up the information later anyways. You have to go to class because of the attendance.
Only reads from book, offers no useful information. Makes a really interesting subject absolutely boring. Painful to go to class, but it was required.

Took this class to satisfy IR requirement. It was a fun class. You take notes as she goes through powerpoint presentations. Videos and listenings are shown to give examples of the material to help remembering for tests. 3 exams, 3 essay type assignments, participation and extra credit is offered. Emily is sweet and understanding if you talk to her.

I only took this class for the fine arts credit. Super interesting class and ended up enjoying watching some of the plays. The plays you watch online for the assignments can be long, but the assignments aren't demanding. Super easy quizzes.

Every week would be a new reading, production, quiz, and discussion. Just busy work but overall really nice class. You could finish this class in a week if you'd like but she still has due dates if you want to pace yourself. Very good class if you already enjoy theatre and want to make accomplishing your art credit a bit more fun! 1 midterm 1 final

Seems like a wonderful person, very into theater. I went into this course thinking I would just take it for the credits, but I feel like a more well-rounded person after all of it. She lets you work ahead to the freaking moon, and is quite understanding. Canvas page needs help though, you'll be struggling for a bit, but it's worth it. 8.5/10.

Jane was a great professor. Only one assignment every week or every other week. You watch a play and then write about it. She is a very generous grader. There are a lot of little videos and articles that the exams are based on, but they are open book with no time limit. She is extremely nice and responds to emails quick.

Does not structure online courses similar to other professors, it was a little confusing at first, but got the hang of it by week 2. You have ALOT of time as the assignments are given 2 weeks apart. Watch movies and plays and learn about Theatre productions. All online, go at your own pace, she's also very easy to email and ask questions to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I took this class online for one of my fine arts requirements for my generals, and it was so cool. You watch a lot of videos of plays and productions and then answer questions about them after, and there is a fair amount of reading that is crucial for the exams. The professor is very helpful if you have a question and gives good feedback.

Jane was an absolute delight of a teacher. I had the class online, but I felt this class was easy as well as informational. I have a theatre background (but not a theatre major) and I loved this class. It mostly consist of readings and videos and then you write a paper or discussion post on it. The quizzes/test are open note and fairly easy. 10/10!

Although this class was interesting and I did learn a lot, there was a lot of tedious work that felt like it took way to long to complete assignments. There are tons of articles that you have to read with each assignment. However, Prof. England is very kind and helpful, so I would still recommend this class. Exams are open book and pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is asynchronous. This is an incredibly easy (and honestly, kind of interesting) course for your fine arts gen-ed credit. Jane is very kind and supportive when she comments on submissions, and has very clear grading criteria. Quizzes and exams are open-note so you can learn without having to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Watching movies and taking quizzes about them. Learning about many different genres of movies, and watching our own theater shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor England really enjoys teaching and having other students learn about the history of theatre. Participating in her class will definitely get you on her good side. Also, you can get her talking for half the class time just about plays you like. Her midterm and final can be easy since she gives really good study guides.
Easy class. Mostly busy work and unnecessary readings. Lots of films to watch, but the quizzes on them are easy.

Super easy class. The professor is very lenient on grading and assignments aren't bad at all. You will have to go through some class videos/material for quizzes and tests, but even that is not that bad.

Lol... so I really did the bare minimum. I watched some of the films. The quizzes are kinda hard if you dont watch the films, but theyre easy. Theres a lot of opportunity for extra credit. I didn't really interact with the professor but she shes nice. a lot of busy work, tests are open book. easy class.

I took theater 1013 online. This class is for non-majors and she has very clear and simple grading criteria. She is very kind & helpful and wants her students to do well. Her midterms and finals are take home and open book. Her assignments are clear and simple. She was great and I enjoyed her class to anyone looking for an easy art credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class for the non-major. She grades very lenient and will give you the points if you do what's asked. There's opportunities for a bunch of extra credit. I enjoyed the material of the class even though I'm not fond of art. This is a half semester class so be prepared to have some big assignments due every couple days.

Jane is an amazing theater teach and a wonderful person. She works with you and wants to help you succeed. Shes very easy going but still makes you put in an effort to get a good grade. Highly recommend, very enjoyable.

She's a very generous teacher with tons of opportunity for you to have the best grade you can get. She offers a variety of extra credit throughout the semester and it's smart to do them because it will increase your overall grade tremendously. There is a quiz or in some cases, 2, every time there is class. If you study, it should be an easy "A".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Has extremely clear grading rubric and instructions. If you do what is asked you will get full points. Is flexible with deadlines ( only a small point reduction per day if you need a little extra time). Assignments are unique, and was a good choice for a non-major class.

There is a lot of reading for the class, but all relative to the course. I would definitely take this class AND Prof again! Super engaging course material, helped the assignments not drag. Professor England is  very straight-forward about her grading criteria and well organised and descriptive.  She makes it easy to get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jane is an enthusiastic teacher -sometimes boring, but she is nice. The point of the class is to read scripts and analyze them, so get ready to read a ton. At least 1 play about every week to read. Some of them are boring, some are fascinating. Quizzes almost every class - do not miss class!! Overall if you attend & read, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Easy class

Overall she's very knowledgeable about the topics that were discussed in class but on many occasions I feel like she didn't know how to make lectures interesting enough. I felt like I did well on many assignments and understood the material but still got B's instead of A's. The group project at the end was awful because I had to do it all.

Dr. Endres is soft spoken and kind. You have to read before each class because there are quizzes, but they are not difficult at all. She just wants to know you at least skimmed the readings. The hardest part was the 15-page research paper, but personally I would rather write a paper than take a test (personal preference). I would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I did not like this teacher at all. Attendance was mandatory, but she did nothing but read off of power point slides that were available online. In a class about learning arguments, nothing was argued. I dropped and retook it online, and the online teacher was able to increase my understanding and engage me far more than this professor.
The class material is pretty basic but she kept it interesting enough... an articulate lecturer who is knowledgeable about the field of communication.

She was ok. I don't think I learned in her lectures even once. But her presentation slides were great, and the tests are the easiest you'll ever take in a calculus course. I would've gotten an A if I didn't have personal events affect my grade. I aced my final and almost got a perfect score, one bad midterm can set your grade back a bit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You just need to listen her and work on homeworks.

lectures optional, 75% of course grade was exams (3 exams 25% each) but prof gave review sheet that was identical to exams so study that and you'll pass. Lectures can be hard to understand due to her accent and different teaching style from how I learn (bias here). Recommend taking linear alg before her class if you want an easy A/B math course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yekaterina is THE BEST. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN. Super easy class and practices are just like the exams. Either way, the concepts are really simple and easy to grasp anyway so you don't need to worry. Yekaterina is really nice and makes sure her students understand everything. There's HW that can take like 3 hours but they're only due every 2 weeks.

Dr. Epshteyn's practice exams reflect the actual exams very closely, so I focused mainly on the practice exams with excellent results. Dr. Epshteyn cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is accessible and accommodating. This was the easiest calculus class I've taken because of how generous the practice to actual exams were.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best prof. I've had. Teaches thing very clearly & intuitively. Sometimes her accent/manner of speaking makes her sound mean, but she's actually very kind and cares. She wants you to understand the material and succeed. Had another class w/ her and thought it was just easy, but decided it's that she's an excellent teacher. well-organized.
super awesome prof! she is super understanding and gives you all the resources to succeed :)

She's got a thick accent, which makes it pretty difficult to learn from her lecture videos. Her homeworks on canvas are tedious, but doable. Like the others say, the tests are also very simlar to the practices, easy. I ended up with a B+ because I forgot to do one HW. She wouldn't raise it because "policy". Don't miss easy points like me and get f

I love this class and that is all I can say. I wish all math classes were like this but alas I remain disappointed. By far one of my favorite classes ever.
