If you are given the opportunity to take a class with this prof, don't miss out on a life-changing experience. The human version of Thurston Waffles the legendary cat. Makes tuition worth it :D

Yekaterina is by far the easiest professor ever. There are 3 exams and NO FINAL, with only 7 homework. One test gets dropped and 2 HW get dropped. HW and tests are both 50% of your grade. Homework is easy enough to do, being 7-15 problems each. Exams are basically identical to the practice exam, they're extremely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class really is only determined by the midterms and the final. The homework is easy enough to do, and the lowest three scores were dropped (out of 8 assignments). The exams are also very similar to that of the practice exams, which makes it easy to get a high grade in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Epshteyn is okay. Tests are easy, always exactly the same kinds of questions as the practice tests. The homework is online so it's a little annoying, but she drops the lowest 3 scores out of 8 or 9. She often gets a little annoyed or doesn't know how to react when a student asks a question, but I think she's just trying her best.

Extraordinarily easy. Limited, online homework and she drops the lowest 2. Tests are the same as the review. Would recommend if you want to get a good grade in calculus 3, but due to the easiness of the class, I feel like I had less of a grasp on some of the concepts than I could have in a more challenging environment.

She teaches well and provides a large, very easy extra credit assignment at the beginning of the semester. Before each midterm and the final she releases an optional review. DO THE REVIEW. The questions on the review will be almost exactly the questions on the exam. She says that she requires the textbook but never actually uses it.

Yekaterina is a great Professor. Sometimes it is hard to understand some words she writes down or says as she is Russian. However, she explains different formulas and then goes through clearcut examples on how to do them. The only thing I don't like is if you have a question in class it usually takes too long for her to understand your problem.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She has a thick accent, so be prepared for that when going into the class. Some people have trouble understanding her. I do like her teaching style though, as she goes in depth into proofs for many of the equations we learn rather than just giving them to us to memorize. Overall, a decent professor, just hard to understand sometimes.

She is a decent lecturer but when it comes to answering questions, she can be very sarcastic because I'm not sure she understands the confusion that students may have. She uses online homework which is a joke because this is a higher level math class. Her tests are identical to the study guides which is incredibly nice.

Very difficult to understand, doesn't answer questions very well. Homework is graded way too hard and you have to write out EVERY step you use. I took Calc two in high school and had a hard time keeping a B in Calc one because of tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sometimes hard to understand and didn't always answer questions during lecture very well. Homework was fair and practice tests were almost exactly the same as the real thing.

She's an expert in her field and is very helpful. This was an REU course and questions were encouraged in and outside of class. One think that stood out to me was that she was actively interested in student projects and discussions in office hours were quite insightful for me.

Intelligent professor for sure, but his lectures can get boring at times. As far as assignments go, he gives you options which was great. However, he encourages class discussion yet he interrupts and loves to talk. I'm sure he'd talk to a wall for hours if you let him. Still, very intelligent and you'll learn alot!

I had Prof. Epstein for 3 of my political science classes dealing with Latin American politics.  He has easily been my favorite professor.  His lectures are so crystal clear you almost don't have to read the books.  I did anyway.  His tests are not easy and he is demanding with your final papers that are usually part of his classes.
Professor Epstein is a very nice person of an interesting characteric and extremely enthusiastic.  I just enjoyed his lectures!!
Talks like a lawyer, but that includes useful reiteration of points.
Smart, but a doofus.

Very knowledgable and kind professor. Class is extremely lecture and reading heavy. Writing assignments/essay comprise the majority of the grade. Work hard and pay attention, also strict grammar so be aware of grammatical structures along with course content when writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Engar is clearly really knowledgeable about all the readings she teaches. There is A LOT of reading (but you can get away with not reading some), just make sure you know enough to write the papers. You can ask the professors to look over your essays before submitting them which is really helpful!

I took this class and thought this professor was knowledgeable but I was clearly wrong. Every assignment is graded very harshly and poor feedback was given and the outline for the assignments was poor. Very hard to improve on assignments. On the final, she was extremely passive aggressive on her comments, stating that my opinion is incorrect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Engar is truly an amazing professor who clearly cares about her students. She is extremely understanding and professional, if you reach out she will work with you. This class is based on readings and participation in class discussions, so if that's not your style reconsider.
Dr. Engar is truly amazing! She challenges you to think critically when it comes society and law. If you are interested in law, I definitely recommend taking this course!

Dr. Engar is an amazing professor. However, you have to actually try in this class. If you don't show up, you're screwed. She is super understanding and accommodating, though. She genuinely cares and wants to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are several books that are required to read over the semester. Ann is super sweet and the class isn't too hard if you apply yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ann is as nice and considerate as Rachel, her teaching partner for this class. The only difference is she is a significantly harder grader on papers. That being said, make sure to try to get pre-submission feedback and it will help on the papers. Ann is also impressively knowledgeable on her field of study and any topics adjacent to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Unless it's a requirement, do NOT take. Communist like grading; passive aggressive if one doesn't agree; grading & feedback are subjective thus does not help; favors students in the program that were there for 3 years; refers to students as minorities as opposed to actual names; rarely uses texts; English teacher teaching law is questionable.

Among the best professors at the U. Dr. Engar is incredibly knowledgeable; she will be able to answer any question you could imagine relating to course material. She is tough but fair as far as grading is concerned. Her React courses are fun, and to this day I still remember the lessons she lead on Marlowe and Shakespeare.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ann is probably the most knowledgeable person I've ever met. She is also very understanding when students are having a hard time or need something. She assigned four essays for the semester, and that was the entire grade. Reading was assigned to every class, and there was a lot of it. She is so sweet, and her class is so interesting.

I really enjoyed her class. She was a tough grader, but her comments were helpful. She lectures a lot but the topics are interesting and she encourages class participation. She was also willing to read our papers and give us feedback before they were due so we could get good grades. She clearly cares about her students and wants us to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I constantly found that she graded materials quite harshly, and occasionally left scathing, and non-constructive criticisms for feedback. On multiple instances I found myself trying to write in parallel to her opinion, and performed better on these assignments as well, because anyone that doesn't agree completely with her didnt "understand".

Dr. Engar is truly the greatest professor I have ever had. She really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. The first semester of the leap class is challenging but very beneficial and it just gets better as time goes on. She answers any questions you have and puts a lot of thought into it. She is incredible and I learned so much.

Great class!  There is a reading assignment every day, which we discuss during class.  She gives great background and insight to the reading assignments.  The grade is based on two papers and two tests (which are also essays).  So if you understand the readings and like to write, this class won't be hard for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Reacting to the Past is a fantastic class and Ann is very experienced with this format. The class is basically like LARPing for college and honors credit. Be prepared to write a lot, from speeches, to any other creative writing piece. Also be willing to have fun with the class and immerse yourself in the games and you'll have a blast.

Ann is a great professor, but all the IT courses are a bit bland. This course at least covered a lot of history dealing with science and not too much religion compared to the others. Lots of essays, but they really help for the final (which is a fair but tough one) and she is willing to proofread your essays too.
This class is very exciting and Ann does a good job of keeping it going. She takes kind of a backseat role in "reacting to the past" classes, but is still completely available for support.

This class was one of my favorite classes. I took it last spring and had a blast! Prof. Engar provides background on the topics explored, but the class is mostly taught by other students. I will definitely take another Reacting to the Past with Engar before I graduate. Can be time consuming, but totally worth it!
awesome professor, loved her class

Finished the Pre-Law LEAP program last school year & I'm glad I did! Even though I've decided not to go to law school, Dr. Engar has been amazing! It gets more fun at the end of the program & you begin to build a closer relationship w/her. This class was super helpful and it's amazing for her to watch you grow as a potential law school applicant.

Dr. Engar was a great teacher, her LEAP class was super easy, great to ease your way if you are just starting college off.  As the class was super easy it was also a little boring, but none of the readings or assignments were too hard, and she is always willing to help students!

Dr. Engar is a great professor - I was relatively anxious about my Intellectual Traditions class before school started, but Engar really eases you through the material. Participation is not graded, which I liked a lot. For papers, Engar was very helpful. She also offered extra credit throughout the semester, and some teachers don't do that.
Great teacher, I learned a lot. The readings were fun and didn't dive right into the law world. Let you ease into it. Papers weren't too hard, good class!

I felt that she was not happy to be there. The books assigned had poor grammar and were not always relevant to what the class was  supposed to be about. The class was meant to be about law in American Society, and she was so focused on different groups in America that the aspect of law was often missing from the class or was briefly touched upon.

This is my 3rd year with Dr. Engar in the LEAP program. She's a nice woman but assigns a lot of readings in her classes. Honestly, she just wants to expose her students to different cultural elements and prepare them for law school. She's a quiet lecturer, not very lively or uniquely interesting. But she's very accommodating with personal problems.

Engar's Intellectual Traditions course was one of the defining experiences of my time at the U of U. I have to laugh a bit at the ratings that describe the topic as "boring." Montaigne and Rousseau are boring? Not if you pay attention! Engar is an inspiration--intellectually rigorous, witty, compassionate. Take her class if you can!

You will read a lot, and it will suck. A couple papers are assigned (make sure whatever you write, you agree with her opinions on the material, otherwise she'll mark you down), and the 10 essays in 2 hours final is hell. Enjoy!

Dr. Engar is really helpful and understanding if you just talk to her. She may come across at first as not such a nice prof, but that's misleading-- she is really nice. A ton of reading though! She lectures on all of it, so if you miss a day of reading it isn't hard to get the concept. Pretty easy class... like I said, just a ton of reading...
She offers creative options for her papers, which is just plain awesome. Seems to get the class more engaged during the Renaissance.
Boring.  so boring.  lots of reading, but she helps out a lot with papers and she grades pretty easy

You will read until your eyeballs fall out of your head.  She's a great teacher, but the subject is boring no matter who teaches it.  The final is a beast.  If you are reading this and you are the kid who got up with 20 minutes left, I hate you.    You will probably do more work with Engar as your teacher than if you had a different professor.
No Comments
Just so boring class.
No Comments

she's very educated and clearly understands what she is teaching to a higher degree than any other teacher i have ever met.  she is probably one of my favorite professors.  although the works we study in this class are not my thing she makes them interesting.  it's not an easy class, it's a good challenge though.
she's amazing!  so brilliant and so educated!  she's one awesome teacher!

I took this class two years ago, and now i can finally vent on how much of a complete waste of time it was.  Engar was on edge a lot of the time and very rude to myself and a few other students.  Graded like a Chinese Communist. Didn't like the class, would recommend dropping it immediately.
She is very nice, but extrememly boring in this class. It's an easy class though
Ann is very organized and hits the main contributions of Western writers clearly.  She takes a little time for class lecture and then leads class discussion.  Among the best instructors and classes.
Quite possibly the best professor I've had at the University of Utah.  I learned a lot from her.
She was very nice and helpful.  The class was a bit hard for me, but not too much.  She explained things very clearly.

This is a very easy class. Exams are completely open note and the practice exams she gives out are very similar to the midterms. She isnt the greatest teacher and seems to overcomplicate very simple concepts. But I still recommend her as a professor.
This class is simply an easy business course. She gave us lectures that prepared us well for each test and that's about it. Nothing dramatic to say here.

The nicest teacher! Always clear and concise in class. Everything she gives you is clearly laid out for you and made easy to understand. Her classes are not very hard but really do teach you lot. In-class practice questions, homework and practice exam questions reinforced learning!

Professor He is a very caring professor. She's super kind and cares about her students succeeding in class, and responds great to questions in and after class. She didn't give us that many hw assignments but she gives you clear criteria for each of her exams.

She was very kind but her teaching methods were not very effective. She would just read off slides and was super monotone. The class was never engaged and I had to teach myself everything before the exams. I showed up to nearly almost every class because attendance was mandatory but never learned anything. At least the exams were open book.

Professor He was a difficult teacher, not in the sense of the content, but in the way that she teaches. There is no class engagement, she reads off the slides the whole time, and her English is very hard to understand. I had to teach myself all the content because the lectures were not understandable.
The material isn't even hard, but she overcomplicates all of it. On some o the exams she had information that we dint even go over in class. Wouldn't recommend the class.

Eryn's accent is thick and sometimes it can be hard to understand her. That being said though, she really wants her students to do well. She makes us Excel sheets to use on the exams to avoid complex math, will stay after class to clarify any questions and responds to emails. She can teach the content well enough so you can understand it if you go.

She has a very thick accent and the way she does most of her math is much different then how I would do it. She is very confusing and doesn't always teach the material correctly and would find myself going around in circles trying to figure out what it was we were even learning. She is very caring, sweet, and wants students to do well.

This class was extremely frustrating. I attended both office hours and TA sessions and still struggled due to unclear expectations and harsh grading. I put a huge amount of effort into a course that isn't even required for my major, yet it felt almost impossible to earn an A. I would not recommend taking this course unless you absolutely have to.

This is not a professor who cares if you understand the material. There is no bigger purpose in this class and you'll be graded very harshly and arbitrarily. It is heavy on logic without enough explanation of formal logic concepts. Ideas from students are shut down. You will be made to feel like an unfit philosopher or thinker in general. Avoid.

Pros:
Knowledgable, funny, light homework

Cons:
Rarely answers students questions adequately, did not explain participation criteria well in the syllabus or in class, grades students logical argument reconstruction but does not provide any formal logic instruction, class always went over time.

Overall, I think Eric is a fantastic professor. Definitely not the super villain people on here make him out to be. However, his class is definitely challenging. Grades are determined mainly by in-class writing assignments (20 minutes to write) that are graded quite harshly. He also doesn't let people know when these assignments are, so show up!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Definitely not as bad as others here have said. He's awkward, but not malicious. Very knowledgeable about Chinese philosophy, but a bit inflexible with student interpretation (i.e., he doesn't really entertain our thoughts much—not necessarily bad). Somewhat arbitrary attendance policy, so beware. Very challenging grader, but generally fair.

Hutton's classes are HARD, but if you do the work you will be so much better for it. This is the hardest class I have taken, and I owe my grade to going to office hours, asking lots of questions in class, and doing the reading. He is intimidating, but he is very receptive to questions provides amazing feedback. I am a much better writer now.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It's hard to fit all my complaints about Hutton into this box. He acts superior to students and often misunderstood student comments, having the unintended effect of shutting down fruitful discussion. I am a third-year phil major and I love the subject, but Hutton's class made me feel discouraged and personally unfit to study philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hutton is very knowledgeable about the subject, however his lectures were really hard to follow and there was a lot of reading that was pretty confusing. But, there was always good feedback on the assignments we would do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is unclear About how he grades things. There is no variation in how he lectures so it is not engaging. He puts down ideas that students give in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hutton is a very knowledgeable teacher. He seems to understand the material very well, yet is unable to convey that understanding to his students. What he teaches and what he wants from his students do not seem to always align. Hutton is a very difficult grader and is extremely apathetic towards his students. Highly do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of fun. It challenged a lot of predispositions I had about ethics and epistemology. All other classes reading and writing heavy felt like a breeze after taking this one. The only tangible things to go on your grade were 5 separate essays. All are written in the span of 45 minutes in class. He also graded participation. Big Oof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid Hutton! He is terrible at giving lectures, by far the toughest grader in the philosophy department and he does not care about his students. I would rather take thermodynamics than deal with Hutton. Worst professor and worst experience at the U. The U needs to reevaluate professors like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's really smart and knows everything you could ever want to know about ethics. I'm a freshman and probably shouldn't have taken such a difficult course but you do get what you put in to the class. I recommend writing multiple rough drafts for exams. It's not so much about understanding the material but being able to articulate a good argument.

He knows the material but he falls short on explaining it at a level students can understand. I didnt know what he was talking about even though I did the reading (which is difficult) multiple times. I found it to be unnecessarily difficult for an intro class however, he is kind enough to give you the essay prompts before an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Hutton is one of the most difficult graders I've had pertaining to papers. He isn't specific about what he's looking for, and then fails assignments without much feedback. He teaches from the readings, without being broad enough to cover what material he expects you to know for the test. Readings are long and difficult.
Professor Hutton has been my favorite at the U. His lectures are very involving and he describes the concepts very well. If you need a Phil History class he is definitely the way to go!

I love this Professor. It is hard to find a good Phil professor but he really engages students with the content. You can tell he is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. He is very approachable and his lectures are funny.  He is a tough grader, but he gives lots of feedback and direction. As long as you are trying, this class is worth it.
Demanding with essay structure and content, but if you are looking to improve your writing techniques then Prof. Hutton is the best you can hope for! Good class for all majors!

Absolutely one of the Best prof. at the U. Yes he can be demanding about papers, but he is more than willing to help you improve your writing. If you want to learn a lot, be challenged, and rewarded take him.
Extremely amazing professor, teaches very difficult topics, but he is absolutely brilliant and you learn tons from him. Everyone should take a philosophy class from him.

One of the most unnecessarily hard intro classes. Have had some experience with philosophy, but not like this. Readings are extremely difficult, but does give helpful outlines in class on readings. extremely challenging tests. very tough grader on writing assignments. almost seems like a lot of work for no real benefit.

Absolutely Brilliant Instructor! He truly knows and lives his profession, and has a great answer for EVERY question you ask him. Many students might say he is strict or difficult, but if you don't want to challenge yourself then you don't belong in college! He makes you find the solutions on your own, but you will feel so rewarded once you do.
Poor explanations of concepts, failed to present material in an interesting and easy to understand manner
Worst Intro class ever. Kids with 2 years of Philosophy under their belt struggled to grasp the basic concepts.
He's SO smart!  He's great about office hours.  It's obvious that his main objective is the student's understanding.  He's a great teacher!!  Take Hutton!!

I took the course Topics in Classical Chinese Philosophy from Prof. Hutton.  He was in his first year, but probably one of the best professors I had at this school. Very knowledgable (no matter what tangent came up as a question he could answer it), very organized, very fair and helpful with comments.

One of the best teachers I've had at any level. Extremely well organized, knowledgeable and he obviously loves to teach. He makes you read, think and work, and he appreciates out of the box essay ideas . Really cares about his students. I can't wait to take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Eric makes lectures very interesting and he is very knowledgeable. There are weekly quizzes and assignments that are very easy and graded on completion. The exams are in person and handwritten, but they are easy if you study a little bit. He's a pretty harsh grader on the essays as the topics are somewhat nuanced.

Professor Herschthal is a terrific teacher who challenges his students. He proscribes a lot of reading including primary sources and challenges his students to think He requires about 10 short essays and two 1500 word essays. He's extremely knowledgeable and really loves to teach. One of the best teachers I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend Professor Herschthal for anyone interested in history! My only small gripe is sometimes he goes on tangents and goes over class time by 5 minutes. However, this class is very manageable, very interesting and he always reviews content of the last lecture at the start of class. He genuinely gave great feedback too.

He speaks loud and clearly and gives great feedback on every single assignment that you do. He makes annotations on your essays so you know what to improve on. He takes the time into putting care in each student.

I thought Dr. Herschthal was great. It is very lecture heavy, but that works well with my learning style. I felt like he genuinely cared for his students and wanted everyone to do well. If there was something that a majority of the class didn't do well on, he would talk with us and give us all the opportunity to re-do it with more guidance.

Really don't understand the negative reviews here. HIST 1700 with Eric was one of my favorite classes taken at the University mostly because the professor was so engaging and we actually got to critically interact with interesting material unlike other history classes I've taken, especially APUSH in high school.

I really liked Dr. Herschthal. He was very kind and understanding. I was surprised by the bad reviews because he genuinely cared about his students and them doing well. I liked his lectures and found him interesting.

HIST 1700. Spends a quarter to half the class reviewing his previous lecture, which usually corresponds to the exam. Go over highlighted events or ones you find interesting. Exams include MC, 1 term definition and application (list given), and a short-response portion. Essays aren't hard. Just make sure you have everything on the rubric.

This review is actually for HIST 1700, but it's not listed for some reason. The class has mandatory attendance and the lectures are long and boring. If you read the slides and never came you'd get the same info. Test's are easy, but the 2 essays are graded harshly. Would not recommend unless you have to.

He was honestly one of the better professors I have had in the three years I have been at the U. He actually care about the material and he cares about his students understanding it. He is also willing to help his students improve their papers and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not too difficult, but super lecture heavy, which can drag on. Harsher grader on papers, but midterm and final were not difficult if you study. As long as you skim the readings and do the short writing assignments weekly, you'll be fine.

I took Hist 3730*
I'm surprised by such harsh reviews! I enjoyed this prof's class a lot. The material was rich, the readings made you think, and he was very kind. However, he is a very tough grader, I/O. I've been a straight A student until I took his class. But, my B+ was partially due to poor mental health, which he was very understanding of.
Mean mean man. I got a five on the APUSH exam and almost dropped this class 20 times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I wasn't formally enrolled in her class, but I attended it a lot anyways, and she seems really chill. People generally liked her, and her lectures got to the point without being boring. She had good in-class activities and interesting assignments. Pretty epic

I hate writing but Erin really helped me with expanding my writing abilities in her class. She was very easy going and understanding when I had questions. She allows a couple re writes per semester if we do bad on one of our papers. She graded things quickly and gave very detailed feedback which I really Appreciated

Erin was extremely helpful with her assignments, that being said she was a tough grader and had a lot of expectations with each paper. She was very understanding and would let you rewrite any paper. 100% recommend
Erin was awesome! She gives really great feedback on papers and she allowed for rewrites on some of them. Definitely recommend!

Fun teacher and definitely willing to help students. She's super nice. In fact, she may be too nice. When she asks a question, no matter what you say she'll reply "exactly, right!" No complaints, though.
Erin was one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is easy to converse with and really cares about her students.

She's really nice and very helpful. She writes really good notes and feedback and she's a very nice person. She's good at teaching and explaining things and she's patient. I HIGHLY recommend taking her class. I took her for two semesters and loved her!

Robertson creates an engaging classroom environment and encourages meaningful discussion. He is supportive and approachable, and I felt he genuinely cared about students' success. There were regular projects that helped me develop my ideas, and the workload felt reasonable. Overall, I had a positive experience in his class.
Robertson is an amazing guy! Honors 1010 is a little weird in general but he did a good job of helping us understand why we were doing what we were doing.
I honestly disliked the class, BUT he's what made it bearable. He was very lenient and very deep/intellectual, overall super chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super chill guy who showed genuine interest in all of our individual projects. He also went the extra mile and helped me secure an amazing internship by writing a LoR for me, despite knowing me for only a few months.

I took HONOR 1020 with Robertson. Would strongly recommend taking a class from Robertson. This is my second class with him and it was a great experience again. He genuinely cares about his students and is a great professor to talk to.

One of the most caring professors I've had at the U. The class is discussion-based, with a focus on three main books. The class and writing structures were unique compared to other courses, but they encouraged the development of new ideas. I highly recommend this professor, no matter the subject.

I took 2211 with Robertson and he is a great teacher. You can tell he really cares about each of his students, and he is very willing to help. He is super funny and his classes aren't boring. Additionally, the books we read in this class were engaging and thoughtful. I would definitely take a class with Robertson again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Had Robertson for both 2211 and 3200 and would highly recommend taking his course. Very passionate and caring about each student's growth as a writer and teaches/gives feedback well. Workload is very manageable and doesn't give out busy work. Each assignment is meaningful for the final paper. One of the best professors I've ever had.

This professor was amazing. He would listen and generally would care about his students. I was having some trouble due to the pandemic and he really helped me through it. The course can be difficult due to how much you need to write but due to the few assignments you can also easily make or break your grade. However, I recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Robertson is definitely my favorite professor so far in college. He cares about his students a lot and always gives good feedback. He is willing to make adjustments and listen to students. Overall, a great guy.

Professor Robertson is awesome. I took him for Honors 2211 as a freshman. He is super cool and funny, and the class is honestly quite fun. Definitely need to do the work, though, because it all leads to the final paper. There are cool discussions in class, and he will let you redo assignments until you get 100%. Highly recommend!

WONDERFUL professor- one of my favorite classes so far. He helps you learn A LOT about writing and develop new strategies that more strongly express what you want to say. Your grade for the semester is based off of your final paper, which you work on the entire time and is a guaranteed A if you do all the assignments and work with him like he asks.

I took Robertson in my freshman year, and his class seriously improved my writing skills. He cares about cultivating each student's individual strengths and really wants to help his students succeed. He is available outside of class, and he is always willing to read over a rough draft before you submit it. He is incredibly knowledgeable and kind!!

I cannot emphasize how amazing Robertson is! He is the consummate professor. 1 Paper with Assignments leading up to it that help form ideas. Robertson is incredibly knowledgeable and he makes you think critically. Your essay ideas will challenged constructively. It will be fun. My writing has improved substantially. His essay feedback is amazing!!

Probably the best writing class that I have taken. Robertson's theme for the class is project-based learning, which essentially means that every assignment given in the class is preparing you for your final project. This eliminates busy work and allows you to guide your own education so that it is relevant to what you are studying. Great class!

Great guy, knows his stuff and shares funny yet relevant stories etc. You write one (1) paper throughout the entire semester in chunks on a topic of your choosing; the paper grade is what you get for the class. However, it's an easy A because Robertson checks on your writing all the time and tells you what to improve and change, Excellent class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Robertson is an amazing professor who is extremely willing to help students achieve their academic goals. He is very knowledgeable and smart without being condescending or dismissive of students' ideas. If you have the chance to take one of his classes, I would highly recommend doing so.

HUGE fan of this guy. A real gem when it comes to being knowledgeable and also entertaining. If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes JUMP ON IT. He was super caring and helped my with my writing by a lot. He also cares about you outside of the classroom and can seriously turn your bad day around.

Mr. Robertson was a great professor. The whole course was centered around one final project paper that was preceded by several smaller papers that build up to the final paper. He was always available to meet and work with us on our papers, and he provided one on one feedback in class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Robertson has been hands down one of my favorite professors. He focuses on open-resource education, which basically gives you assignments that will help you finish the final paper. If you put the effort in, you will get a great grade. He is so funny and inspiring. He has open my mind to new ideas and concepts. He is the best writing teacher!
Very easy course that professor heisler taught well. I can't say I was particularly inspired while taking this course but it was a walk in the park and I have nothing to complain about.

It's a tough course, and the assignments take a while, but the lecture slides actually give you helpful information and are engaging and fun. Heisler actually cares about his students and wants them to do well. If you attend class, do the work, and ask questions, you will do fine in any of his classes

I don't think he's harder than other professors for the same classes because the courses are so standard. He could be a more confident lecturer, but he is willing to adapt the course based on the current students.

Weekly quizzes are based on assignments, but reviewing them carefully makes it easy to score well. The midterm was pretty easy, and you can retake it during finals to boost your grade. Assignments aren't too hard. Labs check attendance via quizzes, so make sure to show up. Participating in class and keeping up with work makes everything manageable.

He needs to learn how to teach cuz he is really bad at teaching and really good at failing students. He makes tests extremely difficult and the practice exam he gives has absolutely no help for the real exam.

This professor has very poor teaching skills. Concepts are not explained clearly, lectures feel disorganized, and it's extremely difficult to follow the material. The class is also homework-heavy. Instead, students end up teaching themselves most of the content.

The lectures are a big wall of mind numbing information. The exams are handwritten and are mostly syntax-related gotchyas that don't really test your problem solving or programming understanding, just memorization of syntax. I have prior programming experience and still only managed to receive ONE 100% on an assignment. Avoid if possible.
Every test is just a slough of "Gotchas" rather than a coherent evaluation of the concepts learned in class. This would be bearable if the exams were not 60% of your grade.

He just isn't a good teacher. His explanations make things more confusing than they really are. I've taken two classes with him (and will have to take CS3505 later) and it's clear that he can't teach. He's trying and I can respect that, but as it stands he has fundamental issues with his teaching style. His deadlines are also harsh.
The lecture barely covers anything on the homework, you mostly have to learn it yourself.
A lot of reading, lectures are long but do not cover the full span of material in readings. Labs are hit and miss on explanation also. Success is dependent on office hours or after class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not sure why anyone would hire this guy to be a professor, the only thing he knows is to take points off for literally no reason.
Unless you are out of your mind, do not take this guys class. You will get points of with no reason.
This guy does not know how to teach, pick another professor.
This professor does not know how to teach
You will get points of your homework without a reason. Unless you have no other choice, do not take this professors class

Not fun, threw curve balls on the tests, didn't fully teach certain topics, wouldn't give actual answers to students questions just a "figure it out". Reads directly off his slides and never goes in depth. Failed half of my lecture class. Wouldn't recommend.

Professor Heisler is a good professor who knows his material well. The lectures were a bit boring at times. His office hours were available but not very engaging—you had to push a bit to get help, as he wasn't very proactive in assisting students.

I took CS 3505 with Professor Heisler, and I can honestly say he's one of the most dedicated and effective instructors I've had in the CS program at the U. His teaching style is clear, practical, and very engaging. He knows how to break down complex software engineering concepts and make them easy to understand and apply in real-world scenarios.

Honestly I thought CS 2420 was supposed to be harder for a weed-out. I will say that it was quite a bit of work, but honestly if you aren't like every student in the class who start the assignments the day before they're due and you also study, you'll do well. He's a pretty good teacher, and gives you a lot of good resources for learning/studying.

Heisler was great. It was between him and Parker and I heard she was kinda rude. I really appreciated that he always recorded his lectures and uploaded slides. Made it really accessible as a student commutes. Just start homeworks on the weekend.
He kinda looks like Nardwuar tho.

I had almost no free time during the semester due to this class alone. The analysis documents are a pain and he refused to give us a rubric for them, so we didn't know what we were getting docked points for. He also didn't give an answer key for the practice exams, so we had no idea if we were doing them right.

While sometimes topics are hard to understand, he was very willing to help clarify anything that was confusing. The course content itself was fairly straightforward, but the exams were tough and made up a large portion of your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fine teacher just really strict and not chill.

Heisler is great!

I spoke with him a few times outside class and he was always happy to help. He has taken time out of his lunch to help me. I don't think many other professors would do that.

There are lots of bad reviews on here, but the majority of the ones I read are complaining about normal college things like due dates.

Most people in here saying that Heisler is the devil or something are just bad, skill issue. His assignments are pretty boring and his lectures can be unbearable sometimes but that's most of the CS degree so far. Obviously not as good as Kopta but not the_devil.gguf
Everything is bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is so hard to concentrate in his class. I always end up scrolling tiktok or something. He never answers any questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, his lectures and teaching style was the best of any of the computer science classes I've taken. The assignments got difficult at the end, and he was somewhat rigid with late work, but honestly it was not bad for a CS class in my opinion. I liked the engagement in lectures rather than just listening the whole time.

By the end of the semester, the homework got super difficult. The TAs would have 13+ students waiting for help in the CADE lab, and they struggled to help us. He gives no exceptions even in dire situations. Tests are hard and grading is tough. You need to have everything perfect before submitting. Made this so much harder than it should have been.

Heisler was an alright teacher, I felt the lectures did an okay job at explaining the topics. He is everything you would imagine a computer science professor is and is very strict on documentation. Do not procrastinate on the homework because it can be quite a lot of work especially towards the end of the semester.

Prof. Heisler was a very good and informative lecturer and if you show up and pay attention you shouldn't have too much trouble with the course. 

However, he is incredibly strict when it comes to deadlines. I joined the class a week late and wasn't able to make up the first lab that I missed even though I wasn't in the class yet.

I took him for cs 1420, and I honestly was really disappointed. He made it a huge point at the beginning of the semester that he wont be giving extra credit or rounding up grades which I thought was unnecessary. His lectures were very mundane and boring, he didn't try to explain anything imo, I had to learn everything myself from youtube.

The pacing was strange with the difficulty of topics not aligning with the time allocated. He offers no leniency what so ever in grading regardless of circumstances. Luckly the topics covered aren't too hard if you have some prior experience. Overall he made this course much harder than it needed to be, with his rigid policies and lack of empathy

He's well organized, but his teaching style was subpar and he DOES NOT CARE about you. He will not offer any leniency or exceptions, and will not offer you any help even in extraneous circumstances. You better be the most perfect student, completely by-the-books if you want to succeed. The only class I have ever failed in my life. Get ANYBODY else.

Pretty difficult course with hard, weekly assignments. The lectures were okay and explained the concepts but could be pretty slow at times. He does upload them afterwards to canvas so you can watch from home. The TA's were super nice and helpful during lab but Eric himself is pretty unforgiving. Definitely treat this as a filter course and prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was quite the hassle. Would not recommend. After this I am debating switching majors or even dropping out. His lectures are absolute buns. He talks like a robot and all the info he says goes in one ear and right out of the other. Probably headed to business.

While the course material is REALLY easy if you've taken computer science in high school at the very least, Heisler's lectures made it appear more complicated without adding anything valuable. I can't tell if he's trying to be friendly or if he's nervous when he speaks. Boring lectures are my biggest gripe, though.

Prof. Heisler's lectures teaches concepts in a roundabout manner that overcomplicates simple topics, for example ArrayLists. Big project this semester is new, which means the instructions are not clear and is way harder than the material in the lectures. If this was my first CS class, I would've never take another one. Please, avoid if possible.

I don't recommend this class. The professor is rigid, lacks leniency, and doesn't value students as people. Miss an assignment by a minute? Too bad. His values harm more than help. No extra credit, no understanding. If life happens, expect no mercy. He should ask himself: Are his "ethics" serving others or just himself? Avoid if possible.

While the lectures are often hard to follow, Professor Heisler knows what he is talking about and cares about students. Exceptions are not often given, but when needed he will work with you. I had to miss a week and a half of class to attend a funeral and he has been very accomodating

Prof. Heisler is a decent professor. His lectures be a bit hard to follow, and require focus, but he answers questions fully and without being condescending. Assignment descriptions were both clear and concise. I had a lot of Java experience going in, which helped. (This class was co-taught with another prof over the summer.)
Terrible teaching style. I attended lectures, but rarely learned anything at all. Roundabout ways were taught simply to show the correct way later.

no extra credit, no correction, not retake for all of the grade components(assignments, quizzes, tests)
and those are hard that even if you spend much time on these
No extra credit, difficult homework, difficult test with only one practice test to prepare for.

Professor Heisler is actually a good professor, his lectures are very informing with good examples of the subject and how he designs his lecture slides and explains them thoroughly. He does have a hard time explaining questions but I've had his 2 semesters in a row and I can see that he is improving on that!
I would never take another class from him. I have never had a professor actively try to get as many students to fail a course as possible but he would say it as a matter of pride. RUN AWAY!

Most of the semester was Prof Heisler slowly and unconfidently teaching basic C++. Lots of arbitrariness when it came to grading & expectations he had of students, e.g one assignment was intentionally vague to promote self teaching, but a classmate got in trouble for doing something too advanced. Refused to round a student's final grade up by 0.01%

Not a terrible lecturer but the homework assignments involve pointless analysis designed to drain your time and computer's soul. Routinely had to run my poor computer for 10+hours straight to analyze alogrithms at pointlessly large scale with no benefit in terms of actual data collected. Brutal if you don't have a very fast computer.

This class was quite boring, and I didn't learn many new topics. Most assignments were uninteresting, lacked complexity, and only covered basic C++. The TAs often docked points for things not mentioned in the assignments. Overall, this has been my least favorite class so far.

He's a fun and goofy professor. There were a lot of questions where he kind of just answered with "find out for yourself". It felt like the lectures didn't quite prepare you for the assignments, it took a bit of research outside of what you learn in class to complete it. There was a final project rather than a final exam which was nice.

I like professor Heisler -- his lectures were pretty good with funny bits (also recorded), and the the assignments were not too hard. The labs actually related to the class content, which was a first for me (most classes have terrible labs...). Overall this was pretty easy for a CS class, and professor Heisler was chill.

I personally loved Professor Heisler, he was very understanding and was on Piazza on Thursdays when the HW was due answering questions personally. He's very accessible through Piazza and after lecture, and he answers questions concisely in a way that makes sense. Solo assignments are easy, but get ready to coordinate schedules for the second half.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Heisler does an excellent job with CS3505. It's definitely more relaxed than CS3500. Lectures are clear and easy to follow. Later assignments very are open ended, and make for an enjoyable group programming experience.

Heisler is a nice dude. The first midterm was hard and he was vague about the level of detail that would be required but he seemed to adapt and the other exams were toned down. He replies quickly on piazza. I feel like in a few years he'll be a really good professor, his jokes are nice. For the material, there's 100+ videos of each DS/A available.

He's a new professor and you can tell. I had him for 1420 as well. His lectures are a 3/5 but he's a difficult grader on homework and criteria will appear from nowhere. Everything I liked has to do with the TA's. Some of them were really good and the rest were mediocre.

Descent is the best word for Heisler. He has amazing lecture slides and is good at explaining the slides, however he is poor at answering questions. Tests are not similar to the practice exams, but the assignments are pretty clear. The biggest thing is that Heisler is not reachable. It seems that the TAs do all of the work and answer questions.

He is not a good professor at all, had a horrible experience in 2420 because of him, doesn't know how to explain the topics properly nor about being a professor at all. Doesn't want students to succeed rather fail, overall nice guy but should not be teaching anything respectfully.

Really enjoyed this class. I appreciated only 1 midterm with a few in person quizzes. No final test, instead a final project. Lectures were clear and enjoyable. Like other professors Heisler uses pollev but with the improvement of not grading it. I watched recorded lectures most of the time. I found that I learned better by watching lectures.

2420 is a HARD class and anyone knows. After the first midterm went so horribly even curved it based on past years.  Also when asking if based on how i did on the midterm i should consider dropping the class, he gave a throurough respinse on how can i am performing and what I should do moving forward. Even including an inspirational quote

I hate pair programming and I hate group work but I guess that's just the 3505 experience. Idk why you would care if he's slightly akward, the lectures are fine and some of his jokes are kinda funny. At the very least there is no dumb final exam, and the midterm was fair, so it was an easier A than I expected.

Prof Heisler seems a bit inexperienced, but he makes up for that by being personable and helpful and approachable. Half of the semester is group projects, find a good group and dont be afraid to switch if you dont like your first group. Heisler sometimes throws jokes into lectures which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Heisler for 2420 and 3505. You can tell he cares about what he teaches and is willing to help during office hours and answer questions during class. His grading rubrics are all very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do

Eric seems like he is figuring out the material as he goes along. Lectures, quizzes and tests are full of C++ gotcha questions that are syntax heavy. Heisler seems very unconfident and shy, which causes his lectures to be awkward and hard to follow. Assignment instructions aren't even formatted, and super hard to follow with many details left out.

He made 2420 a simple a straight-forward class which I not only thirved in but also enjoyed. Although the content was hard and came fast, he made sure to give us enough of a primer for the assignments and later the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The practice exams were nothing like the actual test. He and the TAs specifically said we wouldn't we wouldn't be tested on memorizing 2 whole algorithms, and then made us write almost the entirety of one, as well as half of the other.

Eric has gotta be the nicest guy on campus. His lectures can be boring in the way that Koptas lectures can be boring, kinda monotone but their lectures are informative and useful. My partner and I had a bug on the final project and he, no joke, helped us for TWO HOURS plus. This was way past his office hours and he genuinely wanted to help us.

Really confusing and usually boring lectures. I personally don't know if he understands java, even at the 1420 level. Also, he didn't know how to scroll down on a macbook, if that tells you about how computer science he is. Don't get me wrong, he's a super nice guy, but he makes the class conceptually harder because of the poor explanations.

Eric is a really nice guy. And he is an awesome professor. His lectures are great and his slides are clear.
Thankfully I met him, because I retook CS2420 and I couldn't understand the other professor who taught me the first time. But Professor Heisler is patient and good at teaching. I figured this class out.
I highly recommend Professor Heisler!
Great course. I wish we received more feedback before the midterm exam. You will discuss heavy topics. Professor Beeghly is engaging and fun.

Professor Beeghly had very unclear criteria for grades. Her lectures did not dive deep into course material and the logical elements of the course were often overlooked. I felt like Professor Beeghly did not have a good understanding of the course material.
I loved her as a professor she really promotes a good learning and discussion environment in class, and I felt like I actually learned a good amount for a random class I decided to take for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Perfect Gen Ed class work & discussions weren't so easy it got boring, and weren't difficult. Super understanding teacher and teaches philosophy in a way that keeps it interesting for people who aren't into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely adore Professor Beeghly! She consistently has engaging lectures that lay a wonderful foundation for philosophy. Her grading expectations are clear and she is very flexible when it comes to due dates. Her final project was a lot of work but she gave lots of great feedback and allowed for a lot of creative freedome overall.

100% would recommend her. She is the fastest grader I've ever taken a class with. She'll let you know if you did anything wrong and this feedback on homework really helps you excel on the exams. She is also extremely knowledgeable.

She said I couldn't argue a particular point because it was "empirically true" which doesn't make sense in a philosophy class. Honestly, I think she thinks sociology is philosophy. If you're serious about philosophy then I don't recommend her.
Angering. Don't take her class.

Professor Beeghly was by far one of the best professors I have ever had. I am a crim and FCHD major but had to take this philosophy class for my graduation requirement. She made the class enjoyable, and answered all my questions with kindness and thoroughly. She uses specification grading and geniunly wants every one of her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading for this class. Also, Prof Beeghly uses specifications grading so if you miss one homework question you get a 0. Luckily you always have the option to submit for full credit. The quality of the zoom class was fantastic because it was engaging and interactive. This just overall wasn't my favorite class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Beeghly is one of the most amazing professors I have had. She is so caring about her students and very flexible. We had until the end of the semester to turn in any missing assignments. There was lots of reading but it really wasn't too bad.

Professor Beeghly is a pretty fair professor. She lays out the expectations and they're not too hard to reach. This is because you get feedback and have a chance to use their feedback and revise. Uses slightly weird grading criteria but it's easy to meet. I just got burnout and skimped on my final paper which landed me a B+ on it and an A- overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Beeghly makes lectures really interesting and gives plenty of opportunity to participate, but doesn't require it. She assigns weekly homework but it isn't difficult or time-consuming and really adds to the understanding of the reading. She also cares about all of her students, even in a big class.

Prof. Beeghly is an amazing professor. She cares about what she teaches and even in big classes, she cares about each and every student. She assigns a lot of work but it is all easy to do and not time-consuming. She cares about participation so make sure to be involved.

Professor Beeghly is an amazing teacher. She is really dedicated in teaching philosophy and gives the opportunity for everyone to grow. As for her papers, it becomes really difficult to create, however she gives great feedback and allows everyone to stride for a good grade. Her class does require participation and the readings can get tedious.

Don't buy the books that are required for the class. I didn't open mine once because she goes over the reading in class. She grades papers extremely difficult and doesn't give clear criteria for what she's looking for. You have to write 2 shorts papers and a multiple choice final. Definitely wouldn't take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Good student. Just do short reading and and waiting assignments every week and you'll get a good grade. You will learn more then you think. The teacher is fun.

Erin was really awesome, she was totally understanding of my situation with family and work and always willing to help explain material! Gives great feedback on drafts of papers. She is very knowledgable! Class consisted of 3 papers, participationattendance mandatory, and a final exam.

Erin is a good teacher who clearly cares about what she is talking about. The hardest thing in her class is continually participating as this is a major chunk of your grade. Otherwise pay at least a decent amount of attention and you will do fine. She provides study guides and is extremely nice and helpful.

Lepa is the kindest teacher you will ever meet. She teaches less of memorization and numbers and more of deep understandings and qualitative learning. She is such a humble and down to earth person and acts as a teacher AND an advisor and mentor. She adjusts her class to the students needs, is flexible, and genuinely roots for her students success.

Lepa is one of the BEST professors! I've never met anyone so in-tune with their students, and who cares so much about their well-being. We had a small class, and managed to get each other off-task OFTEN. Despite this, Lepa would find ways to connect our discussions back to class, our future teaching practices, and to the topics we were discussing.

Pretty much everything is graded as either 100% or 0%, so if you do the work it is pretty much impossible to not get an A. The assignments were repetitive busywork, so they were easy but tedious. Lots of discussion posts addressing the same themes/topics over and over just applied to different books. Easy class, but I didn't really learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Left half-way through the semester and unpublished the canvas course before giving our final grades. Unreachable and would not respond to emails or messages - I had to call the English Department and try to contact her through the department head. Did not grade most assignments and projects, and we did not cover 2/3 of the texts.

Lepa is great. I was very wary at first, but became very welcoming towards her teaching style. No syllabus was given, and weekly assignments were orally given during class, but it was a nice change of pace. I am really glad I took this class with them. It was a beautiful opportunity to slow down and think about what teaching means to me.

Uses an unnecessary amount of third party programs, most of which suck, we bought three books and used HALF of ONE, homework is easy but pointless, the professor DISAPPEARED halfway through the class, and unpublished the class from Canvas before posting final grades. I learned absolutely nothing. If you see a class with her name attached, RUN.

She literally bailed on our class halfway through and just stopped adding content and assignments. Even before that what we were supposed to be doing was NEVER clear, we never got any feedback, and now it's the end of the semester and grades from the beginning haven't even been posted. No organization, no direction, utter waste of time and money.

WORST EVER. No organization, feedback, instruction, or teaching. The lack of clarity made this the most stressful class ever bc I was never sure what I was supposed to do. Espinoza's "do anything you want and you'll get full credit" is fitting for a yoga teacher, but not a university professor. Not hard, but not pleasant.

Espinoza is incredibly 2-faced. She's nice in class but seems judgmental in class disucssions. There were insane amounts of reading outside of class. I was on track to receive an A in the class and she failed me on the final due to her biases and opinions even tho I fulfilled every requirement on the final paper. I wouldn't recommend her to anyone
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lepa assigns a lot of reading for ENGL 2600, but it's easy to get an A without doing most of it. My class only met once a week (for 3 hours) but we almost always got out at least an hour early. This is a very easy class, and Lepa is nice and easy to get along with. I would recommend taking this class.

One of my favorite professors throughout my college experience. She is incredibly knowledgeable and really makes you think. I did not know what to expect when enrolling in the course, but I was overwhelmingly surprised by how quickly it became my favorite course. She made me love and care about film in a way I did not believe, for me, was possible.
I really liked her. She's knowledgeable and I really liked that she took the time to explain things and make them clear or less obscure to me.

Leave your ego at the door or you'll walk back out that door crying. If your opinion is wrong, she will tell you so, but the worst thing you can do is have no opinion at all. She knows a a little about everything and everything about a few things, so trust what she says. She's right.
She was very intimidating. She knows her stuff, and she will share it, but she is demeaning and makes you question your decision of studying French.

Grad Lit Theory is going to be hard. That's what you got. And her writing assignments are so demanding! But it's good for you, so take your medicine. You'll thank her daily when you're done, because she knows her stuff, and can explain these convoluted ideas better than almost anyone. OUTSTANDING.

I liked Professor Espinosa. She did a good job in this class. She took the time to explain things or make them less obscure to me. She dedicated her time to make this class interesting. We had some fascinating discussions in class.
This professor has unreasonable expectations. If you want to get a good grade give yourself 10+ a week to study and take good notes. She is extremely boring! Find a different teacher.

It's obvious that she knows her subject well, but frankly, she's just another white lady who thinks she's a revolutionary. Unclear and disorganized in class, arbitrary grading system, ideologically and intellectually puritanical. Certainly knowledgeable but not helpful. Avoid if possible, but unfortunately, the U's Spanish program is lousy.
I want to bang my head against my desk every second I was in this class. She has pop quizzes and she is genuinely uninteresting.

Esther is a good teacher who cares about her students. That being said, she assigns readings on top of homework on top of projects. At least an hour of homework is to be expected every night. If mini-deadlines work well for you, she's your teacher.
Pretty easy class, basic writing. Esther was helpful and fun. I had significantly less homework than my roomates who had another teacher.

Esther was a great teacher for my intro to creative writing class. She seemed genuinely interested in what people had to say, and managed to keep the class fun, encouraging a lot of participation, while creating an atmosphere that was both critical yet constructive. The assigned readings were great, very well balanced. All in all a great class!
Projects are graded in pieces so its very easy to finish on time. Very helpful. If you have to take a writing class take it from her.
Esther really helped me improve my writing. I went from a student who struggled so much in my high school writing classes to an A student and I learned a lot about rhetoric and how to analyze.

Ethan was a very mediocre lecturer, like most Math teachers. He covers mostly hard examples and is a little unclear about what types of problems you will see on the test unless you ask. although he is a very generous grader, cares about his students, and is willing to help wherever needed. You are allowed note pages too.

While he is very lecture heavy, he explains things very well and answers questions well. the course material is obviously tough it's calculus but he grades fairly. even allows a whole front and back page of notes for each exam.

Lectures were very word heavy. He was more conceptual and didn't explain the techniques clearly. Tests matter a lot, but he was pretty generous with grading. Lectures became repetitive and he drags on with problems that were easier than the homework/test.
Only did examples, never actually showed fundamentals

While nice in general, Professor Morgan finds it difficult to teach Math 1070 effectively. He instructs the entire class straight from the textbook in a manner that leaves the majority of the students confused. In general, his ability to teach the material is lacking, and at times, he is unable to provide students with the answers they need.

For Econ 4700 - the lectures were very engaging and well related to topics that students find interesting, but the course is only graded on three exams. You can have a 1 page note sheet so its not too bad, but if your not a good test taker be aware of that. He randomly offers extra credit for showing up to class so its good to go for that reason

I went to class everyday and took detailed notes which I reviewed and edited with information from the readings. He used different methods to explain things (examples, equations, graphs) which was very helpful. Quizzes and exams were open note and there was no textbook required.

Haha... Hilarious.  I really enjoyed his lectures.  He's really perky (which I think is a mix between his personality and his coffee).  No average person is that awake at 8 AM in the winter.  Good class.
Great teacher! Would love to take another class from him! Funny and keeps things interesting. Really learned a lot.
Great teacher. Worth taking a class from him.
Great teacher.
He is a low-talker, even in a tiny classroom I could barely hear him. The assignments were easy, but the tests were pretty challenging.
He isn't the most engaging professor, and doesn't really involve the class in lectures, but he's good to explain everything very clearly. The homework was easy but the tests were hard.
Great professor.

Overall, I enjoyed Ethan's class and feel that I learned a lot. I could see how his process is not for everyone, but for those who applied themselves, there was plenty to gain from. At times it did seem like he was figuring out the curriculum, but he always made himself available for students, which in my estimate is the sign of a good professor.

Mr. Weyand was a complete newbie to the teaching game, he was an astute and intelligent Professor.  I am sure he will continue to take his real world business skills that most Professors lack and translate them into the curriculum while continually improving the learning experience.  Overall Mr. Weyand is a good and more than competent Professor.

Ethan is not qualified to be an instructor.  I have no doubt he can do an accountants job, but he lacks the understanding of how to prepare and translate his knowledge into a manner that is comprehensible to his students.  We attended class for at least 4 weeks before he  began actually teaching. Our first exam was week six. Guess how many failed.

I'm quite surprised that Professor Mishchenko has a low rating on here. If you are passionate about the subject and show interest in the material, he is very engaging. He has been one of my favorite professors and always went the extra mile to break down complex ideas. He was willing to stay after class to dive deeper if necessary.

The course topics are all very difficult, but the professor was extremely proficient at explaining them in simple, easily digestible terms. He was also very good at breaking down the process for solving problems into simple steps which were easy to replicate. Between the professor's resources and the textbooks, I gained a strong understanding.

If you have other options do not take a class from him. His lectures are average and you get the same webassign homework with any physics class. However is tests are the worst thing ever created. My grade was saved by the curve yours might not be

Homework, group problems, and practice exams looked nothing like the tests. I hard failed almost every test, including the final, but aced the homework and group projects. Was certain I'd fail, but he curved the class hella, so hopefully he changes something in the future. Don't take him.

This professor is really kind when I went to him for help. However, his tests, (and especially the final) are nearly impossible to get a good grade on. Instead of testing us on the material we have learned, we are tested on material that is foreign and unfamiliar. Take this course from another professor if you get stressed over tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfortunately Eugene has decided to focus on being a lawyer, more than teaching. Over three midterms, and one final he did not show up to a single exam. The lack of showing up represents the lack of care for his students . Not only that, the course material he taught v. homework v. exams were not cohesive. Do not have him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is a sad, cruel joke. Eugene has set up a system in which there is very little to no connection between the lectures, discussions, homework, and the exams; Consequently, nothing is to be learned in here. It's clear that he knows his stuff but frustrating that he can't seem to share it in a useful, practical, or effective way. Avoid him.

Eugene is the worst professor I've ever had. He needs to swallow his pride and plan a lecture, you might as well watch khan academy during lecture and take a picture of the board just in case one of his obscure examples is half relevant for the exam. It's the weekend before the final and I still have no Idea where I stand in the class. Avoid him.
Don't take him!!!!!!!! He does not care about his students. HIs tests are so hard even though you are not in Physic major

The professor opens the semester with a speech "I'm not here to teach you how to solve problems." The tests are not representative of all the subjects covered but rather one specific thing unannounced to the class. One note card. No curve. Tests are 57% of the final grade. Discussions are group quiz's, not teaching/help session.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is definitely not mandatory. Dr. Mishchenko reads and does examples directly from the book. The tests are easy because they are literally the homework problems with different numbers. That is really the only positive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not really necessary to show up to either the lectures or discussion. The textbook contains everything you need, and solutions to the harder homework problems can be found online (after a bit of digging). Tests are the biggest portion of your grade, but they are easy as their problems are taken directly from the homework.

Awful teacher. Boring lectures not related to hw. TAs don't teach well as mine made mistakes and apologized for not being ready often. 4 exams and one 4x6 card allowed per test. Two flash cards on final. WOW. Worst class Do not take from him
Go to class or you'll fail!!!!!!!!!! Or just copy the homework problems on your notecard like everyone else. The latter is easier to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have no complaints about webassign which is the hw system the physics department uses. He isn't a very good lecturer. Honestly, I would've preferred if he had used Flipitphysics/Smartphysics in conjunction for the last (like I had with 2210) because it at least introduces you to the material.

Like everyone said, this course doesn't teach you physics. His lectures are useless, MY discussion TA was even worse so I had no help from both. His test are directly from the HW, just different numbers. He allows 1 flashcard per test. Tip: make extremely nice flashcards throughout the semester and they will save you for the final.

lmao. I'm typing this review during his lecture, and I'm getting the same amount of information from it than my classmates. A.K.A, the lectures are basically useless. If you have the right T.A, however, the discussions are very useful.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures have no connection to tests and homework.  I do the homework and go to discussion and I get more out of those then I do his lectures. He covers some material that is covered in the homework but that's about it. The tests are exactly like the homework just different numbers.

Currently taking class with him. His lectures are not useful for the homework at all. But that's just part of the deal with physics classes. They can only teach you so much. I am teaching myself by skimming through the book and youtube. The TAs don't really explain much either. So if you want to to take physics, take an easy load.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His style of lecturing is doing a bunch of example problems, which I didn't like at all. Not only do you not learn the theory, it also doesn't help you solve other problems that he didn't do in class.
The answers to the quizzes were all in the textbook and everything was open book
