The class is pretty straightforward. There are weekly assignments and quizzes, but they're usually pretty easy as long as you stay on top of them. I didn't really have much communication with the professor throughout the semester, but everything was clear enough to get through without needing a lot of help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy while also being informative. There were weekly quizzes that were based on the professor's powerpoints, so make sure to always read those. There were also a few article reports, but it was easy to get full points on them. Overall, this class was a good experience for me.

Grade on Canvas and final grade doesn't match saying the canvas grading isn't using her grading system. You never know what's your grade like. And she deleted course right after grades are submitted. Why?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good Professor
She doesn't respond to emails online if you want to do office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had a very difficult time with this class. I took ECON 3100 prior in person, and had little to no issues. But taking this online class felt like I should have been taking a 4500 class or worse. Do not take this class online at all costs. Eunice is a great professor who cares for students to do well. Its very hard online to understand material.
Dr. Han is a very knowledgeable in economics and makes it easy for students to understand. She is very lenient with grading her exams and is willing to bump grades. I recommend taking her.

All the information in quizzes can be found in the homework or lectures and is very straightforward. Eunice is so wonderful to learn from and is always very willing to clarify or explain material. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taking this course online with Professor Han was very manageable. Your grade is only based off of weekly quizzes and a final, but as long as you look at the practice assignments and pay attention it is easy to get a good grade. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Han's class, while dry at times, has been informative and pretty straightforward. While I can't speak for her in-person classes, this online class has been a fairly positive experience. My only gripe is that quizzes can be more in-depth than the lecture material, but her TA explains these concepts well, and I'd say even better than Han.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my most memorable and outstanding professors. You can tell she respects herself and her role as an educator. Wish I could have her in a bunch of other classes too She's so reasonable. She knows the material and makes it easy to learn. I feel like I will actually use what I learned in Labor Economics because of the way she taught it.

Professor Han is a very solid choice when taking ECON 2010. She has detailed PowerPoints that (Pro Tip) if combined make for easy tests and exams via the good ole Ctrl - F function. Other than that there was no mandatory homework and the use of TA led discussion sections give you a place to ask all your burning questions. Enjoy the free A/B

The embodiment of what a good professor is supposed to be. Very engaging and makes a somewhat bland subject become super fun. She is very considerate with grading and tests. She is probably one of the more caring people that I have ever come across. I just wish attendance was mandatory because class participation could have made it 10x better.

Professor Han was very thorough and articulate when teaching this class. I've seen some who complain that she just reads off the powerpoints but she actually explains further beyond the contents in the slides. This helps you better understand what is going on and make the problem applicable and understandable.

Each class session consists of her reading you the slides. Homework content doesn't resemble the slides or exams at all. Because the actual course content is redundant and quite simple, many exam questions are deliberately intended to trick students, so be sure to study hard. It's worth it to buy/rent the latest version of the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were mediocre and repetitive, but attendance counted for a portion of the grade. Homework was completely unrelated to the midterms and final. Midterms and Finals were multiple choice, but they are designed to make sure you actually understand the concepts rather than just being able to do the math.

Lectures are just her reading her slides verbatim to you. Homework assignments go a lot deeper than her lectures but her slides are not a good enough resource to help you do them. Overall grade is moreorless determined by 2 exams that you are ill-prepared for (both of which are 25 multiple choice questions) which are designed to trick you.

I really loved taking professor Han's class. She's very knowledgable and has really great insights. She's also very personable and funny! This class does move pretty quickly but there are a lot of resources to help (ie. friday sessions to review and ask TA's your specific questions, Han's flexible office hours, online access..) Great professor!

This class moves very fast and covers a lot of material. Han tries her best to clearly explain topics, but it's simply just a hard subject. Lectures are covered with powerpoints that can be accessed outside of class at any time. Han is very nice and she will always make you laugh in class. She's always available to help and wants you to do good

She is new to big lectures so she's sometimes clumsy. She is very easy going... too easy I think. Cause there is no attendance or pop quizzes. Every slides for the class can be found online and in lectures she just reads from the slides. Homework and papers are super closely related to the class content and they help improving GPA significantly

Very respectable, she brings a competitive edge to the grading (she taught at Harvard). We butted heads at the beginning but she quickly became one of the best teachers I've ever had.  I have never learned more about a subject than I did from Han. GREAT TEACHER! She is also very personable, the entire class was always 100% engaged.
Very kind professor. By far my easiest class. He's very engaged and wants the best for each student. Easy to reach out to and engaging.

All this class is is quizzes and tests if taken online. The test have weirdly worded questions that are difficult to pick out from lecture slides. Easy class but the tests made me feel angry when I would miss stupid questions.

Lectures are directly from the textbook; you could spend 1-1.5 hours a week outside of class reading the textbook and doing the assignment and just not show up to class.
Concepts can be very confusing; don't take this class unless you're really into the atmosphere and weather.

Took this class to reach full-time. All online, homework is easy, exams are easy but long. Don't buy the textbook, he wrote it, it's a cash grab. answers are on slides he provides or quizlets already made by others. Not great at communicating, takes multiple days to answer a simple question. Use ctr F to find answers on slides and you'll be fine.

The professor is nice but the class was way harder than it needed to be. For one he made us take a lot of long tests throughout the semester and most of the questions were extremely hard to find answers for. The book that he wrote is unnecessarily expensive. The homework is very easy and he drops 1 out of the 4 tests at the end of the semester.

If you read through the content provided youll be fine. I took this class fully online and I wish there was a little more explanation on some modules. I had to use google/YouTube to fully understand some things

I can understand if a professor has difficulties because of Covid, but this professor was unorganized and a total MESS! His slides were filled with grammatical errors, incoherent, and overall unorganized. He just gives you info and expects you to know the material. The tests are filled with jumbled info and he's a tough grader. DON'T DO IT!

Absolutely ridiculous class, you don't really learn the concepts, he just gives you info. You don't know how to apply this information, even though he wants you to do that on his tests. Even when you've studied the study guide he gives you, he puts other information that wasn't on the study guide on the test. Don't take this class what ever you do.

This guy is eccentric, to say the least, but not in the way you want your professors to be. This class felt like a scheme for him to get his difficult, unpopular textbook to sell. He spoke quickly and quietly and his train of thought was near impossible to follow. Take another class.

This class is NOT an easy A. You need to study to get the grade that you want. The textbook is a bit confusing if you're not already familiar with the subject, I would recommend going to lectures. Although I didn't go to lectures I still passed with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very nice guy but the class was very stale. Don't be fooled by the title, you absolutely have to study and put in work for a good grade. It's more about the atmosphere than weather. Some concepts were unusually difficult for a 1000 level class. Only take if you are very interested in the subject. He did give a nice unexpected curve at the end

Great teacher. If you try, you pass. Attendance not mandatory, shows power points in class and puts them on canvas. There are 3 exams and one 10min presentation. Exams are a little hard because what he puts on the study guides and what you think is important, doesn't actually end up on the exam. But he is caring of students and curves grades.

Had an assignment each week that were roughly 10 questions.  Such an amazing professor.  He's more than willing to help you if you have questions about material or grade.  Absolutely love his "Too many books, too little time" sweater.  Such a sweet guy.

thsi class is not an easy a. 1 hw assignment/week.   No final. This class isn't a easy A. You have to attend pretty regularly and study for exams. Sometimes he will post the hw online but sometimes he will announce it in class. Not strict on late work. Material for tests are clear but you should still study. Good gen Ed req.

OK class. Learned a lot. However, attendance is not required, but I think it is important to go to class or your test scores drop. Grade based on five tests only. Professor is really nice guy! Offers some EC. Just don't think since he post's online you can teach yourself. Going to class, reading the book, and studying is necessary.

Chung is a great professor. The lectures are simple and straightforward but not the same as the reading. I didn't do most of the readings but she takes a few exam questions from it. There is one weekly timed quiz and an optional extra credit discussion. The exams are not hard but they are a big portion of your grade.

I would recommend taking classes from Professor Chung. She clearly enjoys what she is teaching and teaches the material in a way that was easy to absorb. There was no homewor, only weekly quizzes and a midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was a great online class, and I would highly recommend it! There was one quiz a week based on the textbook and video lectures. The midterm and final were open note. There were also optional extra credit discussions. Very straightforward and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There was only two tests and just weekly quizzes that were only 5-10 questions. The class is set up very clear. The online video lectures were interesting and very easy to follow which helped with the weekly quizzes.

There was little interaction between myself and Chung, but the class was set up pretty well. Everything was organized, and the class was very easy. She doesn't try to trick you on quizzes or tests. If you're considering taking the class, do it! It's easy and the final isn't as bad as you think.

This class has light readings, incredibly short video lectures (30 mins/week tops), and extra credit discussion boards. Content is easy to understand with clear lecture videos. Weekly quizzes, a midterm, and a final determine your grade. But the midterm and final reuses questions from the quizzes (you can open them both and find 80% of the answers)

This class mainly consisted of reading, and a couple of short lectures every week. There was a weekly quiz every week along with a midterm and final. So your grade was based on just tests. There was also opportunities for extra credit. The class wasn't very hard if you looked at the reading guides and watched the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took POLS 2100 with Professor Chung and she was great! Clear grading criteria, easy-to-understand lectures, and straightforward exams/quizzes. Definitely recommend for the POLS 2100 credit, pretty easy A if you stay on top of coursework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class had readings and recorded lectures every week with a quiz. However, the class has two tests that are worth 65% of your grade, so use the readings and reading guide to prepare for the test. Extra credit through non-mandatory discussion boards was also available. Overall, an interesting and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chung has assignments and lectures that are straightforward. The recorded lectures are brief and very informative. Grades consist of weekly quizzes and two exams. Exams are heavily weighted; however, she prepares reading guides for us to succeed. Discussion board participation results in extra credit but is not mandatory. Simple class.
While I haven't spoken to or even heard Professor Chung's voice, their class has been straightforward and informative.
Very responsive to emails and offers good extra credit opportunities!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes, midterm, and final. Lectures were short and to the point, and overall the class wasn't bad at all if you do the readings (or even skim like I did). Not much class interaction, but I didn't mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: really easy elective, you dont have to study much because the answers are easy to find, overall interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pols 2100 is not a hard class, its pretty clear on what is expected however the midterm and final are very important for keeping a good grade! Just take lots of notes & understand the concepts. She is also very knowledgeable and explains each topic well enough.

Great teacher, just not the best learning and teaching style for me personally!! My book was taken at my work mid semester and let me tell you, you need those things! I thought my grades were fine and then I missed 8 questions out of 70 on exam 1 and then I had a B-, very sad and hard to recover from! Kind of bummed about it but she is a good!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I didnt mind this class, the quizzes are all on quizlet but DONT rely on quizlet for the information. The quizlets will not help you on the tests, and if you dont actually do the work to learn you will earn a failing grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Chung is an understanding person with clear standards for grading. Showing up and doing the homework guarantees a good grade.

Class consisted of weekly quizzes (you can take up to two times), a midterm, & a final. Weekly discussion was extra credit. There were two textbooks needed for the class. Lecture videos could be as long as 20 min up to 1+ hours. Honestly, all the weekly quizzes can be found on quizlet (but not all of the questions on exams can be found on quizlet)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her Peace & Conflict in Asia course is wonderful. She is well knowledged and her lectures are easy to sit through. She tries to be engaging as possible. She does require a lot of reading so stay on top of that for class.

Online class, very straightforward. Weekly quizzes and 2 tests. Participation in discussions is extra credit. Make sure to watch the lectures AND textbook for quizzes; a lot of the quiz material is from lecture. Easy A if you don't miss any quizzes.
Super easy class, just take a multiple choice quiz every week along with midterm and final that is all the homework.

POLS 2100 was straight forward. It takes a few hours per week and she personally records lectures. I listened to the videos on 1.5 speed and breezed through this class. I would definitely take this class if you don't want to spend too much time and effort on POLS intro courses, but still want to pick up the basics.

Most assignments are done in class, but you do them on your own time if you like. Eugene is a great teacher because you learn by doing. He creates fun assignments. You do have to work for your grade, but he is very caring and willing to help. Honestly, a great class, but not one you can breeze by. He helps you become invested in art.

He is a very laid back professor to a fault. Whenever you have a question he points you to the manual for your camera or the internet. He uses his own platform for turning in assignments which can be difficult for non-Apple users at times. I didnt really like him all that much as a professor so I would definitely reconsider taking his class.
As long as you complete the assignments, you WILL get an A. Super easy A
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Eugene is a great guy and a good professor. A little bit disorganized, but as far as Seeing (photography foundations) as long as you pay attention and follow instructions you'll do great in the class. Definitely worth getting to know. I loved how much he pays attention to the content of work, fosters great discussion. A low-stress class
-- Textbook is optional, __never__ used -- Good instructor -- Easy for people who skip class to get behind

Very unhelpful, could care less about his students, very impatient, hardly taught- rather just read from his pre-made assignment sheets, never really gave any feedback. I feel like this class was a waste of time, he really needs to care more about his students. Doesn't answer questions either.

Probably worst at explaining things. When I ask questions he says, "its on the instruction". Ok? I read through like 5 times and I came for help because the instructions are poorly written. You get assignment every class and due dates are end of semester. No email support, updates grade like 3 times per semester, limited support take it from others

Not that he wasn't a great professor, but I probably would have enjoyed taking the course online. I don't know if it was just my specific class, but he did not teach. Assignment files were just put on the server and we basically taught ourselves. I saw absolutely no point in even going to class. Did like the WAY laxed due dates.
Nice guy. Informative class. Easy A.
Eugene is a way chill guy.  He lets you redo all assignments so you can get 100% in the class.  If you do all the assignments, which aren't that hard, you will get an A. Take this for an art credit.

Eugene is a great photography teacher. You will learn how to use different techniques with your digital camera and how to use photoshop. The class is a lot of fun and attendance isn't mandatory. But it is easy to fall behind on assignments if you don't show up to class.

He's a great photographer professor! I enjoyed him a lot. He allows you to redo all your photo assignments to get an A. It's nearly impossible to NOT get an A in his class. Show up to class because it's easier to stay on top of your photo assignments if you do so. Overall he's a good professor.

Don't understand the other comments because he is genuinely discouraging and mean spirited at times. Never had a worse class critique in my life. Actively seeks to tear down work and doesn't feel constructive at all. He is an extremely picky and hard to please teacher. The homework and revisions feel extremely redundant. Workload does not match

I learned a lot from Dan but he is often rude to studens. When asking questions, he will just tell you to google it instead of being helpful. Go in with thick skin, and google technical questions you may have instead of asking him.

dan gives a lot of good advice and feedback to help you become better. come in with an open mind and be accepting to constructive criticism. there is a heavy amount of homework but he acknowledges this himself. just put in the time and show up to class and you'll be good

Instructor publicly singles out and embarrasses students for minor things like file delays or not staring at him. Extremely homework heavy, assignments due every single class. Class is rigid, critiques are harsh and subjective. Experimentation and outside the box thinking highly discouraged. Head of department, enrollment options are limited.

Dan is really warm hearted. He puts a lot of effort into teaching design principles during the beginning years of the program. It really helps further along. The program and my education wouldn't have been the same without him. 10/10.

Dan has definitely made me a better student/designer, but he can be harsh on his students in a way that feels unnecessary at times. He knows his stuff, but if you take a class from him, go in with thick skin and don't take anything personally. Also, show up to class, it's a big deal in this course.

Grades too harshly, which creates an unfavorable environment for learning, placing too much unnecessary stress on students. Assignments are drawn out to the point of redundancy, tedious, and unimaginative. Grading system is based on subjective and often arbitrary criteria. Instructor is high-strung and unpleasant, impossible to please
He really knows what he is talking about but is very strict. Don't feel bad when he critiques your work, it comes out pretty harsh but he has made me a better student.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took Calc 1 twice. Tyler was significantly easier than my first teacher, only really focused on basics. Very approachable. Offered a little bit of extra credit on a few exams. Practice tests were almost identical to the actual exams.
the GOAT, best prof i've had at the U

Evans is easily one of the nicest professors I've had.  Practice exams are super similar to real exams, and he has a lot of office hours. He's super patient, clearly cares about his students, and makes a scary class pretty approachable. He will try to convince you to add a math major though.

Really easy to follow, lectures are well prepared and worth attending, and on tests credit is given if he can tell you get the concepts but make a algebraic mistake (which saved me a couple times)
Additionally he is just nice and friendly :)
this guy is just the best prof
Professor Evans was an excellent professor who made a difficult subject easy and enjoyable.
Amazing professor! Take him!  He is so nice and is very clear on what to expect on the exams.

Dr. Evans was an amazing professor. I am really terrible at math, no idea how I got into precalculus, but when I needed help, he was always there during office hours and hyped to teach. Unfortunately, you will be hearing a lot of x jokes.

Would say the class was extremely easy with ample opportunity for extra credit. Neither of which are bad but we did linger on topics, made understanding easy. Professor was cut, dry and relatively funny. Material was taught as easily as possible while still covering the content as we were introduced ways to derive and apply probability techniques
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although it was a very easy subject, he made it a lot easier. Very respectful and is heavily inclined to listen to any and all feedback. He makes adjustments if needed and really cares about the students. Very awesome teacher. I wholly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: AMAZING! Funny guy, cares about us a lot, and wants each and every one of us to succeed. He gives us the freedom to chose the problems that we desire, records lectures, gives us mulitple chances to get our assignments correct. I love him to death and would totally recomment him.

Great professor. No complaints from me. He did a great job teaching and explaining subjects. We had no notes available for our final exam but it was okay since his practice and overall teaching really helped you prepare.

I really enjoyed this class because of Professor Evans. I was weary about taking a theory math class but he made it super enjoyable and interesting! He makes his lectures accessible by recording them but going in person is best. He makes funny math jokes and overall has a really pleasant personality! You will not regret having him as a teacher

Professor Evans reallly understands students and treats us like equals. He's takes the stress out of a math course, homework isn't bad, lectures are streamed and recorded, he's quick to respond to emails and suggestions. He's good professor and an understanding person.

This was an amazing math course because Tyler gave the whole class freedom in how much homework assignments we wanted for the semester. He also graded more on our mathematical approaches and creativity with solving problems more so than for just the correct answer. He also didn't have exams for this course. Least stressful upper division math.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's Prof. Evans first time teaching the class, but he really ensures everyone understands the material and genuinely cares about his students. Real Analysis is difficult but Prof. Evans makes it a nice experience by having very lenient grading policies and having streaming + recorded lectures.
Professor Evans is a very new professor, but really cares about his students and that they understand the content. Tests were hard but graded very fairly. Highly recommend.

Great teacher, probably the best I've had at the U! He makes differential equations fun which should be considered a superpower. Wish all my professors were like Dr. Evans he's the GOAT. He's funny, very good at slowing down and explaining things, and I did well because I genuinely understood the content. Highly recommend.

Professor Evans is very informative and engaging in his lectures and open to questions. He takes great effort to make sure his students fully understand all of the course content, and he is very approachable both in and out of class.

I sort of respect Dan as a designer but not as a teacher. He is unfair and vague and contradicts himself constantly. He encourages questions, but when his directions are unclear, and someone asks for clarification, he gets mad and attempts to embarrass them. He says he "recommends" certain techniques, but if you don't use them, he gets very upset.

Worst class of my academic career so far. Vague assignment instructions and even more vague feedback on those assignments. Teachers in the design program should be able to be inspire their students, not constantly tear them down. After my experience here I would not even recommend the UofU to anyone.

Dan knows his stuff but in this class he rarely gave constructive feedback. The feedback he gave was vague and harsh, as were his grades. If you are already stellar at what you are doing he will be nicer, but if you are trying to learn new concepts then I would not recommend his class for anything.

Dan was such an amazing teacher. He is very tough on grading, and critique but it always comes from him wanting everyone to be better and be the best that they possibly can. That said, my design skills grew drastically at the same time that I was growing as a person, and he helped out in so many ways. Loved his class and wish he taught more.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dan is passionate and knows a lot about design. He pushes you to become better and helps you not settle on something just because it's "good enough" or something that will just meet the criteria. While he does expect a lot out of his students, it is something that should be appreciated. If you want to become a better designer, take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dan is awesome. He really knows design and he knows how to teach as well.  Homework is tough, expect to spend 20+ homework hours per project.  But it is very rewarding because he pushes you to become better.
Very good teacher, but a little too tough.

Dan is the best professor I have ever had. He is clear, consistent, and very direct. If he doesn't like something, he will say why and offer constructive methods of repairing it. His classes are NOT EASY! He is demanding and will push you until you know the subject through and through. He is exceptional and I'm ecstatic to have him as a teacher.
He really knows his stuff
Dan can be very picky when it comes to get the details and specifics right on a project, but he knows his stuff.

Professor Everett has to be one of the nicest professors I have had. You can tell she really loves what she is teaching. There was five homework assignments and three exams. Both the exams and homework were relatively easy if you had looked at the powerpoint slides and or watched the video lectures.

Signed up for this as a throwaway course. Would have stayed like that if not for Bethany. Opened up a whole new world for me. Her passion was contagious despite our different world views. I recommend this course with this professor to everyone.

Professor Everett is such a kind and funny women. It is simple to get an A in her class if you turn everything in on time. The test averages are around a B+ and she grades the three papers easy. She also teaches very interesting and straight forward material. I definitely recommend taking a course from her!

There were only 5 assignments the whole year, 3 exams and a couple extra credit assignments that were pretty easy. I honestly never watched any of the lectures and got an A. The canvas organization was pretty bad, but it never stopped me from finding my work. Accepts late work for 2 days after deadline w/o penalty, responds quick to emails.
A lot of the points are based on the assignments, which there are not very many of. They are picky in the grading of these assignments. There is a no late work at all policy.
Not sure if she is necessarily hilarious but she does have a way of making the class laugh, she also has a way in making people have synchronized crying with her too.

AWESOME TEACHER. One of the best I've had at the U - test heavy but she gives you the information you need to pass with an A. Extra credit is offered and she is available for office hours :) would definitely take her again.

Dr. Everett was fantastic, she was very fair in her class and I thoroughly enjoyed having her. The only thing I would say was that her TA was very involved with the grading and I don't believe was nearly as fair as she would have been in regards to grading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is an overall good teacher. She knows what she is talking about, but sometimes gets away from the point. Very passionate politically and can be a little annoying with the projection of her views. Overall a pretty easy class if you do the work. She does like 8 super easy attendance quizzes throughout the semester, just to make sure you come.

Dr. Everett is AMAZING! I am very disappointed that I am graduating as she is starting to teach more of the Sociology classes. Take anything you can from Dr. Everett. She is incredibly knowledgable and does research that is truly impactful.

Professor Miller is amazing. She is super funny and knowledgeable about the material. She cares about students and will go out of her way to help outside of class. Highly recommend. Only downside is that she's very attractive and for guys that can be a distraction :)
Very unorganized. Tests are intense. Material on tests not covered at all through material given. Slideshows that she gives make no sense. Not worth it, stay away.
Miller was so nice. She is so knowledgeable and willing to help. Her syllabus is clear and organized. She wants her students to succeed!

A great professor and mentor!  Dr. Miller engendered my own lust for cognitive-neuroscience and helped attain the goals I aimed to achieve.  As a professor, she pulled all of her students into class by using pure interest as her weapon of choice.  No one was required to show up, participate, or do anything most classes require, yet everyone did!

Most of the grade is based on just a few assignments. Instructions are very vague, and if you don't interpret them as she expected, your grade will suffer. She will tell you how to improve in the future, but you can't earn points back. I wish instructions were clear *before* assignments. Participation points and extra credit help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs. As has been said in so many reviews, she does not work well with the disability center or disabled students and has a tendency for anti-black rhetoric. Her feedback is nonsensical and contradictory. I can not tell you even now what she wanted out of any of it. My advice? Do not take any of her classes.

reviews.comment: I am surprised she still has a place as a teacher here given the amount of issues she puts on the disability department and disabled students. This isn't a course for anyone's major. I'm sorry but my class on India shouldn't be taking up this much time, I have stuff for my actual major to study for. Hard grader. Hard, confusing quizzes that she tries to trick you with wording. Very critical on papers too.

reviews.comment: This professor made the course a joy to learn about, her lectures goes in depth and the teacher outlines her expectations of the students well.

Be in class on time, stay attentive in class discussions and read all the material provided through Canvas and you should do fine with her course. Her syllabus is straightforward in how it lays out the topics to be covered and she keeps faithful to it.

Very knowledgeable and passionate about subject matter, I thoroughly enjoyed this class and insightful lectures. I highly recommend for anyone remotely interested in India and Pakistan, I had no beforehand knowledge but left with a lot of newfound interest. Class wasn't difficult if you show up and take notes on lectures.

Christine was great. I really enjoyed taking her class. The material was interesting and she had a great sense of humor. I'm not sure what others on here are talking about, because getting a decent grade is not impossible if you are willing to put in the effort. I 100% recommend this class and professor.

reviews.comment: It seems like there is one resentful student abusing the review system, and giving the teacher a bad rap. That being said, be ready to put lots of effort towards the class. Will probably need to visit the writing center several times

reviews.comment: I thought she was a great professor. She really challenges Business students to analyze, think critically, and write well. I think she is an organized, thoughtful, and challenging professor.

This professor is a Humanities professor that sometimes teachings the business schools humanities classes. I read a lot of negative reviews of her but they are all from business students. If you are in the Humanities you will love this class!! She is incredibly knowledgable and her aim is to help you understand content and not to test you details.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Be ready to receive the most harsh and offensive feedback on your writing. Hard to grasp what she is looking for, it's a guessing game that gambles grades. reviews.comment: This class is incredibly difficult but for all the wrong reasons. If you want to do well in this class be prepared endure harsh feedback and meandering, confusing answers to all your questions.

reviews.comment: AVOID this class at all costs. Class is a joke and a waste of time. 3 quizzes, 2 papers, and 1 written essay final. Papers are extremely over analyzed, and you will get a bad grade if you don't write exactly what she wants or expects. Worst class I've ever taken.

reviews.comment: I went on here and read the reviews for this professor and decided to take this course anyways, DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE! Do NOT take this course.

reviews.comment: Bad class. Has nothing to do with globalization in the business world. Focused on religions and rituals. I'll hire a consultant to do business in their culture, teach me real macro stuff!!! Terribly strict grade

reviews.comment: Christine  is one of the best profs! She presents a wealth of information on India  concisely and informatively, to where after class I was inspired to look up more. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Christine critically over analyzes the two papers that you have to do in this class to a tee; if you don't put what she wants to hear then you will lose significant points. The first paper is due well after the class withdrawal deadline too. She has unnecessarily tricky questions on her quizzes. Take my advice and do not take her if you want an A.
Dr. Everaert's style of teaching is ideal for learning Hindi.  No other language class I have ever taken has been as effective as Dr. Everaert's.  This is an excellent class!!

Unless you are the most politically correct person in the world, you do not want to take a class from Everaert.  If you confuse one of the more than ten different religious sects she teaches you about, she will destroy your papers.  The class is very vague but if you are vague or don't repeat her opinion verbatim,  you will fail.

It's hard to know what to expect from her. She will go to town and stop at nothing to destroy your papers, although her direction on the papers is very vague and abstract. All of her PowerPoints are directly copy and pasted from a quick  Google search and class consists of talking about irrelevant details or concepts.

The class was not clear on the objective.  Paper were nitpicked heavily.  Her comments on my paper were longer than my actual paper.  I enjoyed her class if it had not been part of my major I would have left it.  I'm not sure I really got anything useful out of it.  I think I could have learned just as much ready a couple books over a weekend.

She's incredibly smart, and very very tough. Changed syllabus on us midway through the semester after the class withdrawl period. Originally was supposed to have only two papers and a final paper. Included 3 quizzes at the end. Tough grader. Papers were nitpicked to the dot. First time the class was taught, so everything was on the go.

Josh is a great professor. He is knowledgable, passionate and caring. Josh wants his students to succeed and he's super understanding. If you come to class, you will do well. He gives great lectures and we had tons of awesome discussions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Josh was great all semester! His lectures were really entertaining and he gives study guides before all of the tests. As he did 10 quizzes, I wouldn't recommend skipping the reading or skipping class.
Great class. He is a grades fairly. Had one paper, and 3 exams including the final total alongside 10 quizzes. COMM3050

Really easy going professor! You don't really need to take notes from the lecture because he will give you a study guide with everything you need to know for the tests, I only used the book when I studied for the tests. You do have to give a speech but it's not hard at all about 5 min long, and it's only to a small group. Take his class!

Josh is a really cool guy, you can't go wrong with him. His expectations are very clear and always keeps class interesting. You do have to give a speech in 1270, though, so keep that in mind if that is something that might make you anxious/stray away from taking a course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Josh really cares about his students and their success. He gives you time to work in groups on your study guides before exams. As long as you do the reading, the quizzes and lectures will be easy. I've taken two classes with him so far and would happily take another; he's a really great professor.

Josh is awesome, and hilarious. The course is quite difficult and hard to grasp some concepts, but he makes it a little easier. Tough readings followed by quizzes. Provides a study guide and if you know that you will do fine on the test. You have to read a book and do an analysis paper. No textbook. Josh relates to his students and cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Josh is the coolest professor. Straightforward, kind, and caring. His lectures are easy to understand and his tests aren't hard as long as you do the study guide. This dude is the bomb and I hope to take another class from him in the future. Also, he made an inspirational speech near the end of the semester and I lowkey teared up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Josh is the BEST professor I've had so far! His lectures are entertaining, he's always offering extra guidance, & you can tell he really cares about the students & their success in the class (also, he's hilarious). Lots of reading, 3 tests, & 1 paper. Readings are interesting & tests are easy IF YOU STUDY! I highly recommend Prof. Ewalt! 10/10 guy.
Lectures are awesome, fair grading and  good examples provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: HE is EASY!! everyone here is complaining because they dont study for his class...honestly just take 1 hour of your time after every class period and you will Ace his class with flying colors!!!! EASY A? i think so!! Erying for the win!!!!!!! (trust me, im not the brightest person...hes just that easy)
Professor Eyring makes chemistry seem like a foreign language. In comparing my test with other chemistry students his were much harder and had much more useless information.

Very difficult.  I had to teach myself everything, and if you don't already have  strong background in chemistry, I would definitely not recommend this class.  Nothing he said would be on the exam was on the exam and studying is extremely difficult.

He does not teach the material well at all during lecture, and the exams are extremely difficult.  Going to discussion is helpful as the TA's are usually good.  If you can help it, do not take this class from him! You will have to teach yourself everything!
He teaches us completely NOTHING. things he tells us on the test are actually NOT on the test. Only helpful people are your TA's. this is a class that you will need to teach yourself in.....have fun.

I can't believe I had to take this class to get a degree.  I had to teach myself everything because this man would just go on tangents about things that had nothing to do with the material at all!  He is a nice guy and everything, but he gets way too distracted and the students end up suffering when exams come around.
Boring but easy class.

Uses "Mastering Chemistry Online" for homework, but handwritten exams, which did not corrilate AT ALL! Way too many students in the class, not condusive to asking questions or learning for that matter. He knows chemistry well but not how to teach it! And the Lab TA didn't even speak english. Seriously!
Old man needs to retire and let some young blood teach a subject like this. A little more organization and teaching effort would be very much appreciated.

He is wonderful! His lectures are very interesting. The subject is tough, but if you read your book and go to class you will be set. Eyring has a huge heart and is interested in knowing his students. He is extremely intelligent and knows what he is talking about!
No Comments
Professor Fan was an excellent instructor. He explained the material clearly, responded to emails promptly, and made the grading criteria transparent and easy to understand.

This professor was very nice but not a good teacher. It was very hard to learn from him. He teaches very monotone, straight from the textbook, and if he answered my questions it would confuse me more. Would not recommend taking from him if you want to understand math.
He is very nice guy, and really care the student. The lecture is very easy to catch and the homework is not much that enough to do. Should take this class with professor Jia Fan.

Quite easily the most lenient grader I have ever met. Cheat sheets on all quizzes and tests are allowed and encouraged. CRAZY amounts of partial credit. Plus he's just a really nice guy. He wants you to do well and will make it easy for you to do so. Just make a good cheat sheet before class and ur golden.

Dr Wasilewska was an excellent teacher.  That is not something I can say about most professors.  She really cares about her subject, and has an impressive breadth of knowledge in the field.  It was not an easy class, but incredibly rewarding for me personally.  It is a cliche to say "I learned a lot" but in this case, it is totally accurate.

Professor Wasilewska was the oddest teacher I have ever had. She requires that you call her before every assignment. We're in UNIVERSITY not kindergarten, I don't need my hand held. In her assignments we have to defend incorrect information. Even if your essay is well done, if you don't read her mind you'll get a bad grade. It's madness.

She was weird. Many of her readings were not peer-reviewed and were 20+ years old. She doesn't give assignment instructions, you have to call her on the phone to get them. Then, if you don't give the correct opinion in your paper, she gives you bad grades. She distorts facts and her slideshows have no sources or full sentences. Lots of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wasilewksa is a strict grader and this class is heavy on assigned readings. The key to writing a paper in this class is calling the professor. I called her every week to discuss the assignments and she would point blank say what topics had to be covered to get a good grade. She is incredibly smart and I learned so much from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No grading criteria, her assignments are one sentence and then you end up with a fail if you didn't read her mind. She just posts lectures and articles, the contents of which I doubt she has any memory of. The lectures are nearly illegible, there is not one full English sentence. She also doesn't use email for some reason, and her grading is HARSH.

Dr Wasilewska is tough but fair, her classes are all excellent and while there is quite a bit of reading required as well as mandatory attendance at lectures, she imparts a great deal of knowledge from the texts as well as personal experience. She was one of my favorite professors as I worked through and got my degree in Anthropology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: All learning through long power-points or posted reading excerpts. Essay/assignment grading is tough. Must be detailed. I found the more I write, the better grade I get. Work at own pace for pre-established due dates and assignment prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For this being an online class this was incredibly difficult, all she posts are readings and lectures of 90+ slides that are not very easy to understand. The information she provided is very easy to get lost and confused in. She is an extremely tough grader and I found speaking to her beforehand did not offer as much help as she proclaims. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For an online class in the 1000s youd expect this class to be manageable. she preaches about wanting to help and guide her students through phone calls, text messages, etc. even after reaching out to her and taking her advice into action, be prepared to be disrespected and humiliated with her terrible reconstructive criticism

This was the worst class Ive taken my entire college career. It was an online class and I understand that online classes require a certain level of self teaching but this was entirely self taught. All she did was post reading and lectures with little context. There were quizzes on 5 weeks worth of readings who retains that much information?

This was a great class. Ewa knows her stuff and is very clear in conveying it. Ewa is a tough grader and can tell if you're trying to get by in the class with minimal effort. That being said she is fair and wants all of her students to grow from the class. My one regret is that I didn't contact her sooner. She was immensely helpful once I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: About to graduate and Ewa's classes remain the most memorable. If you are passionate and interested in the topic she is teaching, you will learn more than you intended to. The one thing that helped me earn an A in every class of hers was CONTACTING HER. She wants to help her students! I had phone meetings with her before every paper. Ewa is amazing

Be prepared to read over 100 pages a week along with all of your other classes. Also be prepared to write very detailed essays. Don't think you're gonna get by with anything to basic. This is a 2000 class so the fact that she requires such detailed writing is kind of ridiculous. The difficulty of this class rivals many of my upper division courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class has A LOT of reading so be prepared to stay up to date on the homework, but everything assigned is very interesting. She is good at grading and responding to messages in a reasonable time. I genuinely learned a lot from this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hard class with arbitrary requirements. Jams tons of info into her powerpoints and tests on the most random things, and is strict on papers and every mistake brings it down a letter grade. It's hard to do well in this class without studying like crazy. Ewa isn't helpful and feels that it's OK to expect the unreasonable of students. Don't take her.

I took this class, Anthropology of Humor and Laughter, and many told me it would be very hard. I took it anyway because it seemed interesting. Ewa is interesting, engaging, and her class is easy if you know how to pay attention, write, and apply topics. Easy class. Nice lady.
Difficult grader, jams lot of info into her power points. Doesn't give you good feed back.

Avoid this class and professor at all costs. Lectures are a long convoluted mess that do little to further your knowledge. Ewa is one of those unapproachable, apparently infallible, professors whose exams will straight up fail an entire class. After which she will spend a good chunk of the next class making demeaning remarks to you and your peers.

I took the online class. The multiple choice exams were pretty straightforward, the questions are taken from her powerpoints which are very detailed and helpful. We had to write 3 reflection papers, and I did well on the first one however not so well on the others. However, she was more flexible with the final grade.

Her class was a three hour lecture where she talked nonstop.  Pretty impressive really.  She definitely knows her stuff.  We had three take-home "tests" which consisted of several questions which she expected answered like any paper. Lots of research needed to get a good grade.  Most people got a C or low B. Very tough class.
Clarity is not one of her attributes, could be that english is not her first tongue.
Honestly one of my favorite professors. I am through with my undergrad but her lectures are the ones I remember with great fondness.

Ewa is tough. You will learn more than you ever thought you would. Three exams and two papers due. She assigns a TON of reading. I am taking five classes and half of my study time is just for her class alone. She'll make you work for the grade, as all good professors should. Really interesting stuff - just make sure you have the time!

This professor is confusing to say the least. Essays questions are VERY unclear and she will not budge a millimeter when grading. If you want to get an A you need to write a turn paper for every assignment. I took this class to fill upper level class requirements and it turned into a nightmare. I am a very good student but she is so condescending!

Condescending,rude,and arrogant!0 Tact! Test questions are ambiguous as are paper critiques. She attacks students privately submitted work through discussion posts. If you paraphrase and reword research and give credit to your sight source she will still give you an "E" for plagiarism.   BEWARE!3 cr hr class w/ an easy 23-25 hr pr week work load.

While the content she lectures on is very interesting and done well. You will struggle to meet seemingly arbitrary expectations on the essay tests. Then as a added bonus, your class will receive a lecture in broken English on how bad your English skills are. The novelty of these occurrences fades quickly. I would not recommend this course.

This class was awful, the book was so confusing and difficult to use (she wrote the book).  The lectures were mildly interesting, but didn't seem to have any continuity.  I would not recommend this class.

I took this class freshman year and it was super challenging but really interesting. You have to work your ass off if you expect to have a good grade. It's hard to pin down exactly how she wants you to answer questions in the essay, but she's happy to work with you. Lovely woman!

I took Ewa's class freshman year, which I wouldn't recommend for everyone. I absolutely bombed my first test;however,after that I met with her every week before an exam and ended up getting an A in the three classes of her's that I took.She turned out to be one of my favorite professors.Stundents reviewing here must have given up without trying.

She is extremely interesting and has some adventurous stories! She's a tough grader, and sometimes it's hard to understand the point she's trying to make, or follow what she's saying in class. It's interesting, but I don't think all the work was worth it for a gen ed. She has some interesting opinions on religion, and she will attack your beliefs.

She's a ruthless grader.  Study groups are your best bet, but even then expect to score a lower grade than usual.  She has no problem failing most of the class. Ewa tends to throw questions out of left field, and often it seems that there is an excess of overlap between questions.  I do not recommend Ewa Wasilewska.
Harsh grader, so picky on papers. Wouldn't recommend her. On the personal level, she is so kind and loves to help students succeed but the way she grades might drop your grade to an E, really!!!

Hard class, be prepared to work. Hilarious though! She is the toughest grader I've ever come across. The way she grades your questions is like she was expecting you to read her mind, so that's difficult. But it was a fun class!

Her powerpoints are awful!  Her test questions are ambiguous and she grades extremely hard, even if you are a good student and attend classes. The class I took was a 3000 level and she grades like it is a 5000. I took her class because I needed upper division credits. If you are in the same boat, don't take her classes for the heck of it.

She is brilliant!  She knows her stuff & has so much life and field experience. She is not affraid to let you know if you are not doing well.  However she is really kind, & one of the few profs. who really is in tune with her students at the U!  She wants us to enjoy her class and learn a lot!  Her test questions are a bit to open ended.

If you are going to take a class from this teach you NEED a study group. They are the only way to make it though the test. Really like this teacher. I've taken 5 class from her. none of them were easy.

This class satisfies DV & BF requirements,so don't expect it to be extremely easy. It is fair. Dr. Wasilewska is helpful, competent and positive in her teaching practice. The key to success in this class is like in any other: attendance(not mandatory, but helps not to miss out on any info)& reading. She works with any individual concerns. I aced it

Ewa is one of the most condescending individuals I've ever met. She was openly disdainful of our class, and was not afraid to let us know. Her exam questions are fraught with ambiguity, and her marginal comments are wildly vague and unhelpful. If you want an A, be prepared to write papers that are at least two pages longer than what she "assigns."

Her exam questions were racked with ambiguity and really difficult to understand, which forces you to ask too many follow-up questions. She gives venomous feedback if she thinks you just fudge your assignments so go to class and go that extra mile. She's hard to please, though eager to help.

She does know what she's talking about and her lectures could be pretty entertaining. Her accent does make her a bit difficult to understand and her powerpoints are horrendous. She is the hardest grader I've ever seen, especially given the level of the course. I think she expects too much.

She assigned us homework after the class was over.  Dont take her summer term if you want homework a month after the class has ended.  Shes also a surprisingly harsh grader, given the level of the class.  She was a nice and interesting person though.
Difficult to understand.

HARD grader. She is really tough. Her lectures are interesting but sometimes she just reads from notes because she has taught it so many times. Get a study group- you will need it because she won't repeat anything at the test review. I have mixed feelings.
She is stuborn and not open to other points of view. Really into herself. She thinks that she is great even when she does not know what she is talking about
Ewa has a passion for her subjects, and a lively sense of humor. Make sure you go to her test reviews!
Test are in essay form and are very difficult. She grades very hard
She was an amazing instructor, very good with the class and always willing to take time to answer questions.  Her exams were very very difficult and required a lot of effort, but very worth it

Very smart, but is at the point where she thinks everyone has a basic understanding of what she is teaching. Tests were very hard. She even ruined the traditional mult choice by adding a short answer section. If you take this teacher, go to class, read all the material, and do research on the side so you know what she is talking about (accent).
She's very difficult and I recoment putting forth a LOT of effort in her class!
No Comments
No Comments

Adequate knowledge of topic area, entertaining presentation, organized presentation. Needs improvement with rapport building, and relationship development with students (only talks to certain people).

I found Dr. Wasilewska to be very entertaining in her classes. She's tough but she's that way in order to make you think about things in different ways. She even provides prepared notes to assist you in learning the material. If I could, I would continue taking her classes until I'd taken every one.

I know it is anthropology, but tells too many personal stories and not enough academic information.  This instructor EXPECTS you to purchase class notes, and if you don't, don't expect to keep up with the information.
Goes over a ton of information, it's tough to keep track of it all.

This was a difficult class for me as I haven't taken math in years, but after I got over that hump, I have found it very engaging and not overly difficult. Math is math and will be hard, but Professor Fayolle honestly cares and will help receptive and dedicated students. There is a lot of accurate practice material for exams as well.

The online class is taught by videos made by the U of U math department. The videos don't teach anything so in addition to watching the video to find out what they want you to know be ready to watch 2 or 3 other videos on youtube to actually learn the material. 

**Only take this course online if you can be self taught math.**

Calc II is an intense class, especially online but that doesn't take away from Professor Fayolle's performance. All of the lectures provided are those which are created by the UofU Math Department which were awful. Despite this, Professor Fayolle is caring and acknowledges how difficult the class is so she is willing to help explain the material.

It's Calc 2 so it's going to be hard but the online format I found was really easy. Make sure you know exactly what you're doing and don't hesitate to reach out to Anne, she's very helpful. She will work with you on the problem you're stuck on until you both figure it out. Very fair tests and homework, memorize your unit circle!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is clear that Professor Fayazi has taken the past feedback with grace, as I did not notice any of the complaints in my time with the class. Edit: penalties for all classwork were applied after the final was taken, so I was unable to gauge what my grade was until they were finalized
The grading system for this class is very strange and it's hard to get credit for it, so if you want to learn, choose another class.

The class is not bad. My grading TA was terrible, lazy and excessively harsh. However, the professor is good and really nice. Records all lectures. Homework is not bad despite what others say. You can find solutions in his lectures or in the book and they don't take too long. There are multiple opprotunities to raise your grade.
Lectures are informative, homework was instructional. Labs are kind of hard in the moment but writing the reports is chill.

This professor constantly makes corrections to his own work. The lectures are minimal
In content. Labs are completely unrelated to lecture content, and instructions are very difficult to follow/understand. Grading in this class is absurdly harsh. Most questions are all or nothing with pitiful/no partial credit.

The most anal grader I have had the displeasure of taking at this university. If your work isn't exactly as he demonstrates in lecture he will destroy the grade you recieve, even going as far as to dock points on correct work leading to a correct answer.

The labs for this course are very difficult and do not reflect the material we learn in class. They don't teach us how to use any of the software or how to code in verilog. The professor is very nice but his homework is hard and his lectures are not that detailed.

Don't take the senior seminar with professor Fagan. She is a philosophy of science person and expects you to know so much about science and write analytic papers based on science rather than philosophy. She also grades weekly papers on the readings very harshly with little feedback. Take the senior seminar with some other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Fagan is passionate about philosophy and facilitates a great group discussion. Be prepared, she grades hard and expects high level writing.
Professor Fagan has been both disrespectful to student in the lecrure

Prof. Fagan does not mess around regarding grading and gives relatively few comments about getting a better grade next time. Be wary of using normative language and avoid writing in a way that doesn't involve handholding. Signpost as much as you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Fagan doesn't provide a clear grading rubric for most assignment and is the world's harshest grader. She keeps grades a secret until after the semester concludes so students are deprived of the opportunity to improve their performance. The worst class I have ever taken and the worst professor. Do NOT take her class, it is not worth it.

Good professor. She's always more than happy to spend time to explain and talk things through. Philosophy makes my brain hurt so I felt frustrated in this class a lot, but don't think it's her fault. She grades very hard! Not super flexible/ accommodating with work. Not a prob if you are able to keep up though. Lots of readings, lots of discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Melinda's class was great; there are 10 papers (5 short, 5 medium size), and her feedback is extensive and lectures are engaging. I will say that the papers are fairly hard and there is a lot of reading. A lot. Office hours are very helpful, she is highly receptive to talking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tough class but you get the final exam questions (4/10 will be chosen, and you have to answer 3) a week before the exam. 4 papers due out of 13 weekly prompts - your choice when to do them.

I took this class for a Humanities GenEd and it was a lot tougher than I expected. I love Melinda and she is a very good teacher. If you do the readings and participate in class it is very worthwhile and interesting. However, she is a tough grader. Your grade is based on four papers throughout the semester, so make sure you can write well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I wouldn't say he was the best at teaching, but his policies were great. There are 5 tests total (one is dropped) so none of them are worth too much, which is so nice. It's clear he wants his students to succeed.

Dr. Fehlberg is a great professor all around. His teaching style is easily understandable, and he takes feedback really well. His canvas is lined out very well, and he is more than fair with grading and extra credit opportunities. I suggest taking his class.

I hate stats but he did everything he possibly could to make it interesting. He's a really funny professor who has a lot of empathy if you don't understand something on the first try. He is also extremely good at taking criticism and makes an effort to apply that criticism to his teaching.

I've taken Fehlberg for Dynamics and Statistics, and I enjoyed both classes. I think he's got a good teaching style, and the assignments that he has you do help you learn the material and do well on the tests. He's pretty fair when it comes to grading, plus he's a nice guy and is willing to meet with you after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fehlberg is an amazing professor. Easily in the Top 3 best I've had in my college career. He knows and teaches the material well. His lectures just make things make sense. He is also very friendly, reasonable, accessible outside of class, and provides lots of discussion time outside of class. The material is difficult so just don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mark is one of the most caring and involved professors I have ever had. This semester he introduced some difficult coding problems but he gives you weeks to complete them. It is a hard class and requires a lot of work but overall he is a great professor who will adapt and respond to feedback.

Dynamics is a hard course. This professor is about as accommodating as expected. this class is not for the lazy. if you want to do well in this class you have to spend at least 9 hours a week. there is a big expectation to know MATLAB by now. He has had issues with people cheating on exams. this is not a class to coast by. Decent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mark is the best professor I've ever had, and is easily the best in Utah's ME department. He's a smart and funny person, which made the lectures fun and engaging. He fined tuned the class based on feedback forms he gave regularly, and he genuinely cares about student success. Overall, if you put the effort in, the class is not difficult.

Dr. Fehlberg is a great professor. He really cares about your learning. Don't be afraid to reach out to him and ask questions. He has a semester at a glance calendar so you know what will be covered in each lecture. It is best if you quickly glance over the chapters first. He expects you to do some reading and have an idea of what is being taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: He's awesome, really cares about his students and is a great teacher. This semester he did regular student feedback surveys to make sure we were happy with the class. The homework isn't too ridiculous and I felt like he did a good job prepping us for tests. Quizzes during class about once a week, but he doesn't usually say when so go to class

He makes lectures fun and engaging even when the material gets a little dry. There are pop quizzes at random times so be careful. There was a lot of homework especially near the end of the course. The exams are fair but get tougher as the semester moves on. Overall great class.

LOVE Dr. Fehlberg, he is truly one of the best professors I've had the pleasure of taking a class with. He makes even the hard and boring stuff seem easy and fun and is very helpful and approachable. I hope I get to have him instruct some of my classes in the future. Homeworks can be lengthy and there are 'pop' quizzes (he does warn a class before)

I cannot imagine taking stats from any other professor because it is such a boring subject. However, Dr. Fehlberg was such a knowledgeable and caring professor. He really cares about you learning the materials rather than anything else.

Dr. Fehlberg is a character. I took stats with him and while stats is a pretty boring subject, he tried his best with lots of dry humor in his lectures. He's an awesome guy and although class isn't the most exciting, he gets the job done and is one of the better professors I've had.

Best professor I have ever had. Entertaining, he REALLY cares if you understand his material. Very accessible and helpful outside of class. HW isn't too bad, tests are fair, often has quizzes in class. Honestly just a great professor. Stats is a boring class, but he makes it so good. Stop thinking about it and just take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible professor. The course, in general, is pretty difficult, but he gives many resources and always available. He cares about his students' success, and it shows immensely. Quizzes weekly (not hard, cheat sheet given +review) and 4-6 hw questions a week. He gives extra homework for practice and teaches straight from the textbook.

I took him last year, he was a very fast lecturer and talked with an accent but you get used to it. Lots happens in class so if you miss a class you'll be behind. However, he explained all topics well and thoroughly. Really enjoyed the class
The lecture went very fast. Lots of homework. Math is not my strong suit, and I had a challenging time. He does help the class out during quizzes though.

I came in to the class on day one and he just started going and didn't stop. We only spent about a day or so on the very basic material, then he went to sequences and series. I tried my hardest outside of class to interpret his notes and get help, I still don't know how to do them accurately. Be prepared to write a lot down and study HARD to pass.

His exams weren't extremely difficult but if you don't go to the lectures you will fail. He teaches very fast so it is good to take ample notes. He gave out a ton of extra credit which helped boost my grade by a lot and made the final exam less stressful which was nice.

I liked Fernando, but the learning curve to understand how he teaches was very steep at first. He was really excited teaching series, so 90% of the class was lost. He's the first math teacher ever to not be behind schedule. He tests extremely easy, and curves really well. Once you understand his teaching style, he can be a cool and funny guy.

He goes through the material very very quickly. If the entire class didn't do well on an exam, he spent half the next class saying we should've practiced and prepared more. Didn't seem to realize we're learning the material for the first time. Grading can be pretty harsh -- deducts points for not doing it his way, even if I get the right answer.

Lectures can be hard to follow just because he is so fast. He clearly knows what he's talking about, but he doesn't explain the examples great which can make things confusing. He wants students to do well in the class- he explains what will be on exams beforehand and curves well. If the lectures don't work for you, the textbook/YouTube help a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's really chill with grading and his tests really really really easy. I loved him, but he was sometimes hard to follow along. He should just bear in mind that we are all learning this for the first time, and maybe simplify his explanations. Otherwise def a smart dude, would recommend.

Fernando explained the early concepts pretty well but got too excited when we got to integrals and it become difficult to keep up with him after that. He is a very generous grader but is a little combative when you ask him questions in class and is hard to approach although he seems like a nice enough person.
Awesome Professor

He honestly explains everything super well. He wants to make sure everyone understands too. He loves questions and does a good job going over the math. Only complaint is his english isn't the best, but it isn't bad either. He also kinda stinks at review sessions. BUT he is a fantastic teacher, probably the best math teacher I've ever had.

This class is really hard. He knows his stuff, but he's forced to go a little fast with only 2 hours a week. He posts the notes online and tells you not to take notes in class. Homework takes a while and you need MATLAB. Grades really hard on homework and tests. Practice tests are a lot like real tests and often have problems from the homework.

I think Montana is still a grad student, so her lectures weren't perfect, but they were still decent. She explained things in depth, but it was a bit too much at times. She grades super fairly and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. She's a super nice and caring person who wants her students to succeed, and it shows.

Her first time teaching calc.She got on my nerves a few times.Grading is hard to get a 100% but likes to give a good amount of credit if you tried.There were a lot of times tests would be way harder than HW's / Labs. She gives a good amount of grade rounding end of sem.Lectures arnt worth your time to go to, she just rambles. Good Person, 4/10 Prof

I think this might have been Montana's first or second time teaching calc, so of course it wasn't perfect. IMO she spent too much time explaining things that were somewhat irrelevant, and it also seemed like several simple topics were overcomplicated a bit. However, she is so sweet and very kind and understanding and she wants you to succeed!

This class seems like a lot at first, but as long as you don't fall behind, it's really not bad. Professor Farnsworth has really great lecture videos every week, although some may consider her "woke". There is a semester-long group project which can kind of suck when your group members are not the brightest.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bottom 3 courses I've taken, especially for an online course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jackie is sweet and easy to work with. However, if you want a good score, you need to play the game a bit. She is very biased and likes to insert her own opinion into coursework, but she isn't rude about it. This is a 5000-level course, so standards are high, but if you can eloquently regurgitate material without challenging her views, it's easy.
I would not take this class. There was a lot of busy work and many group projects.

Lots of writing assignments. Assignments were not graded in a very timely manner. Class consisted of listening to the professor's opinions, but in contrast being expected to use research and analysis in our writing. Her healthcare perspectives on diversity and inclusivity are old-school and come across as somewhat underinformed.

This professor does not accept late work and grades very harshly. We were supposed to be able to re submit papers for credit however it is almost finals week and some of these have not been graded yet. She has very strict rules for the class and will not accept assignments that do not follow them. She also pushes her personal ideas on us.

Very hard grader, one small imperfection and you will get docked points. Very rude in her comments and made me feel bad about my work half of the time even though I knew it was good. Instructions of group research areas were unclear and was told that I didn't know what I was writing about even though I followed the prompt. Enjoyed the class.

Class is very liberal coded. The Professor makes an effort to be very inclusive but sometimes to her own detriment. It is not a hard class but there is a lot of busy work and IMO sometimes unnecessary ideology pushed in class. Take this class for a somewhat easy grade which you can turn your brain off and just regurgitate material.
