Get ready for a lot of busy work assignments. A very biased class, despite her claims to the contrary. Said we could resubmit all papers, but didn't grade any of them until the last three weeks of semester, making this near impossible. Pretty disappointed after hearing such good things.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gives all of her personal opinions and makes everything personal even though it's not supposed to be. Most picky grader ever and will make you rethink your knowledge of English.

She is a tough grader. If you believed you were a good writer, she would make you reconsider. The class material itself is great. She inputs a lot of personal opinions into lectures, which I believe is unnecessary and uncalled for.

Farnsworth is a great professor! Everything is easy to understand and the workload is minimal. This class has a group project, but for the most part you are only graded for your own work. You should get an A just for effort alone.

not difficult material but SO MUCH WORK. stay on top of it or drop it. Jackie's lectures are really interesting and I genuinely liked this class. prepare yourself for is how horrible the schedule is. it's so busy, and the due dates are a nightmare. make sure you do all the assignments as they all build up on each other for the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While this class is NOT hard, the way it's structured makes absolutely no sense. Maybe I am crazy, but having a rough draft of an essay due on Wednesday, a peer review of someone else's essay due on Thursday, and then the final draft of your essay due on Friday is INSANE; Gives you no real time to implement the corrections given. Lots of busy work.

Jackie is a great professor. She knows her stuff and fosters a great class environment. There was a lot of busy work in this class including a big group project, but it wasn't hard to get a good grade. There were many extra credit opportunities.

This class was easy and nice for being online. There's a few short assignments due every week, but they're not hard as long you get them in. The papers and group project are what make up most of your grade. The lectures were really engaging and focused on real world situations that happen in today's world. I definitely recommend taking this class.

This was an interesting class from a well-experienced professor. You will spend the entire semester working with a group to research a racial minority's health in the U.S. Be prepared for weekly assignments that are graded easily. As long as you turn your work in on time, it's simple to get a good grade.

Jakie was an amazing teacher and would definitely recommend taking this class if you need an upper-division writing course. She is a pretty easy grader and the final group project is pretty well spaced out. Jackie's lectures are also amazing and she really made me enjoy this subject.

This class is great for your upper-division writing and diversity credit. There's a decent amount of assignments for this class, but not too difficult. This course is pretty interesting and it's nice online. The only semi-difficult thing about the class is a group research paper for the online class. Most of the group project is graded separately.
Fine Teacher, but good lorddddd, space your assignments a bit better. First month or two of the class were very light, but as your reach end of october/november everything ramps up. Unnecessary.

Can't speak highly enough of Jackie. Her class changed my life. Make sure to take her in person and come to every lectures. I personally guarantee you that you will learn so much. Heavy on the papers but they're short and easy. Her class is required for Kines majors and she's the only one who teaches the class. The best human being.

I loved professor Farnsworth, she is an amazing professor and her lectures are never boring. Theirs a lot of little short assignment that are due but totally manageable, as long you complete it she gives you the points. Easy grader and you have a final project with a group of students in the class. By far the easiest and best class I have taken.

This class was pretty easy, especially for a 5000-level class. The professor responded relatively quickly to messages and was pretty lenient with grading in my experiences. Sometimes her responses felt passive aggressive. She offers a bunch of extra credit that aren't much extra work. The final exam isn't weighted much either, so you could skip it.

Jackie is by far the best professor I've ever had in college. Her lectures are so interesting that even if I wasn't taking this class, I'd still want to attend them. There are a ton of assignments so it seems daunting, but as long as you complete them, she's a pretty easy grader. I literally LOVED this class, totally recommend it!

I had this class for a HEDU 3160 credit. There is a lot of reading in the textbook and her final is a 10-15 minute presentation video and you had to perform some type of stress relief exercise. Each week there was 2-3 assignments from the textbook which is really easy. I strongly suggest taking Farnsworth.

She's a good professor but beware the class is very workload heavy. Multiple assignments are due throughout the week, and papers are heavily graded. She's accessible through Canvas and provides multiple extra credit ops throughout the sem. Overall, not too bad of a class. There is a group project and the final exam was a breeze.

One of my favorite professors because she was very engaging with the students and cared about what she was teaching. Her lectures were always super engaging, and the homework was relatively easy. She makes learning such a great experience. There is a group project involved with this class and she was very clear on the requirements for each part.
Amazing teacher and interesting material. Lectures were never boring and prof is hilarious. There are a lot of small group discussions and a big group project.

I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Farnsworth's class. She gave me a whole new outlook on the healthcare community and opened my eyes to certain aspects of health within society that I had never considered before, and she did it by making learning fun.

I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Farnsworth's class. Her lectures gave me a whole new outlook on the healthcare community and opened my eyes to certain aspects of health within society that I had never thought about before, and she makes learning fun.

Great class, great lecture; although at first I was skeptical of what she was saying, she can back everything up with research, just ask! She sent me a lot of articles that went into depth on what she discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jackies class comes off as a little intimidating in the first week, but stay in the class and you will not regret it! Work is not hard, but can accumulate very quickly. Her lectures are amazing and can be applied long after the class. I was a little sketched out on the group project, but it wasnt bad at all. Stay on top of due dates!

This was my favorite class Ive ever taken. The lectures were super interesting and I looked forward to class every week. Homework each week consists of watching a film and writing a page. 3 papers, 1 group project, and 1 group paper. I recommend this class to literally anyone going into healthcare. Prof Farnsworth is the best!!!

Jackie really knows what she's talking about. She doesn't waste your time--all of her lectures are full of material that everybody should know. There's one big group project/paper. About 2-3 assignments per week. Get ready to write. Offers lots of extra credit. All in all, great course. Would recommend Jackie's course!

This class was one of my favorite classes that I've taken in my college career. I could not wait to get to class because it was so interesting. It is important to go to class and put in the work to get assignments done but if you do, you will get an A.

I literally recommend this class to anyone and everyone. This class contains a lot of work but it's all really informative whether you are going into healthcare or not. Jackie is very good at communicating and cares a lot about what she is teaching. Totally would take this class again if I could :)

Jackie is a good professor, very passionate about what she is teaching. I found this course interesting and I think she did a really good job at both captivating the audience and conveying the information. She lets you resubmit papers for better grades. Only downside is she randomly assigns you a group for a group project for the entire semester.

Probably one of the few electives you can take that will actually impact your everyday life. Workload was medium; Couple of essays, small assignments and 1 big group project, & 1 open note take home exam. Doesnt require attendance but youll do so much better if you do. Plenty of opportunities to increase your grade. Overall, highly recommend!

Wasn't looking forward to my diversity credit but this course really surprised me. Jackie is funny, and though I am in a health related field, I found the course interesting and inspiring! The papers weren't too bad, most the work is subjective, and she allows for a lot of extra credit, which was nice.

Jackie was an AMAZING professor, her lectures were so informative I am so glad I took this class! I wish Jackie taught another class so I could have her again, the main papers you write are not that hard she really outlines what she wants so you can do super good on them!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is more of a discussion base class. Attendance matter because you have in class assignments every class, but if you show up you get full points for them. 3 papers (on the 1st and 2nd one you can revise them for a higher grade) and a semester long group project. She offers some bonus points! I loved the class, and Jackie was super nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Jackie is absolutely amazing! I looked forward to going to her class each week! Shes incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about this class and it shows. I would definitely recommend this class to anyone.

Very fun and interesting lectures. Jackie is great at making the lessons enjoyable and she respects everyone's input and opinions. Really easy to pass as long as you show up to class. All assignments and due dates were outlined in the class schedule at the beginning of the semester. I highly suggest this class for the diversity requirement.

She is AMAZING!!!!! Her class honestly changed my life. She respects everyone's opinion and addresses controversial issues in a way where she presents information to just get you to think. Any human (especially someone going into healthcare) needs this class!! Best class I've taken at the U by far.

I just planned on taking this class because it covered two requirements for me. However, she is so passionate about her class I wish I could have her for all my classes. Fun, engaging, and really knows what she's doing.

I have LOVED Jackie. Her lectures are SO engaging and fascinating. She talks about controversial social subjects in a nonbiased, respectful manner. It really opens your mind and helps you understand different kinds of populations. You do write several papers, but they are easy and she is an easy grader. I would absolutely take this course again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think everyone could benefit from Professor Farnsworth's class. I have loved learning from her. Lectures are engaging and open minded. The information she provides is really applicable in health fields and every day relationships. Her grading criteria is very clear. I love writing and she assigns papers that students are invested in writing.

Jackie is amazing! She is passionate about the subject material and makes topics you might not otherwise care about extremely interesting in an engaging way while still making you laugh. The lectures are super engaging and papers are super easy. The final project was the worst part of this class but still really not that bad.

This class was incredible. Jackie made all the topics so relatable and interesting. I looked forward to going to class everyday. She's gives a great understanding of all the topics. She is very clear on what she expects from assignments so keeping up with the class was easy. Would absolutely take again.

Jackie is an amazing teacher! The class is pretty easy, you only have to do three two-page double-spaced papers outside of class so that's pretty easy, and then a big group project at the end which isn't too bad. The class itself is incredible! I came out inspired and I would share everything we talked about with my friends at lunch! Take this!

awesome professor! very clear outline of the expectations for the class -- three papers, many small assignments, one group presentation, one final exam! She wants her students to do well. I would definitely recommend taking her :)

One of the most interesting classes I've taken, and one that I actually looked forward to going to three times a week! Jackie is a captivating lecturer, so learning is easy. Couldn't recommend enough.
Great teacher. Great ally.

This was easily the best class I have ever taken in college. I am not going into the healthcare field but I would still recommend this class 100% to anyone pursuing healthcare or not. Jackie is phenomenal and I wish everyone could take this class!

THIS CLASS WAS THE BEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN AT THE U. If you are interested in the medical field, this class will help you drastically. So incredible. Jackie is fantastic and opens your eyes. At times, her passion comes across as biased but doesn't impact the class too much. Assignments are easy and she is super accessible!

THIS CLASS WAS THE BEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN! Please do yourself a favor & take it especially if you're interested in the health care field. I came out everyday feeling inspired. She's amazing and very sweet her class is easy but you learn so much. You do have a group project in the end but its not bad at all. Take this class you wont regret it!

the first few classes are very imitating however after that prepare to be inspired! Overall it has been my favorite class this semester shes very passionate about the subject and is very knowledgeable.  Big group paper and presentation along with three other two page papers , no readings though and usually she let us out of class early! Take her!

Jackie was an awesome. She was very knowledgable and inspirational. As others have said before she sounds kind of intimidating in the beginning but as the semester passes, and if you get to know her she's really chill. 3 papers, a big group project (presentation and paper) and final comprehensive exam and lots of extra credit. Highly recommend.

She was awesome! One of the most interesting classes I have had yet. At the beginning she seemed intimidating and I thought for sure she would fail us all, but none of it was true. She is a great teacher and puts together an amazing lecture. Homework isn't bad.  Take this class!

Only one test at the end of the semester, which is nice, but there's a huge group project, which sucks. Her lectures are so amazing! She opens your mind and challenges your way of thinking every class! Beware, she's a tougher grader than she seems.

Jackie is incredible. Her lectures were interesting and informative, I learned so much about things I never knew before. She is so passionate and funny. She does have in class assignments on a regular basis, but they're easy. If you go to class, you'll learn something.

Jackie makes points to support/oppose both sides of some really interesting and controversial subjects. Sometimes her passion on certain topics (feminism) borders persuasion, but she generally provides solid information and is well-educated and experienced. Super easy assignments and a final group project with months to plan and semi-lax grading.

She is so passionate about this subject, there would be no in else who can teach this subject as well as her. She gives clear instructions about assignments. She structures group projects so that we are accountable and it's easier. Go to her lectures because it will help in your essays. This is a writing class too, so be prepared to write essays.

Jackie is awesome!! She is so passionate about what she teaches. I loved coming to this class every single day! She gives 6 chances for extra credit, and we just had 3 2 page papers to write along with a group research paper as the final. Fun class! Not to much homework.

JACKIE IS MY FAVE. Always emails back promptly, very kind and understanding.  Super cool lady and inspirational.  I hope to be like her someday!  Opens your eyes about everything in the world and how we view those around us.  She doesn't give herself enough credit, she is AWESOME!  Take this class, you won't regret it!
This class was super easy to get an A in and opened my eyes a lot. There's a lot of talk on homosexuality. Super great professor.

Awesome class, professor is super funny and very passionate about everything she talks about. Shes extremely nice and helpful. The class was easy and the final was online, the final is on the notes you take for group projects. You have to show up to class to turn in assignments. She answers emails back instantly.  Great class, I learned so much.
This class is easy to pass and professor is very nice. i know you will enjoy this class.

Jackie is an incredible professor. She is easily my favorite professor that I have had in three years. Her class isn't very hard as long as you do all the in class assignments and turn in papers. I learned a great deal in this class that I have applied to every day life. I highly recommend this class to anyone in any major.

This class is very easy. It teaches you important things about health and diversity. The only complaint that I have is that this teacher is incredibly contradictory to what she says she will be like in the syllabus. She does not like to be wrong and does not take being corrected when she is wrong, well. She will hold a grudge all semester long.

Jackie is super nice and her class is really interesting and relevant to students. She's really entertaining and the lectures are really interesting. She has a lot of really great information to offer. Overall, really easy class. Just do the work and you'll be fine.

Jackie is one of the best teachers i have ever had. I honestly wished her class was longer. I learned something new and most of all interesting every time i went! She's funny, direct and just knows her stuff. If she taught any other classes i would def. take them. There's not that much homework. No quizzes and no test :)

Jackie is a great teacher! It's a long class but you don't notice it because she keeps it so interesting. Assignments are very specific so getting a good grade is no problem. TAKE THIS CLASS. You won't regret it!

This is an easy A class.  If you need the upper division writing credit, take this class.  Jackie is an awesome teacher and makes the class interesting for a 2.5 hour evening class. You do have to go to class to earn the points.  If you go to class, you will get an A. Group paper at the end.  Take this for an A.
Jackie is awesome, she loves the subject and knows it well. If you can take the time and write decent papers you will do well in the class. I would take another class from her in a heartbeat.

She is an amazing teacher! I took her class over the summer and I always looked forward to going to class. At first the paper/presentation seems a bit intimidating but it was fun and a great learning experience. I highly recommend her class! You will get a lot from this class.

Super easy and nice lady.She really likes the subject because she probably thinks we're too conservative although most of the stuff she taught I already knew. It was interesting to learn a few new things about certain minorities though. Do the bonus points and follow her way of writing in the syllabus  and you'll do good. I ended up with a 105%.

I've taken 1000-level classes that were harder than this one. No text book and the only test is a take home. This was basically nothing more than a common sense course. Occasional 2pg paper every other week. You also have to complete a group paper that's not too difficult. If you need to do your upper-division writing requirement, take this class.
Awesome class, fun and she's reasonable.
Jackie is great!  She makes class super interesting, and she doesn't use a textbook!  I would definitely recommend this class.

I 100 percent recommend this class to anyone going in the health field. I have learned so much about race, gender, religion, social orientation and the class discussion is always interesting. She teaches you a perspective that most people ignore when dealing with things that arent socially normal. Easy class, no book, take home final

AWESOME CLASS. Very interesting. Jackie was great and had a nice sense of humor. For an upper division writing course, she does not grade hard at all. EASY A! Take home final w/essay. No midterms or quizzes. Infinite extra credit!! Can rewrite any paper.

She does a good job teaching the material. I was not a big fan of her telling us that everything is opinion and to own up to it and then she tells us her opinion like it is fact. Also in our easy papers she rips them apart if we disagree with her. Easy class for an upper division class though. Just an easy final essay for the final and a group pres

Jackie is a good teacher. I feel she does a decently good job and keeping the class interesting for a 2.5 hour class in the evening.  There are no tests, not even a final. There are no quizzes. There a few papers, that you get to decided to write about. It's a good class to get an upper division class done.

Professor Rodriguez is a caring, knowledgeable professor. Showing up to class is not strictly mandatory, but there are attendance quizzes that ask you about what you learned in class which is hard to do if you weren't there. The journals and other writing assignments are not hard - just read the instructions, play the games, and do the research.

Professor Rodriguez is casual-but-not-unserious about his teaching, which worked really well for me, and considering that it's for a games class, he was able to interface with the students well because of this. He was very approachable, and easy to catch for a quick question after class. He also accommodates the large class using a question form.

While Fernando is very passionate about games, he is not exceptionally knowledgeable about the industry and mostly sticks to just fanboying over Nintendo. Constantly egged on classmates who just wanted to interrupt and tell jokes, lectures felt useless, however, I was happy with my final paper. He is kind and caring, just not my kinda professor.

While I am unsure if lectures improved from S1 (I assumed working on the project would continue to be a more effective use of my time), the feedback Fernando gave 2nd semester was much higher quality. He and Greg did a good job of at least not actively hindering the group I was in, but did not significantly contribute to our groups success either.

Professor who cares about games and his passion comes across. He was flexible with students for extra credit and extenuating circumstances. The guests he brought in to survey games were really great. Some of the movie days were lackluster as I preferred in-class discussion, but the lectures had a good balance of him teaching and student question.

In 4500 the professors are not super involved. While I didn't find the lectures to be very helpful, the feedback Fernando provided on games was pretty good. Decent professor that will get out of your team's way if that is the best thing for him to do. Nothing I saw that was amazing, nothing that was terrible.

Really great professor. The weekly assignments are incredibly easy and the class has a forgiving late policy as well. Participation isn't mandatory, but it is graded. I recommend attending class regularly since there aren't many extra credit opportunities.

Professor Rodriguez is amazing, so nice and so fun! He makes the lectures feel very informal and is always accessible outside of class (in person, emailing, and discord) I recommend taking him whenever you get the chance, he is an easy grader and gives fun assignments. Very understanding about extenuating circumstances too!

I got that sense that he wanted to make sure students understood the material; he was willing to go over content again if someone didn't understand. He was also understanding when I reached out to him about some mental health issues I was having. The class moved at a good pace as well.

Fernando was the co-teacher for EAE1010, so I didn't get much of a sense of his teaching. He seems like a nice and great guy, though, and one of the times he did teach he had the class bet on a Super Smash Bros CPU tournament to teach us about gambling, so that was pretty cool. He was also good about making sure questions got brought up & answered.

Glen is absolutely amazing; I will be taking every class that he teaches. He cares SO MUCH about the success of every student, and one-on-one conference time is built into the syllabus. Overall AMAZING person, he has truly helped my confidence so much. Take this class even if you're not in journalism, the skills and everything you learn is amazing.

Glen is genuinely one of the greatest professors I have ever had. He is the greatest guy I've ever met. I highly recommend taking a class from him. He is great with feedback and truly cares about every student and their projects. He is an absolute light in this university of mediocre professors.
THIS GUY IS THE G.O.A.T.

I was skeptical about a 3-hour lecture, but Glen is a wonderful professor: he gives good feedback, cares about each student, and makes the lectures enjoyable. He's witty, understanding, kind, and smart. He deeply respects his students and answers our questions thoroughly. I can't say enough good things about him.
One of the absolute best professors to ever grace this institution with his presence. Treat yourself to a class with this old fart before the dreadful day that he retires.

This professor cares about every one of his students and wants to see them succeed! He will take time to review your work if you reach out before the deadline to help you write the best papers possible.

MUST TAKE!!! You will pass this class if you attend the lectures and do the weekly assignments. He wants to see everyone succeed and provides so much help before exams! He's a super caring professor and keeps up with current events to make the class more exciting. His lectures are never boring.

Out of my 5 years of schooling, there has been no other professor that compares to Glen. I came into this class thinking I would not passing law or anything like it. Put in effort in listening to the lectures, asking questions about anything confusing, and simply doing all the assignments that are there.

You will do more than just pass with Glen.

The best professor I have had in my 5 years at the University of Utah. Very captivating, even if you think you don't like law or the content he teaches, he has this magic that will naturally make you interested, making the class very good. Highly recommend.

A really great professor. If you do what is asked of you, you will get an A. He is very thorough in his lectures and is a big help when preparing for exams on review day. He is a very lenient grader and is so passionate about what he teaches. If you have to take this course, I highly recommend taking it from Glen. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was an amazing teacher. Helps his students think critically and was a journalist.

Take 5300 from Glen if you can! He makes the class seem easy. The assignments are clearly defined and he is always willing to answer questions and even repeat himself. Definitely not a boring lecturer. He also asks good questions to make you think about what your are learning.

One of my absolute favorite professors in my U career. I took multiple classes with Glen and every experience was incredible. He's adapted well to virtual teaching and I have not met any other teacher who cared as much Glen cares about his students and their success. 100% recommend.

This man needs to be protected at all costs, he is that wholesome. I took this class during COVID and he was so empathetic. The class is mostly lectures, but he invites a lot of participation from students. His test reviews are awesome, he tells you exactly what is going to be on test and allows for different interpretations and critical thinking.

Glen was my favorite professor this semester. He even made zoom classes interesting and engaging. This class was easy as far as work load goes and still made me feel like I learned more than any other class. He truly wants everyone to pass and his class is awesome. I would 100% recommend Glen to anyone

A very interesting class on media and how it impacts our society. Lectures could be boring at times but are pretty short, and while discussions are mandatory and long, they always proved pretty engaging. I learned quite a bit from this class, and I definitely recommend it to anyone wanting an easy class that is still very relevant and engaging.

Glen is absolutely amazing. He cares about every one of his students and wants to see you succeed. The lectures were engaging and the assignments made me a better writer. Glen obviously knows what he is talking about and his extensive background in the journalism field is evident. I can't say enough great things about him. Goes above and beyond!

Glen is an amazing professor! I never thought I would become so interested in law until I took his course and I instantly loved it. His course was so good it's actually making me contemplate getting a minor in law. If you take any of his courses, you will be extremely satisfied. One of the best professors at the University of Utah!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Glen was amazing! We had to transition to online due to COVID but he made the transition easy. He gives good feedback on your writing which improved my writing a lot. He is always available and encourages to ask questions. By far, my favorite professor at the U.

Feighery is an awesome professor who teaches well, knows what he's talking about and cares about his students! He takes the time to go over each student's articles and gives constructive feedback. Even with the the transition to online, he stayed in contact with the class and still offered tons of help on each assignment. Best professor at the U!

I can't say enough great things about Glen. He truly is an amazing professor. The world could use more caring people like Glen. I have taken him for a few classes now and wouldn't hesitate to take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Glen is a great professor who really helped me polish my writing skills. He is a great professor with great feedback. I would also like to say he is so understanding of his students and tries his best to make things easy for the student and himself. He really is an angel

Glen is a fantastic teacher. 1 hr 20 min lectures once a week, graded in-class activities, and short homework assignments due Mondays. Quarterly essays are easy to complete. Attendance is mandatory, but if you have a medical excuse/family emergency Glen is very understanding & won't penalize you. Glen is the best! You'll learn a lot in this class.
Amazing professional. Great strategy. Motivates you before class

Glen is a phenomenal professor. Hands down my favorite professor. He makes class fun. He rarely used up the full class time and lets you go early if he has gotten through the material. He gives great feedback and is always happy to work with you and go through your assignments. He is flexible with student schedules and wants you to get an A. 10/10.

Glen is an awesome professor. This course is a hybrid-class which only meets once a week and I wished we met more often because the lectures were always fun and interesting. There are 4 major essays throughout the semester and a weekly contribution. My best recommendation is to skim the readings and use Grammarly before submitting assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Glen is awesome! He's super entertaining and knowledgeable. I love that he keeps things current and relate-able. He isn't too hard of a grader, but beware that grammar and participation are super important.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Glen is amazing! He really cares about his students. Some of the readings were hard but he always answered questions and the lectures were great. I took the hybrid class and would recommend it. Also, you don't have to buy a textbook for his class because its all online.

Glen is entertaining and clearly into everything we learned about in class. Papers were short; there were no tests; reading was assigned weekly but was always relevant and fairly interesting. Also, even though attendance is taken, you don't have to actively participate. I took this class as a hybrid.

Really interesting class with dynamic and relevant lectures. Glen was very flexible if you had to miss class. Assignments were usually perfect size with the exception of  some heavy readings. This was a hybrid course so you read 2-3 articles a week and comment on them. 4 3 page papers throughout the semester.

Glen's teaching is EXCEPTIONAL. He works with his students and cares about their success. Front loaded, Hybrid class, meets on Wednesdays. All of the weekly readings can be accessed and completed early after the first day of class. Lecture content is current and engaging. No Textbook. 3 papers total, not too complicated. Gives EC, Don't miss class.

Glen is the best teacher I've ever had here at the University of Utah for sure! He is just amazing all around. There are only 3 major papers, and he helps you understand them so they are not difficult at all. If i could have him as a teacher every semester I so would! KEEP TEACHING GLEN!

What a great professor!  He is very engaged and passionate about what he teaches.  There are weekly assignments and roll taken at every class, but they're easy and it makes up a large component of the final grade.  He makes class a fun place to be in and teaches great material.

Took Glen's class for COMM 3505. It was a hybrid class with responses due Monday and attendance to class on Wednesday. Glen did a great job preparing and making sure things were relevant. There were a couple of papers that weren't that tough.

This guy>> But seriously Glenn or Dr. Duded as we affectionately call him is awesome! His class is super fun, I truly enjoyed myself. Glenn is incredibly easy to approach and is genuinely concerned about his students and wants them to do well. I highly recommend him as a professor at the U.

Glen was the best professor I've had. He was always accessible and cared about students more than anyone I've ever seen. He was dedicated to his research but not to the demise of his students. Well done Glen.

Favorite professor at the U so far. Glen is hilarious and keeps himself updated with current events in the media world to keep the class engaging and interesting. It doesn't feel like you need to be there in class because there are barely any assignments, but that didn't stop me from attending every class.

He is very funny and interactive. Encourages and facilitates class discussions. Classes seem pointless though because there are no tests and almost no reason to maintain knowledge. Two final projects and online meetings. He is good at keeping interest, but likes group conversations.
Glen is awesome! His passion for the subjects he teaches makes the classes much more interesting
My favorite professor so far. DON'T buy the textbook (you wont use it). He's really exciting and loves what he does. He takes role but it is an easy A if you do his assignments.

Glen is hands down the best professor I ever had in my academic career. He was helpful beyond the classroom work in to offering career advice and helping with extracurricular activities. This guy will go above and beyond to help any of his students succeed in life and will never make someone feel bad for not knowing an answer.

Glen is amazing at keeping the lecture interesting.  He put a lot of emphasis on student feedback and worked hard to be a good professor.  He pays attention to students and remembers names even among a huge class size.  He's great and if you attend class you will get a good grade.  Definitely a genuine, caring teacher.

There aren't enough words to describe Glen. Learning is fun with him, his class is not boring and he extremely helpful. He will always be there when you need him. Attendance is important BTW. Best teacher I've had at the u so far.

Glen is AMAZING!!!!!  He is such a nice guy and seems more like a friend than a professor.  He makes his lectures entertaining and really talks about what most students are interested in.  He's very helpful also and you can definitely tell he cares about all of his students.  I took an auditorium sized class and he knew everyone's names!

Glen is awesome! He is funny, and he really cares about his students.He will tell you you don't NEED the textbook hard-copy "Save some money." He gets a little "nit-picky" when he grades quizzes and in class assignments, but he will be there whenever you need him to help(Even at 2 a.m. sometimes)!!! Take this course with him.

WHAT?ONLY 2 POSTS!!!This guy...IF YOU EVER get a chance to take him for ANYTHING..even if its at 7 am (he's a night owl so thats highly unlikely) YOU HAVE TO TAKE HIM. I have never in my life learned so much in 4 months.He's amazing, he relates to us,with ENDLESS experience...Youll wake up & wonder how you ever got through college without him!

Glen is great! I took the class the editing process.  At first I was not interested in the class, but later with Glens help I was very interested.  Glen is the nicest and most caring Prof. at the University of Utah

Glen can be a bit weird and wordy, but he's always there for you. He likes to keep current events into the discussion which makes class more exciting than reiterating your boring textbook. Overall he's okay, just don't do typos or poor grammar on your papers or you're screwed!

Firas gets very excited about statistics, and forgets that for many, this is their first real introduction to stats, so the class can sometimes feel like its moving super fast, but overall the material is not very hard. He grades the tests very liberally, so as long as you understand core concepts you shouldn't be worried. He gives good lectures.

This class requires you to focus on your tests, please pay attention and do the homework, as that is all you need for the test. Also ask questions, Firas is very receptive to questions and takes time to explain anything you may be struggling with. HE also has online lectures which can help you if you have to miss a few classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Firas is an exceptional lecturer. He explains things very logically, starting from fundamental principals, and has great energy. His assessments were challenging, but he was so quick to answer emailed and discussion forum questions, even often late at night. He is eager to help students learn, and is easily one of my favorite college professors.

I took this professor during the COVID pandemic so it was online. No homework solutions, practice midterms, or lecture notes are given so I didn't know what to study. I sent a message to him explaining my concerns which were all sidestepped and not answered. I bombed the midterm and withdrew. One of the worst professors I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gives off a very cold vibe, isn't willing to help much and seems annoyed any time you ask question. Also, when asked questions about the class (homework, what to prepare for for test) he just sidesteps your question. Doesn't post lecture notes either. Just a robot teacher I wouldn't recommend taking.

He is really good professor. Because of COVID19, he did online lecture, but online lecture's quality is even better than onsite lecture. Weekly quiz is really helpful for my ability. And quiz and homework are really helpful for the test and my ability. His lecture note is really good. If you want to study it for machine learning then it is perfect.

This class is made up of quizzes 5%, hw 5%, and tests 90%. Some of the lectures were a bit confusing but office hours were very beneficial! When classes had to be moved online, online lectures were great. Hw is graded on it being complete, if you don't do it, good luck passing, as exams have similar problems to the hw. Firas is a nice guy who cares

Firas knows what he's doing and that's clear from lecture. In this course, we didn't receive mandatory homework but doing the homework was advantageous because all the quizzes and tests were based out of the book and homework. I think the grading scale can seem daunting but don't worry. If you try hard, and I mean really try, you will be rewarded.
Very unclear in lectures, homework takes a LOT of time to complete.

I don't get where bad reviews are coming from. Firas knew all nooks and crannies of the course materials, and although he was a little redundant at times, he did a fantastico job of laying it out! This course covers lot of VERY new material and demands mutant-like double integral skills. I tried to keep up my side of the work and enjoyed the class.

Terrible teacher. Very unorganized and frantic. Does not portray the material understandably. Tried getting help from him in his office but he was not anymore understandable and seemed put out that I was so confused. Tests are nothing like the homework even though that is what he tells you to study. Good luck.
Explains things clearly.  Eager and available to help students with questions.
Nice guy, just not a good teacher. Knows the material, just doesn't know how to show other people how to do the material.
Probably the best math prof I had.  Notes were solid and test were very representative of the HW.
IF U DO WELL IN THE FINAL, WHICH IS NOT VERY DIFFICULT, U ARE GONNA BE FINE, COZ' HE WILL NOT COUNT THE MIDTERMS IN U DID WELL IN THE FINAL.. I LIKE THE CLASS.. IT WAS EASY AND HE IS VERY HELPFUL

Tests were pretty hard.  Not a bad guy.  I would say he was an average lecturer.  There was some sort of curve but a weird one.  It didn't benefit me though.  I'd say he's just average.  He is willing to help outside of class, so that's a good thing, but yea just average.
got a 100%
worst prof ever.  unfeeling.  gave us a chance to replace midterm grades with the final and then made the final goddamned impossible.
No Comments
lectures aren't completely clear and the tests are pretty hard.
HORRIBLE.
Very enthusiastic
Horrible Professor. There are much better choices out there. NO CURVE. NO CALCULATOR. His TA even said he was a dick. Drop his class before it gets too late.
His tests were really hard and he doesn't curve. He does care though and will give you help if you need it

Nothing really to add that others haven't said.  I thought the tests were very difficult and even though I studied a lot, it didn't really pay off, since there was no curve.  So a "good" grade of a 74 (15 pts higher than the curve), was still ju
The man is an idiot... enough said.  The material might be hard, but the guy cannot even speak clearly about it for 50 minutes.
the guy just plain and outright sucks at teaching math..

Absolutely horrible. The man cannot teach, and does not explain the material at all. The midterms are hard, and as mentioned, calculators cannot be used and he does not curve. He's probably the worst math teacher I've ever had.
Jumps from one idea to the next without explaining anything, no calculators..., and won't curve even with a class average of 52%

Hard material, no calculators allowed on exams, no curves despite class average of 50-60% on exams. I learned as much (if not more) from recitation than from lectures. On the plus side, he is very willing to meet one on one and help you learn the material
Worst math teacher ever!
Monotonous, boring, go elsewhere
doesn't explain things very well and is very brief on each subject...doesn't seem to know what he's talking about and isn't ready for the job!!
No Comments
no calculators for kids with no math capabilities (myself included) 61% class average, ****!!
Good at teaching the information.
class average of 54%...way to go firas...and no calculators...wtf????
No Calculators?  WTF?!

This class has a lecture and a lab. The lecture is cool because each time a guest speaker comes and talks about their field of engineering so very useful for someone trying to decide which engineering field they want to go into. The lab was a bunch of group projects that were sometimes fun and other times tricky(coding/equations/unclear directions)

This class was very diverse in what we learned. Many guest lectures, but they were very interesting and informative. Professor Firth was very caring and understanding to all students. Great person and passionate about her teaching.

Class was very straightforward, as it was just an introductory course. However, the lab instructions were not always clear, and there were several assignments each week, some of which were very easy to forget. But the professor was always willing to help, and was very lenient with due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Goated with the sauce.

Process controls is a stupidly hard topic but she's a great professor and made it bearable.

Also I was kinda surprised to see all these low ratings from Chen1077. I didn't know that was a class she taught but the ratings are all coming from non-engineering freshmen so their opinions don't matter as much.

Stacy really enjoys what she teaches and cares about making sure her students understand the material. I had a difficult time with Controls, but Stacy was very accessibly to answer questions and offered extra credit at the end of the semester. The tests were difficult, but I found her to be a fair and generous grader.

This class was boring and time consuming. Dr. Firth did not seem enthused to teach this class and it showed. The lectures were boring and the labs were just unnecessary and tedious. If you know what your major is, take the intro course instead of this course. I just thought it was dumb and a waste of time. Was pretty easy tho.

Didn't seem like she knew what she was talking about and only read straight off of slides when she was giving lectures. The only reason you would need to show up would be to meet your group for one of the many group projects we were assigned to do. Was willing to accommodate me when I had trouble meeting up with groups which was nice.
Stacy is very cool.

Survey of Engineering - Fall 2021.
Dr Firth is a very nice person, but I really don't like how she structures this class. The guest lectures were what I thought this whole class would be, but most were very boring and felt like afterthoughts. Most of this class was about the "engineering design process", which wasn't nearly as helpful.

She's an ok teacher...kind of treats us like kids (does the mom voice). She assigns a LOT of homework for a 2 credit hour class!!! I had at least three assignments due each week with her! And it's all busy work!

Easy A class that surveys engineering. The class is mostly guest speakers lecturing about different fields while she talks at the end about the ongoing group project, but it's a pretty easy A if you follow the directions.

This professor was quite nice and caring the course was quite easy. As it was an exploration course. I found the professor to use lectures quite heavily and the textbook was used often however she was quite accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stacy has to be the worst professor to teach controls. She gives ridiculous problems on all of the exams. Her exams are long and hard. Homework is too long and the book is the worst book to be published ever. She never responds to any emails and her instructions are never clear enough.
Good Professor, very light work load, she tends to talk a lot about her Personal Relationship, and bring up some topics that are feminist, and progressive. Like every class.

Dr. Flum is super chill and very good at what she does. She provides thorough, helpful feedback and cares deeply about her students. Regardless of the class, if she's teaching, you'll have a good time.

Lisa loves what she does and that makes a great mark for a professor! Your writing will surely be appreciated and given feedback! If you're looking to start writing she will take the time to help you. responds to emails fast too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took at RIT. Very understanding and caring. Come to class for the group stuff. There were fun writing assignments and as long as you try, you'll get an A.

She is easily the best lit teacher I've ever had. She is so good at recognizing you and your presence whether it is through your work or your participation in class. Very caring and positive feedback building sort of teacher. Makes you feel very important and noticed, she does not at all make you feel like a unit of the class or a systematic grade.
Amazing professor with an amazing course. 2 discussions weekly with a weekly poem or story due. As long as you do the work, theres no way to not pass. Let's you be creative in your writing.

She is one of the most caring teachers who genuinely wants you to succeed!! She will work with you as well! If you ever have a question or need help, she is easy to get a hold of! She also gives really good feedback!! She lets you express yourself and creative in your writing as well!! I strongly recommend taking her!
Jim has a bad rep, he's a good guy. What I've gathered from others I've spoken with it may be better to take a class face to face with him rather than online.
Jim is a seasoned vet, with many years of experience under his belt. He is an awesome teacher, and honestly he is an acquired taste, it takes some time to get used to but once you do, he is amazing!

He tries to use the book at the beginning of the year but it slowly tapers off. His lectures are interesting but some days we did stuff that didn't have anything to do with giving speeches. At the end of the year we had to rush to complete our speeches and some did not have time to redo them which he promised we would. If you do the speech you pass

I thought Jim was a great professor. I learned so much from both his classes without thinking too hard about it. Not for the squeamish or meek minded. He knows his stuff, and makes it easy to understand it in applicable ways. If you're by the book, expect evaluations and structure, go somewhere else.

Hands down worst professor I have ever had. Tries to be funny by using shock humor, and favors athletes in class. Explanations of concepts were vague, as were homework assignments, although they are graded as if instructions were specific. Grade progress was not posted anywhere online for student review throughout the semester. Not recommended.

I took both 1500 and 3550 from him this semester and the classes were extremely easy.  He does quizzes randomly to make sure people show up and actually gives you the exam the day before so you can find the answers for it.  The last two weeks of the semester he canceled classes.  Easy, sometimes confusing and funny guy.

He is so sassy/hilarious. I enjoyed this class and his ramblings - showed good material and the textbooks/readings/lectures taught me quite a bit about visual comm. Not super hard - do the readings and go to class.

Fisher's class was extremely easy. I probably wouldn't have showed up for most of the semester if he didn't do frequent quizzes. He rambles on and on and the whole class almost seems like one huge tangent. I always did work for other classes during this class so I didn't feel completely unproductive. Funny guy, kind of strange, but easy class.
Great Guy, saves you money on textbook. Quiz every class.

I love Jim, but not for this class. Expectations from either him or the department at large are nonexistent, so it's a lot of guesswork, and his grading was harsh considering the class's subjective nature. Also, be aware that there's a good chance that his personal rapport with you will figure into your final grade, so make a good impression.

He's hilarious. He makes a boring topic interesting and is always there to help. Avoid his class if you're easily offended, but he means no harm. Learning is fun with him and he really knows his material. Go to class! there's a quiz on every class. Don't mess with scrapbooks, your grade depends largely on them and tests.

Great guy. A little bit loco but in a good way. Was a war correspondent during Viet Nam. Waaaaay knowledgeable. Says he teaches at U of U because that's where the most minds need changing (lol, go figure).
funy guy. easy going
I THOUGHT HE WAS A REALLY GOOD TEACHER. HE WAS VERY HELPFUL IN STUDYING FOR EXAMS. HALARIOUS
I have had this professor three times, he's that good.  Be prepared to be offended, yell, debate, argue, and learn.  You will be challenged but you will love every minute of it!
Enjoy!

Take any class you can from Fisher. He is a great teacher, easy to listen to with good examples.  He keeps you interested plus he will do all he can to help you get an A if you are willing to do the work, you have to be willing to do the work.

He's hilarious.  He'll grab your attention from day one because he's funny.  His class is pretty easy, I'm sure most people are going to get A-s or As, but you still have to do some work.  He's good.  If you need Comm 1500 Fisher is great.
He has fun lectures which makes it easy to remember the info.  He also is very laid back and helpful.

He grabs your attention with his humor, but after listening to him speak you leave the class with more knowledge.  He wants you to succeed, and is always willing to help (even though he pretends to be annoyed).
awesome...i love him and i would not trade him for anyone else in the world.  my favorite professor on campus.

Jim's a great professor and can easily and willingly evolve into a great friend. He may not come off as caring, but when you get talking with him he's willing to dedicate all the time in the world to your cause if it's worthy.
Coolest professor ever. Hilarious, engaging and knowledgeable. You will be scrambling to take photography after 5 minutes in the saem room as him!
Great Prof. sure he has an ego...  But still a great teacher, Even gave me tons of playing time for the Comm Soccer Team...
No Comments

Jim's photojournalism kicked my ass and ended up being the best class I've had at the U.  He is a great teacher and it's a shame that I won't be able to take more classes from him sine I'm graduating.  If you want an easy class/teacher this isn't it. He's an honest grader so forget about sliding by.

Mr. Fisher is extremely bright & able to explain things in a manner that the listener understands. He's not ridgid eg."I'll say it once and you'd better get it!" Rather his wide range of experience, in the real world, and in acdemia, blemd as an

Great Comm professor. He knows the media and how to teach about visual media and communications very well. He's very funny and has a good sence of humor. He's also simpathetic of students and what we're going through at diffrent times of the semester/year

His personal teaching style is challenging but engaging.  Teaches to real-life applications and is mindful of the end-of-semester rush--you do a lot of reading at the beginning of the course, but it tapers off toward the end.

You either like him or you hate him.  Have an open mind, and you'll learn more from Jim than any other professor in the COMM department.  Students with large egos won't be able to handle him though.  That's why he's the professor.

The worst part about this class was the drive to the campus. She is an incredible professor who truly cares about every student- she starts every class with a meditation session. Class was often out early and as long as you turn in assignments you're bound to get an A. Her tests are straight from the slides and offers ample extra credit. Loved her!
One of the best and most helpful classes I have ever taken. She loves her job and it shows!

Loved this class! Whitney is an amazing professor, her lectures are fun and interesting. This class gave me good ideas on how to deal with stress and just learn about different kinds of stress and ways people react to it. I would recommend this class to everyone, it's an easy A and you will enjoy it.

Lots of assignments but that's expected for a 6-week class. The reading is hard but you can honestly skip it and still do good on the weekly quizzes. Lots of extra credit is available. Even though its a stress management class it still gave me stress. Ironic lmao

She is my favorite professor I have had here at the U. She takes the time to listen and help students. She is passionate about what she is teaching. She is very understanding and easy to communicate with. She makes it easy to learn and succeed in her class.

One of my favorite professors to date. Weekly quiz and reflection assignment with a few tests and papers spread in, nothing crazy. Tests are pretty easy and she asks the class if you want them in person or online, highly recommend them online. Super funny and easygoing. Was super accommodating to students that needed extra time. Lovely all around.

The exams were hard as the review sheet was very vague and youre given scenario questions and really need to be able to differentiate the terms. Most of the assignments were written and easy. The quizzes require close attention to the online readings. Class was interesting and you get a ton of points for attending so try not to miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, took her for psych 1010. Only took two exams, but does require lots of reading of course:)

Whitney is incredible. She is deeply passionate about the material and enjoys engaging her classes in activities which demonstrate various concepts. Her classes consist of weekly quizzes and thoughts of the week as well as three exams and a couple research reviews. There is also opportunity for extra credit by reading a book related to the class!

Whitney is really nice and willing to help students succeed. I wish she responded to emails more quickly and was a little more organized, but I liked her lectures. She went through the study guide in class before each exam, and that was very helpful.

I would strongly recommend taking this class if you even think you are interested in the subject. My class only met once a week, but I still learned so much. There were weekly quizzes and short papers. We had a total of two tests, one paper, and a ton of extra credit opportunities!
Whitney is the best teacher ever! I would take a class from her again, for sure!

CS3520 is probably the best class I've taken at the U, though the name of the class is a little misleading; this is really a class about functional programming and not interpreters. Flatt is the most intelligent lecturer the U has, and he is really able to teach you how to program, not just how to use a language, in a way no professor I've had can.

Matt Flatt's jersey is for sure getting hung in the rafters when he retire. The class goes like this: he asks a question, offers a solution (through a feature in the language you are building), solves it in class, asks a similar question on the homework. This structure is 1) super easy to follow and 2) very fun. Just go to class and you'll be fine.

check+
Good.

This class was interesting for sure, just don't make the mistake of taking it as an "easy" class like I did. The class requires considerable effort. The assignments were graded very nicely. I would have gotten an A if I did the final :P

I really like Prof. Flatt as a person. I didn't like the flipped classroom style for the course however. You do videos and a quiz before each class. Then, each class involves a student giving a test-run of the new content. Was hard learn in-class as I had go with their thought process. I like welll-structured lectures more. Friendly grading!

Professor Flatt is extremely knowledgable and caring. Assignments have the perfect balance between challenging and fun/rewarding. Grading is very fair and clearly outlined. You walk away feeling like a better programmer, CS3520 is definitely one of the best courses I've taken at the U.

Favorite CS class at the U by far. Although building interpreters is pretty niche, I came out with a broader understanding of how to be a better programmer in general. Everyone in the class had a positive attitude and was there to learn and grow. Don't be a dummy like some and not show up and do the work, Matt is truly one of a kind to learn from.

Prof. Flatt is just great; nothing but good things to say. CS 3520 throws some curveballs, but he's a fantastic lecturer, and I never felt like the class was being moved faster than I could keep up with. I'd take another class from him in a heartbeat.

Out of all the classes I have taken at the U, CS 3520 was my favorite. The homework had the perfect balance of difficulty and fun. The class and grading were extremely fair. This class will override your understanding of programming languages. I would recommend this class to anyone.

Out of all the classes I've taken so far, CS 3520 is may favorite. The assignments are just challenging enough to be fun and the course and grading are extremely fair. The class rewrites your existing understanding of programming languages in such an interesting way.

Dr. Flatt is exceptionally caring. His exam reviews are identical to his actual exams. He tells you the difficulty of each hw, making time management easier. Each student gets 3 late days w./out penalty. He canceled an assignment to give students a break. In his PL class, you will get so much better at recursion.

Functional programming is my favorite CS class I've taken at the U. I graduate in a week. Don't miss your chance to write Racket in a class taught by the raconteur Racketeer himself. (Actually, that word doesn't even apply but you get the vibe.) Seriously, this guy has a Wikipedia page. Look him up. Doesn't help that Mattflatt is so CHILLLLL

Professor Flatt is incredible. He posts videos to watch before each class and always presents the content in interesting and engaging ways. Every assignment is well thought out and he gives great feedback.

Prof. Flatt is an amazing lecturer. His lecture style involves bringing students up to work on a certain problem, and guiding them through it along with the class. It can be scary, but he is very kind and will help you if needed. One of the best lecture styles I have ever experienced. Take this class if you have space, it's really good.

Highly recommend this class to anyone interested in programming language concepts, functional programming, and/or becoming a better programmer. Assignments were reasonably difficult and generally build upon previous ideas.

In a unique style, Professor Flatt displays a working program on the projector and wants to improve it. He then brings students down and has them work on the problem on his laptop. It can be scary, but it is a great experience. He knows the topic of the class in and out and is excellent at teaching the inner workings of a programming language.
Learning Programming Language Theory with Racket from Matthew Flatt, what more do you want? Though I hope that he would teach compilers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely, the smartest Professor I've ever taken. Matt really knows his stuff and I feel like I learned a great deal from this class. I also really liked how everything was structured and organized in the class.

This is a brutally difficult class in the CS program, but Matt is an incredible prof. Get ready to spend up to 20 hours on some of the assignments. DO NOT PROCRASTINATE. However, the grading criteria for everything is insanely clear and the majority of your grade comes from assignments. If you put in time there is no reason you can't get an A.

Here's how 3520 works with Matt, you get weekly assignments which take a lot of time and thinking, expect to need TA help. You get two free late days, and the day after the assignment is due he goes over it in class (so basically two free assignments). The tests are hard but curved. The final is a project with extra credit. This class is doable.

CS 3520 is CS 5510/6510 and the dept lowered it to increases enrollment. Google both, work is exactly the same. I feel DUPED, I wasn't ready for 5000 level coursework. Wasted tuition, damaged GPA. Watched lectures 5x, worked with TAs, I just wasn't ready for it. It's a GREAT class, but it's a GRAD class, take only when you feel ready.

Matt is an awesome teacher! He's honestly one of the smartest programmers I've ever met, and if you have the chance definitely take his Programming Language Concepts class. If you don't understand recursion, you will by the end of this.

Had an amazing class that bends the minds of the usual programmer. Videos are helpful and organized, but it doesn't seem a lot of students actually watch them, which I think is a mistake on the student's part. Only complaint I have is that the language he uses takes a bit of time to pick up and isn't really similar to modern languages
The greatest professor ever!!!Ever!!!!

Flatt's explanations of systems concepts made complex topics easy to understand. His lecture videos were clear and concise, and his in-class exercises were helpful to reinforce the material. Definitely one of the best professors in the CS department.

Extremely accommodating to our class which seemed to be constantly whining about assignment extensions. He makes concepts, which are objectively difficult to grok, easy to understand. His class format was interesting, but seemingly much better than previous instructors teaching 4400. This is the quality of professor that I expect from the U. A+

Flatt is an amazing professor who saved the 4400 class at the U. His lectures are on youtube and in class students do examples. I skipped a lot but had to make up for the work, and there are participation points. The homework is hard but he gives you detailed outlines and a lot of information. It's the last major CS class, its hard.

He records lectures and posts them on youtube to give time in lecture to have students show solutions to homework and example problems in front of the class. Both his recorded lectures and the part of class in which he teaches are excellent, and the opportunity to work through something with his help in that setting is a great learning experience.
He's a fantastic teacher. He really cares about CS and his students. His door is always open to struggling students. He's just a genuinely nice professor who's really a genius.
He knows his stuff.  He enjoys teaching PL because this is his field.  He is an expert in this area and teaches with excitement and patience.

Flatt is a smart guy. He knows his stuff and is passionate about what he does. Which is why I feel bad for him getting stuck with this nightmare of a course, CS4400. He did the best he could given the limitations of the material he was forced to present. I guess that's all I can ask.
He's the BOSS! He knows his stuff like awesome!

Overall, this class was very easy to pass but, Flor was very difficult to get in contact with and took forever grade. There were a couple questions I had about assignments I never got the answer to because of the lack of communication. The class was easy as long as you show up, do the readings and followed the instructions for the assignments.

Tough to contact. Never saw what scores I got on most assignments. I got a 4.0 stripped because of this teacher. Never knew what I did to not achieve an A. Finalized grades at the deadline and left no room for communication or the opportunity to see my percentage in the class.

Go to class and keep up on the quizzes.  If you do -- A or B.  Richard will work hard to help you pass this class.
Really liked taking this class from Fowles, knows his stuff and keeps the class entertaining. I would definitely take another class from him.

This class is extremely easy, he gives you online quizzes, allowing multiple attempts to get a perfect score, later in the semester he begins to give more group quizzes so you do need to attend. his midterm was copy and pasted from the online quizzes...but his final really threw the entire class off,it was much harder than he had lead us to believe
richard is awesome. he's hilarious. his stories and just the way he carries himself in front of the class are great.
Richard is just great! I had so much fun in his class, and it was an easy A. He is very funny too and usually let us out way before class ended.

Fowles is great! He is very smart and does a great job transmitting the material. He is fun while still taking the class seriously. You have to put in the time, but he is very fair. One of the best teachers and classes I have had at the U.
No Comments

Richard is very entertaining and makes the class interesting. He does have a lot of quizzes, but they are not difficult and as long as you go to class you are fine. His tests come straight from the quizzes. I really enjoyed him as a professor.

This instructor is extremely disorganized, procrastinating, and stubborn. Most of the time he just read and put on the board some pre-made notes which he refused to provide to students. Gave a deceivingly easy practice exam and claimed that the actual will be "similar but not exact", and the whole class failed it. Not recommended, even for trigs.

This class and professor will challenge you. Ben didn't give back most of the homework until the last week of the semester. His lectures and style of teaching wasn't adequate due to the unnecessary proofs and confusing explanations. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: worked hard to explain topics well, but in such a tough class, there were difficult topics that the class as a whole would not comprehend. He put in great effort to try and explain in a new way. No curveballs on quizzes or tests, but every point, every homework assignment, definitely counts! Fairly drops low quizzes and labs when calculating grade
The grad students do all of the presenting. He just shows up and listens. He doesn't contribute or do any teaching.

Professor is terrible at teaching. He will ask you to try a topic that he has not taught and then he would not teach it well enough. The homework is online and he would put things on the homework that wasn't taught in class and the homework is for a grade. He also put things on quizzes, midterms, and final that was not taught in class.

The classes he teaches have a lot of valuable marketing information, if you are interested in going into that field. Overall, he's a pretty easy professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, your grade is based mostly on tests. If you attend class or read over the lectures he posts after, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hands down, one of the best professors I have had. He has valuable information to teach.

Ken is outstanding. He is a genuine, highly knowledgeable, and very experienced professor. He has a personable and friendly personality that makes him very approachable. I would (and actively) recommend his courses. You won't be disappointed to say the least. Definitely a personal favorite of mine.

Really enjoyed his lectures and coming to class. Class participation made the class even more insightful with the great feedback from the professor. The guest lectures really gave you a real world aspect of the Principles of Advertising. I recommend this course and professor.
If you show up to class there is no reason why you shouldn't have an A.

Ken is the man! He is seriously awesome, he cares about your grade and if you are learning. By far the best professor i have had in my college career ( i am a senior). He is super funny and keeps class interesting. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! You can thank me later. Cant say enough great things about him, awesome awesome awesome guy.

Best professor I've ever had! He gives you information that you will use for your career (not just regurgitating information)as well as explains things extremely well. We had awesome class discussions and he makes sure that everyone understands things in a very easy way. If you get a chance, take any class you can from him!
He is the man. Best professor ive had
Knows what he is talking about

Foster was by far the best professor I had at the U. His classes a ton of real world applicable information. We also worked with a local company on a real advertising campaign. VERY nice change of pace to have a professor who not only teaches from experience, but also truly tries to impart the knowledge he knows to his students. TAKE HIS CLASSES!

Interesting that people list him as a marketing instructor, he's not.  He's in the COMM department, and is perhaps the greatest asset the department has.  Not only do you do real world work, but he even reccomended me for a job which I was offered right out of class.  Take anything you can from him, if you're interested in advertising.

All he does is lecture on power points. Class was sort of boring, unless you are interested in marketing. Tests are pretty tough, but allows great EC opportunites. Not as easy as I thought, but he is a really nice guy.
Love him!
Best class is the spring semester of his marketing class, you work on real ad campaigns.

This class is a lot of work but it is very useful information no matter where in life you are going. She offers almost 10+% of extra credit in the exam category. So as long as you do your work, you will be fine. There is more work than other classes, but it isn't a waste. Incredibly valuable class if you take it seriously.
I had a 4.0 and had to take this course during my last semester, and it messed up my entire GPA. This class takes no joke 10 hours a week, and it is a 3 credit elective course. I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is by far the worst professor I have had during my time at the U. She assigns loads of menial pointless assignments, is very passive aggressive without being helpful or informative, and grades insanely tough for assignments without rubrics or clear instruction. Overall avoid this teacher if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: A rude and disrespectful professor. Will grade very harshly and will not be kind when asking for help. Assignments were not clear at all. Do not recommend this professor at all!

I have never not once written a bad review for a teacher in my entire life. This has been by far the absolute worst class I have ever taken in my entire life. I strongly advise you not to take this class with this teacher. She grades so harsh to the point where you will question how dumb you are. The course load is just blatantly hilarious.

This might be one of the worst taught classes I have ever taken. The sheer volume of assignments that are assigned for a 3 credit class is blatantly absurd. There is zero clarity on assignments and there is absolutely no remorse on grading. I have never had a teacher that has ever graded me so harshly for the work that I have done.

This class demands a lot of time and attention to be dedicated to assignments that have so little practical value that it's both comical and deeply upsetting. The concepts are not difficult, but her grading and assignments are. The amount of work required to succeed is ridiculous given the material and the course being only 3 credit hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her class is easy in terms of the actual assignments but she assigns an OVERWHELMING amount for a 3-credit class. The worst part about the class is that she grades harshly but provides little to no instructions or rubric. The class isn't intellectually challenging but the workload and grading system make it more stressful than it should be.

PSYCH2250 was one of my easiest classes. The quizzes have multiple attempts, the exams are pretty self explanatory, and the assignments don't require a huge amount of effort. The content is actually pretty interesting as well. The professor grades in a timely fashion & grades/expectations are clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really easy class. Great professor!

Not a very hard course. Took it for my PSY major. All quiz and exams are open note, unproctored, and the questions can be found on quizlet. I don't think I even looked at the textbook once. Interesting content, but not as many modern examples as I would've hoped for. Didn't interact with the professor, but she set up the Canvas page very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had this class online and it was chill. There isn't a lot of assignments, and the exams were open note. I think the subject is interesting and the Professor seems good. You just read the stuff on your own and watch PowerPoints. I did not interact with her much, but she did give me an extension on an assignment which was super helpful!!

She wasn't very present during the online course. The tests were all pretty difficult even if you did the readings and quizzes. The article discussions were easy points. Overall, it felt like you had to teach yourself all of the material. Her lectures weren't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are four quizzes due each month, and they are also fairly easy. The textbook is the only material that you get in the class, but it's interesting to read. There are also a few assignments due, but they only take a short amount of time to do. The exams are also pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria
