reviews.comment: The class was fairly easy. Grade is based on 3 exams spaced evenly throughout the semester. There is one quiz per chapter associated with each exam and they are all due the week before the exam. 3 discussion posts. Overall, an interesting and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Weekley quizzes, some little bibliographies here and there with exams that have super easy answers. Really interesting topic too.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Assignments and tests were super easy, quizzes could be taken over and over again until you get a good score. Tests were really hard, despite being open book and open note. The questions were super specific and there were always at least 2 good answer choices. These tests were 40% of the grade. Be careful when taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The usual for an online class. The reading quizzes, article assignments, and unit exams were all pretty laid back, just like the instructor herself. The content is pretty fun if you're into abnormal psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You can take the open book quizzes as many times you want until you get the scores you want, so I suggest to get 100% on all quizzes.  The exams are open book, but you have only one chance and 2 hours to finish, and they were hard for me.  You MUST read the textbook.  Malinda was always willing to help and quick to respond to my questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She does not provide study guides but her lecture slides are helpful during tests, most of the material can be found on those and in the book (which I rented as an ebook for easy searches). The quizzes did not prepare me at all for the tests so do not use those as a guide for what to study- they just help you know what each chapter consists of.

I took the online course and the lecture slides were literally no help when it came to the exams. Reading the book was essential to passing the Exams. Most of her final grade was made up of quizzes that you could retake and 3 assignments for a single project you do in the class. You can still pass the class even if you do poorly on the tests.

Worst teacher ever! Emailed her multiple times and she never got back to me. Not willing to work with students. Do not take this class solely because of how horrible of a teacher she is! Pointless class. Pointless Teacher. Did not learn a single thing.

I wish when I took this class I took it more seriously. I thought it would be easy but since I didn't try I got a bad grade. If you take this class try your best! It's seriously not that bad. The exams have a two hour limit so make sure you double check your answers -- you'll have enough time!!

I loved this online class! There are 2 tests that are open book and done online and weekly discussions. There's also a couple of papers that are 3 pages each. As long as you do all the work it should be an easy A
what I could feel was just impatient and helpless.

I took this class online and really enjoyed it. Freitag is very organized and clear in her expectations. She was easy to get a hold of and her expectations were not too difficult. There were discussions you had to post, 2 papers, and a few tests that were open book. Super interesting and totally do-able!

It's possible to get a good grade in her class, but difficult because tests have very confusing questions/answers & study guides aren't much help. Deducts points for minor APA errors, but doesn't instruct how she wants APA in the first place. No one ever got 100% on her tests, which is unusual. I'd recommend her, but STUDY hard for the tests!

Worst class I have taken at the U. The grading scale is trying to "get you to learn" so you don't focus on your grade percentage. But it doesn't make sense at all, I didn't learn much and still got a bad grade because the professor is looking for her own very specific answer. I would never take this class again, and it could be structured better.

This is the most ridiculous grading scale I've ever seen. I've gotten A's in o chem, anatomy, human phys, physics, biochem, but because of missing a singular in text citation I can no longer get an A in the course. How is this okay

The grading system is absolutely ridiculous. Assignments are pass/fail and no grade is shown in canvas until the end of the semester. Majority of people I knew in the class failed at least one, if not two assignments. I don't know anyone who passed 3/3 assignments.

This class is absolutely ridiculous. Everything is graded pass/not pass which is then translated into a letter grade at the end of class. Dr. J is EXTREMELY specific about what she expects in each assignment and missing one small thing can lead you to fail an assignment. Do not take this class!

Worst class I have taken at the U so far. The grading scheme is so unusual, there are 3 discussion posts, which are basically essays. Everything is pass/fail, but if you "fail", or "not pass" as she calls it, one of the three discussion posts the highest grade you can get is a D. Do not take this class!!!

Class content is not hard, but it's SO hard to pass on her grading standards. Most nit-picky prof I have EVER met. Doesn't matter how well you understand the content, if you don't phrase a question correctly, you WILL fail. Class is credited like an: A, B, C, D, or F for transcript, however all of her rubrics are Pass/Not Pass. Good Luck!

DO NOT TAKE!!! she is such a strict grader to the point where i don't care about the class i just look if Im going to receive a “not pass” her grading is horrible you can't even see your grade until the semester is over. the exams are 10 essay questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This teacher cares more about following strict, unnecessary rules than actual learning.Her grade lock and nitpicky grading create stress. It feels like middle school getting marked down for unecessary details. She lets you revise, which helps, but the class feels way too tailored to her own preferences. More of a pain to follow her rules than learn
Terrible pass fail grading scale for assignments that don't encourage you to learn. If you fail one discussion post you cannot pass any others for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. J was great. Yes, her grading was difficult and confusing to understand in order to get a pass, but going to her office hours or emailing her helped out so much. She was very welcoming and would explain things until I understood them. She also gave great feedback on how to improve my work before turning them in.

Horrible professor, horrible grading system. You can get an A on every single test and still fail the class because you didn't meet every single NIT PICKY criteria on the rubric for an assignment. She is extremely particular, her rubrics are vague and she will fail you at the drop of a hat, you don't get any partial credit, only Pass/Not Pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr J was a pleasure to work with. Although there is a slight learning curve to class management, after you get past that first hurdle the assignments are clear on expectations. The materials were interesting and engaging, and there is a lot of flexibility in assignment options. Just try your best and double check rubrics and you'll do great!

Dr. J's grading is unforgiving, minor mistakes lead to failure without a chance to correct. If you do extra work in class she says "I won't award students for going above & beyond with a grade but will write you a letter of recommendation for your future & sing your praises" ??? which does absolutely nothing. Consider other reviews before enrolling
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr.J is a phenomenal professor who is educated and excited about the material taught. She gives clear guidelines for her assignments and is willing to answer any questions you may have. While her grading system is different, it prepares you for a work environment where there are specific expectations. I loved her class and would take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment:
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! 

 You can work your hardest and do all the assignments to get an A, but she will be so nitpicky that she will fail you over something little. All the time and effort you put into your work goes down the drain. Save your time and energy and pick a different course. Her grading is so bad.

I DO NOT appreciate this professor's grading system. All assignments follow a pass, revise, or not pass, and you will receive a grade at the end. Like, if you wrote a 3-page essay, she will most likely have you revise it due to her snobbiness (per other students.) You receive 0 credit unless you pass it whereas a normal grading helps you a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
While Dr. J is very educated, she is also very snobby about it. 
She makes it very clear that she is not your friend in any way.

No sympathy. Acts like a drill sergeant. Major control issues. Manipulative. Do not recommend anyone takes her class...just way too extreme to the point you do not even want to be apart of it. So regimented. Not fun to learn, no excitement. Bleh

Professor Franklin is great but she is a tough grader. She lets you know how to get an A but it is not easy because she wants you to blow her mind every time you turn in an assignment. If you are looking for an easy class, this is not it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was kind of a joke. She is a good teacher and makes the best out of a unnecessary class. I just feel like she had to BS most of it. I think I learned 2 things in the class and got an A.

You don't need to attend every class, but it's a good idea to go. She posts lectures online. Tests are hard, study well for them. There's 4 exams (drop lowest score) and a final. Also, a couple easy discussions online, HIPAA/encryption test which is easy, SPSS activities which are easy, and a practicum. Tough class but good instructor
Attendance is mandatory and you can't leave early or arrive late. Beginner friendly class with strong and helpful constructive criticism.

Professor is super picky and is not open to feedback. Her classes are ok if you're a beginner but she expects you to paint a specific way. She docks points if you're late or leave early even of your projects are finished. I would recommend avoiding taking classes from her.

Absolutely mandatory class: If you don't go (no matter what) she will dock your grade HARD. She's also incredibly her way or no way, so she can be frustrating to work with because, even if you think you're right, you're not. Also, good luck reaching her outside of class-- she is genuinely so terrible at answering emails.
She wasn't receptive to feedback.

Really nice teacher. She tries not to be too lecture heavy, but cares a lot about participation. Good beginner oil painting class for beginners. If you try and leave early and she'll mark you absent even if it's 15 minutes and you didn't take a break in the 2 1/2 hours. Goes into color theory. Fun class but sometimes a little too long.

She is a nice professor, the class was fun. As long as you try and she can see that you are trying, you will be fine. Critique days are kind of boring but it is nice to see other peoples work. She is not great at communicating that well about due dates. But your work just has to show effort so if it is only half done, it doesn't really matter.

Attendance was mandatory and if you left early you would lose points. Most often I would finish early and want to leave but couldn't because I didn't want to lose points. Her painting techniques are ok if you are a beginner but if you already know how to paint her techniques are tedious and unhelpful.

Lindsay is one of the best professors i've had! I'm not the biggest drawer but she was able to help me expand my skills and gave really good feedback. I looked forward to having this class every single Tuesday and Thursday. She's a really fun professor and brings pizza during critics. This class was a very nice way to end my day.

Lindsay is the best!!!!! I took her mapping class as part of my foundations series; I haven't really drawn anything since high school but her class reintroduced my love for drawing. She is super helpful and gives fantastic feedback, she really wants to help you improve your art ability. If you have to opportunity to take her class, DO IT!

I needed this class for foundations credit, and Lindsay was super helpful and kind. I can't draw to save my life and she gave me the proper feedback and help that was needed for me to successfully complete each assignment. She graded according to how well I was improving, and understanding the techniques. Would take another class from her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I took Lindsay this fall and her class was fun and I enjoyed almost every day in class. It is nice because just about every assignment will be done in class unless you dont finish during studio time then you will have to do it at home. I recommend taking this drawing class with her

Took her advance drawing class. Great art teacher, really allows the class to figure it out but still giving great guidance. You do not have to be a great artist, she sees the hard work you put into every drawing. If you know you're going to miss more than three classes, don't take it. Participation is a majority of the class.

Lindsay is extremely caring for her students. She believes that people don't have to have a talent for drawing, that people just keep getting better. All she really cares about is that you try your best and put in the effort. Don't worry about being a sucky drawer, as long as you try you'll get a good grade. Participation and attendance matters.

She gives lots of examples to work through in class, but moves very quickly through all the material, and it's hard to understand sometimes. She also encourages people to ask questions, but she can also get impatient and short with you if you don't understand.
I loved this professor and this class. She made lectures fun and they made sense most of the time. Definitely would reccomend.

If you take this class PLEASE take advantage of all the help opportunities, I did not which is reflected in my grade. There are many office hours and the professor is willing to work with you one-on-one. Sometiems she didn't always have the best explainations for things, and she doesn't work out each step of each problem so review stochiometery.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
-speaks loud and often yells in lecture
-most lectures are just an hour of practice problems
-isn't super kind (but not mean) and will call you out if you aren't participating in practice problems
-taught content in a okay way, pretty much only slides and practice problems

If you want a professor that will take time going through material that will be on the midterms, switch to Statler now! Frey is extremely passionate, but you will only do well in this class if you can keep up with her. Does not explain concepts in their fullest. If anything brief summaries. Some people learn that way, not me! Awful handwriting. GL!

Class is pretty easy if you pay attention and do the weekly homework. While I recommend listening, if you teach yourself from the weekly homework you are fine. Attendance is given on a QR code, so just get a gc and have someone send it if you cant attend. Overall not too bad of a prof and class

Frey was an amazing professor! She made each lecture engaging, while also informative. She can get off task sometimes but it adds on to her fun. She held demonstrations with Statler to show different experiments with what we were learning, which I enjoyed. Tests are extremely fair and are not tricky.

Just take the class with Statler. She is a terrible lecturer and will literally skip content that will be on the test. Statler writes the tests and is clear about expectations and she is not. Nice lady, terrible professor. I taught myself this whole class and worked my butt off to barely get an A.

she does not teach at all, class is literally just practice problems. you are expected to show up knowing the weeks material, most of which isn't well covered by the textbook. this is a very teach yourself class and the only reason its a 2 instead of a 1 is because there is a lot of material which is accessible to be able to teach yourself with.

Compared to Ozanklar, I am glad I had Frey, but I ultimately wish I had Statler. So, for Gen Chem 1, go first with Statler and avoid Ozanklar at all costs. Frey just had hard-to-read handwriting and often went too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice prof and pretty funny. However, her lectures often don't make much sense and our not very helpful to learning. Homework helps a lot but does not seem to be made by her. Would very much recommend other profs or online class if your struggle with chem in the past.

Clearly cares about the learning of each student and takes time to explain each concept. Several readings from the textbook; however, most are short. Make sure to review practice questions from the textbook and past exams to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Frey is very passionate about chemistry which shows during lecture. Her teaching however is not very straightforward and her penmanship is not the best. Overall doable class with reasonable homework and quizzes. Do the textbook readings and practice and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Frey is very enthusiastic with lectures, but they are not always clear or helpful. I had to self-study the material beforehand in order to understand the lecture. Homework + quizzes are very reasonable, and the material isn't very hard, but it was difficult to prepare for exams without knowing what kinds of questions were going to be asked

Gina truly cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. There's TA/LA or Professor office hours pretty much 8 hours a day and the tests are extremely straight forward. If you go to office hours and do an adequate amount of studying, there is no reason you shouldn't get a good grade. Very hands on class with little homework (1 hour/week).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She explained things well and has a lot of TAs/LAs that open many hours of office hours for help. Tests are made to be simple and not to trick you. 75% attendance gives you full attendance points. You can make up attendance by attending office hours as well. She seems to want to help students succeed.

Dr. Frey is a very good professor, cannot go wrong with her. Not the best handwriting by any means but she is a nice grader and teaches with a lot of examples. Genuinely excited about the subject, makes the lectures less boring. 

I am solely going off of the year she filled in for Statler, not sure how her specific course is structured.

Professor Frey really loves to teach Chemistry and it shows in her lectures. She is very animated and put a smile on my face every day. Class is much easier if you keep up with the readings for each lecture, but even if you don't you can still do well as long as you go to class and participate. Work all the practice problems in class!

Professor Frey is a great lecturer and makes the topics easy to understand. I love the lectures because they include lots of practice problems that help prepare you on the tests. They are easy to follow and understand. Attendance is taken and it affects your grade. 2 weekly homework assignment but they aren't long or hard.

I loved Prof Frey's class, and she is so passionate about the subject! Its important that you read the textbook and attend office hours when you get confused, and she was always available for questions. The exam questions are really similar to the textbook questions, so make sure you do those! Her handwriting is bad, but overall great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not good at teaching, many homework questions are nonsensical
Take Statler's lecture instead of Frey.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Frey is funny and very. Passionate about Chemistry, sometimes a little too much that it's harder to understand her lectures. Although she does have funny metaphors for things and will run around the class to explain a concept. Attendance is a large part of the grade so be prepared. Also she has really bad handwriting.

Her lectures are very difficult to follow largely because her handwriting is so messy but also because she does not post all the slides and does not really give time to write down the problem. She seems to care a little too much about trying to prevent cheating because it ends up making it hard to learn and complete assignments.
Very good professor! She was always kind and really cares about what she teaches. Lectures usually go over the reading assignments with demonstrations on Fridays. Overall great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Frey is great. Although her handwriting can be tough to read, she is always open/willing to answer questions. My advice in this class: ask questions, study hard, go to office hours, and read the pre-lecture textbook sections! She really wants all of her students to succeed, you just need to show her you are willing to put in the effort!

I love Professor Frey. She makes class fun and engaging. She is loud, charismatic, and full of joy. Her handwriting can be hard to read at times, but she welcomes clarifying questions and is respectful towards her students. Her office hours are very good and her TA's/La's are very helpful. Would recommend her!

Her voice is more than mildly annoying, she cannot control the gen chem class which is basically full of loud uncontrollable high schoolers. Her handwriting is so bad that she uses another professor's slides on canvas for reference notes, meaning what she uses in the lecture and what is on canvas is different. would not recommend.
Handwriting is tough to read

The key takeaway is that the experience of class is disjointed, often it felt like there was limited to no communication between the professor and the people writing the homework assignments, the lesson plans for the discussion sections, and the tests. Resultingly, the class can often feel all over the place which can make it difficult to learn.

She is a super sweet and helpful person. Make sure to pay attention to what she's as her handwriting is difficult to read if you don't follow along. Do the reading before class and take any questions to her office hours; she is super helpful when explaining things one on one.

Tests are graded heavily and worse then what you do in class. I asked her to round my grade from a C- to C even if I have to do extra work, b/c I need a C or better in chemsitry as a req. Her answer, to try harder next semester. I told her I had covid and she still used that against me b/c I was absent in that time frame.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS

This class was definitely hard especially the exams and grasping the material. Overall professor Frey is very nice, and she does her best to explain things, but the handwriting can be difficult to read if u look down and not keep up. Attendance is important because it also counts towards your grade and the little percentage can definitely help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She tries to make her lectures intriguing. Her office hours can be helpful if you have specific questions. Her lectures welcome questions however sometimes she may accidentally embarrass students through her tone of voice when answering.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Frey is a good person and super enthusiastic and you can tell she does really care about her students. She just has terrible handwriting so if you zone out once you will become very lost! Overall she was really nice!

You can tell Professor Frey genuinely enjoys chemistry, and she loves teaching about it even more. She is enthusiastic, and always wants to make sure her students understand the material. It's crucial to prepare for lectures by reading the course material in the textbook and/or watching videos beforehand. Go to her office hours with any questions!

Professor Frey is a very energetic professor. She is very excited and personable with her students. She knows students, even in such a large lecture hall. The structure of CHEM 1210 is slightly weird, but that's not Frey's fault. She does have pretty horrible handwriting and she talks fast, but overall she is a very fun professor. I recommend her.

Prof Frey is a great and energetic teacher, but she moves way too fast and her handwriting is terrible, making it hard to understand what she is explaining. Taught myself the material for most of the semester. I did like how exciting and fun she made things though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very engaging and informative for a massive lecture class, built off of taught material seamlessly. Even though there was a required textbook, I found the lectures themselves to be adequate enough that I did not need to supplement my knowledge with the textbook and only used it in review for the exams (which there are 3 noncomprehensive)

She is helpful, I liked this class a lot. It's not too hard if you are willing to study. I would also like to note studying my lab and mastery is not the best. The canvas quizzes are much better for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Frey is energetic and makes class fun to be in. However, I do feel that you have to teach yourself in this course more than you are taught. If you can stay on top of the lecture videos in this class then you will do fine, but it will be hard if you fall behind. I like her grading criteria because exams aren't worth a lot of the grade.

Prof Frey is the most outgoing full of energy prof I've had. I liked going to her class because she was always ready to give class and make you smile with her attitude. Class is demanding 4 times/wk (you must go) and 2 assignments/wk as well as weekly hw check. Wasnt too bad, just stay on top of videos for lecture
A great engaging professor who taught gen chem 1 very well. She made it very interesting to go to class and always explains questions very well. Would highly recommend taking class with her

Professor Frey is super fun and enjoyable. I didn't like gen chem much because it doesn't really interest me, but it wasn't too bad. The class was overwhelming at first because there was a lot to keep track of, but when it becomes routine it's pretty easy. However, the lectures don't accomplish much as the class is flipped.

Professor frey is awesome she so funny and really loves chemistry. the whole general chem I department is set up with letcures to watch before class then review during class but its just an adjustment. Class is pretty demanding with two to three homework assignments a week, class four times a week, and homework checks on the weekend.
great guy hes super nice and i really like him

Fuller makes you want to learn more. He's fantastic at engaging the class and cares deeply about his students. First day told us to opt out of the textbook and save our money since we won't be needing it. I wish he could be my professor for all my classes this semester. If Fuller teaches a class you're signing up for, go for it!

Tim is the best professor I have had at the U. I have taken this class before and failed it miserably with a different professor. Tim makes it easy, and fun, it makes you want to learn more. His lectures are amazing! You will actually learn. He cares deeply about his students, is always available to answer questions. Take the class from him!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The homework wasn't mandatory but highly recommend doing it. 4 exams including the final but he drops the lowest score. He is the type of college professor you want to have. Made the content easy to understand.

Professor Fuller's grading criteria was often vague and when asked to questions to clarify he would be very unhelpful. The labs were tough and were usually just as unclear as the homework and AID assignments. The design project also took up a huge chunk of time towards the end. The book for the course was great though and so were the TA's.
actually the goat. could fade this class all the time
Josh is a great professor, He wants you to do well. He would always make sure we knew what to expect and what concepts to study for the stats quizzes

Josh is super accommodating and helpful. He will do his best to try and help you get the grade you want. He also offers a ton of EC opportunities. The actual exams are super easy; it's just simple statistics. Plus, you get a full page, front and back, of notes on the exam. The TA is a harsh grader tho.

If you have to take IS 2010, take it with Josh! It is a tedious Excel class, with lots of homework, and you have to study for the test, BUT Josh is the best person to take it from. All IS 2010 classes are hard because the department makes them hard, but Josh is very willing to work with students to help them succeed.

While Excel is a complicated subject to teach, Josh really cares about his students. This was his first semester teaching and, like with any new teacher, he had a learning curve to get over. However, he was constantly trying to get our input, and he was willing to make changes if we were struggling. Be straight-up with him, and he'll help you.

One of the best Chinese teachers I've had! If you are interested in Chinese language and culture and are committed to studying the readings, you will love his classes.  There are some difficult moments in this class, especially with reading and remembering Classical Chinese passages, but it is well worth it!
He doesn't care about his students, and don't clarify anything. He grades hard and makes you stress all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unwilling to hear other opinions, rude (told a student to move or get out of class after the student doodled a smiley face on their notes), doesn't give a grade until the semester is over or provide rubrics for papers because he is "not here to hand hold us" and "doesn't like grading", and he wrote the book you are required to buy... figures

Professor Wu offers a lot of unique insight and holds in depth knowledge of ancient Chinese history and thought. I learned a ton in his course and if you're interested in the subjects that he teaches, then you will greatly enjoy the class. However, coursework can be difficult, especially if you lack interest and Mandarin proficiency.
The professor was very strict at grading, and he barely listened to students' opinions. He can also be very confusing and hard to communicate with.

I took Prof. Wu's Chinese culture class (selected readings of philosophers like Mencius and Confucius). It was SUPER interesting. He is so passionate about the subject and knows so much about it. The class is lecture-based so it can be hard to sit there for 90 minutes, but if you take notes and stay awake you'll gain a lot from his wisdom!
has a great interest in individual success of students and their academic enlightenment

Knowledgeable and extremely well read in subject matter. His courses are difficult if you fall behind. Stay on top of the reading and homework and his classes will be easy and interesting. As always you get out of it what you put in to it.

I took EDU1010 and it was an extremely easy class to do well in with John. The lectures are really boring and he often talks about the same things over and over again, but it's only one class a week so it's very manageable. He is a super kind professor and will help you out with anything you need.

John Funk is an overall great professor, you can tell he is an expert in his field and has a lot of first hand experience. You can slide through his class but 20 Service hours are required and the end of the semester is heavy with assignments but you can do them early. They all require your service learning, if you don't do that you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I had. Attendance is mandatory and his 3 hour lectures can get boring, but he usually let us out early. Very engaging and an overall great guy. He's very understanding as well. I hope to take another class from him in the future.

John is so cool. His class says it's three hours but he usually lets you out early. He's way funny and makes his lectures interesting. If you are really considering wanting to become a teacher, he gives great insights and you get the chance to be in a class throughout the semester and it gives you a good idea of whether or not you want to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I have had some awesome professors here a the U, but John is THE BEST professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and the educational field. He even sat down with me and helped me study for a final in another class.

John was great! He was a teacher for many years, so he knows what he's talking about. You do a lot with your group in class, but you also get to be friends with your group so it's  a win win situation. Would definitely recommend his classes!

Overall a decent professor. Like everyone says, lectures are long and boring. But I do believe he has valuable experience to offer to education major. Don't skip class, that's what dropped me to a B instead of an A!  Stay on top of the 20 hours you have to spend in the classroom. I waited till the end of the semester & it was a bad idea!

Like everyone else says, his lectures are long and boring, but he does try to spruce them up with stories about his experiences as a teacher. He is extremely friendly, and willing to help and give you advice. Be aware, you will be spending 18 hours in a classroom for this class throughout the semester.

His lectures are long and quite boring. He has a great and open minded personality. Good professor and an easy A if you go to pass and turn everything in. Don't buy the textbook, not necessary at all.
Some of his lectures are very long, but he is a great guy with a lot of funny experiences in the education field. Take his class if you can, because he is very nice.
John is so wonderful. He brings treats and is deeply interesting. I loved his class!
Both classes were amazing. In children's lit, you do not need the textbook. Study the lectures. You do however need all of the children's books. Nicest guy on the planet.
Loved this course. John is seriously the BEST.

Really good class with a great book list that the education majors will use in the future. He's a very helpful teacher who is understanding with the assignments. There is A LOT of reading for this class (a book a week) and a few easy quizzes. The lectures are a little long but again, you take this class for the literature!

Really great professor! I had some person issues come up mid semester and he helped me catch up on what I missed so I could still pass the class. He is so passionate about his subject which helped me stay interested in the materials. Plus, some of the children's books I read were so great!

I think professor John Funk is great. He is, not only a good person, but also a great teacher. He always tries to teach everything to his students. I was lucky to be in his class. He is a great techer, mentor, and great resource for every student.

John Funk is fantastic. One of the best teacher's I've had at the U. I took his class only because it fit my schedule, was and int'l credit that i needed, and I was about to graduate in another major. I was certainly glad I took this class and got to get to know John. Great teacher and a fun class. If it is at all possible take any class from him!
John is great.  He really gets his students interested and passionate about teaching!  I hope to have him again in another class
John is great! I really loved this class he  made it fun and was really excited about it. Great class!! TAKE IT.
Love John! He is such a good teacher and really wants all his students to learn and make class exciting! TAKE THIS CLASS
Interesting to listen to, fair in his expectations and always brought cookies on test day.

John was the best teacher.  I have never had a class where I was actually excited to go to class.  He wants you to learn, he wants you to succeed.  He was amazing.  I wish all of my teachers could be like him.

John was a wonderful teacher. He is passionate about what he does, and he brings that enthusiasm into the classroom-plus he brings treats to every class when it is test day....how can you go wrong with a great professor, and treats?!
THE BEST CLASS YOU'LL EVER TAKE!! He really loves what he's teaching and it shows. He leaves an impression on your desire for reading.
No Comments
Wonderful stories, very understanding, really fun.

Tim is the best professor I've taken at the U. His lectures are engaging and easy to understand. He is more than willing to help you with anything you need. Interesting to listen to. I took the 6:00-9:00 pm class, VERY worth it! Highly recommend him.

Professor Fullmer was an amazing professor. He always made the class engaging and fun. He did a great job at explaining the concepts. We had optional homework(highly encouraged to do) that was similar to the exams. He is easily one of the best professors at the U and made this my favorite class of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tim Fuller is in the top 3 professors I've taken at the U. I was really scared for this course, as your entire grade is made up of 3 midterms and a final. He taught us how to use the calculator TVM, so make sure you get a financial calculator. If you have the chance to take Tim for finance, I highly recommend it. W Professor
Best finance professor ever!! Have to take Finance from him. GOAT!
Best professor I've ever had, by far!
Tim is the best professor at the university by a long shot.  He needs to be cloned!  Take him.  You will learn, understand, remember, and know how to apply finance principles.

I am a marketing major but Professor Fullmer's finance class has been bar far my favorite class at the U.  Despite being a 3 hour night class, it's the only class I've ever looked forward to attending!  He cares about students and knows how to teach.  Best professor at the U.

I thought I was going to hate finance.  Then Professor Fullmer completely changed my mind.  He is incredibly dynamic in class with tons of energy and enthusiasm.  Not only are his lectures engaging, he turns that material into a story that makes finance easy to understand and hard to forget.  His class really opened my eyes.
Literally my favorite professor I've ever had

You can tell he's been a professor for a very long time, explains things very well. The tests make up most of the grade but he does help you out and will drop one of the 3 (not including the final) tests if people submit course feedback.

Tim has been teaching for years and you can definitely tell. His lectures are amazingly structured and easy to follow. The class itself seems to be easy to pass if you apply yourself, even a little bit. He IS an amazing professor and deserves all of the praise, but you have to really try and blow everything off to fail.

I really enjoyed Professor Fullmer's class. He was caring, engaging, and clearly cared about student success. I am not good at finance, but he did a good job explaining the concepts in a way that most students could understand. He has three homework assignments, three exams (one of which can be dropped), and a final.

There are only two assignments and three tests not including the cumulative final, but he drops one test if 90% of the class does evaluations. The tests were pretty hard but he's an amazing lecturer and truly does care about his students.

He is a great guy and teacher, but it really doesn't matter. Your grade literally only consists of three multiple choice exams though. Hard to love a teacher when it feels like you can't get an A no matter what you do.
he was a good teacher

There is no doubt that Fullmer cares about his students and class content. His lectures are easy to follow (which says a lot coming from someone who can generally only learn with one-on-one teaching), and he teaches as if he is telling a story. This is the first time I feel like I have really taken something away from a college class.Amazing prof

Great professor and the workload is not too difficult. The class is graded off of just a couple problem sets and the rest is midterms/final. No graded homework but you SHOULD REALLY DO THEM if you want good scores on the midterms. He is very good at explaining material and has a near 5 star review for a reason.

Finance was a hard class for me because of how the department structures it, but Professor Fullmer was amazing. The way he laid out the homework, had his lectures, TA hours, etc, was so helpful. Attendance is not mandatory, but showing up for his lectures is so helpful, and so are the homework assignments. 10/10 amazing professor. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Easily the coolest professor at the university—an exceptional lecturer who keeps students actively engaged while challenging us to think creatively and reflect deeply on the material.
Long live Professor Fullmer the GOAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Fullmer is by far one of the best at the U. He makes course material easy to understand and does a great job at keeping the class engaged. He is very smart and knows how to actually teach instead of just reading off the slides. He's able to use stories within his lectures to make class material seem relevant and interesting. THE GOAT

Take Fulmer's class! He is an amazing lecturer, explains things in a way that makes sense, and cares about every student. The topics can be tricky, but just make sure you're doing the homework and studying, and you'll be fine. Your grade is based almost 100% on exams. Compared to other profs, his material is def the most straightforward.

I never write reviews about professors- but Tim Fullmer deserves one. He is the BEST professor you could have at the University of Utah. He treats you like an adult and teaches stuff you actually need to know in the real world.  Highly reccomend taking a class with Tim!

Tim was hands down the best finance professor I could ever take. I am NOT good with numbers so the fact that I enjoyed this class was crazy. Homeworks were amazing because it had an answer key that was so in depth and explained the whole problem - those are crucial for the exam. 10/10 take Tim
Tim is the best!  I've taken other classes with him, and he is great!  I wish he taught every class here.  Do yourself a favor and take this class.  It's awesome.

Tim is the GOAT!  He is the best professor in the business school.  This is a hard class but he makes complicated material easy to understand and relatable to the real world.  I learned more in this class than in any other business class I've taken.  You can tell he really cares about our success in class and life.

Tim Fullmer is the best professors I've had. His lectures aren't mandatory but HIGHLY recommend you go. He makes them as interesting as possible and it helps you understand the material so much better. He will emphasize this but he had optional homework, do it!! Best way to study for exam is the homework and getting problems similar to the homework

Tim is incredibly kind and wants you to succeed. Heart of gold! He writes all FINAN 3020 exams, so knowing his style early helps. Homework isn't required but is very similar to exams. Exams are decently hard, but there's often a big curve (10%+). If course feedback hits 90%, he drops your lowest section exam, which can really boost your grade.

Absolutely amazing class, easily the best course I have taken. Prof. Fullmer keeps his lectures useful and engaging, not to mention he structures his class how every college course should be. Homework is optional but will help a lot on exams, and attendance is not mandatory. Students who do the HW, study, and learn will do exceptionally well.

Professor Fullmer is hands down one of the best professors I've had at the U. His teaching style is very creative, where during class we would play a simulation trading game, which ultimately helped me learn more and was a fun way to get involved. Highly recommend taking his class!
An amazing professor, by far the best I have ever had. For being a tuff class he does an amazing job explains the material and welcomes questions. Such an amazing class and professor.

FANTASTIC TEACHER! Lectures are engaging and interesting. He really knows how to maintain the attention of his students. As someone who HATES math, Professor Fullmer made this class very doable. Great guy.
awesome professor, loved his themed examples. Sometimes hard to pay attention in class but that could vary from person to person.

Professor Fullmer is an awesome professor, he's fun and also very passionate about finance, he gives students great advice on real world finance activities. Lectures were great, I really encourage anyone who is taking this class to do what he says and practice the homework problems. Practice daily and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tim is an amazing professor. He made difficult topics easy to understand. Related everything to the real-world, not just textbook answers. Attendance is not mandatory but very his lectures are extremely helpful. Homework was also optional but if you do them all you will do great on exams. Tim was amazing!
Best professor I have ever had.

Awesome professor! He knows what he's talking about and how to teach it. He is really funny, awesome to learn from, and really makes you want to got ot class. Most homework is not mandatory.
He is very opinionated, however, and is constantly dropping biased info on taxes, government, candidates (without naming them but it's obvious) etc.

Tim was great, after taking other finance classes I appreciate his work a lot more. He cares about the lectures he gives and he makes them interesting. He gives students obvious paths to success in which the guidelines are clear and I genuinely learned the material to a very satisfactory degree. Shout out Tim, hella good prof.

LOVE LOVE LOVED this professor. the material of the class itself can be a little tricky especially if you don't come to class but he has the best lectures and is able to explain everything so well! most days we would even get out of the lecture early, plus little hmw, the hmw we did have were identical to the exam, hes awesome!

Great professor! Clear slides and his lectures are entertaining and not brain-numbing. Highly recommend doing the Homework even though it isn't graded. Doing the Homework will help immensely for exams.

Tim Fullmer is the best lecturer I've had at the U, no question. He knows exactly what information is actually useful and matters, and doesn't bother making things extra complicated. He is very clear and good at reading the room to make sure people aren't falling behind. His slides are also so helpful- step by step and shows what goes in calculator
Made class enjoyable and fun. He also is good at explaining the criteria in this class and will answer any and all question thoroughly so you understand.
He is a great professor who teaches exactly what is going to be on exams and always give plenty of materials to  do well on exams.
Do the HWs and you should be fine. He has a 5 for a reason.
Best professor!! His lectures are always clear, straight to the point, and interesting.
Super good teacher, lecture slides are super clear so attendance is definitely not mandatory. Really helpful test review and homework material too.
Professor Fullmer is amazing. He teaches so well and is also very kind & understanding. It is the best of both worlds, and you will not find another professor like him.

Fullmer is an amazing professor! Really cares about his students and shows the material very well. Extremely organized and will provide you with all the material you need to excel in the class. Very funny too! There is a required calculator, I got the more expensive one and it worked great. Doesn't do reviews but has lots of practice homework!

Professor Fullmer teaches finance in a way that everyone can understand, even if you're not majoring in it. He doesn't just read off of slides but provides so much information. He's also a very cool person. He's in a band and has a world record? End of story take this class with him. To study for tests, just do the homeworks.

Tim was by far my favorite professor. His lectures and slides are very clear and concise. Tim was genuine coming to class and definitely knew his material. Doing the "homework" actually prepares you for the exam, and there is no bloat work as I call it. I would continue to take his classes if he offered more!
Tim is the best! He clearly communicates and explains materials. He provides multiple resources and makes it as easy as possible to learn.
Such a great professor!!! I love his class so much!!!

Do the homework (it is not graded) and go to the lectures and you will be fine. He is seriously the best professor I have had. Maybe he just compliments my learning style best but I would not suggest any other professor other than Tim.

If you need to take finance make sure you take it from Tim. Do the homework problems (Not for credit) and you will be ready for the exams. He wants all of his students to succeed and makes the path to an A very clear.

Fullmer was funny and made the topics easy to understand. We only had 3 assignments and 2 exams. The slides were easy to understand so you didn't need to attend if you didn't want to. He also didn't require any textbooks.

Tim's a great guy, but my gosh is he overhyped. It seems students these days only value personality and not actual teaching effectiveness. He prioritized presentation style and charisma more than actually teaching in a way that would have helped us see how it all connects to form a whole. Still a good teacher though, just could've done better.

Fullmer is awesome and very understanding. He does not make attendance mandatory which is great because sometimes you need a break. You do have to pay attention well in class to do great- but he creates homework pages (that you dont need to turn in) so you can practice the problems. If you do the homework, you will do well on the tests.

Professor Fullmer is a passionate teacher who really loves his area of expertise. If you engage and participate in all of his lectures, you will be sure to succeed. He provides optional homeworks and practice quizzes to practice for the exams. Exams are heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tim is the best instructor i've ever had. He was engaging and the class topics were easy to understand if you pay attention in class. He gave homework assignments that aren't part of your grade just personal practice. homework is helpful on exams. If Tim is the instructor for a class, take the class. He is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tim is a great professor who really cares about his students. He is understanding when it comes to the few projects you actually submit in his class. I have taken both BCOR 3020 and FINAN 4070 with him and did well in both classes. While there aren't a lot of assignments that are graded you should do them if you want to succeed.

Fantastic teacher, I definitely recommend him. Your grade is pretty much dependent on tests. He will drop a test if he gets 90% course evaluation participation.  If you want to succeed, do the optional homework for each lesson after the lesson, do not wait until the test.

Tim was an amazing professor and he had a great, engaging way of describing complicated concepts.  He made every new concept simple to understand and kept lectures entertaining and funny.  He has a great personality and I would 10/10 recommend him for anyone regardless of their ability.

Easily a top 3 professor at the U. He's dedicated to students and wants them to succeed. The tests were easy for the most part and he drops the lowest if 90% of the class submits the survey at the end of the year. Never considered finance to be a "fun" class for me but it was. The problem sets and homework are vital to getting a good test grade.

Professor Fullmer is truly an exceptional teacher that cares for his students. I personally wished I had gotten a better grade, but hence Finance. I would strongly encourage you to take this class with him, I can confidently say I would have done far worse with other professors given my terrible math skills.
Professor Fullmer is the best professor I've had at the U. Not necessarily an easy class but he makes it bearable. Tests aren't easy but if you study you will do good. Take him!!

Tim Fullmer is honestly one of the best professors I've ever had.  He was the first class at 9 AM when everyone was tired but his energy, enthusiasm, and humor woke us up and kept us engaged which was awesome. If you have Tim for finance you will learn a ton of useful skills and have a fun experience at the same time.

The best professor at the DESB. I'm so glad I signed up for his finance class, he does a great job explaining all the key concepts and answering any questions. He mainly teaches through lectures but does a fantastic job keeping everyone engaged and has a great sense of humor. 11/10 professor.

TAKE ALL FINANCE CLASSES THROUGH TIM.

Professor Fullmer is an amazing professor. He was always very kind to students and willing to help. His lectures were very entertaining, his tests were very reasonable, and overall workload was not too bad for this class. I would highly recommend Prof. Fullmer!

TIM IS THE BEST FINANCE PROFESSOR! The main reason I took my section of BCOR was to be in his class. He gives you cheat sheets on all exams except for the final, and drops your lowest exam. He truly cares about his students and is always accessible outside of class. Do the homework, study well, and you will be just fine. Also, get the calculator.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He was a great guy who was passionate about what he was teaching. This made the class a lot more enjoyable. I would say that it will be a lot easier if you show up to the lectures and listen in

Tim is legit one of the best professors I've had at the U. Finance lectures at this level are not the most interesting, but his humour and laidback demeanor make them extremely enjoyable. Homework is designed to reflect test questions, though it is not graded, so do the homework and you'll do fine on the tests.

This class has been quite enjoyable thanks to Tim. He just has a great sense of humor and does a good job of incorporating it into his lectures. BE AWARE: if someone calling an inanimate object IT offends you, then don't take this class. Great professor all around and would recommend to anyone.
Insightful guy with a lot of experience. He is funny and makes class a breeze. Nothing notable with class difficulty and would like to take more finance classes in the future.

Fullmer is an absolute unit. This is my second class with him because he is the greatest professor of all time. He is very clear about what is going to be on the exams and his HW/lectures actually correlate. Would highly recommend.

Tim is one of the greatest teachers in the finance department. He connects very well with students and outlines course material in an organized fashion. I've taken two of his courses and wish they had him teaching upper division material. Great dude.

One of the best professors I've had while in college. He was the professor that inspired me to take a leap and declare as a Finance major. This class is HARD but Tim gives you everything you need to succeed. The class is curved at the end which is very helpful. Only 3 tests and one assignment. Highly encourage taking this class from him. 10/10!

Professor Fullmer is such a great professor. He truly cares about his students success. Finance 3040 is a difficult class and requires a decent amount of studying, but he makes the material fairly easy to understand.

Tim is my favorite professor in all four years of college-- he single handedly made me switch to the Finance major. Fantastic at explaining concepts and keeping things interesting, extremely friendly, and so good at lecturing I actually looked forward to
Professor Fullmer was amazing. He teaches this and intro to corporate finance. He makes the material very accessible and understandable. His two classes were two of the most informative I've had.

Tim is by far one of the top 3 professors I have ever had. The class I took was a 3 hour night class and he made the lectures very entertaining and easy to follow which made the 3 hours go by fast. He is willing to help in any way he can to make sure you succeed. Truly an incredible professor. HIGHLY RECOMMEND !!!

Professor Fullmer is one of the best professors at the University. He cares about his students learning what is necessary. He relates the material in the class to current things that are taken place. Just make sure to do the examples or take good notes during the lectures.

The best professor in the entire university. His was the only class where I felt like I could say what I wanted and not worry about being judged by the professor. He is the best example how a university should be ran. Unfortunately, this is the ONLY class that I felt this way. And I just graduated.

BEST finance professor at the U. he understands this class is required for people that aren't finance majors so he makes sure to keep concepts simple and understandable. study the homeworks!! thats all I did for tests and I got an A- or above on everyone. best professor ever

This was a great finance class. I didn't get a very good grade, but that was because we were only graded on a few assignments and then 4 tests and I didn't do very well. The conceptual questions are hard. But the calculations in the class are easy. But, Tim is a chill and great professor and works with students to help your grade. Absolute legend.

Awesome professor, explains material simple and well. Always willing to work with student. All Homework is optional, but necessary. 4 exams (1 dropped with class participation in reviews), 1 ethics paper, 1 extra credit opportunity. If you don't study you will have a hard time but if you do study nightly then you could with effort pull off a B.
Professor Fullmer is awesome! He made finance easy to understand, and lectures concise (not 100 slides long).. He's hilarious too and easily approachable.
This guy is awesome. Does his best to keep his political opinions out of the classroom which I appreciated lol. But he seriously cares about the success of his students and it really shows.

Tim Fullmer is the best teacher I have had. He is funny and his lectures are amazing. He will stay after class and answer any questions. He even did live review sessions before each test and he stayed as long as students wanted him to. The material was hard but not crazy hard but he was so helpful and amazing.

Don't know how Tim doesn't have more feedback. Others have said it and I'll say it again, best professor in the Business School. Genuinely a good guy who cares about your success and makes learning the material interesting. Wish I could take him for all my classes.
Best professor in Business School. You will fall in love with subject when you listen to his lectures.

Tim is the type of professor you always hope to get. He makes learning fun yet applicable. I can honestly tell you that his lectures helped me in my own investments. You will not regret taking this professor.
I'm a senior here at the U and Tim is the best professor I've had all 4 years I've been here. He's the man, super hilarious and a great lecturer.

Amazing and funny professor! He Explains all the material very well and tells you what is directly going to be on the tests and final. He also has optional homework that is very helpful to study for the tests. He cares a lot about the students and will help you with any concepts you are struggling on. I would definitely recommend him!

Garrett knowledgeable about the topics relating to the class. Lots of different books to read. All available on Canvas, but lots of sources can become overwhelming. Prof. Garrett did go on side tangents a lot, if you are looking for a class that is lecture heavy and slides this class is not for you. all discussion based and there were no slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures themselves do not have a lot of value, as Prof. Garrett tends to go on tangents especially during discussion and I at least did not gain a whole lot from those tangents/discussions. Discussion also takes up the majority of class and sometimes goes very off track, so the difficult readings assigned for homework are barely brushed over.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Garrett is a super fun professor. His lectures are incredibly interesting, he does like to go on tangents, but overall they are helpful in understanding the materials. There are readings assigned to every lecture that are required. The homework (quizzes and discussions) is easy if you do the readings, and the essays have interesting prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Once again, Gannet has exceeded my expectafions. She is accommodating on all fronts and WANTS to help you excel in her classes. She has changed my perspective about just trying to get a good grade and instead working on learning something new and becoming an expert in the topics she teaches. 1000/10.

Gannet has once again exceeded my expectations. She is truly one of the most wonderful and helpful professor's I've had the opportunity to work with. She cares more about you learning something more than your grade. You will not regret taking any of her classes. 100/10.

Gannet was the first ever professor that provided me long-term insight and helped me get my foundations in atmospheric science well-adjusted. I appreciated the hands on activities in class, being a learner that relies on experience. Lectures were well structured and planned. She also always provided information on out of class EC opportunities.

Professor Hallar explains climate science well, but grading is bad Extra credit in Canvas can lower your grade as it is set up incorrectly, and final grades used a +/- scale not in the syllabus that was inconsistent with what was known throughout the semester. My Concerns were dismissed, and my grade was not adjusted. Track grades carefully.

One of the most kind-hearted professors with a very easy and interesting class to learn from. She explains everything clearly, is highly engaging, and eager to get to know every student. However, she includes small group work in every lecture, so be cautious if that's not your preference.

The online aspect of the class was a little awkward. I think Professor Haller would be great teaching an in person course. Despite the fact the class was online, she made an effort to show us some of the meteorology equipment in person.

I loved Professor Mogensen. You can tell he's incredibly passionate about excel and regularly gave out rewards for participation. He often shares real-world examples that helped me understand how the concepts taught may be applied. The assignments were very doable. 10/10, a great guy, I would love to take a class from him again.

Garrett was a really good professor. His class is big on excel and he is very good at explaining how to do all the steps. He has office hours every week and he replies to you on canvas inbox. I think the bad scores about him were just because he was new and unsure of what to do, so you can discredit them. He also gives lots of extra credit

He was a great teacher even though the content of the class wasn't the most exciting. There's a lot of homework but it's not too bad and he walks through 1 assignment a week so you know how to do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He was very respectful towards students and gave out treats during class. Assignments were very easy and you could always ask him for help

Walked us through every in class lab step by step. HW was very similar to class work. He would grade labs/HW before the due date often giving you a chance to resubmit and get full credit. His quizzes were open book/note and all the info was right there. Very easy A and he is very caring and helpful.

Honesty, Garrett was a breath of fresh air compared to the usual dry, lecture-heavy professors. He was personable and made the class entertaining. There was a good balance of lecture and hands-on practice. He knows what he's talking about and is willing to work with you. Gave out hi-chews, donuts, and gift cards regularly for participation.
He is okay, incredibly boring lectures and activities. He would run through the weekly projects with us which was nice to understand what we were doing.

Prof. Mogensen was different from a typical professor but did a good job overall. Lectures weren't always great, but he's kind and willing to work with you. There's a lot of time consuming homework, but exams are multiple choice. Attendance isn't mandatory, though weekly in-class quizzes require a access code.
He was an interesting man, very frazzled in his lectures. He didn't seem to know what he was doing and always had a problem in his life he would be talking about.

Not the greatest explainer but an easy A. He assigns a lot of time-consuming homework but it is manageable. I highly recommend buying Wayne Jenson's subscription on YouTube. It's $5 a month but extremely worth it. His videos explained any confusion I had with assignments substantially better than trying to email the professor or TA my questions.

Profe Grisel is awesome! She genuinely cares for students and gives helpful insight. I was nervous going into this class having not taken Spanish in 2 years, but it very accessible and she gives you a lot of grace! My one complaint is the homework can be quite overwhelming, but if you manage your time well this class is very manageable.

This class was fine. Ms. Galvez crammed a lot of material into a short amount of time. A lot of the homework felt like busywork that was redundant of content, but not in a practice the language way. Group projects and individual presentations always felt rushed and like they were thrown on the students last minute. Overall easy class though.

Super chill and kind teacher that likes teaching her class. You could always talk to her about any of the assignments and she would be very helpful. Good amount of homework but it was fairly easy, so just show up and you'll be all good. There was also two presentations in the semester but they were pretty lowkey.

The class overall was not difficult. The professor is very kind, and is always willing to help if you need more clarification. As long as you put in effort and come to class, you should be able to pass the class easily. I would highly recommend any of her classes!

Good, relatively easy course.  Straight forward assignments due every week with an eBook to help.  Grisel definitely cares about her students and wants to see everyone succeed.  It is very important that you attend classes because if you miss one day you'll be very confused.  Overall this was a good class and I recommend it.

Grisel is a great professor, so nice and helpful! I am taking her again next year for 2010. You can tell she really cares and wants you to do well. We used an oline textbook and did lots of partner discussions and activities. Great class!
Tests are very difficult and are graded harshly.

Jamie Gagnon has good lectures and I thought he explained topics very clearly, leaving out the "fluff" that we wouldn't be tested on. This course had tough homework assignments and heavy grading. Attendance isn't mandatory though I found it helpful to attend and participate.
Lectures were dry and uninteresting. Just read the textbook and lecture slides to pass. Tests had pretty brutal questioning and were all-or-nothing so pray for your strengths.

His portion of class was better, it was better engaged and explained things in different ways for understanding. I enjoyed his lectures more, and felt better at approaching him. I do think tests were okay, nothing too bad but I would focus on main ideas. He's knowledgeable and has interesting lectures. But it also wasn't the best...

He cares for his students and wants you to succeed. He always made lecture interesting and engaging. Better than Julie. His lectures tend to go quick which is good so ur not bored and forces you to keep up. Explains the concepts straight to the point and tells you what you need to know for exams. Super chill guy, fav prof.

Many people here have mentioned how James talks a lot about his research. It's true, and it can be quite distracting from what we're learning. Just look at the ELO bullet points and you'll be fine. He says he only tests you on general ideas, but beware, there are a couple questions on exams on examples used in class. He's a passionate professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Jamie's class! He makes every lecture fun and engaging, even if the content isn't inherently so. His exams are difficult, but if you study and pay attention in class, all of the exam questions are straightforward. He genuinely cares about his students and doesn't take too much time talking about his research. Highly recommend!

He is a good professor. Half the class is taught by him and the other half by Julie. Compared to her, he is good at explaining things and makes the lectures more interesting. He just has that enthusiasm in his voice. Overall the class is definitely hard and you have to put in the work with the readings and lectures/problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gagnon was a super nice and charismatic guy! His lectures actually helped me decide I wanted to study cellular & molecular biology for my undergrad. He gives lectures in a storytelling format which makes them engaging (for me at least). If I had tried harder, I would have gotten at least an A-. Definitely worth it! I loved his class!

James' expectations are unrealistic. Tests are absurdly hard. Everyone in the class is struggling and they are completely useless in helping. One of the worst professors I have had. He rants about his research and tests us on his research like we are supposed to know exactly what his research lab is doing. Do not take it with James if it is online.

There are profs that have grace and understanding during a pandemic, then there are profs like this. When online they removed extra credit (offered in person), made the tests depend entirely on test-taking ability and not content knowledge, and gave multiple uncaring responses to students pleas for help, if they would even respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor has gained a lot of fame in the past since the biology department is rough. However he is not what he cracks up to be, his recorded lectures are full of useless tangents and discussions about his lab work. Contacting him is also a joy, I have sent 5 emails and gotten zero responses. Maybe he is better in person but online is not good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing cell bio prof! He is great at explaining material and does not waste a moment on making students memorize extraneous material or every single mechanism in cellular biology. Students acquire a concrete understanding of cell bio in an atmosphere that is conducive of success. 10/10!

Jamie is great, you can tell he is very knowledgable in cell bio. The only small complaint I would have is that he tends to read directly off Powerpoint slides, which is fine, it just makes an hour-long lecture drag sometimes. Overall the class isn't too tough, just make sure you understand the ELOs and you'll be set for the exams.

One of the most understanding professors I've had. He's very cooperative and cares for his students. The class is very clear and I'd recommend everyone to take it with him and Julie. You will have a lot of leeway for getting a desired grade. Study the lectures and use the book for the HW and you're all set!

I loved cell biology from Gagnon and Hollien! The lectures were comprehensive and easy to digest. The professors made them interesting by bringing up relevant research that they were doing as well as what was going on at the U at that time. The homework/tests aren't too bad, but get ready to read and study quite a bit for them. Very caring profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking this class, it was co-taught and Jamie definitely was the better lecturer by far. He was really passionate about what he taught and he tried to make sure the topics were conveyed so they were fully understood. He care about the students learning and loving the material more than he cares about grades, so his exams are very fair.

This class was co-taught but I really preferred Jamie's lectures. I was really afraid of cell bio but Jamie was a great professor and the tests were fair and not ridiculously difficult. If you're taking cell bio you have to take it from Jamie.

I absolutely loved James and Julie's Cell Biology class. They taught the core concepts, and really helped avoid the onslaught of meaningless memorization. They supplemented all they teaching with realworld experiments and really helped enforce what is important for cell bio. Their tests are not to hard assuming you paid attention in class. Loved it

James is an awesome professor! He and Julie Holien co-taught Cell Biology, but I have to say I preferred James' lectures. They were clear, to the point, and very informational. I took this course in the past and didn't pass (obviously), but I'm glad that they restructured the everything from scratch. I actually was able to retain the information!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots of homework with unclear/complicated instructions.

Everything is so fast paced, and if English is your second language, good luck understanding what he's saying in his videos. He always chooses awful examples and can't teach to save his life. His exam is incredibly long, repetitive and inefficient. Overall terrible experience with him as a professor.
Mac is amazing professor that only wants students to succeed! He knows what he's talking about and you can tell he cares about the class. 100% recommend

Mac essentially expected us to self-teach the material, as all assignments were due BEFORE he would lecture on the subject. This was incredibly frustrating and made the class much much hard than it needed to be. He would send us into breakout rooms during online lecture, and we literally wouldn't even try the problem because we had no idea how to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The guy is a certified chiller. His lectures are easy to follow. Huge chatterbox though - expect stories and sidetracking. Attendance is graded, but not super harshly. The best encouragement to come to class is the Fintech News every day where students share finance and technology news which is cool. Downside is you can't see your grade in canvas

I really enjoyed learning from Gene. He would tell you what to expect on the exam. He would tell you which topics to study for the most. Really funny guy, and I looked forward to going to his class. To get an A, actually attend class and do the BMC course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: when the classroom was on fire he saved me from the burning building and I truly would be dead without without him. Without gene my days would be dark and he is the light that everyone needs.

His lectures were basically shortened versions of the textbook readings, which were disgustingly long and boring. The course was graded on 4 exams but he dropped one, and you could get extra credit by getting a BMC certification. The double-sided note sheets for exams are responsible for my success in this class. Great guy, not the best teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Levinzon is funny and nice, but the class is harder than expected. Lectures are only PowerPoints, and your entire grade comes from exams and attendance—no homework or quizzes. You get one note sheet for each exam, which helps a lot. Overall, the class requires consistent attendance and solid exam prep to pass if you miss class a lot, I'd pass
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing guy! He genuinely cares and has a dad joke for any moment. Reason I survived the semester he's like taking a class with your dad. Makes the material manageable and gives a lot of feedback. He's very transparent. It's very lecture-heavy but still manages to make if fun if you pay attention! Be a good student and he will be a good professor.
