It's definitely a hard class, and you would have to work hard for it but I think it's worth. I am an international student and I was able to get an A so I am pretty sure everyone could get an A

Awesome professor. Lectures really. She keeps things pretty humorous, and is always in a good mood. Absolutely hope to get her in the future-- only reservation is that you have to buy a book she wrote if you want to hope to pass the long essays.

Worst class I have ever taken. Her online class for hist 1100 is practically impossible to ACE! She grades as if this were a 5000 level course! My 5000 level classes are much easier than this. The book is useless, her power points don't have any information on them. I DO NOT RECOMMEND TAKING THIS ONLINE!

By far my favorite class. Professor Smoak makes learning enjoyable and she tries to connect with each of her students. She is a professor who genuinely cares about her students' success. If you attend class regularly you should be able to get a good grade. Super understanding and fun.

Dr. Smoak is one of the greatest teachers. She makes learning enjoyable, the only reason you wouldn't like her teaching style is you have no hunger for learning. She is laid back and will help you out if you are genuinely looking for her help. One of the best professors and teachers I've had. Both her lower level and higher level courses are great!

Working with Dr. Smoak is a joy! She has an undeniable passion for her subject and it shines through in her very engaging teaching style. She can pack a class session with a diverse range of topics and tie it all into the day's lesson. Reading literature isn't my favorite, but her historical focus keeps me very interested.

Smoak's class is always a pleasure. She has the uncanny ability to let the discussion wander yet can always relate it back to the subject at hand. If history is not generally your bag, take her class, she makes it entertaining while still being informative. Note, there will be a fair amount of reading.

To recieve a good grade in the class, attendance is mandatory but I did not mind at all because Smoak is an amazing professor. Loves her subject matter and will make you love it too. Be sure to attend the test review, doing so will benefit you a lot. I recommend professor Smoak wholeheartedly.
A really cool teacher and very helpful too!

Does not speak to the class like a room of adults, but rather toddlers who are incapable of their own ideas. Doesn't respond to email either. Talks about her own political opinions (i.e. hatred of Trump) constantly w/out connecting ideas to class. Questions are confusing and unanswerable 90% of the time. She is passionate about the subject tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: While passionate about what she teaches, I still don't exactly know what we were supposed to learn. There aren't any tests and lectures are very high-level about humanities. The assignments were a nightmare- redundant, vague and didn't connect with class content. Her discussions consists of long-winded and vague questions. Canvas was unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really sweet professor, but a bit all over the place. Reading paragraphs were pointless and redundant each class. Her questions are either phrased like a statement or very longwinded and nobody knows what she is asking. Big semester-long group project that felt like busy work as well, I don't feel like I learned from it. Feels like kindergarten...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Wachter was very understanding anytime I had missed class or an assignment. She does do popcorn participation, but it's not a problem if you don't know the answer. She truly is the sweetest teacher and only wants to see her students succeed!

She gives a lot of extra credit activities at the end of semester, which did save my grade. Her classes are about discussions and presentation. Make sure you keep 100% focus and take notes. The questions on exams are kind of unexpected. Anyway, for the BUS 1050 class, I believe she is much better than the other professor. At least, you would pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a lovely professor that is willing to help. My issue is that midterms and assignments are subjective. If you answer the question without showing critical think which is hard to measure, you will receive a low grade. This is one the most boring class you will have to take.Instead of attending class, students would rather forfeit their grade.

Professor Gibby-Wachter is a very nice lady but her class is such a waste of time.  She teaches outdated information that is completely useless to present day matters.  It is a requirement to be a business major which is so stupid since this class is utterly useless.  It is a relatively easy class, just painfully boring.

A very easy but exhausting class. She is super nice but her instructions on assignments are not very clear and she takes a while to respond to emails. Canvas is also very unorganized. There is a lot of opportunity for extra credit but as long as you do your work decently you should get an A. You keep track of your own attendance and participation.

I would highly suggest not taking this class. I rarely went to class, but when I did, the lectures were very dumb and I learned nothing. Though I received an A, I had to get a lot of help from my fellow classmates to know what was going on. Her Canvas is highly unorganized and non helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's super nice and understanding. She insists every class on heavy student participation. She calls on one student and then tells that student to call on another student, and so forth. So much class time is wasted doing this because almost every other kid called on doesn't know what's happening. She doesn't spend enough time lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind and tries to make lectures fun, but also makes students participate by calling on each other. Homework is only a few written responses per week, but requires a lot of reading. Exams weigh pretty heavily, and you are only allowed 1 sheet of hand-written notes to use. Was she awful? No. Would I take from her again? No.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to these awful reviews. The whole class is based on popular articles about important topics. Read the articles, talk about them, test on them. She invited all of her students to her house for thanksgiving! She isn't trying to fail anyone, some of these students don't know to self-regulate their coursework and she is laid back.

Not lots of homework which is very nice. lectures are very boring and she calls on students to call on each other which is not ideal. Your grade is almost entirely based on exams which are questions she writes herself and are hard to understand. So much reading and I find it one of my hardest classes even though it is a 1000 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am happy I chose her. She's really understanding and responsive. Online but she does zoom lectures optional. Love the material she chooses to teach, easy to pass exams (open book) sheesh. If you're looking for a low homework class- I suggest elsewhere and good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Second worst class ive taken. Not only is the class itself a drag and there is a ton of reading, lectures are so long and boring and she has students call on one another for participation. She writes her own tests so questions and answers are hard to understand and do not make sense and she also puts material not talked about in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to read an entire textbook. She also calls on people to call on others and I hate that. She expects you to know the answers to all the questions BEFORE she teaches concepts. The tests are a joke.

It's an easy A, but the course in general felt like a waste of time and money. Spent every class talking about student opinions and did redundant 2-paragraph reading responses before every class. Has several group projects, so a good/bad group could make or break your experience. Professor is very unorganized and not great at responding to emails.

Kristina was great when it came to lecturing however she and her ta's didn't really seem to understand how to do the whole zoom thing. She made it clear that she really cared about her students and made it clear that she was well educated in her field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's a very kind, welcoming professor. She is very flexible, understanding, and wants you to succeed. She is very inclusive and wants students to challenge thoughts and ideas that arise. However, some of the assignments were unclear and she took a while to respond to emails. Sometimes she would disregard half the things students said. Not too hard

There's a 2-3 paragraph reading responses due before class, but the readings aren't long and you can usually write a response by skimming the text. There's a midterm, 2 papers and a group project which is considered the final. She allows rewrites on everything and a full page cheat sheet for the midterm (easy grader - just answer every question).

Kristina is a very caring professor. She loves to have in class discussions. There are short reading assignments due at the beginning of each class. Her tests and papers are graded on completion, so its easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a super nice person but she is not a very good teacher. She is very unorganized and she spent most of the class asking students discussion questions that were very unclear. It is an easy A but I do not believe she should be a professor at the U. I did not gain much of anything from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Undoubtedly she is a nice person, but she is a terribly unorganized professor. The lectures feel aimless and always leave me asking what the point of it was. Projects and assignments at times felt vague and barely related to what we "learned." It's unfortunate because I was really looking forward to gaining valuable insight about the subject.

I really loved this class! Some of the readings are hard to understand, but she goes over them during class to help you understand it better. You are only required to do 15 reading responses out of the total readings. She has test reviews that are incredibly helpful and really cares that you receive a good grade! This is an easier Bus 1050 class.
You can tell Kristina really cares about her students. No textbook but lots of readings which is the basis for the concepts she goes over. Would take again, most students did very well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Caring

reviews.comment: No organization to class. nice lady but not good teacher. She is also so PC it is sickening.

She doesn't really follow the syllabus so lectures are extremely unorganized. In class you never cover what the homework or readings are about, so this class is a waste of time. You also don't learn much.

She is an extremely unorganized professor. During most of her lectures, she has us "discuss" for about 30 minutes and no one really knows what we're supposed to be discussing. When she does lecture, its neither here nor there, and she struggles to put a coherent through together. The class was really easy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kristy is a great teacher. Class is super easy. But there is reading responses due every class period, and these readings can sometimes be long. Class is very much so an open discussion. Don't be afraid to give your opinion. No book required. All readings are online. Have papers due occasionally, very tough grader on these. But you can re write.

No textbook. Uses online course articles and excerpts, but can be a lot to read occasionally. Very flexible with your schedule if you have issues come up. If you're good at English classes then you'll be fine. If you also have an opinion and aren't afraid to share it you'll pass with colors. This class requires invested learning and application.
Good Instructor, very reasonable and knowledgable. Engages in critical thinking.

I found her to be a very nice person to chat with, but just not my top choice as a professor. BUS 3900 felt very scattered and discussions were too "touchy-feely." It often felt like a waste of time. She encouraged us to speak our minds and share our opinions, but constantly pushed political correctness.

This is the absolute WORST professor I've ever had. She is unorganized and her lectures have zero relevance to the homework she assigns.  She is consistently 10 minutes late to every class. Only good thing about the class is that it was easy.

Glenn is a solid professor, he is very knowledgeable about sales. We read 2 books and had quizzes on them after each section we read. We had 2 presentations, and 1 midterm which he was more harsh on, although the grades turned out fine. Participation isn't mandatory, so doing well on the quizzes and presentations is encouraged.

Glenn Seninger is by far one of my favorite professors at the U. I've taken his class previously, MKTG 4720, and both had a great experience. His lectures are engaging, and has a set story you follow throughout the semester as a sales rep. Group presentations are well organized and help you prepare if you decide to go into the sales world.

Glenn Seninger is BY FAR the best professor that I have had at the University of Utah. I am in 2 classes with him, and every week I am excited to see what he has in store. He has been an incredible resource in my job search and it is clear how much he cares about his job/students. It has been a privilege to learn from and be mentored by him!

Glenn is very knowledgeable in sales, and you definitely get to see it throughout his lectures. The quizzes and midterm were easy, and there were two group presentations that demonstrated real sales and marketing skills. His instructions on each project were vague, but overall I found this class to be engaging and valuable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Seninger has tons of sales experience and certainly knows what he's talking about. Group projects were very applicable to real life and extremely doable, but I hated how this course had very little structure. He is extremely vague with guidelines and not very understanding. I would not take him again because it was just not enjoyable

Class was easy, lectures were fine. Midterm was easy but very unorganized format. showed lack of effort. Not professional. There needs to be a rubric or something for the final project- is kinda sprung on you, and then you present and are critiqued in front of the class when you had like five bullet points to go off of.

Seniger is a great professor, but I felt the class lacked substance. Most of it was spent reading books, with a graded group project at the end. It felt disorganized and unfulfilling. While it was an easy A, I wished for more meaningful learning experiences throughout the semester. More learning opportunities early on would be worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Seninger cares about his students, he is always willing to clarify directions or help with things outside of class such as resumes and interview prep. Midterm is the same as all the quizzes which are super easy. Final grade is a big group project and mock sales pitch which can be kind of confusing. Overall I learned so much about sales.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: high expectations with little guidance

Loved the class, very real talk, engaging lectures. Professor has tons of real world application to the teachings. His testing isnt hard but he does expect you to show up to class and have a conversation which was cool. His midterm was a collection of all past tests so.. if you studied the material for the previous test the midterm was quite easy.

Professor Seninger told us we would get our money's worth with his class, however I feel quite the opposite. The class has almost entirely consisted of reading two books. The midterm is just recycled questions from those books. As I study for the midterm, I am just memorizing random percents from the books and learning about parenting styles.

Seninger is a great professor! He values his students and gives them real-world connections through guest speakers. He's funny and fairly engaging. Midterm was super late and consisted of a written test & presentation. The midterm presentation was sprung on us pretty quickly, but he usually gives class time to meet with your groups and prepare.

Glenn was great! While I thought his method of teaching sales was unconventional (through role play and scenarios) it was very engaging and I learned a lot. Quizzes and midterm were easy if you read (midterm was just the quiz questions) and the final presentations were straightforward and easy to complete. You can tell glenn care about his class!

This is a dificult class and difficult material. I enjoyed it and felt it was taught well. The exams are hard and it requires a lot of studying. He is very passionate about what he does. I would recommend Glen if you are interested in OSC, but if you are not, you will not enjoy the class.
Very test-heavy class. If you're not into OSC his class is boring but you can tell he's really enthusiastic about what he teaches. Very nice guy.

Professor Schmidt is a very knowledgeable OSC professor. His class concepts will challenge your thinking, but he is very patient and kind so ask him or his TA for help if you're struggling. Take his courses- you will learn a lot!

A very solid professor for OSC, he definitely knows what he's talking about and understands the theories very well. He also runs simulations and programs in class (these are done for credit), which solidified my understanding of the subject matter; overall, a solid class where you can expect to learn a lot.

I really enjoyed taking OSC 5100 with professor Schmidt. He was very knowledgable on the topics. Although some of the simulations were challenging, they were important and a good taste of what a real life warehouse would be like. I appreciated the help and feedback he would give me. If you need to take this class, get it with professor Schmidt.

Dr. Schmidt is very knowledgable in the field of Operations and Supply Chain and you can see his passion for the subject while he teaches. I had never taken an operations and supply chain class before this, but I really enjoyed the subject and class and it changed my perspective on what I want to do in the future. Overall great class and professor!

Glen Schmidt is a great professor. OIS 5100 is a difficult course, but it was split into modules with readings (short) and videos (short). The videos with Prof. Schmidt and Bo were informative and helpful. Although sometimes I needed to watch them more than once to understand.

Professor Schmidt is amazing, the same as his TA Syd. They're so patient and nice, always open, and welcome you to ask questions. However, it was a little bit unreasonable for the grade. Two tests are 50% of your grade, but you have two chances for each of them. 
This class is really hard, need to work a lot. If you want something easy, avoid it.

2 exams that are 50% of your grade. Lectures are horrible and the example problems are barely similar to the ones on homeworks. Exams aren't THAT hard if your study good but this class was probably the worst class I've taken so far at the U. Be prepared to teach yourself over 80% of the material as he does the absolute bare minimum in explanations.

Took this as an online course and liked the way he structured it. There is a lot of material to cover and his videos really do help. Not an easy class and there does need to be effort if you want to do good
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Personally, there was too much work and I had too many questions to be successful and to fully pay attention in this class. It's also taught by the assistant, not Prof Schmidt so that was a bit frustrating. A lot of assignments so be sure to stay on top of it and use resources like office hours.
He make you pay extra for assignment called "little field". Wasting $24 after paying crazy amount of money for your tuition!
I liked this class! It is online so you do need to take your time to read and actually learn. I feel like the tests are easy if you take the time to go through practice exams.

I like Glen as a person but he's pretty obnoxious in a pedagogical sense. He's so disoriented in his teaching and completely misunderstands the whole idea of learning things. The only way to get by in this course is by memorizing Glen ways of thinking and hope you aren't running on an obsolete version of Glen by the time the next exam rolls around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Glen is a nice guy, never seen him be rude before like previous reviews stated. But just because he's a nice guy doesn't mean he's a good teacher. Glen's problem is that he thinks we're all OSC experts so he lectures that way. He just ends up confusing everyone even more and you're better off teaching yourself or going to the TA.

I quite literally wanted to die every single class I had with him. He regularly mumbles through lectures and I pretty much just has to teach myself the content along with the TA office hours being the only worthwhile use of my time to learn the material. Would highly suggest taking another teacher for this course if you can.

As a person he is fine. He is incredibly smart which makes it tough to understand what he is talking about. Lectures were kind of a waste of time because he only went over why people bombed the quizzes. Relied on his self-written textbook for us to read and I never wanted to gut my eyeballs out with a spoon more than I did reading that book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Trash, completely disorganized canvas page you have to stumble through to find anything. Lectures that make no sense with stupid random additions of "the lovely professor" and the "lovely assistant" to waist more of my time. This was an online class and I have never loathed someone more that I have never met.

He has his own textbook so good luck trying to go online looking for help for this class. He also tries to make his quizzes "conceptual" which resulted in difficult quizzes and mistakes as others have mentioned. Sometimes he messed up questions and had to be told to correct our grades. Most people did not do great on his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He has his own textbook so good luck trying to go online looking for help for this class. Most people did not do great on his exams.

Prof. Schmidt is the one of the greatest professors that I have had the pleasure of taking a class from at the U. He is a great guy, and gives amazing lessons that teach the concepts well. You won't regret taking his class. He gives you all the tools you need to succeed in the class. He's just truly an inspiration man.
Glen Schmidt makes sure you know he went and worked at Stanford.  Big Glen covers boring materials in a boring fashion.  OSC has a 100% hire rate out of college because nobody finds it interesting.

Glen is a very smart guy, which is largely the issue with this entry level BCOR class we were required to take regardless of our major. In class, he would almost insult people for answering wrongly or answering in what he might think to be a stupid way. Over time, the class became silent when a question would be asked as we didn't want to be wrong.

I have never in my life had a teacher that actively makes learning harder. During the lectures he argues with the students for half the class waiting for us to say something correctly. in addition you can't even trust every quiz question since we had to convince him to give us points when he would write the questions wrong. horrible mandatory class

In a word, awful. He doesn't teach anything during class and expects you to teach yourself the entire course via old academic papers that he wrote himself. If you're ever confused on something you can't simply look it up for clarification because he wrote all the texts and uses terms that he's made up. Everyone in the class was lost all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but he's just not good at teaching the class subject and expects us to learn from many papers through the canvas, which also is not always helpful. This class is crazy hard for me and it seems like he teaches us like we know the subject when this is just an introductory class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Glen knows what he is talking about. Sometimes he goes fast in lectures because there is a lot to cover. If you have questions, then he will stay after class until the students understand. I would take this class again in a higher course. It was n't his fault that the Business School gave him so much to go over.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Although this class was an intro to OSC principles, it was hard. You do get cheat sheets for exams but mainly study by doing the weekly quizzes, the questions are very similar. I felt like Glen explained concepts in a way more complicated way than needed. But he does curve your exam at the end which is nice. Good guy, just not the best professor.

Glen is a really good guy that wants to see people succeed. However, hes not the best when it comes to actually teaching. He gives assignments for each topic prior to teaching it. Then later skims over it and then quizzes you on it. I get the strategy. He just doesnt do well preparing you for the quizzes. Over, good guy. Could be a better teacher

Glen let me take an exam a month after it was due since I was sick idk any professors that would do that tbh. He was always happy to meet after and outside of class to help, and if you ask for feedback on ur paper he's helpful with that too. I recommend the TA sessions and going over the quizzes (as the exams had virtually the same questions).

Glen seems like a really nice guy and he knows his stuff. The issue is that he thinks all of us know our stuff too when in reality, its an intro class and most of us havent learned anything about OSC. I attended class every day and still got so lost on the material given in quizzes and exams. He isnt good at answering questions, so beware of that.

professor Schmidt is a very knowledgeable professor who knows what he is talking about. The only problem with this is it can be hard to understand his lectures. He teaches at IVY league schools around the world to graduate students so he is used to teaching way above an undergraduate level. Utilize TA office hours, and you will be fine.

For me, Glen made the topic very confusing, but at the end of the semester, he curved our exams to help us out. I would say that you should only take him if you understand OSC, if you do not, then good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Does not give good lectures, doesnt teach the actual topics.

Terrible teacher. The way the class is run sets you up for failure. Doesnt really teach anything in class and expects you to learn everything on your own. Expects you to know the material coming in to the class. Most people in my class were as confused as I am. Do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Me and several of my peers have no idea what's going on. He talks about not relevant things and doesn't explains things in the supplemental videos we are required to watch. He starts off okay through the first test but through the second he goes off the deep end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are THE driest things ever. He goes on in a monotone voice that makes me want to rip my head off. His quizzes are really hard. His slides are jam packed with information and zero context or reasonable explanations. He goes off into details that are so unnecessary for this class (BCOR 3050). Horrible professor. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Just wished the concepts were taught and not hidden in 17 page articles. I felt as if this courses curriculum was modeled off of Where's Waldo, except the teacher can turn Waldo invisible just before you find him. When you sign up for a course with a teacher you usually expect them to give you some sort of guidance otherwise why have a teacher?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very Confusing

Very little teaching actually occurs in this class. You watch very brief videos (avg length is probably 5 min) from his "lovely assistant". And that's it. The rest is yours to figure out on your own. He instructions usually consist of "draw a picture". I passed solely because I repeatedly rewatched the sporadic reviews he hosted.

Be ready to feel like you got thrown into the deep end at the beginning of this class. Glen's teaching style can be disorganized and confusing at times. However, as you begin to settle in you realize that he is an expert in OM. Difficult class, but he's fair on grading and listens to student feedback. Follow his advice on HW to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Worst class I have taken so far at the DESB. HW and assignments are on quizlet but you do not learn anything from it. So that leaves you in a panic for the Exams which are not at all like the HW. He just teaches everything in the most convoluted, confusing ways. He says he doesnt like teach to students shortcuts and secrets to the equations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WORST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN. So unorganized, the actual professor that teaches the class lives in the Netherlands. You will learn nothing and the videos teach you nothing. Don't waste your time and save your GPA by taking it in person with another professor.

This is the most convoluted, nonsensical, unnecessarily difficult, total-waste-of-money course I have ever taken. I understood nothing from this course. The simulations are awful. The professors (there are two, Bo Van Der Rhee is the other one who does all the work) explain things in a way that makes no sense. AVOID AVOID AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is the worst class I have taken in college so far. Glen is the teacher but his "lovely" assistant Bo runs the whole class. The class is terrible. Yes, most the homework and quizzes are online but the test are not found on quizzlet, so you have to learn the material and it is hard. The simulations are terrible also.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Inspirational teacher - very knowledgeable and responds well to students who are eager to learn.

Great professor! He won't let you get away by simply regurgitating facts - he wants you to learn actively, which means you will get to solve some problems and cases, but I would say he's amazing professor. This was by far my favorite class. (If you struggle in his class think of it little bit as a math class - practice problems before test).

If you want an A, expect to put in a solid 10 hours a week for this guys class. He has no regard that you have other classes or a job. The class is super difficult as it is and they have you focus on so many pointless things that its super hard to find time to study for the core subjects of the class. Extremely smart professor, but terrible style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Currently taking an online class from glen and his sidekick bo. This class is extremely difficult to understand and glen expects at least 10 hours of studying each week, and he means it. The homework is very easy to guess and get the right answer, this does not help you on the tests. I would recommend taking this class from an easier teacher.......
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are really hard to follow, it's like he can't tell when the students don't know what's going on. It should be obvious when he asks a question and only gets blank stares and silence. The tests feel like curveballs with their unfamiliar terminology. He's a smart guy, although he really seems unaware of student comprehension until finals
Easy-going but not very clear on the class goals. Most of the class was clueless as to what is happening until the last week.
Is not incredibly helpful or understanding of the class's concerns

Glen uses the Socratic method very effectively in his teaching to encourage discussion from the class and to encourage students to think critically.  Very effective professor and certainly among the best at DESB.  I took every class he taught.
Sadly, another classic case of boomer entitlement, steer clear of the guy

The man is clearly  knowledgeable on his subject, not taking that away from him, but he also very obviously has some sort of major social disorder that just keeps him from teaching in any kind of effective way, and what's worse he doesn't seem to know or care, nor does he want to change his behavior.  It's always everyone else's fault never his.

reviews.comment: Just a sad sad little man, hopes he finds what he's missing in his soul one day
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Impossible to work with.  To be fair I do think there is some kind of social disability going on here so it's not completely his fault, but it still affects the students.  Instructions are NEVER clear or complete, he wants you to read his mind.  He gets weirdly offended and shuts down if you don't fully agree with him, just weird

The exact kind of professor you want to avoid.  Extremely unclear instructions on assignments, the canvas page is set up like he's never used a computer before, and he seems to be more concerned with doing this weird flexing towards his students then actually teaching.  Weird sad guy honestly, not worth the headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Steer clear at all costs, immature and entitled. Instructions for assignments are split between the actual assignment, the syllabus, and several announcements that WILL come because he forgot what he wanted in the assignment.  Missed any of this? That's not his fault, it's always yours, and don't think you'll be allowed to redo and resubmit.
I've never seen a grown man so concerned with making college students think he's cool, pretty sad honestly

Dude knows a lot about this topic and is very straight to the point and doesn't waste time. You will have to read a lot. If you enjoy law and econ you'll like the class. If you ask him for a grading breakdown he'll give it to you in office hours. In your exams you need to use math to explain the concept and use a case from the textbook.

Mark clearly knows the subject matter, but I did not find this class/his lectures engaging (though I think a lot of that is due to the topic itself). As long as you do most (or all) of the reading and follow his instructions exactly, you can do well in his class. I would not have taken this class if it hadn't been required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark is a great guy. As long as you put in effort to learn week by week, you'll do just fine. Online can be tough for a lot of people, but he is very responsive if you have questions or concerns. If you bring in content from the weekly readings into the exams, you'll get As on every one so long as you're a quality writer. Overall, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tests are easy, if you pay attention in lecture, you'll be fine. However, my main takeaway: this guy wants you to read his mind. An impossible task, especially in a toxic environment like his classroom. I wish he left space for other students' insight and opinions but he's clearly afraid of being "wrong".

Professor Glick's class for Marx is relatively easy assignment wise. Light assignments makes the class do-able. The tests are genuinely hard, as he grades harshly as well. The material is difficult to grasp, he assigns graduate level readings and expect you to know the every inch of the material for exams. He doesn't like to offer feedback also.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really interesting class if you like law. He's a somewhat dry lecturer but gets straight to the point. Discussions were easy and honestly so were the two papers. I found that as long as you answered the main point and then added a few buzzwords that were somewhat related he graded pretty fairly. You definitely have to write them in a specific way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class in its online format. Prof. Glick is definitely a great guy and is extremely knowledgeable in the content that he is teaching. His lectures are pretty straightforward and tend to only run about 30 mins, but can feel pretty dry sometimes. Class has weekly discussions with a midterm and final that are essay based and known beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Mark is a good lecturer and you learn a lot. However, he openly admits on class announcements that he was looking for specific answers in essays. He does not give feedback, and his course organization is basically trash. If you can take classes from someone else do, it. Sick of wasting time with professors who want their minds to be read.

He is awesome. Explains things clearly and sets you up for success. All you have to do is think. Yeah I know. Hard to do for some college students who do not know how to form original thoughts and want to just memorize things. If you can think and formulate thoughts, you will do well in this class.

In my online Law and Econ class we had 1 midterm, 1 final, and a weekly discussion throughout the semester. No papers no projects. The exams are long answer responses from a question bank he provides a couple weeks before the exam opens. He's particularly looking for your understanding on the definitions of terms.
Online class. No textbook, you have to read all course material through low-quality, lopsided, and frustrating PDFs. Weekly discussions are participation-based. Tough grader on tests

Glick is super knowledgeable, and it's important to keep that in mind. Also, his lectures are boring and dry as hell, there is nothing that makes it interesting, but what's important is that he is able to get the information across effectively. It's important when writing papers, to write them how he interprets question and material.
Easy class but also very interesting. He was a good lecturer, and I could tell he knew what he was talking about, and was something he had experience and interest in, which helped to keep me engaged.
Hes a fair grader. He gives you plenty of chances to learn, and basically spells out the tests for you, as long as you participate and practice on canvas. Tests are worth 25% grade, so be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Toxic environment. He is extremely divisive. Because he fosters, actually rewards a competitive atmosphere, a positive or healthy learning environment is nonexistent. Many people dont talk because of this. The same ones always talk, and he props them up. Like he has a few besties because hes so afraid to be wrong. Likes grad students only :-(

There is a lot of material to be covered in a short time, and the philosophy behind it all can be hard to grasp.He does a pretty good job of explaining it and applying it to real life examples, but the theories itself in general are just hard to grasp. go to every class, do the ws, and study from them and you can get an A. Only 3 tests for grading.

This is a tough class with a tough teacher. Try and go to class, ask questions (even if you feel judged to do so). Text book isn't that helpful, if I took the course again, I would't have bought it. Just pay attention in lecture, and take good notes. Emphasis on good notes. Lots of good notes.
Funny guy! He brought in outside material from policy to psychology to make the course material more relevant. Wish I was an Econ major!

Although his lectures made the material more confusing, his tests were identical to homework questions and info in book. He does favor certain students but I wasn't one of them and still got an A. Do well on the first 3 tests so you don't have to take the 4th (he drops the lowest test score).

He does not create a safe environment for diverse opinions. He pushes his own political agenda. He favors a particular kind of student over others. Those he does not favor, he demoralises them in a passive aggressive way. The worst kind of teacher there is.

I attended class maybe 3 times. If you know anything about Law or Econ the class is a breeze. Dont bother purchasing either book because you wont use them. All the notes are posted online and the exam questions are give to you in advance. No assignments 2 tests, Easy

Glick is a great teacher, I took his law and Econ that he co-taught with Adams and I thought he was fair but wasn't a pushover. This is a tandem class with Glick formal training as an attorney complementing Adams Economics training. If you like to see more than one side to an issue this is a great class.
I really enjoyed this class. One of the better classes I had as an undergraduate. I highly recomend it.

For some reason stress management was way more stressful than it needed to be. I just did not vibe with this professor and didn't like the way he taught or tested. As a generally straight A student I got a B+ in this class of all classes! I just wasn't expecting it to be as complicated as it was. I mean it's supposed to be for stress management.

Not organized, his assignments are all over the place and do not make sense. He does not seem to care much about students. On multiple occasions other student and I would try and reach out to him for various reasons but would never receive a response. It is a very easy class with great potential, but unfortunately that potential was not filled.

Richardson is without a doubt a very kind a funny guy! From the moment I went into his class I felt very welcomed. He certainly knows his stuff but he tends to get off track and rambles a lot. Instructions for assignments are fairly vague / messy and that can stress some out. Although he is a pretty lenient grader, you'll likely get an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He introduced me to a new passion! It was an honor to take a class with him! Great professor! So inspiring!

Some people may think he is confusing in his lectures, but keep going to class and ask questions, he's actually awesome when you understand his quirks. He has a long background of studying resiliency and not everyone understands what resiliency is (because we're young). This class will help you teach resiliency to other people as a health educator.
Amazing professor one of my favorite professors in this college he is a great person to learn from
He is sooo hot I can't belive it !!!!:D

Dr. Richardson is humourous but VERY disorganized. He never has a lecture prepared. You may as well skip class, becuase you don't learn anything from him. The book and lectures notes created from the book are key to passing the class. You also have to keep tabs on your own grade, as he will probably loose or forget about assignments you turn in.

He is a very nice man. Do your work and go to class and you will get an A. He is very understanding and kind and often grades based on completion rather than content. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. You are allowed 3 absences, but aside from that attendance is required, though you don't do much during class.

I took this class in the summer and thought it was great. I actually had to put effort into papers, but it paid off. There was a lot of discussion and emphasis on current events, which I thought was annoying at first but then grew to enjoy-- I felt so informed about the world during this class. Glenn is awesome. Just follow directions.
Don't listen to everyone else. He's alright. do the work (which is easy), and you'll be fine.

This is a very self -involved teacher.  He's all about his way or no way.  The class tended to focus more on discussion rather than writing exercises.  I personally would have preferred more short writing exercises over the discussion of lady Gaga

NO COMMENT!! ugh where do I start haha! Well he's akward looking, he's emotional, and not a good teacher. The class isnt hard but being in this class made me become stupid so It seemed hard because I don't understand him. I honestly did'nt learn anything, my writing has probably become worse from taking his class. It's just a pointless class I felt

The tests are very similar to the practice exams. If you pay attention during lectures you can tell what's gonna be on the exam based on how much importance he puts on topics ( or he will just straight up tell you). He's not mean if you ask questions, he just looks for very precise answers and he's a little sassy.

The exams are literally copy/paste from the practice exam. But showing up to class made me actively more confused. He explains the significance of a concept well but doesn't explain the concept itself. But hey, they don't call him the Indiana Jones of math for nothing. I think he'd be one of the best teachers here if he actually explained things.

He wasn't only the worst math teacher I've ever had but he also got offended when people asked questions. His tests are similar to his practice tests, which is nice, but he doesn't know how to explain to save his life. I was excited for calc 3, because I heard it would be easier than calc 2, but not with this professor. Avoid taking this professor.
He would hit on the young girl students in class. Would not suggest taking

He seemed to belittle and speak down to his students. He rambles SO MUCH. His TA Delany was such a life saver, I went to her office hours for my homework. What is unfortunate is I went to chat with him to grab my final exam and he seemed like a totally different guy. The textbook can be pirated online and I used ChatGPT on most of my homework.

I did NOT like Professor Golden. Went to lecture for the first month then watched professor Leonard on youtube and got an A because of his videos. Golden will ramble on about things that aren't important, barley teaches the math or the important part of the concepts. The only good thing is is practice exams are like the real ones.

I took Math 1220. I got a D in part because of extreme life circumstances. But I would warn he is not a linear teacher. It was difficult to understand what would be on tests and what was "just fun". Not a super clear teaching style. lecture notes but they are impossible to follow unless you attended the lecture. However he is open and kind.

Calculus III was a blast with Dr. Golden

He grades heavily on his exams, but if you attend lectures and pay attention he is very clear on which kinda of questions he likes and what you can expect

The homework wasn't too difficult and he posts it early most of the time

I think I left the class with my mind blown almost every day

Honestly homework was kind of tough. Lecture does not cover all of the examples.

However exam is easy with review session covering practice exam. Also reviewing lectures for examples that he highlighted helped.
Cheat sheet available!

Lecture+hw+class review+practice exam
=A+
Dont know why rating is harsh but I enjoyed it. Lecture was interesting

Ken is extraordinarily knowledgeable, and I'm not knocking all the research he's done, but that's all he ever wants to talk about. He teaches Calc III like a physics class, which would be fine if all the students were physics students, which I wasn't (CS). Also, he often cuts students off mid question. And he's got quite a bit of an ego.

Prof Golden is an amazing teacher. He is able to relate what you're learning in class with actual stuff that matters! The practice exams help and other stuff is given to you as 'hints' in class where he literally winks saying 'this is something I really like.' He lets you DROP your lowest exam! I could not recommend a better teacher for this class.

Professor Golden's in-person lectures are a waste of your time. While you come to learn, he comes to yell at the class when no one answers one of his 'half-second' questions while we are trying to write the notes. Going to lecture will get you more confused. Lack of examples will be noticeable when it comes to exam time.

His teaching is very mediocre. I stopped attending after the first week. You'll do great as long as you don't waste your time going to lecture, but sadly you'll have to self teach. Take it with him only for the reason his test reviews are very similar to his tests, making things a lot less stressful. PLEASE do not waste your time attending lectures

Professor Golden is an excellent teacher. He uses lots of engineering and scientific concepts, as that's what most of the students in the class are pursuing. Gives very intuitive examples. Could've given a few more examples per topic, but overall really good. Excellent test reviews, attend every single one to get a good grade. He grades very fair.

He was a good professor in the sense that you will understand most of it. I wished he did more examples in class but overall it was a fair graded class. Go to his review session, they helped out a ton especially since exams are 60% of your grade. The final was cumulative but focused on the later stuff and worth 20% of your grade. Not a bad choice.

Exams are 80% of your grade. 50 minute lecture every weekday except Thursday, you have a lab on Thursday that's run by a TA. You'll find yourself skipping lectures towards the end of the year because often its just reinforcing what you already know. Exam study guides are very helpful and the exams were just different versions of the problems in it!

I would've liked his class better if 60% of your grade wasn't the midterm exams. You take three midterms and the lowest score of the three gets dropped, but that still means that each midterm is basically 30% of your grade. The final exam is 20%. so 80% of your grade comes from three hours of performance out of the entire semester.

She is really nice and a generous grader but maybe a little inflexible. Missed the first week of class and an assignment because I got stuck in a storm overseas and didn't have my laptop. She refused to let me make up the credit for that

Keri was a little moody and you never knew which side of her you would get. She really was a good teacher but she could be very cruel and rude at times. She also made a big point of us doing assignments based off of the rubric, but never graded based off the rubric, often times just giving out a random grade with little explanation. Quite stubborn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Comes across rude and not a welcoming classroom at all. Three people I know taking Spanish as a degree dropped out after taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In my humble opinion, Keri Gonzales was not my favorite profesora. She was overly picky about assignments and the work performed and rarely gave full credit for homework in class. Because of this, it was not possible to get a good grade because there was no final.

Keri is really passionate about teaching Spanish, and if you work with her and take advantage of her office hours, she will help you out a lot.  If you do all the homework assignments, participate in class, and do a decent job on the final project, you can get a good grade easily.  Her test are very short and mostly based on vocab - very easy.

She's a great woman, and a great Spanish professor. I highly enjoyed her class and I was able to increase my speaking abilities so much. She chooses interesting topics to discuss, and encourages people to make mistakes. It's a safe zone, where we can practice a new language without judgment. I love Keri, and I recommend this class.
Good professer, lecture heavy but intresting case studies, one activity was really fun
Pretty easy exams and quizzes if you pay attention in class. It seems she really cares about students.

Professor Harutyunyan made it relatively easy to be stuck in a 6-9pm class. Her lectures were clear, she engaged with the class often and made sure we were all comfortable sharing our points of views and having conversations about the topics, and overall I found the course material and format easy. Show up to class every week and study for exams.
This is a manageable class and she is a fair grader. Sometimes I wished the slides had more information to catch up when couldn't attend.
Gohar was very helpful teacher and have a good way of teaching.

She just read off slides the majority of the time. Also even though this is a class talking about philosophy  and ethics, she seemed to have a really hard time accepting other peoples views that clashed with her own. She's a moderately easy grader though. Gives small notecards for finals and midterms

I didn't feel comfortable in this class. The professor's communication style often came across as dismissive or curt, and it made it difficult to ask questions or seek help. Because of that, I wouldn't recommend this course.
The class is heavy on discussion and activities which helps the 3-hour long evening class go by easier. A low stress class and manageable assignments.

Lectures are very monotone and unengaging. She makes the tests so difficult and tough to study for. The study guide had very little to do with the test. The slides have barely any information that will help you study as well. Good luck if you have to take her course. Avoid at all costs.

The class itself doesn't seem hard but she is very unengaging and was little help when we answered questions. Ontop of this the exams were confusing at times and the class average reflected this with the mean often being a flat 70% and the high score being only an 88%.

This professor took off points from my group for someone missing a presentation due to a family emergency. Lacks communication with her students. Most monotone speaker and lectures are long and read off of slides. Little to no student engagement due to this. Do avoid if possible.
Chill and approachable professor. The exams aren't too bad and there are no surprises.

Please try to avoid this teacher. She speaks in monotone about very boring subject matter and does not try to engage the students. She gets mad at students for not engaging in class while being horrible at trying to engage students. It is so hard to not fall asleep and pay attention because there is no engagement with the students. Please avoid.

I really enjoyed this class, we did lots of activities in class and you would get points for writing a couple sentence reflection. Attendance wasn't mandatory but you would miss out on quite a few points if you didn't attend. Only 2/3 tests are required since your lowest score gets dropped, attend class, pay attention and you will pass.
Gohar was great & her lectures were clear and easy to understand. She posts everything in the Modules and has the class very organized.

If you attend class, you will pass with a high A, and actually retain what you learned. Gohar's biggest plus is she does in-class activities that help you completely understand management topics for the class but also stick in your mind afterward. Class is clear, non-stressful, and helpful. Review the slides before the exams to ace them.
Very chill, very manageable class haha. I enjoyed it a lot and have a lot of respect for Professor Gohar
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was easy, and her quizzes are open notes, and exams she allows a sheet of notes. However she is one of the most boring professors I've taken. She talks very slowly and has a monotone voice making it difficult to engage in. I would recommend her if you want an easy class with no homework.

This class was very relaxed and the material was presented in a way that made sense and was easy to follow. I recommend attending all the lectures as the slides are best presented with Gohar reading them to you.

She was super nice and did a really good job at teaching the material. I think she cares about the students and is willing to help out. Super easy class with a great professor! Would take another class from her for sure!

Gohar reads directly off the slides and fails to engage the class on a daily basis. The material in this course was covered in every basics of psychology, BCOR 1010, and BCOR 1050, class I have had so far and feel this class is a truly unnecessary addition to the BCOR block here at the U.
I love Professor Harutyunyan! She is willing to help you out when things come up in your personal life, and she's super understanding. Sweetest professor out there!
Exams were very bad and slides dont help with the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class, but I can't say I learned much from it.
This is a very easy class, Professor is there to help, and assignments and tests aren't too hard.
Super easy class, chill professor, easy A
She is so sweet and this was a very easy class. Would take again.
One of the better BCOR classes, exams were easy, and it was a very low-stress class. Wish more classes were like this one.

Overall an extremely easy class. The professor is very soft-spoken as others have mentioned and the class can get a little boring sometimes but it was only 50 min long twice a week. Overall, she was nice and approachable. Attend class and study the exam reviews and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She stands at the front of the class still and talks for 50 minutes about the lecture slides. The tests are easy and you get to bring a notecard to them.

Professor Harutyunyan can be a little quiet and soft spoken but she is a very good instructor and makes really good review slides for all the exams. I always felt confident going into tests and quizzes as she doesn't try and ambush you with surprise questions the way other professors do. As long as you participate in class you'll do great.
I learned a lot in this class but I felt she went a little fast sometimes. I loved the the team activities.
She presents the material in a clear and concise manner. At the same time, she should have a better understanding that the group needs to be divided equally among the teams.
Professor Gohar is there whenever help is needed. She is understanding and is easy to work with. Her classes are interesting and the role plays are fun too.

I felt like the class was the most pointless class I've taken. She seems like a nice person and I respect what she has accomplished to become a professor. However, this class is almost impossible to sit through. She reads the slides word for word very slowly and monotone. I didn't learn a single thing in class; all learning was done on my own time.

No joking, one of the best IS professors! Professor Gordon made databases easy and interesting to learn. He cares about his students and is always willing to help. Assignments, quizzes, and exams were always very straightforward. The final project was not too stressful either. I wish he taught more IS classes, highly recommend!

Such an amazing professor, he is very caring and I found his lectures to be engaging. The class material is kind of hard to understand but with practice it becomes easier. There is a lot of homework but they don't take very long to do. The weekly statistics quizzes I hated, you would learn a concept on tue and be expected to know it by thur.

I love Professor Gordon so much. He is the light in the business school and truly one of the best professors I have had here and in my life. It was an honor to take a class from him and his TA is chill as hell too.
Awesome, caring guy. Content is boring, but as a person he's great.
super chill
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor and the teaching assistants are really helpful and easy to reach out to. There's lots of homework and assignments due, so be ready to put in the work, as it can add up. Attendance isn't always mandatory at times as there's only lab to do during class. Overall an easy class if you put in the work.
While this class has a lot of work attached, the deadlines are manageable and the lectures are interesting. Gordon is a great guy and makes complicated topics easy to understand. 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: We got behind in the first weeks of the class but were able to catch up. Attendance was not mandatory and he made it easy for us to access all of the material. Responded to emails 1-2 days out and made sure that we understood the material.
Professor Gordon is great, lectures are not mandatory but very informative. Just do the homework and quizzes and you'll pass.
Such a kind professor, will always give the benefit of the doubt. Attendance is not mandatory except on quiz days. Super easy to talk to and get in touch with!

Professor Gordon was the best professor I've had at the business school. Very caring and nice professor who made a serious effort to have each student pass. Attendance wasn't required but can be helpful in understanding some topics more in depth. Would definitely recommend! :)

Professor Gordon is an incredibly caring professor. He is always willing to help his students, and he is very accommodating and understanding when it comes to late assignments. He is one of the best professors I have had, and I would happily take him again.
Professor Gordon is definitely one of the best professors I've ever had! He is very kind and you can tell he cares about each student and has their best interest in mind. He is awesome.

This Professor was super great. He always wants to help you out and is willing to give you the benefit of the doubt. There is a lot of assignments and the excel projects can take a while but if you put in the effort you will definitely get an A.

I've had 5 IS professors as part of the IS minor and I've hated 3 of them. John Gordon was NOT one of those professors.

He's actually a cool dude

Professor Gordon is incredible and adapted to the technical challenges that this class struggled with. He completely abandoned McGrawill assigments due to difficulties. He instead made custom assignments with the help of TA's. This meant far more work for him but gave us the ability to learn better with fewer struggles. Tests followed study guide.

Good lecturer, soft spoken, very good at explaining topics. One thing I liked the most is that in class he didn't only cover strictly course material but also offered career advice and reassurances for all the tech students in the class (which I am not, I'm in the IS minor program). That's something I don't see often.

He is a great professor. Missed or late assignments- he would figure out a way to get you the points. His lectures are a little boring yes, but i still 100% recommend a course from him. Easy course load and exams. He is very understanding when you need more points on an assignment and is willing to help anyone get extra help.

John Gordon is a super chill teacher. You do not have to attend class because there is no attendance but I suggest you do. He is very passionate and flexible whenever students have problems.1-2 hours of homework a week, sometimes less. Tests are not stressful because he goes over EVERYTHING the class before and you are allowed notes on test.

Lectures were very boring which made it hard to learn from them. He kept referring to the textbook that students were unable to access, he knew we were unable to access it, yet the issue never got fixed.

No final, just an argumentative essay. A few worthwhile extra credit opportunities. Wrote only 3 or 4 essays the entire semester so light workload. Even though it's an online class she is pretty quick at responding to a canvas inbox message. I technically didn't learn anything new though lol, this class just gave me the chance to practice writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Up untill now in this class, (near mid-terms) I have learned nothing from taking this class. It has been nothing but memorizing useless acronyms and definitions that have zero practical use. The only slightly useful subject so far has been resume building, but I already had a resume, so that was still unhelpful. Take another writing class.

She was the perfect prof for this class. She was easy to get ahold of, graded quickly, gave great feedback, and was very clear about what to do and graded fairly. DO ALL THE READINGS. They are soooo helpful. I didn't think they would be, but they were. Also just don't get behind. This class was not hard, but it was quite a bit of work.

I love her! She cares about her students, is excellent, and is willing to help you with anything. Please attend her lectures, she's always funny and gives lots of information at once. You won't regret it.

It was my first time taking an in person class after 3 years. She was the best. She is very chill about attendance but I would recommend going to class whenever you can. She says a lot of things in class that will help you with the course. She is pretty funny too. Very chill class sometimes only 40 mins long. She gives out a ton of extra credit!!

Professor Goodman is an amazing professor and genuinely cares about the work you are turning in. She gives useful feedback and is generous when grading. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities, but you will find it easy to get a good grade if you just show up to class and turn in your assignments on time.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Had her for scientific writing. Professor Goodman is really really nice and understanding. She gave good feedback on writing, but didn't grade harshly. Also made herself available to talk about papers. She didn't waste in class time and would let us get off the zoom meetings early if we didn't have anything else to cover that day.

Multiple assignments per week. Boring class, no lecturing at all. Copious amounts of reading. Format is heres a bunch of reading, now do these assignments. Its hard to feel like you are learning anything when structured like that. Nice nice professor, but dont take this class unless its really applicable to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Holly is so much fun!! Her Geology of Utah class is fantastic, with awesome field trips (3 weekend trips; you only have to go on 1, but I recommend doing as many as you can), enjoyable lectures, lots of in-class activities (graded for participation), and a clever and fun final project. A truly great professor; I can't recommend her enough!

I took a teaching/communication course from Holly. She is on the cutting edge of teaching techniques. Every class was interesting, hands-on, and enlightening. The homework was purposeful. It was one of the funnest and most influential classes I've ever taken. She is a true gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Holly was great. In this course, you spend 2-3 hours per week in a K-12 school teaching science. I loved it. You only meet once per week, which is nice. A little homework, but not tons. I recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I liked Smoak a lot and he is good at what he does. He knows that nobody is a history major and his class is fairly straightforward. There is a lot of material and he does assign reading each week. That said, most of your assignments are just writing projects. As long as you plan for those and get them in on time you will have no issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smoak is the man. Would highly recommend his class. The amount of knowledge he possesses is staggering, and he has great anecdotes that make lectures enjoyable.

Professor Smoak really cares about what he teaches about. He is a great teacher and explains the. material well. If you read the assigned articles (which are usually not long) and mostly follow along with the lectures it is super easy. Homework is also graded pass/fail and not a lot of homework.

Greg is really the goat, just go to class and take notes you'll get an A fs. I skipped class a lot but still got an A and the dude does really care about what he's teaching which makes lecture not too bad. Plus saw him at the gym lifting what a legend.

Professor Smoak is really great! You can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching. This class is definitely an easy A, as long as you show up to class and do the readings! My #1 tip for his class is to take REALLY good lecture notes. They help so much for the writing assignments. Other than that, try to do every quiz and most of the readings

I took Honors 2102 with Professor Smoak. The information presented in class was interesting but also required a lot of reading for the week. You'd usually have at least one writing per week on the reading so it will take up a good amount of your time. But professor Smoak gives food feedback and will let you redo things! and discussion was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Smoak knows that nobody in this class is actually a history major. He made it extremely easy with MINIMAL work. As long as you show up to lectures or read the slides, and can write a somewhat decent short essay it's super easy. His lectures were genuinely enjoyable though and he made the class pretty interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Smoak was the first teacher I've had that made History not a drag. While yeah, it's American History, I still learned a ton of stuff I had absolutely no clue about and was not taught in high school history classes. Smoak is really understanding and gives good lectures, and there's a decent amount of extra credit in there to boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class covers a lot of content and it's very important you attend class and take notes/listen to the lectures. If you simply just show up, there really isn't much outside studying you will need to do. There's weekly quizzes, and some discussion projects but the class really isn't that difficult if you attend the lectures and take notes.

Professor Smoak is a great professor. He might not seem like it at first but you will warm up to him and realize that he cares about his students and he loves his job. Lectures are a bit boring but they are very informative and really helpful for the assignments, weekly quiz, and the exams. Overall a very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
This is all of US history through a fire hose. Sooo much information comes at you in such a short period of time!! It's a massive classroom with a lot of reading, but if you pay attention and do the work, it's so easy to get an A. Literally just do the work. 
This is a great intro course and great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Smoak has been by far my least favorite faculty member in the History department. The class I took was a combined course with graduate students and he expected everyone to operate at their level of intelligence. I felt that I was often penalized for arbitrary differences in approach and he was often condescending when I asked for feedback

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have had. Exam grades were very low, and even when the entire class missed the same questions, he showed no interest in reflecting on his teaching or helping students improve.

While Professor Golic is very intelligent - It's clear that he does have the best interest for the students taking his course. No credit for homework.

Golic is so nice and a genius but his lectures are pretty boring and seem unrelated to what he tests on. Shout out to Makenna the TA for carrying everyone through that class

reviews.comment: Professor Golic definitely knows what he is talking about in regards to genetics. Go to lectures and take notes and you will do well.

Condescending to students that reach out to him with questions. I sent multiple emails and never received a response as well. He does not seem interested in students actually learning material, rather he seems more interested in assigning a grade and receiving his paycheck.

Golic is dry at best. The material isnt hard if you have the time to do a ton of reading on your own. Prepare to focus on his lectures though as a lot of test material comes from it. I had a problem with him being condescending with students who genuinely wanted to ask questions in class. I ended up tutoring 2. Too busy trying to look smart.

Class structure needs serious changes. Lectures are dry and not particularly useful, there are minimal resources outside of class to gain practice solving problems, and the discussion sections are essentially TA office hours as you are expected to show up with your own questions.
