reviews.comment: He is funny, very smart and really likes teaching. He cares about his students, awesome guy.

Professor Golic is the best biology teacher I have had.  Do the homework he assigns.  Our test had multiple questions straight from the homework.  This class was straightforward and I learned a lot about genetics.  I would recommend this class for anyone that needs to take genetics!

I thought Dr. G was a good teacher and good guy. He gets frustrated with students that struggle, but if you meet him one on one or just ask questions, he is awesome. He was  dry and funny and always in a good mood. I recommend this genetics course over the others at the U.

There is a test in this class every other Thursday.  This is an absolute mess.  Not a bad teacher, but his class structure is bad.  Usually, he teaches the difficult material the day before the test and so you essentially have to figure everything out with less than 48 hours to go before being tested on it.
Excellent professor, he's cynical, dry, and hillarious.  Ever question from each test is gone over in class and he's excellent at explaining the material.  One of the best teachers I've had at the U.

He was a wonderful professor. Very helpful and clear in lectures and in one on one conversations. Don't need to go to every class but go for reviews because they hint towards test. Overall he made genetics easy to understand but definitely helps to do the homework!That way you ace the tests.

Genetics was a a challenging class, it needed sincere efforts  and I had to study every other day to get a good grade. I wish a I had studied from the very beginning. Dr. Kent is an amazing professor, he is willing to help  the students as long as they ask for any kind of help. Study hard, pay attention to his hints, and complain to him when needed

Dr. Golic is a great professor.  Genetics is not an easy subject but is integral to Biology.  If you are getting a biology degree and don't feel like putting the effort into this class study something else.The complaints on here are more a reflection of the student than Kent. I got a tutor and worked hard at this class to prepare for the BIO GRE.
Godawful class,godawful professor. I learned the material entirely on my own.

Terrible professor. I wasn't interested in biology before and I'm certainly not a fan now. People say he's jolly but I think he is jolly because he takes pleasure out of crushing the dreams of students.

I don't know any sane students that loved this class. I did all the book problems and understood them but his tests just caught me off guard. Get help from the TA's or you'll fail! Golic is a really cool person but he definitely made this class harder and less enjoyable then it should have been

This class is not hard. It's just a matter of attending the lectures and doing the problems in the book.  Golic is more than willing to help students who come in and he doesn't require that you take the final if you do well on the all of the 7 exams. I would definitely recommend this class!

Worst class I have ever taken. All previous interest has been taken away. Doesn't prepare you for tests. Gives problems never seen before. New book has minimum of 5 errors per chapter in problems and answers(and solutions manual) so it is useless. Don't be deceived by his humor and first test. Not curved. Ruin your GPA. Take from anyone else!

This class blows. I am taking this with calculus 2 and chemistry 2 and feel completely overwhelmed. I understand this more than any of my friends and repetitively score at least 10-15% above the average, however the average is around 50% and this class is not curved. FML.
Super hard, super boring.  I'm convinced genetics doesn't have to be that hard but Golic doesn't make it any easier.  He's a nice person though.

If genetics is not your thing, I would suggest not taking it from this professor. His lectures are pretty fast and he only uses the chalkboard. He doesn't add any visuals, interesting stories, etc. It's pretty cut and dry and the tests are very hard.
The material is interesting, but defintely the hardest class I've taken yet at the U.  Read the book and do all the questions multiple times.

Doing the HW is CRITICAL. Almost all tests are straight from the HW but to get an A you'll need to understand the material itself, not just the problems. Just doing problems will get you a B. HW requires a lot of time and the class is very study-intensive but the material is understandable and the exams straightforward. No tricky tests but no curve

This class was a miserable experience. If you can take this with another professor DO IT! He covers 1 chapter (usually 80ish pages) per lecture, and has and exam after every 3 lectures. IF you do have to take this class, I feel for you, I really do. DO ALL THE ASSIGNED PROBLEMS IN THE BOOK! He doesnt lecture on this material very much at all but hi

He's been going out of his way to elucidate information that some students haven't been able to pick up on, but I don't know why since it was simple to understand in the first place. Interesting lecturer, and a nice guy. If you come to class and do all of the problems, there's no reason you shouldn't get an A, since the tests are based heavily on t

The man does not help anyone with anything they do not already know. The book is useless, but you have to read it and answer the questions. Will pull questions out of no where and expect you to be a geneticist without giving adequate information
worst professor I have ever had wrote and talked to the chalkboard and not the class.
Fun guy to have as a professor, but is not good at teaching new material to people who do not already know the subject.
No Comments

Dr. Golic is an awesome professor.  If you are willing to put in the time and effort, to work all the assigned homework problems, and show up to class it's impossible not to get an A.  The class is interesting and Dr. Golic is very fair.  He has a great sense of humor and relates well to students.  Highly recommended!

Pretty easy class. Exams reviews are pretty much what is on the test. Posts all the slides to Canvas. Attendance isn't mandatory but makes concepts much easier to understand because she does demonstrations in class. Super nice professor and exams aren't cumulative! Have and would take her again!

Relies a bit much on slides, but you can tell that she really wants to help students and is willing to help in any way. Even when I missed class, I got all of the information I needed on the posted slides and the assignments were easy but informative.
Good psych professor but relies a lot on slides.

This professor makes a super easy course even easier. She didn't have any exams, so learning the information was very stress-free. I didn't go to class and was able to get all the information I needed on the posted slides.

Dr. Greve is great! She is really kind and caring and it shows throughout her lectures. Attendance was not mandatory and there was no finals, just some quizzes throughout. She does just read off of slides a lot but it wasn't too bad. Overall great and easy class!

Love Professor Greve. Incredibly helpful with questions during office hours about careers and she helped me make a pathway for grad school. Participation is not mandatory, but if you are still figuring out career goals in psych I would highly recommend attending classes. Very kind instructor, and assignments are all easy and not too time consuming.
Very easy course and a good professor. I am excited to take another psych class from her in the spring.

While this professor knows how to teach clearly, her lack of returning grading on time is an extreme detriment to her quality as a professor. Her exam turnaround time was 3+ weeks, and I am currently 28 days into waiting for the Exam 3 score. My final is in 2 days. I don't know if I need to study Exam 3 material or not, and it is very frustrating.
She's really great at teaching and breaking down statistics. Lab assignments have in depth instructions which makes them easy and the final isn't cumulative.
No final or Midterm for this class. Attendance not mandatory, and the PowerPoints were posted on canvas.
She was always so caring and made sure her students felt comfortable asking questions and seeing her for help. Very easy class, but it takes forever for things to get graded.

Super easy and expectations are clearly communicated. A bunch of assignments to keep you engaged throughout the semester but none of them are too challenging. Very kind and considerate Professor, will be taking again for 3010!

Professor Greve pretty just read off the slides, I could do the same amount of work in 15 minutes that we would get through in 90. It sucked to have to take this class but it was really easy. She wasn't helpful as a teacher and she never responded to any emails/ canvas and her office hours were "by appointment" so I couldn't ever reach her.

Dr. Greve is very interested and passionate about her subject. She is always willing to help her students understand and discuss difficult topics. She teaches through powerpoints that are always on Canvas but goes into more detail in class. Assignments are fairly easy with clear expectations and always offers feedback. Would take her class again.

reviews.comment: I love her class so much. She reads off of slides but it's super easy and we have weekly quizzes on the material you can use the lecture slides on. Told us at the beginning of the semester that she doesn't give a final exam! More project based than test based which I think better suits the material. Kind and caring, Maren is an amazing professor.
Do not take her online course.

Dr. Green's lectures are amazing! She is extremely smart and well-spoken, and gets to the heart of history. The assignments are very clear and provide significant opportunities for support for those who need it. All the readings and assignments directly correlate with the lectures. I absolutely loved her class!
Great professor! Pretty easy class.

reviews.comment: She's not bad but not amazing. The class is a lecture with a power point. You have readings/reading responses that really aren't that bad. If you put in the work you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Not sure why some of Mira's ratings are bad. I absolutely loved her class. She's super knowledgable about history and every topic was FASCINATING. Always felt she was willing to help and I learned so much. Papers are long but if you put in the effort it's not too bad! So glad I took this, highly recommend. Thank you Mira!!!!!!

She reads off a slideshow and then assigns readings, then proceeds to give bad grades for “not including material discussed in class” even though her class is a slideshow and I used slideshow notes to write my papers. Makes no sense. Shes also not very nice, will make you feel like a failure for “not including material discussed in class. Illogical

Professor Green is hard to work with. She is late to every lecture. Each class is 90 minutes of listening to her read facts off her slideshow. Sometimes the lectures are not finished in class and students need to finish them themselves online outside of class. She is lazy and if you need help your better off asking the TA's since they are graders.

Mira is a really kind professor, and she gets her student involved in her lectures. Her lectures are much more that just the hour rant a class that sone often are. The class however can be struck at grading. When doing a paper, really read the instructions and do not skip ANYTHING. Good professor overall!

This class is amazing but requires some effort. There's lots of readings and a few papers, but overall as long as you're showing up to class and paying attention it's not too bad. Take advantage of office hours, Professor Green is very understanding and willing to help if you need it. If you're interested in history you'll love this class!

reviews.comment: learned nothing. too depressed over this class to say more

Tianyu Gu is a very nice professor and always helps when needed. You're only graded on a total of 6 case studies, and as long as you put in work and try, you'll do fine. With that, the class was hard to follow, as lectures were long and went fast, and unfortunately, I didn't get a lot from the class. Overall, nice professor, confusing course.

reviews.comment: Tianyu is a good professor! His class is pretty straightforward and grades are determined fairly. As long as you put some effort in and complete the case studies, you will get an A. He is also very helpful, would recommend this class to anyone interested in analytics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tianyu is a nice guy but I don't think he is a good professor. His class is extremely boring and you won't learn anything. The homework that we do have is done all together in class so it's easy to get full points. There are no tests or quizzes, just many long lectures. Professor Gu is a great guy, but I would recommend taking a different class.

Tianyu is an incredibly nice guy and always willing to help, but this course was terrible. It was easily the most dry and unhelpful class I've taken at this university, which is sad to say because Tianyu is a really nice person. I'd highly recommend avoiding this class and taking a different marketing elective if you can.

I took his class online if that makes a difference, but he doesn't give a textbook, examples, assignments, or anything else. He talks and expects you to understand. He does answer questions, but in such a way that you're more confused. Don't take this class if you expect to learn because there is absolutely no teaching involved.

Dr. Gruenwald is a very kind and fun professor. He genuinely loves what he does, so it makes the course a lot more enjoyable. Good with answering questions and interacting with students. Also does experiments in class!

He was a super nice and whimsical guy, just a very pleasant person to be around. The class content can be quite difficult to grasp, but his amiable disposition makes it bearable to learn. However, a gripe of mine was his lack of supplemental resources like practice exams or quizzes, and his study guides weren't the greatest.

Prof. Grünwald is an incredible teacher. He is very mindful of the students. The course was moderately challenging overall with time consuming homework, but he provided many resources. His lectures were very clear and engaging. A digital tablet made it easier to take notes. He is also a talented singer, but you'll have to take him to see.

I hate chemistry but he helped me become a little more engaged. I wish he used lecture slides though instead of notes. Homeworks can take a really long time but there's only 1 per week. And the quizzes are harder than the exams usually.

Michael is a great chemistry professor! He's a funny and engaging lecturer, and actually wants his students to succeed. Chem 2 was a challenging class, but he did a good job of keeping exams reasonable & similar to the homework. Though his weekly quizzes were HARD, and the weekly homework is very long (and even due/assigned during exam weeks).

Was an amazing teacher, cared about us, actually enjoyed being in the class. This doesn't mean that the tests and quizzes weren't extremely difficult (although it is Gen Chem 2). Would recommend this class just be prepared for a hard class.

He honestly has been my favorite chem professor. He was taught very well and make lots of funny jokes. He is super passionate about chemistry and helping other students. I'm not good at chemistry at all but he made it easier for me to understand. I would definitely take him over anyone else

Professor Grunwald is very passionate, witty, and often cracks jokes. His notes are engaging and easy to follow. You can tell he cares about his students' success and is very capable of answering questions and breaking down complex topics. Every week, he assigns homework that can be lengthy and a quiz, which I found more difficult than the exams.

Professor Grunwald is an amazing professor. His lectures are very lively and he really loves chemistry. He cracks a lot of jokes which helps make the class feel less intimidating. His tests aren't particularly hard and he does a good job of making sure you know what concepts are on them. I would highly recommend taking any class taught by him.

I love Michael. The class is not easy, but he works with students and really wants all of them to do well. I loved having him, and I will miss him so much next semester. He even sang us a song on the last day of the lecture. I love him so much!

Chemistry is far from my favorite subject, but he is very engaging and is always willing to have a discussion with you and work with you. He helped me understand some difficult concepts in a simple manner and really made me look forward to learning more about chemistry. I highly recommend taking him for chem!

One of those professors who knows how to teach. Good with questions. Chem isn't my favorite, but his lectures come with notes, and he really tries to make the students happy to show up for that required qr attendance. I feel like if you can get the whole lecture hall to laugh at a couple corny jokes you are doing a wonderful job. Would take again.

He is a great professor, he clearly is passionate about what he teaches and cares about his students. He is very lecture heavy but discussions are helpful if you go to them. I would say he is a tough but fair grader and always gives partial credit. I truly think the people on here that rated him poory are just bad at chem and mad about it.

The attendance cards feel infantilizing, and his lectures are don't really contribute to understanding. My time would have been better spent eading through the textbook or going to outside resources. He is a nice professor who wants you to succeed, though, and is energetic throughout his lectures.

HE IS AMAZING. If you don't take a course from him, you are a fool. I am NOT a chem person and he made it interesting and understandable. Don't get me wrong, this is a tough course (it's chem 2 what did you expect), but he makes it completely doable. If I could take the rest of my college courses from this man, I would. 11/10 would recommend.

I loved Professor Grunwald. Personally, I'm not a big gen chem person but I enjoyed his lectures and he made the class way better. Tests weigh a lot on your final grade so make sure you are prepared. HW (almost) every week was time-consuming and challenging but helped identify weaknesses in material. Attendance is worth a lot! Take with Michael!

Michael's my favorite professor I've had at the U. He's a great lecturer, while being funny and entertaining. I loved this class. As long as you stay on top of it, it was not hard. He also reviewed before every test with no trick q's. 10/10 professor He is so caring and good at taking feedback. This class was a lot of work but was pretty easy

I loved Prof Grunwald! His lectures were easy to follow and amazing. The homework was sometimes long, but it definitely prepares you for the exams. He was always super passionate about the content, which made the class fun. He's for sure one of the best professors I've had!

The lectures were easy to understand, and he was very patient when you asked questions. Even some dumb questions he would answer patiently. Good lectures and homework he gives prepare you a lot for his tests. Easy and fair tests.

Grünwald single-handedly made the experience of learning Gen. Chem II at the U enjoyable and fun. He has a great sense of humor, great teaching style, and the workload is moderate, but keeping up isn't an issue. The discussions are useful, and he creates awesome notes ready to follow and fill-in. Overall, he teaches a great class.
Great professor. Lectures are clear and easy to follow. There's a significant amount of homework, but the tests are fair.

I loved Gruenwald! He was very energetic and sweet. His notes were fill in the blank, which was very effective in keeping me engaged. Homework was extremely difficult and notes didn't help a ton, but there were other resources: textbook, TAs, office hours. If you can finish HW, the tests are a breeze and only the simplest concepts.

He was a good lecturer but sometimes they didn't make sense, and there aren't a lot of examples. Homework is difficult and graded for accuracy, so ask the TAs if you have the right answer. He doesn't curve tests, but did give extra credit opportunity when an average was low. Tests were a big percentage of overall grade, over 50% between all 4.

I loved this class. He puts handmade lecture notes on canvas beforehand which you can fill in with him during lectures, which were some of the best notes I've ever taken. However, his grading is harsh. 3 exams, 1 final, no drops. Homework (10+ questions) every week and a quiz (2 attempts and the average is taken). Lowest 2 of each are dropped.

Great gen chem 2 professor! Attendance is 18% of your grade, easy points. He is super kind and his tests are very fair. If you just go through his lectures and test resources an A is very attainable. He does a great job at simplifying a more challenging subject. Take this class in person, don't be lazy and take Owens online, you will regret!!!
Awesome professor. I hated chem 1 but chem 2 with him was great

Professor Gruenwald has an interactive teaching style coupled with scheduled discussions to work on homework in groups. Effective way to learn to solve problems and to meet new study partners. Office hours were helpful, and the exam study guides were comprehensive. You can tell he really loves chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. G is one of the best professors that I have ever had. He is super organized and his notes are super clear and explanatory. He is such a kind guy also.

I was very surprised that this class wasn't curved. The homework grading was fairly harsh because they only grade a small subset of problems out of the whole homework. So if you mess up on one question you are screwed. The midterms and final were difficult. He makes attendance boost your test grades, but it barely helps you at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gruenwald seems like a great guy, and is a very good professor imo. The course content is inherently difficult like most science courses, but not unmanageable. The problem sets are relatively long, but extremely beneficial. If you do the readings, homeworks, and attend the lectures/discussions, this is not a hard class to succeed in.

When taking his classes, you must be prepared to read the textbook sections beforehand, pay attention in class, and participate during lectures in order to pass. Attending class boosts your test grade, and tests weren't too difficult.  The only downside to this class was being required to turn in homework during lecture times instead of online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This dude sucks. Literally one of the worst professors to have for chemistry. He seems like a nice person outside of a classroom setting but not the best professor. He has an accent (which is not bad but can be difficult to understand) and has one of the worst handwriting I have seen. Was difficult to understand what he was writing. Awful testing!

So, let's just cut to the chase and say he is awful. Just absolutely terrible. One of the harshest graders I have probably met and the worst when it came to curving a class considering how bad the exam averages were. Avoid him by every mean possible even if that means you have to wait a semester to take it with someone else. AVOID TAKING!

Michael seems like a great, even excellent person. However, his lectures contribute very little to the homework or quizzes. His tests are incredibly hard for what its worth, and I'm practically teaching myself at this point. Get ready to learn from your textbook if you take him.

I loved him! Going into thermodynamics, I was concerned. This class is very math and derivation heavy, it's a very difficult class both conceptually and mathematically, but he really knows how to teach this class well. He had amazing lectures and brought humor into them. Lots of homework, but he helps you through it. Hes 1 of the best!

Michael is an excellent professor and a gifted lecturer. PChem is obviously difficult, but he's very available in discussion and office hours to answer questions. Problem sets are long, but you talk about them in discussion, which makes it a lot more reasonable. Tests are conceptual and challenging, but fair. Highly recommend! Learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's Extremely vague with learning outcomes. Homeworks are LONG! Have nothing to do with the quizzes or tests all 3 of which are graded hard!!! NO RESOURCES OR HELP for this tough class. Lectures have maybe 5% to do with the Homework and he has students present during the discussion for some reason. He makes it more confusing and difficult.

Prof. Grünwald's Thermo course was one of the most challenging classes I've taken. His approach to the course is very math and derivation heavy, which works for some people (like me). If you are solid with math and enjoy understanding the why behind equations, he is the professor for you. He really works to make sure students learn the material.

Toughest class I have taken in the chemistry department. Lots of homework and the tests are hard. However,  Prof gives out a template of the background info for the problems on the test. Spent a lot of time trying to figure out what he may ask then actually mastering the lecture/problem set materials.  Exams are open book.

This class was an easy A, but I also did learn a lot. There was once a week a class discussion post, 2 easy and short essays, and an open-note midterm and final. The online lectures were very interesting but you could get away with not watching them. I never used the textbook so I suggest not buying it. Loved this class, I highly recommend it!

Such an easy class, very straightforward with 1 discussion and responses per week, quiz every other week, a few papers and a midterm/final. Every week there is a 10-20 minute lecture, presentations, and a textbook but you can get by so easily with none of these. I found this class and the textbook very interesting but his accent was difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed this class so much, and it was a nice break from all my other stressful classes. Easy A and the content is super interesting, both midterm and final are open book/note. Dr. Wu is also very approachable and willing to help students. Pretty easy discussion every week, two straightforward essays that aren't very long, biweekly quiz

I took an online class with Professor Wu and it was a super fun and easy class. It wasn't a stressful class, so I was able to sit down and actually learn the material which was fun and engaging. Weekly discussions and quizzes every few weeks. Final was open note.

Online class, with discussions every week. Super easy online class if that is what you are looking for. Every week there was a video lecture, discussion (3 comments with at least 60 words) and a 10pt quiz every two weeks. A few short essays here and there but nothing too crazy. Super fun and interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is one of the easiest classes i have ever taken. The content is good, and he creates good presentation and recordings. there are discussion posts every week. every test and quiz was open note.
Super great professor. While I did online, we did not have many 1v1 interactions, but he had very good slides and lectures that were super informative. Liked him a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a decent professor I can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. My only real complaint of the class is majority of your grade comes from exams, but if you take good notes you'll do good on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. He's passionate, and is super accessible, but didn't do much teaching tbh. Most of the content we learned came from the textbook, which was about 2-3 hours/wk of reading. Other than that there are some quizzes, all open note/book, and some short discussion posts. Super easy A, you could probably pass w/o even reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a very kind guy and his class was very easy. All of the contect on quizzes, discussions, and assignments can be found in the lecture slides he posts. Very rarely used the book. There aren't a ton of assignments so if you miss one or two it's hard to make up those points. Definitely recommend.
Professor Wu was great and did his best using Zoom. It was always ready to teach and knew what he was talking about. As along at you read and take notes of the power points you'll go fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: If you fail then this its really on you b/c it's easy. Weekly discussion post (initial comment by Wed and 2 replies by Sun.). Assignment every so often. 2 tests and open book. Textbook wasn't really used by me but it's a good read for further clarification. Tests: MC, short answer (textbook useful here). Discussions are engaging. Organized content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was hard to understand the whole semester, never really got used to his accent. had to try really hard to listen. His powerpoints are good tho, almost all of the info for the tests is on the slides. He posted the slides after he went through them, not before. Pop quizzes & writing assignments in class, he doesn't really mention them until day of
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Mr. Wu is very knowledgeable in his area of expertise. He can be a little bit hard to understand sometimes but his powerpoint makes up for that. Attendance is not necessary but he only announces quizzes and assignments in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Wu has a very strong accent but you get used to it. He cracks little jokes throughout the lectures that not everyone catches, but I thought they were funny. He gives pop quizzes and writing assignments every few weeks, but usually gives a heads up of when to expect them. Pay attention to the lectures or you might get kinda lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Accent is hard to understand but class is easy to pass. Take notes and show up. Tests are fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a great teacher. His accent is a bit tricky to get used to at first but after a couple weeks it's totally fine. As long as you show up and take notes it's not hard to pass with a good grade. He's a super nice guy and loves student feedback and interaction. If you need the credit or are even just interested, I highly recommend.

Professor Guangzhen Wu is a genuine and intelligent man. His class isn't very hard if you show up, take notes, and just try. He explains everything well and cracks jokes throughout the lecture to keep you awake and laughing. He's a great professor and he really cares about his students. You can always ask him questions and he's very nice.

Class format was bizarre. He just lectured by following slides but the lectures were so dry, there was little point in showing up to class. He also talks quiet and has an accent, so it's hard to understand him. Exams were way harder than anything asked in the hw/quiz, but at least they were graded forgivingly. Overall just a MID class.

Tao is a super nice guy, but its clear hes a new teacher. He is very unconfident, and there is a big language barrier, at least for me. His lectures are dry and hard to follow. Tests were brutal because since we had basically no homework, I didn't have any clue what would be on them. Improve on these things, become more comfortable, and Tao is good

The content is really good, but the lectures are not engaging and hard to follow. Slides are given to students, but are not very useful other than to look up the topics through external resources. The course was very low work/effort. 3 short assignments, 2 exams, 5 quizzes. Exams were daunting due to not having any clue what would be on them.

took this class because of all the positive reviews, only to be disappointed. Political views are fairly obvious in his quizes and lectures and he sometimes goes on weird rants.if you take this class just make sure you take those quizes on time and turn assignments in on time or you'll fall behind fast and can't makeup those points you lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dr. Perparim Gutaj makes so much sense of European politics. He brings together deep academic knowledge of politics with extensive personal experience from Europe. Class assignments are straightforward and easy enough yet they will push you out of you comfort zone and challenge your original thoughts. He is very understanding. Take him.

Took online Intro to International Relations with him last summer. Very accessible and easy to navigate his course in the canvas. He assigns interesting material that challenged my thinking comfort and helped me learn and become more critical thinker. I recommend him.

He is awesome!!! Very knowledgable, effective, and candid. He makes sense of politics and political science. You learn stuff that sticks with you. Honest effort and hard work is requested for A grade. No lazy-bones.

One of the worst instructors Ive ever had. I specifically chose him because of all the positive reviews I read . His classes consist of him reading from a PowerPoint the entire time. He is one of the toughest graders and doesnt properly explain how he want the assignment done yet expects you to do them exactly to his standards. Avoid taking him!!

Took professor Gutaj class at SLCC. BEST CLASS EVER! he is amazing! He always has time for questions He gives you a study guide for all the tests if you study you will do amazing You have four tests questions consist multiple choice definitions and a short essay but you can do your essay at home there is one research paper very easy. NO BOOK NEEDED
Simply THE BEST!!! Great lectures, extremely smart, and very personable.

Gutaj is an amazing instructor loves what he does, and is very clear what he wants from you, if you want an A come to class a lot of it is based on his lectures. He has the book as a requirement, simply for reading nothing to better understand the next topic. 4 tests and 1 research paper.  you will do fine if you show up, get involved and listen.

Professor Gutaj is AMAZING! I highly recommend taking his class. I loved every second of it. I am a Political Science major, this was my very first POLS class and I am more in love than ever with the major I chose. Excellent and fun lectures! He is so clear you will think is an easy class but actually is the way he teaches which make it enjoyable.
Best professor I've ever had, hands down. He is very knowledgable and passionate about his teachings. If you make an effort to do the work and turn it in on time, you will get an A.
Excllent professor. Take his class.
I feel lucky to have been able to be a student of his! He's great! Take his class, take his class, and oh take his class!

I am taking Comparative course with professor Gutaj. I was not sure if I wanted to take this class because I am not a Political Science major but I am so happy I did. The professor is awesome, very interesting lectures, excellent class discussions, and very clear what is expected. I am learning more than I ever thought I could. Great professor :)
Amazing professor. I highly recommend him for pols courses. I am already registered for another class of his.

Gutaj is very nice and intelligent. He is willing to help you do the best in the course. I liked his lectures and the analytical frameworks he presents in class. They truly help you see the world and society in a way that I never thought before. He has the ability to inspire you.
Loved loved this class. The professor is really nice and smart.

Professor Gutaj is exceptionally clever and stimulating. Gutaj has an excellent teaching style and is able to break down concepts in amazing fashion that will stay with you for a long time. He teaches with passion and you can see that he loves what he does.
Great prof.!!! Gutaj keeps things fresh and entertaining. Very smart prof. and you will learn a lot about politics in his class.

You will learn a ton on his class. He is very clear on what is going to be in the exams and clarifies everything for you beforehand. Make sure you attend his class as much as you can, take notes, and participate. He is willing to work with his students. Awesome prof.

Before i took Prof. Gutaj's class I had some knowledge about European politics, but after taking this class I can organize my thinking about politics in much easier way. Prof. Gutaj showed me how to best organize my thinking about European politics. Because of him, I am now much more confident studying politics. In short, Prof. Gutaj is awesome.

Before I took Prof. Gutaj's class, i did not know much about how politics and government works. Thanks to Prof. Gutaj, now, I can talk about politics, analyze politics, and form my educated opinion on different issues. Prof.  Gutaj is super smart and will help you get the best grade.

Prof. Gutaj is a great professor. His classes are student centered and not just some guy lecturing all class long. He has great class discussions which really enhance your ability to learn and understand the concepts. High recommended
He is awesome. I loved his class.

I am currently taking the American politics class from Prof. Gutaj at SLCC. The way he teaches this class and how he  is able to explain American government and politics by connecting to the wider field of politics makes it so interesting and fun to go to his class. He is super smart, very clear, and easy to work with. The best at SLCC so far.
Mr. Gutaj makes Political Science easy and fun to learn. He is knowledgable and very good professor.  I enjoyed the way he connects theory with real life situations and examples. I recommend him.
Mr. Gutaj is excellent. He is willing to help you get the best grade possible. Very smart and easy to get in touch with. He is one of the best I have met at the U so far.
Great teacher, great lectures. I would definitely take his class again. Take him and you will thank yourself for doing so.

Mr. Gutaj is an awesome professor. He delivers amazing lectures, he is very knowledgable, and very clear on the material he teaches. He has the ability to inspire his students within and beyond his class. He is awesome in helping you develop analytical and critical thinking and writing skills. I definitely recommend him.

Not very engaging in lecture, mostly just reads his notes and writes stuff down. Seems like he's just kind of an awkward and quiet guy. Exam difficulty is fair but the subject is inherently really hard.

Professor Gulotta is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject, but struggles to communicate with students. Many of the lectures are proof heavy, and you can learn a lot if you work to engage with the content, but this is often difficult. Easy to get good grades on all the exams if you complete the practice exams.

He know all the content himself however he sucks at communicating that with his students. Lectures were boring and he spent all his time showing the proof for each topic. Homework problems were difficult but tests were easy and very similar to practice tests.  You will get a good grade but won't learn anything.  Learning on your own is essential.
Good info but this professor is not super helpful outside or class or when you email. Hard to reach her

Gwen was great! Smart, helpful and a great professor. I would highly recommend this course. Go to class and study and you will do fine. She is not a tricky professor and the material and tests are very straightforward. It is not easy but it's interesting

Gwen was fabulous. Very well read and spoken about Pathophysiology. Had a great sense of humor. Explained things very well and by her lecture notes and learning activities you knew what she wanted you to focus on. I loved her and I loved this class. It was a lot of work, but attend lecture, read the chapters, and study your notes.

A great professor who is always available before and after class for questions. Super fun and helpful. She orients the lessons in a way to engage participation and practice conversation which is very helpful.

Mme. Lacroix is the most incredible French professor ever! She is so sweet, so understanding, and SO extremely helpful. She solely speaks french during class, but she slows it down so that it is easy to understand. The homework is very helpful to prepare for class, but it isn't overbearing. I would absolutely recommend her to anyone taking french!

Such an awesome teacher! I would highly recommend for french students to take from her. She is extremely patient, is easy on students when grading. She is from France so she totally understands that learning another language can be very discouraging. Willing to help students after class, and during class. Clear on what she expects.

This course took an online format and removed the only benefit, flexibility, by adding mandatory hours. It felt like a Zoom call that should've been an email. The structure was chaotic, feedback and concerns were ignored. I didn't learn the material so much as I developed survival skills. This professor needs to be evaluated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Was a really nice really helpful teacher than cared about her students but it was more difficult than the other Physics teachers and gave out a lot of busy work. I also struggled with the leture notes as they seemed busy to me. Great person, tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of effort, but is 4 credit hours. Tests have to be taken proctored in person. beware. The TAs were super helpful. Didn't watch most of her videos and just watched YouTube videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Hahn is passionate about physics and wants her students to succeed. The online homework doesn‘t reflect her exams but the paper homework does. She pretty much tells you exactly what will be on the exam which makes it easy to study for. An A in this class really isn‘t hard and she makes the learning easy too. You get 6 lecture drops too.

It is sad seeing the low ratings for Dr. Hahn. She is a great professor who keeps the class engaged with demonstrations. It is clear that she loves physics and wants to see her students succeed. There is homework that didn't always correlate to her exams, but it wasn't extremely time consuming to do. Understand paper homework, and you're set

This class was honestly a headache. You can tell Dr. Hahn cares about their students, but the class structure needs work. The paper homeworks are redundant and graded very harsh. The homeworks do not align with what is going to be on the exam. The final was unfair in my opinion. Take from rich if you can.

Physics is tough, but I felt very well cared for by Dr. Hahn. They really approach physics as something that is hard for everyone and will answer EVERY question you have during or outside of lecture. Utilize your TAs and Dr. Hahn outside of class and you'll succeed! Lecture & Discussion are filled with helpful groupwork. They also do fun demos!

Professor is Hahn overall a nice professor but her teaching could use some work. There is a big disconnection between lecture, exams, and HWs. You are expected to learn from the textbook. She once made an unsolvable exam question then did not give full points. However there is 3% of extra credit total in the course so you can make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor clearly cares about students and their learning. They give tons of extra credit and HW to buffer your grade. Exams are also graded fairly, and you are given the problems a few days before the exam. The exams are not super difficult, but sometimes were unrelated to course content. Overall, this course is built in your favor.

She seems nice but messed up a ton of times in lecture and on the tests. I ended up not studying much because she usually worded something wrong on the test and gave us credit for it anyway. Luckily there's lots of extra credit and plenty assignments that it is pretty easy to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While there are a lot of assignments due throughout the week this also means there are a lot of things cushioning your grades from exams. They also give you midterm scenarios in advance so you know exactly what concepts you need to study. Overall a caring professor who wants their students to succeed. They also do fun demonstrations in lecture!
They were able to explain the material in interesting and insightful ways. They clearly care about the students. Would highly recommend them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tons of homework (due almost every day of the week) and readings. If you can stay on top of everything you'll be ok, but it was too much for me personally. They have a lot of potential as a professor but are new and inexperienced and it shows. They also did not honor my accommodations, which was frustrating.

Dr. Hahn slips up quite a few times during lectures and tells us wrong info that we have to correct them on. Thus, some of the lectures are confusing and not that helpful. They offer a ton of extra credit and hand out scenario sheets that give you a decent idea of what will be on the exams. Hahn actually listens to class input to improve the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Though she does slip up, lectures are rarely that confusing if you simply read the book, and most of the TAs/LAs were very supportive and helpful. Large amounts of extra credit are offered and partial credit is extremely easy to get. There were a lot of assignments, but they were usually not that hard (only some of the online homeworks were).

Make sure to buy Excedrin by the bulk for this 16 week headache of a class.I genuinely believe this can be a good class if things change, but this for me it was a huge mess. TAs, LAs, & even students have had to correct her during lecture. Hopefully this changes in the future, but until reviews are better take this at SLCC or from another U prof.

Very easy class. The scenarios are given to you days before the test and they give a lot of partial credit. There is a lot of homework but that isn't the professor's decision (same for all physics classes). Professor Hahn is available for study hall and has always taken the time to explain things to me in a way that I can understand. Great Class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hahn is obviously a very caring person, but I would not recommend this class. The lectures themselves are not helpful, and I have learned more from the TAs then I have from the main lecture. I would probably learn the same amount if it were just an online class. The study guides for midterms are not helpful. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The TA's and LA's are really the ones teaching this course. We go more over scenarios and not how to actually use the equations given to us.Also, using canvas seems to be a struggle for them because the due dates are constantly needed to be changed, because they were put in wrong the first time.

I would never recommend taking this class from Professor Hahn. They seem nice but they are thoroughly unhelpful. The class structure makes concepts so much more difficult, and quizzes on readings are due night before lectures. I feel like I've taught myself physics this entire semester. The TA's are more helpful when it comes to learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: "Class is self-taught, lectures useless for homework/tests, but attendance mandatory. Regrade requests for lost points on correct steps is useless as nothing changes, despite her encouragement. Homework doesn't correlate with lectures/exams. Wait for other options, if possible. Overall, class lacks cohesion and is much harder than expected.

Professor Hahn is a good professor and I have learned a lot so far. She gives you many opportunities to get a good grade. The class feels a little too structured for me personally, but it's just a different style of teaching than I am used to. I'm sure it works well for others.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: At a minimum one assignment due every single night, including weekends and on test days. Often the HW does not correlate with discussions and in class lectures, seemingly jumping ahead in material. Obviously a very new teacher which is unfortunate as she is trying, but the expectations and requirements for this class is ridiculous. Do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I tried to think about something positive to start with... I can't. I get she is new, and I can tell she has a good heart, but she simply shouldn't be teaching. I have yet to learn a single thing from her lectures, and she is so so so unconfident when answering students questions. Her TA's were very useless as well. Really just a rough semester.

Professor Hahn cares about her students very much. She is reasonable and willing to work out any issues that may arise. The other ratings are from students who just want an easy A. You should realize that it'll be a challenging course considering it's physics. The class is structured similarly to physics 1 where you read the book before class.

awful. Students ask questions in class and she never has an answer. So many "ums" and "ahs" in her sentences, you can hardly follow what she's saying. Expects you to teach yourself from reading rather than coming to class, but you earn in-class points requiring you to attend her pointless lectures. Do not recommend.

Lots and lots of busywork that is irrelevant to the material we are learning. It's hard to understand what she's asking for on tests. The TAs seem like they don't know what's going on most of the time. Nice person, I get she's a new professor, but definitely not the greatest.

She does a terrible job writing questions, so they are vague and unclear. She refuses to cover material she feels you should have picked up during the readings. All of her students have begged her to go through practice problems, but she doesn't go step by step. Instead she quizzes you on each step and you lose points if you get it wrong (pop quiz)

reviews.comment: Super nice teacher, lecture weekly videos are just long

Dr. Halladay is super nice and engaging. She rarely posts her lectures on Canvas though so make sure to attend class. Assignments were very straightforward and not hard. If you need help she is more than willing to work with you. Would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's funny, nice, and willing to work with students. The terms and requirements can be unclear at first, but the exams are open-note and rely more on understanding the concepts than on answering super-dense questions. She is very proud of her research, so treat her with some respect, and you'll be her best friend.

Dr. Halladay was pretty good. The only complaint I have is that she did not post lectures/content until Monday or Tuesday of every week. The lectures are long, but interesting. There are 4 exams, a final project (genogram + reflection), and discussion boards every week. Overall, this was a pretty good class.

The prof was very engaging with the class and her lectures were straight forward and entertaining. You do write a pretty good amount but nothing too crazy and she's an easy grader. Usually has things due by the end of the week at midnight. For quizzes, make sure you go to class! The quizzes go off of the lectures which she doesn't post on canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors ever!

Dr. Halladay is such a wonderful professor! It is incredibly evident that she is passionate about the topics she teaches which makes the material much easier to learn. The workload is very manageable - there is a large assignment required, but it is broken down into 3 parts which makes it much less daunting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. H is one of the kindest and most genuine professors I've had. She is so approachable and understanding. And beyond that, she is passionate about her course material which is something I find very important. I could not recommend her enough!

Amazing professor! The topics were so interesting and she really cares about your own success and development. The work is pretty chill, there was a big project but that was broken down making it easier. She gave reviews for the exams which was nice and weekly discussion posts. Highly recommend if you're interested in trauma.
One of if not the best professors I have ever had!

Dr. Halladay is the first professor I've had that changed the course trajectory due to students wanting something different. She creates a collaborative learning environment and truly wants to set you up for success as a professional, not just a student. Warning ahead of time: the course content is HEAVY (trauma), so give yourself time to breathe.
Amazing professor. Only had 9 assignments the entire semester and 2 exams. Very simple and straight to the point.

At times this course can be structured poorly, but for a gen ed, its fine. This class is pretty interesting and I would definitely recommend if you're looking for something easy and fun. There is one assignment per week, and on average I would say the assignments took about an hour-two. Exams are directly based on assignments, so pay attention

Not a difficult course, but he insists on publishing the assignments himself every week and often publishes them late or not at all. We missed about 3 weeks and he had to take questions off of the final exam because no one had access to the reading or assignments. A fairly easy class, one assignment a week, he's just sort of unreliable.
His class was fun and easy. Just listen in class.
Great professor! I missed the first test and he let me do another term paper for 80 extra points and went from 45% to a 90%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was not hard, but some assignments can be time consuming. You have to watch a live play at some point but that isn't bad. The Professor has clear instructions however, it can be hard to reach him. The tests are a big part of the grade, but they are not too hard as long as you just read what the assignments told you to. I would not worry.

Assignments are easy, but tests can be confusing. Overall decent gen ed course. I would recommend as a gen ed, as it wasn't too time-consuming, just make sure you do the one big assignment of going to see a play.

Love the class and the work I did, only bad thing is the tests can be confusing because he switches up the wording. He does this so no one can cheat but it can make it confusing. Besides that everything else is easy work.

This class is deceiving, it may look like a light-hearted, easy-going, snatch an arts credit class, but the tests are where you will suffer the most. The weekly assignments are easy to complete as you just read the assigned readings and complete the assignment as you go, but the tests after each unit he scrambles the words and makes it so confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this course online. For someone who isn't a fan of theater the class was "enjoyable" and the homework assignments were easy (there's one due every Sunday). The only annoying thing is he doesn't provide a very clear rubric for the assignments or papers. Would recommend if you need the credit.

This class was okay, it could be better though. I think tests are a BIG part of your grade. I did all the assignments with a 100%, but then the test came about and it dropped 6% for the first test. The wording on the test was confusing to me, but theyre open everything. Just have to find the correct way to read the question I guess.

I would die for this man. This is one of my favorite classes ever, not an easy A if you dont have an acting background but if you do its a great way to build skills. But you wont lose sleep over the class, its a great one to get that fine arts credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hanson was my introduction to Theatre, and I got incredibly lucky to have him. He tries hard to make the class non-stressful and supports positive behavior. Anyone wanting to take a fine arts credit should look for him to sign up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hugh is great, and the class is fairly easy. The key is to do all of the readings, the tests focus on the readings more than anything else. I would definitely recommend this class to anyone who is looking to get an easy general credit while actually learning something.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Take this class! Minimal reading, only one assignment due per week, one paper, and two (online) exams throughout the whole semester. Prof. Hanson emphasizes to keep your assignments short, too, so they're really easy to do. This is a great, easy, and interesting class to fulfill your FF credit.

Hugh is a warm guy and fun to talk to. Unfortunately he really loves talking so a lot of the time was spent just talking rather than actually doing theatre games and working on our acting. I liked him and the class but there is a lot of room for improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Took the class as a fall intensive. I wasn't very interested in the topic, but I really enjoyed the topic the way Hugh taught it. It's not a whole ton of work, as he understands most people taking the class was just to get the fine arts requirement. He knew everybody's name and was very understanding of any situations that came up. Would take again

He takes forever to grade, the articles are insanely boring, and he never responds to your emails. If you read the assignments you will be fine for the exams, BUT his exams are worded very weirdly and sometimes more than one answer seems appropriate. I could care less about theatre and this class didn't help with that.

Hugh does a good job of providing well versed, in depth, feedback while helping you understand the larger picture and  the underlying purpose of this class. The material is laid out properly and cleanly with no surprise exam questions not found in your text. If you complete your reading and participate you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Interesting class, but the professor is unorganized. Test questions were worded strangely or vaguely.
Super easy online class! I took it for an art gen ed credit.

Trent's FILM3945 class was hard, but rewarding. It was lecture-heavy, but they were so informative and useful that I didn't mind. Don't understand the bad reviews; he's an extremely knowledgeable guy with fair and useful feedback on projects. Unwillingness to use Canvas is annoying, but no assignments are turned in on Canvas, so it's not that bad.

I think most people only review when they had a bad experience. It doesn't represent Trent on the whole. He is an amazing teacher and person. A legend in his field who gives you the fundamental toolkit to understand how to make independent film. He cares about the important stuff. A passionate, giving soul.

Trent only grades based on his niche opinions about what he likes and doesn't like. His lectures are never-ending speeches about his own work in the past as well as his thoughts on other people's work. He never explains why he likes something or not, he only says, "good job" or "this is wrong." I cannot believe that he is still being paid to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Full of so much knowledge that he just wants to share. Take advantage of his class and his experience.

Unclear expectations and becomes very abrasive when misunderstood. For someone so particular, he does not seem very interested in offering further clarification/help. Makes you feel like a burden for even asking. Gets caught up on format and will give no merit elsewhere if that isn't perfect. Will not use CANVAS which limits many useful resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Trent Harris is a great life teacher. If you're looking for a by-the-book professor, look elsewhere. Harris is concerned students have the right outlook and adopt habits beyond what textbooks can teach. He made accommodations for me, met me outside of class, and genuinely cared about my learning. He is a great, albeit non-traditional, professor!

Very lecture heavy, and very unclear on what he wants from students. Said he's not a teacher, and I can attest that teaching is not his forte. Very unorganized, left me with more questions than answers. Hardly any practice. If your format isn't right, he ignores your script and has you redo it. Only thing emphasized is premise. Doesn't teach format
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not very organized. Lectures are basic, so most learning is done via reading. Only gives two assignments, which provides very little room for practice and growth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Haber has been one of the best teachers I've ever been lucky enough to encounter. I entirely loved his class, and if I could major in it I would. Excellent, kind, caring teacher who wants students to succeed. Could not recommend him enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: SUPER Awesome professor! I had him for both deductive logic and Philosophy of Biology (although the course codes were not available for me to click on). His grading is not standard, but works well for learning, and he explains it well in class. He is a great guy that cares about the students and listens to them as if his own peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Haber is a great professor. He truly cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He pushes students to do their best and achieve further steps in whatever it is they are doing. Take a class from Haber!!
Have you ever seen Parks and Recreation? Professor Haskins is basically Leslie Knope. If that sounds good to you, take this class. But it's too much for most people.

While I would have liked the class to focus more on the concepts, and less on the math, Jessica is both a fair grader and will do what she can to help you understand the material if you give her the chance. She clearly cares for the material and the students and goes above and beyond to try and give as much information as possible to learn from.

Sort of losing my faith in her class, there's a lot of information overload that she doesn't seem to be able to figure out a way to manage. She is really nice but the way she explains material is so rapid pace that it's hard to keep track. Not really sure what could be done to improve.

Dr. Haskins was a great professor overall throughout the semester. The class structure felt unstable and odd. I lowered my rating because today, the class was curved down from the original grading scale at the start of the semester. This raised the bar to get an A from 92% to 94%, which is very annoying to have changed after the semester ended.

Professor Henderson always came to class prepared to give entertaining and informative lectures. The class structure was predictable and consistent (regular lecture each Monday, short quiz each Wednesday). Quizzes/exams were graded leniently, in a timely manner, and with helpful feedback. I would highly recommend Professor Henderson for CS3100.

Expects you pay attention/do the readings, which is a surprisingly high bar these days. Perhaps not the greatest people skills, but he's very expressive, funny, and knowledgeable. I always enjoy the lectures.
He's genuinely really funny and a great teacher. Everyone's being a stick in the mud about him but he's easily one of the best professors in the entire college of Computer Science.

Had Prof Henderson for Capstone. He doesn't give feedback specific to your project, he just says negative things about what he's seen from others and assumes you also made those mistakes. Gets mad if you're even one minute late to his Zoom meeting. Didn't say one nice thing to our team the entire semester.

Tom is an interesting professor. You can tell he's very knowledgeable, but he rambles a lot, and takes very confusing approaches to explaining concepts instead of being direct and concise. The textbook is vital if you want to know what any concepts mean, but that doesn't always mean it's how Tom wants you to learn it. Fairly lenient grader though.

Pros: 
Responds to emails at the speed of light
Fast grader 
Funny lectures 
Good textbook

Cons
Confusing slides and lectures
Quizzes are extremely hard to study for and I found them really difficult 
You have to email him to find your grades
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tom is a great professor, and very approachable and helpful about homework and quizzes. No true exams, just weekly quizzes and monthly homeworks that are graded leniently. 3100 is hard, but between the textbook and lectures it's more than possible to get a handle and Tom is very helpful in-person and in-email to truly understand.
Goes over things very quickly and expects you to have a very good understanding. Quizzes are pretty tough and the wording on them and the assignments are usually confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are terrible, with slides that are merely clumsy excerpts from the textbook. Attending class adds little value beyond reading the textbook, yet attendance is mandatory.

Professor Henderson is a great guy. Like others have said, he uses technical terms that can be hard to follow, but he makes up for this by being extremely accessible outside of class and very quick to respond to emails. I thought he graded fairly, considering this was a theory class and most of the questions on HW and tests were open ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He refused to use canvas and instead created MATLAB code that you had to download and manually input your grades to figure out your grade. The code was bugged. I didn't know my grade until the last week of the semester. Quizzes every week are nothing like his lectures, as his lectures are completely ripped from the textbook. Avoid at all costs.

The class was great and the material interesting. My one complaint would be that Prof Henderson has a tendency to use a lot of technical terms that can make things tough to follow. Sometimes it felt like asking him a question resembled taking a drink from a fire hydrant, but he would address every question and was glad to answer follow up questions
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unrealistic sized assignments that he expects you to take 10 hours a week to complete, but is easier 40 hours a week if you are learning the material for the first time correctly. Also doesn't care about what you think when answering a question, only what he thinks is correct and that matters, even though he never set clear expectations. Stay away.

To be short, he has high expectations and the homework can be time-consuming and challenging. That being said, he is very conscious of the limits of his students and is super engaging / helpful. He rewards effort in general and provides numerous extra credit opportunities. I really wish I had him for my other required classes!

He knew a great deal about the subject. He used theory as well as code to explain what the differences are. I would've liked to code everything on my own but he gave all the code and insisted of analysis so that was unexpected. I definitely gained knowledge out of this class. Although my grade was just above average, this was a good class

This is probably the worst professor I have ever encountered. He requires his students to make elaborate unnecessary arguments in assignments. Project proposal for a course project has ridiculous requirements and needs to be formatted with all sorts of nonsense. This guy is the epitomy of lots of process and very little content. AVOID
Professional conduct is VERY poor. Henry's language is peppered with extreme profanity. He never provides a rubric before assignments or clear instructions for what is required in an assignment.

Henry is a good professor, but he is terrifying and demanding. He will give you excellent feedback (with consideration and care), but he will never be satisfied with your work. Get ready to become a perfectionist and most likely minimize your persona. Great professor, but he can become intimidating but in a good way at some point.

Henry is extremely skilled and knowledgeable and genuinely cares about your career. He can be abrasive but he's much more interested in seeming intimidating than actually being intimidating. You will not regret any time spent in his class, and if you can't handle him you should consider a different career.

Class might seem intimidating at first but as long as you stay on top of your work and put in the effort, you will do just fine! It is crucial to show improvement from the first assignment to the last but overall, he is great at giving feedback and willing to take some extra time to answer questions if you need!

I got more out of his classes than my others combined and the more you put in the more you get out. He is super willing to give extra help. I would even see him helping any of my classmates out with assignments for other classes. His classes are challenging in a positive way and you often get a chance for a better grade than the first critique.
Henry is someone everyone should aspire to learn from. I highly recommend taking a class with him

Henry gives good feedback, that's about it. Other than that, he is a horrible teacher. At times he is bias and subjective. He will say one thing and then change it during critique. He will say another thing and change it on the assignment page. If you mention this, he will argue with you and drag on the time until you admit you are wrong.
This is my first time writing on this website and i must say! He was awesome! So laid back and so chill! Never had a teacher so cool!

He was and awesome professor reopend some assignments for me at the end of the semester if you show you care he will work with you to get the grade you want hes an amazing professor. Definitely take him even if you arent a pysch major.

He was the best professor I have had! Attending lectures made exams easier, he gives lots of hints. I also found that either attending or re watched exam reviews he posts is extremely helpful as he provides specific review and even more hints. Plenty of extra credit, and he cares!

Great professor. He is very caring and understanding. However, exams can be difficult/confusing if you don't put a lot of effort into the homework and class. Take notes on the lectures, he gives a lot of hints for upcoming exams.
This teacher is spectacular. He's both Entertaining and engaging. Amazing professor I would definitely recommend his class.
The best professor I've had by far! He sets you up for perfect success and is super understanding and genuinely acts like he cares for his students. Would highly recommend taking a class from him!

Genuinely the best professor i've ever had, his lectures were entertaining and easy to follow, but also not mandatory as he posted all the lecture slides on canvas prior to class. The tests were very do-able, and consisted of only material we learned in class.
he's awesome. gives lots of extra credit.

Micheal is an awesome professor. Really nice and helpful gen-ed class or a start for your psych degree. Be ready to read because 4 midterms and an optional final are based on that, and he offered a lot of help, materials, extra credits so it's not hard to be successful in this class. Go to his lectures, they're super good and interesting.

He was nice, easy to listen to, and structured a course that was easy to understand, even in a room of 400+ people. I never got to know him on a more personal level than just listening to him and speaking to him here and there, but he was awesome, and made psych make sense, would take again, love this guy.
Love this professor, so funny and so passionate about pysch
Great professor, very passionate about pyshcology
This professor is very good and knowledgeable in the topics. I would highly recommend especially if this is your first Psych class

Himle was a great professor for Intro to Psych. The class itself is pretty surface level, but he goes into detail on quite a lot of stuff and makes lectures themselves pretty engaging. There's quite a bit of extra credit opportunities throughout, tests are a big part of the grade but if you actually study for even a bit you'll be just fine.

Such a fantastic professor-most people take it for a gen ed, and he explains things at a base level so everyone understands no matter their previous knowledge. Fantastic lectures, so much to learn and really well explained. Would absolutely take again.

Professor Himle's lectures were very engaging, and he provided many examples to help understand topics better. He was clearly very passionate about the subject. Offers a lot of extra credit, and uses a points system for grading. He only keeps four exams and offers five, which means that you can either replace a score or not take the final.

He was such an amazing professor, he offered so much extra credit and was super understanding with extensions. His lectures are super interesting and if you go to class regularly you will definitely get an A.

Professor Himle was so engaging and had incredible lectures. The tests were hard if you didn't read the textbook outside of class, but assignments were easy and there were lots of opportunities for extra credit.
i love you

Professor Himle is a really fun teacher, he talks in-depth about each chapter and will make you enjoy psychology. Very little homework and all exams are open note. There are many ways to earn extra credit and he uses funny real-life examples during his lectures. Overall, would 100% take his class again, he makes you LOVE psychology.

Professor Himle brought a very personal touch to his lectures a drew in every person in the lecture hall. Great subject matter and not too much homework. Engaging lectures and assignments, but grading scale was kind of confusing because it is out of 500. Tests are all open note and open book, not too difficult.

He is so caring about that topic and will make anyone interested in learning more about it. He was amazing in teaching thoroughly and making sure that everyone understood the objectives. He offers multiple forms of extra credit and is a very fun guy in general. He will involve funny real-life scenarios in his lectures.

I was always so excited to go to lectures, this class didn't feel like school. He knows how to make the lectures extremely engaging. I'm blown away by his ability to make this class so easy to get an A but still learn so much. He made the material very relevant to our own lives. I know I will remember everything taught in this class going forward.

Professor Himle was hands down the BEST professor. Super funny guy and a great teacher, he actually taught the information and didn't just read from the slides. No homework other than a few assignments and exams, and everything is open book. He also gives tons of extra credit work. Easy to pay attention in class because it's interesting stuff.

Michael Himle was an outstanding teacher! There is no homework other than recommendations to read the textbook before the class begins (not mandatory). The lectures are super funny and engaging. There are quizzes every 3-4 weeks but everything's open book/note. (TAKE ADVANTAGE OF EXTRA CREDIT! I finished the class with a 106% because of it.)

This professor is amazing! He did a great job teaching clearly and clearing up all the concepts in the textbook that were the most difficult. He gave a lot of extra credit quizzes on the readings so that we were motivated to complete them. He made it manageable to succeed in his class!

Such a great professor! He taught so well during his lectures and I honestly loved learning about psychology in his class. He is very laid back and there is basically no homework only 1 weekly quiz and it's super easy. Offers 50 extra credit points that raise your grade so much, DO THE EXTRA CREDIT (i finished with 102% in the class bc of it)

Prof Himle was awesome. All exams were open book and he had tons of extra credit. Interesting lectures that  make you want to go to class. I have nothing bad to say about him. Excellent professor and excellent class.
Easy class. Open note tests. I went to class sometimes and found it interesting. Take for an easy A.
