I love this teacher, he was so easy going, i never went to class but reading the chapters and taking quizzes were more than enough to maintain a good grade, he is lenient and provides extra credit through the whole semester. Very caring and nice.
So easy. There are 4 exams and a quiz every week but you can find the answers all online. I never read the texbook. Take for easy credit.

Professor Himle is amazing! I really enjoyed his psych 1010 class, he made his lectures fun to listen to and I didn't get bored often. There is a lot of reading, but it's not too bad. There are quizzes and tests but if you pay attention and take notes you'll be fine. Overall, I really liked this class and I would take another with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professors Himle is engaging and passionate about his work. I enjoy attending his lectures even though attendance is not mandatory. I would highly recommend his classes.

Such a fun easy class, more about doing the work (which can all be found online). You get unlimited tries on weekly quizzes (which is mostly all the assignments), exams are easy and open book, discussions are only a couple of paragraphs. Great class, do the work and you'll get an A! He is also very attentive and available via email- take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really loved learning from Dr. Himle. He is relatable, easy-going, and the structure was predictable. Behavior modification is such a fascinating topic, and he made it interesting. You will need to read the textbook but it's a fairly enjoyable experience if you can make it part of your routine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really loved taking a class with mike! Super fun guy really understanding with grades. Very engaging and really nice. Definitely would like to take a class w him again.
Great teacher

Everything in textbook, easy to read, fascinating material, learn alot. Tests are fair/just, if understand will do really well. Option final, drops lowest test, 4 research hours, launchpad quizzes. Cares if ppl understand content. Lecture similar to book, but explains concepts as real world, loves questions and super useful. Favorite class by far.

He is a fabulous teacher! His lectures are not mandatory but I never miss his class because it's so informational and he applies it to the real world. He also loves to crack jokes and make us laugh which makes it feel more personal even though there is like 300 students. He makes it easy to understand and is an awesome prof. Definitely recommend!!!

This class is a little harder than a breeze, but very interesting!  He is a great teacher and I learned so much!  The tests are hard; you do need to study for them.  And you need to read from the online text book and do the online quizzes.  Also you have to participate in research outside of class.  I barely scraped an A through extra credit.

Makes class interesting and fun. Quizzes online through the textbook. Book is online, however, I recommend also having a hard copy. Passionate about what he teaches, so goes off on tangents often, but they're related. There is a lot of information covered in this class, so attend class to further understand the topics. If you read, you'll be fine.

Himle's class structure is beautiful: you can come to lectures - or not - as no credit is based on attendance, 5 or 6 days are reserved for exams throughout the semester (in the syllabus, so you'll know ahead of time), extra credit is offered, and an optional final can replace your lowest exam/fill in for one you missed. Cool guy, great teacher.

This class was tough for me because the tests had a major effect on my grade the professor does give 30 points extra credit which helped my grade a lot and you will have to read a lot but overall an interesting class. Also must do 4 hours of research and mastery quizzes from book to get points.

Good introductory course. I am not a psych major, and took this course to fulfill a GenEd requirement. Nevertheless, it was an interesting class. The class itself is straightforward. Attend lectures, read the textbooks, and take the exams. The final is optional, which is really nice.

This professor is one of my favorite teachers i've ever had. He prepares you well for his tests cause his lectures are so entertaining. He really relates to the younger kids cause he's so cool and young. This class really isn't that hard as long as you listen to the lectures and study by using the textbooks. I would take this class again if i could

This class is my favorite I've taken. Lectures were extremely interesting and Dr. Himle did a great job explaining the material. Reading the textbook is required to pass the tests, but they're easy if you do.

Difficult to ace exams without reading, but usually just reading through the chapter is enough. Offers lots of extra credit. Lectures are really interesting and make you think. Respects students. One of my favourite profs.

Professor Himle is enthusiastic, knows the material really well, is fun and friendly, and gives tons of real life examples of topics covered in class. I read the book, did LearningCurve exercises and got an A on all five exams. He even gives 50 extra credit points! I would definitely recommend this professor to anyone. This class improved my life!
I took his class a few semesters ago, but he was so awesome that I feel inclined to leave a message here. He's hilarious, clear, and makes psychology interesting. I wish I could take his class again.

AMAZING! He is funny, respectful and passionate about this subject. He's incredible. He takes what we learn in class and applies it to the real world. He's very open and makes it clear he is available for questions. Lecture is not required, but are super helpful as well as entertaining. I recommend taking his class!

He is very clear in his lectures, the final is optional and he offers a lot of extra credit.  I had no prior psychology knowledge and was able to get an A easily. I recommend this professor to anyone that needs to take psychology.

Professor Himle is about as good as they get.  He's funny, he's very knowledgeable about his field, he's super approachable, and he really does keep you interested in the material.  Attendance isn't mandatory, and if you just read the book and the lectures that he posts online then you don't even need to go to class.  But you'll want to.
Great teacher. Very engaging and compelling. Really clear too, and he's pretty funny. He'll listen to your comments or questions. Definitely one of my favorites.

He is an amazing teacher and he gives a ton of extra credit. If you do good on all that test you don't have to take the final. It's your choice. He made me actually want to go to class and presented the material in a way that kept you interested in what he was saying.

Professor Himle is awesome. I'd never taken psych before this class, and he made me love it. He makes everything really clear, and gives tons of examples to explain everything. Take this class, it's the best.

Professor Himle is the best. He makes psychology very interesting and keeps the class wanting to learn. Reading the textbook and going over the slides is VERY important. Take his class, you'll LOVE psychology.
Read your book carefully, remember the details as many as you can. You will get an easy A
Good teacher who makes a class that could be very boring very fun.  class is not required but definitely very helpful

Great, GREAT professor! Very clear in his lectures and is entertaining to listen to. He engages the class also and makes sure everything is understood. The text book is also very easy to read and follow.

Even with a class of over 200 students he keeps you very engaged! It's a great class and he's very helpful. Not a lot of one-on-one time with the teacher but it's not really necessary! He makes things very clear during lecture. The textbook is AMAZING too. I loved this course.
Great dynamic teacher! He is funny and very clear in everything he teaches.
Hi mista Michael

Michael is a very kind and helpful professor. He's very willing to help students and is pretty chill. The projects in class were very imaginative and fun. He also made us do class drawing exercises that related to the current project. The class atmosphere was great since he's so kind and easily approachable. I recommend taking his classes!
Michael was an absolute delight for my illustration degree, he was witty and cared deeply for his work and the work of his students.

Best professor I've had in five years of university! I've taken 3 of his classes, all have been great. He's gives the best critique feedback and is purely focused on being helpful for the students. He is also open to feedback in terms of class structure. Its a lot of homework but its all very constructive.
Super nice and chill professor. A few essays, nothing other than maybe an assignment once a week. You get four skips for the semester. Would recommend for a Gen Ed.
Aly covered the subject material in COMM 1270 in a fairly engaging way. Her personal experience in the field made for super interesting commentary as well.

Aly is a student instructor who acts like knowledgeable professor. Lectures consist of a lot of information, but she ensures we're following along and is very caring. Attendance and participation matters as it has a major effect on your grade. There aren't many assignments and they're pretty easy to complete.

Biodesign is a strange class, especially the second semester focusing on the device. You could barely interact with the instructors and do well, but Bob is one of the few I love talking to. Very passionate, very helpful, and does his best to guide you. But please reach out to Micah, he will be by far the most help on any of these projects!

Dr. Hitchcock has a very different background from most professors and it shows. He is incredibly passionate about design, and is very helpful to students who have questions. He is incredibly busy outside of class, but when he is able to help, he can offer great guidance. His lectures are also quite fun even if they have some useless information

Bob is very helpful and incredibly personable. He is one of the few professors that went out of his way to know my name and remember it after I had spoken to him just a couple times. He is always willing to help and answer any dumb questions you have. He can ask really tough questions during design reviews, but they all can really.

As long as you pay attention in class and do the readings, you'll pass. Sometimes go over the readings in class, read them or at least scan them or else the class is really quiet and awkward. Reading quizzes can make or break your grade as well as 2 essays. I found his lectures somewhat interesting, you can tell he cares about what he teaches.

not a terrible professor, but very lecture heavy and it gets very boring. graded off of two essays and two tests and a million reading quizzes (none of which i would do the readings for lol whoops) i would recommend to just read it all though because it dropped my grade a lot. his grading is also somewhat strict but reasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Hinderaker gives some of the best lectures I've had in college. He has a very good understanding of history and its implications. He translates this to students very well. As for the class structure its pretty simple with minimal assignments. The readings are not super long but a decent length. Most are pretty interesting to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's knowledgeable in his lectures and has lots of textbook resources. He's easy to contact but not clear in his feedback or support. Canvas is not organized well, modules are hard to follow. He's a tough grader, hardly ever gives 100% on assignments. His instructions are often unclear and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is an average professor, however his canvas is highly disorganized, no assignments can be found in one place. He's nit-picky about grading and offers vague unhelpful feed back when contacted for help. His required readings are extensive and his lectures can be rather dull. (Almost always requires multiple textbooks)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is very intelligent and well spoken. His lectures are interesting and also easy to understand. He seems somewhat disinterested in his students and teaching. Defiantly would recommend if you can handle reading and like early American history.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy. Is not excited to teach. He grades you on 3 things over the whole semester and if you mess up on one your grade is screwed. He invites you to meet with him if you have problems but does nothing to resolve them. He is not easy to work with and he expects way too much on his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hindracker is pretty cool and his lectures are interesting. He gave us a big research essay to write with a word count of 1500 to 2000 words. I turned in an 1100 word essay and he gave me an A because he could tell I did my research and it was well written.

EXCELLENT teacher. Although he's busy, he made time to help me with my essay before class. He is very understanding of student's needs,  he's funny & clear about his expectations. His expertise is the 1700-1800's. I'm taking another class of his because I loved his teaching style. Focuses most on critical thinking rather than dates. Fav professor.

He is very knowledgeable about his subject and is a fair grader. There is a lot of reading in this class but only 2 papers. Even though this class was on Colonial America, he spends more time teaching about everything before Colonial times which was kind of annoying. He has a very complex vocabulary so you may need to look up some things he says.
Fantastic professor who is completely on top of things. He expects the class to do the readings and challenges them to think, but is very helpful when needed. Clear, interesting, and reliable.
The class was interesting.  He wants the students to get beyond facts and into the meaning of events.  Grading was based on online comment-posting and essay tests.
Great guy. Lectures get a bit boring, but overall he is funny and very helpful.

Great class! His tests and the required papers were fair, but thorough. His lectures and PowerPoints were interesting. Overall, this was a captivating and informative course if students were willing to do the reading. While it was a demanding class, it was a rewarding class.  Poor performance in this class is a reflection of the student only.

Eric is a great guy.  He tries to engage his students by making them _think_ about what history means rather than memorizing a sequence of events. He's very busy (department chair) but still makes time to help; his door is always open.  He's a non-traditional lecturer - visual material, films, etc. Doesn't put up with crap, which is a good thing.

I had to get help from one of the History professors at SLCC becuase his class was so hard and unclear and he was no help when I had questions.  His tests were ridiculously hard and covered nothing that he'd taught in class. He skipped teaching anything about the Civil War and Pearl Harbor. His class and his teaching pretty much sucked. Don't do it

I enjoyed this class. However, it would take her MONTHS to grade assignments. One of my first projects due in her class wasn't graded for 2.5 months. Then she marked me down for the Zoom links expiring. Some weeks were very heavy, and others were very light. It was fun doing heavy research into my business idea though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She really knows how to teach and ways to make hands-on assignments in class to help students learn. She makes you talk with classmates and work together. The mid-term and final are definitely pretty challenging, but if u pay attention in class and listen very well, you will be fine. Not too much homework and no essays/presentations.
Great teacher. Great class!

Prof. Herrick is very experienced. The assignments are more than manageable, just for your own good, make yourself read every chapter and watch the videos. Take the midterm and final at the proctoring center, no matter how stron you think your home internet connection is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best professors that I had. She made it easy to follow along in class and gave you plenty of class time to complete your assignments. I would highly recommend her!!

Professor Heidi is an engaging and knowledgeable instructor. While the work can be challenging, she provides great feedback and is dedicated to helping students succeed. Unstuck study was a game-changer for preparing for quizzes and exams. Highly recommend taking this course with her.

I loved this professor! I had a couple of problems throughout this semester and she would always be able to help me, or if she wasn't her TA could! Her tests can be pretty difficult, but with curves and other assignments its all good. Her TA also looked over my big paper at the end and was able to give me feedback before it was due.
Professor Herrick was very good at making every student feel seen. The course content wasn't too hard, and she made it a lot easier.

She's the best professor I had this semester! She's really open to business discussions in class and loves talking one-on-one with you.The homework load isn't that crazy & the exams are pretty difficult, so make sure to study and attend her office hours. Amazing feedback on assignments. She's amazing and I wouldn't take this course without her!
Really nice and helpful but cares a little too much about a freshman business class. Would still recommend

One of the best professors I've taken. Midterm and final were open note and she always let us out of her 3 hour lecture an hour early. Course load is perfect with just a couple assignments every week. Grading is a little stricter but as long as you make sure to stick to the rubric you'll be good. Course expectations are always really clear.

Prof. Herrick is a great professor! She has very clear expectations. ALWAYS READ RUBRIC! She is willing to help you improve your work outside of class. Her TAs do not always do a good job grading or replying. Sometimes grades are knit-picky. She expects 110% effort on everything.
Dense lectures, lengthy assignments, hidden EC, hard work pays off

A horrible exprience. She decides to punish the whole class since somebody cheated. Other professor also found cheating in their class but they did not take this action. Instead of punishing the cheaters, she punished the whole class. It seems like something that happens in high school, not in college. DO NOT TAKE HER! SHES SO PETTY.
Very fair grader. As long as you show up and do your work you'll be successful. She's very supportive and if you have questions she gets back to you quickly.

Professor Heidi is incredibly knowledgeable and capable, with fantastic experience. She has a degree from Oxford! Great professor, and even though lectures are long, if you listen intentionally, you will learn from this class and do just fine on quizzes and tests. I connected with her despite the class being over 100 people.

This class wasn't as suited for me as I had hoped (I am in STEM), I was often confused by the grading and about what the assignments should be about. It's easy to get stuck with a project you really don't care about in this class so watch out. She is really good at responding to emails and generally a captivating lecturer, overall a good professor.

Heidi is seriously such an amazing professor. She is so kind and understanding and she really wants you to succeed. Her lectures are interactive, fun, and interesting! The tests are a bit challenging but if you pay attention in class, focus on the in-class quizzes, and take notes you will do fine. HIGHLY recommend taking 2040 with her!
rubrics are never clear and TA is on a constant power trip with the grading. quizzes and tests are worded horribly also. would avoid if not a business major

I LOVE HER. i did not like the topic of this class that much, but the way she would teach it made it very interesting and made me want to come. she is great at lecturing and showing fun examples in class. plus she brings a lot of free stuff. i loved it so much i am now a TA for her.
Great professor! This class was not overly difficult, but all grading was clear and transparent. I would recommend taking this class.

How was ENTP 5000 the most challenging class I've had? Biology test score averages, with hardly any room for curving AND strict grading? My favorite part was getting an A on everything but the tests and receiving a B. I sent an email to revise my grade before graduation but received no response. Seriously? Loved her in the past, would avoid her now
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Heidi was an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and her classroom activities are super fun. She explains details without miss and her quizzes are easy. The exams are quite difficult though, but it's open note which is great. Her TA is not friendly
class was super easy if you went to lectures and paid attention. take her she's great!

Professor Herrick was one of my favorites all semester. The class information itself is a little mundane but she does an amazing job teaching and making it entertaining. She is always willing to talk outside of class and willing to help if you need it and gives great feedback. She's an inspirational person and I would take another class from her.

Take professor Herrick's class!  She is the most kind and understanding woman which is so awesome when you are a freshman in college just learning how to navigate everything.  Her lectures are interesting and motivational.  Her course load is the perfect amount where it isn't overbearing but gets the job done.

Professor Herrick is one of the best professors I have had in my college experience. Although the classes are long, she always finds a way to make it fun and engaging. There were really no "busy work" assignments which was really nice. All of the homework connected to what we learning as well as our midterm, final, and final project.

Heidi is an amazing professor. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her TAs grade pretty hard so make sure to read their feedback and use it for future assignments. I struggled to get an A in the class but I would take it again just because I felt like I was actually learning and Heidi is amazing.
The professor is a good teacher, but her TAs grade extremely harshly and she doesnt have clear rubrics for any of her assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Had a two-hour lecture and she made it go by fast! Her fun lessons and practical engagement helped me understand the topic much better! She's a bubbly professor that actually wants you to do well.

Heidi was one of my favorite professors. Her class was so fun and she knows how to hold students' attention. Assignments aren't hard, just sometimes time-consuming.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but you do get a participation grade so it's important to go. She gives breaks every class and overall was great.

Heidi was an amazing professor, super down to earth and really just understanding. You can tell that she actually cares about her students and what she is teaching. Not a hard class at all, just do your work and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really good, well organized, TA helped out a lot, a class that makes you think, and the things you learn in this class you'll for sure care it out the rest of your life.

Professor Herrick was amazing. She explained everything really well and made the 2-hour lectures fun and interesting. She also adjusted grading to match students' feedback. You were always given good feedback on assignments and could set up times to go over assignments if needed. She is very understanding.

Heidi was a dedicated professor with engaging lectures and lively classrooms. She knows what she's talking about and also works with every student who needs it despite large class sizes. I always looked forward to going to this class. Homework was somewhat challenging but if you pay attention in class and do your best work, you'll be just fine.
She is a fantastic professor who makes classes really fun and interesting. She was always happy to answer questions I had about the class. I would defiantly recommend taking her as a professor!

Professor Herrick is an amazing professor. She gives great feedback and the projects we do really help with entrepreneurship. She gave us real world examples and we often applied what we were learning by having to create value with various items. She genuinely cares about her students and I would definitely recommend.

Great teacher with really interesting lectures. Homework is long but not hard as long as you follow the rubric. Actually cares for her students and has interactive and really interesting lectures where she brings in real-life examples all the time. Lectures not required but I enjoyed them.

Professor Heidi is my favorite professor I have ever had. She is an absolute rockstar of a professor and I had to fortunate opportunity to take 2 classes from her this semester. If you have the opportunity to take a course from her sign up right now. The class was so interesting and not difficult at all if you do the readings and show up to class.
Professor Herrick is a great professor! I learned a lot in her class.

Gem of a professor, one of the best due to sheer brilliance & humility. She goes above & beyond to help her students. You can also tell how thoughtful she is with lectures & class activities. Honestly, these are the kind of professors that help positively shape your collegiate experience. I can only hope to do the same for another student one day.

The exams for this class were so much harder than all the course material, which showed when most of the class did poorly on it, despite them doing well in the course. The assignments were kind of tedious, but not hard. This class did not teach me anything.

All of the assignments in her entrepreneurship class are group work. She has a clear rubric to follow to ensure you get the best grade. She reviews everyone's projects and gives good feedback, along with an opportunity to make revisions before submitting for grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was one of the first classes I took at the U, and I really enjoyed it. The class wasn't particularly difficult, and I liked that it made you still think about practical problems in entrepreneurship. Professor Herrick was great and added a lot to the class, definitely worth taking if you can.

Three-hour night class, but Heidi sure knew how to make it more bearable. Have nothing but positive things to say about her - her TA, on the other hand, went on an outrageous grading spree for the first part of the semester. Make sure to read the textbook and be prepared for the midterms. Choose a good group.

Straight to the point. Attendance is mandatory and being an active participant will help you get a solid attendance grade. If you read what's assigned and truly work on the case write ups, the midterms and final will come naturally.

Heidi was amazing! Her lectures were some of the best lectures that I ever heard. You can tell she really enjoys teaching and is really good at keeping everybody engaged. But she is a tough grader so don't slack off!!
Heidi is smart. She knows her stuff. She is passionate and inspirational.

Heidi is great at giving you real life examples and interesting demonstrations. This class in particular is text heavy, and participation is a must to get a good understanding of the material and a good grade.

Heidi knew the material she was talking about and make sure you also had the chance to participate. Her slides were always informative and although the material is dense, not impossible to navigate for the course. There are weekly quizzes that also help with retention. Love it!

At times, she was in her element and was speaking from experience, at others, she was literally reading the slides and rushing to finish class. If you don't read, you will find it challenging but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heidi was a very intelligent, fair, tough, and straightforward teacher. I thought that her expectations were stated and expressed clearly, even if these expectations were very high. My only complaint with this course was that the TA was an extremely harsh grader. My group discussed this with her and she was very understanding and accommodating.

Heidi is willing to listen to concerns of students. If you have issues with an assignment or with material make sure to approach her after class. Give yourself time for case studies. Long group project but given semester to do it. Participation grade for each class.

Heidi made a real effort to make this class not only practical for career use, but insightful in terms of self-awareness. An incredibly brilliant lecturer, who managed to keep a night class engaging through thoughtful lectures and team activities. Additionally, she encourage us to examine ourselves through a strategic lens. Would take again!

Awesome professor and made class enjoyable and fun! Quiz at the beginning of each class so don't be late. The group project was graded pretty tough by the TA. Wish we had a little more direction on how she wanted it done. Overall a great semester!
Prof. Herrick taught our class from 6-9pm. Typically these classes are difficult to stay awake for, but Prof. Herrick always made class fun and enjoyable. She is a very good professor.

Heidi is a very intelligent professor and her class has good knowledge in it if you put the time. If you don't read the book, you probably won't learn much. I found myself not finding much value in the lectures and the lack of feedback on case studies made it difficult to find areas of improvement. Don't read the syllabus she won't follow it anyway
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was a really good professor! She always brought food to class for rewards for participation and participation is mandatory in her class. There is a big project and the grading is tough but overall it was a good class !

Heidi has real world experience and is able to tie that into course topics. She is very encouraging and genuinely wants her students to succeed, while making them earn each grade. Impromptu group collaboration should be expected in every class period and may be uncomfortable for some students, though essential in the real world. Overall good prof

Case discussions were extremely helpful and the lectures were very informational. This was a harder class but the assignments helped us learn and solidify our understanding. One piece of feedback I would have would be to go over the analysis tools in more depth (VRIO, 5 Forces, etc.) by showing examples of how they are used in real analyses.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heidi is a great teacher. She will move fast through the material and has an activity with most lectures. The slides and test hints in class are detailed enough to prepare for the exams. Heidi seems less concerned about covering all the material than with leaving student with a helpful and meaningful experience.

Heidi is an amazing professor with lectures that provides to real world examples. There are quizzes at the beginning of classes, but the entire class reviews the answers afterwards to better understand the material. She gives out treats and gave us pizza on the last day! The material isn't hard to understand as long you put time into it.
She's a nice teacher and there really isn't much homework. Just a couple quizzes, papers, and a group project. Didn't do too bad, but ended up in a group that didn't put in much effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heidi is one of the best professors in the business school, she is also the most attractive professors I have had at the U (well worth going to class just for that). The material taught is really beneficial for any business student and she does a great job at teaching the subject. Go to class, read the assigned chapters, and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She was great, who give out gift out to students on the first day of class? She does, she makes you work for your grade but you will learn a lot of you put the effort into it. Well worth the time and would take her class again over all others who may teach this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Heidi is easily one of my favorite professors at the U. You can really tell when a professor cares and it shows in her class. The only issues I had were with the exams. Exams composing of questions from the question bank are a ineffective way of actually showing knowledge of the material. I wish she wrote out her own personal questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Entertaining class especially for being 3 hours. You can tell she really cares and makes a strong effort.

I thought Heidi was a great teacher. There were times where instructions and expectations were a little ambiguous but overall a great class. She is knowledgeable, kind, and you get the sense she wants to see you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heidi is willing to go out of her way to help you succeed if you get to know her. She really wants all of her students to do well in and out of class. If you are involved in the class, you will do well. Make sure to pick the right people for the group project or your semester may be a little rough since you work on it throughout the semester.
Go to class and pick a good group.

She is really good. Her class is moderately difficult, which is mostly due to the project. The lecture slides really help when studying for the test. A little bit of a hard grader, but I think that was more the TA than it was her. She makes the topics interesting. Quizzes before class are not that difficult since you can use the lecture slides.
she brings snacks to class so participate. lecture slides are super helpful for the tests

Heidi is a killer teacher! She is super knowledgable about the subjects she teaches and has tons of cool experiences and stories to solidify course content. She provides ample explanation for all assignments, and puts a lot of work into each of the class lectures/discussions that she prepares. Shes awesome at fostering a safe, engaging classroom

Great instructor. Knows her stuff and even more importantly knows how to teach and convey it. Is very generous and fun and makes class genuinely valuable each time. Uses slides but makes class very interactive and every bit of media she uses relates directly to that weeks material.

Heidi went above and beyond to help me get into an already full section. I'm glad she did because her lecture were enjoyable and facilitated great discussions, however not all exam material is covered in class. Her choice of TA was poor. He graded all papers and provided extremely low quality feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Heidi is a great professor. I believe she goes above and beyond to find ways to make class more enjoyable. There were class exercises that involved food/treats. She was very open to meeting outside of class to discuss assignments or answer questions. Grading is strict, I do wish there was more verbal direction and clarification on assignments.
Required Class.

Heidi knows this is a hard class so she does what she can to make it bearable. Gives treats if you answer a quiz question & gave us pizza the last day of class. Group project is a lot of work but she breaks it up so it's not overwhelming. Super smart, can tell she knows her stuff.

Heidi was a great professor! Lectures were always clear, and she always kept the content interesting and engaging. Lots of discussion, treats, and in-class assignments. Grading was tough on the papers and case studies, however the criteria was clear and Heidi was always available to meet for help.

Great teacher. Warm, enjoyable attitude. Presents the topics in a clear, concise way. The class was not excessively hard but there's a group project which is a significant part of your grade so be careful who you group up with. TA graded individual assignments too harshly and I know multiple students felt that way too so there's that. I'drecommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Heidi is a great professor! You can tell she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Participation counts so don't miss class. As long as you put in the work, the class is passable. Be prepared to find a good group as the majority of the class is based on a group project. She brings treats on the daily and pizza on the last day!

Heidi is a great teacher though I hated the subject. The lectures were fairly boring to me, to be honest, but Heidi was always willing to clarify or otherwise helpful. However, THE TA WAS HORRIBLE. The TA graded all assignments for the class and was extremely harsh. Talked to Heidi about it and she was understanding but the damage was done

Great professor! Her lectures are interesting and help you further understand the material. Participation does count but you can do good by showing up and being prepared. Overall, I think she is a fantastic professor that cares and wants you to succeed!
Very hard grading up front so you know you're in for a challenge, but after the work is worthwhile. Learned a ton, was challenged, and had a very positive experience overall.

Heidi is an amazing professor. She really cares about her students and wants them to be successful. This does not mean that she will go easy on you though. If you want a good grade, you need to put in a good bit of effort. There are weekly quizzes, three exams (only two count toward your grade), and a group paper/presentation.
She's a good professor (nice to look at too). She gives good feedback where it matters and cares about her students. Careful when selecting teams, you might get stuck doing all of the work.
Well prepared professor. Instructs in a fun and interactive way. If you read and do homework the class will bring the absolute best out of you.

This class was overall enjoyable. Heidi really makes class interactive and easy to listen to. I wish the TA would have graded less though. The grades felt all over the place. Other than that the class was good.

Heidi is very knowledgeable in her field. Hiedi was a good teacher that worked hard to make her lectures interesting (you really should read the chapters assigned in order to succeed in this class) and interactive/hands-on.

This professor really cares and wants you to succeed beyond just this class. The group project requires a lot of application of the course content so choose your company carefully! The drafts are graded tough but this is so your final paper will turn out well.
Heidi was an awesome professor. Even though our classes were three hours long, she was able to make things interesting majority of the time.
I can say Heidi is one of my best professor ever! You cannot imagine how awesome class!

I enjoyed taking class with her. It was a night class and they never go the full three hours. She and her TA both are tough graders, but give good feedback as to why you received the grade you did. She's more than willing to take the time to sit down and help you. Would take her class again.

Heidi is an incredible teacher! She is great at making topics relateable and giving in demonstrations during class. She is very particular about participation, group projects and reading the chapters. Heidi does a great job of giving you a fair chance for full points for every assignment, test, and project but she is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heidi is the best!! She is really nice and encourage students to contribute to class discussions. Definitely read the chapters before class, it helps a lot! I really enjoyed Heidi's class!
Required course that I would not have taken by choice but Heidi was a good teacher but there is a lot of group work worth a good portion of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Man she's great, right??? The class was tough but our professor was tougher. Lots of reading and Impossible tests.
The best professor I have ever taken in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of fun to attend. Lectures are great, and the participation requirements are not a drag. Reading the assigned chapters will prepare you for quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Heidi is awesome! I loved how she would often share inspiring stories about being our best and achieving our dreams. She is available for her students and wants to see them succeed. She relates class concepts to real companies. If you read the chapters you will do fine on the quizzes.

Heidi is nice and often brings snack to class. Lots of hands on activities which made class fun. Someone mentioned that she says "right" frequently and is spot on. Her choice of TA was questionable as rough drafts didn't get above a 7%. He was a harsher grader than Heidi is and she would give points for things he didn't on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heidi is a very nice professor and has fun lessons that are often very hands-on (object lessons). My largest complaint is how many times she will say "right" to end a thought. The first few classes it was extremely distracting and now it's more of a general annoyance. Again, fantastic teacher and relays the information well. Right.
Good class, Heidi knows her stuff (PhD), makes class enjoyable and interactive. Brought candy/treats every class. I would take this class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Heidi does an AMAZING job of making the class interesting. Almost every class involves some kind of activity - often food oriented too, which I enjoy. I wouldn't say the class is exceptionally difficult, but make sure you read the material and really make an effort on the written assignments. It's really not hard to enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Heidi is good. She brought breakfast for our class of 50 people 5 or 6 times. She gave us each a book on the way out after the final. Had guest speakers to class a few times. You will read the whole textbook in her class. She gives you a quiz at least once a week on the reading. Big group project. She was always slow to return grades on assignments

I've had some bad professors here at the University of Utah during my first year here. Hohenegger was by far one of the worst. She has 0 empathy for her students, not taking ANY excuses. She does not know how to teach, and speeds through every single unit. A majority of the class, I was teaching myself how to do the material. Wouldn't recommend.

Consistently made typos on notes, homeworks, and even quizzes. So I always wondered if her resources were even correct. This is an applied course where we only need to know computations, not proofs. But her lectures focused mostly on derivations of theorems, rather than the implementation, which we're tested on. To succeed, must self study lots.

Her relatively easy homeworks/quizzes/exams make up for the mediocre lectures. I have to read the book to keep up with the class content, which I don't like. She also ends her lectures early sometimes, but I wish she would use the extra time to help us review for upcoming quizzes/exams. She has neat handwriting which is good.

Professor was passionate about having us learn less about exactly how to do the problem as much as knowing how to use it. She dedicated some of the classes to student suggested topics(Runge Kuta/Gravity systems). Lectures were useful, and assignments were the testing ground. Assignments difficult but not exorbitant in work. Her research was fun too

She's a super great teacher and is very willing to help outside of lectures. She also provided test corrections and an extra credit opportunity that was vital. Lots of the lectures get "into the weeds" super quickly, and I often didn't understand until I worked on the homework with the textbook, but that might just be the nature of DE's.

Christel is a very decent teacher, her lectures are pretty well done and she is one of the nicest teachers in the Mathematics program. The homeworks are doable, however it is fairly easy to miss points here and there from them, but the averages on the homeworks remain high. Overall, the class was interesting, and very fun to be in.

The lectures for this class were clear and engaging, and I liked that Professor Hohenegger tried to schedule office hours so that everybody who wanted to come would be able to. I found it helpful that she explained things differently than the textbook did. There was a lot of homework on some weeks, but I felt like it prepared me well for tests.

She moves fast through each chapter and hardly explains the lecture notes. Her tests are not based off the review she gives and often the exam will have very little correlation to the material The HW is not graded but sets up what will be on the weekly quiz. The HW sol set has many mistakes making things frustrating. Do not take if you want to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She does a good job of teaching things that she tests on. However, her lectures are sometimes convuluted and more difficult than they need to be. Her tests also range wildely. Some tests are very hard while others are incredibly easy. She also assigns quite a bit of homework, and a lot of it is usually harder than what appears on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hohenegger is a good Calc I teacher, but her Calc II/III combo class is hard. Tests often didn't reflect what was taught in class and example problems are infrequent. HW isn't mandatory, but you need to do it to get decent grades on tests. Otherwise, she is super fun, cares a lot about her students, and is always available for consultation.
Professor Hollenberg made everyone feel included and always answered everyone's questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sarah's Art History & Feminism class was one of the most interesting ones I've taken. Most of class is discussion that she builds around the questions students submit on the week's readings (which are long but interesting). Her knowledge of art history means she has works for every feminist situation and question. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Sarah was great for Signifying Bodies. It wasn't explicitly an art history class, but I learned so much about art anyway. There were quite a few readings but they were definitely worth the effort, and class discussions were always very interesting. Sometimes she could be a little harsh, but not to the point where it took away from the class vibe.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The amount of work you have to put in this class is astronomical. It is an on-line class, but you are still required to have 4 hour-long meetings over zoom throughout the semester! You have to write a short essay and take a quiz every week, neither are easy! She is such a tough grader too. If you want a gen-ed credit, I don't recommend this one.
Group writing projects sucked. Would not reccomned this course for that reason.
I do not recommend taking this course

Sarah is a good professor; I like her lectures, and you can learn a lot of helpful information from her class. However, the grades I received from the TA are vague, and I didn't receive any comments on my writing homework. Besides, the final exam is tough to finish, and there are tons of rules that need to follow.

She obviously loves what she teaches and by showing up, you do learn. That said, I really have no other good things to say about the class itself. Hollenberg won't work with you if you have personal issues/emergencies, and her final is likely one of the most tedious you will ever take. She seems to enjoy making life difficult for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Hollenberg is very smart and knows how to lecture well. The course material is interesting, so I took away a lot of info at the end of the semester. The final was a lot of work bc we had to write multiple essays, but maybe it was only like that because it was online and she knew we would look at notes. Besides that, the workload is reasonable.

Sarah has been the toughest professor I ever had. Not only is she a tough grader, she rarely gives advice or additional resources to help you understand. I have felt disrespected many times in her class. Canvas is horrible structured. I did hours of research only to get no credit, and blamed for wasting her time. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Sarah is nice and clearly loves what she teaches. It is important that you do your readings on time. All the grades that she gave me specifically were easy to understand, but I put tough grader because the grades I received from the TA were quite hard and kind of hard to understand where I went wrong. Overall, good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr Knapp is awesome and funny. Shes passionate and very knowledgeable about her work and is very open minded to new ideas and perspectives. Very kind and understanding with students

canvas is structured very poorly, hard to find stuff, links and directions are squirreled away where they shouldn't be, join links and passcodes for zoom are hard to find and never in the same place. everything unnecessarily confusing. lack of empathy for students w social anxiety. lectures and slides are hard to read, not enough actual art
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A lot of homework and attendance is mandatory, just be prepared to read and keep on top of the material and deadlines. If you do good work then you'll get an A, but it's easy to fall behind. However, the course formatting and instructor make it easy to navigate and understand the content. Just participate and keep on top of the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has a LOT of homework that you have to keep up on. I submitted pretty much every assignment except the ones I knew I could afford to miss, and I still might not get an A. It's really easy to fall behind, but the class structure helps you stay on track. The best advice I would give is to have some sort of reminders for homework deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of work in this class, but it is worth it. The more you participate and do your readings, the more it honestly shows in your grades. Professor Hollenberg is empathetic to her students, and she has intriguing class discussions. Most assignments/tests are in the form of written analysis.

Sarah knows her Art History. I personally wouldn't have taken this class from her if I knew more of the material before hand. There was one lecture and reading which showed very explicit pictures which I did not think was necessary at all. She focuses a lot on social issues, which I think is important, but reduces how much art History you learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm a senior and I had a difficult time with this class. Her lectures were extensive and detailed, although sometimes it seemed she was bothered to be answering questions. The test was EXTREMELY long (well over 6 hours) and some questions we're based on lectures or reading. I didn't feel like my input in lectures was respected or welcomed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you don't have any background with art history I do not recommend taking this class. Sarah expects you to know everything and is a very tough grader. She doesn't provide written notes so it's difficult to know what you're supposed to take notes on. If you get something wrong, she will not hesitate to tease you. I cried a lot over this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sarah is one of my favorite professors at the University of Utah. This course required a TON of reading, but she knows how to push students to be the best that they can be. She was always available for consultations if I had questions and gave feedback that was very helpful. It's an extremely difficult course but entirely worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sarah is by far the hardest professor I have ever had. This was an incredibly difficult class that I found impossible to keep up with. She is very passionate and knowledgable on the material but it was A LOT of work and reading. While she seems nice in the classroom, she looks at students like they are stupid when they speak to her individually.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was miserable. I didn't know that my notes had to be so in depth until the midterm came around because she didn't really inform us. She kind of expects us to know everything? I also did research for a paper that took me forever & I thought it'd help me, and she told me my research was useless. I've never cried over a class so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She seemed like a good teacher at first and in terms of the quality of the lecture this holds true. However, when I took the first midterm I realized the importance of taking very precise notes too late. The midterm requires that you remember images shown in class as well as many names and events. Power points not available outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class a bit difficult b/c I am a non art major. The lectures ranged from incredible to incredibly boring, but she always went over everything needed for tests. TAKE NOTES AND READ. There are some days where she tests on readings and others she doesn't. Participation and attendance are not mandatory but highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This course was structured much like an AP art class. Not too many professors put in the time to have detailed notes (memorized) about each slide. She was always extremely prepared & very knowledgeable. Although, as a non art major, I found the assignments a little tricky. But I learned so much from her & would highly recommend her.

This class really depends on the TA that you get, since they will be doing the majority of your grading. I would not recommend to anyone who is not majoring in the arts (I took this for a Humanities credit). You really have to stay on top of the readings, take your own notes, and pay attention to specific details during the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is a good professor but a very harsh grader. She grades beyond the criteria and how well you exceed expectations. You absolutely need to participate and have an opinion in the class. She is very knowledgable and will call you out if you are wrong in class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took art history in high school and it has helped me out A LOT. If you dont know anything about art history, its going to be extremely hard. Theres a lot of readings shell quiz you on. Shes also very rude. She does ridicules some of her student in front of the class. But she is very passionate on what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you have no background knowledge in art I highly advise you to NOT TAKE IT because it WILL hurt your GPA. There are no written notes, you just look at pictures of art and talk about them so it is unclear what exactly to take notes on/study. The professor is rude & ridicules her students in front of the entire class for very minor things.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at the U. She's passionate, extremely knowledgeable and encourages the entire class to participate. Phones/laptops not allowed in class but I'm glad they weren't because her lectures were so interesting. The class was hard and there was a lot of reading but I'd take it again in a second.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hollenberg is the best professor I've had at university. She is so passionate about the subject and successfully engages the entire class. Her love of the subject helped me to love a subject I used to see as boring. She creates an environment where asking questions is comfortable and participating is easy. Very approachable. LOTS of quizzes.

Hollenburg is really engaging when giving her lectures, and invites the class into a discussion style which makes the class entertaining and brilliant. Hollenburg is more flexible and in your favor as far as grading goes if you attend class everyday. Don't skip out on the reading, you have a quiz every other class on the reading. Very scholarly.

Attendance is not mandatory, but there are in class quizzes and her lectures are important for the tests. There are also a lot of out-of-class readings, so I wouldn't recommend this class if you struggle with reading. Her lectures are excellent though. She clearly has a lot of passion, and we had some great class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You must do the reading because she has quizzes that may hurt your grade in the long run. Also must take notes. She was very clear during her lectures you can tell she has a passion for what she does which makes the class really enjoyable.

As a freshman, this was one of my hardest classes. I took this class to fulfill a GenEd requirement. I didn't like the class at first, but if you really make an effort to enjoy it, you'll end up loving it. I'm glad I took this course because it really opened up my perspectives of art and life in general. Hard class, but worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you listen, take notes, and do the readings it's a really fun and interesting class that's not hard to do well in.
Review for ARCH 3011 (Studio)

She is a nice professor. Her class is extremely lecture-heavy. Don't be surprised by each class having up to 100+ slide lectures. Extremely hard to engage and will give many pop quizzes. It is nearly impossible to pay attention and follow along while taking notes. I do not recommend this class whatsoever; take any other fine art gen ed.
Do not take this class.

Every lecture is just a super long slideshow and always extraordinarily boring. You don't really have to show up, although she does do these in-class assignments and if you aren't there then you will get a zero on them. Test were relatively easy and you never really know what she will put on them.
pop quizzes, lots of notes, moves very quickly

This was an easy class with very little work. If you attended the lecture and take good notes you should have no problem. The weekly readings are honestly semi-optional as they are just topics covered in lecture. Overall I found her lectures to be fairly enjoyable she clearly is passionate about was she teaches.

Lectures are extremely long and not engaging. Not uncommon to have powerpoints with 100+ slides. Each lecture is accompanied with a 20+ page reading that does not have a clear direction. Course material is interesting, but way too much for the time given. Graduate-level amount of reading and lecturing for an introductory course. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. The class format is horrible in relation to assignments, groups, and attendance. Requiring to submit notes is completely unnecessary and quite redundant considering they must be turned in by groups which all take individual notes. The group idea does not work well whatsoever, as it took me until the 4th week to contact them.

Professor Howard was really nice, and she was great at responding to emails, however, she was pretty disorganized. The readings were all over the place, and the layout of the class was a little confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Howard is incredibly nice and wants her students to succeed. Everything is group based so that will pretty much make or break your experience. Just take notes every class and you will be fine. There are super short low stakes quizzes after each lecture (like 3-5 multiple choice questions) but if you listen you will be just fine.

Michelle is nice but not a great teacher/lecturer. Class environment and pacing felt dull and unengaging. Lectures felt uncollected. Every hw is a group assignment and has potential to be a nightmare, as you are reliant on others and communication for your grade. Towards the end, readings were lengthy. Class isnt difficult, but not worth the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Michelle is awesome! She's super sweet and caring, you won't regret taking her class at all. The class is group based, be prepared to read. It isn't hard to pass this class or get a good grade at all. She will be there for you!! Trust me!!!
She is easy going and adjustable, her assignments can be a little confusing at first but if your group is solid then the class is easy!  Def recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Where to begin? From day one everyone could not understand her, or what she is putting on the board. She just copies from the textbook and even then she has a hard time solving them, confusing everyone. You are better off skipping class and reading the textbook. The textbook used is also very bad so its all a mess. Assigns alot of homework/labwork
Shes very hard to understand. Her lecture will makes you fall asleep.

It is very clear that she understands what she is talking about, but she lacks the effective skills to convey her knowledge during her lectures. The manner in which she explains the topic at hand is often very lackluster. She often does not make it clear what the question is asking or what the answer is. Overall it is a very confusing experience.

It's extremely hard to understand, or even hear what she is saying due to the AC of a poorly built room. She may or may not be good for Calculus courses, but for Complex Analyses, she is terrible. She doesn't follow the book, does the examples incorrectly, and I am quite sure she herself doesn't understand the material. Stay away if you can.

It is VERY hard to understand what she is saying.  She has a very thick accent and her pronunciation is not good at all.  I basically had to teach myself everything from the book, because lecture was not helpful. One good thing, she is lenient on grading

I took her calculus class online and passed the course with a pretty good grade. She grades really easy, but there is virtually no instruction for the course at all. You really ought to feel comfortable with teaching yourself out of the textbook if you want to take the online course. Homework sets and test reviews were provided online.
I had the online class. She grades easy but I needed more help than she could offer.

Not THAT bad. She grades way, way easily. You can leave or come to class whenever, and she doesn't like giving low grades, so "effort counts." If you're already good at math, or you can learn from a book, take her so you don't have to stress about getting the A.
Doesn't respond to email, can't understand what she is asking. She doesn't seem to care whether I get help or not. When I ask for help she gets frusterated. Very defensive. Two thumbs way down.
She tries to help but she can't seem to get the examples right or understand what the question being asked is. If you understand thick accents you should be ok.
Is she speaking English? I don't know! But it's only calculus 1, so the material isn't too bad.
She is very willing to help and I think she wanted me to suceed but I couldn't understand a word she said. This is the first class I have ever had to retake!!!

My all time favorite Professor! I would go out of my way to take another class with him. Super funny and great lectures. Just do the reading and go to class. He is opinionated and is willing to debate his point of view. I had this class early in the morning and was excited to go to it.

This class required little participation, but lots of reading time. Be prepared to receive multiple reading assignments after each class. Most readings are from the New York Times and 5 quizzes will be based of your readings. Ron also assigns one written paper (3-5 pages), a midterm exam, and a final exam based off of class lectures.

Ron loves political science more than any teacher I've come across. His lectures, the books, and the tests are all totally different. If you work hard and read the textbooks and attend class everyday, you will pass. If you have a passion for politics you will fit in. If you want an easy A, stay away.

One of my favorite professors. He is very opinionated, but that's what made the class so interesting. Most  professors are liberal, especially poli sci ones, so I can't understand why these other people are so shocked and upset that this professor actually voices his opinion. He criticizes the democrats just as much. Plus, he is hilarious.

Spends most of class ranting about his opinions and what he has read in the newspaper. NY Times quizzes are poorly constructed. They seem more focused on trying to trick the students into choosing the wrong answer more than trying to test your knowledge/ if you read the material. Take this class from someone else.

Definitely very arrogant and liberal--but doesn't try to hide these facts. He can be funny, and while his lectures are boring, nothing is too complicated. You are required to read 4-5 NY Times articles per night, which could be a hassle, but you only have 1 easy paper and 2 tests, which were pretty easy.

Boring class if only taking for gen ed requirement. Pretty easy as long as you study for quizzes and exams (quizzes based on reading ny times newspaper articles and 2 exams) Do the only paper you have to write in the whole class cause it's easy and a lot of points. Professor has a strong liberal opinion but if you agree with him he's pretty funny

Super liberal, but the class is easy. There are like 5 quizzes, 1 paper, and 1 midterm before the final, so I'd consider that an easy workload. He's not very good at teaching what you are going to be tested on, but that's because he doesn't have much to do with the grading process (his TA does all of the work, he just talks about his own ideas).

This class went over many of the materials most basic high school history and/or government classes taught us. The material isn't very hard, but he requires you to read multiple NYT articles a night and then quizzes and the end of the week. So unless you're truly interested in this subject,  get a different teacher.

One of the worst political science teachers. very liberal and not very tolerant of those who aren't. The class was poorly taught. He spends most of his time bashing conservatives and republicans rather than teaching.

Not the worst class, but slightly below average. Assignments were unclear, though study guides for tests were fantastic. Most of the class was common sense and largely irrelevant. You could do worse then this class, but you could also do much better.

I took his interest groups class. He is a great professor who loves to engage the class. He knows his stuff and has a fun way of lecturing. He was very friendly and helpful. He cared about his students. The tests and papers were pretty easy. All you have to do is pretty much show up. Great guy!

I was a political science major, and loved my degree. As much as I love political science Prof Hrebenar was completely boring, arrogant, and his class is irrelevant.  There are many amazing poli sci profs, but he is not one of them.  I didn't think the class was hard, just boring and a time waster.
Great professor! Knows his stuff and is funny. Can be a bit abrasive at first but he warms up. He likes smart students who do the work. Be/do those and you'll be fine
I love his method of communicating with students. He loves to poke fun at both American political parties,which is always a laugh. Overall I enjoy his wit and intelligence. Awesome guy!
Great teacher! Loved the class. He was the only professor I had this semester that i actually liked.

test's are hard but grades on curve, is an interesting teacher and has point of views that are unconventional and very intelligent that will most likely challenge your own. quizzes on ny times articles. overall learned a lot and am taking another class from him.

Do not take a class from this guy he is a jerk. Unless you agree with everything he says and brown-nose him you are not worth his time or a good grade. He is insulting when grading your papers and insulting when you comment in class. Worst teacher I ever had bar-none. I refuse to take a class from this guy. Avoid at all costs!
Here is what happened: if you don't submit your assignment, you get a 0. But if you do submit it, you can get negative points. Period.
I don't recommend him, unless you would like to fail a class, he does not explain concepts well enough, not welling to help and unclear expectations.

I have never been less confident in any class I've ever taken. If you are a pre-med student taking this course, please don't take it with a heavy semester. Martin is condescending, unwilling to work, and gives negative points for no reason. Please go to the office hours if you want to understand anything about the material.

Welcome to the worst class of your undergraduate career! Marting is the least confident, most confusing professor I've ever had, and he is incredibly unwilling to work with students to clarify his teaching. The class is mostly taught by TAs, and if you don't attend every study session can you might as well give up. Good luck, get ready to cry!
his lectures and expectations were very unclear, and he is a tough grader, so I do not recommend his class at all, even if you have to wait for a semester or two due to schedule conflicts.
he never cares about students, and his class is mostly run by TAs, and you won't know your grade until the end of the semester, so I do not recommend him.
he is not a good professor at all so do not take a class with him.

he is one of the professors that I would never like to take a class with him again because he does care about students at all he always talks about his own research, and he is very mean and rude to students for the most part.

he is the most worst professors I ever I hand his lecture are so unclear and won't understand him at all I don't recommend any one to take a class with him he is very unfair and does not care about students at all.
he is a nervous person don't take a class with him he will waste your time.

he is a racist person and all of the thing are done by the TAs and you see couple times and you will not know about your grade until the end of the semester, and he will give a surprise grade which you won't even know how to improve it never take a class with him he does not care about students.

Horvath is an awesome, engaging, prepared teacher, but his homework grading is tough ! You have to attend lectures and go to office hours to learn the material because it is largely inaccessible elsewhere. I thought his exams were reasonable, and grading breakdowns were fair. The attendance points were hard to earn, but honestly I needed that.

Horvath is a nervous wreck. Lectures are hard to follow. He's a genius, but shouldn't be teaching. He likes to emphasize his own research in class and focus on niche studies, making internet surfing for homework help impossible. His grading is ridiculous (lowest score on first hw was -40/40). TAs had a hard time helping due to a lack of guidance.

It is clear that he does not know how to teach, and I feel like I'm in a fever dream every time I hear him lecture. This class is very dense, disorganized, and causes an overwhelming amount of stress. I have never felt so dissatisfied and I am hoping the University gets a better biochem department soon.
I had never before taken a course that felt actively hostile to student success in quite so many ways.

Horvath co-taught with Blair. The lectures are dense, and homework questions are unclear. The curve is very generous. Many students complained he lectured about his research, but the U is a research school...what did you expect? Not amazing, but he's fine. Attendance is required. It's a hard class, but if you take it seriously, you'll pass.

Take this class if you want to be on better terms with God because you will be praying to him everyday that you pass.

Reading his exam questions will give you a stroke. Attendance is stated as not mandatory but "highly encouraged", you will lose points if you do not go to class. Class cheered when his co-lecturer came to teach.

I'm only going to say 1 thing and that will tell you everything you need to know about this professor. You can get negative points on a homework assignment. Yep you heard that right negative points. Someone got a -21/40 on an assignment. If you can take this class outside of the University of Utah, I highly recommend it.

This class was a disorganized mess. Grading is super delayed and unclear. Points are taken off seemingly at random without any justification. There are too many assignments with changing deadlines and expectations.

DNA lab is a completely disorganized mess. It's not hard to get an A in this class, but it is very time-consuming and you never have any idea what is going on. The assignments are not clear and even the due dates are messed up. He has random rules (like no bar graphs) due to personal opinions that make no sense. Do not recommend.

Use TA's review notes for studying for exam (don't use lecture; and study EVERYTHING)

His final was random.I didn't had any time to study for exam because my classes are so cramed. Luckily, I had things that I studied in the exam but it was completely different from last years final. Make sure to study EVERYTHING so you don't miss big easy points.

This course is a mess. The expectations are frequently miscommunicated and very frustrating. Horvath and Rupper take points off at random and heavily emphasize group work, even when not applicable. I would never take this class again and would not recommend it. Avoid this course unless you want to learn nothing and constantly feel incompetent.

He's a nice guy, but this class is a joke. It's basically How To Be A Lab Partner 101(freshman lab). There's very little actual DNA learning, textbook= useless, communication= awful, and grades are really behind. Lecture attendance wasn't originally mandatory, but now it is because he's run out of ideas and is making us debate every single lecture.

His energy was fun and he is really nice and funny - lectures go fast and can get confusing. You have to go to discussions to succeed in the class. His problems were sometimes worded strange but if you look at enough practice tests (which he posts) you'll catch on. A little unclear what you're expected to know but overall I had a good experience!

Dr. Horvath has a lot of nervous energy. His lectures felt rushed and the first exam was SUPER content heavy. He writes problems in ways that confuse a lot of people. Group work was "encouraged" but I would argue it was required to succeed in this class. TA discussions made the difference between pass or fail.

Dr. Horvath is a nice guy, but I do think he's misguided with how he teaches. He tries to teach scientific writing in a way that is VERY confusing. Take the tips you like and then leave the rest behind! You will never do perfect on papers. He even once told our class "Do not trust the rubric". Kind of a dud class, but an easy high grade.

Dr. Horvath was a very nice guy, I just couldn't understand what he was talking about most of the time. He was a lot more clear than his counterpart professor, but I still struggled to grasp what I should be learning. You'll get through this class, just don't expect the absolute best. Don't make this class the reflection of your abilities. :)

Lecture did not help me (this course was also taken during spring 2021). I spent about 10 hours on each of the 8 homeworks. The exams were too long and most students barely finished.
