We were expected to attend TA discussions (multiple per week) to get the info that would be on the test. You can't pass without TA discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class will cost you: Tears, sanity, more time then you have, your soul, the soul of your classmates and the soul of several angelic animals. HOWEVER you will not die and you might get an A if you sacrifice all of the above. ***hardest class Ive ever taken ***learned a lot ***prepare to be confused beyond hope Cry for you

Horvath is a great person and cares a lot about his students. However, he doesn't care about your grade. If you don't use his exact wording on tests, you get marked down. He thinks that everyone should attend TA sessions every day, but the TAs don't know what will be on the tests. Passing grade was a 45%, that's how difficult it is.

Professor Horvath is a challenging grader and a great lecturer. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and will work with you to make that happen, but you need to communicate when you need help --he offers various options for contacting him and responds quickly. 10/10 would take classes from him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was team taught with Baldomero Olivera. One of the worst professors I've ever had. Terribly disorganized, zero structure, lectures were hard to follow and confusing. The TAs did more teaching than he did, his response when you ask a question in class? Go to the TA discussions. Expects everyone to go to 8 discussions a week for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: BioChem 3510 is taught by two professor, and Dr. Horvath is one of them. I always look forward to the sections taught by Horvath, they are always well taught and informative. Since classes have moved online, Horvath has created a ton of sources online, and is easy to reach outside of "class hours" and helpful and wants to see us succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was challenging, but if you attend lectures and discussions you should be fine for the course. Try to go to as many discussions as you can. The TAs are very knowledgeable and are always willing to help. Overall, this was a super hard class, but I learned a lot. Would definitely take again. Dont fall behind!

I really enjoyed this class. I actually changed my major to Biochemistry after this portion. Martin tries very hard, and you can tell that he cares about his students. That being said, he asks some questions that are confusing vs what you went over in lecture. The TA sections are extremely helpful. He is also very accessible, so go to him for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a really great guy. His expectations are a little unclear, so tests are challenging. Very challenging. Go to as many discussion sessions as possible, and ask him questions in office hours. Try not to fall into a pit of despair, it'll be okay as long as you work for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Martin was so difficult to follow during class. I personally liked his co-professor better that taught with him. His tests are difficult to decode and he asks complicated questions expecting simple answers. BioChem was by-far the most difficult chem class I've ever taken. He offers extra credit on the exams and there is a curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Horvath's class was very disorganized and uninformative. His exam questions were written so poorly that students had to constantly ask the TAs for clarification. Exams do not correlate well with lecture topics at all. After many complaints, he tried to elicit student feedback, but he failed to address the most pressing concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Horvath is very disorganized. The way his tests are written makes it hard to understand what is being asked. You can know everything but lose points simply because he gave questions that were poorly worded. Make sure to ask the competent TA's for clarification when necessary. I would never take a class from Horvath again.

Horvath is an absolute mess. The classroom atmosphere is chaotic due to his lack of organization and failure to explain material in a linear manner. He expects you to learn from the TAs in discussions and admits that he is not teaching everything that is tested on, and only a few TAs know the material well enough to teach it. Needlessly hard class.

He expects you to do some reading and go to the discussions. He's very disorganized, but also understanding for students. Nice guy, can be funny. Overall, decent professor. The class is tough, but there is a lot of help from the TA's, so find a couple good ones and go to their discussions. There's a good curve at the end of the class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Horvath was simply great! He posts lecture outlines, videos, and flash cards that help us prepare for the exam. Make sure to go to the TA discussion sessions as they know for the most part what Martin will be looking for in the exams. His lectures were awesome but if you missed them you could probably sill do well in this class.

Martin makes it very clear from the beginning that this will be a challenging class. With that being said, he does everything he can to help you succeed. He posts outlines, is always available to meet, makes instructional videos, and even runs an informative twitter page. His passion for science and teaching make him an amazing professor.

This was a difficult class that required a lot of time and teamwork, but I really learned a lot and Martin was great. He really cares about his students and will do what he can to help you. He is very understanding and is fun to be around because he is so positive. The grading is kind of strict, but I would recommend this class.

He tries to make things interesting and he is pretty dorky. He doesn't explain things all that well and expects you to have a lot of background. His exams were difficult and it's a class you will have to spend a lot of time on. I really learned a lot though and he makes videos to clarify topics.

His lectures were entertaining and he made you think critically, which is probably why some struggled. He really does care: his wiki notes keep things well summarized and he posted youtube videos, which really helped.    This is a 3000 level course. If you haven't figured out how to self-study and get organized, then best of luck in grad school.
Probably the most disorganized class I have ever taken at the U.  They should probably get someone else to teach this course

I understand now why they call him Horvath the Horrible. He is extremely disorganized and jumps right into material without giving you any preface.  His tests are unnecessarily difficult, and he enjoys the fact that they are.  Take Biochem from Heemstra in the fall. SOOO much better.

As a person he is a great guy.  As a professor... not so much.  Very hard to know what will be on his exams.  When you are taking the test it feels like you are reading Greek.  He is a very tough grader.  If you're a great writer, this class will be easy.  If you are not, get ready to work your butt off.  Super critical.

Martin is extremely smart.  He wants students to succeed as is willing to help them in every way possible.  He is not completely clear all of the time but you can use his supplementary materials to solidify understanding.  I have learned a great deal from him, particularly with my scientific writing.
Hard to figure out what he wants you to do. Disorganized and confusing. Likes to think he is a hard teacher because the subject matter is hard, but, his class is hard because he is disorganized.

He seems like a really nice guy. I mean he gave us candy on the first day, but he's a mess of an instructor. He never really explains what's expected and then slams your grade for not doing what he wanted. His class layout was confusing, I never knew what to expect, and his lectures were a mess and not helpful. Avoid him if you can.
Good teacher, difficult class.  Very easy to reach via text or e-mail with questions and provides very good supplementary material.

Horvath was a good teacher. He would often speak too fast and make a mess of notes on the board, but he usually got his point across.  Loved his wiki pages, they summed up what you need to know for the exams.

Martin is a great guy overall but he is really not the best teacher. He tries to convey his message though useful demonstrations but it ends up being more confusing. Be sure to take as many notes as possible and then refer yourself to Youtube and watch a lecture from a different professor to really solidify the concept discussed in class.

Amazing professor. Talks little fast so need to pay close attention in class. Explains concepts really good so that all can understand. People who struggle in this class are likely those that do not study as in most other science classes.

Kept lectures interesting.  I didn't like that he tag-team taught with Olivera.  It made it very difficult to study for exams.  A lot of straight memorization.  I didn't learn anything in this class. I learned more in Cell Bio.  His final exam portion was not at all like he had tested us before.

Nice guy. He talks a tad bit too fast but everything he explains is pretty clear. Sometimes uses lecture notes via WebCT, sometimes doesn't. But when he does, be sure to read those a lot more than the book - that's where all the test questions come from. Discussion sessions before the test are very helpful.

Really good professor.  Detail oriented, but very clear on the things your need to know for the class.  He helped make the subject more interesting.  His tests weren't bad all if you study what he says in lecture and pad it with what is in the book.  He follows the book closely
I've never had a professor make me want to slam my head against the desk. You see the rest of the reviews and they're all true. DO NOT have the displeasure of taking this class.

She was honestly just rude and didn't really seem to like students 
Even in her feedback, when grading stuff, it had a rude tone
Also, just an unnecessary grading system

Poorly worded assignment descriptions, and only refers you back to them if you try to ask any clarifying questions. The lectures were fine. Labor based grading is the absolute worst. Only take this class if you're fine with not knowing about your grade AT ALL, and you're willing to write 20+ pages for the final. Just take this class online, or with someone else.

I would not take a class with Dr. Hunt again. Like everyone is saying the labor based grading system is garbage and the extra work required for the chance to get an A is extremely unrealistic. Avoid her classes at all costs.

Unwilling to do extra work for students but demands an unrealistic amount of extra work from students. The only way to have a CHANCE at getting an A in the course is by writing an additional 8-10 page final paper. Would never take this class again.

She is passionate and knowledgeable but her grading policies and expectations are unreasonable, especially for a 2000 level class. Lots of busy work, including a labor log. If you want to get an A you have to write 2 8-10 page papers.

3120
Unclear grading system that amounts to: did you do more than assigned? 
Second final paper equivalent to about 8-10 pages necessary to get above a B.Things assigned close to deadlines that don't reflect material learned in lecture. She was also inaccessible and did not help. Lectures used outdated material and were biased.

reviews.comment: Horrible, takes actual weeks to grade, I feel bad for her TA he does almost everything, labor based grading dont even get me started. You need to turn in 2 different final projects to maybe get an A.

DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES

reviews.comment: Impatient, condescending, and frustrating to work with. Her passive-aggressive tone over email--which is the only way to communicate with her--is wildly inappropriate for an academic setting. I felt like a burden asking for help or clarification, even though offering help and clarification is roughly 75% of a professor's job. Spare yourselves.

reviews.comment: This course had an absurd amount of reading/writing assignments for an intro class. I got a 17/25 with a comment saying "There's issues with how you cited your sources that will need to fixed for future assignments." I got deducted 8 points for improperly citing my sources and then didn't receive any direction on how to fix it. This is how the majority of the course went.

I'm a senior in COMM and this is the worst class I've taken in my years of college. The amount of work is insane. The midterm paper is extremely tough and time-consuming and the final paper ended up being the same amount of pages as my senior CAPSTONE. So many tedious assignments and points are taken off for the smallest errors. AVOID THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unwilling to assist students. Unclear of information assigned. Not helpful.

This teacher doesn't provide any recorded or live lecture content. The only content the students are given to learn from is 2-3 textbook chapters. Homework is then based on this textbook content and any assignment worth a notable amount of points is graded with so much scrutiny it's impossible for any student to get 100%.
Pedro is a great professor! Super understanding, but doesn't sugar coat things. Pretty fun class, just make sure you have a good group for the water pump.

A great intro into Mechanical Engineering. He's pretty funny and often engages with his many, many students. He offers great feedback, is very forthcoming with students, and explains things very clearly. reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had, loves his students and has inspired me to go all the way with mechanical engineering. Workload is very manageable and if you enjoy CAD this class is a blast. Lots of hands-on building activities and interesting lectures. The funniest professor on campus and is very lenient with deadlines and grading.
Truly one of the best professor I've had in college, he is funny and relaxed but knows when to make you learn. I would recommend his class to anyone that has the opportunity.
The GOAT of engineering at Utah
Awesome teacher, would love to have him as a teacher again

Pedro is a really fun and funny teacher. He brings a sense of family to the class and seems like more of a friend than a teacher. He was always interested in what students were doing in the lab and would take real interest in your group. He would often shorten the days work or make the class what the students wanted.
Great professor! Easy class with no final exam but a group project. Great professor for starting mechanical engineering.

Pedro is really funny and laid back, and he cares a lot about his students and their success. First part of the course is pretty easy but the second half of the semester gets more challenging with a group project, but that mostly depends on who your group members are. Very easygoing and not a harsh grader, accessible by email as well.

Really easy-going teacher. 
Lectures are simple and have easy assignments. Just show up, and do the work.
There is a pretty intense final group project, but it's overall quite simple and you get plenty of time to complete it.
Great teacher!
He is a really sweet person but not great at lecturing. He moved really fast and for the first half of semester he would not really work examples with us. It was difficult to follow along. :(

He's a great person, but not a great professor. His grading is inconsistent and often unfair, and he favors certain students over others. His communication is abysmal!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking his class again. He was heavy lecture teacher with a heavy accent. He did not help at all when it comes to improving your grade. The Final test he didn't even give us a review more so just told us to study all the topics. If you are wanting to fail this is the right teacher. He was a nice guy just not a good teacher.

Nearly impossible to understand due to a thick accent, and is terrible at grading. Had two separate exams where he mucked up and removed points where they were deserved, had to talk to him and get him to fix them. The class itself isn't that difficult, but I had to learn everything on my own.

I took his precalc Math 1080 class, and it was nice. Quizzes every Monday, 5 exams in the semester but you can retake one. Drops two quizzes, and a few hw assignments at the end of the year. His accent is what people have a problem with, but it is not that hard to get used to. He is really kind and funny, not too much homework.
He is a very nice guy, puts a lot of effort into the class. He gives many opportunities to get help, calc is hard but he explains it well.
This professor is an extremely tough grader. He can tough to understand sometimes as well. If you fall behind early, it can be very difficult to catch up again.

Ray is amazing!!! his class was easy to understand and he was always willing to help you understand tough topics. Also, he had practice exams that you could complete for extra credit and you were allowed a full sheet of notes, super helpful. I highly recommend taking Ray if you can.
Ray taught me a lot about math and was super helpful outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ray was excellent. I failed 1090 math my freshman year due to a very poor teacher. I retook it this year with Ray, and wow was the experience much different. He was so helpful, gave us SO many opportunities for extra credit and really cared about his students. I can't recommend him enough. 10/10
Good teacher he adapts to changing situations and needs of students and the lectures were well organized. Quite hard class for me conceptually but I'd take more math classes from him.

Hwai is a solid Linear Algebra teacher. He's newer to teaching, but he's nice and works with you. There's a quiz each week on Monday, but you can fill out a form to take it the next day if you aren't prepared. I did feel like I had to supplement lectures with reading the textbook because the concepts can be confusing but he's very available to help

The university expects 2270 to serve as an intro to pure math, and it doesn't seem like he was quite ready to introduce non-math majors to somewhat pure ideas (I had him in his first semester teaching). Despite this, he was extremely approachable and easy to access outside of class, and was a very fair grader. Would absolutely recommend!

New to teaching, so I can't be upset. Although he taught the course as if it were a math competition. He assumes students' knowledge and doesn't tie modules together at all, or give visuals. Purely proof-heavy. I wouldn't recommend this instructor for linear algebra.
I didn't attend class for the last 2 months of the semester so that could explain why I got a B. prepare to do a lot of self studying if you find math hard.
Probably the worst
Didn't teach the actual content, students in the class corrected him constantly. There was not enough time given to finish the exams, and the exam material was nothing like what was taught in class.

I took trig/precalc during high school, and it definitely helped to have a lot of that info in my mind. I think he does an ok job at teaching topics if you semi-know them already, but it's MUCH harder seeing things for the first time. Constantly made mistakes and had to ask the class to find the mistake. Messy handwriting and would skip steps. Would not recommend.

Constantly makes mistakes in the lectures, doesn't explain anything he was doing in the note packet. It felt like we were watching him do homework. Worst teacher of all time

Okay lecturer, but the guy smells insane. 10 out of 10 would not take this class again.

Terrible lectures, had to learn everything in the math center, also extremely, unnecessarily hard everything, tests, weekly quizzes, ect. This was for math 1100 (bus calc). Professor Simper is a nice guy, but his teaching style is very terrible. Did not allow notecards on exams which was unusual bc other professors allowed it. No calculators. No slides either, and the only way to study was with practice exams full of mistakes.

Did not allow notecards on exams which was unusual bc other professors allowed it. No calculators. No slides either, and the only way to study was with practice exams full of mistakes. Do not take this class from this prof.

Bad teacher, doesn't explain things well and makes exams unnecessarily difficult

reviews.comment: I'm sorry, but he is a terrible professor. This class will go down as the worst I have taken at the University of Utah. I would recommend trying to take this class from anyone else.

Ineffective as an educator. Didn't have any slides and only wrote on the whiteboard. Very dull and hard to listen to. The only review he gave us were practice exams that had errors and mistakes in them which made it hard to study for exams. Also you were not allowed a reference sheet for the exams which were allowed by other professors.

Do not take this class. He deliberately makes his class harder than other professors and reads off a script during lectures. If he took his time to work through problems with the class, the experience might be more enjoyable. Although it seems his answers to questions from students are often convoluted and confusing so this might not even help.

I would rather walk to the Sandy Campus every day at 4 AM than take a class with Hunter again. I came to college to learn, not get useless math concepts shoved down my throat by a professor unwilling to put in the bare minimum effort to be a decent teacher. I found it more useful to not attend class after a certain point and just teach myself.

Please avoid taking any class from Hunter. Save your tuition money and take a class with literally anyone else. Hunter Simper is the worst professor I have ever had. He is unable to see things from the perspective of a student learning concepts for the first time. His exams were long and impossible. The homeworks and labs were punishingly difficult

Attendance is mandatory, as there is a daily warm-up every class this is graded. However, the warm-ups do not cover information that has already been taught, making them very difficult. The professor also reads straight from his book and makes it difficult to follow along in class. I would not recommend taking a class from him.

Pretty average and straightforward lectures, homework, and exams for a math class. Dr. Simper is reasonable, answers questions and gets the point across in his lectures even if they're fairly formulaic. Exam expectations are made clear in lecture and on Canvas. Individual questions felt fair, but exams feel too long for the time limit.  BIG curve.

You NEED to be on top of your course work in this class or you will not perform well. Professor Simper was a smart, goofy guy, but I think he may have lacked the empathy needed to teach this course well. Definitely the hardest math class I have ever taken. Prepare for hours upon hours of homework and studying. I learned a lot, but it was grueling.

The review sessions include him reading off words from a PDF and writing them on the board. Then gives an impossible test with problems we never did on homework. We spent a lot of time on spring, tank, and population problems and proceeded not to test us on those problems but decided conceptual problems were more important. HW is very long!

I have never cheered to receive a C in a class, but there is a first for everything. This course is full of brutal content itself, but the lectures were straight out of the textbook offering no insight or explanation. The exams were beyond difficult and the first one especially was graded critically. Exam averages were low D for the class.

Difficult to know what was expected to learn. Labs, lectures, homework and even tests did not work together or build on each other. Learning from online resources and tutors didn't seem to help much as test's formatting was very particular. Nice and very smart guy but wouldn't recommend taking a class from him.

The lecture is not mandatory but he does not post any lecture notes. Averaging 10 hrs of hw per week plus lab. Canvas is a mess, no review solution for any of the exam reviews, no solution for the HWs, NOTHING. Put way too many questions in a 50-minute test. I have seen graduate students teach way better than him. NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hunter Simper does not care about teaching his students. His lectures are full of long, convoluted examples that he's too lazy to elaborate on-- not that it matters. Nothing you see in a lecture will be on your midterms. Or your labs. Or your homework. If you want to learn, take a different instructor's class.

This is by far the worst class I've ever taken. The exams are extremely difficult and the labs are impossible. People only get through a part of one question, so it ends up being extra homework. On average this class is about 12 hours of work a week. I recommend taking from another professor.

I think the reviews on here are a little harsh, while the class is very difficult, I don't believe it's as bad as stated. It's a tough class, no matter the professor, it'll be hard. However, the amount of homework can be overwhelming, the tests are difficult and the reviews in class are short and not in depth. The lab is good, but the rest is bad.

This class is very hard, professor Simper makes it needlessly harder. I cannot understate this: be ready to put in triple the hours you would for any other class. You will have to teach yourself, then have time to do the HW and study for the tests which have no resemblance to the HW. Simper doesn't care about his students or teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is legitimately the worst class I have ever taken. Dr. Simper's lecture style is extremely confusing and hard to follow. The weekly homework's routinely take 12+ hours, the labs are near impossible, and exams are ridiculous. MATH 2250 is supposed to be a difficult class, but when the average score on an exam is 50, it's the professor's fault.

Hunter has fine lectures, nothing special. However, you get the exact same info from the textbook. Tests are near impossible, way too many questions with not enough time. Labs and homework make workload about 10 hrs/week. Go to TA's office hours instead of Hunter's.

This is by far the worst class I have ever taken. 10+ hours of homework each week, math labs that the TAs in the math center have no clue how to do (they are graded on correctness), and tests that are impossible to finish within the time constraints. I would take a 5 AM, 3 hour daily lecture before I take this class again.

He won't explain the steps he is doing, he'll just randomly end up with numbers. It also seems like he doesn't even look at the homework he is assigning because nothing from the homework ever shows up on the test. It would only be fair to make the tests super hard if the homework matched the difficulty but it doesn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Expect to spend about 20 hours a week on homework. Then spend 15-20 hours studying for a test only for it not to matter because they are impossibly hard.

Hunter is a very smart guy, but teaches this class, which is mainly (if not all) engineers, as if we are all math majors. It is very mathematically technical, and his lectures are poor. He essentially just writes the textbook in full on a chalkboard with very little intuitive/further explanation. Tests are very difficult, labs are near impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Kim is SO nice and will always be willing to give you a good grade as long as she can tell you tried your best. I had her for almost 4 years and while I think her earlier classes are much more organized I enjoyed every class I had with her. She is an easy teacher, but be warned the later Korean classes' content does get difficult!

Professor Kim is a great professor! She goes out of her way to help us learn. Great if you want to learn introductory Korean. Be aware that Korean is a hard language so there is a lot of studying outside of class. She's very accommodating with assignments and answers emails promptly as well! Will definitely take another class with Professor Kim!

If you want to learn basic Korean, you must take Prof. Kim's classes! For a beginner language class, there is going to be a lot of homework/quizzes, so spend some time learning after class. The class overall is very fast-paced, which was the main reason I was personally struggling. If you enjoy a fast-paced beginner class, take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Kim was great! The class was very fun and you learn a lot in a short amount of time. You definitely need to pay attention in class and attend every day in order to get all of the material. There are a lot of tests and homework, but they aren't too difficult. I definitely recommend Prof. Kim if you're looking to take Korean!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is very kind and really tries to help you understand the content to the best of her abilities. Going to class is a must for language development, and the class will become difficult if you don't go. She is very understanding when it comes to late work and the works.

I love Kim Sunsaengnim! She is very easy to learn Korean from and makes the classroom a fun but also very memorable environment. My Korean has come to me so much faster from her class than just trying to learn by myself.
Professor Kim is a really kind teacher, who cares for her students. Her class makes you feel comfortable. She will always help you if you're struggling with Korean.

Very caring and understanding professor. He will help you get your work done if you are falling behind. Very lax on grading. Some students were having a hard time with home life and he was very understanding. He even donated to my cause.

He loves to get the students talking and engaging in discussion. There is a lot of homework, but it's mostly reflection essays so it's pretty easy. He is an easy grader and will let you turn most things in late. The only bad thing about the class was the textbook. It was expensive and although informative it was a very dry read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Was looking for the "Absolutely Horrible" tag but I guess there's not one :( Professor Hyams was hands down the WORST professor I've ever had. All he does it talk in circles about nothing and then keep up overtime in class to just talk more about nothing. I actually felt physically ill in his class from boredom and anger. I am requesting a refund.

When in class, you go through A LOT of material ad fast. There were times in class that the entire class was confused of what was going on. He talks through the material very fast so it is easy to get lost in what is happening in class. The class difficult and the we struggled as a class so he had to curve the grading scale.

He probably created all the good reviews on here. Cannot understand him at all. I sent him questions about an assignment to which he responded "looks fine", then when i submitted assignment he marked most of those parts wrong. He doesnt believe in gpa or helping students be successfull. Totally fine with you failing the course, probably enjoys it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Difficult subject and Prof. Kim can be hard to understand. However, like others have said here he's really accessible and responds to your assignment submissions with notes very quickly. Also, the material isn't graded very hard. Overall a good professor for this subject; you probably won't find better at the U.

Most responsive guy you will ever have.  Always happy to provide assistance and responds with detailed help almost immediately. Gives extra credit question on almost every assignment. English is not his first language, so if you don't understand an assignment due to syntax, ask. Have taken him for both on-line and in classroom. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You probably wont be able to understand him much, don't be scared away. He is a dedicated professor who will be on top of grading and answering any questions if you have them. He takes attendance points so get to class! The quizzes were not challenging and the homework takes some time. He does take home midterms, this is easily the best class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hyeon is by far the best professor you'll find for econometrics. He's a fair guy, always willing to help out, and he knows it's a difficult subject. So especially when it's an intro class for the subject, he'll do everything he can to help you pass
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: literally have no idea what he is saying. ever. do not take this class. worst professor EVER
He's incredibly biased with his grading of papers. He will ignore statistics you've put into your paper in favor of ad hominem. Had to take my paper to another professor to get a re grade

Attendance wasnt mandatory but then there are questions on test that only got answered in lectures! I didnt love that because really the reading and tests and stuff were fine without needing the lecture. But Professor Adams was easy I admit if I went.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy grade and I would have got the A bit was late on too many things. Super easy to work with and yak to on issues. Doesnt let extreme students take over class which I liked. Interesting class lectures and his zoom meetings are funny but long!

He is a cop & it SHOWS. He doesn't respect ANY criticism of cops or their negative role within the CJS and will attack those who find fault. There are weekly quizzes that have so many errors in them with more than one correct answer and if you choose the one he didn't, it is wrong and he won't change it. Do NOT take this class from him.

Its one thing to pride oneself in one's career, its another thing to always feel so personal about comments made in discussions that the professor gets super defensive. Like, the discussions posts I made are legitmate concerns I have in the CJS, just for him to invalidate them or ridicule them.

Professor Adams was great. He is easy to get a long with, replies to emails within a few hours at most in my experience, and cares how his students do. The class was originally on campus but was adapted to online due to COVID but everything was done well. 11/10 would take another class from him.

For CHEM2315: prelab quizzes are annoying and usually difficult to find info on based on just class material alone. Labs were decent but can take a while, ensure your lab notebook contains all observations (write a ton of crap), and thorough notes of the prelab and post lab questions. Do not miss any lab dates and or assignments, should be an EZ A.

I'm actually in Professor Zarhov's Ochem 1 lab which is not listed. But I have a few points:
-Lectures are from 2020, live zooms will likely be during your other classes
-Procedures are thoroughly outdated and experiments rarely follow them
-1 TA is expected to cover approx. 12 groups during labs that aren't thoroughly explained
-SO MANY HAZARDS!!!

BEWARE YOU WILL WORK HARDER THAN YOU WOULD EXPECT FOR THIS CLASS! The procedures for the experiments are awful. Incredibly vague and the lectures are vague as well. Be prepared to basically research everything for the labs. Unclear grading criteria and you'll spend so much unnecessary time prepping for labs. The textbook is useless, don't get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pofessor zarhov is a great teacher. That being said if you are a typical premed worried about denting your perfect gpa you should not take this class( you should also recondsider becoming a doctor) However, if you are truly interested in gaining and understading of organic chemistry and the natural world professor zarhov can help you with that.

Amazing professor! No idea why there are so many negative reviews. All of his tests are fair, and he bends over backwards to prepare you for his final. I recommend Zharov for everyone taking organic 1.

Horrible, tough and rude. I didn't know about his reputation before I signed up, or else I wouldn't have. He wants you to work for yourself, which is fair, but he is inconsiderate in his manner of teaching. Ask other student's who've had him and good luck!!

By far the worst professor I've ever had!  His tests are beyond hard and he could care less if the students learn the material or not.  He's only here to do research.  He's an arrogant, smug jerk and very rude to his students.  He told us constantly that we were idiots and that he was happy there were going to be less Doctors in the world. AVOID!!!

Only went to one of his lectures and it didn't help at all with the weekly quizzes and labs. You have to do a LOT of research online by yourself or contact your TAs to understand what the labs are about. Zharov literally doesn't do anything and your grade really depends on the TAs you get for each time section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zharov isn't too involved in the lab and really only does a little bit of work on the lectures you watch each week. These aren't very helpful at all, and the vast majority of stuff you want to do from the lab is found in the procedure. My biggest issue is the lack of direction and you have to do a ton of outside research or email the TAs often
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zharov  condescending towards students/disorganized. Made him aware of a family trip MONTHS in advance and he was very rude when I reminded him. Grading criteria is easy. Not too much pressure to be perfect in lab. His quizzes are hard and often unrelated to the lab. Easy grader, but a terrible teacher. Had a great TA which made the class alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The TA he chose for my lab was great, and made it real easy for us, but I've heard nightmares abt the other TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very difficult to understand. His English isn't great. Class was easy though. Just make sure to read the lab experiment notes before class.
Awful. He didn't teach ANYTHING that was on his quizzes and assignments, everything I learned in this class google taught me.  He advised on a book to get but it was completely useless as well.

Thankfully I only had him for ochem lab lecture, because I could barely understand his accent and he was not helpful at all. We spent 40 min out of every 50 min lecture taking quizzes with trivial questions about the labs, and he barely went over the lab information. He didn't really seem interested in his students' success. Would not recommend.

He is incomprehensible in lecture and is dismissive when you ask for help. One of the worst professors I've ever had. Introduces NMR with IR spectroscopy before teaching functional groups. Then unnecessarily crams in organometallics in the last part of class. If you take his class, the book is your only friend. Do plenty of practice problems.

Amazing organic teacher. Difficult course, but worth it. Accent not strong enough to cause misunderstanding. He made Organic Chemistry my most interesting class this past semester, and as a result I am taking O Chem 2 next semester, even though it isn't required for my major. I highly recommend him to anyone willing to work.

Amazing professor, I recommend that everyone try to take organic from him. He explains the concepts very well, and does a great job preparing you for the tests. When it comes to the final, he basically bends over backwards to prepare you. If you don't study and go to class you are basically guaranteed at least a B.

hard to understand his accent (sitting up front helps). goes through the material very quickly. likes to put other questions on the exam that were not emphasized in class but students were to "infer" from doing the homework. notes are not very helpful, practically from the book. overall a very nice guy but not a great teacher.

Dr. Ilse is amazing, engaging, & works with students to accommodate them, she wants you to succeed. Grades are based on quizzes from textbook, research paper 1, research proposal 2, in class attendance (extra credit for going to majority of classes), and presentation on research from paper 1. Highly recommend this professor, Ive taken her 3 times.

The class I took was a breeze. I learned more than I thought that I would. Prof is very caring towards you and your education. Low workload & no exams. The class did have one presentation. Not too bad! I would retake her classes if I had the chance to.

Take a class from her! She's a very sweet and caring prof. There were no exams but there are weekly chapter quizzes to replace the exams. There is a presentation and paper but overall, not too much work in the class. As long as you show up and do the reading, you should be able to get an A!

A very nice lady, she is very caring and empathetic with students, especially online. While it was not very hard, I learned a lot because the papers she assigned were of a topic of your choosing, making it easy to get interested and involved in them.

Professor Kim is very nice and seems very knowledgeable. I didn't know much about IT and got interested after taking the class from him. Very organized class. Lectures are sometimes a little long though. If you be there in classes and listen to what he says, you will get a good grade so try not to miss many classes. I recommend the class!
Most boring class of all time. Takes attendance. 5 quizzes all are very easy. 3 exams which are not tough. Group project is not difficult either.

Kim is a very nice person who seems to care about his students learning, but he is very unclear and extremely boring. Lecture after lecture for every class. There are three tests which aren't that difficult if you put in the time to study and a big group project at the end of the semester that can really boost your grade.

Iljoo Kim (SJU) is very straightforward with basically everything he does. The first two exams are so easy, however, the final is more challenging. All the assignments that you do for this class you will get a 100 if you do them. Iljoo just wants you to complete them. Iljoo is not a good fundamental teacher but he is very straightforward.

I think that he was a very good professor that knows how to properly teach. All you had to do for good scores was just attending every class and listen to every word of his saying. I remember this professor was very kind and willing to go out of his way to make students pass. He had great passion for teaching and a wide knowledge in his expertise.

Nice guy but horrible at lecturing. He would go through 70-90 slides per chapter and repeat himself constantly. Content in class was word for word from the textbook. No need to go to class just read the book.

Only managed to get an A due to the mandated curve. Studied hard for all test but got low Bs. Test studied the least for I got the highest score. 95% of lectures are very boring. Tests are super vague and studying hardly helps. Just score above the averages and you should be able to get an A. Didnt seem like he cared about the class much at all.

I have had numerous experiences with marketing before I took this class. However, I struggled in his class because the test questions were too vague, and even reading the material and going to class were not helpful. The best time to talk to him is right after class, but he almost never seems to respond to emails/Canvas messages.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a great guy and you will definitely learn a lot about marketing. Some of it is common sense but it is worth it. His lectures are sometimes dry but he has a lot to teach and not a ton of time to do so. He tries to make it fun though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Respectful, knowledgeable, and super nice! Lectures are sometimes a little boring but the material covered is always straightforward

This class wasn't super difficult but very unorganized. He told us there may be a few questions on the test form the book but there was a ton of questions from the book. Lectures are boring and out of order compared to the book. You have to go on your own and read the book to do good on the test.

The most terrible professor ever. His lecture is incredibly boring. His exam questions are vague, and he never reviews the exams. We had some homework assignments during semester, but he did not get around to grading them until the semester was over. He also didn't post our final grade by due date, so we got an EU grade. I can't believe this.

Ian is a something else. Really nice guy but sometimes I wonder if he really knows what's going on. He takes the entire semester to grades tests, forgets to bring enough tests to class, and sounds like he could care less about being there. I want to give him a good rating but I can't honestly say he truly deserves one.

This guy was nice but his lectures were boring. You show up to class and read the chapters and you'll be fine. He makes you write what you liked/disliked about the lecture at the very end of class just to make you stay the whole time. The 3 speakers that come were pretty interesting though. Should be an easy class overall though.
Really nice guy who cares about his students and puts a lot of work into the class. One of the better required classes I've taken
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is one of the most kind and knowledgeable professors. He is passionate about what he teaches and makes it easy to understand. He tells you from the beginning, the study guide is not exhaustive and there is material from the book on the exam.I attended every class,took notes,studied VERY hard, and got high As on all exams. I highly recommend him!

Skurnik knows his stuff in marketing. His lectures are dry and will put you to sleep at 7:30am but so will most professors who teach marketing to someone who isn't very interested in it. Overall the class is okay.

Skurnik was OK, lectures were OK, class in general was OK. After the tests and everything, my grade was a B but was curved to an A. Tests are mediocre, not too difficult if you fill out the study guide and study it. I started studying about 2 days before each exam. Skurnik hates when people talk in class and will let you know.

Teaches with powerpoints that aren't helpful, and lectures are boring/hard to sit through. Makes you write about what you learned in the class so you stay through the whole thing. Didn't know what to expect on tests - went in thinking they were easy but got 30/50. Vague questions that he never covered. Pretty easy class though, take just for credit

Professor Skurnik lectures each class from slides, was often late and unorganized, and doesn't seem to care that no one is paying attention. By the end of the semester we still had not received the grades on the writing portion of any test which meant over 30% of our grade was a surprise when final grades were posted.

Nice guy. Lectures are very dry and he gets thrown off easily. He doesn't remind you about exams or homework due dates so make sure to follow the syllabus. 80% of exam is from lecture, 20% from required readings. I never really did the readings and I still did good in the class.

Not the greatest professor. My huge problem is his study guide for exams is atrocious. AND.. he will put questions on his exams that weren't even on the study guide. He never does reviews for exams either. Just a dry professor. At least he's nice, though.

Ian was a very cool professor.  For non-Marketing majors, his class is super informative and overall pretty easy.  He shows you some really cool topics that make you think about your reality as a consumer.  Super easy homework, interesting lectures, and average difficulty exams make this class and easy A/B depending on your effort. Enjoy!

He seems like a pretty nice guy. I found the class frustrating however, as about 90% of the exam questions were super easy if you attended class but about 10% of the questions were questions randomly pulled out of the book. I didn't buy the book and I was able to barely get an A.

There are 3 midterms, final exam, and 3 assignments. Assignments are easy. If you want to get A, read textbook. There are some problems he did not cover in class. Tests are easy if you go to class and read textbook. Plus, you need to write short comments about what you learned and turn that in after every class period to get attendance points

Ian Skurnik knows the material well, but has a very dry sense of humor and speaks in monotone. There's learning to be had, but mostly from the textbook. I felt interested and engaged in class about 20-30% of the time. Slow turnaround time on grades. Read the textbook and refer to his slides to prepare for the tests. He will draw questions from both

Pretty boring class so I rarely went. Not that difficult of a class. I dont think he even reads the case study homework assignments we have to turn in. Mostly an easy class but also boring. He makes it sound like you need the textbook but I never bought it and most things can be found on his slides or online if you need help.

Long boring lectures that only covers a fraction of the material that he tests on. Dosn't warn you about upcoming tests so make sure you follow the syllabus. He also dosn't put final grades in when they are do, so that is very frustrating as I am waiting on his course to determine my GPA. I would definitely advise against taking this class him.
lectures are boring af, assignments are easy, exams are horrible. he's really broad on what you have to study for for the exams, and the questions are hard. study everything.

ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE. Literally worst professor I've taken at the U. Does not teach anything just reads off of a bunch of slides. Doesn't go over midterms at all, no reminders or anything ever. Just expects you to follow syllabus and know when they are. DO NOT TAKE WITH IAN. Makes a marketing major want to switch majors. Not an easy A either.

You honestly don't have to study much to get a decent grade. However all the readings are super long (which I gave up on), slides are awful to study from because he uploads them as pdf. Didn't submit grades by the due date and which gave all his classes EUs. Doesn't post any grades an reasonable amount of time.

Classes are long and super boring! Lots of slides that don't help at all for the tests.  Grades take forever to be posted. We didn't get the grade from test 1 until the day before we took test 2. Homework grades were not posted until after we took the final exam. No idea how you're doing. When final grades were to be posted he forgot to do it!

In three years at the U Skurnik is by far the worse professor I have had. His classes are based off of slides with a lot of pictures and little information so you can't study from them. He is extremely boring in lectures and does not make it clear how the info will be on the test. I learned very little in this class. Take from someone else.

Very boring class. Possibly the easiest subject in business to make interesting and relevant to students, yet I found it the most boring of my business courses. I attended class everyday and received nothing out of it. A nice guy but couldn't care less about his students.

Very boring class. Did not learn anything. I came to class everyday, did my assignments including the out of class participation  and the day grades post he gives me an EU grade. I believe this means he just forgot to post them, i was not the only one with this issu. I don't know what else he does but teaching and his students are not a priority.

He lectures a lot on his power point slides and gives real life examples on how to apply some of the marketing concepts. My complaints are that he does not respond promptly to emails and he still has not graded the homework assignments at semester's end, which is nice to know where you stand before you take the final.

His lectures are based off of the power point slides that he makes and he provides examples on how to apply the different marketing concepts. The complaints I have are that he does not respond to emails very promptly and he still has not graded our homework assignments yet and the semester has already ended.

Ian is very awkward. He's not very clear in what he was saying. His class was super easy, but he didn't really teach a lot. I have learned more about marketing in other places than I did in this class.
Presents material well, and tests are very straight forward
clear and enjoys teaching marketing

Ian is the nicest cutest teacher. You can tell this guy tries hard and tries to keep people engaged even though he might not always succeed. I would highly recommend taking this class because it is easy and a great introduction into marketing that doesn't make you want to quit. Great guy though.

Participation is based on a paper you turn in the end of class. Lectures were BORING! Provides study guide but still not that clear and helpful. Overall it was a low stress class but extremely boring and hard to stay interested and motivated.

Meh - nice guy but classes are pretty dull. Gives a study guide for his tests. Also tests on minor details only found in the text/ not listed on study guide. It made it somewhat difficult to be 100% ready on test days.
Gotta love having a teacher that actually knows what they're talking about AND makes it interesting. Nice guy, relatively easy course.
Great class, great teacher! He's really helpful easy to work with. Go to class, take notes, study the slides but don't forget to read the chapters. He does test on things not covered in class.

Skurnik is an awesome professor. His class is really interesting and you learn a lot. What is even more awesome is that his tests actually reflect what he teaches which seems to be becoming a foreign concept up here. He's a super nice guy. Tests are multiple choice.
This class was pretty easy and I learned a lot without reading too much or having strenuous homework. I liked him.

Classes are not mandatory, he posts his lectures online but you will learn a lot more in class obviously, he is nice always in a good mood and always willing to answer questions. We havent taken a test yet but he does give you a study guide the week before the test. So far so good!
Ian is a really nice guy, he's very cheery and classes were enjoyable. The tests aren't graded on a curve, so I was worried about my grade all semester, but the final grades are curved generously.

Chris is an easy going professor. Native English speaker. 

Homework: 60pgs/wk of philosophical reading. 50% is difficult to understand. 

In-class Participation: (10% of grade) in-depth discussion about readings

Final: (90% of grade) You pick a project that incorporates an anti-anthropocentric perspective. Rubric given sporadically during classes

Good dude. He is not great with responding to Email but if you ask him in person he is very helpful. A lot of reading for the class but honestly it is a college class nothing out of the usual. I loved the course.

Prof. Ingraham's passion for the natural environment & the discipline of communications is exciting. He gives constructive feedback but isn't a tough grader. COMM 5360 doesn't have any busywork  it's just reading and a couple of big projects. Prof Ingraham just wants students to learn, have meaningful conversations, and be changed by the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved this class! He is really funny and cares about his students. His class is not really hard at all and if you get in and get the assignments done its super easy. Also you can go ahead as far as you want. Would totally recommend!

This is a phenomenal class! Take it now! This is one of the most interesting and useful classes I've ever taken! Prof. R. equally as awesome! He cares, he's fun, he gives amazing feedback, and his #1 goal is that you are learning and doing well! If you want to get into app programming or just have an amazing class and teacher, take this class!!

Professor I is very smart and has created a course that helps you learn thoroughly while not feeling overwhelmed. I was scared to take this class, but with his help I was able to get an A. If I can do it, you can. He will help you and wants you to succeed. He cares more about you really grasping the concepts all the way than about rigidity. Do it.

It is a great class AAA+++. You will learn a lot to build a solid foundation skills to develop android applications. Professor Richard is always there if you need any help or guidance with your work. Assignments are super easy if you follow the video lectures and read book chapters that is also provided to you. Highly recommended!

This teacher was amazing! Very open about how hard the class was going to be, but was extremely helpful along the way. Swears in class sometimes, FYI. Extensive homework, but the nature of the class made it basically for-credit, so just turn it in and you're fine. Sad to see her leaving the U but to those that find this later, take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Obviously cares about her students and the course content. I highly recommend her class!

Ines is a really outstanding teacher. She really cares about both the subject matter and her students. The class was very interactive and she made sure to meet the needs of the students. She is a natural educator, explains things very well and doesn't mind taking extra time to make sure everyone understands the concepts.

Ines is a darling human being and a wonderful teacher. She's so good at meeting every student's needs and it so willing to help. 20th century theory is really hard, but somehow she made it easy for me to understand. If you need help, Ines is always there for you and she's one of those teachers who actually cares about you as a person, too.

Inese is such a sweet lady, but bless her heart she is incredibly boring. However, she will work with you and do whatever she can to help you. Fridays are group work days and can be unorganized, the Friday packets are a large part of the grade so it's worth going. There are lots of math packets for homework so if weak in math avoid the class.

Prof. Ivans is super sweet and knowledgable on what she's talking about. Sometimes she can get off topic during lectures but it's easy to go back through the lectures online after class. She uses a free online textbook which is super nice. Make sure to go on Friday's if you only want to go to class once a week, and pay attention to the study guides

Personally I do not enjoy this class. The professor cannot teach and if you have a TA they will give you feedback. Since it's 3 days out of the week, on Fridays you have group work and they are unorganized.

Ivans expects you to read from the text book (not even really a textbook, Welcome To The Universe) but it is only about one chapter per week. The homework is extensive but with in class help and an optional, free, textbook, the homework isn't too hard. Ivans obviously loves astronomy and it makes the class better and more entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Would take again

reviews.comment: Inese tries to make her lectures as interesting as possible, but doesn't explain much. Unless you have a previous knowledge of astronomy you will probably get lost in the jargon, so make sure you read the textbook before each lecture. Assignments are easy and there's lots of opportunities for extra credit. She has a unique way of generous grading.
She's super easy to understand and even easier to learn from

She is one of the best teachers I have ever had. And without a doubt, one of the most influential people in my life. I haven't taken any direct courses from her. But, I have worked in her research group for many years. She truly cares about her students. And you can learn a lot.

She left after two weeks of the class beginning and had a different sub every week. To try to combat this, she made it so that all of our homework suddenly did not count and only half the attendance counted. She tried to help but was just way too disorganized. No good.

She is probably one of the most caring teachers at the university. She really wants everyone to get an A, but, bless her heart, she is really really boring. She doesn't teach very well, but she is trying, and is always looking for feedback on how to do better. She makes it easy to get an A!

I took the Foundations of Astronomy course from Professor Ivans, and she's pretty fair. The homework isn't required to be turned in, but all the questions on the exams are drawn from it. She gives you lots of opportunities to get a good grade in her class.
Loved her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Inozemtseva is a tremendous professor she cares about her students and wants them to know that math in enjoyable to learn.

By the way, she's now a Precalculus prof. at ASU. And she is by far the WORST teacher I have ever had. She is incredibly disorganized, and she rarely ever actually teaches us. She only goes over the previous homework from the days before, and then she leaves us to do more homework on subjects we haven't even learned yet. Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took her for both calc 1 and 2, and I would have taken calc 3 with her if she was teaching it. She is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is incredibly funny, caring, and she's a total cutie! She is more than willing to work with her students outside class, and she truly wants everyone to succeed. You won't regret taking her class.

She's honestly so amazing. I knew I was in the right class after she made her first Rick and Morty joke. She's incredibly nice, works very hard to prepare awesome lectures and offers so much outside class time where she will personally help you.  She wants her students to succeed. If she's offering a class, take it. Hands down favorite teacher ever

Julia is the best math instructor that I have ever had. She teaches you the essentials and avoids extraneous information. She moves very fast, but if you work hard and keep up it will pay off. She offers extra credit for those willing to work for it. Her accent is not difficult to understand and she is very kind. I highly recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is the best professor ever. She really cares about her students. I missed two weeks of class at the beginning of the semester and she took her own time to help me catch up. She gives a lot of example questions in her lecture which is so helpful.

Julia is the best teacher I've ever had. She holds hour long study review sessions out side of class twice a week that anyone can go to and she'll help you do your homework whether you've started or not! She's believes that everyone can pass! She's young, and has a very good sense of humor. If there's a spot in her class open in her class, TAKE IT!

Easily the best math instructor I've ever had. She puts in a lot of effort outside of class to make her students pass. She's well prepared and very funny and personable. I highly recommend her class, especially if you struggle with math.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Julia is the best math teacher I've ever had. She is really passionate about teaching and she makes class really fun. She loves to joke around and make everyone laugh, and she gives out tons of extra credit opportunities if you are willing to work for it. She knows what should and should not be taught, so you don't learn a bunch of useless material
She is really nice and caring. weekly easy assignment, solving the assignment problem during the classes. review most of question during the exam

He is very passionate about math and wants to make sure that students understand the material. I went to office hours and he answered all questions I had. All of the students in this class had previously taken either Calc AB or BC and many were shocked that a college math course required work. Go to class, office hours, do the homework, and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have no idea who wrote the last few positive reviews. But it definitely doesn't represent the opinions of the majority of the class. The reviews of the class are not due to student laziness (I spent 30 hours per week on the class alone). Rather, Yannis consistently expected students to know complex proofs beyond the scope of the curriculum.

Ioannis is able to explain things in so many different ways that it's very easy to understand the material once you take a second look at your notes. Ioannis was more than happy to work with students who wanted to put in the work and actually earn a good grade. Too many students expected an A based on prior knowledge and didn't put in the work!

This class requires you to actually be engaged in your learning. His lectures provide a deep understanding of the math in Calculus and helps to really comprehend the computations. If you're looking to rely on knowledge from previous AP Calculus courses to pass, don't take this class. It will actually require you to learn and improve. Shocking.
Very knowledgeable, but also very tough. I often felt overwhelmed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This course was extremely difficult. Calc 1250 is comprised of students who scored well on AB or BC Calc in Highschool. All of us are usually A students, however, the average in class is around a C, with many failing. Ioannis' lectures are so difficult to understand. He's very smart but perhaps too smart to teach this class. Super tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For a student who scored a 5 on the AB Calc test, Freshman Honors Calc I should have been easy. He knows too much about math to explain concepts effectively, his reviews do not line up with the exams he gives out, and he doesn't answer questions other than to write out quick solutions which are "intuitive" to him but not his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: By far the hardest class I have ever taken. Which would be an interesting challenge if he would actually explain concepts in a way that freshman honors calculus students can understand. However, he does not. The tests are not "intuitive" at all like the way he thinks they are. It's the type of class where maybe one student can get an A.

Yannis is a good guy and teacher, he's even funny. He clearly knows his stuff but I had a difficult time relating his lectures to the homework. The content got difficult as the semester went on, but he kept the same speed as the first few easy weeks. The content was difficult for me. I like Yannis but I would go with a different professor.

A complete disappointment. He does not teach in a way that non-Ph.D. students can actually understand. Proof by induction and complex analysis does not belong in calculus. The grade distribution for the class is horrible and when so many honors students who scored well on the AP Calculus test are failing, you know you're doing something wrong.

He can't dumb things down enough for students to understand. He expects all his students to have a background in AB and BC Calc when almost half hadn't taken AB. I personally took AB and never learned most of the techniques he used. He skips steps when he lectures and his tests are strange and unfair. Do not take his class.

This professor is by far the worst professor I have ever received.  HIs lectures NEVER came from the book. They were lectures that he came up with that he thought were important. On top of that he has a strong accent so it is incredibly hard to understand what he's saying. The final grade is based on 3 tests and a group project, that's all he has.

One of the most dissappointing classes I took as an undergrad at the U. Criminology could be so interesting, but this guy could clearly care less about teaching any longer. It's true, the group project is awful. Some interesting speakers and it was an easy enough A-, but I like my classes a lot more engaging.

You never get to see your tests, he just shows up and gives you a score.  He wouldn't return my emails when I had a question about my grade and he was generally flaky. He makes the class seem easy, then gives you a crappy grade.  Their is something fishy about how he determines grades.  The group project sucked - he gives you very little guidance.

Obviously has no real interest in teaching.  Almost the whole football team was in my class so I expected it to be easy; especially when he only lectured for 45 minute of a 3 hour course.  Sure, the class seems easy, but at the end of the semester I ended up with a B+! Maybe if he had showed a little more commitment to the course, so would have I.
Waste of time.  Poor instruction.  Easy tests.  Poor teacher.
not worth the money.  only teaches for approx 60 minutes out of a 3 hour class...some students love it, but it feels a little lacking...i think he might be burnt out

Easy class for the most part. The group project/presentation is the major part of your grade.  Get a good group. No chapter tests; instead, just a mid-term test and a final test.  Both are easy. Be sure to show up on his test review night. Good guest speakers.  Overall, fun and interesting class -- I'm still pissed that I got an A-!
Good teacher. Study what he tells you to. If you go to class and listen, you might actually learn something.
buder cares a lot about her students and it shows. really helpful in office hours.
Learned a lot from Dr. Buder. Micro was not the most interesting course, but she made it enjoyable. Lectures are easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: you'll get very confused
Really hard to understand what she wants us to write on our exams and no extra credits are offered.

very very sweet professor, but if you're a second language speaker you will be screwed. she speaks too fast and she covers all the materials in the book like she was reading from the book to you. her exams are essay questions type of exams and you will never get more than 70%. i don't honestly know is it me or her? please share more about her guys

Such a great professor.  I had her for a night class and we wouldn't go longer than we needed to go, but at the same time she was willing to help out and explain anything if they needed help.  She WANTS everyone to get "A"s - a fantastic professor.
One of the better teaching asst at the University, She is super helpful and very willing to help in class and on exams. Never Studied and and took an A-

Decent professor. Over all she was a super tough grader. At first I signed up for her class online, and then when I saw that you had to write online discussions every week. So i decided to enroll in an "in class" class, but we still ended up doing discussion online every week instead of discussing in class which seemed to me like extra busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Irene is an awesome professor.

Irene Ota will change your life. I have never been more inspired by a human than by Irene. She is incredibly smart. She is kind but firm. If Irene Ota was President, our world problems would be solved.

Ota takes a constructionist perspective(truth is based on how the individual interprets it, ie there is no truth)keep that in mind when you are studying. Write down definitions from lectures because Ota's interpretation of the material is the test, not the actual material. Do this and you will do well Always include at least 3 references. GoodLuck!

Irene is truly a one of a kind person and teacher. Trust me when I say be sure you do every assignment and extra credit opportunity, as each point really does make a different in the end for her grading scale. Her tests are full of trick questions and incredibly hard--ye be warned!

I have never dreaded doing homework more than in this class. It is almost impossible to get full credit on an assignment. She doesn't require a textbook, but the readings are a bunch of articles that she has scanned and posts on Canvas. I would rather have a textbook. Her test questions are confusing and the answers are all subjective.

Irene will change your life. She makes you work hard but you will learn so much. I can't say enough good things about Irene... I wish this class was mandatory for everyone to take because Irene opens her student's eyes and makes everyone a better human.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Tests are very difficult! However, Irene is a great professor and has a lot of great information to teach. Grading can be tough but that's why it's a 4 credit course. Do yourself a favor and don't miss ANY assignments even if they're only worth a couple points.
She is a genuinely nice person and when family matters came up, she was super understanding. Her class wasn't the easiest for me but she is a really good professor. (:

Irene is one of the best professors I have ever had. If you have a hard time talking about privilege, you will be uncomfortable at first, but go for it! She is absolutely incredible and has fantastic insights. I think her class should be required, as it was extremely eye-opening. I learned a ton. The tests are a little hard to prepare for.

I love this woman, but here is my advice -- 1) Don't count on test scores for a good grade, 2) follow the class discussion/critical analysis paper instructions listed in the syllabus, 3) do the extra credit, and 4) she is not trying to change your heart/mind/soul, but know the material and base your papers off WWIT -- What Would Irene Think?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Like many of the other reviews say you absolutely have to be willing to open your mind and look at things from a different perspective to succeed in this class. Even if you disagree with Irene you have to be able to see where she is coming from and why. Her exams are TOUGH and there is no way to study because you have to know HER definitions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you have the same view of the world that Irene does then you shouldn't have an issue. However, if your own opinion and arguments  differ from hers, she will not give you a good grade on your papers. I am a very diligent student, but this class was extremely frustrating for me, I felt like I wasn't heard and wasn't given feedback how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Irene is my favorite teacher! Her class is challenging only if you aren't ready to open your eyes to your own privilege. Be sure to attend class and do the extra credit. I got an A but I had to put in the effort and do all the readings. She is amazing, I recommend her!

You will get a lot out of this class, however if you want an A, you have to work your butt off. Don't ever skip class, ever!! She takes attendance. Get help on the critical reflections so you know what you're doing!! Also, make sure to do any extra credit she offers, you can't get an A if you don't do the extra credit, that's how hard her class is!

This was the best class I've had in college, but it is very difficult with extensive reading. It is also very emotionally taxing as the content discussed is serious and requires introspection/self-awareness. Tests are extremely difficult. Not the class to take if you aren't ready to develop a critical conscience or own your privilege.
she is an amazing teacher! Her class was challenging but essential to my learning! I loved her class!
This was a great class and I learned a lot. Irene will open your eyes to new ideas and you will become much more aware of your own surroundings and the diverse world in which we live. Love her

To get a good grade in this class requires some effort, but the materials are made interesting by Irene's passion and she is always willing to clarify or review material that is unclear to the class. She welcomes comments and none of the writing assignments are long or difficult.
As long as you don't treat his class as a joke, it's really not that bad. He can be a bit dry of a lecturer at times, but generally speaking I thought what he presented was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: World of Dinosaurs was an awesome class. Randy gave long lectures, but I rarely got bored. He was always really excited about what he was teaching, and he made bad jokes all the time, which I loved. He is clear about what he wants you to learn and know for the test, and the lecture notes are KEY to passing the class.

Randall didn't seem to realize that 99% of the students in class just wanted a general out of the way and had no interest in the subject. He treated it like it was a major specific course. He droned on through lectures, never keeping on track, and often stumbled over his own words. He failed to keep his material even slightly interesting. AVOID!!!!
