Seemed like a really nice woman but man this was my least favorite class I have ever taken at the U. Profoundly boring. If it is a required class find a different professor. It is an easy A if you do the assignments on time but its not worth it. She did not seem like she wanted to be teaching. I hope she figures it out.

Worst professor I've ever had. She says um every three words. She uses a really small grading scale- quizzes and assignments out of 3. She will give you a 2/3 for the tiniest thing, usually not even a mistake but something that she wanted more from-instructions for assignments are unclear and vague, so it's hard to know what she actually wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tone used to address questions frequently came across as dismissive, which created a horrible learning environment. She had lectures twice a week and just talks at you for hours. Additionally, explanations often assumed an advanced understanding of coding, which left me and other students confused. The most difficult and unhelpful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are weekly quizzes with 10 detailed questions in a 5 minute time limit so roughly
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not an engaging lecturer. Not enough confidence, clarity, or organization in the slides. Mandatory attendance quizzes every week with tight time limits of around 30 seconds per question. The material is very simple, with much of it being covered in 8th-grade science and math classes, but she somehow makes it difficult to digest.

Has extensively questioned quizzes every day that are 10 questions each and only gives five minutes TOTAL. Its seriously like 20 seconds per question, she is setting us up for failure. After the whole class emailed her about it her only response was "come better prepared" like what??? Lectures go back and forth and do not make much sense either.

She is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. She gives really good feedback and opportunities to correct mistakes. She makes difficult subjects easy to understand, and will help with anything you need. She's super funny and kind, and never made it awkward for anyone to speak up in her class. I highly recommend her.

She is so sweet and caring! Her lectures are very helpful. She explains difficult material in a way that makes it very easy to understand and master. The material is tough at this level but she is very accommodating and makes sure all her students succeed.

I loved Professor Williams. She is so friendly and always willing to help. The class was hard, there was a lot of homework and quizzes. Attendance is mandatory and she wasn't allowed to cancel class.
Professor Williams is so sweet, I highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very clear and concise material presentation

Grading from Butte College! The class was very informational and inspiring as an MCGS course. Lots of articles to read and interpret and many discussions both in class and online as homework. There are no exams or quizzes, just writing assignments to show you have been reading and understanding the class. Give effort and participate in discussions

Rating him from a Butte College course, Chicano American Studies. You write a mini essay every two to three weeks along with a discussion post. It's a lot of writing paired with very long articles and books to base your essay/discussion off of. The content is interesting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am taking this professor's Chicano Studies class. He does a great job getting across his message and shares a lot readings and film from different authors, etc...

One of the best professor that I took for Fall semesters, he was easy going, give you time to do your midterm. also there are no late penalty because he really want you to learn and pass his class. he also helps you if you are unsure on what to do when writing your midterms and finals.

Guzman really cares! He's a great communicator! His course includes great reading, and writing assignments, as well as class discussions. You will improve you all three, while not feeling beaten before or after an assignment. Overall, a really down to earth professor that gives a calming effect in the classroom,  and understands his students.

Prof Guzman is one of the coolest professors I've ever had. He "gets it". He knows how college is and is very understanding if it's not your day. In this class we read (for hw), watched movies (in-class), wrote papers ( not hard if you really get into it), and had intense, powerful discussions in class. Be ready to participate if you want to learn!
Great instructor. Provided comfortable environment in which to discuss difficult topics.

This class is a joke, expects close to 100 pages to be read a week and then write a profound Critical Reflection paper that need to be 2-3 pages.  Just an outrageous amount of busy work for a diversity class that focuses on Ethnic Min Families.  Clearly a professor who thinks his class is the only thing important you will do in your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Isidoro Guzman is a great instructor. The class I took through him was online (ETHNC 3290) and it was very informative. He gives great feedback with every critical reflection. He also is accessible through email and responds in a timely matter.

Isi is a great professor. He understands the material and unpacks it in a way that is really beneficial for students. This class handles difficult social issues and makes students think about the world around them with a critical eye. Isi was opinionated, but never created an environment where someone couldn't speak their mind.
This is a fun class and I think Isi taught it well. You discuss a lot of touchy subjects and he did it without hurting feelings which is nice. He gives great feedback on assignments.

I enjoyed his class and I actually missed a few times because I had some family problems going on and I still passed the class with an A. I just made sure I communicated with him and he totally understood. I did all the assignments, went to the study sessions for the exams, extra credit, did the readings and the class was easy.

Easy class. Readings are expected, but he goes over every single one through powerpoints so you could take notes during class. Tests are easy if you go to the study sessions.  Lectures (powerpoints) are kind of long and boring, but he tries to be helpful in any way he can. Great teacher^^
Isi was an awesome teacher. He was super helpful and approachable and led great discussions. No tests. The readings are also all posted on canvas so there isn't a huge need to get the textbooks.
best teacher at the U

As the director of the History department you might think she actually likes teaching.... if she does she doesn't show it.  She bullies students and has the classic "I'm better than you" personality. You can do well in the class if you work hard and pander to her, but you might have to compromise your dignity to do it.
Thoroughly hateful.  She is Shelob, the cosmic spider who weaves her webs of deception, capturing & strangling all light.  AVOID AVOID AVOID at all costs!

Amazing teacher!!Assignment was to write a 20 pg essay, I had some trouble with finding a concept and after that my first draft was a disaster. Even though Professor Moreira is very busy she was so patient with me and helped me get to a place where I LOVED what I was writing and had a finished essay that I was proud of.She pushes you to be better!
Without a doubt, the most unpleasant professor I have ever encountered. She will make you hate your life and all that is in it.  Her classes are soul-snuffing torture.  Avoid at all costs!

This is the easiest writing class ever; just show up to class once a week and don't let attendance ruin your grade, and the rest is a piece of cake. Not too much HW, essay for final, but easy A with barely any effort.

I love prof Ito! He is a grad student and the majority of his class was a discussion. It was a 50 min session once a week. I thought the class was very easy, with very few assignments. The final paper was a 2000 word researched argument which you could write about anything. 100% loved him as a professor, great choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ito is a grad student but super knowledgeable about basically everything. The entire class was discussion based, most of it student lead. Simple weekly assignments just responding to the reading. There's 3 short papers total. Overall an easy class with a lot of student involvement. He has a slight accent but it was easy to get used to.

I did not understand his material at all and could never find the lessons I needed to pass his class. He does not explain material very well. He is the hardest teacher I have ever had. I had a hard year and he had an exam due the day that something tragic happened to me, he said he would unlock it for me but it never got unlocked so I failed it.

First of all, very rude. I'm not just a disgruntled student but some of his ignorant comments were not needed. I would avoid taking his online class, as he does not explain well and it blatantly rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class online and found it to be quite easy. The material is interesting enough, and the tests were representative of the material covered.
Russ' exams have lots of his lectures on it which is unfortunate for an online class but it is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class was only graded on a few things throughout the semester, which is both good and bad depending on what kind of student you are. There were three papers, four tests, and a few discussion posts. All of the guidelines are clearly stated and if you read over the lessons before completing the test, you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I did better after the first test because I knew what to expect. If you demonstrate to him that you have interest in understanding the subject and want to learn, he is willing to help you learn! He is fast to respond to emails and genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class was really interesting!  It involves participation in online discussions, a couple of easy papers, and tests based mainly on the lectures.  Tests are open book and open note.  Don't miss too many lectures because he pulls a lot of the test questions right from those.

Loved Isabella's lecture notes he provided. Gives study guides prior to tests, weekly reminders, and grades relatively quickly. Textbook is necessary as some test questions come directly from the text.

Professor Isabella was good as far as an online class is concerned. He presents notes on the subject for each week, which are written in his own voice so they are easy to understand and stay interested in. Great class if you're looking to pass with minimal effort. Tests are online, open book, open note, but kind of confusing.
Very easy class. You had to do two of the four assignments offered. I read the lectures right before taking the tests, and did really well.

This professor is very straight-forward, one assignment (the entire semester), offers extra credit and exams are super easy. I did not have the book but I printed every single lesson he posted online and I did just fine! First time taking an online class and I loved it!

On-line:  Dr. Isabella is a wonderful, caring & considerate professor.  Although this course was on-line & as such, there isn't much interaction to be expected, he was still thoughtful & thorough.  This class is FUN!  Lots of reading & tests are challenging so keep up.  Remember... it's not his job to GIVE you a grade, it's your job to EARN it.
Beleive thats tests were difficult, he really likes to confuse you and give you two very similar answers which both could be right. Though the tests were all mulitple choice.

I absolutely loved this online class.  As mentioned, a lot of reading is required.  However, it is well worth it; all of the material is very interesting and fun to learn.  Only one assignment due throughout the year.  I strongly recommend taking this class online if you have the time for reading.

Loved this course.  Three books but the reading is easily manageable.  Make sure to come to class with something to add.  Really make sure to come to class.  There is a project at the end where you basically get to do whatever you want.
CLEAR EXPECTATIONS, NO HOMEWORK OTHER THAN STUDYING FOR EXAMS, LARGE CLASS-SIZE, NO PROJECTS.
He does require a lot of reading but the tests are easy. The assignment was also easy.
Hard class but well worth it.  Expect a lot of reading and a lot of time spent on the paper.  You wont regret taking this class!
Dr. Isabella was extremely pompus.  He believes that his class is the only true class out there.  The course is ridiculous for non-majors.
No Comments
Very straight forward, great teacher.  Teaches in class or online, easiest online class I have taken.
This was a 4 week online class.  He did require a lot of reading, but it was interesting.  The tests were multiple choice and quite easy.  He was very quick to respond to any emails I would send.

This class is pretty lecture-heavy, but Ivan posts all of his lectures online so they are accessible for later use. He does tend to read off the slides but also provides lots of important information if you ask. You have to participate in 10 different classes, and there are 3 midterms that are all based heavily on lectures. Homework is completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was very okay. It is a basic finance class and consists of only lectures, 3 homeworks, 3 tests, and a participation grade. Professor Munoz knows his stuff but does not explain things very well. You have to participate 10x for participation & the homeworks are the questions on the test. If you have no finance knowledge, he is not awesome.

The class was certainly challenging. I learned a lot and the professor made it really enjoyable. Anytime I had questions or concerns the professor always got back quick or was happy to meet in person to help clarify uncertainties. Overall, amazing class and the professor really wants to see his students succeed.

Ivan Munoz made this course hard! I did not learn much from his lectures and his handwriting is almost impossible to read. I had to result to learning from the textbook and Khan Academy to learn the topics on the tests because his lectures were difficult to learn from. If possible take 4020 from a different professor.

(QAMO 3201)Ivan is a very decent teacher who makes his expectations very clear. The three assignments we are given are nearly carbon copies of the three tests that follow. Class attendance is pretty important as he takes down your participation each class, but missing here and there isn't so detrimental. Overall it seems like he knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome class, which covered complex topics. Ivan is an expert in time series econometrics. The assignments are the right balance between relearning what we go over in class and also being challenging. Ivan is also very passionate and knowledgeable, and genuinely wants his students to pursue their passions and succeed.

Very rigorous course! I found Ivan's combined use of slides and the whiteboard very effectiveparticularly because he provided them in advance of class. I printed them out and took notes from the lecture on them which facilitated the assignments and the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Be prepared to learn the material on your own. He is more interested in showing off what he knows rather than actually teaching the material. Lectures are sloppy and disorganized. Will make you regret asking a question in class.

Ivan teaches a very hard course (PhD level Econometrics) and he does it well. He gave me great feedback and when my work wasn't up to par, he let me know. I was inspired by his class to complete a research project in time series analysis. I benefitted greatly. Always answered my questions.
He's organized in what concepts he wants you to learn and study, but it's a little difficult to learn from him. I ended up having to teach myself a lot of the material.

I was worried this class would be boring, but Prof. Ivy is very passionate about the subject, and I loved attending every lecture in person, even though it wasn't mandatory. The structure and grading in this class are the best I've ever come across - you learn for yourself, not for a grade, and in a way that fits you best.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ivy provided a classic experience with quality lectures that ensured I parsed through, and consumed, the material at the best rate I possibly could. One could say the work assigned was no "arbitrarily small quantity". I would have loved to see/progress through more content with Spencer as my Professor. -TBC my friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Professor Ivy virtually and can happily say that he is a great teacher. He had long lectures but was approachable when we were progressing onto new content. Spencer made sure that we would show up prepared so that the class could run like clockwork. I have had a classic experience that I will remember fondly after taking this course.

He did a good job of transferring to Zoom university. It was hard to keep a class engaged when nobody had their cameras on. Spencer did a good job making sure we understood the material, but there were a LOT of readings and some long lectures, so get ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: At first I was a little skeptical of his accent, but if you really try to focus on what he is saying it will make sense. He goes through example problems fast thinking we all know what to do. He knows what he is doing, but he has trouble explaining it so we can understand it. If you are going to have him as a prof., do more work on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You can barely understand him, and what you do understand doesn't make sense. I literally learned nothing in this class (somehow skimmed by with an okay grade). Please don't take.
He's just not a good teacher. Very unclear, very unhelpful, and just overall bad. Don't take him for physics.
Literally the worst  professor ever. Take this class if you want to fail and learn nothing. I would rather commit suicide than take Ivan sudakov's class.
DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM AT ALL

Might be the worst teacher I've ever had. He has to be corrected in class when explaining formulas but then says were wrong when he makes us present? He is very impatient with students and does not explain anything at all to students. Horrible.
HE IS THE WOREST TEACHER EVER. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM

Honestly a good teacher.  He knows his stuff, and teaches the material and then does example problems.  If you ask questions he'll answer them, otherwise he's moving on.  So you've gotta speak up.  Only three midterms, and he drops the lowest two.  Minimum amount of homework.    Also, don't worry about the accent, he's 100% intelligible.
Excellent teacher!  there is no problem in English

Sure, A Lack of english, but he attemps to do his best. He might be little confusing, but with review  you'll get the material. He has a perfect grading scale. You might fail the final and still pass with a B or above.  I would recommend Professor Sudakov, but don't expect to learn the material in class...... Lots of Study Time is essential

Very poor english skills. Does not have the english vocabulary to effectively teach Calculus. When questions are asked by students, it seems he sometimes doesn't know how to answer them in english. Would recommend another teacher if taking this class.
Avoid this guy. Easily the worst professor I've had while at the u. Doesn't seem to care about teaching or his students. Terrible english skills.

Professor Sudakov is excellent. I thought it would be hard to understand his Russian accent when I first went to class, but it ended up being just fine. He really cares about what he is doing and he cares that you understand. He takes the time to personally grade each exam rather than have a grader do it. Highly recommended!!

I was really excited to take calculus but this professor completely ruined it for me. He was frequently unprepared, had troubles making it to class any time it snowed, and just went way too fast. I also felt his tests were harder than they needed to be. Do not take his class. You will feel more confused than ever before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but the class was definitely miserable. He had Webwork each week which took HOURS to complete and homework which was only 4-5 problems so that wasn't too bad. He also went through the lecture notes too fast for me too keep up so I basically just had to go back and learn the content on my own.

He uses webwork and makes it very difficult (needs exact answers), in a given week I have to spend 5 or so hours minimum working towards solutions. I have failed calculus and am retaking it, in my previous calc class, the homework was not nearly as hard.  Also the grading on tests is very tough, your grade will be determined by tests, beware.

I found the lectures to be good, he goes through a lot of examples of every concept. My only complaint is that he would sometimes go on tangents when answering questions. If you do well on the homework the tests will not be very difficult.

Sri is a great guy. He's kind of a quiet guy but when you get to know him he can actually be quite funny. His lectures were not the best; extremely disorganized and hard to follow, but if you can find him one on one, he can be a great teacher. His class was test heavy as most Math classes are but the tests were incredibly simple and easy.

I have little to say about Sri's lecturing because the material was difficult (I needed some time with the book regardless). However, Sri wasn't great at making sure that his students understood things before moving on. Tests were always harder than expected; not much homework (essential in this class) was required; 90% of the grade was from exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: For my class he used WebWork which is an online platform that only grades right or wrong answers. I had spent over an hour on some problems and still got the wrong answer, and because of this I wouldn't get any partial credit. Nothing against Sri this is mostly all about WebWork.

Sri is a good lecturer, meaning that when he is actually lecturing, he is good at explaining the concepts. However, he is extremely disorganized. During the semester, he changed our grading structure several times, including: adding an additional test, removing then re-adding an attendance requirement, and giving take-home quizzes.

Sri is a very nice person. I felt like he truly cared and was very understanding. He does need to work on being more clear and organized in his teaching method. The tests are difficult. I feel that he made 1030 harder than it should have been.

I hate math. Ha. But Sri was very helpful and always liked to make sure everyone understood a concept before moving on. He is also very understanding. He let me reschedule our final because it was at the same time as another one of my classes. Math sucks but Sri is pretty cool.

My love for chemistry grew immensely throughout the course of this class thanks to Dr Lessard. It's obvious he cares about the subject and wants to share that appreciation with the students. What I appreciated the most was his humility. Scientists stand on the shoulders of giants, Dr Lessard encourages us to embrace that.

There wasn't an option for Ochem 2, but he was honestly one of the best chem professors I've had. He actually cared about us learning the content and it showed. He was new and this was his first time teaching organic 2, but he honestly did a really good job with the class. Overall he was a really cool professor, if you take ochem, take it with him.
second comment

He's a cool guy and really wants to help people learn and understand organic topics. Definitely reccomend taking his class. I came out knowing so much more and really filling the gaps that were left from my previous organic studies. He's very good at helping outside of class and is very available for office hours. Sick shirts.

The quizzes were usually difficult because this professor's lectures were just a mess and unorganized. Just scribbles on the white board. Grading system is also ridiculous. Huge portion of the grade is just the quizzes and the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor just quickly touches on homework then asks clear as mud?. He doesnt care about his students. Be ready to find a tutor willing to help you pass. Lectures are so unclear and quick that most students leave class more confused than when they began. He wonders why no students can answer his questions... DONT TAKE CLASS FROM HIM!!

JB is one of the greatest professors I've had at the U. He is a CPA, and doesn't have to teach accountinghe does because he cares about his students. This is a tough class, so if you put in the effort you will be fine. Definitely take 2600 with JB; he's the best!

You get what you put into it. JB is a great professor and mentor. The people who complain are those that dont work hard and want to be given an A without the work. I got an A and I worked for it. Provides opportunity to earn points back on exams when mistakes are made. He cares about students passing and understanding. Study hard and get an A.

Great student advocate. Wants you to do your best. The failure in this case is that he doesnt plan the exam/final ahead of time. Study guide is misleading. Surprise questions and variables that make it difficult to identify what to do. Failed to control disruptive students. Time wasted. Expect to make up for this on your own time. Fair grader.

Terrible teacher. Makes it way more complicated than necessary, because he can't teach clearly and seems to want to screw you over on purpose. He basically vomits notes on the whiteboard that are incomprehensible. You basically are paying to be tested. I had to hire a tutor to supplement the teaching. Nice enough guy, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors for accounting classes! To the point, realistic with his expectations and knows how to compromise between department expectations and reality. Group project, be prepared with choosing reliable members! The only downside is that homework is lectured in Excel, MUST practice by hand to get it down. Very fair grading!

J.B has been my favorite professor at the U. His ACCTG course is obviously very challenging but he cares enough to help you get the grade in pass. If you show that you care and put forth effort by meeting with him and the TA regularly, he rewards you extra credit and sometimes quiz answers. In class he always had a good time and he's a funny guy.

JB is the best professor I have ever had in my college career. This is definitely a weed out class that I did not want to take. However, after taking it with JB, I can say I actually enjoy and understand accounting. He truly cares and will help you in any way possible. Put the effort into the class and make it to office hours and you will do great!

JB is a great professor. The class was pretty difficult but he is a super nice guy and always willing to help if you send an email. I was struggling to understand some concepts that ended up on quizzes. I emailed him and we worked on those problems and it helped tons. I really recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. You will have to learn everything on your own and the quizzes and tests are different than the homework you do. I am not joking about this. I honestly leave class more confused than before. TA doesn't help much either. Homework is also difficult and the chapters are long. It's a living nightmare. NO JOKE.

He is a nice person, but was very confusing for the class. I understood better the TA explaining the content. You will have quizzes every week. And don't stay behind, it is very hard to get an A. He has some good outside experience on the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: JB is an awesome teacher! He was always very clear on his expectations and he taught at a very steady pace. He wants the best for all of his students. I was working on the wrong homework assignments on Cengage and he got in touch with me to let me know. Great guy and great teacher. Take accounting with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I loved taking JB's class! He is an all around great guy and professor. He wants what is best for his students. He is great to work with and I have had no problem in his class. Pay attention and study and you will do just fine. Highly recommend him!

This dude is awesome. He explains concepts clearly and does a thorough job making sure everyone understands. His lectures are also very entertaining. The class is tough and missing lectures makes it very difficult to pass.
Study the slides for exams and you will get an A. Reading not required.
JB is a great professor and has great real life experience. He wants to see his students succeed and is very helpful. I wish I could take all accounting classes from him!

I don't recommend taking the class in Summer; it's not super difficult, but it is a TON of work and reading. If you don't read, you won't understand, because he is not great at explaining. He knows a lot about accounting, but not great at passing along that knowledge. Also he is borderline rude if you ask him questions.
Awesome teacher. Makes class fun but he also teaches you a lot about the subject. You have to work to earn your grade but its not to tough to get an A

One of the best teachers I have ever had.  You will earn your grade, if you slack you will get hurt, but he will do whatever he can to help you if you try.  quizzes are tricky but he gives hints. send him an anti-BYU picture that isn't well known and he will give you extra credit points.

Seriously the best teacher I have had at the U. You have to do the work, but he makes it more than possible to succeed if you do so. Don't plan on an A though its 95%, but he lets you argue reasonable points after the tests if you can somewhat justify why you think you should be right. I added 10% to my grade by doing so.

Everything is based off of the final and midterm, this is very stressful.  He mostly teaches with slides but he pulls out jokes every so often to keep interest. He hates BYU so this can be good tip in negotion of your grade.

Grade based off of 2 tests--midterm and final (comprehensive).  There are weekly homework problems, one has to be submitted on webct.  There's also a few quizzes and cases due, but the bulk of the grade is determined by the 2 tests.  He teaches from the textbook slide show, so lectures are pretty useless and boring. Final was HARD.

Prof. Seagrave consistently showed up to class without a clear plan, often creating the day's lecture during the first ten minutes. She would show us mind-numbing TED talks and fail to provide any substantive information about AI - many of us appeared to know more than her! The class is disjointed and genuinely deserves a more competent prof.

Super chill professor. The nicest woman you'll ever meet, and she cares greatly about her students. The course wasn't interesting, but she did her best to make it. Be ready to participate in discussions and work on team projects. Super super easy A.

Professor Seagrave is kind but a very poor instructor. She uses AI generated packets and doesn't prepare anything in advance. With that being said, the class is very easy and you will not learn anything. She also takes forever to grade.

I took Quest from this professor. She's very all over the place and is late quite often. The class was a little boring and didn't feel very useful. Overall, she's a nice professor, but she still hasn't graded assignments from back in October. The class was fine, but I wouldn't totally recommend it.
She didn't grade anything until the last week of class, so the entire time, you don't know your real grade. She doesn't post when assignments are due and doesn't tell you when she assigns them.
Easy teacher and easy class. As long as you show up, you'll get a good grade

She was super caring and helpful, Her lessons and assignments were easy and engaging, and she also offered many extra credit opportunities. This is an awesome class for incoming freshman that I cannot recommend enough, it not only gets you a required credit but also gets you familiar with resources at the U, all in a stress free environment.

If you're looking for a nice and easy way to boost your GPA, LEAP 1501 is perfect for you. There's rarely homework, grading is mostly done on participation, and there's special lectures with a librarian that are very fun.
Super caring and super chill. Made sure things were pretty stress free and understood

Dr. J was a super nice professor that clearly cares about her students. This class was not focused on taking up peoples time with long homeworks, but rather trying to get people to understand the importance of the material that we learn in class. I would highly recommend this course as your DV credit.

Dr. J is incredible. I loved this class- it was very discussion based and although I normally don't like participating in discussions, the professor and her content made it easy to really enjoy. The classroom environment and activities made it easy to make friends too. Definitely my favorite class of the semester. Highly recommend taking in person!

She recognizes we are all humans, and that college students are probably already stressed out. You can learn a lot in her class, but there is also effort given towards accommodating the general stress levels on campus throughout the semester, as well as individual/personal situations.

I found this professor to be quite helpful and simply amazing to work with. She can be a little difficult to reach when asking a question but overall I enjoyed her and the course. It was an easy class.
Great professor. Pretty easy A. Class semester was over about a week before finals week too, so stress level is definitely low with this class. Definitely recommend!!

Awesome Prof. I really wish I could've taken this class in person. She still made it great and the class was a welcoming refresher to the rest. There is a decent amount of work, but most of it is creative or written. Without a doubt, take her for the gen ed req or just to take her.
Arguably one of the easiest classes I've taken in college. Class is mostly discussion posts, group projects, and participation points. 10/10 take this class with Seagrave.
Some of the assignments are a bit odd, but not too bad. Make sure to participate in class and do the homework and you'll be fine.

Very easy A if you participate and do your work. There is very little actual work, mostly about a page of writing a week. You must particpate and do your part for group assignments. She is very caring and really details what she wants in her assignments.

The WRTG 1010 class that Jennifer teaches is a fine class. It follows a typical class format with small writing assignments here and there, and reading assignments here and there. There are like 4 papers, but they are not hard papers at all. The class is relaxed and fun. If you can write a paper, then your good to go for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great Prof, turns a required class you'd expect to hate into a great one. If you can take her for LEAP, go for it, its a fun class.

This class was easy. It required several group assignments but overall it was easy. Jennifer was really nice and genuinely cared to help but our class was so small, 10 people, it made certain things difficult to go over. You go to class and participate, you will get at least a B.

I don't understand why she has this bad review, maybe she changed these past months, but is not even close to what I saw in her classes. She is really chill and understanding. Her classes have interesting topics and sometimes we even watched a movie and wrote about it. Her homework is easy and simple.

Overall, this professor teaches well, but she definitely has a lot to learn. Her course is beyond easy, but she grades pretty harshly on attendance & participation. This professor is quite unprofessional, she brings her daughter to class, and even discourages our the foreign students in our class from participating in discussions and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Holy this was the goat. i enjoyed her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's really nice, has good lectures, presentation heavy, grades writing kinda harshly compared to other grading but overall not insanely difficult and one of my favorite professors.

Professor Richards is a great instructor. She is passionate and keeps the class engaged throughout the lecture. The only reason I didn't leave a 5/5 on this review is that she refers to the genocide in Gaza as a "war" in her textbook. Quite disappointing.

Jessie is an effective instructor who maintains a high level of professionalism throughout the course. She provides reasonable feedback, however sometimes the grading criteria can be subjective. Jessie is there to relay the information to you, but won't do anything special to make the content interesting. She is warm, welcoming, and inviting.

Jessie is an effective lecturer, but I frequently received conflicting feedback from her and her teaching assistant, which made it challenging to follow their advice. Another peer and I sent her messages through Canvas with our questions, but her responses were often unclear. When messages were sent through Canvas, her responses were vague.

Amazing professor! I took a hybrid class, so attendance really mattered. This class was 98% public speaking, so be prepared for that. She was amazing about getting students comfortable and creating a comfortable class environment. Manage your time well for assignments, and you should be fine; otherwise, it can be a lot. (Lots of discussion posts)

Jessie has a kind and helpful energy. She made me feel comfortable speaking to our class and helped me navigate my first semester at the U. Jessie cares about her class and how everyone is doing and feeling. She brings comfort to the classroom. Take this class, enjoy getting to know yourself and others better, and sharpen your communication skills.

she is AMAZING! 
if you have the opportunity definitely take a class of hers. She is caring, her classes are engaging and it really helped me become a better public speaker. She even has an spotify playlist, that class could not get better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A caring professor always wants to help out and is very lenient. The course did unfortunately feel pointless and was basically teaching you how to not be an asshole in the workplace. Lots of small group assignments but a very easy course. Only useful thing was writing and revising resumes.

Dr. Jessie is absolutely amazing. She created an fun and comfortable environment that helped me grow so much. She is really chill and gives a lot of grace, but also will push you to be better and succeed. As long as you are showing up and applying yourself, you will do well and it will be a really valuable experience. 100000/10.

Clearly cares about students and what she teaches. She helped me get over my fear of public speaking. Tests are weirdly hard but most of the info can be found in the textbook. Jessie is sick, take this class if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Richards is very knowledgeable and you can tell that she cares about her work and her students. She's very kind and always open to questions, discussion, or meeting with her to chat. She has a peaceful persona that's comforting and welcoming. Make sure you don't procrastinate your first research paper.
I love Prof. Richards! Seriously one of the best professors, if not the best, I've had here at the U!

Able to control the flow of the class very well. Was willing to be vulnerable and engage with students. I know that if I have any questions about assignments or anything of that extent I can reach out. She is an amazing teacher and I will always recommend taking her class. I'm hopeful and excited if I can take any more of her classes in the future.
Overall an entertaining professor who wasn't too harsh of a grader and was very understanding.

It's mid-semester and I'm probably gonna fail this class because I wrote the due dates for all assignments down to mark my calendar for the whole semester. Then a few weeks into the semester, this worthless teacher changes the due dates to almost every assignment to be a week earlier without telling us. I missed 2 of the biggest projects cuz of thi

Dr. Richards is an incredible teacher. She teaches things in a very understandable manner and wants to make sure all of her students are succeeding. Everytime i had a grading issue or trouble understanding something i would message her, and she'd reply by the end of the day and would do everything in her power to make sure the issue was resolved.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Took this class my first semester as a transfer student at the U. honestly really connected with Jessie and loved the class. it changed my whole outlook on participation in class (which I never did before). I honestly believe that her teaching style and personality gives her students the confidence to talk and participate.

Jessie is a great professor. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to do well. If you do poorly on an assignment, talk to her. She might let you redo it and get more points. There are EASY points for in class participation so don't skip class. Overall this was a great class and an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jessie is so great! I would highly recommend taking her class. I did the hybrid class and it worked out great. There are more assignments in this class than I had in other classes however they weren't hard. You'll become a better public speaker and presenter than you were before starting the class. She gives great feedback and has great tips.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jessie was a great teacher. The class itself was very simple as long as you participate. The connect of the course was very useful and this should be a class you take. There are 3 projects that you have to do, no midterm or final. All of the projects are recorded and you must provide feedback on yourself. I would take another class from Jessie.

Jessie is by far my favorite writing professor at the U! Highly recommend taking this course from her. The class objectives and expectations are clearly stated and her lectures are informative and useful. The assignment load is fair and she is very flexible with the deadlines and is always willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was awesome! There are three main projects, and they are all pretty easy. This class is an easy A as long as you put in the work. Bring in your work to be revised by a student, and then go home and revise it and she just gives you all the points as long as you do it. I would always show up like 20 mins late to class and she was fine.

Jessie is a super nice professor who really cares about what she is teaching. She wants her students to do well, especially since public speaking is nerve-racking for everyone. Jessie provides ample resources to prepare your for the in-class speeches, but she is a fair grader as long as you show you practiced and researched your topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Jessie Richards was a great teacher and generally cared about the students. She was great with grading and giving positive feed back. Her class was fairly easy and she did a great job teaching the subject. I would take another class from her.

Jessie is a great professor. I would take another class from her. She decided that we didn't need online homework because she didn't want us to spend to much money <3!! This class has project that are fun and not super time consuming. Text reading does have quiz's but its open book and open peer. If you need this class take it with Jessie.
Such a great professor! Very respectful of everyone and everything. She is very knowledgeable in lots of fields and is very open to questions and other help on her assignments. 10/10 recommendation!

Great professor, very nice.  Super easy grader, she doesn't believe in giving anything lower than an C.  Some of the readings and writings at the start of the semester are a pain. There are three main papers none are terribly difficult. I would definitely take her class. Workload is manageable.

Literally love her. Lectures were great and easy to follow, while still being super interesting and educational. Final exam + midterm were EXACTLY like the study guides, and she went over everything you need to know in class. Majority of assignments were in class work, so attendance isn't required, but def reccomended + you can get extra credit.

She is very knowledgeable and kind. Her class was a low stress class that was the bright spot of my semester. I learned a lot while never being stressed out. Her exams are easy and the assignments are all focused on you learning over just being busy work. Highly recommend.

Jennifer is very engaging in her lectures. However, she seems disorganized when it comes to publishing assignments and exam reviews, even though she says she will. To succeed in this class, you will have to apply yourself to the material, meaning the reading, your responses to assignments, and the study guide. No reason you shouldn't get an A.

Dr. Lehmbeck is my favorite professor that I have ever had! Her lectures are very chill and discussion based. This class required a book for the reading but it was only 300 pages and such a good read. Super easy and engaging class!
Jennifer is a very chill professor and always kept her lectures engaging. Participate in in-class discussion and canvas assignments and you will do great.

This reviews is for 4180. Prevention practices. One of her harder courses.  I despise that heroin addicts and pill poppers are EXACTLY the same with no difference. Lesson was supposed to frustrate you to accept both as health conditions or disease opposed to moral issues. Obviously one inject while the other swallows.  Just pretend they're the same

She is strict about phones but is caring and engaging. She has a few low point easy in class writing things that take like 5 minutes that you do in a small group. Very discussion heavy. Two tests and then one one page writing assignment a week its pretty great and she's sweet!

Jen is fantastic! I took 1 course online and 1 in person (both great). In person she creates a great learning environment & while attendance is not mandatory sometimes there is group conversation participation points. She grades easy and the assignments never take more than 10-40 minutes to complete. Jen's lectures are also interesting & engaging!

Took this class online and was a super easy A. 2 papers 1-2 pages long double spaced due every Sunday. The papers are mostly just about assigned documentaries/articles and only about 2 required research which was very simple.  Midterm/final is super short and easy and the answers can be found in her PowerPoint.

She is kind and really made the class interesting. No textbook but there is a novel you read for homework assignments (great book!). Originally there was supposed to be around 7 module assignments but we only did 3. There was participation points for being in class. It was a nice start to my mornings. Tests are easy if you study the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a cool professor. She is an easy grader and expects you to read one book throughout the entire semester. I learned a lot and her tests were easy. She genuinely cares about her students. Always starts class by talking about everyone's weekends and such.

Professor Lehmbeck is enthusiastic about the material she teaches, and she enjoys class participaton. Her assigned reading is very fun, and her lectures are very enjoyable. She is very kind and considerate, and as long as you study for midterms, you are bound to do great! I learned a lot at a good pace!
Professor Lehmbeck is really caring and kind. She tries to get to know all her students and very understanding when it comes to school.

Dr. Lehmbeck is a great professor. She listens to student feedback and adjusts. Attendance is not mandatory, but you definitely benefit from going to class. We read one book and have several short assignments that correlate with the book, as well as two tests, both completely open note. Not a difficult class, but overall worthwhile.
Professor is very knowledgeable. Course is easy, but you need to put in effort. If you don't get an A that's 100% on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: IVC course. A cakewalk. No textbook. However, there is a book called Mountain Beyond Mountains by Tracy Kidder you must read and serves as the basis of the written assignments, which are easy as long as you read the book. The midterm and final are based on the PPT slides and are EASY! Participation matters. Overall, easy A!

She knows what she is talking about. The lectures are very interesting. There is a book that you read throughout the semester that is very good. You write a few papers about it, but super easy. The tests are based on the slides and you can use the slides on the tests. Easy A if you read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Lehmbeck's class was easy. Let's you use powerpoints on tests. A couple reading assignments that are really not that bad. She is very caring and wants students to succeed. Would recommend.

I had a very positive experience in Dr. Lehmbeck's class. She is well prepared and had a good online format during COVID, with videos and slideshows in class, and a lovely book to read outside of class. If you can, take one of her classes, she's amazing, and it won't be too much work but you will learn so much!

For a 5000 level course I thought it would be so much harder. However the 2 exams are based off of the slides in class. There is one book to read and assignments reflecting on it. She has the slides posted in canvas so if you miss something you can go back. It's been one of the easiest courses I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory but encouraged because she will remember your face and wont shy away from calling you out if you miss class or late to the class. The study guide IS the exam. She will even tell you that before the exam. She will assigned one book to read for the whole semester and will ask you to write few short paper about it.

Participation is not mandatory but she will have a discussion every now and then, and that will be the in-class assignment. This is pretty much an easy A class. But she really know her materials. I like the way she teach, she speaks little bit too fast sometimes, thats when you can tell that she is passionate about the topic.
Awesome lectures be sure to read the book and come to class and you will get a good grade!

Jennifer is by far my favorite professor I've had at the U. Her global health class was AMAZING and also very easy. She gives you a review that is literally the same as the test so just memorize it and you'll get an A. The book Mountains Beyond Mountains that we had to read was also awesome. She is super intelligent and engaged in her classes!

She gives stellar lectures and pulls information in from other classes she teaches. Very well-rounded class that will give you solid understanding of the subject. Homework is done in groups during class. Make sure to go over power points before test (sometimes 2-3 questions aren't on review) and MEMORIZE the review she provides.

Jen is my all time favorite professor at the U. I purposely find classes that she teaches. There are a lot of in class group assignments but they are easy opinion pieces. Jen is a caring, funny professor that knows her stuff. I really enjoy her classes.
This is an interesting class.   She makes time fly by with it being a night class.  Be prepared to have group discussions every class period along with a weekly homework assignment.

Lehmbeck is a super nice teacher, who is very passionate.  We had a lot of very eye-opening discussions about global health issues that were very inspiring for me.  The assigned reading Mountains Beyond Mountains was also very good! The one bad thing in my opinion, is that you had to memorize random facts and statistics for tests.  Very easy A tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I love Jennifer. She is a great professor. She interacts with the class and is very funny. She makes sure that everyone participates (she will call you out or call on you) she cares that everyone is involved. I would highly recommend taking her classes. It's an easy A if you participate. But you do learn things because she is interesting.

Professor Lehmbeck is incredible! She's very passionate, funny, and extremely knowledgeable. She makes an effort to engage every member of the class. Her tests are exactly what's on the study guide, and her group projects are fairly simple. Her classes aren't within my major, but I'd love to take more!
Professor is a staunch liberal and is pretty disrespecting of conservatism. Apparently good community health is only possible with high allegiance to the Democratic Party.
Pretty simple and very enjoyably professor. There is the occasional lull in material where class is boring but it didn't bother me too much
She made the class interesting and fun

She talks a lot and she is passionate about talking about the controversial issues in public health. The tests are easy as long as you study the exam review. The exam review is basically the test questions. So study and memorize your answers because her tests are short answer format.

Professor Lehmbeck is a great lecturer. She makes her classes fun and exciting, while keeping the student's engaged. The class isn't too difficult if you stay on top of the readings and pay attention in class. 1010 would recommend to fellow students! I took her class based on reviews on this site and I have to say they were very accurate!

I took both Community Health Issues and Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs from Jennifer.  She is a really great professor who makes time just whiz by.  Easy A.  Her tests are either take home or the review is very similar to the exam.  She is great and I'd def take more classes from her.  One of my faves for sure.

Jennifer's teaching is memorizing material. Class was ok, she had us do a lot of group discussions. Her tests are NOT hard AT ALL. She tells you exactly what will be on them. Just make sure you attend class for points and you should be fine. I didn't use the textbook much. Final is a take home at  least for the summer course.
Great teacher, entertaining, easy to listen to.
This class was very open and interesting to engage in. Jen keeps the class open for discussion and stresses participation. As long as you go and do the assignments i gurantee an A

She teaches it so well.  She stresses responsibility and education for her students and encourages a lot of sharing and questions.  She makes class fun yet assignments and tests are part of the grade.  However, as long as you engage yourself and do them, you'll get an A. I can almost guaranttee it.  Just make sure to show up for class.
Very fun and interesting. the teacher rocks and makes sure the class is fun and interactive. a must class to take

This was my fav class of the semester. I am actually changing my major in order to teach a class like this one day. She is awesome, makes you feel totally comfy, lets you say whatever you want when talking about sex, and is very clear and helpful. This is the most awesome class, TAKE IT NOW!
Super nice and caring teacher! Class was easy and fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This online course was the easiest class I've ever taken. Gets you to critically think about your life and beliefs. There was no exams or essays. How awesome is that?! The professor also works hard to build an online community classroom which is appreciated. She is very nice and understanding. I would definitely recommend her course. Easy A.

One of the easiest classes I have taken. I think there was maybe eight assignments total, and many of it was typing 200 words about the topics. There is one major assignment about interviewing a family program. Its very easy.  Final is easy, its 200 words about anything you learned. Def take this class.

Straightforward online course. Each week wasn't posted until Monday. Had an entire week to do all of the work which wasn't a large workload. Lots of reading but easy. Small interview project that was easy and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was structured differently from most online classes I've taken. There were few assignments and you could not access or view modules very far in advance. Overall, the class was easy and interesting. This professor does not do any lectures so reading is the primary source of information. I'd recommend the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: EASY class. Literally no tests only a few small assignments. Interesting too.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Super easy class, few bigger projects that had to be done in advance, but not an assignment heavy class. No tests/quizzes which was nice! Stay on top of the work & you'll get an A
Great class.  Learned a lot.  No tests, which was a nice change.  A few papers to write and several discussions.
Easiest class i've taken at the university so far. Definitley recommend. You don't really learn anything but it is a very easy A.

This class was incredibly easy while still being interesting. There were never any lectures, just readings and discussions. There were very few assignments so we were able to focus on the learning material. The discussion topics were fun to participate in. She is a fun person to talk to and I would definitely take another one of her classes again.
Jill is nice, easy A, only one assignment or discussion each week.
Easy A, not much feedback or engagement. A couple of papers and weekly discussions.
Jill is caring, super Easy A. You will just need to do a one-page reflection paper for every class and one paper and show up.

I thought that professor Statler was a good professor, but a bit on the easier side. He wouldn't ask questions on exams that had somewhat complex math, and the content on the exams was usually significantly easier than the content in the book. He was very enthusiastic, and his mannerisms and way of teaching were very entertaining
Fun class, lots of demonstrations, and easy exams. Do end of chapter questions because he bases exam questions off that.

He was a super funny guy, his lectures were kind of irrelevant at times. He hides your grade most of the time, which makes it hard to tell if you'll pass or not. I've taken him twice and passed both classes
His teaching method is very good
Teaches pretty well and the TA's are SO HELPFUL and amazing. If you want to get an A put in effort and do the suggested end of chapter questions and you'll be fine.
The class average on tests was a D to C. Be sure to study lots. I like him, but I dislike how he does his tests and how he doesn't prepare us for what to expect on tests.

The teacher did a lot of great demonstrations and he was quite fun and actually was able to teach something that I find hard. You do have to do homework in the textbook and it does not show up on canvas. There are TA's in the class that will help you when you need it.

Great Professor, and is passionate about his students and content. You will not succeed in the course if you do not apply yourself. He also makes sure that the additional resources that are available to us are known and the information to those extra resources are accessible. 10/10 professor, I highly recommend!

Great professor. Manages to make a lecture hall of 300 feel like a smaller classroom. He's was extremely accomodating when I had a technical issue with the online homework and helped me fix my grade. Sometimes he gets lost in the sauce, but it's chemistry, who doesnt get lost sometimes.
He gives great advice, does many demos, and answers questions well. However, his slides are just a tad confusing
I heard multiple people complain about another professor, so if you're taking gen chem I, take Statler or Frey. The class moved pretty slow, but he taught the course well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof. Statler is awesome. In a room full of 300 kids, he tries his hardest to connect with each one, even remembering some by name. He does many live experiments in class, which I loved. He also teaches via practice problems, which are EXACTLY like the ones on the test. Overall, a great guy and the only valid option if you are taking CHEM 1210.

Ignore everyone that says he sucks, this is the easiest class I have taken in my entire life. Statler is hilarious,  a genuine guy who loves chemistry. I spent less than 30 minutes outside of class. A deaf, blind monkey could pass this.

Statler was definitely one of the best professors I've had. He is genuinely interested in what he teaches, and it shows; he is caring and invested in his students, which goes a long way, especially in a 350-person lecture. I would recommend him to anyone taking Chemistry 1210 or 1220.
Statler is great! He seems like he might not be at first, but don't be fooled by the course topic or his calm demeanor.
Hard class in general, he knows what he's talking about, will answer any question

J. Statler is not the one grading everything, but he does teach the lectures. His lectures are easy to understand, and the material is organized well. Don't expect to get much one-on-one attention unless you really try to stand out.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So amazing; he provides great feedback on assignments and fun practical demonstrations. 10/10

Statler is a hilarious guy. If you want to have fun in a huge lecture, take his class. He is incredibly caring and helpful, and will ALWAYS help you if you ask for it. He really gets to know the students who take time to participate and ask questions. Being an active participant in his class will greatly benefit you. I love Statler, you will too.

I found that the experiments in class helped me understand the topics better. He enjoys his job which makes the lectures much less boring. I had one of the other professors for a bit while Statler was dealing with some health issues, and for me Statler was the better professor.

The only gripe I had about his class was that it was an early morning class. Hated that.

Other than that's he's a great professor and his lectures are super cool.

Awful lectures. Poorly explained concepts. 
Lectures are all handwritten and hard to read. Would not recommend for anyone who finds typed notes or struggles reading handwriting. 
Makes rude comments to students during class. 
Doesn't care about class performance and will joke about how poorly everyone is doing.

Jeff was a great guy and a great professor. I'd suggest reading the book, or at least skim through it, before lecture. His lectures were amazing and his demos made it easy to understand the concepts. He got a surgery in the middle of my semester and was out for a while and everyone missed him. Would highly suggest.
Really good overall professor. Teaches mostly via demonstrations which is nice, hands down the best professor I have taken so far at the U. Grades very heavily on exams.

Prof. Statler was great and I very much enjoyed his lectures. Classes were engaging and fun to attend with lots of demos that kept your attention. Exams were very difficult and I put in lots of time to get mediocre scores. Be prepared to read the textbook and do lots of work outside class, but Statler was a very great teacher, just a hard subject.

Statler had really bad an unorganized lectures, Frey had to take over due to health issues and honestly I didn't enjoy either of them very much. Get ready to work your butt off learning outside of class, the exams have very few questions allowing you to get a very bad grade just for missing a couple questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Having experienced both professor Statler and professor Frey, I definitely prefer Statler's lecture style. His explanations are thorough and he is always willing to answer questions. Professor Statler really cares about his student, and he works hard to make lectures fun-- at the end of almost every lecture he blows something up in the fume hood.

Jeffrey is a nice professor but I wouldn't say a good professor. All of learning must be done outside of class and equations are not well explained during lectures. For important equations he will either do one example and expect us to learn then, or have the equation already completed and also expects us to learn from that. Be prepared to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly he wasn't that bad. He made the lectures more engaging and enjoyable. The only thing I would says is that when you ask what to study for the midterms then he'll tell you and i quote, “Just study everything”. Also randomly my grade just bounces around for no explanation and the teacher never explained why.

Statler's class is a mixed bag - the lectures can be disorganized, but he's an engaging teacher. Doing the work is key, as the exams are tricky. unstuck AI was super helpful for practice and study prep. Take it if you're up for the challenge.

He is incredibly kind, but doesn't teach in lectures. He wants you to teach yourself outside of class then come with questions. Not the easiest learning style. Exams only have around 12-14 questions on them so you can only miss one in order to receive an A. You will only pass if you spend hours teaching yourself. No extra credit/curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Loved his teaching style and didn't realize how good he was till Prof. Frey had to sub the rest of the semester due to health challenges. Definitely take Prof. Statler!

Statler is a wonderful professor who makes lectures interesting. Chemistry is hard, but he dumbs it down for you to understand. He gives plenty of practice and wants you to succeed. He is genuinely one of the nicest and most approachable professors.
He was amazing and walked through everything at a great pace.
Good professor, very friendly and lectures were great

Overall a solid professor. Lectures are engaging and often have demonstrations. Who doesn't love a good explosion? If you took chemistry in high school the class is fairly easy but if not no worries, there's lots of extra help if you need it. His handwriting and notes are easy to follow. Tests are easy if you pay attention in class and study.

He gives terrible lectures. Content is not explained in a logical manner. Goes on many tangents. Lacks tolerance for weaker students. 

Has a very old style of teaching.

Statler makes chemistry as easy and straightforward as possible and only tells you what you need to know. I probably study 3 ish hours a week and I do fine. His class does take effort, but not an unreasonable amount and the class is generally underwhelming. Definitely getting him for gen chem 2.
Great professor, highly recommended!

Statler showed great enthusiasm in his lectures with colorful slides and fascinating experiments which made the 7:30 class more bearable. Homework and quizzes were very challenging and I wish they could've been easier. Be aware that the tests are difficult and require you to do very well on them in order to keep a good grade in the class.

His lecture slides are very disorganized and tests and homework problems always seem to be designed as though they are trying to trick you into picking the wrong answer. With exams because of how he sets up canvs you have to get a 100 to keep your current grade. He makes 60 minute exams dispite class only being 50 minutes long.
Statler is great but usually only teaches gen chem 1 and 2 early in the morning so if you're up for 7:30 class, he's your best bet

Statler is amazing! The class takes work, but he's so entertaining and an amazing teacher. You will fall in love with chemistry if you put the work in. I definitely recommend him. He's hands down the best professor I've had here at the U so far!

Be sure to do a lot of practice problems in your own time if you want to do well. His lecture slides and teaching style are antiquated and you will have to spend a lot of your own time studying. The course grading was harsh-doing poorly on an exam has a significant impact on your grade. Regardless, his lectures were entertaining and had many demos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Even though attendance is mandatory at 7:30 am, the class has almost no structure. The lectures go by slowly and there is very minimal course content taught. You basically have to teach yourself everything and sit through early morning classes to watch demos and go through practice problems. Ineffective teaching methods with no strong resources.

Statler is a great teacher as long as you are willing to have class at 7:30 in the morning. I am personally a morning person so this worked out well for me. He definitely cares about his students and explains things well, but this class is very hard. So far the hardest class I have taken in college. If you do not put in the work, you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Statler's class is poorly organized. He uses ancient powerpoints and cannot use technology well. He doesn't respond to emails promptly. He strictly does not curve grades and prides himself on the difficulty of his course (averages of below 65).

He's definitely the best out of other professors teaching gen chem 2. I'm a visual learner and his lectures were helpful as he often used class time to solve problems instead of going over concepts. If you walk in class not having read the text, you won't know what you're staring at on the projector

Easy A class, terrible professor. He DOES NOT TEACH IN CLASS, only does practice problems so you absolutely need to read the book (easily gets you a 97 on each test if you do). Stands by his terribly written homework checks and terrible attendance system (he's very rude if you kindly ask him to edit your attendance grade if his scan didn't work).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was good, but I didn't think he was the best. I think he's the best choice out of the options for chemistry professors, but he never really got through anything in lecture, he did one or two practice problems the whole time then would do a demonstration that never helped me learn. He is definitely a nice guy tho he just didn't really prepare me

He started the semester by telling us that a lot of people won't pass. 
He is not sympathetic to students. 
His lectures are scattered and lack any structure. 
He is using the same lecture 'slides' from years ago. 
Do not take this class if you can help it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Statler makes a 7:30 am course fun. He is very thorough and if you follow his class structure, the class is not difficult. The concepts are tricky but there are several resources that he provides. He's a funny guy and he does a lot of demonstrations so lectures don't feel boring for an hour. I highly recommend him for Gen Chem II.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Get ready to teach yourself everything.

Prof uses lecture slides from 20 years ago. 

Spends most of lecture joking around and doesn't actually teach. 

Attendance is pretty much mandatory.

he was a very funny guy and did alot of experiments in class. tests arent super easy but as long as you do the work he will help you pass the class. attendance is done every lecture and discussion and worth 2pts. its only 2pts but it adds up fast. you can make up the attendance missed
The content is hard but his lectures are very fun.

Despite being an in-person class, this is very much a teach-yourself class, with limited content support. Lectures are insufficient and Statler gets through maybe two bullet points per class, but will test on everything.

Lectures are vague and you really just have to study the content yourself. He's funny and does lots of demos, but not worth it in the lack of content delivered. You get tested every week on the content which doesn't get taught.

He is the best teacher for Gen Chem 1, he is so lively and genuinely cares about you and chemistry, and that is very apparent in his lectures, even though they are at 7:30 in the morning. The class is difficult but if you make sure to study for exams and weekend homework checks, it's really not that bad. I would highly recommend him for gen chem 1.

I don't know a single student who has taken Statler and didn't like him. Super funny guy who makes Chemistry interesting and easier to understand. He offers more than enough help for you to succeed but you won't survive without a significant amount of study outside of class. The class Canvas page was also a bit cluttered and hard to navigate.

My somewhat negative experience may have been an outlier with this professor, but one-on-one he was not very personable and seemed to take it personally if you didn't understand a concept. His lectures are engaging, but would be very confusing unless you read ahead in the textbook. The tests are really easy though as long as you do the homework.

Prof. Statler was a strict professor and had high expectations. He doesn't have an accent, which is a plus. He can be understood clearly and is a great professor. He was not very nice in emails, especially when I had a funeral come up and he wouldn't help me out.
Good teacher, but his lectures were so slow.

Took this class in 2018 as a sophomore-turning-junior in HS over the summer. Very intensive, builds on core chem subjects in a fun way but very thoroughly. Labs felt kind of pointless really, but I liked the experience of working in one. LOTS of math, as it's the language of chem, and the exams were very high-stakes and cumulative.

This class was fine. It was definitely hard to learn from Professor Statler, but the homework are helpful. Class is MANDATORY and you are given daily participation credit. I also really struggled on the tests - they were somewhat long and very difficult. While Statler is a really friendly guy, I wouldn't take chemistry from him again.

I took this professor because I heard he was phenomenal. He was decent, but it definitely wasn't worth going to class at 7:30 almost every day where attendance was mandatory. The tests were quite difficult and stressful for me personally especially on the acid-base equilibrium unit.

If you are going to take gen chem at the U, prof Statler is the top choice for both chem 1 and 2. I personally never thought I would love chem but his passion for the subject is contagious. He also has a way of teaching complex topics in a simplified manner that makes tackling chemistry very manageable.

He is a good guy but does not give extra credit except if you go to lecture. He thinks that is extra credit but it really is not, your test just weighs less, but his class is so early it is difficult to get out of bed.

Mr. Statler is by far the best professor I have ever had at the U. He really wants his students to succeed and he does his best to make sure they do! If you are wondering if a 7:30 am class is worth it...It totally is! I did not apply myself as much as I should have, hence my grade in the class but I never missed a lecture.

Statler is a good teacher and is helpful. However, the problem with this class is 1-the homework often is unrelated to the tests, which is something the prof agrees with. 2-The exams are very difficult and had concepts I had never seen before. He's a good professor but because of these things everyone I know has a lower grade in this class.

Everything you could ask for from as a professor. He cares a lot and very respected by both students and colleagues. His lectures are well thought out and does all he can to help us understand.
