He teaches with a contagious enthusiasm and passion. Only con is his lectures are at 7:30 in the morning and I'm not a morning person.

Professor Statler made gen chem one of the best classes I have ever taken in college. He made every lecture interesting and found ways to show us in real life experiments what he was teaching about. Sitting near the front, being in engaged all class, and doing the clicker questions really helped to solidify the information we needed to learn.

Professor Statler was a great professor and cares about the success of his students. Waking up at 7:00AM to go to chemistry is never fun, but Statler makes it as enjoyable as possible. I would recommend Statler to anyone who has to take General Chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A good professor to explain general chemistry in an understandable way.

Easily the best chemistry professor at the U. This course can be a little tough for non-majors, but Professor Statler is such a genuinely good person who actually cares about how students do in his class that you can't really go wrong with him as your professor.

Statler is such an amazing professor and a welcome breath of fresh air from some of the other boring and uninvolved science/math professors at the U. He's a funny guy and really tries to know all the students he can. His class does have an awful lot of homework but as long as you pay attention, all the assignments and quizzes should be a breeze!

He is a good professor he really challenges you to answer your own question but he helps guide you through to the answer. I very much disliked competency checks at 7:30 am in the morning but what can I say I should've studied a little because when I did do that I could do half of this class in my sleep. He's not my favorite but there is worse.

Statler is supposedly the best professor at the U, but yet I've never had a worse teacher. Completely rude and blatantly does not care about anything but his paycheck. Exams were multiple-choice, wihardly any partial credit. Often does not teach and relies on outdated slides and lecture videos leaving you to learn a difficult subject with no help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even though I took this course online, Professor Statler was very supportive and helpful via emails and was reachable at almost any time for questions on homework, or about the class in general. He is funny in almost every email, makes his quizzes very fair and are closely related to the homework, and genuinely cares about his students' successes.
Statler is just an amazing guy. Not much else to say. If he is an option for your Chem class, take him.

The best instructor of any subject and specialty of any I have ever had. Seriously dedicated to student success and exceptionally accessible. Exams always graded same day and if you work for it you will get the grade you deserve. I cannot recommend Professor Statler highly enough.

Statler genuinely cares about his student's success. When possible, he goes out of his way to individually reach each student given his giant classes. You can tell he has real passion for both chemistry and teaching. He will patiently and carefully reiterate any topic or question you're struggling with in office hours.

He cares for students' progress so if you take his class then do not hesitate to go to his office hours. His lecture is more of a QnA where he interacts with students and he would also demonstrate some experiments from time to time. Remember to do the Dynamics Learning Modules. You should watch his videos before class rather than using the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not only is Statler hilarious, but he is also incredibly kind and knowledgeable. He is always accessible outside of class and really REALLY wants to help his students succeed, so PLEASE reach out to him. I was scared to take chemistry again, but his class was very accessible and fun for a chemistry class!! Very sweet guy and cool demonstrations.

Professor Statler is extremely nice and accessable out of class, but makes poor use of lecture time. He gives you an abundance of resources with little direction (often telling you what not to study, not what to focus on), and essentially expects you to teach yourself chemistry. Paid the price for having taken a second semester from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although his class is at 7:30 in the morning and I could barely wake up every day, I highly recommend taking General Chemistry from Statler. He's the best professor for this subject and definitely teaches you everything you need to know in this class, with a fair load of homework, relatively easy tests, and tons of blowing stuff up (literally).

Prof Statler is the man. Cares a lot and super enthusiastic about chemistry. He clearly loves what he is doing and his happiness is contagious. Very funny, amazing lectures, great supplementary videos on canvas and blows up hydrogen balloons on the regular. I will never take a chemistry course with any other professor.

Professor Statler is truly an amazing professor. He is incredibly passionate about chemistry and understands it is not an easy class but does everything he can to help students understand the material. Truly a gem of a teacher he makes 0730 class fun with demonstrations. The course work is evenly balanced so one bad test will not kill your grade!
He is very passionate about chemistry and it is contagious.

I don't think I'm eloquent enough in English to describe how amazing Mr. Statler is. He changed my perspective on chemistry. His attitude, his class structure, and the way he treats students brings the best out of students. Just go for it, you won't find a professor who teaches chemistry better than him.

I used to struggle with Chemistry, but Mr. Statler had flipped my attitude towards chemistry. Really humble and loves helping students, his material is super organized and he has lots of learning resources. Best gen chem professor at the U; hands down.

Took him for both 1210 and 1220. His lectures are top notch and cover all the material you need for exams. The only problem is the lectures are usually far behind the homework so you will have to either read the textbook or watch his videos. Understanding the somewhat difficult homework is the key to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far the best Gen. Chem professor at the University of Utah.

THE BEST CHEMISTRY TEACHER EVER! He is always willing to meet with you if you are having issues and works with you if you have conflicts. Extremely caring. He explains things very well and makes lectures interesting with lots of demonstrations, even at 7:30AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher but consistently assigns homework on material that hasn't been taught yet/ is due the day that it was taught. Heavily rely on chegg/yahoo answers for that.

Hands down the best professor at the U. Statler really wants everyone in his class to do well. He is available every single day after class for at least an hour if you need any help with the material, so there is no excuse for being confused on a topic. Tests are exactly like questions from lecture. Statler is so so caring and an amazing human.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: what a breath of fresh air compared to other chem professors. He is very understanding and does lots of really awesome experiments in class to make it more interesting. and his grading is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great prof. Don't skip class, and always complete online hw. If you took chemistry in high school; this class won't be very difficult. I had to occasionally read the book, but mastering chemistry and lectures helped the most. Always go to reviews (and Q&A sessions) before tests. If you put effort into this class and study for tests, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Statler is an incredible prof. If you have some basic knowledge of chem from high school and do your weekly hws with some studying, you will do fine. For midterms, study his lectures and the discussion questions. The final is almost all stoich. He is willing to help you and he is such a kind professor who loves his students.

Jeff is nice, but most of your time in class and discussion is spent on clicker questions. The class is flipped, so you watch old recorded lecture videos on youtube rather than in-class lecture. This is unfortunate, and I haven't come across any students who benefit from this. The teachers are glorified clicker proctors rather than true professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jeff is a great guy and loves Chemistry but his lectures rarely teach any problems you need for the exams. He gives 4-5 homework assignments each week that also don't correlate to the exams. Goes off topic a lot his reviews are a waste of time. Wouldn't take it from him unless you're already familiar or have a background with Chemistry.

Statler didn't do much of the teaching, most of your learning occurs online through the textbook and homework. The lecture serves as a review of the stuff you've already had to teach yourself, but overall it's not difficult. The discussion section is almost pointless in terms of learning, but you have to go so you can earn the participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jeff is a caring guy, but he is not a great professor. The class revolves around his demos and TA's doing clickers for points, but very little work in class helps you prepare for the tests. He also has homework due 4 times a week that is not consistent with the curriculum. If you take this class, prepare to show up everyday but still teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Classes consisted of early morning torture clicker sessions. If you miss too many it will drop a whole percentage of your grade. I had to self teach myself. Really frustrating his homework is written by a grad student so it becomes useless when youre preparing for exams or the final ACS. Also, Statlers tests are different than the ACS final. GL
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class requires attention and willingness. If you need help he is always willing to help. If you do not want to help yourself or spend the time to study, you will not go far. This is expected in a chemistry class at a University. Not expected to always have professors who are willing to help whenever you need it. Great teacher.

The class isn't too difficult so long as you keep up on your homework and actually learn the material. 3 assignments and 1 quiz a week. Most of them don't take too long. Prof. Statler does amazing in-class demonstrations and really tries to teach in a clear, easy-to-understand way. He's also very willing to answer questions and give help.

He seems like a good guy, but he really just wants to play, not teach. Also, the homework is ridiculous. The chemistry department has a grad student who writes the homework, so often, it's irrelevant or way ahead of where you're at in lecture. Watching the videos helps, but Khan Academy and SI sessions become your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jeff's the best chemistry professor at the University of Utah. He's incredibly knowledgeable and loves to teach. He's a rare breed of chemistry professor that takes his teaching as seriously as his research. He's easily accessible outside of the classroom and his lectures are very informative and easy to follow. I'd recommend him to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Statler made one of my most hated classes a little easier for me. There was a lot of homework and quizzes, but alongside optional study sessions that he offered, I was nothing but benefited. The lectures were slightly tedious sometimes, as there are clicker problems, but it I would recommend this him to anyone who struggles like I do.

Professor is an amazing gem. I loved his class because he tried to make chemistry fun, a non-fun subject. His exams were okay but you do have to study some. You should expect that at this level though. One of the only good professors in the chemistry dept.

His tests are all online through Madra. You're only graded on clicker questions, online homework & tests. He doesn't write the tests & there are often errors in the questions/answers. He doesn't really lecture. Expects you to put in 10+ hours a week in homework & watching youtube videos of him. Wouldn't recommend unless you want to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst chemistry professor. Made me absolutely hate my favorite subject. His class consists of nothing but random questions that hurt your grade. You will end up teaching YOURSELF chemistry, but it won't be the way he does chemistry so you continue to watch your grade disappear in front of your eyes. Worst class I've ever taken at the University.

He was available outside of lecture as much as he could be and would help students during discussion or even with homework questions. Be prepared for a lot of homework on Madra and the quizzes every week on Madra are a little tough. Smart guy but humble enough to admit when he did not know something.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Jeff was awesome! This class was pretty much all online, didn't learn much in lecture and even less in discussion. Class takes a lot of studying so be ready to invest a lot of time, SI sessions was where I learned the most, Carter was awesome and him and Jeff are always flexible in seeing students and answering their questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class is going to be more challenging to people who need to take for just full-fill the general education class. However, Jeff cares about his students and he wants students to study and participate his lecture. If you are going be science major. I highly recommend to take his class. This class is going to cover decent amount of materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Statler is extremely invested in his students doing good. He will hold Sunday reviews before every exam. He will sit in the lobby after class for students who want to ask questions or need help. There is a large workload, but this is pretty equal for all chem classes. He makes sure his students have everything it takes to succeed. One of the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Statler really wants his students to succeed; he's really supportive and available if you show that you're trying in the class. He expects you to watch the videos before class, and you do practice in lecture and discussion. Go to class, do the clickers for points, and do the additional practice questions in discussion before tests and you're fine.

Statler is a gift to general chemistry students. He has a well-deserved reputation of being the best gen. chem. teacher. He, however, doesn't have much competition as the other teachers aren't well liked. Statler is available during his office hours and always gives notice if he can't make it.
Pretty good.
There are clicker questions everyday but most of the time he just gives you the answers. Lots of time consuming homework but it's not hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are 3 classes you have to take with this class. It is way too much work. If you have a job, good luck. The chemistry department at the U is bull. He doesn't teach material. He wants you to read the chapter, do the homework and ask q's in class, never enough time for that. Homework and quizzes everynight, about 4 hours worth! DON'T TAKE IT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you want to teach yourself Chemistry, then you would love taking Statler! His class consists of him making you watch his youtube videos of him mumbling. Then you go to "class" to try and get your clicker points but since it is such a big class, theres hardly any learning and rude teaching assistants. Textbook? Yeah thats online. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really wish I had Statler for Gen Chem 1! Did way better in his class. Take Statler's class! He loves teaching and loves chemistry. Get to class on time. If you do nothing else, watch his videos. Even though my class was at 7:30 he made it interesting and fun with jokes and demonstrations. Plus the A was worth it.

Professor Statler is one one of the best instructors I have had at the U. If you go and participate in class (and by participate I mean actually ask questions), study and do the homework, as well as seek help when you need it you will do very well.  Anyone who thinks they are going to get an A without working for is a fool. it wont happen anywhere.

Statler is a great guy and knows a lot about chemistry.  He's super nice and encourages participation... The way the course was laid out though, was kinda weird, but I think they're changing it for next year.  Watch his lecture videos; they are super helpful!

One of the best professors I've had. I've read through other ratings and I am confused how there are any negative ones. His videos are entirely relevant to homework and tests. Plus you have the chem help lab anytime you are confused OR you can easily get Statler to help you. The clickers are easy and are basically extra points to boost your grade.

Great lecturer, and more importantly, his class is all geared to get you a good grade on the standardized, national final. He's been in the business long enough that he knows how to prepare his students, and his students get the best average grades. Definitely recommend.

His lectures are horrible.  The whole class is a series of clicker questions.  Inevitably, you will get some of these questions wrong, and you will be able to watch your grade drop during class because clickers are worth 25 percent of your final grade.  The professor cares more about people attending his lectures than learning chemistry.

Don't buy the textbook--it's a waste of money. He expects you to watch 10-15 min lecture videos instead of reading. The homework is difficult & there are 1-2 problems due before every lecture that are based on videos you should watch for the upcoming lecture. Tests are difficult and he doesn't curve. Lectures are basically a bunch of clickers.

I've loved Statler for both Gen Chem 1 & 2! Although many are not a fan of his youtube videos and madra homework assignments, I think it is a great system. Instead of reading in the textbook, you watch a 10-15 minute video about a new concept the day before you learn it in lecture, take a short pre quiz, and then reinforces it the next day.

He is very good at explaining and teaching to simplicity. Does a great job at providing not only a plethora of material to help you, but also is available to help you whenever you need.  Online homework is sometimes very tough and seems irrelevant.. Though that isn't him who makes it.  He is the best chemistry teacher I've ever had.  I'd recommend.

If you are good at chemistry, this class will be very frustrating.  This professor often gives clicker questions during class that he doesn't care what number you enter.  He just wants to penalize anyone who is late or absent.  His lectures are not informative, and he expects you to learn outside of class by watching his YouTube videos.

If you need to take Gen Chem I, this is the professor to take it from.  Jeffrey Statler provides: 1) Lecture videos covering all relevant class material (so textbook is unnecessary) 2) Extra practice problems to study 3) An army of TA's to help 4) Four practice tests to study per exam. It won't be easy, but if you put in work, you'll get the A.

If you are looking to actually learn chemistry, then DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. His tests hardly relate to his online lectures and he doesn't explain how to work problems out during class. Basically, he doesn't teach.

The tests are hard and the class requires a lot of studying BUT Statler is awesome! In lecture, you basically work through clicker questions together. So watching his lecture videos beforehand is a must. He is good at explaining concepts and answering questions. He does awesome demonstrations almost every lecture.
Great teacher. He is very nerdy and funny. Best lecturer

His lectures were nothing but clickers. Never did he actually LECTURE. It was all on YouTube + madra homework + 4 pretests before your actual exam. I understand doing practice problems, but I would rather him lecture in class or else I would've taken it online because it was all basically online. I only came to class to get the 200+ clicker points!

If you are a student who also has a full-time job, good luck. Expect 2+ homework assignments a week that are moderately lengthy. Expect 4 full length online practice tests that are FOR CREDIT prior to every test (due specific days at obscure times). Prepare to be blind sided by countless things like class every day of the week and mandatory attend.

Same standardized tests for all chem 1210 professors so you cant really compare Statlers difficulty. I have heard amoungst students that Statler is most popular chem 1210 instructer (even though he isnt a PhD). Go to class and get easy clicker points. I like his lectures. If you understand the homework and watch his videos, you will get an A.
Interesting lectures! Easy to focus in class. Tests are tough.
He's so into the subject, his enthusiasm I'd contagious. This isn't even my major but he made me enjoy the class. And it's not even my major.

Pros-Professor is knowledgeable & lectures are on YouTube.  Cons-lecture & discussion is required.  I drive 2 hours RT for 50 min discussion where we answer 1-2 questions. It's a waste. I could use that time to study more at home.  Lecture can be the same at times.  I find myself teaching myself at home so it's frustrating that class is required.

He is very rude to students and even says things like "if you were a good student.....". This seems to make many people feel saddened when attending his class and above all, he just hurts their feelings. The way he teaches is terrible. He places all of his lectures online and uses his FULL lecture time for clicker questions. In all, he is awful.
Though the class is not long, and the lectures are interesting, the material conveyed is a bit confusing and the teaching style is definitely one that requires a lot of focus

To start, he doesn't teach anything. All of his lectures are online and his ENTIRE class is based on clicker questions. Furthermore, he criticizes students  with ridicule when one doesn't know how to solve a problem. On the same hand, his job title is "teacher", which leaves the question, Why doesn't he teach? In all,  he is an awful teacher.

Last year, he was fantastic. THIS YEAR, he put all of his lectures online. He does not lecture, but his entire class is clickers. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. You will have to teach yourself and its not worth the wake up.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures are interesting and everything is presented clearly in multiple formats (auditory, visual). Demonstrations are awesome, especially for days when you forget your morning coffee. Heavy clicker use during class, but he posts the formulas on the board for reference. Just be sure to attend regularly.
Great teacher! He does a great job at putting demonstrations in the class to make it less boring. I only had trouble with one exam but the rest a pretty easy.

To start off, he doesn't write his own tests, he uses another professors tests and aren't given the resources the other class has the luxury of; ex. practice tests actually knowing what he's gone over in his own class.
fantastic

Awesome professor, I recommend him to the fullest. I personally hate textbooks and never once looked at it, the OWL homework prepared me for his lectures and the TA's in the discussions were amazingly helpful as well. Class is mandatory for the clicker points, but don't worry if you miss a few; the discussion clickers give up to 5% extra credit.

Endless energy. Always had demonstrations and always has makes time for his students, which was especially astonishing since I know he was taking courses of his own.  If you have to take Chemistry, take it from this guy.  I got a C in high school and an A now.  I'm taking him again next semester.

If you need to take chemistry you should take it with him. Statler is a great professor. I really love taking chemistry with him. He does a lot of demonstartion during the lecture which makes the lecture more interesting. I really understood chemistry with him. I am excited to take general chemistry 2 next semester with him.

Statler is a great professor with lots of enthusiasm and fun demonstrations. Lectures don't always cover the material though so a lot of learning is done outside class. From what I've heard, he's the best professor teaching Chem 1 and 2.

Statler is a good professor that puts a good effort to make class interesting and shows energy while teaching.  Although what he teaches in class is a little different than what the department tests on the exams, he gives students lot of practice problems to master so that we can pass the exams.  Overall he is a good professor.

Professor Statler is GREAT!!! He did a lot of work on preparing classes! He made tutorial video so you can go over the material before class. Also, his class is super super fun since he does a lot of demonstrations.

This class was so much fun; the professor was so into the class and he was so helpful. I loved this class every morning. Even if it was at 7:30 am he made the class worth it to come. And was quite a nice view first thing in the AM
He's the best science professor I've ever had. He does demonstrations in class every time and his clicker questions are easy.

One of the best professors I have ever had. The classes are huge, but he always makes time to meet with you when you need it. He is very approachable, friendly and so helpful. I would recommend him to anyone! His lectures are clear and organized and he makes even the most dreadful chapters enjoyable. A+

Absolutely an amazing professor! Lectures are clear and very well organized, every day there is a demo that coincides with the information being presented. He also makes study/review videos in his spare time, which are super helpful! The material itself can be somewhat tricky, but overall not too horrible. I'd highly recommend him for gen chem!

The best science professor I have had so far! He really cares about the students and is willing to help in every way possible. He encourages questions and doesn't make anyone feel like they asked a stupid question. And mainly he really loves chemistry, you can tell from his excitement over demonstrations. Take him for chemistry!

I've never seen anyone control such a large classroom with such skill. Jeff makes class interesting and worth going to with demos and smart use of technology (pdfs, cameras, microphones, videos, etc.) He speaks clearly and his lecture slides are precise and easy to follow. He spends a lot of time outside the classroom making videos, preparing demonstrations, and being available for students. As long as you do the assigned reading and homework problems you shouldn't have any troubling keeping up.
He's a great professor!I would definitely recommend him. Very good at explaining concepts and giving really life examples. I hated the homework though, it was a pain.
He's a great professor,he's genuinely concerned with students needs, and he answers all questions (good or bad). Excellent clarity in his explanations.
Attendance is mandatory if you want to get credit for clickers. Absolutely read the book if not you will not know what is going on in the class and the test.

Professor feels very checked out pretty much all of the time. Because so many students take this alongside much more time consuming classes, he intentionally makes the class very low effort and "handholdy", which means it's easy to get a good grade, but also makes going to lecture feel very very pointless.

Super nice and understanding. Sometimes it feels like hes just going through the motions but it's very clear what you need to know and how you'll be graded. 90% of your grade is exams and 10% hw. Exams are easy if you study and he gives past exams for practice. This is a great class to pair with a difficult course like mechatronics or heat transfer

Chang is a great teacher. He really wants his students to succeed and is very reasonable with his work load. It is clear what you are expected to know and the topics are explained well. My only criticism is I felt like he could have used time a little better and that would have allowed us to go into more depth in some areas.

I recommend Chang over raemakers if you're taking ME 3000. He's a much more understanding professor and his tests are fair. His homework is fair and he's also really open to making adjustments to the class based on feedback from students.

J is a nice guy but his grading is questionable. He encourages class participation. Grades are not reflective of individual performance and are instead just curved across all sections. I got a signifigantly lower grade than I was expecting becuase of this. Slides are posted online and participation ex-credit is subjective.

You're graded on like 3 things. He's very nice and chill, not strict, fun lectures, group project, mostly lets students do their own thing. I will say, though, he asks the questions back, so you'll most likely be teaching yourself. “Why do people invest in bonds?” “Great question! Why do you think people invest in bonds? Give it a try :D” …

Everything you need is on Canvas. Very few assignments, so turn them in ON TIME or else your grade will be ruined. Easy A, just don't be a bum like me smh. Read the textbook! Group project also wasn't so bad. J is a great lecturer, but you will be confused if you don't keep up with the textbook readings.
He so chill

Professor Li does an amazing job of keeping his students' attention. He doesn't dwell on topics if we aren't interested or already have a solid grasp on them. I also really appreciate how he molds his lecture time around what we need and doesn't just seem to check boxes off on a calendar like so many other professors do. 100% recommend!

I really enjoyed this challenging class. It pushed me to actually think but if you ask questions, the material is straightforward. J's real-world experience sets him apart from most professors at the U, and he's committed to helping students succeed if they show up and put in the effort to understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jiacui Li is a very nice and caring professor. He answers any questions and concerns. He does have a good approach to doing homework, thinking from scratch rather than from a cookbook but making these homework assignments quite difficult. Very lecture heavy but is relaxed with the group project and final.

I love his philosophy on learning and how you should teach yourself from scratch on how to solve a problem rather than going with a "cookbook" approach. He implements this in his homework which is why it's so difficult but honestly it isn't that bad; people just LOVE to complain. Seriously, everyone here got me scared for nothing. He's very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: J is helpful and very nice. Many find his lectures boring but I personally think they are interesting if you apply yourself and the knowledge. The one thing I personally couldn't stand was the 3hr class period but that has nothing to do with J himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: J is an excellent instructor and yes, his homework doesn't have much to do with the lecture, but he warns you plenty of times in advance and is more than happy to give you tips on how to do it. This means it isn't impossibly as some students find it to be, should you seek the right resources. He also has TAs that host helpful Q and A sessions.

A lot of people don't like him because of the homework, but I don't think it's so unreasonable. It may be a little too hard, but J just wants his students to understand the material and think critically. People just want easy formulaic homeowrk that doesn't require them to learn much. Besides, he makes up for it with a pretty easy final.

Never left a negative review on RMP before but I cannot in good conscience leave this class in my rearview mirror w/out warning others to STAY AWAY! His homework has nothing to do with his lectures (he himself admits it), so you're left to figure it out for yourself. Final is also insanely difficult and accounts for 40% of the grade.

J is a knowledgable guy and is a new teacher. He just got his PHD from Stanford, and his homework difficulty reflected that; they were really, really hard. They also are a massive grade portion. Luckily I was able to work them out, but most people did not and that caused resentment, most of it well founded. J needs to learn that we are undergrads.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs. The homework makes up a huge chunk of the grade and he never teaches you how to do it. This is complaining, the syllabus literally has a section saying you won't know how to do parts of it. I've never had a class like this and reccomend you take someone else at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures have nothing to do with hw or quizzes and going to class is pretty pointless. grading is insanely tough and hw is long and confusing. You basically just teach yourself out of the textbook. Avoid at all costs.

This has been the most stressful college course I have ever taken. I don't feel like I've learned anything about what the class is titled. I may have learned something about stress management though, because this class makes me actually want to cry. Super hard homework that takes forever and is a huge chunk of your grade.

AVOID. His effort is there but wow, his lectures are incredibly boring and hard to follow. Homework is a huge chunk of your grade and he explicitly states they are "loosely" related to the lectures, aka, they have nothing to do with anything he teaches you.

Was doing very well in the class until the final exam. Although I performed very well on the assignments, group project, and decently on the final exam, the professor still gave me a ridiculous grade and practically based final grades on final exam performance. His grading model was the worst I've ever seen at DESB. Was close to talking to dean.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Martin is exceptional in many ways. He is extremely experienced, very honest and informed in his subjects. This class prioritizes attendance heavier than any other class I've taken. Your grade will drop significantly from just a few misses. Tough grader especially on the final, notes are always handwritten. Do NOT take w/o pyshio/anat.
I love Mr Martin! Take his classes. As long as you show up for the in class exercise, youll be all good. He is so sweet and passionate. No homework, but attendance is mandatory. Loved this professor.

He was the best professor I have every had!! I had him for KINES 3093 (biomechanics) and he was so clear and helpful. His lectures were short, and his homework and tests were exactly what was on the lecture. he truly wanted us to learn and understand the material. 10/10 professor I loved his class!
I enjoyed both the material as well as the professor. If you work hard and show that you've given effort prior to approaching Martin with questions he's very willing to help.

WORST professor I've ever had. His homework makes no sense and isnt covered in lectures or the book. His idea of helping is saying "It's easier than it looks." Taking the honors for this course isn't worth it if he is the professor.

Jim is a great professor. The class was very easy with a discussion, quiz, and 2-3 scenarios each week. Gave two attempts on each quiz that relied on the textbook. Don't get behind. Lectures were short and to the point. Exams were easy and open book. He is so passionate about the topic and you can really tell!
Fun topic and good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easy online class for gen Des, you still have to do a decent amount of work every week, but the material is interesting and engaging.

I never actually interacted with Professor Steenburgh because I took his ATMOS1000 class online, but the class was awesome — it was well-organized and the content was super cool! Based on that I feel confident in saying he's likely a solid professor in person as well. 10/10 would recommend :)

This class was amazing! If you like winter sports (or the outdoors in general) it's a very informative class about weather and the conditions we have in Utah as well as other areas. Usually 3 assignment and a discussion each week and then two exams. The textbook is the book he wrote and it does an amazing job at explaining everything.
Nitpicks over things that people with actual industry experience know don't matter or are demonstrably false. Dude loves the sound of his own voice.

Jim De St. Germain LARPs as if he is an industry professional, however looking at his professional career he has never once left academia. He uses this persona to justify bad takes as if it is the norm in the industry, however those with professional internship experience know these claims to be completely false

He is ineffective, with disorganized and poor communication with students and TAs. He attempts to teach industry norms and Agile practices despite lacking industry experience, while enforcing a waterfall-style process. Lines of code are used to evaluate student performance. Overall, he comes across as pretentious and out of touch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
- Lectures: 80min of talking at you, not recorded. 
- Attendance is just a Google form. 
- Assignments are 13+ pages long. 
- Only gave Visual Studio (Windows exclusive IDE) instructions 85% of the time. Extra frustrating since the alternate instructor that semester taught using Rider. Often spent several extra hours just on assignment setup.

Feedbacks were given very late; I received my HW 2 score after submitting HW 5. He always uses AI to answer questions on Piazza and doesn't check Piazza regularly. The course materials, assignment description, and tests are super vague. I have to say he is an interesting person with good public speaking skills, but I'll never take his course again.

Great professor for capstone! 

Prepares students for industry by making them realize that being a good computer scientist goes beyond technical ability. He flips the script on the smug anti-social "coder" students who are difficult to be around; you know that ones I mean. Also he's also very forward thinking about AI in computer science.

If you are interested in learning outdated and inaccurate industry practices, all while having most of your grade based off of irrelevant presentations and videos, then this is the class for you. He would prefer that the course include no coding and 20 more pages of writing, while falsely claiming that he's teaching you agile development.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were very helpful and whenever there were mistakes he would correct them quickly. Only complaint is I wished he graded assignments sooner to get feedback on improvements. The class is focused on developing good practices which is hard to do if you don't correct them quickly and end up doing the wrong format on all the assignments.

I wish he used a different technology than Blazor and a different IDE than VS (not available for Mac users). If not for those decisions, 5 stars. Class was made unnecessarily difficult for them. Assignments can be vague, but that is the reality of software and someone has to teach us to negotiate with this eventuality. ~10-12 hrs/week.

Taking his class for 3500 was probably the most challenging class I have taken in my college career thus far. Why is that? The homework load is CRAZY and the grading was so harsh. But Prof Jim really cares about his students and is willing to help. If you want to be successful in this class, be sure to build a relationship with him and his TAs.

One downside to Germain is he doesn't respond to emails, but he is an amazing professor. I was really struggling at one point in his class and he's very understanding and willing to work with you. Assignments are really hard to understand, but go to his office hours for help. I would take any class with him!!

Jim is SUCH a chill guy. His lectures were so compelling and I learned so much through attending them. I went to his office hours multiple times; the dude is so down to earth and gave my partner and I an extension when times were tough. He truly knows his stuff. Also he's just so cool? Bro can juggle, likes ultimate frisbee, so fun. Would recommend

Honestly he is a decent lecturer, but his assignments are very confusing and vague. When this was brought to his attention he just said "That is what the real world is like". Despite vague and confusing assignments, his grading is very tough often taking points for very little things.

Nice guy, just not a very good instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is a decent professor and will help you succeed if you put in the effort to talk to him. However, his assignment descriptions are extremely verbose (40 pages!) and often contain contradictory requirements due to copy-and-pasting from previous years. This led to Piazza and the TAs being flooded with questions, many of which went unanswered.

I took 3500 with Germain during the Spring 24. Honestly, he was dealt a bad hand with broken technology which made the class incredibly difficult, especially if you are a Mac user. He does care a lot about his students and will meet you during and outside of office hours. Gives HW extensions and helpful hints during office hours.

Anyone who tells you that Prof. Jim doesn't care about his students is wrong. It's rare to meet a professor who wants you to succeed as much as Jim does. If u are struggling, go talk to him and I guarantee that he is willing to work with you.
For how little content is in this course, the lectures are engaging and I always got something out of them

great lecturer, tried his best to not make the lectures completely boring. he's pretty funny and explains the basics well. the assignments aren't too hard and are never too frequent. i never felt overwhelmed by homework in this class. the ebook is useful if you actually read it. the tests were well made as well.

Overall pretty good professor, he usually takes a while to respond to messages directly to him on Canvas or Piazza, but there were lots of helpful TAs. Good lectures and a lot of enthusiasm. He used an online textbook that wasn't very helpful, but there wasn't any real work tied to it. He also posted all of the slides from the lectures.

This professor tells you nothing that is going to be on the test. Labs and homework instructions are super unclear. This course feels unnecessarily difficult through the expectation of it to be entirely self taught with very little help.

Unclear homework instructions, with a heavy load every week. Wants you to put so many hours into the course, but all he does is stand there with his Google slide. He does not care about his students, would prefer for you to fail than guide you and help you out to begin with. Overall, get a better professor.

One of the dopest professors , I am surprised his rating is low here , he really cares about his students and helps them learn about not just the class but the real world, how to get a kickstart for your tech career, he gives great advice that not a lot of professors would. He does have some harsh grading criteria for small things on assignments

His tests are a breeze compared to Kopta but his assignments are extremely difficult. Be prepared to spend over 20 hours on some of his assignments later in the semester. He has office hours frequently and his TAs are amazing. Go to class, go to TA and office hours and start EARLY and you will pass.

Assignment specifications are the worst part, they are poorly written and many key things are left out. Most updates are only posted to Piazza or mentioned in lecture, so it is often difficult to meet all requirements using just the spec. The class is also unbalanced, early software practice concepts felt slow while HTML and SQL were rushed.

Prof Germain is willing to work with you. However, he could change his teaching style in terms of efficiency. Assignment instructions could be worded better. He helps with the assignments, but his help timing is worse. If assignment is due Fri, the full guidance will be completed on Thursday. You waste too much time to find info.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Germain was pretty good; he explained topics quite well, and if you had questions, he would do his best to explain and help you understand. I did go to TA hours ALOT. I recommend going to TA hours often, and if you get a chance, learn C#. He likes his acronyms; they will be on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This guy is great! Man would walk us through the assignments in a way he would not give us the answer, but rather guide us in the right direction. Assignments took around 8 -10 hrs to complete if time was efficient, and most of them were pretty straightforward. Midterm was very easy since he designed it to be easy for those that did the cheatsheet.

Prof Jim is a very good lecturer, I actually learned a lot in his class compared to all my other classes. His course prepares you well for the real world. Lectures are very helpful if you go, he also provides a class recording.

Nice thing about him is that he willing to extend the deadline. But the way he explains stuff: bad. He can make an easy concept into a hard one. Confusing slides, unclear and thus lead to A LOT of misunderstanding, trust me, this will cost you over 10 hours just to realize you understand a basic concept wrong, even if you have decent IQ

The class is difficult, yes, but it's manageable. Prof Jim is encouraging and wants students to succeed. He is understanding with deadlines, and extended them multiple times to account for difficult concepts. He emphasizes the skill of learning without having someone telling you what to do 24/7. Engaging lectures. If you can take his class, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The issue is that assignments routinely take in between 10-20 hours and your ability to learn has basically a one to one correlation with your ability to get good answers out of Google for certain things, you pay the university the ~1500 dollars to avoid these things, not embrace them

Professor de St. Germain comes off as very out-of-touch with his class. He's inactive when helping students. The assignment specifications are long-winded (33 pages!) and vague. He drops you off into brand new concepts with minimal instruction and expects you to figure it out yourself. And my grades haven't been updated in over a month.

as long as you pay attention in lectures and know how to google things this class is extremely easy. Professor Germain will spend time in class doing the hard parts of the homework for you. He is also a very lenient grader on the assignments and cares more that you learned something rather than if the answer is perfect.

The assignment instructions are borderline useless, yet getting help from course staff was challenging considering their contradicting answers. Good luck getting even an email reply from the professor. I lost points on assignments for things not mentioned in the instructions or course lectures. Avoid this professor teaching this class at all costs.

He values student feedback and would adjust the deadline. However, his assignments are vaguely written and the instructions are long. Also, as the semester proceeds, 80% of your time will be spent on googling because his lecture does not fully cover what you need. Those are the two reasons why students stay up until 5am for his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: My favorite CS professor by far. He will extend deadlines, the tests are much easier than Kopta's, and his humor is great. Only issues are that he is VERY inactive on piazza and emails. His assignments can be vague as well, but if you just come to TA hours that could be resolved. Overall, I'd prefer him over Kopta despite how great Kopta is.

I think Prof. Jim makes things more unclear further in the semester so students practice making unspecified design choices and justifying them in the readme + getting started early to ask questions. Get ready to learn how to google things and teach yourself to program. I think this class is really just to prepare for the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a nice professor but his assignment instructions/grading criteria need improvement. Very vague assignment instructions making it unclear what's being asked, if you forget one README your assignment score will drop a whole letter grade. Also TAs and the Prof. were little help on Piazza. Several times questions would just never get answered

This professor does care about the CS degree and implores students be better programmers. He is fair in adjusting deadlines and listening to student feedback through lectures. 
However, I find this class very difficult to succeed in. Assignments are awfully worded and vague (especially near the end), help hours are scarce, and he is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment:
The Good: 
Germain believes in the prestige of the U's CS program. He reaffirms your value as a CS student at the U and encourages you to aim for the skies.

The Bad:
His assignments are poorly written. Be prepared to spend 30+ hours per week on a handful of his assignments. The specifications are inconsistent and leave you guessing.

You can get full marks for your actual code but get a D on the assignment (that you spend 10 hours per week on) because you missed a couple comments in the code and couldn't think of every edge case in your test class. This guy is a funny lecturer but this class sucks.

While he is a knowledgeable programmer, the way the class and assignments are structured makes it difficult to confidently get an A. Due to the vague and sometimes contradicting assignment requirements, your code could fulfill the requirements, but you may get a bad grade because you didn't implement it the exact way he intended. Just frustrating

I learned an incredible amount from this class. Jim is very lenient and is always willing to work with students on late due dates (full credit). His lectures are great and his expectations for each assignment is clear. Grading for each assignment is reasonable as well. However, The amount of work is large and you will have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If at this point, you are not confident in you're own ability to teach yourself, DO NOT take this course. Jim assigns a TON of homework and expects you to learn a lot of technologies for yourself. He does alright at teaching concepts, most are simple anyway, and he is very forgiving with deadlines. Very difficult but very rewarding course.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He gives good lectures but his assignments are very difficult, sorely lacks empathy towards students, and is very hard to reach out to outside of class. I would say that if you don't have a lot of outside of school commitments/issues, then his courses are very valuable. But if you are looking for an easy pass, his courses are not the move.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Good lecturer but would often spend an entire class just walking through an online tutorial instead of teaching the material himself. Additionally, he's VERY inaccessible outside of class. It often takes over a week for him to respond to a emails and online discussion questions. This is especially frustrating when his assignment specs are so vague.

Was a good class and i definitely learned a lot, however i will say he made some of the assignments more difficult than need be. TA hours were always busy with students who needed help from his vagueness for each assignment.

Lectures and assignments are relatively vague and require maybe 10-15 hours per week. Good luck getting help from the 5 TA's who have to manage over 150 students. The queue sometimes has over 20 people in it (aka 2 hrs of waiting)

Prof Germain is one of the best lectures I have ever had and honestly is a very down to earth kind of guy. He makes sure to take into consideration students concerns and adjust accordingly. That being said he is going to make you learn, and learn a lot. You need to be dedicated to CS in order to get by, so it won't just be an easy A. Worth it.

Again like another student already said, he shaped the class based on the students needs which was super helpful! His lectures were awesome, definitely the best lectures I have ever had. Very nice in person too :D

Super Funny and Nice Guy, Communication was rough once or twice but it happens, altered the assignment requirements and due dates to suit the needs of the class as needed, If you want to stay on top of what is happening in the class, stay on top of piazza, I cannot emphasize this enough. He is super intimidating to talk to at first, just FYI.

As a senior student majoring in CS, I would like to say prof. Germain is the worst professor I have ever had in CS department (also in my college life). My only suggestion is that no matter which class he teaches, stay away from him. He even changes the instructions before the due date without any announcement. And he is also a really tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice guy, funny lecturer, horrible professor. Mentioning his name to 90% of cs students who have taken a class from him will net you the response "never take a class from Germain." His assignments are open ended for no reason, and can be pages long of completely non helpful explanations. Unless you want to teach yourself, STAY AWAY!!!!!

He co-taught Computer Networking and only did the programming assignments side of it. He is the kind of the professor to teach you the assignment requirements and throw you into the ringer. So you will learn a ton of new material, but you will struggle with your assignments. If you don't like that, i'd be weary about taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take this from Jim. You'll come out of 4000 with a 30 page, single-spaced design document and no project. You are given no time to explore and learn, you're just expected to write pages and pages every week on what your project is supposed to be about. At the end, if your project doesn't match the doc that you wrote blind, you get a bad grade

Had him as the professor overseeing Capstone project. Really challenges you to do more and gives assignments that makes you think about your project. Highly recommended if you're asking for a challenge, but you might be on edge the whole semester. Also highly depends on the team you find for the capstone.
Terrible communication

Jim's assignments are sometimes vague, but that's by design. As you progress through CS (and enter workforce), all instructions will be vague. Implementation is your choice. Funny, charismatic, nice, but also has high expectations and can be intimidating. TONS of homework and tests are hard to study for. Weed-out class, but still better than 2100.

Jim is an awesome guy but his tests seemed very open ended and I thought I had good descriptions for my answers, but still did bad on his tests... His TA's were very different (and very slow) in grading. I waited 3 hours in the CADE lab for a TA and finally when they showed up they said "What".. Very rude and frustrating.

Fantastic lecturer, no doubt about it. The concern most people mentioned was that his assignment sometimes can be hard and almost vague, even for me who has programmed before. Office hour is not that bad if you go there after class dismissed. Some TAs in this class are extremely helpful. Another thing is that grading is subjective, so it sucks.

He normally teaches upper div, so he thought bringing vague descriptions into a pre major class was a good idea (NOPE). Tough class. Expect 12+ hours a week on assignments ALONE. Dont take with any other intensive classes like physics or math. Dont bother seeing him in office hours, line is long. Going to the vague TA's doesnt help either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is horrible at writing assignments, his instructions are always unclear and the homework can take 15 hrs + a week to do. His teaching is alright, but you'll end up learning more from google than from him, he is also impossible to get in contact with, he won't answer emails at all.

Jim is the funniest CS teacher I've had, but he is TERRIBLE at describing assignments and contradicts himself a lot. His Java code is very unorganized and I can't believe it was written by a professor. He doesn't conform to Java standards, and while he tells students to use good variable names, he hardly does so himself. Do NOT expect an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Jim is an awesome teacher. He was lenient with us when we needed more time for an assignment, and would use comedic actions in order to make class more fun. But each of the tests had a completely different format which made it difficult to try to get the structure. It had many facts that you had to have on your cheatsheet to answer. +clickers
All lectures are done using power point.  This makes it hard to listen since it is such dry material

I can understand how some believe that he is uninterested in students success and he doesn't care, but to those people I say they don't know him, and that's their own fault. Jim is no BS type of guy, with a funny sense of humor. He changed course requirements many times to meet the needs of the class. He helped me many times past office hours.

He seems very uninterested in helpful students.  I believe students are in fact encouraged to use every resource possible before he even wants you to approach him.  I know he's busy, but if he teaches, he should have office hours.  Also depends too heavily on powerpoint. I don't know why he's a department head.

Uses powerpoint way too much.  I don't know what people like about him as a teacher.  He teaches too much 'touchy feely' about computer science.  Whenever I tried to talk to him he seem disinterested and wanting me to get out of his office.

Jim works very hard to help his students. He is always happy to help during his office hours as well as setting up appointments for other sessions.  His charismatic approach to teaching is great and the lectures he prepares are structured and entertaining.
Jim is an awesome CS professor. Probably my favorite in the department. Hard, but you'll learn a lot.

Ok teacher, Fairly hard though and seems to think he's the sh*t. In our Mechanical Engineering 1010 class he thinks we're supposed to be 100 percent dedicated to programming when really we don't care. Just stay on his good side and don't ask questions.
He is an ok teacher, but the class 1410 EAE, if you have no experience can be way hard! But you learn a crapload too!
No Comments
PRofessor is interested in teaching the subject, rather than flunking anyone he can find an excuse to.  'Nough said.
Most boring class of all time
Her lectures were boring at times and she did just read off the slide, but I thought the class was pretty easy and she was a very fair grader.

Not a very motivated professor. She uses Stukent for all her lectures and reads word for word from the slides and seems like they were just given to her. There's few homework assignments in the class. Group project is weighted very heavily. Barely any info is given on exams, no study guide, not even number of questions. Easy but boring class.

I don't know if it's because I love philosophy and logic before I took this class but the class was overall very easy.   The professor is very caring if you attend his lectures and review sessions. You can email him questions during exams because they are over the course of a week. Literally just use your textbook for the exams and your good to go!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: doesn't give good feedback at all, you really don't know what you don't understand until your exams. lectures are fine, but the content itself isn't clear whatsoever.

Toxic learning environment. Only had office hours after students went to his supervisor to complain about inaccessibility. No TA. The university tutor did not understand the content and he and my advisor told me to switch to any other professor. I put in 20 hours a week and had an A in the course up until the final, which tanked my grade to B-

I wish to God that someone had warned me about Jonah before taking this class. I was hesitant to give this class a 5 but it was as hard as Calc II. Did I get an A? Yes. Did I put in 10 hours a week? Yes. He's petty and uses a format that you can't get outside help for. He couldn't care about students and only offered office hours once begged?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was the worst experience I've ever had in the academic world. The professor teaches new information as if he is reviewing information you already know. He isn't helpful, and doesn't want to be. Both units go from level one to level 60 in one week. It's not worth it, avoid this professor and this course at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Brilliant teacher. I came into his class knowing nothing about philosophy or why it mattered. Ive learned a lot in his class and highly suggest it to everyone. He taught us invaluable skills that can be used in everyday life, and that cause you to think more deeply about how arguments really work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I have a doctoral degree in a related field, and have 10 years of experience teaching undergraduates in research ethics, probability, statics, etc. This is quite possible the worst teacher I have encountered at the college level. Unclear all-or-nothing assignment, opaque instructions, meandering lectures, way to many barriers to help or learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: - doesnt explain well - blames student often - not clear lectures - does not curve/partial credit -uses Carnap (no one uses it not even tutors) - makes you submit wrong answer and then helps you (doesnt change the wrong) - faster than honors classes - office hours is only one hour on fridays -petty professor

Get help from your peers, or expect to work on homework at the minimum 12-14 hours a week. The way this class is taught is unreal, you really just need to teach yourself. Or beg and beg for help. start a study group, it was the only way we as a class managed.

Only thing we were graded on were weekly quizzes based on the chapters we had to read that week, 1 essay, and a midterm and final. Final was cumulative. Not an easy A. Concepts are kinda hard to keep up with, if you study youll do fine. Not the most exciting class either but I needed the credit so

I knew nothing about logic and was only taking it for a math credit, but ended up loving it. It was challenging, but if you go to class and do your best on the homework you'll learn a lot. Jonah is understanding, loves his job, and is all around a great professor. Dense material but he is one of the kindest and most dedicated profs I've ever met
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: If you don't love advanced logic, you might really have a hard time with this class. He was great at explaining a concept in office hours but not in lectures. He graded assignments so strictly. A lot of the class didn't understand the material or do well on assignments which shows he didn't teach the material well.

Best professor in the philosophy department! Jonah truly cares about his students succeeding and understanding tough material. If you need to take logic, be sure to take it from him (or any other course, he offers). I learned more about philosophy from Jonah in 1 class than I did from the other 12 philosophy courses combined I took at the U.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Jonahs the kindest and most accessible professor Ive had. Really willing to help you understand the material. Good lectures and you can tell hes passionate about this stuff. It was hard to focus sometimes because I had a big crush on him, that was the only downside of the class

Incredible professor. I haven't taken his inductive logic courses, which is his focus, but I have taken two of his deductive logic oriented classes and I think that he has done a stellar job in instructing them. He is very clearly critical of the logics that he teaches, especially in his more advanced courses. His office hours are reliable as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great teacher. I am not typically into this sort of material, but I ended up having fun learning logic/probability etc. I definitely recommend his class. Education isnt supposed to be easy, you have to work for it. If you show up and do your part, you will pass this class. He is extremely fair, thorough, & will help you understand complex ideas
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The homework for the most part isn't difficult or overwhelming, but the online quizzes can be tricky at times. His lectures are pretty good, but sometimes it can get confusing because of the complex and long ways he uses to teach some particular concepts. Studying and getting help is recommended, yet the class nor the exams are too hard.

If you're going to be taking a logic course at the U, you wanna take it from Schupbach. The material on tests isn't necessarily hard, it's just difficult to complete all of it on time. I got writers cramp on every one of his tests I took from writing so furiously. Study and participate in class and you should be fine.

Jonah is an excellent teacher. If you are even remotely interested in the phil. of math/ probability then you are doing yourself a serious disfavor by not taking his class. Very clear explanations, beyond willing to help anyone that is willing to help themselves.

Avoid this professor at all costs. He does not explain things very well and is not a rational thinker. I can not express enough how disappointed I am in the University for accepting someone who could care less about his students to teach and essentially represent the school.

Prof. Schupbach is very helpful and willing to work with students (except most don't even bother to put the work in). Attend class, take notes, do the readings, and you can do well in his class. He is pretty easy going and is interested in the courses he teaches.
The exams were challenging, but he drops one. Never had homework. The group project at the end is buns you get graded on your peers work, and hes harsh.

Junseok Song is not fun to email or raise concerns with. His responses feel rude and haughty, and if you get unlucky with your random group for the project, good luck. He has a way with words where they make you feel like you're the problem. He also likes calling his students out for being late... weird.

Tests were quite difficult with a very lengthy amount of reading for each question. The professor can be a little rude to students sometimes. That being said, he is a great teacher in class and the lectures were very informational and applicable to the business world. We had lots of in class activities that were quite fun and hands on.

I have never felt compelled to write on rate my professor but his rating is far too high at 3.1. I think he writes self reviews. He is impossible to approach. Has a select few favorite students. Does not take feedback well even though he asks for it. He calls out students for being late and insults them. T
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class isn't that hard but his tests are harder than they need to be. Each test consists of extremely long word problems that have multiple answers. You can expect to read about 8 pages worth of information every test. That being said, it's a pretty easy course if you show up and pay attention.

This class was mentally draining all semester. Junseok comes off as condescending and a know-it-all. Lectures are boring, monotone, and loosely match what's on the tests. Exams are rough, many questions require multiple answers and you get a zero if not all are correct. Group project teams are randomly selected, and the instructions lack details.

Likable guy in my opinion, cares enough to memorize students' names. Flexible and forgiving on workload, and would often let us dictate what we would want to do in certain sessions. Lectures can be a bit long, but group activities break them up. Content felt very book-heavy and not super applicable, but I would blame the course and not the teacher.

He's passionate and tries to run the class professionally, which I appreciate, but his tone can feel condescending and made me nervous to email him. Exams are very long and harder than expected. The in-class activities are somewhat fun and class rarely lasts the full three hours.
Long terrible lectures that are not engaging. I would rather skip and take the grade cut then sit there and listen to him ramble for hours. He will also call you out
Absolutely take an online class with him during summer ! It is very easy, super fast and video lectures are very clear. I am loving this class so far and I was preparing for the worst.

This class was really easy. If you attend class, take notes and take them on your exams you will. do fine. Professor Song was really nice and understanding, I got very sick for a week and he was super understanding in excusing me from participation points and responded promptly.

during the first few weeks, my review for Song was 1/5. However, that changed. He turned out to be not that much of an a-hole because he drops an exam, a quiz, and often extends due dates, and provides extra credit. He asked me how I thought I did on the exam which went a long way because it made it seem like he actually cared. TESTS ARE HARD THO.

This was the worst class and the worst professor of my entire undergraduate degree. Junseok is inaccessible, cocky, and will claim to help you out with your career while he lacks one. In his tests, he says he will penalize you for "excessive coughing"

I really like him. I don't know if he changed up his class or what, but I really liked his class. Not to much homework, fun in class activities, was very clear what was going to be on tests, tests were long but not to difficult. Overall think his class was great and would take again.

Genuinely I cannot stand Junseok. He is so incredibly unbearable and has no real world experience, except for maybe a couple internships. He will not email you back if you dont follow his email format and makes his exams so unnecessarily long and difficult.

He went straight from internships to lecturing university students on how to manage. I was disappointed by the complete lack of personal experience supporting his claims. I have run my own buisness for a few years now, selling over 50+ haircuts, and he has no clue how he is misleading hundreds of kids, the future. In his defence, he does not know.

Thinks he's better than everyone else, uses words that nobody understands, is incredibly condescending, and moves on from topics quickly assuming everybody already understands them. He includes an unnecesary amount of information on his slides and makes them even worse by speaking in a monotone voice while reading off of them. Worst prof. ive had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Acts like a CEO without any real-world experience outside of internships. He's very lecture heavy but gets ahead of himself and it's almost impossible to take notes quickly. His tests are very unforgiving.

Don't take this class if you want an easy A or if you are uninterested in learning. Professor Song models the team project based on real world management consulting work, so it is an introduction to business career paths. He met with me in the semester to talk about my career goals and was extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Junseok is an awesome professor with lots of interesting in class activities. His syllabus includes something called a professionalism score, which I think frustrates some students who don't like to follow that structure. I get why they might feel that way, but to me, it feels more realistic to my workplace. That said, he seems fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This isn't a super hard class, but attendance is a must. He has assignments in every class for participation and doesn't work with you if you miss a single one. The lectures are awful and extremely long. He is a good person with a lot of knowledge, but he does come across as slightly condescending. Wouldn't recommend it- a 3/10 rating in my book.

I was not impressed with this professor. Lectures are boring, hard to listen to, and very lengthy. There are so many words on the slides; good luck writing down even the basics. He acts like he is the CEO of the entire school and has had very little real-world experience. One good thing is he gives you a 5-minute break in the 3-hour class.

Prof. Song is excited to explain anything he just learned from his classes & his two internships. He has barely any real-world experience, but acts like he was CEO of Accenture. He lectures quick, slides are not posted till after class; Good luck handwriting notes! Test questions are confusing, he even got a practice one wrong in his class.

Mgt 3030 - The class is very test heavy having many of the questions that come from optional article readings. It's very rude and passive aggressive to students. Also very difficult to deal with if you have any issues when emailing him. The class isn't necessarily hard, just get a different professor.

Junseok is the worst professor I've ever had. He is extremely boring, speaks in a monotone voice, acts better than everyone else, complicates content and communication, makes group project dynamics tense, and discourages students from truly engaging with the class. Do not take him if you want to enjoy management and your semester.

Unnecessarily and incredibly difficult. The lectures are long and boring, with so much to write down on the slides. You better write down everything because he will pick apart the little things and include them on exams. Exam questions are long and deceptive. He does a horrible job at engaging with students and is incredibly condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was unnecessarily difficult, especially as an entry level business class. Lectures were extremely boring, in-class activities felt useless and the tests were incredibly difficult with questions designed to trick you. Definitely would take this from a different professor, if you can help it.

Could tell he was trying to connect with students, but unfortunately fell a bit flat. The course content isn't difficult and yet getting an A as a student who never missed class, studied for every test, and participated was unnecessarily difficult. I'd say my biggest gripe was that the test questions were deceptive and he's a very harsh grader.

Professor Song was a good professor. In-class activities, though required, didn't feel burdensome to come in for, and they were often times actually pretty fun, and more so in the form of games. The only thing that I wish was that he made his exam questions a little less confusing.
Great speaker and very knowledgeable.

Its a good class, and he gives lots of opportunities to get a high grade. Group project heavy and that's the biggest part of your grade pretty much. I took the 3 hour section of the class which is pretty hard for me usually but it is broken up with activities and discussion so not too bad. All the powerpoints have all the info for the tests.

I really enjoyed the readings in the textbook, I do wish the lectures focused a bit more on material other than the GLOBE scores.
