Test were pretty difficult but the material was relevant and organized. Overall I enjoyed this course, the professor does grade pretty harshly so make sure you follow the instructions to a "T".

Professor Song is very knowledgeable and willing to go above and beyond for his students. He holds himself to the highest standards and encourages his students to do their best work. This is one of the best classes I have taken at the U and I would highly recommend taking a class from him. You will be challenged but you will be better for it.
One of the best professors I've had in undergrad. He's smart, funny, gave great feedback and ran the class efficiently as to not waste anyone's time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: In class activities that impact your grade. Lectures were laid back and entertaining. Tests were lengthy but they were not that hard. The only complaint I had was that . Expectations weren't very clear so you had to guess on what the Professor and the TA were looking for, and you weren't sure when you would have a quiz or test until the week of.

Never had a worse professor. Do not take the class with him. Very unprofessional. Test ?'s are long; examples are repetitive. He has terrible communication and grades unfairly and harshly. Lots of unspecified guidelines. The class was overall disappointing. Gives poor study materials/review sessions.

It's my senior year at the U of U, and this class has unfortunately been one of the most disappointing experiences I've had here. Song's lack of communication, unclear guidelines, and unfair grading really let me down, and did not live up to the standards I expect from a college-level class. If it's possible to take it from someone else, do it.

While the class is good and so is the content, the actual execution of teaching was poor. It was never clear when tests or quizzes were happening so if you want to plan your schedule, this class keeps you on your toes. Grading also doesn't seem fair and he plays favorites within the class.

Professor Song made this class so fun and interactive! He had clear expectations and was prompt with emails. He was a really caring teacher and made an effort to make sure he knew every students name and he genuinely care about if you understand content

the best professor ever had. Having anything that effect your grade talk with him, he take care about his students. responds immediately for emails. we had 3 exams and he made us vote if we want in person or online. he made us vote if one of the quizzes be extra credit or regular. If he's giving a class I'm planning to take I'll take it.

Tests were time-consuming and difficult and didn't reflect class concepts very well. I attended most classes and took notes, but the tests are broad and pull from readings that aren't ever discussed in class.  No real way to "study" for the exams.  Class discussions were fun and the connections made were all extremely positive. needs improvement.

Professor Song is an excellent teacher! He cares about his students and is easy to talk to. He is still a new professor, and his class sometimes seemed disorganized. However, he takes input from the class and is flexible if the class asks for a change. Participation is essential to receive a good. I would take another class with him.

Professor Junseok is a great professor. He does care about his students and his way of teaching. Although he does lecture the whole time. You will not leave early for this class. The group project at the end will be very time-consuming. Just make sure that you get a headstart and communicate with your members before it is too late.

This class requires attendance to be successful; in-class activities are graded on participation. You will only get a good grade if you show up. Tests are multiple choice and open-book. His lectures were interesting, and he is a very engaging professor. I would take a class from him again if I weren't graduating this semester.

As a student who is about to graduate, Professor Song was one of the best I had at the school. His class was fun and engaging, and he treated everyone with respect. Though his exams were a bit confusing, when we asked for clarifications, he immediately responded to them. If you put in the right effort studying, you will love both him and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Gives no clear grading criteria and you never know how your grade is determined. Lecture-heavy, "optional" readings show up on the test. Belittles you if you ask questions and tells you you are wrong. Overall the most frustrating professor I have ever had to deal with. He takes the class way too seriously and is honestly just mean.

Lectures are fun & engaging. The tests aren't hard if you come to class and pay attention sometimes the wording on the questions isn't great. My biggest gripe is that we never know when things will be posted/due. The last midterm posting & due date still arent known going into finals week. Expect to check canvas daily waiting for things to appear.

Professor Song is a very good lecturer, and he does a great job of fostering in-class discussions to keep everyone engaged. His tests and quizzes can be hard, but he does make sure to be very clear about what content will be covered. He is a very reasonable professor and will try to change anything if the class raises a valid concern.

He is a hilarious and entertaining professor and genuinely wants to have a good relationship with his students. He is a strict grader and at times I didn't understand how to receive a good grade. Overall, he needs to get better at writing tests in an evaluative and understandable way. I don't think his tests were hard just confusing.
Has very lecture have structure. Is condescending and rude when asking questions. Gives readings but never talks about them and puts them on the tests. Too hard for a 3000 level class.

I took CMP 2400 with Juliette in the Fall. She is a very kind professor who is dedicated to helping her students. However, her lectures are often difficult to understand and she talks in circles. I often dreaded going to this class because I felt like I got nothing out of it each class. There are so many group projects, I recommend making friends.

Assignments can be lengthy, but are easy to do well on. Feedback is good, and the professor is caring, knowledgeable, and encouraging.

Class time is used inefficiently, and lectures are rambly, difficult to follow, and not easy to learn from. 

Lots of reading that is not often discussed. Canvas layout is strangely complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't super engaging and there is a lot of group work, but assignments aren't very difficult and she's pretty chill

She's a great professor and you can tell she wants us to be successful. She's a fair grader and her lectures are easy to follow. The tests are easy as long as you look at the study guide. Overall I would take a class from her again.
This professor was extremely understanding and willing to work with me the whole semester through difficult circumstances to help me finish up the class in a timely manner.
She is awesome! Very knowledgeable and good at her job. She is clear with her grading, and if you have an issue, she is very easy to talk to and get help. Would recommend.

Easily one of the best professors at the U. She is caring, passionate, funny, and amazing at her job. Lectures are interesting and grading is clear. She is very kind, willing to work with all students. She is very flexible and very fair. She does take attendance, but time flies in her lectures. Would 10/10 recommend.
I wish she taught every class ever. Phenomenal instructor! Her lectures are very interesting and she explains them in extreme detail.

He's a nice guy and his assignments are straightforward. The testlets were a bit annoying since they were a lot of memorization but I found the reference sheets he provided to be very generous. I do feel he's somewhat unfamiliar with the content we covered, and I think he might of used ai to help him come up with assignments/lecture content.

David Johnson is the G.O.A.T.! His lectures are very funny, and he's accommodating both in and outside of the classroom. He was very test-heavy this semester, but honestly his tests were fair and if you did the assignments, then they're reasonable.
Got stuck with worst group ever, went to him early with my concerns but didnt help at all. Purposley makes tests tricky, test averages were pretty low this semester
He engages the class, is funny and actually cares. I really dislike CS, but he made me look foreward to lecture. A slay and a half, defo would take again.

Professor Johnson is *the* reason I am graduating from the C.S. Program. His class was accessible to me as a non traditional student, he was accommodating of my disability in class and completely understand of extenuating life circumstances. I have *never* had a professor go to such lengths to ensure my success. All I had to do was reach out.

Professor Johnson sets students up for failure with trick questions on exams covering material never taught in class. He is a harsh grader, deducts points excessively, and offers no helpful feedback. Exams feel designed to trap students rather than test knowledge. Avoid if you want fair grading and reasonable expectations.

Professor David Johnson dismisses valid questions instead of engaging thoughtfully. He ignores industry standards, repeats the same reasoning without clarification, and rejects discussion of modern practices. While the course is well-structured, his lack of engagement weakens learning. Not recommended if you value critical thinking.
I loved taking CS 1400 with Professor Johnson. It is a great class if you want to see if Computer Science is right for you!

DJ is the GOAT!!! He records all of his lectures and is very clear about his expectations for the class. I am usually one to watch lecture recordings from home, but I looked forward to attending Professor Johnson's lectures in person every week. He is also very patient and approachable outside of class. Easily my favorite professor at the U.

CS 1400: Amazing teacher, explains concepts clearly, helped me with technical issues, very understanding and kind. I may be biased because I do have previous experience, if you also have experience this is your sign to do 1420, I def wish I did. If you don't have prev experience I recommend you use your resources, there's lots of ways to get help.
never coded before this, assignment were confusing to me and I didn't skip a single lecture. The assignment canvas pages were super long and a little hard to grasp. lock in.

VERY difficult class and I had no CS background, but succeeding was VERY doable. So many resources to help you (TA hours nearly all day every day, code feedback on Gradescope, extra cred on every assignment) but no one seems to use them. Bottom line, don't take this class for an easy A, but if you actually care to put in effort, you'll learn a lot.

While Johnson himself is a very sweet and understanding professor, some of the TA's in this class were too strict with grading and would take points off for no reason. The assignments were hard, because while Johnson would teach the base of concepts, the assignments were often very hard, I wish there were more resources he gave us to practice more.
Be prepared to read the canvas assignment five times before even understanding what you are supposed to do

Decent professor and fairly funny. When grading, he gives more feedback on code style and readability than other professors, which is good for learning. The one issue is he / his TAs often take more than a month to grade assignments.

I took this class as a person who has never really coded in my life. This is labeled Intro to Programming course and yet, it could not have been harder. The professor is very bad at explaining lectures. The grading is very harsh, deducting points off assignments that are not specified in the instructions..

HATE HIM.  Don't listen to the people that give him 5 stars, they probably already have a background in code. Even if you have a code that works he will search for any reason to not give an A. Lectures don't make sense and assignments take too much time. TA'S CARRY.
He was honestly really helpful and easy to contact if you had any problems. He was also super chill about turning stuff in and genuinely wanted you to learn

Johnson is one of the best professors you can get for the core CS courses. He dedicates so much time and effort to supporting his students and unlike for 3500, this course was very clear and straightforward to learn with. I wish the course structure was slightly different, but he still teaches it very effectively.

weekly assignments; lab is helpful; piazza is helpful.
I went into this class with little to no knowledge about Python and I got an A. You just have to put in the work. Lectures are recorded and on canvas.
One of the best prof at U. I learnt in his class without too much stress like other classes. Very funny and nice person. He replied piazza like he lived there, work ethics +++

I had David Johnson for 1400 and 1410 a while ago when I was a freshman in 2021. I now have him for 3505 and I completely took how amazing he is for granted in those early classes. After, I had Kopta then Germain, and man did I MISS Professor Johnson. Now that I have him again in 3505 I am so so happy. He's amazing, PAY ATTENTION for later classes.

Professor Johnson is a great person and very accommodating, but the structure of the class was poor. There were a lot of people in the class and there wasn't a lot of engagement, though the labs with smaller groups of people helped. The assignments and exams were quite difficult, but are able to show you the real world of computing.

I honestly wish I had just learned Python on my own. I feel like Johnson goes out of his way to make this class as challenging as possible. His practice tests don't prepare you for actual tests; his test questions are overly complicated and make no sense in actual programming; he takes forever to grade anything; and his due dates make no sense.

Professor Johnson is nice enough, but he's a bit... vague. Lots of assignments had a lot of "figure it out" elements, including sometimes how to set up new software that we were completely new to. It also took FOREVER for assignments to be graded, sometimes upwards of a month. He's funny, and friendly, but I'm not wild about how he runs his class.

He is very entertaining and engaging in his lectures. Doesn't just assign busy work. First few assignments are on your own, then a few paired programming, then two big group projects. Only a midterm exam, the final exam is just a presentation. Good course pacing and manageable workloads.

Relates material in a way that makes the learning process easy and fun.
Enjoyable lectures + well-structured and clear assignments. He's also a great guy if you ever get the chance to talk to him.

Johnson is awesome, especially for getting an introduction to Computer Science and Object-Oriented Programming. The best the CS department has to offer.

David is a goofy professor who clearly knows his stuff. I went into this class with zero Python knowledge, took the time to spend 3-8 hours on each assignment, and got the grade. He always responds pretty quickly on Piazza, which helped me a ton. Put the work in and you will be fine.
Take cs 1400 with him. He is good, trust me.
The lectures were pretty entertaining. Professor Johnson's jokes were extremely geeky but they were funny. The assignments were fun to code.

I liked professor Johnson. He didn't make lectures hard to understand, and did the lecture on zoom if you couldn't make it in person ocassionally. Some of the TA's were hard to work with at the beginning. But overall I would recommend his class.

Very nice professor, however at times was very condescending, at the end of class in his goodbye message he straight up said some of the class shouldn't pursue CS because they are a drain on others, this rubbed off wrong on everyone i talked to who read the message, very mean last message imo

I took 1400 with zero prior python knowledge and got by just fine. You will absolutely need to put effort into this class if you want to succeed, homework assignments can take forever. TA's carry the class sometimes. All three exams were decently challenging. All of this results in a class that teaches you a lot of good programming knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is an ok professor, the lectures are in a fast pace. The class was very big so he could not care much. To me, the TAs are the ones that carried this class. Overall, a tough class if you are not know Python in advance
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Johnson is a solid teacher. He explains everything well and his lectures are entertaining / informative. However, c++ can be pretty boring espically makefiles. Group / Partner assignments are super important in the clas so choose good people or else your life sucks. The mid-term really sucked in this class so be prepared for that. Simple class

He was not the best into cs Prof. The big weekly assignments were often long and could take up to a couple hours and did not match teachings in class . Emails were often condescending. only reason I did well was I knew python already. Unfortunately the only 1400 prof.

lame, just an intro to c++ class. Would rather take a different elective. I could learn about makefiles and pointers through youtube, better yet the intro classes could be done in c like other universities & not waste a degree requirement like this.

Cool dude. His HWs are time-consuming so I rely on CADE labs and sometimes piazza. The TAs carried this class for me. As for David, he clearly knows his stuff. He did great on zoom and always checked the chat for questions which is a major plus for me (hardly any other profs do this). Overall, great class, and I learned a lot as a beginner.

Johnson will be easier than Jensen for 3505. He's very accommodating to students (extending deadlines when students were struggling and gave a lightweight hw the week before fall break). There's a midterm but no final exam. Instead, there's a final project which he graded relatively lenient.

Disparity between assignments and what is taught in class. He needs to suggest more resources we can learn and practice from. His assignment instructions can be quite convoluted and long-winded when they could just be a sentence or more.

Assignment level doesn't match information provided in class. I was only able to do hw in this class with prior programming knowledge. This prof. seems to have a time management problem (takes up to thirty minutes to start lessons). For a class which requires 8 + hrs of practice he should suggest specific skills / resources to practice from.

I had a way better experience in this course then I did in the previous intro course using python. I found the projects to be far more fun, and the java language and concepts to be far more complex, and fascinating. David did a great job of presenting these hard concepts in a fairly simple manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! I loved attending his class and I learned a lot about Java!

Johnson is one of my favorite CS professors at the U. I feel like I always learn a ton but his classes are never too difficult. Most of the grade for this class comes from your projects (as I it should). The only thing that was overly frustrating this semester was getting docker setup to program c++ but overall 10/10

He's grown on me a bit after having more classes with him. His class is very accessible online, meaning, while you still need to stay caught up, you won't fall behind just for missing a few lectures if you use the online materials. His TAs gave good help and good feedback on our graded assignments. He gave lots of materials to use to be successful.

This is my second semester taking a class with Prof. Johnson. I have to say he has really grown on me! You can tell he's super passionate about CS and puts a lot of thought into his lectures. They're also really closely related to the homework so go to class!! Homework assignments are hard and long, but help is always available basically 24/7.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Compared to 1410 which I also took w/ him, 3505 was a lot more hands-off. I wish that he would have provided better instructions on setting up some of the technologies we used in class, other than that pretty good. HW load is more the course content than the professor. Very genial with students and has a good sense of humor. Would take again.

He was decent at teaching, though he could be rude to students during lectures. He often was too quiet to hear him clearly, even from the middle of the room. II felt that he felt that he is much better than the students he teaches and doesn't respect them very much. He's also strict on details on our written programming tests, which is weird.

Johnson is not great as a professor and is usually pretty rude, but his TAs make the class bearable and even do a better job than he does at teaching. If youre going to take his class, dont worry too much about lecture. Just power points and TA help should teach you well

He was fine. Far from bad and an easy A if you did the assignments. His lectures were like I had overdosed on ketamine while in a coma though. Completely useless. I went to all the lectures for the first midterm and none for the second, performed better on the second one. I am taking him again, and it is far from a bad class.

Prof Johnson didn't explain things the best for me. Things started to make the most sense during the lab sections where Ly was explaining things. Prof Johnson wasn't the most willing to work with you, and when you had questions the TA answers usually made more sense than his did.

Professor Johnson is a super nice guy and a great lecturer. Sometimes class felt kind of long though and you won't enjoy the labs if the TA isn't good. If you have a question with your assignment don't hesitate to ask for help on Piazza, you'll get a timely response. Also look back at the powerpoints from lecture as those help a lot.

Personally, I didn't enjoy all the lectures but he still was very informative. He records the lectures so if you need to do something else during class you won't get behind. The lab is what helped me the most. Overall, I enjoyed his class and it wasn't difficult if you paid attention and put in the required effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wish games majors werent required to take this class. Its way too difficult for people who have no idea what theyre doing and who have never touched a piece of code in their life. Wish this class could have been avoided.

This class was very challenging. Homework is very heavy and takes a lot of time. Piazza is your best friend so use it! He is a tough grader and I often found myself getting help from TA's a lot but Piazza is a much faster way than waiting in line for a TA
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Johnson is overall just a GREAT teacher. The way the course is setup is perfect for learning programming, and he makes sure to teach where if you really don't have any background you'll still be able to understand and get help. he's always help available in office hours and I love the forum 'piazza' he uses on canvas, it's helped a ton!

Great professor very nice and caring (will definitely give you as much help as you need), however, the homework is beyond entry-level material. Assignments take too long to do with not a lot of time given and are way more complex than what we learn in the lectures, the same went for 1010.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is really easy to get help through Piazza. The homework assignments take a lot of time though and it helps to get help during office or TA hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson made very clear the the assignments we did and the material that was going to be covered in the class. He shows a standard amount of care for his students although he does respond to students very well. His negatives lie in subpar teaching. I found myself being better taught by youtube videos on the concepts than his lectures.

TAKE THIS CLASS! This is actually my third attempt to take CS 1410 and I bet this class is the best. First, you don't have to buy any textbook. The best part of this class is that he gives you a really detailed description and his expectation about an assignment which other professors don't. And he also gives similar examples in the lecture.

Prof. Johnson conveys concepts clearly and with an upbeat attitude that makes his lectures a joy to attend. The subject he teaches is tough, but the workload is manageable. If you are ever stuck or need additional help to understand concepts, he has a network in place to do just that. Great prof, I wish I could have taken him in person.

CS1410 is a serious class, but Professor Johnson doesn't take himself too seriously. The homework is tough (get going on it early) but the lectures and labs have all the information you need to do it. The exams felt pretty tricky sometimes, so study thoroughly for those! Piazza is your best friend, don't underestimate it. Prof's replies are clutch.

Prof. Johnson is a really funny guy, and I really enjoyed his lectures. He was also very understanding and kind, giving us late days as needed if the class asked for them. The course itself was very boring and I fell asleep every during every lecture, but David makes it somewhat bearable. Take it from him, I've heard worse about the alternatives.

Very nice man and a fairly good professor. He replies to questions very fast and is detailed in the replies. Make sure to pay attention and go to lectures because all the material is very important. Homework is can be VERY difficult, especially if you missed the material that it is about. Follow along in labs, if not you may be totally lost.

This class was hard. I would study everyday for this class I still ended up having a 68% test average. The assignments are really tough as well, be sure to go to TA hours. I would recommend retyping his lecture code by yourself everyday, it will help you learn. Getting help on Piazza and emails are quick as well, this class is good, but study a lot

David Johnson knows CS, and that is what matters. His lectures are boring (but I am not a CS person so that may be why) and the weekly projects are so time consuming but if CS is your thing and you actually enjoy it you'll have no problem with Johnson. Oh, and he replies on Piazza at absolutely satanic hours and usually very fast. Does he sleep?

I took this class wanting to learn basic computer science. I quickly learned I was not meant to be in this class but it was too late to drop the class. The projects are ridiculously hard and time consuming and the tests are very difficult. Johnson is an amazing professor but I wouldn't take this class unless it's required for your major/minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors in the program, and extremely understanding. He puts in a lot of time responding to piazza posts and helping students get through bugs in their code. Really awesome professor.

No final, just an easy quiz every 2 weeks. Some weeks with about 15 minutes of homework. Grades fairly, especially with group work. Talk to him if groups have issues and he will adjust grade accordingly as is fair. Like many professors he welcomes question in office hours. Not much material in the class itself but it was easy.

David puts in very little effort in his lectures (they are all black and white, literally). Then he expects you to be perfect with your assignments, walking him through everything and naming everything the way he wants you to. Not worth your big tuition money, you will learn how to program better online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is great! His lectures are fun and always helpful and serve as a great guide for his assignments, which are also pretty fun for this course. He makes it clear what you are being graded on and provides tests to make sure you are passing those tests. He is great at getting students involved making things entertaining.

David Johnson is decent at giving lectures but his lectures usually dont help too much with his homework assignments. He is homeworks are too hard for this 10XX class (which is entry level ). If you have no experiences in programming before, prepare to suffer.

My favorite professor of all time. He is the first professor I've had in the CS department that gives students a fair shot to succeed. He responds to students' questions at ungodly hours of the night, he always makes himself available to help, and wants to do everything in his power to help one succeed. LOVE this professor. Take his classes!!!

Professor Johnson is a good lecturer. He has a good sense of humor and teaches clearly. He also highlights well the pros and cons of different industry standards and techniques. Generous grader on the final project.
Awesome professor. Useful projects and lecture for job hunting. Holiday respected, no homework during holidays. Finally, gave us a curve on grade.

Professor Johnson is definitely by far my favorite CS professor at the U. He is hilarious, and caring. He always responds to emails near midnight and is always on top of helping everyone succeed. This is my second class with him and he makes his assignments fun and very educational. Definitely go with Professor Johnson if you can!

He's a nice guy that's fun to listen to. He's a decent lecturer, but where he really stands out is in his feedback. He is really helpful in office hours and through email, and even took it upon himself to fix a major bug or two in my groups' projects when we got really stuck. Solid professor.
This class was not intended for entry level Computer Science students with no experience. Thankfully I had a friend who is a Comp Sci major who knew Python and helped me out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class is hard, as any CS class is to be expected. Prof. Johnson is really amazing, his lectures are easy to follow and the labs are great, too. There's a lot of homework and the exams are fairly difficult, which is usual for CS. If you can take this class from him, I definitely would.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: David's lectures were simple, but fairly effective. If it is your first time taking any form of a CS class, get ready to spend a lot of time on your homework! Spend time with the TAs or during his office hours to get the best grade.
Professor Johnson was a great professor. He explained things very simply and well. This class had a lab that was extremely helpful and I felt like I learned a lot through the class.

David is an awesome professor.  His lectures are usually pretty entertaining, but he also works very hard outside of class to help you, and will always email back quickly.  The course itself is very easy, 1 homework assignment a week (usually pretty easy/short) and 3 exams.  It is a very gentle introduction to Computer Science.

He was a great teacher and told you what was expected of you. He really showed his knowledge and did a great job of explain concepts. He was funny and his lectures were informative. I enjoyed his class and learned a ton!!

Great guy. Great professor. He knows what he is doing, but he is quite a goof. His lectures were decent and informative most of the time, but when they weren't, oh boy... have fun doing the assignments. They were difficult but very doable.   Tips: Go to class! Put in the work, go to office hours, and he'll treat you right.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His voice is extremely monotone, and the excitement level of lectures is on par with elderly bingo nights. You can tell he's extremely smart, but there's a communication divide between him and the students. Tough, long, and ruthless homework/tests. Study guides are also unhelpful for tests, but the TA reviews are slightly better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really great professor, always answered emails and forum posts really quickly. Good lectures, and very fair when it came to grading. Really cared about all of his students!

David Johnson is a quirky guy and keeps things interesting in lecture. He does a good job of showing concepts in code. The assignments make sense from a learning perspective and were somewhat easy (If you are completely new to coding, don't fret and ask your peers for help). Just do what you are supposed to, lord dejohnso  has your back!

David is so far the best CS professor I've had here at the U. He would respond to my emails super quick. It's a CS class so its going to be hard and you will have coding assignments that are pretty difficult, but he gives sample code and help is always available. Take Advantage of It!

David was an absolutely amazing professor. I took the same class at UVU and he is much, much better than any CS professor I had at UVU. If it's your first time, prepare to do a lot of CS homework, projects take some time but are very rewarding and he helped a lot during the class, and even after He answered any email I sent him, even at midnight!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnson is a great professor. Since I have programmed before so this course is not really hard for me, but still I have learned a lot about Java and programming to which I have not paid attention or which I have not learned yet. He has sense of humor and is very easy to ask for help through forum or email if you need help.

He doesn't explain topics from the assignments enough. He will introduce completely new topics in the assignments and just assume you can figure it out, barely ever even mentioning them in lecture. His assignment descriptions are extremely lacking, and he makes mistakes in his own code constantly. Honestly I don't think this dude enjoys teaching.

He has you use this programming language called scratch, which is pretty elementary in my opinion. This class does not prepare you for CS1410. David thinks scratch is the greatest thing ever. The interesting topics come around at the end of the semester. Plan on 2-4 hours per assignment due weekly.  Using a programming language meant for children.

To be honest, I found David's lecture style to be absolutely dreadful; his sense of humor bored me and I can't think of a single lecture where I walked away feeling like I gained useful introspective in the field. However, he cut me some massive slack when I missed a test and overall was very accommodating to most student's concerns.
I loved this class. Lectures are informative and easy to listen to. All but one project were group projects. Generous grader, assignment documents are very clear.

David is a good guy and I really enjoyed taking this class from him. It's no walk in the park but the hours are reasonable. While I wish I had better clarity on some projects and the setup for them, which can take a long time, he's a cool guy who's easy to talk to and his lectures are enjoyable. I'd take a class from him again.

Tough grader: Huge assignments due Tuesday nights. Put aside a couple hours for them. I believe it was the TAs that graded, but there was zero leniency on them, even though the rubric was hard to follow sometimes. There for you & Hilarious: I found the lectures pretty funny, which helped. He has clickers, so be there. TAs help tons with labs.

Fails to communicate what the emphasis of his lecture is.  Assignments often need clarification and further specifications in the class after they are assigned, and it seems that he doesn't put much planning in. Difficulty not particularly high, but grading seems arbitrary, and it is easy to lose points for aspects that were not communicated.

David was a friendly professor, he tries to crack jokes and laughs at himself sometimes. His lectures are usually very laid back, and he has all the lecture powerpoints online so it's not the end of the world if you miss a lecture. The labs had tons of group work, so be wary. Plenty of TA's to help you out.
Had to read the textbook to understand what was going on. Overall just not the best teacher unfortunately. But she's very nice and she means well.

This professor is the worst one I have ever had. She is physically unable to explain anything simply, and she will somehow confuse you on how to calculate 2+2=4. She is constantly wrong in class, and teaches things wrong often. The class is completely teach yourself. She's just that bad. Her handwriting is illegible and unclear. do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sweet person, bad teacher. Doesn't explain concepts well, meaning you teach yourself; quizzes with no warning what they are on or when. Concepts barely mentioned; then quizzed immediately; canvas full of bugs; incorrect scores leading to unknown grades; and many mistakes while teaching the material meaning you learn it wrong. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard but fair. Other professors teach easier versions of her classes, but Professor Sainath is nothing but helpful, responsive, and kind to her students even when they are severely struggling.

I don't believe Professor Sainath deserves the current score she has. She was nothing but helpful and responsive when I had her. Her lectures may not be the most engaging, but they are detailed and efficient! I can only blame myself for not getting higher than a B. While she is not outstanding, she is more than competent.

Professor Sainath's 5080 course had fundamental flaws. The disconnect between theory and exams left students unprepared, and labeling study aids as cheating worsened the situation. Ineffective classroom management further hindered learning. Prospective students should consider alternatives for a better learning environment.

She is a nice professor but she isn't a good professor. She is not the best at teaching because her lectures are long and often boring. Her homeworks were not at all related to the lecture material. She would not give complete answers to problems in the homework and exams. If you can avoid taking her class please do it will be for your own benefit.

She's really nice and will work with you if you can't make it to class. However, her lectures aren't structured well and tend to be really confusing. You can get easily lost. The homework isn't like what is in the lectures so you're left teaching yourself a lot. She grades pretty easily, luckily.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a nice person. But apprently she has no ideal how to teach.. She doesn't post anything on cavas util the exam so you will be forced to teach yourself...

She is by far the worse professor from the Math Department. Her lecture is just simply out of textbook, but her quizzes and exams are not even from the book or what she taught in class. There is no curve, so do not expect an A even if you worked hard, read everything from the book and did all the homework.
She is a nice person, but not a nice instructor. Her exams and quizzes are extremely hard. Most of the questions on exam are in format that I've never seen in class or even on homework.

She is extremely poor at explaining anything simply. This is the second time I've been forced to take her because she was the only option for a required class. Both times she made concepts we already understood more confusing. Tests are straightforward and easy, but prepare to teach yourself a TON because she won't teach it well.

She did not test on things she did not lecture on, so going to her lectures helped. However, she does have an accent and her handwriting tends to be on the small side so sometimes not being in the front of the class is disadvantageous. She is readily available to help you though, and is a very understanding person.
She's a super nice professor, and her class is very organized, but the lectures were really confusing and I had to teach most of myself through the lecture notes and it was really tough.

Unfocused, sometimes rambling lectures. She'll answer even your most pointed question with long-winded rhetoric that is only sometimes helpful (or relevant). Her class would lead you to believe that there is no structure or methodology to what she's teaching, even when there is. She just won't talk about the material that way.

Dr. Maldonado made her class very engaging, combining real cases as well as her own personal stories. She does weekly reflections, which consist of analyzing research articles that can sometimes be long. There are no tests or quizzes in her class. Attendance is mandatory and part of your grade. I would definitely recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Maldonado's work. Her classes are perfect if you want to improve your reading comprehension and political efficacy. The class is mostly analyzing journal articles, and then midterm essay and a final project. No tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are a large percentage of your grade

Prof. Maldonado genuinely cares about her subject matter, and it's evident in her passionate lectures and readings. While there are a good number of readings each week, they are all interesting and directly relate to the content covered in the lectures.
Really good professor! Lectures were interesting and no tests but in class assignments.

I loved my class with Dr. Maldonado and she was very kind and respectful and let us share our thoughts. I am taking another class with her because I really liked her. Participation was super important though and she was pretty strict about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good and understanding professor, but the coursework is difficult and filled with trick questions. It's practically impossible to get an A, no matter how well you know the coursework. Always look at questions thrice.
Tests were difficult with many trick questions, memorization-based and always seemed like she wanted to hit a criteria for test distribution. Julie may have been better to work with than taught by.

She's clearly knowledgeable and passionate about the material, but she's confusing and her lectures aren't engaging (I taught myself by reviewing slides). Testing is also a pain, tests based on the content she taught (about half the semester) was tough. Wording and overall questions made me feel like I hadn't attended class (I missed once)

There were some lectures where she went so slow in the beginning and then had to speed through the end because of no time left. Some days we didn't even cover all of the slides. Her answers to my questions were really confusing too.

If you take the class with Julie and James, you'll see that she is far better at explaining difficult topics in a simple way. She keeps lectures on-track and only tells you what you need to know, but she's also very nice about answering questions and re-explaining things. She's straight to the point. Pay attention in lecture!!!

Professor Hollien is an extremely boring lecturer. I'm close to falling asleep in almost every class. Plus, she makes her exam questions purposefully confusing and misleading. I'm constantly frustrated when she teaches. Avoid her if you can't teach yourself.

The half of cell bio taught by her was not good. I did not like her lectures. She didn't have any enthusiasm and it made the time go by slow. Next to that she doesn't explain things well and the tests are hard. In her office hours she doesn't answer much. Just tells you to think, and I would say she can be a tough grader.

Dr. Hollien was a nice professor. She teaches some really cool stuff and she shows she's really excited about teaching you these fundamentals. It's super cool when she shows you into her lab and how what you learn in the class can actually be applied. Not a bad choice at all! :)

Just dont even go to her office hours, there is absolutely no point. Shell just tell you to think about it and then tell you youre wrong. she will not help you understand anything, which is literally her job. She is not interested in helping you because you should know this from the lectures. or you should know this from previous classes.

Julie does not care about her students at all and makes it clear that she only cares about her research lab. Awful at explaining things and tests on information that is not included in lectures. On top of all of this, it is impossible to get a timely and helpful response to any sort of question. Do not take this class with Julie.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Julie's tests are ridiculously hard. Not even with open notes, studying, and reading the textbook are you able to do well on the exams or problem set worksheets. She does not help with the worksheets during discussion. Instead of helping, she rambles on and makes the worksheet more complicated. Rambles about her research and tests on it too.

Love Cell Bio with Julie. It's co-taught with James Gagnon and I really prefer her lectures--I feel like I can actually pay attention when she lectures and I've been doing better in the class since she took over the lecturing. Also, you should probably use the textbook--that will boost you to the A- range.

I will start this by saying that Julie has high hopes for the class with a poor follow-through. She does not seem to teach what is tested and then says it's an application problem. While some of her questions are very fair, others are so poorly worded that I wonder if she only knows Bio and not English. Besides that, she is incredibly rude.

Joint professor who teaches cellular biology with James Gagnon. She has an excellent way of explaining material so it is easily understandable. Very happy with how she conducted the class and would recommend to anyone and everyone planning on taking this course.

This class was meh. Your grade is based off 3 exams, and 2 weekly homework assignments online. Lectures weren't particularly engaging, I skipped a lot of classes and read the slides on my own time and did fine. Julie is great though, she's one of the rare profs that you can tell actually cares about her students.

One of the most understanding professors I've had. She's very cooperative and cares for her students. The class is very clear and I'd recommend everyone to take it with her and Jamie. You will have a lot of leeway for getting a desired grade. Study the lectures and use the book for the HW and you're all set! An overall sweetheart!

Pretty neutral choice for Cell Bio. Homework was really easy. She outlined expected learning outcomes and there was heavy emphasis on not memorizing things although when tests came around it was obvious you did need to memorize some things. I never cracked open my book once, but wouldn't recommend doing that...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Julie was an okay professor, she's not the worst, but not the best. She is not accessible outside class nor accommodating. She will go really in depth into topics and then mention it's not important (what is important was vague) and talk way above our skill level and very apathetic. The textbook is not helpful, but her exams were fairly easy.

I absolutely loved James and Julie's Cell Biology class. They taught the core concepts, and really helped avoid the onslaught of meaningless memorization. They supplemented all they teaching with realworld experiments and really helped enforce what is important for cell bio. Their tests are not to hard assuming you paid attention in class. Loved it
This is a great class. Be ready to think! You can't memorize your way through the course. Lectures are engaging and Julie is awesome. She is one of the smartest professors I've ever had.
Great professor. Learned a lot, very little memorization if you are interested in the material
Classes were super fun because she made the slides very engaging. Would recommend!
Great Japanese instructor! She made classes very fun and made Japanese feel less scary.

Kajitani Sensei is so nice. Everything for a beginners Language class was explained really well and easy to understand. there is cold calling in class and lots of conversation with several classmates which is not everyone's favorite but in the end is very helpful for learning. Kajitani Sensei is very patient and understanding!

Wonderful teacher! Japanese is a difficult language to learn starting from english by nature, so the class will be tough. But if you study, prep, and really engage you'll be alright—she's really great at what she does and I learned a lot! Additionally, she's very kind and understanding. I would love to take more classes of hers!

Learning a language is hard by nature. There's a lot of work involved, but Kajitani-sensei only gave assignments that would genuinely help us learn. Kajitani-sensei is the most kindhearted professor I've ever had. She's a fantastic teacher, and I learned more in a semester with her than in four years of high school language classes.

I have been taking Japanese for 5 years, and I have learned the most Japanese while under Motomi sensei's instruction. She is very nice and tries to strike conversation with me whenever she has the opportunity, even when I am not in class. I would love if I could take her for higher levels, but I am glad I got 1 semester with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Absolutely LOVE Kajitani Sensei!! She is so very kind and will help you as much as she possibly can! I loved her teaching style and she really fosters a sense of community within her classroom. No matter what Japanese professor you have, the workload will be similar as it is a tough language, but you'll be in good hands if you are taking Kajitani!

Kajitani is kind, but the class workload is overwhelming. New material was assigned as homework, making lectures less helpful. Heavy self-study was required, with 2 quizzes/week, biweekly tests, essays, and frequent large exams. It's difficult to balance with other obligations. Only take this course if you can commit significant time to self-study.

Kajitani Sensee is one of the kindest and most caring teachers I have ever had. Consistently pushes back deadlines to meet your needs, and loves helping you through putting together sentences in Japanese.Savvy in both Japanese(natively) and English...has better English than most of my engineering professors that..teach in English. S-tier professor.

Dr. Baucom is a wonderful prof who wishes the absolute best for all of her students. She is sweet, wicked smart, and easy to talk to outside of class for extra help or advice about all things psychology and grad school. Abnormal behavior was an easy class that I learned a lot in, and it was low stress due to the plentiful extra credit. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I gave her a "4" on easiness, but it's a class that you definitely can't fall behind in or it will become more difficult.  It's not a class that you can just show up for the exam.  Great teacher, presents the material in a way that's easy to understand.  Came across a little catty a couple of times, but is still really good at answering questions.

One of the best professors I have had! She gives weekly pop quizzes which are not hard if you review the material. Her tests are hard but fair. She gives a practice exam before the tests which are extremely helpful.  It is important to go to class as her tests are from her lectures. I wish she taught more of the core Psych classes!
Sae Kawase is a great professor. She almost always grades homework by the day you turn it in or the day after. In addition, it's always a great environment in her class.

Sae Kawase is awesome! She gives out a lot of homework, but she routinely grades them by the next day or by the latest the day afterwards. As well, as long as you can keep up with the high amount of homework, it's completely manageable to get an A in the class and I think it's a pretty useful amount of practice for learning Japanese.

Sae Kawase was a fantastic teacher! I took her last semester and while her class isn't easy, she's definitely one of the best teachers I've had at the U. She's a very fast grader and usually you're able to get the grade in by the next day, and there's enough engagement with the class that makes going in each day interesting.

I have had Kawase for every class, and I will continue to take courses with her because she is a good and nice teacher. She gives a lot of homework, but it is usually given 100% grades just for doing it (it also forces you to put more thought into the language). As long as you care to learn Japanese, you'll get an A. She is NOT a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She seemed fun at first. The class activities and assignments were fine, but the projects and tests made me doubt I knew any Japanese at all. Grading was harsh, and she acted like we should already be fluent. If you're not already strong in Japanese, this class can be a nightmare, and she's the only one teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly she is the worst professor I've had. It's not the amount of assignments, but if you have mental health issues. Please don't EVER take this class. She will degrade you and make you feel like you will never be able to be fluent. She might seem nice at first, but she is not! As long as she's the only Japanese professor, don't take her class.

Honestly surprised how high of a rating she has, but I have a suspicion as to who is writing the good reviews iykyk. 
She is so unhelpful, instead of having helpful corrections on projects, she will just put a question mark. Or if you ask a question she will just tell you to figure it out yourself. Avoid her as best as you can!!!!

I want to love this prof. she is great in many ways and I adore her humor and teaching style, but as someone who is neurodiverse I am constantly struggling with unclear expectations, overly strict grading, and lack of flexibility I cannot recommend this professor, especially if you require additional help or accommodations.

Wonderful teacher, and the course load is generally equivalent to the amount of effort necessary to truly get something out of this course. She's very accessible outside of class and has compilations of study resources to aid those who need it, which is great. Overall, she has a great sense of humor and knows how to make learning Japanese fun!

Tons and Tons of work. Very hard to balance this class with others, if you are taking a heavy course load on top of this class, it will sabotage your entire semester. Unfortunately Kawase is the only option for 3040, so I cant recommend not taking this class if you are a Japanese major, but tread with caution!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kawase is an excellent Japanese instructor, she is friendly and open to answering questions. Only enroll only if you are passionate about Japanese. Anticipate frequent quizzes with short time limits and a substantial amount of homework that may take hours. She's nice, but the class is recommended for those seeking a challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kawase is by far the best teacher for japanese at the U. She is understanding if you have any troubles, and she is there to help. The only way to fail her class is if you don't do the homework and don't show up to class prepared. I'd recommend her over any of the Japanese professors, but be prepared to study and be prepared to talk to others.
Although the class moved quickly, she gave people a lot of time to ask questions to understand the material. She cared about her students' well-being and ability to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was so fun and Kawase Sensei is a great professor in my opinion. She's super friendly and leaves lots of helpful comments on all the graded assignments. Yes, there is a ton of work but she's an easy grader. Just make sure you have plenty of time to study because this class moves really fast.

Kawase is a fantastic teacher. That being said, do not take this course unless you are passionate about learning Japanese. I have taken other Asian language courses in the past and I found this class particularly challenging. Be sure to have an open schedule because you WILL have a heavy workload -- as well as two quizzes every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kawase is one of my favorite professors. She is a tough grader and the course is very intensive but through participation and effort, students learn an incredible amount in one semester from her. There is a LOT of homework every night and there are 2 quizzes a week so only take this course if you are serious about learning Japanese.

I can say with confidence Kawase is the best teacher I have ever had. You have to do the homework if you want to do well on the tests but its totally worth it. She's super helpful and I cant wait to have her in 2010 too!

Fantastic teacher, but gives a lot of homework. This is understandable because learning language involves a lot of repetition. Despite the workload, she is a very easy grader. It is very difficult to not get a good grade and is more indicative of lack of effort than anything. She is very approachable for help as well. Genuinely fantastic.

This class is super hard but so is Japanese I guess. Tons of homework though it is a four credit hour class so it makes sense. Don't take this class unless you really want to learn Japanese or it's not worth it. There is so much homework. Kawasae is very nice however and accommodating if you have any problems. She's a very good lecturer as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kawase-sensei's class is tough, but totally worth it! There's lots of homework, and many different kinds of assignments and projects, but if you put in the time to study you will absolutely learn Japanese. She works to make the class fun, and provides cultural context! Don't sign up looking for an easy A, you won't pass doing the bare minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There's a lot of homework, and the class is fast, but the organization of her course was top-notch. I have never seen a Canvas page that was so helpful. Extra study materials, all lectures posted, fun content, etc. This class was very hard, but all you need to do is study. Learning a language is not easy but she made it fun and was very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the toughest professor I have ever had. She opens up assignments that are due the next day. If you really desire to learn Japanese this is not a good course as you move so fast its unlikely you can retain any knowledge. If you still want to take her class, make sure its the only course you are taking, as it will take up your whole life.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kawase sensei is one of my favorite teachers that Ive ever had (college or otherwise)! Japanese is tough but shes does an awesome job. She may seem cold at first but as soon as you get to know her a bit more shes hilarious! Lots of homework and a very tough grader, but shes fun, focused, and friendly and I cant wait to take 1020 with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The most unlikable & unnecessarily hard teacher I've ever had. This class was also a ton of work for a 3000 level class. Avoid her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is an immense amount of work, takes an incredible amount of time and the instructor is a harsh grader. However, this instructor is also very helpful and makes a lot of changes to help everyone in the class learn and be successful including extra credit opportunities and a grade curve. Overall amazing instructor just be prepared to work
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor if you can. The workload for this class is far beyond that of any other 3000-level course. It's much worse than the other 5 classes I'm taking combined. She has you do the workbook homework before talking about the grammar in class. She's new to the university so maybe she'll change later on, but this was a horrible class.
Jasmine Khaliq is an amazing instructor! She is good at getting you to engage in the content, assigns interesting literature and is such a kind person. Would absolutely recommend her class to anyone.
Professor Jasmine, makes writing class so much more enjoyable and less stressful and I respect her for it. Thank you professor Jasmine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Khaliq is one of the best professors I've had. She's super understanding and easy to work with. She will help you when you need it and is super flexible when it comes to extensions for assignments.

I feel like I'm so lucky that I got Professor Khaliq for WRTG 2010 because she genuinely cared about teaching the material and made it interesting. There are a lot of writing assignments in her class, so she is very understanding when it comes to extensions. However, she saved all of the grading for the major assignments until the end of the year.

This class is a necessary evil, but Professor Khaliq makes it bearable. She is extremely understanding when it comes to extensions and tries her best to work with you. Attendance started as non-mandatory, but she switched it to mandatory as the semester went on and fewer people were attending class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is a difficult course, but very rewarding. At first the pace is a little slow, go to lecture and find a study group. Completed most of the homework in office hours. Monson is a clear lecturer and wants students to succeed. Good resources available and fair coursework

The lectures generally provided plenty of information for the hw, which were done through Pearson. The exams were 3 problems that covered the main topics learned. He graded pretty tough if you dont follow the exact process he wants. The final project was a little silly and seems unnecessary for the course.

Consists mostly of lectures that are very hard to follow. Even if you can grasp the concept (which will take a lot of YouTube), it won't help you on the exams because they are not related to anything taught in class. Grading is very test-heavy and he is not willing to work on regrades. Going to office hours only shows he cant solve his problems.

Lectures are very example heavy. He gives alternative ways to work through questions but takes off lots of credit on exams when you don't use the formulas he wants. Not very flexible with students either. Not much homework is given so most of your grade is based on exams. He often gets lost in lectures and makes mistakes in his work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible at explaining things. Zero based knowledge. This class should be way easier than he makes it out to be, I attended every lecture and was lost, did not answer questions well either. Had to learn from other professors on YouTube.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very organized and dr monson provides ample resources to do well and opportunities to make up for bad test/hw grades. He posts covid videos for each lecture if you don't go, or he inevitably falls behind and rushes through important things. Homework is tough but the tests are much easier. Consistency made this class pretty easy

Dr. Monson is very smart and cares a lot about students in the class. Lectures were very example heavy and got confusing at times. Homeworks were lengthy but helpful. He does hiking breaks during lectures. He's really good about partial credit on exams. He'd check attendance once per week which was worth 5% of the final grade.

Dr. Monson is a super knowledgeable and caring professor. Lectures are engaging and fun, and he likes to take a "hiking" break during class to talk about the hikes he goes on. The material in this class is interesting, and the book is very well written. If you attend the lectures and do the reading, you'll be in good shape.

My class was moved into Monson's class halfway through the semester so we definitely had a different experience, but as far as lectures go, he was great. He was very example-heavy, which could get confusing, but he kept us engaged throughout the class. Tough grading, not big on partial credit, and exams are worth a lot of points which was rough.

This class is now in person (no longer flipped classroom), and his lectures are fantastic. He does a great job of teaching the material and answering questions, and uses many examples. The class material is pretty hard, but he does a great job teaching it. He is a fair grader, and often offers rewrites on exams. There is a final group project.
He was a really good lecturer and it was easy to pay attention and learn in his class. He was very helpful with answering questions and accessible for questions outside of his normal office hours.

Professor Monson is an awesome professor and very nice guy. He lectures well, but my only critique is sometimes his approaches to example problems seem a bit more complicated than it needs to be. His exams are very fair and the homework load is fair too. Every lecture he breaks to tell us about a hiking adventure to give us a break. It's super fun.

Some of the material in this course gets pretty complex, and Monson did his best to explain it. His lectures were just slides from the textbook, and I never got the sense that he cared about students / wanted to be teaching. Definitely seemed like he'd rather be working on more of his research.

Very difficult class.  I wouldn't have passed this class without a good group of friends that helped me understand the concepts. Be prepared to spend many hours outside of class figuring out the concepts and methods. Do not get behind in this Dynamics or you will struggle.  However, the tests are not terrible.

He has a flipped classroom which I liked because I could go back to review, but if online learning doesn't work for you, avoid this class. I got most of the homework done during class, but you dont actually have to go except for Fridays when there are little quizzes where you get full points if you submit. I felt that the exam were very reasonable.
He will not teach you in class. Multiple lectures had incorrect information.

Ken is by far the worst professor I have had. He does flipped classroom so all the lecture material is prerecorded. Often times he gives one theory video and one incredibly basic example and that is it. His homework and tests are astronomically harder than his examples, and he is little to no help during office hours, he cant do his own problems.

He is one of my best professors that I've had so far. He doesn't move too fast and is very clear when he speaks and is teaching. He uses a flipped classroom, watch lecture videos then review and work on homework during class time. He makes himself available during class, in office hours, and via email. He was also just with his grading.

One of the most ineffective professor I've had across any area of study. Monson has switched over to entirely recorded lectures, essentially shifting the onus of actually teaching the course in a format that supports discussion onto his students. His reliance on Mastering for homework is shameful, and I left this class feeling like I hadn't learned

AWESOME PROFESSOR!!!! He is probably the best lecturer that I had in all my classes. Be aware, he isn't an easy professor. His tests are pretty hard and VERY comprehensive. You need to know how to combine the principles you learn. He made a very hard class enjoyable.
This guy is top notch! Beware of his exams though.

Ken Monson is one of the best professors I've had at the U. His lecture is clear and he does a lot of examples to help you work through the assignments. You are expected to do a lot of problems, but his tests are very similiar to problems worked in class and on the homework. He grades fair and is strict to his policies. Highly recommend this teach!
Ken Monson is the bomb! Best professor ever! Teaches clearly, gives plenty of examples, and helps with questions. Great teacher of a hard subject.

Dr. Monson is one of the best profsesors I've ever had. I took Dynamics from him and don't believe it could be taught better. Teaches concepts crystal clear, is 100% prepared for class and has multiple examples to go over. A difficult course, but with him teaching, failure falls squarely on you.
Great professor. Lectures are helpful as he does many examples and answers questions pertaining to the homework.

I took Dynamics from Dr. Monson and I can highly recommend him. It's hard material, but he only teaches with examples so going to class really helps. He was available for help after almost every class period and genuinely cares about the success of his students!

Professor Sina clearly cares about the course content and the students. The class was very accommodating for the current pandemic. The Group project was very structured and almost a direct application of what was being taught in lecture. Plenty of practice material wish optional quizzes post-lecture. Couldn't recommend him enough.
Weekly quiz

Sina is awesome. He took time to explain every single concept in details. Text book was required but you do not need it, everything you need to know he'll cover it, so save your $$. Best part of the class: 1). He did every problem in his ppt on the board. 2). He did recap of the previous lecture at the beginning of every class ( super helpful).

She is great! She is a little intimidating because she speaks so much in French, but she is quite easy to understand. She is always willing to help students and make sure they are learning. I learnt a lot because she made sure we understood the material. She nit-picks on details, but it is beneficial. I felt like I was truly learning.
She explains things very well but is tough (as she should be). She speaks 90% in French but at a speed that is understandable. I really liked her teaching style.

I really knew my stuff when I left this class. She makes French easy to understand. The class is difficult if you're lazy or not really into French. French is a tough language, but if you put in the effort it's actually quite enjoyable. There was a lot of work but I loved doing it, so it wasn't so bad. The textbook with Quia is a MUST have.
No Comments
Don't take her class. It won't let me explain why but just trust me :)

Professor SK is a great prof. I really enjoyed her intro to phonetics and phonology class; she's great with expanding on questions and makes sure everyone understands. Sometimes, her wording can be unclear, but she clarifies when asked.

I don't really recommend this professor if you're aiming for an easy A. She's a very tough grader, and even if you put in the effort, it's hard to get top marks. The expectations aren't always clear, and the grading can feel harsh. Be prepared to work hard and still possibly end up with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I truly did not enjoy this class or professor. She was lowk condescending the only time I ever spoke with her on zoom. Her assignments are hard and graded harshly. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Prof Kim is low-key mean I had a zoom meeting with her (my first time ever meeting her) and she told me what I can and can't write about in a very dismissive and condescending way. What I was writing about was on topic.

Lectures a little boring but get the job done. Grading kinda strict but some extra credit is offered that helps. There were extra credit Q's on the midterm which helped me get over 100% on it, totally boosted my grade. A lot of the grading is based on 5 major assignments but you have a lot of time to work on them, just make sure you start early!

The class was very interesting and the professor really wants everyone to learn and do well. She gives you extra credit, there are rubrics for every assignment, and she sends announcements at the beginning of the week to remind you exactly what is due and when. She lets you submit anything late for 2 days. Plus you learn stats but it's not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The biggest thing you'll want to watch out for in this class are the long readings. Each week, you'll have 1-3 relatively long, academic linguistics papers to read. Other than that, its a pretty normal upper-level HF class. I found the subject material interesting, but the class' whole presentation was imo pretty dry/boring. Not abysmal, not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Strict grading with little to no feedback. Lots of homework: Each week there are 2-3 brutally dry linguistic research papers that you need to read ranging from 15-25 pages long, and then there are a couple discussion groups and a few quizzes for each article. Several papers throughout course make up almost half of final grade. Wouldn't take again.

Prof Kim is an extremely tough grader, I emailed her letting her know I had Covid and her response was dismissive and discouraging. It feels like she purposefully adds little hurdles to the class to ensure you are stressed. The lectures are boring, for such a potentially interesting subject. VERY difficult. Not supportive. Dont take her class.

Prof Kim has been my least favorite prof yet. You can count on reading and being quizzed on 2-3 dry, lengthy, 15-25 page, small text linguistics articles per week. Three papers make up 40% of the grade, she takes weeks to grade, and does so very subjectively. A+ effort in other classes gets you about a B in this. She is aware of it & doesn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Horrible. Tons of reading and assignments, super tough and subjective grader, and takes FOREVER to get grades back. Does not allow for revisions on most stuff, nor is there any way to earn back credit. Shes a linguistics professor but cant word quiz questions well to save her life. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kim has a very heavy workload compared to my other upper division classes. There are multiple lectures, discussions, readings, quizzes, and assignments per week plus 3 papers. Is a tough grader, leaves no feedback, and takes forever to grade. This class could be very interesting but the lectures make it as dull as possible.
Grat proffesor

Just a terrible professor. If you are not one of his "favorites," meaning participating all the time he will not give you the time of day. His grading criteria for assignments are incredibly arbitrary and the TA grading reflects that. People with nigh identical code have gotten significantly different grades because of the TAs.

Jamie is an incredible professor and makes class really fun to be in. The TA's are horrible overall, cold and indifferent. This class is indeed a weed out class. If you think it's like 1410 ezpz A+, think again.  You will actually need to put in a fair amount of effort to succeed in class, so be prepared. I wasn't prepared sadly so I'm retaking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jamie is a fun professor who makes class entertaining. His lectures are full of funny jokes and strange analogies, plus he records and uploads all of them. He is tough and expects lots of work from you and only helps if you do everything your supposed to be doing. Test are fairly hard but definitely passable. TA's are the worst part of the class.

Jamie is the best professor I've had so far, he knows how to explain things clearly and completely in a way which can keep anyone interested. The class is sort of a weed-out class, but everything in it is vital to know to continue in CS. Also the TAs were the worst I've ever seen, indifferent and incompetent. Don't let that discourage you, though

He's nice and his lectures are not boring (and he records them) but he also is not very familiar with the contents of CS3100. This was his first time teaching it so maybe he will do better next time, but be ready to put lots of your time towards studying outside of class if you want to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Kirby is a good lecturer -- nobody laughed at his dad jokes but I thought they were funny. The class was a bit too test heavy for me, but he and the other professor gave lots of opportunity for extra credit and student feedback. Content was a bit harder than it seems at first glance, so if you're taking cs2100 take it seriously.

This class was taught by him and another teacher. Professor Kirby is clear and concise and he explains things greatly. The other teacher on the other hand it was confusing.
