The class is set up so you do learning on your own and then come to class to review what you read and already learned. Hw is try/no try which was really nice.

I never went to class because attendance was a very small percentage of the final grade. Kirby was a good lecturer, made things clear to understand. Three midterms throughout the semester, allowed to have a notes sheet which is nice.
He is my adviser and he is the best teacher I have had in all my 24 years of education!
Very helpful professor who genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. He is very knowledgeable in the course material.

Enthusiastic, although he's a good rambler.  He really does a lot to help make sure students pass quizzes and tests.  Friedman is both a bad and good thing about his class, but for the most part is very helpful and goes over whatever you need help with in the discussions.
Mike is very enthusiastic and genuinely wants all of his students to succeed.

VERY hard class, good attempts made at explaining the material but theres so much of it in such a short time that its brain overload.  Tests every two weeks covering a lot of material with in depth questions.  Plan on a study session at least once a week.
I recommend this class if you're looking for a more laid-back option for your CW/upper division writing credit. Kim is funny, very kind, and always creates a safe classroom for queer students.

KIM is DA BEST! 
Even thought this is for a higher level writing credit we only wrote about 4 ish papers and it was very easy and fun to do! I really recommend her for any upper level writing credit!

This class was all over the place. We used the textbooks at the start then we didn't, we suddenly had a big project assigned with only 4-6 classes to work on it. It focused on white queers' experience cause that's most of the students. Kim is nice but just allows anyone to state their opinion even if it's unsupported, infactual, or not nuanced.

Kim is very kind and understanding. However the class lacked any structure, and they seemingly made it up as we went. I think they're a good professor, but their desire to make sure every student gets to speak makes some lectures kind of unbearable. I think the class will be really great in like 3 years, but I would not recommend taking it now.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An amazing and very caring human. They're very empathetic and understanding, and try to help you expand your horizons, even outside of class. 13/10, would recommend.

Dr. Kim is such a safe person, and her class reflects that, too. She always listened to anyone who wanted to share, but was also respectful of the people who just wanted to observe (me). You can really tell she is deeply involved in the well-being of her students, and going to her class felt like a reprieve from the rest of college.

Kim really feels like a breath of fresh air in higher education. Her goal is to teach, not to make her students prove themselves. She wants you to think and understand, not work yourself down. She is so understanding and the class is evocative. Easy A, entertaining, and enlightening. Can't hope for better really.

Kim is really awesome. All of our assignments were super engaging and fun. We did a project where she gave us like 10 options and we chose 2. We could do stuff like watching and analyzing a movie, creating a playlist of songs that relate to the class, decorating the transform office for halloween, and more. She's also really chill with late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing
Kim is wonderful. They are a really interesting lecturer. And the class is easy. If you show up and youve done the readings and discussion post you can easily do well in the class

Kim is a pretty great professor! She has a good clear grasp on historical LGBT+ concepts and always invites folks to speak their mind and ask questions. Her class was supported by a few TAs and aside from not really controlling the noise level/energy of the class, it was a good time. The lectures were a space for people to goof off really

Professor Hackford-Peer is awesome!!! I really enjoyed her GNDR 3100 Class that was suppose to be an in person course but due to COVID it ended up being online via zoom. The material we covered she provided, all assignments were explained, her class was engaging and fun. If you do the work, show up to class you'll pass. A lot of reading but great!

Kim was a super awesome professor. I was just in her class for a diversity credit, but I actually learned a lot of things that I was really happy to know. The class was ran by her and 3 TA's and it was always something new every day (in a good way). It was very organized (despite going online with covid). A very good professor!

Kim's class was very discussion based, and required a deeper level of critical thinking. There were readings due each class, but all were engaging and directly tied to and discussed in class. The class was not hard as long as you participated. Kim teaches from personal experience and genuine passion.

Kim is a great professor who encourages her students to think outside the box and be creative. She brings theory to life and although you do need to read lots of text, you engage with it in a practical way that is useful. She creates a fun classroom that allows conversation about controversial topics and where everyone can speak their mind!

The Gender Studies Major Advisor - she is great at leading productive discussions, runs really fun and productive classes, and has an open mind. She is a pretty tough grader and it's absolutely necessary that you go to class to pass though.

I considered the class very easy because of the clear expectations. Show up to class and you will be fine. He goes over main points of the reading in class and tests fairly. Any test that no one got a 100% he would add points to get one there, and any time there was a question many people got wrong, he would add points for that too.

I took class COMM3720, King is very, very rude, he does not care what you have to say and will call you out for no reason. Attendance is not mandatory but then he shames you for not showing up to class. He is not understanding at all and could not care more about your personal life if you are having issues that interfere with the class.

All classes were lectures except test days, very strict about phone use and talking while he is teaching, and will take points off. Does his best to explain everything, will throw in a joke once in a while. 3 exams, the first two are not cumulative, the last one had a lot of questions from the first two exams. Gives time for all homework in class.

comm 3720, great professor. First class I have felt where he wants people to learn and not overload with busy work. All "homework" is done in class hand written  3 exams which are significantly based on lectures which attendance is not mandatory. final exam is just a bunch of similar questions from previous exams. 10/10 class will take again.

Dr. King was an interesting professor. He is very straight up and clear with his expectations for class. His lectures are long but he gives a break half way. My biggest issue with this class was that some of the quiz questions were confusing and the answers were no where to be found. He does allow team work and open note on quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have at the university of Utah. He never explained the concepts he intended to teach and offered no help to us students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For a mathematics lecturer, Christian is incredibly good at explaining concepts. He is very dedicated to helping students succeed and encourages students to go to his office hours. He is a tough-grader because will not accept late-work under any circumstances. He has group quizzes and lets you use ample notecards for exams. Studying is a must!

Christian is really unforgiving and he is simply not adept enough as a professor to forgive how harsh his course is. More times than not he does not care to help the students that are struggling and there are next to no resources to catch up. He moves really quickly and exams are way too difficult.

Christian is very patient with students and is very helpful when it comes to answering questions or demonstrating specific problems. If you show up to class and ask questions when you are having trouble, you should have no problem with the class, and should find this teacher very helpful.

Prof. Knapp was super funny! She always made me laugh during lectures when appropriate. She is very passionate about anthropology and it helped me focus. There is a ton of reading in the class, so if its not your things, I would not take this class. This fulfilled my DV credit and was definitely helpful to understand different groups if your premed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgable, and the class is super easy, but so boring. Just lectures and outdated videos. For a subject that is so complex, there was no discussion or debate. She is not good at explaining things or making things interesting. She said attendance is mandatory, and took it every day, but hasn't made any grades for attendance?

If you agree with her very strong views and biases on politics you may like her. I did not agree with them which made when trying to speak up a very hostile enviroment even though she preaches accepting everyone no matter their view. I felt as if i said anything wrong i would fail the class.

Dr. Knapp is a great professor! She's very kind and loves to engage with students. I thought the exams were pretty easy. The final paper was a bit tough but she gave me an A so I can't really complain. Would take again!

Professor Knapp is my least favorite professor I have ever had. I was very excited for the course but a lot of it was repetitive and the lectures were boring. She has very strong opinions about the topic and doesn't like when people disagree with her. There are 3 quizzes, a 5 page midterm and a 10 page final. She does NOT answer emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Knapp is incredibly knowledgeable. Her lectures are always entertaining and informative. Grades are based on attendance, the midterm and final, and a few quizzes. The midterm and final are both pretty long take-home essays, but she's not a harsh grader. I've taken multiple classes from her and enjoyed them all!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes! Dr. Knapp isnt the best at navigating canvas and zoom, but in person classes are wonderful and inspiring. She is very kind but gives useful feedback

She is great and engaging, even though homework was pretty minimal (other than a midterm and a final that are easy to get interested in). Very nice and understanding, every day I was in her class I learned at least like 3 things. A super interesting and enjoyable class.
Was very unorganized. Have heard this professor is better at other classes. I found lectures boring and were so hard to attend

Sex & Gender was one of my favorite classes ever! Not only is the subject interesting but Leslie shows interest and knowledge of the subject. Quiz questions come from lectures so attend and take notes. There is a final research paper and you can pick your own topic, yay! Overall, the course is easy going if you do the work & Leslie is flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Leslie is a good and nice teacher and cares about her students. Rarely any homework. You just have to show up and take good notes so that you can pass the quizzes. The midterm is answering two questions in essay format but you're able to do it at home. The final is a research paper 10-12 pages and topics related to sex and gender of your choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was probably one of the most disorganized classes I have ever taken. The lectures and assignments don't correlate well. The Inquizitive assignments were probably some of the most tedious things I have ever done. Tests essentially require memorization of the smallest details taught. Her communication was sub-par and she was difficult to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Switched into this class a week into the semester on the day of an exam, and I was given no extension on the exam or any past due assignments. There's A LOT of videos and material in this class too so I was playing catch up from start to finish. Switching into this class after the semester has started? Don't. Before the semester? Be prepared.

Mrs. Knapp is a nicest lady. She really cares about the subject she's teaching. The ONLY complaint I have is her test. She gives amazing lectures and what to read in the book, but her test throws you for a loop. The tests aim is to trick you. But overall nice teacher, just really hard tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had a few problems with the course. One being that her TA grades all the work and his corrections are harsh. Two the midterm and final questions were vague. Third getting help on the research project was a no go. And lastly, the course did not meet its objectives that the university set.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: There was a lot of discussion which I liked plus there was lots of options for extra credit.

I really learned a lot from this class. I didn't have much interest in the subject until I completed this course. The tests were open book/note, & tests/lectures were available online. The online lectures were a bit hit and miss in terms of continuity, but its not anything reading a chapter or two of the textbook won't fix. I recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Leslie is a good teacher-from the few weeks she was actually there. Not sure if this is a regular occurrence, but at the beginning of the year she was sick so Alan Rogers did the first few weeks of class on the theory of evolution (he basically lectured his book). The book really isn't required for the course, tests are open book and online.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Solid professor, really knows his stuff, and is a great network connection in the field.  A bit of a scatterbrain and his inability to clearly define what he is looking for, can inhibit your ability to understand the task. Overall, tons of learning from his class, but tough papers, and he can be a harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Even though attendance isn't crucial for passing, It'd be ridiculous not to go. Ted is an excellent lecturer. Plus, he is single-handedly the greatest dad-joke teller of all time. Apart from the jokes, he serves as deputy director for Salt Lake's MPO which is a great resource to have as a planning student interested in the field. 100% recommended.

I like Ted a lot and Im taking another class from him. Very knowledgeable, always there to help. Sometimes his organization or expectations of assignments are a little crazy but he will always answer questions or adjust. He makes lots of great dad jokes.
Ted is an experienced planner that creates interesting dialogue during class.  He is more than fair when considering others, highly approachable and he makes class fun.

Tascha is amazing, although there is a lot of homework, there is a lot of extra credit i took gen chem 1 and 2 with her this year and i never regret it i got A in both just by attendance and doing all extra credit work with her you got a, lot of chance to get a better grade in chem also she appreciates it when you contact her for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor who made chemistry fun and easy to learn. The class is worth the ride out to Sandy. Even though she grades attendance and has a short quiz every class, they help you succeed in her class, and the quizzes are open notes and tend to be easy. She does a sign homework, which are sometimes long, but she offers extra credit on each one.

Tascha is awesome! I'm not one to send in ratings, but I had to for her. I failed gen chem when I took it on the main campus last year and was super discouraged, but Tascha made it finally make sense. She also cares a lot about her students and makes classes fun. I'm so glad I took chemistry from her.
A quiz EVERY CLASS. HOURS of homework a week. Was not worth driving to Sandy for her class. Save yourself

Perfect class with a very good professor. He adds notes to every assignment and is always willing to help you if you need it. Would definitely recommend.

I think Kris is great teacher! He break down the content very well for students to understand. Participation is matter and actually key to be great in his class. Kris is very charismatic and cares about accessing all of his students, even when the course is online. I really enjoyed how he teaches sociology. The lectures are interesting and I loved learning about research from him. I also struggle with the more mathematical side of sociology, but his class made it easily understandable.

Kris is a great professor to take any soc class from. The course consists of a group research project that is graded pretty strictly. Kris is definitely knowledgeable in the social aspect. I enjoyed the lectures regarding social inequality. The class consists of two exams (open note) and two group projects. It wasnt too hard but he does grade attendance so make sure to attend class!

Mr. Young explained the course material well and was dedicated to making sure that we all understood exactly what was expected and required. The class began easier than it ended. There was not a lot of work required in the beginning, but by the second half of the semester we were doing group work in class and more assignments out of class.

She gives a lot of work in a short amount of time and then is a tough grader. We have 6 hours a week and she spends a 3rd of class time either teaching obv but also doing group discussions, I wouldn't mind these in fact, i think they do help, but she gives too much homework/ projects that you have to come in on your own time to finish.

reviews.comment: She genuinely wants you to fail. This is not a joke. She will do everything she can to degrade your work as much as possible, no matter the effort you put in. She's the worst. She won't tell you why she degrades it either; she'll just hate everything you make.

changed due dates on canvas 3 times and pretended she had never changed it, asserted that it had always been the same and responded rudely when we asked about it. Constantly creates small inconveniences with assignment requirements. Assignments are generally boring/odd and do not contribute to the understanding or enjoyment of ceramics.

Shasta is an adjunct professor who does not deserve her job at this university. Condescending, rude, and uncaring. She made several students in class cry because of her comments and talked poorly about us to her TA in front of us. Genuinely don't understand why she's working here.

Too much time was taken up by outside discussion posts, research presentations, and lectures. I felt like we did not have enough work time in class, and I used a lot of my free time trying to catch up on most projects. She is a very hard grader. I've taken nonmajor art classes before and this one was unnecessarily hard.

Ms Krueger was a disrespectful, patronizing, and ineffective teacher. She was dismissive, passive-aggressive, condescending, and her expectations were confusing and unclear. Her method of grading were biased by her emotions and preferences. It didn't seem to matter how much time, effort, and sincerity you put into an assignment or project.

I took her for Art 1070 (despite what it says), which was a beginner class. I had a background with ceramics so I wouldn't say I learned a lot, but a lot of her advice was helpful. reviews.comment: Terrible class. Shasta was extremely rude and disrespectful to all her students and expected everyone to know basics when this WAS a basic class. Made students spend $$$ on cords to present on an ancient projector and wouldn't share her own technology and was extremely rude about it to people who couldnt afford to spend money on useless things.

This class was awful, I hated it. Shasta was extremely disrespectful and talked bad about students with the TA both infront and behind their back during class. This was a beginner class and she expected everyone to know what theyre doing and graded extremely harshly with no explanation. Dont ever expect an A. Worst class ever...AVOID AT ALL COSTS

I hated this class. She was extremely disrespectful when she talked to students. She was very rude when you asked a question and would not answer it. I sat near the front and she would talk crap about students with the TA everyday even though most of us could hear her. Extremely disrespectful and has made people cry. Do not take this class.

Shasta was extremely disrespectful to students both to their face and behind their back. I sat near the front, so I often overheard her saying bad things about students to her aid. Shasta is very unclear with instructions and does not provide technical training or lectures. Ask a question and she'll respond with a question. Uses the textbook a lot and has canvas assignments for them. She does not use class time well and most of us were left in the dark for 2 1/2 hours per class. Not compassionate to students at all.
Rude teacher and will not answer questions.
This professor will talk down to you and treat you like you don't know anything. She also is not willing to help you and is only ever condescending in her tone.

Shasta refuses to answer questions and talks down to students. She only gave one "lecture" over the course of the class, and the rest was us essentially teaching ourselves. Don't expect to get an A--she didn't give out a single "A" on any assignments me or my friends turned in, and we were always marked down randomly without clear explanation.

Shasta was a bad professor. Her grading criteria was so unclear, I never knew what she wanted. She was unwilling to provide any helpful feedback or suggestions, but dropped our scores when we turned in projects that didn't perfectly meet her unknown expectations. In fact, she didn't give out a single 100% on anyone's projects. Wouldn't recommend!

I have not met another student who has positive things to say about this professor, so I'm not sure who's writing the good reviews here. Very tough grader. Doesn't teach lectures or provide demonstrations or feedback in class. Unclear expectations and critiques. Eager to knock points off of your final grade no matter how hard you work.

Shasta's super cool, the book you need is design concepts, and u do need it. It's important to show up as there's a lot of in class participation. She does work with u when you need help. If u do a group project and your groupmates mess it up, then u do get docked some points. However, this was only a problem with the first assignment and thats it.
Most things happen in class so don't skip.If you listen and look at canvas you'll be fine.

Shasta is very helpful. Don't be afraid to ask her questions. She is laid back yet involved. We often got out of class early. She doesn't just hand out 100%'s though. Make sure you are following the rubric. Also participation in discussions is a big part of your overall grade.

She was a great teacher for the given class, although I didn't love the class itself (given time constraints and school provided curriculum). She was very helpful and motivating, ceramics definitely aren't my forte but she made it interesting.

Shasta is great! She had cool assignments that were actually enjoyable & gave you creative freedom. The only things I got docked points on was for group projects if someone else didn't hold their own. 
The few quizzes we had were short, easy & open book. If you miss class shell give you a way to make it up. We only met once a week which was awesome
Lots of reading. Exams are pretty hard and the TA isn't the most helpful

reviews.comment: Karen Kramer was a chill professor; her lectures were fine. It's not my favorite subject, so I wasn't very engaged. As long as you study for the tests they are super easy.
This class had a lot of reading due each week. Expect to read many chapters and articles. The exams are a bit difficult despite the fact that there is a exam review given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: interesting course but the lectures were not engaging, slides are meek, and the required reading load was hefty. the labs were the most simple, interesting part of the class. exam review didn't cover everything that was on the exam. final project was fun but she refuses to have us email it to her, instead requiring a USB ($ and inconvenient).
-midterm and final exams unreasonably hard given only classwork demanded was a weekly discussion post

Dr. Kramer is extremely smart and knowledgeable, she is very clearly an expert in what she's talking about. I would absolutely take a class from her again. Be prepared for a above average amount of reading, and for the study guides to not entirely cover the exam.

Not very engaging lectures, and my biggest issue was the exams. Only 2, but they were both 100 questions with only an hour and 20 mins. I felt rushed the whole time and overall there was so much going on in the test it was difficult to perform well. The in class labs were also kinda confusing for me, but they're doable. Wouldn't really recommend.

I took this course online, Karen has a grad student named Janet Baide instructing the class. They have pre-recorded lectures and 2 exams. The midterm was AWFUL it was 77 questions with 100 minutes. The entire time I felt rushed. The questions were SO confusing. Would never ever recommend this class it was awful and uninteresting. Awful class.

Dr. Kramer is great. Her lectures incorporate a lot of her own research, which is really interesting. There are lots of readings every week and she will ask questions about them in class. Grades are based on some labs, two tests, and a group project. The labs were all very fun! Attendance isn't required but you won't do well if you don't show up.

reviews.comment: Very dry classes. Not charismatic in the slightest which makes the class hard to engage with.

reviews.comment: Although it was an easier class, it was one if the least exciting I've taken. The material is very interesting but she shows no enthusiasm whatsoever, so the lectures are boring. reviews.comment: Professor Kramer was a really good lecturer. Questions and homework go through her TA (who was absolutely wonderful). There is a group project. Lots of reading. Very interesting content. I enjoyed her teaching style. She makes sure that the students are updated. Not that many assignments to be graded on so more pressure to do well but none of the assignments are too hard. The exams were hard to get an A. She is slow to respond to emails and canvas notifications.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are boring and difficult to sit through. The class material is interesting but the lectures just felt like they went on and on forever. Prof. Kramer is very intelligent but not an exceptional teacher. The tests aren't too hard if you pay attention to lectures and study.

Prof. Kramer is an extremely kind and great professor. The course is not super heavy, and homework is easy. If you follow the instructions, you receive full credit. She is especially understanding about tests, and if you have rationale for why you answered a certain way, but you were marked wrong, she'll reassess and often give the points back.

Karen is phenomenal instructor with a wealth of knowledge to share. Although the course was ridiculously reading and assignment heavy, it all made sense in the context of her lectures.I will certainly be going to her for more guidance and help in the future. PS. She does fieldwork with the Maya, which is really cool if you're into that!

A very interesting course given by an anthropology researcher, so she knows what she's talking about. There were 4 labs, mostly done in class, a midterm and a final. The lectures are helpful for the tests, just make sure to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: I really like Prof Kramer. She does have a reserved personality which some might find a little boring. Great class for understanding how to analyze and apply human foraging research. The class has several small assignments which are all to prep you for a final paper, in addition to the exams. Small class, lots of participation.
If you show up to class and actively take notes, you should easily pass this class. If you're not interested in this subject, I would not recommend it.
Class is very dull, and are hard to capture your attention. tests and assignments are alright, but her lectures are really boring and not that interesting.

This is the nutrition class that everyone needs. I took this course in 2024, and I still think about it all the time. Sabine is fantastic, and the class is genuinely low pressure with lots of great information! And cooking classes sometimes too!

I love Sabine! This class is lots of fun and she makes things easy to understand. She is very good at understanding and engaging her students. We also have fun food labs where we get to cook and eat. Highly recommend this class.

She was an amazing professor. Her lectures were very interesting to listen. Most nutrition classes I would zone out, but I actually wanted to listen to her talk. She is funny and so sweet. While we did have classes that had in-class participation points. Most classes that did stated it on canvas so you would know. Would take a class with her again

Does not explain any assignments, makes due dates super unclear. I would try to submit assignments but it would not accept submission, which would lead to me getting a failing grade. Super unhelpful teacher.

I had gotten out of the hospital and missed 2 weeks of schoolwork dropping my grade from an A to a F. I asked him if there is anything he can do and a WEEK LATER he responded saying he could dismiss one math assignment and one test out of 12 other assignments. If you want to meet Helen Keller take this class because you will not be heard or seen.

Does not care or provide help for students. Lacks communication through email. Not helpful, does not provide any lectures. Homework provided is mostly not even on the test. Does not listen to feedback at all even when asked to provide.

Gives out an absurd amount of homework and half of the homework isn't even useful for the tests and is just time consuming. Has everyone attended a zoom meeting where he does not attend or help out at all. Does not provide any lectures to help just has everyone do self learning.

Professor takes up to a week to respond to any email and does little to nothing to help understand he topics. There are no lectures and all of the course work is through ALEKS. Worst online course to ever be taken. Does not communicate with students about coursework and preparations.
From my experience if you don't want to teach yourself outdated work that isn't even up to date I would not recommend this class..
If you can't put up with the coursework I would not take this class it's expected you spend hours on quizzes, and assignments just to not know what's important on the exam.

Beware if you take this course and expect to get an easy A. He takes ages to grade your exams and give good feedback. Feedback lacks information needed to help you succeed for future homeworks, quizzes, and exams.
lazy professor provides no lectures nothing to follow from. You're expected to learn everything by yourself with no leads.

Course is insanely difficult online due to you learning absolutely nothing from his course. All his provided study preparations are all out of date.

In my experience none of the quizzes and homework assignments would ever match up with the exams.  I would understand everything on the quizzes, exam reviews, and homework and would up failing every exam.  Just don't bother taking online math and go in person if you feel like it won't work for you.

I HIGHLY recommend taking a class from Predrag. I struggle with math and he was so kind & caring with everything. Lots of opportunities to succeed,  and he clearly wants you to succeed. Hardest class I have ever taken. Lazy professor and unorganized TA's. His content is outdated. His tests were so ridiculously hard. I had a friend in another 1060 course on campus and her course was much more organized and had a better professor. I would not recommend.

He's a very nice professor and works with his students to make sure they are understanding the material and have every chance to succeed. this guy is horrible when it comes to online school, most disorganized and laziest of professors
He is overrated, hes hard to understand, makes you feel dumb if you ask a question and doesnt explain anything. Avoid him.

If you have an option DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! I took his math 1010 class online and he was awful with organization. He had different dates posted then when things were actually due. He clearly loves math. At times I got the feeling that he didn't quite grasp why we struggled with certain topics, this coupled with the dry lectures made it a frustrating course at times. He was always happy to answer questions but often his answers didn't seem any clearer.

Predrag was honestly great. Calc 2 is often said to be the most difficult of the math ladder, but he made it bearable. He's super approachable and easy to understand. reviews.comment: Super nice guy. As long as you show up to class and pay attention it's easy to do well. We hardly used the text book, but it was nice to have for review material. Homework was also light, which was nice.

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. He makes sure the students really understand the material and he always answers questions. The homework isn't too long or hard. The exams were a little bit tough but he let you use a sheet of notes on the test so that helped.

reviews.comment: Predja is a great guy, he cares a lot about making sure the class understands before moving on. He does make a lot of small arithmetic errors so pay attention and call him out if you notice something. Homework was relatively easy and tests are exactly what you would expect after doing the reviews.

So, the professor himself is a pretty great guy and he's really intelligent. However, I think he overestimates how much his students know about math sometimes and skips steps that need to be explained. I also feel like as a class we needed him to start slower with the basics instead of diving in. Get a tutor if you take this class and struggle.

reviews.comment: This course was taken in an online format. It was difficult to have communication with Predrag, as he took a considerable amount of time to reply. By the second week of class he was calling everyone by their name! He made sure that you got it, and even if only one person didn't he would go over it and explain it differently until you got it. He really is so nice and an awesome teacher. Very understanding and easy to work with.

Predrag's teaching skills are adequate.  It's important to show up for every class, take good notes, and  study for the exams. Just put in the work and you should be an easy course.

reviews.comment: Predgie is awesome! He got to know everyone's name and actually cared about our understanding of the material! His TA Katherin was the BOMB, seriously so helpful and approachable! I hadn't taken math in 5 years and I was super nervous for this class, but it ended up being great! Show up and do your work and you shouldn't have a problem passing!
Good professor, if you don't understand something he will try to explain it differently until you do. Available for questions all the time.

Predrag is an awesome guy but makes math so much more confusing. I learned more from the SI's in this class than I did him. Miss class say goodbye to 16 participation points that can't be made up. Homework is fairly easy if you pay attention.  If you are good at math then this class will be a breeze for you, if you aren't, I wouldn't recommend him.

Take notes! He's kind of confusing and tends to make things more complicate then it needs to be. If you know of a way to do math then do it your way. As long as the answer is right, he doesn't care how you do it. If you have questions don't be afraid to ask!

I have always struggled with math, but if you go to class and do the assignments, you will do well in Predrag's class. He is great at explaining concepts when you don't understand and really wants his students to do well. I would recommend him to anyone willing to go to class!

Never struggled with math before until this class. Teacher is really confusing and not very clear. If you have a great knowledge base of math than you will do fine but if you are looking to be taught something not the class for you. Professor likes things done his way or you won't get it right. Best Math Professor I've ever had! He wants you to succeed and will do all he can to make that happen. Explains very well and willing to take extra time to explain. Attend every class and study the exam guides and you'll do well! Highly Recommended.

Predrag is GREAT!  He is very good at explaining things and he wants everyone in the class to understand the math.  He assigns homework, but you don't turn it in toward your grade.  There's biweekly quizzes, which are pretty easy, three tests, and a group project.  The math is very useful for real-life situations, with an excellent professor.

She was fine, it was such a boring class, not her fault, but still. She was super messy, always grading at the last minute, and would forget to post assignments due the next day. Attendance isn't required, but says she will give extra credit pop quizzes if you show up and proceeded to only do one the entire semester.

Professor Rand was an amazing professor. I would strongly recommend attending SI sessions and lectures. There are weekly quizzes but no exams. The SI sessions give you questions you might see on the quiz and review material learned in class. There are two projects throughout the semester but are pretty easy and leniently graded.
Love her, her lectures were so interesting and easy to follow and she was very thorough on the topics she taught

Patient and understanding. I went to her office hours because I was completely lost on a big assignment and she took the time to walk me through each thing that I asked about. She's clearly passionate about her areas of expertise and it made the class fun to be in.

I really loved this class. The content was genuinely interesting for me. It was my favorite class this semester. That being said, the exams are broken into smaller ones and are about every two weeks. You need to make flash cards, the content is not subjective. You need to know names of very specific things and be able to describe them. SHOW UP.

Professor Rand is great! She is a kind person and gives good lectures. There were 6 tests, but they are less heavy on the material compared to taking 4 exams. She does drop one of them so only 5 count. You do have to put in the work to study for the material, but it is not hard. They do a review session before each one and it helps a lot.

Dr. Rand lectures in a way that is comprehensive and easy to understand. She is always open to helping students with content. The content itself is not too difficult as long as you attend lectures and read the textbook as a supplemental resource.

Dr. Rand is an awesome professor who is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. The class is not super difficult as long as you study and attend lectures. She wants you to succeed and provides the resources necessary to make this possible.

This class was challenging. We read several peer-reviewed articles and wrote two major papers that were APA style papers. However, Dr. Rand is the best. She's down to earth, interested in student success and overall just very informed and qualified to teach this course. If you work hard and stay on top of it you can do well in Dr. Rand's course.

reviews.comment: Also had her for cognitive psych. Overall she is great, both classes are fairly easy and she's good at answering questions if you need. Not too many tests or assignments, so I recommend her if you want to learn while not worrying too much about your grade in the process.

Dr. Rand is amazing! The material for this course was easy since it's a psych major requirement, but she's so kind & is always there to help her students. There were usually assignments every week, but they were super quick to complete. The tests weren't too hard, but going to class helps a ton. Definitely recommend Dr. Rand for this class!

I've had Dr. Rand for a few classes and I can honestly say she's one of my favorite professors. She genuinely cares about her students doing well and her lectures are interesting and engaging. The tests make up a big portion of your grade but as long as you fill out the study guide and watch the lectures you'll be fine.

Dr Rand cares about her students greatly and is a super helpful professor! Her lectures always included examples that allowed students to better understand the material. I highly recommend taking a class from Dr. Rand!
Honestly pretty easy class, and professor was very easy going. Gave my group a bad grade on a project and gave us some time to fix our mistakes - after which we all got As. Would recommend

Kristina Rand is a great professor, vey fast to respond to questions. The class is very lecture heavy, watch the lectures and fill out review questions as you watch them. Two exams (w study guides) and they are worth 72% of the grade. After each lecture is a short quiz, if you get 80%+ on them it equals extra points on each exam. Two papers too.

Watch all the lecture videos. You get study guides but there is a lot of information that you don't always know what to focus on. There are quizzes or short questions due every week, nothing crazy. The professor is easy to get a hold of through email/ canvas. I learned a lot but I would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst classes I have taken. I took online Sensation and Perception. You'll watch excruciating video lectures, write papers that aren't worth anything towards your grade, and take mini quizzes that give no expectation to the context of the Exams, which were worth 72% of your grade. Disappointed for sure.
The Instructor was fine. There are prerecorded lectures you watch each week that range from 30 minutes to an hour. Weekly quizzes and a group Project that you work on throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was intimated by research methods, but Dr. Rand is fantastic. She will not move on until everyone understands the concept she is teaching, and she does lots of example problems. Very accessible outside of class for questions, and does review sessions for each exam if you need extra help. I would not take this class from anyone else.

Tough class but not impossible. She does drop your lowest test score so if you tank one you can still get an A. Class is very test heavy and the tests are pretty difficult. She does give you a study guide before that is pretty similar to the exam. Make sure you listen to every lecture all the way through or it'll be super hard to pass.

Dr. Rand cares about the progress & success of students to a degree seldom cultivated in R1 Universities. Her class (Psy 4800) overlap with another class. Dr. Rand showed up a half-hour early every snowy morning that semester, for a single student, to ensure I didn't fall behind. Brilliant, knowledgeable, engaging, charming & dedicated. EZFavorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: For Psy 4800 Dr. Rand guides your development towards the research project, APA experimental report, required to obtain the human factors certificate. Each section of the paper (e.g.-abstract/intro/results etc.) is discussed clearly, informatively & empathically while in juxtaposition to a reasonable and smooth time-line. Best lectures of my U exp.

Dr. Rand is a fantastic professor! She is very caring and works to make sure that all questions are answered. Given that this was a research methods class, the lectures were a tad dry but she made them interesting with the supplemental lab work. She also had a great structure to the class where her grad TA's taught the lab portion.

Amazing teacher. She really cares that her students know what she expects from us. Learning materials are straight forward. Tests are straight forward. She wants you to succeed, she wont try to trick you on tests. Because of this, I learned so much in this class compared to science classes. Easy to talk to and ask questions. I highly reccomend

Dr. Rand is a very good teacher. I love the way she explains the material. She is very clear, fair and I love how she cares about you if you have questions. I would take all my PSY classes from her. It is not a difficult course, you just need to follow the lectures and take notes. Glad I took this course!
Excellent class! Her modules and outside resources made the material intersting and fun to learn. Her quizzes and tests were straight forward if you did the reading and studying ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was worried about this class because I don't have an anatomy background, but Kristina made everything easy to understand. She also makes the lectures interesting with humor. The tests were somewhat hard because there's so much information you have to remember, but doing the study guides really helped. She also allows extra credit, which is nice.

Kristina is AMAZING! I absolutely loved taking sensation and perception from her! The material can be challenging at times, but Kristina always had a fun metaphor to explain it and if we were all struggling with a concept she would take the extra time to ensure we understood! She is fun and helpful! Take a class from her!

I took this class on campus; Kristina is a fantastic teacher! She's well-spoken and very willing to help clarify any questions you may have. Her lectures are clear and her commentary is hilarious. Attendance wasn't mandatory but her powerpoint lectures are really hard to understand if you don't get her personal comments in class.

This professor is extremely nice, friendly, and enthusiastic about the material she teaches. She also shows you cool Ted Talks. Sensation and Perception will be a relatively easy class for you if you are detail-oriented like I am. I used to be a bio major, so the "draw pictures and explain" format of some of the test questions worked well for me.

She was super helpful! I went to her for some advice and she was immediately open to helping and offering guidance. Her homework's and labs were really awesome and I felt like I learned so much from her. She was great!

Dr. Kramer took over the last 1/3 of Physiology. There was an immediate improvement in organization and content clarity. Her lectures were interesting and the homework was very doable. Although the final exam was tough, It pertained to what I had studied to prepare for the exam. Kramer brings structure and support to the classroom environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Kramer teaches the latter 1/3 of the class, and is certainly much easier than Dr. Clark. Her homeworks are very applicable to the tests, and the lectures are very interesting and straightforward. MAny times you need to ask questions because she jumps over things, or read the book. The labs are a lot of work, so start early, but she's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kramer was amazing. I had her during a covid semester and she was very flexible and understanding of our situations. Her class was a lot of work, but I felt like she explained material very well! I appreciated that she recorded her lectures ahead of time so we could watch them when we had time. Highly recommend.
Dr Kramer walks the line between entertainer and educator. She is a bit intimidating at first but is actually quite approachable. I enjoyed my time in her class.

Dr Hawkes is a fantastic and deeply caring teacher who trusts that her students come prepared and ready to engage with material. Keeping up with the lectures, paper readings, and textbooks readings, as well as asking her or the TA for help is key to doing well on the exams, of which 3 make up the entire grade. Not a hard class, but a hard subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hawkes is inspirational and EVERYONE at the U should take her class. It will be hard. But if you care enough, and make that extra effort, you will learn a ton from the best to ever do it in BE.

The fact that this is a 3 credit hour class is a joke. This class took up the majority of my semester. Grading on the tests is hyper-specific, never listens to student feedback, and frankly she's very rude. She clearly knows her stuff, but that doesn't make someone a good professor. Don't take behavioral ecology if you don't need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: NOPE NOPE NOPE. I'm usually a straight A student, but this class was terrible. Her lectures are sometimes unintelligible and she looks for VERY specific criteria in essays. Went to her office hours for clarification and left more confused. NEVER gives a direct answer. Class rides on whether you did the readings. Don't take if you don't need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor! If you actually want to learn something instead of just getting a passing grade, and are willing to put in the work then TAKE HER CLASS! you will be richly rewarded for! Always available able to meet if there's a concept you don't understand. Very prestigious, brilliant, and kind. If you want an easy A, don't bother.

Her notes/comments of the weekly papers were not legible and did nothing to prepare you for the exam, as they started grading at 75% and gave or took points from there based on how much detail you went into the answer. If you can simplify your answer, don't! Great lecturer, but horrible at teaching.

Absolutely one of my favorite professors and  classes I have taken.  Do all the readings for this course! There are A LOT through the semester, but if you keep up and attend lecture you can succeed. Essay tests are difficult but doable. Don't take this class unless you're willing to put in the time and really want to learn.

I don't feel like she ever defined a single term.  Nothing straight forward about her teaching, always talks around what you need to know. Essay tests as others described but she won't say how she wants you to talk about the terms on her study guide. You could know them very well and get a poor score on a blue book essay. Don't take behave ecol!

Hands down smartest professor I ever had. Ask a straightforward question and you will get an answer more elaborate than what you get in a textbook. Her class changed my life, and gave me a headache :)

Supposedly this is the hardest class in the Anthro department, but I did not think it was too bad. The class is based around 3 exams and a weekly essay. Each exam is preceded by a study guide that contains about 30 terms 6 of which she will directly lift for the exam. Exam essay is take home and similar to the weekly essay. I liked Hawkes!

I took art 2201 btw. Beth was awesome and one of the best teachers I've had. Her class is very easy to pass if you just show up and do the work. She is very kind and doesn't talk down to you. She explains the assignments very well and gives good lectures. You are graded on your effort, not by how “good” something looks. Overall I loved this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Beth is amazing, I've taken a few classes from her now for my degree. She is so kind and is a fantastic resource if you need help with anything. You won't regret her class.
Beth is the best professor I've seen; she is so kind and patient. If you have not decided whether to take her class, do not hesitate; just register!

Beth was the best professor I have had at the U. She is kind, encouraging, passionate, and authentic. Taking her class re-sparked my love for learning. She shows great passion and knowledge about her work. She shows interest in every individual and she embodies everything a professor should be. If you have the chance, take a class from Beth!

Professor Krensky has easily been the most understanding and helpful professor I have had so far. She genuinely cares for the students and reaches out to you separately for class matters. She will help with any problems you might have regarding the class and is nothing short of amazing. Highly recommend taking Intro to Art Education with her.
Beth is so great. I really enjoyed her class. She makes it really easy to pass her class, and she's crystal clear about all the things you need to do to get a good grade. Her class is very fun.

Ultimately, I just do not see the upside for this class. Dr. Kurzhals will probably be seen once, therefore you are very much at the mercy of which TA you get. I had a good TA and a good lab group, so once I settled in I enjoyed the class. Still, it was just not worth it credit-wise.

Prof. Kurzhals does a poor job at organizing the TAs. The grading is wholly uncoordinated between various TAs and the rubric. Even after using office hours for about a 4-credit course worth of time, the lab reports lost points on the most minute errors. Expect grading time to be on par with international mail to/from the Middle East.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is impossible to get ahold of. I tried asking her about sport-related absences all semester after asking the TAs to text her multiple times to try and get her attention. I ended up just barely missing an A because she failed to communicate. Avoid at all costs.

Dr Kurzhals runs like 20 sections of lab a week, so you don't see her too often. But the class is decent. The TAs will fix your assignments for you and get you 100%. The labs aren't too bad and there's no penalties if your experiment doesn't work, unlike the chem labs.

This is a very standard intro lab course. There are weekly lab assignments which you have to do - a prelab and a notebook plus three lab reports. It is a little bit time consuming. But the class is an easy A if you just read the instructions. TAs will fix all your assignments for you in office hours too. Canvas has all the requirements listed out.

This class requires a decent amount of effort. Like a lot of labs, it does feel like more work than 1 credit should be. BUT the requirements are clearly laid out. The grading is following the rubric which is always given. Dr Kurzhals has every week on canvas. The TAs will fix your assignments for you too.

Not seeing the professor in class doesn't mean she's a bad professor - that's just how big college lab classes work. 

The class is easy if you are willing to put in a tiny bit of work and the TAs in office hours will check all your assignments for you. All the assignments have instructions and rubrics on canvas too.

Dr Kurzhal's lab is an easy A - just get the TAs to check your work before you submit it. The rubrics are always on canvas with all the instructions you need. 

TA corrected my entire assignment in office hours so I got 100% when I submitted it.

Average for the lab notebooks is ~18/20 and that's 90% or A- average for the class. Meaning half the class is getting an A. 

People complaining need to go and take a chemistry or other college lab and then they wouldn't complain. 

Literally read the instructions for the assignments and you'll get an A every time.

People who don't like Dr Kurzhals don't understand college lab classes. 

Everything you need for the class is on canvas. The TAs would check my work before I submitted it and then I always got an A. 

The labs are relatively easy. Some time on the lab reports is needed. But the TAs will literally check it for you.

Got graded by at least 3 different people including the professor. Each contradicting each others grading. Labs don't get graded for almost a whole month, how and I gonna learn from my mistakes for the next lab if I'm not gonna get the score back till I'm 4 labs in. Didn't get my mini report 1 grade back till the of day mini lab report 2 was due?!

Your group/TAs decides your experience. Kurzhals is fine, I only saw her twice, and the TA's teach and grade everything. My one gripe is that grading takes over a month to do, meaning you don't get feedback until you've already submitted the next 3 assignments, which irritated me to no end. Read instructions posted each week and you'll do fine.

"Professor" is a generous term for someone who essentially serves as a glorified boss to the TAs who teach the course. I saw her 3 times all semester, and she focused on the TAs on these occasions. However, she makes her presence felt through her harsh grading of lab notebooks, for which the guidelines are unbelievably unclear and inconsistent.

This course was mainly tought by TA's, but instructions and expectations are outlined well. Dr. Kurzhals was in lab occasionally and offered really helpful feedback, especially on lab reports. People complaining about her never being just wanted a reason to complain. Her not being there shouldn't impact your grade.

Anyone complaining about Dr Kurzhals not being in class doesn't understand how college teaching labs work. She can't be in your class every day because there are 4 sections running simultaneously. 

If you read the instructions, you'll do well. TAs are great and if you get them to check your work either in lab or office hours you get an A.
This professor was great, she was very understanding when it comes to tough circumstances as long as your reaching out before due dates.

When I emailed Dr. K with a question, she wasn't helpful at all. Her response was rude, and in class she complained in front of students how annoying it was to respond to all of the emails she had received. She was rarely in class but when she was, she was overly stern and derogatory.

Dr Kurzhals' lab was the best one I've taken at the U. The grading is exactly what it says on Canvas. Anyone who does badly isn't reading Canvas or checking with TAs. 

Her TAs love her and that says a lot about the kind of person she is. Well respected.

Dr. K was rarely in class, gave only destructive criticism, and made the lab stressful. She complained about students to the TAs in front of us, and her instructions were unclear. Grading was harsh and inconsistent with the average for a lab notebook being 17/20. The only good part of lab was my lab partners and TA. If I could give her a 0 I would.

You don't really see Dr. Kurzhals. She came in like 4 times the entire semester. She was nice and helpful when she came in but everything is taught by her TAs. It was a pretty easy class The graders are picky about the tiniest things like grammar. This class could also go by a lot faster if it didn't take so long to get the actual lab started

This class is an easy A. There are drops if you want to skip or use them to improve your grade. The assignments can take a little bit of effort but as long as you read the instructions, you will get 100%. They have office hours to help as well and tonnes of TAs.

People who complain about the class are not reading the Canvas page to know what to put in their lab reports. If you read canvas and just do what it says, you get 100%. 

Also there are a bunch of drops in the class for low scores. 

The TAs mostly run the labs with multiple labs running at once. Dr Kurzhals oversees them and will pop in.

They are never in class, and every time they are, they are usually only there for 5 minutes and is always passive-aggressive and rude. She doesn't actually grade anything, the TAs are in charge of everything. Instructions for assignments are always unclear, and no matter who you ask, whatever advice they give you always ends up being wrong.

Never in lab and dont even bother to contact her because the answer is no. Her lab TAs are a hit or miss, I had chill ones for our in class but my lab paper graders were on an ego trip behind their little screen. Had to work for that A ngl and some of the lab work is rot but the project is somewhat interesting. Recommend a fun and rich soil sample

Dr. Kurzhals showed up once during the first class and claimed to be too busy to come by more often. The teaching TA I had was amazing, and I would rate her a 5 if I could. My grading TA was awful, however, and would take off at least 1 point every time for no reason. Forgot to italicize a single letter? -1. Put in the due date wrong? -2. Awful.

I think I'm gonna repeat what everyone else has said, but I mean to mention it too. Dr. Kurzhals is hardly ever in the lab, and whenever she is, she is mean and passive aggressive. 

Another thing is that the class has the most vague instructions for what to actually to do, and yet they grade so strictly. 

It sucks that this class is mandatory :/

Dr. Kurzhals is hardly ever in lab so this is more about the class, not her. Lab TAs are great but the assignments are tedious. You are provided vague grading criteria for notebooks and graded strictly. If you have previous bio lab experience expect to be bored and a little frustrated. Upper level biology labs are more enjoyable than this one.
This class is hit or miss depending what TA's you get. You only see Dr. K a couple times a semester. The TA's are the ones grading everything and running the whole thing

This class is not taught by the professor herself. I only saw her once or twice. My TAs were amazing and carried the class quite well, but other sections may not be so lucky. My biggest gripe with this class was that the TAs were not the graders, making it confusing on how points were awarded for our assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally saw her twice, even though she said she would pop in to every lab section every week. Everything is graded by TAs, and lab is run by a TA (mine was great). The pre-lab quizzes had ambiguous questions that were occasionally hard to understand and even harder to find the answers to in the textbook.

Dr. K barely showed up to any of our labs, it was ran by TA's, and when she did show up she was condescending and passive aggressive whenever we asked her a geniune question.  Also, your TA's don't grade your assignments so the grading criteria is not clear at all. Still possible to get an A so don't worry too much.

Professor was never there, she flat out said that she wouldn't show up to our labs cause it was "late" and she wanted to go home at 4:30. If you have a good TA then the lab is great but the graders are not your TA so there is no constancy with what you are told and how it is graded. They can be nice or very strict and often don't follow the rubric.

I enjoyed this class, but only because I had a good lab group and a great TA (shoutout Hetvi). Dr. K barely showed up, and when she did, it was neutral because she always had good input, but I only saw her 3 times. If you show up and do the work, you'll have no issues. Make sure you submit assignments correctly; she will NOT let you make them up.

This class was so much fun. Although the class is solely run on TA's, so you are LEARNING just from other college students that may only know as much info as you do. Since August, I have met Dr.Kurzhals maybe twice, and she was nice on giving feedback, but she is never there. Graders are harsh.

You never see her and never know who is grading your assignments. The grading is a variable unknown to Earth. Nobody even knows what the expectation is. Each TA states different things about what needs to be included. RIP all freshmen who take this.

Dr. K is an amazing professor. She runs all of the 1615 labs & has a lot of students. If you want to meet with her individually she is easily accessible. I feel that people that don't like her, don't understand how labs are run. If you read Canvas, the syllabus, and the rubrics it's not hard to get an A in the class. My FAVORITE bio professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly saw her probably twice the whole semester. She doesn't even teach it's just the TAs doing her work and they don't know what they are doing. The Tas are as clueless as you are and the TA graders are either too harsh or mark you down for stuff they claim isn't there but it obviously is.

The class structure is so convoluted. Dr. K manages all the lab sections (600+ students across all of them) and has final say on grades, but she has only showed up once for ab 5 min. The labs are taught by TAs, who are undergrad students who Dr. K selects. There is a separate person who grades assignments HARSHLY. Dr. K is unreachable via email.

extremely rude for no reason, know-it-all. ask her for a regrade because of her horribly worded weekly quizzes with trick questions, don't expect any sympathy or assistance. unfortunate that she is the only 1615 lab instructor, I would have chosen just about anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is really not a good professor, have to drop the class. Unfortunately, she is the only teacher for Biol 1615 right now
Dr. Kurzals is an amazing professor, and she truly cares about the success of her students. The course is difficult, but you will get an A if you apply yourself and attend class.

Class was mostly run by TAs but my TAs were really excellent and they seemed to like the professor as well. This lab is chill, well directed, and graded really easily (I got 100% on most of my submissions).
She is the "Best" bio professor I ever have, she will "Enjoy" having you over, sign up for her class
It is ridiculous, I have no clue about how the class is structured but your grade of this class is up to two helpless TAs hands and this is the worst class I have ever taken at the U.
Bad communication, grading is arbitrary, and worst of all the policies of the course changes throughout the semester up to this professor's discretion

I've never made a complaint about a class in my life. However, this class is dreadful. There is no structure with grading. My grading TA was AWFUL. I am a 4.0 student, and this is the hardest class I have ever taken. You are not graded by the rubric or the quality of your work. I was graded based on whatever the TA felt like, no structure at all.

Dr. Kurzhals is very knowledgeable and is definitely one of those professors you need to get to know on a personal level to understand. Shows up to class every other week but picks really good TAs. Lab is pretty straight forwards but the grading TAs for the lab reports are brutal, so definitely seek advice from your TAs for the lab reports.

Rebecca is very condescending person. Just look at her policy quoted "If you do not have appropriate footwear and your legs completely covered you will be sent home to change and you will lose points for the days". She changed her policy on syllabus arbitrarily based on how she feels during the semester. Good luck taking the class
Rebeccah Kurzhals, one of the worst bio teachers I ever have. Oh, actually, she is the worst.

Rebeccah is not a nice teacher, not even a nice person. She doesn't give a damn about the class, but assigned most of the works to TAs. She can comfortably tolerates her TA swearing in the class environment. Disgusting!

Rebeccah only looks nice on the surface. If you know her deeper, she is very indifferent to people and arrogant. She doesn't care about who you are. She can't handle a little problem that raised in the class. She blamed people before she even understood the problems. ugh, what a hideous personality!

This lab is mostly lead by the TA's she chooses but she drops into lab and gives good feedback and give good guidance on what to do and what would help with what was going wrong and help clear any confusion we had.

The class is run by TAs who are amazing and helpful. Professor pops her head in every once in a while and likes to see how everything is going. Make sure to submit work on time and always communicate with your TAs if any issues. I loved this class and the experience I had.

Dr. Kurzhals was a nice lady. The class is run by TAs, but she would occasionally pop in and talk Biology with you if you showed interest. She assigned more work than she and her TAs could handle grading in reasonable time, but honestly, that isn't that bad in the long run. Easy class if you try. You've got this! :)

The TAs mostly run the class but mine were very knowledgeable and helpful. You slowly work on your final lab paper all semester, so you don't have to do it all at the end. For grading, if you got a bad score and talked to them, they would offer opportunities to redo it for more credit. Kurzhals would sometimes come to class and give us feedback.

Most of this class is run by the ta's. Sometimes the grading is a bit too opinionated in comparison to the rubric provided. Overall, it's a fun class that you get to work with lab partners that often become friends. The TA's are super friendly and helpful as well. The professor often comes in to supervise and give advice/feedback to your experiment

Horrible professor, she lets the TA do everything and they are extremely inconsistent graders. My team would submit the same report individually and get different grades for each person. She would use the excuse "i cant discuss other students grades" and not help. Class is not organized, provides no instruction on how assignments are graded.

I didn't actually see this professor very often throughout the semester, but when I did, she was very excited and willing to help me interpret the results and formulate the next steps. The only people you could count on seeing every week were the TAs, who seemed half the time like they didn't actually know what was going on. They also graded weird.

Dr. Kurzhals was fantastic. But she doesn't grade any of your assignments, so the fate of your grade lies in the hands of 2 clueless TAs. They gave vague instructions but graded harshly. I thought this was an easy A class and wow I was wrong.

She'll take off 50% for stupid submission errors, literally ridiculous and cost my entire grade. I understand taking off a couple points for a submission error, but taking off 50% when I got 100% on the assignment is bs.

So here's the thing, I've seen her a couple of times because the class is taught by two TAs, but every time she came by she seemed really enthusiastic. Since she jumps between lab 1615 & 1625, you wont see her often, but she will answer questions or gladly look and marvel at your results with you. The class is very fun and exciting too.

This lab was a huge waste of time. The class is taught by the TA, I saw the prof maybe 3x all semester and she was condescending and vague if you asked her questions. For the weekly labs, you're told what it is, but you have to figure out how to do it on your own. There are weekly quizzes, but minimal resources to help with it aside from Google.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took a chemistry class from Dr. Kuntz her first year as a professor at the U, and she really changed my whole perspective in chemistry. The classes and labs are hard, because it is still a difficult subject. But she will help you as long as you need and will demonstrate concepts in different ways until you get it. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!

I took chem lab over the summer and was not impressed. We did half of the labs online, and half in person. I didn't even meet the teacher and just interacted with the TA, so I have no idea if I would take her again. I just really didn't like the format of half online and half irl. There were completely different criteria for the different formats.

Professor Kaci, is a very entertaining professor. You can tell she is genuinely interested in teaching and what she is teaching. I did find the frequent quizzes that are weighed heavy to be a bit frustrating. But overall found the class not too difficult and I am not a fan or am good at chemistry.

Dr. Kuntz is still the best Professor I've ever had.   I went to all of her office hours and most of the time I was the only one there, so it was just 1 on 1 tutoring. She is extremely smart and is truly passionate about help her students learn and giving them the best experience.

Honestly, after seeing the rate my professors for Kaci, I thought it would be a good Chemistry experience. My experience was the opposite, the lack of homework made it hard to practice for exams. Office hours were not very helpful and the exam keys tended to have a lot of errors. The way she taught in lecture also did not make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best chem teacher. Makes it super easy to understand and takes time to go over student questions. Take her class no matter what. If it's a 7:30 discussion time, it's still worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The TA makes or breaks the class. Switch to another section asap if you don't like your TA. The lab report grading was sometimes overly picky and unclear, especially because they limit your response to 1-3 sentences. Ask for help with your lab reports if you're confused and a TA will walk you through it

Dr. Kuntz teaches chemistry very well and works with massive class sizes to make sure students learn the material. She buffers the final grade with your attendance score but does not doc for not attending.

For a class mainly taken by freshman students, or at least students newer to chemistry this is a tough lab. Though the class can be self explanatory it can be tough especially the work load. If you struggle with time management maybe take less credits since for a one credit class it requires a lot of time outside of class, especially if you work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is run by TAs but out of all the times I've interacted with her, they've been nice. While grading on the labs can be quite harsh, help is easily available in the chem lab study room. If you have even the smallest amount of prior knowledge in chem, you'll be fine.

For Chem Lab 1,Prof. Kuntz was not ideal. The class was run mainly by TAs but the few interactions that I had with her checking in on my class were terrible. She was always pointing out something wrong in a very condescending way and did not offer help. The grading was also horrendously inconsistent, receiving zeros on questions I clearly answered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the chem labs are fun and enjoyable, but difficult. the reports are difficult and getting in touch with the professor herself was a nightmare. the TAs are awesome though. if you read all of the reports and make sure you understand the rubrics you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Kuntz runs her lab through the TAs who can be inconsistent at times with grading and not entirely on the same page. However, if you show up to all of the labs and submit what the teaching team is looking for on lab reports you can get an A fairly easily. Two labs drop, so if you miss some or do poorly there is some buffer.

While I'm sure prof. Kuntz is a competent and excellent teacher, she is difficult to reach and has extremely harsh grading policies, where you can recieve a failing grade for issues with formatting that were not communicated clearly in the first place. The course is not set up for student success, and Prof. Kuntz has a very hands-off approach.

Impossible to reach outside of class. Unclear directions, poor grading. Never even actually saw her in lab. Lab often didn't feel totally applicable to what we were learning in lecture. TA was great. You can pass this class, but so much about it is annoying.

She's super sweet and will work with you. Do the work and you'll get a good grade. DON'T give your excel charts to your partner! (I did this and had to go talk to her, save yourself the trouble and don't share anything with your partner on the post-labs).

Dr Kuntz wants you to succeed. This is very apparent in the way she sets her courses up. I have taken 3 classes with her now and loved every one. 
Explains things clearly and provides extra resources for you to use if you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grades paper with Ai and it doesn't even work.
She is the best gen-chem professor. Very effective at teaching! The U has the best chem department.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I only had Dr. Kaci Kuntz as the Instructor for my lab. We were required to handwrite everything for each lab, including several pages of instructions (this often took over 30 min). Do not bother trying to print it, they won't even let you do the lab. They say it's to make sure you read the safety and procedures, but why not do a test?
I would die for Dr. Kaci Kuntz.
shes so sweet

Kaci is a great professor. She knows her stuff and gives you every opportunity to succeed in her class. There were times that lectures were a little fast/confusing, the exam reviews also didn't seem very consistent with the actual exams at times, but she gives you chances for extra credit and assignment drops, etc.
