The prof is ok, but hard to reach (including on canvas). The course content isn't difficult, but your grade is based on how much your TA likes you. Most TAs are awful. They all grade differently and often disagree with the professor. My TA said that my class was stupid and that she hated us to one of the students. The professor didn't help us/care.

Super solid prof. She would sometimes spend too much time on practice problems in class. Her grading scale seem super confusing at first, but it is actually super nice and makes your tests weighted very low as long as you attend consistently. Super nice lady!

My lab reports were graded at least 3 weeks after submitting every single time. I was also expected to take the finals which is recreating previous labs with no directions without ever receiving feedback/grades on 4 of my labs. Grading is also very subjective-totally depends on who your TA is.

I also had her for 1220 and I do not like the way she teaches. It is so slow and she only goes over the easy stuff and then the test has super weird confusing questions. She tries to dumb down the material to make it easier but that just makes it more confusing especially since I took AP chem. Attendance is kind of mandatory it's weird.

Dr. Kuntz is great however the TAs that run lab aren't. Lab reports were always graded weeks to months late. Had to turn in labs for 7 weeks with only one lab having been graded with feedback. Lab content was weeks before lecture content. We were forced to figure out labs we hadn't learned to do yet. Went into the final with 4/9 reports ungraded.

She's good for the lecture but lab is horrible. It's run by the TAs but you CANNOT do well in this class without going to office hours and getting EXACTLY what to say in your report out of the TA. They expect you to have a phd in chemistry before taking this class. It needs to be worth at least 2 credits.

Best professor ever! As long as you attend lectures and discussions that is already 60%+  of your grade. Study for exams but even if you dont do amazing on them you can still easily get an A. She gives out extra credit for quizzes as well so dont worry too much about those.
I absolutely love professor kuntz. She is great

For the lecture, Kuntz is amazing but labs are run by TAs which makes it difficult. It took a lot of time for reports and the lab final is performing a lab final by yourself (lab decided by the number you pull). It took a lot of time but I think that it could've been worse. Pre-lab quizzes, attendance, and lab reports make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kuntz was one of the best professors I've taken here at the U. She has clear lectures and takes the time to go over more difficult topics. There are weekly quizzes similar to the discussion worksheets and the homework. If you attend the lectures, do the assignments, and review the material, you'll most likely finish the class with an A.

Overall very easy Gen Chem I class. She weighs out exams and assignments in a way that makes this course easy to get an A or a B in and offers a lot of extra credit to make up for missed quiz and homework points. I'm taking her for Gen Chem II next semester. Highly recommend.

Best lab professor. Very passionate about chemistry and teaching, and very helpful for students when they need it. W professor, we love her, we miss her class. Has the best TA's and a very snazzy lab coat

For CHEM1220: Very good lecturer, always covered material needed to be known on tests to a tee. Would never be convoluted helpful at office hours, generally was an understanding person, online lecture recordings were available. Tests were not too hard great prof.
Kaci is amazing. She has great energy and understands how difficult being a student is. She is down to earth and always has a great chemistry joke to make you laugh.

Professor Kuntz is a very nice and funny person. Her teaching style didn't work super great for me personally. I still did well in her class, but I sometimes got frustrated from her disorganization and somewhat unclear explanations of topics. She tends to oversimplify things, which I personally thought made topics harder to understand at times.

She was chill I guess, I'd sometimes be like, "nah can you check this answer though", and she'd be like "yeah" and be like "that's right" and it's not right lmfao. But, like, it's whatever I guess 'cause, like, we get extra credit I guess :/

Kaci is the worst at responding to emails. I'm still waiting on a response to an email I sent over a month ago.. I've had to go through several TA's to even get her attention and she is still not accessible. She is a fine professor if you never need any outside questions answered, because she will never respond to you.

Professor Kuntz is alright but their lectures can be pretty dense, making the class difficult. If you don't need to take chemistry, I honestly wouldn't recommend taking it. The tests and quizzes are really important and make up your entire grade. Be prepared to study.

Kaci Kuntz is an angel sent from above. I went into her class thinking I hated chem, but turns out its not that bad! Her lectures are easy to understand and she does a really good job at explaining complicated topics. If you go to class, do the homework, and put in a few extra hours to study for exams it is easy to be successful. I love Kaci Kuntz!

Kaci is a great professor! Her passionate for chemistry is shown in ever class she teaches, from her daily jokes, little demos, and overall enthusiasm. I never really liked chemistry, but the class was fine.

Kaci is the best. If you come to class, read the book and study STUDY, you'll do great. I was nervous going into college-level chemistry after not having done it since high school but she makes it so beyond easy. People who left bad reviews are just complaining about their grades because they didn't put enough effort in like they should have.

You will not regret taking chemistry from Professor Kuntz! She is AMAZING!!! She teaches with passion and enthusiasum. She makes sure everyone understands the material and provides lots of opportunities to succseed. I chanaged my schedule to make sure I had her for chem 2! She is the BEST!!

Dr Kuntz is amazing. She explains things clearly and obviously cares about you as a student. 
Loved the way her lectures were presented.
Get ready to hate your life.

The worst lab at the U? Yes, quite possibly. Get ready to spend hours upon hours a week for this lab. Seriously, how is my 1 credit gen chem lab so much harder than my 4 credit gen chem class? Grading is an absolute joke. No criteria at all, it is tedious and stressful. I have never complained about a class until this lab. DO NOT TAKE!

Dr Kuntz is by far the best professor of my college career. She cares about students and is genuinely invested in their success. 

Her course is very well structured and sets you up for future chem courses well. You will be able to succeed by simply following the guidelines and using the lab TAs.

Professor Kuntz definitely is a super sweet and funny professor, but the exam that she gives out expect you to know very indepth of the material, I took gen chem I with Swanson that's sharing the class with her and I feel like the exam in gen chem I was more fair, but her lecture is more enjoyable.

Professor Kuntz was a good professor. It felt like a massive waste of time and I am not sure I learned much throughout the semester. The labs were not hard but they were hard to follow along with sometimes. There was quite a lot to keep track of for a one-credit class. Some of the stockroom staff were not the most approachable or kind.
Always pick Professor Kuntz's classes if you can. Very well set up for labs. For lectures, she is super good at explaining concepts, and really cares about students.

Dr. Kuntz is an amazing professor, she keeps class fairly entertaining and made chem feel way less overwhelming. Overall the test and class are challenging but not more than expected for a college Chemistry course. Weekly homework and quizzes, and participation help your grade for sure. I would definitely recommend taking 1210 from her.

Kaci was fantastic. Her lectures were always fun, even if she had to sprinkle in a couple of terrible jokes. Regardless, she has a great personality for teaching, and her passion for chemistry is obvious.

Meh. Had a lot of things on the lab report rubrics that weren't clear that we actually needed to include in answers. Quizzes were WAY harder than they needed to be, and 90% of the time the lecture and lab didn't line up at all - which means you're trying to teach yourself an entire concept based on a 4 page introduction and 5 minute video. Not good

This course is set up really well and Professor Kuntz is amazing. 

If you do the lab reports before they are due and ask the TAs for any help, you can easily get an A. 

Lots of things are done to support your grade and are in your favor.

10/10; if you can take her, you should.  She explains everything perfectly and knows how to teach complex topics.  If you have to take this class, take it with her.  You will not regret it.  She made gen chem 1 seem easy, and I was scared for this class.

Dr Kuntz is amazing. She goes above and beyond. She is well respected and is very knowledgeable. She is on your side. 

Class is super well structured. The Canvas is well set up and easy to navigate. Requirements are super clear.
Very easy to follow lectures. Slides are posted before and after class. Explains things super clearly. Very easy to understand what will be in the exams. Highly recommend for Gen Chem 1.

If you're taking her for the lab, you likely won't see much of her - the TAs run the lab. With my few experiences with her, she was nice and energetic. However, sometimes her grading rubrics were really specific with what your answers should include, so it may be worth asking a TA to look over lab reports to see if you could add more details.

She is gr8 at making things less confusing when she can + giving students the chance to ask questions. She also makes sure to teach concepts in multiple ways so that everyone who might have a different preferred learning strategy can understand the material. She is also very nice and understanding, loves to interact w/ students, and adds jokes.

Dr. Kuntz clearly loves to teach and genuinely cares about her students. She takes feedback and admits when she is wrong or if she doesn't know something. She's respectful, kind, and entertaining to listen to.

Dr Kuntz is an extremely knowledgeable, empathetic, caring, and fair professor. She is so helpful during her office hours and will stay half an hour after class to talk with students. She is energetic during lectures, shows demonstrations often, and makes chemistry less intimidating. She does not treat this as a "weed-out" course.

Professor Kuntz is lovely. She makes the concepts very easy to understand and gives you lots and lots of practice to make sure you get it. There are also lots of homework assignments and weekly quizzes, but they're super easy points that will buffer your grade. Overall a fun and easy class!

Absolutely amazing. Lectures were engaging and helpful. It was clear what was expected on the homework, quizzes an exams (would tell you what is needed to be studied for exams). Was always willing to answer questions during and after class. Definitely recommend her.
CHEM1210 (Gen Chem 1) with Dr Kuntz is great. Her lectures are great, she has the slides available before/after class for you. She explains things well and is engaging.

Professor Kuntz is one of the best Professors I have had at the U! She is very caring and is always there to help. During the labs she would often walk around and help however she could. Outside of the classroom she was very quick to respond and always there to help whenever she could. Overall I would highly recommend taking one of her courses!

Professor Kuntz is great friends with her students and tries to have lots of discussions. If you don't attend the lectures though, you won't pass the class. Tests are on the harder side but doable. Her teaching style worked really well for me, but expect to put a lot of work into the class if you want an A.

Prof. Kuntz is very kind and looks for opportunities to help her students. In her lab class, one doesn't have much direct contact with her as she has 500+ students and many TAs actually running each lab. However, she is extremely organized and keeps the course work always up to date. She helps students succeed in and out of class.

Professor Kuntz is very kind and you can clearly tell that she cares about her students. I went to her office hours for help often and I recommend doing the same if you take her class. Chem lab can be challenging but you have help available so it will be a breeze if you go to her.

Passionate about what she teaches, and lectures in an effective manner. Taught us lots of helpful shortcuts to remember things & was big on demos, which made classes fun. I always felt prepped for quizzes and exams because she would give us lots of prep material. A lot of HW and study, but you feel like you've earned the grade you get.

Prof Kaci lectures are great, she explains everything clearly and twice over so you you can really understand. She also does practice problems in class and explains how she would solve the problem. Very great overall :)

She is very passionate about chemistry and making it exciting to students. Her lectures are often overly general so be sure to supplement with the textbook for exams, but her office hours are very insightful. Most of the grades are determined by homework and participation which is fairly easy to get a good grade in. Overall, I recommend!

She gave a lot of homework and participation was mandatory but dropped the lowest three. Grading was clear for all homework and exams. If you study the material and homework you will do well on exams. But lectures tended to get confusing at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was amazing! I very much loved her class. The little jokes at the beginning of every lecture were lovely. I would def take her class again.
Nice teacher, very enthusiastic!

Lab was not too bad although it was a long class time it never went the full three hours. Even though some labs are dropped, you should still go to most because the final consists of a self directed experiment with a first come first serve. So you should have basic knowledge on most. It was fun to try different experiments!

She really cares about her students and does a great job delivering the lecture material in an interesting way. she makes the class enjoyable and is very vibrant with her lectures and makes it engaging. If you put in the work and time to study for the exams, you will do great. There are a lot of points from participation and homework.
Great at teaching!
Cool
Amazing teacher

Pros: Very caring professor and hilarious. Accessible + sincere. Gives practice tests before midterms + final. Homework focused.

Cons: Sometimes can become a bit lost and little wayward at times during lectures, but his sincerity outside the class + easy exams overcomes this challenge.

Overall excellent, would take him again in a heartbeat.

Professor Kuntz's research aligns closely with the content of this course. It is clear from his lectures that he cares very much about this subject and teaching people about it. Most importantly, he provides exceptional intuition for a topic that can be rather difficult to wrap the head around. I strongly recommend anyone to take a course from him.
Man i did not have a class with him but i wish i would have taken him instead of TUCKER HERMANS

This professor is my favorite professor of my college career so far. It's evident how passionate he is about teaching the material, and his sense of humor resonated well with my class. He also is great at taking feedback and implementing it into his lectures. I would take every class from him if that was possible.

He is extremely caring/funny! He ensures you learn everything, and his lectures closely follow UC Berkeley's course. Exams were very reasonable and had a non-cumulative final. Assignments were extremely interesting and satisfying to complete. He da GOAT.

Prof. Kuntz is a fantastic lecturer. AI is an interesting subject already, and his demeanor and teaching style just make it all the more fun to be in his classroom. There are some reasonably tricky concepts that get taught in AI, but I never felt like anything was being glossed over or brushed past. I'd take another class from him in a heartbeat.

Professor Kuntz is easily the best professor I have had at the U. His lectures are very enjoyable to attend. CS4300 has some pretty tough concepts to grasp, but he breaks them down and explains them in very helpful ways. He is very flexible, funny, and he knows a lot about the content he is teaching, which is always a great thing. Highly recommend!

Pros:
-funniest professor I've ever had
-wombo combo of outstanding lectures, HWs, and projects to help learn concepts well
-great class organization
-most question-friendly class environment I've ever seen
-super clear grading criteria

Cons: 
-Perhaps overly thorough. We got behind on the class schedule and missed some fun subjects (HMMs, NNs)

Extremely high quality lectures; Alan will make sure you understand everything. Alan is clearly passionate on what he's teaching, and he's funny! Only complaint I have is the spacing on assignments/projects. He would assign homework that overlapped with the projects, even though we had so many weeks with nothing due.

Good class even better professor! The lecture content can be difficult to understand at times, but rest assured, professor Kuntz will make sure you understand it in order to do well on the assignments and exams. The hardest part of the class was for sure the programming assignments, especially the first 2, but doable with a partner. Overall solid!

Easily one of the best professors I've had. Lectures are engaging and informative, and relatively easy to understand given the subject matter. Homework is fair and helps to further understanding of concepts. Very interesting class, would highly recommend.

He is one of if not the best Prof in the CS department. Lectures are funny and interesting. Makes VERY complicated problems approachable. Handful of homework assignments and projects 1 midterm 1 final. Very straightforward.

Like everyone else has said, he's a phenomenal teacher, I really hope the U doesn't lose him. He teaches you relevant and useful AI in a digestible way and also in a way that challenges you, it's really great. Thank you Prof. Kuntz!

Easily my favorite professor I have ever taken. The concepts were interesting and recent (he talked about Starcraft, my favorite game), which made him feel extremely relatable and understandable. He is super funny and you are missing out every time you miss a lecture. He cares about his students and his TA's and it shows. Please take Prof. Kuntz.

Excellent professor, covers the material well and clearly cares about the students. The class is one of the best I've taken and while it isn't a super high workload, I still feel it was an excellent introduction to AI concepts.

This professor is caring, and very knowledgeable. Whatever you don't like about professors, this professor actively tries not to do. He tries his best to not test on things he hasn't given you graded homeworks back for. He also jokes around and it's a good time if you are in person. Zoom isn't as good. He is also good about answering questions.

While Alan's workload can be quite heavy at times, particularly if you choose to work on the programming projects alone, his excellent teaching more than makes up for it. His are some of the best lectures I have ever attended, and his attitude alone works to hold student's interest. I STRONGLY recommend Dr. Kuntz
His make complicated concepts easy to understand, It is easy to know what will be on the tests, and the assignments are very educational. I would take any class he teaches.

He is a good lecturer and provides a great learning environment for his students. The workload is relatively light for a CS class, and he provides many resources to help you succeed like recorded lectures. Just make sure you're on top of the assignments as my grade was determined by 15 things. I highly recommend taking his class as an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, made this class fun. I would highly suggest any class he teaches. CS4300 was one of my favorite classes I have taken so far; practical workload, good lectures, and some really fun programming assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He can explain/break down complex topics in easy-to-understand English. Assignments felt appropriate in length. Records all lectures. No tests. Overall an excellent instructor.
The lectures for this class were awesome, and I learned a lot from the projects and homeworks. He is a great professor that is really in tune with how to teach students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was a good professor who explained the material well and made sure that we were able to understand the context. He would allow us cheat sheets on the exams which were very helpful. There was also many different extra credit opportunities to improve your grade and help you understand better.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: After taking this class I have gained a better understanding of math. There are weekly quizzes but there are always opportunities to redo quizzes for a better score. As long as you put in the effort you can pass this class. And topics covered on midterms and the final are always specified as well. The professor was also very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mr. Vinhage was a very lovely professor and I enjoyed having him for math 1090. He offered a variety of extra credit opportunities and quiz retakes. We were allowed a front and back cheat sheet on every midterm and the final. He does a great job of providing study resources which helped a lot of my peers get good grades.
i thought i would major in chinese but this class inspired me to take more math classes. amazing lectures and enthusiasm, thats why they call him "the big homie" kurt.

The professor's lectures were amazing, how-ever I found when it came to the homework/exams the professor would write the questions with tricky wording and only someone that's mastered the content could answer them. I'd recommend this professor to "math enthusiasts", but couldn't recommend this professor less otherwise. Also no practice exams.

Professor Guner is an AMAZING instructor. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and would recommend it to anyone that needs to fulfill a history gen ed. He loves what he does and you can see it in the way he teaches. He makes sure everyone feels comfortable regarding the certain topic and allows us to discuss controversial ideas w/out disregarding anyone

I took Prof. Guner's Online History class this summer and was quite surprised. Your grade is 1/4 discussions, 1/4 essays, 1/4 the midterm, and 1/4 the final. His essays are not too bad, just argue any point you can think of and justify it and you should be fine. He gives out a study guide for both exams, if you fill in all of it you'll be find.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Guner is a really amazing guy. I took HIST 1510 online  from him and it was great. You knew what you needed to do each week and what was expected. Although his tests are open book and open note, they are 100% essays and can be pretty difficult. If you don't really study you'll be in real trouble. Great class!
Best professor ever!

I loved taking this class from Kurt. If he could teach all of my History classes at the U I would actually walk away learning something. I highly recommend taking a class from him. He is hilarious too.
I usually hate history because most lecturers are extremely boring; but his lectures were very easy to get through, even funny oftentimes.

Dr. Kuban is very personable and intelligent. If you get to know him he will be understanding with you as a student. Don't slack off, he can recognize that quickly. Work hard for the class, and you'll get the grade you deserve.

He is a great teacher and is very young so he is very enthusiastic about teaching!!  He keeps classes fun and the work load is not that heavy.  The only thing is that he has pop quizzes (super easy, can use notes) at the beginning of most classes.  So you have to attend.  I would definitely recommend taking this class with Adam tho!
This is an overall good class. The professor is well organized and keeps things pretty interesting. The assignment load is pretty light as well.
Very helpful, but there is some type of homework each class. Great teacher though.
Strange guy, but super smart and usually entertaining. Lots of reading, most of it very difficult. Pretty nice grader despite what he claims.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kubarycz's class is unconventional but engaging. Prepare to be challenged and have your thinking expanded. Complete the readings, participate actively, and leverage tools like unstuckstudy for study prep - it'll pay off with an A.

Lots of reading, it's not super organized either so you'll have 50 pages for 2 days and 2 pages for 4 days. He's good at giving lectures but I found majority of the content boring. He wasn't a super harsh grader, he gave A's if you submitted the assignment, despite getting all 100% my final grade was an A- somehow.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is crazy but in the best way possible. He'll bring up weird topics but always does it respectfully and in an engaging manner. I loved this class and learned a lot of random things I did not know before, and for that, I wil always be grateful. There is a lot of readings for this class, but they are all interesting. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can succeed in this class as long as you cater to Brian's ideas and act as though you agree with everything he says. Be ready to listen for an hour straight as he rambles and gets sidetracked, talking about anything BUT the assigned reading. The readings are long and boring, lectures are under-stimulating, and Brian is repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has been THE most impactful instructor I have ever had He has helped me form a self-identity He was made to teach honors courses It is not required to attend or to do the readings however you should do both Ideas coming from the readings rather than the facts He fosters community that is interested in the world I WANT to take more of his classes

Although I have so far little experience with other professors at the U (I have just finished my first semester here), he is my favorite professor BY FAR!!! He does everything right:

Outstanding (Dare I say Magical) Lectures
Gives Considerate and Incredibly Thoughtful Feedback
Easy Expectations
Super Fun (Optional) Field Trips

10/10 Life Changing
Brian is a walking stereotype of an elitist academic that dogs on worldviews that are not his own, but acts as though everyone shares them. Texts are great, discussions are tiresome.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor but his criteria can be a bit confusing. I would suggest utilizing his office hours and participating in online discussions because you will not get much of a word in person. He is very knowledgeable but he sometimes goes on tangents. There is a lot of required reading but he does not quiz you on material however.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Brian's class will challenge you, but he will also push you to grow and to think critically about what you are doing/what you were reading. His class does get frustrating at times, as sometimes it does not match the course description and sometimes it is hard to get a word in during discussions. This class was truly a college experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is fine, however, Brian commonly insults class intelligence levels and acts as though no one knows anything. Readings are dense and oftentimes posted slightly last minute. He's a very picky grader as well. He's a cool guy, the class structure is just disorganized and he holds everyone to a high standard even though he doesn't convey it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Was not very sure what his expectations were from me the whole semester as everything was up in the air. I work better with structure, but some people don't, so if you do not like structure take him. His unconventional teaching style was very interesting and fun but I was confused a lot of the times. Be prepared for him to go on tangents.

Brian Kubarycz is unconventional. If you are conventional you will most likely have a difficult time in his class. He's challenging. You can literally feel new brain cells growing. Participate and speak up in class. Do the readings beforehand. If he understands your personality by the end of the course, you will probably get an A.

It is supremely important that you participate in class. Complete the readings, try to answer questions in class, and ask for feedback during the assignments. The few assignments are relatively straightforward, however the 10 page final essay can seem daunting. Be prepared for class to get super weird and super awkward.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every class is just a discussion on some readings he assigns, but it often diverts into different conversations. The readings are difficult but you can find something to contribute to the class discussion, even if it's just a personal experience. He really cares about participation, so just try to say something once every class and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you are an average student, PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! The whole class is focused around long and meaningless readings. The in-class discussions of the usually 50 page readings account for a large portion of your grade. Brian talks for most of the discussions, agreeing only with opinions that fit his views and dismissing everything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is titled "Magic & Technology," but it's more of a philosophy class. And while Brian has a lot of interesting ideas, he's not the best teacher. Every class has participation earning discussions based on new very long readings every class, but Brian talks through 80% of each. He also treats anyone who doesn't get his viewpoint as an idiot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class is discussion-based with a lot of readings. You do readings for each class, and sometimes there will be 2 or 3, up to 50 pages for each reading. The discussions weren't super interesting, and most of the time you listened to Brian talk the whole time. You also only have a few assignments - which he grades really harshly on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was simply one of the hardest grading professors I have ever dealt with. The course was simply the more boring online course I have ever taken due to the multitude of readings. His final project was 10 pages long for a freshmen-level course. During discussions, he would often attack students' arguments as if they were personal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: LOTS of readings in class, with discussions for each. No due dates for discussions, assigned at seemingly random dates. No structure. Discussions impersonal and overly professional. On the flip side he responded to every top-level post if you did it within a reasonable timeframe. Slow grader, I've still not received my final grade for Spring 2021.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lots of works assigned as expected in the class, but final is incredibly difficult and long. 10 Page single spaced essay on an topic assigned by him makes it hard to work on other classes at the same time. Don't take this class if you are expecting hard finals for other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking his class. I took his class online and I didnt learn much. There are too many reading discussions but there is never a due date. You are only graded on 4 things and he grades extremely hard. He will call an assignment a kindergarten assignment then give you a B. Save yourself and your GPA. Maybe hes better in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the online version of one of his lectures and he was little to no help for the whole semester. He just expected us to follow a personal blog and read 70-80 page articles at random times. He was very disorganized and the two assignments we did have he was very harsh with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Brian is a nice guy, but I wouldn't take a class from him again. He says grades are based on participation, but there aren't a lot of chances to speak up in class. Make sure to write on the blog at least once a week and this term we only had one graded assignment: the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best professor I ever had. He really knows how to think, he really knows how to engage students' minds through unique reading assignments, meaningful discussion, and creative activities. He really helped me take exciting risks with my writing. I ended up taking several classes from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had by far. He is incredibly egotistic and cares nothing about student success. He's one of those professors that actually believe that a B is doing excellent in his class and won't bat an eye to giving you a C. Don't take the class unless you want to ruin your GPA in college.

I enjoy this professor a lot but I know a lot of students that did not like him. The assignments are one 2 pg essay, midterm group paper, 10pg final. How to get an A: -write on his blog at least once a week (you'll understand if you take the class) -Talk at least once per class -Send him your papers for him to check and comment on
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Although, he only graded on a few things- namely participation and your final- it wasn't that hard. So long as you showed up, and read the texts and had something to say, you'll be fine. Lectures were funny. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Make sure you talk in the class, this is the most important thing to do.

Brian grades a lot on participation but doesn't really give you a chance to speak and doesn't really note who does actually speak. He doesn't encourage other viewpoints and really only agrees with what he says. Grade is entirely based on participation, a group midterm, and a 10 page final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Brian is well-spoken, so he talks non-stop in class about the readings but easily gets off track and ultimately rants about how universities are just machines that pop out grads as quickly as possible without nurturing learning. This is great if you care about what he's talking about, but it's difficult to get in your participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of reading is assigned, but barely anything is covered in class. Brian rants about everything under the sun all class and calls it a discussion. He asks for student participation but really just wants you to stroke his ego and tell him how great he is. Your grade at the end of the class is based on how much he likes you. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Your entire grade for the course is based upon your participation in class, but Brian gives you very few opportunities to speak as he spends the whole class period talking himself with few pauses. I would only recommend this course if you're willing to be aggressive to speak up and talk to him outside of class hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love philosophy- this was not it. I wanted to read authors like Thomas Aquinas. Instead, we read a thesis on magic systems throughout the world's history. Way too much reading that we never covered in class. He lectures all day and calls it a discussion, then makes you feel dumb for arguing against him. Find someone else for IT2.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brian was interesting and always had a lot to say. However he also asked you to participate, and never provided opportunities since he lectured the whole time. There was also a ton of readings in the class, which tended to be difficult to manage, especially since the questions he did ask were about specific parts and his particular interpretations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Brian is interesting- I think people either hate or love him. If you resonate with him, he'll leave you feeling introspective and part of something larger. Those who don't vibe with him may find him grandiose and his lectures are pretentious. But, if you keep an open mind and heart, you'll love his class-- it might even change you for the better.

There is one key to passing Brian's class: get to know him. He is readily available for office hours and you must take advantage to talk with him and get to know him, and make sure your presence is made known in class. Class consists of him talking the entire time about assigned readings. Entire grade was based on 10-page final and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Brian is unlike any professor Ive had, in the best way possible. It was a tough class, but I learned a lot talking about ideas and points of view Id never considered. Participation is key, he wants to see that you care and want to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brian loves to talk. He lectures for extended periods of time with no breaks. However, his lectures are interesting; he is able to relate the class texts to his students' lives in an interesting fashion. He is a very intriguing person and I learned a lot in his class. There are very few assignments in his class, so be sure to put effort into each.

Lots of reading, but a lot of people didn't read and could still pass by by just adding off what he said in class. Says he wants engaged class discussions but he just rambles all class without allowing for comments. He pushes his narrative of what the texts mean and isn't receptive to other ideas. The grade at the end felt arbitrary & unclear.

Brian is basically the best professor I've had so far as a student. His class was challenging, but he works really well with you and he's all around a cool guy. He's super dedicated and you can go to him with any issues. I completely recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Brian is the best professor that I have had in my young college career. His lectures and discussions are very informative and educational, while also being interesting. I had him in a three-hour class and it honestly felt shorter and more fun than my shorter classes. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wow he is a dedicated professor! Brian lives and breathes what he teaches. I have never had such engaging classroom discussions, especially about text written 2000 years ago! His class is very difficult because you HAVE to do the readings and participate, but if you put in the work he will make sure you get a lot out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's one of the most interesting people I've ever met and his lectures are usually really interesting so the long classes fly by. Most of the class is discussing the readings, which you should at least skim even if you don't understand them. I cannot stress enough how important discussion participation is, contribute anything you think is relevant.

Brian lectures without any notes and without stopping for the whole class. He assigns a lot of readings each week. Your grade is based off participation, a group midterm, and a 10 pg final paper. He posts everything on a blog where it's hard to find all the readings. He's very smart and a cool guy , but I would not recommend taking his class.

He means to be confusing, because he's just trying to make his students think and adapt to an environment they haven't been in before. Keep in mind that all he wants is a reaction from you, and there is no right reaction. He assigns lots of readings, my advice is focus on the ones that interest you.  Some people love him, some hate him.
You have to be a quick thinker in order to participate amidst his ramblings.

He seems like he knows what he is talking about, and can go on for a long time and string along different ideas while leaving most everyone in the dust.  Your grade is based almost entirely on participation.  Prepare for a lot of reading too.  There are a about 2 papers which are graded, but the rest is graded on participation.

Brian is an amazingly intelligent guy & understands all books & philosophers almost to a faulthe babbles on for hours & considers it a "class discussion." He also doesn't take any new ideas in, though he pretends he encourages it. Your entire grade is based on 1 paper & class participation, though you really have to be aggressive to get a word in.

He just talks and talks, with no apparent point. His "discussions" are really just him talking to a class of hands up. He has a king complex of sorts and the class is really all about him. He is very well read and very intelligent but he doesn't like to reuse words so he is unclear. For the assignments, I'm not even sure HE knows what he wants.

Brian is a really cool guy, but as a professor I would not recommend him to anyone. I left just about every lecture completely confused, and he assigned so much reading material that I constantly felt overwhelmed and didn't know what to prioritize. He rarely gives good feedback, and even when you ask him for help, he rarely is satisfied with work.

Kubarycz is a very intelligent person, and what he says is fascinating. My issue with him is that his class is a nightmare logistically. He expected 120 pages of reading for each day of class, twice a week. He is very inconsistent in what he says. He will ramble on all class about what you discussed the previous class. I DO NOT recommend.

He truly is brilliant. He's engaged in the conversation and has interesting takes on thing. However, his teaching style is very untraditional. If you don't talk, you won't get a good grade. Simple as that. No textbook, but large amounts of online readings. As long as you attend class, read, and participate, you should be fine!

Kubarycz is unlike any professor you've ever had before, but in a good way. He's extremely intelligent, and he conducts his classes like a jazz solo. Participation in class discussion is absolutely essential for a good grade. Kubarycz doesn't hate science majors, he just realizes that science isn't the answer to every interesting question out there

People either absolutely love Brian or absolutely hate him.  His lectures kept me engaged, and I liked his creative interpretations of our readings.  He doesn't give a lot of feedback, and he can't stand science majors.  Taking his class was a growing experience for me.

This is a great class if you are willing to put in the effort to read the materials and actively think about it. Brian is very knowledgeable about what he lectures on and if you have an open mind you will learn things in his classes that you won't find in any other class. A lot of students don't do the readings and don't get much out of the class.
He is a nice guy, but his class is a joke. If you read everything and think about it, you can learn a lot. If you don't do any of the readings, you can still get an easy A.
He's a good professor. He is very honest with his students about what he expects of them. Be sure to talk in class, you get out of it what you put into it.
Very likable guy but his class was a joke. We didn't follow the syllabus at all and didn't even cover the course subject matter. I was very disappointed.

He's great at teaching and every class is interesting. It made me like the humanities. He also gets to know his students well. But if you're a science major, be wary--his views on us are offensive at best. If you're reading this, we aren't all passionless. Most of us aren't. =[

He's a really cool guy. really unconventional, and i liked him a lot as a person but i didn't like his teaching style.  he reads a little much into everything and the whole class is mostly you listening to him and being confused. participation is very important so speak up. its not hard though. basically you get what you want out of the class.

Brian is a genius. All you have to do to get a decent grade is show that you care even a little bit about what he has to say, and express your thoughts about it. And he will give you an A. Super easy and an extremely awesome class. He knows so much about everything.

Brian is one of the most unique and interesting professors I've ever had. He definitely is not a traditional professor - but that's not a bad thing. He's knows what he's talking about, and his class lectures are incredibly interesting and you can learn a lot from him. A large part of your grade is participation - make sure you talk in class.

One of the best teachers I have ever had. I took 2 semesters of IT with him and had a blast. I also got an A in both classes. Do the readings, participate, write a decent and original paper and you should be fine.

Brian's class was one I always looked forward to. The readings were challenging, but discussions were usually lively. Brian's lecture style is real and engaging, not stuffy and boring. If you like learning and broadening your horizons, take his class!

Brian is brilliant and I enjoyed his class but he has a very ... unique teaching method.. and is not open to new or differing opinions. he needs to be taken back down to earth sometimes, but you will learn a lot in the class and it is sufficiently challenging as an Honors course as far as material is concerned but not overwhelming

Brian's weird and has a very different view on life and college than most people around here do. Class was based entirely off discussing the readings (he doesn't make you buy textbooks and posts the class readings on his blog instead), and your grade comes from mostly from a final paper. Overall one class with him was enough for me, but he's cool.

Quite disorganized class and really huge unrealistic quantity of readings within a small timeframe. This class could be really wonderful but fell short due o organizational issues and too much (and too dense) material for the short time spent on each reading. Spend more time getting depth not shallow breadth!
Basically, read the assignments and ask questions and talk and you WILL get an A.
Highly amusing and pro at leaving the boring out of literature. be creative on the final and your grade goes to the top.
By far the best professor I had at the University.

Kubarycz is probably the best teacher I have ever had. Anyone who does not receive an A is an idiot because he states clearly at the beginning of the semester that he grades on participation (saying something once in a while) and [appearing!] to know the content of the reading. Super easy, just talk.

Although this class was interesting, I felt he was extremely unfair in his grading. It is based purely on participation and a 10 page final paper. He provides no feedback and little direction but still grades according to his specifications. Waste of time.

Brian's the best. Recognizes the difficulty of readings but emphasizes making an effort. VERY beneficial to do the HW; you'll have something to say in class and the final is 10pg paper related to readings. Legitimate interest and participation gets the grade, go on the fieldtrips he sets up. He's sexy and the smartest dude I've ever met.

Very unconventional. Grades are based on the 10 page final paper, and how much you talk in class. There is no way to tell where you stand grade-wise throughout the semester, so if you're a person who likes structure, skip this one. Brian seems to know what he's talking about, but you get the feeling that he's just saying random s***.
Worth doing the readings. Makes class more interesting. Not your usual Honors class - which is a very good thing.

Brilliant guy, doesn't really have anything worthwhile to talk about though, it's pretty much just talking about essays and other various writings in class. You don't need to read the reading assignments cause he doesn't test them, the only homework he gives are a few 2 page reviews, and one 10 page final.

Interesting. He is either brilliant or a great actor. Seems to need to make a statement with his dress, but I wasn't sure what it was. Definitely passionate which is always good, but vague and sometimes difficult just for the sake of being difficult. Definitely some one to learn from, directly or indirectly.

This is a very non-traditional class. Brian will very likely not assign a textbook.  Instead you'll be looking at the writings that a textbook would reference. Participate often and try not to parrot back in your assignments and you'll do fine. Don't get bogged down in writing notes in class either, just go with the flow. It's an excellent class.

Loved class and Brian, but it was extremely difficult.  Pay attention, participate in class, and write a lot on the online journal and you'll do fine.  He is also super liberal and doesn't love LDS people/doctrine.

He's a nice and interesting teacher. He loves what he teaches but can be difficult to understand. The homework was often overwhelming and difficult to understand. There are no tests or quizzes, just a a ten page paper due as a final. It feels like he grades based how much he likes you so make sure to participate in class a lot.
Excellent class!!

Brian knows what he's talking about and does everything he can to make sure that his students do as well. His passion for teaching is unmatched in my experience so far. Speak up (even if you're wrong, he'll appreciate it!), pay attention, and let him know that you care about his class and you'll be fine.
Brilliant professor.  Made classes fun and interesting.  If you want to do well in this class, you should try to consistently participate in discussions.

If you spend any time at all at the field house gym, you'll see him there. ;) Extremely intelligent, though he seems to get along with certain people/mindsets better than others. If you make an attempt, you will get rewarded for it. At least pretend like you care about all the old philosophers!
Simply, the best professor that I've ever had. Ever.

I had Brian for honors writing and I thought that his class was awsome! We had to read a lot of philosophy and a lot of it went right over my head, but Brian's discussions of the material really expanded my thinking. He was very clear about what he wanted in the papers we wrote for the class. I really learned how to write well in his class.

I wasn't going to say anything besides the usual student survey, but this professor should lose his job or be penalized. He didn't teach the class anything; the consequence is that this semester I am missing the necessary foundation in order to succeed in my more advanced classes. So I have to spend more time and money getting proper instruction.
Alright professor. Really weird acting. Didn't comprehend stuff he was saying. When asking for help, says more weird stuff. Really confusing. Really cool and nice though.

Disorganized, talks about seemingly nothing. His final had not guidelines, and then he marks down for not meeting the expectations that he had never expressed. Likes to remind everyone how long "he has been in the business" in response to independent thought he doesn't agree with while simultaneously assigning "Pedagogy of the Oppressed."AVOID HIM!
Brian is a great teacher! He is interesting and one of the smartest people I've ever met. He knows his material well and makes class fun.
Very cool, down to earth guy who puts a lot of effort into making sure the students understand what he wants, and has the appearance of a rock star to boot.
No Comments
No Comments
great guy and very cool to students.  Quite a bit of work, but he gives you a break in your final grade if  you try hard to keep up.  I've never met a student who doesn't like him.
Probably the best teacher I have ever had!
Well read, well spoken professor. Extremely intelligent. Unconventional approach to instruction. Not an easy A, but worth every minute of effort. Your mind will EXPAND!
goood guy, very unconventional for an honors prof.

I took Math 1100 with Professor Kwak and highly recommend him as a professor! He is very open to feedback and based on class sentiment would shift how the course flowed to fit student's needs. He offers opportunities to redo your exam grade if you scored poorly and the homework problems have 20 attempts to help in mastering the material.

Took his Math 1100 Bus Calc class. Excellent teacher, very nice to students and quite approachable. Offers lots of extra credit on tests and explains concepts in way that makes them easy to learn. As long as you do the hw you will know what's going on. Nicest man in the math department. Really great professor for math. Liked math after his class.

I just took his Math 1100 bus calc class (math 1050 was the only option) and he was great! Retook this class after doing terrible in the accelerated summer course and he taught it so simply that I actually enjoyed math again. Adapts classes to student needs and is super responsive to emails. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. Highly recommend!

He is AMAZING! Took his Bus Calc class. I was worried about going into this class, I am not generally a math guy, but he made it feel so smooth and completely learnable. There are tons of opportunity's for extra credit and he is very generous on his grading. The concept is tough, but I would never take another math class if it wasn't from him.

Professor Kwak is one of the nicest professors you'll ever have. He is caring of all of his students, passionate about what he teaches and very patient. His stuff is "learnable", you just have to have the effort because if you aren't amazing at math, sitting in the lectures every week isn't going to cut it so be prepared to put in some effort.

Professor Kwak is nice. He drops two lowest assignments and quizzes and one midterm. He is willing to work with students if problems occur. I personally found his instruction a bit confusing. However, there is so much material on the internet for the topics. I didn't go to class, just learned from the homework and internet and did fine. I like math

This class was very disorganized. It was an online course, but the material was so unorganized and confusing on what assignments were due when and included in what module. She grades everything on a 2 or 3 point availability. Grades so hard. Very difficult class to get a good grade. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kwynn took a difficult course and made it understandable. She presented the material in a way that was relatable and encouraged political engagement rather than just feeling depressed about societal problems. She's really understanding and reasonably accommodating.

This class was hard. It is an advanced writing class, so be prepared. Utilize the U's writing center and other resources or you'll end up with a B+ like me. She gives a lot of feedback on your papers. Just apply all the feedback you can, and DO NOT procrastinate your assignments. Good luck to you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A majority of assignments are 2-5 points each, which means if you miss 1-2 points, your letter grade for that assignment can drop from pass to fail. Some of her feedback is good, but I felt like some of it was suggestive (i.e. say it this way instead of that way) and I was still docked on points for it. Also, takes too long to respond to emails.

I love Dr. North! She genuinely cares about her students and makes the class so engaging. She loves to answer questions and is really available over email. Her tests were very true to what she teaches in class and very fair. She gives learning objectives that are accurate to what she tests on. Best professor I have ever had!

Dr. North cares for both student success and student experience. She makes it clear what is required of her course, and provides material and lectures that sufficiently prepare students for exams and future classes in the major. She is extremely enthusiastic and seems to really love teaching.

I had her for 1020. North is a mix. She is very passionate about her work. She does what she can to prepare you, but also expects you to have knowledge of pre-reqs you won't have taken. She boasts about herself a lot and her work tbh, she is very kind, though. Nothing is really reliable, but she cares about the learning.

Professor North's class is fun to go to but the zero room for error speaks of lack of respect between her and her students, I have had to go through rigorous processes fighting for credit for attendance and one missing assignment that was left out of the canvas modules so I missed it.

Over all lack of care for anyone and lack of respect earns 1/5
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. North is a very engaging speaker and I found her journey to becoming an educator to be very inspirational. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about medical innovation and research, which contributes to a positive class environment.

I really respect her, she is so cool! She doesn't really lecture in this class because it is a seminar class but when she did you could tell she was extremely knowledgeable. She grades fairly but holds you accountable, which I respect (this is a CR/NC class). The only reason I didn't give her a 5 is because she doesn't answer emails.

Dr. North has very high standards when it comes to grading at least in her BME 1010 course. She will not accept any late work that except for 1 single assignment in the semester which you can make up with a contigency assignment she'll determine. Attendance is mandatory as daily quizzes are in her class as this is a class to understand the major.
Wonderful professor who cares about his students!

Very helpful in office hours and actually cares about students. Professor Dawson makes lectures interesting and enjoyable, and they don't feel as daunting. Tests are a little rough, but that's more so due to the nature of the topics learned in class.

He is a very kind and caring professor. He was knowledgeable with the content and could answer most questions. Preparing for his exams can be difficult as practice exams either weren't provided or were very different from the exam. His grading felt fair and exams weren't excessively difficult. He is thoughtful with course setup and feedback

I love this guy, amazing lectures, very understanding. Our lecture was 80 minutes and it felt like 30 every class. Exams are a little difficult but reasonable if you are putting in effort, lab section is a little dry, but simple. He does a lot of his work on the whiteboard so I recommend making it to every lecture.

Dr.Dawson is a great professor. His class wasn't the best but Physics 4 is a hard class in general. He was very nice and accessible outside of class and took feedback from the class very seriously. I would definitely take a class with him again in the future.

I got an A in both Physics I & II with Dawson. FlipIt lectures horrible, but using Walid Harmaneh's videos for homework & the Serway + Jewett textbook to learn concepts I did well. Don't expect to learn anything in lecture (I only attended to take the quizzes) & use external materials + work practice problems prior to test to get a good grade.
Made the topic confusing.

For the love of god dont forget about ANY of the stupid flip it Physics lectures. Apparently hearing the same exact thing two times over is critical to your learning experience. For some reason there is no way to make up any of those points. I have a B not for lack of test or quiz performance, but because you have to watch these useless videos

Lectures aren't good. My suggestion if you take him is get Chegg for homework and test scenario's. Use power point and TA sessions for help and studying. Become friends with your discussion group. Grades are based on a point scale so if you end up doing well you can fail the final and still pass. This class is doable but requires self studying.

Kyle is a very accessible instructor. You can ask him any question with varying levels of depth and he will get back to you. Class was physics and I do not get it. I passed the class but it was very difficult. He provided many thing that made it easier to pass the class. Lectures arent very helpful. Mostly have to work hard on your own.
Kyle is a great professor, and I have now had him for 2 semesters. At first, he was a little shaky, but he adapted and listened to students. I would definitely recommend Professor Dawson.

The lectures don't really help. It might be a better use of your time to study outside of class. Doesn't really do examples, rather he shows how to derive equations, not to use them. A large part of my learning was googling the homework to find out how to solve problems. He doesn't effectively answer questions and his polling system doesn't work.

I retook this class for a better grade, and I have to say the structure that Kyle has is much better than Springer. Tests were multiple choice and he gave you the scenarios of questions that would be on the test. So you had a pretty good idea of what was going to be asked. Group assignments were dumb but the TA's helped with the answers.
not a very good physics teacher. doesnt seem to want to listen to the students feedback after being told the problems with his method of teaching tests after tests
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lectures don't help. Group assignments are tough. The grading scheme for the exams is very unforgiving (multiple-choice questions, 10 T/F questions worth 2 points each, and 5 scenarios, each with around 3 questions worth 4-8 points for a total of 20 points for each scenario).

In short, I do not recommend Kyle for Physics. Poor lectures just covering concepts and deriving formulas, zero example problems (doesn't really "believe" in them), rarely writes on board. Tests and group assignments can be ridiculously difficult because we don't really do any problems or see relevant examples class.

He's a nice enough guy, but this class is structured horribly. His lectures are useless. He gets too deeply into the concepts without getting into actual mathematics. Quizzes test on material before the relevant homework is due, and on material that may have been barely touched in lecture. Criminally bad, he solely depends on subpar FlipitPhysics.

It would be great if discussion sections related to the material focused on in class. Professor is a smart guy, but refuses to give any relevant homework for out of class use. Discussion sections were graded harshly and the weekly quizzes were not related to the lecture content. He also "doesn't believe" in doing example problems using numbers.

Basicly Kyle is very out of touch with good teaching practices. He told us that he hasn't taught a Physics class in 20 years and it shows. Quizzes are unrelated to the exam as well as homework, BOTH are VERY hard. Don't expect to get your grades back anytime soon. NO CURVE and 93 is an A. Physics is tough enough DON'T take it from this guy!
Young, enthusiastic and excitable, with a lot of astronomy experience so expect an astronomer's perspective.
kyle was awesome! I really enjoyed his class. He really pushed us and inspired me to dive deep

Kyle Barrett was a wonderful professor and I am DIGGING to see if he teaches more classes. I had a few traumatic things happen during the span of my semester with him and he was nothing but understanding, accommodating, and kind. His class was interesting to be in and you can tell he has a love for what he does. I would recommend him to anybody.

Professor Barrett was interesting. He gave really good feedback on assignment but he would attack your opinions and prove them wrong even though this class is based on what you think. Other than that he makes you work for your grade but it's an interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his "theory of knowledge" in the fall 2018 semester. Excellent class: great discussions and interesting material, especially in the Trump era.

Digital Culture was a very fun and interesting class. It's quite a lot of reading, especially since I was in the 6 week condensed version (ie 1 novel a week). I actually liked that he graded tough because I learned a lot and he gave good feedback.
he sux he has so much homework and doesn't accept late work

I would not take this unless you have prior knowledge of coding language. There is a lot of reading already, not concerning coding, and learning it from a textbook leaves me studying 10+ hrs a week. Which is ridiculous for a 2000 level english class. The professor is nice, lecture videos are short, although they might be more helpful if longer.

He seems nice enough I guess, however you need to read 60+ pages of condensed reading and write 800 words per week along with labs and quizzes. Insane amount of work for just a 2000 level class and a class thats mainly taken for just general education.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't walk, run, to get Kylie as your professor. She is so kind and understanding, you can tell she genuinely cares about your grade and well-being. The class and lectures were clearly formatted. She always took student input and tried to make things as easy as possible for us. Love you Kylie!

I really enjoyed Dr. Rochfords class. She created a space that cultivated social interaction in a productive way. She worked really hard to make her lessons interesting and interactive so that you could actually apply the concepts you were learning during in-class activities.
She was kind, but ultimately this class was a waste of time. Everything taught was common sense. Exams are intentionally misleading. Participation tanked my grade.

I'm so chopped at school, but I actually really enjoyed this class. Super nice and understanding professor. Attendance is mandatory, but you're allowed 3 excused absences. Didn't matter to me, though, because I didn't miss a single class. Grading is very test-heavy, so study up.
Professor Rochford was very nice, you can tell she really loves what she teaches. Attendance is mandatory and slides are very important for the exams.

Her lectures were mostly engaging, I'm just not interested in the topic. She does care a lot about student success, so she's happy to help if you're struggling. Exams were super easy for me, and I barely studied. There is a big group project due as the final, so pick wisely.

She was a good teacher; as long as you attend every lecture, do the homework and pay attention to class slides then its fine. Exams are definitely doable if you follow along with the slides and study beforehand.

I didn't love her but I didn't hate her. Her lectures were really long and required taking a lot of notes. I kinda found myself dozing off and getting bored. Exams were a little challenging because it requires you to really understand the concepts, because questions are all scenario-based based so definitely study

Professor Rochford was so awesome! I really enjoyed having her for management, she explains the material very well and made class fun by having us do some group activities throughout the semester. She is really caring for her students and is very accessible outside of class.

Kylie is amazing! She knows what she is talking about and is able to make her students understand the material. Her lectures are really engaging, she's not just standing in front of the room talking about different management styles for the whole time, instead you are working with others in the class and applying your knowledge. Great professor.

Kylie was a nice professor. Class weights heavily impacted your grade. She's accessible out of class and was quick to reply. Talks to you like she's HR - not ideal at times. Very concerned about ethics in class. LARGE group project - choose team wisely. Exams were situational ?s, class concepts difficult to understand without real-world examples.

Kylie is amazing. You can tell how much she cares. She is knowlegable and always goes the extra mile to make sure her slides are clear and consistent. Her in-class activities are a lot of fun and really useful in learning the material in a hands on way. I can't reccomend her enough

Honestly the Professor herself wasn't too bad, she really did a good job at explaining the material. That being said, she definitely assigns a ton of quizzes which you really need to be on top of, otherwise your ending grade will really suffer. 
Also her Exams were really rough, the questions were just really tricky and you didn't have enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: BEST management professor ever! everyone in my class, including myself, loved her. So caring and understanding. She still has rules she has to follow and a curriculum, so the class isn't a suuuper easy A. But it was definitely one of my easier classes in the business school, and one of my fav professors. I promise you won't regret taking her!!!

Very caring and understanding. Her class isn't difficult if you attend lectures and study the slides. There are two exams (study the slides and apply them-she also gives review videos), a group project (plan ahead with your group), homeworks (very simple), and pop quizzes (drops one, might as well do the readings to get full points).

Not too much work, It was do-able. You just need to pay attention. She lays out the exams pretty much completely in her review slides so as long as you learn and pay attention you should be able to pass the exams!

She always tried to have something interesting in each lecture. Most classes were fun and definitely worth going to. There was lots of reading but they were from the textbook. She is a great teacher and she tried to make this class as easy as possible for students.

Professor Rochford is an amazing professor! Her lectures are extremely interesting and I feel that everything that is taught in her class is essential for business majors. She respects and cares for her students, and will purposely lighten our workload on days where she knows we have exams. I loved attending her class. 10/10 would recommend.

Professor Rochford has been a great instructor this semester. She really cares about her student's mental health and she would always bring positive energy into her teaching. I would definitely recommend her.

Love Kylie! So inspired by the women teaching this year. Prof Rochford is entertaining, clean cut, smart, and I loved her class 10/10. Tons of group activities but it's honestly essential. Prof Rochford is partially the reason I chose this section of BCOR.
Great class. Professor is knowledgeable and will call BS when she sees it. If you turn up and pay attention the content is not difficult.

Unless you are studying for your Master's Degree in Management, you won't do too well in this classIt is not an easy A. She deliberately tries to deceive you on quizzes & tests by wording questions in the most confusing way. This isn't just my opinion, this is coming from 10+ other people in my class. Truly the worst teacher I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Rochford is a fine professor. Her material isn't too hard, her slides are helpful, and the class is overall fine. What I begin to have a problem with is her attitude. She comes to class everyday with a frown on her face, and often gets short with students . Plus, she assigns 3 page papers that are worth 1 point. Wouldn't reccomend her.

Kylie is a great professor and she's very nice. This class is lecture heavy and she goes pretty quick, but don't worry because her review slides will prepare you well for the Exams. If you get a good grade on the first two exams you don't have to take the third and the group project we had to do wasn't bad at all.
Kylie is awesome! She is refreshing and made learning a topic I was not much interested in, interesting. Totally would recommend and loved her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ight lets be real. Kylie is awesome... the management core classes are an absolute waste of time with no relevance to anything. its just memorizing a lot of stuff and regurgitating information that useless. but u got this man, i believe in you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kylie was a great MGT professor. She recognized that many of us weren't MGT majors and realized that her class wasn't our top priority. Therefore, she makes it easy for you to miss an assignment, or even a test. Very lenient grader and the lectures were interesting. Lots of in class group work and a big group final though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved this class, her lectures were awesome. I learned a lot from her. Each lecture had some sort of activity, game, or discussion so class goes by quick and you aren't taking notes the whole time. I had fun in class and felt like I could apply the concepts from class to the games. She is really great, definitely take this class from her.

I love her class! The material isn't difficult if you study. I simply didn't jive with the material but I passed the class! Group project in this class. Deal with any issues early on, don't wait! Very approachable and willing to talk with students. She is clear on what you need to do. I would take a class from her again. Take this class from her!

Those who say she is a tough grader most likely did not follow the homework requirements or attend her lectures. I actually found that she was one of the most organized professors at the U I've had. Her grading criteria is very clear. She does require attendance and has a strict phone policy. Her class was very easy if you just pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You have to attend her lectures if you want to pass. There is a lot to study and understand. You will lose points if she sees your phone out. Very harsh at grading and probably too harsh. This isn't a Masters course, but she treats it as such. Group project isn't hard but you want ot choose a good group. Class is just okay. Online might be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class. Not sure what the awful comment is all about. Exams are not that hard. She tells you exactly what you need to know. Average for the last exam was almost 90%. It's college, not high school or kindergarten. I feel like I actually learned something useful. I didn't find the lectures boring, there was often an activity.

Class is extremely BORING. She grades you very harshly, when she's not that great of a teacher. Lectures are her chance to spew how much she thinks she knows. Tough grader for a 3000 level course. Group project is easy. Exams are overly hard, too much to know with these exams. Narrow it down Kylie! Does this need to be so hard? No technology here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Please take her class if you are taking 3680 at the U. She is very clear on expectations and really knows the subject. It was her first time teaching this course and she did amazing, she will only get better. One of the few professors out there who truly seem invested in her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There's no book, but you'll need to purchase Harvard Business Publishing for readings. She's very engaging and has interactive discussions. You have a group project based on things you learn in class to apply to resolving an organizational issue. The exams are heavy but review the slides and readings and you'll do fine. I highly recommend her class

Kylie was great! She cares about students outside of class. She even eliminated a large assignment entirely due to concerns that we were burnt out from other classes. Overall, the class is not difficult if you study and take notes during lecture. She is very entertaining, and most class had an activity involved, which was fun. Great class overall.
