I didn't mind this class and actually learned something from the group project. She mixes in exercises with lectures and they are helpful. As long as you study for the tests properly they are not too difficult. It was her first semester so she was a bit up tight and started taking attendance at the end. Liked taking the course from her though.
This was a great class. You have to put in some work but it's worth it. I got a lot out of it, more than most of my college courses.

Kylie is the BEST. She genuinely wants to make it an enjoyable course. It is an entertaining lecture and she keeps class lively. She is a tough grader but gives clear expectations so its easy to get 100% on your assignments. Her tests are clear and very easy to study for. She is ALWAYS willing to work with you on anything you might need help with.

Extremely rigid and unsympathetic. Assumes the worst of students and offers no flexibility, even in genuine situations. Made the class feel cold and discouraging. I lost all interest in art history because of how this course was handled. Would not recommend.

Extremely harsh grader. Most assignments are graded out of three points, with no fractional grades. The last point can be docked for the pettiest reasons, leaving you with a D on the assignment regardless of your efforts. The class average on the midterm was a D, which was an assignment graded out of 25 points. Take an easier class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I missed one class because I was exposed to covid and he uses "missing class" as an excuses to not go over what I missed. He would not go back  and explain 2 terms I did not fully understand for the homework. I received a 1 out of 6 because he simply did not want to explain.

I had his Arts of Buddhism class, and loved it. Having taken many art history courses, I found his class to be both informative and easy to pass. The grading was all based off of two tests and attendance. Prof. Kyan was very nice and pretty funny. I never heard angry outburst from him. Technology is not his friend though X)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not a fan of Art History in general, but this class was so much more interesting than any other Art History classes I've ever taken! Winston is very knowledgeable and overall very helpful if you have any questions. Sometimes he can be a little snappy if you happen to ask a question that he has already gone over, but overall he is great.

I like this guy!  I only wish he was more transparent on feedback.  So many professors are imprecise and expect you to figure out their super vague feedback!  Then, if you're not Alan Turing and can't decipher their remarks,  you get a bad grade. What's the point of feedback if it's not somewhat constructive, or at the very least, decipherable.

Easier class but if you want a teacher that just reads off slides the ENTIRE time and makes the class extremely uncomfortable and awkward then take this class. I found it very difficult to have to desire to attend class because it's not like I couldn't also read off slides on my own time. He's a weird chap and had a few random angry outbursts.

This class was average. I found myself falling asleep during the lectures because the professor rambled on and on. Kind of an awkward class because no one would talk when discussion was encouraged. The course material was cool and interesting and the work load is not bad. Not an easy A but not too hard either.

Interesting class. If you pay attention you'll learn a lot. He really knows his stuff although sometimes he goes off on tangents. The class can be dull at times but what do you expect with a powerpoint lecture. There are relatively few assignments and if you pay attention you'll get a good grade. The TA was a harsh grader though.
Just write some papers the whole semester and you get an easy A!!
Great teacher, all he does is make you write some papers and thats the whole class.  got an easy A

The class was graded on whether you show up and do the work. There is no out-of-class work. If you miss multiple days, you must come another day to make it up. Kyle was very good at communicating and ensuring students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super chill the type of professor who loves his craft and teaches it with passion, be prepared to enjoy his dumb jokes. His class is not hard but make sure to ask specific questions if your confused. If your in a class that already knows the tools of the trade he will create a new design challenge for you to follow its always fun.

Pretty easy class overall. The lectures could be kind of boring, but he told you pretty much everything to memorize for quizzes and the midterm. It's mostly about the final project which is designing a show in teams. Your grade for that is still mostly individual, so even if you have a bad team you'll do fine.
Great professor! Lectures are a little dry but he tries to make it interesting. There is a group project to design Hamlet but it's a lot of fun and not very difficult.

Kyl was born to teach this course!!! She is a great lecturer on this topic and she really truly cares about the students and their opinions/experiences. At first, it seemed like there were a lot of assignments (monthly journal responses, a book report, and a creative piece along with quizzes) but they were all pertinent and valuable for me. TAKE!!!

Professor Myers is super knowledgeable, and she had lots of interesting resources to show the class. The class itself was very easy; there is an assignment and a quiz due every Friday, and they're all explained very well. The hardest assignment was a short book report. Overall she's a really good professor, and you'll learn a lot in her class.

This past semester classes went online half way through due to COVID-19. Dr. Myers was so incredibly supportive. She wanted to know how every single one of her students were doing and how their mental health was. She constantly checked in and gave us lots of resources. She also made online school interesting! She seriously deserves an award.

Dr. Myers was one of my favorite professors at the University. Her class was engaging, fun, but also something you had to put in work for. It wasn't hard, but there we're a lot of interesting readings that you should keep caught up on for an A.
Her Criminology class was amazing and she made lectures fun. She also had a few guest lecturers which were cool too.  I took her online Gender and Sexuality class too and loved it!
The class is easy as long as you put in the work and do the assignments
Kyl is awesome and super easy going. She gives you exactly what will be on the test and there are no trick questions, like so many other teachers do. I would take her class again in a heartbeat!

She is one of the best professors I've ever had at the U. She's super attractive and very enticing. You genuinely want to go to lecture because they are SO good. Her tests are straightforward and she gives you everything you need to get an A. I also got pretty sick and she was really helpful and allowed me to make up stuff.

Kyl has great lectures and opens it up for discussion with the class. She is also very enthusiastic about what she teaches and makes sure you have all the materials available to you. There is quite a bit of reading however it is interesting and is very topical. Grading is consistent, logical, and timely. Would take this class again in a heartbeat.

Kyle is an amazing teacher. I took this class after my freshman year in high school, and Kyle made me realize how amazing some professors can be. His lectures were very in depth, and he included many explanations of theorems in order to explain why certain functions are performed. Easily the best math teacher I've had.

Good teacher, very Knowledgable. However, he is rather dishonest in his dealings. Offers to drop assignments for attendance at Math department events, but doesn't ever actually follow through and drop the grade. Also dishonest with his grading scale, don't listen to what he says. Just trust the syllabus, not his word.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The assignments were just problems from the book, there wasn't a gazillion like most teachers do, it was just enough to practice each topic and you could do more if you wanted. Tests were exactly on things we learned, nothing extra hard, if you could do the homework you could ace the tests.

He's very young and still a grad student, probably in his 20s, but he still surprised me by being easily the best math professor I've ever taken. He was able to explain the subjects better than teachers I've had that have been teaching longer than he's been alive. Highly recommend, not much homework either.

Grad student who gives really good lectures. You can tell he is very passionate on the subject because of the rants he sometimes strays off topic on. Overall, he is a funny guy, a cool dude, and a damn good Calc professor. 10/10

Focused a lot on the theorems instead of examples and that made it a little hard, but he was very passionate about math. Plus he's a very caring teacher and bonus is kind of cute... recommend going to the math lab once a week to get help with examples and homework.

He may be a grad student, but he really understands and takes the time to explain the concepts that are so key to understanding Calculus. The homework does take a fair amount of time but if you can understand the homework and study the review packet, you will be okay on the exams. Definitely would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kyle is very articulate in his lectures. He will make the subjects very clear to you, and he cracks jokes every now and again. I was worried to take this class from a grad student, but Kyle really knows his stuff and his a great teacher as well as a great mathematician.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I struggled in every math class in high school but Kyle Gaffney made me get it. Super funny, very interesting guy, knows everything about gambling and sports probability, excellent teacher and seems to be an excellent mathematician. One of the best teachers I've had at the U and by far the best math teacher I've had anywhere. Recommend him highly.

I was retaking math 1050 and was worried about taking it from a grad student but Kyle was a really great teacher. He explains everything very well and makes it easy to understand, he really knows what he's teaching. Even if you struggle with math like me, if you're consistently going to his class and don't skip, you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gaffney is a grad student but his knowledge of math is insane. All around good teacher. He is a little awkward but actually really funny. The homework is not bad and the quizzes are free points.

Gaffney is a grad student, so don't expect some amazing teacher. He was really awkward at first, but now he's more chill & cracks jokes every now and then! If you miss once or twice a week, it won't hurt you; just make sure to review the notes online so you don't fall behind. He does quizzes every Friday, but they are open book/open people.
Cute, but no-nonsense.

Sean is a cool guy but he didn't really seem into teaching. He only seemed passionate when he vaguely talked about his research. Lectures dragged, unfortunately. Labs were really hard. TA was helpful during labs. Lots of HW... Sean is obviously very intelligent, but I'm not sure he's meant to teach - especially a lower level class like 1210.

Sean was an interesting professor to say the least...
He assigned lots of homework and did not give any practice tests before exams. Exam prep was not good. He reads mostly out of the textbook and lectures are very boring. He is not super passionate which made it harder to pay attention. I'd recommend getting a different professor.

Pretty much everyone in my class failed, his lectures were unhelpful, his explainations made no sense and left everyone confused, if you don't have to have this professor then don't take it form someone else

Professor Lawley is a very good teacher, but his teaching style seems better suited for upper-level math courses. His lectures assume students already have a strong foundational understanding, and he focuses heavily on theory and proofs rather than examples. I would recommend using the library tutors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sean was very approachable, but you have to be prepared to work. The homework takes time, which is reasonable considering the advanced level of the course. It wasn't ideal that the entire grade was from quizzes/exams, but he was very clear that if you did your homework, you'd be fine, which was true. Attending class was important too.

Entire grade was based on quizzes and exams. Lectures were directly out of the textbook. Quizzes were every other class period and based on textbook problems which the instructor never discussed. Office hours were ill-timed - falling after the weekly quiz so getting help was very difficult. Overall, unreasonably stressful for no good reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's one of the best professors for mathematical biology.  He prepares for class and his course material is more up to date than many of the semi-retired professors who teach more of a 1990's perspective on math bio. I'd take another course with him in a heart beat, inspirational guy.

VERY hard class and he doesnt make it any easier. Weird structure with every single question asked on quizzes/exams from a known set of 700 so I didnt learn how to really do probs, only memorize. Office hours were after quizzes and before the next hw was released so they were obsolete. Lectures were recitations from the text. Choose another prof

Sean is very clear in lectures and takes time to explain things in different ways. Quizzes were tough sometimes but were based on homework mostly and lecture notes. Both mid-terms were reasonable, but I felt he mislead us as to what to study for the final. He did drop the 2 lowest quizzes and 3 lowest HWs. Plus he curved the grade at the end.

Sean was a good guy, I think he is a newer professor but he did a good job. His quizzes got kind of annoying and his tests are a little too long but the test questions are basic homework questions so that's a good thing if you do the homework. He dropped 2 lab packets, 3 homeworks, and 2 quizzes from our final grade.

I took 3 classes with Lary throughout college. Hardly any homework, and exams are not too difficult as long as you are paying attention during the lecture and review slides/study guide. He always has extra credit on tests. Lectures are engaging and very interesting. I have learned so much from him - if you get the chance to take his class, do it!
More like Larry Goats

Very cool guy. If you ski or snowboard this class is a must. Professor is easily approachable and has some awesome stories. Always liked showing up to class. If you take notes and study a couple hours for each test you should do very well. Would happily take him again

Professor Larry is great. He is very kind and he wants you to succeed in his class. If you show up to class and put in the work for quizzes and tests, he will make this class worth your while. He is very clear about what is on the exams so go to the exam reviews. I definitely recommend him to anyone.

Larry's passion for teaching is obvious and contagious. He makes topics like environmental science, geological history, and avalanche awareness easy to get into. The online setup can be a bit confusing at first, but if you attend class and pay attention, you'll get what you need—mostly just use the textbook.

Get ready to read because the textbook will make more sense than the lectures. He seems very knowledgeable and passionate; I just was not understanding his teaching. He is very unorganized online, and the canvas page is confusing to navigate. He calls the exams "objective assessments", but they are just essays. Overall easy class though. ENVST3210

I LOVE LARRY! what a skiing legend. he started class with his shred cred and it only got better from there. i expected a chill class with a bunch of ski bums but instead learned SO much about climate change and the environment in relation to skiing! larry is SO sweet and loves what he does. cannot recommend him enough. favorite college course yet!!

I have taken a few of his courses and this applies to all. He is a fantastic lecturer and a very fair professor. All of his assignments are challenging yet doable and as long as you are interested in geography they are somewhat fun to do. He usually offers opportunities to work with him in his lab at the start of the semester which I recommend.
Professor Coats is funny and knowledgeable. Attendance isn't super mandatory but it makes the quizzes and papers easier. Lots of extra credit was offered and the material was interesting.

Such an awesome class! Larry is an incredible, thoughtful professor that truly cares about his students. The 2 homework assignments are extremely straightforward, as are the quizzes and exams. As long as you study for the midterm and the final, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and super knowledgeable,he puts a ton of effort into his lectures and slides, show up to class and take quizzes, as long as you take most of the quizzes he will give you 100 percent. Show up class before tests as he will go over all the material and make sure to ask questions. Amazing professor highly reccommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor, his lectures were very entertaining while also getting the information to stick. he has some humor and great stories that connect the the modules. Little things were graded but he wasn't the hardest grader. Excepted tons of answers. Overall one of the best professors i've had.

This class was harder because I am not science savvy. The lectures and information were very interesting but it didn't click with me very easily. There were two BIG and LONG homework assignments, but they were a huge grade boost if you complete them with thought and effort. Online cuz covid otherwise I probably would done better and stick more!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Larry is one of the best professors I've ever had at the U! He's not only EXTREMELY knowledgable about the course material, but he's clearly very passionate, too. Tests were fair, and while attendance was mandatory (clicker quizzes), the lectures were always worth it! I would totally recommend his classes! :)

This first test was difficult but once I knew how to take his tests they weren't that bad. Take notes during class and make sure you go to the class period before the test day because he will go through the whole review with you! Ask questions! Make sure you study the review well because the test questions can be confusing.

Dr. Coats is THE professor to take global climate change from. I learned a ton in his class. He's passionate, funny, and kind; lectures are possibly the most interesting I have ever attended. His exams are worth a large portion of your grade but they aren't challenging if you go to class, pay attention, and take notes (he's so good you'll want to).

Larry is an extremely nice and caring man. I would 110% recommend the class to anyone who truly loves skiing/snowboarding. This was my favorite class I have taken at the U. Really cool snowfall collection & analysis project. I ended up walking away learning a ton of stuff as well. Tests are more than fair. Really cool speakers. A+++

He's very passionate about the subject. He tailors the tests to what he covered that specific semester in lecture, so it never feels like you're being tricked. He really cares that you know core concepts and doesn't get caught up in trivial details, which is awesome.

MUST TAKE HIS CLASS. Best professor ever. He is very understanding and knows the subject well. He is always there to help you and leaves you thinking after class. I think about what I learned in that class every day. Not a lot of homework and when he assigns homework it is easy and interesting to learn about. Great class, better professor!

One of the best professors I have ever had! Professor Coats is passionate about teaching, and gives some of the best lectures of any teacher I've taken. He is amazingly knowledgeable and posts some great information online, going above and beyond to inform his students. He is a pretty nice grader, and you will love his classes!

Larry is very passionate about geography and his intellect shows. He works with you to get the grade you want and there was barely any homework. He's a very nice and fair professor. The only complaint I have are the study guides. They were not the best but he does go over every single question the day before the tests.  Pay attention, ask questions

Larry is awesome! When I heard the U offered a Geography of Skiing class as a science credit I knew I had to take it. Larry makes the course super interesting and engaging. He shows that he cares about his students and genuinely wants them to do well. Final project was actually pretty fun, and the tests weren't bad with his reviews.

Larry is a great professor (one of my favorite at the U) He is great about explaining what he wants you to learn and is very reasonable in his expectations. You do have to use your mind and participate and gain knowledge to meet his expectation. I have taken his Natural Hazards class as well as Field Study and really enjoyed both classes very much

Intro to Natural Hazards: Larry offers clear information into natural processes. If you pay attention in class and read the chapters once you'll pass easily. He belabors his points, gives plenty of time between quizzes, and makes sure you understand what he will quiz you on. Good man. Entertaining. He's done a lot of cool stuff.

Classes are usually hard, but he is good. If you're not interested in the subject of the class, you may not do too well. I took a course that I didn't know anything about prior to his class and was completely lost all semester. However, he is great. He really knows his stuff, and loves what he teaches. Always willing to help and wants his students to do well.

I've had Larry before and I enjoy his courses. He's very helpful, always available during office hours or email, and displays a thorough knowledge of the subject material. His tests are my only complaint. At times, they seem purposefully deceptive. ("Check all that apply"-type questions specifically). Other than that, he's wonderful.
An awesome professor! He's very helpful and clear, the tests aren't hard at all. He'll tell you what you really need to know. It's interesting and he doesn't sound boring.
Fun class, learned a lot. Larry is a great teacher. Very clear! He does study groups before exams which helps a lot!!

Good professor and he is really nice :) This class is interesting and kinda fun. The exams are a little weird but class is not painful to sit through. He is very knowledgeable. We also talk about current events related to class.

The best Prof. I have had!!! Loves what he does, loves the subjects he teaches!! He is always willing to help. Need to attend class to keep caught up, but it is never boring. I will be taking more classes from him!! Almost thinking of changing my major cause of him!! Larry totally Rocks!!! Kinda hot for an older guy!!

I have taken three classes from thi professor. I really like his teaching methods. You have to go to class to stay caught up. But all of his lectures are really interesting. I would recommend taking from him.

Best prof i've had at the U. He is really smart and definatley loves this subject. You have to go to class to get the information, but he is always willing to further explain things. The tests are fine becuase he'll let you know what you need to know. He is really teaching, he doesn't trick students. I would take another class from him
Genuinely worst class I have ever taken. Harder than anatomy. Professor unreachable and class taken over by another prof after the first midterm.

only graded on 3 tests. no extra cred or hw. he was totally inaccessible and another prof actually had to take over half way thru. overall not super hard but be prepared to read and watch all of the video material. proctored exams often glitchy.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Josh is nice, but beware, the formatting changed, so 100% of your grade is exams. No assignments, no extra credit. The textbook is nighmerishly long (it takes 2-3+ hours per chapter), and he doesn't specify what will be asked. No lectures, just YouTube videos and research articles. An interesting class, but the formatting almost ruins it all.

Changed the outline of the class so there are ONLY 3 exams that go on your grade! No credit for any readings or discussions. I'm a good student but might not even pass the class. SO HARD, lots of reading, difficult exams, bad setup.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors from my time at the U.

One of, if not the best, professors I've had. Very hands-on and passionate about what he teaches. I couldn't recommend him enough. I thought that because it was online, it would be harder, but the professor made it so engaging that it was very easy to follow along week to week. Will definitely be taking another class with this professor

Joshua is a very caring professor and takes his time to get to know you if you show interest in the material and show genuine curiosity to learn and apply yourself to the class. He responds promptly, grades everything, and sets clear expectations. Your chances of doing well in this class are 100% if you put in the effort; nothing hard about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor LaReaux is an amazing professor. I took the first session online summer class. He is very engaging and provides great and personal feedback. The class had readings, quizzes, and written assignments each week. Study the quizzes for the final exam and you'll do fine.
One of my favorite classes because of the professor. He's clear about how he grades and he gives amazing feedback. He keeps the information current, and he's funny. Just stay on top of the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved his class, super interesting material and he always added current events. The class was structured well with lectures/videos, textbook reading, and a quiz each week, and some weeks a writing assignment too. All writing is opinion based and critical thinking, and he gives great feedback. Easy class if you stay on top of your work.

I cannot understate when I say that Josh is the single best professor I have taken in my life. If you need to take 4900 take it in person with him. He one of the most caring individuals I have ever met, and really makes an effort to connect personally with each of his students. He is extremely caring, honerable, and hilarious!

Professor LaReaux makes this a simple class with only a handful of graded assignments (1-2 per week + midterm + final) and gives 20 "mulligan" points of extra credit that cover anything that comes up or boosts your grade at the end of the semester. He was also very caring of all students and made sure that everyone understood his feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor LaReaux is a great professor, I have only taken online classes with him but he does a really good job at keeping the course interesting and showing that he cares. I think he has given helpful and insightful feedback on every assignment I have turned in. 10/10 would take a class from him again.

He is a super chill and nice guy, class isn't difficult. He often puts videos to watch within timed quizzes which is bothersome. Everything is due on Thursdays at 5 which is a bit inconvenient for students who have to work a lot during the week. Wish due dates were on Sunday. Easy A though.

Joshua is one of my favorite teachers as he is super engaging with students and gives wonderful feedback on assignments, This was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken and was super intrigued by the content. If you enjoy sports and everything that revolves around it TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Lareaux is one of the coolest people I've met. He's super fun and gives great feedback on assignments, he cares for his students and doesn't make content difficult. He engages students and encourages us to involve ourselves. One 10-question quiz and one written assignment were pretty much what you had every week. Take this class!

One of my all-time favorite professors at the U. He actually takes the time to read your papers and gives feedback on the entire thing, line by line. His feedback is always uplifting and confidence boosting. He cares about what he's teaching and makes it natural for students to care too. Perfect class to take during a harder semester.

LaReaux is the best Professor I have ever had. He truly cares about his students and gives work that is atually meaningful and can impact you if you put the effort in. Take him for 4900, although I know there is a waitlist for his class, it's for a reason, he is the BEST!!!!!

He makes the class very doable especially when taking a heavier course load. Usually just 1 written assignment and 1 quiz every week. The module content is honestly really interesting, and he does his best to make sure the content is engaging and easy to access. Loved this class!
Very kind and thoughtful professor. Personable, and really interesting class!!!
Best professor experience at the U so far. Feedback is exceptional, and he really cares about his students. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, such an amazing class to be apart of! This class got me so into sports medicine and the sports world! Learned a lot of new things! Josh definitely cares about you, sends you reminders about homework, and all in general an amazing professor and person! Definitely HIGHLY recommend taking his class!!!
Cool guy and a super easy grader. Learned lots.

I actually went into this class with no interest in sports, but I ended up really enjoying the material. It was a very interesting class and the weekly assignment were just about the same every week (quiz & short paper). He gave great feedback & is very interested in his course material. You also get 1 week off of your choosing, which doesn't hurt
Josh was a great professor! You have an assignment and a open-note open-internet quiz a week, which is very manageable and typically very easy. Easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. LaReaux truly cares about his students. You are expected to complete the work, but he rewards effort. He is super funny and a very relatable person. He inspires his students and wants them to succeed in the real world. 11/10 experience with him.

trust me: take this class when you have a heavy semester. It's literally the easiest KINES class there is. Quiz answers are on a certain online flashcard site, and the weekly writing assignments were never too difficult. I don't like sports so I was bored at times, but if that's your thing then you'll love this class.
Amazing professor I would gladly take again! Gave great feedback on all of our papers.

This class was easier than most, with few assignments that seem like they are just busywork. Easier A. Interesting controversial concepts within the sports community. I am not sure if I am the only one but he would grade my assignments and put negative comments or point out things I didn't do but then gave me an A on the assignment every time...?

You'll read a chapter in the textbook a week with a quiz on it that is open note/book (command f - your best friend). You also have a paper every week, but they are not ad at all. It basically is to check and see if you read and watched the content (if any) for the week. I never got less than a 100 on any of the papers. He is a very understanding!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Hard to get into contact with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class is self-directed and there is an internship with the course. I loved the internship I was placed in but because of COVID, the online format of this course was not the best. When I told him my concerns he would listen but then never update us or tell us how to submit with those changes. He did say that next semester would be better tho.

Josh is the greatest professor on campus. The most caring professor you will ever meet, he wants you to be a success. He makes boring diversity topics interesting and engaging. You will want to be a better human after taking his capstone class.

This is a hybrid class, meaning you do most of the work outside of class and then during class, you discuss what you learned. Most of your grade is quizzes and assignments that are very straight forward. As long as you do your homework, this class is an easy A. Professor Lareaux is very laid back and makes his lectures interesting.

Follows a nice formula- each week you read a chapter, take a quiz, and write a short paper. Fun class and actually learned quite a bit from the readings. He (and the TA) gave pretty thorough feedback on the written assignments most of the time, which was cool.

This class was pretty easy, there is always one quick written assignment and one quiz due each week. Everything is online and open-note so getting a good grade is not hard. The teacher gives good feedback.

Josh has been my favorite professor at the U! This class was an open discussion as well as some lecture, but he honestly wants to hear people's opinions and doesn't get offended. He's funny and easy to talk to. He wants to see his students succeed and will work with you. He gives great feedback on assignments. Take his class!
I loved Josh's teaching style. The class was informative and he cares about the topics and the students. He is perhaps my favorite professor.
Great professor to take for online class. One assignment and one quiz due every week on Sunday night. I recommend you get the ebook textbook because you can search for quiz answers.

This is an online class. Lots of work but not too hard. It is a lot if you work full time. The coursework was broken down into sections. If you don't complete the section, you can't move on. The quizzes were annoying because I had missed questions that there were many right answers for. He gives powerpoints and expects you watch movies online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took this class online, got an A by doing the assignments and quizzes. Assignments weren't hard at all, quizzes were a little tough, but use your power points and book and you'll be fine. You can go as slow or fast as you want, but there's usually a quiz and assignment every week due on Sunday.

This was the best online class I've ever taken. Professor La Reaux made the class fun--it wasn't just lecture notes and quizzes, you also watched video clips and movies. The quizzes can be a little hard, but as long as you have the textbook you should be fine.  I would recommend this class to anyone, and would take it again.

Lareaux was by FAR my favorite professor for all of college. He was so motivational and such a great teacher. He truly made me want to come back and take more classes. He is awesome as a teacher, mentor, and friend. If you have the option to take the class from him...  DO IT.

This is a great class and Josh is a great professor. Very clear and interesting lectures, he cares about his students, and is reasonable and helpful if you have a problem. Attendance not mandatory, but he gives out free test questions when you come. Never took notes (PPTX online), never read the book ("required" text not necessary). Finished at 95%

Josh cares about his students and loves connecting on a personal level. He rewards people who show up for class with test answers and questions, but does not punish people who skip. He really knows his stuff and the lectures are a pleasure to attend.

Dr. Lair is a great professor. She's intimidating at first (still is honestly). She's tough on grading and rarely if ever gives full points for participation. But you're GUARANTEED to improve in her class, and she clearly cares deeply for her work and students.

Madame Lair was an excellent French professor. She wants you to improve your French skills and your grade will reflect your effort to work towards increasing your proficiency. That being said, she is tough when it comes to grading, but as long as you are in class every day and complete assignments, you will be successful in this class.

Dr. Lair is a great professor. My time in this class vastly improved my French skills. The class is rigorous and Prof. Lair will challenge you but she does so knowing that you can improve. High workload, but each assignment felt important and contributed to the learning objectives. This class is a must-take if you want to improve your French.

I decided to take this class because I was considering doing a French minor, but I decided not to after this class. I showed up to every class period and only received grades for six days of the twenty-something days. The grade I received in this class didn't accurately reflect the work and effort I put into it.

I LOVE Madame Lair. Easily one of my best french profs I've ever had. She is so kind and incredible at creating a class environment where students at every level still learn. She's been so clear about what homework needs to get done, and every assignment is curated so well to what we need to know most. Her feedback is incredible. Would recommend.

Dr. Lair is definitely scary and intimidating, especially at first. Her class is fun and engaging and if you put in the bare minimum amount work, you'll see improvement. She grades pretty tough and is super reluctant to give full credit on anything, especially participation.

Dr. Lair is encouraging and teaches effectively. You must participate in class, though the participation grades are ambiguous and she refuses to clarify them. If you attend every day, are on time, and raise your hand, you still won't get full points. You will lose points for absences unless you provide an obituary or a doctor's note.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Incredible professor! She help me improve my French immensely. She gives in depth, insightful feedback on writing assignments, and is truly great. Honestly, she's one of my favorite teachers. If Dr. Lair's name is on a course, sign me up!

Dr. Lair is intimidating but personable at the same time. Although she's strict, she works tirelessly with her students to make sure they understand the material. This class was not accessible outside of class at all, so attendance is a must. If you want to work hard and improve your French, Dr. Lair is the right prof for you.

Dr. Lair is super intimidating at first, and she can be really tough if she feels you aren't trying hard enough. She is a really good professor though, and I definitely learned a lot from her class and would take a course with her again.

Dr. Lair definitely may come off as intimindating at first, but don't let that fool you, because she has a heart of gold. Make sure to communicate with her, and stay on top of stuff, because if you do, she will absolutely help you when you're struggling. She and I had a heart-to-heart and it totally made me reevaluate the way I approach learning.

This class was a bit of work and the topic was not something that interested me personally, which is why I struggled a bit, but Dr. Lair is a fair grader, makes sure you are learning, and has you put in a lot of work. If you take her, just know that you are in for a journey, because she is there to make sure you are challenged.

Dr. Lair is very much a professional professor and takes her teaching very seriously. She dislikes it when people skips class and will make your life very difficult if you do. She will, however, recognize your hard work and grade fairly if she knows that you are trying and improving. She's there to help you succeed, not to fail you.

One of my favorite professors! I learned a lot from her classes and all the effort I put into it was actually worth it. I am taking another class with her next semester because even if she really makes you work for your grades I feel like she recognizes your effort. Don't forget to do a composition EVERY time before class and the online assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her lectures don't seem to follow any particular format and are extremely unorganized. However, you can't miss class as she announces everything in class (almost nothing is announced on canvas). It is extremely difficult to keep track of everything.  The textbook is a good resource, and the online assignment MyFrenchLab has great practical value
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: So awesome, saw that I have Professor Mcbrayer for another class I'm taking this semester and almost jumped and did 4 backflips in my room.

Prof. McBrayer is a spectacular professor. His lectures are engaging and he is very funny. He is super understanding and chill. If you do your part and participate in class you will be just fine. The only real assignments are a weekly discussion and a final paper which is giving a rebuttal to an AI written paper which is cool. Highly recommend.

The professor and class structure was great. It was very easy but still impactful and I learned so much. Every two weeks, you read a chapter in the online textbook, finish an InQuizitive assignment, watch a couple lecture videos (with short integrated quizzes), and write up a discussion post. I put the lectures on like podcasts and it was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took his 5-day intensive world religions course. I learned a lot both from him and the textbook. Daily discussions and reflections after class. Very simple midterm/final exam. Worth taking it to complete your gen ed and diversity class. There was one two-hour zoom session towards the end of the semester, but that's it.

Professor McBrayer has been a great teacher, and his class has been amazing. He likes to make video lectures fun and playful, and they're enjoyable to watch. The class workload is easily manageable and not difficult, it just involves a lot of reading. There are no real tests or quizzes. Highly recommend taking his class!

McBrayer's Problem of Evil is one of the easiest classes I've taken throughout college. It's an easy A if you show up, do most of the readings, and do the weekly 1-2 minute video response. My only issue with the class is that McBrayer can be passive when encouraging/directing in-class discussion. Because of this, the class can feel a bit too short.

I took the one-week intensive World Religions course and loved it. It I got to learn a lot about different religions while not having to stress too much. Graded by pre-lecture quizzes (infinite attempts), attend, discussion posts, and then 2 open book exams at your convenience. Learned a lot while having fun. Couldn't of asked for anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor McBrayer's class. This was the class I was dreading the most at the start of the semester since I thought the material would be pretty boring. However, I ended up really enjoying the material and there are a lot of good interesting readings. The class was pretty easy, just do all the assignments and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor i absolutely loved his online class, he always found some way to make the lectures interesting and fun, seems like a great guy. Hes always open for questions and the course was structured very well I would definitely recommend!
I took the FLEX class and it was nice. He's really chill and makes the classroom environment very inviting and fun. Is good about being open to questions and answering them if he can.

I loved this World religions class! His lectures were amazing and always had answerable questions during them that keeps you  participating. I loved the insights and how he didn't discuss his own religious beliefs. He recommended topics to look up and where to look them up if you were interested but were not required. 10/10 recommend.

McBrayer is a fantastic professor. I was very impressed with his ability to teach about a subject as sensitive as religion without letting any bias or agenda slip out. He is very knowledgable and teaches in a way that gives you genuine interest in all of the religions covered. It's not a difficult class by any means but does require some effort.

Professor McBrayer did an excellent job teaching an entire course in just one week (I took the intensive course). He kept our 8-hour-long lectures fun and educational and made sure to add in a decent amount of breaks. His schedule organization was impressive and he presented the information in a way where everything was built off of each other.

His teaching was effective. Class was easy and genuinely interesting. The homework allows you to answer questions until you've reached the grade you want. The exams were based entirely on the lecture material so you don't have to do the reading if you don't have time (exams are also online and open resource). I didn't even buy the second textbook.

Since I had his online class, I can tell you that he is not great at teaching through this way. I don't know how he is in-person. He pre-records lectures that are at least 40 minutes long and there are tons of them you have to watch each block. The textbook he gives you to read is the worst textbook I've ever come across.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Landon was so chill, almost too chill haha. I took the week long course which was really fast paced , but could get dull because 8 hours a day. However, the class is super easy and very interesting. Learning the basics about religions was eye opening, and I appreciated how simple the class was. If you need the requirement, take his class. Easy A!

Landon makes the course for world religion worthwhile by being super informative. His easy going personality also fits very well for a class that can deal with confronting people's own personal beliefs. Easy recommend!

Took the week long version of this class. Was very fast paced (as expected), but Professor McBrayer was very enthusiastic and was able to crack a few jokes here and there. For a week long class, I learned a lot and the class was well structured. If you are really into religions, I would take a longer version of this class; I wish I had!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McBrayer is THE most chill professor. Due to covid it was online. He got us free access to our online textbook and weekly quizzes were linked to the website (inquisitive). If you want a 100, you keep answering questions till you get it! His recorded lectures and study guides have everything for the test and has fun humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For this Masters course in Philosophy of Science, Dr. McBrayer delivers. The course is more a seminar than a lecture, and as such class time was very conversational and even argumentative. Be prepared to read and write alot. The reading is definitely interesting, spanning things such as mathematical realism to the "arguments" around climate change
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Landon's lectures were super interesting and I learned a lot in this course. He made controversial subjects easy to discuss and never shot down any of our ideas. Weekly discussions were easy, but the tests were a little tricky sometimes. Great prof for a gen ed requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Landon is a great choice for this course. While he is not a business major himself, he makes this class bearable and tries to get the class involved in the discourse. The weekly readings are a bit dull but Landon is a very easy grader. His study guides may seem daunting but his easy grading makes up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really cool guy! Relates well with the students and gives awesome philosophical analogies and examples when answering students questions. It is obvious he is well-versed in the material and he relates well with the students. Definitely would take him again!

Lectures from Dr. McBrayer are amazing and very interesting. Do the weekly reading in addition to the lectures because sometimes his weekly quizzes will contain questions he hasn't answered in lecture. Exams are not bad because he gives a study guide for the midterm and final.

Cool class. Attendance isn't mandatory but I'd go listen to the lectures, they are not bad. 10 weekly readings (takes about two hours at most), a midterm and a final which are easy if you do the study guide he gives you.

I would highly recommend taking this course from Prof. McBrayer. The content is incredibly interesting and you can tell Landon is passionate about it. Attendance isn't mandatory, but going to each lecture definitely helps you on exams as well as the weekly quizzes. You can also find cheap options for the textbook online via Amazon.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher and has some great informative lectures. Has one quiz a week and if you do the assigned reading the quizzes are extremely easy. Landons course is very fun and interesting, and if you pay attention, do the reading, and show up to class youll pass with ease. The one issue I had (in my class) was the grading was extremely slow.

Landon is a good teacher! He is pretty young and even though the way he talks is down to earth he still knows the content. I took the condensed week class. There was a lot to learn in a short amount of time and it was lecture heavy, obviously it had to be. Small group activities and talking to class but nothing too scary. I was happy I took this.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: LOVED this class and LOVED the teacher. I looked forward to lectures and the coursework wasn't ridiculous. This was not taken for my major, but was one of my favorite classes!

Great teacher, learned a lot from his class. Bumped my grade up half a percent to an A without me even asking. Has quizzes every week on a random day so you have to show up to class, but don't have to pay too much attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gives really great lectures that basically teach you everything you need to know to pass the class. Quizzes are random so be sure to attend class. Not the easiest A but you'll pass!

Understanding that most people who take World Religions aren't philosophy majors, Landon does a great job breaking down philosophical concepts in correspondence with religious diversity. This class is genuinely very interesting. As long as you attend the lectures, you'll do fine on the weekly quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Landon is great, but his lectures aren't the most organized. They can also be a little dry. But he's clear with what you should know for tests and that's all you need really. Not a bad class, just not a great one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Landon is a decent teacher, but his lectures can be kind of boring because he reads off of an outline most of the class. He does try to get the class involved to his credit and most of the guest speakers were really interesting. Graded work included 3 short papers, 2 tests and weekly quizzes. He takes ages to grade work though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The classes are well laid out, easy A if you pay attention to the lectures or do the reading. He takes a long time to grade.

Great teacher with a clear outline of what needed to be done for every week. His video lectures were informative and made it east to do the assignments. This class actually requires effort, so don't expect an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Landon gave great video lectures and as a result this was the most effective online course I've taken at the U. If you're looking for an easy A the doesn't require hours each week, this probably isn't for you.
He is very willing to go out of his way to help, and his class always has a stress-free positive environment.

Perhaps he's not like this for his other classes, but for World Religion he seemed extremely apathetic and lazy. He's not on canvas, which makes contacting him and keeping track of upcoming events very difficult. He doesn't update study guides, so what you spend hours studying might not actually reflect the test. He's easy going, but not helpful.

Landon is a very good teacher.  He's very helpful.  He's casual and straight forward.  Reading the text and attendance aren't "required" unless you want to pass the class.  He's generous with his assignments and expectations.  If you show up and put a little effort into the class you will learn a great deal.
Awesome professor! He is super chill and knows a lot about the subject. This class can get pretty heated, I mean you are studying religion after all. I highly reccommend any class from him!

Extremely condescending. Gets defensive and rude when asked simple clarifying questions in lecture. I'm not sure where the university found this lady. I think maybe she should spend more time in her lab and less time teaching, because she clearly doesn't seem to be very good at it.

reviews.comment: Harsh grading, Problem sets due at Friday 1 pm, Lectures not helpful, Barely any resources were provided.
