reviews.comment: Leslie has a unique approach to teaching that has even earned her a reward. You have homeworks, group projects, and tests every three weeks. The tests aren't too difficult since there only so much can be covered in five classes. She really cares about your success and understanding of the material and will work with you if you're not getting it.

She definitely deserves that teaching award she got. She is an awesome lecturer. I learned a ton in dev bio, I think that having a small class size defiantly played a big role on the class being so focused, interactive and creating a friendly learning environment. You do got to put some work in, but Leslie is always there every step of the way :-)

Leslie is the most interactive teacher you will ever have in college. She will know your name, is interested in your success, very approachable and very enthusiastic. You have an assigned scientific paper that is discussed every class and you will have to answer a question on it. Tests are hard but if you understand the papers you will be ok.
I did research work in her lab for a few semester. Leslie is a very difficult professor to work with outside the classroom.

I took cell bio in 2003 - I thought her tests weren't too bad. I even remember her using dancing to explain chaperones in DNA folding. She got annoyed once when I asked a question in review session -the question was beyond what was on the exam so it wasn't uncalled for. She's an ok lecturer/professor but I can't recommend working in her lab.

She is the best teacher! She tries to make class interactive and fun since it's a smaller class than her 2020 class (way small! like 14 ppl)and puts up webcasts to prepare you before class so you can discuss it. I didn't even have to study much before her exams, awesome exams! If you support it, she'll give you points.
Awesome graphics, good problem sets

I struggled to be interested while she was lecturing.  She doesn't involve the class well.  It is quite boring.  If you can study and learn the important stuff on your own that will help but then she throws some random questions on the test that have little to do with anything lectured or read. I was not satisfied with the class.
best teacher i have had, has an awesome way of explaining concepts so that you can remember them.

Unless you're a mind reader I wouldn't recommened taking it from her.  Her tests have ridiculous questions, she lectures too fast, and be prepared to take a beating if you try and ask her a question.  She gets very angry, especially if you try and talk to her one on one.  Take Gard, he's hard but very predictable.

absolutely horrendous.  take GARD!!!  please, for your own sake, this woman is evil and has her favorites.  she doesn't teach well at all, refuses to answer insightful questions, and leaves all of her grading up to power-trippin' TA's.  avoid at all costs!
horrible, though she may have a reputation of being easy her tests are horribly written and is not based on the material taught

she is energetic, but she makes things too complicated.  tons of memorization, but is good prep for more advanced biol courses.  when asked questions, she gets really short and doesn't know what they are talking about
Very difficult to understand.  Questions students for asking questions.  Seems irritated that a student doesn't understand a topic from her lecture.
She says she wants you to know the general overall idea, but then tests specifics...BEWARE!!!  Took two of the four tests to figure that out.
No Comments

fav professor. He gives 6% worth of extra credit. So sweet you know he loves teaching and interacting with students. 5 Exams just know how to prioritize time and use all resources. Class isnt mandatory, he provides his lecture notes after but hides critical material so THAT you go to class. He made sense but with some topics he went over quick.

My first professor that seemed to really care what he was talking about. Class was easy to get a routine of. I did not read the textbook but was able to create good study tactics through his assignments. Loved this class.
such a fun lecturer! very good at explaining things and making sure his students know the expectations as well as the material.

Absolutely fantastic instructor! I really loved this class. His lectures are so interesting; he clearly understands the material, even the content that's not developmental psych. He gives you so many opportunities to succeed too. Seriously, just do the readings, the quizzes, the easy extra credit, review the lecture notes, and you'll do fine.
Prof Raby was very knowledgeable and his Lectires are layed out well. He's passionate and cares for his students. Use the resources given to study for exams. Very well structured class

I liked Professor Raby! I thought his lectures were super interesting and he cares a lot about our education. The exams can be a little tough, just make sure to study the study guides super well, instead of cramming. I enjoyed his class!

If you are fascinated by developmental psych, take this course! Raby is extremely passionate, knowledgeable, and an experienced researcher. His lectures are engaging, the content is unendingly interesting. Show up (there are 8 "pop quiz" in-class activities), take notes, and you'll do well. One of the best psych courses!

By far my favorite psych class I have ever taken. Professor Raby is a fantastic lecturer and tries to deepen the understanding of psychology to his students. The exams were difficult but passable with solid studying. The only other grades were 4 essays and in class assignments. He also offered an optional cumulative final to boost your grade.

graded on 4 quizzes and 4 essays. The essays aren't graded harshly, but the TA is picky with sticking to the page #, and formatting requirements. Quizzes are in person, closed note, and require a very, very, thorough understanding of the material. The professor is one of the best; lectures can drag and be boring, but they are crucial to success.

He tells fun stories in his lectures but you better take good notes AND read the textbook or you'll struggle on the tests. I found him engaging and extremely likeable. Never needed help outside of class but if I did, I wouldn't have been afraid to ask.

I enjoyed this class. The Professor is cool and is good at teaching, the material is also engaging. There are no exams, just 12 quizzes and 4 papers. Overall, you got to put in some work, but it should be an easy class.

I would not recommend this class at all. The quizzes are hard to understand. You're also under a small limit making them stressful to complete and have enough time. There are four essays, and you're graded rough on them. The lectures are really boring and long. Also he doesn't offer any extra credit, I don't know why people on here say he does.

Dr. Raby is one of my favorite psychology professors. His lectures are interesting, and you can tell he cares about his students and his work. The class is not the easiest, as assignments and quizzes are structured so that you have to be prepared and really understand the material, but it is nothing too crazy as long as you decently apply yourself.

You can tell he truly cares about his students, but his lectures are a bit numb sometimes given the class content. 12 tests make up 60% of the grade rather than tests, so preparation for those is a must. 4, 3 page writing assignments every month and random inclass assignments. Quizzes are fairly punishing if you don't do well but overall good class

Easy class, definitely should have earned an A but the TA's are rough graders and the quiz drops don't improve your overall grade. Class content was a snooze, it felt like AP Psych or 1010 all over again. Prof Raby is very nice and caring. Good prof, weird grading, meh content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the best professor I have ever had. He makes the lectures very interesting and engaging and uses a lot of examples to make content memorable and easy to understand. He is funny and relaxed and it is evident he cares a lot about his students and making sure they understand, and is just a really good professor who is very likeable.

Dr. Raby is a great professor, his lecture was very interesting and easy to understand because he gave a lot of real-life examples. There were 12 quizes instead of big exams, those quizes were not that easy because they were based on real-life practices, but you'll be good if you attend every classes and have the notes with you. Definately take it!

He has good lectures and encourages everyone to come to class. He had a few in-class assignments that you could only complete in class that day, but he let you drop 2. He didn't have any tests/finals and just had us do weekly quizzes which were relatively easy if you went to the lecture. The 4 writing assignments were pretty easy.
He's nice and consistent.

Dr. Raby is amazing! The class is lecture heavy, and although attendance is not mandatory the quizzes are difficult if you weren't in class. There are no exams and instead he just does 12 questions quizzes(open book, ope note) each week which is a fair trade for those who hate exams. It is an easy course if you attend class and take notes!

To succeed in this class, all you have to do is do the readings and the extra credit. Attending lecture is also beneficial, but you do not even have to study to do decent on the tests. Raby wants everyone to succeed and is not out to trick anyone. Great professor, interesting class.

IN PERSON, CLOSED NOTE, ON PAPER TESTS! He makes this class way too hard for a gen ed. Everyone else that I have talked to that has had a different professor said that this class was really easy, but his class is in fact not. You have 6 exams throughout the semester, and he drops the lowest. Study guides dont help whatsoever. I do not recommend.
Love this professor super understanding and interesting lectures. Offers a lot of extra credit and tests are straightforward.

Raby is a great professor. His class is very lecture heavy and the exams are kind of long and require decent effort but he definitely wants his students to succeed and structures the class accordingly. There are lots of opportunities for points and extra credit. You'll get out what you put in.

Prof Raby has structured his class in an organized, straight-forward way. I was never confused about what I was supposed to do for homework or what to study for tests. He gives insightful lectures without making them feel boring. As long as I was doing the reading and mostly paying attention in class, I had to do very minimal studying.

So much studying for a gen ed. Do not take this if you're looking for an easy gen ed. Making a quizlet for the everything that will be on a midterm is 100+ terms. There are five midterms you have to study for throughout the quarter so you'll be studying a lot every couple weeks for them. Overall WAY too much work for a gen ed.

This is an amazing class. It's set up as a lecture with the options of viewing online or in person. If you miss a class, he posts all the information/slides to canvas. He is very flexible and fair. When there isn't enough research opportunities, he provides alternate assignments. Same goes with the exams. If there was a trick question, he drops it.

I was worried because this semester was online and I dont do well with online classes but prof raby was really engaging and lively and was able to pass along the information in a really straight forward way.

Was his first semester teaching online and it wasnt that bad. Attendance is not required and he uploaded his zoom lectures every time along with his slides. You dont need the book but Id highly recommend it just because he used some info from the book that he didnt talk about in class on exams. Hes super chill and funny, I liked his class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Raby was very passionate and his lectures were easy to follow. He drops the lowest test score and most course credit comes from readings/ open note quizzes. If you can take the time to study for a few hours before each test, this will be an easy class. Happy to meet with students outside of class.

Raby was an awesome professor. You can tell he's super passionate about what he teaches, and really makes lectures enjoyable and interesting. Most of the class grade comes from exams, but he supplies test reviews for each test that clearly outline what to study. He really cares about the subject and his students. I very highly recommend his class.

Pretty solid guy. Classes consisted of a lecture, with occasional (very few) in-class activities. Since attendance was mandatory, these assignments ended up counting for extra credit. Otherwise, grade is mostly made up of your exams and a couple of essays. Overall great class. Definitely felt like he knew what he was talking about.

Raby was a real fun professor in the sense that he always came to class with a positive energy even if the rest of the class was dead. 95% of grading is based off exams but he really provides you with study guides so you can pass them. He even offers an optional exam at the end for those that need it. Highly recommend for into level psych class.
Amazing professor. Makes lectures very interesting. Tests are not bad if you study early and are prepared. 10/10

Your final grade primary comes from exam scores so definitely study. If you're not good at exams it's hard to get a great grade in this class. Most of the time the book has more info than the lectures so its not mandatory for you to attend class. You have to participate in research studies but those are pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Raby really cares about his students and he is very clear about what is expected of you in his class. Follow his study guides, learn the vocabulary and you will excel in his course. There are two papers that are meaningful applications of the content learned. He is passionate about Social Development and it shows.
He's great. He's hilarious. If you're looking for an easy class, this is it. I never studied and I passed with flying colors. Bless this man.

In this class although its an easy A you also learn so much! The only homework is an online textbook and you are required to read it as well as take a quiz and an extra credit game/questions. I would recommend always doing the extra credit. I didn't go to class but I did study a lot and I went to the reviews before the test and ended with a 98%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was Mr. Raby's first semester teaching and he did a great job, one of the best classes I've taken. Its full of lectures,  weekly quizzes which you are allowed a page a notes. Class has 3 exams which if you study his slides you will do fine. Allows for you to drop lowest test score and 2 lowest quiz scores. Very passionate teacher.

She's a good professor but her classes are very boring. Attendance is 10% of your grade. I didn't show up to class twice and my grade went from 100% to 90%. She also has many assignments due at 11:59 am and not 11:59pm. Missed some assignments because of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took QUEST 1130 with Dr. Pedersen. She was incredibly nice and inspirational when she gave lectures. Her class was very reading heavy, but otherwise I have no complaints.

Though I didn't love the class, I thought Dr. Pedersen made the material easy to digest and relevant. The class wasn't too difficult, be prepared for the Quizzes, the first one was very difficult. Overall she was a good professor who actually cared if you did well, she was very flexible, just reach out before hand.

Great professor! Sometimes the lectures were a drag but she was very lenient and willing to work with you. She even reaches out to struggling students to check in with them. TAKE NOTES ON THE PRESENTATION. That is the majority of test content. She was very easy to get ahold of if needed. I highly recommend Dr. Pedersen.
Textbook not really required, I didnt use it once. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Louise is awesome! Very approachable, nice, and knowledgable. Course material is super interesting, great intro class. Four papers, they're tough if you don't care about the material. However she provides great feedback and honestly is an easy grader if she can tell you're trying. Attend class. Also textbook readings aren't required

I took the course from her online.  The material is SUPER confusing and she uses big words to sound smart.  Be prepared to write a paper weekly and deal with a lot of people that get offended by EVERYTHING.  I would not recommend taking this course from her.  Look elsewhere.

For a difficult subject like Organic Chemistry, many students are looking for a professor who strives to make the class as easy as possible. That is not Dr. Looper. He wants his class to challenge you. Read the textbook (I can't overemphasize this) and do the book problems. At the end of the day he curved grades dramatically, so I can't complain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ryan Looper is a cool guy, but the class was rough. Lectures were way too fast and completely disorganized; you could barely copy everything down before he erased it. Canvas page was also a mess. The exams were incredibly difficult and basically nothing like the homework. Would not recommend taking the class.

VERY difficult class, but amazing prof. He's super funny, gives really good examples, and his lectures are very fast-paced and visual (he's always drawing things out on the whiteboard), which works great for the way I learn, but it doesn't work for everyone, so be aware of that. 

Don't take his snark seriously - he wants you to succeed :)

Dr. Looper is a great person but not a great teacher. His canvas page was very unorganized and his tests were unnecessarily difficult. His lectures were just him writing on a white board so if you missed lecture too bad because no class notes were ever posted. He has his way of teaching and doesn't budge so be prepared to teach yourself a lot.

Ryan is a great professor and an even greater human. You can tell he is passionate about his work and genuinely cares about his students' success. Try your best, ask for help, and you will be glad you took his class :)

Wanna feel like an idiot? Take honors OChem from Looper. He's nice enough but his lectures are confusing, he doesn't use any sort of powerpoints, and often goes off on tangents about his research. In the days leading up to the final I studied 14 hours a day and only managed a 70%. 50 point x-cred assignment at end of semester, he curves the class 2

Prof. Looper is AMAZING! His class is challenging but it is entirely worth it. If you really really really wanna learn Organic Chemistry, I would definitely take it from him. He is really passionate about the field and his lectures are phenomenal. Go to Discussion! His problem sets and exams are brutal but he and the TA's are always there to help.

Looper clearly knows his stuff, but if given the chance, I should NEVER have taken his class. Very harsh. Laughed when I failed the first exam, and said that some people just don't get OChem. Long lectures that have nothing to do with the homework, and has no interest in helping you outside of class, but he will if you persist. Didn't learn anythin
Looper was one of the best professors that I have had in a while. He is hilarious and very helpful if you go to office hours.

He is an incredible professor.  It is clear that he is enthusiastic about OChem, and wants to relay that enthusiasm onto his students.  He demands a lot, but he's also more than willing to help you if you show sincere interest.  Don't take his sarcasm/criticism seriously.  He truly wants everyone to do well.

Wonderful lecturer and teacher, but the exams are extremely difficult. Often pulled mechanisms from his own research. On the other hand, he gives you a hands on experience to what organic chemistry really is, not just a superficial view. Pushed students to learn organic chemistry above and beyond the average Ochem 2 course. Overall, very good!

Dr. Looper is a wonderful professor. His lectures are very clear and easy to understand. His exams, however, are the hardest I've ever taken. He does end up curving the class, because most his test averages were in the 40s. Overall a great course!

I took the advanced org chem lab from him. His lectures were interesting and he lectures very clearly. The lab was actually cool, and he took a great interest in every section's work. He expects you to understand the material, so you must study well.
If you want to learn Orgo-go with Prof.Looper. He's crazy demanding but obviously 'cause he wants you to love the subject like he does.

I really enjoyed his class.  He's very sarcastic, and can make you feel dumb at times, but he usually doesn't mean it.  He is incredibly smart, and his tests are the hardest I've ever taken.  If you enjoy chemistry, and like to work hard, take this class!  Discussion attendance is necessary to do well.

Incredibly hard. He made fun of students that were having difficulty with the class.  Despite my interest in Ochem I had an extremely hard time learning from his teaching style. His expectations are too high for undergrads.  He's very educated and knows the subject well, but it's not worth taking the class.
Hard but fair. Incredibly good lecturer... pushes you to learn above and beyond

Honors OChem 1 & 2. Very hard tests; studying will not get you very far. Discussion attendance necessary to do well, more than even lecture attendance. Most examples from the book, but doing the problems doesn't help. Sometimes grad problems show up on the discussion sets, which are hard but doable. If you like chem. then take it--you learn a lot.
The BEST professor I have ever had.  I ended up changing my major from Biology to Anthropology and graduated with B.A. in Anthropology.

Professor Loeb pushes students really hard with reading and writing, but I learned more in his class by far than most all classes I have ever taken. Just realize if you take one of his classes to go easy on the credit hours.
Tons of reading (5 texts)and additional weekly (20-25 pg) articles.  Seems to get side tracked a lot.  Likes to make off color or unnecessary references to women and sex.

Loeb is a great guy and makes class a joy.  He is also one of the only cultural anthropology people at the U--he keeps hope alive for the students interested in something other than evolutionary ecology.

This professor is challenging!  I worked hard, got a good grade and learned a LOT, but none of it was free.  If you like reading, take this class.  If you don't like reading, don't even think about it!

His classes are tough but I've never learned more! He's very helpful and wants you to do well in his class, but he expects you to do the readings and critically analyze them.  He's funny and his lectures are exciting and interesting.
The class is very interesting.  There is so much reading, it gets a little out of control.  He's tough.  I enjoyed the content of the class, but I'm avoiding taking another class from him.
He is very smart and interesting.  there is a lot of reading in his class but it is managable
he is the worst professor i have ever had.  please save yourself and dont take his class!

Professor Lobell is clearly an expert in his field. He sets high expectations, but everything he assigns is relevant and helps you succeed in the course. His classes encourage participation and thoughtful debate, which makes lectures engaging. He also brings strong insight into current international politics, adding valuable real-world perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible teacher- very knowledgeable and passionate. First half of the sem is very history heavy but its needed, recommend having some background in foreign policy. Pay close attention during his (amazing) lectures and exams will be fine. He notices who participates and who doesn't- a LOT of reading but all interesting!

I really liked this class. However, it was a little difficult given I don't have a strong background in foreign relations. With that being said, I dislike how he didn't put grades into Canvas until the end of the semester. Unlike many professors, his exams were closed note, which is fair, but something to note. Smart guy with lots of experience.
While having two handwritten, in-class midterms has both positives and negatives, Dr. Lobell does a great job of preparing you for the final research paper throughout the course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went into this class with low expectations as foreign policy is not my interest. However, this class by Professor Lobell was exceptional. As long as you do the readings and go to the lectures you'll be okay in the class. Your grade is dependent on 4 things (3 tests, 1 paper). The paper is short but the tests are material heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While the professor is an amazing lecturer and gives good feed back he is an insanely tough grader. Papers I wrote that I thought for sure were B+ A- tier papers received B grades routinely.

Professor Lobell is very thorough about the way he presents the material. He truly helps you understand the implications made by different academics in a way that becomes applicable to the real world. If you are doing Political Science at the University of Utah, then this is a professor whose class you must take! Some dense reading, but worth it!

I took Lobell because of astounding reviews on this website, and I am very disappointed. He's experienced with teaching, but absolutely everything he says is about securing U.S. interests with no care for how it affects the rest of the world. He has no interest in human rights or global poverty, only the U.S. economy, and it shows. Disheartened.

Best professor I've had. Makes sure you can understand and apply the principles to current events.   Two tests at the middle of the semester with a well-researched paper due instead of a final.   Attending class is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've had. Interesting. He goes of on tangents- but they're related and helped me to get the point. There was a LOT of reading but I found it interesting. He expects you to do some mental heavy lifting to get a decent grade, but he helps you along the way and is available for questions and direction.

He is an expert in his field, and you can tell that. But when it comes to teaching sometimes I would hear a classmate answer one of his questions, be rejected, and then Professor Lobell would say the exact same thing the classmate said.  Also be prepared to say what HE would say on your tests because any other ideas are a docked grade.

Lobell is really smart. His lectures are very  interesting and he encourages participation. I think because he is such an "intellectual," he has a hard time relating to students. I've had professors that I could almost consider friends, but he definitely is not one of them. He's a nice enough guy, but he just seems a little distant.
Seriously get ready to read. Seeks participation from students. Class covers a wide range of theories all for American Foreign Policy starting from the end of WWII

Professor Lobell is a great professor no doubt. He is very knowledgeable about the subject. However, his class is pretty tough. You have to do the readings and come to class and even then, if you do not not political science to a certain extent then you will be very confused. Don't take this class unprepared.
Dr. Lobell was wonderful, there is a lot of reading so be prepared for that. The lectures are always worth it especially if you didn't have time to read.

Absolutely outstanding professor!  Took two classes from Dr. Lobell this semester and loved them both.  He has an excellent teaching stlye and a great ability to break concepts down and make them understandable.

Prof. Lobell is by far the best professor I've ever had. You can tell he has a passion for American Foreign Policy and has been teaching this course for a long time. The best part is how he ties theory to history in a way that makes the theory practical. I would suggest this to anyone and everyone, but be prepared to read a lot of material.

Good Professor. By far the best lecturer I've had in Pol Sci. However, he is difficult if you don't enjoy a huge reading load. Assignments are not bad and he is a fair grader. However, you do have to work.

The dude knows his stuff. If you go to class each day and take good notes, you should be just fine. I had no idea why so many people said that he was difficult. As far as I'm concerned, he was pretty clear.  His lectures tend to be a bit boring at times. The assignments were the easiest that I've ever encountered. 3 tests in all, not too bad.
Professor Lobell is a good lecturer, even when he has a large class. There was a fair amount of reading for the class, but it was all useful and interesting.

Lobell was always super prepared, clear, and knowledgeable. Gets information conveyed clearly and easily. Ties concepts together well, and made the drier parts of the class pertinent and interesting. 3 tests are the majority of the grade, but if you listen to his lectures, they're easy. Highly recommended.

Professor Lobell is probably the smartest teacher I've had in my four years of college. However, he is incredibly difficult. I don't regret taking his class, but you definitely have to work for your grade. You have to do all of the readings which are long, and it's good to participate in class discussion. Take him if you want to learn poli sci.

Professor Lobell is probably the smartest teacher I've had in my four years of college. However, he is incredibly difficult. I don't regret taking his class, but you definitely have to work for your grade. You have to do all of the readings which are long, and it's good to participate in class discussion. Take him if you want to learn poli sci.
Dr. Lobell is a great professor.  He really knows the material

Alot of reading, some videos, which help in understanding concepts, overall well structured course with everything you need to succeed available through Canvas. Test are open-book so would definitely take notes throughout the readings. A con is some HW's required watching an 1hr documentary, not so bad if the readings weren't as long as they are.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't post videos or power points explaining the material. It's like he types it up as a paper and you have to read it and teach yourself which is frustrating, considering it's a lot of content for a 1030 class. No textbooks are required, homework and quizzes are fairly easy, but you basically teach yourself

Overall I liked this class, but I wish there would have been lecture videos instead of just slideshows for us to read through. I enjoyed most of the materials and liked learning a little bit about the human impact of earthquakes and volcanoes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class pretty fun with the way Prof. Miyagi set it up. There isn't exactly an actual textbook, but a series of home-made html sites that have a fun retro feel to them that act as the textbook. If you just do the reading and watch the videos on time, there's no doubt you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, easy to ask questions and clear grading. Fair amount of homework. As a chemistry major, I think this class is pretty easy as long as you attend and pay attention. He is a very knowledgeable professor and very good at his job. The lab portion is interesting. He is very helpful and hands on during lab.

(This is all for the online class by the way)
Lowell was incredible! If you use 3 hours/week for readings and an hour for videos, you will do fine. Weekly quizzes are open note, but you are expected to retain the material for the two exams. I didn't do well because I didn't have time to study like I normally do. But overall a well structured course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has a heavy test focus and the tests are quite difficult since they are closed notes. This makes it hard to earn an A in this class. Assignments and quizzes are fine but tough exams make up 55% of your grade. I would not recommend this class because the amount of studying required for an A is far too much for a gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you need an easy international requirement fulfillment, take Living with Quakes with Professor Miyagi. Grading is super simple, open-note quiz every week on the quick online lecture you read, and about half of the weeks have an additional homework assignment that takes no more than an hour, most just involve watching a documentary. Two Exams.

His lectures do not help with your homeworks very much. The tests are all concept based which conflicts with the homeworks and lectures which are mainly equation derivations and a limited amount of explanation. Do not take a class from him if you are not able to sift through complex mathematics in order to teach yourself what he cannot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lol I am a geology major and this class seems way excessive in what we have to memorize. Earth mat is like the opposite of structural geology. If you like chemistry and lab analysis this class will be good, but if you're more of a structural geologist like me earth mat will be awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Required memorization or 70 mineral chemical formulas. I will remember the general elements/molecules of each mineral group so memorizing individual minerals is an insulting waste of my time.

Lowell is a great teacher. Earth Mat I is a two-professor class. So, you'll have Lowell and probably Dr. Bartley. The first part of the class is the mineral paper, and it's all Dr. Bartley. But go to Lowell for help too! He is always there for any questions and is really fun to talk to. Hard class, but get help from Lowell, and you'll be fine.
Good teacher. Really wants to make the students succeed. Very easy to talk to.
Dr. Miyagi is awesome. He is younger, cool and very helpful in and after class. He is very approachable and clear in his lectures. I would love to take another class from him.
Dropped his class after 2 days because he was making review topics confusing. The professor is hard to understand and has very little experience. Switching to a different section would be best.
Funny guy make sure you pay attention to lectures they're the majority of what you're gonna learn but the homework homework is easy and if you know the stuff exams aren't bad.

He is very smart but awful at teaching. I had to teach myself all of the concepts on my own and that is the only reason I did good in this class (plus going to the math center). Goes off on tangents a lot and doesn't really know how to answer questions when asked in class. I would switch if possible to a different section.

Horrible. Class has zero pacing or structure. Almost all in-class examples are theoretical and convoluted, which are no help for homework/exams, and he goes so fast and in so many different directions that we're scrambling just to take notes, with no time to process or figure out what questions to ask. 

He's insanely smart, but he can't teach.

He understands the material very well which is where credit can be given. But, due to his lack of classroom experience both as a professor and as a student, it made calc 2 harder than it should've been. Overall, not a good professor in general, and if you can, swap your classes so you don't get him.

Very hard course and tests. Professor is hard to understand at times and doesn't give many example problems, but curved the class at the end so that 38% of the class got As. This meant that a 70+ was an A... making the course have a lot better outcome for a lot of students.

Don't take this prof. He seems to know what he's talking about, but he has told the class that he's never taken a calculus class and in my opinion can not teach at all. 90% of the class skips lecture and only shows up for the no-curve exams. The only upside was weekly homework worth 300 points each.
Would not recommend, teaches too fast with very few practice examples shown in class. Does make a few good jokes throughout the semester though.

A very difficult professor. Does not teach well in the slightest, doesn't know how to answer questions and always gets super nervous when asked. If you can, avoid this professor at all costs and take someone else! His averages are 50% on midterms without any curving of the grade. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. 

Take Jeremy Brightbill instead, he is good.

He just isn't a good teacher. All the midterms had a 50% average with zero curve. Hard to understand both due to a language barrier and lack of preparation for lectures. He even recommended students swap out of his section at the beginning of the semester (I wasn't lucky enough for this to be an option). Avoid at ALL costs.

He had no idea what he was doing. He does not know how to teach and he also grades really harshly and almost made me lose my scholarship. He is the worst teacher I have ever experienced in my entire academic journey. Drop the class while you can

Though it was a long process, I dropped his class because I felt like he wasn't the best at explaining topics. When I would ask Yi Luo a question, I never received an answer that helped me understand. Calc 2 is a challenging subject, and there are definitely better teachers at the U who are more accessible and do a better job explaining it.
Avoid at all costs
This professor had a final worth 35% of your final grade and the average was a 58% with no curve.

His class was very difficult even though I had taken calc 1 before. He sometimes rambles on topics that are very confusing but only tells you that you don't need to know it at the very end. He is still learning how to teach and I saw him progress throughout the semester.
Makes absolutely no sense and seems more like he's teaching himself instead of the class sometimes. The average of our first quiz was a 20%, if you can get out of his class, do it.
He made my life so hard and made me almost lose my scholarship! He is extremely difficult to understand and made the tests so hard and with questions we never went over.
This class was easy and yet I still feel like I learned a lot. Dr Lopez is very personable and knowledgeable.
Lukas is a great lecturer and I always enjoyed going to class. Super chill dude as well, i'd recommend.
I would suggest going to class, makes the tests much easier. Prof Lopez is super nice and always down to chat. Super easy class.

Professor Lopez's class was easy and educational. His class consisted of reading off a powerpoint, but he would go into more detail and would have the class discuss about different topics. Class does say to be 3 hours but it will usually be an hour and a half. Assignments were fairly easy and had clear expectations. Would take his class again.

Professor Lopez is very engaging in his lectures and fun. He likes you to participate and discussions are part of class. I think that these are fun since we can see different perspectives. There aren't many assignments, and all the assignments are fairly easy. If he finishes the lecture early, then he lets us go early which is really nice.

The class was frustrating at best, after doing two majors in this subject I felt I knew much more than the teacher but had to figure out the way he thinks in order to do well. No learning was done. Class was supposed to be 3 hrs long and would be less than 2, with most of it the teacher reading off of slides and asking for opinions from the class.

TAMU: Manages to make interesting material into bone-dry lectures. Homeworks are like the notes. Majority of the exam problems are like the notes, but god help you for the 2 questions that require obscene assumptions that aren't discussed in class at any capacity. Those questions will be worth ~65% of the exam and he doesn't curve. Just don't
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The overall content itself is not too difficult, but if you fall behind, even if it is bc you are sick, catching up is brutal bc of how unwavering he is about accepting anything late. Lectures are often hard to follow bc there is SO much info on every slide, and he will ONLY publish the slides for the current lecture AFTER the lecture is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolute gem of a human being. Extremely organized lectures, incredibly fair, and genuinely cares about his students. One of the only profs I've had who cares so much. Have a question, comment, concern, etc?? Just ask. Extremely reasonable and fair.

Really condescending in emails, so make sure you basically only contact him if super necessary. The grading sucks--you will literally lose points for the stupidest things. Be on your toes in this class !!

Dr. Timmins provides very useful and insightful lectures that provide basically all the information you need for the class. He is also quite accessible after class for questions and during his office hours which is necessary to truly master the material. Sometimes the grading criteria for the class is a bit weird, but it is still very doable
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: EASILY the best prof. from the BME department. Lectures are organized, easy to follow, and super relevant for the HW/exams. Timmins was accessible by email and took the time to give good explanations for any question--honestly my only class that didn't even feel like it was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Timmins presented the most organized course in the BME department by far. Even though the course was online, he recorded the lectures beforehand and held weekly discussion groups. Lectures were self-contained and homework reinforced the concepts. You can't ask for anything else!

Lectures are extremely slow, dry, and boring. It's like he's trying to get students to tune him out. There is no good written material (book, slides, notes) to learn from. I enjoy the subject but sitting through class is pure torture. The exams are very different from the homeworks, which also happen to be the only problems you'll get to practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment:
Professor Garrott frequently released us from class (after we came) because he was sore from his soccer games. He stopped answering emails at the end of the year and gave us all A's. I can't speak much to the course content, because there wasn't much of any.
I had other poli sci friends be less lucky and get terrible grades with no explanation.

Professor Garrott is a decent professor when you can get a hold of him. He is not great at communicating with students, and when he does, minimal feedback is provided. He is a hard grader which makes it hard when the readings are confusing, and have pages cut off, making it hard to read the entirety of a chapter.

One of the most engaging professors I've had. I've taken 4 courses with Prof Garrott and enjoyed all of them. Expect dense reading, structured lectures, and class discussion. I appreciate how accessible Prof Garrott is should I have any questions.

I have no idea what happened in this class. Basically we were assigned readings that made no sense, he did not explain them and then gave you quizzes that I still can't find where they were in the readings. Also a very difficult essay grader, I got my worst grade in this course and had a 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most disappointing and frustrating classes I have taken. It was a waste of my time, I could have received my upper division credits in a much more enriching class. The quiz questions were bizarre and not taken from the reading well. The essays were graded harshly despite little guidance given. It was uncomfortable to ask Qs, he was rude.

The absolute laziest professor you'll ever encounter. You are not graded by anything he teaches you, because he doesn't teach you anything. You get assigned a textbook and you write 3 essays on that textbook and you get docked if you don't agree about the things on the subject that he didn't teach you. Biased, unorganized, sloppy and lazy.

Prof Garrott is awesome. I took two courses from him in the same semester and had a great time. He doesn't take attendance, but going to class really really helps, especially with the papers. I didn't do all of the reading, but going to class and skimming all of the books was enough. He's very very fair and I learned a lot from him.

Grade only depends on three essays and two tests. His T/A is not very specific on the grading which didn't help future papers in the class. Like how this professor pushes for student discussions and opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: kinda lazy because he takes the whole semester to grade a paper and cancels class half way through it, almost like he didn't really care. the quizzes were given randomly and only began the very end of the semester which was weird. lectures also seemed like he was winging it and didn't prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class was tiny - maybe 15 people. 5 DENSE textbooks to read. Only 3 papers required. Allowed a rewrite on 2 out of 3 papers. Professor Garrott is a nice guy and very respected in the field. However, when he encouraged participation, he seemed to chastise students when they didn't bring up a topic he wanted to talk about.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Garrott is a very smart person who has some solid insight both on the philosophy and government side of the law. His class grade consists of 3 quizzes, 3 essays,  and a midterm and a final (study guides for those). I thought it was fairly easy and learned quite a bit, PS the book is only really required for the tests.

Professor Garrott was a good professor, a little confusing at times, but overall but his TA  was another story... Unclear on how he graded tests and exams. From what I have understood the class average on the final was a 75%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Garrott is incredibly knowledgeable in the Political Science/Philosophy field and has even served in local government for a number of years. TA was a tough grader but both he and Dr. Garrott gave constructive feedback. READ THE BOOK AND GO TO CLASS!

Amazing professor who is really passionate about the subject. The class is really insightful if you have any interest in politics at all. He is easy-going and showing up to class and doing some readings will get you an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Garrott is a great lecturer. He's funny and he always encourages participation. The class can get theoretical at times so he makes sure to prompt questions. The readings are essential to the class since the grade comes entirely from three papers written about the readings. I would highly recommend this professor to anybody!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Luke is a very engaging professor, that challenges students to consider his personal brand of community-based politics while also encouraging them to solidify their own political leanings. With real-world experience on the city council and years of experience in academia, students can expect a satisfying mix of theoretical and practical polisci.
Very clear study guides for tests. Writing assignment expectation very clear.

Ive taken 4 classes from Garrott. You have to do all the readings or you wont get good grades. One of the best POLS professors on campus. Just like ANY other professor he expects University students to read, write, and comprehend concepts at a University level. He is willing to metwith students and answer questions. He has real world exp in pols.
Had Garrott for Intro to Political Theory. Really nice guy and knowledgeable. Class is mostly discussion of readings. Total hipster by the way.
The only professor I'd like to have at 8 o'clock on a Monday morning. He's easy to follow, funny, and really wants you to engage so he's sure you understand.
Prof. Garrott is brilliant, yet very accessible. His classes are very well-structured and if you pay attention, you'll learn a lot. I highly recommend taking any class from this professor.

This class was a struggle.  Took it over the summer, and have yet to experience a class worse than this one.  Unorganized and difficult to follow this class and Garrott were not up to par with a college class.  The textbooks were used for one week each and cost a total of 55$, what a waste.  Avoid taking this guy unless you like bad classes

While he isn't that bad, he sometimes has a tendency to talk down to students, the T.A. was the worst. He was a grad student that expected way too much out of an into/lower level class. Anyway, he doesn't post slides online & his handwriting is terrible. Also, his tests can be a little ridiculous. The questions/material can be very obscure.
I've now taken 3 classes with Garrott, he is one of the best political science professors at the U.  All of his classes have the same format, no tests and one paper due at the end of the semester.

I loved taking this class from Luke.  He comes off as a hip guy and someone that is very approachable.  He loves classroom discussion and seems to have a solid hold on the material he is teaching.  I love his teaching method and would recommend Luke to anyone looking at Poly Sci classes.
One of the best on campus. Understands students, and responds well to those that show interest in the subject. If you take PoliSci, you need to take Garrott.
It's like he says everything I wish I could say.....but better!  Really though, brilliant guy. Very interesting to listen to.
Garrott was awesome.  If you go to class and you'll do fine.
Great teacher. Very knowledgable and precise. Makes things clear and also entertaining.
Political Ideaology. This guy is fine. it's hard to concentrate cuz he's so charming. but he's brilliant, interesting, and way cool to everyone.
very good professor.  so hot.
This guy is for real.  For cutenss!
Cooperative, Universalist, Thinker,

I took his Communitarianism Senior Seminar. Class discussions were very engaging and he doesn't directly lecture that much. Kind of a hippie, but he didn't get on a soapbox at any point during my class. Cool guy.

While he presents himself as fun, I found him to be condesending, rude and a sophist. His class was the least useful of any class I have ever taken in 4 years of college. He simply wants his students to parrot his ideas, nothing more. If I wanted a guided reading and discussion group, I would have joined a book club for a lot less money.
Gives very good and interesting lectures.  One of my favorite Professors.

Very interesting class...he keeps you interested in the material, and deals with current issues in his lectures...reccomend strongly for anyone intersted in law or philosophy! Great teacher, with great material, and interesting reading, and assignments
he is soo cute and a very good teacher.

Garrot is the BEST professor I have had at the U. He is all about the students and getting to know them on a personal level. He is very envolved with the community and the school. Very smart and funny and is ALWAYS there if you need any help. I have learne
nice guy.  dont remember the class much, got an A-, stimulating discussion.  and he wrote me a letter of rec for law school.
Very vague on some assignment requirements. Subjective grading policies.

Kind of a hip professor.Sometimes he's hard to understand, but he will totally explain anything you dont get until you get it.Doesn't rant and rave about his personal political viewpoints. He just does his job, and teaches his class well...
Great class discussion. Very clear, interesting. Very concerned about students.

He was a great professor! While the exams were a little difficult, if you use his slides, practice questions, and pay attention in class, you will do great! He loves a group project and connecting the work to the real world, so that is something to be aware of. But I really enjoyed his teaching.
Last minute made the class hybrid, never saw him during the semester. was basically taught by the TA's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking Dr. Moyer-Horner online because it's extremely difficult to remain engaged in such a hard homework-heavy class.

Very harsh when it comes to grading, points will be taken off for the smallest of mistakes and it was hard to get office ours. Discussions seemed useless to me. He was kind when I emailed but the course wasn't taught well for me.

Moyer-Horner was not very knowledgeable in the class he was teaching. He often would just read off of the slides for the week instead of giving hand on instructions (this was a lab class). He also was a harsh grader and did not provide any personal feedback for assignments, instead providing broad feedback to the whole class. Wouldn't take again!

I thoroughly enjoyed biology with Dr. Horner. The lectures were quite interesting, albeit sometimes long, but I enjoyed the material. There's a lot of assignments to keep up with. As long as you listen to the lectures and do the reading, you should be fine. Don't be afraid to ask for help. He also hosts exam and quiz reviews which really helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall this class was very hard. I spent 10+ hours a week on this class alone. The homework load alone was overwhelming. The tests were worded so different from the quizzes to the point that it almost didn't make sense. The exams were heavily weighted and the class average never got above 75%. He was an ok teacher but the course itself is brutal.

I personally didn't think that class was hard, but the professor made it just difficult to understand his answers and enjoy the class. It wasn't the content that ruined this class for me, but the horrible ways he taught this course.

Avoid at all costs. Content is not difficult, however there are anywhere from 4-6 assignments per week. The professor also doesn't provide much feedback when it comes to tests and quizzes, he refuses to release the correct answers even months after they were taken.
Super boring. This class was what I was looking forward to, but it sucks when taught by him.

While this class might not be the most difficult, this is probably to worst teaching I've encountered at the U so far.  A few questions on test and quizzes are often not covered in lecture. No feedback is given after quizzes either. It's up to you to figure out why your answers don't match his thoughts.
Just know that you will have to retain a lot of information, so if you don't do that very well, I would recommend taking this class at a community college

Favorite professor that I have had so far in college. Serious mannered but makes his lectures fun to participate in. Many assignments but they tend to be short and easy to complete. Always see him at the life center, what a G.
This teacher is very underwhelming, I have his class at 8 am and he hates being there and is so plane and boring , he has no emotions and reads off the slides. His test are so hard

Professor Horner had very engaging lectures and I enjoyed them. This class has a lot of outside work to do so it was one I spent most my time on with multiple assignments and a reading per class. The LA's were super helpful and the discussion exists for you to get that help and ask questions.

Participation 100% matters, Clicker questions bump you grade up 6-7% at the end of the semester but the class is still difficult.  All about conceptualizing, not regurgitation. He's on autopilot and doesn't care.
Not flexible

Lucas was a great teacher, but some of the test questions asked were horrendous. That being said, discussions were ran well, and are crucial if you want to do well in the class. Lectures were pretty decent, and he clearly knows what he is talking about.

Professor Moyer-Horner is a good bio professor. His lectures are long, but they make sense and really help with tests and quizzes. Bio 1610 has a lot of homework regardless of what professor you have, but Moyer-Horner helps our understanding of the material for sure! I think he is one of the best bio professors at the U.

He's a mid professor but if you've taken AP Bio and are generally science-y brained, you should cruise. He is super uncompassionate when it comes to excusing absences due to genuine sickness even with a a doctors note or when other's have had trouble with iclicker and brought it up to him. He has no sympathy. Don't expect to get excused iclickers.

If you take notes and pay attention in the lectures you should be good, study guides he provides are pretty much one-to-one with test content. Overall class is generally easy especially if you took AP Biology in the past. Participation via clickers is pretty annoying so you have to be in class most of the time to receive credit.

The class is mostly about memorizing facts and there's a lot to memorize (the main reason this class is hard). The professor did his job which was to teach but the student learn it.  If you don't have a good memory, this isn't the class for you. The textbook is super resourceful for quizzes and exams so understand and memorize it.

Professor lectures so fast, lectures are miserable and do not correspond with the textbook. Tests are worded so horribly, I feel like they're designed to make you fail. I scored above the median score on EVERY SINGLE ASSIGNMENT and only pulled a C. This class is not designed to be passed.

I look at this page and see a lot of freshman who are learning the hard way that professors don't hold your hand in college. Lucas is a great guy and his class expectations are very clear. His lecturing skills need work, but he is a fresh prof and this will come with time. If you are a capable student then don't worry about 1610 or 3470

Dr. Horner is a terrible professor. You never know what your grade will be. He curved the entire class down only ONE percentage point after the average on the final was a 55%. There are a lot of assignments but I think they do help to learn the material better. His lecturing is very monotone, just reading off the PowerPoint. reviews.comment: His curriculum is super easy at the beginning, but it gets tough fast. He is no nonsense, but provides many resources (there are a ton of office hours and the bio learning center). Go to class & discussion, read the book, do your assignments and try your best and you'll be fine.
Such a hard class. He is awful at lecturing. Even if you paid attention to his lectures it won't even help you on the exams. Exams were awful !!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most offputting thing about this professor is the way he answers students' questions during lecture. I would rather be left in confusion than be belittled in front of 250 other students. The average on the final exam was 50-60%, showing that nobody could learn from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: In this class you will need to stay caught up on the course material if you want to do well. There is a pre and post class assignment for every class. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The tests are very difficult to pass, and he recommends studying past quizzes however doesn't release the correct answers on them. Having a study group will be your best friend. reviews.comment: Overall, really good teacher and you will get at least a B if you apply yourself. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Avoid this class at all costs.

Dr. Moyer-Horner is not a bad professor. His lectures are clear. TA's are very helpful. However, this class is not easy. If you don't study, watch the lectures, take notes, read, or do the assignments, you'll definitely fail (like, no duh). Tests will require you to study. It's a weeder course... if you can't do it, reconsider your STEM major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Horner was overall a decent professor. Half your grade is an easy 100% (HW and clicker points graded on completion). Don't take this your first semester of college, take chemistry first, and go to tutoring!

reviews.comment: A lot of people are really negative about Dr. Horner on here, but I felt like he did a good job explaining Bio at this level. People complaining about this being too in depth are in for a surprise when they get to any of the next biology courses. He offers lots of homework thats a completion grade and the tests are a fair test of the material.

The absolute worst class Ive ever taken. Material on exams isnt covered in enough depth and stuff shows up on tests that youve never heard of. WAY too hard for intro.

reviews.comment: Awful teacher! Was very boring during class and often found myself going to sleep while in lecture. Wasn't very interactive class either. Just about every topic didn't make sense, but maybe Biology just isn't for me.

Final was all over the place and made it feel like I had learned nothing all semester. Too much stress for one class.

Very good teacher and person. However, there was lots and lots of homework associated with each class. Staying up to date with the material was, to say the least challenging. He did well with adjusting to covid protocols and did well online. The only real complaint is that his deadlines are very strict and he doesn't bend them no matter the excuse.

reviews.comment: Tests and quizzes were very difficult and asked about very specific parts of the lessons. Make sure you pay attention to definitions and use flashcards to quiz yourself so you remember specific terminology.

89% is an A- even though the average is around 60%. Doesn't set curve, extremely dull lecturer, tons of busy work, never gives feedback, final test doesn't correspond much to material, impersonal vibe. Just an awful class in every way. Attend weekly reviews, make a Discord, and read the textbook daily. Do all pre/post class stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--So many papers

I am a normal straight-A student- made the dean's list my first couple of years. I don't think anything else needs to be said.

reviews.comment: He class is very boring and it is very hard, find a better professor at any cost.

This was not a terrible bio class, but Horner makes it harder than it has to be for a fundamentals class. Lectures are confusing and I hardly paid attention because I would always learn much better through the LAreview sessions. All quizzes, exams, and mid-terms are quite difficult but not impossible if you study enough. Horner is good pick overall
Good lecturer. Tests are hard bug reasonable if you are a good student ull do fine.

His lectures were dry. You learn a lot more and much more in depth by reading the textbook. Not the greatest professor, he didn't seem to know what he was teaching some of the time. But, his class was much easier than the other Bio 1 class and he seemed to be a better professor. The class slides are useless and I only got through this class by reading the textbook. His tests are easy as long as you've done the required readings.

Lectures are dry at best. Class has a boring lecture usually followed by a worksheet that's fairly easy. Exams aren't horrid but expect some questions that don't really have to do with what was covered in the course, or questions that are oddly specific. Prof usually answers questions with 'I don't know'. Show up to class to do the stupid clickers.

Lots of homework. Drawing assignments were helpful, online homework was busy work. His assignments made me more worried about turning them in on time than actually learning the material. reviews.comment: He does a good job at teaching and telling us what will be on the final.

This guy doesnt seem to care about answering your questions. He leaves it to his TA and LAs. Every question he does answer however is very vague and poorly explained. Often with a shrug. His lectures arent very useful since the exam seems to ask more specific questions.

Dr. Moyer-Horner is a decent Bio teacher. I was in his online hybrid course, and homework and assignments weren't too hard, but the reading is excessive. I took it online so my experience may be different... but what I learned is just to read the textbook chapters once or twice and review them before the exam and it was easy. reviews.comment: Exams..

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't extremely hard, but I took many high level biology courses in high school, so I may not be the best example. My AP Bio class in HS and a good background knowledge of chemistry helped me. Never went to class because I found lectures long, boring, and not in depth. His finals pretty much suck. (Class average 57%) You can tell he cares and is trying to help but his exams are the complete opposite no matter how hard you study.
