reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No final, three midterms (he drops one), few assignments. Takes attendance sometimes. Sometimes things discussed in class that aren't on the slides will show up on the test. Easy material and he was an entertaining lecturer. Very approachable. Once I asked how I could improve one of my answers on an exam (I got 2/4 pts) and he gave me full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this teacher! She is so nice and caring of her students. You can tell she is really passionate about what she teaches. The class was not hard at all, and the assignments were never too much. She is really understanding and offers extensions on every assignment if you ask for it. I would 100% recommend this class and teacher for anyone

I took Gender, Performance, and Performativity with Professor Deboeck and she was great. The class wasn't always the most structured (readings didn't always align with discussion) but was great otherwise. The research project seems intimidating at first but she gives great feedback and helps you with it in stages.

Very easy class to get an A in if you don't miss more than 3 times. I wish the class was more structured it was all just discussions that might not have to do with the readings. Very kind and allows extensions on every assignment.
Professor Deboeck is amazing! Had her for GNDR 1100. Very kind and thorough with what she expects. Assignments were extremely easy and she allows extensions on all assignments. Highly recommend!

Professor Deboeck is incredibly intelligent and has amazing lectures. I was disappointed if I had to miss class because she facilitates fascinating discussions and chooses great reading materials. The reading for this class was not too difficult or lengthy. Though there was a final paper, she made sure the writing was split up over the semester.

Learned so much from this class, History of Gender, Performance, and Performativity. Professor Deboeck is very welcoming, passionate about her classes, and always ready to help if you ask. Would definately take another class from her, and I highly recommend this class and any others that she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy the way that this professor lectured. She did not use or follow the slides that she posted, which was confusing. The lack of assignments outside the market project also made it hard to tell if I was understanding the material. I often felt lost during her lectures and unprepared for her exams.

I'm not sure why Lynn receives such a bad rating. Her class is very linear and self explanatory. While lectures and homework can get repetitive, at the end of them she guides the students through the answers! Her exams are easy if u attend lectures and do all the hw.

This class is graded mainly off of 3 quizzes and an international country review paper/presentation. If you choose a country that no one else chooses you'll have to present by yourself for 10-15min. The tests are extremely hard but can be found online with minimal differences.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems very nice, but lectures are very hard to follow along and dry. If you are not good at math/finance, I don't recommend as teaching yourself with the materials given makes it impossible (all textbook/scattered, not enough problems). I have watched the videos 3 times and made an extensive sheet for the exam(you  bring one) and still felt lost.

Nice Professor, but does the bare minimum

The lecture slides, homework, and materials are recycled from the textbook provider, and can all be found online

The exam reviews are nothing like the exams, so studying with them is a waste of time. Grading is weird (Our group was deducted 10% off the final because someone stuttered in our presentation)

Overall, this class is pretty easy if you paid attention during the other finance BCOR class and seems like a review. Lectures are dry as others have mentioned and she just reads off the textbook and does the problems in the back, but that can be helpful. Assignments are easy and straight forwards, exams are somewhat easy just  review the concepts.

Okay, I have taken multiple classes with her, and the lectures are slightly boring and slow. Besides that great teacher if you can actually concentrate and have an interest in quant-based finance. The only issue I believe is she solves questions a lot rather than focusing on telling the concepts. She is really friendly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's is very kind but her lectures are awful. She just reads material off to you then does practice problems in the back of the book. It is very hard for what she teaches to stick because she's so dry and all over the place. She provides an exam review that is pointless and doesn't help prepare for exams because no one knows what to expect

She is a kind person, but easily one of the worst professors I have ever had. The textbook that she teaches from comes with pre-made slides that she uses, and just reads off of in her lectures. She doesn't even bother making her own slides, or writing her own practice problems - everything comes from the book. Lazy professor, awful at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very difficult class, horrible professor. Tests arent similar to lecture. Take from someone else

Biggest issue with this class was the hw. You do questions at the back of the book to practice and they are not graded, so I felt like I never knew what to expect on tests. Lectures are dry cuz this material is boring. She does have some cool guest lectures. Class feels like a waste of time when we already have to do 2 other BCOR finance courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just the least interesting class Ive ever taken. There are lots of great professors at the U. Take someone else
She doesnt explain what is wrong about the homework and grades stuff in an unfair way
Take this class if you dont want to have a good time
She acts like she cares and then gives unclear instructions that make assignments a million times harder than they should be. I wouldnt recommend overall
She doesnt ever do office hours or answer emails. The only time to ask questions is online during class
This was such a weird class. Mrs Myers is an ok teacher, but she made me feel like I was in junior high again
Least interesting class Ive ever taken
Boring class, easy A, she feels uninterested in every lecture

she's great if you actually care. She posts the zoom lectures on canvas after class but you need to attend the live session to avoid falling behind. She is super straight forward, just do the end of chapter problems 2-3 times before the quiz and you will ace it. The final has a crazy time crunch so study hard and rush through the multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is very distant and hard to reach. She also makes no attempt to connect with the students. The only reason for attending class is to get participation points. Other than that, there's really no reason to attend class. You're essentially expected to learn all the material on your own by doing the end of chapter homework problems. Don' recommend

Means well and wants students to understand the material. Lacked in the ability to explain concepts thoroughly so I had to use the textbook more often than not. Lectures are dry but she prepares you for the test with slides and practice problems. Avoid taking night classes (6pm - 9pm) with her at all costs.

There is no clear teaching structure. You are on your own. The lectures and quizzes are not connected at all and you will find yourself having no idea as to what is going on. Unless you figure out how to teach yourself, good luck passing. I should have taken this with someone else. She's nice, but her teaching method is ineffective and vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You should do the ungraded practice problems before class so that you can get those extra credit points and have an easier time understanding the material. A lot of the time she won't go over her own version of problems which makes it hard to apply some concepts into studying material for the quizzes. Unless you're some genius, go to class.

I've had Lynn for two courses now, and I have nothing but good to say about her. Yes, her lectures are a bit dry, and very note heavy. Sometimes quite tough to keep up with the writing on the board. However, she will always do what she can to help her students and is a very sweet woman. Exams are tough, but engage in class and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It seemed like you were expected to learn a majority of the material on you own and come to class to practice problems on the board. The participation questions were always harder than the one you practiced. Extra credit was offered daily for performing a problem in class on the board. Hard to pick up the material haven't taken prior finance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class was extremely lecture heavy and she randomly does participation assignments to incentivize going to class. These can hurt your grade if you don't go. Lectures were very boring and hard to follow, would have been better off reading the book. Have to study very hard to get a good grade on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hated her class structure. She takes attendance so you have to attend class, her lectures come right out of the book, she doesnt elaborate on anything, and she refuses to use PowerPoint... instead she writes on the board which is way too small to see.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lynn is an industry professional and is very knowledgeable about finance. Her tests are really straight-forward from the lectures and slides. You are advised to do assigned homework end-of-chapter problems and you will score above the average if you do them. The final is hard but she prepares you well. Many extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lynn is a really nice lady. She may seem a little strict but she's actually very lenient and curves A LOT at the end. She is very clear on what she's gonna quiz you on so make sure you go to her review sessions before each quiz. Do the hw questions on the board, it's such an easy way to get extra credits.

She is a nice person and you can tell she cares about her students. However, she gives you no study material for quizzes or the final. Other professors gave out reviews for the final but she did not. She goes over problems that are in the textbook that are super easy in comparison to the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Honestly not sure why Lynn has so many negative reviews. Her lectures can be a little dry but keep in mind its Finance. She taught the material very well and made it so easy to understand. I felt very prepared for assignments, quizzes, and the final. I did sit front row in her class and took good notes. It was a tough subject but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: I think Lynn is very straightforward in her teaching style. She lays the material out in front of you quickly, but as long as you put forth some effort into your homework (which is not very hard) you should do fine. Be sure to ask a lot of questions if you don't understand the material, she is very good to clarify.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice lady, but not a good professor. Writes entire lesson on the board which is just a replication of the slides. Has no meaningful insight  that helps students learn the material. Lessons and homework are superficial and easy, but the tests are in-depth and difficult. At least she gives extra credit, which is nice.

I really didn't like her teaching style. She taught very little, and just went over questions in the book. Her way of going over the solutions was having students come up and show their work on the board. Several would come up at a time to do different problems, so if you didn't figure it out on your own, good luck. Not much homework, which was nic

She is clearly is very passionate about Finance. It feels like she expects all of her students to share the same passion. Her class includes many homework assignments that are relatively easy. There are 4 exams, the second of which I found I was difficult.

There's 1 final and 3 quizzes (tests) in this class along with textbook & non-textbook homework assignments for the chapters. Quizzes 1 & 2 weren't bad but the entire class scored really poorly on the 3rd. Attend this class so you don't miss homework due dates-- they're not always posted on the syllabus. This class proved that finance isn't for me!
Has like 5 or 6 assignments that are pretty easy.  Tests are tough. Lot of homework. She just goes through power points and then goes over problems.

International Finance. One of the nicest people you'll meet, but not great at teaching. Lectures consist of her basically transcribing word for word the content from the book onto the white board. She gets flustered when asked to expound on concepts. I found lectures pointless, as the material can be learned just by reading the book.

Decent teacher, though the subject matter was so boring to me it was difficult to pay much attention. You get full points for even attempting the homework so always try, even if you get it wrong (which you most likely will, it's tough). Quizzes are hard even with studying her guides. Do the weekly country info and homework and pray on quizzes.
She is very knowledgeable about the subject matter, and is very willing to help you out with any problems you are having.

Lynn is an all-around average professor. She's not incredibly difficult, but she doesn't make the material easy to understand. She follows pre-made slides, isn't connected with the class, and doesn't explain anything further than the slides or the book did. Her homework is reasonable, but it doesn't match the exams because they come from a database
Enjoyed her lectures

She's nice. She'll help you whenever you asked her questions. She's not the best in teaching the material tho. I never study for her class, only type everything that is on the study guide onto the cheat sheet. I got robbed by receiving a B+, but if you do every assignment and do decent on quizzes, you will be fine

The grade in this class is based on participation problems, 3 quizzes, and the final. For the quizzes, you're allowed to have a double-sided cheat sheet where you can write down anything you want. The material gets hard, but Lynn teaches you well and prepares you well for the big departmental final.

This is the most unclear quantitative class I have ever taken. She only gives like 5 math examples per chapter, glances right over difficult material then treats entire chapters on tests as fair game. Lynn is very nice but is a terrible instructor.

Lynn was not a great professor.  She reads STRAIGHT from the slides and speeds through the example problems.  She makes what should be a relatively easy class way too difficult.  Her tests are very tricky.  BEWARE.  Take this from another professor.

I LOVE LYNN! I was so scared to take this class, but now I can say I am an active investor who is well aware of what is going on now. I felt like she answered my questions concisely, and was always so patient because this is a difficult subject. She made me love investing, when it made me cringe before.

I took 3040 and 3050 from her and liked her a lot. Many students struggle with these classes, and they're not easy, but read every chapter and come to class and youll be fine. Theres not much homework.  She allows 1 pg of notes double sided for each test in 3040 and 3050. Only negative is that she sometimes goes way too fast during sample problems.

First things first. All the finance teachers are terrible at the U. Lynn-Meyers is no exception to that. Lectures consist of her reading directly from the power point. It could be because I am a night student and maybe she isn't a good night professor, but she was lazy and was never in focus for the class. I got nothing from this class.

Worst mistake I made during my college career was to take a finance class from Lynn. Very nice, but painfully incapable of teaching at a college level. She is very unclear about concepts and her tests minimally reflect what she discusses in class. If you have a question about a concept she explained, she will generally have to refer to her notes.
Difficult class.  Gotta read and do the practice questions in order to grasp concepts.

I thought Lynn was very helpful and often talked about real world applications. She taught me how to invest wisely in the stock market. She is very straight forward about what you need to know on the test. She even allowed a one page cheat sheet! Her tests were not too difficult if you attended class and listened. She is a little trickster though

Overall, she was helpful and nice. The material takes some time to learn so if you're not doing your part on the reading it will seem like she speeds through the lectures. She went over each of the practice problems and helped students with questions. There was some discussion on real world topics, but not a whole lot.
She is very nice instructor.Her class is open and she try to help any student that feel hard with course material.
Went too fast for most of the students in the class... asked a question, got an answer from some super smart kid and went on... didn't get much out of this class.
Taught like high school, too much technical, not enough discussion...great class for those who want to be technicians.  Nice lady, but not much real world experience.

She is a good professor and I would recommend her class.  However, as someone for whom math is not a strong point, I would disagree with the previous comment that her class is easy.  You do have to put forth an effort, as the quizzes are fairly difficult, I thought, but better than a lot of profs.

Lynn is an excellent professor. I've never had such a nice professor! She really cared about the students. Lectures were great, material was very interesting. Grade is basically based on 4 quizzes (25 M.C. questions). Super-easy math involved (for me - I've done more than Calc III).
Awesome class, super fun to see plants in habitat. I found it easy but I already knew the material well beforehand, so others may find it difficult. She knows a lot about botany though.

I took field botany over the summer and it was my favorite class I've taken at the U! Lynn makes botany super interesting, and even though I didn't know anything at the beginning, I learned so much in such a short period of time. I only wish it was a longer class

Had Lynn for field botany and it was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at the U! Lynn was very clear with expectations and was very caring and helpful. Uses a lot of visual tools to get her point across, and clearly was very knowledgeable about plants native to Utah. Made me love plants even more and I'm now pursuing a career in botany!
I did a PCR based project on plant DNA looking for polymorphic markers (RAPDs) in Dr. Bohs lab. Her enthusiasm and guidance was key in setting the direction of my career.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bohs was very passionate about her subject, and I appreciated that. She's not like most professors at the U who just care about research - she's cares about teaching us. She was kinda disorganized with lectures, which made studying kind of difficult. She mentioned things that she didn't clarify were important. Still, not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lynn was awesome! She was very nice and caring. She knows what it's like to be in our shoes as a student and grades/tests very fairly. She is a tad disorganized in lecture, however if you do the study questions and homework and write down what she writes on the board you will be just fine. Tests are very doable and come directly from lectures!

Her powerpoint were nice and organized, but when she writes down what she's talking about, it's all over the place. I kept having to figure out if she was onto a new topic or not since she always went back and forth so you have to stay on top of her lectures. Tests were more indepth and similar to past ones.
One of my favorite Biology teachers at the U. You can tell what info is important during her lecture. You pay attention, you can definitely get an A.

This class was unorganized. It is hard to stay interested when half the time you are trying to decipher the unorganized power points slides. Tests go into great detail that one wouldn't expect. The professor was nice and she seemed willing to help whenever you asked, but I found this class to be more difficult than advanced biology classes.

Professor Bohs covered the plant section of this class. It was pretty boring material but she taught it well. You have to go to lecture to do well. She covers a bunch of plant types and tests you on them right from the lecture.
Very funny professor! I loved going to her class every day because she made learning fun and she was very engaging.

Great teacher for this class.  She loves plant systematics and shows when she teaches this class.  Very smart and expects a lot but you are in college not High School.  When she teaches BIOL 2010 she isn't as good. She is very helpful 1 on 1 but very busy and nearly always gone.  One of my favorite at the U.

Purposely tries to confuse on quizzes. Doesn't respond to emails. Rushes through lectures and does not expand. You can survive but you won't understand. Never explains the projects thoroughly. Takes a long time to grade but has high deadline expectations. If there is anyone else to take the class you need - take them.  
CLASS: COMM 5580

This is boring! I'm taking PR and campaign cases with him. He gives out quizzes after he lectures the following classes and WHEN I TELL YOU THEY MAKE NO SENSE! He will tell you one thing will be on the quiz and then the quiz looks nothing like his lecture. half the time he doesn't even get through the whole lecture and then gives the quiz anyway!

Professor Lyons is extremely sarcastic and dry humored, but he is an amazing professor. I learned a lot in his class. He also really wants you to succeed. Getting an A in the class is really easy, if you put the work in. He gives a lot of extra credit, but you do have to study hard for his tests. Make a study group and focus on the bolded material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ms Van Dam was a bully when I took this class. She regularly belittled beginning acting students. I don't know what she's like now - I took the class a long time ago. Basically an unprofessional bully. Oh, she used to brag about being in a movie with Scott Glenn.
She's so fun and laid back.  I love her class!  She helps you AS you do your scenes.  If you ask she will help even more. Great teacher.

Unfortunately she may be the worst professor I have had yet. About 80% of class time is wasted, she is very rude and condescending at times. I feel like I didn't leave her class a better actor, not even a little bit. She has very little valuable input and does not permit any constructive criticism from the students. No acting method is taught.

This class was very effective as a film WORKSHOP, not a class. If you want to learn how to be a good actor, I would take another class. If you're looking to tune your skills on camera, she will definitely help you. Lynne is very strict and can be kinda mean, but she has a lot of experience and can help you get into film acting outside of class.

I would agree with the previous posting. The teacher doesn't do any acting exercises with students and doesn't give any monologues to work on. She doesn't cooperate with one if she is "right" and doesn't except one's opinion unless it's something unimportant to her. She is rude at times. And she may disregard your email. However, some may like her.

The teacher provides comments on performances, but doesn't do much actual teaching. You get a script, perform (usually the next week) and get mostly useless feedback (only positive is allowed by students).

One of the best professors I've ever had! Not only did she have an amazing personality, but explained things in a way that was very easy to understand and intriguing. She's so kind and always gave a lot of helpful feedback. Would definitely recommend!
She is the nicest person ever. If you go to her for something, she most likely will accommodate you and help you out. I appreciate her allowing the class to be fun and shes truly the best.
Took Writing 1010 with her and the attendance was for points. Pretty funny and chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The best professor around I swear! She is so kind and caring. Her essays are always fun to write and really let you see a different side to yourself. Very understanding with different situations I had a lot of orthodontic appointments and she was super cool about it. :) 10/10 experience.
Very clear on writing assignments, and willing to talk to students 1 on 1 about their papers. Makes class really fun and educational.

Suksdorf is a great professor.  He clearly outlines the expectations for class in the syllabus and truly wants his students to walk away from the class as a more "learned person".  Gives answers to quizzes, holds flexible office hours (very beneficial), and has unique discussions.  Participation is 15% of grade so make sure you attend & talk.

The lectures were more student-opinion based and every single class was just a discussion. Readings were very long and confusing, but the final was not too hard if you attended class. Miserable group project/essay. Easy quizzes, he gives you all of the answers so you just memorize. This class can be as interesting or boring as you make it

His lectures are fascinating and filled with humor.  He always talks about current events, and relevant topics and stories about his life that add to the lectures.  Does come off a bit condescending if you're not careful with how you come across, but it's just a part of his personality.  You should read because participation is worth 15%

I loved the way Professor Suksdorf presented his class.  There are 4 maybe 5 quizzed you take which he gives you the answers to before hand.  2 papers and 1 group project.  Besides that all you have to do is participate in the lectures based off the readings.  I really enjoyed this class and learned a ton.

Lynn is a great professor. Always able to give good examples and real-world insight. There are only 4 lectures throughout the year and every other class is a socratic discussion format. Almost always interesting. You never have to do the readings, just read in class and then make a comment built off what he is saying in class. The essays do suck.
Difficult class, class content does not apply to quiz/exam, professor is condescending and patronizing, classes are boring. Be prepared to listen to him talk about himself and his professional life.

Lynn's lectures are really interesting and interactive. However, if you take his MGT class beware! His lectures do not necessarily match the test and the quizzes are SUPER hard. Almost all the class failed the quiz and he did nothing about it.

If you're looking to receive an A in Foundations of Business (BUS 1050), then Suksdorf  is the professor for you. If you take notes, you'll ace the the five question quizzes. Prepare for tough grading on writing assignments as well as a few group projects throughout the semester.

His class is actually the easiest out of every professors who teach BUS 1050. You just need to come to class, turn in everything, sometimes speak up and introduce yourself to the professor, write down everything on the board and you will get an A. No reading required.

His class discussions are pretty interesting, though the papers you have to write...not so much. He knows his stuff but thinks he knows everything. He likes to single out people to participate during class, so be ready for that. Just a so-so professor.

Lynn acts like his class is super hard but it's actually not. His goal is to make you a "learned person" which he will repeat hundreds of times throughout the semester, but never seems to accomplish. Most of your grade comes from random quizzes based on what he writes on the board during class so pay attention and do the readings.

This professor uses the Harvard style case study. It is very fast paced, and unless you read the material before you come to class, this professor will go out of his way to embarrass you and make you feel stupid. The good thing is that if a person has a stupid comment, this professor will not hesitate to humiliate them into not talking again.

Great professor and awesome guy. Very knowledgeable about the subject and always used real life, often personal, examples. Reading the textbook and going to class are essential, but if you do that it isn't to hard.

Dr. Suksdorf was a great professor. His discussions are always interesting. You must read the book and pay attention in class to do well on the quizes. Otherwise, he is a great professor with clarifying examples from his life.

purely discussion, three papers, four quizzes, take home final. strict grading on quizzes, given @ random. go to class, its essential. write down everything on the board, those are the quiz questions.

Class discussions are always interesting but biased to his liberal opinion and usually not significantly related to the class. The required 10 page group paper was the most miserable experience of my college career...quizes are easy.

It seems his students either loved him or really disliked him. I enjoyed his class. He made us think and he applied what was written centuries ago to our world today. I was not excited to take this class but he made it enjoyable and I ended up loving it. I would highly recommend his class.

I got very ill the semester I took his class and he said I could make up the quizzes I missed (which he usually doesn't allow) but then told me I never did (WHICH I DID!!) so he gave me zeros. He was unfair about the situation and wouldn't admit he lost the quizzes I turned in. I talked to the dean about him because it cost me my grade. STAY AWAY.

Kind of strange professor. He acts like his class is super tough & you have to work really hard, but honestly it was not that hard to get an A. You don't have to do half the readings & you could still pull it off. The main thing that bugged is his cockiness. I'd say look for better if you can, unless you don't care about boring but easy classes.

Mr. Suksdrof is one of the nicest most unique professors I have ever had. I looked forwards to attending the class everyday because it really got me thinking. Mr. Suksdorf does a great job at making sure you understand what is being taught by using lots of examples. This is a discussion based class and has been very useful. "HIGHLY RECOMMENDED"!!!

This was hands down, the worst taught class I have ever participated in.  The professor had no interest in advancing the understanding of the students.  He showed no commitment to the class (he did not show up on more than one occasion without notifying the class) and his lesson plans came straight from the teachers aid of the textbook.  AVOID!!!

Horrible teacher.  Never gave anything back.  Wouldn't respond to emails. Actually laughed at students requests for grade information.  We had no idea what grade to expect because there was no feedback given at any point during the semester.
HORRIBLE CLASS, DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME.
No Comments
Gave extra credit for showing up. Very easy tests and grader. Lectures were somewhat boring and repetitive. He also looks like the ant from bugs life

I've heard his lectures are great, but I personally could not pay attention for the life of me. Maybe it's because political science bores me out of my mind, but it felt like he was just reading off slides the whole time. He gave extra credit for showing up, though, which was nice. He's probably better than I remember, but eh.

I had a hard time staying awake during his lectures but that's def more of a me-problem, whenever I was awake I learned a lot and thought they were pretty interesting. Good teacher. Textbook takes a looong time to read. You'll have two papers that are kinda hard so I'd stay on top of those. Both exams are online and open note which is very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a great class to take! There was usually one quiz a week based on each chapter in the textbook. The chapters can be long, but weren't too bad. The midterm and final were open note. He gives extra credit if you attend class, and the lectures are really interesting. I highly recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very politically opinionated. Bias

Lectures are jam-packed with information, and McCrain clearly knows the ins and outs of civics and political science. The textbook is similar in this regard -- if you're not into taking lots of notes, you may want to reconsider. However, the class does offer an impressive amount of knowledge if you're willing to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professory McCrain was amazing! Lectures were very interesting and informative. Attendance gives extra credit. 2 essays, 2 exams and weekly reading quizzes. 3-5 hours of tedious reading per week. Despite the 400+ students, he constantly took time to answer questions and engage with the class.

Prof McCrain is fantastic! He is very passionate about the subject. I found his lectures to be informative and enjoyable. The textbook is NOT well written, and there is a lot to read. The weekly quizzes and exams are mostly based on textbook content, so its important to pay attention. We had 2 essays, and the TA's provided good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A good professor with a lecture heavy class, other than weekly inquizitive, light on the homework, only 2 essays and the 3 tests. Very knowledgeable and passionate about political science as well as a good speaker.
Not too bad especially for an intro class.  If you have no background in polisci, make sure you read the books. He gives good opportunity for extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Maybe this class sucked was because it was online, but there was only 1 lecture over zoom a week and he squeezed so much content into 1 hour. He talked fast and hardly gave time to take notes or ask questions. Get ready to basically teach yourself if you take this class. Not much homework was given but tests are important & he gave no study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: McKnight talks extremely fast even when you ask him to slow down. Tests are about 95% of the grade and the extra credit is pretty difficult to achieve. Lessons are recorded but all it is are videos of him talking about the slides and still not slowing down. Very difficult teacher who doesn't seem to respect students or want to help them succeed

If you make yourself familiar with the lecture slides, you will do well. A recording is also available if you're unable to attend the class. Tbh, I only studied from the lecture slides and haven't looked at recordings for the last third of class and still did fine. Just be prepared to study with slides packed with info.

He was great; he cares about your success in and out of class. I recommend rewatching lectures and listen to his explanations - prepare exam answers beforehand for any possible questions, and ask him questions. The TA's are VERY helpful so meet with them. This is a hard and time consuming class so be prepared to put in effort and memorize concepts.

Dr. McKnight was great. He cares about your success inside and outside of the class. This class is hard and time consuming. Meet with the TA's, as they know what is most likely to be on the exams and will help guide you. My advice is to go over the lectures and listen to his explanations - prepare your test answers beforehand and ask him questions.

If you aren't a great test taker, run. This is not the class for you. 4 exams, 95% of your grade. If you get one wording wrong, the entire question is wrong. Expect to spend hours on end trying to learn every single word on each slide.

Dr. McKnight is great and his class was really helpful for MCAT studying imo! The course is fast paced, so I recommend being caught up w/ the videos before class. I always stayed for the 2nd 1/2 of class, which is reserved for doing study Qs with the TAs and prof. He also would come early to answer questions before class.

Robert McKnight is a very kind person, but he just teaches a difficult class. There is a lot of material, and I spent a lot of time studying for tests. Exams are 95% of your grade, with the other 5% coming from in-class quizzes. His pre-recorded lectures were hard to follow for me, so I didn't really use those.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a hard class. The first time I ever got a C+ in my school life. Compared to the other professor who teaches Physiology he is really nice. But the class and the lectures are really hard and heavy with material. If you put in effort of course you will pass. He makes the tests himself and omg were they hard even if you did study.

McKnight is funny and knowledgeable. To succeed in this class you have to rewatch the lectures and make sure you understand EVERYTHING- usually I did this through youtube because he could be confusing when explaining stuff. Just be confident in what every slide means and you'll be good for the exams. Gives some extra credit, grade is mostly exams.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. Extremely disorganized and spoke scattered brain as well. Never explained why the test answers were wrong, and extremely inconsistent with grading too. I would not recommend this professor for this class. Way too much info and extremely overwhelming to understand what would be on the test or what was a random fact.

Amazing professor. Amazing class. My only issue is I have crippling text anxiety and the class is so test based. So if test taking is not your skill it will be extremely difficult bc your grade is based off 4 exams. No exams are dropped

100% worth the drive to Sandy. He is so knowledgable, funny, and makes lectures interesting. Not to mention you learn so much about physiology but also clinical applications and some pathophys. Flipped classroom style with an hour of Q&A every lecture made studying way easier. If you can answer the study questions you will do well on tests

Dr. McKnight was a great professor. If you go to lecture and UNDERSTAND nearly all the in-person class slides then you'll get an A on exams and quizzes. Exams are fair and based on the in-person lecture slides and some of the longer lecture slides and videos he posts online. Q&A time after class is VERY helpful. The clicker ECs were engaging.

Professor Mcknight is the reason I took the class on the sandy campus, and the 30 minute drive on Tuesdays and Thursdays were well worth it! He lays out the class in a way that is incredibly doable- by dropping 3 quiz scores and doing clicker questions for extra credit. He will always stay after class to answer questions and help review.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McKnight has been one of the best professors I've had in college. He is very knowledgable about physiology and I think has a good teaching style that helps you learn. He doesn't want you to memorize things, but rather understand the topic. Some concepts are tricky, but he clarifies it well. Grade is 95% exams and 5% quizzes. 10/10 class

Big thing is that 95% of the grade is tests. However, I get it, I feel like he makes it clear that he tried other options to cut down on cheating. The tests themselves are a LOT of material that you'll be expected to understand, but they're not tricky. He curves the tests, and removes questions if he feels that he didn't cover it well enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought he was a great professor. The course in itself is difficult, and he lets you know that. But he very willing to help you succeed as long as you are willing to put in the effort.

McKnight is the best choice for human physiology at the U. He is straight forward with the material and doesnt try to trick you. Study the study guide and youll do great, and go to his review sessions. Hes super smart and not rude when you attempt to answer questions. He really does want you to know the material, so participate if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you want good grade, be ready to commit. Outside of the 4 hrs/wk in class I went to TA sessions (+2hrs) and solo studied (+2-5hrs). He is SO knowledgable & clear on what he expects you to know. Rely on the the study questions to GUIDE you on what his focus is on the test, but go through EVERY slide. Understand the whole process, not just facts
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The grade was basically based on exams, but there were in class clicker questions and quizzes that went towards your grade. He focuses on the essential, applicable topics he wants you to always remember and not specifics you'll forget in a month. He learns the names of students and likes participation. His study questions are essential for exams.

Dr. McKnight is my favorite professor that I've ever taken at the U. His class is definitely not easy, you have to earn your grade, but it is very doable and he gives you all the resources to succeed. I learned so much in this class and learned the why, not just the what. I highly recommend this class and professor. He wants students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Phys is not an easy course by all means. His course is very biochem heavy so expect that. There's a lot of memorization. If you're taking biochem he does a good job at prepping you for that. Lectures are not very interesting as he reads from slides. Tests are hard, but there is some extra credit possible.

This professor actually has a good sense of humor and tries to be lenient, but he really struggles with teaching. It seems like he's teaching himself and he doesn't realize that the students he is teaching aren't at his level of expertise. Also, his tests are extremely hard (90% of grade) and the study questions only help you to a certain extent.

Lectures are not interesting, he just reads from the power point. Class is all tests, with 10% dedicated to quizzes and in class questions. You could never come show up to class, read all the power points, only show up for tests, and still pass with a solid A. Hate going to class, and often ignore lectures and do my own notes. Tests are hard.

Definitely take physiology from Mcknight if you can. He is a super relaxed guy. If you put in the effort you can easily succeed in this class and get a good grade. The grade is broken down like this: 95% tests, 5% quizzes, 5% extra credit.

Professor McKnight was a great professor. He gives study questions which match closely to his exams. He also arrives early to class to go over the study questions. If you go to class you can receive extra credit. His class is definitely not easy and requires a lot of studying. I can say I left this class with a great understanding of physiology.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible Professor, told us numerous times he only teaches in order to get grants from the university to further his research in physiology, he does not enjoy teaching. I went to his office hours to get explanation on a question from a test and he called my friends and I annoying, and stupid that we went out of our way to get something explained.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great Professor, very interesting and engaging in lecture and ties in cool examples of physiology into lectures. Stick to the study questions he gives you and really focus on those. McKnight has some troubles with using technology, but that shouldn't affect how great of a professor he is.

Dr. McKnight is a great teacher. The class is difficult in its nature. You can follow his lecture and study to understand the basics, then you will see the big picture. He gives you the study guide which is very helpful to know what he expects from you. TA session is very helpful as well. I would recommend it to anyone who is willing to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of the best Biology teacher I have ever had! He is a really fun lecturer and a really nice professor. I do not think he is a hard grader despite what other reviewers say. There is no homework but quizzes are super easy and everything on the test had been gone over in the lecture and study guide that he provides. Clicker extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was a difficult class it has no hw, just quizzes and tests. Quizzes are not bad, but the tests are hard. They are worth basically your entire grade. He does give 5% extra credit for coming to class during clicker Qs. Toughest test grader i've ever had. one wrong word in a sentence  wrong answer. "the" vs "a" could be wrong. Memorize exactly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not an easy class in terms of grades. I had fun in class, but the only problem was with the tests, they are hard, it's not all multiple choice. The average on these tests are like a 60 and no curve given. Lectures are not bad. Quizzes are easy, Homework is easy 100, And overall not a easy class but will get extra credit (5%) if you go to class.

Good guy, but boooring lectures. quizzes are super easy. You will get extra credit for coming to class and answering clicker questions, he will basically give you the answer. He is ready to help. He has a review sessions almost every week  and is super helpful. Wouldn't take him again but learned a lot and would recommend him for once.
Authentic and real. Dean knows how to keep it interesting.
Take Dean's class. 100%
Dr. McGovern knows how to connect with people. He pays close attention to the way the class discussions are moving and who's voices are missing.  He creates a very inclusive classroom.

Class was mainly run by peer mentors (and I do wish he cracked down on them a little more for certain things), but overall he's super funny, caring and kind. Great prof to take class with for the times he was there!

Although the class was mostly run by peer mentors, Dean always chimed into our discussions and was overall an amazing professor. I had so much fun in this class and that was partly because of how kind and caring he was! Take 1010 with Dean
The course content is manageable, but the overall experience can feel cold and inflexible. This is better for students who are highly independent and do not need much guidance, grace, or support.

Students should know that this professor's communication style may feel very rigid and unsupportive. The course material itself is manageable, but grading and communication can be frustrating if you need flexibility or clear guidance. Keep records of all communication, read every policy carefully, and clarify expectations before major deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this as an online course so I know absolutely nothing about Megan as a physical teacher tbh. But the canvas page was really well organized and clear, all of the assignments and quizzes were consistent and easy to follow. You can skip the video lectures and extra readings-just look at the summary slides.

I don't remember a SINGLE thing taught in this class, yet I got by with an A. Just look at the study guide textbook + normal textbook during quizzes and you'll be right as rain. I stopped watching her lectures halfway through the semester and still managed to do well. Discussion + Quiz + Self graded lab almost every week, but it's pretty easy.

This class was incredibly easy and required little effort. Getting ahold of Professor Reynolds can be tough; don't expect your issues to be resolved. You are pretty much on your own. Assignments are easy and labs are self-graded. Keep up with the work and you'll be fine. Don't expect any huge takeaways or deep learning though.

I think Prof. Reynolds does a good job at describing what to expect on assignments throughout each week. She also wants her students to succeed the best way they can which is another good indication about her. The class is also easy if you're good at Statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is easier than I expected. The quizzes follow the textbook really closely, you don't need her lectures if you read the book, since she basically reads the chapter. All of your interactions are through the TAs, she's not very involved in the class. There are easy discussion points and extra credit. For a stats class, I was surprised.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Megan is the best professor Ive had, hands down. Cares for all of her students as individual and treated us as her equals. The course is heavily discussion based and offers a lot of important perspective. But really, I loved Megan. One of the few professors Ive met who understands that mental and physical health is more important than a grade.

I am so glad I took this class! Megan was super caring, and really helped me learn how to read research papers. She made class discussions a safe place to share personal experiences, and I've come away with a much better understanding of social inequality. Quizzes and exams were not hard at all. Can't recommend enough!

I loved Professor Reynolds. She is one of the most caring professors ive ever had. The course was not too hard at all, and I really enjoyed it. I found the topics to be very important to discuss, and the environment was very comfortable. It was definitely my favorite class of the semester, and one of my favorite professors.

Exams tougher than practice ones. Weekly labs easy. 1 pg of notes can be used on test (write down word for word her slides). More concept focus, less on practicing math. Top hat needed (36$ish). Final paper unclear (no feedback b/c it's the last thing u do). Attend. large part of grade and quizzes taken on app daily. Funny and email accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She teaches the material very slowly, but attendance is mandatory. I was bored out of my mind the whole class. The material was easy, tests were easy for the most part, although her study guides were wrong a couple times. She doesn't like it when students disagree with her, seems to get offended easily. This class was a waste of time.

Tough professor and sarcastic. Open to discussion but questioning her amounts to high treason which she will inform you of through a passive-aggressive email. Would definitely not recommend her class.

Megan was awful. She makes you download a $25 app that's the same as a clicker. She also spends the first 15 minutes of class talking about nothing. At the end of the semester, she gave me an incorrect grade for the quizzes and when I asked her about it, she literally would not tell me where the number came from. Easy material, horrible teacher.

1) She does powerpoint lectures, for a math class! So it's very difficult to follow the process 2) No homework assignments, which sucks because you don't get any practice with the calculations or the material 3) Her practice tests are super easy but then the exams are impossible and filled with things she never taught.  -Just take class online

When I first started the semester, I was super excited because she made us aware that she would not let us fail. However, her class was super confusing/hard and her explanation of things were not clear. For the final paper, her instructions were pretty much, "figure it out yourself" because she gave none. She also said that no one would get an A.

There's a difference in sarcasm and ignorance of other's backgrounds. She made comments that were micro-agressions. She changed syllabus very often (almost every class). Canceled class four times with questionable excuses. Math was never explained, she only had vague power points and talked for all of the class.

Megan has a very sarcastic personality which I know several students didn't love. She switched the syllabus several times, making it a little hard for people to keep track of due dates and things, but if you are in class she very thoroughly keeps you up to date. Assignments are almost identical to tests. She knows her stuff! I learned SO MUCH!
SO boring and rude to students. This class was a total waste of my time
she not really organize with her course materials and she did not explains anything to you, not SI.

Professor Metos was an excellent professor! She was caring and gave great feedback that helped me improve. She shared great stories that made class super interesting and fun. I learned a lot that applies to my career and life, like public speaking and business writing. I highly recommend taking her!

This hybrid class is a 100pt grade book with 1 lecture a week. Melissa makes sure you are understanding what is being said and makes sure to not overwhelm her students with homework or outside of class time. Everything can be done within an hour if done efficiently. Overall I would recommend taking this professor

I don't really like English-related courses in general because I struggle in them, but this teacher felt the best teacher I could've gotten, despite my dislike of the course. She's a very fair teacher, a little strict with the grading but gives good feedback that makes you understand why you got the grade that you got.

Professional Business Comm. Hated the public speaking part. But there were good pointers on how to improve public speaking. Attendance was important for this class, and often graded. Sometimes she is a little stingy with the small details in grading. She also randomly calls on people if people don't volunteer. But for the most part seemed caring.

I took biz comm from professor Metos spring semester. She made us speak in front of the class a lot, at first I hated it but I dramatically improved my public speaking and professional communication. She helped me beef up my resume too for class credit. No cap the other reviews about her being young are true but it made it way easier to communicate

Professor Metos is incredible! She makes Writing 1010 fun and inspiring. Her energy and passion for writing are contagious, and as a young, relatable professor, she creates a comfortable and engaging environment. She truly cares about her students' success. Take her class—you won't regret it!

Professor Metos is the best writing teacher that I have ever had.  She cares deeply about the success of her students and was very willing and helpful in the revision process.  I went into the 1010 class terrified of all the essays I would be writing in college but she provided some great tools and strategies to make the process much easier.
Good prof. She was super chill. 1010 sucks but the mix of classic and contemporary content made it enjoyable. This was way better than my first 1010 that I dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was really nice and made the academic writing process approachable for a non-native English speaker. It was good to have a young woman professor who was also a woman. She is very kind and understanding. Writing is so hard so I still got a B.

Super cool, very attractive and high quality corpus. Given that the class is required I enjoyed this professor for the work super chill and it seemed like she actually cared about making the course substantive even though it was gen ed. as a non writing focus student highly recommend.
Very good professor, made coming to class easy and worth it. Personable with students absolutely loved this class.

This was my second semester with Marissa, and she's super awesome! She truly cares about her students. The class is fun, easy, and helpful for finding your path in COMM. Attendance matters, and there's a lot of writing, but it's a great and manageable course!

Marissa was such a caring and understanding professor who taught me very valuable skills about public speaking. she made class fun, enjoyable, taught things in a way that was easy to understand, and was insanely helpful. she gives amazing feedback and wants you to succeed. please take a class with marissa you wont regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very much a quiz/exam heavy course, but I think that's the norm for every 1050 class at the U. The lectures were fast-paced, but he did a good job working with what he had. Also, attendance isn't required, but if you want to succeed in the class definitely go to the lectures. It made everything much easier, and there are guided notes to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If I didn't have a good highschool teacher to teach me Algebra I would've failed. He consistently made topics more confusing and would even do problems wrong a lot. I ended up just not going to class and only taking quizzes and exams. If you do take this class with him, use Organic Chemistry Teacher on youtube to learn what you need.

Do not take this class unless you want to be left completely confused. This guy had us taking quizzes every Monday about topics we had just covered in class. His lectures were all over the place, and he often left certain things out that students needed. You will struggle.

Dr. Meegan was a great professor. He was very patient and understanding that we have lives outside of school. There are lots of assignments for this class, but most of them are short. I would definitely recommend taking his class to fulfill a social science credit.
This is a very hard class, take the online one.
he won't work with you at all on dead lines and is not compassionate at all. Wouldn't recommend to anyone

Professor Megan is so so good! I took Psych 1010 at 7:30am and it was hard to make it some days, but all of his lectures are posted online and easy to watch on your own time. He is very engaging and a fun professor and the tests aren't too hard. If you're like me, you definitely need to study for the tests but it's all pretty straightforward!

He has everything ready for you like if you want to get a head start with his essays or do the homework in advance everything is open on canvas. He gives you terms for the exams and responds fast to emails. He is incredibly nice and encourages you to succeed. I enjoyed his class.

One of my favorite professors. He was super kind, funny, and very animated in the way he taught. he also incorporated guest speakers which was super fun! A lot of the material he taught has really stuck with me and helped me in my next psychology classes. Great professor!

Professor Meegan is super energetic and is a nice guy which makes the lectures pretty good. The assignments are easy, but the exams are a lot harder and aren't similar to the homework. There are a couple of essays which are graded tough, but other than that it's a decent class.

I took PSY 1010 with Meegan. He is one of my favorite professors! My lecture was at 7:30 am so it was hard to get there but he makes them very engaging. He is funny and animated and explains most concepts by using real-life examples. There were a couple papers, quizzes and 5 exams. The workload was manageable. I totally recommend taking his class!
Took his 7:30am class but he was somehow pretty lively and kept the spirit high. Hardly had hw, and it was all easy, but you have to study a LOT for the tests, they're pretty challenging

Super good professor but he makes things due at 7:30 am and he knows it makes no sense but we should just deal with it. Its really easy to forget about assignments when they don't show up on your canvas dashboard until after they're due. Other than that, his lectures are pretty great and the curriculum is super interesting.

He's a super energic, made coming at 7:30 am worth the hassle. The class was super easy and at most I only had to study for 2 hours including hw a week. The test all you had to know was how to imply all of the terms and then you're set. I got above a 90% on all the test. Great teacher and really fun gen ed for me to do.

I loved Sean's class. He was super engaging and animated in lectures, and always made sure he was accessible outside of class for help. The assignments are super straight forward and simple. His tests can be a little difficult even if you attend all lectures so I still recommend that you study :)
I took Meegans 7:30am class but he made it easy to be there and stay awake. He is a very funny guy. Attendance isn't mandatory but it helps being there for lectures.
Its way too broad. Probably one of the hardest classes Ive ever taken. Be prepared to be confused on what it is you are actually being tested on and when.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Meegan is incredibly engaging and finds a way to make even a 7:30AM lecture enjoyable. He offers a lot of extra credit if you put in the time to do it (participating in psychology studies). I attended about half of the lectures and studied off of the posted materials and exam study sheets and I did very well. You do have to study.

Overall, a really enjoyable professor. He was funny and entertaining and somehow managed to make a 7:30am lecture enjoyable. While there's a lot of homework, it was overall fairly easy to complete. The only problem was sometimes it was a bit difficult to know what exactly to study for the tests.
The 7:30am class was hard to get up for but he made it interesting. He's very animated and so he kept me engaged. If you go to the study sessions and do most of the reading you'll have an A no doubt.

Meegan is awesome. He is very humorous but also was able to effectively cover course material. His exams are pretty straightforward, but I recommend attending the offered SI sessions as they helped me be more aware of what exactly was going to be covered on each exam.

Sean is funny, he keeps his lectures interesting because of his personality. I went to almost every class always did the homework and never scored very well on the tests. I think theres a lot of mixed information in the class and it's hard to know what to study. Overall I would take it again but approach it differently.

The information given in lectures, reading from the textbook and the information needed for tests are all completely different. Super hard to know what you need to know for the tests because it's all different.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He explained things pretty well and was very easy to work with. There were plenty of tests, but they were all fairly easy.

Sean Meegan is a very energetic and enthusiastic professor with a solid knowledge of his topic areas. His class is complete online-accessible with all homework, quizzes, and lectures being on a website you sign up for. His exams all have review sessions that make it very easy to score well. This class is a very easy A if you do the hw on time.

You should be able to attend the class in order to get an A from this class. In terms of memorizing vocabulary is also important that you have to exactly understand then able to classifying the differences on similar vocabs.

Professor Meegan made his boring lectures interesting. Due to the fact that an intro to psych class does cover a vast variety of information, there is a lot for you to take in for each exam. Expect ok--tough exams, and make sure you study for a considerable amount of time for every detail that he mentions in lectures.
He is very outgoing and the most entertaining professor I have ever had. Assignments are easy, but a lot of busy work. Drops the lowest test grade out of the 5 test.

The professor was kinda quirky but he was a nice guy who enjoyed teaching, i really enjoyed this class its not super difficult but I would recommend reading the book and I would definitely recommend not taking it at 7:30am like I did, that was my only regret. Overall he's helpful, brings treats, and drops lowest test score. T.A. is available

Lectures are interesting. Most of the homework he gives out is online reading assignments once or twice a week with really easy quizzes.  The test are not bad as long as you study.  Its a really easy class  and very interesting

Mr. Meegan's class was really fun and informational. I had a 7:30 class and he kept my attention really well. There are 5 tests, but he drops one of them. He also offers extra credit if you do 5 more hours of psych experiments. The reviews are an absolute necessity, but if you go to class you will pretty much already know everything.

Homework was VERY easy. Lectures are okay but not necessary to pass exams if you get the text book and attend study sessions. Study sessions is where I really learned the most and helped me do well on exams. Does not curve assignments or grades. Homework is essential to passing the class.

Dr. Meegan has been one of my favorite Professors throughout my college experience. Don't get me wrong, his class is tough and you're going to have to put the work in, but he teaches in a way that makes you want to study and learn more.  Keep up on the reading, he will help you see how your knowledge can be applied if you have a basic understanding

The online assignments are extremely easy to do.  The tests are harder, but he gives you a vocab list to review.  He doesn't test on definitions, but on how you can apply the word to the real world using examples.  He gives examples in class so it's best to attend.  Overall a pretty decent teacher
great professor. very interesting lectures.
SUPER EASY CLASS! Fairly interesting. Professor is enthusiastic so keeps lectures interesting. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Assignments and exams are pretty easy. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Pretty easy class, do the assignments online and do well on tests and you're good. His voice drives me insane and his lectures are pretty boring. I slept through most of his class, I'd say go to class and try to pay attention he uses examples as test questions.
Pretty cool guy. I didn't go to class much because his voice drives me crazy but he was a really good professor. Online assignments help you to get an A on tests. Take this course, it's worth it!

I didn´t read even read one entire chapter, just did the assignments, quizzes, etc. I always attended class except when sick and think it helped a lot! I didn´t put lots of effort in it...only studied terms the day before the exam and got an A-!!! Take his class, you won´t regret it! Super easy if you pay attention! :)

Great class. I'm  about to graduate with an engineering degree and taking psychology was  a very good decision. His lively attitude was refreshing and almost all of the topics are applicable to daily life. Tests are much easier than i had anticipated after learning so much content.
okay class. Easy A if you try.
Nice guy but not a great teacher. The class is mostly vocabulary and memorization

I took psychology in high school so it was kind of a review.I hardly used the book. His lectures were fine but not fascinating even though I love psychology I would fall asleep in class some times. His tests were multiple choice and easy if you go to the SI sessions and look over the vocabulary list he posts online.Nice guy though and very friendly
Not a very good teacher! talks about nothing then 2 days before the test gives you 100 vocab words to study. dont like how he teaches some might, it leaves for a lot of stuff to do on your own.
Good professor but makes you feel like he hates you! Made me change my major. Not really cooperative when you need his help. He's not my favorite

I loved psychology in High School so I thought I would take it here at the U. It was a bad decision, the class is difficult. There's 200 kids in there and it's at 7:30 am only half of us ever show up because he doesnt really teach anything everything is straight from the book. So basically even if you attend class it's still you and your book :(

He never knew the answers to questions and often gave incorrect information as parts of his examples, which was irritating.  The class could have been interesting, had Meegan not gotten all his lesson notes directly from the book, accented with youtube clips.

Dr. Meegan was really entertaining. It was a 7:30 class, which I thought would be awful.  But he usually had loud music playing and sometimes brought us treats, especially on exam days. The material was interesting but make sure you read the chapters.  I felt that about 20-25% of the exam was based from the book. Altogether, a decent and fun class.
Very hard to discern what would be on the tests even with study guides.
fine

Course was difficult, because the instructor would change every week and the book wasn't helpful--I think it was written for high school. The online activities often didn't work and were lame.  I would not recommend this course with this format.  The Prof was a good teacher, but he only taught for 3 weeks at best.

My only advice to you is that if you dont have to take this class for a major in psychology, dont take this class. Its hard to tell whats on the test and what to study for, and it seems like no one cares about you, which is true because its trying to week out kiddies. Dont take this class.

I really didn't like this professor.  I cringed when he opened his mouth because his voice is so high pitched.  Random people would come in and teach every week.  Tests were very hard and it was very unclear what would be on the tests.  I think it was just a psychology weed out class.  I would tell anyone not to take it.
He was a very good Professor, although he was never around. We always had someone new teaching the class! It was such a great class though! I learned a lot!
Very outgoing and class is easy if you study enough.

Professor Metz is a nice professor, he cares about his students. But how do you teach an „Intro to German Studies Course“ and hardly talk about WII? I had a hard time with the chosen content, he pretty much covers 4 pieces of text throughout the semester. Also prepare for most of lecture to be given in English, disappointing for a German class.

Metz is one of my favorite professors! We just discussed the books every class. Being quiet I didn't often raise my hand, but when I did, I felt like he listened to and acknowledged my point and talked more about it. He was very flexible when things came up with my schedule in terms of being absent, and overall super nice.
He's an amazing Professor and human being

Dr. Metz is passionate. Every lecture is passionate and he wants to hear your voice. He is interested in your own opinion, where he often also says you don't need to use secondary literature. His German is good, but he still makes some mistakes. He really cares about his students/' welfare. You will need to write a lot. He gives a lot of feedback.

Professor Metz has been my favorite professor at the U so far. While the class requires a decent amount of attention, its fairly easy as long as you give it your best and you participate. Hes very approachable and cares about his students a lot. Also, listen to his feedback and try to incorporate that into future assignments.

I've had professor Metz for both GERM3550 and GERM3900. Professor Metz is one of the best professors I've had at the University of Utah. He cares about his students and cares that they learn. He's very knowledgeable and very approachable if you are struggling. His classes will stretch you, but you will learn how to critically analyze literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading and LOTS of class discussion. The readings can range from short and interesting to long, dry and boring. DO NOT write papers the night before, he notices and will dock your grade for it. The final test is a discussion with another classmate in front of the class. Metz is a nice guy though and is incredibly approachable with needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Well, to say the least I will never take one of his classes again. I have never been so frustrated in a generals class before. Hated every second of the class and will never recommend it to my peers. You read like 6 semi good books, they're quite boring and on top of that, the papers are absolutely horrendous to write. He was nice I guess.

I have taken various GERM4900 courses from Metz because of his choice of literature and his discussions in class. Metz is passionate about German literature and cares about his students. You will learn how to write an essay and see a piece of work through several perspectives. This class with stretch your mind. Take lots of notes for your essays.

I had Dr. Metz for a graduate seminar and I loved it. He is energetic, insightful, and genuinely cares about his students. His teaching is engaging and his feedback on papers is very helpful. He has a rich theoretical background from which he draws. Highly recommended to those interested in theory, comparative literature, and literary study.
Metz is great. I could listen to him talk all day - his lectures are fascinating. He'll make you understand literature in ways you never thought possible.

Metz is one of the best teachers I've had at the U. He's very forgiving if you're not a great German speaker or writer. Really nice guy who sincerely wants you to understand the material instead of worrying about your grade. If you get a chance to take Metz's course, do it.
Respectful of students varying abilities. Knows his stuff! Will help you grow as a writer and student.
Talks too much. If you do not agree with his opinion, you will not do good in class.
A ver nice man and is willing to work with you.
No Comments
Very understanding of tough circumstances as long as you communicate.

Overall, awesome professor. I learned a lot about various types of drawing techniques. She is very chill and was a easy grader. My only complaint is that she made us buy stuff that wasn't used very often in the semester.

Don't listen to the 1/5 reviews, Annette is not a harsh grader. This is coming from someone who believed they had very meager artistic skills. She becomes aware of your limits and considers them when grading. The class is fun, but some assignments feel pretty long. She mostly gives clear feedback, but she has a quiet voice in a loud classroom.
Highly recommended learning how to draw before taking this "basic" drawing class.
She grades fairly harshly. I recommend drawing before taking the class to be successful.
Pretty nice and caring professor, but cared a lot about never missing a class. Didn't even give the normal 1 - 3 free missed days.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was by far my absolutely favorite course ever! i loved that i co9ulod go ahead and pace my self at my own time. Great feed back was always given. 10/10 class
Good professor, everything is laid out so you can get ahead in the class.

reviews.comment: I took this class online, so I did not interact with her that much, but she seemed generally nice and understanding. NO LATE WORK! It gets docked by a lot (from 2 points to 1.5).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: SHE IS SO AWESOME! Heather is so caring and constructs very good lecture videos, however the lectures follow slideshows which you can choose to directly use as well. All information is concisely stored though heavily explained, making for clean notes which are easy to reference later. She is GREAT at teaching! I'd heard good things, it is true!

The lectures were all online and easy to follow. There were many discussion posts and a few assignments. However, my problem was with the exams. The exams mostly consist of 60 questions in 60 minutes, both multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blank, which I found did not give me enough time to take the exam thoroughly and sufficiently.

Heather was kind and her TA was helpful. She made an already interesting course load more accessible to people with no background in sociology/criminology which I appreciated. I think she should focus on pacing online classes better-- telling students to finish an entire book in a week wasn't great. Also, her discussion boards had zero requirements

The content was super interesting but for the most part, she was pretty condescending on her comments. The class being out of 100 points was super frustrating too. I did all the work plus watching every lecture and she still  gave me a lower grade than I wanted.

Highly recommend the online version of this course for anyone looking for an easy diversity credit. Weekly disussion board assignments based on lectures can be easily done without actually watching the lectures.  The books were interesting but even assignments based on readings could be done by glancing at sparknotes. Not a harsh grader whatsoever.
