reviews.comment: Heather was, and still is, one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. Her criminology course, while not easy, was super interesting, and I'm so glad I took it. It really made me think of so many things I never thought of before and changed my opinion on so many things.

have taken this teacher for criminology as well as sexual assault and again next semester. Love the way she lectures and tries to explain everything. You must listen to the lectures to get a good grade on the tests.
Great lectures, tests are hard.
Hard grader, weekly discussions and heavy exams.
Great lectures with lots of homework. Test Heavy and Tough grader.

reviews.comment: Hard  and Low grader, weekly discussions, hard quizzes. I will not take any of her classes again.

reviews.comment: Interesting topic but tough grader, 2 tough exams, you have to read two books during the semester, homework and discussions every week.
Interesting topic but tough grader, 2 tough exams, you have to read 2 books during the semester, homework and discussions every week, she takes forever to grade.

Good professor and gives good information about women and crime. Although, her grading isn't the best. Everything is worth no more than 2 points even the extra credit. A final paper worth only 10 points and exams are more than half of the final grade. It's ridiculous.

Professor Melton's lectures are very informative and interesting. There are weekly discussion posts and occasional assignments, but most of your grade depends on test scores. If you watch all of the lectures and study your notes, you should be able to succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Melton is phenomenal. The class is composed of short assignments, discussions, two tests, and a final paper, really not too bad as long as you watch the lectures and study for the tests. All assignments were relevant. Dr. Melton is clearly very knowledgeable and is a great lecturer, I was never bored and absorbed so much. Highly recommend!

Dr. Melton is by far one of the best professors at the University of Utah. She is actively involved in research, is very knowledgeable, and very approachable. Wish I could have taken more of my classes from her.

Love this class. It only lectures because there is no required textbook, but they are interesting. A majority of the lectures felt like I was watching Youtube for fun rather than it being a boring lesson. Not many assignments and graded pretty leniently. The tests are worth probably around 70% of the class and are hard if you don't study much.

Discussion boards and assignments every week that you get 2/2 on if you do it. Tests are hard and not online, you have to study, and there are 2 exams all semester that take up your entire grade since other assignments are 2 points. Do well on the tests and you'll get an A. One final paper, easy. Extra credit 5 points too, easy. Tests are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I've taken a couple of her classes. I like her a lot. There are surprise assignments in SOC 3565 and there are a lot of assignments in SOC 3561. She's a very generous grader and does offer one extra credit assignment. You have to read the books she assigns, but the material is very interesting. I would take more classes from her for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Women & Crime was a solid class. Course work consisted of 4 exams - 25 points each (drops lowest score), 5 in class assignments - 2 points each, one book report - 5 points, and a final paper - 10 points. Also required you read two books as they are on the exams. Attendance is not mandatory, but you need the lecture notes to do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Melton gave good and informative lectures but be prepared to take detailed notes and study them well before each exam. The exams are 60% of your class and based almost completely on the lectures. If you don't do well on the exams then you won't do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance optional but there are 5 surprise in-class assignments. Extra Cred. can only be taken once (2 pts). Notes online aren't completely filled out and you need to go to get the full notes. You will not pass if you don't have them (exams are taken from them). Tests are hard but she holds review sessions. No txtbook (1 novel tho). Amazing!

reviews.comment: exams are mostly based on the lectures, don't get the textbook. exams are pretty hard, and they affect the grade a ton but she usually bumps the score up a few points. lectures are pretty good but pretty long. she knows what she's talkin about
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are on lectures she posts online and also from the textbook and a book she wants you to read for the class and it makes up most of your grade. For an online class there are a lot of little assignments to complete but most are easy discussion boards. Wants a lot of incorporation of material directly into whatever assignments, gets redundant.

reviews.comment: Heather is a pretty solid professor with a lot of evidence to support her lectures. Her assignments and discussions mostly ask for your opinion rather than knowledge of the textbook. Her exams are pretty tough, but added 1.5% onto our scores this semester and are mostly based on the review guides she provides.

The class (Women and Crime) was interesting and Heather taught it well. She did well at handling sensitive subjects and gave great lectures. You do not need to attend or do the mini-assignments to pass, as long as you can do well on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took the online class of intro to criminology. The lectures are long, there are at least 30 to listen too, and her voice can be annoying at times because she spoke close to the mic. The assignments were only worth 2 points, which is nothing because they weren't easy. The tests were 60 questions, but they are only 30 points.

Lectures were interesting and homework was fairly easy. The tests were very difficult, even after studying the study guide they didn't match to the test most of the time and she only gives you 60 min for 60 questions (10 or so which are short answer) if she would just increase the time on the test even by 30 minutes, it would have helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great professor. Has you listen to recorded lectures so it's like you're in class. Assignments/discussions are due weekly but they're easy and mostly about your opinion. One 5pg paper about a topic of your choice. She did a great job of making the class interesting, interactive and fun. Would definitely recommend!

Heather is a great professor who really cares about what she teaches. Unlike a lot of other online classes, the lectures actually make you feel like you're in a real class getting the same experience. There are two tests that are based entirely off the lectures.

Heather is a great professor who really cares about what she teaches. Unlike a lot of other online classes, the lectures actually make you feel like you're in a real class getting the same experience. There are two tests that are based entirely off the lectures. There are discussion posts and homework due most weekends, but they're simple to do.

Heather is an amazing instructor i loved her class. She has 3 exams which are easy if you do the study guide and attend her review session. Her lectures are extensive with lots of slides but the material is very interesting. this was never a boring class, i recommend taking classes from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was so easy! It was very educating and interesting but wasn't awful. Would take this professor again.

If you're not a liberal then get ready to feel as if you can't voice your opinion and maybe even uncomfortable. She is a hardcore feminist who believes prostitution should be legalized. Wait, what?   If this is mandatory then sell your soul to the devil and write your paper on the evils of the white man.

Wonderful online teacher!  Recorded easy to listen to lectures that were interesting and insightful.  By far the best online teacher I've had.  I took this as a half-semester, expedited, summer class--the tests were a bit challenging, covered a lot of material, so make sure you study.

As long as you attend class and take good notes, you'll be fine. The tests are straight forward, Heather is super passionate about the material, and she is straightforward and flexible. I loved this class!

Heather is really awesome. Her lectures are really important for tests, but there are only three and then one 6 page research paper which she gives you lots of time to do. She does offer extra credit for events. The tests reflect the lectures and she provides review sessions and sheets. assigns a textbook for women and crime but IT IS NOT NECESSARY

Dr. Melton is one of my favorite professors that I have ever had. She is passionate and really knows a lot about criminology. Her passion makes the lectures interesting, and overall I think she is a skilled lecturer. She is very reasonable and fair in grading. I highly recommend any of her classes.

Discussion posts & assignments are easy & pretty short. 1 research paper due around finals, but you have a while to do it. Some test questions are really easy and some are hard.... so just study the lectures, take your own notes from them, and do the readings when assigned. It is interesting stuff so you won't get bored. Easy A if you work for it.

Great online lectures, I learned so much, and she is fun to listen to that is always a plus. Her tests are hard, but if you study the material well you will do fine. This is not an easy A class, but totally worth it.

I took this class online and it was a bit of a challenge. Here grading criteria was out of 100 points total which really sucked. Your grade is basically the tests and paper and the tests are worth the vast majority of points. When I missed 6 points on the first test, that alone dropped my grade to 94%. If she gave more points then it would bebetter

Heather is nice and class is lecture heavy. She teaches off of power point slides. She's a bit disorganized so you just need to take good notes to understand the slides. Don't buy the book. Very helpful if you ask questions during test. She wants you to succeed. She's a mom first, then a professor. I hear her online class is disorganized.
She is very straight forward. If you like online classes this is a good one to take.
Sometimes gets off track in lectures, but great professor overall!

Melton's awesome.  Had her for three different classes and I enjoyed all of them.  Word to the wise: DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOKS FOR ANY OF HER CLASSES!! Her classes are SUPER lecture heavy. If you study and take scrupulous notes you'll be fine. The lowest grade I received from her was an A-. If you're interested in Criminology, take her classes.

I had Professor Melton as an online teachers for Criminology and Good Cop, Bad Cop. She had great online lectures, that were never boring. The exams weren't too bad, and the paper wasn't too long either. Overall great classes and great teacher! Really admire

I took Dr. Melton's Women and Crime soc class and really enjoyed it. She is really nice and is such a good teacher. She takes the time to make sure that the course material is clear. Her tests are not too hard and she drops the lowest scored one. Textbook use was low. I definitely recommend taking a class from her.

Dr. Melton is a great professor. She's definitely one of my favorite professors. She's very knowledgeable, she's personable, and she makes class fun and interesting. Her tests aren't easy, but they're not horribly difficult. If you go to class regularly, you can easily get a good grade. The lecture material is much more important than the textbook.
She is a good teacher but this online criminology class wasn't easy.  You had to read a book and do a report on it and her tests weren't easy at all.

Dr. Melton is a great teacher, her lectures are very interesting and she explains things well. Lecture notes are provided in Power Point. Assigned reading material was very interesting. Class was not difficult. Some of her tests were a bit tricky (phrasing and multiple choice answers), however, she drops the lowest test score for your final grade.
She is a great teacher and well prepared for her class. She supplies the notes. If you ever need help, she makes time for you. You learn alot and you enjoy the class.

She is by far the best teacher at the U.  She is always there to help out her students, you will honestly learn and enjoy everything she teaches.  If you study for her class you will do just fine, considering her notes are easily read and easy to understand.  I highly suggest taking any of her classes, Ive already taken three.
Material she teaches is fascinating, and she is easy to work with.  I recommend taking her classes.  Really the best professor I"ve had this semester
She just had her baby, so congrats on that :) She is very fair professor and knows her stuff. I will look for her classes in the future.
Heather really is cool--and she can relate to the questions we have on the material.  Very fair-minded, I really enjoyed her class.

Dr. Melton is fun, interesting, cool, and she looks pretty hip too, so students can probably really relate to her.  I love the way she teaches, and she has notes posted on webct. She's always up for questions and helping a student out. She's fair too!

This class was rough, but honestly I learned a ton as well. Shawn has only taught this class a couple times before, so he's very open to feedback, and adjusts the class as needed. Tests are HARD, but he tends to hint at what will be on them, so if you show up to lectures, you should have a good idea. Shawn is overall a good professor though.

Professor Miller is passionate about human anatomy. I took his summer class, which covered more material in less time. I wouldn't recommend it unless it's necessary and you can commit several hours a week to studying outside of class. That being said, Shawn really does want his students to succeed, just make sure keep up with the workbook!

Shawn was a very good professor . He was super knowledgeable. He did ramble and we would get behind be he would adjust exams accordingly to where we were in lecture . Anatomy is hard regardless of what professor you take it with . I would definitely take it with Shawn again. You just have to put in the time for this class

Shawn rambles a lot during class lecture and can never stay on track with the syllabus. His tests are really hard and he never really explains exactly what will be in them. He's the type of professor that if he talks about it for even .01 seconds then it will be on the test. 

He also never answers his email

Anatomy is a really difficult class. You have to put in the work for this class no matter who you take it from. You need to read what it recommended and listed in the text book, and you need to attend lectures and labs. He's an amazing professor. His rating here is from students who don't put in effort and take it out on him. He's fabulous.

reviews.comment:
Shawn Miller,
The man is smart don't get me wrong, he knows his material VERY well. Does he know how to teach it in an efficient manner, not a chance. He will ramble at times about things going on in his life and often spend way too much time on specific topics. Did he flaunt a 42/75 average for the 2nd exam 3 years in a row, yes. Don't take

reviews.comment: When i registered for the class, I was unaware it heavily features dissecting cats - I also feel that having individual dissection was not the best way to teach comparative morphology as there was little oversight or direction and few clear lines drawn between homologous structures and muscles during actual class time.
Interesting subject, but the lectures are really boring and hard to get through. Exams are graded pretty hard, and its difficult to know what he'll emphasize on the exams. The TAs are great.

This class was one of the worst experiences of my life but I'm glad it was Shawn who taught me through. Shawns not afraid to speak his mind and I respect that. He definitely gets off topic and forgets us students aren't as smart as him sometimes, but he is happy to work with you to help you succeed if you show that you want to. 0/10

Dr. Miller is a sensational professor and we should all aspire to be more like Dr. Miller. He's been extremely caring, understanding and flexible with myself. Dr. Miller has been bar none the best professor I have ever encountered at the university.

Dr. Miller is definitely super knowledgeable on the subject of embryology, and it's worth taking the class to get exposed to the material. There were some aspects that were difficult to understand, but overall this was a great class. This was less focused on physiology but more on anatomy and structure.

Super knowledgeable Prof, uses a textbook, lab manual, and lab time to help students succeed. Nice guy and brings his dogs to class! Lectures are interesting and relatable (things on disease, drinking alcohol, sports etc...). Iconic U class for pre-healthcare students but everyone know's it's a lot of work! I loved it!!

Despite all the negative reviews, I had an incredible experience with Dr. Miller. His enthusiasm & passion for anatomy is inspiring & helps students absorb the info! Yes, the class is challenging but that would be the case for any anatomy class. His so called "tangents" are often relevant & sometimes funny! Work hard & have fun! You can do it!!

Anatomy is difficult but I thought Dr. Miller did a good job of explaining the material. Dr. Miller is fair and willing to work with students. Sometimes goes on tangents about not relevant material. Exams are hard but this is a hard class. If you put in the work and don't fall behind you'll be fine. Some extra credit and slight curve.

Lectures were the only way to gain the information for the exams yet spent the majority of them rambling about non-course related content. Tests were short and did not match what was emphasized in lecture. Professor was discouraging when asked for help saying that lecture should be more than enough explanation. Avoid taking any classes from him.

Class is incredibly hard. The low rating comes from everything else though. Lab is impossible if you have anything other than this class in your life. Even if you attend office hours, there will be newly dissected pieces on practicals that look different. Exams are graded very harshly and there might be an image from a completely different textbook

The worst prof. Late a lot and went over time always. Unprofessional. Constantly behind in lecture. Lecture required to get content, no supplemental learning material. Bad at writing test questions, and got defensive when I tried to get points back. Doesn't know how to use canvas, so couldn't see grades. Resistant to curve the class. 10/10 avoid.

Shawn was a great instructor. While the lecture wasn't mandatory, passing is unlikely if you don't go. That said, the lectures were great. He is passionate about his work. He was always willing to talk to students and help them. I always felt like it was graded fairly. I would recommend Miller to anyone taking Anatomy.

First day of class he asked the class if there were any transfers students to which a few students replied yes and when asked from where there was a few schools listed but when one student mentioned she transferred from a community college his immediate response was "you should just drop this class". That set the tone as him being an elitist.
Advanced anatomy is a tough course. Be sure to attend the office hours and ask Shawn and the TA's about anything you don't understand during the lecture. The exams are fair but challenging.

Dr. Miller was very knowledgeable but really struggled lecturing. He went on lots of of tangents, lectures contradicted the text, and grading criteria was unclear. He also decided 2 days before an exam that we would have more material on that test than was written in the syllabus. Tests were hard but the workbook prepares you for most questions.

This class was really hard, and you probably definitely need a light course load while taking if you want to do well. Aside from the course itself, Dr. Miller is AMAZING. He genuinely cares for his students and has so much passion for teaching and learning. I'll be taking more of his classes is possible. Make a lot of flashcards and you'll make it!

The class was difficult for sure. Shawn is nice, but can get side tracked very easily. Lectures tend to turn into long tangents. He tests from the lecture itself and the manual. Read/color the manual before lectures. Try and keep up with the workbook bc questions were similar on test. Go to as many TA sessions as possible! They saved me :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grade is based on: Extra credit, 1 midterm, final, and question sets. You are allowed to use a notebook on exams in this class. If you spend a lot of time preparing your notebook you will do well. The midterm and final match closely to the material outlined in the lab handouts. Shawn is also a fair grader and will listen through rebuttals.

I wanted to love this class. I wanted to enjoy going to lecture... but honestly, this class was awful. He rambles SO much. It's hard to pay attention. His test questions were often worded very poorly and he wasn't willing to hear your rebuttal. It's nearly impossible to guess what he wants you to know for the test. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH SHAWN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolutely brilliant: Shawn is excellence in teaching incarnate. He never fails to demonstrate complete mastery of and enthusiasm for his subject. BIOL2325 is a HEAVY workload, no doubt. To succeed in his class, you need only follow his advice to the letter: don't get behind!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 3 tests and lab constitute your entire grade. The tests are so unfairly worded that even the TA's acknowledged it, and Miller is too busy writing his PhD thesis to be bothered to help students. Even though you're being charged full tuition theres no SI, no extra help. It's absolutely ridiculous. Lecturetangentsgiant waste of time.

I would not recommend taking his class during the summer or any anatomy class during the summer. Its a waste of money and fault UofU as much as Shawn for it. you're expected to know his lectures the next day w/o the chance to study, give you homework w/o any second chances or feedback, and lab quizzes on things he hadn't lectured on yet (mucsle).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: DO NOT take Human Anatomy in the summer with Shawn. I cannot say enough times how difficult this class was. The lectures were long and unengaging. 50 percent of the time, the lectures were incredibly off topic or he would lecture for a long time on subjects that didn't even matter, leaving very little time for the difficult stuff. Just don't do it.

Lectures are quick and unorganized, and it's very easy to get lost. No reading. In my other classes teachers have narrowed down areas of study to focus on for exams, he will not. I would definitely not recommend taking his summer semester classes. Unless you're able to go to office hours, you won't be able to verify your workbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Do not take the Vertebrate Morphology lab from Shawn.  He expects WAY too much from you for a 4 credit hour lab.  You will end up putting much more time into this class than you thought you would.  It is even harder than the 3 credit hour lecture.  Not to mention the averages were VERY low and he does not curve.  Terrible "professor."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you are a book learner I would not recommend this class. There is an optional book but from the words of shawn,if something from the book is different from the lecture you must take what you heard in lecture as any answer for the test. Was a straight A student for 4 years until I took this class, his teaching style just didn't fit mine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved the lab, It has been one of the most informative and fun classes I have taken. Due all to the TA's, though. Shawn wouldn't even look me in the eye when I asked him questions. Most of your grade is from tests, which are created to fail you. He uses obscure facets that you may or may not have been fortunate enough to run into. Hope I passed.

Great Anatomy teacher- some may fault him for going over material quickly, but in a shortened summer semester, had to be that way.  I went to office hours on several occasions to get help from him and TA's and always walked away with a better understanding.  I also thought he was very fair on test grading.  I loved the lab as well.

Comparative vertebrate morphology lab was amazing! (I'm a biology nerd) Great teacher, very helpful. To do well you must attend every lab, you have to ask lots of questions and there is A LOT to memorize. If you study hard you will never be surprised by the tests, they are very straightforward.
Human Anatomy is a very tough subject.  While I've heard Mark is better, as long as I put in the time, I did ok with Shawn.  He is highly intelligent but a little boring.

Miller is very bright and knows his stuff. Flies through the material. You have to go to every class and every lab or you will fall behind. Do your workbook and study your slides. Tests are ridiculously hard. He grades even harder. Read test 2 or 3 times before you even put pencil to paper. Likes to test on exceptions and tiny tiny details.

Good instructor- Difficult subject matter. Keep up on your workbook stuff and you'll do fine. The lecture was great - esp. considering it was summer and a shorter course. Shawn did a good job of letting us know "what might be on  an exam" overall great instructor!(ATTEND LECTURE & LAB & DO THE E.C.)

I learned so much in this class and it was so far my favorite class but Sean did an awful job with tests. For the final he put on lots of material that we spend 2 minutes on in lecture...it was the worst test I have ever taken.  It seemed like he just randomly picked questions and he didnt ever remember to what detail he explained things in lecture
mladen has probably the best intuitive understanding of mathematics of anyone i've ever met. insanely cool guy and despite being so smart, conveys his knowledge very well in lecture.

Professor Bestvina is my favorite professor in the math department. He's brilliant and has an intuition for math that has made me a better mathematician. He tests are tricky, but he offers tons of extra credit. He's a great lecturer and if you want a future in math, you should definitely take a class from him.
mladen has an incredible intuition for mathematics which is conveyed in his lectures! makes it look ez

Grades homework very harshly, but exams are surprisingly easy. He prepares you very well for the midterm and final. He's a great guy and pretty funny too, always quick to answer emails etc. Definitely take a course from him but just be VERY explicit for your proofs on homework.

Dr. Bestvina explains material really well and he really knows his stuff. He may not be the most charismatic instructor in the math department, but he really cares to teach his students and his lectures are really well organized. In essence, come to class, do the homework and you will probably do good in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Mladen Bestvina is the best. He really cares about his students and whether or not they will succeed, but doesn't baby them. If you want to do well in his classes, you have to put in the effort and find your own drive. Topology is the coolest.

It was the wirest clas I have ever taken. There was no textbook and the 4 mid-terms were extremely tricky. Moreover, The online-assignment were totally filth. I used to like math when I was in Hight school. However, I really hate it when I took this class. I strongly recommand each and everyone of you to find another teacher for this class.

worst class of the semester....basically....not having a book for the class was the worst thing ever...the tests were very tricky and the homework was ridiculous, find a different teacher if you can.....

Dr. Moore is awesome! He is very passionate about what he teaches, and it shows. I'm taking him for the Kines capstone (4900) right now as well, and I couldn't recommend him enough. Probably one of the best professors I've had at the U.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why people ike this guy so much. He will take points off of your weekly journals without telling you why. These make up almost all of your points in the class as well. He also just does not do a good job and is making any of the content he teaches any bit interesting. It's also just some of the most recycled high school-like content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher and an easy class. He cares about the subject and makes it easy to understand with lectures and 2 writing assignments (1 in class, which is counted as attendance, and 1 outside of class, which was a one-page journal assignment). One midterm which is open note, and there is a final project. Only one day of class per week.
Loved Dr. Moore's class, he was always super engaging and involved class discussions rather than lecturing at us. Just go to class and complete the 2 weekly assignments and you'll get an A.
Professor Morgan made the class very engaging especially across cross language barriers, The weekly questions were always engaging and an interesting assignment. Create a country is a fun project.

The class isn't hard, pay attention to instructions and deadlines. I took an upper division discussion-based class from this professor and the problem was that he loves to talk and often doesn't leave room for actual student discussion. Not a bad prof but room for improvement.
Easy and interesting lectures. Good result.

Professor Porter is one of the most understanding professors that I have had so far at the University of Utah. He is very caring and works with you as long as you communicate and are within reason. This class requires a lot of reading and hard work which is why you should get ahead in the weeks prior. Make sure you make friends and work together :)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I did the week intensive. DO NOT TAKE this class from him in one week. Do not trust the grades that people have on their reviews, they are not true. Final grades won't be up for another month, yet they say they have an A. I busted my butt and will be lucky to get a B. Worst school experience I've ever had. And that is saying something.

I took fall intensive. This is an exhausting week. If you want a B/C in the class, it's manageable. If you want an A, do not plan to do anything else that entire week -including sleep. Seriously. A students in this class slept about 2-4 hours a night. But Porter is caring, smart, accessible, and a wonderful teacher. I would recommend this class.

I appreciate that he doesn't just lecture straight from the book, meaning, I don't read the chapters and come to class just to have him regurgitate exactly what I just read. He's funny as well! Makes the class a lot more enjoyable. Also he talks/sounds almost exactly like Hank Green, so if you're into crash course videos, this is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Porter was a reasonable professor as promised. I think he has good intentions and desires to do right by his students. However, his lectures seemed a bit far reaching for a 100 level course and it was difficult to extract the concepts he tested us on from the lectures that he presented. Tests were heavy on essay-type questions so I felt unprepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and intelligent, but inexperienced. Facilitates interesting conversation both in class and one-on-one. Nice dry sense of humor. Lectures sometimes become a bit tangential, but productively so. Course is a bit of a retread of high school-level civics. Do the readings and learn the vocab and you should be fine.

I took Porter's POLS 1100 class in a week at the Murray campus. Talking about political science for 8 hours a day was brutal but he made those 5 days as painless as possible. I highly recommend Porter. My roommates took the same class from another teacher and hated the class. If you need an AI credit take POLS 1100 from this guy.

The assignments for this class took over 2 months for her to grade, so I have no idea what my grade might be. The class was easy overall. Lectures basically had all the answers to the quizzes and exams. It was a good class, just the lack of grading in a timely manner was frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mukta is a nice professor, but the class feels disorganized, and the referenced anatomy is sometimes questionable in accuracy. Mukta seems like she is knowledgeable, but her knowledge does not always transfer well to the course materials. Consider taking with someone else, but not the end of the world if not.

This was a hybrid class where we were expected to do the lectures on our own before class, yet we would sit in class while the professor would read the same lectures for the entire period. The class had barely any meaningful content yet the assignments were graded very harshly and the exams were very specific questions. Take 3550 online I promise!
Mukta is awesome! It is not the easiest class, but she definitely cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

I love Mukta as a professor, she gets a bad wrap but she truly is my favorite college professor I have had! She knows what she is talking about and if you just do the work and read the research you shouldn't have an issue with getting an A. Both this class and biomechanics can be tricky but if you meet with her in office hours you will surely be ok

Take this class with a different professor or take a different class. She reads of the slides the whole time and when you ask a question she will just read the slide in that part and not explain further. The exams are worded very tricky, even if you know the material you might get it wrong. Video lectures are an hour, 30 minutes of her saying "um".

Mukta isn't a bad professor, but is clearly better suited as a researcher. She is very knowledgeable, but there is a bit of a disconnect when it comes to teaching. I took her for KINES 3092, so if you need to take that class, it is pretty easy with her. Just 3 exams, a few assignments, and a final project. Just make sure to watch the lectures!

She does read off of her slides a lot. She is very slow at grading assignments which is frustrating. My main issue was the wording on her tests, the questions are hard to understand and a lot of the questions didn't have a clear answer to it. There was some extra credit but, the extra credit didn't do much.

Contrary to a lot of the reviews here, I actually enjoyed have Joshi as my professor. She is a little bit hard to understand and some of her assignment instructions are unclear, but those are probably my only critiques. Overall, I think she was a very kind and helpful professor. She was easy to reach and I really liked the content she covered.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teachers like this make me wonder what I am going to college for. She's nice but all she does is read off her slides, and she's hard to understand. Very disappointing lectures on a topic that is very interesting.
She gives very boring lectures, she just reads off slides the entire time. She is super slow to grade and very vague with feedback. Also very hard to get a hold of. Do not recommend.

she reads off of the lecture slides that came from a previous professor and seems she does not know the information herself, don't expect her to clarify. exams are "closed note" but the exam review is just a combination of all slides from the module. she also talks very quietly so do not take this class if you are hard of hearing or can't sit close

She didn't put in grades for our assignments until the last week of classes so I had no clue if I was doing well or not. Her lectures were boring and she didn't have any study guides for the tests. There wasn't much expected to do outside of class and her assignments weren't too hard to do.

Joshi is a terrible teacher. She is very boring and droll in her presentation. She reads off from a PowerPoint with no class participation for 2 hours each time and it's like she's seeing the information for the first time with us. She takes forever to grade, most things being graded at the end of the semester. Her difficult exams are open note.
she doesnt grade anything until the very end of the semester so youre not sure what grade you have in the class. her lectures are pretty boring, but assignments are relatively easy

I approached professor Mughal on the first day of class to work out an arrangement for me to take the midterm early since it was scheduled the same day as my WEDDING DAY. He laughed at me and his exact words were, "You should have planned around the midterm." It was the most demeaning any professor at the University of Utah ever treated me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take Professor Mughal if you want to understand statistics.  He will give you an excellent foundation, and he really works through all the material in class so you're never lost when you leave the classroom.  Tests are a little harder but if you've done the homework you'll be fine.
Good class. It seems like i felt like I understood the material really well but the tests were tricky and i didnt do as well as I hoped. Hilarious guy though.
I really enjoyed his stats class. It was very fun, and he explains business concept very thoroughly.

Great prof (maybe the best one at the U), very knowledgeable, explains heavy concepts clearly. Hard class, many tests, case-studies, midterms, comprehensive final. Online lecture videos are very helpful.

Prof. Mughal required that I attend class to take the midterm on my wedding day. I told him the first day of class I noticed a conflict based on his syllabus (3 months out). I asked if I could take the midterm early. He looked back at me and said I should have planned around it. Terrible professor. Really needs to lighten up.

I really liked this professor! His class wasn't too easy but he was great with all the examples he did in class. If you go to class and do the suggested homework then you will be fine!!! The material is not very exciting but he is funny and makes jokes, I even laughed and I had his class at 7am!
This man is an egotistical bigot He does not explain his work because he does not know how. Makes fun of kids when they ask a question.

I enjoyed going to class.  Homework nor attendance were required and he let us work in groups for take home tests and cases.  The tests were easy when I did the suggested homework and reviewed the take homes.
He is a really good teacher.  REally fun lecutres

Professor Zhang is a great professor if you don't try to learn from him. He made me confused about things I knew, so just watch the online videos. He gives out so many extra credit points, and the tests are worth so little that you can fail them and still get an A. If you go to his office hours, he will straight up give you the solution code.

I put in literally 0 effort and still got a B. It's like prof. Z made it his life mission to make this class as easy as possible. Between blatant cheating on tests, and oodles of extra credit points, I'd be surprised if someone failed this. When people talk about grade inflation, this is what they're referring to. Thanks for an easy semester, prof.

Professor Zhang was a solid professor because he offered a lot of ways to succeed in his class. The videos he posted were super helpful and the extra credit opportunities were also great. A big recommendation I would give is to be sure to review and understand C in and out before you dive into this class. Overall I enjoyed it and felt like I grew.

Excellent Professor, he cares about his students and gives them every opportunity to succeed at every turn. He puts his lectures as preloading material for class essentially doing a flipped classroom, so you can consume the material at your own pace.
Good professor, gives a lot of EC opportunities, and is generous with deadlines for assignments. Exams are all online, and grades are curved. Often answers Piazza questions

Mu Zhang's teaching methods aren't the best (not helped by a flipped classroom), but he is very generous. All homeworks receive a minimum 1-week extension, with extra credit being offered if you submit it within the normal 2-week deadline. On top of this, all exams were online and open note, including the final. Made a notorious class manageable.

If you want a professor that holds you to a rigorous standard, Mu is not for you. But personally I'm not super interested in content of 4400 and man does he make the class easy; super lax assgn deadlines & extra credit, take home exams fully open note, even curved one (idk why lol!) just very easy. Probably hell with Kopta (but fun too im sure lol)

Mu is kind of a mid professor overall. His lectures are ok. It's a flipped classroom so I quickly realized there was no point in going to class (the online lectures are good and taught by a different professor and Mu's in person lectures are kinda pointless). The assignments are hard but you learn a lot. He is an overall forgiving prof and curved.

The flipped classroom sucks. Mu is extremely kind and its almost like he doesn't want anyone in the entire class to fail; he made the final assignment optional and gives out a multitude of EC options. The material is insanely complicated but he does his best. You won't fail with this guy teaching. But yeah flipped classroom can't motivate me to go.

I agree with other posts that this professor was fair with students and was overall pretty lenient with due dates and generous with extra credit. That being but his lectures were a bit hard to understand because English is not his first language.

CS 4400 is hard and is flipped classroom. Professor Zhang is great. He gives extra credit opportunities and extensions on every assignment. 

He's super sweet and responds to a lot of Piazza questions.
Nice person

CS 4400 is difficult no matter how you spin it. Dr. Zhang provides students with every possible opportunity to do well in this class. Extra credit, three full weeks for assignments to be submitted for full credit, and his practice exams are very helpful. Highly recommend Dr. Zhang if you have to take 4400.

From how jealous my friends who took this in fall 2022 with Zhang were when I described how the class was going this fall, I infer that Zhang is the sort of professor that takes a growth mindset. Zhang is very generous when it comes to reasonable grading requests (especially in the realm of grading), and gives many XC chances. Mid lecturer tho.
He's a very nice person but it can be very challenging to understand what's going on during lecture. I really hope he works on this because I think if he did it would make this class much easier.

This professor is an OK lecturer, although he does talk extremely quickly. The videos that are mandatory before class (usually 30+ minutes, 2x a week) and a quiz afterwards adds so much work to this class and is a huge pain. Asking questions outside of class is a huge waste of time as it takes days or even a week for a response, if you are lucky.

Best professor ever! Second time taking this class as I got a very low grade last time & to the people complaining about his teaching, it's miles better than the last prof I had so... I think they just can't handle the material. He made the class as easy as possible. This is an intro course as well, intro to systems.

This teacher and the TAs are completely inaccessible outside of class and I don't think they talk to each other either. The day before the midterm we didn't know if it was in person or online and I attempted to ask the TAs and they didn't know either. Class time is useless as it's just a repeat of prerecorded lectures with no questions answered.
Terrie lectures. Doesn't seem like he connects at all to students. Asks terrible questions and never checks for understanding.

CS4400 was a very tough class. We had pre-lectures videos and quizzes, but it made the in-person lectures seem redundant and not helpful. It was very difficult relating the lectures to the homework. The labs were a bit more helpful but still confusing and hard to follow. However, Zhang was willing to give extensions and offer extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Like the other review says, CS 4400 is gonna be hard no matter what. Prof. Zhang is caring though, and will try his best to help you and also try to make things fair. We also mainly learned from pre-recorded lectures between classes, then Prof. Zhang would review/explain in his own way in class.

4400 is a hard class as it is. There were pre-lecture videos before each class that went over the content that Mu discussed in lecture, so sometimes the lectures were redundant. Mu gave extensions to assignments and offered extra credit if turned in at the original due date. He is very helpful in office hours so try to stop by!!
This was my second class from Prof. Myers and though his classes tend to be really PowerPoint heavy, he is really accessible outside of class and the final projects are always really interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took Biomodeling from Chris and really enjoyed it. There were a few assignments that ensured that we actually understood what was happening in lecture without being busywork. The final project was set-up well and I enjoyed the class overall. The only note I would make is that it was a little bit slideshow-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: His tests are meaningless. The questions on the tests are long like a week long project! Before every test he said the test will be shorter, but, 98% of the class was always writing when the time was up.   In the last final the average might be in the range 50s or 60s % , will see. Teachers like this discourage students who want to do well.

The test was so long that it would require 3 hours for a normal person. Some people indicated they did not even have time to read questions thoroughly.  He doesn't write a single word on the board, only goes through slides. Now, it makes sense why his tests are long! Because he doesn't probably write much!  Power point has replaced writing!

I LOVE PROF MYERS. If you take one political science course while at the U, take it from her. She is so passionate, knowledgeable, and flexible. Literally the perfect professor for students who are motivated to learn. Feminist political theory is a class centered around discussion, with a few quizzes, and two papers. Learned a ton & loved it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was the second class I took from Professor Myers. Her teaching style is lectures focused on the readings that were assigned for that week. There is a lot of reading for all of her courses. It was clear Professor Myers was knowledgable on the subject. However at times her comments did not match the tone of what was being discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ella Myers is my favorite professor. Her course is reading heavy, but its necessary to discuss the theory. Myers is a vibrant and Brilliant. You don't have many assignments in the class, and she is difficult grader. But she always tells you exactly where you could improve.

There were many uncomfortable moments in the class where the class didn't feel inclusive. The professor did a poor job of facilitating healthy in class discussions, and only showed evidence on one side of each argument. This was easily the worst class experience I have ever taken. She also required printing out everything which was really annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class. And felt like as long as you skimmed the readings and attended lecture you could get a good grade.

Professor Myers was solid. Great lectures and around 10 quizzes throughout the semester. Honestly, going to the lectures is more important than doing the readings (though your essay assignments will be based on the readings). Quizzes are easy if you take good notes during lectures and she provides a lot of opportunity for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ella Myers is a great professor! She had clear guidelines for all assignments and essays. Quizzes are weekly but directly relate to readings and discussions in class. She gives good feedback and offers extra credit (at least when I had her). Overall, great class and would definitely take one from her again.

Such good lectures, the best by far that I had this year. Professor Myers is incredibly engaging and answers questions so clearly. There is definitely a lot of reading for this class, but she does such a good job explaining it all that even if you don't get to all the readings, you will still understand the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eloquently spoken, don't try to argue with
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Myers is excellent at her job. Every class has great discussions and is well structured, Quizzes are straightforward, and Myers gives detailed feedback on analytical papers. Myers, too, is a very respectful and friendly person. I highly recommend Myers and cannot wait to take another one of her courses in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Myers is probably one of the toughest graders I have had. She makes you work for the grade, BUT she provides ALL the tools so you can get the grade you want--you just have to utilize them. She is incredibly passionate about what she teaches, very knowledgeable and I learned a lot. I would definitely take one of her classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Myers is, undeniably, an incredible professor. She'll make you work for every grade you get, but really encourages critical thinking. The class isn't easy, but it's so worth it for the growth you'll see in your thinking and writing skills. If you get the chance, take any of Dr. Myers' classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This was a great discussion class. Ella guided all the conversations very well and the assignments are clear from the beginning of the semester. We read so many incredibly important works. I loved this class and I would take a class by Ella again.

Professor Myers is one of the best professors I've had at the U. She doesn't make you remember facts but rather to think critically. There are three short quiz essays and a final paper. If you read the material and understand the lectures you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved POLS theory with prof myers. One of my favorite pols classes I have ever taken. I learned so much and enjoyed her lectures. She makes you work to learn it is so worth it. You come out of her class with a new perspective on life and so much more aware of different politcal theorists and thinkers that you can apply to your daily life.

Professor Myers is my favorite instructor by far. She is attentive and very inclusive. She made class fun and I really enjoyed learning from her. She gave clear instructions of all assignments and gave everyone the opportunity to share their thoughts. She is very passionate about what she teaches and I genuinely learned so much from her.

The most rewarding class in my time at the U. The final paper was a challenge, but it was a great experience. There's a lot of reading that you have to be ready to discuss it every class, so don't skip it! More than anything, her class taught me to think. This is a class where you will get your money's worth. I wish I'd had more classes from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Myers is an amazing professor. At first, she can seem kind of intimidating, but she is really funny and extremely kind. I have taken GNDR 3900 and POLS 5140 with her and I would definitely take more. No electronics allowed in the discussion-based class but she helps connect you to resources if you need help to buy/rent/print the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I went to this class for one day and knew it wasn't for me. She requires every single reading (100's of pages) to be printed out and brought to class. She doesn't allow any sort of note-taking unless it's on paper. As a student who primarily uses kindle books and google docs to save money, I knew this class was a no go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: There was a lot of reading, a lot. And we were expected to print out everything and bring it to class, sometimes the readings were over a hundred pages long and we would still have to print it and bring it. Class participation is a must. But She was super helpful and really makes herself available to help. One of my favorite professors at the U.

Class and discussions were really fun and I learned a lot. There is a lot of reading, but as long as you read, discuss, and write 3 essays then you will do great in the class. It is really a really difficult class, but really worth it in the end. I really recommend Professor Myers.

I have had Prof Myers for two classes, intro to gender studies and feminist political theory. I loved them both and am taking another class from her next semester. Show up to class, write 3 essays, and you will get a good grade.
If you work hard, you can get an A.

Professor is very caring and wants the best for her students. She is easy to communicate with and is available outside of class to answer questions. There is a group project that it is worth a lot, but you have the option to request to do it alone. She gives useful feedback on assignments, but does often take a very long time to grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was frustrating! She was nice, but every class felt silly and her lectures had no substance and were repeated. 3/4s of the important assignments didn't get graded until 3 hours before final grades were due meaning I had no clue what was going to happen and she was a tough grader. Look for better options for 2010

She gives lots of homework, but the homework is very doable and extremely helpful for future projects. She does an amazing job of making big tasks into many small ones and breaking down the steps. The assignments are graded easily, but the three essays (worth most of the grade) are graded tough. Slow grading on the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Picking this professor is one of the worst decision in my college life, just pick another one.

Tbh, this is the worst writing professor I have ever taken in this university, She gives random grades and does not care about the students, working hard in this class is useless since she will still take points off randomly.
She does not care about students, she always gives random grades. DO NOT PICK HER
The lecture is pretty boring and really does not teach you anything, she also does not give good feedback since she always grade your papers without a clear criteria
She does not give clear grading criteria.

Nancy is a lenient professor who had straightforward assignments and low-stress lecture content. She gave good feedback on papers and would assist students in class to help revise their essays or start their drafts. She also offered corrections on the major assignments which was a good way to provide extra credit while also accepting late work.

This class was pretty easy. Jensen is never super clear on assignment instructions, and her feedback isn't great, but all assignments are pretty easy. Also, she is an easy grader. The final project for this class involved a sizable group of students, which meant a little more effort in the second half. She was pretty lenient with everything though.

Nancy is a sweet professor who means very well and knows what she is talking about. Her lectures are pretty standard, and honestly could be skipped if you feel that you are already a competent writer. She gives great feedback on assignments, but is typically doesn't get assignments back to you right away.

Great prof! Workload was pretty light and reading was helpful but not mandatory. Asyc class, we met once a week with everything else online. There was one longer term group project at the end of the class that comprised of 2-3 papers. All papers were super easy as long as you made an effort on the draft. Prof gave lots of helpful review/comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Let me join 4 weeks into the school year and gave me lots of time to catch up

For a senior-level writing class, Prof Jensen would be amazing. She gives thorough feedback on every paper. However, she grades harshly for an intermediate-level class. Start the essays early and correct your mistakes for extra points, as the top score is rarely above a 93 before corrections.

Professor Jensen's class was quite repetitive since everything covered in lecture was already given to students as a document. Lectures were slow and not very useful. However, the ability to redo major assignments makes it a bit easier to score higher. I felt that this professor made it unnecessarily hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's not a bad professor and the class isn't hard at all but the lectures are i n c r e d i b l y boring and while attendance isn't mandatory, sometimes she'll have assignments due by the end of class so you'll miss points there. But like I said, incredibly easy class, just do the papers and peer reviews.

This class was an easy A class but you do lots of peer reviews and papers. Papers don't have to be very long. Class is super boring. I went to every class and I fell asleep every time and was able to go onto canvas after and get all the information I needed from the class notes she would post. Don't forget about assignments due before 11:59PM

She takes off lots of unnecessary points throughout the semester but grades easier for the final paper for some reason. She made this class more difficult that it needed to be. I recommend getting a different professor.

I took her class during COVID and she seemed to struggle with anything tech. As a result, her lectures were unbearably boring if they were working at all. Outside of lectures, however, she was very helpful and gave good feedback on papers. I imagine she is much better at teaching in person, but I wouldn't recommend taking an online class from her.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Gives good feedback--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nancy was a really good instructor. She was very easy to talk to and gave good information. There is some reading in the text book, but she has all of the readings on Canvas so I didn't purchase a textbook. The CEL project was kind of annoying because our nonprofit didn't really know what they were doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Jensen is a good instructor and knows her stuff. Be prepared for a lot of useless lecturing though. The content of the class could probably have been presented in a 50-minute or even a 20-minute class rather than a 90-minute class. Do the papers and show up prepared with drafts for peer revision and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you stay on top of it if you take the online class (which I recommend), lots of peer reviews. She also allows you to make changes to your assignments for a week after she grade them to bump up your grade. I found the class to be a pretty easy A. I don't think I wrote a paper longer than 4-5 pages maybe?

Overall was a pretty easy class. She gives you a chance to revise final formal assignments for a better grade and won't grade lower then what you already got. There are a lot of assignments but they are fairly easy and can be finished quickly. She gives great feedback and is quick to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Overall, it was an easy class. Prof. Jensen gives great feedback! You have the opportunity to redo the formal writings which is super helpful. She is quick to answer emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Obscene amount of busy work. Eg one of the assignments is a research paper, but instead of just writing a paper, she makes 10 assignments out of it that are useless on top of the paper itself, ie a research log where you have to keep track of when, where, and how long you did research, or drafts of bibliographies including summaries of each source.

I loved Prof. Jensen's class! I felt like this was what my LEAP class was supposed to be. I made a lot of new friends and looked forward to going to class even if it was at 8:30 in the morning! Prof. Jensen gave me very good feedback on my writing and encouraged a learning environment that is unmatched! Take Prof. Jensen's class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very nice and smart professor, lenient on due dates, always available to give feedback and help you improve. Overall very good professor, would recommend taking her classes.
-- Textbook is used occasionally -- Strict grader -- Boring lectures
Great Professor and gives good feedback, but do not expect an "A"
N DAWG is pretty Chill, but her Lectures are  boring, but she does give good feedback!! she loves and prefers being called N DAWG.

The class is easy if you go, pay attention and follow directions. Nancy is very fair, kind, and willing to help students as much as possible. She is the sweetest lady. The assignments are standard level, nothing too difficult or time consuming. Loved this class. Definitely improved my writing skills.
Professor Jensen was great. Simple enough class, as long as the assignments are done, attendance isn't a huge deal. Expect to improve writing skill.
Nice and approachable.  Help you with what you need.  Works with you if things are late.

K this is the deal. IF u want an easy A for this class, letter the teacher peer review your essays. she gives 3 essays  through out the whole class. Just have her peer review it during her hours in her office and u should get an A. simple enough?

Professor Jensen was very helpful. She was always in her office and willing to respond to email. I learned a lot in her Business Writing Class. It was a lot of work, but worth the effort. She really knows her material and was never absent. She was one of the better professors that I have had at the U.

Class was fun and easy but she grades the writing assignments pretty hard. If you don't want to work too hard for just one class, then search for a different instructor. But in general, Jensen was a pretty nice teacher and I really learned stuff from her.

I haven't completed this class yet but I had to step in because I can't believe Nancy gets negative reviews.  She's everything a professor ought to be: helpful, knowledgeable, and willing to work with students.  You still have to do the work, but she's not going to send you to hell for turning in something a day late.

She's an okay teacher. Lectures a LOT. I love writing, but... I dunno, every time I was in the class, I was just... not into writing ANYTHING. Too many lectures about grammar, which you should already know by the time you hit WRITING 2010.

DO NOT TAKE WRTG 2010 from her!!! you get the same lecture every day! i counted one time how many times she said "thesis" 51 times in forty minutes! just will always ask "why, why, why?" about anything and everything.  can't read her hand writing
You can not read her hand writing by the way

She repeats the same thing over and over in every class. She'll always say that in your paper you need a thesis and paragraphs linking back to the thesis and the conclusion has to relate back to the thesis. I honestly thought it was pointless, but I had to take it because it was a gen ed class.

Professor Makarem is a good professor. I appreciate how much the U is going towards being modern in this class with giving us phones and showing us how to implement AI in the apps. That was cool. The assignments were easy and the tests were hard. Honestly more than anything this class teaches you how to read documentation.
Easy class, tests were difficult though. Lectures were recorded so attending class wasn't mandatory. The group project was fairly easy as well.

Dr. Makarem is extremely organized and posts slides, examples, and prior exams. He ensured there were TA hours at almost every hour of the day. Lectures were so easy to follow, it was almost boring, but the reenforce ensured learning. The assignments took time, but were effective teachers. I had no prior programming experience, but had no problem.

While you could tell he's a nice guy and wants to be helpful, this class is blatantly too difficult for an intro class, especially a class required for multiple majors outside of CompSci. The tests are extremely difficult, and on top of that you're given less than 45 minutes to complete them. If I had to take it again I'd just do it online.

Professor Makarem was a VERY nice professor, but it kind of seemed like this was his first semester teaching. Again, one of my kindest, most understanding professors this semester, but not a lot of resources outside of class to help, especially for an introductory course.

I am the opposite of a computer person, I struggled to even download the software necessary for this class, but professor Markarem helped me so much. I would go to his office hours and he would take the time to genuinely help me understand. He knows his stuff and is always willing to help students

Not a lot of resources outside of class to help, grades through an autograder that works 20% of the time, and lectures are a repeat of the textbook, which in and of itself was unhelpful. The professor absolutely knows his stuff, but expects students who've never coded before to grasp his concepts in 0.5 seconds.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I believe that Naina Phadnis is genuinely one of the best professors at the University of Utah. The class was tough- but she supplied us with everything we could ever need. She gives so many materials and extra credit opportunities, it is obvious that she wants everyone to get a good grade. She is so funny and kind, loved the class!

Dr. Phadnis is very passionate and gives engaging lectures. Her questions on case studies can be a little open-ended and then graded harshly, but there are lots of opportunities for extra credit. Make sure you know every detail of the slides. This class is difficult but mostly straightforward and very interesting!

Naina is easily the best prof I've had. She is so clearly passionate about this class. It's fairly content heavy, but she structures this class in a way that makes it so much easier. She's super willing to answer questions, quick to respond if you need help, and also hilarious. Genuinely inspiring me to consider microbiology jobs.

Naina Phadnis is a good professor and is known to be the best Cell Bio professor along with Gagnon, with whom she tag-teamed the class. She was clear and detailed. Her army of TAs hosted many optional discussions with which you could increase your knowledge and bolster your grade. I left well-prepared for Biochem and Genetics.

Her energy is amazing and you can tell she understands the material on such a deep level. Her lectures are so fun and engaging. She is so well organized and kind. You will know exactly what to anticipate for exams and will know exactly how to prepare because she tells you explicitly and also gives so many resources like study guides and mock exams.
Very kind you can tell she knows what shes talking about

Naina is amazing!! Not only does she teach the material in a easy to understand way, she does so with compassion. You can tell she truly cares about her students learning because she will go over something repeatedly if you don't understand. Lots of assignments in the course, but she will be there to help through it all! Def recommend!!!
She genuinely cared and had office hours or TA study sessions practically everyday. The material was presented organized and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a super passionate professor and is willing to help you understand. The course material itself can be hard and she is a tough grader, you will lose a lot of 1/2 points on things. But she drops a lot of assignments at the end
Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. She is an incredible lecturer and cares about her students so deeply. I 1000% recommend her class

Dr. Phadnis is an amazing teacher! She's always lectures with an insane amount of enthusiasm, and you can tell she really cares about her students. She's easy to reach out to and will do her best to help any issue you have. Her slides are FANTASTIC. During lectures you should download the notes and take notes on them. Just try and you'll be fine.
Love her! Lab was fun! There is a final exam which is strange for a lab but overall very due-able.

She is fantastic and super fun but honestly the class is a lot of work. Just do the reading and theres a lot in the modules. I was new to canvas and wasn't very good at it so i missed a lot of her posts but she does a lot extra in there that can help like videos explaining the homework and posting study methods.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sweetest professor, very down to earth! She explains stuff repeatedly if we don't understand it well and is always open to questions in and after class. Easy to meet with and very helpful. You just need to make sure to show up and stay on top of assignments. Heavy load class, but she handles teaching it well.

I would consider her one of the best professors at the University of Utah. Her lectures are amazing, she's extremely knowledgeable on every single topic and wants you to not only know the content but enjoy it too. If you have questions she is very easy to talk to. The course has a lot of assignments but all BIOL 1610 courses at the U are like that.
Prof explained concepts well. I just thought tests were hard.

Naina is wonderful. She is thorough, responsive, caring, smart, and has a great sense of humor. She is willing to spend a while after class to help work through a problem/assignment. Her accent can be a bit hard to understand so it's important to always pay attention in lectures. This class can be difficult but the professor is great :)

Dr. Phadnis is among the best at the U's dept. of biology. Extremely passionate professor that exudes enthusiasm that is infectious to her students. Doesn't weigh you down with unnecessary busy work assignments and is accessible outside of lab. This microbiology lab was very enjoyable and I cannot recommend it enough.

Dr. Phadnis is an absolute gem of a professor! I genuinely enjoyed her course. She is very friendly and approachable, and it is clear that she values her students. She provides the resources you need to do well in her class. I think the exams are very doable if you study. Other assignments included pre-class quizzes and fun case studies.

Naina is amazing. She cares so much about what she teaches and ensures her students understand and want to apply the material. She sees potential in everyone. Her content is straightforward, as are her exams, so study and you'll be fine. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Dr. Phadnis is the best professor I have had in my 4 years at the U. She genuinely wants all of her students to succeed, you just have to show effort and try. Biology is not my strong suit, and this class has been challenging, but I wanted to write this before registration for next semester to encourage others to take a class with Dr. Phadnis.

Dr Phadnis is an amazing lecturer and I had lots of fun attending her classes. Homework was graded harshly, but exams were easier. She has a lot of knowledge from teaching many courses and labs, so she answered questions easily and seemed excited when we were understanding.

One of the best professors at the U. She is prepared for lectures, very organized, and tries to make class fun. Expectations are clear and she is very patient with questions. Course content is also interesting and structured well. Curves grades to the top 5% of the class, but if you go to lecture and study well you can definitely get an A
She Is the best biology Prof I have had so far!! She explains topics so well and it makes it very easy to understand!!

She is such a sweet person and she is so supportive of her students. She taught every day with a smile on her face and did a thorough job answering questions despite it being a huge lecture. The class was a lot of work but it was more because you have to put some effort into fully understanding the topics. I recommend yt instead of the textbook.

I absolutely ADORED Dr. Phadnis. She was such an amazing professor! Our lectures were filled with jokes, laughs, and I looked forward to class. I can tell Phadnis truly cares for her students, before every quiz/exam she reminds us that a score does not determine our worth and provides SO MANY learning options. I loved her and this class. 100000/10!

Professor Phadnis was great and engaging throughout the whole semester. She is very funny and kind. The class can be a lot of work at times but it is manageable. Make sure to do EC quizzes and all the hw as the points add up in the end!

Dr. Phadnis cared if you understood the contents she was teaching, she was great at teaching. There's also a lot of resources available to help you understand the content as well. She's really nice and understanding, but will not accept late work. There are drops that can be used. Attendance is really important for clickers.

Dr. Phadnis cares about her students' academic performance as well as their overall wellbeing. Her lectures were thorough and she explained things in different ways, and always tried to cover any common misconceptions. I would definitely take Dr. Phadnis for any course as she cares about her students more than a lot of professors do!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You get what you give in this class. Phadnis is a very nice and caring professor, her lectures are presented via slideshow making it easier to follow along. Make sure you stay on top of your homework though it adds up in the long run!
Professor Phadnis is great and would recommend! Make sure to do extra credit! She is very funny and you WILL  need to study. Super kind and wants you to succeed

She is amazing? She really cares about what she is teaching and for the students. Most of the material she explains is easy to understand but you must attend the lectures. You get a lot of points for that and it really helps your grade at the end of the semester. The draw to learn assignments are very annoying but helpful.

Dr Phadnis is super awesome. She is very friendly and encourages students to engage in her class. I found her to be very knowledgeable and capable of communicating said knowledge, but the course has a lot of material and most of the grade is from exams. Super interesting class, but not a great class for poor test takers.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis is a phenomenal teacher, by far the best of the BIOL1610 professors. She's caring, funny, and genuinely wants her students to understand the material. If you have to take this class, take it with Dr. Phadnis!

I've been waiting for this one fr. Dr. Phadnis is a real one. She's caring, smart, and is overall a great prof. She's very humble, but can answer any question with a clear answer. If you attend the majority of lectures as well as discussions, you'll be set. Workload is manageable if you spread it out. DO THE EC QUIZZES!

professor phadnis was really great! very caring and interested in making sure you succeed. the tests are hard but are an easy B+ if you study. participation points really matter and bring your grade up a TON at the end of the semester, so make sure to go to class and discussion. also plenty of drops to help boost your grade later on!!

Dr Phadnis is a great professor! She shows so much care for the students. Attendance is graded, but she allows drops within each category of grading. Generally difficult class, if you just show up and put in a bit of work, you can do great in this class. She gives so many resources for you to learn and succeed. Super funny and kind professor.

I loved Dr. Phadnis. We did have clicker questions in class so you can't often miss but she keeps her lectures interesting.
