She is clearly passionate and cares about her students and the content, making it easy to learn. There are a lot of Draw to Learns and pre and post-class quizzes but you'll have that regardless of the professor.

She is such a fun and interesting lecturer. You can tell that she really enjoys teaching and wants to see you succeed. She is by far the best biol 1610 professor. On the last midterm our section scored 12 percent higher than Dawson. This class is one of my favorites and I definitely want to take a class with her in the future. There is extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Biology itself is a tough course but if you attend class and actively try in this class you will do just fine. She is the best bio professor out of all of them she's engaging and wants her students to succeed. She's also funny and her course is organized to a tea. I would 100% take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes. I already love bio but she made it even more enjoyable. Such a fun and easy class. Professor Phadnis is so helpful and such a great teacher. 100% recommend.

She is the best!! I am in the STEM field so I love bio... but besides that I feel that professor Phadnis does an amazing job teaching and keeping everyone engaged. She is the best bio professor I've had and I'm premed. Attendance is mandatory but her class is definitely not boring. I loved this class.

While the class itself can be tough, if you READ THE TEXTBOOK, take good notes and study, you should easily pass. She makes lectures very engaging, with class slides posted on modules as well as other lecture/study help. There is quite a bit of homework assigned, but nothing too serious. She's funny and she really cares about her students.

I'm convinced that Dr. Phandis is the best professor you can take for Bio 1610. She's super passionate about biology, cares about her students and explains the material really well. There is a ton of workload for this class but plenty of study hall hours and TA's to help. Don't take Renae, she don't know how to use technology and sucks at lecturing

Dr. Phadnis' class was an incredible experience. Based on what I've heard from other students, she is the best 1610 professor by far. Despite the massive amount of material the class covered, she always managed to stay on track and go over topics that students found difficult. Just do your part, and she will go above and beyond.

Arguably the best biology professor I have had, Dr. Phadnis truly cares about not only students learning the material, but also outside of class and their success.  She is a great professor and as long as you put in the work, she absolutely gives you all the resources you need to succeed in her class

This class is hard but as long as you put in the work you'll be fine. Read the assigned readings before class as they help a lot with some topics. Professor Phadnis is really caring and will help you if you ask. Take advantage of every extra credit opportunity because they will save your grade. Probably want to take some chem before this class.

Knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. The workload was pretty light for a class covering as much as it does, 4 relatively small assignments per week. A very merciful and sympathetic professor.
Lot's of lecturing, not of teaching

Professor Phadnis is great. She teaches a tough course, but offers plenty of help, extra credit opportunities, and genuinely cares for her students and how they are doing in class. The content is dense, but she answers questions as she goes and is willing to slow down if needed. Bio 1610 has a large workload, but in-class resources make it doable.

This course is basically the IRL version of the House MD show. A lot of memorization and correlating structure to function. Honestly is difficult but rewarding. Dr Phadnis has this course to help students prepare for medical school, but will help you individually if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis is a passionate and knowledgeable person, as one of the 2 professors instructing the class she was very open with us and course guidelines are clear and fair. For me, an engaged student, I appreciate her ability to nudge us into good study habits. 1610 is a tough class in general, youll need to earn the grade, but youll learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She yells at the class during lectures, she degrades students for clicking the wrong response on clicker questions and forces your camera on. She is very hard to understand and follow in lecture and struggles to dumb things down for someone who has never experienced biology before, yet its a low level class. I cannot understand why she is the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: this was by far one of the most interesting electives in the biology department. doctor phadnis was really nice and seemed to care about and wanted to help everyone in the online class, although I found her a little unapproachable. the exams were easy if you put in the work and use the study guides/resources. also gives extra credit

Professor Phadnis is an amazing professor for the intro bio course. She explains material thoroughly and is straight to the point without extraneous information. Equipped with clear expectations of what to learn during class, she can take a poorly performing student and turn them into the top student with the mindset she instilled. Awesome prof!!

If you want to pass the class, you need to always be paying attention and do all the work. I left class A lot of the time feeling as though I didnt understand the concepts that were important. She tried to shove a lot of information into a short amount of time, leaving you to have to go to go TAs and LAs for lots of help during your own time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I put in a lot of time by doing the pre-class assignments, post-class assignments, and draw to learns. To study for the exams make sure to comprehend the material found on the powerpoints and the draw to learns. The TAs and LAs were super helpful and so were the study guides. She's very caring and will reason with you when you request for regrades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Im going to counter the former review by saying DO pay attention to the negative reviews as well. These are not just disgruntled students who didnt work hard and didnt get a free pass. Class consists of pre and post class assignments, quizzes (weighted heavy), and in-class worksheets. Every point matters. Prior experience with CHEM matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would ignore the bad reviews. She definitely makes you work for your grade and is clear on her expectations and objectives from the FIRST day of class. She is very passionate and caring and wants her students to succeed! If you put in the extra time to study and pay attention to lectures you can learn so much from this class! I really enjoyed it.

If it was not for the TA's and LA's you would not pass, there is really no clear goal of what I am trying to learn or what there is to learn to prepare for a test. She is not a good lecture but has an overeliance on clicker questions that ultimately helps no one. Bad professor but good TA's and a lot of busy work that takes up time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Phadnis is not very good at testing what she teaches. During her class, I would study what the TAs taught during their review sessions and what she would give out as review and test on something completely different. You learn a lot but the study guides and tests are not parallel to each other. Really just have to memorize everything to do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis is great at making complex concepts accessible to the average student. Her grading makes it easy to recover if needed. Her TAs are a great resource, she trains them well. She readily responds to emails and is flexible w/ arranging times to discuss course material. Her optimism is so inspiring. Truly a beautiful person inside and out.
You will not do well if you do not study the 45 lecture slides and memorize everything on them. Worst teacher ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis has amazing lectures and really cares about her students. Her quizzes and tests are difficult, but if you study and go to class you should get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't be lured into a false sense of security because exams are multiple choice. She makes them tricky! But she's one of the most caring professors at the U. She'll work with you. At graduation, she was cheering for anyone whose name she recognized. Don't fall behind. Do independent study ?'s. She and her hubby definitely both deserve a raise.

Dr. Phadnis is one of my favorite professors at the U. Her love for microbio is contagious and her lectures are fast-paced and engaging. The grade is based off of the exams so keep on top of the material.
Dr. Phadnis is helpful and caring. She knows her stuff and engages with students. I really have enjoyed both her lecture and lab. Top notch teacher and I would highly recommend her.
Excellent professor who truly cares for her students. She will do anything she can to help you succeed, you need only ask. The course is not difficult if you put the work in.

Nice lady who wants her students to suceed. 3 MC exams, 7 pop quizzes, 1 MC final drops 1 exam and 3 quizzes gives EC and grades on a slight curve. You know the quiz questions in advance and gives study guides for all her tests. Very doable class if you put in the time before the tests. I studied a couple of days for the tests and got in the 90s.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Naina was one of the best professors I've ever had.  The energy she brings to class and the passion she has for microbiology is so evident in everything she does.  Her lectures are fast-paced but incredibly interesting and the tests are manageable.  She is extremely approachable and really cares about her students.

Hybrid and online classes are not the best for learning the science. I think you miss a lot from not having class and other students asking questions. Instructor is okay. She wants to do a good job but is difficult to follow or maybe it is just the hybrid format.  I would have learned more in a regular class.

I took the hybrid course and thought it was great! The course is divided into two week modules and she's very clear with what she expects. The workshops could be a little intense, but she's always willing to answer your questions and make sure you understand. If you set a schedule for yourself early on then you'll really be fine. And read the text!

I took the hybrid course and really enjoyed it. You have a workshop with a packet that you have to get done before the class ends which can be pretty stressful, but you can use the book. The homework load isn't bad, and if you don't want to listen to the online lectures, if you just read&take notes you'll be totally fine. Your final grade is curved
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Hybrid class structure worked well. Engaging lectures and videos. Participation and group work helps a ton! Difficult, but interesting. Phadnis was very clear and enthusiastic in workshops. Did a great job of focusing on the difficult topics. Charismatic and an overall great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis is an exacting teacher, and if you are not intrinsically motivated and don't watch the online material it's very easy to fall behind.  The unique structure of this course isn't for everybody, but she makes it work.  She is enthusiastic, her lectures were clear, and she has a very favorable grading structure (A- starts at 88% for 1210)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm taking her online/hybrid course this semester... It's a nightmare. She treats you like high school students. Finds the most miniscule, twisted ways to ask questions, and grades tough, no lates. The workload is intense. An assignment due every sunday night, and there's also brain breaks, workshops and quizzes. Take a normal class w/someone else!
Disappointed in every aspect of the class. She can also be very rude and expects you to know everything from the get go. Please stay away from taking her Microbiology Lab class.

I don't know why she has any bad reviews. This is an amazing class with good, tough material. She lets you drop one of the midterms and you know the pop quiz questions in advance. You have to put in study time but she has MC tests that are extremely do-able. You can tell she loves teaching students and wants you to know microbio!
Disappointed.

Have you ever attended an auction?  That is Naina's lecturing style.  Unfortunately blazing through lecture slides doesn't equate to comprehension of topics for most of the students.  Fortunately, the 5% of our class that had either taken the class previously, had other micro bio experience, or were Rain Man kept the curve at bay.

I would ignore the bad reviews for this instructor. This instructor let you know EXACTLY what you had to do in order to do well. If you didn't do well, it is kind of your fault. Her lectures were super clear and she made a point to let you know what was important. She gave you plenty of material to let you know what you would be tested on.

Dr Phadnis is a wonderful lecturer, she is very engaging and really cares about student success. She makes a large class feel small by answering all questions with a clear answer (as long as there is one). Test will challenge your knowledge of material so reading and going to class are very important.

Professor Phadnis is over-all a good teacher.  She is very knowledgeable in the subject of Microbiology.  She is relatively new to the academic teaching environment and her ability to portray the material can use some refining.  However, listen to her lectures and review the slides before the exams and you will do well. The tests are MC.

She lacks in good feedback.  Also, the grading in this class is not clear at all.  You never know where you stand in the class and she switched it halfway through the semester.  A lot of writing in this class.  If you think you're a good writer, think again.  Very subjective on the writing and will make you question whether or not you can write.

Fairly poor professor.  Mediocre lecturing ability and grating personality.  Grading is based primarily on multiple choice tests which are fair but difficult to study for because of the wealth of material in the class and poor focus during lectures.

Really fun and enthusiastic. She is very easy to learn from. The tests are tough, but they aren't impossible. The tests are mostly multiple choice which is super nice. She is extremely helpful and is always open to answer questions. I really admire her!

I almost don't believe all of the bad ratings on here. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, I highly suggest you show up. She is so kind and if you show up to class, it is extremely easy to get a good grade. If you even relatively care about school and plan to show up to class, Nabita is an awesome professor.

She's nowhere near as bad as her rating makes her seem. If you go to class you will likely be one of few people there and get to know her. Overall coursework is very easy but lectures are very dry and boring. You could probably pass her class just by looking at the slides and figuring it out. Iv'e had way worse professors.

This class was boring but Professor Penmetsa was good. If you know and understand the HW you will do well on the exams. Go to class tho,not for points but the models we built in class would be difficult to replicate on your own.

Nabita Penmetsa is probably the worst professor I have ever had. Between the course material, grading scale, and teachability I would give her a 0 on all. I attended almost every class and though I understood the material despite her confusing curriculum and got absolutely hosed on every exam. Do not take a class from Nabita!

Nabita is one of the worst professors in the business school, Having no other option, as I had to take her class during the BCOR block. Her teaching style and lectures are simply awful and disorganized, making it difficult to do homework/quizzes. Furthermore, she is insincere when asking questions or helping with assignments. Would avoid!
Awful professor and I highly suggest you seek another professor to learn the content from this course. Majority of students did not show up after the 3rd week of the semester.

Had Nabita online and in-person. Online it was hard to understand her, but this in-person class was great. She is lively, kind, and most importantly- teaches things clearly step by step. I'm not quick with math, and any mathematics was clearly and slowly explained, so homework and tests were no problem, and I actually learned interesting concepts.

Lectures can be boring. Gives lots of online resources so you could pretty much take the whole class online and never come to class if you wanted. She gives great examples and walks through all of the homework assignments in class though, so it is worth it if you do attend.

She tried her best. It was hard to understand her bc of her accent, but you could follow along, you just have to listen closely. Lets just say that she was not meant for teaching, but she does it anyway.

This class could be great, but the amount of mind-numbing busy work made me completely disengage from the class. The amount of PackBacks genuinely made me want to cry out of boredom. The quizzes and homework were also pretty awful. She knows what shes talking about, but the class needs to be completely restructured.

I would not recommend Penmesta as a professor. Lectures are not mandatory but if you don't go to class and participate you will not succeed. Also, I have had to get resources and templates from other teachers because she doesn't give us them. I find it hard to follow along with her.
The professor never responded to emails or messages. Very hard to understand, and made the whole class mad confusing. I didn't like her made the class stressful.

Honestly, this class was not the best. The professor never responds to emails and the only people you can ask questions to are the TAs. If you want to understand the material, make sure you go to the labs. She does not give out any extra credit if you are struggling. It is easy if you put in the work. Just hard to reach.
I believe this professor tries her best and cares about her students. Unfortunately the material can just be a little tough to grasp and the course being online made it harder.

Earlier on this class was infuriating. I was being unfair. Once I actually took the time to watch the lecture videos and follow along doing the practice quizzes (she posts both for each quiz) I got terrific scores. I still believe the live lectures are not helpful, but if you do the practice with the videos you will be fine. No prior stats exp.

I hated this class. She did not teach the topics in a manner that was understandable. I only did well because I had already taken stats in high school. This class is basically a stats class but done with excel. She does not answer questions in a helpful manner.

Was very disappointed in the way the class was run. It doesn't seem like she knows the material she is teaching as there were several times in lectures where her math was wrong and she didn't take ownership of the errors. Students were penalized for mistakes made by she and the TA on quizzes and tests. Get ready to teach yourself everything.
Took over a month to respond to my emails, struggled to articulate key concepts, never adequately covered test material, learned more from 20 minute labs than I ever did in class.

I took this class with no previous statistics knowledge. BIG mistake. I hate to be very rude but this professor is awful, and it is very hard to follow what she is talking about in lectures. The tests are also very difficult. I learned a lot more going to the lab discussions then I ever did going to the lectures. Take this class from someone else.

We were supposed to be doing an in-person class and we were moved to zoom, which had its ups and downs. My only complaint is that I never felt like  I was learning anything from the lectures. So I stopped going to class and just met up with a friend weekly to help me out. I literally learned more from my friend rather than from my professor.

In order to get an A, you need to have taken a Stats class before.  I can't imagine taking this class otherwise.  Attendance wasn't mandatory cause all of our classes were just recorded lectures/zooms. 
Take this class if you

- took AP Stats or the equivalent
-Have a busy schedule and can't attend classes

Aww, did you miss a question? Oh, you want to know what you missed to learn from it? Too bad. Very little chance to improve your grade if you don't do so well on the exams. Assignments are weighted as pretty much nothing. Everything else is weighted so heavily that missing one on an exam drops your grade significantly. Hard to get ahold of. DON'T.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was basically teaching yourself the material. Many of the homework's are done by guess checking and hoping that similar material is on the test. This class was also supposed to be in person this semester and we have not had single in person class. The grading for this class is very test oriented and comes with a lot of busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This has definitely been the worst class I have taken so far. The class I signed up for was in person and three quarters through the semester we have not had a single in-person lecture which has been very tough to learn pretty much anything so far. The quizzes make no sense and even though I will get an exact answer it will often times be wrong.

I felt like the professor taught nothing that would actually be used on the tests or homework. Essentially what this class is is teaching yourself everything from your own research and guessing and checking on the homework, and hoping somehow the questions will be the similar on the test. Never explains the logic, you just get lucky or don't.

Good overall professor, would recommend spending extra hours during exam weeks to get assistance on the practice quiz or homework. The only problem in the class is that every single question you miss on exams will really hurt your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Penmetsa creates unnecessary difficulty by having the course be graded on a total of around 80 points. Meaning, you will miss a large percent for missing any questions on an exam (no partial credit). Participation is also important but she has no means of keeping track of who speaks. It feels completely biased on whether or not she likes you.

She could improve on her ability to teach this concept to students. Although she is kind and happy, she failed to effectively teach OIS. I would not recommend her for this class. She is crass and avoids answering questions from students. Overall, she isn't helpful and I am lucky I passed. Take from someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her accent is not bad at. She could speak a little louder but there is typically enough space to sit near the front. You are graded on three homework assignments and three exams. If you understand the practice exams you will do so much better in the actual exams. She teaches very well and will not move forward until she has answered your doubts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This teacher cannot read the class. She is condescending towards students and within 15 minutes of lecture over half the class is doing something unrelated to the course.

Her handwriting looks like that of a second grader, she should not be allowed to teach in large rooms because those in the back won't be able to read anything she writes. Extremely dull and reads directly from her slides unable to expound on anything. Attending her class has been something from a nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the most boring class I have been in. Everyday I went I was so bored after 30 min I had to leave. She will stay on the same topic for way to long and then when she moves on with the lecture, she is still talking about the same thing. Every student in the classroom keeps themselves busy with other class work or they sit on their phones.

I did well in the class and then apparently got a terrible score in participation even though I did show up to every class and tried to make comments when she asked questions. Good teacher, goes over the material well but don't assume showing up and making a comment a day counts as good participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof Penmetsa did a good job teaching the material.  She has a pretty thick accent but you get used to it pretty quickly. I material is math and algebra heavy. She comes from and engineering backgrounds so she can skim over the math rather quickly but was always open to answer questions. 2 homework sets, a midterm, and comprehensive final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I found this class to be tough. She has a thick accent that is very hard to understand and moves through material quite quickly. Graded on two assignments and two tests. Bright side is she gives practice tests that are very similar to the actual tests. She knows her stuff and is very smart. But class is very dull and boring.

Professor Penmetsa is a little difficult to understand because of her accent, but she knows the material very well. I found the class to be extremely easy. It includes 3 assignments and 3 exams. The exams are extremely similar to the assignments, if you figure out how to solve the problems in the homework the subsequent exam will be easy.

Great professor, you can tell really likes teaching. The first exam was very hard for me but once I got used to her "style" the next ones weren't too bad. Yes they were hard  but you just need to study. Her practice exams were almost like the actual exams, same format, same concepts. She wants the class to participate so make sure you do.

Nabita is a very nice lady. she got confused by students questions quite easily and had trouble answering them. I benefitted a lot by going to her TA. Her TA was able to make sense of a lot of things Nabita struggled to clarify.
Super easy course. I did not receive any substantive feedback on my assignments from Dr. Ansari. Just generic stuff like good job or nicely done

Great class! On assignments explain really in depth your answers, they give lots of great feedback on assignments and are very kind in feedback. Exams are based directly on study and slides and are easy if you stay on top of it. They are very good at explaining topics with sensitivity and care and offered alternate assignments as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class had 3 teachers so im not sure who the main one was, but overall, not a too hard class. The only thing was that there are 3 big exams that record you while doing them and they are kinda hard. I felt more pressure while doing the exams while being watched but got decent scores anyways.
Such an easy class. Exams are online and posted on numerous sites. Not worth a 4 credit class.
Her real-world advice is wonderful. Very personable and approachable. Truly cares about students success.

Fantastic and charismatic professor who loves what he does. The assignments are fun and challenge you in new ways. So many TA hours, and the TAs were super helpful. A lot of extra credit but it was challenging to get. Only a final exam worth 30% that is hard to prepare for. He gets a 4/5 because he is poor at answering questions and providing help.

Super strong and entertaining lectures and a well-organized course. Projects were fun, relevant, and offered lots of challenging extra credit opportunities. He has clearly made some drastic improvements to the course since some of the older reviews, and it's now arguably one of the best taught courses available here.

Professor Nagy is the best professor on campus regarding computer security. He is very passionate about fuzzing (which is what this course was about), so he teaches it well. He is very accessible outside of class and wants you to think and learn when you ask questions. The fuzzing course he teaches is also very fun and interesting as an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecture class. I learned a lot. The only bad part was the final in the end where it made me go from an A to an A- (it was weighted 35%). Besides that, I enjoyed the projects and the TA's were very helpful.

Professor Nagy made a 4000-level class a lot easier than I expected going into it. This course is a great entry to computer security and sparked my interest in it as a career pursuit. Nagy is a very fair and accessible professor and his assignments with all the resources are fairly easy to navigate. It will be easy if you dedicate some time to it.

This dude is absolutely sharp. Makes assignments fun, story like journeys while also being extremely applicable to realworld security. Has EVERY resource possible to make sure you can complete assignments. Ignore ALL prior bad reviews...Nagy comes to class excited every day ready to teach. Very rare in todays academic world. Also GOATED TAs.

I was hesitant about taking this class given the previous poor reviews, but I found this professor to be one of the better CS professors. You can tell that he puts a lot of effort into his lectures and wants the class to succeed. One downside is that this professor uses pollev to mark attendance to lectures, so you have to show up!
Ignore prior reviews he has fixed the class. Goated
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Talks fast but covers a huge amount of material in a very manageable way. His lectures are engaging, he cares about the students and makes adjustments to accommodate, and he's got a light-hearted way of steering the class. If you attend every (or most) of the classes, you can 100% get an A.

This fall semester is apparently a complete 180 from last Spring. It seems Prof. Nagy has heard all those criticisms and implemented changes. The lectures this semester were interesting and engaging and the homework is long, but there's enough time to do it and ask questions from TAs who know what's going on.

Also, plenty of optional extra credit.

I was terrified to take Nagy's class after everything I heard last semester. Glad to say he's COMPLETELY turned this class around. Lectures are interesting, the workload is not at all overwhelming, and homeworks are challenging but VERY fair with lots of resources to help (and plenty of extra credit). This is a fantastic intro course now.

Taking 4440 was tough with him because it was the first semester he taught it at the U so the TA's weren't much help. You will always know what is due and when but if you don't go to office hours you will struggle. Conceptually Nagy made everything easy to understand but implementing the hw's and partner projects was a challenge without help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a rough class. This class had almost as much work as ALL my other classes combined. TA's do not help you, the instructor gives unhelpful guidance. Homework requires a plethora of time and effort, and lectures only help with like 10%. You need to code in like three different languages in this class. Average score on final was low 70%.

He is overall a good person and works to make lectures interesting. The problem is less him as a person and the class structure overall. The lectures do not really help you with the project assignments which take hours to complete. The class covers way too many topics and uses python as its language (which many dont know how to use)

This class is far too difficult for a CS elective. The professor seems to have a hard time understanding why assignments are difficult, and often labels homework questions as being "easy" even though they can take hours to complete. His lectures don't make any sense.

The class is overall very disorganized, and concepts don't really seem to flow together well. The course covers many difficult topics, but he doesn't do a good job explaining them in a way that makes sense. Assignments require far too much research outside of class.

I found this class to be one of the most interesting classes I've taken here at the U. Assignments are tough but there are resources to help you through it. It feels that Nagy cares about the success of his students and is always looking for feedback and ways to make the course better.

The professor is still new, so his assignments have sometimes been too difficult. That said, he has been quick to learn and take feedback from his class, and the later half of the semester has gone much more smoothly. The guy is engaging, and he cares that his students do well. I have no complaints.

Most aspects of the assignments have nothing to do with what's covered in lecture, so lectures are useless. He only gives general explanations for some concepts, but when implementing them, students are left clueless. His answers on the class forum are vague and unhelpful. Lecture content must be restructured to make it relevant to assignments.

Prof. Nagy has done a good job adjusting his lecture content and style to align with student needs. The homeworks and projects are difficult, but can be done. He is extremely helpful outside of class. He is vague about hints when asked online, but gives more detailed help in person. His lectures are entertaining and very informative.

Professor Nagy's behavior outside of class is unacceptable by someone who is representing the university. Professor Nagy when asked questions will provide vague and not helpful answers. He will single out students who confront him about these issues and will check RateMyProfessor for negative reviews. He did single out a student on piazza for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nagy clearly has expertise and understanding of computer security. The homework's are difficult but not impossible to do with a little bit of googling and reading online forums to help clarify things. He teaches at a very high level and expects you to dive deeper into the content through homework and projects. I would not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He only provides a very general, hand-wavy, high-level overview of the concepts he teaches in lectures, so in homework and projects where you have to implement the concepts discussed in class, you have no idea what to do. He does not go nearly in-depth enough and is also extremely unhelpful on Piazza, providing vague responses only.

This class is difficult but far from impossible. Nagy is new to the University and the TAs haven't taken his course so they have not been as helpful. This will change as students that take the course from Nagy become TAs. Nagy tailors his lectures for each class and doesn't regurgitate content. He responds quickly on Piazza and promotes learning.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CS 4440 is a vital class and the assignments reflect this. Nagy's assignments are challenging but promote understanding. To succeed, focus on understanding the tools before trying to solve the problem. Nagy's course sets up students for professional success after graduation. Take this course from Nagy if you want to get the best value for tuition.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is a nightmare. HWs are much more difficult than 4150 or 4400, but only 3500 required as pre-req. Lectures teach high level concepts and then HWs require intimate knowledge of low-level details not taught in class. No amount of reviewing lecture slides is helpful. Avoid this professor if you value your mental health

Expects you to be a master at content covered in courses that are NOT prereqs of this class. When you ask for help he gives vague hints then proceeds to say hes there to help you in class when in reality hes not. Worst class I've ever taken at the U hands down. Someone needs to let him know its intro to cs security, not cs security experts class

Terrible professor who teaches surface level principles and expects us to psychically understand the deeper concepts and implementations of computer security. He and his TA crew are patronizing and the course is pretty demoralizing. As someone who has to work during the semester, this course demands far more than 3 credit hours of work.

Professor Nagy's computer security course is a tough one that requires you pay attention, attend lecture, and test your knowledge. Assignments and projects have been tough, but highly rewarding and effective in teaching me the material, also seem to be intentionally vague as part of the learning outcome. Lectures are engaging and fun.

Students ask: Is it possible to create an end-of-string terminator character?
His answer: Trial and error. 
So, why I spent thousands of dollars and learn nothing?
He will never teach you how to do homework; if you ask him, he will ask you the same question.
So, if I know the answer, why do I ask him?

He does not teach how to do homework or projects, its completely up to you to figure it out which is almost impossible if you have no cryptography experience. He ends class early and only goes over very vague basic things in lecture slides which do not help on homework. Help hours do not help either, still gives vague basic answers that do not help

The Lectures end 30 minutes early!!!! I'm paying thousands of dollars for this yet he ends class 30 minutes early to "help on homework" Bro maybe we wouldn't need that much help on homework if your used the 30 minutes like how you are supposed to and teach us we wouldn't need nearly as much help on the homework.
Natasha Seegert is very nice but almost seems slightly like a younger kid's kind of teacher which is not everyone's favorite. She is very approachable though and loves to talk.

Professor Seegert has been the best professor I have ever had. She is caring, takes the time to get to know everybody, and creates an environment where everyone wants to participate and engage. The course material was engaging and not too difficult, but also fun. This is the only class where I am SAD that it is ending. She is nothing but amazing.

Professor Seegert learns every single student's name and creates a comfortable class community. It's a refreshing environment where students feel like they can talk to each other or laugh at shared experiences.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is passionate about her teachings, she does NOT like technology. For COMM 2020, the lectures were all typed. We were required to watch movies and screenshot times for our responses. Due dates are a bit odd especially for discussion posts, YOUR post is due Thurs but your responses to others is due Sun It comes off your taskbar after Thurs though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Seegert did a great job making the material clear and engaging. Her lectures were informative and sometimes humorous, which made the class enjoyable. The workload wasn't overwhelming and she kept the full-term online course manageable. Overall, a positive experience that motivated me to do well in class 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ridiculously specific and convoluted grading standards especially for an online class. Definitely on a bit of a power trip
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Seegert seems to pride herself on being a great dialogist, and she is a good listener, but her discussion questions avoid the possibility of any conflict or true understanding. She's obsessed with the kind of “both-sides-ism” that treats fascism as a school of thought. She also assigns almost exclusively busy work. But she means well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was fairly easy in my opinion and the lectures were quite juvenile, suitable for high school students. Take this class if you want an easy way to get an A and some credits, but not if you care about academic integrity or complex discussion. Assigned readings were biased and unacademic, but were taught as if they were the law.

i took 2360 consuming the earth with prof seegert, and while shes a very nice and caring person, be ready to spend hours on her assignments which are honestly just busy work. shes a lovely person, very sassy and funny, but you wont survive her class without reading all 7 weekly readings + heavyyy participation + veryyy specific grading guidelines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't recommend.

Difficult course with a lot of reading, with tests expecting you to understand the nuances of key terms. However, she provided lots of opportunities for extra credit and actively engaged in getting feedback on course material to improve her course going forward. She respects and will hear points of view from all directions.

I thought this class wasn't going to be challenging but it is so much busy work! She also grades incredibly hard and you have to email her separately to get feedback on each assignment. For almost every week, you have to watch multiple films that are hours long and then about them with specific examples after. Unrealistic work load for 3 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Natasha Seegert is strict but also really cares about her students. I felt encouraged to engage with the material and the class. The weekly discussion posts worked really well with my strengths. I find smaller more frequent assignments to be more approachable. I disliked that the assignments were due in the mid afternoon. I struggled to fit them in
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was one of the most fascinating and eye opening classes I have taken at the U. Dr. Seegert is an amazing professor and cares deeply for each of her students. She is very understanding and will accommodate for you. If I could I would definitely take a class from her again!

She was very passionate about what she was teaching & made it interesting. I was nervous when she said students were not allowed to use electronics for note taking and such, but ended up really enjoying the way she encourages students' learning. Tests are in person and require thorough studying, but if you study, you will get an A in her class.

She's deservedly well-respected though personally arrogant; an effective educator but not a good mentor. Attendance, technology & grading policies are belittling for the modern age, though she'd argue they're conducive to engagement. "I don't care if it's your wedding day, you signed up to be here", yet took several unexpected mental health days.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Seegert is exactly what you want in a professor. She is passionate about her subject and her students. She sent multiple emails about opportunities for students to take advantage of. She gives extra credit and I would take any class from her. There is a good amount of work but I definitely learned a ton.

Prof. Seegert has been one of my favorite professors thus far in my college experience. She cares about her students and always made sure to check in on me when I was going through a difficult time. She is reasonable and always makes sure to keep lectures fun and interesting. She is so awesome and I hope to take another class of hers.

Professor Seegert is very thoughtful and engaging. Cares about feedback from students. If you participate, you'll get a good grade. I've taken two classes from her and enjoyed both a lot. She goes the extra mile in her online classes and it shows.

Overall the class wasn't difficult. However, there was A LOT of homework. A quiz, discussion post, and essay every single week. It took forever to get grades back and the tests were not automatically graded. Due dates were at 2:00 p.m. (you can submit up until 11:59 without punishment) which was kind of confusing and pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Seegert's class online during the pandemic, and she was incredibly supportive and understanding. During my semester we had two assignments and a quiz due each week, one paper for the entire semester, and two tests. Very interesting class and I really enjoyed the films we were assigned!

Dr. Seegert comes off as kind of strict on syllabus day, but is actually pretty relaxed. Though the book was helpful and needed to be cited on assignments, most of the content on the tests came from lecture. She really encourages participation and is super knowledgeable. You have to do the work, but it's super manageable/not overly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Natasha Seegert is one of my favorite professors I have ever had. I gained so much from her Visual Communications course. She forces class partipication- like seriously she will sit and sip her tea until someone raises their hand. However, don't plan on missing a single class- her definitions aren't anywhere online and you won't pass without notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy class to pass if you attend the lectures and take notes. Tests are basic and only require you to know the vocab learned in lecture. Outside reading can help but I did not buy the textbook and was not affected by this.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Tasha gives great lectures and she makes it easy to take notes as she writes everything she expects you to write on the board. She is also willing to talk outside of class.

Dr. Seegert is an amazing professor. As long as you do the reading and pay attention in the lecture you will do fine. She doesn't allow electronics in class and you need to attend. Not an easy course but you will gain a lot from it if you put the work in. Unlike many comm courses at the U, this one actually challenges students to learn.

I took two classes with her, Visual Comm and Rhetoric: Aristotle to #Twitter, both of these classes were HEAVY on reading and participation. Including reading quizzes and at times discussions on canvas that were required. However, the students that actually did the reading always thought the tests were easy and passed with flying colors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She has mandatory attendance and does not allow ANY electronics in class (cell phones, laptops, etc.). Long and boring lectures, and she can be very condescending. I thoroughly enjoyed her class. She does a phenomenal job teaching. Lectures were incredibly fun, she clearly stated the material you needed to know, and everything she taught was relevant and interesting. She is strict on attendance and it does affect your grade. Gives extra credit, clear study guides, pop quizzes, no homework other than 2 essays.

Natasha is an amazing professor. She takes the time to make sure everyone understands the information and has fun, interesting lectures. Her tests are  easy if you know the information and studied. She also gives great feedback on your papers. She makes this theory class fun.  I recommend taking this class from her.

She's an amazing lecturer who's really clear and gives definitions to everything. I have both text books and have read some assignments, but her lectures cover everything you need to know for the tests. She makes participating really easy and fun. If you take decent notes that you understand, you'll be fine for tests and any reading pop quizzes.

Dr. Seegert is a wonderful teacher! She seems really strict at first, but she really isn't that bad. She just asks that you not use electronic devices in class. It's definitely a good idea to have the textbook, but I honestly haven't read any of it and I'm doing just fine. But you MUST be present for lectures or you will fail. Love her!

Amazing class! She really promotes discussion and makes you think about what you are learning, not just memorizing. Make sure to use correct formatting on her papers! Her class will help you with classes you take after, as well as with life. Very applicable!

Easiest class I've ever taken. I never read the textbook (if you have any sense or knowledge of American politics, you won't have to either). He was very nice and understanding, easy class overall.
Amazing class. If your complaining about it, that's a skill issue.

Easy A but I still learned a lot.

Took his online class. Highly recommend. Class was interesting and fairly easy.

Great professor.  I have taken four of his online classes in the past year or so.  He gives clear expectations and is very helpful and available.  I learned a lot, but never felt overwhelmed by the work load.  I highly recommend any of his classes.

Best professor on campus! He provides great stories from his experience as a prosecutor that help apply the material in an easy manner. Easy paper. Midterms and final were a little tough, but he provides a review so you can prepare. If you study, you'll be fine!
Best class on campus. He knows his stuff since he actually works in the field. Easily the most practical and interesting class I have taken to date.

Online class.  Teacher is extremely clear on expectations and class is super straight forward.  Weekly discussions, quizzes, and a final made up from quiz questions. Saxton is very nice and his class is not hard at all!

Professor Nelson is super chill, makes the class so simple but still gives great feedback and helps you become a better writer.
He might be a grad student right now, but he's a goated professor.

Even though it is his first year teaching, he knows what he is doing and always tries to make his class more fun and engaging for other students, which he succeeds in. For those of you who are planning on taking Writing 2010 for either credit or interest, I recommend this professor and his class.

Judge Nelson was the absolute BEST professor I have ever had at the U. His knowledge and expertise in the field are unmatched. He goes on rants but they are relevant and interesting. The workload is not hard if you try. If you want to work in law taking a class from him is a MUST.
Easiest class I took this semester. He is very willing to help, and the material is not complicated at all. I HIGHLY recommend taking it.

You will have to do quizzes and from 1 to 2 discussions each week, and there are 3 main essays that take more than half of your score. Just be aware of this and turn everything in on time!

Steve is a great professor, and his class is very easy. He emails back quickly and grades in a timely manner. The sections of his courses are very large, and a lot of kids have a ton of random "what if" questions, and he answers them all, so the classes tend to drag. But that is my only complaint.

Super knowledgeable guy. Goes on tangents about his experiences but always loops them back into the material and makes lectures easy to listen to and pay attention to if you like the material. Gives super cool opportunities outside the classroom if you're interested in a career path in this area. Easy A and great class! Take anything with him

Grade in this class is based off of consistent (but not difficult) weekly homework assignments as well as a few papers and then your final. Steve is a very caring professor who is good at accommodating students, and I always got great feedback from him on my papers. Be sure to stay caught up on your assignments, it will make your life much easier.

Great professor and a great guy. I took his online class and he did a great job of explaining the content via online lectures and had clear expectations for how he grades. I would highly recommend him. :)

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer, very engaging and knowledgeable. The class itself was once every two weeks and about three hours long which was a lot, but I'd say it was worth it.

I don't like history/pols, but I felt like steve did an amazing job applying what we were learning in class to modern and ongoing contexts. Discussion posts were on interesting topics, and if you do them you get full credit. His grading on the essays could be a bit arbitrary and harsh, but it's not hard to keep grades up with other assignments.

Spent about 12-15 hours on homework between readings, podcasts, and writing.  But Steve is a great professor clearly passionate. If you do the assignments with just a little effort and you are guaranteed to get a good grade. Lots to do, but if it's done this is an easy A.

reviews.comment: Great professor who is clearly passionate about the subject. No tests; however, weekly discussion assignments and case briefs. Can be a lot of writing depending on the person.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love Steve. He's an attorney and has a doctorate, so very knowledgeable in both law and political theory. Missing a few weekly discussions can determine if you end up with an A or a B so be careful

Prof. Nelson cares about his students and wants them to succeed in his class. He will dock you for late work but it's clearly outlined in the syllabus so just stay on top of things. Class is just 1 discussion and 1 inquizitive quiz that you take until you get 100% per week, 3 essays, and 1 final. He's an easy grader but still gives good feedback.

Steve was great, very approachable and clear about what he wanted from you in terms of papers. He gives great feedback on your papers and it's clear that he genuinely cares about his students. Definitely would recommend!!

Weekly discussions and quizzes, including three essays (4-6 pages.) Quite a bit of reading and writing. What an easy A. The requirement for this class is very minimal, with only 4 4-pages essays for the whole semester. The weekly assignments are very little, can be finished in less than an hour every week! A very easy A if you ask me. I wish all my profs can be as easygoing as he does!

Professor Nelson is a great professor to take at the U. He knows what he's talking about and is very understanding of students. He values feedback, and the class is graded on a couple essays and weekly quizzes.

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved my class. We had to convert to online lectures at the last minute due to COVID concerns, and even though this was disappointing Steve did everything he could to present a fun and engaging lecture each time we met. He is very reasonable about the need to make arrangements. I also hate every lawyer I've ever met, except for Steve.

Overall, this class was fairly easy as long as you do the homework and quizzes. You're mostly graded on a few essays and a final exam. Read the textbook, because it really helps with the quizzes. Just make sure not to fall behind or it can get difficult to catch up. Good professor. Easy to reach out to if you need help with something.

As a prosecutor, he gives a perspective that isn't really heard of in Universities but makes sure to be inclusive of all perspectives. Two podcasts are used to supplement lectures and they're interesting. If you fail his class it is because you didn't do the work which he gives time to complete. His course really made me evaluate my career choices

Great professor who gives you time to get assignments done. Very knowledgeable and understanding. Gives great feedback on assignments. Course was broken into 3 essays with weekly quizzes on readings, a midterm, and a proctored final exam. Would take more classes with him.

Steve is awesome. I took him for my admin theory requirement in the MPA graduate program. The entire class is graded on 3 main essays, a final essay, and a final (take home) exam. He gives amazing feedback and goes over all readings during class. Though attendance is not graded lectures are very interesting and he shares real world stories!

reviews.comment: Steve was a great professor. This class involves a lot of reading/writing but if you put in the work, you'll do great. Quizzes and Discussion boards every week.
