Very meticulous. She's fantastic but pretty old school and very picky about what she wants. Overall great lady and great teacher just be ready to do some work. Go to her meetings and talk to her and shell like you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Newton cares about her students and gives very clear feedback on assignments and excellent advice in lectures and modules. I feel very comfortable asking questions and enjoy interacting with her whenever I go meet the professors in person!

She always gave very clear, positive, and personal feedback, and wanted to build relationships with students. Also very caring and respected. Assignments and lectures were given at the beginning of the week and due on Sundays, all relatively easy and only a few larger assignments/projects. Very good intro course if you are considering Kinesiology.

(Taught with Dr. Magiske) Even though this was an online class, they pushed to meet her students in person and gave amazing advice at meet-and-greets. They love what they teach and it shows. They care about your success overall, not just in this class. This class wasn't hard and was a great introduction to kinesiology. Great people, great teachers!

If you push everything to the last minute and believe that asking your professors to raise your grade through an email is your style then Dr. Newton's class is not for you. While at times she may seem very intense and intimating, Dr. Newton is a very caring and highly educated person. She is highly respected and loves helping her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She really cares about her students

Nice professor and wants students to succeed in life, but is not the best at teaching. Very biased though and opinionated about certain careers and topics in the class. Tests were based on her opinions. Assignments were graded very harshly with minimum/vague feedback. This course does not serve justice to the kinesiology degree and its topics.

Professor Newton was great! She had a very great canvas setup that made the online course easy to navigate and understand. She also always answered my emails in a very timely manner, which I really appreciated. She also gave really great feedback on assignments. Overall, had a great experience with her as my professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Newton was easily accessible for any questions and guidance. Although this was an online class, I found it easy to navigate and convenient. The course was definitely challenging though, mainly being that it is vital that you do the readings/watch the lectures to get a good grade on the quizzes and exams even though they are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Newton cares a lot about her students. It is unfortunate that the only option for KINES2500 is an online format. Professor Newton is a kind person who expects a lot out of students. My only complaint in this class was that the online format made expectations of what might be on tests unclear.

Super kind and supportive professor and a pretty easy class. She responds fast and was always very helpful. The exams are the only thing that can be a little tough. She also seemed reluctant to give 100% on assignments; I would get docked as little as half of a point with no explanation as to why. Nothing too crazy, just gets annoying sometimes.

Dr Newton is a great professor, giving out sage like wisdom and advice. Her class is easy and do it at your own pace. The weekly quizzes can be hard, but they are open book so use CTRL-G to help search for answers. Watch every lecture recording (they are short, and can be put on 2x speed) because these are what the two exams are based off of.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my least favorite professors. She expects you to know a lot of stuff that doesn't really matter for Kines. She'll say that all the stuff you'll learn in this class is super necessary but at the end of the day, I haven't used a single thing that she taught me since I took her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class isn't hard, it has interesting content. However, Dr. Newton is a very harsh grader. On every assignment that wasn't on info from the textbook (meaning papers and projects), I never got full marks because she always found something wrong with them. Honestly, I was very frustrated throughout the semester because of her opinionated grading.

Maria Newton was sort of dry when it came to her lectures and the quizzes were sometimes very difficult. I would have to listen to her lectures sped up because it took her awhile to get her point across. However, she was very responsive when it came to emails.

You have about 2 assignments due at the end of each week (discussion and a quiz). You can do the bare minimum and am pretty sure you would still get an A or B. This class falls in the category of one of the easier classes I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 10/10 class. It was difficult, but Prof Newton cares a lot about the subject and she wants every student to succeed. The biggest chunk of your grade is from 3 assignments, but if you follow the rubric and dedicate time to you'll do great.
I loved Newton's explore movement science class! There were weekly lectures (they're slow so watch on double speed), weekly quizzes, and a few papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader. Not engaging.
I liked this intro class with Dr. Newton, it was pretty simple and straight forward

Her lectures were a bit dry. It was pretty difficult to understand the details of the lecture based on how she presents and organizes her presentations. Your grade is based only on 6 assignments, including participation points, so if you bomb one assignment itll be hard to get back on track. 1 individual paper, 2 group papers, and 2 exams.

Newton is such a good professor in the way that she cares for her students. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS and let her get to know you. Her class is interesting and she does her best to make it exciting for everyone. Beware of her exams. They are opinion based so it makes it hard to get an A

Newton is an AMAZING professor. I learned so much from her lectures and often left wanting more. This class made me change my graduate school route to sport and exercise psychology. That being said, tests were incredibly hard and papers/group projects were graded harshly. Regardless of this, an absolute must.

Professor Newton is actually a really great professor. She is really kind and cares deeply about her students. The only issue is that her tests are, in my opinion, very biased. She will teach the material you need to know for her conceptual exams, but if the answer does not match with her views she marks it wrong. Also grade heavy on papers
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Newton is an amazing lecturer, just be ready to participate. If you are engaged and answer questions you will do well in the class. There are only a handful of projects and a few tests. There is absolutely no busywork. She genuinely tries to connect with students and is an amazing mentor.

Dr. Newton is actually a great lecturer, however makes the class a lot more difficult than is required. Her multiple choice exams are confusing as they are very opinionated and grades the papers assigned as if we were in an honors writing class. I would suggest taking it with another professor but she is the only teacher for this class in the dept
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams were very tricky and conceptually heavy.

Dr. Newton is a great professor. Her class was very interesting and unique. She does a great job of making class material applicable to real life. You are graded on few things so you need to work hard on every assignment and study hard for every test. That said, she is very easy to reach out to and is quick to give the needed help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Group work is fine until your group sucks you all end up getting a mediocre grade. Maria did a great job at getting her objectives across. I love her personality! However, the other pitfall is she has opinionated tests. There were several questions that were tricky because you had to guess what she wanted as the answer

Marias class is not super hard if you show up and do the work that she asks you to do. The class consists of 3 group projects and 3 exams. She is really good about meeting up with students outside of class to help you with the projects or exams. She tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A. For sure would take a class from her again.

Maria is a super nice lady, but she is the director for graduate studies so she teaches her class almost like a graduate class. Make friends that you trust in this class because all your papers will be group papers. Her tests questions can be hard to understand because of the vocabulary she chooses. I would take sport psych before taking her class.

Dr. Newton is an amazing professor.  By far one of the best in the ESS Department. She is extremely knowledgeable about Sport Psychology and Sport Sociology. She is always willing to meet and chat, and has the student's best interest in mind. That being said, she challenges you. She expects you too think critically and push yourself.
Dr. Newton is really fun and the class is interesting. Pretty straight forward: 3 group projects and 3 exams.
Maria is great. She really likes everyone to express their opinions and not be judged. Not the easiest class, but she is definitely a great professor.
Great teacher, always willing to help out with anything. Has a sense of humor. Fun class.
Pretty easy material, you just have to show up.

Jeff goes off on tangents throughout his lecture and ends up just indoctrinating you on his own opinions.Very disappointed with the way he taught Business Law because I was genuinely excited to learn the material this class. However, classes would end up being him trying to flaunt how knowledgeable he is in the law and his superior political view.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: A great teacher but does not allow for any other opinion than his own. He will not listen to you as a student because the only person that can be correct in the classroom is himself. Do not take this class with him if you want to feel heard or contribute your opinions. He instills a feeling of fear and anxiousness in most students.

Jeff is an amazing professor who teaches using the Socrates method, which is highly respected by top institutions. I have now taken two classes with Jeff, one being Business Foundations of Thought, and the other being Business Law. He is hands down one of the best professors in the business school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was so scary but it was the best class I've taken so far. I learned so much and the class discussions made it easy to learn the material. Make sure to do/ understand the readings since he cold calls to answer questions. I would take this class again if I could. Loved the professor and the class. Pay attention and you'll do fine

Participation is key in his class but he gives you so many options to do so if you don't like to talk in class. He is super funny and definitely knows what he's talking about. I learned more than I could have every imagined in this class! Definitely take him! Not that I think you have a choice... but he's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Has no ability to communicate effectively.  Tests are non reflective of the material discussed.  Lacks in preparedness.  The worst part....he is the only option for the class.

This is not the teacher you want to take for intro to podcasting. She is very harsh with grading and makes things more complicated than they need to be. I genuinely spent more time talking to her about how to do these assignments so I don't fail than actually learning something, she expects perfection coming from an introductory level class

Maria is awesome! She works in radio so she brings a lot of real-world knowledge to the table and you learn a lot about the media industry. She's very flexible and willing to work with you if you communicate with her. She gives good feedback and lets you resubmit assignments for a new grade which is super helpful. I would take her class again!

absolutely insane workload had her for two classes and each one was barely attainable. both were also intro courses! she doesn't listen to her students when they discuss the immense workload with her and how there is not enough time outside of class to properly complete the assignments she's giving ONE AFTER ANOTHER. stay away!

Maria was awesome! She is actually better known as Maria Shilaos from KSL Newsradio. She really cares about her students and is flexible if you try hard in her class. She is great about giving feedback and in some cases lets you correct your mistake for a better score. We only had 1 test (midterm)- and a couple of quizzes. Would take again.
Super passionate lecturer and kind professor, very interested in challenging his own and your own way of thinking. Projects are fun and easy, but super deep. 100% take what you give kind of course.

Professor Nguyen is an extremely knowledgeable educator who is very passionate about the material that he teaches. He gives excellent, engaging lectures and interesting, fun exams. I can't recommend him enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grade consists of  5 total exams and participation. There's something to read every time before class but as long as you show up, you don't really have to read them. Doesn't use power points so he can get a little confused sometimes and drag certain topics. Changes the syllabus depending on what the class wants more of. Not a stressful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nguyen is caring, understanding and helpful but the language barrier is a legitimate challenge as she does not speak english very well and has pretty poor handwriting and grammar. It's not a hard class to succeed in; you get several tries on assignments and there are extra credit options. I did find myself going to class less and to Youtube more.

She doesn't speak English very well so it can be hard to follow her lectures. Her handwriting is so hard to read and her grammar is awful on tests and quizzes. You either get it or you don't. I felt very unprepared for tests and quizzes and was worried about not passing all semester even though I'm a good student.

Professor Nguyen was great! She is always willing to help students and she replies to emails fast. There is an extra credit opportunity almost every day. The homework is not that hard pretty much usual 12th-grade math, but, there are 3 finals total and 1 group project. Attendance is not mandatory, but you can get extra credit if you go.
Very clear expectation and daily opportunities for extra credit. Definitely take this class.

IVC class has a participation point every class. Recorded zoom link and lecture notes provided most of the time. However, her handwriting is hard to understand. Tests are worth 60% of the overall grade. Overall, did not feel the teacher cared about me passing (reached out before the end of term). Big "you either get it or you don't" mentality.
The tests are 33 pages front and back, with little to no guidance of what to study and how to prepare. She told me I should be studying 42 hours a week if I want to pass.

This was a great class.  IT WAS EASY actually for a science course wit all lecture notes that were labelled what we needed to study for tests.  She's good at using Canvas -- those people have never taken classes in the Business school  The people who complain probably don't belong at the university.
This porfessor posted all the class notes, gave us a lot of guides, and curved our tests.  She really made the materials easy to follow, and it was a very well organized person.

This course was honestly insane for an entry level class. Everyone is just trying to get their Gen Ed out of the way. This course was horribly designed and made to fail you. Study guide didn't exist and you had to differentiate what was important or not through the 60+ pages lecture slides + reading the book. Everything is broad. I don't recommend.

She seems like she cared about what she teaches, but her test was crammed with question and were super long. It was very hard for me to do well in her class. The number of things I had to study was very overwhelming just for a general ed. She is a kind person, but her teaching and test style was absolutely not for me.
One of the nicest professors I have ever had. Great teacher. Material is a little extensive for a 1000 level course, but she does not grade harshly. Pretty much only get graded on tests.

Dr. Nicoll is a very sweet lady but her class was frustrating at times. The department didn't give her a grader which meant that the class was mostly lectures and tests (the tests are difficult BTW), plus she wasn't good with Canvas and didn't update grades on said site. TBF, she was very lenient with final grading, but my experience was messy.
Great class. Interesting topics and very good lectures and a field trip. I recommend everyone tske a class with her. She is a very knowledgable person and she knows her stuff.

I am not a science person at all and I loved this class. I recommend taking it with this teacher because they know the topics and really explain the material well. I had to drop the course in the middle of one semester and when I retook it I found Dr Nicholl to be a much better lecturer. The textbook is good.

This woman is amazing and not afraid to tell it how it is. I was sad when this class went online because COVID; her class was the only one I was motivated to show up for. There were a few "quizzes", low stress. The biggest part of the grade was based on 3 exams that were straight-forward. If you didn't do well, she would allow corrections on tests.

Dr. Nicoll was an amazing professor, you must take an initiative to learn in her class. Test are fairly difficult not by difficulty of questions but by the amount of material each test covers. She is very willing to help you have an understanding of the material all you have to do is show up and ask intelligent questions. laziness won't pass.

I enjoyed this class and found the professors explanations and lectures easy to follow. I liked how she does not assign busy work. She told us exactly what to expect on each test and really coached us towards the tests.

Teaches in the European style and I have found it to be a very effective way to learn. Depending on what class you take from her, you either have to take difficult tests or write very detailed papers on self selected topics. Very good instructor!

Very little homework, so prepare to study for tests. Tests aren't bad if you take good notes every class, and review all material. She's very knowledgable about the material, I just wish her energy was a little higher.
Good course, overall. Recommended.

Kathleen is a wonderful professor who I would recommend to anyone. She is unquestionably an expert in her field. When midterms and finals come around, get ready to work. Her tests are very hard, but she grades them fairly. She expects students to be scientifically literate, and she talks to her students as equals. She does fun field trips too.

Kathleen is a wonderful person, I truly enjoyed my time in class. I would not dissuade anyone from taking a class from her. Her sense of humor makes lectures more interesting. If you get an opportunity to go on a field trip with her, take it! My only warning would be that her courses are test heavy, and the tests are harder than you would expect.

Dr. Nicoll is a sweet lady. She definitely knows her stuff and when she gets going on topics that she really knows, you can tell (aka deserts). The class itself was interesting. There was a book that was mostly used for assistance with the lectures, but if you miss a class definitely read the chapter. Only 3 tests, and they were hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took Campaign Management (3160) and Forum Series (3910). Nick was great in both classes, and neither course was overly difficult. I really liked the class discussions and structure. For campaign management, you intern for a political campaign 5 hours a week. For forum series, you attend 10 Hinckley forums throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Campaign Management (3160) and Forum Series (3910). Nick was a good instructor in both courses and clearly cared about students and the subject matter. Not hard courses and I enjoyed discussions and guest speakers.

Easy class that completes one of your generals while getting a polsci credit. It was once a week, so there wasn't much time to get to know the professor, but he was very nice and I enjoyed the weekly lectures. The rest of the class is attending 10 forums throughout the semester, which is easy and yields free food. I even went to more than 10!

Prof Cockrell is a good professor, but doesn't invest a lot of time into this class. It's an easy class though: show up, go to forums, write short papers, and you'll be good. An easy but boring 3000 level poli sci class.
Difficult class, lots of homework, and test heavy. However, very good lectures and he is an excellent professor and as long as you put in the effort you will be fine.

Dr. Nielson is great. His lectures are easy to understand and he presents everything clearly. He shows examples during lecture of real life applications of the material that you are learning which helps me understand what's going on. Home works can be difficult but definitely prepare you for exam, and he posts lectures online.

Expect to spend 6-8 hours a week on homework, plus more time on your own, if you want to understand anything. He didn't provide any study materials for the final, which had a 60% average. I only got a good grade in this class because I spent about 12 hours a week on my own watching other lectures. His exams are “multiple choice” (actually 15 FRQ).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nielson is an incredible and inspiring professor. He has guided lecture notes which are very helpful, and he makes lectures fun and interesting. Strengths of Materials is a difficult course and requires a lot of work to do well in.

I took the online version. It was ok, it wasn't hard, but it wasn't easy. He curves all the tests, and pretty much everyone fails them since it's online. If you get good grades on the homework and at least a 50 on the tests, you could get an A. Seems like a good guy tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Class I took was fully online. Professor was very helpful in describing/giving feedback on certain concepts/assignments. Homework was 30 question quiz each week, two tests, and final project. No zoom, learn at your own pace. Felt I learned a lot and understand the concepts very well and there was always tutoring sessions if needed.

Professor Wolfinger is a nice guy, but I'm not sure how good of a math teacher he is. I struggled quite a bit with his lectures because they were just narrated PowerPoint presentations. In a math class, I expect more of a hands-on approach. He is quite entertaining and that made the lectures more bearable, but be prepared to seek outside help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
His recorded lectures were long and thorough, and he was extremely communicative. He gave me personalized help on several occasions over Zoom and email, and was always friendly and quick to respond. Curved grades definitely helped me pass with an A, so just try your best and it will be fine.

That said, yeah, he's odd. Enjoy the ride!

I didn't even try really for this stats class and got a B in the class. Thank god for the class, assignments, and exams being curved or I would of got a E or D. Put in some effort and you will be fine. Fairly fast at grading the curve and not a lot of homework. Odd guy but chill.

Nick was an ok teacher but that's not what you want when you are taking a higher level stats course. He rushed through content and got off topic a lot. I left class every time with zero clue on what was going on. I basically taught myself all the content. Tests are so hard, if he didn't grade on a curve, I know I would've failed that class.

Awful teacher.  Slurs words, doesn't explain things clearly, looks disheveled and unprofessional, appears to be on drugs, lots of example math problems have to do with sex/women.  Makes the class uncomfortable.  Does not show example problems step by step.  Worst teacher I have ever had in my life!

The semester I took this course I suffered a lot from my mental illness and professor Wolfinger was more than understanding and willing to work with me through these issues. Material is spread out in a nice way and I would absolutely recommend this professor.

I loved Nick! Marriage and Divorce was a super interesting topic and he make the lectures fun and filled with great information. He's really funny and nice. There is a midterm, final, and a paper. You don't have to show up to class for participation but you won't learn the material since he doesn't do slides on the topics. It is more so discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Hoping I reach students BEFORE they enroll in this class. DO NOT sign up for Wolfinger's course. He is intelligent and has done some really interesting research but is NOT a good teacher. Class attendance isn't required but it doesn't even make sense to show up in the first place, he fails to cover essential information- you teach yourself or fail.
This course is hard but Professor Wolfinger tries to make it fun and interesting.

He is a really nice guy and a really good professor, but unfortunately the class itself is just terrible. I am having a really tough time with the course, but I feel like if I had him for a different class I would really enjoy it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is the WORST teacher I have ever had. He doesn't lecture well and even though I am in his online class, I have friends who are in his physical class and they are having the same or worse time with this course. He's already on probation for having bad grades and to make sure he doesn't get worse grades he curves everything. Horrid teacher!
If you teach this class be prepared to teach yourself the material.

He was really rude for me when I asked him about grading questions.  I would email him frequently when I was confused about something (it was an online class,) and he just mocked me and made me upset.  Terrible professor and rude person. I would like to add that his lecture videos are annoying because he records them with his air conditioning on.

I had 2-3 study groups and we had no idea how to work our problems. He's very confusing with his lectures and sometimes doesn't seem like he knows what he's doing. He seems to be passionate about his course but has a hard time communicating how to solve problems. I basically had to teach myself this course but I managed to pass.

Would not recommend this teacher. This was his second time teaching Statistics, and it was not a good experience. The professor is not very organized, and teaches in a confusing way. Tried to get a tutor to help me, and he said I was being taught the wrong stuff.

This teacher is by far a great teacher I took this semester. He's hilarious and made this class really entertaining about marriage and divorce. If you need a upper division class take this. He only has 2 tests and a paper and you get participation credit. He is really nice to talk to if you need anything from him. Can't wait for his other classes!
Enjoyed this course.  Textbooks good for reference but not really required.  Learn STATA not SPSS or SAS.
great class
Great class.  Pretty easy and really interesting.  He's a zany professor and is a lot of fun.
No Comments
One of my favorite courses I've taken at the U. Nona really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. As long as you put in effort on your assignments and never use AI, you will get an A.

You can tell Professor Brown cares a lot about her students, and she appreciates those who put in effort to learn and take away things from her class. This class was so interesting (all about Black Mirror!) and I thoroughly enjoyed the content. No tests, just three main projects. I would love to take a class from her again.

Professor Brown is mid to good in most things, but is abysmal in organization and transparency. Exact due dates, including the major projects that made up 85% of the grade, were released 1 week in advance, canvas pages often contradicted each other, and Q/A response times were poor. Knowing why points were deducted isn't a thing, even if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Brown required a valid citation technique but demanded it be used incorrectly. I would not recommend her course because you will be taught the wrong things and graded poorly if you do things correctly. She insists on writing that mirrors your "discipline," but shows no interest in learning about the disciplines before critiquing students.

Communicated technical issues I had with her and worked things out, then still gave me 0's for turning the assignment in late. Takes forever to respond to questions. A ton of reading and long videos. Told us to expect to spend an extra 3 hours than we would any other class. Takes over 1 month to grade anything. Clearly doesn't care. HEAVY workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She did not appear to want to be teaching the class. She claims to be there to help but would not respond to questions within a reasonable timeframe. Her instructions are incredibly vague and contain contradictory requirements. The online "lectures" are jumbled and difficult to follow. The information is good but lacks instruction.

Most of our grade was determined by three projects we did. These projects are not very complex but do require some effort. If you work on them a little bit every week once they are assigned, they will be no problem at all. 
Nona Brown wants her students to succeed. Ask her, and she will do her best to help you if you are confused or falling behind.

Wish I would have dropped this class. It's all about Black Mirror, and have weekly pages that are confusing and full of long readings and videos that would take many hours to finish. I was always confused, and help from the teacher would come delayed and not that useful. It's a class you have to put a lot of effort into.

Though it was online she was an amazing professor. My biggest weakness is in writing and yet, she was able to help me through emails and was glad to review/correct my work when asked. Very caring and very well-thought-out professor.

Professor Brown does an amazing job with her Black Mirror class! It is project heavy and it takes up a majority of your time and there is a lot, A LOT, of reading but the tests are open book which makes it somewhat easier. She's very nice and responds quickly to questions. You don't need to buy a textbook since they're all provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nona is one of the most caring professors. She really wants you to succeed and always makes sure that everyone is on the same page. She'll even push back deadlines if you're not able to complete the projects in time. She has really cool multimodal assignments that get you out of your comfort zone. Also hilarious and wants to get to know you!

A few major papers are essentially what determine your grade. Quite a few in class participation points that warrant showing up every time. Overall very understanding and very accommodating. She would always ask what we were comfortable with as far as timelines go and even pushed back due dates if it was what the class wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was my first upper division writing class, and it was online. I had tons of questions, but she always answered them quickly and thoroughly.  She certainly believes in peer reviewing before a paper is turned in. It's a little bit of a pain, but definitely worth it.  Good class, great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Easy A. I spent around 20 mins per week on this class. It was easier than a high school writing class (I'm not complaining). You will learn to write a resume, an email, and a pamphlet. Just don't miss any projects because there are very few. She grades a little tough because the course is so basic and she will only award an A for exceptional work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: To add to my comment from 12/06/2016, this class was only easy due to the fact that I came to class prepared everyday and Nona gives you the resources necessary to make the class "easy" if you choose to do so. Read every last assigned reading, use her grading feedback on papers to revise and resubmit, always turn in your best work and youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Nona is awesome. Easy classes, but you actually delve into the details behind the texts. Super understanding and easy to work with. I'm taking a class from her again next semester.

AMAZING. hard but you should expect that from a 4000 series class and one that counts for 2 credits to boot. engaging and interesting lectures, applicable projects and shes funny and is available and gives good feed back.  did i mention visual rhetoric counts for two different credits?
She is willing to help her students, very approachable and well informed.

Great teacher, i would recommend Nona to any student as she is helpful and caring. one of the best teachers at the U of U for sure. I took writting 4030 and 3018 from her and both were a great experience.

Nona gives great feedback throughout the course of the semester. Assignments aren't tough if you have a basic understanding of business. Nona sets you up with tools to succeed in her class. She updates Canvas frequently and is very quick to responding to emails. Highly recommended!

Nona is a professor who really cares about her students. As long as you make a real effort, you can do well in her class. She is always willing to meet with students and edit papers before due dates. You actually feel like a better student/writer after taking her class! I highly recommend her.

Nona is very kind and encouraging and is always willing to help if you need it. She has 3 major papers and 1 extra credit assignment and you can revise 1 of your essays for more points. She gives extra perks to people who take her on campus class vs Online class FYI. Honestly its an easy A if you put some effort into her essays. Easy grader overall

Extremely kind, positive, and constructive. Gives great feedback on assignments and is willing to give extra time and advice. I was in her online course, but met with her on campus when I ran into difficulties on a paper and was so happy I did. Would recommend her class to anyone.

She is so awesome! I feel like I learned a lot in this class even though it wasn't an overloard of work. We only did 3 or 4 papers the whole semester but they were really helpful and we got good feedback. I would SO recommend her!
THE best teacher at the University of Utah.
really chill professor

Nona was a good teacher. Her selection of text and lecture was a great help. I felt like her feedback was very constructive and useful as well. She wasn't easy, but she was reasonable with her grading. I totally recommend her if you need a writing credit.
She is so helpful and way nice... I enjoyed her as a teacher a lot.

This class seems to be all over the place, several students were confused as to what is required and when is it due.  I think a simple web site updated regularly would clarify some of the misunderstandings.  The teacher was very helpful and forgiving.

He is super sweet! If you're taking his chem I class, make sure to come in with a baseline understanding of chem, or be ready to do a lot of self-teaching outside of class. He made good grades attainable if you put in the work.
Amazing guy, knows what he's doing and keeps most lectures interesting.

Dr. Noriega is the best teacher I have ever had. Personally, I had never taken AP Chem so Honors chem was difficult but Dr. Noriega always made me feel smart and like he believed in me. I learned a ton. Love this guy!!
Noriega was one of the best profs. I've had. He cared a lot about making sure everyone learned and did his best to have engaging lectures.
The tests felt more like applying the concepts to actual scenarios rather than simply memorizing facts for a multiple choice.

Dr. Noriega has been my favorite professor thus far at the U. Though the exams are more difficult and make you connect multiple concepts together, there is a generous curve and he is more than willing to help you succeed. He is a true teacher who challenges you to learn, whilst also caring about your success. I highly recommend him!

Professor Noriega was so helpful in Honors Gen Chem. All of his lectures were engaging, and he focused on our understanding of the concepts rather than memorizing random things. There were 4 midterms, but he offered extra credit points and graded on a curve, so it actually boosts your grade if you pay attention in class. TAKE CHEM WITH NORIEGA!!!

This is a rating for his 1211 Honors Gen Chem class. Professor Noriega is a phenomenal teacher who actually cares about his students. While there is a lot of homework even during exam weeks, his lectures are helpful and he is very welcome to answering questions during his lectures to help everyone understand better. A true teacher.

Rodrigo is an awesome professor, even if I disliked his class. I think that quantum chem is a subject that's impossible to teach in an enjoyable way, but Rodrigo is definitely the best you could hope for. He really cares about his students, and would move exams if they conflicted with peoples' schedules. Tests had a generous curve which helped too.

This class may feel like you are drowning at first, but if you try your hardest and ask for help to be sure that you understand the content to the best of your ability then you will succeed in the course. This is a very abstract topic, and Professor Noriega clearly does his best to help you learn it but it may not come easy to all.

No one understands the content, and he UNDERSTANDS that no one understands. He curved everything, gave out PLENTY of redemption for basically everyone to get an A. Hard freaking class, but honestly it worked out in the end and he cared

One of the most caring professors I've ever had. He gives a lot of redemption if you do badly on midterms, and he also curves the exams. He genuinely wants you to do well and understand the content, even though it's very confusing and complex. Attendance is not mandatory, and he records lectures.

Up front, this class is very difficult. Who would have guessed, Quantum Chem is really hard! However, Professor Noriega is easily one of my favorite professors. He is fun, passionate, and engaging, and cares so much about helping you learn quantum. He cares more about you learning than worrying about a grade, and is generous with his scoring.

Professor Noriega is easily one of the best professors I've had. He understands how challenging this course can be and genuinely wants his students to succeed. His lectures are engaging, and he records all of them, which makes it easy to stay caught up if you ever miss class. He's a phenomenal instructor and a truly caring educator.

CHEM3060 is a very hard class to understand. Dr. Noriega made it possible to mess up on a midterm and still survive with a good grade. He is generous on grading and curves most tests with some extra credit. There was not very much time for office hours. This class requires a lot of effort and time to effectively understand the material for tests.

He was amazing. Physical chem has always been my worst chem subject, but he met outside of office hours/class just to help. Coding heavy, I had to relearn MatLab, and he was really helpful through my struggle with it. Material is really difficult, but the lab helped me understand better. The fact I got an A astounds me, but it was all him

I learned a ton from Dr. Noriega. He's very willing to help outside of class. I really appreciate that he had the labs set up so there was dedicated time to work on data analysis. There's lots of analysis to do, but all of the labs we performed are very relevant and enhanced my understanding of physical chemistry. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Made a 3-hour class engaging and even fun. If you pay attention in class and follow along with the textbook, you'll do fine.

I took his Econ 2010 class. It was very heavily based on the textbook and readings. The exams were open-book and open notes, so it was pretty easy to pass the class.
Now I am taking his 5190 class, and there was a big jump in toughness. He keeps the content very relevant, and the content seems to change. is a scatterbrain, but a very great person.

Knows his stuff but kinda scatterbrained and teaches concepts somewhat out of order. Really nice and really funny guy. Not too hard of a class, read the textbook if you don't understand from the lectures but otherwise readings aren't super necessary. Class is not too hard to get a good grade in and the tests are all multiple choice. .
So rude
Knows the subject but is an awful teacher. Not friendly. Never admits when he's wrong. Overall pretty rude. Would not recommend.
He knows economics. He doesn't know how to teach you it. If you can self learn from the reading you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took his poverty and inequality class and it has been one of the best classes I've ever taken. He demands that you read a lot but the professor is enjoyable to listen to and is passionate about the subject. I would highly recommend anyone take a class from him.

You will read until your eyeballs fall out. He is a very funny guy, but kind of terrifying when he calls on people randomly. He doesn't take attendance, but you should still go. It'll make the tests a lot easier. He posts study guides for the tests, which is helpful. There are only two tests, so make sure you study!

Waitzman is hilarious, you will laugh every lecture but he is hard to follow sometimes. He knows what he is talking about and is very educated. He grades hard and expects you to study but you will learn a lot from the class. Definitely worth taking a class from him.

Professor Waitzman is fun to listen to, but not a good teacher. He knows his stuff, but has difficulty explaining. Always attend class, he uses and tests on terms he mentions in class that aren't in the book. I wouldn't recommend him unless you need a good laugh during the day.

Class was 'fun' but I ended up getting the worst grade of my college career from him. His tests are difficult. made up of multiple choice (worth 2 each) and then 4-5 T/F explain questions. The T/F are worth ALOT and he is looking for VERY specific answers. If you have him, good luck! Be prepared to study LOTS!
Really enjoyed this class. Professor is really very funny and made the subject interesting
testing

I took econ as a social science from professor Waitzman.  The readings were interesting and eye opening. I thought the class was well organized and covered a lot of relevant material. Good professor.  I'd recommend him.
It is really hard to focus on what he says in class because sometimes he tends to go off topic.
This guy is hilarious (good thing since the subject can get mighty boring sometimes). He's a pretty good instructor and you can expect to hear plenty of New Jersey bashing.
Awesome professor. Inspired me to be an econ major four years ago.
He looks and acts like a monkey. Very funny, especially his laugh. You will have to work in the class, but it is a riot in there.
If you attend lectures and do the practice midterms this class she makes this class pretty easy

Overall, a very good and engaging professor. However, you will need to spend time outside of this class learning the material to complete the homework and study for quizzes and midterms. She would go over the basics in class, nothing more. Homework took all week and was more advanced than what we learned in class.

The main gripe I have with this class is that attendance is mandatory. Other than that Dr. Brown is an excellent professor and cares for her students her assignments are clearly written and well done. The lectures are actually discussions and they are fun and I looked forward to class each time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: No one wants to take ethics but we all have to. Professor Brown did a great job at making such a class bearable. The block projects were straightforward and if you put in an ounce of effort on the rest of the class you'll be fine. Plus she isn't even that strict about students perusing reels during class. Try to take ethics with her if you can.

Brown is the best, 1400 was the first cs class I ever took and she did an incredible job at explaining the basics. She's super kind and helpful, the TA's were pretty good. Weekly assignments could be tricky but there are a ton of resources for help. Her late policy for work is nice too. I can't recommend her enough!

This was not for 1400, it was Cs3090. I made an account here just to rate how great Professor Brown is. CS3090 was an interesting class and she was extremely educated on the topic but still very interested in student opinions. The class is an easy A if you attend and participate, with just a few homework. It also discusses important ethics topics.

She is a great professor and understanding teacher. Her policy for late work is nice, and tests are not really challenging if you engaged with the class assignments and papers. She and her TAs team are also very helpful with questions about assignments.

For an outsider I thought Prof. Brown was pretty good at teaching and introducing the material. She had some great lectures and made it fun and interesting. The assignments were not great and difficult, the TA's were not great. Expect to spend some time on the class.

This is the worst professor I've had in college. When he lectures it feels like he is learning the material for the first time too. Almost every single class a student would correct him because he was confused or said something wrong. The exams are unnecessarily hard, he has a huge ego, and can never take accountability when he is wrong.

Didn't give me the option but I am currently taking him for OSC 3440 and it is a nightmare. He has never taught the class and started off the semester by saying the curriculum seemed way too easy and so he throws his own twisted curriculum in. He constantly tests us on random things said in videos he shows and like half of them are IS!

Dave covered all the topics in an engaging and interesting manner.  He weaved his experience on various technologies.  He tried to engage with his students through his questions and being available on text and zoom.  His webinars were good and concise and available 24x7, which was helpful because the quizzes and labs were very intensive.

He is a very kind professor — approachable, supportive, and understanding. The class has one midterm worth a big portion of the grade, but the labs and group project help balance it and make the class easier to manage.

Professor Norwood's Networking & Servers class was the best course I took at the university. His extensive experience shines through, and his teaching style is practical and focused on real-world applications. The labs were hands-on, reinforcing the material. His clear explanations make complex topics easier to understand. Highly recommended!

This class was truly outstanding! The professor is incredibly knowledgeable and his approach to teaching made a real impact. The project in this course was unique and stood out from all the other classes I took at the U it was both engaging and highly practical. I only wish the professor taught more courses at the U. Highly recommend!

I was really thinking I liked this guy at first, since he has good video lectures and is clearly very knowledgeable... Then I reached out to him about an issue I had with a quiz question. Like others here have said, this guy has SERIOUS ego and communication issues. I am not looking forward to the rest of this course.

6640 was a very challenging class and Professor Norwood was a great teacher. If it's your first networking class then you might struggle but it's worth it. Learned a ton of useful, real world stuff. Quiz every class so keep up with the readings. Cengage labs are terrible but hopefully that changes in the future. Would recommend but buckle up.

Professor Dave Norwood is an exceptional educator who truly stands out for his teaching abilities and dedication. He is highly responsible, ensuring every lecture is well-prepared. His teaching style is clear, engaging, and effective. I highly recommend Professor Norwood for anyone seeking a knowledgeable, supportive, and inspiring instructor.

He has clear ego issues, that much is certain. It takes a special type of person to write your own reviews on RMP. He finds twisted enjoyment in making concepts harder than they need to be, and he treats every lecture as an ego booster and power trip. This class is a great excuse if you want to drop out of school.

Dave was generally unkind when reaching out for help/assistance. He refused to understand that the material might have been hard to understand for some students and, rather, assumed every student struggling was lazy and unmotivated. He made the weekly quizzes with AI to try and "beat" AI cheating, but it just beat anyone with reading difficulties.

Great professor if you're into networking or servers! His materials break down complex topics well, and he's very supportive if you need extra help. Plus, his real-world experience is impressive—he launched Trusted Network Solutions, so he shares insights from the industry that make classes feel relevant. It was a rewarding and practical class.

Professor Norwood cares about lot about his students and his students experience in his classes. The class itself can be difficult at times, especially with the breadth of material that's covered. But Dave is always helpful and challenges you with a helping hand. Man's a wealth of knowledge. I encourage you to ask him questions!

My biggest gripe is the group project. Dave told us we had done a great job, and I based my group members feedback off of what he said on their portions. Come to find out they had done an awful job and we missed half the points on their portion, getting a C- on the whole thing. I don't understand why he would lie. 0/10 professor.
Dave is fantastic, he provided so much help on the group assignment. Plus, he is very understanding and his lectures are insightful. He's also really funny, making the tough topics more bearable.
Dave is like Dolores Umbridge from Harry potter. Absolutely insane ego issues and is just there to brag about himself. The IS faculty failed us all by hiring him.

Dave falls short in every aspect. He will tell you you're doing great on the massive group project, only to turn around and give you a C. He shows no real passion for teaching and seems to just be there for the paycheck and to brag about how smart he is. Extremely disappointing experience.

Professor Dave Norwood demonstrates exceptional teaching abilities. His teaching style is dynamic and engaging, capturing the attention of every student in the classroom. He has an uncanny talent for breaking down even the most complex concepts into easily digestible parts, ensuring that students thoroughly understand each topic.
You will be fighting for your life from day one. He truly does not want you to succeed. He just wants you to know how great he is.
I think he is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class and professor contributed to about 90% of my burnout from the semester. Proctored midterm, really tight time limits for quizzes (and you can't go back to questions), basically zero guidance for labs, and topped off with the worst group project.  If you're only minoring in IS, this is your sign to take literally any other class.

Dave fails to deliver as a teacher at every level. He can not explain concepts in simple terms nor does he want to. He has an ego issue and enjoys over complicating the material. Like others have mentioned, this man will review your group project, says it looks great, and then dock a ton of points with really no explanation. 0/10

Our group project was worth 30% of our grade and we had to submit feedback before getting the grade back. The structure of the project meant it would be time consuming to see if your peers actually did a good job. So it's easy to give someone decent feedback but then find out that they did terrible and now you're stuck with a bad grade.
Take this class if you believe that suffering builds character. Dave enjoys creating confusion and frustration as he hopes that it will make students attend his webinars.

Never had a Professor who so condescending and unhelpful. The 5 star reviews are because Dave makes students write him a review to get a rec letter. Said our group project looked great and gave us a 70. Server lab instructions are also outdated so a few of them take significantly longer

The worst professor at the U. The silver lining of this course is that you can bond with any student in the school of business over how terrible this class and professor are. The group project is unfair. Dave reviewed our project said it was PERFECT then gave us a B with no explanation. Lectures might as well be in Greek - NOT beginner-friendly.
He is a great Professor, and has a good relationship with students.

This professor was genuinely awful to deal with. He wrote the first half of the quizzes for the class with AI in an attempt to ward off AI cheating, and all it qualified to do was make it that the students that utilized AI were able to pass as the quizzes were so incomprehensible. He was unkind when reaching out for help/resources.
He is very knowledgeable professor , if you are looking a career in networking he is the best

Dave's modern pedagogy fosters holistic learning, encouraging book supplements and industry updates alongside lab practice, just like in a real-life job. After this class I learned how to prepare for certifications, gained skills that boosted my resume and subsequent performance in courses like Cybersecurity. My favorite part was the group project
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, Dave seems like a chill and smart guy. But doesn't know how to teach, most of the learning is going to be just from googling things or reading the textbook. He is also the worst grader. He gives feedback on the group project but then turns around and gives low scores for everything even when he says a part looks good.

I failed this class because I had surgery and wasn't allowed an extension. It literally would take me 5 hours to do a single lab and they are actually really hard. You are required to read 100+ pages of week to pass the quizzes. The professor doesn't care about you. Seriously take any other class instead of this one.

Professor Norwood's teaching style reflects a potential issue with ego, as seen by unclear communication, inflexible policies, and a lack of responsiveness and respect for students. The focus on punitive measures for cheating suggests an emphasis on control rather than fostering a collaborative and supportive learning environment.

The professor has a major ego. He enjoys making things difficult for students. In-class lectures are a waste of time but yet they're required to go to. Overall this is the worst class and least favorite, least rewarding, least enjoyable I have taken at the U of U so far! Avoid Norwood!

One of the best logical professor I have had in my life till today. He is very approachable and most importantly he loves teaching. I did not have a major interest in the subject but his passion towards the subject pushed and reignited the fire inside me. If there is anyone who wants to build a career in Networking & Servers then this is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Labs are difficult. Professor Norwood seems to find amusement in students being confused. Lab instructions are vague and you're not allowed to ask the TAs to see if you're doing the labs correctly. Completly ruins the learning experience. Avoid this class and even the IS program. Just go get a CS minor instead + an accounting or finance major!

First of all, I am sure that these reviews on here are fake due to Dave Norwood being insecure about his class. He always got upset when people did not show up to class when there was no in-person quiz those days. You don't learn much by going to class. Dave is a difficult grader, he grades harshly on group discussion board posts which is crazy!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lol pretty sure these good reviews are written by Dave himself given how much of an Ego he has. Gets upset when people arent at class, yeah that's cause no one learns anything in your class and skips to just read your slides. Just rambles on and on. The class should be structured like B-Law. Dave seems like a good guy but shouldn't be teaching.

Professor Norwood's IS 4440 course was a wonderful experience. Although some might say that this class is boring as far as content goes, Professor Norwood is anything but boring. Homework is reasonable and instructions are very clear. He cares about his students and is happy to help out if you ask. Norwood also offers great office hours.
Overall, I really enjoyed professor Norwood. Dave is such a chiller-- very funny, very understanding. However, his class is not always engaging.

Norwood was one of the best professors I've had. Super down to earth and cares about his students. He stayed after class for hours to meet with groups for the final proj. Lectures can be boring, only complaint is that when it came to grading for the final projects was that he would say that something is good and then doc points for the same thing.

I truly enjoyed IS6640 with Dave. He has a ton of industry knowledge and is there for his students. Lot of really negative people in my class who expected him to tone down difficulty to cater to student with non-technical backgrounds, but this is a truly GRADUATE LEVEL course. If you put in the work and participate, you will succeed.
Absolutely phenomenal professor with great real-life experience and is always dedicated to helping students. Material is well laid out and labs are challenging but fair.

His lectures were awesome and intriguing. And he is communicative. So, you get a good constructive feedback. His course contents are up to date, resourceful, and practical. I would recommend him and his class.

Every week I have had amazing learning moments that impact my current job in really big ways. This is the exact reason I came back to school after many years.  I thought going back to school would be good, but it has been transformational.  The program you have helped build is amazing.  My experience so far has greatly exceeded my expectations!
Dave is very supportive for the students when in need. His class is very interactive to learn.

This class is very boring which makes it hard to get through, especially online. Start on the labs early because they were the most time-consuming part of the class. Make sure to meet with him at least once or twice for your group project and it will help your grade immensely. The midterm is hard but it's a small part of your grade. Good professor.

Professor Norwood has exceptional knowledge in his field and is always ready to share that with all his students. I enjoyed his way of teaching as it kept all of us so engaged into learning new and interesting things. I would recommend Prof. Norwood to all my friends.

Professor Norwood has exceptional knowledge in his field and is always ready to share that with all his students. I enjoyed his way of teaching as it kept all of us so engaged into learning new and interesting things.

Professor Dave Norwood really helped me a lot to understand the concepts of this course. His lectures were amazing and the in class quizzes which he organised helped me to revise the topics which I learnt in his lectures. He also provided feedbacks and support during the group project.

Professor Dave Norwood really helped me to understand the concepts of the course. His lectures were amazing and the in class quizzes which he organised helped me to review the topics which we learnt in each lecture. He also provided feedbacks and his support during the group project.

Great professor. Very friendly. Networking and server class was very helpful for helping me develop basic networking skills. Exams were difficulties were was about average, I was able to get an B+ on it.
Avoid it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: WARNING When looking at other rate my professor ratings for Dave Norwood please disregard his high scoring reviews. In order to get a letter of recommendation he requires you to give him a good score on rate my professor. When taking his class the instructions were purposefully unclear and was unreliable when asking for advice regarding assignments

I don't think Dave's bad scores on here are a reflection of him but the course. This course is NOT easy. You have a lot of definitions to memorize, most are acronyms that mean nothing. While it's online, Dave will always be accessible. He literally stopped his day to call me on his cell phone when I needed help. Good professor, hard/boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lectures, I could retain concepts well after attending his classes. His teaching style is extraordinary and I really enjoyed his classes. The coursework was extensive but he managed to keep our attention throughout and helped us gain a good foundation in Networks and Servers.
Good Professor! He has weekly online discussion every week.

Dave is a good professor. He cares about his students, and if you participate in the course, you will easy to pass this. The quiz and lab are not very difficult, just do some research and reading and you will be fine. In short, if you engage in the class, you will earn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: He is one of the best in the University. Always does the best possible things to make students successful. Approachable, respectful, and always helpful. Coursework was quite updated and he did his best to make our foundations stronger by keeping us engaged with hands-on experience of our learnings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dave is a great professor. He wants everyone to succeed, and does his best to help each student help themselves. I did not have much IT background, and so for me this class was a lot of reading, and studying. I found that Dave helped to make the dry information interesting, and enjoyable. In the end I liked the class, and appreciated the knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Dave has been doing whatever possible to point students in the right direction. There are challenges along the way which mostly is to do with students' effort. If you don't invest sometimes in this class, there is no way you can achieve what you wanted.

I can admit a class requires putting in some time; it's not an easy A. The professor is so helpful along the way, guiding and directing in the right direction. If a student is not investing some time, it's so easy to point at the professor.

Professor Dave is always open to help; he is always willing to go the miles to help students. He likes to warn at the beginning of the class that the class is not easy and students should invest enough time for a good reward. I can't blame the professor for a student's failure; honestly, personal commitment and dedication are needed to this class.

IS6640 is intended for graduate students (so you need to take ownership of what you want to learn), wanting to learn tech, but with no background (it doesn't go very deep). I think Norwood does a great job giving examples of how the concepts are applied in the field. The labs are structured to give some hands-on practice, although it is limited.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Norwood was great for IS 6640. Coming from someone that doesn't have a background in IT, I was worried I wouldn't do well in the class. Dave does a great job breaking down what he expects of his students. I will say lectures can get a bit boring, but that comes with an intro course. Not sure why other students haven't liked his class.

The lectures teach you nothing and lead you nowhere. The books are the best resource you have for the quizzes and labs. If you know how your home router works or how to ping DNS servers, you should be exempt from this class. You don't learn much.

He is a good man, but not a good teacher! He doesn't care if the students are learning. I thought it was a core class for people who don't have an IT background. But I think that he doesn't know that, as he said: "If you don't have an IT background, what are you doing here?" If you wanna low-grade to learn nothing, you're in the right place!

Dave's class is the one I have studied most and learned less about. It is not built for students learning. It has over 100 pages of reading each week and quizzes with 1 min to each question. The lectures are literally what is in the book so it doesn't add much. And If you use online resources, he will accuse you of plagiarism. Run away from it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dave and his class is an absolute joke. He is a terrible professor and an even worse human who only cares about hearing himself talk. If I could rate him a 0 on everything I would. Save yourself the trouble and avoid dave at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Did not create his own curriculum and material. Homework does not match problems worked through with class despite requiring 70% completion of them to pass.

Alex is a phenomenal professor, and sets students up for success. Thermodynamics can be a tricky subject, but Alex presents the material in a way that is clear and concise. Homework assignments can be difficult and lengthy, however this sets students up well for exams which are typically easier than the homework. Strongly recommend this professor!

Prof. Novoselov is an excellent teacher, he's very knowledgeable of the content and explains things super well. He's honest when concepts are tricky and does a great job of putting them into words. His printed notes are very helpful. Homework is sometimes really long (up to 8 hours) but exams are easier versions of the homework and aren't too bad

Prof. Novoselov is one of the best teachers I've ever had at The U. He is very passionate and inspiring; he definitely knows what he is talking about, and I loved Thermo because of that. He respects students and is friendly and easy to reach out. Grading was fair and there was a curve at the end of the semester when I took the class as well.

Great professor, always willing to help you understand things if you have any problems. Is not one of those professors who wants people to fail, he doesn't beat around the bush but wants you to actually learn and understand material rather than scrape for a grade! Would definitely take again.
Great professor that knows what he is talking about. Responds outside of class super quick which is a plus when you are working on the hw. Only thing I wish was the class was harder.

Sergazy moves incredibly quickly, if you skip a class or are late you won't be able to catch up easily. His handwriting is really hard to understand so it's tricky to take notes in this class, but notes will save you in the end. He is friendly and very funny, but it is difficult to learn in his class if you aren't super engaged.

reviews.comment: 1:This professor has no particularly strong basic skills. this was the worst class taken in the whole econ degree. His lectures are horrible, he doesnt even lecture he just posts videos to khan academy and calls it a day. You cannot understand anything he says. And when you ask for help he is never there. Absolutely never taking a class from him again.

Professor Up seriously gets it. All his lectures are very informative and class is super casual (tons of student participation). Assigned textbook sections are fairly short but assignments (papers 1/wk) take time. Anytime I emailed, he was accessible & he gives tons of feedback. I knew he cares. And he's flexible. All together, he's fantastic.
Definite language barrier, but class was a breeze. He likes to tell jokes so lectures are kind of annoying. Little assignments due every class, one final, one paper, one presentation. Easy.

Up is really great. There's a little bit of a language barrier, but for the most part, he's solid. He likes to tell little jokes, but he's pretty relatable and fun. Class was fairly easy, though dont forget to do your homework!

reviews.comment: Oh my god this guy is the worst teacher I have ever had. He doesn't explain things clearly, he spends half the time asking why you're not laughing at his stupid jokes, and he cannot teach. I literally had to teach myself all of the material in this class. The only reason the textbook is essential is because you can't learn from the teacher.

I took Math for Econ. Easy class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but because there is no textbook, you need to come to  class if you want to learn. If you pay attention in class you will do fine on the tests. Half the class only showed up on test days and then they whine that they got a bad grade LMAO! Assignments are easy too and reflect the test.

He is kind of hard to understand. We only had 3 assignments and 3 tests the whole semester so it was necessary to do good on all Six. You can miss out on class if you already understand the concept. If whole class does bad on an assignment or test, he grades on a curve luckily.

Your entire course grade depends on 13 lab assignments that must be worked on in class to receive credit. The enforcement of this attendance policy was inconsistent between students. His usual response to questions is to tell you to read the instructions again. Very frustrating course but doable if you put work into it.

Course 1980 for Physics entry majors. was not a choice above. It was a useless 1 hr required class. He had a guest lecturer for every class, professors way above a freshman's understanding. Doctor's note if class missed. (Who goes to the doctor for the flu or even Covid - $$) Not an inspiring class to lure in physics majors.

Tino is a nice professor and definitely has good intentions. However, don't expect him to answer any of your emails if you need his help. I reached out to him 5 times over the semester and he didn't respond, not once. Happy I had prior knowledge to Python programming before taking this his class because that's how I passed. He didn't teach me much

Bill is such a funny professor, he swears all the time and gets straight to the point. Honestly, I wish that he taught more marketing classes, but if you're curious or want to go into advertising TAKE THIS CLASS. Even if you're not this is still such a fun class and not stressful at all.

Bill is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so intelligent and passionate about creative advertising. In fact, he is very well known and high up in the advertising world. He really cares about inspiring every student to reach their full potential. TAKE HIS CLASS!

One of the best teachers I've have at this school.  He's a legitimate pro and he has a brilliant, creative mind.  Super passionate about what he teaches and very, very helpful when it comes to concerns.  He actually cares that his students learn something. AND he keeps things real with you.

The class is now Quest 1110. The class is not what academic advisors claimed and does not help for major exploration. It is participation heavy and practically a philosophy and political science class. Heavily focused on the IR aspect. I do not recommend it to undecided freshman.

Study guides are broad and not very helpful. I would not recommend.

This class does not follow the syllabus schedule, and the teacher will go on random tangents. It is lecture and participation-based, and you have to take notes because they directly correlate with the exams. Exams are open note, and so are the take-home quizzes.

If you take this class intending to learn about the role of law in society you would be sorely mistaken. This class had three required readings all on southern lynchings of African Americans. By no means am I saying that race relations and its role in current society should not be learned. However, the content of the course should reflect the name.

Toughest grader ever. In a class full of future lawyers, the grade point average was an 83% in Law & Communities going into the final... while the whole year she would belittle us with, this is the easiest A you will ever earn.

This professor makes lectures very difficult to follow. It seems like she is just rambling about current events and it's impossible to know what to take notes on. Tests are difficult. Nora Wood is absolutely amazing and very inspiring to any young woman pursuing a career in law and/or politics. However, she does love to hear herself speak and will not hesitate to steamroll her students durring discussion or presentations.

Very political. I enjoy law and history and have done very well in these classes in my past; but we don't do anything in this class other than talk about things that are barely relevant. End of the semester and the essay we're writing is about microaggressions in
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

Dr. Wood only discussed race the entire semester. I am a person of color who's interested in CRT but this was excessive. reviews.comment: I love Professor Wood. Her lectures are really inspiring and you can tell how passionate she is about what she's teaching. You'll do great in her class if you put in the work and participate.

Dr. Wood is the BEST! Get ready to learn a lot, have fun, and stay engaged. There wasn't a second I was bored in her LEAP class. This professor is awful if you want busy work take this class. Her grading is not consistent

Dr. Wood is a hard grader and will humble you, but she teaches great material and provides meaningful lessons in her lectures. Attendance is mandatory so plan on coming to every class. If you participate and turn assignments in on time, you'll easily become likable and she's a great mentor to have.
Dr. Wood is my favorite professor that I have had so far. I have learned a lot about topics that I am passionate about. If you care about the material and work hard you will do great.

Dr. Wood is intelligent, caring, and wonderful. Her course content is eye-opening and she is obviously passionate about it. Wood's lectures encourage participation and she wants to hear from students. Her kindness shines through every class. Wood's grading scale is more difficult, but only because she wants you to grow as a student and person.
Go to class prepared and participate. Great profesor and great relationship with students.

reviews.comment: Professor Wood grows on you. I definitely did not have an amazing experience my first semester but after a while she became a mentor. She has definitely become one of my favorite professors at the U.

For a state/local govt. class the content is all over the place, definitely not what I was expecting. It feels almost like a 1000 level course, very introductory. Unnecessarily a hard grader its honestly so bad. Very interesting class but she graded way too hard on papers and other assignments. Great class and caring professor but make sure you take notes and attend class. You have to get the exact answer the wants otherwise its wrong.

Dr. Wood was a really great professor. As someone who doesn't have similar political views to the majority of campus, I was worried headed into this class.
