reviews.comment: Dr. Wood's Honors American Institutions class was amazing! She covers a lot of meaningful material, you learn A LOT:)and the things about history and critical thinking then and now have helped me in all my other classes. If you need help or have a problem just ask, she will accommodate. I have anxiety when it comes to essays, she was understanding.
Professor Wood is great! She doesn't assign a lot of work, and what she does assign is meaningful. Her tests are very easy because she gives you the test questions on the "study guide" a week before.

Dr. Wood is an amazing teacher. She really knows what she is talking about and is passionate. Yes, she is liberal, but she encourages participation from all viewpoints. If you read the textbooks that she assigns, this class really is not difficult. I received very high scores on her exams and essays. Participate in class and you'll be fine.

Professor Wood is a great professor and one of my all-time favorites. Show up to class, do some of the readings (like skim through things) and you will be fine! Piece of advice: cater to her when writing essays and you will pass no problem.

Woah I can't believe these reviews. I am a republican and have taken three classes from Dr. Wood. She is awesome. Super nice- not the same old boring professor that you typically get. Go to class, give input and know your stuff and she will love you. Hardly any reading just know the main subjects and take good notes! She also preps you for exams.

This class is the worst. Dr. Wood interrupts during presentations, will always claim to know more than you do and will knock you points if you have your own opinion that doesn't match her own. Her tests are VERY specific and if you don't use the EXACT words she wants you to use when answering her questions, it will be marked wrong.

I took Nora Wood's class and I found that unless you are a snowflake it will be hard to pass.  Class is often taken over by liberals that reach victimization.  I wrote some knock out papers and was barely getting  a b when in all my other classes the  same type of papers were getting 95's.  If conservative take class and rip  her with facts!

I did not enjoy Dr. Wood's class at all. She's a nice woman but I couldn't stand her class. I felt like I was being forced to have her opinion on things as opposed to developing my own. reviews.comment: Amazing Prof. She cares about what she's teaching and what students are learning. Class is a little content heavy, but nothing too bad. Most material is interesting and relevant. You will have to show up to class and read the books. Very understanding and cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is really very easy. The book will help you pass but it isnt necessary. You can find every answer online. The discussions can be pretty interesting if you put the effort into it.

Dr. Wood made class very enjoyable. She used many different teaching methods including movies, short clips, computers, and many other things that made the class fun. The leap program in general is really great! You will read and take quizzes on the books. Also a group presentation and paper at the end of the semester.
Great class very Interesting! She teaches very well and I really enjoyed her class. You have to show up and you read four books!

I absolutely loved Wood! She was understanding, sympathetic to my home life emergencies, and was more than willing to help me with my major.  I wish I could take her for every poli sci class I had.  Lectures were in-depth and informative, and the course work and expectations were laid out with no questions. 10/10, would recommend.
I loved Dr. Wood! She is very helpful and understanding. She keeps things interesting and doesn't skimp on important information. Going to this class was really fun.

I took American Presidency from Dr. Wood.  I thought the class was great.  She presented the material well and did a good job at engaging the class.  She knew a lot about the executive branch and the history thereof.  Exams were essay-based and one research paper was required, where she was extremely helpful throughout the entire process.

The course was well organized and covered topics that were timely and relevant.  Dr. Wood was accessible, communicative,  and provided good feedback.  It was imperative to keep up with the assignments to do well in the class.  She set the course up to encourage good discussion and interaction with other students.

I have really enjoyed Nora's class. She has helped me to really think critically and open-minded. She can tend to let her liberal side take control but she is very good about letting students voice opinions. She has grasped everyone's attention which I think is a great quality of a professor of political science.
Took online. Quizzes are unclear because multiple choice answers aren't always consistent with material in the book. Egotistical and overly critical (and not in the constructive way).

I took this class online and was a little disappointed that Prof. Wood didn't post lectures. There were usually 2 quizzes a week on chapters in the text and 3 written papers. She's a pretty harsh grader, but the papers don't have to be long. If you have an interest in gov. You'll probably enjoy this class.

Nora was one of my favorite professors. She really knows her stuff and knows how to teach it very well. It would be a good idea to ready the lectures but you will do well on the exams if you go to class. She is more than willing to talk if you have questions. She is great and I highly recommend taking her class!
Lectures tend to be taken over by student comments and rants.  Lots of reading from text book and books she puts on 2 hour reserve.

She is passionate about her subject and it shows in lecture.  Quizzes couldn't be easier, she practically gives you the answers.  No homework. Exams aren't bad, she provides study guides with everything on the test and she's very easy to approach. Great Teacher.

Glorified gradstudent, thinks shes a prof because shes 60somethin. Exams do not reflect lectures, unrealistic expectations. Halflecture is unrelated to course. Instructs wrong information, I got the REAL FACTS when comparing her lecture to established online sources.  Ridiculuosly imposes her political views.  Good Luck!

Really nice and helpful. She always emailed me back right away if I ever asked any questions. The class is also very easy because she gives practice quizzes and tests which are exactly like the real ones, just with different numbers. Put a minimal amount of effort and you can get an A- at least.
I dont know what the others are on about- I guess she was not as good in the past. Now she is super nice and makes a difficult subject very manageable. I give her 5 out of 5 stars.

She was extrememly hard to understand, taught material much too quickly, and explained things poorly when asked questions. She was a sweet person, but not suited for teaching especially a calculus class at the college level. I am sorry I ever had to suffer through this for a semester, and I feel bad for anyone who has to in the future.
i hate her.  she has a bad accent that is super hard to understand.  she is super hard to learn from.  i would not wish her class on anyone.

Accent makes her very difficult to understand, and she goes through concepts very quickly, assuming you already know everything. She assigns way more homework than other calculus teachers and grades very harshly.
Very hard to understand due to her heavy accent and assigns loads of homework.  Expects too much of her students and while willing to help, is not very fair.
No Comments

She knows her stuff. She kind of talks over your head sometimes, but all she has you do is an essay midterm and final, and a final paper. The books help you understand the material, not necessarily her. But she very smart and pretty relaxed about attendance.

Missed first week, out of the country, showed up late every day offering various excuses (usually 5-15 minutes late).  After 2 weeks of teaching the class, she skipped another week, and that's where I'm at right now.  So far the material is very, very easy.

I was so scared to take stats online but this professor is amazing. He made his own workbook and textbook that make everything SO understandable and easy to learn. You have to take the time to to read the chapter and follow along in the workbook with notes but if you do that you will pass the class EASILY and learn a thing or two along the way.

PSY 3000 online is doable! I was nervous but Professor Gordon has everything laid out very well. You will be using your textbook and workbook. Tests must be taken in the testing center but it is easy to schedule a time through Canvas and you get to use your workbook on the tests! Just write down as much as you can in your workbook for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Oakley is hands down one of the most inspiring professors I have ever had the privilege of being enrolled in his class. He genuinely cares about you learning the material. He is the author of the textbooks you use, you have to show up to class so you can fill in information in the book from his slides, but your can also use the other text
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I can't say enough about this professor, math has never been a strength for me and he was able to explain it in a ways that I understood, even in an online class! seriously wish this guy could teach all my classes..

You can use the workbook on the exams and labs which was extremely helpful. Gordon is honestly so passionate about his work, he takes time to explain thoroughly and helped in so many ways. He uses amazing examples and I overall enjoyed his class. If you have a chance ask him about his research in Peru, its extremely fascinating.

I've taken both 3000 and 5290 applied stats from Gordon. He makes Stats as enjoyable as it can be. He wrote the book you use (very inexpensive text book and workbook) and has a gentle self deprecating sense of humor that makes reading the lectures entertaining and takes the intimidation out of dry, complex statistics. I took his grad course for fun

I was really nervous about taking this class, especially taking it online! It turned out to be one of the best math classes I have taken. Material is clear and easy to understand. DO THE WORKBOOK!! You can take the workbook into test and if you complete the assignments in the workbook you'll do great on the test.
Great textbook, best online math-esque course I've taken. I would definitely recommend. The in-person exams are often easier than the online tests and quizzes.

This was a very easy yet very rewarding statistics class. There are two books, a lecture book and the workbook that you use for notes. You can use your notes on any of the quizzes or exams, making both fairly easy. This is probably the best class you can take for a gen ed or psych major and a great example of how online classes can be stress free.

Without a doubt, one of the best professors at the U! I am NOT good at math, but I got an A in this statistics class because of how it was taught. It's not a walk in the park, but is extremely well organized, and the textbook and workbook make things simple, so an A is realistic no matter the level of your math skills. HIGHLY recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: 10/10 would recommend taking this class! If you're like me and love a good organized class, this is the one for you! The workbook assigned with the class provides a clear outline for what you should know and if you go to class, you don't need the textbook. More notes than what he tells you to take in the workbook aren't necessary at all.

Dr. Gordon did a great job teaching this class. There was an online version and an in-class version. He wrote the textbook that you use for the class, so you don't need to show up to get the information. I liked the class though because he would give you the information he thought was important and that would show up on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dont be fooled this class is easy to get by but you MUST not slack on the information its easy to bs it and cheat but dont do it. He allows you to do all homework until the deadline for 100% but if you're not studying the exams will destroy you and hurt your grade tremendously. This class is easy but not an easy A unless you put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is very straightforward. Read the book, do the workbook, take quiz( which you can take as many times as you need). It is online so you pretty much teach yourself from the workbook. However, I found the textbook extremely helpful, clear, and even laughed at times from the  voice in the writing.  Take this class!
He sets the class up so it's "easy" as long as you do the work. And he makes sure the work is relevant.  He keeps it as simple and well organized as possible.

Do NOT take stats from ANYONE ELSE but Mr Gordon! He has a workbook you fill out and get to bring into the tests with you( uh, hello easy A!)! Redo quizzes/homework assignments as many times as you want until deadline. This was the easiest A math class I've ever had AND I actually learned a ton!

I LOVED THIS CLASS. you bring your workbook to exams (meaning you'll pass every exam!) and assignments can be turned in three days late without points deducted. You take a quiz on every lecture, which are so easy and you have unlimited tries! exam questions also comes from some quizzes as well! easiest online class ever

The quizzes about those lectures are extremely specific and do not reflect what was taught in the lectures.

What should be an enjoyable and interesting class becomes difficult and tedious. Exams reference extremely specific information that plays no larger role to any learning objectives. Olsen uses outdated language and spends half the time justifying it. She seems quirky and nice irl, so I truly do feel bad leaving a bad review.

This is the first course that I have ever received below a B. Professor gives poor feedback and the amount of reading assignments for two weekly quizzes is a lot. Along with extensive articles for each weekly modules, the lectures are all long videos of her talking. She skips some slides that are important to know for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was really frustrating to have this professor sending canvas notifications every time you had not turned an assignment in, even if it was still a FULL day before the assignment was due! The lectures lacked info that was on the quizzes and made the topics lose its sense of purpose as to why we were learning it.

This professor was not what I expected. The quizzes do not reflect a lot of the info learned through her lectures and supplementary videos and her grading on those assignments are all over the place. I agree with others on this platform that her language was rather outdated and could be offensive at times for those who are passionate about CSBS.

Really interesting topic, underwhelming experience. Lectures are disorganized and information that ended up on the test was passed over frequently. Questions on the quizzes, midterms and final did not always have a clear answer, these made up the majority of her grading. Would often use outdated language when referring to indigenous groups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wonderful & worthwhile content of other cultures that makes you realize your privilege. The professor rants and gets off track a lot. No matter how hard I studied, questions were tricky and answers were not always concise or clear. Overall a good class but a very tough grader because of her wording. Recommend if you want to work very hard for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love love love loved Professor Olsen! Her class, Women Cross Culturally, was such a gem. There were lots of lectures, but most of them were fairly short (this was online) and really interesting, so I never felt like I was watching too much. Lots of readings, all of them short. I would 100% take again. (Watch lectures in 1.5x speed though).

Due to COVID-19 this class had to be moved online and she made the transition so easy. The class was wonderful and I loved her lectures. She shares her own personal experiences and the experiences of other women. I learned so much that applies to my own field of study and I'm not even an Anthropology major.

Great professor! Lots of lectures. If you do the reading and listen to the lecture you should do fine on the quizzes and tests. Very nice lady but does not allow late or makeup work so make sure to turn things in on time.

I was so excited for this Women Cross Culturally class and was extremely disappointed. She often taught with a "boomer" point of view, was really disorganized and never clear on what exactly she was trying to get across. Seemed disconnected from current events, issues and movements. It's easy to get an A but class but lectures are painful.
She is fun and very sarcastic. she can get off topic and rant but its okay. Read the books! if you have anthropology background it is a walk in the park
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought this class (Women Cross-Culturally) was a great class. The material we read and discussed was my favorite part. The lectures are good but not amazing, but if you read the articles and come prepared, you will really enjoy this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Class was intriguing but the wording on the exams were a bit confusing, when I attempted to discuss with the professor she gave me a lot of pushback.  I did all of the other assignments and I got an A on all of them but my tests dropped my grade to a C. Very frustrating experience. Also: do not debate her in class, she will not have it.

Easy and interesting class. The professor knows her stuff and offered different ideas without discrediting other points of view. It was funny because a lot of what she taught made people mad, but it was cool for me to get another explanation to a lot of these issues. Funny lady!

I was super disappointed in this professor. I had high hopes for this class but it fell just short of mediocre. The professor is all over the place, especially in her lectures. She frequently went on tangents about her home life or arguments with fellow co-workers. I feel like the subject had a lot of potential and I am just really disappointed.

Olsen is super scattered. She frequently bragged about students threatening to take her to the dean. Her grading is inconsistent. She frequently mocked students from previous classes. I dont think I will intentionally take her class again because I feel she cares more about telling us about her home life than talking about the subject.

She is a good teacher. She allows you to learn and understand without overloading you on homework or causing stress. Very easygoing, and the class discussions helped me to be able to process what I was learning. I know some say that they are off task; but only if you have a stereotypical view of the way learning is supposed to take place.

I absolutely love her as a teacher. She has real experience in anthropology. I've taken every class she offers. Her classes are so entertaining and she is hilarious. Honestly, i think she is the best teacher ever.

Olsen is genial and her class is not difficult. Her lectures are pretty bad; unorganized, unprepared, and difficult to follow. She interjects with a lot of personal commentary that can be humorous but can also be distracting and off topic. She also allows students to sound off and interrupt to an obnoxious degree. Her feedback on papers is useless.

I absolutly loved her and her class!  I thought she knew her stuff, even if she can be a bit scatter brained!  She doesn't sensor herself, and she didn't require us to either.  It made it much easier to have discussions that we all learned from instead of dry boring lectures!
She's very funny and knows her stuff!
Interesting Class, not too hard if you go to class regularly.

I didn't think the exams were very hard at all. She basically told us what was going to be on them, and it was only a matter of going over my notes and the readings. It's and interesting class and she's an awesome professor. Doesn't censor herself and I loved it.
Very funny, a very amusing teacher. She knows what she is talking about. Like the other person said though, her tests are hard and she says they are not.
No Comments
No Comments
She is very unorganized. And her tests are harder than she leads you to believe.

The class was great. i learned a lot about he subject, and started looking differently at why we act the way we act. only problem was i was a little unclear about what one of the assignments consisted of... other then that, fantastic!

She's definitely a bit scatterbrained, like the last person said...but I really like that about her. She's funny, and she makes going to class fun. I really liked her class...even if I didn't do that great in it.
She seems a little scatterbrained, but she is really interested in the topic she is teaching, she explains things in a mannor in which you will remember.  I really enjoy this class!!

Pretty sassy, definitely very well-respected. No late work !
He's very into experimental literature and the more incomprehensible your writing, the better. He calls everything a cliche, from using the phrase "bared teeth" to "furrowed brows". He's very inspiration in encouraging creativity, but be prepared for a lot of critique.

My favorite professor to date. He is so passionate about what he does and makes an effort to encourage and inspire students. I'm extremely grateful to have had the pleasure to take his class. I have no clue what grade I have in his class, however, but when you learn so much and enjoy so much, it really ceases to matter what mark you get.

You will for sure learn a lot, he is mostly great with two big caveats,  -Unclear what makes great vs good vs bad vs failing participation. This is actually nice in it encourages participation albeit sometimes paranoia induced participation.  Unusually hard, even for 5000 level class. In fact, it probably doomed me to poverty.
Beautiful hair, beautiful brain.

Lance is really something. I will admit, he's tough. But he makes the work totally worthwhile. The lectures were great and the community created in his class is really strong. I especially liked that we got the analytical papers out of the way first, and the rest of the semester was fun and creative. He'll be on sabbatical, but 2016-take it!

Best way to get an A in his class is to believe there is no such thing as words. The best grade I got in his class was a Presidential portrait painting with slander written all over it. Come on! a painting gets an A in an English class?  The guy gets off on anarchy. Never understood his grading. Unclear expectations. Hated his class!

His grading scale is tough but he's very worth it. Very smart, nice guy who's a pleasure to listen to. His lectures are fascinating and the reading is really interesting.  He's open minded and welcomes new ideas from students. If you put the effort in his class will blow your mind. Stickler on due dates so get started on work early.
Exuberant, helpful, enthusiastic, and of course brilliant and intelligent.  A fun class.

Om is a mathematics graduate student that teaches courses. He is interested in helping people learn and is willing to go over things with you.  His accent is very strong which can be very frustrating.  The course is very straight forward so if you keep up with the work you should do fine.

Om is a decent teacher. He only takes grades from quizzes and exams so homework is not mandatory, but will help you get a good grade. He has a thick accent, at times is hard to understand. Sit on the first row and you will be fine. Do homework, and do well on exams and you will do alright.

Om has a thick Indian accent that can be difficult to understand. However, he knows this which is why he's always willing to help his students after class and during office hours. Moreover he is a super nice guy with a heart of gold. He's pretty funny too. It's not an easy subject but I took MATH 1100 with Om and got an A. You can too.

Professor Ono was fantastic, cared about the material and the students. Any time I emailed him with a question, he always responded fast, his feedback was thoughtful and helpful, and his lectures were engaging. The only thing is that he takes a while to grade things, but other than that, he was great.

Professor Ono does not provide clear grading criteria, and then grades you harshly and take MONTHS to do so. He lectures almost directly from the textbook and rambles on for the entire class. He demands participation from students, but then disagrees with every point that they make. I would not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely condescending professor who acts like he is smarter than everyone. Does not have any respect for his students. Takes forever to grade and does not provide clear grading criteria. Wants you to memorize the textbook because he wrote it. Do not take this professors class.

Very condescending and patronizing professor who does not respect his students. Lectures consist of him rambling and talking nonsense. He writes exams/assignment descriptions badly, then takes months to grade them harshly. He once yelled at us about outdated grammatical rules. He has no set office hours, but forgets when you make an appointment.

Highly recommend him! He has lots of passion for what he teaches, and I found his lectures to be extremely interesting. The course wasn't too stressful, and as long as you read the textbook and view the slides, you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, Professor Ono is an interesting professor who cares about what he teaches. The class felt very doable! This class was taken during COVID on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Had some issues, and he helped me through them. Very understanding guy. Would recommend.
Luis is a young professor, so he can relate. He explains things pretty well. I learned a lot in the class. Taught me to research. He's got an open door policy even for an online class.

This class was interesting. Some assignments are the usual, but some assignments made me think about politics in the world. Helped with my writing. Is very easy on quizzes and other assignments, but tough for writing/essay assignments.
Tests, papers, and other assignments. Don't miss class or tests will be difficult. Test cover class discussions and some of the readings. Will let you rewrite papers if you talk to him.

The professor must've changed the class because I didn't have horrible experiences like all the other reviews. I took it online, and it was pretty easy. You have cases to review and write about every other week and then just weekly "self assesments" but they were just about the readings. Exams were a little tricky and theres 3 of them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Worst professor at the U.

chat GPT can do a better job at teaching those topics to be honest. Exams are extremely hard! with no idea on what question did i get it wrong because i am unable to view the answer of the exam. This is the worse class i ever taken there is no lecture that go through previous exam. study material were not helping in preparing the exam what so ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this professor. He is not the one that grades your writings, his TA does everything. The professor is very slow and extremely hard to listen to. His exams are really vague and just seem pointless. I would take this class with a different professor. I have talked to others and they loved this class from different professors.
Don't take this class with this professor!

Great teacher that genuinely cares, very organized. The quizzes could be submitted late and for full credit. There are a lot of case write-ups that heavily affect your grade, so be prepared to write and make sure to use the course concepts. Tests are difficult, but they are open book and he curves the course. Always replies quickly via email!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures seemed roughly thrown together and unorganized. He would often make students present for half an hour then immediately lectures on what was presented. This was among the most boring classes I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Perspective: my raw grade for this class was 67.2%, and I ended with an A-. Orie admits his class is difficult. However, he fails to realize that relying on "the curve" can only get you so far. Even thoroughly reading the textbook and attending all lectures will do little to help you. His quizzes/exams are overly convoluted and hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Orie Shelef is a terrible professor. Lectures consist of him reading directly from ppt slides. I learned more reading from the textbook than attending lectures. HIs study guide also comes directly from the textbook, so I don't see the point of having the study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He was one of the hardest professors I've ever had. You have to read the text book intensely and make sure to know everything from the chapters before every class bc there's no warning on quizzes. Also, on his quizzes and tests, the wording of the questions is very confusing so it makes it even harder. He's very intelligent but not a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Shelef is one of the best professors at the University of Utah.  I took his class in my last semester as an undergrad and he easily added more value to the class than any other professors I've had.  He has high expectations for his students but I would take any class that he is teaching without thinking about it.  Absolutely phenomenal.

I love Micheal! He is so helpful and his lectures are super clear and easy to understand. I hated math in high school, but I've taken 2 classes with Micheal now and I'm looking forward to a 3rd. Also I think he's so funny.

Prof Van Opstall is very nice, very accommodating, and is a great lecturer. His lectures are always filled with examples, he takes time to answer all questions, and he never runs out of time. He does everything effectively and succinctly. I'm a Computer Science student, and I did just fine in his class.

I'm convinced all of his bad reviews were written by the same person who was salty they got a bad grade. As long as you pay attention in class you should be able to do fine. He's super easy to get extra help from and very nice

Van Opstal is definitely an odd duck but he runs a pretty tight ship, knows his stuff, and teaches very simply. His class isn't terribly difficult if you have time to study and practice the problems. Homework assignments were absurdly long sometimes and didn't really help you prepare for the heavily weighted quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher. He is very good at explaining how to solve the problems. He is nice and straight to the point. I wish all my math classes could be taught by him. As long as you put work into this class, it wont be too bad. He allows notes on all the quizzes and exams which is very helpful. He listens to student feedback very well.
Michael is a great professor. He explains things so well and I genuinely have never had a better math teacher. If you show that you want to succeed in his class he will help you succeed.
he is super nice and understanding. Dad vibes for sure, if you need help just ask makes it easy to feel comfortable.

He will gives you homework on top of homework. He assigns a lot of assignment and he definitely not lenient on grading. He will find the smallest mistake you make to take points off. His exams are extremely hard so expect to study a lot before each exam. Hes definitely the worst professor Ive taken with. Try to avoid him if you can.

Dr. Van Opstal is a great instructor. He really cares about his students. If you come to class and do your homework, you can do well on the exams. There are a lot of really unfair reviews of this instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I really struggled with math in  high school and this class was a second chance for me. Professor Van Opstall is great a explaining everything in the class and leaves a lot of room for questions if you're lost and really wants to make sure that everyone understands the concepts. The class itself wasn't easy but he made it bearable.

Really made History of Mathematics come alive. The lectures walked through all the topics clearly. One of my favorite classes. His teaching style made all lecture material available online afterwards.

He is a pretty good teacher. He is really helpful in class, and answers any questions about the material. He expects a lot of effort from the students though. But you leave the class feeling like you really know the content. Overall, a pretty good professor.
He makes math classes easier to sit through; he's entertaining, patient, and passionate.
I really enjoy his class and find his guidelines for the class clear. When presenting the material he allows for questions, and is good at explaining.

He was very clear in our lectures, and assignments reflected what was presented in class. I'll admit he's not easy though. He definitely expects a heck of a lot from you, so he's probably not ideal for a lower-level, general math class. If you're a math major, don't be so scared. If you're looking for a general, probably try and avoid him?
his teaching is horrific
EXTREMELY rude
What Van Opstall does as a instructor is exactly what the ideal professor should NOT do!
Refuses to help let alone discuss contents of his class with students.
THE WORST, COMPLETELY UNHELPFUL!!! AVOID HIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!
Awful! Careless teaching, bad pacing and has a narcissistic attitude. This guy is will not help you!

Class consists of showing up and following Canvas instructions. The most difficult part of this class is midterms/finals. It's cumulative, so understand every lecture as u go. Pay attention to the canvas instructions, even if u think they're easy and will remember later. Midterm prt 2/2 was open book, final consisted of one large project.

Pretty easy class. The professor was very willing to help student. You just show up and follow the instructions on the canvas page most of the time. The midterm and final projects were challenging but not impossible, and I felt that they helped me understand what we were doing a lot better.
He is an awesome professor and uses canvas effectively. there is a group project towards the end of the semester. expect small quizzes and class participation. overall not a super difficult class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: perfect math teacher.

I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. This class shouldnt be boring but the professor makes it boring. The homework and test are graded very strictly. If you miss any steps on your homework or test youll lose points on it.
Ive never felt like I learned so much in a math course ever. This was the best experience Ive ever had and I highly recommend.

I adore Ornella. She genuinely wants to see students succeed. Her lecture notes were incredibly helpful, and her exams were very fair. She was frequently accessible outside of class. She's so patient, kind, and sincere. ODE's wasn't an easy course, but she does a great job explaining the concepts. A real gem.

This is by far the toughest 2 credit hour course I have ever taken. Expect to put in some serious work. I had to put in more work than most of my other 3-4 credit hour courses.. The homework was very long and graded very strictly and so were the tests. She was super helpful during office hours however. I did learn a lot though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lectures are very fast paced, although this is more because of the material that is required to be covered in class. The professor is very eager to help with any questions you may have. I would definitely recommend taking this course from her compared to any of the other 3150 professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is a lot to cover, so it moves quickly. If you skip class, this isn't the course for you. That said, Dr. Mattei is fantastic. I love her grading and teaching style. She's tough, but delves more into the math and derives equations to really help you understand the topic. She's also always very willing to answer any question.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite math instructors I've ever had, and would take a course from her again in a heartbeat. She was entertaining enough to keep me interested, and was able to take the time to explain difficult subjects for every student in the class. She wants to see you succeed and pass the class.

Since this class was online, I didn't have much opportunity to interact with Orhan. The class itself was great, the notes are all you need to do the assignments. The tests are almost exactly the same as the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Good teacher who offers extra credit by class attendance. She really knows her stuff but is often quite confusing during lectures. I learned mostly form online homework assignments.

Orhan is a solid professor.  She is from another country so sometimes it is a little hard to understand what she is saying and the point she is trying to get across.  You get extra credit for attendance so make sure you attend if you want extra points.  Tests are literally identical to Hw.  If you do well on hw, expect an "A" on the tests (& final)
Very enthusiastic about Economics. The course itself is really easy, and Prof. Orhan is willing to answer any questions and help students in any way. Very helpful, easy course.

Professor Orhan does her very best to help you understand the material given in class.  She has a very thick accent so she can be hard to understand sometimes.  She gives plenty of time for tests and assignments to be completed.  Her final was super easy and based on basic concepts we had learned throughout the semester.

She went over concepts again and again, so if you don't understand, you will. And if you do, you're bored. The homework and tests are online and not super hard (but the tests have a time constraint). Know the homework, and you'll know the test. There's a final that she gave a study guide for. Go to class and she'll curve your score up :)
Awesome teacher. A few easy papers, a couple of presentations. Too bad this is her last semester at the U.

Probably one of the best teachers I've ever had.  Very energetic and entertaining.  I learned alot in this class. In MGT 3810 she has random outlines that are due from the textbook.  Also has you do a couple presentations/interviews.
Learned alot in an otherwise boring class
She was an excellent professor. Very energetic and engaging. The material could be boring at times but she made it fun to learn. I would recommend to take this class.
Very fun teacher. If you come to class prepared, you will get a lot out of it.

Jackie knows her stuff, and leads very engaging discussions. Be ready for heavy weekly reading assignments, and frequent writing assignments. She does not pull punches in her feedback of your poetry/essays, but her criticism is well-thought out and fair, and she is willing to work with you if you are struggling. Difficult, but rewards effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Jackie is smart, passionate, and has a good sense of humor. This course was focused on analyzing Emily Dickinson's work (although the author changes with each semester). We read several poems per class and took pop quizzes. Jackie isn't too harsh of a grader, is happy to work with you, and offers great feedback. I think most of us did very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jackie is eccentric and passionate. The entire course was discussion based-- attendance mandatory. She didn't take role, but attending class in important because she doesn't allow students to write on things discussed in class. 3 papers in total and an annotated bibliography with quizzes on the reading everyday. Harsh grader but loved every minute

Jackie has a funny personality, but what others say is true. She's super critical and wants you to interpret poetry exactly like she does. It's not that bad, and she gives you so much opportunity to get help and succeed in the way she thinks you should. But by the middle of the semester, I didn't feel like I was learning so much as getting through.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take any classes from Jackie. As a person, she's pretty cool. But as a professor, I've never met someone more rude and incompetent in my 5 years of university. Don't expect a good grade if your opinion differs from hers. She was dismissive of students' thoughts and was sometimes blatantly mean. Avoid the anxiety and get a different prof.

Never have I been so discouraged from sharing my interpretation of what we're reading in an English class. Grades you based on whether your initial reading of the text was the same as hers. Incredibly nitpicky about trivia about the text and will tell you you "didn't read carefully enough" if you don't remember the name of a side character. AVOID!

Went very slow and made sure everyone in the class knew the material well. He offered a lot of extra credit work throughout the semester, and had many opportunities to get extra tutoring. There was homework after each class, and a quiz every 3 class, all of which were quite easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is nice but his teaching style seemed that he just wanted everyone to learn basically outside the class and have questions for the class instead of him really explaining and waiting for his students to really understand the math problems.

Life changing professor, for the worst.

I was very adamant and trying to speak with him about my situation and he blew me off. Unfortunately I will be unenrolling from the U, and I think things could have been differently had been willing to talk with me, but that did not seem to be an option on his part.

if you want a good grade in math, do not take this class from this professor. I never once felt like I learned anything even tho I did the homework. His teachings really don't make sense at all and I felt insecure about asking questions the whole time. Save yourself and find a better professor.

take this class if you want to fail. attending class is mandatory yet u learn nothing. grade only based on test that he never teaches. when i was grieving due to family member passing he didnt care and made me fail the class. even after getting an obituary and talking w/ the dean he wouldnt let me do the final exam. homework doesnt relate to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love his class, he is always helpful. If I had questions, he would make sure I understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hands down the most I have ever struggled in a class. You can't understand him. He doesn't know how to teach 150+ students at one time. It was very hard to ask questions because he didn't understand what students were asking. Homework was lots of problems but only grades on 3 and didn't know which 3. Isn't very understanding.

He is very difficult to understand during lecture, not due to his accent, but just because he is generally terrible at explaining the content. The homework is generally far more difficult that what he does in class and often not related, and he grades it extremely hard. Most of your score in the class will be the difficult tests and homework
Brushes over super important details which make the lectures meaningless. Think it's his first year so hopefully he fixes it but jesus, that was awful

He is easily one of the hardest professors I have ever had solely due to what seems to be inexperience. Attendance was a complete waste of time as the material he focused on in class was vague, and rarely present in the lab portion and exams. Many point-heavy topics were brushed over in lecture and HW was insanely long (and due on test days).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hands down the worst professor I've ever had. He has no clue how to teach in a classroom setting. He is impossible to understand and he won't explain how to do things. His tests are insane and you only have 50 min to do them. Also, he assigns a ton of homework which he only really gives credit for 3 random problems, but he won't tell you which.

This class is difficult but the lectures and slides do help a lot! The quizzes are fairly easy but the tests are more difficult. I think if economics is something that interests you this class would be easier to understand but if not then it could be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Taught by Rudi Von Arnim for the most part who is great, but Daniel put in a few lectures which actually helped a lot. Quizzes are based almost entirely off of the readings which are pretty ok to read, but it is on international trade theory, so there is only so much fun that can be had. Overall a really understanding guy and very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Daniel understands the content he is lecturing and is patient when explaining to make sure everyone understands. He incentivizes the student to engage in class providing space to answer questions about the content. Be prepared to read. Quizzes are easy, but exams are a bit difficult. You can reach him outside class and schedule office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: For context I use CAD for work, but i learned a few new things. she is a very knowledgeable and helpful teacher and will help you learn civil 3d. assignments are easy, as long as you participate and pay attention you will pass

Extra Credit was offered on every exam, and it was fairly easy to get all of it. There was weekly homework assignments that were not too long. She tries to prepare you well for the exam by making study guides that are very similar to the exams.

Gaby taught AutoCAD and made it really easy to learn. She walks around the class to help with homework, and was great at helping when stuck. Even when we went online (bc of COVID), she made thorough homework guides, and responded very quickly when I needed help. Random grades for attendance, and midterms were basically homework. Excellent professor
Great prof, hard material but he made it easier to understand through lectures.

hard to communicate.

A great professor the bad rates and comments are very false. Professor Park was an amusing and interesting lecturer. He was very straightforward we only had four tests, one very easy group project, and no homework. Studying and using the review TA videos will make the tests easy.

Always looked forward to class. The class would actually be fully entertaining and interesting. His lectures were a solid 10/10. He has an amazing personality and is super cool. There are four exams that are VERY simple if you apply yourself and literally just watch the review vids. The group project is very doable. Would definitely take again.
4 exams, no homework, no real life examples, just definitions and lectures. Exams easy if study

I honestly don't think Joowon deserves the score he has here. I've loved taking my class from him, he did a great job at covering material and getting students ready for exams. Joowoon Park is one of the most uninspiring and boring professors I've ever had. He seems to think this class is a joke and doesn't take it seriously at all while expecting all his students to. Very childish professor. He doesn't care about his students and doesn't allow questions in class. Don't let positive reviews get your hopes up he's a very rude and arrogant professor.

Professor Park was clear, concise, straight to the point. I think that's why a lot of people have issues with him. However, if you are able to take direction, you will do great in the class. He extended so many quizzes for us because of stress from other classes and discounted a lot of the unimportant course material. Its a great entry-level class.

Not allowed to ask questions in class. Told to hold them until the end but if you do, he looks at you like you didn't even pay attention and is very rude. Professor Park has been an amazing professor this semester! reviews.comment: Use an AI proofreader for the 500+ page pdfs. Get a group EARLY. Pray for a responsive group too. Quizzes can be a bit misleading, but doing it /w the group is fairly easy. Do not take this professor. Treats his 1000 level class like its a graduate level glass with his grading. He wants to be more important, and takes it out on his students. Grades absurdly harshly.

Professor Phillips is one of my favorite professors. If you actually watch the lectures and read the unit materials, his quizzes aren't very difficult. Mid-term and Final are group essays that are pretty easy if you find a group early in the semester. Really cool guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class! Quizzes are open book, open web—use anything. Midterms are just essays, and if you work in a group, they're quick and easy. One key tip: join a group early in the semester! It's allowed, and once groups fill up, finding partners gets tough.

Overly-long lectures, too many videos, not formatted well for online, quizzes are unnecessarily difficult, and not a lot of options to get a good grade. I'm a 30 year old man with a full-time job, needed it for a gen-ed requirement and it just feels like he's trying to dunk on freshmen instead of making this class accessible. Lame.

I took this gen ed because I am an econ major, but it hardly related to my studies. There is no textbook, but two long books that are 784 and 544 pages. reviews.comment: Love this guy and his bolo tie!

reviews.comment: Taken 3 courses by him. Good professor overall pretty hard grader for undergraduate students but very lax for graduate students

Lots of reading but it's not too difficult because for the midterm and final you work in groups and those account for most of the grade. Lectures can be very long too so if you have poor time management it's smart to be able to split those into multiple days.

Make sure to take notes on the lectures and videos of the week, you'll need them for the quizzes. The quizzes are challenging, they are not easy. The project questions are also very challenging and he also gives bonus points if you decide to do the projects as a group so you can take advantage of that. I would recommend this instructor.

This is an ok class. You can work in groups for quizzes and the written midterm and final for extra credit. Be ready to save around 2.5+ hours a week to watch all of his videos not including the reading. The grading for the written exams are pretty harsh, but if you get yourself a good group you can get a good score on top of your extra credit.

I took econ1740 online, the class was okay, very boring topics. Lots of readings, weekly quizzes. You can do the midterm and final with a group (you get bonus points). The professor seemed nice though!

Boring. Way too much reading paired up with at least 2 hours of lectures and other videos and midterm and final were essays that seemed to be graded by PAs. there is no extra credit or late work accepted. Grade scale is odd so unless you get 100 on everything, you wont know your grade until they adjust it. Quizzes were hard and tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: At first, I was looking forward to this class. I'm a finance major & I actually find this very interesting. You might as well, but do not consider this class at all if you have a job. This class may be easy for those who have the time, but for those who work full time (like me), it's impossible. Too much reading, very hard quizzes. Be very careful.

He does everything possible for everyone to get an A. Grades rely mostly on midterm and final, but they are essays that, if done in a group, give 2 points extra credit. Everything is graded out of 14 points; anything higher than 12 is an A. There are lots of videos to watch, but only a weekly quiz for the primary assignments.

He is a great professor! My only advice is being willing to communicate with him! He wants to help you succeed and do good! Keep on top of the work and you will be fine! If you are a procrastinator--you will drown.

BEWARE, your grade is 90% for the final/midterm and 10% on quizzes. The quizzes are absurdly difficult sometimes for a gen ed course. There were so many announcements with walls of words about confusing grading scales and rubrics.

Totally choose to take the quizzes at the beginning of the semester, they pad your grade lots and when you work with a group, youre bound to get a good score. You can figure out the answers with the internet if you didnt read the assignments before the quiz. The papers were easy with a group

I had Professor Philips for 2 classes Econ 5120 and Econ 5470. SO worth it! He is the kind of professor who expects you to write good papers, but wow do you learn a lot. Classes feel like hes just telling stories, but they all build on one another to teach the material in a memorable way. His classes inspired me to want to do undergrad research.

Other than that, great class and teacher.

He then made his own video (usually 30-40min) to summarize and explain everything. It was a very enjoyable class. Easy to get a B, but a little tough to get an A.

This is the best professor I have ever met. He is pro and patient, caring much about students. And he is easily to get in touch with and he also teach some methods of thinking and experience of his life to students.

If you removed every in-person lecture from this class virtually nothing would effectively change. Basically just read through the slides when teaching the material. If you actually have any will to live do not take this class, you'll question this universities ability to hire competent people who actually made it past 5th grade math. If there was a category to select awful I would have put that down.

I mean it's an easy A but fair warning it's the most boring class I've ever been in.. doesn't make a connection with you and talks like a robot! I think I've learned more from the TA's the one time he wasn't there then when he has been the whole year! Overall stay away if you want a good teacher
He is the most monotoned person ever.

This professor has horrible lectures and the class is unable to follow what he's saying. He does not slow down or give clear instructions. The only way to be successful is through the TA's. His online resources suck and assignments are nearly impossible to complete correctly.

He loves the subject, but he was not meant to teach that class. He always goes fast during his lectures, so there is not point in taking notes. Definitely try to get this class with other professors.
Incredibly boring class, professor just reads lecture slides word for word in a monotone voice. Also makes attendance mandatory. Class is still easy but would not recommend

Ted is a good teacher. I had his class online, sometimes it's hard to pay attention to the whole 80 min class. He was good at explaining excel and always went back and answered questions if students had any. Overall he was a good teacher, I would recommend taking 2020 from him.
He is an NPC

Ted Peterson should be avoided AT ALL COSTS. He lectures too fast and when you ask him to repeat what he said or did again, he does it even faster. This professor was excruciatingly boring. It's going to require skill, perseverance, and determination to make it throughout a class without succumbing to sleep. The assignments assigned are ridiculous. It's not a difficult class, but when exams count for 40 percent of your grade, it's difficult to stay motivated with busy work that barely counts.

i took this class online over the summer, and it was not too bad at all. i barely watched the lectures and would just google something if i did not know how to do it. i did hear that if you have him in person or during a regular semester, it is different and he is not the best though.
Professor Peterson was ok. The class is centerd around the use of Excel. His lectures moved fast, but he was willing to repeat some parts if you asked. The homework and exams were generally easy.

Easy class, but very uninteresting. Professor Peterson cares about the material but doesn't seem too enthused about teaching, and it was a struggle to stay awake in class. It's a mandatory class so it's not like it really matters.

Peterson was actually a good teacher, he has a monotone voice that put me to sleep. Lots of homework however none of it was really hard, just time consuming. I feel like he knew what he was teaching but just read off of the PowerPoint the entire time. When he would work on Excel, he would move super fast and when we would ask him to do it again he would move equally as fast. This made it hard to keep up with his excel stuff. His tests were very easy and open note which was very nice.
Ted is a great professor. He does go fast, but if you ask him to go over it again he is more than happy to. The Exams are easy and are completely open notes which is nice!

He could not teach to save his life. Stood there with his monotone voice and read the presentation. Went so fast through excel.
