Goes way too fast and explains things horribly.  Impossible to keep up.  Every time I asked him a question he just said "well you did it wrong". obviously bro thats why I am asking for help.  Overall the worst professor I've ever had to deal with.

Very excellent professor! His lectures are quite fruitful. Since he is in the information systems department, his lectures regarding BA and IS are quite interesting. His course had made me determined to major in IS. He shows enormous patience while teaching Excel.

Be prepared to teach yourself and waste hours outside of class doing so. If you work full time this class will call demand you call out if you are not a master at Excel. The professor moves too fast and doesn't teach you anything, however lectures are mandated. The professor is a good guy but an awful teacher.

I was nervous to take his class because of the reviews on here, but now that the semester's over the class really wasn't bad at all. I feel like there isn't enough time in class to cover all the material that people want, but honestly the stuff on Canvas is more than enough for what isn't covered. Exams are a breeze if you follow the study guide.

Pretty average professor, nothing major stands out. But he does go over excel formulas really quickly. Pretty much all of the homework you can follow along with the examples and get an A. The lectures can be pretty boring but if you stop paying attention you'll be completely lost.

This class was horrible. The lectures are mainly used to go over Excel formulas but he goes WAY to fast and even when you ask him to go over it again, slower he goes the same pace. Hard to keep up in class during excel and a majority of the class usually ends up doing something else on their computers. Overall hard class when it goes to Excel.

You should know that the elements of this class (lectures, homework, and tests) had nothing to do with each other and many of the things you were graded you had to teach yourself, as they were not even slightly covered in lecture. Professor Peterson was anything but informative or helpful, and treated teaching this class like a chore.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was horrible and boring. The professor doesn't teach so much as he reads through someone else's lecture slides. He goes through everything quickly and when asked questions, he does it even faster. The assignments hardly related to the lecture and are busy work. The tests are hard and confusing and the content isn't discussed in class.

This bloke doesn't explain any of the Excel stuff in a good way-he speeds through it and when asked to explain again he goes through it FASTER!! He gives barely any time to do the final and half the stuff covered on the final he never talks about in class. This foo is not a good teacher if I had more characters I would write a whole essay on him.

First off, you learn almost nothing related to your homework in lectures. He moves much to quickly and does not know how to explain things. Next, the final. The first 20 questions of the 40 question test was not covered in class or in readings. We were given excel workbooks we had to finish for the test, and were not given enough time to finish...

Professor Peterson was a great professor. I had no desire to learn about information systems and he made me enjoy the class. The homework videos are super helpful and honestly I didnt go to class for like 2 months and I got an B+.

Honestly. I like and dislike his lectures. I like his understanding of students and I believe he tries to really teach us and not destroy our lives with unrealistic expectations. I wish he had a little bit more fire in class but he's easily understandable and doesn't frustrate me as a learner.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a best professor for sure, you can get A easily if you do all of assignments and take quizzes. Final and midterm questions are not difficult.

Overall, Professor Peterson cares and genuinely wants you to pass and learn. He makes sure everyone understands during each lecture and answers all questions, even over Zoom. He tries to make class more exiting with occasional Kahoots but sometimes his monotonous way of speaking gets tiring.

Sorry Ted, but this class was horrible. I took stats with him once a week for three hours and it sucked. He has such a monotone voice and goes through slides so fast you could never keep up. By the end of the semester no one showed up to class unless there was a exam. It's easier to just go through the slides and use the book to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He teaches like he doesn't know what he's talking about. Half of my notes taken in class say "see slides/read book" because he goes through a slide in 10 seconds before he moves on. He also heavily emphasizes utilizing excel, but rushes through all the formulas used without writing them out beforehand. If you fall behind, just quit listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have taken two classes from Ted and just signed up for a third. His way of teaching is clear and anytime you email him he will respond quickly. He goes through things fairly quickly, but does multiple sample problems and makes sure that there are no questions before he moves on to the next topic. He really cares about you learning and succeeding.

Ted was a very nice guy, but it was difficult to take this class from him. It wasnt obvious that he knew what he was talking about, but he regularly made mistakes while lecturing and had trouble conveying the material to us students. By the end of class, only about 1/3 of the class regularly showed up because we were all teaching ourselves anyway.
I enjoyed the subject matter, which made the class much more manageable. Ted is very intelligent and nice, however, the way he taught the material wasn't working for me, so expect to self-study.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You will have a total of 100 points on your grade in this class so know that there is no margin for error. The tests are disorganized, many times they contain errors that he corrects during the actual test, and they are extremely difficult. This class is not "technically" quantitative intensive but definitely should be listed as such.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class was centered around self-learning. There was a weekly homework and quiz assignment. (Near the end there was 2 per week) The class is split into halves. The first half consists of Connect readings, and the other half is Excel/Access. If you commit to reading, taking good notes, and studying for the quizzes, it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: By far the worst & least forgiving (not always bad, but in this case yes) professor I've ever had. Quizzes and projects must be turned in every week and if you miss something your screwed. The course is online so of course, you'd expect technical difficulties. Ted, however, doesn't allow any makeup work if something goes wrong with canvas... cuck..

Ted is a good professor who has a broad knowledge amongst many business topics. This class was well structured with clear expectations upfront. Be ready to practice outside of class for the tests and be willing to participate in a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ted was very responsive to emails, made time after class to answer my questions and answered my phone calls over the weekend. Course requirements were laid out on the syllabus very clearly. Brought in guest speakers which were an added bonus.

Most horrible professor I have ever had in my entire education (preschool-college). Lectures are excruciating to sit through- speaks in a completely monotone voice, reads directly from powerpoints, and the introduction to what will be discussed during class takes up half the class time. Very rude in email and one-on-one & no grading criteria given

Took the class online. Had one assignment to do every week, due on Saturday. For the first and last part of the class it was a reading and then a quiz, which were both very easy to do. In the middle we worked on projects with excel and access. I budgeted an hour a week to the class and got a 97%. If you do the work, you'll get an A.

Took the class online, was skeptical at first but ended up with a very high A. Do the work and get an A. Simple as that. Can't comment much on the professor, but seemed like a cool guy. Some of the book chapters were fairly interesting as well.

Ted is a great professor for this class. It's not a walk in the park but it's much easier than I anticipated. I had it over the summer and it was once a week for 3 and a half hours. We didn't go the whole time and often got out an hour earlier. Ted is very direct and follows his syllabus very well. 3 tests and 3 homeworks. 1 page of notes for exams

Lectures were kind of bland, but I learned quite a bit. He leaned heavily on his TAs, which made for a confusing time when they were unorganized and unclear. But deadlines were flexible and he was generally pretty understanding.

This was an intro class so he didn't assign much homework! :) The lectures were entertaining, and they were also mandatory. That being said, I feel like most of the teaching in this class was really done by the TA in the lab period, and he often had to pick up the slack because the the instructor often struggled to stay organized and on schedule.

His way or no way, an insanely tough grader, you'll never reach him outside of class, and will literally nit pick Every. Thing. You. Do-- This man really made me want to lay in an open field and reconnect with the Earth. Like genuinely, I have never been more spiritually exhausted by someone who contributes absolutely nothing to the film industry.

Steven was a fine professor. he only taught the lecture portions and a lot of the information seemed very standard and baseline. Not that it isn't important you just might be familiar with a lot of the information already. The TAs teach the actual production and feedback section, and my TA gave very specific and subpar feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were nice, but kinda bland. Obviously knowledgeable but a bit self-reverent and felt little respect for undergraduate students specifically. Course isnt properly spread out, leaving a lot of crunch for projects at the end of the semester; however, very flexible in submission (due date is never really the due date)

I took 3630 from Steve and really enjoyed it but wouldn't recommend it to anyone who doesn't want to pull all-nighters animating. The lectures were interesting and everything except the projects were pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Steve is a very poor professor.
He didn't have start our film assignments until over half way through the semester. He expected us to finish three film assignments within that timeframe plus presenting them in class. He is very nitpicky with everything, docking points for the smallest of things.
He used my videos without my permission and refused to take them down.

Steven is a very nice guy and obviously cares a lot about what he does. However, his grading system and feedback is very black and white, it's either what he wants or it doesn't work. Animations are VERY labor intensive, especially near the end. Be prepared to spend 5-10 hours a week on work with little to no time in class.
The first part of this class is very slow, but once you start making films it gets a lot more fun and engaging.

Steven is honestly just a really goofy guy (you'll know when/if you take him what I mean). I will say, when making your films, it's kinda either his way or no way-- as in he will NOT hear you out if he disagrees with you. That said, it's a very easy class and if you struggle with attending class, it's not MANDATORY but there is an attendance grade
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, likes to have longer classes. Be aware that he has lots to talk about, so keep yourself busy but not distracted in class. He is quality driven not very stressed on time.

Gave some really amazing lectures that made it apparent that he's truly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. My only warning is that he isn't very receptive over email or Canvas and it's better to go to him directly in class if you have a concern.

He's a great professor but beware of the 3 - 5 hour long lectures!!! There are also hidden episodes within the lectures so skipping the lectures is a big no-no but I usually put it on 2.5x speed to bring the lecture time down from 5 hours to 2 hours or so. The journals are part of the grade but your essays count for the majority so don't mess up!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Project intensive class with a final test (6 major projects, 6 smaller ones, 4 critiques of everyone's projects, 1 final test- 20% of grade). Very overwhelming and time-consuming. Not very flexible with covid. Arbitrary grading system. Seems to care more about the camera/framing over the quality of the animation itself. Never got my animations back

Condescending professor, not trying to be rude, but he wanted the class to buy his own textbook even though his PowerPoints were summaries of the material. He couldn't use his time well, it was a 4 hour class that met twice a week and we got so behind in the curriculum. He didn't post his PowerPoints or offer any more material for students.

By far the best professor I have ever had. In addition to having a laid-back personality and great sense of humor, he also has amazing taste in music, film, and all associated subjects. He is extremely knowledgable when it comes to his profession. Sitting in class from six to ten every week was more than worth my time.

Nice guy, good class. I learned a lot. Since this was a overview of production I wish he would have gone over all the types of sound more as well as some more basic must-know editing tips.  I don't feel like there's enough reason for me to take the editing or sound classes, but there was just enough left out of this class that leaves me in-between.

Loved his class! He made the lectures fun and interesting. Really flexible on due dates and really helpful on assignments. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I never wanted to skip! Highlight of my day was his class!

So let me make one thing clear. Steve is an awesome guy. However, I took a sound for film class and if you have never had any experience with programs like Adobe Premier, final cut, or have no experience with sound equipment, you will most likely have a hard time in class, like I did. Make sure you're ready to do about 5 projects.

Steve is awesome. No due dates, gives you all of the questions on the midterm and final a week before you take them. Very knowledgeable and a lot of fun. But don't buy the textbook, you never once use it or even reference it.

If you are able to take a class with Phillip take it. He is such a caring professor but you also will learn so much with his classes. Very understanding professor, so it was good to balance other classes while taking his class.

If you get the change to take one of Singer's classes, you definitely should. He is passionate, knowledgable, and SO NICE. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you show up, he always has a great lecture. He is so understanding when it comes to deadlines and grading and clearly cares so much about his students.
Great professor. I learned a lot without the burden of excessive busywork.
Phil is a chiller fr! His 3320 class is very straightforward and graded easily. However, I feel like I learned a lot of good things:)

Great guy. Has real world experience in this field and teaches it incredibly well. Very understanding and will work with you to help you learn, no matter what you need help with. Very respectful of student mental health. The papers are not easy, but they are fun and flexible. I barely went to class but learned a lot when I did and still got an A

Hands down the best professor I have had in my four years of college. Very knowledgeable, accessible outside of class, genuinely cares about your wellbeing. Interesting lectures. He spent our entire last class speaking about how to set our lives up for success. Truly a wholesome dude. Register for his class early because it fills up fast.

One of the VERY BEST professors I've ever had. Took special interest in me and my projects. Very obviously cares greatly for his students' mental health and well being and gives extra time on projects if needed. Graded on 5 projects that are connected and based on your choice of topic. First half of semester lectures set up second half projects.

Prof Singer is extremely understanding, and the rating that called him a wholesome dude is so accurate. He cares about his students deeply. The course material wasn't the most interesting, but I didn't mind the class. Lectures were kinda boring. But he's super chill, and I learned quite a bit.

Professor Singer is a great professor. While the class is fairly dense, he's easy to learn from and provides good feedback. He's very understanding about mental health issues as well which makes him all the better. Overall he's just a wholesome dude and I would highly recommend his class.

Avoid him if you can, but it's not the end of the world. I had a really hard time understanding what he was trying to convey. He couldn't really explain things in plain english even with students asking questions to clarify.

He's a nice enough guy but just can't explain the material in any understandable way. He can't really answer questions students ask him either. It feels like he's making it up as he goes. He tries to find any excuse to make you lose points, he wants you to fail. I would avoid him if possible but it's not unbearable.

One of the most valuable classes I've ever taken. He covers so much useful stuff, and his posted notes are super helpful. However, his lectures are really hard to follow. He uses a lot of mathematical notation, his handwriting is bad, and he didn't pause to let us wrap our heads around things or give plain-English explanations often enough.
The worst professor ever

Jeff Philips seems to be loved by everyone in the department and for good reason. So far I have only had a 1-credit seminar class with him but I can still safely say that reputation is earned. His passion and communication skills are stellar enough to make him stand out among the faculty. No idea how he is as a grader, though

Class was a high level overview of many topics. Lectures, notes, textbook are very mathematically dense, which helps give practice for reading papers. But also can be very difficult at times.Tests and hw are more straightforward however, and were not too difficult in the end. Group project is worth 40% of grade though!

He is a very chill person, however his lectures can be confusing and can be hard to follow. However, he responds to every student's discussion question when they need help without fail, and very quickly too.

The lectures are truly horrible for the most part and so is his handwriting as you cannot understand anything, his book is a little better but not good in general as there are no labels for anything, so you basically have to figure out everything by yourself. I learnt more from ChatGpt explaining me the same concepts than his entire semester.

Not a good professor I would say, he is a nice chill person but the way he teaches is horrible, makes simple things overcomplicated and not a single proper example used by him in his course, the homeworks are abstract and take some time. The exams are easy enough but because of his way of teaching, it is hard to understand anything.

I technically didn't even take his class, I just want to say thank you to professor Phillips for leaving his lecture recordings from last year available on Youtube; he was able to actually teach me probability and statistics while Ross Whitaker could not.

Unclear and will string you along. Its good he understands the material, but can't get the message across. Only way to please this guy is you basically have to discover time travel and more. Don't waste your time on this guy. I doubt he has ever held a job outside of being a professor. No real world experience at all.

He used the R program to explain a lot of stats, which to me was not helpful. Honestly, his lectures were confusing and didn't often feel worth going to. However, he is a fair grader, doesn't assign too much work, and has very good lecture notes that he posts outside of class. He also has lots of ways to view the lectures.

I think he goes a little to quick on the important concepts, and sort of assumes a lot of you. It's hard to gauge the difficulty, as the questions would either be absurdly easy or absurdly difficult. He is, however, a very nice guy. He clearly is trying his best, and I feel as though he will become a better professor as time goes by.
He provided many ways to succeed. The online notes were comprehensive and easy to understand. He was also caring and very reasonable.
He is so "good"! a very "smart" guy!

Once I asked him a question, he just said "I don't know if you are familiar with the concept but..." that he showed off something that he did not teach and I completely have no idea what he was talking about. His course is simply a nonsenes.

Lectures are incredibly high level and went over my head basically every time, I also struggled to relate the lectures to the homework. Didn't post solutions to the homework which made it incredibly hard to study, they said that to get solutions go to help hours but sometimes those aren't accessible.

The lectures were quite rambly and I didn't know at what points during the lecture did he want us to learn specific things. His homeworks are incredibly confusing and many connections are expected to be made from the confusing lectures to solve the hw problems.

Jeff is a really nice guy and he tries to help the students. But his lecture is hard to understand. This class itself is easy. Since there r a lot misunderstanding going on with the homework, and the professor/TAs seem prefer in-person office hours, it is hard to get a quick response on hw clarifications. More difficult than it should.
I spend more time trying to understand what the questions are asking in the homework than doing the homework problems themselves

I have been confused on homework many times as well as others many other students in the class. Jeff expects his students to show their works on homeworks while his works to the students being untidy, unclear and very confusing.

Jeff is a decent guy. He makes easy concept difficult and explains things in a confusing way, the homework is very confusing when I found some similar examples on khan academy about the same concept in the homework. If you want to succeed in his class, you should find resources outside of the class or online (Youtube)

The content is quite difficult, but Jeff makes it as digestible as possible in lectures. HW assignments are fantastic at guiding you to mastery of the concepts. He wrote the (VERY USEFUL) textbook and gives students a free PDF (based). Quizzes/exams are fairly easy if you put in the time on the HWs, and you are allowed a generous amount of notes.

Pretty nice guy. He really knows the subject. Lectures are hard to understand at times because the material will go over your head if you aren't seasoned in linear algebra and stats. Hand writing can be hard to read at times, so I recommend sitting in front of the classroom. Make sure you keep up with the homework and prep for the quizzes.

HW and Quizzes map directly to the lectures, lectures map directly to the book, and Professor Phillips wrote the book.  Following lectures carefully gives an incredible intuition on all computations that are done and set you up for success in the HW and Quizzes.  Recorded/Zoom lectures, open note quizzes, awesome class.

Among the most organized classes I've been in. Not only was felxible with in-person/online by having lectures recorded and attendance not mandatory, but had lecutres live-streamed on YouTube, Zoom, and VODs saved to YouTube.

Jeff is a ridiculously smart and nice guy, who clearly knows the material inside out. However, the level of mathematical literacy Jeff expects from his students is very high. If you are comfortable with discrete, statistics, and perhaps even analysis, then this class is doable. If not, expect to put in a significant amount of time into this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but I have never had such basic concepts presented in such confusing ways. His lectures only complicate his already messy and confusing textbook. This class would probably be fine if we had better resources. I don't recommend his class unless you want to spend all your time Youtubing these concepts on your own.

Jeff is a very knowledgeable guy. The best part about him is that he will listen to ideas which may relate to extra-extra-cirricular activities. His lectures often go over the top of your head, but Data Science is supposed to be like that. The statistical knowledge presented in this class shows theory is very important in Data Science.
He is an amazing professor and a brilliant guide. His lecture notes are wonderful. The Data Mining class was super interesting.  He is also an amazing mentor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a very open and nice professor. He never hesitates to answer questions and always encouraged us to reach out. Despite this, the class's rapid pace and his tangents relating to proving mathematical concepts with theory often confused a lot of people. Overall a great professor and an alright class.
Some elements were taught in a confusing way, but besides that, he was an excellent teacher who was always open to questions and his office hours were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved the way he teaches. His exam grading is fair and encouraging, and he is always open to feedback and criticism. I would take every math course with him if it were possible.

Lots of homework every week. Most of it was stuff not covered in class. His lectures are long but mostly informative. Other Calc 1 professors allow note cards for exams and he doesn't so just keep that in mind. Overall pretty chill but could be better.

Explained concepts in THE MOST confusing way. Lots of homework every week, sometimes on material he never covered in class. He does allow for unlimited retakes on homework assignments though. Check-ins every day and a quiz once a week. (No retakes, no late submissions on them).

Super lenient on grades, curves test questions really mercifully, homework questions are take it till you make it, labs are mostly participation, drops the lowest grades in every category (including a midterm if you do better on the final). Everything is explained very simply, so it's a good class to take if you suck at math

I took her for 3090, computing ethics. Your grade is all projects, in-class assignments, and discussion posts. If you miss more than 3 classes, it starts affecting your grade. Discussion posts are tedious. It can be an easy A if you show up and participate. Gave an extra credit project that gives you 2% on top of your final grade, which is sweet.

The flipped class teaching style doesn't work & the course is paced too fast. We often had an exam, homework, & two pre-lecture quizzes due in the same week which is too much for a 3 credit-hour class like this. She is confusing to follow in practice problems. Worst class I've taken & she made it more difficult and stressful than it needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures for this class are extremely fast paced. The professor briefly introduces topics and rushes over every example problem. Tests were extremely rigorous consisting of problems not found in the textbooks/class examples/HW. However, I do think the grading was lenient and as long as you read the text book and do the HW you should pass.

The lectures for this course are close to useless as they are fast-paced and very confusing which are two things that do not go together. When asking clarifying questions during lectures I felt more confused after my question was answered than I did before. Additionally, the test for this class contains material not covered and are very difficult.

This professor put problems on the test that were completely out of the scope of the complexity of what we learned in class. (not that we learned anything in class) She couldn't explain concepts in lecture and every time a student asked a clarifying question she completely misinterpreted the question and uselessly restated her previous statement.

Her class is completely wasting your time because her slides are messy. Also, her style is rushed, you need to do the next chapter's homework when you take this chapter's test this week. So, be nice to yourself, it is better to read the textbook when you plan to go to her class. Trust me, I got 92+ on all three tests and I hardly go to her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do yourself a flavor, and try to take cs2100 with different professor. You dont want this class to ruin your grade, like me. I have friend who took this class last semester with different professor and it was passable. Phillips is the worst professor so far in my uni.

This has been my most disappointing university experience thus far. I think discrete maths is an interesting topic, but I can't help to feel apathetic from Professor Phillip's instruction techniques. You have to learn subjects on your own time, then go to lectures where you "practice" applying these concepts at an unrealistic pace.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't teach everything on the test. The test has questions we weren't taught in class. On the most recent test there was notation that was never explained in class. She had to get on zoom during the test because she realized her mistake, but wasn't present during the actual test.

Honestly the worst professor I've ever had. Class is a complete joke, lectures are essentially useless because her explanations are rushed and do not properly reinforce concepts. All real learning is done outside of class on your own time, which I'm sure makes her job easier, but not yours. Class is heavily weighted towards tests too.
"Prove this massive equation has a solution that is either odd or even. You have 3 minutes"

She's one of those professors who force students to spend unnecessary amounts of time to prove her worth.  The homework isn't hard, just tedious and long.  She also makes us learn the lecture material before we go to lecture with pre-lecture quizzes, so instead of paying tuition, I could take this course on YouTube.  The lectures are also a waste.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She failed to do -1-1.

I've taken this class from a few different professors. This professor was much nicer and gave some extra credit opportunities than previous professors. The structure of this class was the same for multiple professors so there is no way around the tough speedy pace of this class. I would recommend taking this class with her, she is easy to talkto

Professor Phillips is teaching style is that of a glorified Udemy course, were most of your learning will come from outside resources such as google, and YouTube. Tests had questions on logic not found in the book. Content taught in lectures didn't match the textbook, and the textbook didn't match the quizzes. Grading is strict! Prepare to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Does not teach course at all. You will have to depend on online resources like TrevTutor. Quizzes (which make up the majority of the grade) will have concepts not taught in lecture be careful of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and don't take her class. The subject is tough enough already. You don't need to torture yourself any farther. Unless... You are really into that kind of thing c: ! But if you do, just prepare to put in the many extra hour by yourself trying to comprehend logic WITHOUT knowing the system. Take Philosophy class before this helps
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While the professor takes her time to answer questions, often times, her answers were still unclear. Her lectures were often on practice problems. She mentions that we need to do the full step on tests and homeworks but doesn't show us how actually complete the full step. I do not recommend taking her class.

The homework was never related to lectures, lectures were never related to tests, etc. She gave entirely different questions on the test to force students to think of problems differently for every question. It was difficult to grasp onto concepts and apply formulas. Core concepts that should have been covered more were always brushed over.

Prof. Phillips is the worst professor I've had. She doesn't teach. Instead she has you watch Youtube videos posted by TrevTutor before class & does practice problems in class. Your grade is based on 7 in-class quizes & the final with about 10% based off HW. Her quizes are confusing & is nothing like the homework. I learned more from Google than her

Professor Phillips is by far the worst professor I have ever taken. She does not explain things and then when you ask for clarification she moves on without explaining anything. This class is terrible and no one should ever take it from her. I have heard the Math department has a harder but better version, consider that first.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bei is a great teacher and she explains concepts fairly well. The score of CS2100 is heavily towards quizzes which I think is not best weight. To me the course is really trivial, since it claims itself a CS math class, but not math-y as real ones such as math analysis. Be prepared to work and ask if you do not understand, the mileage may vary.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The grade is heavily weighted towards the tests, and she tricks students because the HW, labs, and study guides do NOT reflect what is on the tests. She does this intentionally to "make students learn how to think."  Also the TA's do not know how to solve problems, so good luck asking them for help. Would not recommend this teacher to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. He keeps expectations clear for daily quizzes and exams. Although the class is challenging, Professor Pickett makes you want to succeed. He is one of the most well spoken people I've met. Watch the videos, practice the problems, and take good notes in class to get an A.

This class was difficult and packed with content. I struggled to adapt to his format of watching videos before every class and then a quick explanation during class. There was no way to know what you had learned in a class unless you took note on every single step he took in class.

Loved Scott. Took him in the Fall for this class and failed because I missed the first month of class while I was working. I took him again because he's the best lecturer this school has. He keeps you engaged with a boring subject, and I like that you have to take a quiz every class, which keeps you on your toes with the material.

Scott is wonderful! The lectures are amazing and although the content is difficult, Scott takes the time to make sure the class understands. Quizzes aren't too difficult as long as you're paying attention & watching the videos prior to class. The classwork is hard, but Scott is able to make it fun with personal stories and jokes.

Scott was a great tax professor in my opinion. Quiz every class time had helped me succeed the midterm/exam  (7 or above you get 100%, 6 or lower you fail, 4 quizzes gets dropped)
But make sure to ALWAYS watch his video lectures and do the problems before you go to class! Memorizing the formulas/concepts/layout as it will help you on the quiz!

Ok professor but the testing environment is where it falls apart. There's a test every single class and they don't reflect the study materials well. The grading is just lazy, any quiz below a 70% is an F, anything above is an A, which punishes students in both directions. He needs to invest more time in study guides, test prep and grading methods.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Scott is not a terrible professor but he's terrible at certain things such as test creation, study guides, and his online lectures. There is a quiz in every class period, and the practice problems he gives are lacking when it comes to the actual tests. Study guides are beyond vague, and he will test you on a single sentence in a 40-minute lecture.

Terrible professor. Grades are calculated by quizzes every class and 2 exams. The quizzes are incredibly nuanced and ask super minute and random details from an hour's worth of videos due before class. Avoid if another professor is available.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Scott is the best professor I've ever had. He changed the way I viewed tax, as I'm sure he did for many others. I would say he is the only professor that I found worth the differential tuition. It's amazing how he is able to do something for decades, but be able to explain and teach it effectively to people seeing it for the first time.
I found the class to not be intuitive at all. There's a quiz every class period with only 4 drops. The material isn't very clear, and his wording can be very confusing.
Pickett is maybe the best professor ever! So so knowledgable and engaging. I just love him, and really respect him. I would love to take every accounting class with him.

Scott sets you up for success in his class. Quizzes at the end of each class, but he grades them really fast and he is not trying to trick you with the questions. He is very intelligent but so down to earth and kind. Hands down the best professor at the U. Somehow makes tax pretty interesting!!

Scott is exactly what every professor should be like. He is extremely sharp and smart, and he has an exceptional ability to explain difficult tax concepts in a way that is understandable. He would never blame students if we all missed a problem on the quiz, and rather he would say that he should've taught it better, and then would go back over it.

Easily the best professor in the Accounting department, which is saying a lot. He is very considerate of unexpected circumstances and is very accessible outside of class. You can tell that he actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Absolute gem of a person.

Very funny and a genuine guy. He has entertaining stories and you can tell he really cares about student success. Also, very knowledgeable in his field and does a good job of explaining topics and clarifying terminology.

This course was very interesting and you read papers on (mostly) modern genetics. My biggest complaint would be that there was no feedback on how we were doing, so we had no idea what our grade was until it was submitted. Second biggest complaint was being given very long papers with little time to read them - difficult when you have other classes.

Advanced Eukaryotic genetics - Super great lectures but immense work load with a tight turnaround. I seriously learned more from this course than from any other that I have taken at the U despite the fact that it was only a half semester course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Waaay too easy of a class, I studied for it using review material from BIO 1610. No prepared lecture slides, just a scribbled piece of paper. He did dress professionally and did not take crap from students which was nice! Wish the class would have been more intellectually challenging.

Terrible and lazy class format. There are 7 exams overall (every other week). In total, 25% of the class time is spent taking a test. His lectures were so scattered and unhelpful, and he didn't follow the book at all. I was successful only because I have no test anxiety and can memorize things quickly. If that doesn't sound like you, good luck

He is clearly very knowledgeable and fascinated by genetics, this class wasn't bad at all but if you missed a lecture you probably wouldn't do good on the exams. His lectures aren't very structured, but his exams clearly demonstrate any material covered in lecture. DO NOT depend off of the book offered, that's more of a supplemental option.

Obviously it's going to be a more difficult class, but hands down the best professor I've had at the U. You get what you put in to this class. I studied a lot but have come out with a much greater knowledge and interest in genetics. Only wish that he was more specific on what we should know for exams. A lot of info with no idea of what to focus on.

This class was easy, but this professor made it unbearable. He consistently berated students for their questions if he didn't deem them worthy of class time. The entire grade is based off of exams. On several occasions, students with the exact same answer were given different scores. TAs were often uncertain on course/learning expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have mixed feelings about Dr. Phadnis as a person, but he is an incredible and engaging lecturer. There are a lot of exams, but they only cover 3 lectures maximum. Exams are relatively easy to take. He can be quite curt when answering questions, but overall, he is a good lecturer. The best Genetics professor at the U for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genetics is obviously a more difficult subject but Prof Phadnis is more than reasonable in grading! He was understanding in special circumstances and therefore offered a makeup exam for students that had to miss one due to a valid reason. If I could take him for other classes, I would!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I get the impression that this professor is very knowledgable in his subject, but he has no idea how to teach. His lectures are hilariously difficult to follow, as he will randomly switch between topics with no warning or explanation. I left class everyday confused on what I should know, and what I was supposed to learn.

This professor seems to be geared more toward genetic research and rote memorization rather than helping students gain a good understanding of genetics. I feel this class is not preparing me for a professional environment whatsoever, and I have gained little understanding of genetics from his teaching.

This professor is geared more toward genetics research rather than understanding the critical concepts of genetics. Lectures are all over the place, and it doesn't seem like the professor has solidified his teaching knowledge on the subject. This professor relies more on memorization rather than conceptual learning.
A 100 point exam every other week. His study guides are pointless. He is passionate about his research but not about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis is a very animated lecturer, funny, and very intelligent. However, his inflated ego gets the best of him most of the time. Occasionally in lecture he would make mean comments and refuse to answer students questions. He also lectures using a notebook and limited slides, so if you're an iPad adult be wary! Easy class if you like genetics!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Phadnis gave the most entertaining lectures I've ever attended by a long shot. Go to discussions if you want a 100% exam score. He responds VERY fast to emails, and every time I've asked him something in private he's been very respectful and accommodating. Ultimately, you will get out of this class what you put into it.

Phadnis is a good professor as far as being funny and engaging during lecture but his exams are difficult (few questions, large points) arbitrarily tests you on material from anywhere in the world of genetics

I shared a lot of frustration about Dr. Phadnis that my classmates did this semester. I often left lecture without clarity on what I should take away & tests were extremely hard and frequent. Despite the difficulty, I found him to be one of the most passionate biology professors I've ever taken and I left the class very inspired about bio!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Phadnis is easily the worst professor I have experienced at the U in 4 years. He regularly talks down to students, is happy to threaten your grades if you don't "make his life easy", and writes ambiguous questions that would receive massively different scores depending on who graded them. The material is easy, Phadnis makes it hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor, huge ego, and enjoys asserting his dominance over struggling students. Makes students feel dumb when asking questions. Uses intimidation to get students to work in the class. Only cares about research. Horrible with logistics. Won't record class or provide slides. This class gave me more anxiety than any other class I have taken.

He doesn't care about his students at all.  He won't answer questions.  If you struggle he will tell you it's all your fault because other people can do it.  In general just a jerk.  Only reason to take his class it that it's so easy.  He won't help you at all though so if you find genetics hard and need extra help he is not the teacher for you.

Luckily i did well, but the classes are him literally reading over the textbook and then giving his own personal experiences. The tests are short and points are stacked so if you mess up one question your mark goes down by two grades. Canvas is super disorganized and you only have a day and a half to do homework assignments

Dr. Nitin Phadnis was a funny guy. I struggled a lot in the class, but he was definitely the better teacher of the two. He is engaging and keeps you awake during lecture. Not a bad choice for intro genetics.

professor phadnis was a great professor prior to moving classes online. but soon afterwards, he became very unreliable and was impossible to get a hold of. i feel like he didnt want to teach anymore and left us hanging for weeks with no material after promising to do so.

He's hilarious and cares about what he teaches to his students. There are seven exams + 1 comprehensive final. Reading the textbook and doing the HW helps a lot since he sometimes picks questions directly from them. He's charismatic but approachable so don't be afraid to ask questions and talk to him. One of the chillest professors I've had!

Phadnis truly makes you work for your grade in this class. There are exams every other week, which is a lot of work, but the material you are expected to know is always clearly stated. Skipping lecture won't do you any good, but I never wanted to skip anyways because his lectures are amazing. He is engaged, hilarious, and hand crafts every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Phadnis is an excellent professor. There are 7 midterm exams which are difficult but not impossible to ace. There was a large amount of extra credit possible throughout the semester, at least 70+ points, (exams are 100 points each) This will be a hard class no matter where you take it but Dr. Phadnis makes it enjoyable and helps you through it.

He'll make it terrible semester on his students. 8 tests total which are not pertinent to what is taught explicitly in class. So frustrating! He'll tell you one thing and expect you to know all details, methods, experiments, etc. that pertain to it. If lucky, you'll stumble upon the answer online and hopefully remember it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Phadnis is an enthusiastic lecturer but has been disorganized and scattered this semester. He has been absent from many lectures and the exams are unfair, material do not correlate well to concepts taught in lecture. I learned much of the material on my own through the posted study guides and attending class was unhelpful.

honestly this guy may have given up this semester or something. I read all the glowing reviews and was excited to take genetics from him until I was in the class. He has missed over 7 lectures at research symposiums and will have his guest lecturers write exams that are extremely difficult and not consistent. Dont waste your time.

You will be paying upward of a grand to take genetics, so read this review. 7 tests plus a final. First 3 tests are fair. Tests become harder, he gives you practice problems and vital/new information the day before the test. Charismatic lectures, but more into research than actually teaching. Save your $ and take genetics elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor was all over the place. His pacing the room was very distracting and he rushed through things. I couldn't process what he was talking about. There is a lot of outside book learning and on your own learning which is frustrating because we pay a lot someone to "teach" us. He cares a lot about his research, not so sure about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers on campus. Dr. Phadnis is extremely passionate about genetics and is a great teacher. There are 8 exams, but they help you stay on top of the information and only test on you two weeks worth of lecturers, making the material much more manageable. The class starts out easy and gradually gets harder so stay on top of it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: OK. 7 midterms sounds awful, but really is just made it so I didn't forget anything before each test. This guy is a genius and yet is still is in touch with pop culture references. You will learn a ton in this class. He makes it entertaining to learn it. Do the homework assignments, work through the study guides, and you should be golden.

Absolutely loved both the course and his teaching style. He is exciting and animated when he lectures while at the same time doing a great job of allowing discussion and questions. He takes every students questions seriously and really does a great job of treating all students with respect. Very impressed. Definitely a tough class however.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nitin is probably the best professor i have ever had. You have to take 7 exams and a final through out the whole semester. You really have to work hard to get a good grade. Make sure you go to TA sessions. I have learned enormous amount of stuff from the TAs.  I would definitely take another class with him.

I can't say enough about this professor! He is so passionate and truly cares about his students and their success. He gives 1 test every other week, so 7 tests and one final. It seems like a lot, but it helps you not slack off with studying. Attend lecture, do the study guides, and go to class ready to learn. This class won't disappoint!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is not enough that I can complement about this professor! He gives tests every other week - which is actually really helpful with staying up to date on the material.  His passion towards genetics really makes the class come alive and makes you want to succeed.  He is a great teacher and genuinely cares about his students success.

Truly an amazing professor. You MUST attend class, as he uses chalk/verbal teaching styles. Use your in class notes to fill out the review sheet sent out by the TAs, study this, and you will succeed. The homework will help you understand the concepts. 1 test every other week. 7 tests, 1 final. He either drops the final or 2 tests. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hardest class at the undergraduate level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor on campus. His love for genetics is contagious and his lectures are entertaining and super informative. Test based class with more analytical problem-solving rather than simple information regurgitation. Fantastic class, I would recommend it to anyone.

Your really have to work your butt off in this class. There are 7 midterms and 1 final. But Dr. Phadnis is an awesome professor who cares about your success. Every lecture is always STIMULATING. He has some of the best TA's at the university in my opinion. At the end, you WILL have learned ALOT of new concepts in science. Really amazing professor!
Phadnis's class is super fun.  Do your homework, study hard and you'll get an A.  I loved this class.  Absolutely worth the work.

Dr. Phadnis is an amazing professor. His lectures are super clear and whatever is ambiguous, the TAs will help out with. He's really passionate about genetics and it's infectious. He also uses the board when giving lectures, so you're able to write out notes with him as he's explaining things instead of reading off a slide.
amazing passion for genetics it's quite infectious. the structure of the tests determines if you really understand the material . his tests are mostly based of intuition.

I would not recommend Dr Pierre. Her lectures are poorly formatted. She doesn't use lecture slides. She just writes on the board randomly. She has also been mean to students with disabilities. She called them out in class for being annoying because of their accommodations through the school being "extra work".

Dr Pierre is clearly very knowledgable in her field. But her approach to students is not good. She was pretty mean to students, particularly if you went to her office hours or emailed her. Lectures were just her writing on the board, so hard to follow. I would avoid her classes.

Dr Pierre refused to give CDA accommodations, despite it being a university requirement. 
CDA investigated her and she still refuses to this day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Pierre was very rude during office hours. She is ok during class to students. But once she's in a one-on-one setting, she'll tell you to try harder and that you aren't smart or putting in any effort. Heard other students had the same experiences in office hours, with super mean comments from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Went to office hours and she told me I just need to try harder and didn't help at all. Lectures are not based on slides - she will just write on the board and you have to hope you can keep up and follow.

omg lol.  where to start. all she does is write notes on the board and really thats it. no pictures, no way of getting the notes later. SUPER funny, like in a sardonic condescending way lol. She teaches because she has to. a 50% is a passing grade, 80% is an A because it seems shes not interested in teaching so thats how you can pass, its ok.

No credit given for working on tests - if you get part A wrong, but do the correct working on parts C - E, you still get 0. 

Lectures are hard to follow. 

No lecture notes posted. When asked for extra resources, she said I should just "study less". 

Avoid Dr Pierre.

I feel like Dr. Pierre is overhated. The class was hard, but that's because the content is difficult. I don't believe she's condescending either, rather she puts a lot of responsibility on the individual and has high expectations--as any upper div professor should. That being said, the class can use more structure, but is otherwise fine.

I disagree with a lot of the negativity here. I never felt as if Dr. Pierre did not care for her students. She is quite forward, but I do not think she is condescending. It is absolutely necessary to attend lectures, and the exams can have mean/difficult questions, but overall, I felt as if I gained a strong foundation for Inorganic Chemistry.

Lectures are mandatory unless you have someone to send you notes. She posts all of the previous exams and copies and pastes many of the questions from old quizzes and exams. The TA was amazing and did most of the heavy lifting for this class, but the professor made an 80% an A in this class.

The single TA for the class carries the whole thing. Dr Pierre is a researcher not a teacher - it's clear she isn't made for teaching. 

Lectures are hard to follow. Not really given any resources. No lecture notes uploaded. Very little support for students.

After taking the final TODAY, I can assuredly say she is the worst. Our final consisted of 27 pages and didn't even show up to the classroom to give us our final it was just our TA. The exam started late because not everyone had a copy. She doesn't care for her students, we collectively are just an afterthought to her. I support the comments below.

CHEM3100 is not that hard, but the way Dr Pierre has set up the course is terrible. 

She doesn't seem to care much about students. Her office hours are really condescending and rude to students. 

You have to teach yourself a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE inorganic chemistry, but this professor is doing her absolute best to make me loath it. Hardly takes questions during lecture; extremely condescending when she does. Goes FAST through material. Study guides are 1 exam or quiz from past semester and exam WILL be more difficult. No respect for and blames students. exam-graded only. good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Valerie genuinely cares about her students. The class is hard and the content is hard. Valerie provides extra credit opportunities for people who attend lecture. I never post on these boards, but after seenig all the hate I needed to clear things up. I do wish there were more TAs and that the lecture notes should be posted.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The only teaching is within the lectures, which are terrible. The only people who rate this class well are people who don't have any responsibilities outside of school and spend their whole day studying. 

Professor Pierre refuses to provide lecture notes. If you're not in class, good luck.

Old school style professor, but if you go to class and study her old exams and quizzes, you'll be fine. No curve but an A is an 80 and passing is a 50. TA office hours could totally be better organized. I actually have really liked her class and teaching this semester. Just have to put in the work outside of lecture and it'll pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Get ready to self teach. Only learning you'll do will be at home or from other class members. Dr Pierre won't teach you very well.

by far the worst class I have ever taken, 1 TA for 90 students. less than 2 hrs of Office hours No posted notes, only graded on tests and quizzes. Good luck in OH she is very condescending when you ask for help. Only prep. for her exams are the ones she gave students in prior semesters. She clearly prioritizes research over her students,& it shows.

The problem sets on canvas which are meant to help you study are just screenshots of the textbook. 

Might as well self teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
The grading in this class is rough. The assessments are ok in terms of fairness - the questions are usually a reasonable level, but the grading is harsh. 

The lectures are terrible. Not worth your time. But there are no notes, so if you don't go, good luck. 

Professor was not made for teaching. Should stick to research.

No lecture notes. Lectures are hard to understand. She doesn't seem to care about the class failing. 

Newer to the University of Utah and needs to stop being so happy when students fail.

Worst chemistry class I've taken. The content is actually interesting and fairly straight forward. However, Dr Pierre's teaching and approach is not. She doesn't have any notes. She will mention something in lecture once and then test it. Her office hours aren't helpful - she will just tell you that you should have listened in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are really hard to understand. Go to class, understand 10% of it, go home and teach yourself everything, except she doesn't post her lecture notes.

Professor Pierre is clearly an expert in her field of chemistry, but doesn't seem to understand that students aren't. She will be annoyed when people don't know the chemistry she's meant to teach. She has made fun of people in office hours for not understanding, but then doesn't try to help them understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Professor Pierre hates students and likes to see them fail. No notes from lectures, one TA for the whole class, grading is harsh. No curve. No exam drops. No support for students.

Exams are on Friday, every 2nd week. New content learned on Wednesday lectures WILL be tested on, even though there aren't any office hours offered prior to the exam to help make sense of the content. Pierre is condescending, talking down to students who come to her with questions, and gets upset when we ask for more practice and resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Pierre doesn't give out her lecture notes so if you miss class you have to hope you have a friend who was there. Says that people will stop coming if she puts her lecture notes on canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Pierre provides zero lectures notes. 
She explicitly states that she will never curve, even when the average is 55%. 
Blames students for not doing well on tests. 
Doesn't teach concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE Rick. He's the best professor I've ever had, and I would take more from him if I could. His lectures are informative, and he's hilarious. He is a fair grader and will work with you to improve your writing. I learned a lot, and my writing improved this semester. He treats students as adults and builds an environment that you want to be in.

Conterary to other people I did not like Rick, he gave assignments with laid back criteria and graded extremly hard with no guidelines. The work is super easy and most of class was just him ranting or telling us to fix what we submitted. He gives time to fix work and extends deadlines super long. I felt like he was passive agressive.

Rick covers all the different sides of strategic communications but mostly focuses on journalism. If you need to take COMM 4590 I couldn't recommend him more. His class usually lasts two hours once a week and I look forward to it. His feedback is constructive and he isn't afraid to point out how you could improve. Highly recommend.
My favorite professor I have ever had. I wish he taught more courses so I could take more classes from him. Learned a lot, and was given great tools and knowledge that I will use in my career.

Best professor I have ever had. His lectures are fun and engaging. He brings in plenty of guest speakers who offer valuable information. He gives great feedback on all of the assignments and wants his students to succeed. I have learned very valuable information from his class. 10/10.

Rick was one of the best professors I've had at the U! He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Work isn't overly hard but he leads awesome discussions. He provided more "real world" examples and assignments rather than busy work and essays. Amazing!! 100% reccommend!

One of the best professors I've had at the U. A funny, genuine, nice professor who wants you to succeed. Once a week class, weekly quizzes that he lets you use your book on and main assignments are papers including the final. Papers are relatively easy if you like to write/ are good at writing, not usually long either. 10/10

Rick is an AMAZING professor! He is very down-to-earth and truly wants his students to succeed. The class was only 1x weekly, so attendance was important, but he would go over things the class needed and help with any homework assignments given. Hilarious, loud, and super cool. By far my favorite professor I've ever had at the U. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!

Intro to News Writing was the title of the class, mandatory for my strategic communications major. The class was only once a week from 6pm to 9pm, but he made sure we never went past 8:30pm which was really nice. Always willing to help you with your writing and answer any questions. The textbooks are required for open book quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Super nice guy who genuinely wants everyone to do well. I felt like the class was boring by nature, but he tried to make it relevant. He is a fair grader and is very reachable outside of class. I would definitely recommend him over the other writing professors.

Dr. P is a great professor and a pretty entertaining lecturer. Sometimes the classes felt a little boring but overall I would say he was very effective at his job. He's clearly passionate about linguistics which helps, and he is always interested in talking about random, seemingly unrelated things that somehow always tie back into the topic.

Online classes are always a little stressful, due to the professor not explaining things well, but Dr. Pischnotte was so amazing. Explained things well, really cared about what grade you were getting, and gave amazing feedback on papers, quizzes, and other assignments. Definitely take this professor for writing, you'll learn good things.

Dr. P is a good professor but he's definitely odd. The class was easy enough and interesting. He would review the exams by going over the actual questions in class so there was absolutely no reason to fail. Was worried about the final, a group project, as it's worth 30% of the total, but my group put in almost no effort and we finished with a 96%.

He's a great guy, but his lectures dragged on. Most of the course material was self-explanatory and a lot of it was outdated, especially the films he had us watch. The exams and assignments were easy. I felt frustrated in his class because there was potential for interesting conversation but he mainly stuck to the basics in the PowerPoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pischnotte was a wonderful professor. I felt appreciated, heard, and valued in his class. There are three major projects in his class, but all three have assignments leading up to the due date which make things a lot easier and force individuals to avoid procrastination. I really enjoyed having him as my professor!
Dr. P was one of my favorite teachers I've had very caring and funny guy. The stuff we learned is pretty basic writing technique, but I do feel more invested in my writing. Would recommend him 100%.
Dr. P was great. He was a bit of an odd ball, but he was very engaging and made the lectures an enjoyable experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Totally amazing guy. There are lots of papers but they're easy topics. Definitely recommend him if you're good at English and want to have some fun.
Dr. P is the best! He is a kind hearted human being and is a great teacher. 11/10 super cool guy would take this class again!
In short, Dr. P is the best.
Knowledgeable one

Zeb was one of my favorite professors i've ever had! He is down to earth, very relatable, and very easy to talk to. He grades assignments quickly and fairly. I've never gotten below a B on any of my papers. His lectures did seem to drag out a bit from time to time but they were very helpful to look back at when it came time to write my papers
Professor Pischnotte was a great professor. His lectures were always interesting and he always found a way to make them relatable. He's very approachable and funny.

This professor is outstanding. He can be interesting in many ways to make the lecture enjoyable. I would say this was the most interesting course among all courses I got in that semester. Show up to class and do the homework, you will get an easy A+!

Love this man. If you have stuff going on just communicate with him and it won't be a problem. I turned in all my my missing assignments the last two weeks of the semester and he graded them all with full credit. I ended up with an A. He's great! As long as you show up and do the work you pass.
I love this guy! He's a great man
nice man!

Zeb was a fantastic professor! I had to retake Writing 2010. let's just say my previous professor was unfortunate. I was dreading taking the course again but actually ended up enjoying it greatly! This class is stupid and a waste of time and money. Zeb is a terrible instructor. He goes on so many tangents and is so confusing when explaining assignments. He's an easy grader and the class is easy overall but it's so mind numbingly boring.

Zen is awesome! Such a fun class, easy grader, provides help, anything you need he'll help

Zeb is an awesome teacher! He's a chill guy that uses funny stories to explain concepts and often lets the class out early. I still felt like I learned a lot, my skills in rhetoric writing improved greatly and I loved being able to write about topics that interested me. I highly reccomend him!

Professor Pierce was a great WRTG 1010 teacher. She taught writing through monster media, which was one of the most interesting writing classes I have ever taken. I recommend, just get ready to write!

Sara is honestly the best teacher, I took the week long intensive course and loved every minute of it! I loved hip hop before the start of the class but after the class I have a deeper love for it and more respect. Sara lectures are amazing and I love how passionate she gets during her lectures.

Sara is a solid professor. She's very knowledgeable about what she teaches and takes the time to get to know each and every student. Sara is great! I took the week long intensive history of hip hop class before spring semester and I am so glad I did. Dr. Pliner is great! She took responsibility for when students struggled early on and made many positive changes to the class.
