It felt like nothing ever made sense in this class. His exams are based on arbitrary facts pulled from lecture rather than overall concept. He also had grammar and spelling mistakes on his exams
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One thing you can't miss is that he is chill and non-judgemental.

Once I sent him email with critical statements about his class and lecture, I expected some email that is confrontational. Instead, he responded me with gratitude by saying "thank you for the inputs" and informed me the reason and choices involved in designing the class. That was surprising and I am grateful for him being my professor afterward.

Wayne will not ignore your question. In fact, once I asked him about some questions that he doesn't know after class. The next time he came to class, he made a detailed slide about it to answer my question. Surprising!
He cares his student enormously.
Wayne is a very kind and relax person. There was once he stopped to me on campus. If you happened to know him more, he is a really nice person.
Wayne is a very unrushed person. He does not have much expectation on you. He is very patient and kind.

Lectures are reading off slides, which isn't that intuitive. Content is easy enough, covers 1/2 of content until second instructor takes over. Covers concisely what is to be expected on exams from slides, DTL, and past quizzes. Quizzes are every 2 weeks and are take home. Class is easy if you study for it, lot of buffer for your grade HW & Clicker.

Lectures are practically read right off the slides which is helpful for what you need to know, but he goes really fast so it's hard to write things down before he's moving on. Pay attention to the examples he uses as you might have to explain one on a test/quiz.

I'm surprised he doesn't have more ratings! I took his lab class and it was great. Half semester and graded by homework, pop quizzes and notebook. His class emphasizes techniques ranging from PCR to bioinformatics tools. Honestly this is one of the most useful lab courses I've taken, I highly recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes come straight from text.  Tests are mostly from slides. He makes his tests hard and long to set a high standard.  Those are his words.  Grades on curve.  He often forgets what he had planned to say about certain slides, making lectures choppy and unclear sometimes.
No Comments

Exams are extremely difficult. I studied using all lectures and practice tests and still got D's. Unreasonably hard for an online non-major business class; don't take it if you want an easy A. She also messed up the grade book all semester, so my final grade was much lower than what was shown.

By far the worst professor I've had at the U, and it's online! I would say on average, I spent 10 hours a week reviewing material. The tests are extremely hard and reflect only part of what is taught in the lecture and readings. The content is a lot and there are over 250 terms to memorize. If this wasn't a requirement, I would stay far away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy class. Mostly relatively easy McGraw Hill assignments. There is an essay towards the end of the semester to look out for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: don't even know what this prof. looks like wkly assignments (3 small ones) done & graded thru mcgraw-hill. 1 writing assignment in semester took me abt 3 hours. drops lowest 6 grades. if ur looking for an easy class, take this one from this prof. one of the easiest i have ever taken. defs just a grad student who needs to be a TA for that $$$

Do not take one of her classes. Our entire class was structured over McGraw-Hill Connect, with no lectures or anything else provided by her. The entire class is a copy and paste. All readings, and all graded through the website, so good luck calculating your own grades. There's a problem when you don't know what your professor looks or sounds like.

I thought this class was great. Use the study guides to study for the exams and you will do fine. Assignments/quiz due every week and one written project. Also, you are allowed to use a cheat sheet on the exams. Solid class, easy A.

You hardly interact with the professor in this course. All coursework & assignments are conducted through an online textbook. There is a quiz & two assignments due weekly, but they are very easy. The midterm & final are a bit tough, since the only material to study is literally reading the textbook. One final paper, not too difficult. Easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Portillo is a pretty chill guy but for someone who has TWO degrees in theater, he grades insanely tough on the papers. One of our first papers asked us to write about our own PERSONAL experiences we have had regarding race, yet the class average was 68 percent. Goes to show someone who has little knowledge on a subject should not grade heavily
A subpar teacher without any substantial field experience.
Great class. He's very knowledgable and cares about the subject matter.  The class has an academic feel while still being very accessible.

Letterpress is one of those things where you have to have someone basically holding your hand through the initial process if you want to get really good at it. Marnie is that kind of instructor. She's very thorough in her explanation and always stops to help if you need it. She's always open to hearing about your creative process and encourages it.

I think Marnie is an excellent professor as she has a very caring and maternal personality. However, I wish that the studio was more accessible during working hours. Additionally, cleaning the presses was so challenging, so it would be helpful to prepare yourself with a lot of energy. Printing requires a considerable amount of time in the studio

Marnie is an absolute gem! She tries her best to make letterpress an accessible art, and you can really tell she cares about the studio, equipment, and her students. She's kind, funny, and is very accessible outside of class. She's always willing to spend extra time with you if you're struggling and the resources to use equipment are thorough!
Not a good experience, which is a shame since the book arts program seems so interesting.

Marnie obviously knows what she's teaching.  She shows that she has real knowledge of the subject through demonstrations and who she brings in as guest speakers.  She is one of those teachers who makes you work for your grade.  You have to put in the time and effort to do well in her classes.  She is super helpful, if you ask!

For as many people that sign up for the class, there isn't enough equipment to accomodate them. And, even when you do have access to the equipment, your access to the print lab is limited by the hours it's open. There are things to learn via tests and quizes, but it's so trivial. If you want to be treated like an elementary student, she's your gal.

Ashton is difficult to work with. Does not respond to emails frequently and won't generally work with students if they have an emergency. The syllabus will be shoved in your face if you can't make a presentation. If you attend you will pass, its a gen-ed not much to say there. Overall very easy class, just ensure that you can make every session.

Ashton is a nice and incredibly brilliant guy. He is open to questions and does a good job at explaining concepts. Sometimes I found the course material to be boring and unoriginal (stuff we learned in high school), but it was easy to understand and the quizzes were mostly term memorization.

Ashton was a great professor, he's young so he's pretty chill. He is very straightforward with his lectures in a good way and is really good at giving feedback. With such dense assignments you need to do in the class there is no need worry, he isn't that harsh of a grader. He was very understanding and always able to work things out with students.

I took his public speaking class and I was so scared of public speaking. My voice and hands were shaky during my first speech and he was super kind about it. His lectures were informative and engaging. By the year's end, I improved at speaking and felt a lot more confident. I got a lot out of this class and will use what I learned in the future.

11/10! Ash is super relatable and gives great advice for understanding your speeches. He often points out any personal mistakes or stories to help give the class a good laugh, even at 9 am. Homework is easy- 4 speeches and 3 quizzes. The rest is listening and taking notes on how to talk in front of other people. One of the best experiences at the U

Ash is such an awesome professor. He really cares about his students succeeding and understanding his class. There's 4 speeches w/ outlines. Super understanding if anxious he helps you prepare and gives great feedback. Looking for an easy A? comm 1020 with Ash is your best bet. Quizzes are easy, answers are in the slides. Attending helps understand

Ashton is great!!! This might be his only class, but if you have him for a class I recommend him. He is really funny and REALLY cares about his students and their learning. He would ask us what is effective about his teaching and anything that might help us learn better. He gives great feedback.

His speaking skills are also VERY impressive.

Very kind and understanding professor. Super approachable and lovely to talk to. Made the class content easy to understand. He went at a pace that allowed everyone to ask questions and really understand the information.

Dr. Powell is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are clear. His homework and tests are challenging but fair. I would highly recommend making friends with people in the class so that you can lean on each other during difficult sections. He gives a detailed equation sheet on exams and allows you to bring your own as well.

Does not teach everything you need to do the homework assignments. Often cancels class and does not supplement the missed lecture with a proper video.
The homework is very difficult and he expects it to be done in a very particular way, but he will not tell you that way. Probably one of the most confusing classes I've taken.

Dr. Powell is the best professor I have had in the University of Utah. I had him for both Heat Transfer and Smart Systems. He cares about his students and goes above and beyond his duties as a professor to foster a relaxed learning environment. Even though the class was hard, his teaching style helped me understand the material and enjoy the class.

Dr. Powell is really good at helping you understand the material as well as helping you grow professionally. He had a couple of small projects that I originally dreaded, but came to like as they helped me to not only understand the subject better but also helped me to better understand a variety of different tools.

Dr. Powell is an amazing professor. He really cares about you understanding the concept rather than plugging in numbers into an equation and coming up with a solution. HW is not too bad, exams are fair, and he does have mini projects that you do which helps better understand the concepts. Also offers a lot of extra credit.

Doctor Powell is an awesome professor. The best part about him is he really cares about students. He is really passionate about helping students get jobs and internships. Not a lot of teachers do that and I appreciate that. Class room wise, he really wants students to understand the concepts. He wants you to get the idea behind the problems.

Kody is the greatest professor ever. Even with this being his first class ever, he truly inspired us to become better people and engineers.  I hope to be an engineer like Kody. That being said, the homework and his lectures don't line up, so expect to read the textbook for every single problem. Not exactly a bad thing, I learned a lot that way!

One of the best professor I've had so far. He helps you out when you need it. The class is engaging and very interesting. There's no way you can fail this class! Show up, do you assignments  & take like 3 quizzes and your final easy project. BAM! you would get an A or B. I would 110% recommend if you need an HF credit or if you're majoring!

Professor Con was absolutely my favorite teacher yet at the U. He cared about his students, he helped them when he thought they needed it, and he even had a professional background in journalism! I would recommend everyone to take Con Psarras as an intro to news writing teacher if you want to actually learn/care about journalism and media writing.

Constantine was a perfect instructor. He is highly intelligent and knows how to teach to the younger generation. He works with you and wants you to succeed. I was sick and missed a huge workshop and he worked with me so I wouldn't miss the points. I would recommend him to everyone! He is the best professor I have had in years.

Con was a perfect teacher for a news writing class. He has years of experience which he uses every class as real life examples. Classes are great and really engaging.  Is a pretty easy grader, but also challenges you to make better work.  Con has been a great inspiration to pursue journalism, and has a ton of connections to help you after school.

Professor Patel was a wonderful professor to have, and one of my favorite professors I've ever had the opportunity to learn from at the U. She was very supportive and flexible, making sure to give students as many opportunities to succeed as possible.

I want to start this off with saying I absolutely loved professor Patel, she was helpful and accommodating every class and presented hard material in a very digestible way. The only criticism I would have is her lack of availability outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Priyam stated MULTIPLE times she "isn't used to teaching undergrads." She has office hours once a week and is not great at answering emails in a timely manner. She cancelled class a bit. This class is very PROOFS based and the homeworks can be really difficult. The "exams" are video projects and are fairly easy. Doesn't update grades in Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Frequent homework with easy problems assuming you understood the lecture. Much of our grade was based on two video explaining concepts in discrete math, I think the rubrics provided clearly explained what you needed to do.

Really good at explaining concepts and answering questions clearly, very supportive and kind. Clearly loves both math/teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Patel really cares about her students. She understands mental health issues and constantly checks in with us and offers extensions as needed. Bi-weekly homework, but most of your grade is two "exams," which were actually videos we had to record. This was a refreshing change from having to study for tests. One of my favorite math professors by far.

INCREDIBLE PROF. youre missing out if you dont take topology from her! Established researcher and extremely knowledgeable yet very kind and helpful. Content was not easy and will be challenging if you arent into pure math, but grading is forgiving and no written exams, only a vid explaining a concept in topology.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Not accessible outside of class. If you miss and try to ask for help she's not great about giving it. Her tests were designed to be tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Patel is amazing. She is fairly organized and gives great lectures, but most of all, she is passionate about topology. It's fun to have a professor who is so excited about the material and sympathetic towards students.

Never posted homework or test solutions, and wouldn't explain when asked, so it was hard to study for tests. Rarely answered emails, and was difficult to reach outside of class. Showed up late or didn't show to scheduled meetings when you couldn't make office hours. Extremely harsh grading and designed exams to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Patel is great. She knew what she was doing and she really wanted you to succeed; but she wanted you to work for it too. She used guided notes in her class which helped out. Some students didn't like her teaching style, so maybe it wasn't for everyone, but I definitely learned a great deal in her class.

She is incredibly organized and does a great job at explaining topics through examples. She's also very understanding and ready to help those who put in the effort. Her lectures and handouts are built more for math-oriented students though.

Homework is super easy but doesn't prepare you for the very difficult tests. Lectures are 80 mins of him speed-reading 70+ slides. You'll need to spend a lot of time teaching yourself outside class to succeed. He grades hard. If you want to really learn and pass, take Prof. Wood instead.

He doesn't do a good job explaining topics. I never felt prepared for the tests despite doing all the homework, going to all the lectures, and studying hard. It just felt like trick questions and he finds any excuse to take points away.

This professor doesnt know how to teach. His lectures are agonizingly difficult to both pay attention and actually learn from. His lectures and assignments are so easy and out of sync that when exams are given it almost seems like a joke covering almost none of the materials covered both in class and in assignments. avoid this guy at all costs.
Great depth of subject; in fact, I even used to discuss about his rearch with him and its pretty cool
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One word bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst prof, would never take the course again.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Good lecturer, I didn't have a hard time with his accent personally. Although sometimes he asks questions to the class and then leaves awkward silence and doesn't allow anybody to answer...
Lots of opportunities for extra credit and student feedback, but the class is a bit too test heavy in my opinion. Lectures are unfortunately mandatory.

Does have an accent which can make it hard for some but it is easy to understand if you pay attention. Class overall is lecture heavy and not setup very well. All learning is expected outside of class and then come to class to review/practice. Homework is try/no try which was nice.

I had a hard time understanding Prof Soni because of the accent, but I do think if you can get past that he's a great lecturer. He's available and approachable outside of class. Midterms aren't too bad, he allows a notes sheet.
Interesting subject, difficult projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Run! Run! Run!
Projects are really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Projects are really hard for those who has no experience.
Course and Projects are very difficult and rush every course. Grading is harsh.

Professor Kalla is one of the best professors I have had at the University of Utah. His way of explaining the materials made every new concept feel naturally motivated instead of regurgitating from a book. Although the concepts in the book were very useful and necessary for passing, it did not feel like they came out of nowhere, thanks to Kalla.

Dr. Kalla is a great professor, but his class just seems to need refinement. The lectures are great, but test difficulty can go beyond what max homework difficulty is (I think). Tests (final, (2) midterms) were 60% of your grade and no extra credit existed. This class just seems like too much to chew at once. Doable, but its going to get messy.
Interesting course. More of maths. Had to definitely work for it. But easy on the grades.

Although this class was a difficult class, Kalla helped us understand in class anything in the book that I had trouble with. Although sometimes in class he would go off rants and when he wrote on the board it was like chicken scratch notes so I had to go through and refine the notes so I could understand them-however it was an fun/interesting class
a great professor.
Very bad prof

I often come back to read his negative reviews just to make myself feel better. No essay I have ever written has been graded with such ambiguous severity. feedback like "dont use 'impactful'" but no explanation or alternative suggestions to improve wordchoice. almost changed major because of how awful he made me feel

oml this rmp page is scary... and honestly, it holds some merit: Preiss is a tough (and vague) grader and is INCREDIBLY blunt, which can sometimes hurt. But he wants to make you better and if you engage in class and ask questions you will go far. He can make wild claims one-sided claims, but use your critical thinking skills and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I didn't take this professor but every other English major I met told me of this man's violence. Beware of this professor. Be like Peter and betray your savior three times before taking this professor.

This class was a nightmare. Every essay is just regurgitating his lectures back to him, so don't do anything original! He was very condescending during lectures, and didn't create a space for critical thinking. You will learn his take on the material, and not the material itself. His responses to essays are also petty and unnecessarily rude.

Don't do it! Don't take this class. My counselor suggested it and I have trust issues now. 
First essay he destroys everyone. 
You're grade is dependent on meeting with him outside of class, but he is terrible at emailing. He discussed all female writers on one day. The essay criteria is not clear, and you will have to cater grammar to his taste.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're going to take this class, you may want to pick up a pair of knee pads along with your books. Preiss is not a tough grader; he is impossible. He is rude, egotistical, condescending, has no regard for anybody's viewpoint but his own, and if you don't stroke his ego just right, he will become bitter towards you, and you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. He is very condescending and rude, and if you don't write exactly what he says in the lectures you will fail. He has a very specific point of view on everything and if you disagree with that you will be punished. Don't take this class from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Preiss is incredibly intelligent but will make sure that you know that you aren't. His feedback is harsh and I definitely cried reading it but it made me a better writer. Participation and 4 papers are the things that are graded. Do the reading & listen really well to regurgitate the lectures onto the 4 papers like he wants you to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TRIAL. BY. FIRE. I cry after I get every assignment back. The first professor to tear apart my writing. That sucks. One of the most brilliant professors at the U. His feedback is REALLY valuable but VERY harsh. Very willing to help you, and is kinder in person (so don't be scared). He made me a better writer. Get ready to LEARN. Very witty.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors Ive ever had. Listen to the other reviews!!!! He is condescending, rude, his lectures are not engaging, and if you ever say anything to disagree with his ideas/interpretations, he will belittle you in front of the entire class. The entire class is based on 3 or 4 papers. He TEARS YOU APART on these papers. So good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class takes the light from your soul and makes you hate professors on a personal level. He is awful. He has a fetish for Shakespeare and is mind-blown when you cant love it as much as him. How he grades your papers is so tough, he makes you question your sanity as a competent student. Dont take this course. Don't. Don't do it. DO NOT!! DON'T
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take this class as your absolute last option or if you have a Shakespeare fetish or if you are parents will pay for it and you don't care. Just don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed this Shakespeare course after previously taking another class he taught; both were fascinating. He was very helpful & I appreciated his meticulousness when grading my papers; he provided meaningful feedback that helped me weed out what was unnecessary, deepen my critical engagement with the texts, & grow as a reader & writer.

You will probably question your entire life when you get your 1st paper back, covered in his criticisms. He can actually be pretty rude. Also, make sure you have the EXACT version of the book you are reading or you will be called out in front of everyone for not being able to follow his syllabus.

Very tough course. His criticism/grading was more condescending than constructive. Liked to make it a point that he was more educated than his students. Isn't very receptive to other view points other than his own. I've had tough professor's before, and I agree that he crosses the line from "tough professor" to "rude professor."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, even though it was hard as hell. He eviscerated my writing, which was precisely what I needed to become a better writer. If you can defend your readings of things logically, and if you try to improve, you should be fine. Go to his office hours - he'll help you get your ideas into good shape for your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Condescending and rude. Won't entertain any ideas that he didn't create on his own. Truly a space where you must repeat what the professor says and stop when you start thinking creatively. His lectures aren't awful but they are unproductive. Crosses the line between "tough teacher" and "rude teacher".

Probably one of the hardest classes/professors I've ever had. Be ready for EXTREMELY hard grading and feedback as well as a higher expectation for knowledge on the subject. BUT, he is very knowledgeable about English and if you apply yourself and take advantage of his help, you will learn A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the most condescending person alive. He will make you question your decision of your major. He is not approachable at all. His opinion is the only opinion that matters. I'm a straight A student and will have to take this class again. He will make you cry. If you value your GPA don't take this class!! Just avoid this professor at all costs.

Preiss, while blunt and somewhat deprecative in his feedback, is immensely knowledgeable about the course material and demonstrates a passion for facilitating academic growth in his students. This instructor never fails to reinforce his reputation as among the most difficult professors in the department and stands as a formidable test of an individ

He's very smart and knows the material, but in the papers he's only looking for his regurgitated lecture. He doesn't like new or differing opinions. He is the rudest grader I have ever had. It's not helpfully critical, it's just mean critical.

I've taken Preiss' class as an undergrad as well as a grad student, and both classes were phenomenal. He's my favorite instructor. It IS possible to get an A in his class, you just have to work really hard. He's very helpful if you go to his office hours, and he respects students who make an honest effort in his classes. His lectures  are the best

DESTROYS your papers. He will tear them apart if you try and put your own opinion in. He really knows the subject and his lectures are really interesting though. Definitely do the reading before class because he gives pop quizzes.

Hardest professor you will have at the University of Utah. Period. He is also close to impossible. He has his own imaginary "style guide" in his head that you only have access to if you visit him during office hours. Will dock your paper for using words he personally does not like (ex: utilizes, because, etc.) Be warned, or brace yourself!

This Shakespeare class is one of the hardest I've ever taken. The information is fascinating and Preiss is obviously very well educated. He is a tough grader and his feedback is brutally harsh - and he knows it. It's meant to help you grow and see all your room for improvement.  If you pay attention and echo is patterns of research - you'll be fine

He is extremely condescending and his essays are the toughest. He abuses you when he grades your essays and says that you will thank him later for it. He's a nice guy when you talk to him one-on-one, but he isn't to anyone's interpretations of the texts besides his own. It was a very tough class.

Richard is one of the most intimidating professors I've ever had. He's cynical, abrasive, & brilliant. He's a very tough grader, but it IS possible to get an A in his class. He takes a long time grading papers, but I appreciated his thoroughness. He pushes you, and, ultimately, his class was one of my favorite classes. Side note: he's very witty.
I learned a ton in this class, but it was the hardest of my English classes. Preiss is tough, but he wants you to do well.

Preiss is a very difficult teacher. If you do not have time to talk to him during office hours don't take his class.  He seems like an ass but he is only trying to push you...A LOT!! I learned a ton from him and want to find as many classes as I can, although I do not get as good of a grade as I do in my other English classes I learned a ton.

Preiss is admittedly smart, but he's also opinionated and condescending. Grading isn't based on forming an opinion, but in mirroring his opinion. He makes wild extrapolations based only loosely on the text. If you're taking this course, be prepared to regurgitate his opinions, and hope you pick the points he finds important.

Preiss is obviously extremely intelligent and he clearly has a passion for his subject matter, so he can be quite engaging. However, because he is so passionate about the material he tends to be very opinionated and closed off to other interpretations of the text. Not so great in class, better to discuss paper topic etc. with him during office hour

He lets u make up ur own questions for paper topics which is extremely hard. but if u go into his offices before each paper he ups ur grade substantially. Ended up learning sooo much. Yes e was difficult but so worth it

Honestly Preiss is VERY difficult. Its his opinion or no opinion. This idea is what made the class difficult. I couldn't agree with his opinions a lot of the time and rather than reading/listening to another input he grades you down. If you are looking for a challenge he is your guy. Speaking with him, really funny and nice. Hard professor!

If you are up to a challenge, feel confident about your ability to interact with the text and boldly articulate those thoughts, then you should take his class.  He is not for the faint-hearted, and his warnings about the feedback from your first paper will still not prepare you fully for what you'll get.  Don't be scared, just prepared!

If he wasn't so rude and unapproachable he would be a great teacher. The class would be more interesting and engaging if he would allow students to explore their interpretations and ask questions without putting them down. Your papers and comments have to match his ideas or they are no good.

Obviously very knowledgeable, but seems to treat Undergrad students as Grad students - expecting too much for an Intro course. Paper comments are often pithy and unhelpful. Likes to demonstrate the material rather than teach it. Paper topics range from challenging to schizophrenic (one "question" involves multiple REQUIRED sub-questions).

He will not spoon feed, especially with writing assignments.  Likes inventive ideas if they've been thought through; if you don't get it go get help outside of class.  Otherwise, original and very good on context.

Professor Preiss is VERY HARD, but I learned more from him in one semester than I have in years!  If you are a tender hearted person DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! He isn't nice but he will help you.  Also, it is hard to know what he expects a lot of the time which I think is part of his strategy.  Overall, I loved his class, but it wasn't easy.
Over critical.  Rude.

Listen, folks: not for those who think education is being confirmed in their errors or who confuse ignorance with "creativity". Those not interested in learning and the risks therein need not apply. If you believe reading, thinking and writing are easy, you won't get him or the material.

Writing assignments remind me of throwing darts at an imaginary dart board. Unclear about expectations, rips you a new one on papers, offers advice that does nothing. Has problem of supporting students who think what he thinks, and generally shoots down anyone with an idea different from his, or deems it too shallow. If you want a prof. that will m

He completely refused to discuss the Da Vinci Code at all! He just doesn't want students' minds to be free!!!! :( Also, it turns out that all of these writers have been dead like, a really really long time.  !!!

Organized and interesting lectures are limited by his authoritarian teaching style.  He is not supportive of student's creativity or deeper exploration of the subject matter.  Color inside the lines, or else!
No Comments
He's the most pedantic, worthless **** at the U of U.

The final is pretty much a joke, as he goes over all the answers in person.

Girls beware! The professor was really sexist and touched some of the female students without their consent. I honestly recommend against taking this course because of his behavior. Class was super easy, and would have been a lot of fun if the prof didn't make everybody so uncomfortable. Prof sometimes freaked out over tiny things.
Very cool instructor and gave good feedback on how to improve your bowling technique. An easy and fun way to get an extra credit into your schedule. Would reccomend

Super fun class as you get time allotted in your class schedule to just go bowling. He teaches you a lot about bowling that you aren't required to retain. Class is easy, you just show up and bowl. Your bowling performance doesn't have any effect on your grade. He gives you all the answers to the exam too. Pretty funny and cool guy that will help your bowling score a ton. He had a couple random freak outs about insignificant things but it wasn't common.

Beginning Bowling - Fall 2021.
It's a bowling class. Troy readily acknowledges that people take this for fun, which is why the test is so... simple :) He still teaches a lot though- my bowling form improved a TON, and he takes the time to individually help everyone as they work on the things he teaches.

Troy was a chill instructor, he gives you a lot of information, but you don't need to retain it. He gives you tips on how to bowl better, but lets you be unless you ask for help. He helped me double my average, he gave good, constructive feedback and was able to help me with technique, even being left handed. He's a really friendly, cool dude.

Troy is an amazing teacher! I increased my bowling average from about 80-90 to over 120! The class is a ton of fun, basically after he teaches you the basics about bowling you get to come to class everyday and compete against other bowling teams in the bowling tournament! Extremely easy class. Would definitely take again. An easy way to get an extra credit into your schedule.

Can be creepy.
He is super caring about each student and that they can succeed in his class. Best teacher for the class. TONS of extra credit ( a whole entire grade letter bump)
Carson is super great and very lenient -- He makes sure you get a good grade
WHAT ARE YOU WAITING FOR ?? REGISTER FOR HIS CLASSES ANY OF THEM HE IS AN AMAZING TALENTED GUY YOU WILL NOT WANT TO MISS A SESSION OF CLASS. CARSON THANK YOU FOR WHAT YOU DO!!!!
One of the best in the department you will love it!!!
His class is so easy he literally makes sure everyone is encouraged to learn by giving extra credit opportunities, and making the class fun.

There's a reasonable amount of work but as long as you're on top of them you should be fine. Just don't let it stack because some excel assignments take time to work on especially capstones.
Awesome professor!
Carson was probably one of the best professors I have ever had. Simply, because he provided a lot of extra credit opportunities for the students. His exams weren't that difficult.

Honestly my best professor this semester. He is very young but smart, cares and understands what it's like to be a freshman. Carson was a super good teacher to have.

This guy is the GOAT!!! Teaching for his first full semester and I didn't even notice, everything went smoothly except the course assignments which were not his fault but the directory's. Carson you are the guy I would 10000% recommend anyone doing IS 2010 to take this class with him. Thank you Carson!!!
Great class & I learned a lot. Be prepared to have lots of little assignments, but it is 100% manageable.

His first semester teaching but he was good. The class has a lot of assignments and lectures and there were some issues with the content but that's not his fault. He definitely tried his hardest with the class and you could tell he really cared about his students
His class took complex topics and made them straightforward and easy to digest. His deliverables clearly ladder up to the learning objectives for the class. He is caring and reasonable.
Very respectful professor who gives clear guidance on class objectives that match his lesson plans

I can't say he goes above and beyond, but he meets the requirements. Try to get started earlier than later on the group project.

Professor Stan is an exceptional educator. With his extensive market experience, he delivers practical and straightforward classes. His supporting materials are also very useful. I would definitely enroll in any other classes taught by him.

Stan was a great instructor. He's knowledgeable and brings a lot of practical and real world experiences. Stan is reasonable and a great personality. His class can be heavy on theory with databases and there is a lot of SQL programming you have to get through in a few weeks time, but Stan is patient and offers extra credit to bump up your score.

He's a fun professor, and did a good job teaching the material for the most part. Some lectures were a little too fast for the complexity, but there were time constraints to meet. I didn't think the reviews prepared me for the exams as well as they could've, because they were too vague or not precise enough.
At the beginning of the classes, he might seem serious but with the time you get to like how he addresses the content and compares it with his real-life experiences.
I really enjoyed the class and professor. I thought that his way of teaching material which to me was difficult made it easy to understand and I felt like he was good at conveying and teaching.

Professor Stan was a great instructor. He is a subject matter expert and taught the material in a way that was understandable to even the most novice person in the classroom. He was patient, understanding, and willing to answer all questions. He is reasonable with his grading scale and provides opportunities for additional credit. Great instructor

Loved his class. The lecture could be fast paced as it covers lots of materials in short amount of time, but it is very well structured and easy to follow if you actually focus on the class. He is super friendly and gives lots of encouraging feedbacks.

He is one of my favorite professors! He is generous with grading and truly wants his students to succeed. He would never let us fail without support. He explains concepts clearly and teaches very well. I honestly wish all of my graduate courses were taught by him. He genuinely cares about his students and goes above and beyond to support them.
Thoughtful and provided work related experience and lessons that helped put the coursework in perspective.  The TA he had was also helpful outside of class on the labs and assignments.

The professor is boring, and its a boring class just needed to take for credit. The assignments were easy considering working with python but he let us use AI to code. Major issues in both assessments and assignment feedback. Exam questions were poorly constructed, misaligned with the taught material, and lacked clarity, resulting in a stressful and confusing testing environment.

He's a really good professor that cares and will work with you. I took his class online during the summer. Pretty easy, things would be due just once a week. Some group work which can be hard for an online class if you don't stay on top of it. I enjoyed the class and the professor.

Really good professor and happy to help students. A bit frustrating because you would ask a question and he'd either say "i don't know" or would give a vague answer that isn't really helpful. This class can be a bit fast if you have absolutely no experience coding.

Jeff was a great and knowledgable teacher. The subject material wasn't necessarily interesting to me, but that doesn't mean that it might be more interesting to someone who likes linguistics. Material was sometime shard to understand, but there were never any tests, just a few assignments, a group project, and a short final paper.

Best teacher I've had since I've transferred to the U. Helpful and approachable. Always available for meeting outside of class. Will work with your schedule of last minute problems arise. The couple quizzes throughout the semester are super easy if you pay attention and they are online. Great teacher great class! Would definitely take again.
Taught using slides and bookwork. It was alright, but some of the questions on the test were so far out from what we studied. He also take FOR-EV-ER to respond to issues, like his site being down.

This was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. Attendance is not mandatory, but showing up for class is  helpful for the homework and quizzes, despite what the other reviewer said. This is not an easy course and is a LOT of work. Don't blame Jordan for doing poorly. He is willing to help you understand the concepts, just ask him!

This class was took a lot of time due to Jordan explaining the material in a confusing way. If you are able to create a study group you will do MUCH better in this class. If you have a busy schedule I do not recommend taking this class!

You can definitely tell Jordan knows alot about Statistics, but he is absolutely AWFUL at teaching it. I'm sure if I was a Stats Major I could easily understand what he was trying to say. Going to class is useless becuase he just talks in circles. You're better off teaching yourself, I know I did. TAKE SW 3000 instead

This class was definitely not easy.  The math part wasn't particularly difficult, but Jordan explains things in a very confusing manner.  What I do like about him is that his exams are open notes and book which is nice. I did well in the class but I had to use other resources and I had to spend long amounts of time to figure things out for myself

Unfortunate that a required class is taught by a tech adverse individual. If you have a difficult time understanding thick accents, good luck!!! Half of lectures are from original professor, half from this one and they DO NOT align. Only good thing I can say is she is sometimes flexible with due dates if you tell her you're struggling with content.

FSC 3370. Professor always got back to emails and was very kind. However, there is a group project in this class that made it difficult. Fair class and teacher. Group quiz every Friday. Attendance not mandatory.

reviews.comment: His accent can be very hard to understand sometimes. The weekly quizzes are quite difficult. Becuase I took AP calc it was mostly review, but if I hadn't this class would be insane.

Pretty good for a pre-cal class. He has an accent but you get used to it. The homework online, textbook is free. There are weekly quizzes so you need to be prepared for those. There were two midterms and a final that are worth 40% of your grade. He hands out study guides for all his tests and his finals are very similar so its not so bad.

The homework was very reasonable, maybe 2-3 hours a week at most. His course is much more theoretical than practical, which isn't necessarily good or bad, but I liked it. His lectures were clear and concise, and there was more than enough time to ask questions. He adapted his syllabus and style frequently based on student feedback.

Horrible!! Homework is extremely challenging, he is a tough grader on exams and expects the students to know much more about the class even though he teaches. The most difficult and confusing math class I've ever taken. Also assigns homework over university breaks which does not seem fair. I strongly DO NOT recommend anyone to take this class.

This has by far been THE WORST class I've taken in college so far. The homework is very difficult compared to his lectures and doesn't help prepare for the exams. The lectures are confusing and challenging to follow. The work required is that of a 5000-level class even though this is supposed to be a 2000-level introductory class. Avoid this class!

Diffy is a tough subject, to begin with. He takes his time to make sure every student understands the material. He gives plenty of learning opportunities with office hours and weekly hwk. The hwk is tough but again Diffy is a hard class so don't be surprised by hard hwk. His tests are relatively easy compared to his hwk.

This was probably the worst experience I've had in a class in college. This is supposed to be an intro class and he gives homework at a 5000 level. His lectures go over every single person's head. He grades very harshly without a clear explanation as to why you lost points. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!!!

Sucks when you might have to retake this class with someone else now because the teacher you picked doesnt value your education AT ALL. I did all of the homework and quizzes and still got a poor grade which sucks now. 2020 is the worst YEAR!!! DONT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM

reviews.comment: This is not an easy class but Prof. Quin will make it worth your while. The textbook is in English and it's heavy on social and economic analysis. Lectures make you see Latin American civ and cult from a different perspective, not the typical cultural clichés. But you have to be willing to do the work to learn.

reviews.comment: Super sweet professor! She is so understanding and makes learning super easy. Ensures we are all knowledgeable about the material and goes over notes a lot in class. There is a lot of homework, but if you stay on top of it then it is super easy and manageable. If you don't do it though, your grade will really be affected.

Wiggins was a great professor. I took 1010 and 1020 with her. I already knew a lot of French before coming, so it was very easy for me. Regardless, she made sure everyone understood where we were and clarified anything necessary. She was very generous with grading.
Such a good professor. Learned a lot from her and would totally recommend. She let us out early from our 2 hour class which was super nice!

I had her for french 3116 3117 and 3118 not 1020 btw, but she is a great professor grades very easily and cares for your grade and is very nice. You will not see little if at all quizzes, and just a lot of writing and participation

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Wiggins was an amazing French professor. She spent time really making sure that students were understanding the topics being covered and provided lots of practice opportunities! She was also a very generous grader. There is daily homework but it is manageable and not very hard.

I took the regular ECE 1230 + Lab. Rasmussen definitely cared about her students and her lectures were so chill. She is a bit confusing to understand sometimes but she is always open to questions. Your grade is mainly determined by exams, but you are able to retake all of them at the end of the semester.

The tests in this class were incredibly easy with a favorable grading system. Professor Rasmussen cares about students and does a good job explaining topics. The accelerated class was not difficult in the slightest and I would highly recommend this course.

I really enjoy this professor. She is super nice and is easy to ask questions too. Her canvas page is a bit messy but overall it's not too bad. I do wish she went a bit more in depth during lectures. The class environment is really calm and the TA's are super helpful.

Prof. Rasmussen as a person is very kind and more than willing to help you learn. However, the course is horrendously unorganized, it is unclear what exactly to study for, and the majority of the class is just as confused. If you actually want to learn, read the textbook or find outside study materials.

I took her for the new accelerated ECE 1220/1230/1235. I do believe Angela Rasmussen is a goated person, and her passion about what she is teaching definitely shows, but this was the most unorganized learning environment of my entire life. Some of the TAs were completely useless, the canvas was complete unorganized slop, and the labs were crappy.

She is very clear and always is willing to help you if you're having trouble. There isn't much homework, but the quizzes and homework can be annoying because they're only a few questions each. While she does do partial credit and makeups, messing up on a single question can be the difference between passing and failing a test.

Graded on very few things, namely: weekly homework, weekly quizzes, and four exams (none cumulative). Homework was time consuming but not hard. Quizzes are a pain in a butt and drop your grade a bit if you fumble. Exams are hard and require studying or they will tank your grade. Rasmussen is all over the place but she is kind and accommodating.
Very nice person and accommodating, but the class was just hard to follow and everything in it felt random and difficult to follow. Feel like she made it overly complicated, but was a nice person.

Teaching an Intro to Circuits class I can't imagine as easy. For that, Professor Rasmussen does a pretty good job at explaining things in different ways until everyone gets the topics, and is more than happy to explain her thought processes. The 1240 course was easy if you actually study/practice on your own. You won't get it down the first time.
way better than cotter.

Very nice person and was willing to accommodate, but was very disorganized with exams, homework, and quizzes hard to follow. The best word that I would describe this class would be random, a lot of spontaneity.
Professor was nice but often late and disorganized. Lecture notes were hard to follow.

I had 2210. She was trying her best but was thrown into teaching this class short notice and clearly didn't have time to be doing so. I could tell she cared because she always asked for feedback and was very responsive. Exams were open note and grading was forgiving. Unfortunately, the class was a bit of a mess which made it more difficult.

While there were a good number of assignments, she makes sure you have done enough of them that you are plenty comfortable with the problems and material before a quiz or exam. Lectures are on zoom and recorded but try not to get behind as there are a lot of little things you might miss that end up on the exams. Lab was challenging, but fair.
Great experience. Did a great job at teaching difficult material to an audience of students being exposed to the subject matter for the first time.

Amazing professor, lectures, and class layout. I felt like the class structure prepares you well for the exams and I actually understood the content. Professor Rasmussen is super flexible and willing to work with her students!

Prof. Rasmussen is the best. She gives the best lectures and posts so much learning material there is no reason for you not to know what's going on. 
She's a little disorganized and sometimes forgets to post things (quizzes etc.) But overall, an amazing professor.

This has been my favorite ECE class to date. She cares about the subject and about her students. Lectures are very similar to what's on the exams. Class time is mostly spent going over numerous practice problems. Labs are definitely time consuming as well as homework, but the homework is also very similar to what's on the exams.

Dr. Rasmussen takes complex electrical concepts and boils them down into some easy steps that can be used to solve any of the problems in the class. For each subject she hands out note packets with explanations and procedures but they've been copied so many times that they're illegible. She prepared us well for the tests and I got 'A's on them all.

Dr. Rasmussen is an awesome professor. Her lectures consist of several examples very similar to those that are tested. The homeworks can be long but she always answers questions on them during class. Coursework is well reflected on exams and quizzes.

Looks like my review got deleted so I will try this again. Very unorganized, Tests are worth most of your grade but there are only 3 problems on each midterm so it is very difficult to get a good grade in this class. You have to learn everything by yourself.

First time taking a class with Angela. She is very smart and knows how to teach. Her lectures reflect what is on the test. She gives small lectures and does many problems during class. Answers any questions and helps during office hours. Labs are time consuming as well as homework. But tests are okay as long as you go to class and follow along.

New homework are due every week, none of them were graded in time. So, you don't get any kind of feedback when you need. You have to study on your own, as concepts and background are not given on any topics. Each class time will be spent trying to solve 1 to 3 circuits problems without first introducing the basic concepts.

Materials are presented in a awful manner. The handouts, solutions, or examples provided are so blurry that you will have a headache trying to decipher.  Homework and tests are never graded in time. The tests were not given back even after 2 weeks. More than that not a single assignment or quiz was graded even after first test.

Angela memorizes the students names.  She was forced to teach this class, that's why it's not her forte.  She does a pretty darn good job considering that.  She grades mercifully especially because she understands that she struggles to teach it.  Shame on the U o U for making her teach this.  This engineering dept's organization is very poor.
She is a great professor. A little hairbrained, but always willing to help. Also there were a lot of mistakes in her notes, but she fixed them as they went along. Very easy to get an A.

I enjoyed classes taught by her, she follows her notes for lecture and that's it, derailing lecture by asking something bizzare can ruin the class for everyone.  The best lectures were the ones with most the questions after she go through her notes.  I also had her for my sen proj advisor and she will help you if you need it, just talk to her.

Although this professor is a nice person to talk to in her office hours she uses pre-prepared slides she does not teach outside of such slides and they are riddled with errors. I barely passed this class because of this, if someone asked her a question outside of her notes she would give student a blank stare usually and say "I don't know"

Nice person but terrible professor.  She does not seem to have the time to prepare and teach effectively.  Bad communications skills.  Organization is terrible. Never in her office. She doesn't seem to have enough practical knowledge to answer questions. In my opinion she should stop teaching or change drastically.  Again I like her as a person.

I had ECE 2280 with her and she was a very nice but a terrible teacher. She doesn't seem to have practical knowledge. She can't understand let alone answer questions. She is unorganized and her teaching style of using a pre-made PDF that had tons of mistakes was not effective to say the least. I would not take a class from her if I could help it.

very bad professor. does not follow the text. half her notes on the website are wrong. She does not put any effort teaching. She just uses some notes she took from books here and there, if you ask her anything out of that she does not know the answer to it.

EXCELLENT professor!  She taught the class well enough that I never once opened the book and was able to get an A.  One thing to remember is that it is an engineering class and REQUIRES practice (homework) in order to keep up.  Resources were provided to be able to prepare for all the exams as long as one put the time in to learn the material.

I took both 1270 and 1020 with her. Since the 1020 is a self base studying class I managed to get the CR grade. However, I strageled to get a good grade in her 1270 class. She seems like she knows things but she does not know how to teache things. I passed the class just because I had a tutor.

Had her for 2 classes. I didn't do well in either. I wasn't up on the reading.  Engineering courses really suck up your time and Rasmussen's class is no exception.  Its hard to separate the difficulty of the material from the teaching ability of the teacher. She teaches a fair class, but you're responsible for learning the material.

Had her for ECE 2100 and ECE 3110. Gave tons of homework and assignments. Second class she was better as it seemed more her forte. Doesn't seem to understand questions from students very well. Good professor overall
Every semester she has gotten better and better.  She is one of my favorite professors and I would never hesitate to take more classes from her.
Ok teacher but does not follow the text.

I had her for her first year teaching at the U of U, but signals and feedback systems didn't seem to be her forte. Had a "deer caught in headlights" look when asked questions. Hope she's improved since then.
She doesn't teach the whole period.  She needs to actually prepare a lecture for the full class period.

Shalabi was a good professor. Lectures are just going through the provided textbook and filling it out. You are not graded on attendance but the lectures or filled out textbook are not provided online. So, if you miss a lecture, it is difficult to make up.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rania is extremely passionate about teaching and cares a lot about participation! Class is everyday, with one quiz a week, and lab on Thursday's. If you pay attention and copy everything she writes down into your packet you will do well. She drops 3 quizzes, 3 labs, and a midterm at the end of the semester if you have a higher score on your final.

She was genuinely happy to be teaching. Her lectures are very engaging and her teaching methods are clear. She is also very open to helping you succeed in this class. This course is homework heavy yet if you plan it out correctly, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rania Shalabi has the unique ability to turn complex ideas into simple and understandable concepts. She connects with her students and wants them to succeed. She knew each of us by name and understood our learning at an individual level. Her lectures are thoughtful and helpful. I highly recommend taking a class from Professor Shalabi. She's great.

Professor Rania is the BEST Business Calc professor. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is great during lectures and gets through materials in a timely manner. On top of this she goes above and beyond to give students extra material help. I would recommend taking her over the only other professor offered to teach MATH 1100

I took Business Calculus 1100 with her and she did an amazing job making the hard concepts and the class, easy to excel at. I felt very prepared for the exams and quizzes, and her note sheets every class helped learn the information in an effective way. 10/10 the best math teacher I could have asked for to take my first calculus class.

Took Math 1100 with Shalabi. She genuinely cares and explains material clearly. Lectures follow the content closely and highlight what's on tests. The class is hard because it's calculus, not her teaching. Fast-paced with lots of homework and quizzes. Stay on top of it and ask questions—she's helpful and wants you to succeed.

She was way better than the other business calc professors at the U. She  actually went through the material and the content was very similiar to the quizzes/tests/homeworks. She also explained each new concept.

Professor Rania Shalabi is an awesome Math professor! She's extremely kind, caring, and makes a great effort to help. She provides multiple ways to solve a problem when available and even goes over the homework problems before and after. The LA in my Lab was very helpful and was always happy to help, I found the Labs were very beneficial to me.
Dr. Shalabi is kind and very approachable.

reviews.comment: Professor Rania does not speak English well, many words can be very distracting, and she goes fast she  also loves to use the overhead, not the grease board. 2 quizzes per week. one in class, one in the lab. The TA in lab class is not a useful learning tool. No roll call taken after 1st couple wks. Prefers overheard with laptop vs grease board.
I loved her class! This professor is very clear, so caring and an amazing teacher and person.

She's patient, approachable, and truly invested in her students' success. Her lectures are clear and engaging, and she's great at breaking down difficult concepts. While the coursework can be a bit demanding with regular assignments and quizzes
Rania is fantastic! She genuinely cares about her students and makes sure everyone stays on track. Her explanations are clear, and she's always willing to help if you're stuck.

Rania is incredibly supportive and always there to help. She'll reassure you and reach out if you're struggling to understand something. There's quite a bit of homework and quizzes, but her clear and straightforward teaching style makes it easier.

The professor is truly amazing! She is incredibly caring and passionate, and her lectures are always engaging. However, be ready for a lot of assignments and quizzes. Keep in mind that calculators are not permitted.

She definitely has an accent but its pretty easy to understand. Class was good, i've never been good at math and she made it clear and easy to understand. Class has lab run by TA's to solidify any questions and get some extra practice in.
‏Wonderful professor! She is a very caring and passionate professor and her lectures are interesting! Be prepared to so many assignments and quizzes. Calculator is not allowed.

I loved Professor Shalabi for this class. She explains topics very well, and is always willing to answer questions and help you to further understand topics. She makes an effort for her students to understand and apply what they are learning. I highly recommend!

reviews.comment: She will continue and ramble on for hours and hours and you will not understand what she is saying. She will not teach you and for each exam you will have to study hours and hours just to pass the class. She goes at a crazy fast pace and you do not know what she is writing. Does explain the steps that she is doing. No calculators at all for exams.
Rania will work with you, reassure you, and reach out if it seems you don't understand. There is a lot of homework and quizzes but you can follow her. She is straightforward and clear.
The professor explains as the book says, attendance is important to make sure you know the info and you are up to date. She is a pretty fast replier and will work with you if you need help.

first of all she will rant too much about the lessons we're learning and over explain things to where it could easily be simpler, second of all she usually has 2-4 homework assignments due each week, and third of all she has a strong accent so sometimes it's hard to understand her

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't have the best explanation technique, sometimes she over explains and it can make it just harder

She talks at 97 mph so you can't understand anything she's saying because you're writing down things from page 2 when she's on 13 so don't take.
Lectures don't make sense and I feel like i'm not learning in class but with friends outside of class.

I feel Professor Shalabi genuinely cares, and wants her students to succeed. I like her accent. I love that she is an educated hajib wearing woman. It's great we can drop our lowest quizzes! She could have better control of the class, and explain some concepts more clearly. Saying “Does that make sense?” repeatedly doesn't make it, make sense.

Business of Agriculture with Dr. Shrader was really fun. Not as much math as her other classes, but it was way interesting to learn about agricultural markets and current events. Group projects are actually fun. happy I took this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I honestly loved Shrader, and it was evident that she truly cares about her students. She's flexible with office hours, responds quickly to emails, etc. Overall in my opinion, the class can be a bit boring sometimes, and the exams are def tougher than the practice ones, but if you apply yourself from the start, you'll be fine.

Shrader is the best! I had her for QAMO 2010 last semester in teh large class. Her handwritten notes to go along w the slides were helpful, and she always posted teh slides. I liked her connections to the real world. Def listen up in class, go to the tutor pool, and study the practice tests, and you should do fine.

Dr Shrader's class is overall great! she does require mandatory attendance so its important to go otherwise your grade can get docked points. as long as you do the weekly quizzes and do the practice tests a couple times before completing your exam you should be totally fine. she also curves the class on a pretty generous curve which def helps out

I liked Dr. Shrader. She uniquely used hand-written notes that transferred nicely into students notebooks. It's tough teaching a class with 250+ students but she did it, and she did it well. My recommendation is to do your homework and take the practice exams a few times pre-exam. The actual exam often has similarly structured questions.
Do your practice exams and you will be fine
She's amazing and always has a positive attitude. You can tell she has a passion for what she does

reviews.comment: Classes are taught in big lecture hall so it can be hard to concentrate. The notes she takes are terrible and she is bad at explaining things but the class is curved heavily.

reviews.comment: One of the professors that I've had. The tests are tough, but everything is curved and her and the TAs are super accessible if you need help. Participation does matter, its apart of your grade and it makes a big difference in how well you understand the material. She was a very fun and engaging lecturer and I learned a lot from the class!
Shrader reallly knows her stuff. I am loving the modeling of markets and competition with algebra and calculus. Truly grateful that she is challenging us and teaches as if we are intelligent.
I hate that this class is mandatory, she moves too fast on the material and doesn't upload the in class notes to study for the test. You can't miss any days and over is not a good class.

This class was taught in a massive lecture hall making it hard to learn anything. She explains things fine but I found it was easiest just to go to the tutor pool and learn the entire unit before the exam. class was curved like crazy and most students averaged around a 75% on the exams but realistically if you study moderately getting a 85+ is easy
Shrader is my favorite professor this semester! The class is so interesting that I may decide to take calculus and take her qamo 3010 next.

this woman is the pink girl from the harry potter movies. words cannot describe how frustrating she is. one time she screamed at us because ‘we don't listen to her, she's a woman'. dunno where that came from but go off queen

All the Qamo 2010 sections seem to cover the same content, and there's a lot. Professor Shrader makes the lectures interesting and works through practice problems. She has been really happy to help me during office hours and explains things great. An awesome professor and is there to help. I hear the curve is generous if you put the effort in.

She is fun and seems to be a good person. She is enthusiastic about teaching and seems to care to a certain extent about her students. She has plenty of office hours. ON THE OTHER HAND, there is no textbook for QAMO 2010 but she tests on subjects she didn't go over in class. She has criticized the students for not knowing things she didn't teach.

Dr. Shrader is knowledgeable and approachable, but her class has challenges. Grading in-class questions on accuracy feels unfair since the material is often new. She's lecture-heavy and introduces content late, sometimes right before exams. Laptops/phones are banned without permission, which feels restrictive. Pay attention during class!

I really liked the class structure and our professor, Dr. Shrader. You need to complete the online lectures and readings before class, then class is more discussion based. Tests were hard and I didn't expect to finish but they were curved. Need to be active in class. Calculus is used.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was a great professor but the curve system was bizzarre. Some semesters the curve is very generous while others it is not, for the same content. Makes it unevenly graded.
Class is a little hard. She made exams super hard for some reason and then gave a very generous curve. Good teacher though, clearly likes what she does.

Great professor, gives long lectures that sometimes drone on, but during the lectures she does a problem that is nearly identical to what the homework will be which really helped me grasp and apply the material! Very kind and accessible, would definitely take classes with her in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She has a flipped classroom style which was the first I've had, but the lectures before class weren't too long and if you needed any clarifying, she would explain at the next class. Overall an effective course and I feel as though I learned a lot from her. The only grievance I had was her "no technology" rule, otherwise a successful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Shrader was awesome for QAMO 3010. Her lectures were always enjoyable, and she takes a lot of care to explain difficult concepts repeatedly through examples. The tests were straightforward and generously graded. Homework wasn't too difficult, each set maybe takes 3 hours and there's at most one per week. Shrader is a great professor.

Had Dr. Shrader for QAMO 3010. Super kind teacher. Her lectures are well structured, and she makes notetaking easy. No papers. Problem sets and prep assignments and readings weekly, but it does not amount to much work at all. Exams follow the class material very closely, so If you feel prepared you will likely do well. Recommend for QAMO students!

If you don't have experience in economics do not take this class period. Although Shrader was a good conversationalist, I did not enjoy the flipped class style. She does not record lectures and post them and the TAs are very tough on participation. If you're going to take this class, be ready to read a lot.
Very challenging class if you don't have economic background. If you are a QAMO major I recommend taking 3010 over 2011.

Great teacher! Extremely nice and breaks down the material very clearly. Make sure you go to class because some of the topics can be complicated and hard to figure out without the background in class. This class is generally on the harder side, but my class had a really nice and big curve at the end.

If your a QAMO/Business major I would recommend, and if not I would not recommend this professor. As a senior this is the only professor that I had that had mandatory attendance, and their TA would literally watch and track if you spoke EACH class, also the final exam had irrelevant probs like; "what was that quote I always said in class".

Shrader is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's knowledgable, kind, and the reverse classroom structure was extremely effective. The content of this class was difficult but she made it understandable. I recommend her to everyone!

Shrader was an outstanding professor for this class. The class is flipped, so lectures are online, and discussions are in class. Make sure to read the articles as they are main focus for prep quizzes. Make sure to study hard, but the class is not too difficult. The rough draft of the journal is graded like a final, so make sure you revise it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Shrader and this class. This class was very interesting and I love the topics we learn. She is a good teacher and we have good discussions in class.

Best professor Ive had in the business school. Didnt even get the grade I wanted in her class and I would happily take it again based off of the value I felt I got from learning in her class. If you want an easy A look elsewhere, if youre here to learn things that will impact the rest of your life, Shrader will go above and beyond expectations

Shrader is an amazing person and is helpful if you go to office hours but the class is incredibly hard for really no reason. Participation is graded in that you have to do more than just talk, it's weird. The tests are made with the goal that no one gets 100% and are confusing at best. I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you can help it.

Shrader is a nice person but the class is unnecessarily hard. The quasi-flipped class structure makes it hard to engage with the material. Her tests are also extremely hard, and makes the average a B with few getting above that. She is super helpful during office hours, but there is only so much you can do outside of exams to help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Shrader is a nice instructor and cares for her students. However, I had issues with her class since she is a tough grader. Sometimes the content was incoherent and difficult to understand. She's a tough grader but very understanding. It was difficult to get an A, but pay attention in class.

I had a love-hate relationship with Shrader. Throughout, the semester I didn't love how harshly she graded and the level of difficulty of the tests. When the semester ended, I realized that it was all worth it. She really cares about her students and makes a TON of time to work with students outside of class. Also, just super kind.

Dr. Shrader is very nice, helpful, and cares about her students. She's always available to help if needed and responds to email questions quickly. She gave us access to PDF copies of her lecture notes. Open note exams helped a lot; she believes that it reflected the real world better that way. Extra credit was available, always do it.

Super nice professor, but hard material and grading. Dont expect to get extra credit by emailing her a sob story, she makes her deadlines and criteria very clear. Go to her office hours and she will be super helpful.

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at the U. Computer Systems can be pretty challenging but he makes this class fun when it could other wise be super boring. The lectures are really entertaining and he has a fun way of talking about things. For most classes I skip lectures as I deem them not worth while, but his were.

He's just a chill guy. Hard class for sure, but him and his TAs provided a lot of help (the TAs this semester are goated fr). At first I was worried about him not recording lectures but the slides are very helpful. Sometimes I have trouble understanding the slides as well but the TAs did a great job in explaining the slides again.

Professor Regehr's lectures are very good and I rarely needed to reference the textbook. Assignments are hard but a lot of fun. Exams were incredibly difficult, but he applied a curve. This is my favorite course I've taken at the U.

Regeher is an awesome professor! Lectures are a bit dry and not recorded, but he does post the slides, sometimes even before class. He listens to student feedback on what we need, and he gives good feedback to us through piazza. Approachable and helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Decent speaker, lectures are always interesting + easy to follow, seems to be well respected and has taught many courses. However, he assigned ~200 pages of dense reading for the first week which is inexcusable. Also he ensures his TAs don't help with homework because "it defeats the purpose" according to him. He was good professor... a decade ago.
