reviews.comment: If you get a chance to take a graduate level course with John, please do! He's passionate about the subjects, and the classrooms turn into discussions, with course content following what people are interested in. The homework assignments are challenging but fascinating, and he's super helpful in making it a not stressful, but very educational time.

This class is a waste of money in its current state(Covid restrictions). Both professors are unhelpful, even when messaged directly. The online material is horribly unorganized and unintuitive, and nothing gets graded for weeks. There is also 0 understanding for students adversely affected by covid.

John Regehr is a pretty decent professor. He explains things that are relevant to the weekly homework (Half of the semester's hw is done on Scratch). But honestly, you don't have to go lecture at all, because you'll be practicing the material in lab the next day. If you don't understand anything, you can always go to the CADE lab for help.

Took CS 1030 for my intro class as a freshman at the U (i'm a CS major). Labs are a must-go. Not only for credit, but I def learned A LOT more in lab than lectures. Assignments were slightly difficult because I did them last minute, but nothing too insane. Lots of kids in this class already took CS in HS. Don't be discouraged if you didn't. :)

Prof Regehr is one of my favorite professors I've had at the U. Lectures are awesome, and worth paying attention to, tests are easy if you do. The programming projects are challenging, but reasonable, and always fun. I wish we'd had time to do more of them. Honestly a great class that isn't tough if you put in the effort. It taught me a ton.

Does not take into consideration the knowledge of the student so his lectures are not cared to what the class knows at all.
Maybe it was the course content but John keeps my attention during his lectures. This isn''t true for the large majority of classes I attend.

Great professor. Extremely helpful.  Stays after class to answer questions and makes sure the question is answered satisfactorily. Very helpful during office hours as well. Quick to answer emails and active on the message boards to make sure all questions are answered.  Welcomes questions and answers them full. Fun assignments. Wished we had more.
Excellent professor. Always willing to help. I feel extremely grateful to be able to take a class from him.
Confident, Clear and Simple.
No Comments

Dr. Reimer is so awesome. Its a smaller class of like 25ish and she is approachable and its very easy to ask questions and she really wants to help you learn the material. Only reason I got a B was because i'm bad at math but she makes it as understandable as possible. She's the best.
The absolute best math professor I have ever had.

I LOVED Jody. She is such an amazing professor, she is a wonderful teacher and will work with you to really make sure you understand the material. She is also just wonderful to chat with and so relatable. She's very funny and nice and is so open to getting to know you.

Dr. Reimer was one of the best math teachers I've ever had! She would take extra time to just sit with me and remember basic algebra (in a good way) and even helped give me advice about going to grad school! She really does care and does her very best to make calculus a not scary subject to approach. 10/10 do recommend!
Dr. Reimer is great. There are difficult concepts taught but the way the class is structured really forces you to understand and learn rather than memorize. She is very understanding.
Dr. Reimer makes learning difficult math concepts fun and she clearly cares about the success of her students.

Warning, this class uses Rstudio, the spawn of a graphing calculator and a coding language. Still though, despite this, Professor Reimer was great at explaining complex calculus concepts and building off of previous lectures and concepts. She did use a different method of grading, checkpoint grading, which I found to be a little bit confusing.

Let me start by saying, if you ever get the chance to take a lecture from Jody, Dr. Reimer, DO IT. I took her class for CALC I and II. She is so smart, and explains things very well. She takes time to answer questions about the algebra on tricky problems, because sometimes it gets confusing. TAKE her class, you will not regret it.

reviews.comment: She responded to my questions very quickly. The practice tests were very similar to the actual tests. Very good teacher, would recommend!!

Jody was by far my favorite professor I had this semester. She cared about our success, was willing to do what it took to help us succeed. She was very positive and seemed to love what she's doing. Would 100% recommend her for anyone thinking of taking calc.

Jody is truly a wonderful professor. She cares about the success of each of her students and puts in the work to help her students succeed. She prepares you so well for each test and grades fair. Her lectures are not manditory however the required lab attendance is manditory. TAKE HER COURSE!

I find it very hard to get a math professor that I like and teaches sufficiently. Jody Reimer is one of my favorite teachers. She is super sweet and is very fair in her grading. She is always willing to work with her students and always seems so happy to be doing what she does. Definitely recommend her for anyone thinking of taking her class!!

reviews.comment: Coop is the best kind of weird you'll find a teacher. While he rambles often, he presents information on a level that isn't over-filtered and strenuous. The textbook for the class is online and free, and the homework can be done pretty quickly.

He was amazing and very intelligent in his lectures.  He tried his best to make class interesting and was not afraid to show his humanity to his students.  Papers were doable and he graded fairly.  Very nice and genuine guy.

He is hilarious and enjoys discussing his personal life. Great class to get through the credit as long as you do the assignments, not as great if looking to learn anything new. More than willing to be there for help if it is needed.

Expect to be asking lots of clarifying questions on assignments. The lectures are long, boring, and at times inappropriate or uncomfortable. He has a tendency to ramble and speak on very personal matters. The papers are easy, but boring, dull, and hard to complete because he pushes the due dates back for almost everything. He is very unorganized.

She is not good. Genuinely never grades anything and is so hard to know what your grade is. Way too AI focused and is insanely broad on projects. Docks you for points for things that were never even required.

She's quite nice but very inconsistent; she would override the syllabus and change project instructions at the last minute. Additionally, many assignments were very busy work, with a lack of merit fully created by AI. Then didn't grade the assignments from February until April. It became frustrating when drawing with crayons in class. Nice person.
Very boring and unengaging professor, but the class is extremely easy to do well in.
She's a pretty boring, monotone professor but knows her stuff. This class was extremely easy and the exams were a joke.

I strongly don't recommend taking a class with Rita S. The grading is unclear, emails go unanswered, and Canvas does not match how the class is actually run. Attendance is marked as “not required,” yet you still get points taken off from assignments she creates. The class feels unorganized and so confusing. Choose online through any other source.

Class was easy enough. But if you value having a relationship with your professor, I wouldn't take this class. Professor takes months to grade and students have to correct and double check their own grades. Would not recommend

I took MKTG-4760 & MKTG-4730. She has great guest speakers who are actively hiring students. AI friendly. Surprise (easy) in-class assignments to make sure students show up. Expect 1-2 out of class "real world" assignments. No exams. Only critique is assignments can be random and not clear at times. Show up and check canvas. Finished with 98%.

Good lectures and guest speakers. Nothing was graded until the last week of calass. Unfortunately missed a couple classes and got so lost...Didn't respond to any emails until the last day when the Final was due. Canvas wasn't changed from the year before so it was very confusing

Taught along with Paul Campbell, and they were pretty good professors but the course was bad. Due dates kept changing and had no descriptions. Had to do 3 hours of cold calling as an assingment. Dont take this class if your not interested in sales.
The lectures were pretty interesting as an urban ecology student! The lab projects were also pretty enjoyable, you will learn how to use adobe illustrator.

he made this class fun and exciting, each week for lectures we would have a different topic to discuss. the work does get a little intensive with essays, labs, and quizzes each week but the grading is simple. all of his lab teachers are amazing too, the final was an essay which as long as you follow the rubric and template, youd get an A.
He knows his stuff, is very knowledgeable, and is very personable. This class was a prerequisite for the architecture program, but was arguably the easiest one out of the three.
educated and professional
I love this man. Best Proff I have had.

I loved this class and it was super easy. The only thing I didn't quite enjoy was the lab section of the class as the TA's weren't very knowledgeable and in my experience made it feel like I was on my own for the lab assignments. Other than this super easy class if you simply show up.

overall a very easy class. the labs were a bit difficult since you were basically on your own. lectures were interesting however this class could've easily been online or hybrid. at times it felt useless going to lecture but you do have to submit a quiz after to get points. one page essay due weekly but grading was very unclear and inconsistent imo

You aren't tested on any of the lecture content but there is an attendance quiz at the end of every class. It's password protected but the questions are easy to answer if someone sends you the password.

The class was very lecture heavy as there were very little notes and information available outside of the course. Attendance is not mandatory but if you don't show up to the lectures it is difficult to do good. The professor is amazing and knowledgeable, she makes the info easy to understand. In class exams but assignments are very easy.

reviews.comment: Ritterbush was a very sweet and hilarious individual. However, she was disorganized and never kept track of her thoughts. Even the TAs were lacking information about notes, tests, and other things for the class. For the final, she gave us no study guide and told us to study our notes, even though most weren't even filled out during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Every week you get resources like Wikia/videos/slides to help complete your homework. Super understandable about working in a group, with a partner, and by yourself. You get to choose so no stress there. You get feedback on what you did wrong. The quizzes have multiple attempts, including the exam(s) which are just questions from the quizzes.

I took Professor Ritterbush's class for a gen ed, and was surprised by how much I loved it. You learn so much, her lectures and notes are very effective, but you honestly don't have to do much work. She's also a hilarious person. I would definitely take again!

LOVED THIS CLASS!! We got to go to the zoo and aviary for free for field trips! Quizzes and exams you get multiple attempts with answers shown and she reopens assignments so you can always get a 100 on your work. She is so sweet and flexible. Do the work, get an A! Such a good professor and such a fun easy class to get gen-ed out of the way! 10/10
Tests are difficult but the class is curved. Very knowledgable, friendly, and funny guy.

reviews.comment: Extremely light homework but heavily graded on exams. He is super knowledgable and will help you if you need it!
Best professor I have taken in college. It is a more challenging course but he makes it very exciting and enjoyable, if i could take every finance course in college with him I would.
All time chiller

Overall, Professor Ringgenberg was a good professor. He's a nice and funny guy and, if you like finance, the course is interesting. The work is not hard but the exams are and the final is cumulative and he's pretty vague about what's going to be on it. If you just come to class and do the homework, you'll get at least a B though.

reviews.comment: Professor Riggenberg was a fantastic professor. I thoroughly enjoyed his class. I wish he could teach all of my classes. I had a hard time with Finance concepts before this class, and now I feel more confident in answering more finance-based questions. Highly highly recommend this class!

Called the finance god for a reason. Relates real life events to what we are learning in class. Knows so much about the subject and does a great job at going in depth but the same time helping you u detest and what you need to know. Some stuff in the class can be a little challenging but nothing bad at all. Wish I could have him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ringgenberg is without question the best professor I've had. I sit in class wishing that he could be the professor for every class I have. His lectures feel like a gripping story as opposed to a dry academic rant (& I'm not a finance student, FYI). He is receptive to questions, a clear communicator, a fair grader for HW/tests. He's 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Matt is a really smart guy and knows his stuff. He does a lot of lecturing on concepts, and not so much on computational procedures. His tests have mostly computational questions, it makes it hard to get a good grade unless you do the practice problems in the book. He does curve the final grade, so dont freak out if you dont do well on one test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He curves the grades generously and the homework he gives is super easy and almost non-existant. His tests are hard, but thanks to a generous curve, if you study and try hard you do fine compared to the rest of the class. He doesn't use the textbook at all which is nice, but means you need to take good notes to help you learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great lectures. You can really tell he cares about what he is saying and teaching. My favorite parts of the class were his asides about his work experiences and his research. Very interesting viewpoint, and a fairly easy class

Personally, I absolutely loathe finance. 3040 was beyond awful, but Matt's style of teaching will help you understand finance easier. If you don't like finance, the lectures will be boring. However, he's very flexible and generous as long as you put real effort into his class, homework, and exams. I recommend taking him for 3050.

His first semester was Fall 2016. Ignore what people are saying, I hate Finance, and he made it much easier! At first he went too fast and didn't put formulas on his slides, but he had everyone anonymously write what we liked and didn't like about him, and that came up, and he corrected it. Great professor, and very, very smart! I'd take him again.
Good Teacher, Your grades are made up of only a handful of assignments, projects, and exams. So not a lot of room for mistakes, and make sure that you don't miss due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The assignments and tests were based off of lectures and his slides. Excellent lecturer and enjoys interacting with the class. He has a paper trading group project that was really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I didn't learn a lot from Matt. I attended every class and lecture, but found that I was better off to teach myself by reading the textbook, and watching other professor's lectures on YouTube. His slides for his lectures were very unorganized and not really helpful.  I would recommend taking this class from a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Ringgenberg was great! One of my favorite professors this semester. He is knowledgable when it comes to finance. Attend his lectures, study his slides, take advantage of his practice problems, exams, and tests, and you will do great in his class. He has fun assignments and his lectures are always interesting.

Prof. Ringgenberg's first semester at the U and I had lower expectations, but he turned out to be one of my favorite professors. Cares about all students, likes when people participate, talks about current news, very knowledgeable and seems to have a decent amount of experience in the financial world. Tests, homework and project were great.

RK Yoon recently moved to University of Houston to teach Math. I was a student in her MATH 2318 Linear Algebra class. She is very passionate and knowledgeable. She also replies to emails fast and are always available for students' questions. Her homework assignments and exams are reasonable and she gives a lot of Extra Credits. Definitely a 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: RK was the best math teacher I have ever had! She gave me the confidence I needed for future math classes.

Professor Yoon made this class so fun! She rephrases concepts multiple times, so if you don't understand the first time, you have another explanation. Her grading is very generous and tests were similar to practice tests. She always has clear answers to questions. She has a bit of an accent, but is still easy to understand.

RK is a super nice and flexible. The homeworks are fairly straight forward and not very long which is nice. There are weekly quizzes, but it is easy to make up points that were lost. Tests can be difficult, but she gives a lot of partial credit so getting a good grade is pretty attainable. I strongly recommend RK!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: RK really cares about her students. She always gives us the opportunity to make up points for quizzes and wants to make sure we understand the material. Her lectures do go really fast, but the notes are on Canvas the next day or two. The tests are hard but she gives you a "cheat sheet" to bring, and posts a practice exam a few days before.

RK was a great professor. She can explain her lectures very well and her lectures are very thorough. You don't have to take notes because she uploads her notes on Canvas. Pay attention though or it will get very tough. Her exam-reviews are kind of helpful on the exams so study from them. Provides good amount of extra credit and doesn't grade harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have to take Calc 1 absolutely take it with Instructor Yoon! I loved her! Homework, quizzes, reviews, and exams are based on class notes and correlate so well that you get good practice getting familiar with concepts and making sense of different applications. Lectures are clear and if you have any questions she will take the time to explain
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very nice, however she was bad at teaching. Over half the class had no idea what she was talking about, she would ask the class if they understood and everyone just sat there. Our once a week, hour long labs with our TA was when we learned the most. Many times no one knew what was happening in class and we just had our TA teach it to us.
she is amazing, very caring and defiantly understanding

Double check that the lab is required with advisor. Exams were pretty straight forward and easy to do well on. Lab instructions are vague and sometimes contradicting, assignments took upwards of 8 hours weekly. Any and all provided resources are unhelpful or don't respond.

The lab for this class is ATROCIOUS. needs a rework so desperately. writing this as my code runs for 45 MINUTES because of how horribly the instructions tell your to write it. class itself is not too bad but the lab will have you spending 10+ hours on a one credit classs.

He seems like a cool guy that cares and his lectures are all right. He mostly reads from slides with an occasional example problem. His biggest problem was definitely how he writes homeworks and labs. There are usually a couple errors and they are usually super confusing.

On most lecture topics, Dr. Stoll would look at the slides and say “most of you should know this already,” then move on without explaining, even though most of us hadn't learned them yet. The class was also unorganized - he didn't post assignments when he said he would, exam and lab questions always had mistakes in them, and grading took forever.

I actually liked the material and project by itself, however he's got to be one of the worst professors I've had. For example for the project he gave us the wrong equation, I went to him THREE TIMES one week showing him they were wrong. After the third he gave us the right one. My group might have been the only to finish the project correctly.
Heavy Lecture, Homework hard af . Please don't take this professor

This class used way more than 3 credits of my time. The assignments are 10 pages long and its a puzzle just trying to figure out what you're supposed to do. The TAs don't have office hours and nobody answers their email. I wouldn't do well without using AI and classmates to decipher the rosetta stone labs near the end of the semester.

Kind of boring lectures, but the class was 80 minutes long, and numerical methods inherently isn't exciting, so it's not entirely his fault. Kind of hard content, but you'll pass as long as you go to class, pay attention, and turn everything in.

The hardest part about this professor is that his hws are really hard to understand. He is also newer so he's ironing out the kinks. Numerical methods I think is a slow subject and he did a pretty good job making it not a complete drag.

For the semester that I took this class it seemed so unput together, grades came out slowly (i.e. a 2+ weeks for grades to come back). The instructions for homework and lab are extremely unclear and hard to understand what they want. The final project was given very late into the semester and I feel we weren't fully prepared.

Attendance isn't taken but on wednesday we has a quiz that is for participation. Homework is nothing compared to his lectures in class. Labs are just TAs doing the work for you and he expects you to memorize full lines of code. We get no note sheet for the Lab exams. This class is pretty difficult if you don't have a buddy to help you through work.

His examples in class are simple, but they are messy. The HW is 20 times more difficult, and uses Pearson. The exams are about as hard as HW, but has partial credit and a big curve. The final project was very unclear and was more about matlab coding than dynamics. Reading the textbook will help with all concepts. Grading takes forever (2-3 weeks).
He kinda just didn't explain things very well. Tests seamed unrelated to practice material and homework.

Rob is such a great dude but he is more focused on his research than his students. His examples in class are long a tedious. The homework are alright as long as you read the book a little and go to office hours when needed. The tests though are worth over 70% of the grade and are usually unrelated to the practice and homework material.

Has potential to be a good professor, but assumes students know previous material by heart so he ends up not explaining much at all. In-class examples, homework, and exams seem to all be separate from each other, so you can't really use one to study for the others well.

Rob has made me consider switching majors. His lectures end up confusing you more then before. He goes through examples in class, and skips his steps while expecting you to understand what point of the problem he's at. The HW is insanely difficult relative to class examples and you will spend hours not knowing what you're doing. Avoid this prof :(

Wasn't qualified. She's does sound design not 3d design. She had no business teaching this class. As a teacher for the class I honestly give her a 1 but she tried so she gets a 2. She began her examples without warning and mumble instructions quietly while doing them so following along was difficult but she did record them so I'd watch those later.

She deliberately graded the most important project at the very last moment so that we wouldn't have time to revise and get a better score. And she did it to prevent students from writing course feedback about this action (because she intentionally delayed it until after the feedback deadline).

Professor Runyan is a kind, hardworking professor. Despite our class being a bit of a guinea pig class when it came to Asset Pipeline, she made sure to set aside clear goals and expectations for us on what we were supposed to achieve. Even though I joined this class not knowing how to use UE or Maya, I left this class comfortable with both.
Really helpful particularly because graphs and the formula aspects of economics/math is very difficult for me personally, she really helped out and is accessible
Super friendly and helpful and her lectures are very clear + the slides are uploaded early
Awesome!!!
Easy class but pretty boring. Super nice professor and if you get all your work done and make sure to take good notes you'll have no issues.

I feel that Ms. Ruetschlin needs to do a better job at keeping her students engaged. Other students in my class are falling asleep after she presents slide after slide, bringing no skillful teaching methods to the table. She doesn't provide any in-depth, insightful explanation at all. It's an easy A , but I would not recommend.
is very good at explaining concepts and making them easy to understand. one of my favorite professors.

I love this woman. She was so kind and knew how to teach. Things were only graded by quizzes and problems, as well as a midterm and a final. Everything was open note, which really helped me grasp the concept of the class. Overall she was amazing, so I recommend 10000% take a class from her!

The class was taught in a lecture style with a lab once a week. She was a great lecturer but I gained more out of attending my labs due to being able to work on quizzes and application problems together, which helped me learn more effectively. I got over 90% on both my midterm and final with little outside work when I attended my lab sessions.

1 quiz and 1 problem set per week basically. kind of difficult not going to lie. one midterm and one final each only worth 10% each which is nice because I am a terrible test taker. the whole class is lecturing, and i cannot keep my attention span lasting that long. i also only went to the friday class one time so lol

Catherine is the best Professor I took a class with, she's really understanding and flexible with the assignments, attendance wasn't necessary but was helpful and enjoyable. I didn't know I'd enjoy taking an economics course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Would highly recommend Professor Ruetschlin, her lectures were informative. Attendance wasn't mandatory but it is good to go to the class. The class was much more enjoyable than I assumed an ECON class would be.

I highly recommend this professor. The way she structures the course makes it very easy to stay on track, and it's never overwhelming. Her lectures are in-depth but she explains everything in multiple ways using applicable examples, making everything really easy to understand. She is truly talented, knowledgeable, and passionate in her field.
She's great! Pretty easy class, guaranteed A if you attend the discussion sections. She really knows what she's talking about and is very articulate.

Professor Ruetschlin was amazing! Very nice, and a great teacher. The class is based on quizzes, application problems, and exams. Attendance isn't mandatory because the PPT's are posted online. It is recommended not to save all of the application problems till the end since it can be a lot of work. Study guides are helpful for the exams.

Professor Ruetsclin's class was very easy. Every week you have a new quiz and set of application problems; quizzes have one attempt, while application problems have two. All the answers to the quizzes are in her slides, and the TA sessions go over application problems. Don't buy the textbook. You do not need it. Definitely attend the review days.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's awesome, class is super easy. As you do the application problems and quizzes make sure to look over the slides. After the first midterm it seemed like the weekly quizzes and application problems got a little harder

Professor Ruetschlin was so great and I would totally recommend her for ECON 2010. The class is definitely lecture based and can get very boring at times, however, she is very caring and kind. If you get the chance have a few conversations with her because she is very knowledgeable and a cool person.

The lectures were succinct and very useful. Her assignments and quizzes were also useful in reinforcing what you learned in the lecture. I highly recommend her; this class has helped me build a great foundation so that the econ classes that I am taking after have been much easier, and I understand more because of how much I remembered from herclass

She was an excellent teacher! She definetely knew what she was talking about and made her lecture very interesting. She covered all of the material that you were graded on and she was extremely helpful. I highly recommend her as a teacher.

As an intro for microeconomics she made every topic relevant to current affairs and clearly explained everything we covered. Never needed to go through the textbook since her lectures detailed everything you needed to know.

Professor Ruetschlin is amazing.  She has taken a topic that I didn't have much interest in and made it my favorite class. I look forward to her class, and I appreciate how much she cares about her students' success.  She is a wonderful teacher, she always makes it clear that she is there to help her students, and I highly recommend her class.

She's honesty such a great teacher, I like the homework and weekly quizzes a lot. She is very knowledgeable and cares about her students a lot. Econ is a tough subject but she makes it pretty easy to understand with real world examples. She moves her lectures at a great pace and everything that needs to get done is always made clear!

Professor Ruetschlin is the perfect entry-level economics professor. She clearly outlines and communicates her expectations for the class, and makes it easy to enjoy listening to her lectures. The content is covered at a steady pace which requires consistent attention while also allowing for a missed lecture here and there. 10/10 would recommend!

Great introductory Economics professor. I declared my major in economics after taking this class. The grading is really strait-forward. You listen to the lectures, read the textbook, and do a couple quizzes on them. The professor is always available to help you 1 on 1 during the office hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking a class with her. She is very respectful and truly wants to help her students. She makes classes engaging and understands that Covid has hit us all hard. Her tests are tricky but her lectures covered everything and she is always willing to help. By far the best professor to teach Econ if you are taking it for of Gen Ed.

Easy if you actually pay attention. Don't have to show up everyday but she does give a question at the end of class every other week or so to submit. Provides study guides for the midterm and final which is clutch. Don't really have to use the textbook at all. If you try to just coast along, don't expect to get an A, you'll fall behind quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Solid teacher. The other reviews are people who just hated econ in general and/or lazy. If you actually pay attention in class, the concepts will click and she encourages you to meet with her if you don't understand. Many 10 question quizzes and 4 problem sets + tests. Not hard at all if you put effort in. Friends in this class helps tremendously.

Your grade is based on weekly quizzes, 4 problem sets, 3 group presentations, and 2 exams. Everything you need to know is covered clearly in the lectures. She also posts study guides on canvass a week before the midterm/final. Her lectures are good and class discussion is encouraged. Another incentive to come to class is that she's a solid 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework assignments aren't always straightforward, and in-person lectures are absolutely disorganized and unbearable. If you are sick, she'd rather you have to come in and get everyone else sick or else she will dock points. The only way to get an excusal is to pay to see a doctor to write you a note which not everyone can afford. Do NOT take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If there's another option go with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: this class wasn't impossible to pass, just impossible to go to. she would often go off on tangents, and talked to much for you to actually learn in class. she is not a very good teacher, and everyone seemed to be annoyed by the last day.  i feel lie she meant well, but you would learn more Spanish buying the book and reading it, which she makes you

Adjunct professor. Unclear instructions, changes due dates often, the entire class was pretty exasperated with her by the end. Doesn't use the canvas calendar properly, very confusing lectures about the material, repeats herself a lot. 4 essays and 6 (I think?) tests

The class is relatively easy but a complete waste of time. As another commenter said, she speaks very quietly. Most of the class is spent in groups where she gives you time to read a section from the textbook (no need to do assigned reading). I wouldn't take another class from her but I think she has left Utah.

She talks very quietly, like she is mumbling to herself. Which means that no one can hear her. In a foreign language class, being able to hear is extremely important. It's as if she has no confidence in being in front of people, she can't express herself, and she is completely disorganized. Avoid taking a class form her if possible.

Ruchi is the best professor that I have ever had. She tries her best to prepare students for careers after university, and that comes through in all of her lessons. She is one of the brightest people I've ever met, and I loved taking Trailblazers with her.

Ruchi does not care. She acts too cool for school. She talks down to students. Grading is not straightforward. Im not sure how she is teaching with such a negative attitude. I would never recommend taking her class.

Ruchi was a great professor for Trailblazers. She focuses on ensuring that this class is something that you take with you for the rest of college/your career. She's pretty flexible and willing to work with you as long as you ask for help! Make sure to utilize the TA as they're super helpful and nice. Great class if you need internship experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ruchi is an incredible professor that really cares about her students. She works closely with her TA to ensure that grades are fair and that students are getting enough help. For Trailblazers, she really lets the students take charge but she will still guide us. She also is really good about extending deadlines if the class needs more time!
Ruchi is amazing! She really cares about her students and it shows. This is a professor to stay in contact with after class is over. She wants to see her students succeed!

Ruchi is a professor you want to stay in contact with after you finish school. She strives to provide the tools, resources, and information that will help you succeed in any role that you do. The project was the best hands on learning experience I've had at the U. Take advantage of time to meet with Ruchi if you can, she's a great support.

Ruchi is definitely one of the best professors I've had in my college career. I think she does a really good job tying her course content into the project. She is very student oriented and wants her students to succeed. That being said, the program requires a lot of work if you want to succeed. If you half ass the project it will really show.
Ruchi is awesome!! She genuinely wants to help her students succeed and tries to give students as many opportunities as possible. The guest speakers she brings in are awesome too.

Worst experience in a class at Utah. Ruchi lectures negatively about businesses and consultants but is quick to state that she was a tier 1 consultant. She brings a lot of women's studies into lectures when it truly isn't relevant. While she tries to be cool and relate to students, I get the impression she didn't relate when she was a student.

Ruchi was in consulting and therefore thinks she is the consulting queen. This class is an integrative experience where students consult with businesses. She placed herself as way more valuable than any of the clients and grades you such regardless of the client opinions. Useless lectures on topics that students have had full semester courses on

By far the hardest class I have taken at the U, but by far the best professor I have had. Dr. Steele is incredibly knowledgeable, caring, and just a stand-out great guy. He knew everyone by name. I overall learned so much about chemistry in this class. Highly recommend.

The hardest and most math-intensive class of my Chemistry Degree. He is an amazing lecturer and professor. GO TO OFFICE HOURS and discussion, and do homework with someone else ( HW took me between 8 and 12 hours a week). We did not know the grade scale till after the final (A was an 80), but it was a fair scale based on our performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is both the hardest and the best class I've ever taken. Go to office hours. Find a friend to take it with. Homework will sometimes take 10 hours to complete a 10-problem problem set. You'll be stressed about your grade, but don't be; my semester an A was an 80%.

This class has robbed me of every ounce of intelligence I thought I had going into my last semester of college. Despite that, he is a great professor and is very approachable. I do wish the grading scheme were clearer. If you haven't taken linear algebra and are not strong in math, be prepared for a humbling experience.

Honors Gen Chem 1 was certainly difficult professor Steele adds a lot more content than regular Gen Chem and the tests are much more difficult. However, professor Steele makes up for it with a lot of extra credit and he is very kind and passionate about what he teaches. I also think this class has set me up better for future chemistry classes.

Professor Steele is awesome! Chem1211 is challenging but he made it fun and was always willing to answer questions. Something he said that stuck with me was “it's your job to come to class, but it's my job to make class worth coming to”; he does his part by making class interesting so just make sure you do your part too! 10/10 would recommend :)

Great prof! He's super fun and his lectures are engaging, especially because he gives plenty of examples. Very compassionate, has lots of ways to explain things, and genuinely wants everyone in his class to succeed. 
Just keep in mind: chem 1211 is a SUPER difficult class, so don't go into it expecting anything else. It's a ton of work.

Didn't realize how ridiculously hard this class was until I took chem 2. No reason for an intro chem class to have average test scores of 60%. Did not prepare me for chem 2 since he added so much extra content that was only necessary for this class. Not helpful info for most students. He would be much better in a specified class, not gen chem.

Prof Steele is awesome. He teaches so well and really cares about your learning. This class will set you up for smooth sailing in chem 1220. The exams and homework are really hard but he really wants you to succeed and is always there to help. 
If you're not ready to have to work hard to get an A, don't take this class.

Steele was such a great professor. I went into his class with very little knowledge of chemistry and even though it was hard, he made the class very enjoyable and inspiring to me. Even though CHEM 1211 is a 1st-year class, it is HARD, he recommends 3 hrs of studying per hour in class but it's an amazing class if you know what you are getting into.

Professor Steele is great! This class was pretty hard but it was very educational. Make sure to stay on top of your readings because they will be helpful. Attendance isn't taken but my biggest advice is to go to class!

This was 100% the hardest class I took all semester. The exams and homework are challenging, and it requires a lot of work. You can tell that it's an honors class. However, Professor Steele cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He was very accessible, even late at night. Go to office hours. The class is worth it if you try!

I really enjoyed Professor Steele as a professor, I just found the topics to be too difficult. Often his homeworks would be extremely hard, the reviews for tests would be super easy, which left the tests being in the middle and about things we didn't cover in class. Be sure to read the textbook and don't be afraid to ask questions!

He really cares and wants you to succeed. The class is a challenge, but definitely doable, and he provides everything you need to succeed. Always available for questions, either through office hours or email. You will get really good at thinking conceptually instead of just plugging and chugging equations. Best course I took this semester!
He was a really nice teacher and he cared so much for us! It's obvious he wanted us to succeed. His tests were difficult, but he gave lots of extra credit. I learned so much!

Professor Steele is a great professor. He always had an answer to every question asked. Hes willing to work for you so be sure you work hard in his class. Even though his class is tough, Professor Steele is very understanding and accessible via email and office hours, sometimes he responds passed midnight. Also read his 2005 RMP at UC Berkeley :)

Steele is a great guy that will always make an effort to make sure you understand the material. However, don't rely on lectures/textbook, sometimes all you need to understand something is YouTube. If you're struggling, definitely set up a meeting with him, his encouragement really helped me this semester. There's never a dull moment in his class.

Prof. Steele is one of the most kind and dedicated people I have ever met. Always attend office hours - it is practically an extra class, but it is a big key to success. Difficult midterms that determine a large portion of the grade. He is very generous at the end of the semester with extra credit and class curve. Do your best and he will notice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I took the Honors version of Gen Chem, and I will say that my experience with the class was different because all of the Gen Chem classes (and also the professors) were combined. So, a lot of the problems I had with the class weren't Prof. Steele's fault. But his lectures were less straight forward than other professors'. He was very understanding.

Professor Steele is very patient and willing to help students with homework and understanding concepts. This class is not easy, but his character and ambition are very motivating. Be sure to ask Professor Steele for help whenever needed; he responds very quickly to emails. He will not make exceptions for extra credit or dropping extra scores.

Steele is a really good person and overall pretty good prof. Expects you to have previous chem knowledge. Sometimes answers questions with complex explanations and doesn't simplify enough, but you can tell he really cares about his students and wants to help. Weekly quiz makes or breaks your grade. Easy homework, tests are hard but manageable.

Steele is great. Since this course was online for me, I had weekly optional discussion sessions, and he cleared all my questions up for the weekly quizzes, which were tough, but ultimately, fair. He asked his students how they were doing and cracked some jokes, and really tried to prepare us for tests. Make sure you study the homework though!

If you dont go to his office hours, you will not do well. I could listen to him talk forever though, he has a golden mind. However, it will be a HARD class if you dont go to his office hours and ask questions. He is a kind man though and the world is a better place with him here. He goes above and beyond to help his students. Kind and pushes you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Steele's class was one of the hardest classes I've ever taken but by far one of the most enjoyable. His enthusiasm for the subject is infectious and inspiring. He makes the homework and exams difficult, but it is possible to get an A if you put in the effort.

Pleasantly surprised by this class. Steele is caring, engaging, and easy to contact. 2 good TAs for class of 50. Tests hard but doable, study! Fun Lectures. Class environment surprisingly cooperative & healthy. Tips: Detailed handwritt. notes, read textbook thoroughly, visit office hours, go to class, make study friends. Do end of chapter text. ?s
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very intelligent guy, works hard to make everyone learn and enjoy chemistry. Fair tests, but some tough grading. He is always open for discussion and debate, however, and is far more concerned with understanding the material than getting good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He made the honors course really to be honors

Steele is the best professor I've ever had! He's really caring, engaged, and passionate. Overall, he's a very effective teacher. Not too much homework, tests were challenging but fair. This class will be difficult if you haven't taken AP or IB chem in high school. I thoroughly enjoyed my semester in Steele's class.

Absolutely awful. No partial credit on exams. Either 100% or you fail. No practice problems in class. Homework doesn't reflect tests. Teaching PhD level subjects in entry level class. Everything extremely complicated. Unless you already have a chemistry degree, you will fail. Worst class Ive ever taken.
He is one of the best professors I ever had! He is an awesome teacher, passionate about the subject and wants you to take something out of his class. He really makes Quantum fun and doable!
