Very kind and open to honest conversations. Funny and engaging in class. Always willing to help. However, the course lacks consistency—homework, content, and exams don't align well. Exams seemed designed to lower the average, but the 70% retake cap helped. Overall positive, but structure needs work.

i absolutely hate accounting, but i LOVED him. by far my favorite professor. owned up to the fact that the accounting department lowkey is the worst and he tries his best to work around it. genuinely the best professor TAKE HIM.

It is so clear that professor Silvers cares. He takes the time to answer each and every single students questions and sits with them to explain concepts their confused on. He makes accounting so easy to grasp. Just apply yourself and I mean really apply yourself. Acctg isn't easy but if you try, professor Silvers will make it a breeze.

This is for 3100 (Managerial ACCTG). Professor Silvers is the best one I have had. Accounting is simply not an easy subject to learn, but with Silvers just made everything click. His method for teaching is different from the other professors. You just have to apply yourself and pay attention to lectures, everything there will prep for exam.

Accounting is never going to be easy, especially if it is your first time around taking it. However, he really cares about his students and getting an A is manageable. If you PAY ATTENTION DURING THE LECTURES, it is very doable to get an A. Great guy too.

Super nice guy and great teacher, is happy to explain things when you aren't getting them, had a great TA too. Class is hard compared to other business classes, but he was generous with assignment grading and grade curves.

Professor Silvers was probably one of my favorite professors I have ever had!!!!! Accounting is known to be a hard class, but he made it so much better. He would stay after class and answer all my questions. He had higher class averages than the other accounting professors. He is the most understanding professor, and will work with you to get an A.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. Accounting is really hard & he knows that & does his best to help students succeed. Pay attention during his exam reviews he practically spoon-feeds you the exam material. Exams are hard & heavily weighted but not much homework. Considered switching my major because of him.

If you're deciding what block to choose and you have the option of Professor Silvers, it is the best thing you can do for yourself. He cares so much about the success of his students and does a great job of teaching accounting. It is a very difficult class. Tests are hard, but Silvers prepares you well. Few assignments and lots of studying time.

Silvers is the best possible professor for accounting in the BCOR block. The class is extremely hard, but that is because of the accounting department, and Silvers is the best way to make your life *somewhat* more enjoyable. The review days are extremely helpful and Silvers gives AMAZING study advice. Super caring and understanding professor.

Silvers is the best professor and a must have for the BCOR block! He's fast-paced but you are engaged the entire time. Extremely understanding and patient. Ask questions if you have any! He encourages it and will walk you through it until you understand. Challenging course but he makes it as easy as possible! Review days are absolutely valuable!

Take this man for the block if you can! He prepares students for exams really well; review day is a must! He will teach you what you need to pass exams. He will answer any question and make sure you understand the topic. Very accommodating with homework assignments. I suggest attending lectures because he will simplify accounting for non-majors.

Professor Silvers is terrible and definitely, the worst professor I have had during my time at the U. Silvers has little to no understanding of what students go through and makes it his mission to make his class as difficult as it can be. Silvers puts trick questions on exams and his lectures are extremely difficult to follow. Do not take this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So caring and really wants his students to do well. Even if his learning style doesn't mesh with yours he is very approachable and actually wants you to understand the material. He's funny too.

This was his first time teaching online. He struggled to adjust to exams online. He worked overtime to go through each student's exam question by question to give points where possible to bring up the grades. Lectures were fine, only issue was the exams (at least for me). He was encouraging and cared about his student's esteem. One of my fav profs.

Silvers really cares about his students but is not the best professor. Maybe it was that his teaching didn't match with my learning but it seemed that he made things more difficult than they were especially for an already hard class. I definitely feel like I taught myself Managerial Accounting
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Tough class. Roger is a cool teacher and very approachable and easy to talk to. But class is tough and the tests are hard. He never really tells you what the tests are going to be on. Has pop quizzes so beware. TA help is life saving. Very dry class but Professor Silvers tries hard to make it entertaining which is appreciated.

no need textbook. He provides handouts. Go to class (there are pop quizzes), study ppt slides and handouts, especially problems, then you should be fine. You can see the same problems that you did during class on exams. You need to study only what he covers during class.

Wonderful teacher. The concepts may seem easy/intuitive at first, but there are so many nuances so make sure you do your work! He's very accessible to students and extremely willing to help. I probably wouldn't have gotten a good grade if I didn't reach out to him and get help!

Great Professor. Really condensed the class and simplified the learning by using his handouts he gives out each day (don't buy the book and don't miss class much). The lectures and material matched the exams exactly. He spares a lot of time to review and answer questions both in class and out of class.

Professor Silvers is by far one of the best professors I have had in my collegiate experience.  He teaches solely from his packet handouts, which prove to be perfect study material along with his review.  Going to class is necessary, but he makes it fun.  Very quick to respond to emails and willing to stay after class to help. CHOOSE SILVERS!

Never opened the book once.  Teaches from slides and worksheets he gives you.  If you miss class he notices and won't help you get back on track.  He says it's not his responsibility to help people who don't come to class.  Pretty nice guy though.  It always seemed to surprise him that everyone always did horrible on his exams.

One of the best teachers at the U.  Many don't like him because they want an easy A. He makes you work for it and quickly responds to questions.  He doesn't focus on the math, which helps you learn the concepts better.  I would recommend him to ANYONE!

Roger is a fairly new professor, he still seems to be trying to find his place while teaching. I enjoy the lectures and his real world examples. I felt that the exams were harder than expected. The exam preparation was also difficult. The class was difficult but then again so is Charles. your choice
Makes a boring subject more interesting with real world information.

Doesnt answer emails, doesnt provide good study guides.  Everything that is tested on comes from a testing bank so he doesnt really have any idea whats on the test because he doesnt bother to go through it.  Hard class when you are trying to do everything yourself.

Worst Prof I've had at the U. Entire class is pointless lecture read from powerpoint slides that were given to him. Terrible at helping students and wont reply to emails. The study guides before the final and midterm are 50-60 pages long and the least helpful tool he could have given us. He comes off as LAZY. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS FROM THIS GUY

Prof. Skipper is an amazing lecturer and makes sure to review concepts from Calc 1&2 that may have been forgotten. Tests were pretty hard, and she would put questions that covered concepts not on the practice test. Some homework problems were so hard that the math tutors couldn't do them, but she was very helpful during her few office hours.
She's a good teacher, but she doesn't fully explain the material and teaches very quickly. She also doesn't give practice questions for the exam.

Absolutely loved her. Started taking her office hours in the second half of the semester and 10/10 would recommend. She reteaches difficult topics and goes over homework and exams to help you prepare best for the final.

She brought energy to every lecture and was clear about what was expected from the class. She is sometimes tripped up by questions, but she always does her best to answer everything and you can tell she genuinely cares if the class understands the material. Not an easy topic, but with her lectures+some supplemental learning an A is very reasonable.

Prof. Skipper's lectures were clear and adequately paced. She is happy to answer any question that might come up and tries to make sure the class as a whole understands before she moves on. She provides many resources to prepare for the exams, is super kind, and has an extremely generous grading scheme. Cannot recommend enough!

I took calc 3 from Mishel and although he is a nice person, he is not a good teacher. I stopped going to the lectures and instead copied notes that he posted online. In his lectures no one knew what he was talking about and when someone asks a question he responds as if they are stupid for even asking. He knows his stuff, hes just bad at explaining

Cannot teach at all. Most people complaining are in Calc 2 but this in Linear Algebra is on a whole other level. Homework is self-taught, long, and won't be graded til the last day of the class. Stopped going to class after the first unit because I was battling myself falling asleep and inability to understand a single concept he was discussing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this guy's class, unless you plan on learning everything on your own.
This guy cannot teach. Find a different professor if you can't teach yourself.

Nice teacher but cannot really teach. I did not go to class after the first month of the semester and just thought myself from the textbook because it made more sense than him. Grade was based entirely on three midterms, one final, and 8 homework assignments. Exams were hard but fair.
not great as a teacher in general

Skendri definitely seems nervous teaching. He teaches directly out of the book and isn't great at answering questions, so I've stopped going to class and have just been studying out of the book on my own. He is nice though - he let me postpone a midterm so I could take care of my boyfriend after he got surgery. I just can't do his teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was an absolute joke. I took him for Calculus II, it was his first semester teaching. He knew the material, but had no idea how to teach. I had an A in the class from homework, but I had to figure that out on my own. I ended up dropping the class entirely because he confused me so much. DO NOT TAKE FROM THIS PROFESSOR.

Mishel is a nice person who knows the concepts well he can't answer questions in a different way than he originally explained them, and he teaches almost directly out of the book. I've ended up just not going to class and studying from the textbook. I will say, he is very accommodating and will help to make sure your grade stays up if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Skenderi seemed like a nice person, but you could tell he was nervous teaching the class. He spent a lot of time talking and then performing examples for the class. You can tell he understands the concepts but has a hard time explaining them. I learned everything from the book and stopped attending class because I found it too confusing.

Professor Skenderi was very accommodating to circumstances the whole semester. I would say that he teaches math like a high school teacher so if you like that kind of teaching he is the right professor. I really enjoyed being in his class and learned a lot! even though i didnt show up all the time.

If you go to class you will pass, there are some daily assignments. McKenzie does move quickly through her slides, but so do most professors. She is available outside of class time for any help needed. Assignments and lectures were fun and informative. No test was extraordinarily difficult. Great teacher.
McKenzie was great. Always helped answer clarifying questions in discussions. Has a great grasp of the subject matter.

McKenzie's slides consistently lack critical information which she quickly goes through and if you don't take the note you're out of luck as she's moved on. Her answers to clarifying questions often make it more confusing somehow. Finally, she never admits to errors. Tip:do not waste time buying the texts - you'll never use them and be out of $100+
He stinks as a professor.  Very condescending.  Only teaches to build his ego.  Should not be at the University.

Difficult class with mediocre professor. Very abrasive personality. Intimidating and addresses student questions in a condescending manner. Teaching method is archaic. Visual learners will have great difficulty with this professor.
tough class worst i have ever taken
Skliar is a great teacher.  This class was very interesting and I learned a lot of useful information
He treats you like you can't hack it, but is nice when you sleep through an exam...because you were up til 4 am doing his homework the night before...

Tough but fair. Put forth the necessary effort and you won't have any problems. Unlikeable at first, but towards the end of the semester became more friendly and approachable. Covered the material very well, and I feel very prepared for my next math class.

Fantastic Professor. His class is challenging, but if you just put in some effort to learn the material, then you'll come out of it more than ready to move on to MATH-2250. I did not at all feel like I was the top of his class, but now that I'm in ODE's, I feel really good about the material.

Took Eng Calc II from him. At the start of the semester, his rating here had me worried. Now, it's clear that he's a very good professor, despite his harsh and low ratings here. Tests were fairly constructed, assignments accurately reflected learned material, and additional "lab writeups" made me better at visualizing and putting math in words.

He's one of the worst professors I've had at the U. He wend on and on about his research and side topics ignoring those of us having trouble understanding the actual subject of the course.  He seemed bored with teaching and unsympathetic with those of us who hadn't already learned calculus in high school.
He seemed hard in the beginning, and his class was in no way easy, however overall I think this is the math class I learned the most in. And, he curves the grade in the end.
Over complicated explanations, seemed more interested in showing off his math prowess than in helping student understand the material.
One of the worst professors I have taken. Prefers to build upon his own ego rather than teach you what you need to know.  I do not recommend.

One of the worst math teachers I have had. Not at all interested in pursuing any other class that he teaches. I'm confident he knows his stuff, however, it is my observation that he is not a teacher because he enjoys it. He seems more like a post-doc student who is obligated to teach against his desires.

This guy hasn't been teaching the class very long.  He stood in front of the class and said that he was proud of how hard his tests are.  We're getting about 40 problems a week, and the test problems are more difficult than the problems done on the homework.  If you want to learn ODE, take it from someone else.
Amazing, funny, smart, inspiring, etc. she makes everything fun and understandable- very rare.
Awesome professor

She was one of the best instructors I have ever had the privilege of studying under. And her fashion sense was impeccable. And I am worried a little bit about her obsession with Axel Rose. But, that's ok. I see where she's coming from.
great teacher, enjoyed her lectures. would take another class.

You need to come to class (attendance is taken and scored). His lectures aren't the most exciting youll hear, but he knows his stuff. What I really enjoyed about the class was the assignments. The class was rigorous (it was a PhD level course, so what do you expect?) but we were given real world problems to evaluate. I would take his class agai

Eric is a decent professor. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but he often left students behind in his lectures because they were sometimes dull and he over-elaborated. Despite the fact that only six of us showed up to his class, he didn't learn our names. However, his assignments were very interesting and I really enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall an effective teacher, the content is dry but is presented clearly.  The lecture presentations are available to students so they can used for referencestudy material.  Most of the homework involves statistical software so that makes things a little tougher (but still manageable).  I would take another class from this instructor.
If you're not interested in theatre, he's not for you.
Just take his class for credit if you need it, he's charming and charismatic but honest and sincere when the writers need it.
Tim is awesome! He listens. He gives advice in a way in which you the student (writer) gets to make decisions. Phenomenal teacher.

Read all of the plays he assigns! If you do, the tests are easy and the discussions are interesting. There's a quiz almost every play or article. You have to read like twelve plays. Professor Slover is very knowledgeable and helps you see how analyzing scripts is helpful in your real world theater experiences. This class was super interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy but really interesting class. Read all of the plays because you have quizzes on all of them but if you've done the reading, they are really easy. Lecture heavy but they are never boring.
Black Theater.  He was awesome!
Tim is a very passionate and fun teacher who really makes the classroom experience enjoyable.
What's not to like about Tim Slover? The best professor EVER, not to mention...he's SMOKIN' HOT!
If Tim's teaching the class, it's worth going. Period.
Great listener, great teacher, overall, just awesome. The first day was spent asking our opinion on how he should approach our large class size. VERY cool.
Who doesn't love Tim?!
Charismatic, brilliant, cheerful, interested...everyone should take the opportunity to learn from him.
The best damn teacher ever!
Tim is the best!  a wonderful teacher, very knowledgable, approachable, and fair.  I'll be glad when he's back from hiatus next year!

Fantastic professor, fascinating course! Professor Slade is an excellent lecturer, is wiling to work with students, and grades in a way that feels both fair and encouraging rather than punishing. The homework in this class was actually productive and useful, not even a hint of busywork to be found. I highly recommend this professor, he's excellent!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great lecturer - he gave us incomprehensible papers, and then managed to make them make sense in his gripping lectures. There were no tests in this class, and he instead allowed us to apply what we learned to a real final project, which is a fantastic way of solidifying the material. Only downside was that he overemphasized Indo-European.
Extremely interesting professor, very lenient grader. Lectures were very interesting, and homeworks were pointed and helpful.

I had Professor Slade for a business linguistics class. There were only 4 HW assignments, 1 midterm, and a final project.  Homework assignments were fairly easy, but the midterm was ridiculously tough. Luckily the final project is what really matters. The class overall was pretty easy.

He gave long and sometimes droning lectures while he went over theoretical stuff. But when he started to go over the topics we would have to replicate and understand for the homeworks or tests, he was very clear and explanatory. He was really responsive to questions and was always willing to help students grasp the material.

I am not a Middle East Studies major, it is clear that this professor has a particular bias toward students who follow him and major in Middle East Studies.  He showed no interest in other students, and repeatedly blasted other professors at the University as being stupid and not qualified to teach.  Strange  Prof. do not recommend him.

This was one of the worst classes I have taken at the U. The Professor is arrogant, talks about himself and other professors all the time,  and he never finishes a lecture.  He sure has a beef with the University.
I have taken many classes from Dr. Sluglett and he is wonderful.  He can be a bit hard to follow at times, but it is worth it to learn from such an excellent scholar and an all around nice guy.
Sluglett is a tough grader, but he's extremely helpful.  He will make time to meet with you so you can improve your writing and thus, your grade.

Sluglett is a solid teacher, but his style isn't for everyone, there were no formal tests, all of your grade is tied up in essays that you write. He is helpful though, you don't have to go to class but you do need to meet with him to discuss your papers before you get your grade. Also his lectures are more general info, not well structured.

I loved this professor, so much I'm taking another class from him. It is NOT an easy class. Heexpects a lot of work but he is very helpful in assisting in accomplishing thos expectations. He actually is interested in teaching you and with the papers he basically builds your bibiliography for you. Not an easy ride, but your writing WILL improve.

It's like trying to listen to an aged ozzy stutter away with his lavish english accent.  by the end of the semester I would only see 5 to 6 other classmates.  the other 35 chose sleep over his rambling antics.If you take this class, I reccomend an unlimited text message plan. class notes are impossible. At least he hands out papers over tests.
Interesting topic. Awful lectures. papers are long (10pgs) but manageable. He's kinda a wanker at times, but to each his own.

Critical eye. She's looking for upcoming artists for her Intermedia Sculpture program. If you want to grow as an ARTIST take her class. If you prefer an easy class, avoid it, but remember: artists tread deep waters nor are defined by medium. Wannabe cowards remain shallow and believe in "medium as the message."

I was forced to take her 3D design class as a prereq. for my photography major and if you aren't a sculpting major don't take her class! She is unhelpful, and spends the entire class period talking leaving no time to work on projects.

AWFUL teacher,  she totally has favorites and she grades very hard.  No one is getting an A that I know of.  Her projects are very time consuming and she only gives you a couple days to do them. I would recomend someone else, if you have the choice.

She never likes anything there is always something that could be better or fixed. even the best project of the class didn't get a perfect score. I don't feel like she teachers much she just throws you into a project and then she critiques you once you've turned it in thats hows you learn what not to do. I wouldn't recommend her. take steffensen
A tough grader but knows what she's doing. Tends towards favoritism at times but you can learn a lot in her class.
She was great really helpful.

Snowberg is more concerned with being viewed as the smartest person in the room than helping his students understand the material. Quizzes are full of trick questions or missing information where you have to guess which imaginary direction he saw in his own mind. Incredibly condescending. When 90% of the class is confused he refuses to adjust.
Professor does not take critiques well and his methodology of teaching doesn't cater well to student needs.

This is great class and you learn a lot about yourself. The downside is the assignments are due at 5am but it wasn't to bad if you just finish them the night before. He does a great job at making you think about what you personally care about and how you should take it into the real world.
He's not very good at teaching, also his assignments are due at 5am despite the class not starting until 4 pm.

This professor is very knowledgable. Learned alot in the advanced ceramic courses. The classes are alot of detailed work. Be ready to go in on free time. Grading is very opinonated. I found wheel 2 and glaze the most work.
Great class. I learned a lot. You have to do a lot of stuff outside of class, but it makes sense. If you didn't then it would be impossible to really learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you put in the work, this class can be a lot of fun. Brian is a great help and there is always time to practice out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is ALOT better than the other wheel teacher. He will take time into teaching detailed. If you have a question, you can ask. If you are in wheel 1, go to the extra time, if you have to do 4 bowls, do 12. Take time in all of the projects to excell. The final is pretty easy if you go over everything he talked about.

I had a blast in this class, but don't get me wrong, I worked many extra hours earning a good grade.  Brian Snapp is totally awesome in that quirky art teacher kind of way, and the environment was very friendly.
No Comments

Love this guy. One of the most encouraging teachers I've ever had, not to mention his exceptional taste in music. I credit him for any sculptural confidence I might have... and then I repay him by going into graphic design.
Not a good teacher, very indimidating and unhelpful. The class is fun but he makes it very hard. It was my most stressful class

Kasera definitely tried to make students succeed. An 80% is an A and he sometimes added extra TA hours. However, he should've covered a lot more of the coding/debugging side of networking. Without such, you have very little direction on coding hw. His hw and exam reviews also doesn't well reflect his exam questions.

Exam questions are very different from practice exams and hw. Lectures have very little coding examples so you often have no sense of direction on programming hw. He does have a generous curve though. You do get a month to do each coding hw.

This class is a "figure it all out on your own" class. For his coding hw, he asks you to write a program that does this but his lectures doesn't provide you any guidance on HOW to do it. He gives ZERO coding demos. You often have no sense of direction on where to go.

VERY generous curve (80% is a A) but there's a catch. No example problems in lectures to help with hw or tests. HW and test questions are different. Some coding demos would be nice but there's none, leaving students completely lost on coding assignments. Even submitting the hw is complicated as he doesn't use gradescope or canvas.
Very strict late policy, and very difficult to work with as a professor. Knows his stuff, but is generally unkind.

I had this professor during COVID, so the lectures were through Zoom - though I don't think that affected how awful the class is. The majority of the assignments come straight from the book, the slides themselves aren't made by him, and the projects are punishingly vague. Considering the TAs do the grading, I question how much work he even does.

This is easily one of the worst professors I have ever had the chance to take a class with. In lectures, all he does is read off lecture slides and seems unsure of himself most of the time. You have to essentially teach yourself everything because you will learn literally nothing from his lectures and you're forced to read the textbook yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He cares about his students and wants to see everyone learn something about Networking. I think the class could of been structured better, he taught with slides off of what i'd call his "Networking bible" (Book he helped write). So everything in the class was slide-oriented textbook chapters. He had a VERY generous curve as well. 80% A's.

He manages to turn interesting concepts into boring confusing things we have to memorize for the exams. One of the worst cs classes I've taken at the U. It's a shame because I've heard such good things about Computer Networks while it was being taught by someone other than Kasera.

Kasera means well and can be funny, but he spends too little time on concepts that we get tested on. His test reviews are absolutely worthless, he doesn't do any example HW problems in class, in fact lectures are just a jumbled rehash of what you can read in the book. Expect to be teaching yourself most of the semester. Or better yet, dont take him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am not sure why he has got such a low rating here! He is an excellent prof! His teaching materials are very well organized. Also, his top-down approach of teaching networking is excellent as most of the juiciest stuffs are there in the app, ip, and transport layers. Keep it coming Prof. Kasera!

He has knowledge of the subject but has very poor teaching skills. During lectures he just writes random computations without explaining anything. When you ask him a question he either says its off topic, or to read it in the book. He doesn't care about students learning, and takes off after class asap to avoid questions. Homework is very vague.
Interesting class exploring many protocols dealing with network security. Be ready to spend some time on homework and programming assignments.
A subject-matter expert. Shows great enthusiasm in teaching the class. Better to attend all lectures as some homework assignments and exam questions are based on class notes.
He has some potential, but he needs some experience. He's still a little nervous giving lectures.
No Comments

For years I struggled with mathematics and assumed this class would be no different.  Robbie is a phenomenal instructor. His lectures are very clear and understandable. You must show up for each class, prepared to take notes! I can only pray the rest of my instructors will match his professionalism. He will be missed! Godspeed Robbie!

Robbie is a great teacher - clear communicator, respectful, sociable, and always always always willing to answer a question, even the most basic ones. He'll work through problems clearly and completely, with guidance on multiple ways to achieve the answer to allow students to learn what's best for themselves. Teaches students to think. And fair!
Had him as a TA for Math 20C at UCSD. Best teacher ever.  Makes everything clear understandable.  He is always willing to help.  Wish he was my professor.
The material isn’t easy but he’s a great teacher that makes it approachable.

Great teacher, fair assignments and tests. Very clear and loves to help students. Although, it would have been nice to know when tests were ahead of time out of the class room, big surprise coming to class, and "oh goody!" a test I haven't studied for...(Just so happens I miss the only day he announced it in class.) Overall Great teacher!
Comparable to Kevin Tucker in teaching quality and looks, but not age.
Fairest class I've ever taken.  Homework is relatively easy, and exams are built from problems out of the book. Professor teaches very clearly, it is easy to learn.
He goes at a fast pace. But he explains very well.
I love strong dudes.
He's the coolest nerd ever!
Robby is very available to students. He teaches very clearly, assigns easy and fair exams, and wants students to succeed.

Such an amazing and caring professor. Works very hard to curate a very positive and collaborative studio environment. If you need to take Arch 2630 you should try your hardest to get into his class even if it's a night class.

Mike is an AMAZING teacher!! He genuinely cares about everyone's success and is willing to dedicate hours outside of work to help students with their portfolios for the Architecture Program. He gives great feedback and is overall very funny! Totally would recommend taking his class!!
I loved this class! Mike is super chill and he gives great feedback. Super low stakes class, he is very understanding.

This class reignited my love for hands-on creativity, and I'm so glad I decided to take the book arts workshop class over the regular creative writing course. Being in the Book Arts Classroom felt magical every time, and I wish I could go there again. The assigned readings were always interesting, and the projects were fun and easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really recommend this course if you can fit it in your schedule and it count toward something. It was very simple and did not take too much time each week. I took it over summer and very well worth it. TAKE THIS CLASS you won't regret it.

Jamie is so awesome! I had her for a Creative Writing/Book Arts hybrid class, and it was so great that it made me add another minor to my repertoire. I was already very well-versed in creative writing and fiction especially, but Jamie made me appreciate the physical side of creating linguistic art. Always looked forward to her feedback :)

Not a fan. I was out of town for the first three classes of the semester and they were rude. Talks too fast, hard to understand. Ideas are too abstract to stick. I honestly feel like I didn't learn anything. Also, due dates are at bad times. Would make things due at 2 pm on a weekday.

Although some of the material was contemplative and interesting, it felt less like this class provided me a lens to view art through, but made me redefine my own beliefs to fit a single perspective on art history. Although well intentioned, Dr. Solomon often came across as condescending to those who struggled to grasp their ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought an intro class called "why is that art" would be fascinating. I was wrong. I feel that i learned nothing, and wrote 5 FAT papers for virtually nothing. She's kind of passive aggressive, and just overall seems to expect way too much. She's not MEAN, but definitely not my favorite professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures were super interesting, but the professor was often sarcastic and slightly condescending towards students. They did not give a rubric for assignments or even a good description of what the task for the assignments was. Overall, the class was interesting and easy, but hard to understand in terms of how our grade was determined.
Class is engaging and not very difficult. Be prepared for lots of field trips though and some events outside of class. Not very many large point assignments. Lots of group projects.

dr. soloman is an outstanding professor. Their lectures are super informative and clear. There is not a lot of reading. They are a bit of a tough grader, but as long as you show your understanding and draw connections you are good. The best prof i have ever had an super kind and understanding. easily one of my favorite classes i have taken.
The class was ok the final paper made me want to drop out of college.12 full pages required for an intro level art class is wild.

A very good professor who makes it clear what is expected of you. I do not have a background in Art by any means, but the professor gave great lectures and assigned interesting readings that helped me learn and do well. Everything is laid out clearly in the syllabus and was easy to follow. I would take another course from this professor for sure!

This class was super interesting, but because of the Honors component, it wasn't graded by a lot of things, and when it was, Virginia expected a lot from you. I would say that if you have experience in writing things well in less than an hour, you'll do fine - since that's what the midterms are like. Virginia is super funny, and cares a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Solomon was genuinely caring and very easy to work with. They were very clear with the expectations set in class and project due dates- there was a lot of writing. Very understanding when it came to attendance and due dates and was an overall amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be ready to really read, take notes in class, and make sure you come to class ready to ask questions. Great Lecture super passionate about their area of study and it shows. Tests are made up of short and long answer essay questions about the topics covered so be prepared to use your notes to back up your visual analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Solomon's educational background seemed to ensure this class would be very interesting, however throughout the semester they only read off their notes, wouldn't answer questions, and was quite sarcastic towards students, which made them unlikable. The lectures were very boring, and they wouldn't even explain the assignments thoroughly.

Very kind teacher, a lot of online homework but it's pretty easy, regular quizzes in class that aren't bad if you pay attention. She cares a lot about her students and will help you if needed, engaging classes that taught me a lot. Highly recommend.
This professor had mandatory attendance but made the class nice and fun
I had her for Spanish 1020 and 2020. She is very patient with students and wants everyone to do well. Highly recommend!

Rosario is really nice and accommodating. She's easy to reach outside of class, but beware of MindTap (the homework software). MindTap crashes frequently and tech support frequently can't solve the problem for days. If you come to class and do the homework it's an easy A because Rosario is a really nice grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took 2020, not 1020 but she is so so kind and sweet. Learned a good amount in her class and she was very patient with students who needed to brush up on grammar. Attendance is madatory, but if you just show up to class or communicate you'll be totally fine. She is a sweetheart.

attendance policy is very strict- go to her class if you have her. 8 absences are only allowed, but she cares about what she teaches and if you talk with her about late work and retakes, she's accommodating. just wish her attendance policy was less strict

On mindtap we have a lot of assignments every week, other than that it's easy going. She is very good at lectures and making sure you understand the concepts. She is very kind with her corrections. We do test reviews right before every exam. I highly recommend and I have learned a lot through taking this class.

Rosario is very kind, but can be strict with attendance and tardies. She was great at teaching the language aspects of spanish class, but a little less experienced with teaching cultural, historical, political portions of the class. I would highly recommend her for SPAN1010 and 1020, but not necessarily for SPAN 2010 or 2020.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking an Honors IT with Dr. Sohn. Your participation MATTERS, you have to show up to class, do the readings, as well as PARTICIPATE in discussion to do well. Few assignments, but lots of reading. Sohn's feedback helped me improve my writing and reading comprehension skills with high difficulty readings. He's also pretty funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Prof. Sohn is so funny and I really enjoyed his lectures. This subject material is so interesting and unique, once you get past the initial weirdness of it all. Attendance is really necessary, and required. I had a lot of fun with the papers, and communicated when I was concerned or had questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Sohn's classes, given I've taken multiple at my time here at the U. He is funny and knows every one of his students personally. However, his papers are quite difficult, but he does give your final grade fairly reasonably.

Loved this class! Professor Sohn is fantastic and really wants his students to stretch their mind. He is not a tough grader as long as you focus and try to understand what is talked about in class. Take good notes! Grade is based on a 6 page midterm, 8 page final, three 3 page small papers and PARTICIPATION. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sohn is very passionate about the class Divine Wandering but he expects everyone else to share that same excitement. there was at least 10 pages of reading for each class and he grades hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Grade is based off three papers, three journal responses and participation. Prof Sohn gives A LOT of feedback and suggestions on papers, but his grading criteria is completely unknown to the students. Class grades are only available at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I got a lot more out of this class than I expected. Sohn is a great teacher, and really wants his students to learn. I spent a lot of time in this class, but all the work and grading felt very fair, and he was very understanding to student situations. The readings were fun, and I felt like I actually got better at writing through it.

This class is not difficult if you actually put the time into studying the lecture slides provided and the textbook material. Material is thick but doable. She does go a bit fast in class with her slides.

she tests things that she didn't even talk about, and the slides are missing so much information that she says in class. also, she doesn't lecture very clearly and rushes through slides at an incredible speed because of spending too much time answering questions in class that aren't even related to the lecture concept at hand

Amazing professor. Most reviews are pretty accurate. Course itself covers some pretty thick material. Don't expect an easy grade just because the professor has high reviews (could tell some students did that in our course). Show up to lecture, keep up with the material, take exams serious, and you'll do great.

Exams are a breeze if you study. Coming to class and doing the quizzes count for 25% of your grade. Sophie introduces many research opportunities on campus to students during lecture; I found my research job through this class! Sophie cares about her students a lot, and the TAs are also lovely!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish she would just make the book required so when she does test on the book it's actually doable. The recent average was a 79% and we have tests back to back pretty much. Just say "read the chapers" for the test instead of letting us do horrible on the exam since we didn't read. Very misleading

She might have been a better teacher before covid but this class just sucks. If you took any neurobiology anywhere else already then this class is super boring to sit through. My brain just shuts off half way through because she talks the whole time. Not very interesting and hard to listen to her for an hour and a half. Exams are very doable
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Caron is a very intelligent woman and she is clearly very passionate about what she teaches. I wish she taught more neuroscience courses, as I would take every class from her, if I could.

I really like Professor Caron, she really knows what she is talking about and gives some interesting lectures. Sometimes her lectures tend to get a little tedious and boring but her exams are very doable and she always offers Extra Credit! The TA's are awesome.
I don't even know how could someone have something bad to say about her. She's amazing!

Dr. Caron is a great professor. Her lectures were fun to watch, entertaining and informative. Grading was fair. There were a lot of opportunities to participate which made the online format not so bad.

Dr. Caron is the best. She's a genius and so passionate about neuroscience - plus, her slides are always so entertaining it's no struggle to pay attention. She's also the most understanding professor I've ever had and she really cares about helping her students succeed.
The best professor in the Biology Department. Her lecture is so interesting and inspiring. She respects students and listens to students' feedback.
This was my favorite class. A lot of discussion, exams are fair and Prof Sophie is always ready to help!

Sophie is the most impressive professor I have had a the U! She is brilliant and genuinely wants to inspire her students. She has been invaluable as a resource for graduate school and moving forward in college. She wants to help and wants to see her students succeed. Take this class if you can. If they had a Neuroscience major I would have done it!

I've never had a professor who had their lecture down so well that we always got through things and were out of class on time. Dr. Caron is a great instructor/professor. I think she does a nice job at explaining the material and covering enough material to encourage students to think about the future of neurobiology. It's a must take course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sophie is a passionate neuroscientist who really cares how her students do. Lectures are packed with info, so stuff can get lost because there's so much to remember. She is forgiven, though, because her real job is as a PI and not a teacher, and she encourages feedback to improve this newer class. I'm sure future classes will only get better.

Sophie is a great professor who genuinely cares about her students and is passionate about the field of neuroscience. Her lectures are thorough and interesting and she talks a lot about current issues and advances. She makes a concerted effort to engage students in discussion, unlike many classes where you can get by without saying a word.

Dr. S was super nice and make sure to send out a video at the beginning of each week letting us know what the homework was for that week. The final project is pretty hard and takes a while but overall, not the worst thing ive had to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class and professor was fine. They're very strict with APA formatting and will dock points for any mistakes. There's a couple essays and the final project is a 60-80 slide power point. There's 5 discussions that can be lengthy and quizzes nearly every week. Follow the slides an get things turned in on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was annoying with the APA citations. I would regularly get marked 1-2 points down for forgetting a single period in my APA citation. Other than that this class is extremely easy. All of the quizzes are easy so no need to worry about your grade in this class. Also the slideshow at the end is very long but very easy.

Automated online course. Very little teacher interaction. Too much grading focus on APA formatting. Weekly quizzes with gotcha questions. 65-85 slide final project. Too much material covered, not enough time on core concepts, don't take this class if you have a heavy course load.

The class is online, which was nice. The assignments honestly do not take very long to do, and the rubric is very clear, so it's easy to get good grades. It's very important you get assignments done on time, because late work isn't accepted, but they are all due on Sundays, so it's not too hard to keep track of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took NURS 2100 online because it counted towards a gen ed required by the U. Unless you have an easy course load, I would not recommend it due to the several quizzes, discussions, critical thinking assignments, outside source material, and chapters that need to be completed each week. The grading of APA citations was strict and unreasonable too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Springer was very helpful in helping develop physics knowledge within coding.

He is a great guy, his lectures can get a little boring and seem like they are off topic but he always is explaining very interesting physics. Definitely one of the most qualified professors at the u, super nice, tests are very straightforward, practice tests are the best resources for the test, they help so much. I would recommend for sure.

Dr. Springer has had a bad reputation in the past, his lectures are a bit boring at times but I truly do believe he cares about what he is teaching. His curves are incredible and as long as you do the practice exams before the midterm you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Most boring professor. Learned nothing from lectures. Pearson mastery was 10x better of a teacher. He rambles about nothing. Doesn't ask meaningful questions and when he does he does t explain anything.
The class was 3010. But easy class, easy homework for the lab. The final project was a lot of fun to do.

I'm not sure why all the reviews are so negative. With Springer, as long as you show up to do all the labs (which are basically participation), do the homework and "quizzes" which are both online and are essentially busy work, and use the practice exams as reference for the actual exams, then you will get an A even if you never go to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Springer despite his awful reviews. I regret it with every fiber of my being. His lectures are usually below 40% attendance because they're incredibly useless. I cannot stress this enough: you will not learn physics taking his class. The only reason anyone passes is because of his insane curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Homework and Quiz every week that were super difficult. Never actually answered questions during lecture. Basically lectured based on the assumption that we already knew everything. Spent much more time on derivations of equations than actually helping us to understand the equations and usually glossed over the important stuff

Prof. Springer was a great professor in my opinion. People complain about his pre-lecture assignemnts and "tough" homework where in reality the pre-lectures are the appetizer to the entree. Watch pre-lectures the night or morning before lecture and then go to lecture with questions and you will thrive in this class. Homework isn't hard as they say.

Professor Springer makes Physics 1 a worse class than it needs to be by filling it with busy work and bad lecturing. He also requires the purchase of two online resources, one for graded "prelectures" and another for online homework. His lectures are mediocre at best. He assigns more homework than necessary, even the day after the midterm.

Lectures aren't too great but he posts all his lecture slides online which is convenient for homework and studying for exams. There is a lot of homework assignments but they are short and typically simple. Generous on grades, big class. The class is easy with previous experience in physics. Exams seem to vary in difficulty.

Take this class if you've taken physics before and did well. The lectures usually don't cover much more than the four minute long lecture videos. The examples he goes over in class are quite simple compared to what he asks on exams. That said, he does offer extra credit opportunities and grades with a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: this guy oozes apathy. he simply doesnt like teaching and it shows. lectures are worse than a waste of time, he could find a way to make adding integers complicated. oh.. and he actually went out of his way to mock a student in lecture. crazy.
Homework almost every day with no clear direction. Test questions were out of left field. Doesnt seem to care about his students.

Not the best prof available by far, but if you need to take phys for your major and don't need to retain the information he is a solid choice. So long as you complete all of the work and do average on the tests you should pass with an A

Springer is terrible. You are required to watch prelecture videos outside of class (that are due at unreasonable times) and all he does in lecture is go over the prelectures and does not know how to explain it well. The homeworks aren't terrible but do not reflect what's on exams (there are a lot) whatsoever. I relied heavily on the curve to pass.

This is Physics for scientists and engineers. If you took AP or IB physics in high school, I HIGHLY suggest this course. I only went to the first day of class, skipped a midterm, and ended with a 105% in the course. He curves all of his tests and gives up to 10% extra credit to your final grade.

Don't take this class from Springer, He's boring and won't work with you. Homework online is easy but won't do you any good because his tests are ridiculous. Asks questions of things you've never seen on any previous homework assignment.

This is, unequivocally, the worst class I have ever taken. It is not a particularly difficult class to succeed in; the average is 84.0% (standard deviation 20.7) in the last week of the semester, but very few students understand the material. All homework is done online. All lectures are done online and repeated (monotonously) in class.

Springer uses the flipped classroom, which means you learn everything from prelecture videos and then go to class the next day to hear him repeat the same thing but in a monotone voice. The only reason I went to class was for the clickers. You definitely teach yourself everything through flipitphysics and webassign. I learned nothing from him :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Literally just takes the pre-lectures and mumbles on about the same material for a grueling 55 minutes. Tests are similar to homework but challenge your knowledge. Class is test heavy with only 2-4 questions on the test so knowing your stuff is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I'm unimpressed, you have online pre-lectures, and in his lectures he mainly repeats all that was already covered.  He's a good instructor, and explains well, but needs to go deeper in his teaching.  primarily online learning.  homework is webassign with lots of tries.  He does clicker questions in class.  Need to know concepts well for tests.
Dr. Springer is an awesome instructor. He really cares and explains concepts well. This class was one of the funnest classes I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I was dreading this class the most, as I don't like old literature, but Prof. Wall's enthusiasm for the subject sold me, and this became one of my favorite classes. He's incredibly nerdy, which I loved, and is clearly very passionate about the things we read. It was a great intro to the world of early literature!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took the first session online summer class. It was not a difficult class but the set up was sort of strange. There were two lectures each week and they were written. You would have to type in text boxes and then submit pdfs. There were three papers. The professor provided feedback which was at times.

Professor Wall is very easy going, he's very passionate about the plays we talked about in class. Definitely make sure to show up to class because he will tell you what questions are gonna be on the exams. He's very helpful, but he is super lecture heavy but the class was really chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super subjective grader for a class that I went to all the lectures for and read the books. Do not take this class if you do not like theater.

Show up to class! If you go to class he gives you the answers to everything on the exam. He is enthusiastic and passionate about what he teaches, and wants his students to succeed. Exams are open note, open book.

I took this class assuming it would be a pretty easy A and based on the curriculum it should have been it was very simple. However, this professor only bases his grade off of 5 exams so if you don't get a high score on all of them you can't pass with an A. DON'T TAKE IT
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about this subject which is fun to learn from. I do not like reading or writing whatsoever so I was not the biggest fan of this class and struggled a tiny bit. If you go to class, he will hint at the exam questions which really helps. 5 in person essay exams with no rubric which is scary sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a breath of fresh air. He encourages students to think, participate, and apply themselves. The tests are essay-based, and weren't graded with a rubric, which helped me explore my own ideas and engage with the content. Super funny, and an engaging lecturer. Don't take it too serious and you'll have a lot of fun and learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Spencer at a lower-level course and loved it. At the 5000 level, I was overwhelmed by how sporadic his feedback was. He has very specific criteria for grading papers, so make sure you have him revise them before turning them in. Otherwise very long lectures and I was not a fan of his interpretations of the readings.

I love Professor Wall, and I cannot wait to take another class from him. He by far taught me some of the most in the English department thus far. He loves what he teaches, he engages the class, and he has given me a deep love for multiple literary periods. Please take his class! You will not regret it. 
He gives super helpful feedback on essays too

He's pretty good, and it's always nice to see a passionate teacher. I'm just annoyed that I had to take this as a business student because there isn't much of a connection to business in this class. I feel like the course planners for the business curriculum just wanted an excuse to make student read old English lit
Spencer is great. He gives good, clear feedback on your papers. His lectures were always enjoyable and interesting. He is extremely accommodating, caring, and kind.

Spencer is a wonderful, caring professor who is obviously very passionate about what he teaches.  Every lecture is full of material and it is very enjoyable and thought-provoking.  While attendance isn't explicitly mandatory, he grades participation by pop-quizzes and other in-class assessments, so definitely attend as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Extremely tough grader but more than willing to answer questions and give guidance, plus you're given a lot of time between big papers. Some lectures can be dry but mainly if no one participated. Do the reading, engage with the class, ask questions, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Spencer was very nice, he allowed paper extensions which took a lot of pressure off me. Also, he is very quick to answer emails.

Professor Wall is very passionate about Theater and it comes through in this course. He allows paper extensions which were very helpful, however, the grading was pretty particular. If you follow the guidelines for each paper and read all the required text, it is an easy course to pass.

Spencer is amazing! His lectures are interesting and he obviously cares a lot about what he teaches. He's a VERY tough grader. I never got a 100% on any of his papers, and I consider myself a great writer. If you do the readings, pay attention to lectures, and work hard, you'll be ok, but you definitely won't get an easy A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Spencer is one of the best English profs I've ever had. His lectures are very thorough and engaging. I felt I learned something important every class period, which is something I can rarely say. I did struggle with the weekly/biweekly 1 pg essays with very specific prompts, and if I could change one thing it would be the prompts or the # of papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: There are 2 pretty long lectures each week, but Spencer made them really clear and he was very funny too! There are lots of papers, but most of them are only one page. The papers are graded pretty harshly, but if you follow feedback and do the lectures you'll be fine. He's very caring and offers extensions for anything you need, no questions asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Spencer is a great professor. Like others have said, he can grade papers quite harshly, which is frustrating, but he does give very clear feedback. I would gladly take another class from him in person in the future, but online was a lot work. His lecture worksheets were all 12+ pages with several questions each.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: It's a writing class. There's bound to be lots of writing. Prof. Wall builds upon your previous writing, so the last bigger research paper is something you've been working on through the semester. He gives good, clear feedback and is willing to work with you anytime! Solid guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Spencer is amazingand yes, he prefers being called Spencer, not professor Wall. Most professors are really passionate about their disciplines but have a hard time conveying that and making it contagious. Spencer doesn't have this problem. His lectures are engaging, insightful, and just generally pleasurable. Absolutely take a class from him.

Very organized online professor, with clear expectations. Makes the weirdly indefensible claim that early modern plays are all somehow post-modern meta-commentaries on theater, which overrode the core thesis of the course and filters into assignment expectations. Grades on specific guidelines rather than writing quality, but available for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Online 3701 with Prof Wall wasn't too bad. There were two pdf "lectures" each week that you need to answer questions about the assigned texts, but it was graded on participation only. There were also 5 papers throughout the class. He's a slightly tough grader, but gives good feedback so I was able to increase my grade with each paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was the easiest English class ever, even with the content being Shakespeare. Lectures weren't mandatory but Spencer explained the material every well in class, so they were very helpful for comprehension. Graded on three 1-page papers, one 3-page paper, and participation. No tests or final and overall a fun and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Spencer is a fair grader, and is very willing to work with your specific needs. He is generous with extensions, and will take the time to go over your work one on one. He teaches with enthusiasm and a lot of energy, while still taking the time to go slow when the class is covering more difficult material. Be ready for class discussions & reading.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I really liked Prof. Wall. he gets the whole class involved in his discussions and really made his material interesting to us. He was always a fun guy to listen to and clearly understands the material very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: While the class topics are quite boring and really do not relate to whatever you will be majoring in that is business related, it is clear that Spencer has a great passion for literature and his job. Your grade is based simply on participation and three papers from reading and videos you watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took this class over summer and was half semester. The professor is very passionate about the topic, but it's hard to make a class about Shakespeare interesting. Most of your grade is a couple papers and participation, which is in class things. Announces when you'll have a quiz. Tough grader, but gives good feedback if you ask b4 turning them in

I took this class over the summer. There were no exams and just 3 1-2 page papers that made up a large part of your grade. He is a nice guy and I would take this class again. The lectures are very boring to me as I find no interest in Shakespeare. He is also really helpful with editing your papers before you turn them in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Really nice and approachable, very willing to give you extra time on papers. Extremely passionate about the material. Will give pop quizzes, but more often than not he'll warn you about them (plus he lets you use your book and notes). Is a little tough with grading, but as long as you put a little effort into your papers you should be fine.

Professor Wall is a very passionate, cheerful, kind and nice man. However, he is a tough grader when it comes to papers, and loves to give out pop quizzes. The class itself was rather boring and dry, and I still don't understand how he got away with teaching a class about Shakespeare Plays in the College of Business...

Very smart, enthusiastic professor who tries to get his students to care as much as he does about material. Very nice guy, lectures are a bit boring, but a very tough grader. Don't let his cheeriness get to you, you will get reamed if your paper isn't perfect or close to it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Wouldn't have wanted anyone else for my teacher. Gives good writing feedback, is funny and always cheerful, and genuinely cares about his students. You can tell he's a good person. Would take again.

She is a great professor but I will say that she/ her TAs grade very harshly. If you have the right answer and process but miss a label on a diagram or have an arrow pointing the wrong way, be prepared to lose 1/3-1/2 of the points and she offers no extra credit. Tough class to get an A and I don't feel like my grade reflects my understanding

Professor Spear is incredibly nice and approachable, as well as an amazing teacher. Her lectures are incredibly understandable and I found all of the homework to be easy while following my notes from lecture. The exams are all predictable too, with all content very similar to what you've seen in homework or lecture.

Dr. Spear is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. She is extremely committed to structuring her class well and she is excellent at explaining things methodically. I took 2010 (statics) with her, and while it was a bit difficult, it was entirely fair and well structured.  Getting an A is hard, but possible. Everything is graded by accuracy.

Spear is far and beyond the best professor that I've ever had. She is clearly dedicated to her teaching and is invested in her students' success. She is very clear in her teaching objectives and the lectures are very entertaining. Grading is broken down by points on every HW/test. You know exactly what she expects. Do the HW and ask Q's it's an A .

Dr. Spear is an excellent professor! She takes the time to thoroughly explain the minutia of the course material, and makes absolutely certain that students understand the material, even if that means going back and reviewing an old chapter. There is a lot of homework, but Dr. Spear will always help you on it if you are struggling.

Honestly 10/10 professor. Hope I end up taking another course from her. She's clear on the objectives of the class as well as on the tests. Go to lecture! It's not worth it to miss plus, Dr. Spear can be pretty funny sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is one of the best engineering professor at the U. She teaches the material with lots of examples and has clear expectations of what she'll cover in the course and by the end I learned a lot. Tests are also representative of the material so no surprises. I recommend taking her course if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at the U. She knows how to explain concepts very simply. The homework assignments are challenging . She will only curve tests if she feels like she needs to, which usually doesn't happen. Overall, amazing professor and I enjoyed attending her class even early in the morning.

Very serious about cheating. Dont try. Other than that, she honestly is a great professor. Teaches well, nice, respectful, tries to be funny and good natured. Homework is manageable and tests are simple and straightforward. I would definitely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She actually teaches the material and she grades all the work more on process than if you got the correct answer.
She knows her stuff, her research is really cool and she connected everything in the class to her research or the research of some of the students in the class.

Dr. Spear has clear expectations and brilliant lectures. I was intimindated going into Finite Elements, but she made the material understandable. The homework and tests were fair. The final project was challenging but ultimately a great way to tie the whole course together.

Dr. Spear is a great professor. She goes out of her way to make sure she is available to help students. Try not to miss any lectures and do all the homework (twice a week). Test questions are very similar to homework questions.
DR ASHLEY SPEAR is a great professor. If you do all the homework by yourself , you can answer all the exam questions. Don't miss the lecture !!

Dr. Spear was an amazing professor, probably the best I have had in this ME department. She is good at explaining and doesn't move too fast. She also really wants to help her students, so if you are struggling go to her office hours they really help!
Dr. Spear is a good teacher who does her best to help you understand. Some homework assignments are difficult but are really helpful for the exams.

Best teacher that I've had in the Engineering school. She is super organized and very approachable. You know exactly what is expected of you and she is there to help. I had her for her first semester of teaching undergraduates and I was blown away at how dialed in her class was. It felt like she had been teaching the course for 10 years.

Prof will either make you fall in love with material science, or hate it. If you're MSE, take him. If not, you may not like it. Personally the subject matter was interesting, however the intensity of lectures will give you whiplash. Homework will take a long time so work together. Friendly and passionate, but a little disconnected.

Very passionate about Material Science and it helps to make classes engaging. Difficulty comes from disconnect of lectures and homework. Topics in class are way easier to grasp then the homework. Tests are hard but if you follow the study guide and use the cheat sheet you will have a big advantage. His YouTube channel has lots if examples for HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Sparks is very passionate about what he is teaching, he is very nice and always willing to answer questions. The homework is extremely hard and you HAVE to go to his/ta office hours to complete it. You can bring note sheets to each exam, and you will get a good grade as soon as you study for it. I am glad that I took his class.

Homework are based on real event in life at its 100% more difficult. I can see he is passionate about what he's teaching but he's too smart and is teaching at a very high level. He has youtube videos that I found helpful to watch before class and on top of that read the chapters and attend office hours and maybe you'll pass this class. Good luck!

WAY too hard for an introduction to MSE. The homework takes 6-10 hours to finish because the problems assigned are 5x as hard as material we cover in lectures, or even harder than material covered in the textbook. The only way to do homework is through office hours and online research. Not to mention the exams... (40% average is norm) consider this

Sparks knows his material. Homework is ridiculously hard, only way to get through it is to attend TA help sessions or spend 10 hrs/week on it. His tests are even harder. First midterm class avg was around 25%. What's the point in making exams so hard everyone fails? Also shamelessly plugs his own research / youtube videos / podcast. Narcissist.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I'm in my second class with Professor Sparks. I took his intro to MSE class and it was without a doubt the hardest class I've ever taken. However, he is so knowledgeable and is a fair grader. His lectures are interesting and engaging. Take him whenever you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is very enthusiastic about Material Science and what he teaches. Homework is very hard and takes 9+ hours, not including reading or lab. Use the TA office hours they are the true key to passing the class. Lectures are good just lots of material covered and very few examples. Be prepared to suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As a person, he is super cool. Very funny, lots of memes, would totally hang out with. His class is horrendous. HW takes 8+ hours and is impossible to do without TA office hours. Would recommend to take at SLCC. Lectures are very general and HW and exams are mastery level specific. This class has no business being this hard. Run for your life.
He's so good for the Intro to Materials Science course that I low-key have a crush on him now.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He loves what he does and I can respect that but this is supposed to be an introductory MSE course but he treats it like a level 5000 course. The things he talks about in class have nothing to do with the homework and the homework takes 10+ hours to do because you have to research everything. Almost everyone I've spoken to is completely confused.

Sparks tests are ridiculously unrealistic. HW takes 10+ hours per week. He grazes over the material in lectures when his HW and test questions demand a much deeper understanding. He is enthusiastic but does a poor job of 'dumbing things down' and actually explaining the information at a students' level. Test avg was typically in the 40-60s.

Phenomenal professor. The definition of a person who loves their work. Homeworks take 6-10 hours per week and tests are very hard. However, he curves the average score on every exam to 80% so try to collect as many points as you can rather than getting stuck on a single question. Good luck!

Have you ever taken a class and had a horrible professor, so you go online and find this one random dude on youtube that is an amazing teacher and makes the content seem easy and interesting? Sparks is this guy. He loves and knows about his subject so much that it's hard not to join him. The class is hard but I doubt any professor would be better

I know that you are supposed to spend 2 hours studying for every hour spent in lecture but Sparks makes sure that his homeworks take 10+ hours to finish. Even when I sit in office hours surrounded by the smartest guys in the class it takes us over an hour to finish one problem. Class average on the first test was a 41%. He is a cool guy though
Very hard class. Lectures about way too much stuff to even keep up. Tests and homework are incredibley hard. The homework every week takes several hours
Super hard but very worth taking. I learned so much. Makes tons of extra resources available to help students succeed.

Sparks is the best professor I have ever had. He is beyond enthusiastic and committed to seeing his students succeed. He demands a lot from the his students, but the time and knowledge learned is well worth it in the end.

One of the best professors I've ever had if not the best. This class is obviously hard, but he honestly puts so much effort into trying to help you learn that it isn't as bad as it could be. I've learned the most in this class out of any class and I really, really enjoyed him as a professor. If you have work ethic you can do well in this class.
