What can I say? He is a great guy but the class just moves SO fast. Week 1 homework and you would think you were in a 3, 4, 5000 level class! Most students are terribly confused and fall behind quickly. Most of us think when we see the homework each week "Where on earth do I start?" Tests are savage and unrealistic. Take elsewhere if possible.

This is up to date the hardest class I've ever taken. Our grade consisted of daily clicker quizzes, weekly homework, and four tests. It wasn't unheard of for homework to take upwards of 15 hrs to complete, however there are more resources than most classes to help you (most don't finish). Dr. Sparks applies a generous curve to his (brutal) tests.

The first thing I would say is having gone to lectures and reading the textbook, the lectures are basically worthless. The lectures cover no new content and less than the book. The homeworks take 4-10 hours and the exams are usually curved 25 points. It's kind of a weed-out/ hurdle class. Labs and demos are cool, we did blacksmithing, electrochrom
His lecture was good but does not cover enough. He only teach the surface of the material but exam question is hard and more deep than what we learn in class.

Sparks' lectures are gold.  Ask questions when you have them, go to office hours when you need to, and be thorough in your equation sheet and you'll be set. He is an enthusiastic professor, and I highly recommend him.
His lectures where very interesting. You could tell he was very passionate about what he was teaching which made the course more enjoyable.

He's a nice guy and really wants the students to be successful but to the point that it kind of hurts his rating. His tests were so hard at times, it was as if he thought we were all geniuses; he would often throw curve ball questions on tests.  Go to office hours for homework and get the participation points to absorb the hits of low test scores.

Taylor is a very good professor. He is very passionate about the material he teaches and excited to work with students. I highly recommend this course from him, just know this course at the U of U is very difficult. Not the professors fault, he teaches what is required. His tests are fair and he applies a generous curve as necessary. Great guy!

Gives it his all, but course is super difficult and he's just not very good at translating things into simpler terms. Grading is ***BRUTAL*** and at times make littleno sense. One exam I did excellent in when I didn't know half the material, another I failed miserably when I thought I aced it (friend aced it thinking he had failed.)
Tests only have three questions and had too much hinging on whether or not you forgot one equation. Consistently tested on material that was not sufficiently covered, or outright passed over.

New professor just began this past year in the materials science department. Has done his best at stepping into the professor role and the role of a researcher. Is very good at relating to students and getting them involved.

There are 4 parts, one for each month of the semester. A HW quiz and a section quiz are due each month (so 4 of each). The notes are fill in the blank, so super easy. I felt that she explained the math very well. I didn't struggle with it much. I did find the tests fairly difficult though. It requires knowledge, and not just skimming the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course is broken into four sections and there are large amounts of work due all in one day. It felt like I was constantly scrambling to get stuff done. Also, the canvas page was hard to navigate. Also, the quizzes were way harder than they needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor did not supply ANY supplemental learning material. You are only expected to read the textbook, then get tested on it. There are two assignments that don't require any estate knowledge, a midterm, final, and a huge comprehensive case at the end. I didn't learn a thing, because I can't teach myself from a textbook. Got an A though
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heather was incredibly accommodating for me and I could tell she really wanted me to pass her class. I'm not a math person but with a little bit of studying the quizzes were not the worst thing in the world. Rating her a 5 because I truly would not have passed this class if she hadn't been so kind.

The actual content of the course is super relevant and I learned a lot from this course that will be helpful in real life situations. She uses power point presentations for lectures with quizzes after each section. 2 projects that weren't difficult but required time to complete. Effective course and good instructor.
You do have to study for the quizzes but other than that its smooth sailing.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good Lectures. Projects and tests are easy if you try. However exam study guides weren't very helpful, and exam questions were made harder than they should of been. Probably because the source material is high school level concepts being taught in a 3000 level college class.

I could not hear the presentations no matter what I tried. Super frustrating. She's funny and nice. The class is super easy. There's one homework assignment + accompanying quiz and a section quiz due every month or so. Cumulative final but she drops your lowest scores so you don't even have to take it. Also she absolutely hates contractions????

Took the class online. Homework and Quizzes were straight from the lectures. No surprises. Lectures were very informative and easy to follow. Pleasant voice to listen to. She does go on a few tangents but I found it made the material more interesting. The project was awesome to help prepare for retirement (start now!). Take the class online.
The midterm and final were really really hard . I was very dissapointed with the grading . The homework were really hard too . However, she was a really great lecturer and with good sense of humour.

I took this class online. The lectures are confusing because the instructor goes off topic. The way of she explains concepts is confusing and not to the point. If you have time to actually pause the lectures to comprehend what she is saying, this class is for you.

I guess I don't have the good luck everyone else did. This teacher goes off on tangents SO much it's hard to focus on the material. She also posts presentations that are 2 hours long (and are obviously from past semesters) and talks far too much about her family. She knows her stuff but really this class is difficult.

I took this class online. It was fairly easy. The teacher gives lots of great resources to help you succeed. The lectures are all posted online, but the instructor goes on tangents easily. Just do the notes, and homework and you should be fine.

Heather is awesome. She has a great attitude/sense of humor. I was nervous about the class, but it turned out to be great (very useful info). Lots of stuff to remember, but cheat sheet allowed on final. Recommended!
Great class!  Learned a lot of good information that I will apply in my actual life.

Heather was a very fun teacher and this was an awsome class! I was nervous to take it but I learned so much and it is stuff I will use for the rest of my life! I would recommend this class to anyone even if it is not in your major. The tests were a little bit difficult. She makes the class a fun place to be.

Heather had a really great sense of humor.  She although there was a lot of information and assignments, they were not that hard.  The only difficult assignments were the mid-term and final due to so much information to memorize.  Otherwise I would definately recommend her for her flexability with assignements and overall fun class.
She is great! Very willing to answer any questions or clarify assignments.

He started off strong in the semester, but as it went on no one could contact him, the modules werent being opened up, and there was no clarification on assignments. Usually I love my history classes but hes made me second guess my major.

This professor has made it really hard to enjoy this class. He hasnt communicated with anyone in over a month. He doesnt respond to emails or anything. I submitted a complaint to the head of the history department. I wouldnt recommend taking this class with him.

He never answered any of my emails the entire semester, and I could never get a hold of him during office hours. Besides that, super easy class. Almost everything is online including all the tests and powerpoints. He claims to take attendance based on an attendance question but I went probably 5 times and ended with 100% attendance and an A-.

He rarely communicated and from what I experienced, never responded to emails even when they prompted a response. He also frequently misspelled things which created more work because you had to try and figure out what he actually meant. From my experience overall, he made an interesting subject become a bothersome chore.
Class is fairly straightforward, lots of reading and quizzes. Very strict about late work, but gentle when grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the most incredible professors that you will find at this university. He cares SO much for his students and for them to succeed, and he will push you too. If you are interested in pursuing research on campus, consider reaching out to him. I did a UROP and received credit for CS4950: Independent Study with him. No experience is not a problem.

He is the one of the best professors I've ever had at the U, along with Dr. Kopta. I've never learned this much from homework and project. His course is well-structured and solely for students' growth. I love how his lecture slides are organized and clear. I can see how much effort he puts in each slide.

Semester is not even over at the time of writing this. Vivek is very smart and knowledgeable, but his lectures are so disjoint. His office hours aren't much better. Class is mostly grad students. Could be just me, but it is near impossible to learn from him because he can't explain things simply. ML is difficult but shouldn't be THIS difficult.
He is a great professor and probably the best professor I have had at the U so far. On the same level as Prof Kopta and probably better than him in lectures

He is the professor with very high knowledge and has the extraordinary teaching skills. So which makes this course to be out standing one in all regards. The way he explains reasons for everything using the math and intuitions were awesome.

Vivek knows his ML, and cares that you know as well. His lectures are great, and the project/assignments are expertly crafted to help you really learn the material. He is chill, funny, and very easy to respect. He is thorough to a fault; as a result we didn't quite get to the neural networks assignment. Other than that complaint, outstanding prof.

Vivek's lectures are extremely engaging and easy to follow and understand. The assignments do take some time, but that's to be expected for a course like this. He's very approachable during office hours and is happy to answer questions or provide clarification. Overall, he's great at teaching, and if you want to take ML, take it from Vivek.

This is THE prof you want to have for ML. If your interest in ML is only as deep as the promised salaries, skip this class. You should be ready to grapple with theory, math, and ethics in uncomfortable ways. Vivek is really good at bringing it all together and making it make sense. Be ready to work hard and be rewarded in kind.
Lectures are largely useless and focus entirely on theory. Assignments are very long and large portions of knowledge necessary to complete them are not included in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Useless theory mumbled lectures. He Doesn't care about outcome of the 'Machine Learning' course. Not at all recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Machine Learning has been my favorite class at the University and I cannot recommend Dr. Srikumar enough. He has a real talent for taking complex concepts and explaining them purely and succinctly in plain English. The assignments take real time, but are at exactly the right level to further your understanding. Amazing class, amazing professor.
Good professor. Tests are scantron which is nice for an OIS class. Concepts really made sense as he would relay real world situations for everything.
Covered exactly what he said he was going to cover.  Had a good understanding of the subjects.  The tests were fairly difficult, but if you did the homework and came to class they were very easy.

Sriram's class followed the textbook exactly.  I did well on the tests because the problems are pretty much the same as you do in the book.  He is very long winded.  Also he will grade hard on the group project too.

A fairly good and clear teacher, but very boring.  Never made it through a whole class period.  Tests steadily get more difficult, and he doesn't seem to work with the students very well, although maybe it was just me. No help given with class project, which was hard.

This prof. experimented with an entirely case-based class structure this semester so no book was required, which was a plus. However, you read a LOT of cases and they are mostly LONG! One semester project is required, and you must turn in an assignment every class. Material is simple and straight-forward, though. Good elective class.

Yotam is goated. Don't listen to other bad reviews. They were written by students with no experience actually learning from him. If you go to office hours and stick with the class, you will have a great time and will learn a lot of good math. He is a cool dude also and you will enjoy it if you give it the chance.

He is a really awesome guy and he will always keep you engaged but sometimes he doesn't explain topics super well during the lectures. I would really recommend going to office hours. They are game changing.
Good guy. Gave good explainations when you ask. Go to office hours that will change everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind guy, plenty of extra credit opportunities. The tests are somewhat difficult, but he lets you know what's coming, very few curveballs. The first week of this course, you will want to drop out, but he does that on purpose, so just push through it gets better. Homework load is light, and class enviorment is super fun.

If you take this class get ready to learn absolutely everything about it on your own. He assumes everyone knows much more than they do and can be rude if you don't know the answer to a question. He is funny though and he's a very very lenient grader. Study up on your own and it's an easy A, but if you want to actually learn from him good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is no materials provided for the entire course besides the textbook. There's no course modules with information about the topic. Studying for the exam is IMPOSSIBLE. The prep exam consists of 5 questions, aside from that there is no other provided materials aside from the textbook link that doesn't work.

Class attendance isn't required, but going most days will keep you on track. Yotam is funny, quirky, and genuinely cares about his students in his own way. He's always available during office hours and works hard to ensure you understand the material. Keep open communication with him and youll be fine. I'd definitely take another class from him

This is for his online course, College Algebra 1050 (it isn't listed here). This has been the absolute worst experience with a professor/course I have ever had. Every student has complained about no response when emailing him. There were a lot of errors in the structure of the class that we had to point out. Average test score for exam 1 was 51%.

By far one of my favorite professors of my college experience! He has an amazing sense of humor, loves to tell jokes, and is very passionate about teaching. Though the class topic itself is challenging, he is willing to help you understand the material, you just have to put forth the work needed to achieve.

Yotam is a great professor. Some people may dislike the sometimes long explanations of certain mathematical principles, but he wants people to understand math more than a plug-in-play formula. His lectures are great and help a LOT with understanding the material. He is a great guy and wants people to learn. Put in the effort and you will do great.

Yes he has a bit of an accent and not the best handwriting, but he is a great professor, office hours are very helpful, and he encourages participation from everybody. If you pay attention and participate in class you will quickly become friends. He is caring for grades and wants to help in every way he can. PARTICIPATION IS KEY

This professor is not only lazy but impossible to understand. His accent is tough and his handwriting is at times unreadable. Usually a min late to every class, leaves class the second its over, office hours are a chore. If you don't understand something he might make you work it out in front of the class struggling at every step.

I didn't like Professor Svedin. She gave us TONS of readings! You know...one of those professors that thinks their class is the only one you are taking. I also hated that she didn't have powerpoints. You just had to listen to her talk for hours on end...overall not a fan
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lina was a wonder to work with. It is always so nice when you get a professor that actually cares. She engages with students, is open to after hour questions, and is opening to helping students any way she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class was amazing, I truly got out of it knowing a lot more about public policy. The professor is great, intelligent and truly cares which was such an inspiration. I highly recommend at least taking one class with her. It is challenging but if you do the work you will do good. It was one of my most challenging classes but definitely my fav!

Dr. Sundar is one of the highest regarded professors at the University of Utah, David Eccles school of business. I'm so grateful to have had her several times.  She is so kind and respectful.  She is always well prepared for every lecture and is without a doubt an expert in her field.  You will love her class!

His grading methods were very unclear and confusing. My grade on the first exam, taken in September, was randomly increased by three points during finals week with no explanation from Mr. Tan. Additionally, Mr. Tan's provided study resources for the two midterm exams left much to be desired, and he put questions on the test not covered anywhere.

Might be the easiest online class I've ever taken, considering passing is a 55%. The course itself is difficult, I mean it's Calculus 3, but I felt I was propelled in the right directions. He encouraged us to go to office hours as much as we could, as in he was actively there to help us learn despite it being online.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His tests are pretty hard although the good thing is that he does give a lot of extra credit and also curves the grades sometimes. There is a lot of homework, and his online video lectures are pretty good. Never met him in person though (because it was an online course) but the canvas is well designed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The worst math professor I've ever had. He refuses to make any accommodations even if you go to him weeks in advance. He gets off on watching you struggle and failing students. He's literally evil. should not be a teacher.

What everyone else said- lectures were vague and exams were always a surprise. Homework was way too heavy, and we don't go over similar problems in class. I never felt like the tests were similar enough to the practice tests. I learned more from the supplemental videos. Lowkey passive aggressive, he was upset that we didn't do great on the tests!

He honestly wasn't that bad. He's a pretty good lecturer in my opinion compared to other professors. He was passive aggressive like other people mentioned . Honestly I was scared to ask him questions because he would get kinda mad if you didn't know . His grading is pretty good . I would say he's pretty average, not amazing tho

He was passive aggressive, condescending, and would cold call on people. Extremely fast paced and spent only one class vaguely going over each topic. He didnt curve exams even tho averages were 60%, but he did curve the grade scale for the class. HW and exams were significantly harder than what was covered in class. 3 midterms, weekly quizzes + hw

Honestly not great. The resources he provided us were very helpful. And his Canvas was very well designed. But, he was less a teacher and more a rule enforcer. He was not very lenient, and the entire class was self-taught. His one redeeming quality was that he curved grades and gave more points because we struggled so much. Wish I took someone else

I can't tell if he was trying to be funny or not but nonetheless he came off as very condescending in all communications. He is an ok teacher that to his credit puts a great amount of effort into his students and is willing to help but his overall lack of patience and consideration made the class more difficult to endure than the actual content.
Lots of homework but it was possible to get great scores on it if you spent enough time. Did act as if the entire class was inept at points but was a good lecturer besides that! Would recommend :)

I enjoyed his jokes in the surveys. If you do your homework in advance and review the lecture notes properly, you'll probably do well. Exams are not easy due to true or false questions (standard response questions are fine in my opinion) but it helps you learn a lot. Try to attend study sessions! He actively helps students whenever we ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have really enjoyed taking calculus 1 from Professor Tan. He always wanted to help me with the questions that I had. I think he explained the concepts in a simple and clear way. He tried to create discussion in class, but a lot of us didn't answer his questions or participate in discussion. We probably didn't want to look stupid.

Was hardest required class for my degree (3.92 GPA). Prof. Sundar is brilliant, but lectures don't prep you for the brutal homework/exams (65 final median). TAs/Piazza often unhelpful. Course was unnecessarily hard--38.1% overall was a C-. Final grades/curve weren't released until last minute, causing panic. Poor way to run a class in my opinion.

The worst professor at the U. Did not care about his students and would not listen to feedback. Failed so hard at teaching that when everyone failed the class, he curved the grades so hard that a 30% would pass. Never take a class with this professor. 5 Assignments every week as well.

While the lectures can be interesting, they do not prepare you very well for the assignments and tests. There is a batch of assignments due each week, and I found that at least two of them would require a lot more time to research more into the topics in order to complete the homework's. The final was extremely difficult.

Algorithms is a hard class, but I think Sundar teaches it very well. Most of my general criticisms are nitpicks. I think that the questions in exams/homeworks often leave out detail that is then required as part of the answer, which leads to annoying point deductions. Very generous curve at the end of the course however, and he's a cool guy.

Hari is a decent professor overall. He is a good lecturer, and the assignments are usually well-crafted to learn the material. He does have a tendency to repeat ~30 minutes of last class at the beginning of the next class, and the assignment design is occasionally unfair (mod arithmetic was rough). Exams are tough, but curved. Not great, not bad.

Hari is a very engaging lecturer and genuinely wants students to fully grasp concepts before he moves on. You can retake quizzes until you get 100% and coding assignments can also be resubmitted until you pass all tests. His lectures are very easy to follow and takes notes on and grading is fair and motivated by student success.

Hari really cares about his students success. He makes it his personal responsibility to engage you, and takes responsibility as his failure if he doesnt get an engaging crowd. If you have the eagerness to learn in this class, Hari will take yoi there

The class was informative and Prof Sundar is really smart. I asked him a few questions after class and he gave poor or unhelpful answers. Start the hmwk early since it takes a while to do. Study like mad for the tests because theyre difficult.

Hari will do a lot for a student in order for them to succeed. There's weekly homework, but it is so easy to contact him for assistance or clarification. He will make time for you in order to clarify concepts. His quizzes are challenging but you get unlimited tries, so by the time you get a 100% you can end up learning a LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I almost did not take the class because of the previous ratings, but I am glad I did. Professor Sundar is not the best lecturer I have ever had, however he knows his stuff and formats the slides in ways that are very helpful for the homework. You can succeed in this class as long as you look over the material provided and work hard on the homeworks
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hari is a fair and reasonable professor. His lectures can drag a little bit if he gets off in the weeds, but he cares and knows his stuff. He is accessible outside of class and is helpful if you go to his office hours.

You have a much better chance learning the material somewhere else, the amount of examples he uses are far too little to provide any help on most of the homework. Tests average is around D+ with no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Usually I come out of a class feeling like I've gained a new skill. The way this class was run I feel like a have a vague idea of several concepts but no new technical aptitude to show for it. He doesn't respect holidays by assigning regular homework for example Thanksgiving. Assignments are often too ambiguous to answer without the help of a TA.
Hard to understand - very thick Chinese accent.

She is a caring professor and understands that you are more than just a student. I emailed her when I was sick, and she was understanding. There are 2 or 3 assignments a week and a few quizzes. It wasn't super difficult but not an easy A either. She doesn't accept late work, however there are a few extra credit opportunities through the semester.

Im surprised Su doesn't have any ratings yet. I have taken several classes from her and every one has been a great experience. She is really dedicated professor that cares about her students. In her courses you can pass without trying and probably even get an A out of them, but putting in the effort is 100% rewarding.

Great professor, and a very easy class. Graded on only like 6-10 things and was really only based on completion. Errors in this class didn't matter. If you did the work, you got an A. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes the sweetest professor Ive ever had and his work is very easy.
Mr. Swensen was one of the best instructors at the U. He has a clear grading criteria and is willing to help students. He's replies to questions in a timely manner and does his best to answer them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is the nicest professor Ive had. If you ever had a conflict with deadlines, he was more than willing to extend it. Hes very understanding and super funny. I would recommend him as a professor but not the class. There was a lot of papers to write and I didnt feel like I learned anything new.

Lectures were heavy but he made them as fun as one could make them! Grading was clear, and he was super flexible on deadlines as long as you came and spoke with him. He wanted everyone to be successful, and he was very understanding of everyone's situation. I would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He cares about his students but you must go to class and stay focused because his tests are hard. He gives you a cheat sheet during exams and he gives lots of extra credit opportunities. He wants you to get a good, but the material is difficult!!!
He is a really fun professor and genuinely loves economics and teaching. He is very laid back and chill.

Professor Sarangi is very very kind, understanding and caring for his students, however, doesn't teach microeconomics, rather talks at you about them. Ive never been more confused in a class in my life.
Hard to understand. Doesn't explain things, just rants.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Economic History course.
Grading was unexpectedly difficult to understand. Otherwise the readings were interesting and the lectures were nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Enjoyed the class!

I suggest you don't take this class with him. He doesn't seem to care about the performance of his students.  Flies through the material, hard to even take notes. Doesn't listen to suggestions. Does not know his subject.  It just hurts students.

He cannot explain anything! The man thinks he is too good to be teaching us. He has no business teaching a class that he can't break down to teach others. I went to a local high school teacher and she helped me pass. He doesn't have the clearest, simplest explanations. Funny accent and a sly personality. Go to tutoring and AVOID him at all costs.
I never wore my seatbelt while driving to school because I wanted to die before making it to his class
I don't know what bro wants, I don't know how he wants me to do it. Wakes up just to give me a bad time.

I'm not sure what the School of Computing management was thinking when they put a new professor in charge of two of the most important classes in the department. He held a grudge the entire year after I went to the department head to complain. At least we get the good real world experience of learning to deal with a totally crap boss.

He didn't seem like he knew what he was doing with a course that has been taught at the University of Utah for forever. I'm sorry that this was many people's last class before they got into their full computer science major. Hope they stick with it.

Nice guy, but courses are kind of a mess. I'm not sure how his more traditional CS classes are like, but many people were quite frustrated by his capstone class. His canvas page was pretty unorganized. There were important links in random places and it was hard to know what was due. He also didn't have a clear grading criteria which was frustrating

I'd advise you to stay away at all costs, but it's not like you have a lot of choice for senior capstone. Swaroop has a fundamental misunderstanding that his role as a professor is not to be a dictator, but instead to facilitate the project and to make sure things actually get done. Avoid conflict at all costs, The Grudge learned her thing from him

Swaroop seems like a good guy. From my point of view, the course had a very appropriate level of difficulty, the annoying part was the lack of clarity. Often times on tests and assignment writeups I found myself wondering exactly what was being asked. If he could be more consistently clear it would do wonders for the course.

Swaroop is such a nice guy and will help you anytime he is in his office. He wants to improve and his exams and lectures got much better throughout the semester. He is a fair grader and will curve if necessary. My only big gripe is I didn't like using his custom components API and I wish he was on piazza more

Swaroop wasn't as bad as a professor as a lot of these reviews are stating. Although some of his lectures and assignments were unorganized, if you asked for clarification he would try his best to go over what you had a hard time understanding. Midterms take a lot of studying but know that a lot of the questions require critical thinking. 8/10

Swaroop was decent towards the end, however, when he first started it seemed like he never taught anything in his life. His assignments are all over the place, the tests covered things that were not explained or even mentioned in lecture. No text book for self study. Turn around time for grades was ridiculous, upwards to a month and a half! AVOID!

Difficult professor and difficult class, but I did feel like that pushed me to learn. He is a very knowledgeable guy and is very willing to listen to you. The class was extremely disorganized. The TAs were almost never prepared for lab, some of the projects were ambiguous and needed clarification. Accent really is not an issue.

Really boring lectures, disorganized labs, large pair-programming assignments every week. Nice and knowledgable but slow and not the best lecturer. Midterms/Final definitely requires alot of studying to do well. Accent isn't as bad as everyone might say. Probably wouldn't take a class from him again.

Swaroop was a really good Profesor and always went the extra mile to help those who needed help. He is definitely knowledgeable on what he teaches. Lecture slides where hard to refer back to so take notes! Overall I think he was a great Profesor and he was really understanding when it came to issues students had with grading or labs.

I know others were harsh but it's hard class so chill. He has great lectures and if you ask him any question 1-on-1 he will always help. Very nice guy and not afraid to admit he's wrong. I would definitely take his class again. Also, goes the extra mile on Piazza and grinds out assignments in the middle of the night. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is my third time taking CS2420. Dr. Joshi is by far the worst professor I've had teach it. Assignments are too big, test questions refer back to assignments and lectures instead of standing on their own so if you forget something you may be completely unable to answer a question, heavy accent makes listening difficult. Doesn't curve grades.

Prof Joshi is a fine lecuture and takes in student feedback and adjust the course accordingly. Prof Joshi is also great with working one on one with. His tests are hard so be prepared to spend a LOT of time on the homeworks. Most of these other complaints are based off the course 2420 and not Swaroop. His accent isn't that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class with him is a total nightmare. Lectures arent helpful and his exams are way too hard. No matter how hard you study it doesnt seem like you will get anywhere. His programming challanges are even worse. His expectations seem to be way too high. I understand that the class is designed to be tough but he seems to be going over the top.

first class in my college experience I had to withdraw from. Swaroop has an accent that can be hard to understand sometimes. He's very intelligent and knows what he is talking about but has a hard time teaching how to apply it. Despite my best efforts, I felt like I couldn't succeed in the class. Now I gotta reconsider my life lol

Absolutely horrendous professor. I don't normally complain about accents, but he has such a thick accent that it's difficult to decipher what he says. Assignments are all partner work even if you can complete them on your own. He explains things okay, but only responds to followup questions with tangentially related responses that are useless. Etc.

This was the most frustrating class ever. Very tough grader with very few assignments. Sam provided organized lectures but was never clear about expectations and didn't hesitate to take off points when you didn't do it his exact way. He was dismissive of my questions and concerns. I had to teach myself from the textbook to get the grade I got.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Math 1220- Calculus II

Sam is a grad student, but despite other negative feedback, I had no issues with him. He's very nice, and genuinely seems to want everyone to understand what he's teaching. He takes lots of questions and does his best to answer questions with examples and explanation until he's sure the student understands. Very nice guy.

Mr. Swain is a very straightforward, tell-it-like-it-is teacher. He was very honest and stated that he wasn't impressed with the way the textbook explained things. His lectures taught the material in a different way, which I found helpful. He was also very kind and helpful in extenuating circumstances. His tests reflected the course material well.

This class is great if you're majoring in a mathematics-heavy field of study. If not, then you may see his lectures as more difficult than other professors. Be prepared to invest lots of time, and realize that the material may be frustrating at times to you. It is VERY important that you go to office hours with questions that aren't understood.

I took a condensed Trignometry class that was a full semesters worth of math put into 6 weeks. Sam was very helpful during his office hours. He was always able to answer my question and made some math homework easier for me. He's a really nice guy.

Okay so it is not the hardest class by any means, but if college algebra is at all new or ehh to you this is absolutely not the man to help. He told us only come to class if it's helpful. So I'm like AWESOME, but no, cause I would have to go to class to learn it, so then I would pull up to class and literally want to be anywhere else. SOOO BORING

Sam was mediocre at best. I'd say he's at most a 3.5/5. Sam tried really hard to be a good teacher, but he taught certain subjects a completely different way then the textbook and videos he provided said. The way he explains things is confusing and asking questions only makes us more confused. Half the class stopped showing up after a while too

Worst professor I have ever had. Sam is extremely quiet, monotone and difficult to understand. He does not properly prepare his students for the tests and does not give any idea whatsoever of what will be on the tests. The class consists of tons of homework and having to learn lessons and watch videos on your own in order to know what is going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As someone who wasn't learning algebra for the first time, Sam did a fine job refreshing my knowledge. I did have to teach myself the subjects before class in order to follow the examples in class, but if you put in a little work, this class was not very difficult if you have a basic understanding of math.

Sam was one of the worst professors I have ever had in my lifetime. Sam is very hesitant about all of his answers and teaches like a turtle, yet covers 3-4 sections every day. He may be a great person, and does try to help students outside of class (albeit very horribly), but he cannot teach to save his life. Stay away from this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this course. Although attendance was not mandatory, you get extra credit (added to your final exam grade) if you attend class. Professor Swanson could be difficult to follow, but the practice quizzes/worksheets from discussion were very helpful. Don't be discouraged if you fail the first exam-I was able to get back to an A.

She was good considering the amount of people she was lecturing. She explained things thoroughly, I just had a hard time paying attention in class. The quizzes kept me on track so I was able to do good on the tests. Not too much homework.

Shes as good as she can w/ 350 students who won't shut up during lecture The homeworks easy it let you retry infinite times. SO many ways to get extra credit. Some TA's were good others not, theres tons of resources &office hours. if you actually try and realize that this is college and you have to do more than just show up then it wasnt hard
Sit in the front of the class and participate, and you'll be fine.

Doesn't teach well. Remember just because someone works at a university doesn't mean they have any capacity in teaching. She provided lots of opportunities to get extra credit, so that's a plus, but she is not suited to be teaching intro classes, and her TAs were just as bad. 
Very nice on a personal level.

Professor Swanson knows her chemistry but when it comes to teaching, her lectures are over irrelevant information and she teaches way too fast. She also assigns about 2-3 homework assignments each week that don't pertain to what we are learning. Her tests are also hard with questions we never go over, but she gives lots of extra credit.
She just doesn't teach the material well and also blows through what we actually need to know and spends time on things we don't need to know but she thinks they are cool.

Lectures are hard to follow and complicated. She gives a ton of extra credit opportunities. Do the following to do well: go to your assigned class discussion EVERY SINGLE WEEK to get help from TA's (you are f*cked if you don't), do review slides for the exams (not the practice tests), do the review problems in the book before quizzes & do the HW

This class is extremely hard if you don't already have a good grasp of chemistry and physics. You'll have a quiz or exam every week and they are not easy. Lectures are too short for the material covered and she doesn't completely finish her work before moving on in the lecture or on to the next topic.

Lectures are annoying fast and material is covered quickly with limited review or examples, just tosses ideas and expects you to know them. Quizzes are weekly on previous content and are short. Tests are not too hard, easier than the study guides provided. Chem 1 isn't too bad but bad teaching makes it harder for no reason.

Professor Swanson is nice and makes it clear that she has a deep understanding of chemistry. However, she is unable to translate what she knows to students in gen chem 1. Assumptions are made that we already know what she is teaching. I have had to teach myself most material due to lectures being so confusing. Take from professor Kuntz if you can.

Prof Swanson is clearly very smart and passionate about her projects in chem, but she is not a good teacher for beginners. She speeds through lectures very quickly, saying things like "we all know this already, right?" I realized pretty fast that I would be teaching myself with the textbook/other resources. If you can, take from Professor Kuntz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Swanson makes learning chemistry miserable. She explains everything as if you already know the concept, how to perform the equations, etc. and moves at a ridiculously fast pace. If you can get Ms. Kuntz, I highly recommend her. I attended several of Kuntz's lectures solely because of how abysmal Swanson's lectures are. She's great!

Sweet lady, NOT good at explaining basic concepts in the sense that she overcomplicates things - slides are packed full of needless graphs that distract from the main point of the slide. TAs for discussion is even worse. Reviews are him partially solving a question, which confuses everyone. Kind of seems he doesn't know what topic we're even on.

Lectures weren't great but using MasteringChemistry and the online videos she posted for each module helped you learn the material. Test scores were low but she would curve the grade in everyone's favor. Gave out a lot of extra credit. Not the best at lecturing but will give you plenty of opportunities to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. She rushes over important topics that are present on homework and tests leaving students very confused. The average for lots of tests and quizzes was a 50% but she gives out so much extra credit it's the only reason I ended with an A. Most of the time I learned more from a 5 minute video on youtube than her 50 minute lectures.
Professor Swanson knows her stuff. The material of the class is rapid and uses MasteringChem for Homework. She is a fair grader, but expect questions on the homework you haven't yet learned about.
She is a pretty good professor and her lectures really help. She does her best explaining what are really hard subjects to comprehend. Love the layout of the class.
Definitely a hard class. I learned most things in the class on YouTube and the textbook because every time I came out of class I was always really confused.

Swanson obviously knows her stuff, but is just awful at teaching. I dont think I learned anything from her lectures, and the only way I got through this class was because I took chem in high school. Beyond confusing. She is willing to work with students, but just doesnt know how to teach. I wouldnt recommend this class, find a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Terrible at lecturing, would be better off just teaching yourself from the book and slides. Rushed through important topics and went off on confusing tangents that didn't relate to course material. This is the kind of class that gives your a headache every time you go and literally everyone is confused.

I took ENGL 2095 just for the credits, but fell in love with the class thanks to Prof. Swanstrom! She really is an amazing teacher and made the subject matter very interesting. She gives feedback on almost all written assignments. Discussions are interesting and the homeworks/labs are honestly fun. Attendance never felt like a chore.

Lisa is a great teacher! Participation definitely matters, but I was able to make up those lost points with an easy extra credit assignment. She gives very clear feedback on assignments. All the readings were on Dropbox, so no one had to buy textbooks.

Professor Swanstrom is an excellent teacher! She gives extensive feedback and her lectures are always interesting. You will be reading about one novel per week with a short essay for each text. Reading and participation (and in turn being in class) definitely matter. She is great though. One of my fav profs. I learned a lot from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Best professor at the U! If I took her class and that's it, I could be a better teacher than most teachers out there. She is extremely clear and goes out of her way to make sure everyone is learning. I wish every teacher could take this class!
She is AWESOME. She will teach you so much and is incredibly real.

I had Dr. Swan's content literacy course, and it was one of the most useful I've had in the education department.  She focuses on classroom application, and methods I haven't seen before.  Useful, fun, funny.

Sydney is genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had within my entire schooling career. She is so caring, thoughtful, and understanding. I felt like I really belonged in this class, and she always had time to visit with students one-on-one. The environment curated in class is very inclusive, and you are given so much creative liberty!

Sydney has, by far, been my favorite teacher I've taken so far. Fair warning- her warm-ups are weird. You'll usually do social experiments and games that go along with 4D art. They're are no tests and all the homeworks is super simple and light. She's extremely flexible and will open up and extend deadlines if the class needs it.
Sydney is the sweetest professor! She was very understanding and willing to work with me through a rough patch. Definitely recommend her class!

She is an incredible professor and a great introduction to your first year of fine arts and the Art Education program. She was always kind and caring, able to include everyone in the class, and engaging. Attendance is essential, but she's very understanding if you have a valid reason for not attending class! 10/10 class

Sydney is a lovely professor! She is very fun and cares about every student's needs. The class was easy. We did some readings and crafted a notebook and a quilt. She is a very open professor. Please always be kind to her because she will help you succeed as a student.

Gave a lot of work that was useless and did not have any impact on what we were tested on in the exams. The skills we learned about in excel was very useful. Just wish that was all we learned and did not have to do assignments like pack backs and hands on projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I felt he took a while to grade and hard to understand.

Love this man! He emphasizes the Excel portion of the class, and the concepts are taught through videos (pretty easy). Really good prof to have before 2030. Told me he would repeat the concept 100 times for me. He likes to be sarcastic with students when no one participates, which brings life to the class. You can tell he cares for his students.

Syd was a great professor for this intro to business class. He was always extremely clear in his delivery and you can tell his is very passionate about his work. His class times are flexible and if you score well then you only have to attend half of the classes. It is an easy class if you go to review sessions and keep up with class material.
Lots of writing in this class. Good feedback on writing, though not too helpful with grammar. Condescending at times. Will help if you ask for it.

If you have a chance to join the honors college at the U, I would strongly recommend against it. They're two-faced with lofty promises and no attempt follow through. The advising is awful and they emphasize a liberal education at all costs, even when it's detrimental to a particular student. The classes are jokes but filled with busy work.

Sylvia expects a lot out of her students. People take her classes thinking they'll be able to skate by. You need to be present, participate, and put in solid effort. She recognizes students who work hard, and will often become a mentor figure to them. You put in what you get out
She will not listen or try to help you. Her ego is pretty big and if you try to bring up a concern she wil shoot you down.
The class should've been more exciting than she made it.

She isn't mean, but she tends to sternly hold to her views. She clearly presents her ideas and is open to variations on these ideas. She is not, however, extremely accepting to views that vary significantly from hers, which feels a little problematic in a class that is supposed to be as open as this one is.

Great and interesting class. Very difficult though, be expected to know a lot of material. I recorded lectures and printed notes, and would review often. The final was difficult, midterms were doable. He curved the grade though, so even if you don't do well on the final, you can still be successful in class. If you put in the time you'll do fine.

He expects you to know a lot of detailed physiology & does not go back to refresh memory of old concepts. His lectures were boring and hard to remember. I suggest buying the textbook. I passed thanks to the curve but I felt like I didn't know one answer on the final because "all of the above" & "a and c" are available answeres on most questions.

This class is not easy. His lectures can be dry but they are mandatory if you want to get a good grade. You have to work for your A in this class. Textbook may be required if you want supplemental information. Overall, a good professor and difficult class.

The lectures are supremely boring, despite his occasional attempt at humor. Attend class and pay attention. I would purchase the book if I could do it over again, to confirm ideas and information that were missing in his slides. Overall, this was a very tough class but the curve at the end helps.

My recommendation to pass: record lectures with an app and review often. Go to class everyday. He does pop clicker quizzes but they aren't hard. Tests were hard. 2 midterms and a final plus quizzes make up your grade. I didn't use the book, but wish I would've to clarify. Teacher doesn't help much, usually makes you talk to the TAs. Hard class.

Dr. Symko is an old guy. Teaching since the 1960s, it kind of shows. He is really passionate, although be prepared to have to teach yourself a few things. He is happy to explain things, although not always super thoroughly. He is a cute little guy, and he really cares about his students. Lots of office hours- you can even call him. A good teacher.

AVOID HIM!! Test averages were 50 %, his lectures don't match the homework. His exams didn't reflect what was on the hw nor the lectures. I spent 6hrs a day doing his hw, went to the TA tutoring sessions, SI sessions, had a private tutor, attended all his lectures and his discussions and was getting 40% on his exams. Take from someone else.

Lectures do not align w/ homework and expectations of student knowledge are far higher than prereqs for the class. I have gone into his office hours several times for clarity on homework questions and every time left frustrated. He is condescending and has ridiculous grading schemes. For missing 2 Qs on an exam, I got a 76%. I do not recommend him.

His lectures are simple but exams are extremely difficult. Cute old man who uses chalk and writes in cursive. The exams are nothing like what his lectures are. Averages were about 40% on all exams. Go to his test reviews. I stopped going to class after fall break and got my highest exam score. Overall, I would highly recommend taking elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but hard class. Tests can be much harder than homework, and the averages were around 50%. There's a massive curve, but you'll have no idea what your grade is until the very end. To do well, you should attend lecture, do the homework, work through problems in the textbook and exam reviews, and attend Symko's reviews before the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Don't take this class unless you already have a solid general knowledge of physics because his lectures aren't helpful. They're word for word out of the book. His homework is hard but the worst part is how much there is weekly. The exams are RIDICULOUS. It was discouraging that the class exam average was around a 45-55% for a general physics class

I thought Symko's lectures were VERY helpful. The homeworks and exams are hard but he gives you everything you need in lecture. Such a nice guy and funny. Also there is a crazy curve. I don't know why people said the lectures weren't helpful because they are. They just aren't word for word what the homework is.

The lectures make sense (be prepared to read cursive on a chalkboard) and are decent. HOWEVER, there is webassign homework twice or three times a week, with 10 problems, that don't usually reflect any of his lecture points. I literally yahoo'd every question, though try to figure it out yourself 1st. Yet, there is a HUGE curve! Exam scores avg 50.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Definitely a tough professor. However, a huge portion of the class gives up a few weeks in and the class is curved from a B-. Read the chapters, go to his test reviews, and utilize office hours. I had a rocky start, but after doing what is stated above I really turned my grade around. Personally I really like Professor Symko and enjoyed his class.

Very Helpful teacher but his lectures can be somewhat general and thus, it takes quite a bit of creativity in the homework and tests to expand on the concepts. His tests are difficult as they are always extensions of the concept that make it impossible for people to memorize their way to a good grade.

His lectures are interesting but right out of the book. However, the tests are NOT based on the book OR the homework. They are usually 50% averages so thankfully the class is curved and the average is about a B-. It was a super hard class and although he is the most charming old little man ever, I would not want to take it. Ever. Again.

His tests are insanely hard, he gives problems that were never went over in class. He is very nice though and is willing to help you if you take the time to ask him for help. There is a curve, since test averages are in the 40's, but you don't know your grade until the end of the class.

Disorganized. He just takes examples that are already worked out from the book and regurgitates it on the chalkboard (these are simple examples; The tests are MUCH more difficult). The averages for his tests are low (last test the average was 43%). You have no idea what your grade is until the end. Also, TAs in discussion won't help with hw.

Orest is a great teacher who really truly cares about his students. If you ever have a question or feel the need to ask him to clarify something after class he will gladly work with you. His lectures are full of examples to learn from which can be unclear so be ready to read your physics book. Overall great teacher and amazing guy.

Despite a lot of students criticizing Symko, I found him to be a great professor. To succeed: go to class, take good notes, do your homework, attend discussion with a good TA, do the review problems to study for each exam (most important). Exams can be tough, but easy A in the end if you do the above due to the high curve. Don't be lazy.
Worst teacher I've ever had. He is so scattered and unorganized. I wouldn't take another class from him.

I hardly ever went to his lectures as I found them not helpful at all. However, the materials are really easy if you do some reading and do the weekly homework. Exams are easy since he allows a note card for notes; I got over 90% for all of his exams. Huge curve for exam grades.

Good luck for all you poor souls who plan on taking takes Symko. My class averages was 58100, 51100, 41100, 41100. His tests are not easy at all. But just stay average above. Because If you are atleast average you will get a B. With that said, good look taking Symko's General Physics class, may the odds be ever in your favor.

I would want Orest  at my family holiday dinner, the man is straight up charming.  He states at the beginning of the semester "this is going to be tough, just like getting in shape!  Running and doing sit ups are not easy but you do it, this class is hard but doable, just do it!"  I went to SI sessions and had to track down the best TA to do well.
Dr. Symko is coolest cat this side of hipsville. Super cool dude, knows a lot of jazz, man, he was swingin'!

This guy is so confusing and ridiculous. He won't even listen to your question before he starts to talk over you. The homework takes hours to do because it is so difficult and there are 2 due each week. His tests do not reflect at all what is covered in class and were ridiculously difficult. He just doesn't really care about his students.

The notes aren't very organized and I had a difficult time keeping it all organized. The homework was difficult and the tests were near impossible. The average for the class was under 50%. It was curved but I always felt terrible after taking a test.
Dr. Symko is always willing to help. But his notes are a little confusing and not organized at all. Most of the classes end up having to be curved. So, just keep up with the class average.

One of the most frustrating professors I have ever had to deal with.  I feel bad for Physics majors with someone like this involved.  He is confusing, doesn't explain what he wants on tests (even though he tells you he does), and answers your questions before you even have a chance to finish them.  Also, chooses horrible texts.  Avoid if possible.

If your in physics, this will be easy. if not this will be hard. He told me this class can be hard even for physics students(IDK) but he is always willing to help the student. He is more concerned about how much you learn and not what you do on the test. Test and hw is hard to worry he grades on a curve bc its such a hard class.
pretty good professor.  awesome accent :)  really nice guy.  only complaint is that theres never enough time to finish his tests.  other than that he's a great teacher to take the class from.

hard subject, easy homework, great professor, very good lectures. exams are much tougher than lectures and homework and averages are very low, but you just have to do one standard deviation above the mean to get in the A- range, which is pretty easy since most people that take the class are not that bright.

This professor teaches well. Physics is a hard subject for anyone. Dr Symko is willing to give you his time and attention. He can be a poor listener at times so be direct with him. The class is far more difficult than you would think. A "C" on his tests was a 38. He super hard but willing to help.

Symko is one of the NICEST professor I have ever had! He's always willing to spend time outside of class to assist you with any questions you might have. He uses vivid examples to help you understand the lecture. However, the content of the class is difficult so it might be easy to get frustrated with him when you don't understand the material.

Make sure you go to him to ask for help he will really help you, like give u  answers.  Sometimes in class the information is unclear, but just read the book. There were assignments i didnt turn in and i felt like i was going to fail the class but he took care of me.
Class was quite easy, make sure you go to him for help!  He will give you answers to all the assignments.

Professor Tang is not as bad as these posts make her out to be. She is not the typical friendly professor, and has tendencies of being rude towards students, but purely as a professor will provide you with everything you need to do well in the course. If you put in effort, you will do well, simply showing up to lectures is not enough.

Professor Tang is very unprofessional and blamed me when she gave me wrong directions to fix a problem. It got to a point she made me leave during the middle of class to go cry in the restroom after humiliating me in front of the class. She made the classroom a hostile environment that many students stopped showing up. Don't take O-chem from her.

Ming Lee has been the worst professor I have had at the U. She does not care about her students, is a poor lecturer, and can be challenging to understand. Her attitude makes her unapproachable to student questions. Please try everything to take DeLuca instead.

Professor Tang is by far the WORST professor I've ever had. She does not thoroughly teach you all of the material and then will incorporate concepts on exams that were never discussed. The only reason I did decent in this class was because of the TAs and from my own studying habits. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER.
Professor Tang expects the best from her students. The class is tough, but if you keep up with the textbook and go to office hours, it's doable. The class is also graded on a curve.

Ming Lee Tang has a fundamental misunderstanding of what it means to be a helpful and inspirational teacher. The TAs carry the class with Tang as an expensive backpack for the U. She once said, "Don't submit regrade requests if you got the question wrong, because, well, you got it wrong."

Instead of explaining concepts, she just shows you what to do and expects you to get it. My friend and I were in a car accident and both got concussions. We had to miss classes and she docked points to a failing grade. We both went from a B- to a D+. She refused ADA, which isn't allowed, so luckily the dean removed the class from our transcripts.

Professor Tang's lectures are clear and easy to follow. Read the textbook and use office hours. Unlike the other ochem professors, she doesn't give any extra credit, but does grade based on a curve. If you want to know ochem, take Professor Tang. If you want to be handed out an A, take Holly.

I am not writing this out of anger or hate, I received an A in Tangs class, I did very well on every exam. O-chem is a really hard topic that takes a tremendous amount of effort, the already hard class is made harder by tangs teaching style. If you approach her with questions she acts confused on why you don't know the answer to the question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The most I can say is that she is unapproachable and an extremely harsh grader.
Do not take her! You will have to retake the class if you do. She thinks all of this is common knowledge and is not helpful.
Without a doubt the worst professor I've ever had. I wouldn't wish her class on anyone.

Do not take this class if you want to learn or be treated with respect. The lectures are very confusing, she is a strict grader and will often not answer questions but just tell you to read. I have heard her be rude to her TAs in discussion too. Very unprofessional when asking for points back on an exam too as she will often become combative.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Proffessor Tang was good. I will admit she was a very harsh grader on tests, but if you went to office hours she was willing to help. You can't succeed in this class without reading the book and using the T.A.s. The discussions were extremely helpful. The overall grade is based on only a few tests, but there was a very generous curve at the end.

This was a very difficult class, but I don't think Professor Tang was as unreasonable as some of the reviews mention here. My one-on-one interactions with Professor Tang were very helpful. She clearly knows her stuff and I found the discussions and textbook useful. The class is heavily weighted on three exams and a final with a generous curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very disorganized and confusing. Tests are very harshly graded and partial credit is very minimal, you could be missing one atom and miss the entire question. Tests are also poorly worded and it is very easy to not see a question. She is also very condescending towards the students who aren't doing as well as she would like.

She's not merciful in tests and can be intimidating. I relied mostly on the TAs who carried the class. Also, I mostly did everything in zoom screenshotting her lectures to Notion which benefits me far more than note-taking. OCHEM is hard so don't slack off or else you fail. It's that intense. This is my retake and I learn more from TAs thankfully.

WARNING! DONT TAKE THIS TEACHER! She sets unrealistic goals for her students and when those goals are not met she treats you very rudely and gaslights you because you are not at her level. Only reason she gets a 1 rating is because her TA's carried this class for her and I can't go lower. She writes unnecessarily difficult exams that average 50%.

One of the worst chem professors I have ever had; 80% of the course is exam-based (class average is a 50% usually), homework is due before class and is often unrelated to the lectures, her lectures are hard to focus and boring. Very harsh and condescending, don't take this class with her. She is ruining the chem department

Talia is hands down the best professor I've ever had. She cares so much about her students, is always available to help, teaches the content well, organized, and provides extra credit. Literally best class I've ever taken.

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever taken a class from. They did an amazing job teaching all of the content, and you can tell they are very passionate about their work from all the interesting extra content they add throughout the lecture. They always take the time to meet the students where they are and cares a lot about the students.

A QUEENN!! Such an amazing professor who clearly cares about her students and their success. Passionate, engaging lectures that made me want to come to class every day. LOTS of extra credit! Easy A, but I actually felt motivated to learn because of her.

Young, relatable, and new faculty. Clear syllabus (lecture clubs, exams, 1 project), passion for material, connects content to current literature. Brought answers, literature, and insight to the next lecture from class questions. Reading text book helps. Refreshingly challenging exams. Promotes undergraduate research and scientific literacy.
Best professor ever. Lectures are very organized which makes it easier to learn. Exams are tough but not too tough. Not much homework, but will teach you how to read a research article.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor was fine, but his teaching style wasn't the best. I saw someone say that anyone who didn't do well didn't try, which isn't true. Exams are 75% of your grade, and homework is the rest. Class averages were low. A midterm had to be curved, and partial points are hard. On the bright side, the final is a retake, and exams can be curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor seems like a good guy, but the class felt harder than it should have been. Grades are only homework and exams. Four exams total (one retake), worth 75%. Practice exams are very old (some from 2006). Notes are handwritten engineering paper. The final average was 35/105, and another midterm had to be curved due to many failures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows the content well and teaches it well. No attendance based grading, plenty of practice material and provided answer keys for the homework before its due. Low ratings here are just for students that didn't try. Test content was lecture and homework content. He is not some researcher who puts lectures on the back burner, dude is charming

Tests are 75% of grade. Grades harshly on tests and they are only 4-5 questions each. On our second midterm he included a concept we talked about in class for 5 minutes so the average for the test was 60% and he was forced to curve. Practice materials for the final were from 2005-2006. Lecture notes from 2011-2014. Wish he cared about the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for CS 3130, 3 tests make up 75% of your grade, the average on most tests were about 75%, one average was 60 and he curved to 74%. One test gets dropped, the tests are only 3-4 questions. TA's graded harshly.

You honestly don't have to show up to class to even do well as long as you keep up with the lecture videos he posts on youtube. The practice exams aren't very reflective of the actual exams, but the in class examples are helpful. The grade is heavily exam based, but curves are given if the median is low. For every exam, cheat sheets increase by one

The class materials are outdated, with notes that have not been updated since 2011 and are handwritten. The lectures are extremely difficult to follow because the instructor jumps around and often seems unsure about what to cover. Even if you work hard, the concepts are not taught clearly, and you will end up wasting time.

This was a wonderful professor even though he had prepared notes he made sure he answered any questions in class. The Exams clearly reflected EXACTLY what was going to be in class so if you simply came to class you knew what to study for, I didn't have much interest in this class before I took it, afterward I understand Prob. & Stats are important.
if u wanna live past college, just dont, dont even try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Pros:
1. Responsive; very open-minded, to the degree that the professor lets her students contact her using a phone call and text message. Also, she usually replies by the following day.
2. Provides necessary resources
3. Grades quickly
Cons:
1. Busywork, busywork, and busywork
2. Too much little assignment. 
3. Untraditional Canvas module style

Alright avoid professor Karren if you can. She's got such an ego when it comes to the papers. You have to write on one of the blandest topics of CSR. She's very strict on grading and expects a lot from the students. All the reading and textbook modules are a waste of time and money and could just have easily been looked up on the internet.

The worst class I've ever taken taught by the worst professor I've ever had.

Avoid at all costs trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Teri was a lot tougher of a professor than I had expected. At first, all of the assignments were super easy, then they got exponentially harder towards the end of the semester. Overall she cares a lot about the success of her students and is really easy to work with. Just a lot tougher of a grader than I had expected.

Abysmal class. You cannot make any mistakes for a rough draft of a paper. She says there is "a gold mine of information" when looking for academic resources. Then a few weeks later says we probably don't have any because we haven't done as much research. Awful class and teacher.

A lot of assignments that you have to do which isn't as bad as you think. What is really bad is the 7-8 SINGLE SPACED paper you have to do. This includes a SWOT analysis and other tedious requests. Personally, I think that is a joke to have that much as a SINGLE SPACED assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Teri is a fantastic teacher. There is a lot of homework, which can coincide with projects and begin to feel like too much. However, assignments are relevant and helpful to each project. The class can seem disorganized but Teri is always available for questions. You will do well if you follow instructions and commit to doing the work.
There are 40 assignments for this class so be prepared for a lot of busywork.

This course requires a $150 online textbook to complete assignments. There are assignments literally every class even when we have massive papers due on the same day. I would not take this class again. The professor does not really teach anything yet is critical of papers on things that she does not understand herself.

This is a busy work professor. There are large & time consuming assignments every week. Content of papers & assignments are not hard at all, but frustratingly time consuming. Very easy to get an A if you are willing to spend time doing homework and papers.

Rebecca is really caring and supportive outside of class. She holds office hour every day and extra review sessions before each exam. She also provides very well structured handouts and summaries of studies for each lesson. Her grading is also very fair with bonus credits during exams and grade replacements.

Rebecca is visiting at Carleton College, and I have really enjoyed LinAl with her. She is super caring, and clearly wants students to understand the material and do well. She gives lots of opportunities to do well, including grade replacement on the final. My only gripe is that every once in a while, she would assign hw beyond what was taught.
Rebecca is amazing. If you take the time to go into her office hours she will make sure you succeed and go out of her way to help you in any way she can.
It's a tough class but very doable. She goes very fast in lecture and can be a bit confusing but one-on-one she's amazing. Definitely go to her office hours.

Very helpful one-on-one, but teaches directly from the book and won't slow down to explain. Uses only examples from text and rushes through them far too quickly. She is heavy on definitions, but doesn't explain them well. Be prepared to teach yourself.

Dr. Benney is passionate and very knowledgeable about environmental politics. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to both understand the material and succeed in the class. The course involves a lot of lectures and reading, so staying on top of the material is important. She also really values critical thinking, esp. in essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Benney! She is so educated and she was awesome for this class. There were only like 5 assignments throughout the semester, so just make sure to try hard on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures and LOTS of reading. Tricky part is that reading is so broad and there are few assignments. Sometimes is was hard to figure out the main points of the material. There's one quiz, four papers, and one online discussion. The TA was INCREDIBLY unhelpful and I felt like Professor Benney didn't really gaf about her students at times.

Very nice person who cares about her students and the course material. The entire grade was basically 3 essays, however they were manageable if you started early. Though, there was lots of reading so be ready for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tabitha is very funny and super down to earth. She does care about her students and is very engaging with the class. Class is extremely reading and lecture heavy, but if you actually do the readings and attend class you will be just fine. Had two 6-8 page papers, a few smaller [preparatory] assignments, and a final exam that was all multiple choice

Professor Benney's class is graded based on three papers, but she makes it pretty easy to understand how to write these papers, and isn't a super harsh grader so if you put in the work your efforts will pay off. She's really kind and willing to meet with you outside of class and she gives great advice. It's lecture heavy but easy to understand!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Benney is fun, down-to-Earth, and incredibly intelligent. I loved learning from her research experience mixed with some of her personal commentary.
