reviews.comment: She puts so much into every lecture. She teaches because she wants to and she is good at it. There are papers every week, 2 pages single spaced, and 4 4-5 page double spaced. They are extremely easy though and if you do everything it is really easy to get extra credit on every assignment 10-20%. Grades attendance heavily. So you must show up.

Her lectures are great. She shows lots of music and film related to serious topics in social inequality. I highly recommend taking this class if you need to take the DV/BF gen ed. You'll learn a lot but the grading is very fair for the weekly essays and the exams.

I took her class five years ago (2013) and still remember her lectures. She had a huge impact on how I saw the world and taught me a lot about myself and the world. I've gone out of the way to recommend her to people outside of the social science field because she has a lot to offer students and her passion about the subject is unmatched. A+ prof!

I went into the class with low hopes (as it does cover gender studies), mainly for the 2-for-1 GE credit. You watch pretty intense stuff, I always get an adrenaline rush after attending class

Beautiful human being inside and out. Very passionate about what she teaches and all of her students. She wants everyone to learn and works hard to create a healthy environment in her classrooms
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: This is the most amazing teacher I've ever had. I'm now doing a Soc minor just to take all her classes.

Professor Martinez is an amazing professor. She makes lectures interesting and supports her students. Her classroom envionment is very friendly and accepting. Expect a short reading and 1-2 page assignment weekly. There is also a paper due in the middle of the semester. Follow her instructions and you will easily pass this class.

This is the 2nd class I've taken from Theresa, and she is still the best professor I've ever had. Her lectures are so engaging, it's the only class I have never drifted out in. Weekly small readings/papers, 3 exams. Does take attendance daily, sometimes has pop quizzes, but super easy. The material was very interesting as well. Theresa is incredibl

There's a reading every week with a different type of response paper. They were easy and she is an easy grader. There are many opportunities for extra credit. Martinez is incredibly passionate and fun! She cusses a lot but she is so lovable. Her class however, won't teach you much about inequality. It covers what everyone already knows. Still fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: By far the best professor at the University of Utah! Take any of her classes and you will not regret it. SOC3381 will change your life and you will never look at the world the same. The content is so important, everyone should be required to take this class. Would take 10000 times over again if I could.

Theresa is the best teacher I've had at the U! She is passionate and I looked forward to going to every lecture. You explore a lot of interesting topics which inspired me to also take her Deviant Behavior class! As far as your grade goes, it's super easy. 3 exams & 2 essays. I got extra credit on both essays and 95+ on all 3 exams. Just take notes!

I wish I could take her class(es) every semester... She makes her students engaged and wanting to learn. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and her tests and assignments are easy if you go to class. 12/10 would recommend taking one of her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: From the first day I looked up to Professor Martinez, she is so inspirational. Her lectures are amazing and has made me view the world in a better way. I hope to take future classes of hers and will always keep recommending her class to my friends!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: If there is one professor at the U that you should take a class from it definitely should be Professor Martinez. She cares so much for each of her students and on the first day of class, despite having 100+ students just in that session, she knew every single persons name. She makes you feel so many different emotions and is such a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Theresa Martinez is my absolute favorite professor. She is a beautiful human being who really cares about her students. She takes attendance and you won't pass if you don't go, but her lectures are great. Her assignments aren't hard and neither are tests. By the way, be prepared to get freaked out on the first day, she knows EVERBODY'S name

Theresa is by far one of my favorite professors at the U of U. She is hilarious and is always cracking jokes or telling stories which is what makes her class so interesting. She has a very strict no talking and no electronics rule. There are TONS of extra credit opportunities and her tests are not something to stress about as long as you are going.

She's so cute and entertaining. Normally in lectures I keep checking my clock for the time to go by faster but in her class time just flies by and I wish the class went for longer! I love her energy and personality because it doesn't even feel like a lecture. I'm now considering double majoring in sociology because of her. Awesome teacher

TAKE HER CLASS!!!! Theresa absolutely changed the way I view and see the world, and has made me want to minor/double major so I can take as many of her classes as I can. Deals with tough issues and is very real and open about them all. You will get an A if you just participate and do the assignments. This class was AMAZING and should be required.

Hands down one of the best professors I've had in any subject or program. She is passionate, fiery, brilliant, and so woke. She had us read books and discuss them thoroughly, as well as write about them. The books dealt with difficult issues such as rape and racism, but all of us in the class were changed by them! I plan to take her again.

I have taken one class with her and I would take more in a heartbeat. I wish I could find a way to work her classes into my major but I have considered taking more of her classes just because she is that good of a professor. Absolutely, my favorite.

Martinez is the best teacher i've ever had in my college career. The first day you go in she knows everybody's name no matter how many she has in the class, she is caring and passionate and engaging. She changed my life after just one class. Amazing person, amazing teacher.

I know it says Sociology of Rock N Roll but it should be music cause she covers all lectures from blues, hip hop, to grunge and metal. Dr. Martinez is a professor you should take to see a teacher who is passionate about what she teaches and the class opens you up to different kinds of music and how they influenced or were influenced by generations

I've never had a more effective, and compassionate professor than Theresa. She cared about each and everyone of her students and wants everyone to succeed. She has a way of captivating the students' attention for the entire class time, and she teaches such emotionally taxing subjects with grace. Take a class from her, she will change your life!!!

I've taken 3 classes from Dr. Martinez so I think that in itself says a lot!  She has a paper due almost every week but they are based on interesting topics.  Be prepared to get randomly called on, so make sure you've read the required reading!  She also grades for attendance.  All 3 classes I've taken from her seem to have the same format.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Theresa Martinez is easily one of the best professors at the U. She is so inspirational and has a personal connection to what she teaches. I really enjoyed her lectures and she was very easy to contact. Light reading assigned outside of class and minimal HW. Midterm and final were small papers to be completed outside of class. Highly recommend.

Professor Martinez by far has more differing opinions from my own than any other professor I have had, however she is a fair grader and she is very open-minded and friendly to those who may think differently on various subjects. She knows her material and she is able to teach in a way anyone can comprehend. I would recommend her to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVED Theresa. She makes class really fun and one that you actually want to attend. I went in not really even knowing what sociology is and she changed my life forever. If I could take every SOC class from her I would. Book is cheap but you can easily find articles/summaries online. Tests are all on canvas or you can write papers.

Honestly my favorite class taken. She is a amazing professor who really cares and is passionate about her subject. Great class. Don't be late. Also reading is mandatory for tests. I plan on taking more classes from this professor because of how great she teaches.

Professor Martinez is caring, inspirational, and well-respected among her students. She cares so much about the topics being lectured about in her class that often, Professor Martinez would get teary eyed in the middle of her lectures. Tests are taken online and very straightforward; you can choose between an essay or multiple choice test.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took an intro class, so I believe a lot of her zeal was misplaced. She tended to treat us as high school students; constantly shushing, not allowing computers, etc. However, it was very simple to pass and the criteria was very clear. She has a lot of passion for her subject.

Amazing professor. I loved attending her class, the lectures are exciting and captivating. She truly loves what she does and cares about her students and will learn every ones name. She is  the best professor i have ever had and have taken several of her course. There are 3 papers to write, she gives you the topic and you write it off the material.

I only took this class for the diversity credit, but it turned out to be my favorite class of the semester.  Martinez is a phenomenal professor and while her lectures are mandatory, they're inspirational and fun.  She always wants to know what you have to say about the films and music she shows you.  10/10 would take again

Prof. Martinez was great! In SOC 1010, your grade is based on attendance, 2 papers, and 3 exams. The papers are only two pages long, and the exams are taken online so they are open book. Her lectures are interesting and she shows a lot of great media in class. I'd definitely recommend taking this class from her!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It is an amazing; I took her class for my major: Sociology. I already fall in love with my major because of her. She changed my perceives from the society and made it better to become more visual. Also, we usually watch movie and music to understand author's perceptive by the society. Her class is worth our times even too many students.

Theresa is one of the best professors I have ever had. She truly cares about her students and is very passionate about what she teaches. I have taken three classes from Theresa and I have loved each and every one. Even if you're not a Sociology major, you should still take at least one class from her--you won't regret it.

Theresa was the best professor I've had so far. I enjoyed coming to class. She relates to students really well and makes the classroom a great environment. Attendance is taken at each class and effects your grade. Lectures are entertaining, she uses a lot of media which is nice too. Take notes and you should do fine. 3 tests and 2 papers, that's it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Holy Hell. Theresa is the most inspirational teacher I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. The subject matter can be really hard to stomach but she will help you discover your voice when it comes to speaking about current issues. TAKE HER CLASS. You wont regret it.

Not only did I love this class, but because of Theresa I decided to add a Sociology minor, just because of it, completely out of my field for a Cell & Molecular Biology major. The most inspiring professor I've had so far. Oh and she is REALLY hot!!!
Fantastic, keeps students interested.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This is by far the best class that you will take from the University! I loved ever second of it and you really lean alot. She is definitely the best professor on campus. It is because of her that I decided to add a sociology minor to my degree and I'm a Cell & Molecular Biology major. Oh and she is really hot by the way!!!

Theresa is by far the most inspirational teacher that I've ever had. She really dives into the subject material and relates it to her own personal experience. It oftentimes got emotional and was very eye opening. Regardless of your major, I highly recommend that you take this class or one of her other classes. Easy A if you do the work.
love dr. martinez! one o the best teachers at the U!
She is very energetic and she loves what she teaches. She is clear about it and you're likely to stay interested. Don't skip class because that will be you're ultimate downfall

Look, its a super easy class. Put in a little effort, do the assignments, take notes and you're golden. My problem with her was her constant injection of her political agenda into lectures. She also didn't give very good feed back on your assignments and left you wondering why you didn't get full points .

Professor Martinez is a once in a lifetime professor. She really cares about every single student. Her lectures pull you in and you really feel the connection. If you ever have the opportunity to have a class with her you should take it. She makes going to the University of Utah worth it!
Wonderful professor. You had to work for the grade, but if you tried you would get an A. I would totally take this class again because she changed my life.

Martinez obviously cares for her students and pushes each of them to succeed. On the first day of class, she had already memorized many of our 200 names. She is quite passionate about what she is teaching and always allows for people to speak their minds without being attacked. I learned a lot from her class, and she is definitely a lot of fun!

LOVED THIS CLASS! It will definitely be challenging not so much with assignments but more personally. There are things we learn/talk about like race and gender. It can be difficult for some people but for me it was a very eye opening class and made me realize many things that I was unaware of. I recommend this class! Life changing!

Love the way Theresa teaches and her enthusiasm. She loves what she does and it is so obvious. I would take this class again and the assignments are not hard they are actually pretty easy. Tests are also easy as long as you take good detailed notes during class. But its not hard to do that because her slides are detailed and so are her lectures.

Awesome Professor, knows how to captivate you. It's because of her I decided to add a minor in Sociology, and I'm a Cell & Molecular Biology Major, two completely different spectrum's.... that's how great of a teacher she can be!
Theresa is great! Her lectures are amazing and very interesting. She is very passionate about what she teaches. Definitely my favorite class of the semester!
She is my FAVORITE!
I've taken three of her classes and I will take more. Her lectures are awesome, she is an easy grader, and she accepts late assignments. As long as you take good notes, you'll get an A.

Definitely one of my favorite professors at the University.  She's very PASSIONATE about the subject, which makes it so much more interesting to learn about.  The movie and music clips she uses are relevant and make an impact.  You will leave her class with a completely new outlook on inequality within the U.S.

Theresa is an amazing professor and you will never be bored in her lecture. However, she treats her students like kindergartners. Despite her constant swearing, she will yell at students for not taking notes, not looking at the bored, or not looking "interested". She even has moved two people who were barely talking to each other in class.

Hands down the best professor ive ever had during my college career. She is an amazing person and her lectures will change you for the better! She absolutely loves what she does and is very passionate about her teaching. If you go to class, take notes, and do your work she will pass you. I wish I could take a class from her every semester.

Always had the most amazing  lectures. She doesn't worry about political correctness and gives creative homework assignments. Attendance is mandatory but you will actually want to go to class and if you email her a legitimate reason for missing class, she will generally forgive the absence. Even if you don't speak up in her class, she knows you.

Theresa is a phenomenal professor and is passionate about what she is teaching. Every lecture was amazing and has truly influenced my life. At first her workload seems overwhelming but the assignments are creative, short and she is a fair grader. Her exams are essays, but as long as you attend class and take notes, you will ace them.

Theresa is an amazing professor who respects her students while also challenging your views. She expects you to work in her class but she will go out of her way to help you. Her assignments were creative and you have to think outside the box to do them. highly recommend taking any class from her

Professor Martinez is an inspirational teacher who is passionate about her work. Attendence is extremely important! Be on time, take notes, and you'll be golden for tests! The tests are actually essays, so the notes are crucial for them. She truly cares about each of her students and wants them to succeed!

Great professor! I really enjoyed most lectures. However, I was frustrated because her essay assignments are generally vague and open-ended, yet she would take away points for specific things she wanted to see that were not mentioned. She swears by "not using rubrics" but it would be really helpful to know what she is looking for. Still, an easy A.
Great and fun lectures, fairly easy tests, as long as you take notes in class you're good to go!

Loved her class. She is very passionate about the subject. She keeps the classroom very engaged and interested. One of the most interesting classes I've taken. The class is not hard at all, but I learned a lot. Tests are based off notes so go to class. It's not that hard.

She really cares about the class and everyone in it. Very passionate about what she teaches, which helps everyone want to be there. Really great class. Even the assigned readings were interesting but not too long.

Theresa is by far the best teacher I have ever had. Her Dev. behav/Soc cont. class will blow you away. Wish I could take her every semester. She is a very engaging and empowering teacher. She is very clear about assignments and her test are all essays. Don't worry! she gives you plenty of notes to write your test on. Take her!!

Easily one of the best professors at the U. She's passionate and carries herself in such a strong way that you love the class, whether you're interested in sociology or not. She cares more about you leaving the class with an intention to make a difference, rather than throwing tough assignments at you. Highly recommend taking one of her courses.
She is an amazing teacher and makes class very fun and entertaining. I enjoyed going to class and listening to her lectures. I would highly recommend her as a teacher and I think she was fantastic.

She is passionate and will make you passionate. Her class can be a lot of fun. It is different from any class you will take. She does; however, pick favorites and her ego is a little large. She made some statements that were iffy and when I researched the 'facts' she presented were not from good sources. I would recommend at least 1 class from her.

Her passion is amazing. I learned so much in one semester just because of it. She does cuss a bit, which some people at the U won't agree with. To me, it more exhibits when she is passionate about a topic. I wold definitely take this class again each semester until graduation and recommend her to all my friends.

Awesome class, fun and interesting. Homework is easy and there is two papers a midterm and a final that is optional if you attend class everyday. Teresa is awesome and loves what she teaches. She can get a little out of control and she curses a lot (some people can't handle that). I recommend the class.

Professor Martinez was amazing, by far the best professor I've had thus far at the university. She has a strong passion for what she teaches, and she presents the material in a very real way. Actively listening in class will almost guarantee your grade. Amazing professor, awesome class!

I have to disagree with all of the positive raves about Dr. Martinez. The subject matter of the class was interesting, but I disliked her class. I think she could have used song and movie clips that were more relevant to the topics. She favors some students over others. She's admirable, but on a high horse. I'll never take another class from her.

By far the best professor I've ever had. I've learned more in her class this semester than I have throughout my entire college career. Make sure you go to class and do the readings, as long as you do, it's a very easy class. I highly recommend taking from her, but be prepared for some intense and potentially uncomfortable discussions.
Best professor at the U.

Dr. Martinez is an amazing professor--probably my favorite at the U.  She really cares about her students.  Her class is discussion-based and participation is mandatory.  You need to attend class (which is fun anyway) and do the readings--she'll call you out if you don't and make you write an essay.  Pretty easy grader.  Highly recommended!
very smart lady and easy to get along with. The classes she teaches are mind opening.
She's an amazing professor, just make sure you do your work and know your stuff! She appreciates honesty and hates excuses. Classes are not to be missed, and you don't want to miss them either!

She cut a huge corner, making the class final optional(which undermine the validity of the class).  She repeates urban legends as fact and goes off on irrelevant tangents.  She is passionate, and certainly does care about what she teaches.  She is engaging.  But it would have been nice if I she would have been more rigourous in verifying some of he
She brings the intensity.  A kick ass class!
Best prof I've ever had.  She cares about the subject, and makes you care about it.  You don't want to miss class, because her lectures are riveting
Great professor!  I really admire her!  She's an amazing woman! Loved all of her classes.
Theresa is the best  professor at the U. She is brilliant and hard but you will not forget her message. Long Live Theresa!
Amazing professor!!  Would love to take more classes from her.
She LOVES what she does and it totally shows.  AWESOME professor to have.

A friend recommended I take a class from her and I was not disappointed. She has a passion for what she teaches and she helps you open your mind about things. I enjoyed her class so much that I took another class from her the following semester.
One of the best professors at the U. She truly cares about the material and the class. You NEVER want to miss class or a reading, but she makes it all worth it.
All about attendence but is probably the best professor I had all through college. She cares about what she is teaching and knows things first hand.  Dr. Martinez rocks!!
No Comments
She puts her heart into this class.  Lots of work in the course, but she is great.  Lectures are very interesting.

Elpitha is passionate about her beliefs which can come off strong, but she is very caring. Her style of teaching is VERY hands-off. Sadly, this style is an immense obstacle to me. She is engaged, however. And she is available outside of class and willing to help where she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Elpitha is one of the most difficult, most inspirational professors I've ever had. Don't take her classes expecting to be able to skip class/slack off/turn in mediocre work. She doesn't coddle you like most professors do, which is nice real-world experience. Ask for help and she'll go to great lengths to help you figure it out.
Great teacher.

So unnecessarily feisty.  Can be helpful sometimes, but generally comes across as aggressive. She does this to "push" you, but can be very negative, which made my entire class feel unmotivated/discouraged throughout the semester. Don't take unless you have to for you major!
Bad teacher, bad help, group projects don't reflect skills needed.

Elpitha can  be insensitive and rude, she will call you out in front of everyone. It is possible to get on her good side, I guess she acts that way so you can push yourself. But, I was highly discouraged and did not want to attend her class, I felt unwelcome sometimes. Her assignment were unclear as well.

Best professor I've had to date. Extremely helpful in developing ideas and willing to aid you along the way. Sometimes gives vague assignment descriptions but is happy to clarify on a personal level. Excited to take any and all classes that this professor teaches.

Elpitha was the hardest and most rewarding professor I've ever had. She expects the most out of you and will push you to your edge. She is very nice and gives honest feedback on everything. I would recommend her any day!

Elpitha is feisty and can be rude. She wants everyone to do their best and she wont take anything less. However, the assignments seem pointless and she does not explain them until after you do them. She will ridicule you in front of the class if you do not do well. Attendance is mandatory.

I had microeconomics with him and it was a three hour class from 6pm to 9pm. Despite the late hours he still managed to make the class interesting. Very funny guy talks a lot about his personal life but somehow ties it into the class lesson. He explains things very well,  is willing to negotiate on tests, come to class he tells whats on the tests.

George is a super laid back guy. He KNOWS HIS STUFF. He just finished up a PHD in Econ and has worked in the markets for over a decade. If you are interested in the financial side of economics, he is the professor to take. The class was enjoyable and if you want an A you will get one.
This was an online class, but prof Tsilis was extremely helpful. And he made class interesting. If you do all the assignments, you'll get an A. Highly recommend a class from him.
AMAZING, AMAZING, AMAZING!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
George is an awsome professor. I would take his class at any chance you get. He grades easily and takes a real life approach to teaching.

Horrible teacher. Powerpoints were too crowded and useless. She made you feel stupid if you asked a question in class. However, she held really helpful review sessions and gave you practice exams. Her worksheets were really helpful for the exams.
Great teaching and wonderful examples

Talks way too fast, everyone gets lost but she doesn't understand why. Lectures are really confusing. Definitely knows stats but doesn't know how to teach it. Easy tests, easy quizzes. Just go to class and use the worksheets she gives you.

Smart lady. Most of the time cranky. Changes her mind about assignments all the time. Makes excuses for herself too often. Makes students feel stupid in class, especially when asking questions. I went through this semester feeling like I was going to fail every day because of her. She ended up giving me an A. All that stress/anxiety for nothing.

Good intro class to take for Psych. Her exams were open-note, which was helpful in compacting large amounts of material we had to learn. She may seem cranky or moody on certain days but most likely she'll accommodate your needs if you just talk to her. She expects a moderate level of commitment from students & uses a lot of video clips in lecture.

She did know her stuff. But... Unclear. Favoritism. Often cranky. Changes her mind about what is due and posts one comment on OLMS. (She expects you to read her mind.) Exams are TOUGH, be very quick. She gets mad when she offers opportunities to watch lectures online or take a late exam and students do that. She was frustrating.
Expectations on exams unclear. She uses a lot of supplement articles, lecture, and book with little direction as to what you can expect on the exam. Method of examination is disorganized.

Professor Saccomano is very nice. She gives good feedback on your assignments and is willing to work with you in any way you need help. She accepts late work and is very clear on her grading criteria. Very easy course and I'd take another class with her again.

Trish was one of the most caring professors I have had at the U. She ensured expectations were clear, she was understanding of when life got in the way, and she gave comprehensive feedback consistently that was insightful. HIGHLY recommend Trish!

I cannot recommend Prof. Saccomano enough! Take any class with her and you won't regret it. She is so caring and gives really nice and positive feedback for every assignment. She is also really good about answering emails if you have questions. She's the best!

Tricia is the best professor I have taken so far. She is so passionate about her job and is also so knowledgable. We had a bunch of guests come in and teach us different lessons and we went on field trips to other schools. I had the best experience and I learned so much. I would highly recommend this class if you are studying elementary education.

Tricia was the best professor I've had here at U of U! Her lectures are long, yes but they are extremely entertaining and informational and she is hilarious. I learned so much about teaching in this class, I wish I could take this again. If you are a future teacher, take this class you will get so much out of it!

Trish is so sweet! She puts long responses to your submission & talks about how interesting your paper was and that the careers that came up suit you. She pays a lot of attention to her students and shows she cares. One of my favorite professors. If you put effort into your assignments this class will be a breeze. I greatly enjoyed the course!

It seems like he teaches it as if it's common knowledge but it's not. I basically self taught this class to pass the tests. Homework on the week of the test is diabolical too. Also kind of sarcastic, which made me not want to ask/answer any questions.

It's such a shame because it is very obvious that he loves the subject at hand, but he is just a bad and disprteacher. Lectures were illegible, far too fast, and some questions were somewhat waved off as rudimentary. Would not recommend unless you want every other math class you take to feel like a relative breeze.

Passionate about what he teaches and very lenient on deadlines and grading, but the homework load can be heavy with other difficult classes. Lot of useful material is provided, but canvas page is kind of a mess

Overall a nice guy who provides everything you need to be successful. Class does require a lot of work but he is a more than fair grader and has a reasonable curve for the difficulty. + every lecture is recorded and livestreamed on zoom

The homework and tests themselves were difficult but the scoring was lenient so it was not hard to get a decent grade (plus homework was often allowed to be turned in late with no deduction). The lectures were messy and feedback on assignments was hard to decipher.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Treibergs is an impeccable teacher in everything except for teaching. Super nice, gives extra credit on tests, provides keys to past exams, and zoom recording on every lecture. He is so passionate about math that class gets so lost in his equations and it's impossible to follow relatively disorganized notes. Don't take unless you're a math major.

His feedback on assignments outside of the written papers is horrible. He doesn't explain why points were removed and often will just cross out answers. This is followed with unreadable handwriting that he uses in the lectures. That combined with a fast lecturing pace make it extremely difficult to keep up.

His handwriting is completely unreadable. The lectures will go through 25+ slides completely filled with writing in which he will only discuss for a moment before skipping. The only things that get expanded on are the easy topics, and homework has nothing to do with the stuff learned in class. Would not recommend to anyone.

He was all over the place. Homework is usually unrelated to lectures and exams (which were brutal). He is a very harsh grader. The average on the final was in the 50's and no one got above a 90. The papers were the easiest thing in this class, and even those he would demolish you with negative feedback. His canvas is also a mess. Do not recommend.

Lectures were poorly explained with poor handwriting.  It partially history, but most is doing math as it was done centuries ago without any of the tools you have now. Offices hours were not helpful, and the papers were the only easy part. Textbook poorly explains formulas and math concepts at times.

Treibergs does not lecture well, handwriting is terrible and pauses so much in his lectures. Everything has to be submitted on paper. in. His exam reviews will have 500 concepts to study only to give 5 super hard questions. 

Also: this is not "history of math." It is a rigorous math course with 3 papers all about math and technical writing.

I'm a bio major and took this class. It wasn't difficult and it's quite impossible to fail. A passing grade is 35%, you have to go out of your way to fail this class. There is a lot of HW, if you try you'll get some credit. You are allowed cheat sheets, so look at his previous exams. 3 papers which was the easiest part of the class.

Treibergs is a nice guy, but math history with him is an insane amount of work. Weekly hw with difficult math problems, 3 essays each 5 pages long, a midterm and a final. It was nice that I could turn in homework late for full credit, but almost every homework assignment made me want to pull my hair out.
Tough

The one positive is the grading is curved in your favor, I thought I had to retake. Extremely hard to learn unless you are a math savant. The textbook was impossible to learn from, way too dense. The concepts in 3210 are grueling to grasp, and he taught as if we should already know everything. Also he has bad handwriting and blocked the board.

I took Math 1310 class which is a beginner engineering calc class. He teaches like it is a high-level class, and if you ask questions, he makes you feel like you know absolutely nothing and puts you on the spot until you get it right or give up. He stands in front of the board, writing random problems while not telling you anything about the topic.

worked well with my learning style - he follows the book, and so i just didnt attend lecture and read textbook on my own. gives great feedback on hw and mt, and an A is 78%, so i would def recommend his classes if u like self learnin (probably not recommend if new to analysis / upper level math)

I was on track for a C-. I transferred professors and earned an A-. The average score for his midterms is 50%. The other 3210 professors had average midterm scores of 80% so I transferred into one of their courses halfway through the semester. Lectures are unnecessarily complex for our level. Midterms are twice the difficulty with half the time.

Literally was one of the only students that showed up to class and STILL failed - UNTIL he had to curve the grade so hard that I ended up with a C+ somehow.  Stands in front of the board while writing blocking it with his huge body, not receptive to feedback, etc.  Midterm medians were like, 45/100.  No joke.

Professor Treibergs clearly has a great understanding of all the topics and is nice enough. However, his hand writing is very hard to read and he often skips steps that he can do in his head, that can make lectures and reviewing difficult. His grading system is nice but needed. Honestly just read the textbook and youtube and save yourself the time.

He's definitely a nice man, but unfortunately his teaching style is incompatible with my learning style. He stands in front of a board, draws things, and expects comprehension. Ask a question? Risk being scolded for being a foolish fool. Go to Khan and youtube instead of lectures. The grade scale is generous, but you'll certainly need it to be so.

I will start by saying Professor Treibergs is very nice and clearly cares about his students. I had to stop attending lectures because I was getting nothing out of them. I had to start studying content from the book and from other online sources to get the material. So overall, lectures were no good. Grading was fair enough.

No matter how much I'd like/need to take a class, I would absolutely never take one from him again. He's condescending and his lectures can be broad enough that something ends up wrong or generalized and you're completely tripped up by it later. I dreaded going to this class.

He's fair and has a generous grade range with opportunity to make up points you missed on exams and drops lowest score. He's very open to questions and will do whatever he can to help you understand. Explains things well. The only issue is his handwriting is pretty bad and cluttered. You need to listen to what he says as he writes. Otherwise great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class I ever took. Excelled in the sequel with a different instructor. He knows his stuff, but if you're afraid of being berated in class I'd definitely avoid raising my hand. His method of grading is confusing, albeit lenient. Which made it difficult to know where my grade was at. Might have had to change, but he also didn't use Canvas.

This class is definitely difficult, and prof. Treibergs helps to some degree. He is knowledgeable of the course and will help you when you need help. The tip I have for this course (and math courses in general) is to ask for help. However, the lectures were a bit fast and mostly following from the textbook, but participation is important in class.

Truly a brilliant individual, but not the greatest at passing his understanding on to students. Lectures are dense and require an insane amount of focus. Exams are brutal, and the homework is even harder. Luckily, he understands how difficult his course is, so he is quite generous with the curve. I scored an average of 67% on exams, and I passed.

Very friendly guy, but he seems oblivious to the difficulties of transitioning from lower-div to upper-div math, and made me feel dumb on countless occasions. I thought I'd grown up with a very strong math background -- but it seems, from his perspective, I'm just a fool who's in over his head. Better teachers would have tried harder.

This class is extremely difficult, by far the toughest class I have taken at the U. Andrejs really wants to see you succeed though, so if you attend class regularly and do the homework you will be fine. His tests are very hard and he is a tough grader. He moves FAST when lecturing. Very nice guy though. Likes to call on people in class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Way too heavy on proofs. We are barely finishing Chapter 2 and it is the middle of the semester because he is obsessed with making us learn a million proofs. Most people in this class are not math majors so I'm not sure why he does this. He also makes things awkward for people who don't like to talk.

Treibergs prides himself in "challenging" his students. If challenging means personal attacks towards an eager undergraduate's intelligence--then yes, he is challenging. I was excited to take his class, but after 15 weeks with that man, I considered dropping math completely and just ending my life. It's fine. I passed the course, but at what cost?

This guy is a great professor. I had him for 3210 as well a few semesters ago! He's really tough and he doesn't like excuses, but you'll learn a ton. He's very accessible outside of class, and he uses that one on one time to really help you grasp the concepts-- he won't think you're stupid. I enjoyed my 2 semesters with Treibergs, take his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lectures difficult to learn from because he tends to face the chalkboard and explain things while he is writing it down. I had to teach myself most of the material. But he let us use the textbook on exams and R Studio on homework. The project at the end of the semester was really useful. Curved our grades at the end. Not much help outside of class.

Loves math and teaches it well. Whole class is on a curve so you 100% cannot get below a C- unless you literally get zeros on everything. Home works are tough and there's no solution manual, so go to his office hours and you'll succeed. Get full page cheat sheet for an exam and can use prior ones on next exams (so 4 total sheets for the final)
He's a good teacher, some don't like him but he knows what he is doing and is excited about it

Ive taken Lin Alg, liked it, and done well before so I rarely attended. He was an awful lecturer when I did go, and actually picked me out in class (not cool, severe social anxiety). After that no desire to go. Moderate tests, but his practice questions are not relevant. Weekly HW. The book taught me way more than he could.

IMO, Treibergs is average or slightly sub-average as a lecturer which, unfortunately,   means he is difficult to follow in lecture-based math courses. Expect to study hard on your own to grasp material. Tests and requirements are very reasonable but not particularly easy. Personally, Treibergs is a very nice guy. Overall, reasonable but avg quality
Quiet and has no flow to his lectures; its almost impossible to tell when he is transitioning between concepts or sometimes even example problems.

Stands in front of the board while he writes muttering to himself. Which makes taking notes extremely difficult. Your entire class has to participate / ask questions or he'll move right along. Whenever I asked him for help he'd give advice. Main resources were Khanacademy and the book, because lectures were very dense.

The homework is never ending. He takes doubts in class and during office hours, but expect hints at the most, not solutions. He pushes you towards the answer but never gives it to you directly, so if you ask him doubts in class, expect a discussion, not an explanation.

Analysis is a very difficult subject, but Treibergs does a great job helping his students understand the material. You can tell he genuinely cares about making sure everyone gets it. He's not quick to compose his thoughts, but that's part of why he's great -- analysis is a subject that needs to be taught slowly. I highly recommend this professor.

Treibergs loves teaching analysis. He's built up a mathematical lexicon that helps you visualize the concepts, he's friendly, and he doesn't throw curveballs on homework or exams. Foundations of analysis is a freakin' difficult class, though. I really liked this prof, but you've been warned.
Professor Treibergs has a rotund approach to teaching math 1070.

He has a habit of muttering to himself while working away on the chalkboard, then turning around and asking "got it?" when you're getting your first chance to see what he's been muttering about for the last few minutes. Sure, he's a very nice guy, but I don't find him to be an effective professor.
Analysis is the hardest math class I've had to take. I've always hated proofs, but he made it interesting and easy to understand. Very nice professor and always willing to help on homework problems.

This guy is kind and as helpful as can be.  He isn't one of those people that put others down because they don't know something, but instead he helps you to understand. I think he is one of the best teachers in the U of U math department.

Professor Treibergs is one of the best math instructors I have ever met. He also gives a lot of care to his students. Though his exams are relatively hard, I bet you enjoy his class if you have interest in differential equations or applied math.

He's very fun :3 Really wants to help you learn in the most effective ways. I never felt bored in lecture, he teaches beyond what the slides say, so much so that we often out of time before he gets through it all. Plus a lot of jokes that made it feel more lively/comfortable. The course itself is 10/10, more SWE than just plain coding.

Great instructor, I have nothing bad to say about his lectures. The course material and assignments were all straightforward imo, but they are time consuming. He does pollev, so attendance is graded. Midterm and final were pretty free.

Travis Martin definitely tries to keep his classes entertaining with a dry, but funny sense of humor. He has a daily participation grade that is very easy to get full points for. Assignments are straight forward if you are keeping up with the lectures. Would definitely recommend for any class if he is an option as your teacher.

So far my favorite professor in the CS program (had him in 1410 as well). His classes are difficult, so be prepared to put in the time. He purposefully makes his classes difficult so that you learn the skills that you need to succeed in programming. He wants to help you learn so if you don't understand topics he is willing to help explain things.
Sometimes his code demos didn't even work, but overall an average CS teacher and experience. He was open to answering a lot of questions, though

Pros: He posts the slides and code before each lecture. Easy to ask him questions during class, and he answers them very well. Exams weren't too hard
Cons: The later assignments are very long so start them as soon as possible

Pros: The course is well structured via Canvas, you can find past lecture slides, recordings, and quizzes.
Cons: Exams don't have a clear topic structure, uses OTHER prof. exam material as practice exam when he has his own material.
Note: Started doing 'code chats' were you talk with a TA (via Zoom) about the code you've written on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is really good at explaining the material. Lectures were always fun

He clearly understands his field very well and often explains it pretty well. He codes for most of the lecture time, which is a little hard to learn and understand. However, he struggles to explain concepts in simple terms when a student is struggling. The assignments are long; be ready to start early.
Pretty fair and funny dude. Had code chats which made some grades based on how the tas felt that day but not bad overall.

Favorite shape: circle 
Color: green
Euclidean solid: dodecahedron
Dinosaur: Argentinosaurus

These are things he was asked and he answered bc he's funny like that

Professor Martin is clearly knowledgeable in his field, but this translates to him being stumped when a student is unsure about a concept he has known for years.

His lectures covered a lot of material that would aid in exams and HW, but he'd code the whole time - it was not very effective for learning. 

8/10, do your work to do well though
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love you Travis Martin
Just because someone left google to come teach at a University doesnt mean he is a good teacher.
Excellent Professor, cares about his students and ultimately wants them to succeed. Materiel heavily depends on lectures.

Awesome professor. He's funny, his lectures are interesting and helpful, and his TAs team is really supportive. Be careful because his practice exams will not actually help you in the real test at all, his exams cover almost all knowledge from his lectures, so pay attention in lectures and labs will help you pass this class.

Professor is extremely smart and knowledgeable. Whenever I had questions or struggled with concepts during class, I regularly attended his office hours, and he always provided clear explanations along with helpful examples. Highly recommended!
I think it's harder for teachers who teach difficult things to get good reviews, and I think this is definitely the case here. Overall he did a pretty good job I'd say

Travis was an awesome lecturer. I struggle to hold attention in lectures, but I was able to in this class. 4150 is a HARD class, but Travis does about as good as anyone could at teaching it. Students complain about hard exams/assignments, but IMO Travis's expectations are that students are at the level of competency they should be at this point.

CS4150 with Professor Martin is the best CS course that I've taken at the U. He has all the qualities of an ideal professor, and the homework he assigns prepares you for his tests. I think that some of the complaints about the course are valid, but all work required for the course can turn you into a master of algorithms.

This class would benefit from being renamed 'Watch Me Code'. The lectures were extremely ineffective because he coded the entire class. When students requested to have the code available, he said, "I have 20 years of experience; I don't expect you to understand what I'm doing." How is this an effective learning model for students who want to learn?

Travis Martin is not a good professor in my opinion, he expects intro level students to know everything there is to object-oriented programming and was dismissive and difficult to follow. He's to0 theoretical and java specific that it was hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Travis Martin's CS lectures were ineffective and dismissive. He insisted students “just know” material yet ignored genuine questions. Slides lacked engagement; live coding was too fast. Feedback was minimal, and failing exam averages doomed students despite solid coding work.

Travis is a passionate teacher. I really like the excitement he brings to class, but he is a very theoretical professor. I think he is better suited toward coding classes than theoretical classes like 4150. He is a very "hand-wavey" professor, and this isn't the best for preparing you for the brutal homeworks in this class.

He explains difficult concepts very clearly, and is very helpful if you ask him for help with an assignment. There are a ton of resources for help in this class, the TAs were generally really helpful, labs were great. Allows a cheat sheet on exams, which were pretty easy if you understood the concepts from weekly assignments.

Hands down my fav professor in CS. Lectures are well organized, recorded, and I like his sense of humor. Yes the class is challenging, but are you really learning otherwise? He offered test corrections and a curve on the second midterm. He does not hold your hand and treats you like an adult. I expect other mad reviews suffer from a "skill issue"

Martin is not accommodating to the majority of students. He got his PhD in Algorithms, so immediately it was clear that he knew what he was talking about, but he expected students to understand everything during lecture, and if you didn't welp better go rewatch the lectures and reread the book until you do. Overall, he kind of made me hate school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: All the 1410 reviews frankly just seem like inexperienced students experiencing a large learning curve and what CS is like for the first time in college. Professor Martin is one of the best in the department, you should sign up for a class he is teaching every chance you get. His classes are hard, but life changing. Could not recommend more.

I honestly did not enjoy this course, the professor explained the material well but his grading system was not good at all. I would do extremely well in all the coding assignments but If I get a slightly low test score my entire grade would drop drastically and there was no form of extra credit.

Avoid if possible. Hard to learn. TAs are great, but lectures go very fast and boring. If you have a question, he will sometimes skip over you and won't answer if you ask too many questions. Does not answer questions about assignments, makes you look on Canvas, even if it does not have the answer.

I've got a love hate relationship with Prof Martin. His lectures are engaging, funny and recorded. Lots of homework and it's all pretty hard, but you learn a lot. Exams are fair but you have to study. Overall good, but definitely not accommodating for unusual circumstances. Lost out on several assignments because of life stuff I couldn't control...

The professor is way too boring. It is hard to stay focused because he goes so fast and you get behind in lectures. The labs are terrific. He doesn't answer everyone's questions. In-class polls for credit every day. He expects you to know everything after he covers some of the details of assignments in the last few minutes of class.

Travis has a good lecture style, stays after class to answer questions, and includes poll questions to keep the class engaged - contrary to some other comments. He also does expect students to be submitting their own work. I imagine some of the comments saying he's been known to remove students from the program are from students that cheated.

He is a great professor and teaches algorithms so well, the way he explains stuff is easy to understand and he is very approachable and always tries to answer all the questions in class itself. couldn't have asked for a better professor for this course.

As a computer scientist, Travis is great. He is very knowledgeable and can help you with any questions that you might have about Java. However, his lectures are some of the most boring that I have encountered in my collegiate experience. He doesn't to anything to keep the class engaged, and the 1h20m lecture consists of him programming in Eclipse.
the subject is tough but he is a good professor.

2420 part 2. Travis is a nice chill Prof doing his best to interact with 400+ students. The assignments aren't hard, but very time consuming(start early). Tests can have "bs" questions, however that's how any CS class is, so build up that note sheet. Also has mandatory questions as attendance. Challenging, but fun.

The professor's teaching style can be quite challenging. Although he was previously employed at Google, he no longer holds that position, which seems to influence his approach in the classroom. If you decide to take his class, be prepared for strict and demanding standards. Note that he has a record of removing students from the computing program.

The professor's teaching style might be off-putting to some. His confidence, likely bolstered by his tenure at Google, does not always translate into effective teaching. Be prepared for a rigorous and potentially harsh environment, as he has been known to enforce strict standards that could lead to students being removed from the program.
The class makes you want to off yourself but he makes a lot more tollerable.

He's super smart and good at teaching in a concise way. Sometimes things move a little fast, but that's because you're advised to do the reading before class. Lectures are engaging and attendance is taken through polling throughout the lectures for credit.

Great professor. Works hard to make lectures engaging/interesting. Helpful during office hours. The class can be tough but not impossible by a long shot. Just takes the proper amount of time and effort to succeed. Hope to take more courses from this professor in the future.

Super cool professor. Had great energy during the lectures. But during 1-on-1 talks, he seemed a little timid and even impatient at times. Regardless, he was usually nice and accommodating. The class was easier than 2420, but there's only one midterm and final, worth 45% of your grade combined. But if you know what you're doing, you'll be fine.

Travis' lectures are pretty clear and explains things well if there are questions, contrary to the other comments. Difficult-ish class but all CS classes should be expected to be difficult. Assignments were long but were useful to learn. TAs were great, saved me a lot of time. Shout out Spencer, he is so helpful and is so real.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Travis himself is pretty great, fun lectures, young and energetic. The main thing, and this is partly Travis' fault, is that the TA's in this course were absolutely horrendous.If you didn't draw 3/20 of the good TA's for hours/lab, you were being talked to by an arrogant, non-expert who will smirk at you if you don't have light mode on your IDE off

Travis is such a great professor. His lectures are extremely well put together. Travis has industry experience with Google and other great tech companies. He is a tough grader but it never doesn't make sense. If you lost points it's because you could have done better, and he will make sure you wont repeat your mistakes. Highly Recommend.

there are quizzes at the beginning of every class and those count as an attendance grade. Can use a cheat sheet on the exams and that's nice. LOTS of TA hours and definitely use those to your advantage. Lectures are recorded. Sometimes lectures can be very painfully boring, but he really goes into detail and makes sure everyone understands topics
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Martin is my favorite CS professor I've taken so far. He makes class fun and light whenever he can, and is super helpful and accessible outside of class. Start assignments early and take advantage of TA hours and you will be successful in this class.

This is the best class/professor combo I've had in CS so far. Travis is very good at teaching and answering questions during class. He clearly is very passionate and makes class fun. He's the kinda funny/cool CS guy you wanna become. This is the only CS class I look forward to going to. The projects are time consuming but easier after taking 2420.
Nice person, lectures can be boring. Explains things pretty well but the assignments are harder.

3500 is a hard class; Travis is doing his best with it. He's pretty funny and lectures are engaging enough, although they are not always helpful. Assignments are very difficult in the second quarter, but he does give a lot of resources to help you finish them. Available outside class if you need help. No unreasonable policies or anything imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Compared to other CS professors, he can be one of the toughest. If you are looking for help from him, all his responses will be very vague and will usually leave you more confused. Exams in this course don't test you on what you know and how to program, but rather if you know small details and niche concepts.

I loved this class with Travis. He made the class fun and interesting. I found his teaching style really engaging and his excitement for the topics is clear. He's easy to talk too and gives good feedback. I would describe him as the cool professor and he has a very impressive background in industry. Would recommend!

He is a good lecturer. Some of my friends think he is monotone, but the subject can make it seem that way. He's very straightforward and gets things done quickly. I wouldn't say he's my favorite person, but he's a good professor!

Professor Martin is honestly a pretty solid professor. He knows how to explain every single question/topic discussed. His hw assignments are hard, but that should be expected since all CS classes have hard hw. His tests can be time-consuming, but his practice tests prepare you well for the actual tests. He is a great professor, just a hard class.
Do not take this professor. His lectures are disorganized and messy. Although he is smart, he is a horrible professor. Often times most people would leave the class more confused.

An extremely time-consuming class, explanations confusing for coding homework. Weekly assignments=
5-10 hours a week. Many students lost. I got help from neighbors, IT coders who said assignments were not applicable for IT coding positions. Go to TA review hours offered. U of U makes CS impossible to weed out even good students. Majoring -go to UVU

Most of the reviews on here are clearly biased, good review get thumbs down. This course is very easy, perhaps even too easy. Each class is basically a large discussion, and a weekly assignment is to do a Canvas discussion asking a question, and responding to classmates. Travis is a great professor overall, and is a really good addition to the dept

4150 is a hard class no doubt, and that's what it seems these reviews are based on. Travis is an excellent professor, the assignments prepare you well for actual algorithmic interview questions. The class was curved up by at least 5% in the end, and he wants everyone to succeed. He is very accessible, and always takes time to answer questions fully
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor can teach well, but his grading was astronomically impossible. Every assignment was lucky to have an average of 75%, and the final had an average of 65%, and nothing was curved. If you take 4150 from this professor, your GPA will be lowered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Martin and Kopta were nothing short of awesome over the entire semester. Not only was the course material interesting, but it was also one of the first times a CS class felt like it could apply to the broader world of software. Overall 10/10

4150 was a very difficult course. Martin tends to go through the lectures very quickly, including a ton of examples, but not taking the time to go through one slowly, step by step. There are weekly programming and written assignments, and I would estimate about 20 hours of work a week. We did not receive any extensions. Grades were curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is very organized and knowledgeable about the content. He is very passionate and energetic in his lectures. He and Professor Kopta co-taught CS-3500 and they seemed like the "dynamic duo" where they complemented each-others strengths. Prof. Martin is a fast speaker but he always has clear and organized thoughts and lectures.

Taught alongside Daniel Kopta. Professors were good with lectures and answering questions during them. Very respondant outside of class on Piazza or Canvas. Assignments were time-consuming, but grading criteria were always clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Let me preface this by saying that the actual course, CS 4150 is STUPID hard, and I would spend anywhere from like 5 to 40 hrs per assignment, depending on the material, outside of reading the textbook, etc.

That said, Travis is fantastic, he's very accessible, takes feedback, and active in discussions and supporting students. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Martin is not only brilliant and passionate about algorithms but he cares that his students come to a level of understanding of algorithms in which they are inspired and passionate about algorithms as well.  The hardest but most fulfilling CS classes I've taken.  Be prepared to work extremely hard (15-20 hrs/week) for 15 weeks for ~B+/A.

4150 is a tough class, but Travis is excellent. His lectures are very well thought out and interactive, and he obviously knows his stuff. Homework + quiz + reading every week is very demanding, but if you keep up the content is very well put together.

Prof. Martin is very talented. However, he is not a good teacher. He does not explain concepts well enough and gives very few examples in class apart from the ones in the textbook. There are 1-2 quizzes, 1-2 chapters worth of reading, a written + coding assignment EVERY week. This class is extremely stressful and easily takes up 15-20+ hours/week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you're rusty of 2100, you should invest time to review it. You should do lots of leetcode to strengthen your coding skills. If you do, you can significantly reduce the workload for yourself. If you don't have this foundation, you will fall behind in this class.

Rough Class. I feel like Professor Martin expects an especially large amount compared to what I've heard of other Alg professors. Compared to 4400, I felt like this was twice the workload, which is certainly saying something. I felt more confused after lectures than I did going into it and found self-study and the book better than lectures.

Currently taking this class right now. It is ruining my mental health. He assigns really difficuly assignments every single week. CS 4400, which is supposed to be comprable in difficulty, had 1/2 the assignments this class does. Can't stress how terrible an experience it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Would be perfect if grades didnt exist. Martin teaches truly useful problem solving skills on genuinely challenging problems. Issue is, in the context of being graded, it turns a very valuable learning experience into an extremely stressful one. If you can tolerate getting less than an A, take it from Martin; otherwise wait for somebody else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: In response to the person who gave a 4 star review- took this class again the next semester with a great professor, one who goes through examples in class, thoroughly explains ideas and does not require a religious adherence to a textbook to compensate for shallow instruction. Completely different experience
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took 4150 from Martin as his first every semester teaching and you could tell, but he got much better as the the year went on. 4150 is the 2nd hardest class at the U behind 4400 so some of his reviews reference the class more than it does him, He really cares about you and will spend a ton of time on piazza and in TA hours to help you understand

some homework assignments were fairly easy, others seemed like satan's magnum opus There is an EXTREME reliance upon the textbook. He expects you to read, take a quiz, then come to lecture so he can explain to you very simplified versions of textbook questions, then refers you back to the textbook when you don't understand 50% of grade was tests
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is a wonderful person who clearly understands the material and asks us if we're confused because he'd love to clarify. The problem is that he is just not good at actually transferring what he knows or wants to teach to his students. He makes an already complicated subject worse. You can be brilliant but be a terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Will update after class is over. So far it's been a nightmare of flipped classrooms and overloading on homework. Not a graduate level class, but significantly more time consuming and demanding than the graduate level class I'm taking concurrently. Travis genuinely seems to care, but has unrealistic expectations for his curriculum
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This teacher is disrespectful. She wants you to raise your hand and ask questions and then acts like you didn't do your reading if your definition is one word away from what she wants. I took a class survey and 87.5% of the people who participated didn't like this teacher. The following 12.5% were neutral. Avoid her class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with this professor! A very tough grader and assigns an excessive amount of work for this course. Attendance heavily affects grades and even being just 5 minutes tardy.
Her instructions are very unclear, she's very confusing and would not recommend this teacher!
When she explains stuff is a little confusing and tough, don't recommend this professor. Gives too much homework snd is hard like if I didn't have other classes.

I've never had a professor so bad at teaching. Has unclear expectations for the essays and does not provide actual feedback on drafts. Says that she is willing to help, but won't answer or find time to actually help when you reach out. This is a useless professor who should never be allowed to teach again. How she is a teacher is a miracle.

Her criteria is so specific and long but not very detailed in explanation. She gives work as if you have no other classes on your plate. Would not recommend unless you wanna be constantly writing with long long lists of specific requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Writing 1010 with her, which isn't the class she usually teaches. There were quite a few technical difficulties, but she responded to her email pretty well and resolved them. I don't enjoy writing so I didn't love this class, but I could tell she was passionate about what she taught. Didn't like the course, but didn't mind the teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly worst professor I have had during my time in college. Doesn't ever get around to grading assignments and when she does she will take off points with no justification. Says that you need to write according to your "Discourse Community" but then will fail you if she doesn't agree with what you're writing. Find another professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS TEACHER AT ALL COSTS!

I had to constantly remind her actually to post the material for the week. She has a long list of criteria for sources that can be hard to follow based on your topic. I had a run-in with that because she replied to my sources with a snarky comment and basically told me I was wrong after following her criteria. Can't do her job.

Pat is a quirky guy who pretends not to care/that he hates his job, but he secretly does care. Very entertaining class

he graded everything the day before grades were due which made things stressful. it is hard to talk to him about things and it doesnt feel comfortable. but when you need help and ask he would give suggestions harsh or not harsh.

Don't take this class if you expect to learn anything... All the lectures are online and were recorded on a microwave 10 years ago. As a future architect I hope my buildings don't fall down because I never learned structure from Pat.

HOLY, where do I start? This man is terrible, I've never seen a professor care less about his job and his students than this man. Great class from a great teacher.  This man is brilliant!

Professor Tribone is out for your best interest if you do YOUR part. The business mathematics class is fast pace in its material yet he teaches it clear and efficiently. (Took him for 1105) Tim is an amazing professor and really cares about his students. I'm not a math person and have always struggled with it, but in Tim's class, I scored super high. He does teach very fast and gets flustered quite easily, but he is such a nice guy, and if you stay after class, he will help for however long you need. TAKE HIM

reviews.comment: (I took MATH1105 with him). Dr. Tribone is a wonderful professor who does everything to help his students succeed. Fairly easy to pass the class as long as you study for the 2 exams and final and one midterm is replaced if you score better on the final!
Absolutely loved taking a class from him! He cares about each of his students, but more importantly is an amazing teacher. He will always help if you ask and wants each student to succeed.

Tim is extremely caring and kind towards his students; they are always his top priority. Tim always checks for understanding amongst the class and is excited to help you learn. He is always prepared and is clearly very well-versed in his subjects. I recommend Tim to anyone taking a class that he offers.

FAVORITE TEACHER THIS SEMESTER!!!
I had taken this class before but had to retake it because my teacher wasn't very good but Tim was an amazing teacher! He explained everything so good and had so many ways to earn extra credit, he also provided so many resources to help if you were struggling!!

he was great. lots of LA hw sessions/ review session and had office hours often and was always willing to help students after class, especially before exams. though the hw administration was kinda frustrating sometimes, exams were just like class, if not easier and grades are very fair with lots of opportunities for extra credit. would take again.

For MATH 1050 -- Amazing! He breaks down everything well and I actually understood how everything worked. He and his TAs/LAs had a lot of office hours, review sessions, and homework help. There are weekly small quizzes, three exams, and one comprehensive final. Would recommend! He is pretty chill and really cares about your success.
Was super cool

I actually had him for Precalculus and he was great. The course was extremely fast paced but he had office hours and answered all emails super quickly. He explains things very well and would go over ever instance of a problem so there were no surprises on his exams.

One of the most amazing professors that I have had in my life. If you have a chance to take 2271 with him: do it! Tim is very caring, and respectful, and takes his time to make sure everything is clear. There are a lot of extremely helpful office hours plus he has a discord server which makes communication extremely easy. Tim is amazing!
Discord communication was great. Someone would post the lecture notes for each class. The exams and quizzes were easier than the homework. Loved this class.

Tim is not only my favorite professor, he is the best teacher I have ever had. He will prove to you every day that he truly cares and wants you to learn. Above all else, he has an unmatched passion for learning. This, I think, is his best quality. He just loves math and loves to learn. Tim has challenged my mind, and truly feels like a friend.

Honestly one of the best professors/teachers I have had in the last decade of schooling. Tim is incredibly kind and cares deeply about his students learning. He is also very lenient and understands that students sometimes need more time to finish some assignments. If you have the opportunity, I recommend you get Tim as your math professor

Tim is one of the best professors I have ever experienced. He cares about his students, is incredibly fair with grading exams/homework, and knows what he is talking about. He is just a very genuine person. Make sure you will show up to class though, as it's difficult to catch up on lectures if you start to slip up.
If 2271 is available, take it.

I'm genuinely honored to say that I was one of Tim's students in his Linear Algebra course. While he was a bit timid when giving his lectures, he is simultaneously passionate when it comes to fundamental courses such as Linear Algebra and realistic in understanding the capability of his students. Tim is a great math teacher. He delivers concepts well and is good at connecting them to larger ideas. He clearly really loves Linear Algebra so now I kinda do too haha. He also just seems like a cool guy and good person. He also would respond to questions at what seemed like anytime day or night. Very great addition to the department. Take him!

Tim was absolutely great at lecturing and providing help in and outside of class. He is always willing to spend time helping students with topics they struggle with. Highly recommend taking any course from Tim.

Tim was a great professor for Linear Algebra. Ended up feeling like my most manageable class during a particularly rough semester because he did a great job at teaching. His tests were a bit on the difficult side, and very long, make sure to go quick. He has a lot of tests throughout the semester but that means less things to study for the test.

Professor Tribone is an amazing professor and one who is genuinely deserving 5/5 stars. He cares deeply about wanting his students to succeed, and is incredibly passionate about the course content. He presents the material in a way that is very easy to understand/follow and makes you eager to learn more. I absolutely recommend Tim as a professor.

Professor Tribone was amazing for MATH2270. His lectures were well-written, and I understood the content quite well. He did many outside-the-class review sessions, so going to those is recommended.

Tim is easily one of the best math professors I've ever had. He makes great use of diagrams and proofs in his lectures that make the concepts we learned perfectly clear. He makes sure to give time for everyone to ask questions, and he's very approachable in and out of class.
Tim is awesome. He explains things very clearly and makes sure that the class understands the material well.

This professor is very nice to all of his students. If you are a student who has a great interest in Math, you should take his class, because the way he conveys knowledge is amazing. He not only defines new things, but also proves them and try to show where they come from. Highly recommend!!!

Tim is a great professor! He answers any questions the students have during his lectures very thoroughly. Hands down, the best math professor I've ever had. He's very caring, his lectures are very easy to understand and he always ask and answers questions from students before moving on. His tests are not too difficult. 100/10 would definitely recommend if you guys are taking math 1210.

Tim is a fantastic teacher. He is very patient and genuinely cares about helping his students learn. He answers questions with great detail and makes sure everyone understands before moving on.
