Both the greatest class and professor I have had at the U; Cheng is kind, has a great sense of humor, and is extremely knowledgable about literature. A class on Joyce is in itself difficult, and Cheng is a tough, but fair grader; but he helps -- with amazing feedback -- a lot along the way. Couldn't recommend enough.

LOVE prof. Cheng!!! He is so funny and so kind. His exams are so hard though... but he grades essays pretty fairly (depending on the course). I've taken 2 courses by him and am signed up for another one in the fall! His lectures are pretty long and there is little to no discussion in class. He always stays on topic and explains things really well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The material is very difficult & if you don't go to lectures you will have no idea what's happening. The class is graded by 2 papers and 3 tests so you really have to do well on everything to get a good grade in the class. Prof Cheng is very passionate about the subject & wants you to succeed. If you're going to take this class, take it with Cheng.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Oh, Prof. Cheng. This is not an exciting class to begin with, and I'll be honest, I was interested in the topics in the beginning, but after a while the class became repetitive. This is a memorization heavy course, which I frankly, don't have time or patience for. He is a nice guy, but I wish I had taken this class elsewhere!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is clearly very knowledgeable about the subject, and he is passionate about the issues we discussed in class as well. However there were so many books and so much material to cover that there was some confusion on many of the topics. There was a short response paper due every week, a few quizzes, along with one final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading from several long novels and weekly writing assignments. Classes consist of (sometimes long) lectures and class discussions. The class requires a lot of work but Professor Cheng presents many interesting ideas which can make discussions fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Has a thorough understanding of the given literature in class, yet has less than stellar teaching methods. His lectures become repetitive and, frankly, boring. There is no variation in his style and he has little concern for the learning of the student; rather, he simply seems to lecture to show his comprehension of the subject than to teach.

Great professor. Seriously a sweet guy. If you make an effort, he'll notice. The lectures are really interesting and you can tell he loves the subject. There are three papers and a couple of tests, including a final. The tests were the hardest part. If you can memorize book quotes, you'll be fine.

Professor Cheng is an intelligent man, who is passionate about the subjects he teaches. He has a bit of a stutter, which makes the lectures difficult to follow. Listen closely and take thorough notes. Be sure to study all of the texts, especially in the poetry section, as he gives quizzes and tests on passages from the readings.

This is the best class I have ever taken! Lots of reading. Weekly writing, but you choose the topics & he gives detailed feedback that really inspires new ideas. Discussion based classes with only a few lectures. Show up & get involved & you'll get an A. This class really changed how I think about colonialism, race, nation, & identity
Does not help you at all! I went to his office hours and email him and he wouldn't help me.

Prof. Cheng is one of the best professors I've had at the U. I really enjoyed his class. However, it is fairly tough and he doesn't grade easy. If you attend class and take good notes, it is not difficult to succeed. I would definitely take a class from him in the future. He is very insightful and passionate about what he teaches.

Good teacher for Lit 2. A lot of the papers are just reiteration of his ideas and he doesn't often accept other interpretations. However, the class is pretty interesting. I would recommend him for this class.

Good teacher. Obviously very passionate about the subject, gives adequate feedback, and is concerned with student success. Wrote me several letters of recommendation willingly. Learned a great deal in this course and felt Cheng was very approachable and kind.

Pros: Open to different ideas. Flexible with paper topics and due dates. Doesn't require attendance (keep in mind his lectures are full of information that is important for papers). Great at engaging class discussion Cons: Mono-tone boring lectures/tangents.  A lot of writing and reading.

Cheng is very knowledgeable.  Yes, he does interrupt on occasion and he has his own views, but he's extremely bright and makes the class very interesting.  What he discusses is sometimes hard to grasp because of it's depth.  You won't find him showing disney movies and playing patty cake, real discussions.  He's a harvard grad,and teaches like one
This guy is not helpful and can be a real jerk!

Very smart and dedicated to his work.  That being said, I've never met a more rigid English prof, in the sense that he never seemed accepting of ideas different than his own.  not really a good quality in a career based on interpretation.    you could do better, but you could do a lot worse.
Fascintating, Amazing Teacher.  You will never study with a someone as powerful as Prof. Cheng.  The best class I have ever taken in my life.
Unnecessarily difficult class and exams. Graded by few things. No practice given. Challenging concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went into mental illness because of the exams. I started to be sad about everything and my life because of the exams. It is a scam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Idk why I am paying so much money for my master's degree to go to mental illness. I won't get a job in this market anyway, and now I am mentally ill.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exam grading is very strict, and I never knew what they were looking for in the exams. The class did not prepare me for the exams. The class is too heavily relied on the exams grading (which is outdated and colonial). He is old styled and outdated in his teaching. This class is a scam. Do not take this class. I lost my hair, sleep, and sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with him. His teaching is subpar, and he only covers a few easy questions in class. Additionally, the homework is insufficient to help us prepare for exams. The class should not be curved, and the homework should have more problems to help us prepare for the exam. The exams are extremely challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will never know what your grade is in this class because the professor refuses to put your grades on canvas and he just tells us to see what our grades would be (he says he will curve the class based on how we perform in it). When asked for practice exam, he just gave us the same easy questions he taught us in class. The exams were way harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His CS 6810 class is quite literally the worst class I have ever taken in my entire university-level education. The class is graded on very few things. Each homework has only 2 or 3 questions, and each hw counts for 8% of the final grade. There are very few homework assignments, and the exams (midterm + final) count for 60% of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participate Participate Participate! Good grading if you work ahead of time. He is clear and concise on grading and for projects, he will review your material and give feedback ahead of time if asked. Caring professor if you actually spend time participating.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Second class with Rudi. He's a great guy, but this class was very different to the last one I took. The lectures are short and only gloss over major concepts, so it means that 90% of information is from the textbook, which for me made it a lot harder than it had to be. Discussion posts and projects were hard to get an A, but quizzes were easy.
Good professor. He likes you to stay well informed, get a subscription to The Economist or Financial Times.

His class was very structured and organized.  He stayed on track with everything - which I really appreciated.  Some of the assignments are great because they translate into your relevant lifeour economy right now.  Great professor.

He is very helpful and responds to emails quickly, also has a few simple projects that will help you in your future and are not difficult. He has quizzes and tests which are done online on your own computer and on your own time. He said that he will probably start doing this with he's in person classes as well. I recommend he's online class!!!

The content of the course itself is arduous, but as long as you assert yourself a little bit, you will get it. He had us do projects that REALLY helped us understand the concepts. He is eager to assist those that are struggling, as well. He is pretty awesome and I recommend him.

To the previously posted comment: he's a professor, so of course he understands the subject. Rudi expects more from himself than his students, but that doesn't mean his class is easy. You need to read and do practice problems or else you will fall behind. Grading is fair, but the tests are difficult. Take his class online if possible.
Professor was fairly unhelpful. His grading was arbitrary and undisclosed. Avoid at all costs!

Prof Von Arnim is an extremely smart economist. His intelligence is though a little too advanced for undergraduate students.  He teached economics as if you are in a graduate level class.  ECON 4020 is very quantitativley intensive and if you don't understand what the equations are tyring to explain, you will become lost...QUICKLY!

Professor Voltz is by far my favorite professor throughout my entire college experience. Her lectures are amazing. She engages with students with such a kind and empathetic tone which instantly makes you feel comfortable sharing your thoughts or insights. Do yourself a favor and learn from this incredible teacher.

My absolute favorite professor ever, she is so enthusiastic and funny when she lectures. She wants you to do well and really cares about her students! I wish she taught every subject because she genuinely is just all around the best teacher. In hist1700 there are 4 books to read and 2 assignments, they are not bad!!

I skipped classes. Lost points for in-class assignments. Wrote fake essays on books I didn't read. Tons of reading online aswell. Her lectures are amazing though, I regret not going. Study for finals incredibly hard, you get a reference card aswell. Seriously regret not going to lectures. If you go to lectures, you will get an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Voltz has amazing lectures. She makes history interesting and is very passionate about what she teaches. Your grade is based off in-class assignments, two essays, and two tests. You must study to pass, but her tests are very straight forward and based off her powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was by far my favorite class taken this semester. Professor Voltz's teaching style was engaging, and she put a new and interesting spin on material I have been taught repeatedly in my lifetime. I highly recommend her for anyone wanting an interesting and educational class. There were occasional attendance checks and pop quizzes with warning.

Professor Voltz is just amazing. She is so passionate about what she teaches which makes the content easier to understand. There are not a whole lot of assignments besides little in-class assignments. Best of all, she offers lots of extra credit!!

I have taken several classes with Dr. Voltz. She actually inspired me to change my major to History. She is very enthusiastic every day and there's never a boring moment in her class. She digs into the deep, hard aspects of history and that's one thing I really appreciate about her. Take as many classes with her as you can, you WILL NOT regret it.

Great professor! She makes her lectures interesting and fun to listen to! Has in-class group assignments every day that are really easy, their mostly there just for participation points. Take lots of notes! Her tests are exactly what is taught during her lectures. Hands out a study guide with exactly what she expects from you on the tests.

Professor Voltz has been my favorite professor so far. Her lectures are fun and engaging, and she offers a lot of extra credit. There are only two tests, the midterm and the final, and they are totally doable if you study. Make sure you do the reading she assigns each day. There are a lot of in class assignments, so make sure you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Cares very little about his students and their education.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nathan Vooge could not care less about your education. No lectures, no discussions, nothing with any meat to it. He literally just said, "Read your textbooks and make a group project." Never specified what he wanted us to do with those projects, and is a tough grader. Grading things he never mentioned. I wish tenure didn't exist for profs like him.

Nathan means well, but the class is structured in a way that makes it confusing to follow. There are very few graded assignments, and the course material is difficult if you have no prior knowledge of linguistics. Test questions are intentionally worded to stump you, which I feel is very unfair to those who genuinely try to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class online as a gen ed and got my backside handed to me. Very tough class and I would highly recommend selecting any other class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I've ever taken. Assignments and group projects were so advanced and difficult it wasn't even possible to complete them. The textbook didn't help at all, and the professor's lectures helped even less. He has a gift for talking up a storm without ever actually saying anything useful. Avoid this professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Personally I would NOT recommend this class to anybody. The online lectures were very monotone, it required a lot of reading, and the tests were extremely hard (even when using the textbook and videos).

A lot of people seem to really dislike Nate, but I actually really appreciate his style of teaching. He's unorganized and tends to change the syllabus around throughout the semester, but it is always beneficial to the student. He's a really easy grader and really nice. Definitely take his class for an interesting experience and a semi-easy A.
The tests were almost impossible to do well on. I could never get the correct answers even after using the textbook. Take another gen ed, this one is not worth your time.

Weird for an online class. Really tough. But Easy A if you are willing to put in the work, just time consuming. Honestly I felt like this was an awful class for online. Should be taught in person, it would have been much more effective. Group assignments online are weird. Book is provided online, but thought to read.. and really hard to understand

At first I was not a fan of Nathan. But, I grew to like him more throughout the course. He was helpful in emails and does seem to want everyone to learn the material and succeed. I however do not recommend this class. The material is just difficult (not professors fault) and quizzes are near impossible. Take a different gen ed course lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Vooge lacks effective teaching abilities and enjoys long and loud tangents. Nearly everything I learned was from the textbook and additional research I did on my own. Class provides much needed extra credit for grade-padding. Test and quizzes are very difficult and tricky. Vooge expects too much from students at this level.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I hated this class. The course material is hard and the quizzes are so confusing - each question will have 6 answer choices, one of them being "the answer is not stated", which happened to be the correct answer on multiple questions! Not cool!! The worst part though... GROUP PROJECTS. My group was horrible and Nathan really didn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Everything I know I learned from the textbook, not Nate. He's terrible at explaining things & tells you when answers are wrong but never gives the right answer. He gives feedback but his handwriting is illegible. Lots of group work, everyone gets the same grade even if they didn't help. Also DO NOT sit on the front row, he's so loud you'll go deaf.

This is the hardest 1200 level class I have ever taken. I took it for my last general at the U thinking it would be a relatively easy class. His quizzes were way too hard. He really tries to trick you on them. Definitely don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really nice professor, but he gives credit to people who do not participate in group projects. One or two people can do all the work, and all 5 in the group will pass. You can look at the class high, low, and average in all classes at the U. The people who have done nothing didn't receive lower than a 90% because no one received lower than that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Overall an OK experience with an online class. Very straight forward on grading. I wish I spent more time reading and studying the material for the exams. A lot of group work, and at home quizzes. Final Project in the class seems challenging. Felt unorganized at times.

I took this class for my last general requirement, and it was one of the hardest ones I took. For a 1200 level class, it was way too hard. The quizzes are way too tricky for the level of class it is. Definitely would not recommend. However, he is a pretty funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took this class as a GE, but it was WAY more work that I wanted! 2 exams (scan in work), 3 group projects (prepare to get bad grades b/c can't work together well), 5 quizzes (tough, but open book). Use the book - his powerpoint lectures are vague. Pad your grade with extra credit (discussion boards & speech labs). Only way I got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: If you've read other reviews, and are thinking, "I'll just take an online course--how bad can it be?" stop right now. Nathan literally assigns group projects to his online classes. You'll be assigned a random group (the same one all semester) and will have to try to do four projects using only email and Google Docs. Absolutely NOT recommended.

He was the worst Professor I have ever had. Don't bother asking him for help outside of class, he is far too "busy". Just because you know the subject, doesn't mean you can teach it. Nate should stick to doing research. I wouldn't have passed the class if it wasn't for the book. I passed the class thanks to Andrew Carnie, not Nathan Vooge.

I loved taking courses from this professor! He is extremely passionate and, as long as you attend lectures and pay attention, you will pass. The students who struggled in his class are the ones who didn't belong in the major and didn't have a passion for the material.

He is the definition of a great teacher. He does not just repeat what has already been stated in the book. He challenges what the book says and what you know. This class is only enjoyable in you read the book and show up to class. Very organized and knowledgeable.

The class was only easier on me because I had read the book before hand. The Teach didn't give proper instructions, he would simply give is busy work instead of explaining and help us out! He didn't fully answer students questions, he would belittle students who did ask questions. The teacher didn't teach, I recommend taken a different  teacher!

Nate is pretty good teacher. I think he really read these reviews and has worked on his teaching methods. The class is hard but if you go he gives extra credit every single class. He's sorta awkward but really does want to help to the best of his ability. SO MANY GROUP PROJECTS so be prepared and field work. I actually enjoyed this class and Nate.

Professor Vooge is very passionate and well-versed in the field. As a Linguistics major, the information was enthralling and important to me. If you are not majoring in Linguistics, the class is probably not for you because the information is not easy.   One BIG key to passing this class - SHOW UP! He gives extra credit for in class work!

This man should not be a teacher, and I am surprised he still is allowed to teach classes with such bad reviews on EVERY platform. He does not teach anything at all. Everything I know about Phonology (the class I took from him) I learned from my Intro to Linguistics course or the textbook and not from him. He's VERY unorganized and confusing.

avoid him. The worst teacher I ever had. Always condescending, always bragging about his non-existing researches. Never helpful. Totally unclear. A lot of exams and quizzes.  I was in an intro to syntax class, but my book and peers helped me way more than he did. He would say he did not think you could be able to complete assignments. Discouraging

Vooge is the worst professor I've ever had. He is very smart but he does not know how to teach. Instead, he rambles about complex topics. Considering this is an "intro" course in syntax, I would expect him to teach the basics and expand, but he seems more determined to convince the class how brilliant he is. I had to teach myself everything. AVOID

Professor Vooge is very difficult! He is not kind or patient either. He goes so fast and goes on random tangents that don't even make sense. He doesn't explain clearly at all. It is a painful class and if you can avoid taking him, do so at all costs!!!! ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE.  He blamed a few of our classmates for cheating when he was NOT clear.

This was a great course. Vooge was very accessible if we needed help; either he or his TA responded to emails within a few hours. The course was not easy, it was definitely challenging, but in a good way. Overall, I was impressed with the instructor and the course.
One of the WORST classes I have ever taken. Words cannot describe how frustrating this INTRO class is. I hate it and will NEVER EVER speak highly of prof Vooge or his class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Open quizzes first day that they are released and follow along with textbook and powerpoint modules while doing them. Also, always check discussions as extra credit is offered. These concepts are difficult, but Prof Vooge will help you. Don't slack, and you'll get a good grade! After this course, you'll know the material VERY well.

I am taking his online 1200 linguistics course and I am quite unhappy about it. The quizzes are worth 45% of your grade and they happen to be quite impossible to pass. They are full of trick questions. He does provide extra credit, but it barely helps your grade. Also, he explains the material in too complex of ways for a BASIC ling course. Avoid!

So I was really frustrated when I started this class, and then I started to realize that I am fairly sure Nathan is somewhere on the genius side of the spectrum,which made his sometimes odd, obsessive behavior easier to handle. You will not understand this class, but his grading is more than fair, and if you do the work, you will pass the class.

I have had some bad professors in my day.  I have NEVER had a professor that is this bad!  He obviously knows his stuff, but has NO business teaching anyone anything for the rest of his life.  Don't even bother asking for help.  He full on tells you he wants you to be confused.  He is a nice guy.  Just CLUELESS!!! Terrible teacher. Avoid if you can

This is the worst professor I've ever had. His quizzes are impossible, not because the material is difficult to understand, but because of the way he words questions; and even if you read the book and his powerpoint slides, there will be a question or two beyond your knowledge. Total condescending ass and unhelpful in email correspondence. AVOID!

Answers to questions seemed curt, but fair.  The TA's study sessions were helpful--pretty much a must for the exams.  Lots of different ways to study the material--podcasts, textbook, group projects, etc.  Group projects were okay as long as fellow group members were on top of it; they were frustrating when not.

VERY tricky questions on quizzes and exams. They are brutal. TA sucks - literally took a month to get project/midterm grades back. Unacceptable especially when we need them to study for a final. I did learn a lot though and I like how the tests can be submitted online - NOTHING is on campus at all which I like.

I agree with the previous comment. He tries to prove his intelligence by degrading you on simple questions asked. It isn't hard to answer a question without being rude. Its called being a professor which means teaching and to do that productively usually means helping a student to understand something they may not.

He is too smart for his own good. Likes to show off that he knows so much and won't explain things so we can understand. He loves what he "teaches" though. You basically have to read the texts over and over again to try to understand this class. This was one of the hardest college classes I have ever taken, because he makes it hard to understand.

Professor Peter Von Sivers taught this class very uncomfortably, as though cemented in an era lacking in global perspective. Additionally, he will disregard even the texts which he assigns for reading if they are not in line with his understanding of how and why historical events unfolded. To get an A, recount his monologues as theses.

Professor Peter Von Sivers poorly sketched the history of the Middle East and generally was ill-informed. Example: He claimed that Avicenna's (Ibn Sina) name suggested he was of Chinese descent, because the word 'SEEN' in Arabic means 'China', however though they sound the same, Sina is spelt with a different 's' than 'Seen' in Arabic.

A little confusing, and a little disorganized. He enjoys lecturing, and he knows a LOT, but he also expects you to know a lot in your in-class essays. He wants DETAILS in his 15-minute in-class essay tests, but there are SO MANY it's hard to know which ones he prefers. Hard grader. Getting the "gist" of it isn't enough. KNOW YOUR DETAILS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Just don't. Save yourself the trouble.  I am a very organized straight A student and I have never been more frustrated with a class in my four year college career. Lectures are DRY and so boring, his book is equally so. Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you take this class as a requirement like I did, prepare to read A LOT. The textbook assigned is one that he wrote and all tests are based on the readings. DO NOT do outside research. There are two unannounced tests, one midterm, and one final. They are all short answer questions and he's definitely a tough grader, but read and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Everything is based out of the book he wrote, tests quizzes etc... honestly you could get the book, read and never attended class except on test days and get 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Von Sivers is a very intelligent man but he's unfortunately not all there. It took him three weeks just to read my mid term paper and when he finally did the man gutted it. Not to mention the final is in two weeks and now he tells me he never got my paper and that I am at threat of failing the course? with A's on the tests? unacceptable!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I started taking this class and halfway through the semester decided that I would rather have a W on my transcript than wait and see was this professor was going to give me. He assigned ATON of reading that if you do not do you fail. Tests are super hard and he grades them even harder. I took the W and took a different international credit.

The most painfully boring class I've ever taken. It consists of this: 4 quizzes, 2 tests, listening to Professor Von Sivers ramble for 50 minutes 3 days a week, and a text book that is even more dry than the lectures. If you get behind on reading you're screwed-lectures won't make sense, quizzes are so specific. Nice guy but would not recommend.

DO NOT take this class. He is a nice guy, but in my opinion a terrible teacher. The lectures could not be more dry, he hardly uses any visuals and just talks at you the whole time, never asking questions or encouraging student participation. The pop quizzes are far too difficult in their specificity. He think students should be happy with  Cs.

Great professor, he uses his own textbook which is published by oxford press. Quizzes were sometimes a little confusing. Readings and Lectures cover different material, and either could be on the quiz. He gives great study guides for tests.

I took intro. to Islam. The class was way too hard, you need to study so much if you want to pass. 3 timed and wordy exams and 3 research papers. The participation grade is based on how good your posts were on the discussions and on the number of hours you spent studying the online material! Bad quality videos (many) and a lot to read.
Brutally hard, tests full of trick questions, 200 pages of reading a week, super hard grader on tests.

Wonderful professor. Interesting and engaging lecturer. Cares about students, while maintaining and upholding honorable academic practices; expecting the same of his students. Patient, very, very knowledgeable. Highly recommended.

I got the biggest kick out of his accent, it made listening to his lectures more entertaining. His reading requirements were time consuming so by the end of the semester I was just reading a summary the textbook provided online and taking notes on lectures rather than reading the books, and I still got a good grade.
Professor von Sivers was GREAT!  He really helps guide you with your term papers, and is a excellent speaker.  And, of course, he really knows his stuff.

Unless you are really into middle east history avoid this professor. I took this as a requirement and regret it. Only two short quizzes and two papers but beware as he is very critical. His lectures are vague and unorganized even with an outline. He does not return emails much so you have to track him down. He knows a lot and expects you to also.

Difficult professor and expects much from his students.  His tests are challenging but he NEVER throws any unfair curve balls.  He is more than willing to help students with anything.  Very kind man and very approachable.  Highly knowledgeable on Islamic themes.  Recommend him for any course...

Professor Von Sivers is very knowledgeable, his accent for some people takes some getting used to, but it's not a big deal. He's a funny professor, and he will do anything he can to help you in class. We had two large papers, and two quizzes in class, quite a bit of work but not difficult.

pretty hard class. He is hard to  understand but he knows what he is talking about. Tests are difficult.You have to write down information exactly how he wants it to get a good score. Only mid term and final with three book reports, a lot of reading and a lot of studying to do well.

Professor Von Sivers is a great man. He is not American, therefore he speaks with an accent. it was a little difficult for me to understand him sometimes, not his accent, but his choice of words... i never really knew when i was suppose to take notes on something or not. I would get so confused i would fall asleep in class. He is a great person!
No Comments

Islamic Spain was an interesting class. Professor Peters is a cute German guy. However, looks aren't everything...he's smart too. He knows his stuff. My issue was that he lectured for an hour and twenty minutes, twice a week with out a break. I needed a break. Too much info. I mean stop to breath or something.
Prof. Wang is great. Exams were pretty easy especially if you do the practice tests and you had the option to drop the final. Homework was not too bad either and the class is so chill.

Dr. Wang's course was enjoyable and doable. Two group projects throughout the semester instead of exams, weekly homework, and a few 1-hour lab demos. She inspires lots of discussion during lectures and encourages you to apply the concepts to your research. She cares deeply about students and getting to know them. This course is an easy A.

Prof. Wang is a thorough and considerate instructor. She prepares you well for the tests with the homework and the class pacing was very reasonable. Only hang-up was a very thick accent, but she understands this and is patient with the class if they don't understand.

Dr. Wang is very caring and she has a very straightforward teaching style. She provides all the necessary materials for the exams and the course in general and wants everyone to succeed. It is easy to get a 100% on her exams, and she has a very fair grading style. If you go to class and do the homework, you will be just fine.

She is the worst professor to ever exist. She does not teach the class, just reads off her slides in a monotone voice and you have to rely on previous exams to teach yourself the material before the exams. Half of us didn't even show up for the classes because she is that incompetent in teaching. I have no idea why she is still teaching.
She was very passionate about the craft. Just be honest and don't use AI and you are set.
will push politics on you almost every assignment. More like an elementary teacher. Also, dont even think about using chat
Unclear, unhelpful, and didn't answer questions and concerns I had.
Great professor, would recommend. Exams were VERY fair, no curveball questions

Unfortunately had this Prof.  I did not find him to be very professional in his demeanor and interactions with my class. His lectures are interesting,  however the quizzes were on anything. It was difficult to prepare for the quizzes. Mostly he seemed self-centered and unprepared to TEACH students - expect to learn more at home than in class.

LOVED Dr. Werner and this course. I'd take it again in a heartbeat. Even though there is a lot of information, he is specific about what is on exams, and lectures are interesting where you also feel comfortable asking Q's. I def recommend sitting near the front and attending all lectures, but don't worry too much about reading "assigned" papers!

This guy is really interesting, and his lectures are great, a much better genetics class than the usual genetics. The grading scheme is that you either get an a, b, c or fail. No + or - so say goodbye to your GPA if you don't get a A. and it's graded pretty hard. He said he would curve but that didn't happen with our class.

He made the tests on the fly and TAs came up with the key. Exam averages were low because of how in-depth the exams were. Quizess every Friday in class, on Canvas. 3 writing assignments & exams total. So fun and intriguing to hear him lecture, then you realize you're going to be tested on "anything" from the slides and a dark cloud takes over :(
professor wang is the best i have ever had throughout my study at the U. I am taking advanced mechanics of materials. He's a good teacher with grate attention to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I am retaking this course with Prof Fu now, but I still think Pro Wang was a better teacher based on my experience last time. The project is no joke, way too hard for most students
Fantastic professor. I had vibrations with him and it was by far my favorite class I've taken. It's a difficult class but the lectures are great and he's a very lenient grader on exams
I guess he's alright, kinda funny
I hate vibrations but i like dr wang
I took numerical methods from prof wang two years ago. I just thought he was ok at that time, but then after two years, I now think he is actually the best professor I've ever met.
I am in vibrations right now. I guess he's ok, better than most professors here. Could be more organized in things though. Also the project is somewhat confusing to me.
I like this professor especially for his lectures, but the exams and HWs are too hard.(I m taking Vibrations)
Best professor I have ever had so far at the U. But the course content is way to hard for me. You need to be very prepared in terms of coding skills BEFORE taking this class.
I actually took the advanced mechanics of materials with him. Amazing professor. But the textbook was not very good
This course is too hard for me, but I can honestly say that I learnt a lot from Professor Pai Wang. He is probably one of the best in the university.
Great professor, but very hard course. You need to work very hard on coding.
For 6300. Great teacher, lectures could use some refining touches. Teacher cares about the material. The amount of homework is a touch unreasonable given the amount of tests you take.
I love Prof Wang's lectures, but I hate the project.

Pai Wang is extremely smart, but he tried to pack too many things in most of the lectures. Sometimes it was hard for me to keep up. But I still consider him a good teacher, especially if you go to his office hours or schedule a consultation.
Best professor ever! The class is pretty damn hard though

I took it several years ago during COVID, so the course was a bit weird with the online lab session. I did not know the usefulness of things in the course at that time. You really got to focus on this as it include many required things for many other stuff

The lectures were fast paced but the hw was doable with the info. Hw got difficult more as the class progressed. Be prepared for a lecture and lab midterm as well as two finals and a final project. The project was difficult and took lots of time, but the tests were almost identical to the practice exams. Attend lecture for info instead of notes

I took the course with Prof Wang in Fall 2024. He was a superb lectuerer and always tried to help. However, the term project for the lab part of this class was way too hard for any student at this level.
The lectures are thought-provoking and useful. However, the coding project is way too hard.

Easy lectures. He also posted all the lecture slides online to help with homework. He is a very nice person in general and willing to help all the time. Gave out a practice exam. The lab is awful this year but it was not his fault.

Pai is REALLY smart, but that's also his biggest downfall. He struggles to bring things down to the students' level. The TB is really helpful. Be ready for some of the longest HW's and Labs the major offers. Exams also have the tendency to be brutal but are graded leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are incredible and very thorough. Lab was usually pretty easy, and the TA was willing to help if you got stuck. The class covers lots of new info, but he gets through it and explains where it comes from well. My only complaints would be with the grading rubrics, and almost getting a 0 on the final project due to an issue by the grading TA.
Great professor to have. Takes time to answer questions, extremely knowledgeable, and funny.

Pai fully understands what he teaches. Clear from the beginning that you can't cruise in this class, you must put in the work. Regardless of the professor, the difficulty would be the same. Wang explains things clearly, and the slides are thorough. His office hours are incredible and genuinely helpful!f Labs can be long but really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hard class that many students are prepared for. Professor wang does his best and it shows. No matter the teacher the class requires a lot of work so be prepared.

ME EN 2450 is a hard class, and Pai's lectures weren't the clearest. Looking back at lectures after class oddly proved to be more helpful than being in class. Midterm was open notes, and the final exam was open computer (no internet). Labs are tough, but if you get a good TA you'll do well in the class. Pai isn't the best, but certainly not bad.

He is an (unnecessarily) hard professor for the first few weeks until the deadline to drop the class ends. After that, he is a lot nicer. He's a good lecturer, and clearly states what's on the exams (no surprises). As long as you put in the effort and work, you should do fine. The directions on hw and labs are usually confusing, so ask about them.

As long as you make it to the withdrawal deadline then things will get considerably better. Pai is incredibly knowledgeable on the topics, maybe too much so because it can be easy to get lost. The homework is almost entirely coding but class exams are NOT coding but are very closely tied to what's covered in lecture. Pai really isn't so bad though

I am leaving an updated review. My previous review was 1 star. Throughout the semester, Professor Wang has made an effort to improve his class. I feel that lectures are clearer and assignments are more manageable. Pai Wang himself has made less threatening comments and seems to be suddenly nice. This isn't my favorite class, but it's not the worst!

The first half of the course was quite difficult and the lectures weren't easy to follow, though Professor Wang genuinely considered student feedback, and adjusted the class accordingly, for which I respect him. While he can appear intimidating, he is actually great in one-on-one scenarios. Exams were very fair, and he properly prepared the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is not nice. He constantly threatens failure and uses scare tactics. Not one lecture goes by without him saying something like "if this is hard for you, you're going to fail", after giving you 30 seconds (literally!) to do a problem that should take at least 5 minutes. He makes easy things seem hard and is bad at explaining things.

He was well-organized, homework problems and exams were based directly off of lecture material. He did a good job of going over the lecture material in a way that made sense and was easy to reach out to with questions.
The lectures are awful. Manages to make simple concepts incomprehensible. Extremely boring lectures that are hard to follow. Repeatedly tells students to drop the class, is extremely unsupportive.

Pai isn't an amazing prof, but he certainly isn't a bad one either. He's really nice if you talk to him even a little bit. This class has a lot of hw (between the lecture and the lab), but it is certainly manageable. Know thr basics in matlab and python and be prepared to take a visit once and awhile to the tutoring center and you'll be fine.

Professor Wang is awesome. If you have a decent understanding of coding you will be completely fine in the class. His lectures are interesting for the most part, and his homework is enough to help understand the subject, but not overwhelming.

Not too hard to stay on top of the homework. His lectures can ramble on but they are posted on his website so they are easily accessible while doing the homework. The class content isn't hard as long as you have a good base in coding and can read pseudocode Don't listen to anyone on here saying he is bad, definitely one of my favorite professors.

This class is difficult but doable. Prof Wang isn't a perfect lecturer but puts in lots of effort to listen to feedback and make his lectures better. He really wants you to succeed but won't hand it to you on a silver platter. Do not take this course if you can't code. If you don't mind these things, I wouldn't sweat this class too much.

Very frustrating class. The homework doesnt give enough help/instructions to do by ones self most of the time. He teaches simple things in a complex way, and his rude comments when you get the wrong answer during class dont help. Must have decent coding knowledge before taking class.

This is proving to be a "gatekeeper" course, which is frustrating. Any effort to say "this material will be hard" is taken despite the fact that teaching the material doesn't HAVE to be too bad. If the homework wasn't needlessly tedious and graded harshly to the point of deducting over half an assignment for things not specified not being included.

I would NEVER recommend taking this class from him, as he made things way harder than they had to be. I might as well have read the textbook and paid to take an exam because I can honestly say I learned nothing from him. At all. He was inconsistent, confusing, and needed to plan out his semester better. But a very funny and nice person overall!

Considering this was Professor Wang's first time teaching as a professor, he is not as bad as the other reviews say. He is very accessible outside of the classroom and always responds quickly through emails with thorough answers. Labs were not that bad (3 hours/week) and homeworks took just as much time. Final exam was open note and open computer.

Expect to spend a good chunk of time on the homework every week. Labs are tedious, and the TA's are mostly terrible and unhelpful. Although clearly very smart, the professor is not good at teaching and is very hard to follow in lecture. I didn't find the accent too bad, but he moves very quickly which makes it difficult to understand. Thumbs down
Guy barely speaks english... had to take this class twice and first professor was 10 times better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pai (He prefers his first name) I a fine person. Only problem is his teaching skills. Lectures are not helpful, you might as well stay at home and read the text book. Thankfully the TA I have is awesome and bends the rules pretty frequently. This class feels like a 6000 level Programming course. I am confident I will pass. But with pain.

reviews.comment: Oh my god I cant even believe how bad he was. He sprints through the lecture and he has such a thick accent that the lectures were useless, I dont even know why I go anymore. The labs are annoying and my TA is useless(Im pretty sure he smokes weed every day before class). Its hard to teach yourself bc the textbook is mind numbing. Avoid him

reviews.comment: She was very upbeat and interested in all our projects. Class critique was helpful and I like that it was heavily peer guided. Participation matters. She would also come by individually to give us critique and help us improve our projects. She was very invested in seeing students push their concepts further.

reviews.comment: Maike is a very understanding, engaging, and fun professor. She loves what she teaches but isn't overbearing. Projects are crafted to have personal connections and creative freedom.

reviews.comment: She made me feel like some of my projects weren't good enough and not respectable. BUT, she seemed pretty nice, just that she wants stuff done a certain way. She can't spell good ahah she warned us at the beginning, Just saying this because personally, I can't spell either.

reviews.comment: This class is easy and she tells you what to expect to be on the exam. Very interesting class.

I would not recommend taking this class from her as a freshman. 

It goes heavy into biochemistry, which might have been good—if they were a co- or prerequisite, which, since it is an entry-level class, it doesn't have. I would sit this class out until you have a good background knowledge of chemistry.

Class was disorganized and confusing, multiple hour+ long assignments due on the same day, review sheets didn't have what was on the exam, etc. Blatantly doesn"t care if anybody passes her class. One of the midterms had an average of 63% and the students were put on blast for getting a bad average.

This has been arguably one of the worst experiences I have had at the University of Utah. Many times my classmates and I have tried to ask questions for clarification and have been met with sarcasm or a condescending comment. The large amount of coursework also was stressful. Do not take this class if you have the option to.

She talked down to us as if we were the dumbest people she has seen in her entire life. She is extremely picky when grading. It is impossible to get 100% on assignments. Over half the class failed the midterm and she said  "I don't care if you all fail". Her flipped classroom is a joke and an absolute waste of time. Be prepared to slave for hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She assigns so many papers and assignments and doesn't seem to care about students. I was scared to go to her classes. She only gives back criticism on assignments and I felt like she was never satisfied with my work. It was demoralizing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Middle of the road, but you can pass without too much trouble if you get the work done. Plays favorites. Doesn't give good feedback or help clarify questions. Design procedure for the class is divorced from that used in the private sector.

This professor does not communicate with her TA, they operate on completely different grading procedures. On top of that, she provides little to no instructions on her individual homeworks, and assumes her students know every little thing she wants. She can also be very condescending at times when you ask her questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mike is visibly excited about the material every day. There's quite a bit of reading, but it's worth every page. The class is very well taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Gods & Monsters with Mike, and it was a blast with him. You can see his passion for the material, as well as see that he genuinely cares for his students. There are 2 pretty fun papers and 2 short quizzes throughout the course of the semester. If you need an Honors IT, take this class with Mike!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mike was an amazing person, and he is very passionate about what he does. He was always open to talk about assignments and readings, and he made the class really fun. Two easy multiple choice, true false, and fill in the blank tests. Two pretty fun essays. Loved the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, interesting content, loved his class. 10/10 recommend. Never felt overwhelmed in this class
White was absolutely great. The class is super interesting, and as long as you keep up with reading (not hard), you'll do fine.
Mike is a super caring and passionate professor. 100% recommend taking a class by him!

reviews.comment: Mike is a great professor. We had a couple of decently heavy reading assignments but he goes over everything so thoroughly in class that it is an easy class. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him do it. 100% would recommend. He is funny and I enjoyed attending his classes despite not being interested in the subject.

Professor White cares about his students. Even though this HONORS course was graded by very few things, the tests were incredibly easy. There was a lot of reading assigned, especially since it was a 2nd half summer class, but I learned lots from his lecturers. Technically, you wouldn't even have to do the readings to get an A and understand the txt
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor White is a fantastic lecturer that looks at texts from unique perspectives. I would highly recommend this course as an honors credit. The class grade is based on two easy 15-question tests (as long as you pay attention) and 2 essays. The workload is very manageable and he gives great feedback for essays.
AMAZING! Loved this class, would def recommend if you enjoy reading interesting books and essays.

best professor at the U. i didn't do a single reading throughout the whole year, i just went to class and payed attention and did just fine on the quizzes. his lectures are very interesting and entertaining even when you didn't read anything lol. im honestly really sad that i wont have him as my professor anymore.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. White is an incredible professor. The subject matter in LEAP 1230 is very interesting, but the open discussions are where the course really shines. Dr. White is a really engaging speaker and the classrooms ideas and interpretations of the texts feel like they really matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: absolutely love him. decided to take another class from him next semester that i don't even need because I loved it so much. he is very understanding, and his lectures are so interesting. lots of reading, but they are fun books and we always talk about them in cool ways

Dr. White was awesome. Reading heavy but the books and material are interesting. I'm assuming it's not for everyone but if what makes a human a human is an interesting topic to you, you will love this class. There are only a few assignments graded but all the quizzes and assignments are easy (writing heavy).  10/10 class and 10/10 professor.

reviews.comment:
IT: Gods & Monsters - Spring 2022.
Even though Zoom format makes things less personal, Mike is a super engaging and caring professor who really loves what he teaches and wants his students to get something out of it. I'm very glad I took this class, and given the chance to take another class from him, I'd do so in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
For Gods and Monsters.
Professor White is an awesome professor. He always makes his lectures very engaging with many chances to participate. For graded assignments, there are only two easy tests (just pay attention and you'll ace them) and two essays with a lot of creative wiggle room allowed. The texts you read are interesting as well.

If you need to take IT classes, take them with Mike White. He is an amazing teacher and gives great feedback. His IT classes are only two essays, two 15-point super easy tests, and participation. If you send him your work early, he'll give suggestions and give a good grade. Best teacher in the honors college by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mike is a super fun teacher and his lectures are always super fun. All you have to do is come to class and listen and read the texts assigned. The quizzes are not bad at all, just pay attention to the main ideas that he hammers on in lecture. He is super fun and a good resource and easy to work with if you need help with the two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. White is clearly passionate about what he teaches and shows that in his lectures while also engaging in class discussions. As long as you do the readings and come to class you will pass, although he is very flexible about absences. He is willing to work with you if necessary. He formats the class in a way that encourages engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof White is hands down the best professor I've had at the U. He's clearly passionate about literature and keeps the class engaged in discussions. The readings were really interesting and not a chore to get through. We had two (very easy) multiple choice tests and two essays where he allowed a lot of creative freedom. Easy A, still learned a lot.

Such a good guy. Have to read before every class but usually the readings aren't long and he makes sure you understand the content before going in depth. Two essays which are graded very easy. Two short quizzes designed to be easy A's. Mike was so friendly and wiling to listen to every point of view. Won't fail if you don't read before every class
Mike is a great professor, and really passionate about what he's teaching.

Gods & Monsters was a really cool class that could've easily been the most boring class ever if taught by another professor. Really good at leading interesting discussions that involve everyone, even people that typically might not engage (like me!). You get from the class what you put into it, in terms of learning and grades.

reviews.comment: This is for the 2810 Gods and Monsters class. Be prepared to buy a few books, but not textbooks. He's really nice and the papers aren't long or very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The best professor I have had at the University of Utah. His class is very easy, and consists of 2 reading quizzes (over multiple readings, and he tells you which ones), 1 argumentative paper (easy), and 1 final paper (you can choose between a dinner-party type paper, or another argumentative). Easy grader, and amazing person. Brings snacks at end.

Only 4 graded assignments: 1 midterm paper & 1 final paper, and 1 midterm quiz & 1 final quiz. You read a lot, but every reading is really good and Prof White has amazing discussions on them (you'll do fine if you miss readings). Funny, approachable, from Canada. Really cool guy.
Dr. White is great. I really enjoyed his class. The material was engaging and I liked the discussions that we had in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I had at the start of college. He is kind and funny. He is great at lecturing and it is always interesting. He truly cares about his students.

He's a very nice teacher and is enthusiastic about his lectures and passionate about the readings he assigns. It's like a generic high school English class where you analyze text and discuss themes and symbols and other abstract meanings. Attendance is important; I have an A- because I had work and was late or missing here and there.

Great professor. Easy class, interesting lectures and great discussions. Brought in donuts twice. Only had to write two papers and a few easy quizzes. Hes a very fair grader, and is mostly focused on a general understanding of the books assigned.

Easy A as long as you show up and do a majority of the readings.  The professor gives meaningful and benefitting things for the students to read so it's not a problem actually completing it. A lot of class time is spent with discussions so it's really easy to stay interested. The teacher is also great and caring for his students, very lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mike is a genuine guy, and his class is very enjoyable (especially if you like literature). Treat his class like an English class, read the novels most of the way through and you'll pass no problem. His lectures are thought-provoking and objective, and I learned a lot from him.

He engages the class in interesting discussions about the readings and actually makes it fun to come to class. His tests were easy and was a fairly easy grader with essays. Overall a great professor, would recommend.

You attend everyday, listen to his lectures, and do most of reading assignments then you will be guaranteed with A. He is willing to help you and he is very nice guy. Although the topics we covered were bit boring for my taste. Easy A class for sure, if you attend and participate.

I signed up on accident thinking it was an exploration class but it turned out to be an environmental class, but it was really cool! He's really nice and not intimating. Keep up with your homework and you'll do just -- and theres not even a lot! Hes an awesome professor :]

This was the best professor i had last semester, his quizzes and tests are base on lectures he gave; which, was extremely easy. It wasn't mandatory to go to class, but its recommended. He was willing to work with you, and his readings will show up again throughout your college career.

Dr. White was on e of m favorite professors this semester.  All of the reading thats he assigns are surprisingly interesting, and they are stories mostly.... not boring textbook equations and such.  His lectures are interesting as well. Definitely a good professor.

Dr. Micheal White is a pretty cool guy he knows a lot about literature, but doesn't seem like some strung-out manic-depressed literary hippy, but instead he is a very approachable person. His lectures and instructions are very clear, and his assignments are not too hard. Also, most of the textbooks are just literature books.
chill dude who wants people to learn and try
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super willing to help all students. Wants you to succeed and is super passionate. Met some super funny people in this class. The essays were not too bad but definitely take some hard work.

He is awesome. Has great stories. Gets to know his students and cares about them. It almost felt like a hangout more than a class. One of the only teachers who I would get a drink with. Super cool guy. Pretty easy course and just a pleasure to be around.

If you are planning on taking 3420 over the summer as an easy GE credit, I would look elsewhere. Because the class was so short, the workload was more than I was used to, especially for a GE. 
That being said, I enjoyed this class more than I thought that I would. My writing improved, and I learned a lot about environmental writing.

I took Professor Werner's Environmental Writing summer class, and I found the experience to not only be eye opening due to the depth of the course curriculum, but the class was also a space for me to feel safe and supported in my exploration of the humanities relative to our natural environment in a creative, and engaging way. Max is the best!

Professor Werner is an elite professor. As long as you are respectful and try your best you will succeed. An easy way to get a good grade is to participate in class. He is passionate about his subject and gives good feedback of how you can improve your writing. The students who don't like him are the ones who do not make any effort.

It seemed Max made his lectures on the spot and had nothing to do with assignments. Very random tangents with touchy subjects. Discourse was rarely open for students to share as Max often took over the “conversation”. Syllabus and rubrics aren't provided, instructions are vague, and feedback is unclear and rude. I wouldn't recommend this professor.

Great Professor! The class was super fun to take, and he was always there to answer questions and provided good extra credit opportunities. So sad that I am not taking a class with him next semester. Hardest part of the class was just all the writing, so if you are not a writing major or don't like to write would not suggest this class.

A highly responsible professor, patiently addressing any questions, delivering clear and well-structured courses. There is a substantial amount of classroom interaction among students. The content of the course is progressive, allowing for a comprehensive learning experience and practical application of writing skills. Highly recommended!

Overall, Professor Werner was a great instructor and I would definitely take his class again. He cared for his students, wanting to make sure they succeed, as well as trying to keep class interesting/engaging. A majority of the work is clear and straight-forward, however, it is important to put a lot of your focus into the essays and participation.

Although his class was quite challenging, Prof. Werner did an excellent job teaching. The assignments, in particular, did much to improve my writing. Although his grading criteria were somewhat confusing, the feedback he offered often made up for it. Overall, an involved, passionate, and accommodating teacher to those who needed it.
Hes a great professor makes lectures fun and interactive. assignments are fairly easy and theres not too many
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor is my favorite professor I have had at the U! He is very willing to help students get the best grade they can. He always helped me if I messaged him needing more explanation or help. He is very forgiving but also respectable. 10/10 teacher, definitely take his class.

Max feels way to strongly about writing, he used words such as "attractive" when a student comes to class and "sexy" to describe a piece of writing. He always has a lot to say, as if he is making it up on the spot. He expects you  to have the same love for ALL of his assignments. However, his assignment criteria is vague and unhelpful.

Professor Werner is a caring and passionate professor. He welcomed every student by name as they entered the classroom and created a very welcoming environment. I would simply complain that for a 1010 class, he graded quite harshly. Grading rubrics were also quite opaque. His feedback was very useful, but quite ruthless for an entry course.

The class is the brainchild of Professor Werner, it is not like a typical Environmental Writing class. If you want to write traditional research papers find a different class. Otherwise he is a great man and make sure to use his resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Werner is a fantastic professor. His approach to the subject matter was refreshing and inspiring. His class has been one of the most valuable and memorable that I have taken, and I would recommend him as a professor without reservation. Class was informative, collaborative, and purposeful, with no sense of busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This man cares A LOT about writing and you can tell. He is very enthusiastic, but can talk too much about it sometimes. He is a tough grader, but he does give very clear feedback on essays on how to get a better grade. he does offer final essay exam makeup which is noice. You will learn in this class for sure.

This class focuses on writing about war so if you are not interested in the subject, then it's not gonna be fun. His canvas page was always super confusing and messy and he always got lost while looking for specifics on his page. I think he can be pretty harsh on grading which is unfair since he doesn't ever have rubrics. Overall he's okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Werner has truly made my freshman year at the U the best. He helps you with essays he assigns so you truly understand what you are writing about. He gives amazing feedback. Also, his lectures are very fun and interesting to listen to. I would 10/10 recommend this professor to any incoming freshman.
He is really nice and gives good feedback on all of the assignments, but there is a lot of tedious busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Werner can be great, his feedback is brutally honest, almost cruel. Some may like it, some won't. He has a clear grading criteria and is very open about writing and his passion for it. Otherwise, he is just very intimidating but cares a lot, so be sure to attend office hours and ask about assignments, you will do good in the class.

This guy is the best professor I had freshman year. He wants you to succeed, and He will do next to anything to help you do that. He doesn't accept late work under any circumstance except if you make arrangements beforehand. His essays are not specific but are broad so that you write what you want to. He just looks for structure and progress.

Max is one of a kind. He leads discussions in class and mediates them well. Most of your grade comes from one main investigative paper with a couple of smaller ones here and there. Participation matters, if you miss a lot, he notices and docs you. But class was entertaining!

Professor Werner is one of the best English teachers I've had. He is clearly passionate about what he does and is willing to help with your essays. We had a total of 3 papers due for the whole semester and they each only needed to be about 3 pages in length. He's big on participation, so be sure to share your ideas.

He is am amazing professor who is passionate about what he teaches. Only downside is that sometimes he will shut down his students ideas that do not align with his own. He really cares about his students and doesn't give many assignments especially compared to other WRTG2010 classes.

Prof Werner is amazing. Provides great feedback and is so passionate about what he teaches. He's always happy to help, he enjoys other perspectives. Attendance isn't mandatory but he makes you want to go to class. You have one 12 pg paper, 2 updates and an oped. A few small assignment throughout, but super easy!

Werner is a passionate professor who I would recommend to any dedicated student. Students who value a letter grades over experience should look elsewhere. It takes a mature student to appreciate this professor. As another reviewer said earlier, he puts a lot into this class and expects the same from his students.

Highly recommend. Max makes himself available to his students and gives very constructive feedback. I really improved my writing. Class discussions were very engaging and everyone was involved. A big portion of the class is a group project where you work with a non-profit. It gives you a lot of real-world experience. Great class, great experience.

Dr Werner was a great teacher.  I enjoyed his classes a lot.  He was extremely respectful, very approachable.  When he saw me on campus he would always say hello.  It was apparent that he appreciated and respected his student.  He could be a hard grader at times but was always there to talk about the assignment and give feedback.  Great Class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader, and is also vague on what he wants from an assignment (or he writes so much you have to review it multiple times).  If you put effort into the class you can still come out with a good grade. I'm already in the workplace (11 years) , and these assignments are not relevant to what one would encounter in the real world.

If you're OK with a hard earned B+ then take this class. If you are annoyed by professors who dock 5-10 points off every assignment for arbitrary reasons, do NOT take this class. The group project made it easy to compare grades and every one of my group members were docked 3+ points on every assignment for not being able to read his mind. GOOD LUCK

Prof. Werner leads great discussions and welcomes varying viewpoints and ideas. I found that the more I participated the more I understood, learned, and progressed. This course is a classic case of reap what you sow; I put in the work, asked questions, and left with a new perspective.  Great course, well done Professor Werner.

Max really feels strongly about this class and has a lot to say about it, but consequentially he expects you to care about it just as much. Of course, you should care about and engage in every class, but he really expects you to take every assignment (there is a surprise one every week) as seriously as he does, and he grades accordingly. /

An overall miserable experience. This was an Honors course intended to teach how to write at a research university and it utterly failed to teach anything of use. The lectures were improv style, featured highly triggering material. I expected more writing and critique. Non-existent syllabus. I would not take a class from this professor again.

He's a great teacher that I wish I could have again in the future. He's really helpful and will always be there if you need any kind of ell on something. Sometimes I felt he was a little unclear in his instructions but once I asked again he was able to re explain them for me and it was clear to my understanding. He's great! I recommend him!

Werner demands a high level of effort from each student, but it's only because he knows you're capable. For those of you complaining - BUCK UP, BUTTERCUPS. Critical thinking is  the best part of writing, and Werner encourages you to explore your thought processes and test your limits as a writer. Brilliant professor, even better human.

Max is a great guy, and he genuinely wants his students to do their best. However, his assignment criteria is vague and unhelpful. He lets the students have discussions which makes it a really fun class, though not great for real-world application if you're serious about professional writing. I usually hate group projects, but that was my fav part!

He is a really fun teacher, and easy to talk to. He is slightly everywhere. If you return in corrections for a paper don't expect to get it back for at least two month. Some of his assignments are vague and confusing so it is important that you go to class. Make sure you have a good group since the group project is a semester long project.

Max is a COOl teacher. There is a big group project, but it's not difficult. Some of his assignments were actually really fun. He wants you to write a lot about your jobcareerprofession, which makes it easier to write and more realistic. Overall, i really enjoyed this class, and I usually hate writing. I'd DEFINITELY recommend him for writing!!!!

Max Werner is an intensely passionate professor on writing and the environment, and the passion emanates to the entire class. If you walk in ambivalent towards policies and procedures regarding meaningful protection, preservation, and promotion of environmental themes, Werner's passion will leave you touched.

For any other writing class, he would be a blast. He was enthusiastic and passionate, however the class did little to teach the skills students would expect from this course. Pretty easy A, no tests, little homework. I would recommend looking for another professor if professional writing is a skill you need.
Awesome professor! Really helpful and tells you how you can improve.

Really good guy, always willing to help if you ask for it. He teaches writing in a different way that involves the students a lot rather than just lecturing. The assignments are really fun and you learn a lot. I highly recommend this class!

Extremely unclear assignments. Class had nothing to do with professional writing. Instructions were overly verbose and unclear -- when asked to clarify, he would just say "read the material." Avoid. Very frustrating class.
Class format is discussion format. Good teacher overall. The class waas ok. Not a lot of homework just bigger assignments. He's helpful.

He is the best teacher I have ever had! I loved going to class! I got a lot better at my writing because of him! He is so helpful and will meet with you anytime! I took honors writing from him so it is a pretty hard class, but I got through it with an A- because he was my teacher!

Max is a great guy.  He is very passionate about teaching and clearly enjoys doing it.  He is extremely professional and will do anything in his power to help you succeed.  He doesn't hand out A's, but if you put in the time and work you can easily do well in his class.

Replies quickly to email. Dedicated to helping the students, when they ask for it. Open to different ideas. Not a lot of busy work and homework. There's a lot of class discussion and he emphasizes participation in class discussions!
He's a pretty good professor-passionate. It wasn't uncommon for him to go on some random tangent that none of us understood or agreed with though.
This professor was extremely helpful in helping the class and teaching in a manner that made you think and appreciate writing. He helped me to understand the importance of how you phrase a sentence.

Professor Werner's class is extremely helpful for those who are planning on going to grad school as it helps you prepare for research and higher level writing.  Professor Werner himself is engaged with his class and full of passion and knowledge for writing. Not to mention he is a pretty awesome teacher all in all!
dr. werner is a great writing coach.

I wasn't a fan. I felt the assignments were very ambiguous with regard to their intent. There were very few exercises that helped me professionally. There was a service learning component that was worth half your grade. That's fine, but the fact that it's team based makes it unreasonable.

I love this professor! It was so refreshing to take a class and learn things that will be used after graduation.  The assignments were challenging but the Mr. Werner was always available to help.  He also gives you the opportunity to revise your work. I definitely increased my professional writing skills by taking this class.

Excellent professor!  Makes writing fun and interesting.  His assignments are very useful to real life circumstances, and he really makes you think about the meaning of the words you use in writing.  He grades difficultly, but if you come to class and do the work, you will be pleased with the outcome.
Excellent professor. Very helpful in writing "real world" documents and memos.
