This is the second class I have taken from Professor Werner because he is such a great instructor. He actually cares about individual students and is  always willing to give extra time to help when it is needed.
I have had Professor Werner for two writing classes now because I have enjoyed his teaching methods so much!
Thanks Max. The class was great

From the very first day I could tell that this professor had a genuine passion odor the material and beyond that, he cares very deeply about veterans and what happens to us.  I would recommend this class to all returning OIF/OEF vets and to non-vet students as well.

Professor Werner was a great teacher for Writing about War.  He was interested in the material and facilitated some great discussions.  He was also open to hearing views from everyone and all sides of issues.

I really enjoyed professor Werner's class. He was very helpful and I really enjoyed how engaged with the students. He called you by name and made you felt very comfortable in his class. His class combined the perfect amount of challenge and fun. I would highly recommend taking professional writing from Professor Werner
Werner is a great professor. He really takes time to know each student and provide helpful insight. He grades fairly hard but is overall great!

Professor Werner leads very interesting and intellectual discussions. It was unfortunate that I had to withdraw from the course. His grading is fair, and he really works with the students to help them get the most out of the course. Overall, one of the best professors at the U of U.

Werner was my favorite professor at the U! He showed me the effect creative writing can have on an individual. Also, his class projects gave me the opportunity to serve the community through new found writing skills. He is very helpful, available, and creates a safe environment for open and critical thinking.

I have taken two courses with Maximilian Werner and they were both fantastic experiences. I was able to improve my critical thinking and reasoning. Werner is a genuinely caring individual that is always open to help his students. He also is very good at responding to all inquiries in a timely manner. WRTG 3015/2010 were great classes.

Very nice teacher! He was willing to work with students on an individual basis and always asked students what their opinion about assignments and papers was. He was very thorough and explained things very well.

Werner is one of the best professors I've had.  His class projects create practical uses for professional writing that I have carried over into several other projects.  He is supportive and caring towards his students and creates a safe environment for open and critical thinking.

Fantastic professor! He helps you think about your writing critically, and is most definitely a guided learning professor. Did a great job with my class. 5 Stars :) He was always as helpful as you would let him be. Great class, and yeah, he like the environment. Really relaxed class, always fun to go to.

I really enjoyed this class on Professional Writing. Werner's teaching style allowed me to learn the importance of word choice as well as how to effectively present information in a concise manner. He is always willing to help and is very clear on his expectations. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot from him.
Okay professor but never explains assignment or makes much sense. You dont learn how to write better you learn how to pick a topic he likes so you do okay. easy class but frustrating.

He is by far my favorite writing professor.  His classes were always interesting.  He is really passionate about writing and I felt like he did a great job at transferring that passion to us.  You will love his class
Great Professor and cool guy. Made 2010 entertaining and an enjoyable experience. As long as you stick to the paper guidelines, you will do well in the class. I highly recommend his class to anyone!

Great professor. Extremely passionate about what he does. As long as you stay on top of your assignments it will be a great experience. He is also very good at replying  to emails. Never actually used to book so it was kind of a waste of money. Max learns everyone's name and make the class a really enjoyable experience.
You will not learn how to write in this class, just learn to how to think the way the professor wants you to think.

This Class had weekly quizzes that had very short time limits. These quizzes were very hard and would really harm your grade. Homework assignments weren't too bad, but exams were very challenging. Dr. Whitaker's teaching was very all over the place and hard to follow. You're better off going for the textbook.

We had a quiz where there were technical difficulties. Instead of accepting he messed up and giving everyone 100%. He chose to hold students back by 30 minutes. 

He also frequently mistaught things in class. He's a specimen of a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Less than useless

After the first few weeks, lectures felt like a waste of time. He barely went over anything useful, and would throw in jokes such as "I hate my wife" or mocking The Youths (aka, us.) Constant technical difficulties with Canvas. I should've expected the "curve" on the final to be another accident, but it was still a nasty shock when it was "fixed".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
There were constant problems with lecture notes, lecture recordings, quizzes, homework, and even exams. Fun fact, the course website file system was exposed, meaning you could view future homework questions ahead of time.
If you're forced against your will to take this class, you're better off reading the textbook while also watching Khan Academy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All around a confusing professor.  Doesn't know how to work canvas, rarely responds back to student emails, lectures were beyond confusing, and the nail in the coffin was acting like we got a curve on the final to only take it away a few hours later with ZERO announcements.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor frequently excludes information from lectures that appear on homework, quizzes, and exams, frequently responds to questions in a very passive-aggressive tone, and frequently takes a significantly long time to respond to student questions about homework, even on or around the due date. Grading is often nitpicky and condescending.

Instructions not clear
Harsh on grading
Don't take it for fun
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not 1 lecture was clear and organised. It seems like he would make up the lecture along the way because of how many mistakes he was messing and getting confused. He spent the final day of class reviewing what was NOT going to be on the final "for fun". Most assignments are a mix of R coding and word problems, & get ready to be besties with the TAs

Professor Whitaker seemed very enthusiastic to teach this class at the beginning of the semester, but unfortunately that didn't last and it became clear throughout that he did not put much care into this course. Mistakes in homework, unclear lectures, and there were not enough info sheets printed for the final, which contained vital information.

Ross Whitaker is easily the worst professor in the CS program. Terrible lectures (half the time not even covering the necessary information) are made worse by zero coordination with TAs and constant mistakes in grading and with Canvas. We were "taught" R in this class, which meant we had to figure it out ourselves (just like everything else).
Puts the S in S&M. Terrible structure.  Terrible support.

Worst professor I have ever had, and I have never said that before. Lectures don't cover anything, very little resources for learning outside of class especially since he doesn't follow textbook or standard stats curriculum. Lazy, unbelievably disorganized, TAs seem poorly guided. Luckily not a crazy amount of work.
This class is a combo of difficult homework, tough grading, and unstructured lectures. His exams are awful. Be ready to do a lot of learning on your own.

Shoehorned into this position by the KSoC's desire to teach existing math classes in order to get more differential tuition. As a result, he does not know how to teach stats effectively. Homework ripped from previous semesters made harder by adding more problems to each. Hieroglyphic lecture slides and his skills with Canvas are infuriatingly bad.

Weekly Quizzes that are NOT easy like he claims they are. Brutal homeworks. He uses notation that is different from the textbook and then expects you to know the textbook notation when you take the exams or do the homework. Going to be retaking this class with a better professor because I feel like I haven't learned anything in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He presents his lectures pretty good vocally, but every other element of this class is bad.  Recordings, lecture notes, examples that relate to homework, and support provided to students are poor.  He's absent more often than any other professor I have had (this is for a clas of 250). TA provides the backbone for the course.

This professor lost my homework and tried to blame me. Additionally, his lectures and thoughts are poorly organized and he is unresponsive to numerous student questions on the discussion board. Choose literally any other professor.
Bad person & professor. Chicken scratch lecture slides.
The actual Instructor is the TA.

He is an awesome researcher but not a responsible teacher. The reused slides are not detailed about the content covered in class, and he explains theories in very abstract ways which sometimes confuse a lot students.

Ross is a great teacher, and lectures in a very relaxed manner. Be prepared to think critically and you'll do fine. If you want an A in CS2100, master Proof by Induction and Proof by Contradiction as early as possible (before he assigns it).

Overall he's not a bad teacher, but he's kind of scatterbrained. For example, e confuses himself when explaining problems sometimes. He also reuses his old assignments and timelines, and because of that he ended up with a quiz scheduled for Thanksgiving...
The ultimate professor for the ultimate fun class to get some credits while exploring the beautiful outdoors in Utah. 20/10.

Tim is simply the GOAT. He is a thrill to talk to during hikes and absolutely loves his job. Him and Melany are the best. Recognizes many of his students take these classes for a few desperate credits and tailors the experience extremely well. The hike we went on was advertised as 12 miles but was really 9. Really knows what he's doing, love Tim!

Tim White is the best. He made camping in 50 mile per hour winds and sandstorms fun. He made canoeing 50 miles the funnest camping trip of my life. Any outdoor adventure class with Tim will be a treat.

Canyonlands trip. The hike is around 13 miles. Campsite we stayed at was amazing. You have to write a paper about a chosen topic before the trip and you have to present about the topic at some point ON the trip. Presentations are very laid back. At the end of the trip, there is a "final" where you answer questions about other people's topic. FUN!

I took a beginning canoeing class from Tim on the White River, near Vernal, Utah. It was around 35 miles of paddling over 3 days, so if you are interested in that amount of exercise it is more than worth it! It is a beautiful stretch of river! There is a 2-page essay with a 10-minute presentation which was pretty easy. Tim is pretty laid back!

I didn't find his lectures very effective; I usually learned more from the book than the lectures. He could also give quite condescending answers when asked questions, even fairly valid ones, which isn't a vibe to say the least. Not sure how chem1220 was but if I had to retake gen chem ll I'd probably try it over Professor White's chem1221 :/

I took his honors chem class. Professor White is a very smart guy, but his lectures are only kind of helpful. Homework and tests are pretty much all based on the textbook, and he does pop quizzes on days with less students. My main issue is that he's constantly picking on students, and seems to enjoy punishment. Ask a question at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Grade is almost entirely based on tests. His lectures didn't help much, classmates said they learned most material from the book. However, since his class was so hard he did extra credit and such to make sure very few people failed. The toughest class I've taken. Go to office hours, read the book, and be patient for success in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor White wasn't a very good teacher. He would put a bunch of already displayed problems on the projector and just scroll through them. I would have done so much better if would have taken the time to solve things and go through them. He cost my friend her scholarship and didn't even think about raising the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor White was a solid professor. Lectures were mostly example problems so I would recommend at least skimming the chapter beforehand. The material can be tough at times, but lectures were kept interesting with occasional demos from Professor Statler. He was very accomodating with office hours and let us use a notecard on the last exam.

Prof. White was awesome! He's funny and is really good at explaining the material. In this class, the tests are written by a different professor and there's not getting around them, they're hard. There's also a required in class component (clickers) so don't miss class! You definitely have to work but it's not too bad of a class.

I don't understand why the recent reviews are so negative for her. It's an easy and interesting class about design principles and human usability of software. The group projects are fun and I haven't had to spend more than 45 minutes on any assignment. Any reviews before Fall 25 are for a previous different class than this one. Genuinely fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: pointless group projects that don't prepare you as a computing professional. Doesn't let you use technology in class and treats us like 5 year olds.  makes "participation" the point of the class when she can't get anyone excited about the material. Seems completely unprepared to teach...i dont know to basically every question.

Taking this class with Wiese felt like jumping through hoops. The actual content and assignments weren't technically hard, just time-consuming and difficult to navigate. Expectations were unclear. Micromanaged our group projects, requiring a weekly team check

Professors Wiese is very unconfident and hesitates when answering students questions. Although the course is on human centric experience, the workload she expects is very inhumane.. Harsh grading all the assignments. You learn by reading a text book, doing a ton of writing week after week in a team. Midterms are not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Overall prof. Wiese isn't bad, she just has very clear and incredibly extensive grading criteria. Do exactly what the assignment calls for and you'll get a good grade and you'll learn a lot.

The majority of the class is group projects, but provided you get a decent team, the workload is less than most CS classes, and around 1/2 the class ended with an A. Expect a lot of writing though.

Prof. Wiese is one of the nicest professors I've met, really willing to work with students, and seems really passionate about the material she teaches.
She is not suitable to teach this class, and she doesn't understand the teaching content at all. Chaotic classroom, with tedious homework.

It is criminal how many papers and group projects Professor Wiese requires of this class. Many of her instructions for her assignments are frustratingly unclear with small details that are very easy to miss and lose a lot of points on, and it is YOUR grade that suffers for it. I should've heeded advice and skipped Professor Wiese's class. Horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prepare for tons of busy work unrelated to HCI. She acts like you've never worked in a team before and she actually thinks a reflection after every assignment on 'teamwork' is a good idea. It's clear she has no idea what's she's doing. Her degree is related to teaching and it really shows. Please take a class from a REAL CS professor and avoid her.

The primary issue with this class is that it attempts to be two classes at once. Half the assignments are not related to HCI and are centered around teamwork. These are the "busywork" everyone complains about. They have nothing to do with HCI, are clearly thrown in to fill gaps in her course plan, and piled on top of an already heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: It saddens me, but I'm not surprised to see the negative reaction here. The class was indeed quite disorganized, and it was pretty difficult. Prof. Wiese makes you work for it. But I do think what I learned was relevant and valuable. I think her style and course layout is excellent for self-driven individuals, and it is a refreshing breath of air.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am senior and this has been the WORST class I have taken in my entire education. Wiese would deduct points if you voiced your frustration in Piazza forums, effectively discouraging students to make any negative comments publicly. I don't think I learned anything in this class. I was excited about HCI, but now she ruined it for me, forever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I have never had a class this bad. Ever. The content was interesting but the teaching by Wiese was so bad that Im convinced any high school student could have taught it, you will not get anything out of it except a bunch of busy work, a hate for HCI and a waste of time. Lectures were aimless. Homework was random. Organization nonexistent. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Quite literally the worst organized class I've ever taken. Wiese likes to give very specific and redundant grading criteria, and then throws it out the window and grades subjectively anyway. Even following her exact feedback on what to fix still results in a lot of missed points. For your sanity, please stay away from this awful, awful course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. Seriously. Assignments were not announced in enough time and expectations were not made explicit enough considering how harshly she grades. This was the most stressful class I had all semester. Some groups had a better time than us, but no one understood the class activities. I learned how to please Wiese, but not about HCI.

65% of the grade was group projects. Lots of writing. The class was disorganized, but this was her first semester. She seems passionate about HCI and expects a lot from her students, but she is very approachable outside of class to help. She offered a lot of extra credit. If you do not like giant group projects, I would avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: While this class was disorganized, I think I learned a lot about how HCI works in the real world. Professor Wiese was always willing to offer detailed feedback, and had feedback vs actual deadlines to improve assignments prior to final submission. There was a lot of writing involved, but I thought it was fair given there was no code implementation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Prof. Wiese was completely unorganized and the structure of the class left me wonder if there was anything I learned. Every single class was a mess, and when we were put into breakout rooms the general consensus was 'we have no clue what to do'. SO MANY POINTLESS PAPERS! Just busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worked extremely well with my accommodations.

I would have gotten an A if it weren't for the 2 IRL Public Select essays that he has us write. He doesn't grade half of the stuff until the end of the semester, which makes it very hard to guess your grade, because I thought I was going to get an A. But this class is very easy and common sense if you aren't racist or can understand prejudice.

I took Dr. White online but really enjoyed his personality and accent, and thought the class was very well set up. It was easy to succeed and Dr. White's syllabus was clear; I was never confused about assignments/tests/policies.

Honestly, just keep up with the class calendar and you'll be fine. The weekly summaries are busy work, but it's not anything that's taken me more than an hour a week. For the research article reports, I suggest looking up a pdf summarizer - it's saved me a few times from stressing out over the IV, DV, etc. No exams, just some extra credit quizzes.

Very interesting class/content that was inhibited by the professor. The lectures are long and confusing and many of the tangents seem to have no purpose. The PowerPoints make no sense; they feel like notes for him, not for the student. No one shows up to the class so there is very little discussion. Also the homework is mainly busy work.

While this was an online course, I found Dr. White's lectures to be really engaging! I feel that he breaks down the material in an accessible way, and this is one of the few online classes I found to be really enjoyable. Assignments are pretty simple. So long as you follow the criteria and do the reading, you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul was a great professor! Really funny guy - the class itself was ungodly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is fine, but it's not great. It is really boring and the content doesn't feel helpful at all. There are 12 quizzes and a lot of assignments. You're graded pretty easy on the assignments so that's nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy Class, but can't say the same for the Professor or TA's. Tough Graders and lots of homework and quizzes.

Tons of busy work! 45% of your grade, via 4 "homework" assignments, is in the hands of TA's who will scrutinize your APA formatting regardless of how closely you follow THEIR guide; you don't learn about psych as a prof, you learn how to jump through hoops (this seems meant to force students to participate in research for extra-credit to get an A).

he assigns a ton of homework, most of which is busy work. Uses pop culture references in his quizzes which aren't fair if you are from another country or not into geeky pop culture. Terrible lecturer. He likes to talk about himself and fumbles his way through a scripted lecture.

He takes forever to grade the material or return emails.

I felt like all the material learned in this class was useless and could've easily been explained by an academic advisor in under 30 minutes. The professor is really smart/insightful but the lectures were boring given the material at hand. If you take this course online, you have to meet with the professor in person to talk about your grade.

This is probably my least favorite course I have taken. The online class is very hard to navigate and the grading is quite harsh and takes forever. It's a low level class with an unnecessary amount of work. Nothing I did in this class really felt like it mattered for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Only advice I can give is to work well ahead of the "schedule" that he gives. Due dates are all over the place (quizzes 2 weeks after the fact, assignments don't align with weekly topics). Lengthy lecture videos, often off topic, difficult to follow. Teaches from a, "You must be new to this. I know what you need, so just listen." philosophy.

If your references aren't 100% correctly APA formatted, you'll get docked a whole point. That builds up. Lecture videos are unnecessarily long. To do well on the quizzes, be sure to read the textbook and attached documents in the module (which good luck finding, cause the canvas page is a mess.) Wish I could've taken this class in-person.

This class was made way more difficult than it had to be. The organization was a nightmare and the syllabus/course info was spread out all over the canvas page. Grading was also extreme- full points taken off for minor citation errors. Textbook was a waste of money, all the answers are on quizlet.

I don't understand the reviews on having difficulties with the online PSY 2010, its an easy course with a moderate workload for a low division class. As long as you do the reading and watch the weekly videos you will succeed. One of the easier entry level psych courses I've taken.

This class is unnecessarily hard. Lectures and notes don't help on the exams or quizzes, it seems he just makes up random questions that aren't associated with what he teaches. The multiple choice answers are closely similar. He/ TA's are extremely tough/ unfair graders. My grade keeps taking massive hits and I'm extremely stressed out.

This is an easy class made unnecessarily difficult. Like everyone else is saying, the online class is hard enough to figure out. Very unorganized and it is incredibly difficult to get a hold of him. The grading was very harsh, I would get full points taken off for tiny mistakes in APA format. He isn't really understanding.

This teacher is pretty much a joke. The class itself is pretty easy and straightforward but the teacher is extremely unorganized and uncommunicative. He posts a weekly update that doesn't do much and the Canvas page is impossible to navigate. Couldn't get a hold of him even though he gives out his own personal phone number. Easy class overall tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Online class, so you can pace yourself which is nice but some of the grading can be harsh. Pay extra attention to grading rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff, definitely teaches interesting material. Tests can make or break your grade but is lenient and offered EC often. Tests are open note/book and online at your own time with a time limit so if you take good notes and read the questions well you can get a good grade no hassle.

This class was made so much harder than it should've been by this professor. the TA's were really kind when it came to grading but I had so many assignments and quizzes due at the end of each week that it was ridiculous.

Some of the assignments get wordy for no reason. The instructions can be unclear, and navigating the course was a learning curve itself. Overall, this class was fine and easy to pass. I do agree that most of the assignments are busywork. There was some useful info, though, and I found a professor I want to work on research with through this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The grading criteria isn't clear and the TA's are unnecessarily harsh and can take upwards of a month to grade the homework. Prof seems nice, but you lose points in the most useless areas that ultimately tank your grade. Essentially, this class is made out to be harder than it should be. It should be about content, not arbitrary preferences.

Honestly one of the worst classes I've ever taken. I'm a Psych major, but feel like this class did absolutely nothing in helping me towards my career. The worst part was that the homework was all busy work. There was no point to it at all.

He's caring and engaging as a professor, but fairly disorganized in his lectures. I appreciated how much he listened to student feedback in relation to due dates and grading, but it was frustrating to have 50% of my work not graded by the last week of class. Assignments didn't feel completely relevant to what was being taught in class, either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a caring and lively professor. This course had lots of papers but he was easy about moving moving deadlines when necessary. His lectures are really interesting and he does a great job of creating fun and meaningful interactions with his students. When it comes to assignments, he wants feedback on if students find them worthwhile.

Paul was such a sweet professor, but he was very disorganized and his lectures were oftentimes hard to pay attention to. He is super passionate and knowledgeable, but I was very frustrated with how long it took for him to grade things, and I felt like a lot of his assignments weren't applicable to what was happening in class lectures.

The small assignments can feel like busy work at times, but if you stay on top of them you'll be fine. Tests are very easy with the study guide he provides. His lectures are interesting, and he usually throws in a nerdy reference of two. I could see this class being somewhat overwhelming to a new freshman, but should be a breeze for others.

a lot of stories in the lectures which made them much longer than needed. Exams are easy, do all the practice quizzes a few times and fill out the study guides. Assignments are easy, make sure you get the citation format correct. It may seem like a lot @ first, but every assignment has a FAQ thing so yeah don't stress. good class, easy A

Nice guy. Passionate about psychology and the course content. WAY too much homework. It doesn't matter that it's not all that difficult. The sheer amount of work required is absolutely ridiculous, especially cause it's all busy work. They aren't meaningful assignments. They're his way of a) controlling your participation and b) giving his TA work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Paul White is highly knowledgeable. However, he goes on constant tangents during his lectures so its very difficult to follow them. You have to really read both textbooks. His assignments are a joke so the class is an easy A. If you wanna pass the tests just review the study guide he gives out and youll be fine. Communication isnt his strong suit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. White is a heavy science nerd that's very passionate about what he teaches. He used examples from Star Trek and Star Wars to relate to students and offers extra credit. I personally learned from his online PPTs and practice quizzes. There were 2 tests, some worksheets, but mainly discussion forums where you asked and answered questions.
This professor using tough grader TA who is Kimberley Johnson. so it can be easy to get dock point off.

I have previously taken a class from Dr. White, the psychology as a profession online class. I really liked the online lectures. In person his lectures were still really thought provoking and I learned a lot about diversity. However, his test in this class aren't as straight forward as they were in the other class.

This class is an easy A and waist of time and money. I went to class once and ended with an, and I can tell you this class did not advance my knowledge is psychology whatsoever. The one class I did go to he kept repeating he is, "waiting for the day everclear, rum, and tequila cures all ailments" and then proceeded to talk about taking speed.
Paul is an amazing lecturer, and this class was fascinating. One thing to be aware of is the due dates for discussions, because if you forget them it will strongly effect your grade.

His lectures were sometimes difficult to follow due to him going off on many tangents. The reading material was interesting and the assignments were straight forward. The one thing that I did not care for was the test format. It's the type where there are multiple correct answers, but you have to pick the "most" correct answer.

Dr. White is one of the most amazing professors at the U. Intergroup relations was my second class with him, and it really was a blast. Your grade is based on 10 2-3 page essays, 2 exams, and a final project you write in sections throughout the semester. White is incredibly funny, smart, and caring. The class focuses on prejudice and in-group bias.

This was a very good class to take if you want to know more about the careers within the field of psychology. If you don't want to know about that, it isn't very applicable. You must participate in the discussions to receive a passing grade, but the assignments aren't hard. Prof doesn't grade much until the end of the semester.

Pretty easy class. There are two exams and lots of homework. Dr. White is a very entertaining lecturer, so even though attendance is not at all required he is fun to still come to class for. I'd recommend this class because it's easy, has a good teacher, and it teaches you about psychology in a cool way.

Honestly this class was really easy. He doesn't do attendance so pretty much after the 2 exams, which are early in the semester, its a breeze to pass. He was a good professor, but the subject was kind of boring.

Great class. Several simple straightforward assignments due throughout the semester and two exams. Exams weren't bad as long as you follow along with his lectures. Offers some extra creditdo it early in the semester.

Most of the homework was through canvas and they were all worth 5 points or less. There were only 2 exams and no final. Class was super boring, I stopped showing up after the first exam. All of the power points are online. Honestly, this class is a joke but it's an easy A as long as you do good on the exams and do all the homework assignments.

Dr. White was a great professor, he is extremely knowledgable, and passionate about psychology. He's a nice guy. Show up to class, take notes, and ask question when you need, and you'll pass. He is also really good at replying to emails, and being reachable outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class was alright. For an online class it was pretty easy. I will say that it was pretty difficult to watch his lectures though. He talks very slow and goes off on tangents very often. Be ready to read two different textbooks, but I found them to be pretty interesting. Be aware that your assignments won't be graded until the end of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I found his class very interesting! There's a lot of little assignments you have to do that aren't worth many points, and most of the grading comes from exams.  If you don't go to class his PowerPoints would be really hard to completely understand (he posts them online), but he explains everything well in class with good examples.

I enjoyed Dr. White's lectures.  It was fun to listen to.  I took the Psy 2010 class online and I am an older non-traditional student.  Having lived a little, I enjoyed what I learned and was able to connect with what he was saying.  I enjoy his stories.

Took Dr White's Psy2010 class. Interesting class. Beginning focuses more on psychological research, other half focuses on learning the different fields of Psychology. His quizzes had a lot of star wars references in them. Too many surveys were done in this class, almost one a week. Other than that, he explains everything well in his lectures.

I took this as an online class and I just really don't learn well in online classes. That being said I think this is about as good as online classes get. I took his integrated class and he makes it really easy for you to succeed! I think if it hadn't been online I would have really loved this class, I'm just not a fan of online learning.

This class was really cool! Learning about prejudices and stereotypes and what to do about them was very informative. Paul knows the material well. I didn't like how he taught using PowerPoints. There are only three tests, and they can be hard if you don't study AND understand the notes. The 3 papers and 10 short assignments weren't bad.
Great teacher who has a ton of experience in the research field. He goes off on tangents quite a bit, so if that's your thang, then here ya go.

I was bored out of my mind in this class. Take in mind that I am a psych major, but I absolutely hates the class. It was torture. His tests are confusing because he has so many characters and he just phrases the questions weird. Turn in the assignments on time, you think "oh, it's only 5 points" but it catches up to you. Worst. Psych. Class. Ever.

The most important part about the course was turning in your HW assignments on time. Exams were generally easy, but somewhat confusing due to the characters and people he uses for questions, specifically Star Wars references. I suspect he was at the midnight release of the new movie. Overall a good online class. TA was slow at grading.

I would have enjoyed this class more if it weren't for the exams he gave. All of the questions are the "multiple right answers but choose the best one" type and you basically have to read his mind. He also fills the tests with a lot of characters and details that distract. I kind of had a hard time understanding his grading style as well. Ok class.
he is very confusing, not many things he says make since. he has slides and online videos you can watch though. there are 2 tests in the class and that's it

I took this class online and it was great. He posts the lectures that you can watch but I mostly just read the texts and studied for the tests. The assignments are SUPER easy, just make sure you submit them on time.

Super easy class. First half is basically a review of psychology. Second half is about psych careers, so it's slightly more interesting. Assignments are easy, and there are only two tests. Extra credit is easy to get. DO NOT BUY THE STANOVICH TEXTBOOK. It's totally unnecessary. But make sure to buy the Kuther and Morgan book to do the assignments.

His class is very easy.  I didn't study at all and passed with an A.  This class uses a lot of common sense where you can guess the answers on his tests.  He is interesting to listen to.  He is a great teacher if you are still looking for a career in psychology.  If you already know what you are going to be doing, this class is a bore.
Very easy

REALLY EASY. I took this class online and it was a breeze. I never read the text book unless we had to use them for certain assignments. We had book questions on Mondays and other online assignments due on Thursdays. (5 questions) If you want to do well on the tests, DO THE QUIZZES. I hardly ever watched the lectures because they were so long.

White is an amazing teacher! He makes lectures interesting and always cracks jokes. Only two exams that are multiple choice. There is an assignment due every thursday but there only five questions long. He also gives out extra credit points for participating in research. HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS TEACHER!

This online class was direct and clear-cut. Do the assignments and read the textbook and you should be alright. I found that the lectures were unstimulating, though it was convenient that they were posted online right after they were recorded. Not a difficult professor or class, but you still have to put in some effort.
He responded quickly to emails and was very helpful when I needed to reschedule an exam due to a family emergency.

Interesting guy, boring subject. Psychology as a science and profession was a bore, but I liked Dr. White. He's funny, charismatic, and nerdy but defiantly fun to be in the same room with. Only 2 tests and easy assignments. Use the online quizzes to study for the tests, they're more helpful than the "textbook." Films and puts up all lectures online

I've taken multiple classes from Dr. White. He is one of my favorite professors. His classes are interesting and lighthearted, and he is more than willing to go out of his way to help you. Highly recommended.

Course was easy enough. The majority of your grade is based on homework assignments (about 70%), participating in research (5 hrs mandatory), and two short multiple choice tests. He seems nice enough, but he is not very good at public speaking (awkward), so I stopped watching the lectures about half way through, still got an A.

Great online class. This was my first completely online class and it was helpful. Some of the information was good to help me know more information about psychology jobs/resumes/internship things. Easy to keep up with the workload online. Tests were easy if you read the slides!
Easy class, lots of busy work. Tests were kind of hard, but only worth 10% (each) for your final grade. Didn't do so hot on tests, but still got an a
Very smart man. Knows his stuff. The class wasn't of high interest for me, but it was a fine class. Dr White was very easy to communicate with when I needed to. Easy tests.

Great guy, easy to talk to, very interested and enthusiastic about the material.  Funny guy, sometimes his jokes fall a little flat, but yeah he's funny and entertaining for the most part. I had him for intergroup relations and psy 2010 and enjoyed both classes very much.  Powerpoints and class notes will get you through most exams/quizzes no prob.

Lectures get a little boring, but the guy is hilarious otherwise. If those classes with three make-it-or-break-it tests a semester screw you over, his Attitudes and Persuasion class is a great choice. The class consists of three tests, some papers, and discussion board stuff. Attend class to get details not on the powerpoint slides.
Boring lectures, but good information. Tests are easy if you study even a little. One of those that tries to be funny, but it's just awkward.

Boring class, I don't know if it would've been much better with another teacher. I found myself not listening to hardly any of the lectures but if you read the book you'll get an A anyway like I did. His voice bugged me, but I think that's because he sounds like my bothersome brother. Easy class...but boring.

Great teacher! I took 2010 online and it was very easy. Watch the lectures/go to class, do all assignments (easy but interesting one page writing assignments), memorize the power-points and it will be the easiest A. There is reading, but it pretty much is identical to his lectures. I recommend taking any classes with Dr. White.

Super passionate teacher who does his own research. It does suck when he has guest lectures, but when he is leading the lecture, it is super fascinating. The final project is a group presentation. 1 easy assignment throughout each week (a couple of paragraphs). Attendance is required and accounts for most of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such an interesting and important class! Dr. Anderegg clearly cares so much for this topic and his passion made this class so engaging! Definently recommend this class and any class he teaches!

Professor Anderegg is great he is a great lecturer and has amazing guest lectures that are relevant to the course. However, half of my class was taught by a TA who wasn't great. So depending you may get a bad TA teaching half. Tests are open note so take good notes and the class is super easy. If it was just Anderegg it would have been a favorite.

Watching Prof. Anderegg's lectures made me genuinely so happy. He starts each one by saying, "hello" in the warmest, sweetest way that automatically puts me in a much better mood. He is also incredibly intelligent, humble, down-to-earth, and passionate. Even though his courses' materials may be complicated, he explains them very thoroughly.

This course was basically online with lectures posted to canvas weekly. Exams are open note as well. The group project itself was super cool, but the group I was assigned to didn't do their work which was frustrating. Other than that, I loved this class. Very sad, but super interesting. The professor is amazing and I def recommend him :)

Professor Anderegg is amazing! This class was more of an online-type class with pre-recorded lectures and 1 weekly assignment but it was super straight forward. All the mini-exams and the final are open note. Loved the topics we covered and how Anderegg would have us relate it to things we're most passionate about.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The worst part of the class was the quizzes, which were very difficult and sometimes very specific. He was accessible outside of class for general questions, but regarding test questions, it is what it is, can't argue points. The other assignments were fairly easy. There's a group project, some are more work than others. Sad but interesting class.

First, let me stress one thing. His exams are all open note, but you NEED to pay attention in lecture and study hard before the exam or YOU WILL NOT PASS. If you do those things, pretty much everything will push you towards an A. The only other work was the CEL project, but that is not terribly hard and you get to pick what you do for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was a very interesting and sad class, Dr. Anderegg was a really cool professor, the class only has one assignment which is research paper so there is a lot of pressure to do good, and 3 tests, though they are open note and online don't let that fool you they are VERY hard!

I thought this class was a nice break from honors cell bio and ochem this semester. The lectures were engaging and I learned a lot. Going to class for me was enough to absorb the material with minimal studying before exams. There was some time involved with the CEL project but I thought it was worth it. To me, this was a great elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: super tough grader. made an easy class difficult and so boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking this class. You have to rely on 1-2 point surveys for you to keep your grade up, she doesn't offer extra credit, and she will ignore your emails regarding your concerns and questions. Nor she will make any kind of exceptions regardless of how hard you try.
This was definitely the hardest class I've taken in college yet. The majority of your grade is based on 3 exams that are impossible to get a good score on.

I think this class was awesome! I loved that the lecture videos were easy to follow, they are a bit time-consuming. There isn't much homework other than a weekly survey due to make sure you paid attention to the lectures. The tests are easy if you are on top of your readings and lectures! Great class and she gives back good feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Perfect example of "having a college degree doesn't make you smart." She did not create any contents of the class; another professor made the lectures, assignments, etc. There were assignments worth 1 point that she would not let anyone turn in even a minute late. She was smug. You can get away without buying the 3 books required. Multiple papers.

Wolfe taught with another professor during the fall2016 semester. The other prof had complete control over the lectures which were often long and tedious. We did eventually receive access to edited lecture slides. Most of my classes have been online and this was the top for time spent. To do well you need to stay on top of the reading and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Allison refuses to put up lecture slides from an online course and calls it "on purpose" because she doesn't want us to be able to just take notes on slides. She claims a preferred learning style "watching lecture videos" and expects students in an online class to conform and accommodate to her lecture videos, which are an hour long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She doesn't show you what your grade in the class is until the very end of the semester. For me, that's hard because if I miss an assignment or do poorly on a test, I would like to know what I need to get to make sure I will pass the class. Even on Canvas where you can input X% on any assignment it would calculate what your end grade will be.

Worst class I have ever taken. Constant busy work that if you do not do perfectly, you will receive a terrible grade. Doesnt explain the expectations clearly, especially for the first assignment, so practically everyone failed. My friend received a better grade for practically the same work and there was no explanation given for the docked points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class in my last semester of college thinking that a 2000-level course would be a walk in the park to round out my college career. Wrong. This class was the most intense of all of my courses this semester. There was more work required for this class than almost any other class I have taken. Avoid if you want an easy class you can ignore

Only take it if you have to, it is not the worst class by any means but, this has to be one of the hardest graders Prof. EVER. If you don't follow what she says perfectly, and it's usually kinda vague, then good luck. So much HW, that mostly feels like busy work...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Wright is a great teacher. Her assignments weren't too hard but for the discussion posts you did have to read from the textbook and watch the weekly lecture video. Overall if you participate in class you can get an easy A.
Does not care about her students.

This class is too much work for an online class. Weekly zoom lectures, additional lecture we need to watch on our own, 2 different textbooks with heavy reading every week, and supplemental videos. They must have forgotten about all other online classes due to the pandemic. Bridges Eatchel is a prof included in this. Both nice but too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor, knows the subject and has a lot of experience in the field. Grades notes from reading (you can opt to do a project and write an essay instead). Attendance is graded. Tests are basically memorization and regurgitation of the book and lectures. Every little thing on the study guide is on the test, and vice versa.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst Instructor I've had! She gives little to no feedback to let you know how to better your next assignment. Grades so tough I could have almost done no work to get the grade she gave me after turning in an article I wrote. I honestly don't get her grading system. Avoid taking her class!!!!
She is a wonderful woman and professor. Great class. She will teach you a lot about life and society.
Awesome teacher! Awesome class! You learn a lot but it's not difficult and she is an amazing instructor.
Claudia is an AMAZING teacher.  Her Gender Studies class (gender and contemplative issues) was one of the best classes I've ever had.  I highly recommend that class.
I was not aware what my grade was going to be until a day before grades were due, and professor was not super helpful with assignments and directions were pretty unclear.

Since the first day of class, I realized that this could be the most interesting and impactful college course of my life. Great jokes, great storytelling, and a great attitude. The professor adapted the course material to cater to what we cared about.

If you only need one reason, this class is worth taking just to spend time with Rob. He's a truly unique and genuine person. Apart from that - challenges norms and explores commonly conceived notions.
Rob's class is not one to miss. His lectures are condensed in time, but just as valuable. Don't pass on the optional dinner discussions afterward!
He's obviously really into the subject. Loved the lack of work and listening to the speakers.
He's hilarious, lectures are engaging. Also...he's not bad looking

I took this class as an intensive american institution over fall break and Professor Wright made this class totally worth it. His lectures and activities are interesting and the assignments and final exam were clear and not too hard to complete.
He was entertaining, and the lectures were great and easy to follow.

Honestly, I stopped attending class halfway through the semester, not because of Seth but because I don't like mornings. Every class I attended was very informational and had a chill atmosphere. Seth is kind and incredibly helpful. I highly recommend attending class but if you can't, if you are willing to put in the work, you're grade will be fine.

I have never left a review for a prof before, but I have to for Seth because he is PHENOMENAL. Such an engaging lecturer and truly so caring - if you have the opportunity to take a class from Seth, you definitely should. I loved my POLS 1100 intensive experience because of him!
I loved being in this class! I was not interested in politics but he made everything so easy and fun! He always knows how to cheer you up and he also speaks Spanish!
Professor Wright must be the best professor at the U!
Amazing professor. Super kind and actually wants you to succeed. Tests are also open book and open notes.

Outstanding teacher! Merciful with late work and cares a lot about students and current situations. He is also very open to hear students' opinions on certain subjects during class and is open for disagreement. He shows great character and integrity and teaches and display very interesting subjects and topics through his lectures.

This professor is a merciful grader. For the weekly discussion posts, write 100-200 words with respect and good points, then you get full mark. The quizzes can all be found on textbook, or ONLINE. His exams are also not hard. EASY A and ideal for general education requirement!

Super easy class but loved the information I learned. Seth cares about his students and is extremely gracious. The requirements for the class were clear and the workload was very minimal. Would 100% recommend taking this for a gen ed.

An intensive Fall break course so it was naturally long and lecture heavy, but Seth is extremely caring and helpful. He gives you everything you need to succeed in his class and understands the mental battle that intensive courses bring. The last 3 hours of class are reserved for a quiz that only takes 20 minutes so you can usually leave early.
Good lecturer, super funny, and enjoyable. Weekly quizzes and discussion boards but that's pretty much all of the content in the class. Quizzes and final test/midterm online and open note/open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seth is the best professor I have ever had! His lectures are engaging and he genuinely cares about the success of his students. I wish every class was taught by Seth.

An amazing teacher with an amazing and invincible attitude. Seth is literally the guy from the "he is the most interesting man in the universe" commercials. He's the kinda guy you'd wanna have Brunch with. Truly a wonderful teacher and I hope he enjoys today's Bang! (Im genuinely surprised he's not already Sponsored by Bang, Because he should be)
He is a very lovable and caring guy. Genuinely brings up your mood and is very understanding. He is passionate about what he teaches and wants you to understand what you are being taught.
love him

Seth is amazing and always caring for each of his students. He's very approachable and I know if I had any issues, I could talk to him. Classes mostly consist of lectures; however, he encourages discussions. You don't need the textbook to do well in the class.
Very easy class and a wonderful professor. I could've passed the class without going to the lectures. Easy assignments yet and engaging class if you want to discuss politics!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really liked professor Wright! He was always so helpful and caring to what each student needs while also making sure all material is covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've ever had. Cares for each of his students, extremely respectful, and above everything else wants you to do well.

Dr. Seth R. Wright is perhaps the best Professor I have had during my first two years at the U. He truly cares about his students and does anything he possibly can to help them. Take a class from him! I promise that it will be worth it!

Seth Wright is an excellent professor. He is unbelievably accommodating and you can really tell that he truly cares about the well-being of each of his students. I highly recommend him. He is a great professor, lecture-wise, and really exceeded my expectations as a student. 10/10 would recommend.
Makes lectures interesting and very willing to work with you and help you out. I've recommended him to many of my friends and wish I could have more professors like him.

His lectures are simple and easy to follow along. Quizzes and midterms are online. Chapter reading is pretty easy. Always has interesting stories that tie into the lecture. Overall a really good class!

He has been the best professor I've have thus far, he is very caring and will make an effort to get to know you, he preps you well for exams and quizzes, he only really assigns a discussion and a quiz every week, and a chapter reading that it usually pretty interesting. He is an outstanding teacher.

Seth is a great teacher. He is enthusiastic about the subject material, and he cares about his students. I went through some medical problems while taking his class, and he was very accommodating. He makes sure his students understand what he requires and prepares them well for the exams.

Seth is a really good guy and I loved being in his class. I took the intensive session where the entire course lasted a week. He did a great job making sure we weren't overloaded with work because of the amount of time we had to spend in class every day that week.

Professor Wright is a good guy. His class wasn't crazy difficult, which is appreciated because of covid, and he constantly reaches out to make sure that you're getting the attention you need. 10/10 would recommend.

Seth is one of the best professors I've ever had in the U. He puts a lot of effort into teaching. He is so enthusiastic and inspiring. His lecture is informative and interesting. He cares about students and always provides great feedback. He makes me love American Government!

I had Wu for an AP calc 1 review course. I could definitely tell he didn't care about this class as much as his others. He frequently came completely unprepared to lectures and didn't show up to his office hours. He wasn't very helpful when we had questions and was often disrespectful to students who asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Wu is a very nice guy, and a decent lecturer. He makes sure to go over plenty of solid example problems during class, and gives you what you need to work with. However, he is sometimes difficult to understand in his explanations. He is super nice and willing to answer questions and explain until you get it though!

Prof. Wu was a good professor to have, his lectures weren't too difficult to follow, but occasionally, he would make a small error that would be soon corrected by an observant student. The course was 85% based on exams, so be prepared to know the content for those exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher. You have to watch the board closely while he does his examples, as he will sometimes say the wrong word while writing the correct thing, or vice versa. He is very willing to answer questions throughout the class. Don't buy the textbook until after the first week, there was an online version for my class.

Best Calc II professor. Grades very leniently. Is willing to explain things in greater detail when students have questions. Only one homework assignment a week (not more than 2 hours to finish) and tests are only 5 questions or so, and are generally easier than homework questions. Was hard to understand his accent at first but I got used to it.

Nice teacher and an easy on you grader. Would not have made it through with an other professor. He can be difficult to understand at times but his English is good enough. Will respond to emails fairly quickly and willing to help if you need it. Overall I would recommend this teacher to any student at the U.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is a good guy and will make accommodations for you if you ask. He trusts that his students are intelligent enough to make up for their own mistakes and dose not punish you to hard if you have a bad exam. I failed 1 of my test and still made it out okay. He is a merciful grader and wants you to do well. His English isn't bad either.

I was skeptical to take Prob & Stat Inference online because of all the bad reviews. I am glad that I did. This was one of the easiest classes I have taken in college! Buy the book, and teach yourself. Her lectures were confusing and not helpful. Weekly homework, and 3 midterms. I took AP Stats in high school, and this was easier than that.
This is not a easy class, but she made it easy. Its hard to get an A in this class. She gaves efforts and extra credit which is easy to pass this class. I would like to take class from her again.

Taking an online class from her was terrible. Her English is incredibly poor; her teaching nonexistent. Her "teaching" involved uploading a 240p shaky video of the homework problems that you couldn't even see the #s. Made me question why I paid so much for tuition. Only plus is she doesn't have a ton of assigned HW throughout the course.

Wu moves very quick, as others have mentioned, so be prepared to dedicate extra time to the material if you are uncertain during class. I had a hard time following the lectures, but Professor Wu was always quick to respond to questions and was very accessible to meet with outside of class. Overall, her courses demand time and dedication.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: following  the class and review, you will pass the homework and exam easily. take home final will be little bit hard, but it's ok.

Sophie is probably the hardest professor I have ever had while attending the University of Utah. It is hard to understand what she is talking about and she moves very quickly through the material just assuming that you know what is going on. This makes things more difficult when you are studying something like statistics. Skip on this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: the worst teacher ever. 3 tests. This would be fine if there was any material to help you. No feedback. Gah!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Non-coherent feedback from the professor on assignments and tests. There are assignments each week that are worth 0 points. Your entire grade is determined by three tests, with no options for extra credit. Lecture/reading heavy, be sure you have plenty of time set aside. Be prepared for a lot of calculus, and to teach yourself the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This teacher doesn't actually teach. As others have said she posts other lectures and grades are only determined by tests not the assignments you actually do. Her comments and instructions aren't in complete sentences and good luck deciphering what she actually wants you to do. Feedback from this teacher is a joke. Don't waste your time or money.

Sophie is probably the WORST professor of all time. She puts NO effort in any of her lectures. She literally posts youtube videos from other professors as her "lecture" and your entire grade is based on 3 tests. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!! She provides examples of test questions but even then docks you points for doing exactly what she showed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took her online for Intermediate Microeconomics. By far the hardest teacher ever. Unless youre amazing in Calculus, don't take her. It's basically just taking calculus for the second time with little to no economic concepts. AWFUL.
This was the worst professor I've ever taken a class from. Unclear and quite frankly useless when it came to explaining microeconomic concepts.

Great person overall and funny, but the class takes up a lot of your time to do the reading. Does occasional pop quizzes, but they're super easy if you've been paying attention. Exams were harder than I thought and even had questions on geography and dates, the writing portion was easier. The lectures were very boring most of the time but bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Wynne is very kind and has a super likable demeanor. His lectures tended to be a bit dry for my taste, focused a little too much on history rather than the exciting content of the myths. Still, it was an interesting course that didn't require too much work or effort. Study for the exams, though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher. he is very passionate about what he teaches. Expect to do a lot of textbook reading in this class. The quizzes are easy since he gives you the answers beforehand. you just need to read the multiple books to be able to understand the questions and answers.  He creates good study guides for the modules and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: John Wynne is a good professor who does his best to keep students engage. I feel like this class was incredibly easy with one reading quiz a week being the only thing required other than a midterm and a final. I struggled with his lateness, he was upward of 15-20 minutes late to almost every other lecture. It was very frustrating
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor and good lectures. He's pretty funny and he's very interested in the subject which is nice. Tests weren't super hard but it did weight a lot in the grades which kinda sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Wynne is a great teacher with a clear passion for his subject.

Prof. Wynne is a funny guy and very passionate about the subject. This class was taken online and included some heavy readings + quiz due mid week and 2 lecture videos + a discussion due by Sunday. Lectures averaged an hour each and he speaks fast so 2x speed is not always an option. Interesting subject though!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Does really well in a small class setting. He is really helpful in teaching you small tricks to help you remember grammar. My Greek language skills greatly improved.

Professor Wynne was amazing! He made lectures both informative and fun and was clear about what would and wouldn't be on finals. He uploads his study guides online with all the information that will be on the finals. He made topics such as Roman history relevant to 21st century America. Overall a great guy and fantastic teacher.
Professor is very good grader. He is lenient. However, the lectures do tend to get slightly boring. I would recommend they be maximum 30 minutes so that our attention does not divert.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Wyeth is an easy guy to work with. He gives good feedback and doesn't give too much work in my opinion. He certainly helped me become a better writer and was happy to do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wyeth was a good prof, but the lectures were often unnecessarily long and boring. The assignments are easy, but there are quizzes on the readings so be sure to at least skim them. He is a really nice guy and clearly into writing, but I found the class a little boring for my taste.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He didn't care, at all. It seemed like he was just talking about the class topics at the top of his head. His tests didn't reflect much, it reflected on the reading but since we had different versions of the same book, he didn't update the syllabus for the page number information. Tests were hard in terms of he didn't cover it.

The class is entirely graded upon 3 papers each worth a third of your grade with a little participation. Lectures were long and quite often unclear. When clarity was asked for the answer was often more confusing than before. I would only recommend this class to Philosophy students and those with a high interest in it. Do not take for a general ed.
Provides good structure and the opportunities to do well

You have to write a short essay every week and contribute to class discussion. I didn't find the files on weekly lecture notes until after midterms.. they helped so much! The exam questions are taken right from them and I would've done so much better if I read them sooner (you could even pass weekly readings because of how detailed they are)

Wyckoff is by far the most boring professor on this campus.  He just paces and flings his arms around.  He lectures more like he's talking to himself rather than the class.  It was a 50 minute class of him talking to himself and everyone else trying to stay awake...

BORIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIING! 1- walks back and forth, back and forth, back and forth....... 2- Think he likes the sound of his own voice 3- Have to interrupt to ask questions or answer questions he poses because he won't stop to call on you or actually wait to hear your thoughts 4- Read & write a paper (alot) and nothing is real life applicable

This class is easy, but you might wonder if J. Wyckoff is the world record holder for having the most boring lectures. He reads his slides word for word and adds a bit of commentary. There is no discussion. The class grades are exactly 3 papers about 8 pgs each and 2 participation grades for each semester. Easy, boring, but fulfills a requirement.
Great professor who cares about his students. His theatre classes will definitely get you out of your comfort zone, but his class was so much fun. He can be a kooky guy, but in the best way.

Took the acting for non-majors and Xan was by far the best professor i've ever had. Honestly a good dude and cares about his students. In the class you mostly do acting and alot of scenes require two people or more. Ate lunch with him and the rest of my class. 10/10 would act again.
A lot of time-consuming busy work and I wouldn't recommend it if you're just trying to get credit. Nice teacher but expects too much for 1013, non major-specific class.

I honestly loved professor Xan! I'm not a theatre major but really enjoyed his class! It was an online class; definitely wish it was an in-person class. I'm sure it would have been an amazing class. Going to miss reading his emails/ messages/ feedbacks

Course work was pretty easy as long as you watch the assigned movie or play, however they were very time consuming. A lot of the times the instructions for assignments were not well defined so I would always have to ask him and in the instructions he would include details that were not necessary. Didn't really learn much from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Xan was absolutely amazing! I am so sad that we got put online for the second half of the semester. Going to his theater classes was one of my favorite parts of school this semester. He is so funny and easy-going and absolutely loves his craft and his students. Amazing teacher! No matter your major, you need to take this class!

I took an online theatre course to get done with one of my credits. However, he taught some really cool things in the course! The assignments were easy, but sometimes tedious. One of the easiest, but also coolest classes I've taken!
Fantastic class. Felt more like fun than a burden (most of the time)
I loved this class! Xan's a great teacher and very laid back. Assignments include 3 play reviews, and a monologue and scene performance. If you like acting, take this class!

Xan just LOVES his subject!  I've always thought theatre people were weird and quirky, but Xan is normal, you wouldn't suspect he's a theatre guy.  FUNNEST CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN!!! You will LOVE coming to class!!  And because he has a PhD in psychology he really helped me emotionally act and connect with the audience rather than just physically act
Great teacher!! made the class really interesting and it was my favorite class. He helps teaching you acting skills and if you just want it for a fine arts credit, you will love it! great teacher.
Okay teacher
Teacher is a great guy. I've never taken a theater class, but I think I might take more because of what he taught me. If you have a chance, take a class with him, you won't regret it

Theatre was my major at a previous University, I had that dream destroyed by a teacher. Xan Johnson fixed my broken dream he is an amazing man and teacher who has a way to rekindle excitement and sculpt you as a student as well as inspire change in you as a person. We had tons of engaging intellectual lectures- we can miss 3 days but no one wanted
Great professor!  You just have to go to class and keep up but the work is not hard.  Easy fine arts credit!

Xan is a great professor, he makes class exciting and reasonable. Attendance is necessary (which I learned the hard way) He takes the time to get to know the students on a personal level, adjusting to different learning styles and allowing you breathing room. Great professor TAKE HIS CLASS!

Xan is a great professor, as long as you show up for class and do the assignments you will pass. He allows you to rewrite papers for better grades also which is nice. You are required to watch several plays and write reviews but they are clearly outlined and almost a no-brainer. He's fun, I reccomend taking his class.
Very casual and understanding--has psych degree and will give great advice.  I learned how to juggle and relax.  I've never missed a Pioneer play since.  Watch out--he sometimes doesn't wear shoes.
Seems to be under the impression that he owns the place.  Lashes out when feeling threatened.

Xuesong Bai is one of the best math teachers I've had. When he's teaching, he thinks like a student to answer your questions before they come up. His practice exams directly reflect the exam. He teaches at a weird time but it's worth it if you want an A.

His name is actually Xuesong Bai, not "Bia". He was very funny and quirky, and was quite approachable. A very nice guy, but not good at teaching. Less and less people showed up each class, which is a reflection of how effective his lectures were. The tests directly reflected the study guides and were relatively straightforward.
Maverick is a great guy and clearly cares a lot about his students! His tests are very easy and reflective of the study guides. Ill miss him and his Love Live anime girl face masks.

Maverick is one of the best. Once you get to understand his teaching style, the lessons make a lot more sense. He always explains why certain equations work. 10 homework problems a week. 3 midterms, questions were easier than homework and lab questions. He really cares about us, asks if we have questions, and is overall a super sweet teacher.

I took this class during COVID. He posted lecture videos instead of doing online lectures, so you can do them at your own pace a rewind. It wasn't convenient for asking questions, but you will get a lab section with a TA. He responded to all my emails, and is kind about grading. I learned easily in his class. Frequent but not overwhelming homework
Great professor. The course required a lot of independent effort to stay on track. I still learned useful material, but the class would have benefited from an in-person option.
Yasi will change your life. I learned so much from this course and Yasi's heart-centered place-based approach blew me out of the water!
Lectures are well organized and insightful

Professor Yasi has been one of the best instructors I have ever had. The course content was interesting and up to date and the projects and assignments were enjoyable.There was a lot of good readings and videos sometimes I couldn't get to all of them so I didn't read everything in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I recommend Yasi to anyone looking for a professor who genuinely cares about their student's well-being and learning.

I do not recommend this instructor, I learned nothing from her class, the quizzes were middle school difficulty, I didn't even have to read the material, just guessed everything or looked at the documents really quickly. Online class but zero student engagement. If you are interested in the topics, just google them don't waste your money and time.

Look elsewhere if you are trying to fulfill your diversity credit. Weekly homework included four 20-70 page readings a week along with 1-2 videos/movies. Readings were often dense and required substantial unpacking, but discussion is always student led and professor failed to add anything substantial to the discussion. Very politically opinionated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework
