reviews.comment: Class organization is a mess. During any given hour and a half class period, almost no presentation form Professer Shaker happens. Instead, the job of teaching is offloaded to students during class discussions, which leaves actual class concepts vague and lacking.
Lots of reading which is such a pain, cool material though. Tests were easy along with essays and the final. Good for a GE and was easy to manage.

Very enjoyable course and professor! Yasi obviously cares about her students and the content she uses. She makes this class enjoyable and interesting and also up to date! Would recommend Professor Yasi to anyone.

I took an online class and some final and important assignments did not have the most clear instructions and didn't have the correct due dates. However, she is flexible and responds to emails quickly. There are not many assignments in this course, but there is are pretty long final projects that take a lot of time.
Professor Yasi is so knowledgeable and intentional. She connect course with current events too

10/10 class and professor. It is such an interesting class and I am very happy I took it. There are no exams just lots of discussions but the best part is that the main focus of the discussions is sharing opinions with each other and learning new things. Definitely recommend this course with Jeff.

This class is amazing! Professor Yancey does a wonderful job helping you through tough topics. There is a lot of writing in this class, but it is more like journaling and the topics covered are really interesting. You earn a lot of points throughout the semester, no exams of quizzes, so it's easy to get a good grade if you complete the work.

This class is laid out through 6 modules. Each one has a 500 word paper, a current even discussion posts, and then 5 discussion posts (each being about a short lesson). If you turn it in and comment, you get 100%. It seems like a lot of writing but its almost like journaling. Dr. Yancey was so helpful. He takes late work and communicates well.

Lectures are hard to follow and often feel disorganized, which makes it tough to stay confident in the material. Students frequently have to clarify things during class. Weekly quizzes and no exam flexibility add pressure. New material right after exams is frustrating and overwhelming.

Teaches the class so fast that you can't write down any important information if you didn't print out the lecture slides the day before. Tough grader on tests, and many individuals in the class failed tests because he didn't disclose that we could only use a four-function calculator and not a graphing calculator.

Doesn't know how to teach a class. Asks bland questions, goes on his own pace and keeps going to the bell no matter where we are as a class. Not a single person speaks in here, no room for makeup work and if you miss it, you miss it.
Terrible, do not take this course with Sage

Poor instructor, doesn't know how to teach a math class. Little opportunity for help outside of class, no resources provided. Instructions are always unclear, grades hard. 0 opportunity to makeup assignments regardless of circumstances.

She remembered everyone's name and was kind. She took time to answer your questions, however the material was very hard and I passed the class due to help from other students. She teaches very quick and the material hardly ever made sense. Tough grader. She was helpful but didn't always have the best explanations in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 10/10 do not recommend she is very judgmental and in my opinion is mean spirited. Does not teach well and just babbles on.

Sara Yeo is a nice person and I have 0 personal issues with her. However, she doesn't structure her class in a way that's accessible to most students. The lectures are far too long, way too much information, and she doesn't post them later. Also, Liz, the TA I had, doesn't explain things in class and has a bad attitude. Overall, not a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I just want to say all the comments down below and true and I am so glad this semester is over so I don't have to come to this class anymore!!!!

This class is not one of those classes that are hard because the teacher makes you work for your grade. It is hard because the teacher does not know how to teach and this information is new. The second you walk in she expects you to know everything about QR and makes you hate it by the end of the semester.

This teacher could care less about her students. If it were possible to kick teachers out she would definitely be out. She talks 100 mph and puts questions on the test that she did not even talk about in class. The TA is only there for her own good. goes through the information fast and grades hard if you do not understand her bad teaching!

Everyone has that one really bad class they take in college. This was the class for me. I highly recommend not taking it if you are not required. I did not learn anything. The TA was hard to understand and very annoying. We all worked together on homework and the TA gave everyone completely different scores. This class is a disaster!!!!!!!!!

This has been hands down the hardest class I've taken at the U and not because of the content. The teaching is awful and Professor Yeo goes out of her way to make the class harder than it needs to be. She says it's against policy to post the slides and she instructs TAs to rip up your quizzes if you need to leave lab early. It's unnecessarily hard.

If you are not a Strat Comm major I highly recommend not taking this class. Good luck to those who are taking it as a requirement. This class is by far the worst class I took in college. The teacher and TA were a nightmare to work with. Both were very hard to understand and demeaning!!
By far the WORST professor I have had in college!!!

If you can take this class from another teacher and do not get Lianne as your TA!! They are both hard to work with. I wish this class was not apart of the Comm major. I got nothing but a big headache out of it!

I have worked in research and taken a stats class. This class does not relate and the teacher is not good! Her and her TA struggled explaining SPSS. They do the minimum needed to help their students out. I was very disappointed to see that the TA I had will be teaching next semester.

I went to every class and lab. When it came to the quizzes and tests I felt like I had not been to a class at all. She is hard to understand and assumes students already know a lot about this topic. If you ask for help you will not get the help needed. The TA and Teacher make the students feel dumb.
I would read out of the book to get what you want out of the class and quizzes. Professor Yeo is the worst professor I have had in college and this has been the worst class.

This class was not hard because of the workload. It was hard to understand the teacher, her TA and the steps needed for each assignment. This is a hard topic and something I would love to learn but disappointed in the teachers and TA I had this semester. They were unclear when explaining data and made students look dumb.

She is not easy to understand. This is a hard topic and she could careless about her students. I really think she finds joy in watching students fail in this class and in life. She is the mist unhelpful teacher I have ever had. Her TAs are just as bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is THE WORST class I have ever taken in college. Professor Yeo is so clueless. She goes through powerpoint way too fast, is not accessible or willing to meet and just plain old does not know how to teach. Information on the tests are not talked about in class or in the book. Very frustrating class and even more frustrating teacher!

I put more time into this class than my other classes and got the least out of it. This teacher could do research but is very bad at explaining it. Her lectures are very boring. She moves very fast, so be prepared to take pictures of the slides. She is a very robotic and carless teacher.
She is by far the worst teacher I have had in college! Be prepared to teach your self from the book! The TA Lianne is just as bad at explaining information.

Very uncaring!!!! Your tipical (bad) college teacher that could care less and goes through the slides as fast as she can. A lot of students retake her class and get nothing out of her class. Highly recommend not taking a class from her!!

Did not understand or learn a lot from lecture and lecture slides were not posted online. Not very helpful in explaining concepts at all. Only the TA was helpful. One of the worst communication classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a good professor and knows what she's talking about, the class itself is just a lot of work. The exams are intense even though they're online. You work on a research project with a group throughout the semester. If you have to take this class, I would take it from Yeo. If you don't have to take this class, don't take this class.

She seems like a nice person, but her lectures are boring. Everything she talks about comes straight out of the textbook, and it's actually a lot easier to understand everything if you just read the textbook. Only reason to go to class is to take pictures of the images on her slides, she uses them in the quizzes. The group project was a nightmare.

This class is info heavy so taking notes & putting in time with the text is important to doing well. The labs with this course are better than learning everything in lecture. The group project was challenging as you get thrown into it but you're not expected to get it all right and the mistakes make great lessons. Also Sara is funny sometimes.

Before I took this class, I heard tough things about Professor Yeo. While taking her class I realized that all of the build up was for nothing. Sara was nice to listen to while lecturing, she was loud for everyone to hear, and she didn't overwork the brain.

Sara seems like a nice person, but that only gets you so far. Get ready to take notes! No notes, tables or figures are ever posted online from lecture so if you miss class you're in trouble. She does not expand on anything and is brutally unclear when it comes to assignments. Group projectsnightmare. You will be confused if you take this from her.

Jokes not allowed. Worst class I've ever taken in my entire college career. Ask her a questions about what she's teaching and she says "hm, I'm not sure." And gives a terrible explanation. She's everything that's wrong with the education system. Not trying to teach you anything. Doesn't care about students.
Sara was a joke as a professor. If she put half the effort into teaching her classes as she did into picking her outfits then maybe her classes would be half decent.

She is very helpful if you come to her with questions. The weekly quizzes that she gave were very easy, you just had to skim the chapter to pass them. The midterm came unexpectedly to most as it was excruciatingly difficult compared to the quizzes. Make sure to put good work in on your assignments as she doesn't hold back when grading.
Worst professor I've had yet

She is super nice. New to teaching. She has text-book knowledge of data analysis but has not worked in same field that her students will. When lectures are difficult, she struggles to explain using simple terms or examples. Instead, often deflects requests, "You'll understand later in the semester when we do it." Then she quizzes you before you do.

Not sure where she got her teaching degree but she does NOT know how to teach. Intro to Quantitative Research really isn't a hard class since I've sat in on it for no credit and now taking it for credit through her and you would think she's teaching in a different language. Not helpful what so ever. Went to her office hours and she's no help.

Overall a pretty chill class: 3 papers and 3 tests. I got 100% on all the papers and averaged around a 93% for the tests. The online lectures were all very short but there is a good bit of reading. The tests sometimes had some random questions that you had to do the readings to know. He was also completely MIA for the first half of the semester.

Prof. Yavuz is one of my favorite professors. He is very knowledgeable and open to discussions, and his lectures were always really interesting. There were two midterm papers and a final paper, and if you listened in class, you can easily get an A. He takes into account your attendance (whether or not you're a "tourist").

I took POLS 2200. The professor was great, but the TA was awful. They submitted our final grades without ever grading our final or quizzes. A few things they said we'd be graded on were never actually graded. You must come to class as he only lectures and writes on the board. The professor was knowledgeable and a pretty funny guy.

I took POLS 2200 Comparative Politics. He is a great professor, when I went to his office hours he was very fun to talk to. HOWEVER, HIS TA WAS EVIL. My Final was never graded, and she never put the quizzes we took in Canvas, despite grading and handing them back to us.

I took POLS 2200, and thought this class was great! If you can get over his at least once a lecture comments about his dislike for Trump, then this class is interesting. There were very few assignments, but they were easy. The midterm and the final were just written papers that you did at home. Overall, I would recommend taking this course.

Do take his class. I am pretty sure Yavuz is a genius. He just won a superior teaching award and now I get why. Take freestyle notes, I find it easier to stay engaged with his lecture style when I am processing on paper.

Professor Yavuz is very knowledgeable about the topics he's talking about, although he does have what one classmate called "interesting takes." Very off the cuff and has an eccentric sense of humor, but the coursework is easy to understand and he's a generous grader.

Honestly one of my most favorite professors I have ever had. Hakan is so understanding and nice. All you need to do is show up to class and turn in your assignments. He talks most of class but I have learned so much from him and really enjoyed his class. He is not a tough grader, you just have to show up to class and turn in homework.

Incredible professor. Takes the time to explain any and every question you have. A lot of lecture, but as long as you are willing to do your own research and use the textbooks, you will be totally fine to miss lectures. The guest speakers that were scheduled we amazing.

I took his class for MID political science and he did a great job giving out the lecture, was  caring and willing to work with students if assignment was missed. His Test and Quiz's were so easy he gives you the rubric on what to expect. The class presenters were also nice to listen to.

I took both POLS 3440 and POLS 4400 at the same time, both of which he teaches. Both classes were very interesting, though his lectures can be a bit difficult to follow and he's very old-school (print out essays to turn in, barren Canvas page, etc.). As long as you write everything down, though, you'll be fine.
Yavuz distorts historical facts and presents his interpretations as facts. Be very careful if you take his class.
Avoid for all costs! Save yourself money and time. I also researched that he supports Gulen movement. He is a religious clerk. I recommend to avoid for all costs.

I honestly don't understand why he has a low rating.... The class was interesting, although a bit disjointed. His lectures were short, and to the point, and very few items to be graded on. This is my second class with him and I have gotten A's without much effort on my part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class on comp pol of the middle east didn't involve much empirical political science literature, just tons of history and theories explained as fact. If I wanted a history class, I'd have signed up for one. grades in my class were very high. Lectures are repetitive and often wander. Hard to take notes. Scheduled some good guest speakers though.
Often what he teaches is factually false. I would not recommend taking a political science class from a professor who distorts the historical record.
He is very disorganized. He takes forever to grade papers. His lectures are super boring. Do not recommend at all.

Don't listen to the hate Professor Yavuz gets. He knows more about the Middle East than perhaps anyone at the U. There were only 5 assignments the entire semester (a book report, a research paper, and 3 exams), but if you did the readings and paid attention, these were a breeze. I didn't even attend class 90% of the semester, and I got an A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Yavuz presents the Turkish perspective very well but he is not knowledgeable about other perspectives so you end up getting a one-sided understanding of international relations in the Middle East.
He gives false accounts of historical events so you have to be on guard and double-check what he says in class.
The absolute worst professor I've had! Avoid him like the plague!!

reviews.comment: He makes his lessons so difficult and it is very hard for me . I'm hard working student and this class is for my credit and I really dont want to mess it, but he makes it impossible. We are suffering. Please help students like me.

reviews.comment: lectures are very boring and dull, goes on tangents and rambles about content that wont be on the test, a lot of time content he talks about is factually false. Very harsh test grader, takes points off for minuscule things. If you want to learn, avoid taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Yavuz is extremely knowledgeable in the nuances of political science and international relations in the Middle East. I recommend this class to anyone who is interested in these topics. Thanks, Professor Yavuz!

The most excellent professor in the department of political science. Arguably the best professor at the entire University. The University should consider themselves very lucky to have an excellent professor like him.

This professor was not helpful at all. Doesn't use Canvas, doesn't have study guides, and his lectures are him writing a word on the board and then talking about it. His tests are difficult and it doesn't help that there is no study guide. He gave us questions to study, but they were not on the test. He also doesn't respond to emails by students.

reviews.comment: Great guy, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Yavuz really knows what he is talking about and the class is fairly easy if you actually put in effort ... while i understand the lectures seems super redundant at first its because a lot of it interconnects one way or another... understanding professor with passion for the subject but students like to fool around
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Yavuz is a very educated person and very well-renowned in his field. He's also very kind. I liked his lectures. However, the class was confusing for me. Expect to do the legwork in figuring out what is expected from you, as he won't give you much. There were no study guides for quizzes which were more like tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you do not take a class from Yavuz during your time at the U, you are doing yourself a disfavor. His lectures are amazing, and often you learn the most from the papers that you are assigned to write. He gives great feedback, is approachable, and is always willing to help you improve.

Professor Yavuz focuses on lectures and papers. He does not require attendance, and he will spend an entire class period using the chalkboard. Overall, his teaching methods taught me a lot about the Middle East. I find myself remembering concepts from his class two years later. My final paper was around 18 pages, but it was so, so worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend taking a class from Professor Yavuz during your time at the U. His lectures are amazing, he grades fairly, and he assigns work that actually helps you learn the material. If you want to learn something about the Middle East AND get a good grade, take a class from Yavuz.

I absolutely love Prof. Yavuz. His lectures are for the most part organized, with no power points (writes on the white board), and he is very knowledgeable. Sometimes he goes on tangents, however, they are usually very interesting. Had multiple papers, including both the midterms and final (thus, no in-class exams). Overall, learned a great deal!

Honestly, I can see where some of the other reviews are coming from. If you don't put in your best effort and pay attention, you will fail. If you are passionate about the MIDE and don't mind at least 3 unfavorable comments about Trump per class, than you will do great! Keep up with the reading, write good papers, and you will get an A.

Super boring lectures, punctuated by some funny commentary on Mormonism and Donald Trump. Participation is minimal since he asks no questions, and if you raise your hand to comment 9 times out of 10 he doesn't have his hearing aid in. Grading is relatively difficult on quizzes and papers and feedback is nil. Knows his stuff but would not recommend

There are two types of people, those who know their stuff, and those who have to ability to teach it. This professor calls into the first category. He is definitely knowledgeable in the subject, however he is very disorganized and is very textbook heavy. The amount of reading required would be alright if this were the only class on your schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was very funny and an  interesting person in general. His class is an easy A. he is easy going and what I love about him is that he likes old fashion whiteboard and marker! and  did not use NO POWER-POINTS which is great, I'm sick of all these professors showing up to classes with a laptop and just show slides throughout the  semester.
He is great and very funny.
The Best Prof at the U
He's a good professor overall. He would do the best to help you pass. However, the points he addresses in class are somewhat vague. He is so ambiguous, you never know what to expect from him.
Great Professor
I like his teaching style. One who is interested in middle east should join his class.

The professor is one of most disorganized professors on campus,  he talked about subjects that had nothing to do with the topic of the class.  He never engaged the class in any discussions, and took forever to  grade the papers. Not recommended, better take another class.
The professor seemed to know only about Turkey, did not have knowledge about other Middle Eastern countries.
Great teacher, very interesting class and he brought in other professors to teach different sections of the subject! Good class, although perhaps a little limited.
Very knowledgeable, helpful, learned a lot. If you get prepared, you should do well with the exams.

Professor never truly exist. His TA takes care of everything, a tough grader. They expect you to write a ton for every 1/1.5/2 points small assignments. And if there's ANY tiny bit flaw you won't get full points. Their standards are higher than some graduate level classes' professors. Avoid this class, run!!
Approachable, kind and willing to help students
Enjoyed learning about China. PPTs are very helpful.
He is very knowledgeable and easy to approaching.

Dennis Wei is not a very good professor although he tries his best.  He is incredibly difficult to understand, I understood maybe 50% of what he said.  Sometimes he is rude and condescending towards students, that said it's not the hardest class offered for the credit requirement it fulfills.

Professor Wei was not at all helpful in his class. Most of the study guides had irrelevant information that was polar opposites to the tests. It was very hard to understand him in class and I felt as if this was a self taught class.

Huge waste of time. Professor Wei is extremly unclear, only provides really vague powerpoints to study with. Required reading didn't follow materials well, everyone was shocked at how the midterm did not follow studyguide at all. Take a busines course elsewhere.

I genuinely tried to understand the material during class, but I often found the lectures difficult to follow. As a result, I relied more on studying outside of class, where I realized the concepts were actually much easier than how they were presented during lecture.

If you take this class be ready to rely on the PP slides to pass. They usually reflect what will be on the tests, so they are very useful. She can sometimes be hard to understand but really does want to help you pass the class. She offers a curve and gives EC if you show up to class. Group project before each test, but only take 2-3hrs. Tough final

She means well, and is very easy to get a hold of if you need to meet with her or if you need clarification. I appreciate that she asks for feedback. On the other hand, she can be difficult to understand with her accent. Doesn't offer enough in depth examples, but the slides are a good representation of what you get tested on. Material is hard!!!

Choose a different FIN3040 instructor.  Professor Pan would be better off working in the corporate world.  She is extremely knowledgable and capable, but her thick accent doesn't lend well to teaching finance concepts.  You will need to attend each lecture and study the textbook in depth.  Be prepared to work hard (3-4 hours/week outside class).

Handwriting was extremely hard to read. She was difficult to understand and taught more like we were experienced in finance instead of this being our first finance class ever. I learned everything off youtube instead. She was very unclear and didn't go into detail when working out problems.

Couldn't read anything she wrote on the board. She spent forever using ppt slides to talk about theory then spent very little time actually working out the problem on the board. She knows the subject well but can't simplify it for people. I learned everything off youtube instead and did well on tests.

The problem is she is honestly TOO smart for this class. she does calculations in her head, leaving you to guess where or how she did it. The material isnt too hard but class time is spent focusing on understanding her English through her thick accent rather than the concepts presented. She does offer great test reviews in slide form.
The class was straight forward.

She is one of the best professor I have ever had.. I learned so much from her..This is not an easy class, but spend time to read book, review lectures slide, group acitivies you will do well in exams..

She is by far one of the best professors at the university of utah. The average on our exam was a 74% and trust me that is a wonderful average for this course. Numbers don't lie. Many people don't like her because they want an easy A! She's sweet sincere and teach extremely well. She test you on materials that she ONLY TEACH! I 100% recommend her
terrible at explaining concepts spent hours studying with classmates and still did poorly 70% average for the midterm test as a class.

She reviewed examples and problems in class thoroughly. She wanted to ensure everyone understood the concepts before moving on. Is the most responsive teacher I have had for questions outside of class. I generally received an email response from her within 20 minutes after sending her a question. She is clear, explains underlying concepts well.

I would have gotten an A anyways because I actually tried and put in the work... but Pan was still the worst teacher I've had in college. She gives one easy example per chapter and then gives ridiculously hard ones on tests. Refused to turn the mic up or place it better in a class of 150... so it was easy to become lost within 5 minutes.

Barely Speaks English. Class is no help. The class average on the final was a 68%. I should have gotten a D in the class but it has to be graded on such a severe curve I got a B-. Otherwise the whole class would've failed.
The lab manual was pretty much nonexistent, but the TA still made everything clear and helped us a lot. His support really improved the whole lab experience.

The TA was very knowledgeable and approachable. He was always available to answer questions and gave helpful explanations that connected lab techniques with underlying organic chemistry concepts. His support made the advanced lab experience much more engaging and productive.

Chem 2315 was a fantastic experience. The professor made even the most difficult concepts approachable and provided clear, practical guidance in the lab. The experiments were well-structured, and I felt that my lab skills improved throughout the semester. I would definitely love to take his class again!

He's a great guy and cares about his students' success. 4 midterms and 12 quizzes make it feel like it can be a lot but he drops the lowest exam and no final. He is so sweet and would definitely take a class with him again.
Great professor

This class was super hard for me, but it made it super doable and accessible. He tried to help students as much as humanly possible. He is so sweet and super funny. The lectures do get long and slightly boring though.

Dr. Yoo was very nice, as well as being thorough and clear. He was great in terms of accessibility, and was really willing to make sure that illness or unforeseen circumstances didn't ruin your grade. Really awesome guy, and his research is super interesting too. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for Cell Science (Honors version of Cell Bio) and he was awesome. Cell Science is an incredibly difficult subject, and he made it doable. My class had 13 quizzes, 3 of which were dropped, 4 midterms, 1 of which was dropped, a presentation, and a quick paper. He made review slides and an extra credit assignment. I recommend him highly!

This course pushed me and taught me a ton. I valued it for a bunch of reasons, but mostly because it made me rethink how I write. I really appreciated all the feedback, edits and suggestions Marcie gave. I'm going to carry those lessons with me as I work toward a career in in the field.
Videos, guest lecture, videos, and guest lectures. She is more worried about the flashy then the content.

Marcie is genuinely one of the best instructors I have ever had. She did a great job at connecting this course to the real world and teaching us skills that will benefit us when we're looking for jobs post–grad. She's the kind of professor that you want to make proud, if that makes sense.

She had engaging lectures and prepares in-class activities for us to interact with each other. She treats her students as equals, and not as people below her. One of my favorite professors I have had at this school.

I took COMM 1500 with Marcie, and she was a good professor. The course was lecture and video-heavy, so attending class wasn't always too exciting. The textbook was available for free in the library. Marcie cares about her students and explains material well it is heavy topics sometimes and the one thing I didnt like was the seating chart all year.

Good class and good professor. You have to write a story every other week for more than half of the class then work on a final story. Lots of writing but she gives really good feedback and if you apply it you'll get better every time. I learned a lot and was glad to have Marcie as the professor.

She's a working journalist and knows what she's talking about, but she's a really tough grader. I learned a lot and probably would have slacked off if she would have let me. You have to work hard for it but if you do, you become a much better thinker  and writer.
Great professor. Well spoken and straight to the point. Very flexible and easy to reach for supplementary instruction. Assignments were useful and straightforward. Would highly recommend.

Great teacher. He is very flexible in nearly all aspects of the course and the assignments. Grading is very fair as long as he can tell that you put some effort in. You just need to make sure that you study and do all of the work that is assigned, and you will be guaranteed to succeed.

Lectures were clear and easy to follow. 
All lectures posted to Canvas after class and accessible. 
Assessments were fair and set up well. If you put in any amount of effort, you will be successful in this class. 
Would take this instructor again if I could for any economics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a reasonable but very traditional professor. Lectures, homework, exams. That's it. There isn't any hand-holding, like dropped exams, extra credit, videos, practice exams. I wish he would have discussed the bigger context of the material and it was sometimes hard to tell which formulas he gave us we needed. The labs were poorly run though.

Dr. Young's "Analog Circuit Design" course was much better than his Circuits 3 course. The material is very advanced, but the course is structured in a way that continually builds in a sensible way. He posts notes, but they are hard to understand. However, if you attend lectures, he is great at slowing things down and making these easier.

He was good. The exams are cummulative. The final was easy except he added a topic that we only briefly went over in class and never had on the homeworks so that was annoying. You MUST attend lectures, he doesn't do any recordings. He also doesn't give any kind of review for the exams, but the homeworks are pretty good practice for what you'll see.
Don't, just don't.

Avoid this professor at all costs. For the past two months, every week, there's a lab, a project, and a homework assignment to submit. His exams are ridiculously long for how much time is permitted and people often run out of time. Just avoid!!!

Gets into the weeds during lectures in what seems like everything that you won't actually get tested / given homework on. When it comes to things you need to learn for the course he gives very short explanations and what seems like no actual examples in class. His tests are not atrocious but he has lied about what sources will be on the test.

This may only be for 2280, but he was awful. Nothing learned in lecture was applied in lab or even a lot of HW. Midterm 2 contained the entirety of midterm 1 + the new content. He also lied about the content that would be on midterm 2. The homeworks are copy and paste of other professors. There's also no practice material to prepare for anything.
Every exam is cumulative and content from old material are harder on the following exam. His he assignments are long but they help tremendously with exam prep. His deadlines are annoying tho

Darrin Young is probably my favorite ECE professor. Lectures are very well-prepared and topics flow logically. Homework can be long, oftentimes taking several hours to complete, but Dr. Young is willing to help if you get stuck. Exams are very similar to HW, and very fair IMO. I highly recommend any EE/CE take this class, you'll learn a TON.

Lecture notes are posted. LABS are disorganized and brutal!

reviews.comment: Professor Young was an extremely good professor. He was a fair grader and his lectures were very good and helpful for the homeworks and labs. Big workload, but that's how any ECE class will be.

(Spring 2019) Professor Young has provided the best lectures I've experienced at the U. He relates the concepts to industry and his own experience. The labs didn't have a stable deadline, but both the professor and the TAs were extremely understanding. They would ALWAYS push back assignments if requested which caused for a stockpile at the end.

The entire class was very poorly organized. He has no idea how to use Canvas, and within the last couple weeks (including finals week) He's assigned every assignment, lab, and project that he forgot to give us over the course of the semester. I haven't gotten to bed before 3AM for past three weeks. Working sun up to sun down. Massive workload.

Unreasonable deadlines. Uses recycled homework, NEVER wants to go over homework/exam review questions. 2 midterms, 1 final,  9-hws, 5 labs, 3 projects. Take it from someone else. Other professors give you a chance to retake exams and final is optional. NOT this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Yeagle is a very empathetic professor! She is a great person. The workload was a lot but because it was a half-semester class. Just put a lot of effort and you'll do well.

reviews.comment: She's nice and caring even in an online course. She also makes a lot of typos which I find funny. If you're taking the half semester course, there's a lot of reading to do. There's also a group project where you record a presentation together.

Doctor Yeagle was extremely nice and the assignments in class can be interesting but the reading was overwhelming. It is a half a semester class so expect a lot of reading and be prepared to fall behind on the reading because there are too much.

Took this half-term course online and wow was there a lot of reading! Expect to finish three books and read multiple articles per day. The modules are chaotic, but the grading is pretty easy! FILL OUT THE STUDY GUIDES for the tests! There's also a group project that was tricky to coordinate. I would recommend this course by Yeagle:)

reviews.comment: Amazing instructor! Was quick to message back with any questions I had while taking the online course. I would recommend taking this course if you want to cover an elective.

reviews.comment: I took two economic classes from Professor Yeagle and they have been some of my favorite classes ever! Professor Yeagle is incredibly kind and she took the time to give thoughtful feedback on all of my assignments. The things we learned about opened my eyes and gave me a valuable perspective on the world. It was a privilege to take these classes!
She was sweet but too much reading. I honestly couldn't keep up.

reviews.comment: I took health economics with Professor Yeagle and absolutely loved it! It was a half semester class, so there was quite a bit of readings and small assignments each week. Dr. Yeagle has the potential to have a wonderful class. She is very nice and introduces some really great material. HOWEVER, the amount of work she gives in her class is extremely overwhelming to the point where you can't learn or take the time to really grasp anything she teaches. You're forced to get the material done mindlessly to keep up.

The study guides are necessary for the test but ask stupid questions that are unrelated to course content and end up being around 30 pages of content per test, which is every other WEEK. its made stupidly hard for no reason

I think it is ridiculous and needs to be evaluated.

I loved Anne! She was very cheerful and was super insightful on a lot of topics. All of her quizzes and exams were open book, and pretty much directly off of the study guides that she provided. The only downside was all of the reading you had to do to fill out the study guides.

Anne is kind person-HOWEVER, she is definitely not suited to host an online class. Anne is amazing! She was my favorite professor all through our college. The knowledge I learned from this class I carry on currently with my career. She is caring and kind and focuses on mindfulness!

Professor Yeagle is amazing! Shes great at what she does and I loved learning from her. Shes really smart, caring, funny, and strong. Her expectations are very clear and the work is easy and interesting just as long as you pay attention and show up.

Dr. Yeagle is amazing! So responsive and caring however the class was very disorganized. There was SO MUCH going on it was hard to figure out what we were supposed to be turning in. reviews.comment: Class feels very left-leaning politically. I've taken two classes from her, and she assigns great books to read. She never really uses graphs or numbers more complicated than a percentage.

Anne is such a good teacher. This was my second class with her, and it did not disappoint. Read the homework and do the review sheets she gives you and you will do great on the tests and in the class there is also a group presentation where you will learn a lot and then present.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Anne is so wonderful! Her Syllabus is very clear in her expectations. She is also extemely understanding and always willing to help in anything she can. I LOVED this class and have learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Yeagle's class is a paradox, her class instead of having mid-term or final exams, she will give lots of quizzes or exams during the semester, which is nice, but be aware, with the quizzes, there also have group presentations, individual presentation, and group papers, AND TONS OF READING!! and never ever miss single one of the class. stress out
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Yeagle is my favorite professor at the U. Economics is a topic that can very easily become dry and detached, despite having enormous implications on human livelihood. She makes it very personal, thoughtful, and will make you consider your own beliefs without attacking you. Everyone should take a class from her, seriously! Take the class!

This woman isn't just a stellar professor, but an amazing person. She is smart, funny, and strong. She encourages open and real discussions. Begins class with a mindfulness exercise. Great group project with relevant topics. Awesome guest lecturers. Assigned readings are a must, they are engaging and important. Learning from her should be mandatory

This was one of my favorite classes of all time. Dr. Yeagle is strong, smart, and caring. She'll make you consider the deeper implications of every reading. This class will challenge you without murdering you. I'm going to take classes from her in the future!

Easily the most left-wing teacher I've taken at the U. The class is labor econ, but you will spend the entire semester talking about subjects from socialism and Marxism to white privilege and the evils of America and its corporations. This isn't inherently bad; students should have their beliefs challenged. But just know it's very political

Starts each class with meditation/mindfulness. Lots of articles to read along with a couple of books, some have study guides. Gives extra credit on tests. Likes when students speak up in class. Willing to talk about potentially controversial topics. If you are easily offended, do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Yeagle is by far one of the best professors I have had at the U. She is clear with her assignments and grading, gives her students every opportunity to succeed, and she makes learning fun! Not only is she professional, but she is personable. If you are an economics student and you don't take her class you are missing out!

Half semester class, and only once per week. Zero exams, and the assignments were extremely simple. The class is designed to introduce you to the HSP major, so it's super laid back. There was a group project near the end which I didn't love, but it wasn't difficult by any means. Anne is very caring and understanding, and was very lax on grading.

Her class was so interesting and has been my favorite class ever! Since it was a half sem. course, we had to read A LOT, and 80% of every class period consisted of an exam. Her exams weren't hard if you actually do your readings or finish your study questions! most of the exam questions came from that. 10/10 would take a class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was a half-semester class but she was an awesome teacher. Always willing to help with any questions you may have. Textbook isn't required. We wrote several short-essays and did a group project towards the end. If you show up to class and participate you will get an easy A. Love her! Will take her for other classes

This class was only half a semester but it went by pretty quick. It was really easy so long as you did you work. A few assignments that were pretty straight forward and then a group project that was kind of annoying but yet still pretty easy.

She should be teaching philosophy,  as mentioned by others, she is a very nice person and an easy A.  However, her Sex Drugs and Crime class has almost nothing to do with economics, she never mentioned the black market once during the entire semester.  Her, extreme leftist political agenda can be hard to tolerate.

Yeagle is an interesting professor who has a lot of life experiences. She loves group discussions. She takes attendance every day and it adds up over time so you better show up. Her class is super easy so just show up and you can pass.

Anne Yeagle is one of the most caring, fair, and helpful professors I've ever had.  I truly learned so much from her class.  She is really open to opinions and doesn't hesitate to voice hers, which leads to great class discussions.  If you do the reading and participate in class, you will get an A. Honestly, she's one of the best at the U.

Anne Yeagle is an amazing educator. She has a clear understanding of material, excellent communicator and she is very helpful. Sex, Drugs and Crime was not only a great class, but it was complete with great teacher as well.

LOVED THIS CLASS! Anne is a great teacher, the course content was interesting and made you think, and the class isn't very difficult. There are quizzes nearly every two class periods which is a little tough, but as long as you study and attend class its easy to do well
Easy A, She's helpful, class material is outdated though.  Interesting subjects but class feels redundant and very boring.

Anne was very helpful when it came to understanding material that can be at times hard to understand. Her liberal approach also was a plus. While there ere times we both agreed to disagree she was fair and sweet. Learned alot from this class.
Awesome teacher!  One of the best at the U.  If you go she'll help you! You have to go though or you have no chance of getting an A
little odd at times but the class was enjoyable, very clear on whats expected....no mid term or final...small quizzes virtually every week

Really cares about her students. Will help anyway she can. Had a lot of class work, quiz every week, 1 pg paper almost once a week, group 30 min presentation, however work not too difficult. If you miss 1 class it will be harder to get an A. missing 2-3 or more will make it impossible.

As long as you attend class and finish the readings an A is in your future.  Yeagle is extremely helpful and approachable; however, she has A LOT of energy (a little difficult after a night on the town).  Labor Economics is definitely worth taking from Yeagle.
She is very nice and willing to help if you show real intent and interest in the subject
world expanding

I loved this class. I learned so much in this class and I liked going to hear her stories.She keeps the class interesting and has a way to relate everything she talks about. She is by far the best teacher that I have had at the U.
Great professor~her teaching style is the most effective of anyone I have ever taken classes from.

Perhaps one of the Best teachers at the U I've had so far! She really wants you to pass her class and its not that difficult. No comprehensive tests overloaded with bogus questions. Just straightforward mini tests on chapters learned with topics covered. If I could clone her for a professor for every other class I have to take I'd definitely do it!
Get professor... I loved her.  She really does all she can to help you succeed.  Very interesting topics.  Just do the reading and study and you will be fine.
she was my favorite professor so far, she is resppectful to everyone even when she doesn't agree with their view.

This class and teacher are great! I learned so much and her style is the best.  Just have quizzes on the material you learn in class, and no comprehensive tests.  She is the best econ teacher I've had at the U and I am almost graduating.  She's Money!!
No Comments
very good teacher...loved her class!!
I love this professor, I took 4 Economics classes from her.  She is easy to understand and her classes are straight forward.  You get plenty of time to discuss different topics.
Nothing special, but she is fair and her tests are easy.
I thought it was gonna suck but  I learned a lot from her!  It was easier than I thought it would be.  Good DV credit.
No Comments
Great teacher and she chose a great textbook, too.  Would definitely recommend.
No Comments
No Comments
She is an awesome instructor. Very helpful and nice.

She is the worst teacher ever. Don't ever take any classes from her. She speaks too fast, doesn't post any material online, doesn't explain homework, puts down students who give wrong answers in class, and gives pop quizzes only when she sees students leaving her class. She is literally out to dock points any way possible.

Worst teacher I've ever had. She gave me a zero for a quiz because it was the day my stepdad passed away and I didn't come to class. She reads off the power point, class is boring, she doesn't make sense, and she grades hard. I didn't learn anything from her. She speaks broken English and gets mad when you're confused. Can't believe she's a teacher
She was very helpful and hands on with her instruction. She in very talented and helped each student's project become better and more professional. Genuinely interested in her students.
She's a horrible teacher, and she doesn't explain herself well

She is just reading off the lecture that another professor wrote. She is very unclear and kind of makes up the grading and assignments as she goes along. I would definitely not recommend her even if you love the classs subject because she is a tough grader

She knows what she is talking about but does not do a very good job at explaining concepts to you. Refers you to a website or her lecture slides if you are confused. She gets mad and snappy with you if you don't understand the concepts. She is a tough grader, if you do one little thing wrong or you don't do it "her way" she docks you major points.

Very humurous professor, for these types of professors she is very outstanding and is also very helpful and interactive during lectures. Highly recommend I came into the class expecting it to be one of those classes and professors I was completely wrong.

I enjoyed the content of the class, but the format may not be for everyone. The lectures were prerecorded and had to be watched before classes, and classes were used to complete group assignments. Shundana is an great professor and is knowledgeable and approachable. The course is somewhat disorganized but thankfully I had a good group.
Tenure is a crazy thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great personality! She knows her stuff as well. You do feel like you are hearing from an expert. But she isn't necessarily great at lectures. Lots of quizzes, homeworks, and readings that will drive you insane. Her lectures are rants. Class averages on tests are low, and I didn't see someone get a perfect score ever. Readings are vital for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Yusaf is a very funny person, but also a highly disorganized one. Her grading is all over the place, and your final grade will not match the one on Canvas at all. She has very unorthodox ideas, and chooses weird subjects to focus on. I did not learn much from her, because her lectures consist mostly of rambling and getting side tracked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most disorganized people I've ever met. Her teaching style is extremely confusing, and she uses big terms without ever explaining them. Her slides are terrible, and have so many words that you would never be able to read. She doesn't know how to receive feedback without feeling like she's being personally attacked.

I really disliked the group project system that she implemented for my class which made turning in assignments unnecessarily complicated. So much is in the workbook but it is very useful. She is interesting as a professor and maybe would be better in smaller courses, but she has very long presentations and I didn't enjoy the class much.

All you did in class was fill out a packet, you had to watch lectures and take quizzes before. I had an A in the class and the day before the final the grades for every assignment were put in and my grade dropped to an 80.3%, I was stressed because I realized I was unprepared for the final and doing a lot worse than I thought.

I could not stand listening to the 3 hour lectures, it was information overload and I didn't gain much from it. One lecture she stated, 50 minutes in, that she didn't know what she was saying until like 3 minutes ago... She also pointed out how the class looked so sad but didn't give us many breaks.

Shundana Yusaf is really disorganized. Her Canvas page is a nightmare and her lectures are incomprehensible. She doesn't organize her statements well and nothing she says makes sense. I like her as a person, and she's really funny, but I haven't learned anything from her, especially concerning architecture.

There are so many lectures each week and the quizzes are extremely specific and timed. She rambles on and often her sources contradict one another. I can't tell if what she is saying is factually true. The only thing that got me through was a group of friends that I made and we took the quizzes together. Avoid doing the work alone or you'll suffer!

If you are taking this class as a Gen-ed, DON'T!!! Unless you like listening to a billion slides lecture with no textbook or even clear slide, very limited timing in quizzes, and crazy hard exams, then be my guest and take the class. I don't find this class helpful at all it's just anxiety.

This professor needs a serious overhaul to her lectures. Instead of having actual notes on a slide to take, she shows a couple pictures and then describes them without ever having a point. Makes it incredibly difficult to take notes and figure out what you need to know. This lack of clear lectures shows on the quizzes when most wasn't discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most of the class is actually discussing religions rather than architecture. It is also hard to focus with her constant comments on how much she hates trump, men in general and her clear disdain for 99% of the religions we covered. I may not believe in those religions either, but that doesn't mean I should be dismissive of those who do, ya know?

I understand that things are hard for the professor due to covid and the various limitations, but I have not found her class structure to make any sense, especially online, the random and oddly specific quizzes are absolutely terrible, and they're something that the students have asked her about but regardless they are just not good at all.
She is very nice and a good professor, but once she sees people slack off or not care about the class. She will make the class hard for you.

Shundana is an absolute riot, there will never not be a class period where you laugh. She does three or so mini quizzes during each class to make sure you're paying attention and have read the lecture. These quizzes and the two tests (midterm and final) can be done in groups, so fear not. Definitely would recommend her to another student.
Dont take this for an easy gen ed. She is an amazing teacher, but its a hard class to get an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was absolutely phenomenal.  The lectures were spectacular and she has a lighthearted and hilarious approach to the content.  This class was more about the historical evolution of architecture and was really more of a social sciences class, rather than an art class.  Attendance was mandatory; she takes roll every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This class was hard because of how she grades. Your entire grade is based off in class online quizzes. Sometimes there are canvas/internet issues, or if you miss a class and there are quizzes your grade will drop dramatically. I wish she let you make up quizzes or offered extra credit papers. Her outfits are amazing. Wish I could take for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is tough and extremely feminist. Also hates Trump (yes, she makes sure you know this during her lectures). If you miss more than 2 times in the class, she will drop your grade. Got a bad grade because I missed class. Class isn't really about the history of architecture, but the history of religion. Tests are in groups of 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is not a class for the light hearted. Needs attention and notes.

I originally took this class cause I thought it was like building stuff out of balsa wood... it's not... She's knows what she's talking about and her tests are group tests, so sit next to smart people that will pull their load. She also tends to not be too clear on what's important information. She also hates historical men a lot, but deal with it.
She aiight

Great, passionate professor. She skips around a lot and doesn't emphasize the things that are actually important, almost everything is emphasized. You take every test in groups of three and it is miserable if you have slackers in your group because it takes all three to search for exact wording in notes. She has some interesting stuff to say.

This professor is not organized, the class should be renamed the history of religion and how it affects architecture.  We spent at least two weeks going over how homo-sapiens built stick huts and put art on walls. If youre actually interested in architecture, then this is not the class for you.  Easy "A" with smart people in your group.

Lectures had tons of information and sometimes they are hard to follow. ALL the tests are taken in groups of three, even the final. Tests are also open book and open note.   Pro Tip: Download all her lectures before the tests. There is key information in the notes section.

This class is definitely not an easy Gen Ed class. She is a super intelligent woman and seems to make a not so tough subject into a really hard and confusing one. Has group tests that are open book, internet and notes and yet it is the hardest test you could ever take. If you decide to take this class, GOOD LUCK!

If you're hoping for an easy Gen Ed, this is not the class for you. The class is extremely in-depth for a level 1000 class and is overwhelming. Shundana is extremely intelligent and would be great for a major in Architecture, but the depths the class goes to are way too deep for a Gen Ed.
Awesome professor! Took for Intro to Architecture 1615 my freshman year for an FF credit. Great lectures, lots of reading, super funny and entertaining.

Took her Intro to Architecture class this past semester. You HAVE TO TAKE NOTES if you have any desire to pass. All of the quizzesexams were with a partner, so that makes it a little easier. Very awesome at engaging with the students. Will definitely take her grad classes when I get there.
I loved this teacher and this class!! She's really interested in helping you learn, not just getting through the lectures. She's flexible, incredibly knowledgeable, and hilarious.  AMAZING teacher.

This professor makes a gen ed class extremely difficult as he is completely disorganized on Canvas. Instructions for projects would be in two different locations and extremely lengthy, making it nearly impossible to understand the actual prompt or criteria. And have fun with the 70-question syllabus quiz that's impossible to get 100 on.

He is actually my dad. Pretty solid Dad, I think I got pretty lucky, but I know how you guys feel. He lectures to us on a daily basis, just about any topic he feels like. I am glad I don't have to take his class though lol I think I'd die.

If you take this professor, get ready to get a million announcements from him for "optional readings". He also is SO wordy with his instructions. It ends up being so confusing because there so much unnecessary info. He just needs to get to the point so the actual important info doesn't get lost. Do not recommend him.

I don't exactly know where to start. The truth is, I really can't rate this professor. He may be fantastic, but the instructions for the first assignment, when copied and pasted into Google Docs were 11 pages long!  Eleven!  And at the end of reading every single page, I was still not clear about what the assignment actually was! Good luck.
Ok class, if you are one who likes to read a lot of papers and and work independently this class is for you. Otherwise I'd pick another class with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for credit but didn't know what I was getting myself into, the professor has excellent communications skills with the students and seems like he cares but doesn't make up for it when the class begins. Don't recommend taking fcs from this professor ever again.

Average professor. Communication is great at start but once things pick up as a facilities class the professor will leave you in the dust. Asked the professor many times for options to improve within the class but he refused my messages and failed to show my class as taken under school portal. Awful experience 3/10.

Professor Yu is honestly disorganized. The assignment descriptions are at least 4 pages long. His comments on papers can come off as rude. He posts a huge long announcement every week. Honestly, he grades impossibly the average score is always under a passing grade. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone. It's boring and hard he isn't nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is one of the hardest classes I've taken. There's tons of reading, some really complex stuff, and some serious projects. Professor Yu really cares and gives very specific instructions. I've emailed him several times over the semester and he's written back with more care and detail than any other professor I've had. (free textbook pdfs too!)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Yu is a great professor but he does except you to do A LOT of reading. Overall if you put in the effort by participating in the class discussions and taking the quizzes/exams, the class is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Other than the 5 exams, you just have to work for your grade but if you take it online even exams are online and open note. He is a hard grader BUT very fair, if you have questions you can ask him and he will help you. Not a bad class at all and there is only very few assignments, just be prepared to work.

So. Much. Reading (and writing). Each week includes a chapter from the text book, 3-4 articles (some are quite lengthy as well), a video lecture and about 20-30 slides that are all required reading. Exams are open book/notes, but you have to know what youre talking about when it comes to the writing assignments. Hardest class I've taken to date.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Zhou's class was quite boring, and you most definitely do not need the textbook. That being said, it is very straightforward and he gives good feedback. There are three quizzes and one exam throughout two weeks of the online course. Be prepared to be bombarded with emails and announcements though. Not the worst, not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The online Summer semester you have to spend 16 hours a week, reading, studying you take 13 quizzes, 5 exams 3 quizzes will not be counted and 1 exams will not be counted. reading 1-2 chapters/wk. But each module is 3 weeks long. If you read and take notes it is okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yu is very engaged and truly wants you to succeed. There was a ton of reading! He expects a lot and "suggestions" are actually requirements. He expects you to engage in discussions. 2 papers were required along with the weekly readings and lectures. You will work for your grade but he is fair. Challenging course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The course is entirely online, & is by far the worst organized course I've ever had. I've had to remind him twice to open up modules so I could continue working - one was opened 1 week late, yet we are still expected to do 2 weeks of work in 1 week or fall behind. Feedback is confusing & the content requirements for our papers change weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Yu truly cares about his students, so if at any point any concept didn't make sense he was easy to reach and was always willing to help. The class consisted of 4 midterms, an optional final, and 13 quizzes for which he drops the lowest 3. You MUST participate in the group discussions (5 total) to get an A in this class.

Professor Yu cares about his students. Yu is very accessible if needed answering any questions or concerns I had promptly. Lots of open book quizzes (although like previously mentioned they are basically 4 hour scavenger hunts), 5 tests with lowest dropped (optional final? Yes.), a few participation posts, and some assignments. Very organized.

This class was fun, but just because of the good textbook and because I was interested in the material. The tests were basically 4-hour scavenger hunts and there are about 13 of them throughout the semester, plus exams. Also, the way he writes the exams is a little confusing because English is his second language. Overall a decent professor.

Best online professor I've had. He is fully engaged and very communicative. It's a 4 credit course, so expect to work for it. I'm not the biggest fan of online courses, but I would be if they were run like Pro. Yu runs his. Organized, helpful, engaging. Bravo!

Online class that was well organized. 4 credit class so there is a lot of busy work. Prof. Yu is willing to meet with students for study sessions prior to exams.  Open book tests are not easy; if you don't know the answer you need to know where to find it. Study and you will do well in this class. Online is convenient for those who have busy lives.
NOT an easy class, but Prof. Yu employs some great tactics to make it easier for students to learn the material and do well!
I definitely enjoyed this class.  It was difficult but not impossible.  He returned emails quickly.  I also loved the textbook.

The class was easy, but the professor is a poor lecturer, so I rarely attended. I taught myself the material with LLMs. The infrastructure was lacking: the TA was terrible, grading was painfully slow, and emails went unanswered. Tests were poorly designed. Find a different professor!

I took PHYS 2210, but this class was super easy. Never went to lecture and passed all the tests. Discussion was very helpful and it was good working on problems with friends. Literally so chill that on the last exam I heard someone playing Minecraft during the exam.Homework was good and you always got credit for trying, even if you made mistakes.

Very chill course. Two lectures and a discussion per week, I showed up to all of them but you can choose whatever works best for you. Homework is sometimes challenging but never felt like busy work, and the exams are generally easy. The class just felt good, and despite learning some very advanced topics, I didn't feel a ton of pressure.

YP was not an easy professor. He leaves you in the dark the whole semester about your letter grade. The course is pretty rigorous, but YP goes very quickly and is quite harsh when you ask questions. Prepare to do a lot of homework and say goodbye to your social life. Exams are pulled from textbook so that is a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: YP was funny and was clear about what was necessary for a grade in concept. Tests were homework questions. Main qualms are that he is a harsh grader and doesn't believe in grade inflation(Which doesn't work in a place with mass grade inflation). Office hours were effectively necessary, and while helpful, killed enjoyment in the subject itself.

Expect a large amount of homework, and many hours in the tutoring center. You are expected to know everything in the textbook even if it is not covered in class. Pacing is very rushed. Feedback is almost nonexistent on homework and tests. Expect to have no clue what your actual grade is as the class is not curved until final grades are released.

Just sign up for William Nesse or Wesley Hamilton. YP covers twice the material and doesn't provide outside of class resources. His grading is very harsh and comes in late, but you only get minutes points, no useful feedback. He wasn't a bad teacher, but he doesn't qualify as good either. Expect too much time in the tutoring center.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Lee makes his class work hard, but he never pulls any tricks. His goals are clearly stated "this test is based on homework. This final is based on old tests" giving opportunity to prepare. He is a lenient grader to account for how hard he makes his class work. Would recommend for high level math.
Good professor, but I took the honor's version. Don't take honor's unless your prepared to work fast, a lot, and hard. The professor's funny and a lenient grader, but you have to know your stuff.

YP is tough but fair! His tests are based strongly off the HW. He doesn't throw any curve balls. He is open to arguments for better grades, and he curves heavily (at one point, 50% was a B-). He tests a lot, but the tests are only 8 questions and all based off hw. He is good at pacing and is willing to stop for questions. Would take again!

Excellent professor. The class is proofs based, but as long as you understand the theorems, and can prove them, the tests are a breeze. All test problems come from the homework or the book, nothing is out of left field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He's approach is pretty good. A lot of midterms and a comprehensive final based on those midterms.Keeps you on toes throughout the semester, but that helps you ace the final.Very decent personality and great professor.Very approachable too.
I would strongly recommend this professor. His class is a lot of work, but it is well worth the effort. He is very good at explaining difficult concepts, and willing to reiterate or answer questions.

Very good Professor for people interested in the subject. His goal is for everyone to gain a deep understanding of the subject material taught. If you want to take his classes for the easy grade rather than for understanding material, I would not recommend him.

Professor Hecht's class was not hard with few assignments. He's also an easy grader. This class was an extremely easy A (just go to class, he grades attendance). My only issue was how irrelevant his lectures were (also confusing), and he doesn't explain assignments well, so you have to ask questions (but he'll explain it to you).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hecht was great! Some of the media or videos he'd show were really strange but still interesting. Super nice and chill professor, and he was a pretty easy grader.

Very chill professor. You get three papers to write for the whole semester, you choose your own topic and keep it throughout all your work. Go to class because he tracks involvement and attendance. He is a very nice and easy grader. For in class work you will be doing A LOT of free writes. I wish he was better at explaining assignments.

Prof. Hecht is the absolute best! He makes everything very engaging and relevant. We spent a lot of time talking about current events, analyzing music videos, and looking at sort of obscure media. He genuinely cares about people's opinions and we did tons of small group work. Other than the 3 essays we did there wasn't really any outside work.
Quiet guy, but what he says counts. It's important to participate of your own will and put effort into bringing deliverables to get the most of critique. Very talented designer.

Great human being. Down to earth and makes you feel included and inspired. He cares about his students and the work that you bring to the table. He isn't a harsh grader, but he explains everything extensively and gives you a decent amount of time for projects and assignments. To me, zak is more than a professor.

Zak is a chill professor, and he gives reasonable feedback. I just wished he would add descriptions and instructions to the rubrics! It was pretty hard to follow up on some of them. Always pay attention to what he says! Also, he needs to be more organized when creating assignments. But, besides that, he's a cool dude; I recommend his classes.

Provided a unique contrast to Thi (The other lecturer for this course), brought a calm, methodical, design-informed mentality to the class that really benefited the lecture material. Gives good feedback if prompted. 100% A get out of it what you put in kind of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jose no doubt knows his stuff about game design, but that does not mean he is a great lecturer. He just doesn't know how to translate his knowledge into an engaging lesson. Thankfully only lab took attendance so I eventually stopped coming to lecture and just went to lab and that was chill. I will be avoiding him in the future.

Jose's course consists largely of huge difficult writing assignments, and small "Game Design Snacks" that are almost impossible to receive a full score on. You must write 1,900 page essays, and read through a literal book and all previous Game Snack discussion submissions to make sure that you don't write about the same subject as someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:

reviews.comment: Slimy is the best word to describe Jose Zagal. As an ethics professor, he made us buy his own book from Amazon. His slides are poorly designed, he barely knows Canvas, and he treats students poorly. This guy has issues with self-esteem or something because he has a gigantic chip on his shoulder. I would not take this class or talk to Jose Zagal.

Green flags: passionate. 
Red Flags: No recorded lectures, very bad at using Canvas, no posted slides, boring labs (honestly why have labs), mostly a class about board games, unclear grading requirements

Loved the lectures, but I wasn't a fan of the grading, readings, and poor feedback. The readings were needlessly long (30-40 pages) and we were required to read 2-4 per week.

If you want to do well, cite the readings when responding to exam questions, and be VERY specific in your responses - refer to the text/question. HIGHLIGHT THE READINGS!

reviews.comment: Be aware of the Exam

reviews.comment: The lectures were excellent, but the assignments were horrible, and the TA grading was awful.

This guy is an egregious professor.

First, he forced us, in his Ethics in Video Games class to purchase his own book from Amazon. Not very ethical. The people not in his class should buy his book, we paid to have him and his insights, but all we got was the book. He seems to be discontent with himself and takes it out on his students. Do not take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ethics in games is a fun class! I took it in the summer session so we basically need to finish three fat papers in less than two month, and we also need to write a lot in midterm and finals. However the class is well organized so you will have enough time for the draft, feedback and refinements of your paper if you are on the track.

reviews.comment: this professor sucks, want us to come up with 100 different board games within 4 days, he always think his idea was true but ignore the facts that not all of us wanted to be a game designer, we are taking course just because it's required, avoid him if possible.

Lied about a participation thing during a TA session, gave little information on a midterm (Class average was 11/20), went to TA session for help, and basically told me to just "Study More" with no extra help on where to go and what areas would be best. One of the most frustrating teachers to be under after 4 years of being here.

I took the summer block class but assignments, participation, and exams were all reasonably paced. Readings were a bit rough but I'm sure a regular semester would be much easier to manage. Take notes and try to participate, but discussions and Zagal's personality make the class engaging and enjoyable. Hope I have an excuse to take Zagal again tbh

The grading in this class is unbelievably harsh. The average on the assignments is always around a D, sometimes a C. I don't see any reason why it should be this way considering most people probably try their best to please the criteria for this class. It's just never good enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Genuinely miserable class. I wanted to like this class so badly. Some of the lectures are genuinely interesting! But the amount of what feels like pure busy work that is assigned is ridiculous. I was forced into taking this as a Junior due to the low level of sections offered and as a Junior I DO NOT HAVE TIME FOR BUSY WORK!
